{"artifact_digest":"sha256:e7efd8b61a5711af4d596bc1d1c7e829fa34028b3da8963bdc574ef24e27fd99","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/e7/e7efd8b61a5711af4d596bc1d1c7e829fa34028b3da8963bdc574ef24e27fd99.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:e9089ff16a3df49fc1d91f4ede3602b031163aba909e7ad3b360042dd0d5187d","bundle_entry_key":"autoregressive-forward-kl-padded-mask-oracle-separation","bundle_id":"population.t410-padded-nested-mask-oracle-separation-v1","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"oracle complexity; average-case complexity; autoregressive models; forward KL; random masks","draft":"w739/bundle_008.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:complexity.cryptography:autoregressive-forward-kl-padded-mask-oracle-separation","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# A padded, nested-mask oracle for the forward-KL separation

T410-w739-C015 v1. Target: 2. Kind: moved.
Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty priority is claimed. This is a direct
oracle construction, rather than an invocation of the reported IR2 oracle.
It does not assert the additional, unnecessary hypothesis H of C013.

## Statement and model

There exists one Boolean oracle O such that NP^O is not contained in
P^O/poly, but for every fixed uniform polynomial-time O-relative family of
nonnegative rational weights w_L(x), |x|=L, with polynomial output bit length
and positive normalizer, and every fixed positive integer c, there are
polynomial-size O-relative AR models Q_L with polynomial-bit dyadic next-bit
probabilities satisfying KL(P_L||Q_L)<=L^{-c} for all sufficiently large L.
Finite exceptions can be hardwired into nonuniform models. Polynomial time
uses the usual explicit-query oracle model: writing a query of length q
costs at least q steps; oracle circuit size bounds query length and count.
The quantifier over weight families is uniform. No polynomial-time compiler
with instance-uniform approximation guarantees is asserted.

The hardest step is compatibility: a weight computation can read smaller
helper queries, but those queries must reveal no information about the
fresh mask used to truncate that weight. Sections 3 and 4 prove this step.

## 1. Base table and random masks

For every y of length n>=2, independently choose a uniform bit b_y and a
uniform n^2-bit string z_y. The unique accepted witness in row y is b_y z_y.
The base interface B(y,w) is 1 exactly for this witness, and 0 otherwise.
Encode a base query with an initial tag and self-delimited y,w, so its length
is at least n^2. Invalid encodings answer 0. The finitely many shorter rows
can be fixed arbitrarily. In particular

    A={y: there exists z in {0,1}^{n^2}, B(y,1z)=1}

is in NP^O, and its length-n truth bits are the independent bits b_y.

Independently of the entire base table, choose masks as follows. Put
a_n=floor(n^{1/3}), g_n=max(1,floor(a_n/4)), H_{n,0}={0,1}^n. For
1<=j<g_n, choose H_{n,j} uniformly among the subsets of H_{n,j-1} of size
2^{n-j*a_n^2}. These integer sizes are valid: j*a_n^2<=n/4. Choices for
different n are independent; successive choices use their conditional
uniform laws. Put H_{n,j}=empty for j>=g_n. A nonempty-mask step has
conditional per-row probability delta_n=2^{-a_n^2}. For fixed D, eventually
g_n>D and |H_{n,D}|=2^{n-D*a_n^2}>=2^{floor(n/2)}.

All random variables form a countable product of finite probability spaces.

## 2. Helper queries, defined by induction on their actual length

The other interface is a padded helper query of actual length N. Its fields
are a deterministic machine description M, input length L, unary clock T,
integers a,p, a prefix h with |h|<L, and a bit index j<=p. Require p>=2,
a>=1, all fields fit in a header of length at most T^2, L,p,a,|M|<=T,
and T^4<=N. Remaining padding is zero. Invalid requests answer 0.
The actual length N is a parameter of the helper, not just padding ignored
by its meaning. One AR model will use the SAME N at every prefix and digit.

For this helper define k(N,n)=max(1,floor(log_n N)), n>=2, using exact
integer comparisons, and let K_n=H_{n,k(N,n)}. Simulate M for at most T
steps on each L-bit x, using the actual answers to all helper queries it
makes. Such queries have length at most T<=N^{1/4}<N; they have already
been defined by the induction. Base queries are answered from B, except
that the entire simulation is discarded as soon as it queries ANY base
row y in K_{|y|}. On a nondiscarded terminating run, decode its output as a
nonnegative rational weight; invalid or negative outputs have weight zero.
Call the resulting finite weight v_N(x). Let R_N be its normalized law if
its sum is positive, and uniform otherwise.

Let alpha=2^{-a}, S_N=(1-alpha)R_N+alpha U_L. For the requested prefix h,
form the exact next-one probability s=S_N(h1)/S_N(h). Round down to the
grid of mesh 2^{-p} and clip the numerator to [1,2^p-1]. Return digit j
of the resulting p-bit numerator. This defines one Boolean oracle, by
induction on N, for every realization of the base table and masks. All sums
are finite; the oracle has no computational-time restriction. Arbitrary
rational denominators therefore cause no definitional problem. For each
fixed query the recursion is finite and the answer is measurable.

Two facts are useful. First, truncation can be described on the untruncated
reference run: v_N(x) equals its reference weight if none of that run's base
rows lies in K, and equals zero otherwise. To see this, compare the runs up
to their first visit to K. Second, truncation is a subweight for EVERY M;
no monotonicity of M's original weight in oracle answers is assumed.

## 3. Dependency and fresh-mask lemma

If a helper of length N can access base block n, even indirectly, then
n^2<=T<=N^{1/4}. Thus log_n N>=8. Put k=floor(log_n N). Any smaller helper
called by its simulated machine has length N'<=T, and, if it can access n,

    k(N',n)<=floor((log_n N)/4)<=floor((k+1)/4)<=k-1.

If N'<n^8, it cannot access block n at all: its clock is smaller than n^2,
and its recursive helper queries are shorter still. These assertions follow
by the same induction on actual query length used in the definition.

Consequently, for an active current mask H_{n,k} (k<g_n), every helper
query of length at most T depends on masks of that block only through
H_{n,0},...,H_{n,k-1}. It depends on the base table in that block only outside
H_{n,k-1}. More generally a helper of length N depends on block n only
through masks up to k(N,n) and base entries outside H_{n,k(N,n)}; if it
cannot access that block it has no dependency on it at all. This follows
inductively because a current simulation aborts before reading any masked
row, and every called helper has an ancestor mask containing the current
mask. Uniform fallbacks, sums, smoothing and rounding preserve this property.

For fixed N,M,L,T, condition on the entire base table and, in each active
block n, the ancestor masks through k(N,n)-1. Condition also on the complete
mask chains of inactive blocks, whose current masks are empty. All helper
answers at lengths at most T are then fixed. The current active child masks
retain their conditional uniform laws, independently across blocks. In
particular their per-row conditional inclusion probabilities are at most
delta_n. This remains true even though the reference weight law depends
arbitrarily on the base table and the already constructed helpers.

Let u(x) be the NONTRUNCATED weight of M with this base table and these
actual shorter helpers, and suppose Z=sum u>0. For each fixed x its reference
trace has at most T base-query rows. The conditional union bound gives

 E[ (Z-sum v_N)/Z | reference data ]
       <= T * max{delta_n: k(N,n)<g_n and n^2<=T}.                 (1)

An empty maximum is zero. The reference law u/Z is already fixed under this
conditioning, so there is NO assumption that a tiny old prefix mass remains
tiny after a new witness is planted. No witness planting takes place.

## 4. The maximum in (1) decreases faster than every inverse power of N

For an active n, writing a=a_n, we have

 log_2 N < (k(N,n)+1) log_2 n <= g_n log_2 n
          <= (3a/4) log_2(a+1).

As N increases, the minimum a of an active block tends to infinity: bounded
a allows only finitely many n, each with a finite threshold n^{g_n} beyond
which its mask is empty. Thus uniformly over active blocks

 a^2/log_2 N >= 4a/[3 log_2(a+1)] -> infinity.

It follows that for every fixed K, the maximum delta_n in (1) is eventually
at most N^{-K}. The extra factor T<=N^{1/4} can be absorbed by increasing K.
This is the purpose of the cubic-root mask depth and square cubic-root
erasure exponent: the masks eventually exhaust at small blocks, while every
fixed polynomial query length still leaves exponentially many hidden rows
at the corresponding large block.

## 5. Forward-KL models for every uniform efficient-weight family

Fix one uniform weight machine M and a clock T_L polynomial in L which
bounds its runtime and output bit length on the actual oracle. Increase the
clock to bound L,p,a and the header. Taking a polynomial clock with fixed
coefficient and exponent is allowed; there are countably many such choices.
Invalid or negative output clipping does not change the target weights.

For a fixed desired exponent c>=1, put ell=ceil(log_2 L), L>=2,
a=(c+4)ell, p=L+a+(c+5)ell+2. Choose N_L=T_L^4, increasing T_L if necessary
so its padded header fits. All queries for this model use this same N_L.
Its reference weight is exactly w_L, because its shorter helper queries are
the actual final-oracle queries, already fixed by the induction.

Write r_L=(Z_L-sum v_{N_L})/Z_L. From (1) and section 4, for every K the
unconditional E r_L is eventually at most N_L^{-K}<=L^{-K}. Markov's
inequality with epsilon_L=L^{-(c+4)} makes Pr[r_L>epsilon_L] summable.
The first Borel-Cantelli lemma implies r_L<=epsilon_L eventually, almost
surely. No independence between lengths is used. Intersect these
probability-one events over the countably many machines, polynomial clocks
and integers c. If a candidate machine has zero reference normalizer, define
r_L=0 for the probability estimate; the claimed conclusion is used only at
lengths with positive normalizer. Conditional on the reference data the
normalizer is fixed, so this convention preserves the estimate.

On the good event, R_{N_L} is the target conditioned on its nondiscarded
reference computations. For r=r_L, write

    P_L=(1-r)R_{N_L}+r W

with some law W (choose it arbitrarily if r=0). Finite log-sum, with the
component label retained and then discarded, gives

 KL(P_L || S_{N_L}) <= d(r||alpha)+r KL(W||U_L)
   <= log(1/(1-alpha)) + r [L log 2 + log(1/alpha)].              (2)

Here alpha=2^{-a}<=L^{-(c+4)}, and a<= (c+4)(log_2 L+1). On the good
event (2) is O_c(L^{-(c+3)}).

At every prefix, both next-bit probabilities of S_{N_L} are at least
alpha*2^{-L}, since the corresponding joint prefix probabilities have that
lower bound and the conditioning prefix probability is at most 1. Rounding
and clipping change each next-bit probability by at most 2^{-p}. Therefore
the relative decrease is at most

    beta=2^{L+a-p}<=L^{-(c+5)}/4.

For beta<=1/2, each log likelihood ratio from S to its rounded AR model is
at most -log(1-beta)<=2 beta. Summing over L symbols adds at most 2L beta
to (2), for ANY target law. The resulting KL is eventually at most L^{-c}.

The model retrieves p digits for each requested next probability from the
same padded helper. N_L,T_L,p are polynomial in L; writing all the queries
and unrolling the computation gives polynomial-size oracle circuits and
polynomial-bit dyadic probabilities. This even gives a fixed uniform model
construction per M, clock and c, with an eventual guarantee. No distribution
sampler, target CDF, partition-function algorithm or instance-uniform compiler
is needed. A finite set of exceptional lengths can be represented by
nonuniform hardwiring with one larger constant size bound.

## 6. Circuit hardness survives every helper

Fix d>=1 and a sufficiently large n. Set D=d+2. The mask H_{n,D} has at
least h=2^{floor(n/2)} rows. Select its lexicographically first h rows.
Fix all masks and the base table outside these rows. By section 3 every
helper query of length at most n^d is now fixed independently of the h
remaining pairs (b_y,z_y): any helper that can read this block has mask
index at most floor(log_n n^d)<=d, and hence its mask contains H_{n,D}.

Here is the needed elementary direct-product bound. An arbitrary
deterministic procedure may make at most Q membership queries to h rows,
each with an independent uniform pair (b_i,z_i) in {0,1} times [M], and
then predict all h bits. Other oracle answers are fixed independently of
these pairs. Its probability of predicting the entire bit vector correctly
is at most

    2^{-h}(1+1/M)^Q <= 2^{-h} exp(Q/M).                         (3)

Proof: memoize repeated queries. After the first positive answer in a row,
its complete row is known and future queries to it can be simulated locally.
Thus at most one actual positive answer is needed per row. A response
transcript is specified by a subset of at most Q positions for its positive
answers. If it has k positives, these are in distinct rows and prescribe
their (b_i,z_i), probability (2M)^{-k}. The final guessed bits prescribe
the remaining h-k independent b_i, with probability 2^{-(h-k)}. Ignore
negative-answer constraints, which can only increase this probability.
For this transcript and successful prediction the bound is 2^{-h}M^{-k}.
Summing over the at most binomial(Q,k) possible position sets and then over
k proves (3). This argument is valid for adaptive queries: fixing the
response positions fixes each queried cell and the final predictions.

For any size-n^d circuit, evaluate it on all 2^n inputs in a fixed order.
This is one procedure with Q<=2^n n^d relevant membership queries; all other
answers, including ALL its helper answers, are fixed as above. Use
M=2^{n^2}. Hence Q/M tends to zero. A correct circuit must predict all h
selected bits, and has conditional success probability bounded by (3).

There are at most 2^{poly_d(n)} circuits of size n^d, even allowing arbitrary
oracle gates with query lengths bounded by that size: encode at most n^d
gates and at most n^d input wires at each gate. A generous encoding uses
O(n^{2d} log(n+2)) bits. Union bounding (3) over all these circuits gives a
summable sequence of failure probabilities, since h=2^{floor(n/2)}.
The bound is independent of the fixed masks and exterior table, so it also
holds unconditionally. Borel-Cantelli, followed by a countable intersection
over d, shows that almost surely A is not in P^O/poly.

## 7. One common oracle, status and review boundary

Sections 5 and 6 each describe probability-one events in the SAME product
space of base tables and mask chains, with the helper oracle determined
from those variables by the SAME length induction. Their intersection has
probability one and is nonempty. Select an oracle in that intersection.
It has both required properties, proving the stated Target 2 separation
for the uniform rational-weight interpretation of the dossier.

The independent reviewer should check especially section 3's joint
conditioning argument: a shorter helper must depend only on ancestors of
every current active mask, including when it internally ranges over every
possible input and prefix. No earlier verdict or unpublished IR2 proof is
being used. All probability bounds above are analytic; finite diagnostics
can check the clock inequalities and small direct-product cases but cannot
certify the infinite construction. The claim remains UNAUDITED.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:7fb9c9afe5a87a97e026839e729b8f6f178c17ddd20f4eacb05e0db7a0041543","revision_digest":"sha256:00d2831f64b57a304109a75b5091c04e7bb9ec5d93de7877189559dee5e69c20","source_id":"own-work:T410-w739-C015-v1","source_revision":"2026-10-21T00:09:51.564470+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma 26 of arXiv:2606.17859, 'Full $\Gamma-$expansion for the level-two large deviation rate functionals of non-reversib'] Let $\mu_\epsilon$ be the sequence defined in
\eqref{recovery_seq_inter}. Fix a
$\widehat{\bb X}_p(\cdot)-$equivalence class $\mf D\subset \mc S_p$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\mf D$ has two or more elements, then
\begin{align*}
& \limsup_{\epsilon\to 0}\theta_{\epsilon}^{(p)} \,
\ms I_\epsilon(\mu_{\mf D,\epsilon})\,
\leq\, \bb I_{\mf D}^{(p)}(\omega(\,\cdot\,|\,\mf D))
\\
&\quad 
\,+\, \omega(\mc M_p(l_{\mf D} ) \, |\, \mf D)\,
R_p(\mc M_p(l_{\mf D}) \,, \mc M_p(l_{\mf D}-1))
\,+\, \omega(\mc M_p(r_{\mf D} ) \, |\, \mf D)\,
R_p(\mc M_p(r_{\mf D}) \,,  \mc M_p(r_{\mf D}+1)) \,.
\end{align*}
    
\item If $\mf D$ is a singleton and its element is a transient state, then
\begin{equation*}
\limsup_{\epsilon \to 0}\theta_{\epsilon}^{(p)} \,
\ms I_\epsilon(\mu_{\mf D,\epsilon}) \,\leq
\, R_p(\mc M_p(l_{\mf D}) \,, \mc M_p(l_{\mf D}-1))
\,+\, R_p(\mc M_p(r_{\mf D}) \,, \mc M_p(r_{\mf
D}+1))\,. 
\end{equation*} 

\item If $\mf D$ is a singleton and its element is an absorbing state,
then
\begin{equation*}
\limsup_{\epsilon \to 0}\theta_{\epsilon}^{(p)} \,
\ms I_\epsilon(\mu_{\mf D,\epsilon}) = 0\,.
\end{equation*} 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Let T be an index set, and suppose that for every finite subset (t_1,...,t_n) of T we are given a probability measure mu_{t_1,...,t_n} on (R^n, Borel sets), such that this family is consistent: it is invariant under permuting the t_i together with the corresponding coordinates, and marginalizing mu_{t_1,...,t_n,t_{n+1}} over the last coordinate returns mu_{t_1,...,t_n}. Then there is a probability space carrying a stochastic process (X_t)_{t in T} whose finite-dimensional distributions are exactly this family, and this process is unique in law. Due to Andrey Kolmogorov.
title: Kolmogorov extension theorem

\[
\bigl((Y^n)_{n\ge0},(\mathcal M^n)_{n\ge0}\bigr)
\]
be an \(E^{\mathbb N_0}\times E^{\mathbb N_0}\)-valued random element whose
law is a subsequential weak limit of the laws in
Proposition~\ref{prop:weighted-tightness}. Then, almost surely, for every
\(n\ge0\), every \(t\in[0,T]\), and every

\begin{align}
\langle Y_t^n,\varphi\rangle
&=
\langle Y_0^n,\varphi\rangle
+
\int_0^t
\langle Y_s^n,L_s\varphi\rangle\,\dd s\notag\\

M_t^n(\varphi),

[Definition def.lesspeaked of arXiv:2603.11043, 'An asymptotically optimal bound for the concentration function of a sum of independent int'] Let $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ be finite measures on integers.

Let $\epsilon \ge 0$.
We write
\[
\mu_1 \preccurlyeq_\epsilon \mu_2
\]
    and say \emph{the concentration function
    of $\mu_1$ is $\epsilon$-dominated by the concentration function of $\mu_2$}
if for each positive integer $j$
\[
    \mathcal{Q}_j(\mu_1) = \mu_1^+(I_j) \le (1+\epsilon) \mathcal{Q}_j(\mu_2) = (1+\epsilon)\mu_2^+(I_j).
\]
When the measures are probability measures, we extend the notation $\preccurlyeq_\epsilon$
to random variables distributed according to them.
For exact domination (i.e., the case $\epsilon = 0$) we use notation $\preccurlyeq$ 

to mean
$\preccurlyeq_{0}$.

body:
h: Z^d -> [0, infinity) subadditive: h(x+y) <= h(x) + h(y)
h(x) <= r|x| for all x and some r > 0
g(x) := lim_n h(nx)/n (the limit exists by subadditivity, and g(x) <= h(x) always)
CHAP with exponent a > 0 and correction phi in Phi (positive nondecreasing on (1,infinity))
no probabilistic hypothesis whatsoever

THE TWO PROPERTIES, VERBATIM FROM THE SURVEY.
  Good increments: Q_x(a,phi) := { y in Z^d : h(y) <= g_x(y) + |x|^a phi(|x|) and g_x(y) <= g(x) }, the second condition being there to prevent overshooting the increment.
  CHAP (convex hull approximation property): h satisfies CHAP with exponent a and correction phi if there is L > 1 such that x/alpha lies in Co(Q_x(a,phi)) for some alpha in [1,L], for all rational x with |x| large enough.
  GAP (general approximation property): there are M > 1 and C > 0 with g(x) <= h(x) <= g(x) + C|x|^a phi(|x|) for all x with |x| >= M.
READ THE DIRECTION CORRECTLY: g(x) <= h(x) is free from subadditivity; Alexander's content is the REVERSE inequality, an upper bound on how far h can sit above its own limit. A quotation that reports 'Alexander's bound' as though it were two-sided has claimed the trivial half as part of the theorem.
WHAT IT IS FOR: applied to h(y) = E T(0,y), whose limit g is the time constant, it converts a 'good skeleton path' condition into a rate of convergence to the limit shape. The FPP payoff is a separate application with its own probabilistic hypotheses - see the non-random-fluctuation state-of-the-art node.
SOURCE: Alexander, K. (1997), 'Approximation of subadditive functions and convergence rates in limiting-shape results', Ann. Probab., 30-55. (The survey bibliography prints the volume as '1', which looks like a typo; lane P4 did not verify the volume number.) Statement and both definitions read in Auffinger-Damron-Hanson, '50 years of first passage percolation', arXiv:1511.03262v2 (AMS University Lecture Series 68, 2017), subsection "Alexander's method", tex lines 2014-2033.
VERIFICATION STATUS: survey-claim. Lane P4 did not read Alexander (1997).
title: Alexander (1997), Theorem 1.8: if h is a non-negative SUBADDITIVE function on Z^d with h(x) <= r|x| for some r > 0, and h satisfies the convex hull approximation property CHAP with exponent a > 0 and correction phi, then h satisfies the general approximation property GAP with the same exponent and correction, that is g(x) <= h(x) <= g(x) + C |x|^a phi(|x|) where g(x) = lim_n h(nx)/n. The theorem is purely deterministic - no probability enters it.

[Thm 3 of arXiv:2609.03185, 'Uniqueness of tangent flows in free boundary flow'] There exist constants $A=A(n)>0$ and $\beta_0=\beta_0(n)>0$ such that the following holds.

Let
\[
X_0=(x_0,t_0),\qquad x_0\in B_{\frac{r_0}{2}}(0),\qquad -1<t_0<0,
\]
and suppose that the flow is defined on the time interval $[t_*,t_0]$ where $t_0-\beta_0\kappa^2 \leq t_* < t_0.$ Suppose that $\mathcal E_0$ satisfies
\[
\mathcal E_0 \geq \int_{M_{t_*}} \phi_{X_0,G_0}(x,t_*)\,d\mathcal H_g^n.
\]
Then
\[
r\longmapsto e^{A\sqrt r}\Theta_g(M,X_0,r) + A\mathcal E_0r^2
\]
is increasing for
\[
0<r\leq \min\left\{\sqrt{t_0 - t_*},\sqrt{t_0+1}\right\}.
\]

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2411.11415, 'The ballistic limit of the log-Sobolev constant equals the Polyak--\L{}ojasiewicz constant'] Suppose that $f \in C^2(\R^d)$
has a unique global minimizer,
and that there is a constant $L> 0$
so that $\Delta f \leqslant L\,(1+\|\nabla f\|^2)$.
For each $t > 0$, let $\mu_t  \deq  \frac{1}{Z_t}\, e^{-f/t}$ be a probability measure.
Then $C_{\msf{bLS}}(f)$, defined in~(equation eqn:cals of the paper),
exists if and only if $C_{\msf{PL}}(f) < \infty$,
and in this case
$$
C_{\msf{bLS}}(f) = C_{\msf{PL}}(f)\,.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Main result: \bal{} log-Sobolev equals PL

[Proposition 6 (Closed-form gradient refinement) of arXiv:2608.25116, '\method: Gradient Refinement and Progress-Aware Exploitation for Query-Efficient High-Dime'] Let $k_\calD(\cdot,\cdot)$ denote the GP posterior covariance after observing
$\calD$. Then $\alpha_{\mathrm{ref}}(\bz)$ is independent of the unobserved
value $y_\bz$ and equals
\begin{equation}

\alpha_{\mathrm{ref}}(\bz)
=
\frac{\|\nabla_\bx k_\calD(\bx,\bz)\|^2}{k_\calD(\bz,\bz)+\sigma^2},
\end{equation}
where $\nabla_\bx k_\calD(\bx,\bz)=\partial k_\calD(\bx,\bz)/\partial\bx$.

body:
[Lemma 21 (The limiting infinite count chain) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] Let $Y_t$ be the Markov chain on $\Nbb_0$ defined by
\[
        Y_{t+1}\mid Y_t=k\sim \Bin(k+1,q).
\]
It has a unique stationary law $\pi$.  This law is the distribution of
\[
        Y_\infty=\sum_{r=1}^{\infty}B_r,
        \qquad
        B_r\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(q^r)
\]
with the $B_r$ independent.  Moreover,
\[
        \pi(k)\sim \frac{q^{k(k+1)/2}}{(q;q)_\infty}.
\]

body:
[Defi The coupled processes of arXiv:2607.19658, 'Hitting time mixing for random $k$-cycles'] We define four Markov processes
$$
(X_t)_{t\ge t^*},\qquad
(Y_t)_{t\ge t^*},\qquad
(Z_t)_{t\ge t^*},\qquad
(\rho_t)_{t\ge t^*}
$$
on a common probability space as follows.
\begin{itemize}
\item The process $(X_t)_{t\ge t^*}$ is the original random $k$-cycle walk,
evolving according to the transition kernel $P_n$. Let $\tau$ denote
the first time at which all elements have been touched.

\item The process $(Z_t)_{t\ge t^*}$ is initialized by $Z_{t^*}$ and evolves
according to the original transition kernel $P_n$. Its marked set is
updated according to marking scheme B. Let $\tau_1$ denote the first time at
which all elements have been marked.

\item The process $(Y_t)_{t\ge t^*}$ is initialized by $Y_{t^*}$ and evolves
according to the modified transition kernel $Q_{n,t}$. Its marked set is
updated according to marking scheme A. Let $\tau_2$ denote the first time at
which all elements have been marked.

\item The process $(\rho_t)_{t\ge t^*}$ is initialized by $\rho_{t^*}$ and
uses the same $Q_{n,t}$-moves and the same marked sets as $Y_t$. Its action
on the current state is modified as follows.

At time $t+1$, sample $\sigma\sim Q_{n,t}$.

\begin{itemize}
    \item If the sampled move marks exactly one new element $i$, either through
    a dummy move or through a one-unmarked $k$-cycle, set
    $$
      M_{t+1}:=M_t \cup \{i\},
        \qquad
        S_{t+1}:=S_t \setminus \{i\}, \qquad  \rho_{t+1}:=\sigma\rho_t.
    $$

    \item If no new element is marked and
    $\operatorname{supp}(\sigma)\subset M_t$, set
    $$
       M_{t+1}:=M_t,
        \qquad
        S_{t+1}:=S_t, \qquad  \rho_{t+1}:=\sigma\rho_t.
    $$

    \item If no new element is marked and
    $\operatorname{supp}(\sigma)\not\subset M_t$, first update
    $$
        M_{t+1}:=\sigma^{-1}(M_t),
        \qquad
        S_{t+1}:=\sigma^{-1}(S_t).
    $$
    If $k$ is odd, set
    $$
        \rho_{t+1}:=\sigma^{-1}\rho_t\sigma.
    $$
    If $k$ is even, then, conditionally on $M_{t+1}$, choose an unordered pair
    $\{U_{t+1},V_{t+1}\}\subset M_{t+1}$ uniformly and independently of
    $\rho_t$, and set
    $$
        \rho_{t+1}:=(U_{t+1}\,V_{t+1})\sigma^{-1}\rho_t\sigma.
    $$
\end{itemize}
Let $\tau_3$ denote the first time at which all elements have been marked
for the process $\rho_t$.

\end{itemize}

\qquad
(\mathbf{D}^{-,i} \sigX[\cdot])_s

\]

[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2604.01701, '\bf Chung-type laws of the iterated logarithm for $m$-fold weighted integrated fractional '] (Li and Linde \cite[Theorem 6.1] {LiLinde1999}) Let $\{Y(t);t\in [c,d]\}$ be a continuous, centered, Gaussian process with 
$$ -\log \pr\left(\sup_{t\in [c,d]}|Y(t)|<\epsilon\right)\preccurlyeq \;(resp. \ll)\; \epsilon^{-\alpha}\Big(\log \frac{1}{\epsilon}\Big)^{\nu}, $$
where $\alpha>0$ and $\nu\ge 0$. Assume that $K(t,s):[a,b]\times[c,d]\to \mathbb R$ is a kernel function which satisfies the H\"older inequality 
$$ \int_c^d \big|K(t^{\prime},s)-K(t^{\prime\prime},s)\big|ds\le C\big|t^{\prime}-t^{\prime\prime}\big|^{\gamma },\;\; t^{\prime},t^{\prime\prime}\in [a,b], $$
for some $\gamma \in (0,1]$ and $C>0$. Then
$$ -\log \pr\left(\sup_{t\in [a,b]}\big|\int_c^dK(t,s)Y(s)ds\big|<\epsilon\right)\preccurlyeq \;(resp. \ll)\; \epsilon^{-\alpha/(\alpha\gamma +1)}\Big(\log \frac{1}{\epsilon}\Big)^{\nu/(\alpha\gamma +1)}. $$
In particular, 
\begin{equation}  -\log \pr\left(\sup_{t\in [a,b]}\big|\int_a^tY(s)ds\big|<\epsilon\right)\preccurlyeq \;(resp. \ll)\; \epsilon^{-\alpha/(\alpha+1)}\Big(\log \frac{1}{\epsilon}\Big)^{\nu/(\alpha+1)}. 
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 11 of arXiv:2604.01701

[Theorem 9 (Laplace-survival and Poissonization) of arXiv:2607.04467, 'Bernstein Functions at Work:\\ Coalescents, Copulas, and Subordination'] Let $\zeta\ge0$ with Laplace transform $L_\zeta(x)=\E e^{-x\zeta}$, and let $U$
be uniform on $(0,1)$ independent of $\zeta$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] If $\Prob(\zeta>0)=1$, then $\xi=(-\log U)/\zeta$ satisfies
$F_\xi(x)=1-L_\zeta(x)$ for all $x\ge0$. For arbitrary $\zeta\ge0$ the same
holds on the extended half-line with $\xi=\infty$ on $\{\zeta=0\}$, and
\emph{no} finite-valued $\xi$ can satisfy the literal identity for all $x\ge0$
when $\Prob(\zeta=0)>0$.
\item[(ii)] If $\kappa_t\mid\zeta\sim\Pois(t\zeta)$, then
$\E[x^{\kappa_t}]=L_\zeta(t(1-x))$ for $0\le x\le1$, and $\kappa_t$ is realizable
from i.i.d.\ uniforms via the exponential-interarrival construction of a
Poisson process.
\end{enumerate}

body: In mathematics, a sheaf is a tool for systematically tracking data attached to the open sets of a topological space and defined locally with regard to them. For example, for each open set, the data could be the ring of continuous functions defined on that open set. Such data are well-behaved in that they can be restricted to smaller open sets, and also the data assigned to an open set are equivalent to all collections of compatible data assigned to collections of smaller open sets covering the original open set.
title: Sheaf (mathematics)

AUTHOR-DERIVED, UNREVIEWED exact finite witness. In the independent standard-Gaussian quadrant polymer with two vertices per path, the two paths share the origin and choose either (1,0) or (0,1). M_2=g_0+max(g_1,g_2). With OU time t>=0 and g_t=e^(-t)g+sqrt(1-e^(-2t))g' for independent g', the expected number of shared maximizing-path vertices is R_2(t)=3/2+arcsin(e^(-t))/pi, and Var(M_2)=2-1/pi. Thus R_2(t)>=3/2 and its independent-environment limit is 3/2. A bound R_2(t)<=C exp(-c t) for all t with finite C and c>0 is false. Centered-overlap estimates must also account for the first-chaos variance floor. This is a proof-step counterexample, not a disproof of polynomial variance improvement.

[Lemma lem:finsys of arXiv:2607.05671, 'Bi-infinite systems of singularly interacting Brownian particles and the KPZ equation'] Fix an initial distribution $\gamma \in \mathcal{P}_0(\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{Z}})$, an initial condition $x = \{x_i\}_{i \in \mathbb{Z}} \sim \gamma$, and Brownian motions $\{B_i\}_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$ as in Section (ssec:biinfinite of the paper). Let 
$X = \{X_i(t), t \in [0,\infty)\}_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$, $L = \{L_{(i,i+1)}(t), t \in [0,\infty)\}_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be as in Definition (def:biinf of the paper). 
\begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]
\item For $i_1 \leq i_2$ in $\mathbb{Z}$ and $M \in \mathbb{N}$, on the event that $\mathit{K}^*([i_1,i_2],[0,T]) \leq M$, for all $i_1 \leq j \leq i_2$ and $t \in [0,T]$, 
$$
X_j(t) = X_j^{[i_1-M,i_2+M]}(t),
$$
where the system $\{X_j^{[i_1-M,i_2+M]}\}$ is defined as in (equation eq:finfam of the paper). 

\item Suppose that for any solution to (equation eq:asym_eq of the paper) with some initial distribution $\gamma$ and 
satisfying some property $(\mathcal{P})$, for all $i \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $T \in (0,\infty)$, $\mathit{K}_\nearrow^*(i,[0,T])$ and $\mathit{K}_\searrow^*(i,[0,T])$ are finite almost surely. Then solutions to (equation eq:asym_eq of the paper) with initial distribution $\gamma$ and satisfying property $(\mathcal{P})$ are pathwise unique.
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemma lem:finsys of arXiv:2607.05671

[Proposition prop: existence for discrete systems of arXiv:2411.05924, 'Non-negative Martingale Solutions to the Stochastic Porous Medium Equation with Sticky Beh'] For each $n\in\mathbb N$ there exists a stochastic basis $(\Omega, \mathcal F, \mathbb F, \mathbb P)$ supporting a $U$--valued $Q$--Wiener process $W$ and an $\mathbb R^n$-valued process $\mathbf u_n$ which satisfies the SDE (equation eq: discrete dynamics Rn of the paper) on $[0,\tau_n]$ and which is constant on $[\tau_n, T]$, where 
    \[
        \tau_n := T \wedge \inf \{ t \geq 0: \mathscr E_n(\mathbf u_n(t)) \geq h_n^{-\kappa} \}.
    \]
    We call the triple $((\Omega, \mathcal F, \mathbb F, \mathbb P), \mathbf u_n, W)$ a \emph{martingale solution} to (equation eq: discrete dynamics Rn of the paper).
title: Proposition prop: existence for discrete systems of arXiv:2411.05924

body: Let (F_t)_{t >= 0} be a filtration satisfying the usual conditions. An adapted, right-continuous with left limits (cadlag) process (M_t)_{t >= 0} with M_0 finite is a local martingale if there exists a sequence of stopping times tau_n increasing to infinity almost surely such that, for each n, the stopped process M^{tau_n}_t = M_{t and tau_n} is a true martingale. Every true martingale is a local martingale, but a local martingale need not be a true martingale unless an additional integrability condition, such as uniform integrability of the family {M_{t and tau_n}}, holds. [standard, e.g. Revuz and Yor, Continuous Martingales and Brownian Motion]
title: Local Martingale

[Theorem thm:q-adic-linear-pvar of arXiv:2604.05941, 'Banach spaces of continuous paths with finite $p$-th variation'] Fix $p>1$, an integer $q \ge 2$, and $a\in\mathbb R^{q-1}\setminus\{0\}$. Assume that the sequence $(\xi_m^{(p,q)})_{m\ge0}$ converges as $m\to\infty$. Then the series (equation eq:q-adic-series of the paper) converges uniformly on $[0,1]$ to a continuous function $x$. Moreover, $x$ has linear $p$-th variation along the $q$-adic partition sequence $\mathbb{T}_q$, namely
    \[
        [x]^{(p)}_{\mathbb{T}_q}(t)
        =
        C_{p,q,a}\,t\,\lim_{m\to\infty}\xi_m^{(p,q)},
        \qquad t\in[0,1],
    \]
    where
    \[
        C_{p,q,a} := \mathbb E\Bigg[ \bigg| \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\rho_q^j\,\eta_{D_j}(a) \bigg|^p \Bigg] \in(0, \infty),
    \]
    and $(D_j)_{j\ge1}$ are i.i.d.\ random variables uniformly distributed on $\{0,\dots,q-1\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:q-adic-linear-pvar of arXiv:2604.05941

A non-negative function f: X -> [0, infinity) is called (a, b)-self-bounding if there exist functions f_i: X^{(i)} -> R (where X^{(i)} omits the i-th coordinate) such that for all x in X and all i: 0 <= f(x) - f_i(x^{(i)}) <= 1, and sum_{i=1}^n (f(x) - f_i(x^{(i)})) <= a * f(x) + b.

 Then for each $k \in \N$ we have
 \[ \p\left[ \text{$\Eannharm_{z,j'} \cap (\Gresbdball_{z,j'})^c$ occurs for more than a $1/10$ fraction of $j' = j,\ldots,j+k$} \right] \le ce^{-bk} . \]

[Proposition thm:adaptive-suboptimality-CS of arXiv:2608.25551, 'Beyond Optimal Rates in Stochastic Optimization: Trajectory-Adaptive Stopping Rules'] Suppose Assumptions~(assump:strong-convexity of the paper)--(assump:stepsize-bound of the paper) hold. Let $t_0 \ge 4$ and $\eta_t = 2/(\mu(t+1))$ for every $t \ge t_0$. Then, for every $\alpha \in (0,1)$, the process
\begin{equation}

    U_t^{\mathrm{sub}}(\alpha)
    \coloneqq
    \frac{1}{S_t}
    \left[
        \frac{1}{\mu}
        \sum_{s=t_0}^t
        \left\| g_s \right\|^2
        +
        \frac{\mu t_0 (t_0-1)}{4} Z_{t_0}
        +
        2\,\mathfrak H_\alpha\left(V_t^{\mathrm{sub}}\right)
    \right],
    \qquad
    t\ge t_0,
\end{equation}
is an upper confidence sequence for the weighted-average suboptimality, in the sense that
\[
    \mathbb{P}\left(
        \forall t\ge t_0:\
        f(\bar x_t)-f(x^\star)
        \le
        U_t^{\mathrm{sub}}(\alpha)
    \right)
    \ge
    1-\alpha.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Confidence sequence for $f(\bar x_t) - f(x^\star)$

For integer n>=1, let L_n=n, K_n=2^(n^2) singleton paths of unit weight, all X_i equal one shared N(0,1) variable Z, and beta_n=n. The covariance is PSD with maximum diagonal 1. Then log D_xi=xi Z but F_beta_n(xi X)=xi Z-n*log 2, so the normalized hard-min mean is 0 and normalized soft-min mean is -log 2, for every fixed xi>=0. Thus beta_n->infinity alone does not transfer individual soft-min levels uniformly in network size. This xi-independent bias cancels in endpoint differences; the example is not an endpoint-difference counterexample or a planar LFPP model.

body:
[Proposition prop:goodset of arXiv:2507.10531, 'Quantitative central limit theorems for exponential random graphs'] For all small enough $\varepsilon > 0$, there are some $\eta, \gamma > 0$ such that for all large enough $n$ there is a set
$\Lambda^* \subseteq \mathcal{B}_p^\eta$ satisfying the following properties, where $X \sim \mu_\mathsf{H}^\eta(n,p)$ and $(X_t^x)$ is the
Glauber dynamics conditioned on $\mathcal{B}_p^\eta$ and started at $x$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Roman*)]
    \item
    
    The set $\Lambda^*$ is large, i.e.\ we have
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbb{P}[X \in \Lambda^*] \geq 1 - e^{-\gamma n}.
    \end{equation}
    \item
    
    The chain started near $\Lambda^*$ stays in the good region.
    Namely, whenever $\mathbf{d}_\mathrm{Ham}(x,\Lambda^*) \leq 1$,
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbb{P}\mleft[X_t^x \in \Gamma_p^\varepsilon \cap \mathcal{B}_p^{\eta/2} \text{ for all } t < e^{\gamma n}\mright] \geq 1 - e^{-\gamma n}.
    \end{equation}
    \item
    
    The set $\Lambda^*$ is connected under the nearest-neighbor relation.
    Moreover, for any $x,x' \in \Lambda^*$, we have
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbf{d}_{\Lambda^*}(x,x') \leq 2 n^2,
    \end{equation}
    where $\mathbf{d}_{\Lambda^*}(x,x')$ denotes the distance within $\Lambda^*$, i.e.\ the length of the shortest nearest-neighbor
    path between $x,x'$ which stays inside $\Lambda^*$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 14 of arXiv:2506.15037, '2BSDE with uncertain horizon and application to stochastic control in erratic environments'] We say that $(\mathbb{P}, \beta)$ is a weak solution for \eqref{eq:Driftless SDE} if the distribution of $X^{t,x, \beta}_t$ under $ \mathbb{P}$ is $\delta_{x(t)}$, where $\delta$ denotes the Dirac measure and there exists a $\mathbb P$-Brownian motion, denoted by $W^{\mathbb{P}}$, such that
\[
X_s = x(t) + \int_t^s \sigma(r, X_{\cdot\wedge r}, \beta_r) dW_r^{\mathbb{P}}, \quad s \in [t, T], \quad \mathbb{P}\text{-a.s.}
\]
We denote by
\[
    \mathcal{N}(t, x) := \left\{ (\mathbb{P}, \beta): \text{ weak solutions of \eqref{eq:Driftless SDE}}\right\}
\]
and by $\mathcal{P}(t, x)$ the set of probability measures such that there exists an $\F$-optional process $\beta$ such that the probability coupled with the process $\beta$ is a weak solution of \eqref{eq:Driftless SDE}.

body:
[Lemma 12 (Orthogonality of the orbit director) of arXiv:2608.15805, 'Spectral duality structures and the Fisher--Rao geometry of reset distributions'] For each orbit $O=\{z,\sigma(z)\}$, write
$\mathbf v_O=(\sqrt{\kappa(\sigma(z))},\sqrt{\kappa(z)})$ for the
\emph{critical vector}, whose direction realises the critical
ratio of Theorem~\ref{thm:paper3}\textup{(i)}. Then the director
of Lemma~\ref{lem:orbit-collapse}, which spans
$\operatorname{im}M_O$, is
\[
\mathbf d_O:=\bigl(\sqrt{\kappa(z)},\ -\sqrt{\kappa(\sigma(z))}\bigr)
\;=\;R_{-\pi/2}\,\mathbf v_O,
\]
where $R_{-\pi/2}\in SO(2)$ is the rotation by $-\pi/2$ of the
Euclidean orbit plane. In particular $\mathbf d_O$ and
$\mathbf v_O$ are orthogonal \emph{and of equal Euclidean norm}
$\sqrt{\kappa(z)+\kappa(\sigma(z))}$: the director is not a new
object --- it is the critical vector viewed from the orthogonal
direction, with no deformation whatsoever. Consequently:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(i)}] the two components of $\mathbf d_O$ have
opposite signs;
\item[\textup{(ii)}] $\langle\pi|_O,\mathbf d_O\rangle=0$ for every
$\pi$ satisfying the critical ratio.
\end{enumerate}

body: For first-order logic, Godel's completeness theorem states that a formula is provable from a set of axioms by a standard formal proof system if and only if it is semantically entailed by those axioms, that is, true in every model satisfying them. Equivalently, every syntactically consistent set of first-order sentences has a model. Thus first-order provability and first-order semantic truth coincide, so the usual first-order proof systems are sound and complete; this does not extend to second-order logic under its standard semantics. Proved by Kurt Godel in his 1929 doctoral dissertation.
title: Godel's completeness theorem

body: Let A be an n by n complex matrix with entries a_ij. For each row i, the Gershgorin disc D_i is the closed disc in the complex plane centered at the diagonal entry a_ii with radius R_i equal to the sum of the absolute values of the other, off-diagonal entries in row i. Every eigenvalue of A lies in at least one disc D_i. Moreover, if a union of k of these discs is disjoint from the remaining n-k discs, that union contains exactly k eigenvalues of A counted with multiplicity, and the complementary union contains the rest. Proved by Semyon Gershgorin in 1931.
title: Gershgorin circle theorem

[Proposition 55 of arXiv:2609.02065, '\textbf{From Bowditch's question to Goldman's conjecture for type-preserving representatio'] Let $\Sigma = \Sigma_{g,p}$ with $g\geqslant 2$ and $p\geqslant 1$, and let $s\in \{\pm 1\}^p$ and $n\in \big\{\chi(\Sigma) + p_+(s) + 1,\dots, -\chi(\Sigma) - p_-(s)- 1\big\}$. Suppose that one of the following condition holds:
    \begin{enumerate}[(1)]
        \item $p = 1$,
        
        \item $p = 2$ and $s = (+1, -1)$ or $(-1, +1)$,
        
        \item $p\geqslant 2$, $p_+(s)\in \{0,1\}$ and $n\leqslant -\chi(\Sigma) - p_-(s) - 2$,
        
        \item $p\geqslant 2$, $p_-(s)\in \{0,1\}$ and $n\geqslant \chi(\Sigma) + p_+(s) + 2$,

        \item $\chi(\Sigma) +p_+(s) + 2\leqslant n\leqslant -\chi(\Sigma) - p_-(s) - 2$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then $\ELns\cap X^s_n = \NHns\cap X^s_n$. Consequently, $\mathcal{E}^s_n$ has full measure in $\NHns$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

The right regular representation of S3 contains its two-dimensional irreducible representation, and equivariant operators can independently specify a matrix in that block. Let X have a probability law on R with E|X|^7<infinity, mean m, and central moments mu_k=E[(X-m)^k]. Normalize free Brownian motion as convolution with a semicircle law of variance t. Its unique sufficiently-large-time global density maximizer obeys m-3mu_3/t+(5mu_5-22mu_2mu_3)/t^2+O_mu(t^-3). With epsilon=1/t, the equations E[1/(r+epsilon(u-X)^2)]=1 and E[(u-X)/(r+epsilon(u-X)^2)^2]=0 have a C^3 branch at the limiting point (epsilon,u,r)=(0,m,1); finite seventh moment justifies one-sided derivatives and a C^3 extension in epsilon, and the global-mode lemma identifies the branch. An exponential quadratic moment implies this hypothesis. The remainder is law dependent and no originality certificate is asserted.

Label: proof (worker checked), independent audit pending w346. No novelty or full-problem solution certificate. The mode here means the global maximizer of the canonical continuous density.

Let X have mean m and finite variance sigma^2, and let mu_t be its law freely convolved with a semicircle law of variance t. If sigma=0, mu_t is a semicircle centered at m and the assertions below hold directly. Assume sigma>0. Put

    B=(sqrt(2)+2)sigma,
    A=B^2+sigma^2=(7+4sqrt(2))sigma^2,
    T=1024 A.

For every t>=T, mu_t has a unique global mode. That mode tends to m as t tends to infinity. If E|X-m|^3<infinity, putting M3=E|X-m|^3 and K=A(B+sigma)+4(B^3+M3), its location M(t) satisfies the explicit estimate |M(t)-m|<=36 K/t for t>=T. If E|X-m|^7<infinity, then

    M(t)=m-3mu_3/t+(5mu_5-22mu_2mu_3)/t^2+O_mu(t^-3),

where mu_k=E[(X-m)^k]. The threshold is a proved sufficient bound, with no optimal transition location claimed. An exponential quadratic moment, as in the original classical question, implies the required seventh moment.

Use the general Biane parametrization from Hasebe-Ueda, ALEA 15 (2018), equations (2.10), (2.13), (2.14). With w_t(u)=v_t(u)^2>0, it reads E[1/((u-X)^2+w_t(u))]=1/t, the density at psi_t(u) is sqrt(w_t(u))/(pi t), and psi_t is a homeomorphism. Hence global density maxima correspond exactly to global maxima of w_t. The function v_t is continuous and tends to zero at both infinities: for any a>0, E[1/((u-X)^2+a)] tends to zero as |u| tends to infinity by dominated convergence, forcing w_t(u)<a eventually. Thus a positive global maximum is attained.

Jensen's inequality gives w_t(m)>=t-sigma^2 when t>sigma^2. Indeed, at w=t-sigma^2 the reciprocal expectation is at least 1/t, and the expectation is strictly decreasing in positive w. Every positive solution also has w_t(u)<=t. Let u_* be any global maximizer and w_*=w_t(u_*). Then w_*>=t-sigma^2 and

    E[(u_*-X)^2/(w_*+(u_*-X)^2)]=1-w_*/t<=sigma^2/t.

Chebyshev gives P(|X-m|<=sqrt(2)sigma)>=1/2. If r=|u_*-m|-sqrt(2)sigma>0, the last expectation is at least (1/2)r^2/(t+r^2). For t>=4sigma^2 this implies r^2<=2sigma^2 t/(t-2sigma^2)<=4sigma^2. Consequently every global maximizer lies in I=[m-B,m+B].

For every u in I and t>=T, Jensen similarly yields t-A<=w_t(u)<=t. Set epsilon=1/t, r_t(u)=w_t(u)/t, d=r_t(u)+epsilon(u-X)^2, and

    C2=E[d^-2], J=E[(u-X)d^-2].

The positive implicit solution is smooth in u and r_t'(u)=-2epsilon J/C2. Its stationary points have J=0. Differentiating J along this solution gives

    J'=C2-4epsilon E[(u-X)^2 d^-3]-2r_t'(u)E[(u-X)d^-3].

Uniformly on I, E[(u-X)^2]<=A, r_t>=1-epsilon A>=1/2, C2>=(1+epsilon A)^-2>=1-2epsilon A, and |J|<=4E|u-X|. For epsilon A<=1/2, |r_t'|<=18epsilon E|u-X|, so the magnitude of the final term is at most 288epsilon A; the middle term is at most 32epsilon A. Thus J'>=1-322epsilon A>0 for t>=1024A. At least one global maximizer exists inside I, is a positive interior stationary point of w_t, and therefore has J=0. Strict increase of J permits only one such point. This proves eventual uniqueness of the global density maximizer without a compact-support or unimodality assumption.

As t tends to infinity, r_t->1 uniformly on I. The functions J(u) tend uniformly to u-m: split the integral at a bounded |X-m|, use uniform convergence on the bounded part, and dominate the tail by a constant times |X-m|+B. Its unique zero u_t therefore tends to m. The same truncation argument gives E[(u_t-X)/d]->u_t-m, so psi_t(u_t)=u_t+E[(u_t-X)/d]->m.

If M3 is finite, |d^-2-1|<=16|d-1| and |d^-1-1|<=4|d-1| because d>=1/2. With E|u-X|<=B+sigma and E|u-X|^3<=4(B^3+M3), the equation J=0 yields |u_t-m|<=16epsilon K. The spatial map then yields |psi_t(u_t)-m|<=2(16epsilon K)+4epsilon K=36K/t. All constants and hypotheses are explicit.

For the second-order expansion, translate m to zero and work with F(epsilon,u,r)=E[1/(r+epsilon(u-X)^2)]-1 and J(epsilon,u,r)=E[(u-X)/(r+epsilon(u-X)^2)^2]. Finite seventh absolute moment makes these functions C^3 up to epsilon=0 from epsilon>=0, for u near zero and r near one. Every derivative of total order at most three is dominated by a constant times 1+|X|^7 when r>=1/2. To use the ordinary C^3 implicit-function theorem, extend to epsilon<0 using the degree-three Taylor polynomial in epsilon at zero, with its smooth u,r-dependent coefficients; this matches all partial derivatives through order three at zero. No reciprocal expectation at negative epsilon is used. The Jacobian with respect to (u,r) at (epsilon,u,r)=(0,0,1) is [[0,-1],[1,0]], hence invertible. The resulting C^3 branch has a Taylor expansion with O(epsilon^3) remainder and is the unique global-maximizer branch already identified above.

Writing r=1+c1 epsilon+c2 epsilon^2+O(epsilon^3) and u=a1 epsilon+a2 epsilon^2+O(epsilon^3), direct expansion gives c1=-mu2, c2=mu4-mu2^2, a1=-2mu3, a2=3mu5-14mu2mu3. Inserting into psi=u+E[(u-X)/(r+epsilon(u-X)^2)] gives -3mu3 epsilon+(5mu5-22mu2mu3)epsilon^2+O(epsilon^3). Translation back yields the displayed formula.

[Definition 6 of arXiv:2609.01574, 'A linear bound for Fujita's freeness conjecture'] A \emph{pair} $(X,\Delta)$ consists of a normal variety $X$ and an effective $\mathbb Q$-divisor $\Delta$ such that $K_X+\Delta$ is $\mathbb Q$-Cartier. If the boundary is not assumed effective, we call $(X,\Delta)$ a $\mathbb Q$-sub-pair, or simply a \emph{sub-pair}. A germ $x\in(X,\Delta)$ consists of a pair and a closed point $x\in X$. For a divisor $D$ on a normal variety and a prime divisor $F$, we write $\mult_FD$ for the coefficient of $F$ in $D$. If $F$ is a prime divisor on a birational model $\pi\colon X'\to X$, write
\[
 K_{X'}+\Delta_{X'}=\pi^*(K_X+\Delta),
 \qquad
 A_{X,\Delta}(F):=1-\mult_F\Delta_{X'}.
\]
The sub-pair is \emph{sub-lc} if $A_{X,\Delta}(F)\geq0$ for every prime divisor $F$ over $X$. A pair is \emph{log canonical} (respectively, \emph{klt}) if $A_{X,\Delta}(F)\geq0$ (respectively, $>0$) for every prime divisor $F$ over $X$. A prime divisor $F$ with $A_{X,\Delta}(F)=0$ is an \emph{lc place}, and its center $c_X(F)$ on $X$ is an \emph{lc center}. 

For an effective $\mathbb Q$-divisor $\Delta$ on a smooth variety $X$, we denote by $\mathcal J(X,\Delta)$ its multiplier ideal \cite[\S9.2]{Laz04}.

[Lemma lem:conditions of arXiv:2503.21737, 'High-intensity Voronoi percolation on manifolds'] Let \(\xi \subset \mathbb R^d\) and \(\eta \subset M\) be locally finite deterministic point sets.
    Let \(\rho \in (0,1)\) and let \(r > 0\) so that \(8r\) satisfies (equation eq:radius_condition of the paper).
    Let \(x_0 \in M\) and \(\varphi \in \pazocal{E}(x_0,8r)\).
    Then the following conditions imply that \(\varphi_*\pazocal{G}_{M}(\eta)|_{B_{\mathbb R^d}(0,r)} = \pazocal{G}_{\mathbb R^d}(\xi)|_{B_{\mathbb R^d}(0,r)}\).
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \emph{Equality (EQL):} \(\varphi(\eta) = \xi \cap B_{\mathbb R^d}(0,8r)\).
        \item \emph{Robustness (ROB):} \(\xi\) is \((r,2\rho)\)-robust.
        \item \emph{Small cells (SMA):} \(\diam_{\mathbb R^d}(C(x,\xi)) \leq r\) for all \(x \in \xi \cap B_{\mathbb R^d}(0,r)\) and
                \(\diam_{M}(C(x,\eta)) \leq r\) for all \(x \in \eta \cap B_{M}(x_0,r)\).
        \item \emph{Similarity of metrics (SIM):}   \(\mathrm{d}_{\mathbb{R}^d} - \rho \cdot r \leq \varphi_*\mathrm{d}_M \leq \mathrm{d}_{\mathbb{R}^d} + \rho \cdot r\) on \(B_{\mathbb R^d}(0,8r)\).
    \end{itemize}

[Lemma lem:ldlt of arXiv:2607.05226, 'The Exact Worst-Case Tail Probability under Bounded Kurtosis'] Let $G$ be symmetric $n\times n$. Perform Gaussian elimination without pivoting, treating
the diagonal entries in order: if a pivot is negative, stop; if a pivot is zero, require
its entire row and column to be zero and skip it; otherwise eliminate below it. Then
$G\succeq0$ if and only if the elimination completes, i.e.\ every pivot encountered is
$\ge0$ and every zero pivot has an all-zero row.

body: In probability theory, the theory of large deviations concerns the asymptotic behaviour of remote tails of sequences of probability distributions. While some basic ideas of the theory can be traced to Laplace, the formalization started with insurance mathematics, namely ruin theory with Cramér and Lundberg. A unified formalization of large deviation theory was developed in 1966, in a paper by Varadhan. Large deviations theory formalizes the heuristic ideas of concentration of measures and widely generalizes the notion of convergence of probability measures.
title: Large deviations theory

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2606.17381, 'Large deviation principle for friendship-biases\\ in Galton--Watson trees'] {\bf [Target LDP]}

\begin{itemize}
\item[{\rm (a)}] 
The family of random variables $\{Z_j\}_{j\in\N}$ satisfies the LDP on $F_0$ with rate $j$ and with good rate function
\[
\Lambda^*(\theta) = \sup_{t\in\R^3} \{\langle t,\theta\rangle-\Lambda(t)\}, \qquad \theta\in F_0,
\]
which is the Fenchel--Legendre transform of $\Lambda$.
\item[{\rm (b)}] 
For every $\theta\in F_0 = [0,2] \times [0,\infty) \times [0,2]$,
\[
\Lambda^*(\theta) = \inf_{\nu\in G^{-1}(\theta)} I(\nu),
\]
where $G^{-1}(\theta)$ denotes the pre-image set $\{\nu\in\mathcal{P}(E)\colon\, G(\nu)=\theta\}$.

body:
For f(v,p)=v[a+b tanh(kp)] with fixed b,k>0, logistic Euclidean gradient flow has an exact complete basin classification. If |a|<b, the unique finite critical point (0,atanh(-a/b)/k) is a hyperbolic saddle with stable graph v=-sign(p-p*)sqrt(G(p)-G(p*)), where G'=2h/h'. Above and below the graph the two matching-sign escaping limits have open basins. If a>=b every finite initialization escapes positively; if a<=-b every one escapes negatively, including a=+-b. Here h(p)=a+b tanh(kp), G(p)=a p/(bk)+a sinh(2kp)/(2bk^2)+sinh^2(kp)/k^2. The stable graph is defined only in the straddling case |a|<b. For a>=b all trajectories escape positively, and for a<=-b all escape negatively. Normalized joint limits are (+1,0) and (-1,0), with hard selection and zero loss on escaping orbits. Joint margin means lim f/sqrt(v^2+p^2), not a homogeneous angular objective.
One positive example, two fixed scalar token values a+-b, attention gap 2kp, trained shared head v and scalar p, continuous time.

Here g(f)=1/(1+exp(f)). Historical draft labels below refer to the original proof-writing date, before that PASS. The local stable-manifold source is now verified: arXiv:1602.04915, stable_manifold_arxiv_v1.tex lines 222-225, Shub III.7.

# Target 1: affine two-token joint model (unaudited draft)

## Definition and conclusion

Fix a real a, b>0 and k>0. The two fixed scalar token values are x_+=a+b and x_-=a-b. Their attention weights are sigma(2kp) and 1-sigma(2kp). The trained parameters are a single shared prediction multiplier v and an unfactored scalar attention parameter p. Thus f(v,p)=v h(p), h(p)=a+b tanh(kp). One positive example is trained with logistic loss and Euclidean gradient flow. Tokens, b, k, and a are fixed, not independent trainable heads. This is an explicitly defined two-token extension of f=v tanh p. It does not cover every meaning of joint two-token training.

If |a|<b, there is exactly one finite critical point (0,p_*), p_*=atanh(-a/b)/k. It is a hyperbolic saddle. Define

  G(p) = a p/(bk) + a sinh(2kp)/(2bk^2) + sinh^2(kp)/k^2,
  F(p) = G(p)-G(p_*).

Then F>=0, with its only zero at p_*. The exact stable manifold is the graph

  v=B(p)=-sign(p-p_*) sqrt(F(p)), with B(p_*)=0.

Every point v>B(p) satisfies (v,p)->(+infinity,+infinity). Every point v<B(p) satisfies (v,p)->(-infinity,-infinity). Loss tends to zero in both basins. They are both nonempty and open. The stable graph has planar Lebesgue measure zero. Normalized joint parameter directions tend to (+1,0) and (-1,0); selected token values tend respectively to a+b and a-b.

If a>=b, there is no finite critical point and every trajectory satisfies (v,p)->(+infinity,+infinity). If a<=-b, there is no finite critical point and every trajectory satisfies (v,p)->(-infinity,-infinity). The boundary cases a=+b and a=-b are included: a zero-valued endpoint token does not create a finite stationary point or a finite-initialization basin escaping to that endpoint. All these conclusions concern forward time.

## Proof

As in proof 001, set ds/dt=g(f)>0, giving v'=h(p), p'=v h'(p) with h'=bk sech^2(kp)>0. Since |h|<=|a|+b and |h'|<=bk, there is no finite-time blow-up and s->infinity. Direct differentiation yields G'=2h/h', hence C=v^2-G(p) is constant.

When |a|<b, h vanishes only at p_*, and G decreases strictly to its minimum there and increases strictly afterwards. Also G tends to +infinity at either end, by its exponential terms (coefficients proportional to b-a on the left and b+a on the right). The shifted integral v^2-F is therefore conserved. Linearizing the s-time vector field at (0,p_*) gives [[0,h'(p_*)],[h'(p_*),0]], with real eigenvalues of opposite sign. In t-time multiply by g(0)=1/2. Near p_*, F(p)=(p-p_*)^2+O((p-p_*)^3), so the displayed graph is smooth with slope -1 at p_*.

The graph v=B(p) is the negative branch of v^2=F and has p' pointing toward p_*; monotonicity and the absence of any other zero imply convergence to (0,p_*). The positive branch escapes to the two matching-sign ends. For v^2-F=D>0, v keeps its sign and |v|>=sqrt(D); p'=vh' has constant sign. If p were bounded in that direction, h' would have a positive lower bound along its compact range and p' could not be integrable. Thus p diverges to that end, and the invariant forces |v|->infinity. For D<0, p stays on one side of p_* and a positive distance away from it. Hence h(p) has constant sign and magnitude bounded below. It follows that v diverges in that sign; the invariant then forces p to the corresponding end. These cases yield exactly the partition above/below B, even when p_* is nonzero.

When a>=b, h is strictly positive at every finite p; G is strictly increasing. Moreover G maps the real line onto the real line. For a>b its left exponential coefficient is negative. At a=b its exponential terms cancel at the left end and G(p)=p/k+O(1) there, still tending to -infinity. At the right end G->+infinity. For a fixed orbit C=v^2-G, there is a unique p_min with G(p_min)=-C. Hence p>=p_min always, h(p)>=h(p_min)>0, and v'=h(p) forces v through zero and then to +infinity. For all sufficiently large s, p increases; if it were bounded above, p'=v h' would preclude boundedness. Thus p->+infinity. The case a<=-b follows by (a,v,p)->(-a,-v,-p), which preserves the gradient-flow equations and the prediction. This also checks the zero-endpoint cases without an asymptotic assumption.

Finally, on any escaping orbit the leading positive exponential term of G at the selected end gives |p|=(log |v|)/k+O(1). Therefore |p|/|v|->0. The finite limiting h at that end has the sign of v and nonzero magnitude, implying f->+infinity and the stated directions and loss limit.

## Consequence for the proposed strict-saddle route

Define the natural joint directional margin on an escaping orbit as lim f(v,p)/sqrt(v^2+p^2). The two basins have margins a+b and b-a when |a|<b. The supremum possible asymptotic normalized margin is M=max(|a+b|,|a-b|)=b+|a|: the upper bound follows from |h|<=M and |v|<=sqrt(v^2+p^2), and each endpoint magnitude is achieved along its matching escaping branch. If 0<|a|<b, one entire open basin has strictly smaller margin b-|a|. Its planar measure is positive, so any initialization law assigning positive density throughout the plane has positive probability of this suboptimal selection. Each finite point in that basin has a neighborhood with the same limiting selection. Thus a universal strict-saddle or measure-zero-basin assertion for suboptimal joint selections fails for this whole parameter family and this definition of joint margin.

This does not contradict a fixed-prediction-head attention-SVM theorem. It does not identify a canonical homogeneous angular flow: f is not homogeneous in (v,p). It classifies actual limits and basins of the specified joint flow. [Mydef 1 of arXiv:2607.25986, 'Asymptotics of a two-species particle system associated to the doubly parabolic Keller-Seg'] Fix some $\rho_0 \in \Pp(\R^2)$ and some nonnegative $c_0\in L^\infty(\R^2)$. 
Consider the canonical space $C(\R_+,\R^2)$ equipped with its
canonical process $(w_t)_{t\geq 0}$ and its canonical filtration. Let $\Q \in \Pp(C(\R_+,\R^2))$
and denote $(\Q_t)_{t\geq 0}$ its family of one-dimensional time marginals. 
We say that $\Q$ solves the non-linear 
martingale problem $\mathcal{(MP)}(\rho_0,c_0)$ if
\begin{equation}

\int_0^t \int_{\R^2} \int_0^s \int_{\R^2}   (K^{\theta,\lambda}_{s-u}(x-y) + 
|\nabla K^{\theta,\lambda}_{s-u}(x-y)|) \Q_u(\dd y)  \dd u   \Q_s(\dd x) \dd s < \infty,
\end{equation}
and if for any $\varphi \in C_c^2(\R^2)$, the process
\begin{equation}

M^\varphi_t:=\varphi(w_t)-f(w_0)-\int_0^t \Big[ \Delta \varphi(w_u)+\chi \nabla \varphi(w_u)\cdot 
\Big(\nabla b_s^{c_0,\theta,\lambda}(w_s) + \int_0^u (\nabla K^{\theta,\lambda}_{u-r}\ast \Q_r)(w_u) \dd r \Big) \Big]\dd u
\end{equation}
is a $\Q$-martingale.

[Corollary eq:EGWtoEOT of arXiv:2609.03094, 'Discrete Gromov--Wasserstein Duality: Algorithms and Isomorphism Testing'] For any $\varepsilon \geq 0$,   
$   \mathsf{EGW}_p^{\varepsilon}(\mu_0,\mu_1)$ can be expressed as $ \inf_{u\in\mathbb R^{r_0}}\sup_{v\in\mathbb R^{r_1}}\left\{\frac 12 \|u\|^2-\frac 12 \|v\|^2+\mathsf{EOT}^{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{B}_1^{\intercal}v-\mathrm{B}_0^{\intercal}u}(\mu_0,\mu_1)\right\},
$
where $\mathsf{EOT}^{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{B}_1^{\intercal}v-\mathrm{B}_0^{\intercal}u}(\mu_0,\mu_1)$ is the EOT problem $\min_{x\in\mathcal K}\left\{\left( \mathrm{B}^{\intercal}_1v-\mathrm{B}_0^{\intercal} u \right)^{\intercal}x-\varepsilon(\mathsf{H}(x)-\mathsf{H}_{\mu_0}-\mathsf{H}_{\mu_1})  \right\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: From EGW to EOT

body: In probability theory, a Chernoff bound is an exponentially decreasing upper bound on the tail of a random variable based on its moment generating function. The minimum of all such exponential bounds forms the Chernoff or Chernoff-Cramér bound, which may decay faster than exponential. It is especially useful for sums of independent random variables, such as sums of Bernoulli random variables.
title: Chernoff bound

Every set can be well-ordered: for every set X there is a total order on X in which every non-empty subset has a least element. Over the Zermelo-Fraenkel axioms ZF this statement is equivalent to the axiom of choice and to Zorn's lemma, so it is a theorem of ZFC and is not provable in ZF alone.
ZFC; in ZF without choice the statement can fail

body:
[Definition Stochastically continuous Feller semigroup of arXiv:2412.01381, 'Ergodicity and mixing for locally monotone stochastic evolution equations'] We say that $(P_t)_{t\ge 0}$ is a stochastically continuous Feller semigroup if for every $x\in H$ and every $r>0$ it follows that
\[\lim_{t\to 0} P_t^\ast\delta_x (B(x,r))=1
\quad \textrm{ and }\quad
P_t(C_b(H))\subset C_b(H),
\]
where $B(x,r):=\{y\in H:\|y\|_H<r\}$,
$\delta_x$ denotes the Dirac delta measure at $x$
and 
 $C_b(H):=\{F:H\to \mathbb{R}:\,F\textrm{ is continuous and bounded}\}$.
title: Stochastically continuous Feller semigroup

[Definition def_permutation_permuton of arXiv:2412.07258, 'Permuton limit of a generalization of the Mallows and $k$-card-minimum models'] If $\sigma \in S_n$, let $\mu_\sigma$ denote the permuton  with joint p.d.f.\
$f_\sigma(x,y)=n \cdot \mathds{1}[ \sigma(\lceil n \cdot x \rceil)=\lceil n \cdot y \rceil ]$ if $(x,y)\in (0,1]^2$ and zero otherwise. Let $F_{\sigma}$ denote the joint c.d.f.\ of $\mu_\sigma$. Thus,
for $i,j \in \{0, 1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ we have
\begin{align}

F_\sigma\Big(\frac{i}{n},\frac{j}{n}\Big) &= \frac{1}{n}\sum_{t=1}^{i} \mathds{1}[\, \sigma(t) \leqslant j \, ]=\frac{1}{n} \cdot\left| [j] \setminus D^{(n)}_{i+1} \right| ,
\\ 
V_\sigma\Big(\frac{i}{n},\frac{j}{n}\Big) &=
 \frac{1}{n}\sum_{t=1}^{n} \mathds{1}[\, t \leqslant i \, \text{ or } \, \sigma(t) \leqslant j \,] = \frac{i}{n} +\frac{j}{n}-F_\sigma\Big(\frac{i}{n},\frac{j}{n}\Big).
\end{align}
title: Permutations as permutons

[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2604.11921, 'Replica symmetry up to the de Almeida--Thouless line in the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model'] \label[proposition]{prop:soft-mtg}
The process $M_t=u_x(t,X_t)$ is a martingale on $[0,q]$ and satisfies
\[
dM_t=\beta u_{xx}(t,X_t)\,dW_t.
\]
Further,
\begin{equation}
g'(t)=\beta^2\E\big[ u_{xx}(t,X_t)^2\big]
\le \beta^2\E\big[\sech^4(X_q)\big],
\qquad 0<  t<q.
\end{equation}

[Thm 2 (Positive mass theorem and rigidity) of arXiv:2608.29427, '\small Positive mass and rigidity \\ for asymptotically flat tangent bundles'] Let $(M^n,g)$ be a complete asymptotically Euclidean manifold with decay rates
	\[
	\sigma_a>\frac{n-2}{2},
	\]
	and suppose that $\scal_g$ is nonnegative and integrable. Then the ADM mass of each end of $M$ is nonnegative. Moreover, if the ADM mass of an end vanishes, then $(M,g)$ is isometric to $(\mathbb R^n,\delta)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Positive mass theorem and rigidity

[Thm1 17 of arXiv:2608.29797, 'Mean-field branching SDEs: propagation of chaos, scaling limits and phase transitions'] Let $X$ be the solution of the logistic mean-field equation displayed above
with $X_0=x>0$. Then the following assertions hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] (Exact no-hitting criterion) $\mbb P_x(\tau_0<\infty)=0$ if and only if $am_t\geq\sigma$ for every $t\geq0$.
\item[(ii)] (Almost-sure hitting under eventual subcritical immigration) If $\limsup_{t\to\infty}am_t<\sigma$, then
$\mbb P_x(\tau_0<\infty)=1$. In particular, this conclusion holds when $a\leq a_\star^{\rm log}$;
\item[(iii)] (Classification by the interaction strength) $ a_{\text{hit}}>a_\star^{\rm log}$. Moreover,
$\mbb P_x(\tau_0<\infty)=1$ if $a<a_{\text{hit}}$, whereas
$\mbb P_x(\tau_0<\infty)<1$ if $a>a_{\text{hit}}$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm1 17 of arXiv:2608.29797

[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2607.12384, '2607.12384'] For \(t>0\), the following properties hold. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}, ref=\textup{(\roman*)}] 
		\item 
		For every \(x\in\mathbb R\), 
		\[ G_t(x)\ge0,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}G_t(x)\,dx=1, \] 
		and 
		\[ G_t(x)=G_t(-x). \] 
		\item  The kernel \(G_t\) satisfies the scaling property
		\[ G_t(x) = t^{-\beta/\alpha} G_1\left(t^{-\beta/\alpha}x\right). \] 
		\item  There exists a constant \(C>0\) such that \[ \|G_t^{1/2}\|_{L^1(\mathbb R)} \le Ct^{\frac{\beta}{2\alpha}}. \] 
		\item  There exists a constant \(C>0\) such that \[ \|G_t^{1/2}*G_t^{1/2}\|_{L^1(\mathbb R)} \le Ct^{\frac \beta\alpha}. \]

body:
[Proposition prop:CE-law-with-floor of arXiv:2509.04333, 'The limiting law of the Discrete Gaussian level lines'] Fix $n\geq 1$. Let $V\subset \mathbb Z^2$ be a connected domain, and consider the \ensuremath{\mathbb Z\textsc{gff}}\xspace model $\pi_{V;F}^{\xi}$ with a floor at~0 imposed only on a subset $F\subset V$, and boundary conditions $\xi$ that are $H+1-n$ on a $*$-connected path in $\partial_{\mathtt v} V$ and $H-n$ elsewhere so that they induce a unique disagreement polymer $(\gamma,\{D_i\},\{h_i\})$ in $V\cup \partial_{\mathtt v} V$ that contains boundary disagreements\footnote{We say the disagreement polymer contains boundary disagreements if it contains a bond dual to ${\ensuremath{\mathsf u}}\mathsf v$ for ${\ensuremath{\mathsf u}},\mathsf v\notin V$.}.  Then for $\beta\geq \beta_0$, the law of this unique disagreement polymer $\gamma$ is given by 
		\begin{align}
			\pi^{\xi}_{V;F}(\gamma) =\frac1{Z} \exp\bigg(-{\ensuremath{\mathscr E}}_\beta(\gamma) + \sum_{\substack{{\ensuremath{\mathsf W}}\subset V \\ {\ensuremath{\mathsf W}} \cap \Delta_\gamma \neq \emptyset}} \Phi({\ensuremath{\mathsf W}})
			\bigg)\prod_{i\geq 0}{\widehat\pi}_{D_i^\circ}^{h_i}\big(\phi_x \geq 0,\, \forall x \in D_i^{\circ}\cap F\big)\,,
		\end{align}
		for a normalizer $Z= Z(V,F,\xi,\beta,n)$ and a decoration function $\Phi({\ensuremath{\mathsf W}})$ as per (def:disagree-polymer-len-energy-decor of the paper).
		
		Moreover, if we further have $|F| \leq L e^{\kappa\sqrt{\log L}}$ and $|\partial F|\leq L^{1-\delta}$ for fixed $\kappa>0$ and $0<\delta<\frac13$, denote by $D_0$ and $D_1$ the regions of $\gamma$ containing the boundary vertices of $V$ at heights $H+1-n$ and $H-n$, respectively, and let
		\begin{align*} E:=\left\{|\gamma|\leq L^{1-\delta}\,,\;
			\;|F| - |D_0 \cap F| - |D_1 \cap F| \leq L^{1-\delta}\right\}\,,\end{align*}
		then the following holds
		for all $\beta\geq \beta_0$ (not depending on $\kappa,\delta$). The probability distribution given~by 
		\[ p_{V;F}^{\xi}(\gamma) := 
		\frac1{\overline Z} \exp\bigg(-{\ensuremath{\mathscr E}}_\beta(\gamma) + \frac{|D_0\cap F|}{N_n}+ \sum_{\substack{{\ensuremath{\mathsf W}}\subset V \\ {\ensuremath{\mathsf W}} \cap \Delta_\gamma \neq \emptyset}} \Phi({\ensuremath{\mathsf W}})  \bigg)\prod_{i \geq 2}{\widehat\pi}_{D_i^\circ}^{h_i}(\phi_x \geq 0,\, \forall x \in D_i^{\circ}\cap F)
		\]
        for $\gamma\in E$, where $\overline Z = \overline{Z}(V,F,\xi,\beta,n)$ is a normalizer, satisfies		\begin{align}
			\pi^\xi_{V;F}(\gamma \mid E) =(1+o(1))p_{V;F}^{\xi}(\gamma)\,.
		\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:kernel-sum of arXiv:2609.02544, 'A finiteness theorem for geodesic Leech wheels'] Let $M\ge3$, $R=\floor{(M-1)/2}$, and $\rho=\rho_R$, so that $R\ge1$ and the kernel $K_R$ of Lemma~(lem:kernel of the paper) is defined. Suppose $S\subseteq\{0,1,\ldots,M-1\}$ has $\abs S$ elements, of which $h$ exceed $R$. With $\zeta=\mathrm{e}^{2\pi i/M}$ and $F(z)=\sum_{a\in S}z^a$, if some $U>0$ satisfies $\abs{F(\zeta^t)}\le U$ for all $t\in\{1\}\cup\{2,4,6,\ldots,2R\}$, then
\begin{equation}
  \left(\frac\pi2+\rho\right)U
  \ge
  \sum_{a\in S}K_R\!\left(\frac{2\pi a}{M}\right)
  \ge\rho\abs S-\pi h.
\end{equation}

[Proposition 17 (Singular sine-cone limit) of arXiv:2609.02788, '\textbf{Quantized Einstein Metrics on \(S^7\) with \(SU(3)\)-Symmetry}'] Let $h_2$ be the nonnormal Einstein metric on $SU(3)/T^2$ determined by
\[
 f_1=f_2=\frac1{\sqrt5},\qquad f_3=\sqrt{\frac25}.
\]
Then, on the regular part and after the natural equivariant identification,
\begin{equation}
 g_n\longrightarrow g_{\mathrm{sc}}:=dt^2+\sin^2t\,h_2
\end{equation}
in $C^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}((0,\pi)\times SU(3)/T^2)$.  The metric completion
of $g_{\mathrm{sc}}$ has two conical singularities, and its tangent cone at
either end is the asymptotic cone of $g_{\RF,*}$.

[Lemma lem:ExpIneqM of arXiv:2608.30848, '\huge \bf Limit Laws of the Iterated Logarithm Under Sub-linear Expectations'] Let $\{X_n; n\ge 1\}$ be a martingale difference sequence on a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\textsf{P})$ with respect to the $\sigma$-field filtration $\{\mathcal F_n\}$, and assume $|X_n|\le c$ a.s. Then
$$ \textsf{P}\bigg( \sum_{i=1}^n X_i\ge x \text{ and } \sum_{i=1}^n \textsf{E}[X_i^2|\mathcal{F}_{i-1}]\le y\; \text{ for some } n \text{ hold} \bigg)
\le \exp\bigg\{ -\frac{x^2}{2(xc+y)}\bigg\}.   $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:Xt-from-V-to-U of arXiv:2507.16188, 'The noisy voter model with general initial conditions'] The following holds for every {\upshape\texttt{good}\xspace} collection $\{V_i\}_{i=1}^m$. Let $\tau_i$ be the minimum $s\geq 0$ where the backward dynamics, started at time $t_1$ from every $v\in V_i$, has its surviving history reach size at most $3$ at time $t_1-s$, or $\tau_i=t_1$ if the backward dynamics reaches time $0$ before this happens. Further let $U_i$ be the surviving history at time $\tau_i$. Then there exists some $C=C(q,\theta)>0$ such that
\begin{align*}\Big\|\prod_{i=1}^m\mathbb{P}_{\mathsf{x}_0}\big(X_{t_1}^{(i)}(V_i) \in \cdot\big) - \prod_{i=1}^m \mu_G\mathord{\upharpoonright}_{V_i} \Big\|_{\textsc{tv}}^2
\leq C\, &\mathbb{E}\bigg[
\sum_{i=1}^m
\Big\| \mathbb{P}_{\mathsf{x}_0}\big( X_{t_1-\tau_i}^{(i)}(U_i)\in\cdot\big) - 
\mu_G\mathord{\upharpoonright}_{U_i} \Big\|_{\textsc{tv}}^2 \mathbbm{1}_{\{\tau_i<t_1\}}
\bigg] \\
&+ O\big(e^{-8(\log n)^{1-\frac\upalpha2}}\big)\,.
\end{align*}

[Theorem theo.SRW of arXiv:2411.19145, 'On the intersection of critical percolation clusters and other tree-like random graphs'] Let $R_\infty^k$, $k\ge 1$, be independent SRW ranges on $\mathbb Z^d$. 
\begin{enumerate}  
\item[(i)] If $d\ge 5$, then for any $k\ge 2$, there exist positive constants $c_1,c_2$, such that for any $t>1$, 
$$\exp(-c_1\, t^{1-\frac 2d}) \le \mathbb P(|R_\infty^1\cap \dots \cap R_\infty^k|>t) \le  \exp(-c_2\, t^{1-\frac 2d}). $$ 
\item[(ii)] If $d=4$, then for any $k\ge 3$, there exist positive constants $c_1,c_2$, such that for any $t>e$, 
$$\exp(-c_1\, \sqrt{t} ) \le \mathbb P(|R_\infty^1\cap \dots \cap R_\infty^k|>t) \le  \exp\big(-c_2\, (\frac{t}{\log t})^{1/2}\big).$$
\item[(iii)] If $d=3$, then for any $k\ge 4$, there exist positive constants $c_1,c_2$, such that for any $t>e$, 
$$\exp(-c_1\, t^{1/3}) \le \mathbb P(|R_\infty^1\cap \dots \cap R_\infty^k|>t) \le  \exp(-c_2\, (\frac t{\log t})^{1/3}). $$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem theo.SRW of arXiv:2411.19145

Own-work draft, proof (unaudited), T280-w716-C6 v1; C5 v1 is independently checked (urn:mb-agent:7a4f9e38007c2a28 PASS), classified SPECIAL. Fix k>=1 and q in (0,1). Use C5 reference constants at residual fraction q/4: m=k+1,h,T,d0 and pre-crossing bounds |a|<=H, |b|<=H^2/2, ||w||/sqrt(d)<=G. Define K=1+max(H,H^2/2,G), M=20(1+K)exp(K+4K^2), L=M^2+M, epsilon=min(h/3,1/2,sqrt(q)/(2M))*exp(-L*T). For each d>=d0, uniform unit-sphere inputs and known unit axis u, every initial law with a0=b0=0 and a coupling to j uniform on {0,...,k} satisfying ||w0/sqrt(d)-j*h*u||<=epsilon almost surely learns any unit-L2 polynomial of degree at most k in sqrt(d)*x.u to full residual energy q by time T under ordinary all-parameter Euclidean population mean-field flow with activation exp. Cluster laws may be continuous and nonatomic and weights may be off-axis. Balanced masses 1/m and the prepared normalized-weight neighborhoods are explicit assumptions. In normalized coordinates zeta=(a,b,p=w/sqrt(d)), the original flow is -diag(1,1,I_d/d)*(D Phi_zeta)^*r, with Phi=a exp(b+p.X) and X=sqrt(d)x. Dimension-uniform sub-Gaussian operator derivative bounds give ||f-bar f||2<=M Delta and Delta(t)<=Delta(0)exp((M^2+M)t) in essential-sup characteristic distance. The reference q/4 crossing then yields the q bound. This is a positive-width extension of an engineered warm start; it does not derive that warm start from degree-1 training, prove random-start or new-direction times, or close T280. No novelty or independent/formal certificate asserted.

body:
Let P be a product measure on {0,1}^E and let A_1, ..., A_k be INCREASING events with the same probability. Then max_i P(A_i) = P(A_1) >= 1 - ( 1 - P( union_i A_i ) )^{1/k}. More generally, without assuming equal probabilities, max_i P(A_i) >= 1 - (1 - P(union_i A_i))^{1/k}. The name comes from the case k = 2, where the bound reads P(A_1) >= 1 - sqrt(1 - P(A_1 or A_2)): if the union is very likely then at least one of two increasing events is likely, quantitatively. This is the standard device for turning a statement like 'some crossing of a box occurs' into 'a crossing in a specific direction occurs with probability bounded below', and it is the engine of Zhang's argument that theta(1/2) = 0 for bond percolation on Z^2. The events must be INCREASING, since the proof is Harris-FKG applied to their complements; for arbitrary events the inequality is false. [standard; e.g. Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed., proof of Theorem 11.11, and Bollobas-Riordan, Percolation]
product measure
all the events increasing (the proof uses FKG on the decreasing complements)

body:
For any connected simple graph G with maximum degree Delta, the chromatic number satisfies chi(G) <= Delta, unless G is a complete graph or an odd cycle, in which cases chi(G) = Delta + 1.

The bound includes maximum degrees Delta=0,1,2: a connected graph with Delta=0 is K_1, with chi=1; a connected graph with Delta=1 is K_2, with chi=2; for Delta=2, every non-odd-cycle connected graph is 2-colorable, while an odd cycle has chi=3. Thus for every connected simple graph of finite maximum degree Delta, chi(G)<=Delta unless G is complete or an odd cycle, in which cases chi(G)=Delta+1.
G is a connected simple graph with finite maximum degree Delta >= 0

[Definition 4 (Aggregated seating sequence) of arXiv:2606.01881, '2606.01881'] Let $\mathcal B=\{B_r:r\ge1\}$ be a partition of $\mathbb N$ whose blocks are ordered by their least elements:
\[
        \min B_1<\min B_2<\cdots.
\]
Given a seating sequence $C=(C_i:i\ge1)$, define the aggregated seating sequence $C^{\mathcal B}$ by
\[
        C_i^{\mathcal B}=r\quad\text{if and only if}\quad C_i\in B_r.
\]
This is the external, block-level dynamics: it records which block is visited, but not which original table inside that block is chosen.
title: Aggregated seating sequence

[Defn Radical and irreducible quotient of arXiv:2506.01306, 'Asymptotic of Coulomb gas integral, Temperley-Lieb type algebras and pure partition functi'] Let $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_{n,p}$ be the invariant bilinear form on $V_{n,p}$ defined below. The \emph{radical} of $V_{n,p}$ is the null space of this form:
\[
R_{n,p} := \{ x \in V_{n,p} \mid \langle x, y \rangle = 0 \text{ for all } y \in V_{n,p} \}.
\]
The \emph{irreducible quotient} of $V_{n,p}$ is
\[
L_{n,p} := V_{n,p} / R_{n,p}.
\]
title: Radical and irreducible quotient

[Definition def:Skorohod-integral of arXiv:2603.01823, 'on a fractional stochastic heat equation arising from the disordered pinning model'] Let $D=\{1,\cdots,\mathrm{max(D)}\}$ be finite or let $D=\mathbb N$, and  $u$ be a random process on $[0,T]$ measurable with respect to $\sigma(\xi_k:k\in D)$. Denote
$$u_k:=\langle u, e_k\rangle_{\mathcal H}=\int_0^T\int_0^T e_k(t)u(s) |t-s|^{2H-2}{\mathrm d} t{\mathrm d} s.$$   
We say that $u$ is $L^1$-Skorohod integrable with Skorohod integral $S$,  if $u_k\in L^1$ for each $k\in D$  and $U=(u_k,k\in D)$ is $L^1$-Skorohod integrable with Skorohod integral $S$ in the sense of Definition~(def-Skorohod of the paper). We  denote the $L^1$-Skorohod integral $S$ for the random  process $u$ by 
\[S:=\int{\raisebox{-.82em}{\hspace{-1.18em}\scriptsize \bf o}}\hspace{.7em} u \,\xi.\]
title: $L^1$-Skorohod integral for random processes

[Lemma lem:bottle-events-TwoStream of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix $\lambda \in (0,1/2)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$.  
Let $i$ be a sufficiently large integer and suppose that bin~$i$ is a bottleneck. 
Let $j= \lfloor c_{\mathrm{b}} \log i \rfloor$.  
Let $\overline{z}\in (\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0})^j$ be a $j$-tuple such that, for all $x\in [j]$, $z_x \geq \lambda W_x/4$. 
 Let $Z=(Z^A,Z^B)$ be a two-stream process with birth rate~$2\lambda$, send sequence $\overline{p}$, and start time~$\tau$ where 
$\mathrm{dist}(\overline{\mathrm{arr}}^{Z^A}_{[j]}(\tau) ,\overline{\mathrm{arr}}^{Z^B}_{[j]}(\tau))\gtrsim \mathsf{Po}(\overline{z},\overline{z})$.
(We do not make any assumptions about
$\mathrm{arr}_k^{Z^A}(\tau)$ or $\mathrm{arr}_k^{Z^B}(\tau)$ for $k>j$.)
Let $T' = \tau + i \lceil  \exp((\log i)^{2/3} ) \rceil$.
Then $\mathbb{P}(
\mathcal{E}^{Z^A,\mathcal{N}}_{\leq T'} \cap \mathcal{E}^{Z^B,\mathcal{N}}_{\leq T'} \cap 
\mathcal{E}^{Z^A,\mathbf{s}}_{\leq T'} \cap \mathcal{E}^{Z^B,\mathbf{s}}_{\leq T'}
) \geq W_i^{-1/6} $.

[Lemma S_bound of arXiv:2607.22480, 'Distinguishability threshold for random geometric graphs'] Under the \hyperref[setup:star]{Setup ($\star$)}{}, we have
\begin{align*}
\log \mathbb{E}[e^{S}]&\leq A_s+\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\sum_{s<i<j\leq n}\lambda_{si}\lambda_{sj}\lambda_{ij}-\frac{1}{2d}\sum_{s<i<j\leq n}\lambda_{si}^2\lambda_{sj}^2\lambda_{ij}^2
+\frac{1}{d}\!\!\sum_{\substack{s<r\leq n\\ s<i< j\leq n}}\!\!\!\!\!\! \lambda_{si}\lambda_{sj}\lambda_{ri}\lambda_{rj}\\
&+\frac{1}{d}\!\!\sum_{\substack{s<r\leq n\\ s<i< j\leq n}}\!\!\!\!\!\! \lambda_{si}\lambda_{sj}\lambda_{ri}\lambda_{rj}\big(\lambda_{ij}(z_p-\lambda_{ij})+\lambda_{sr}(z_p-\lambda_{sr})\big) +\widetilde O\Big(\frac{n^{3/2}p^{1/2}}{d}+\frac{p^2n^3}{d^{3/2}}+\frac{p^2n^4}{d^2}\Big) .
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 14 of arXiv:2606.23896, 'The one-point Schreier Poisson boundary of Thompson's group \(F\)'] Equip \(\mathbb Z_2^\times\) with the standard 2-adic
metric \(d_2(x,y)=|x-y|_2\). The harmonic measure \(\nu\) is
exact-dimensional, and its pointwise dimension is

\[
\dim\nu
=
\frac{
-(2-\sqrt2)\log(2-\sqrt2)
-(\sqrt2-1)\log(\sqrt2-1)
}{\log 2}
\approx 0.9786600844 .
\]

Equivalently, this is the Hausdorff dimension of the measure \(\nu\).
