body:
[Thm Existence of arXiv:2506.01746, '\bf Optimal Bregman quantization: existence and uniqueness of optimal quantizers revisited'] Assume that the distribution $P$ satisfies the moment assumption~(equation eq:Integrabilite of the paper) (with $r=2$). Moreover, if     

 $U$ is unbounded and $d\ge 2$, assume that  the $F$-Bregman divergence $\phi= \phi_{_F}$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
\forall \xi \!\in U

, \quad \liminf_{x\to \infty,\, x\in U}\phi_{_F}(\xi, x)= \sup _{x\in U} \phi_{_F}(\xi,x).
\end{equation} 

\medskip
\noindent $(a)$ Then for every $n\ge1$ there exists an $n$-tuple $x^{(n)}= \big(x^{(n)}_1, \ldots, x^{(n)}_n\big) \!\in U^n$ which minimizes $G_{n}$ over $U^n$. Moreover, if  the support (in $U$) of the distribution $P$ has at least $n$ points then $x^{(n)}$ has pairwise distinct components and $P\big(\mathring C_i(x^{(n)})\big)>0$ for every $i\!\in \{1,\ldots,n\}$.

\smallskip
\noindent $(b)$ The distribution  $P$ assigns no mass to the boundary of Bregman--Voronoi partitions of $x^{(n)}$, i.e.
\[
P\left (\bigcup_{i=1}^n\partial C_i\big( x^{(n)})\right) = 0,
\]
and $x^{(n)}$ satisfies the $\phi_{_F}$-stationary (or master) equation
\begin{equation}
P\big( C_i(x^{(n)})\big)\,x^{(n)}_i  -  \int_{ C_i(x^{(n)})} \xi P(\mathrm{d}\xi) =0, \quad  i =1,\ldots,n.
\end{equation}
 
\noindent $(c)$ The sequence $\displaystyle G_{n}\big( x^{(n)}\big) = \min_{U^n} G_{n}$ decreases as long as it is not $0$ and converges to $0$ as $n$ goes to $+\infty$.

\noindent $(d)$ When $d=1$, the above claims $(a)$-$(b)$-$(c)$ remain true without assuming~(equation eq:boundary-lsc of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Existence for $r=2$ and $n\ge 2$

body:
[Lemma 45 (Stability of the scalar variational problem) of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Let $\mu_d,\mu$ be probability measures on $\R$ with finite second moments,
and suppose that $m_{\mu_d}\to m_\mu$ and $s_{\mu_d}\to s_\mu$
locally uniformly.  Fix $c>-1$ and $\zeta\in\R$, and let $\omega_d,\omega$
be the unique solutions of
$\omega_d+\zeta=c\,m_{\mu_d}(\omega_d)$ and
$\omega+\zeta=c\,m_\mu(\omega)$, respectively.  Then
\[
\omega_d\to\omega,
\qquad
s_{\mu_d}(\omega_d)+c\,m_{\mu_d}(\omega_d)^2
\to
s_\mu(\omega)+c\,m_\mu(\omega)^2.
\]
The same conclusion holds in probability if $\mu_d$ are random and the
local uniform convergence holds in probability.

[Markloflemma 10 of arXiv:2609.03112, '2609.03112'] Let $\{\lambda_m:m\in M\}$ be represented by the rational theta data of
\cref{lem:rational-theta}, and let $w$ be a smooth angular weight.  Suppose
that, for $w$ and $w^2$, the weighted Weyl law
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{X\to\infty}\frac1X\sum_{m\in M}
 w(m)\varphi(\lambda_m/X)
 =d(w)\int_0^\infty\varphi(t)\,dt
\end{equation}
holds for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\R_{>0})$.  If the irrational affine
coordinate is Diophantine and $m=n$ is the only bulk collision on
$\operatorname{supp}(w)\times\operatorname{supp}(w)$, then
\begin{align}
 &\lim_{X\to\infty}\frac1X
 \sum_{\substack{m,n\in M\\m\ne n}}
 w(m)w(n)
 \psi_1\!\left(\frac{\lambda_m}{X}\right)
 \psi_2\!\left(\frac{\lambda_n}{X}\right)
 \widehat h(\lambda_m-\lambda_n)\notag\\
 &\qquad=d(w)^2
 \left(\int_\R\widehat h(s)\,ds\right)
 \left(\int_0^\infty\psi_1(t)\psi_2(t)\,dt\right)
\end{align}
for $\psi_1,\psi_2\in C_c^\infty(\R_{>0})$ and $h\in C_c(\R)$.

[Corollary 8 of arXiv:2606.31528, 'Well-posedness and stationary distribution of free stochastic differential equations'] Assume the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:stationary}. Let $\mu$ be the stationary distribution for the solution $\{U_t\}_{t\geq 0}.$ Then for every $ f \in C_c^3(\mathbb{R}) $, there exist constants $ C_f, C >0$, independent of $ t $, such that

\bigl| \tau\bigl(f(U_t)\bigr) - \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(x) \, \mu( {\rm d} x) \bigr| \le C_f e^{-C t} \|U_0\|_2.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

$\mathcal E_\tau(\xi):=\{\eta\in\{-1,1\}^{\Lambda_M\setminus\partial\Lambda_M}:\xi\oplus\eta\in \mathcal E_\tau\}.$
Then there exist deterministic boundary data
$$
    \mathcal P_0(\xi),\; \mathcal P_1(\xi)\subset \partial\Lambda_M,
    \qquad
    \mathcal U(\xi)=\{U_1(\xi),\ldots,U_m(\xi)\},
$$
satisfying the assumptions of Definition (def: boundary connectivity event of the paper), such that, with
$\mathcal Y_\xi,\mathcal X_\xi,\mathcal R_\xi,\mathcal S_\xi$ defined from these data as in Definition
(def: boundary connectivity event of the paper), the following identities hold:
\begin{equation}
    \mathcal E_\tau(\xi)=\mathcal R_\xi
    \quad\text{if }\tau_i=0,\mbox{and }\mathcal E_\tau(\xi)=\mathcal S_\xi
    \quad\text{if }\tau_i=1.
    
\end{equation}
Here, the equalities are identities of events in the inside
configuration $\eta$.  If $\mathcal E_\tau(\xi)$ is empty, both sides are
understood to be empty after the corresponding boundary data have been
defined; such exterior configurations do not contribute to conditional
expectations given $\mathcal E_\tau$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem T:locally attracting of arXiv:2411.01364, 'Global Dynamics of Granular Media Equations via Stochastic Order'] {\rm (Local attractor).} 
Let $P^*$ be an order-preserving semiflow on $\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R)$.
Assume that there exist a positively invariant bounded open set $B\subset\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R)$ and an order-bounded closed set $K\subset\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R)$ such that $K$ attracts $B$. Assume further there is only one invariant measure $\mu_{0}$ in $\overline{B}$. 
Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
    \item If $\mu_0\geq_{\mathrm{st}}\omega(B)$ and there exists another invariant measure $\mu_{-1}<_{\mathrm{st}}\mu_0$ with an increasing connecting orbit $\{\nu^{-1,0}_t\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ from $\mu_{-1}$ to $\mu_{0}$ such that $\nu^{-1,0}_{t_{-1}}\leq_{\mathrm{st}}\omega(B)$ for some $t_{-1}\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\mu_{0}$ attracts $B$.
    \item If $\mu_{0}\leq_{\mathrm{st}}\omega(B)$ and there exists another invariant measure $\mu_{1}>_{\mathrm{st}}\mu_{0}$ with a decreasing connecting orbit $\{\nu^{1,0}_t\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ from $\mu_1$ to $\mu_{0}$ such that $\nu^{1,0}_{t_{1}}\geq_{\mathrm{st}}\omega(B)$ for some $t_{1}\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\mu_{0}$ attracts $B$.
    \item If there exist another two invariant measures $\mu_{-1}<_{\mathrm{st}}\mu_{0}$ and $\mu_{1}>_{\mathrm{st}}\mu_{0}$ with an increasing connecting orbit $\{\nu^{-1,0}_t\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ from $\mu_{-1}$ to $\mu_{0}$ and a decreasing connecting orbit $\{\nu^{1,0}_t\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ from $\mu_1$ to $\mu_{0}$ such that, $\nu^{-1,0}_{t_{-1}}\leq_{\mathrm{st}}\omega(B)$ for some $t_{-1}\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\nu^{1,0}_{t_{1}}\geq_{\mathrm{st}}\omega(B)$ for some $t_{1}\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\mu_{0}$ attracts $B$.
\end{enumerate}

depending on $l$ and $v$,

\E[\nu_{A,\varepsilon}(z)^{2 l}]

\end{equation}

[Lemme 57 of arXiv:2604.00635, 'Large deviations of the periodic Toda chain'] Let $\mu \in \mathcal{M}_1(\mathbb{R})$ be atomless and such that there exists $\theta>1$

$$

\Int{\mathbb{R}}{} |x|^{\theta} \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \, < \,  +\infty \qquad  \mbox{and }  \qquad  \Int{\mathbb{R}}{} x \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \, = \,  0 \, .

$$

Then, there exists a constant $\eta_0(\mu)> 0$ such that for any $0 < \eta < \eta_0(\mu)$, there exist $K_1, K_2 > 0$ such that

\begin{align*}

\Int{-K_1}{K_2} x \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) = 0 \;, \qquad \mu\big[ [-K_1; K_2]^c \big] \,  \leq \, \eta \;, \qquad

\Int{}{} \mathbbm{1}_{[-K_1;K_2]^c}(x)  |x| \, \mathrm{d}\mu(x) \,  \leq  \, \eta \, .

\end{align*}

Furthermore $\mathbbm{1}_{[-K_1;K_2]} \to 1$ as $\eta \searrow 0$ $\mu$-almost everywhere, in an increasing fashion. Finally, there exists $C>0$ such that

\beq

K_1+K_2 \, \leq \, \f{ C }{ \eta^{   \f{1}{\theta-1} }  } \;.

\enq (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2608.18557, 'Randomly Permuted Orthogonal Products and Fast Dimension Reduction'] Let \(P\) be a rank-\(m\) orthogonal projection on \(\R^d\), let $\rho=\max_{j\in[d]} P_{jj}$, and let \(q\) be a probability measure on \([d]\). Set
	\[ \sigma^2 = \frac{\rho \|q\|_2^2}{d}, \qquad M=\rho\|q\|_\infty.\]
	If \(\pi\) is uniform on \(S_d\), then
	\[
	\probb{\pi}{\norm{PD_{q_\pi}P - \frac{1}{d}P}\geq t}
	\le
	2m\exp\left(
	-\frac{t^2}
	{12\sigma^2+4\sqrt2\,Mt}
	\right)
	\qquad \text{for }t\geq0.
	\]

[Proposition 4 of arXiv:2608.30409, 'Gradient estimates and volume doubling for locally finite weighted graphs with $CD\psi(n,-'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be a locally finite weighted graph. For all $x,y\in V$  and $f,g\in \ell^{\infty}(V)$, the following properties hold 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $P_{0}=I, \ \ P_{t}P_{s}=P_{t+s}$.
        \item $f\ge 0 $ implies $P_{t}f\ge0$, and $f\ge g $ implies $P_{t}f\ge P_{t}g$. 
        \item $P_{t}\textbf{1}=\textbf{1},\ \ \left \| P_t f\right \|_{\infty}\le\left \|f \right \|_{\infty}$.
        \item $\partial_{t}P_{t}f=\Delta P_{t}f=P_{t}\Delta f$ for $t>0$.
        \item $p(t,x,y)>0$ for $ t>0$.
        \item $p(t,x,y)=p(t,y,x)$.
        \item $p(t+s,x,y)=\sum_{z\in V}\mu(z)p(t,x,z)p(s,z,y)$.
        \item $\sum_{z\in V}\mu(z)p(t,x,z)=1$. 
        \item $\partial_{t}p(t,x,y)=\Delta_{x}p(t,x,y)=\Delta_{y}p(t,x,y)$ for $ t>0$.
    \end{enumerate}

body:
[Theorem Propolemiko of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] Let $l > 1$ be a real number. Let $A$ be a random Hermitian matrix of size $N$ and
  assume that for every $r \in \mathbb{N}$ one has
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{N^l} \log \mathbb{E} [H \text{} C
    (x_1, \ldots, x_r, 0^{N - r} ; \lambda_1 (A), \ldots, \lambda_N (A))] =
    \sum_{i = 1}^r \Psi (x_i), 
  \end{equation}
  where $\Psi$ is a smooth function in a complex neighborhood of $0$ and the above
  convergence is uniform in a complex neighborhood of $0^r$. Then the random measure $N^{- 1} \sum_{i = 1}^N \delta \left( N^{- l}
  \lambda_i (A) \right)$ converges, as $N \rightarrow \infty$, in probability, in the
  sense of moments to the Dirac measure $\delta \left( \Psi' (0) \right)$. In more detail, this means that any moment of the former measure converges to the corresponding moment of the latter measure in probability.

[Thm 22 (Growing-target surjection moments) of arXiv:2608.06576, 'The Resultant Distribution Method: Universality for $p$-adic Random Matrices and Polynomia'] Fix $L>0$. There exist constants
$c=c(p,\epsilon,L)>0$, $C=C(p,\epsilon,L)>0$, and
$n_0=n_0(p,\epsilon,L)$ such that the following holds.
For every $n\geq n_0$ and every finite $\F_p[t]$-module $G$ satisfying
$$
r:=\dim_{\F_p}G\leq L\log(n+2),
$$
we have
\begin{equation}

\left|\E\left[\#\Sur_{\F_p[t]}(M_n,G)
\right]-1\right|\leq C\exp\left(-c\frac{n}{\log(n+2)}\right).
\end{equation}
In particular, for every fixed $L>0$,
\begin{equation}

\sup_{\substack{n\geq 1\\
\dim_{\F_p}G\leq L\log(n+2)}}
\E\left[\#\Sur_{\F_p[t]}(M_n,G)\right]
<\infty.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Growing-target surjection moments

metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:048f65dac46216c4e256fc7be3369792347ff4627bf6fc4d8e77c0bc2564a8fe","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/04/048f65dac46216c4e256fc7be3369792347ff4627bf6fc4d8e77c0bc2564a8fe.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:01206d6ebf0d8659f42bf613a2f917d326ca1cbcacd37d248ec55d046cb75c7a","bundle_entry_key":"i0005-c2","bundle_id":"population.i0005-four-dimensional-parking-partials-002","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"interacting particle systems and random-walk potential theory","draft":"w661/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.particle-hole:i0005-c2-draft","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# I0005-C2 v1: a dimension-free isolated-hole criterion

Novelty: KNOWN (generalization/repackaging of Bou-Rabee–Panagiotis, proof of Theorem 1.6, Steps 1–3, PDF p.28). The explicit criterion is supplied as a reusable reduction, not an asserted solution of I0005. Audit status: unaudited.

Fix d≥1. Consider a jointly translation-invariant random configuration on Z^d of hole indicators H(x) in {0,1} and active-site indicators B(x) in {0,1}, with H(x)B(x)=0. Let h=EH(0)>0, a=EB(0), and let distance be ℓ1. For an integer R≥1 put

S_R=sum_{0<|x|_1≤4R} E[H(0)H(x)].

Let F be the event that the origin is strictly closer to a hole than to every active site (the distance to an empty active set is infinity). Then

P(F)≥binom(R+d,d)·(h−S_R−a/2)_+.

In particular, if a≤h and S_R≤δh with δ<1/2, then

P(F)≥(1/2−δ)h R^d/d!.

For a time-indexed critical particle–hole process with a_t≤h_t and h_t→0, it is sufficient to find fixed b>0, δ<1/2 and R_t=floor(bh_t^−1/d) such that S_{R_t}≤δh_t eventually: this yields a positive lower limit at least (1/2−δ)b^d/d!. No assumption of independence among surviving holes is made.

## Proof

A hole at y is isolated if no other hole lies within distance 4R of y. The union bound shows that the density i of isolated holes is at least h−S_R. Centers of distinct isolated holes are more than 4R apart, so their closed ℓ1 balls of radius 2R are disjoint.

Each active site contained in one such ball sends one unit of mass to its center. It sends at most one unit, because the balls are disjoint. Translation invariance equates expected outgoing and incoming mass: to see this directly for the nonnegative translation-covariant transport T(x,y), Tonelli gives sum_y ET(0,y)=sum_y ET(−y,0)=sum_x ET(x,0). The outgoing expectation is at most a. Thus the density of isolated-hole centers whose radius-2R ball contains at least two active sites is at most a/2. Call an isolated hole good if its ball contains at most one active site. Good-hole density g is at least h−S_R−a/2.

For a good hole y with one active site z in the ball, select the closed coordinate orthant based at y opposite z: each coordinate sign points away from z, and choose the positive sign if z_j=y_j. If there is no active site in the ball, select the all-positive orthant. These choices commute with lattice translations. The intersection of this orthant with the ball of radius R contains exactly binom(R+d,d) lattice sites, by counting nonnegative integer coordinate vectors with sum at most R.

For w in the selected intersection and the unique active site z (when present), coordinatewise opposition gives |w−z|_1=|w−y|_1+|z−y|_1>|w−y|_1; z≠y follows from H(y)B(y)=0. Any other active site v is outside the closed radius-2R ball, so

|w−v|_1≥|v−y|_1−|w−y|_1>2R−R≥|w−y|_1.

Therefore w is strictly closer to the hole y than to every active site. Selected intersections belonging to distinct good holes are disjoint, since even their radius-R balls are disjoint. Send unit mass from each good hole to each site in its selected intersection. The expected outgoing mass at zero is binom(R+d,d)g. Incoming mass at any site is at most one and is zero outside F, so P(F)≥binom(R+d,d)g. If the lower bound for g is negative, use g≥0 instead. This proves the first inequality.

Since binom(R+d,d)≥R^d/d!, the second follows. For the time-indexed assertion, h_tR_t^d→b^d as h_t→0, and taking a lower limit proves the stated constant.

## What remains at dimension four

For the sparse source law, a_t=P(A_t(0)>0)≤EA_t(0)=EH_t(0)=h_t by conservation of signed expected density. Thus the precise unproved input is

sum_{0<|x|_1≤4floor(bh_t^−1/4)} P(H_t(0)=H_t(x)=1)≤δh_t

for one fixed p in (0,1/4], b>0, δ<1/2 and all sufficiently large t. Establishing this input would produce a d=4 counterexample. [OPEN PROBLEM - not a proved fact. Stated in arXiv:2601.16580, 'Coin flipping and waiting times paradoxes: Why fair coins are exceptional' (openquestion environment labelled oq:random-patterns).] Fix an alphabet size $s$ and a full‑support probability vector $(p_1,\dots,p_s)$ for the i.i.d.\ source
(in the coin case $s=2$ this is $(p,1-p)$, with $p$ possibly equal to $1/2$).
Let $T=T_1\cdots T_L$ be a \emph{uniformly random word} of length $L$, meaning that $T$ is chosen uniformly from the $s^L$ words in $\{1,\dots,s\}^L$, independently of the source.

\begin{enumerate}\itemsep3pt
\item[(i)] What is the limiting distribution of the \emph{normalised} mean waiting time
\[
Z_L(T)\;:=\;\Pr(T)\,\mathbb{E}[\tau_T]
\qquad\text{where}\qquad
\Pr(T)=\prod_{j=1}^L p_{T_j}\,?
\]
(Equivalently, $Z_L(T)=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{B}(T)} \Pr(T)/\Pr(T[1..\ell])$, so $Z_L(T)=1$ exactly when $T$ has no proper border.)
\item[(ii)] For two independent random words $T_1,T_2$ of lengths $L_1,L_2\to\infty$ (for instance with $L_1-L_2$ fixed, or with $L_1/L_2\to\lambda$), what is the limiting law (or typical value) of $\Pr(T_1\!>\!T_2)$ under random tie‑break?
\item[(iii)] In the coin case ($s=2$), what proportion of pairs $(T_1,T_2)$ (at fixed lengths) have the property that the map $p\mapsto \Pr(T_1\!>\!T_2)$ is monotone on $(0,1)$ (cf.\ Open Question~(oq:monotonicity))? How does this proportion behave as the lengths grow?
\end{enumerate}
Heuristically, proper borders are rare for large random words, so one expects $Z_L(T)$ typically close to $1$, and $\Pr(T_1\!>\!T_2)$ typically close to $1/2$ unless the length/profile creates a systematic advantage; make such statements precise (including fluctuation scales and tail bounds). (Verbatim from the paper's TeX; symbols are the source paper's. Stated as open/conjectural; no resolution of it was found in the paper's own text by the rules of problem_index.py - a paper may still prove special cases of a conjecture it states.)
title: Open problem: Typical behaviour for random patterns

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2608.27828, 'Scaling limit of the 3D abelian Yang--Mills Langevin dynamics'] Let $d=3$ and $\bar\beta=1$. Let $\xi=(\xi_1,\xi_2,\xi_3)$ have independent space-time white-noise components on $\R\times\mathbf{T}^3$, defined on a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$, and let $\xi^\eps$ be the lattice approximation (equation eq:Disc_white_noise of the paper).

Let $I$ and $\{h_\lambda\}_{\lambda\in I}$ satisfy Assumption~(assmp:YMAction of the paper).
For every sufficiently small $\eps$, let $\lambda_\eps\in I$ and write $h_\eps = h_{\lambda_\eps}$. Let $\theta^\eps$ solve the DeTurck-gauge-fixed lattice Langevin equation (equation eq:NParaDisc of the paper), with $h=h_\eps$ and (possibly random) initial condition $\theta^\eps(0)$, up to the stopping time $\tau_\eps$.

Let $\theta=(\theta_1,\theta_2,\theta_3)$ solve the continuum stochastic heat
equation
\[  \partial_t\theta_i
    =
    \Delta\theta_i+\xi_i
\]
 with (possibly random) initial condition 
 $ \theta_i(0)$ 
 for  $i=1,2,3$.
Fix $\kappa>0$ sufficiently small and let
\[
-\frac23+\frac53\kappa<\eta<0,
\qquad
\gamma=\bigl(\eta+\tfrac12\bigr)\wedge 0.
\]

Suppose that there is a deterministic constant $M<\infty$ such that, almost surely,
\[
\sup_{0<\varepsilon\le1}\|\theta^\varepsilon(0)\|_{\mathcal C_\varepsilon^\eta}
+\|\theta(0)\|_{\mathcal C^\eta}
\le M.
\]
If
$\|\theta^\varepsilon(0);\theta(0)\|_{\mathcal C_\varepsilon^\eta}\to0$
in probability, then for every $T>0$ and $\delta>0$,
\begin{equ}
\lim_{\eps\to0}
\mathbb P\left(
\tau_\eps>T,
\ \|\theta^\eps;\theta\|_{\CC_{\gamma,\eps}^{-1/2-\kappa,T}}
\leq \delta
\right)=1.
\end{equ} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2608.27828

[Definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] A complex random variable is a variable $f:X\to\mathbb C$. In the discrete case, the law of such a variable is the complex probability measure
$$\mu=\sum_i\alpha_i\delta_{z_i}\quad,\quad\alpha_i\geq0\quad,\quad\sum_i\alpha_i=1\quad,\quad z_i\in\mathbb C$$
given by the following formula, with $P$ being the probability over $X$,
$$\mu=\sum_{z\in\mathbb C}P(f=z)\delta_z$$
with the sum being finite or countable, as per our discretness assumption. In general, the law of such a variable $f:X\to\mathbb C$ is a probability measure on the complex plane.
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'

[Corollary Cor:ftc of arXiv:2411.13030, 'Classification of the limit shape for 1+1-dimensional FPP'] Let $p$ be a semi-directed path from the origin to $(n,{\lceil v n \rceil})$ and let $\varepsilon>0$. For each proper divisor $K$ of $n$, divide the cylinder $[0,n]\times \mathbb Z$ into $n/K$ strips and count the ratio $\eta$ of strips in which the slope of $p$ is bounded from above:
\[
\eta:=\frac K n \left|\left\{ i\in \{0,...,n/K-1\}: \, f_p^*(K(i+1))-f_p^*(K i)\le K(v_n+\varepsilon) \right\}\right|
\]

body: [Proposition 43 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let \(X\) be a qcqs smooth \(k\)-scheme and let \(D=D_1+\cdots+D_n\) be a simple normal crossings divisor. Let \(\varnothing\neq I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and assume that \(D_I\defeq\bigcap_{i\in I}D_i\) is nonempty. Let \(\pi\colon Y\defeq\Bl_{D_I}X\to X\) be the blow-up and put \(D_Y\defeq(\pi^{-1}D)_{\red}\). If the pair \((X,D)\) is log HT-split, then the pair \((Y,D_Y)\) is log HT-split. In particular, the underlying scheme \(Y\) is HT-split.
title: Proposition 43 of arXiv:2609.00567

body: A directed set is a preorder in which every pair of elements has an upper bound. A net in X is a function from a directed set D into X, written (x_d); it converges to p if for every neighborhood U of p it is eventually in U (there is d0 with x_d in U for all d >= d0). Nets generalize sequences (take D = the natural numbers) and repair the tools that sequences fail to capture outside first-countable spaces: (i) p is in cl(A) iff some net in A converges to p; (ii) f is continuous at p iff x_d -> p implies f(x_d) -> f(p) for every net; (iii) X is compact iff every net has a convergent subnet; (iv) X is Hausdorff iff every net has at most one limit.

Let X be a bounded subset of R^D and f(x)=ReLU(Wx+b), with real W in R^(D by D), b in R^D. Let the adapted network have L>=1 width-D ReLU layers, fixed base weights W_1,...,W_L, trainable biases at every layer, and additive weight updates Delta_l of rank at most R, 1<=R<=D. Put B=W_L...W_1 and E=W-B. Assume the same nonsingularity hypotheses as the Zeng--Lee matrix-product lemma: all W_l and all B+LR_j(E) for integers 0<=j<=R(L-1) are nonsingular, with nested SVD truncations. If R>=ceil(rank(E)/L), there exist updates and biases such that the entire adapted network equals f at every x in X. This card states only the exact-representation conclusion of Lemma2/detailed Lemma9, not their separate quantitative approximation bound or printed ReLU error identity.

body:
[Lemma OU flow property of arXiv:2603.14163, '\LARGE \bf Tail Bounds for Queues with Abandonment: Constant, Moderate, Large Deviations, '] Let $p>1$ and let $X\in \mathbb{R}^d$ a random vector with law $\mathcal{L}(X)\in\mathcal{P}_p(\mathbb{R}^d)$. Let $T:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ be a Borel measurable map such that $Y:=T(X)$ is a real random variable with $\mathbb{E}|Y|^p<\infty$. Let $Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ be independent of $X$. For $t>0$ define
\[
F_t := e^{-t}Y + \sqrt{1-e^{-2t}}\,Z,
\]
and let $f_t$ denote the density of $F_t$ (w.r.t.\ Lebesgue measure). Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item (OU representation) \textnormal{[fang2022wasserstein]} The family $(F_t)_{t>0}$ is the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup acting on $Y$; equivalently, $(F_t)$ is a version of the solution to the SDE
        \[
            dF_t = -F_t\,dt + \sqrt{2}\,dB_t,\qquad F_0=Y,
        \]
        where $(B_t)$ is a standard Brownian motion independent of $Y$.

    \item (Smooth positive density) \textnormal{[johnson2001entropy]} For every $t>0$ the law of $F_t$ admits a strictly positive, smooth density $f_t$.
    \item (Commutation of OU semigroup and differentiation) \textnormal{[bakry2013analysis] [bonis2020steins]} For every $t>0 , k\in\mathbb{N}$, and $g \in C^{\infty}_c(\mathbb{R})$,
        \[
            \frac{d^k}{dx^k} P_t g(x) = e^{-kt} P_t\!\Bigl(\frac{d^k}{dx^k} g\Bigr)(x),\qquad x\in\mathbb{R},
        \]
        where $P_t g(x):=\mathbb{E}[g(F_t)\mid F_0=x]$ is the OU semigroup acting on $g$. Moreover,
        \[
         P_t \frac{d^k}{dx^k}g(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1- e^{-2t}}^k} \mathbb{E}[h_k(Z) g(e^{-t}x + \sqrt{1-e^{-2t}}Z)], \qquad x\in\mathbb{R},
        \]
        where $h_k(x) = (-1)^k e^{x^2/2} \frac{d^k}{dx^k}e^{-x^2/2}$ is the $k$-th Hermite Polynomial.

    \item (Continuity equation) For every $t>0$ the density $f_t$ satisfies the continuity equation
        \[
            \partial_t f_t(x) + \frac{d}{dx}\bigl(f_t(x)\,\rho_t(x)\bigr)=0,\qquad x\in\mathbb{R},
        \]
        where $\rho_t(x):=-\partial_x\log f_t(x)-x$ is the score function of $f_t$.

    \item (Score representation) \textnormal{[bonis2020steins]} For each $t>0$ the score admits the conditional expectation representation
        \[
            \rho_t(F_t)\;\overset{d.}{=}\; \mathbb{E}\!\Bigl[e^{-t}Y-\frac{e^{-2t}}{\sqrt{1-e^{-2t}}}\,Z\;\Big|\;F_t\Bigr],
        \]
        and, consequently,
        \[
            t\mapsto \|\rho_t(F_t)\|_{L^p(\mathcal{L}(F_t))}\in L^1((0,\infty)).
        \]

    \item (Moment bound and weak continuity) The curve $t\mapsto\mathcal{L}(F_t)$ is weakly continuous on $(0,\infty)$, and
        \[
            \sup_{t>0}\|F_t\|_{L^p}<\infty,
        \]
        (equivalently $\sup_{t>0}\|x\|_{L^p(\mathcal{L}(F_t))}<\infty$).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma OU flow property of arXiv:2603.14163

body: For a linear NAE triangle system with k triples on r coordinates and fibre A (the set of sign vectors in {-1,+1}^r with no triple monochromatic), the correlation excess is c = k*beta - ell, where beta = log2(4/3) and ell = r - log2|A| is the unrooted defect. c > 0 means the fibre is larger than the independence prediction 2^r (3/4)^k (positive correlation among the constraints); c is exactly additive over coordinate-disjoint unions and over blocks glued at a single shared coordinate (spin-flip symmetry makes every block fibre split evenly on any coordinate).

[Definition 4 ($\mathbf{X}$-controlled paths) of arXiv:2605.08844, 'Signature Kernel and Schwinger-Dyson Kernel Equations as Two-Parameter Rough Differential '] Let $p \in [1,\infty)$ with $\kappa = \lfloor p \rfloor$, and let $\mathbf{X} \in \Omega G_{p, \omega}([a,b], V)$.  

Let
\[
Z : [a,b] \to \mathrm{Hom}(T^{<\kappa}(V), F),
\]
and suppose there exists 
\[
R : \Delta_{[a,b]} \to \mathrm{Hom}(T^{<\kappa}(V), F)
\]
such that
\begin{equation}
Z_{t} = Z_{s} \circ L_{\mathbf{X}_{s,t}^{<\kappa}} + R_{s,t}, \quad a \le s \le t \le b,
\end{equation}
where, for every $\eta \in T^{< \kappa}(V)$, 
\(
L_\eta : T((V)) \to T((V))
\) is 
the left tensor multiplication operator, defined by
\(
L_\eta(\xi) := \eta \otimes \xi.
\) 
Then we say that $Z$ is a  $\mathbf{X}$-controlled path if there exists a finite constant $C$ such that for all $a \le s \le t \le b$, any $\eta_j \in V^{\otimes j}$, $j \in [0:\kappa)$,
\begin{equation} 
\| R_{s,t}[\eta_j] \| \le C \, \omega(s,t)^{(\kappa - j)/p} \, \| \eta_j \|.
\end{equation}
title: $\mathbf{X}$-controlled paths

[Definition def:well_connected of arXiv:2506.07158, 'The diffusivity of supercritical Bernoulli percolation is infinitely differentiable'] We say that a triadic cube ${\scaleobj{1}{\square}}\in \mathcal{T}$ is \emph{well-connected} if there exists a crossing cluster $\mathscr{C}$ for the cube ${\scaleobj{1}{\square}}$ such that:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item Each cube ${\scaleobj{1}{\square}}'$ with $\size({\scaleobj{1}{\square}}') \in [\frac{1}{10}\size({\scaleobj{1}{\square}}),\frac{1}{2}\size({\scaleobj{1}{\square}})]$ and ${\scaleobj{1}{\square}}' \cap \frac{3}{4}{\scaleobj{1}{\square}} \neq \emptyset$ is crossable.
			\item Every open path $\gamma \subseteq {\scaleobj{1}{\square}}'$ with $\diam(\gamma) \geqslant \frac{1}{10}\size({\scaleobj{1}{\square}})$ is connected to $\mathscr{C}$ within ${\scaleobj{1}{\square}}'$.
		\end{enumerate}
		We denote this unique crossing cluster $\mathscr{C}$ by $\mathscr{C}_*({\scaleobj{1}{\square}})$, and call it  \emph{the maximal cluster} in the cube ${\scaleobj{1}{\square}}$.
		
		A triadic cube ${\scaleobj{1}{\square}}$ is said \emph{very-well-connected} if it is well-connected, all its $3^d$ successors,  $9^d$ second order successors, and $27^d$ third order successors are well-connected, and its size is larger than $10000$.
title: Well-connected and very-well-connected

[Lemma 91 (Conditional trace-class Stieltjes interchange) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let $R$ be a $\mathcal G_0$-measurable c\`adl\`ag increasing
$\mathcal S_1(H)_+$-valued path with $\mathbb EV_T<\infty$, put
$V=\operatorname{Tr}R$, and write
$\mathrm dR_s=r_s\,\mathrm dV_s$.  Let $F$ be a jointly measurable
$\mathcal S_1(\mathcal F_\wedge(H))$-valued process satisfying
\[
 \mathbb E\int_{(0,T]}\|F_s\|_1\,\mathrm dV_s<\infty.
\]
Let $\widehat F$ be its conditional expectation with respect to
$\mathcal G_0\otimes\mathcal B([0,T])$ in the Bochner space determined by
the finite measure
$\mu(\mathrm d\omega,\mathrm ds)=\mathbb P(\mathrm d\omega)\,
\mathrm dV_s(\omega)$.  Then, for every $t\le T$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E\!\left[
  \int_{(0,t]}\mathcal B_{\mathrm dR_s}(F_s)
  \middle|\mathcal G_0\right]
 =\int_{(0,t]}\mathcal B_{\mathrm dR_s}(\widehat F_s)
 \quad\text{in }\mathcal S_1(\mathcal F_\wedge(H)).
 
\end{equation}
If $F_s=X_s\otimes X_s$ and
$\mathbb E\int_{(0,T]}\|X_s\|^2\,\mathrm dV_s<\infty$, then
$\widehat F_s$ may be taken to be
$\mathbb E[X_s\otimes X_s\mid\mathcal G_0]$ for $\mu$-almost every
$(\omega,s)$.

Let f: {-1,1}^n -> {0,1} with x uniform on {-1,1}^n, Walsh coefficients fhat(S) = E[f(x) prod_{i in S} x_i], derivative D_i f(x) = (f(x with x_i = 1) - f(x with x_i = -1))/2, and q_i = P(f(x) != f(x with x_i flipped)) the probability that coordinate i is pivotal. f is unate if for each i, D_i f >= 0 everywhere or D_i f <= 0 everywhere. If f is unate, then (1/4) sum_i q_i^2 <= Var(f) <= (1/4) sum_i q_i. The upper bound holds for every f. Either bound is an equality exactly when f is constant or f(x) = (1 + x_i)/2 or (1 - x_i)/2 for some i.

x is uniform on {-1,1}^n

 and $L:I\to \mathbb{R}$ be a strongly $\alpha$-convex function.
Then 
 \begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] $\alpha(0)=0$ and
     \[
        \lim_{t\to 0} \frac{\alpha(t)}{t} =0,
    \]
    \item[(ii)] $L$ is a strongly $\widehat\alpha$-convex function as well, 
       where $\widehat\alpha:(I-I)\to\mathbb{R}_+$ is defined by
       \begin{align}
        \widehat\alpha(u):=\sup\left\{  \frac{\alpha(tu)}{t} : t\in(0,1] \right\}, \qquad u\in (I-I).
      \end{align}
  \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.02491, 'Generalised Random Parking for Trapeziums on a Strip'] In this article, we study a generalisation of R\'{e}nyi’s car-parking problem in which isosceles trapeziums are sequentially deposited on a strip. We derive an explicit formula for the parking constant in terms of the lengths of the two bases, recovering the classical rectangular and triangular models as special cases. We further obtain quantitative finite-size asymptotics for both the expected number and the variance of deposited trapeziums, with convergence rates that depend explicitly on the geometry of the deposited particle. In particular, although the recursive construction involves two different substrate geometries, their variances have the same leading asymptotic density. Finally, we show that the parking constant depends non-monotonically on the ratio of the two base lengths and possesses a unique minimiser, so that the least efficient shape is a genuine trapezium rather than a triangle.

[Proposition prop: N_n to N of arXiv:2605.01444, 'From second moments to pairwise negative correlation: \\applications to minimal and unifor'] Let $\omega_n = \mathrm{MST}(K_n)$ be independent samples, let $\rho_n$ be a vertex chosen uniformly from $V(K_n)$ (independent of the $\omega_n$), and set $N_n = \deg(\rho_n;\omega_n)$. Let $N$ be the degree of the root $\emptyset$ in the WMSF on the PWIT. Then
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty} {\ensuremath{\mathbb E}} _\mathrm{MST}^{(K_n)}\big[\deg(x;\omega)^2\big] = \liminf_{n\to\infty} {\ensuremath{\mathbf E}} _n(N_n^2) \;\geqslant\; {\ensuremath{\mathbb E}} (N^2)\,,
\]
where ${\ensuremath{\mathbf E}} _n$ denotes expectation with respect to the joint law of $\omega_n$ and $\rho_n$.

body: The Barabási–Albert (BA) model is an algorithm for generating random scale-free networks using a preferential attachment mechanism. Several natural and human-made systems, including the Internet, the World Wide Web, citation networks, and some social networks are thought to be approximately scale-free and certainly contain few nodes with unusually high degree as compared to the other nodes of the network. The BA model tries to explain the existence of such nodes in real networks. The algorithm is named for its inventors Albert-László Barabási and Réka Albert.
title: Barabási–Albert model

[Defi nice12 of arXiv:2507.20324, 'Non-existence of several random fractals in Brownian motion and Brownian loop soup'] Let $\gamma_{s}^{(j)}:0\leq s\leq\tau^{(j)}$, $j=1,2,\ldots,p$ and $\eta_{s}^{(k)}:0\leq s\leq\tau^{(k)}$, $k=1,2,\ldots,q,$ be planar curves started on the boundary of a fixed annulus $A$ (with centre $x$) and stopped upon reaching the opposite boundary circle. This configuration of curves is called $\alpha(p,q)$-nice if
\par
(1)\;$\{\gamma_{s}^{(j)}:0\leq s\leq\tau^{(j)}\}\backslash A\subset\mathcal{B}(\gamma_{0}^{(j)},\alpha|\gamma_{0}^{(j)}-x|)$, and
\par
(2)\;the set
\[\bigcup_{j=1}^{p}\big\{\gamma_{s}^{(j)}:0\leq s\leq\tau^{(j)}\big\}\cup\bigg[\bigcup_{j=1}^{p}\mathcal{B}\big(\gamma_{0}^{(j)},\alpha|\gamma_{0}^{(j)}-x|\big)\bigg]\cup\bigg[\bigcup_{j=1}^{p}\mathcal{B}\big(\gamma_{\tau^{(j)}}^{(j)},\alpha|\gamma_{\tau^{(j)}}^{(j)}-x|\big)\bigg]\]
and the set
\[\bigcup_{k=1}^{q}\big\{\eta_{s}^{(k)}:0\leq s\leq\tau^{(k)}\big\}\cup\bigg[\bigcup_{k=1}^{q}\mathcal{B}\big(\eta_{0}^{(k)},\alpha|\eta_{0}^{(k)}-x|\big)\bigg]\cup\bigg[\bigcup_{k=1}^{q}\mathcal{B}\big(\eta_{\tau^{(k)}}^{(k)},\alpha|\eta_{\tau^{(k)}}^{(k)}-x|\big)\bigg]\]
do not intersect.

[Theorem thm: equivalent asymptotique r fini pour les caractères suffisamment de points fixes of arXiv:2605.28770, 'Cutoff profiles for conjugacy invariant random walks on symmetric groups'] Let $r\geq 0$. For each $n\geq 1$, let $\sigma_n\in {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{S}}} _n$.
Assume that $f_1(\sigma_n)/\sqrt{n}\to \infty$. Then as $n\to \infty$, uniformly over all $\lambda \vdash n$ such that $\lambda_1 = n-r$, we have
\begin{equation}

[Corollary cor:dirichlet_tilted of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Let $f\in D(\mathcal{L})$ be real-valued and let
$\mathcal{E}(f,f)=-\langle\mathcal{L}_S f,f\rangle_\mu=\langle\nabla f,D\nabla f\rangle_\mu$
be the symmetrized Dirichlet form of Eq.~(equation eq:dirichlet_setup of the paper). Then the
quadratic forms of the tilted generators admit the representations
\begin{align}
  \langle \mathcal{L}_k^\rho f, f\rangle_\mu
  &= -\mathcal{E}(f,f) + k\langle V, f^2\rangle_\mu,
  
  \\[2pt]
  \langle \mathcal{L}_k^J f, f\rangle_\mu
  &= -\mathcal{E}(f,f) + k\langle v_{\textrm{s}}\cdot U, f^2\rangle_\mu
     + k^2\langle U\cdot DU, f^2\rangle_\mu,
  
\end{align}
where $\langle g, f^2\rangle_\mu = \int gf^2\mathrm{d}\mu$.

body:
[Definition def:macro-regions of arXiv:2606.19507, 'The $t$-Split Two-Periodic Aztec Diamond Model'] Fix $(x,y) \in [0,1] \times [-1,0]$. 
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item If there are two simple saddle points on $\mathcal{C}_2$, then $(x,y)$ is in the \textit{frozen region}. 
        \item If there are two simple saddles points not in the real part of $\mathcal{R}$, then $(x,y)$ is in the \textit{rough region}.
        \item If there are two simple saddles on $\mathcal{C}_1$, then $(x,y)$ is in the \textit{smooth region}. 
    \end{enumerate}
    The boundary of regions occurs when saddle points coalesce:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \setcounter{enumi}{3}
        \item If there is a double saddle point on $\mathcal{C}_2$, then $(x,y)$ is on the \textit{frozen-rough boundary} of the model. 
        \item If there is a double or triple saddle point on $\mathcal{C}_1$, then $(x,y)$ is  on the \textit{rough-smooth boundary} of the model. 
    \end{enumerate}
title: Macroscopic regions of the two-periodic Aztec diamond

body:
[Prop Arnold of arXiv:2606.24793, '\LARGE Random sequential nearest-neighbor coloring on trees'] Let $(I_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be the inter-arrival times of a record process of an i.i.d.\ sequence with diffuse distribution. Then
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(i)] We have $$\lim_{n\to \infty } \frac{\log I_n}{n}=1 \mbox{ a.s.}.$$
    \item[(ii)] For any $n\ge 1$ and $i_2,\ldots,i_n\ge 1$,
$$\mathbb{P}(I_2=i_2,\ldots, I_n=i_n,\ 2^{k}\le I_k\le 3^{k} \hbox{ for all } k> n)>0.$$
    \item[(iii)] For any $c\ge 0$ and $n\ge 1$, we have $$\mathbb{P}(\forall m\ge 0, I_{n+m+1}\ge c \mid I_1,\ldots,I_n)\ge \mathbb{P}(\forall m\ge 0, I_{m+2}\ge c)>0 \quad\hbox{a.s.}.$$
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 20 (Quadruply augmented double-hive partition function) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{lem:double-partition}
Let \(\bar a^2,\bar b^2,\bar d^2>0\), put
\[
\bar T:=\bar a^2+\bar b^2+\bar d^2+\bar f^2,
\]
and assume either \(\bar f^2>0\), or
\[
\bar f^2<0,
\qquad \bar T<0.
\]
Set
\[
A=n\bar a^2,\qquad B=n\bar b^2,\qquad
D=n\bar d^2,\qquad F=n\bar f^2,
\]
and let \(p_{\mathrm{dbl}}\) be the maximum-entropy density on
\(\mathbb D^4\) from Lemma~\ref{lem:double-maxent}, with raw parameters
\(A,B,D,F\).  Let \(a,b,d,f\) be the corresponding geometric side lengths,
as in Lemma~\ref{lem:tet-analogue of GangNar}.  Then
the normalizing constant 
\[Z_{\mathrm{dbl}}
=
\frac{(2\pi)^{3n/2}}{V_n(\tau_n)^3}
\left(
\frac{ABDF}{A+B+D+F}
\right)^{n^2/2} = \frac{(2\pi)^{3n/2}}{V_n(\tau_n)^3}\left(\frac{
9n^3|\mathtt{tet}|_{abfd}^2
}{
4
}\right)^{n^2/2}
\]

Consequently,
\[
\ent(p_{\mathrm{dbl}})
=
\frac{n^2}{2}
\log\left(
\frac{\bar a^2\bar b^2\bar d^2\bar f^2}{\bar T}
\right)
+\frac{15}{4}n^2
+O(n\log n).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem lem_app_G of arXiv:2603.29711, 'Strong Feller property, irreducibility,\\ and uniqueness of the invariant measure\\ for st'] Let $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, $\delta>\frac d4$, and $\varsigma\geq2$.
Then, the following properties hold.
\begin{itemize}
 \item [(i)]  There exist a constant $C>0$
 and a positive sequence $(L_\lambda)_{\lambda>0}$
 such that, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, it holds
 for every $v,v_1,v_2\in H$ that
    \begin{align*}
    \|G_{\varsigma, \varepsilon}(v)\|^2_{\mathscr{L}^2(H,H)} &
    \le C \|(\operatorname{I}+A)^{-\delta}\|^2_{\mathscr{L}^2(H, H)}
    \end{align*}
    and
    \begin{align*}
    \|G_{\varsigma, \varepsilon}(v_1)-
    G_{\varsigma, \varepsilon}(v_2)\|^2_{\mathscr{L}^2(H,H)} 
    &\le \lambda\norm{v_1-v_2}_V^2 + L_\lambda 
    \norm{v_1-v_2}^2_H \quad \forall\,\lambda>0.        
    \end{align*}
\item [(ii)] If $d=1$, for every $\sigma\in[0,\frac12)$, $\delta>\frac d4+\sigma$, 
and $\eta\in(\sigma,\frac12)\cap(\frac 14, \frac12)$
    there exists a positive constant $C$, 
    depending on $\varsigma, \sigma, \eta, \delta$, such that 
    \[
    \|G_{\varsigma,\varepsilon}(v)\|^2_{\mathscr{L}^2(H, V_{2\sigma})} \le C
    \|v\|^2_{V_{2\eta}} \quad\forall\,
    v\in B_1^\infty \cap V_{2 \eta}.
    \]
    \end{itemize}

[Dfn 14 of arXiv:2609.00758, 'Deformations of Compact Calabi--Yau and Fano Varieties with Isolated Singularities'] Let $Y,S$ be complex spaces and $f:Y\to S$ a smooth morphism. A {\it simple normal crossing divisor on $Y\to S$} is an analytic subset $D\subset Y$ such that for every $y\in D$ there exist an open neighbourhood $U\sb Y$ of $y,$ an open neighbourhood $V\sb S$ of $f(y),$ an open neighbourhood $W\sb f^{-1}(f(y))$ of $y,$
an $S$-isomorphism $U\to V\times W$ and holomorphic local coordinates $z_1,\dots,z_l:W\to\C$ such that $U\cap D$ is defined by $z_1\cdots z_k=0$ for some $k\le l.$
title: Definition 14 of arXiv:2609.00758

body: In mathematical statistics, the Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence (also called relative entropy and I-divergence), denoted $D_{\text{KL}}(P\parallel Q)$, is a type of statistical distance: a measure of how much an approximating probability distribution Q is different from a true probability distribution P. Mathematically, it is defined as $$D_{\text{KL}}(P\parallel Q)=\sum _{x\in {\mathcal {X}}}P(x)\,\log {\frac {P(x)}{Q(x)}}{\text{.}}$$

On the 8-coordinate spread frame where the twisted frame integrals of the Fourier route grow, Phi exceeds the eps = 0 bathtub by a few per cent for laws of bounded range (fine combs 1.51 vs 1.37 at N = 4, 8, 16, flat in N; mostly estimator bias) and by a factor 1.1 to 1.7 for combs at the integers (N = 4..12, depending on s and beta), a factor that grows slowly with N while Phi itself falls like 1/N. The local maximal functional int dp sup_{|l| <= 1} rho_{L,P}(l, p) is 1.0, 0.52, 0.28 (integer combs N = 4, 8, 16), 0.91, 0.77, 0.68 (fine combs), 0.38, 0.17, 0.09 (N teeth at spacing N^{-1/2}); the windowed bound of Proposition 5.4 is 2 to 10. Calibration: the worst-hub Monte Carlo estimate scatters by 1 to 4 per cent between seeds at 4e7 samples, so eps-differences of 3e-4 from one seed are not evidence of monotonicity.

[Theorem 40 of arXiv:2512.07202, 'Hitting Probabilities for Hypoelliptic Differential Equations Driven by Fractional Brownia'] Assume that the family of vector fields \( \mathcal{V}=\{V_\alpha\}_{\alpha=1}^d \) is equiregular on \( \mathbb{R}^N \) and satisfies Hypotheses~\ref{h1} and~\ref{1.2}. Let \( Y_t \) be the solution to the RDE~\eqref{density1} where \( \mathbf{B} \) is the canonical lift of a fractional Brownian motion \( (B_t)_{0 \leqslant t \leqslant T} \) with Hurst parameter $H\in(1/4,1)$. Fix \( 0 < a < b \) and \( M > 0 \). Then for any \( \eta \in \left( 0, 1/H \right) \), there exists a constant \( C = C(a, b, M, Q, H, \mathcal{V}, \eta) > 0 \) such that the estimate
\[
\mathbb{P}\left( Y([a, b]) \cap A \neq \emptyset \right) \geqslant C  \mathrm{Cap}_{Q - 1/H + \eta}(A)
\]holds for all compact sets \( A \subseteq B_d(o, M) \).
Here \( Q \) denotes the homogeneous dimension.

body:
[Theorem thm:3.2 of arXiv:2608.27474, 'Nonlocality of Cover-Time Changes Under Edge Addition'] Let \(H\) be a finite connected graph with distinguished vertex \(c\),
and assume \(W=V(H)\setminus\{c\}\ne\varnothing\). Form \(G\) by
adjoining three new vertices \(s,u,v\) and the three edges \(cs,cu,cv\),
with no other edges incident to \(s,u,v\). Let

\[
G'=G+uv,
\qquad
m=|E(G)|,
\]

and start at \(s\).

Work on a product probability space. At \(c\), give every directed
departure edge \((c,z)\) an independent rate-one Poisson process. At
each ring, attach an independent mark having the law of a complete
discrete simple-random-walk excursion that starts with \(c\to z\) and
ends on its first return to \(c\). Marks belonging to distinct rings are
independent. The superposed ring order is therefore an i.i.d. uniform
sequence of departure edges, exactly matching successive departures from
\(c\) in the discrete walk.

Let:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \(T\) be the artificial time at which the remote vertices \(W\) have
  all been visited by remote excursion marks;
\item
  \(A\) be the artificial completion time of the old local pair
  \(\{u,v\}\);
\item
  \(B\) be the artificial completion time of the new local triangle
  \(cuv\);
\item
  \(R_T^{\mathrm{rem}}\) be the physical length of the unused suffix of
  the terminal remote excursion, from the instant at which the last
  unvisited vertex of \(W\) is first visited until return to \(c\);
\item
  \(\mathscr G_T\) be the sigma-field generated by the remote artificial
  ring times, departure labels, and excursion paths only through that
  first completion instant; and
\item
  \(J=\mathbb E[R_T^{\mathrm{rem}}\mid\mathscr G_T]\), the conditional
  expected unused remote suffix.
\end{itemize}

Use independent local marked processes to define \(A\) and \(B\), each
independent of the common remote process defining \(T,J\). Put

\begin{equation}
a=\mathbb E e^{-T},
\qquad
b=\mathbb E e^{-3T/2}.

\end{equation}

Then \(T,A,B,J\) are integrable, \(a,b\) are finite, and

\begin{equation}
\boxed{
\delta_s(G;uv)
=2\mathbb ET
-2(2m-1)\left(a-\frac23b\right)
-2\mathbb E\!\left[J\left(e^{-T}-e^{-3T/2}\right)\right].
}

\end{equation}

[Lem 2 of arXiv:2609.03418, 'Sampling and Density Theorems for the Fractional Opdam--Cherednik Transform'] Let $\{\mu_j\}_{j\ge1}$ denote the positive spectral parameters determined by 
$$ \Psi_{\alpha,\beta}(\mu_j) = \varphi_{\mu_j}^{\alpha+1,\beta+1}(1)=0,$$
and set
$$ P_j^{\alpha,\beta} := \int_{-1}^{1} \left|\varphi_{\mu_j}^{\alpha,\beta}(x)\right|^2 A_{\alpha,\beta}(x)\,dx , \quad j\ge1, $$
and
$$ M_0:=\int_{-1}^{1}A_{\alpha,\beta}(x)\,dx. $$
Then
\begin{align}
\left\{ \frac{1}{\sqrt{M_0}}, \frac{\varphi_{\mu_j}^{\alpha,\beta}}{\sqrt{P_j^{\alpha,\beta}}}, \frac{(\varphi_{\mu_j}^{\alpha,\beta})'} {\sqrt{(\mu_j^2+\rho^2)P_j^{\alpha,\beta}}} :\ j\ge1 \right\}
\end{align}
is an orthonormal basis of $L^2\big((-1,1),A_{\alpha,\beta}\big).$ Consequently,
$$ \left\{ \frac1{\sqrt{M_0}}, \frac{G_{\mu_j}^{\alpha,\beta}} {\sqrt{P_j^{\alpha,\beta}}}, \frac{G_{-\mu_j}^{\alpha,\beta}} {\sqrt{P_j^{\alpha,\beta}}} :\ j\ge1 \right\} $$
is a Riesz basis of
$L^2\big((-1,1),A_{\alpha,\beta}\big).$
title: Lem 2 of arXiv:2609.03418

[Corollary cor:shot-nois-field of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Consider a simple marked point process 
\(\tilde{\Xi} = \{ \tilde{x} = (x, U(x)) \}_{x \in \Xi}\) on \(\mathbb{R}^d\) 
with i.i.d.\ marks \(U(x)\) taking values in a Polish space \(\mathbb{K}\).  
Let the shot-noise field \(M\) on \(\mathbb{R}^d\) with values in \( \mathbb{R}\) be defined by
\[
M(x) := \sum_{y \in \Xi} \zeta(x, \tilde{y}), \quad x \in \mathbb{R}^d,
\]
for some measurable function \(\zeta : \mathbb{R}^d \times (\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{K}) \longrightarrow  \mathbb{R}\) 
such that \(\zeta(\tilde{x}, \tilde{y}) \le \phi(|x-y|)\) 
for a fast-decreasing function \(\phi\) as in~(equation varphibd of the paper).  
If the ground point process \(\Xi\) has fast summable exponential mixing correlations as in Definition~(def.A2 of the paper)(i.summ-exp-mixing of the paper), 
then the random field \(M\) exhibits fast \textnormal{BL}-mixing correlations 
as in Definition~(d.omegatmixing-field of the paper)(i.BL-mixing-field of the paper) and~(i.mixing-field-fast of the paper).

[Thm main-SPDE-thm of arXiv:2601.19145, 'Stochastic Persistence in Infinite Dimensions'] Suppose (sass-A of the paper)--(SPDE-lyap of the paper) hold. Let $(x_t, \theta) = (u_t,z_t,\theta)$ be the solution to (equation SPDE of the paper) with initial condition $x_0 = (u_0,z_0)$. If $\Lambda < 0$ then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
     \item For all $u_0 \in C(\overline D;\mathbb{R}^d)_+ \setminus \{0\}$, almost surely, all limit points $\mu$ of the random measures $\mu_t = \frac{1}{t}\int_0^t \delta_{u_s}ds$ on $C(\overline D;\mathbb{R}^d)_+$ as $t \to \infty$ satisfy $\mu(\{0\}) = 0$.
        \item $u_t$ is stochastically persistent, meaning for all $\epsilon > 0$ there exists a compact set $\mathcal{K}_\epsilon \subset C(\overline D;\mathbb{R}^d)_+ \setminus \{0\}$ such that for all $u_0 \in C(\overline D;\mathbb{R}^d)_+ \setminus \{0\}$
        $$\mathbb{P}(\liminf_{t \to \infty} \mu_t(\mathcal{K}_\epsilon) \geq 1 - \epsilon) = 1 \,.$$
        In particular, for all $\epsilon > 0$, there are $a,A > 0$ such that
        $$\liminf_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T} m(\{t \leq T \mid a \leq \|u_t\|_{L^1} \leq A\}) \geq 1 -\epsilon \quad a.s.,
        $$
        where $m$ denotes the Lebesgue measure on $[0,T]$.
        
        \item There is a measure $\mu_+$ on $C(\overline D)_+ \times \Theta$ such that $\mu_+(\{x_u \neq 0\}) = 1$ and $\mu_+$ is invariant for $(x_t,\theta)$ in the sense of (inv-meas of the paper).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm main-SPDE-thm of arXiv:2601.19145

The belief propagation recursion for marginals consists of factor-to-variable messages hat{nu}_{a->i}^{(t)}(x_i) proportional to int_{y_a - sum_{j != i} A_{aj} x_j = A_{ai} x_i} dx^{[i]} prod_{j != i} nu_{j->a}^{(t)}(x_j) and variable-to-factor messages nu_{i->a}^{(t+1)}(x_i) proportional to pi_{beta,p}(x_i) prod_{b != a} hat{nu}_{b->i}^{(t)}(x_i), where pi_{beta,p}(s) proportional to exp(-beta |s|^p).
beta > 0
p >= 1
t in N_0

  Fix $\alpha \in [-2,2]$ and let $\Delta^{\mathrm{Euc}}, \Delta_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{Euc}},\Delta_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{LQG}},\chi,\chi',\alpha_{\mathrm{max}}$, and $\alpha_{\mathrm{min}}$ denote the deterministic constants from the statement of Proposition~\ref{prop:zero_one_law}. Then, almost surely, the following hold as $\varepsilon \to 0$.
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item 
  $\dim_{\mathrm{Euc}}(\Gamma_{-1,1}\lvert_{[\tau_\varepsilon^-,\tau_\varepsilon^+]})\rightarrow \Delta^{\mathrm{Euc}}$,
  \item 
  $\dim_{\mathrm{Euc}}(\Gamma_{-1,1}\lvert_{[\tau_\varepsilon^-,\tau_\varepsilon^+]} \cap \cT^\alpha_h)\rightarrow  \Delta^{\mathrm{Euc}}_{\alpha}$,
  \item 
  $\dim_{\mathrm{LQG}}(  \Gamma_{-1,1}\lvert_{[\tau_\varepsilon^-,\tau_\varepsilon^+]}\cap \cT^\alpha_h)\rightarrow \Delta^{\mathrm{LQG}}_{\alpha}$,
  \item 
  $\chi(\Gamma_{-1,1}\lvert_{[\tau_\varepsilon^-,\tau_\varepsilon^+]})\rightarrow \chi$,
  \item 
  $\chi'(\Gamma_{-1,1}\lvert_{[\tau_\varepsilon^-,\tau_\varepsilon^+]})\rightarrow \chi'$,
  \item 
  $\alpha_{\mathrm{max}}(\Gamma_{-1,1}\lvert_{[\tau_\varepsilon^-,\tau_\varepsilon^+]})\rightarrow \alpha_{\mathrm{max}}$,
      \item 
      $\alpha_{\mathrm{min}}(\Gamma_{-1,1}\lvert_{[\tau_\varepsilon^-,\tau_\varepsilon^+]})\rightarrow \alpha_{\mathrm{min}}$.
  \end{enumerate}

[Definition def:lift of arXiv:2412.05491, 'Near-critical and finite-size scaling for \\ high-dimensional lattice trees and animals'] Let $\mathbb{T}_r^d = (\mathbb{Z}/r\mathbb{Z})^d$ be the $d$-dimensional discrete torus of period $r$,
with the spread-out edge set inherited from projecting the $\mathbb Z^d$ edge set
$\mathbb{E}=\{\{x,y\}: 0< \|y-x\|_\infty \le L\}$ to the torus.
Assume that $r \ge 2L+1$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Lift of a walk.)}
Let $\omega=(\omega_0,\omega_1,\dots,\omega_n)$ be a torus walk
starting from $\omega_0 = 0$ and taking steps from $\mathbb{E}$.
The \emph{lift} of $\omega$ is
the $\mathbb{Z}^d$ walk $\bar \omega$ defined by $\bar\omega(0)=0$ and
\begin{equation}

\bar \omega(k) - \bar \omega(k-1) = \omega(k) -  \omega(k-1)
	\qquad (1\leq k \leq n),
\end{equation}
using the identification of $\mathbb{T}^d_r$ with $\Lambda_r = [ - \frac r 2, \frac r 2 )^d \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$.
The restriction $r \ge 2L+1$ ensures that the lift is a bijection
from torus walks starting from the origin
to $\mathbb Z^d$ walks starting from the origin.

\item \emph{(Lift of a lattice tree.)}
Let $T$ be a torus lattice tree containing $0$,
so that for any $x\in T$,
there is a unique self-avoiding walk in the tree from
$0$ to $x$.  The \emph{lift} of $T$ is defined to be the union over $x \in T$
of the lifts of those torus walks to $\mathbb Z^d$.
This defines an injection from
torus lattice trees containing the origin
to $\mathbb Z^d$ lattice trees containing the origin.
It is not a surjection because lifted trees cannot contain
any pair of $\mathbb Z^d$ vertices that project to the same torus vertex.

\item \emph{(Lift of a lattice animal.)}
We use the lexicographic order on $[-L,L]^d \cap \mathbb Z^d \setminus \{ 0 \}$
and on $\Lambda_r$, and we use the order on $\Lambda_r$ to induce an order on
the torus vertices.
Let $A$ be a torus animal containing $0$.
We first grow a spanning tree in $A$ recursively as follows,
starting from $\{0\}$.
Given the current tree,
we choose its first
vertex which is incident to an edge in $A$ that would not create a cycle when added to the tree,
and we add the first such edge to the tree.
The process terminates
in a spanning tree $T$ for $A$ when no further edges can be added.
We lift $T$ to a $\mathbb Z^d$ tree $\hat T$.
For the remaining excess edges in $A \setminus T$,
we write them in the form $\{u,v\}$
with $u$ less than $v$ in the torus vertex order,
and we lift the edge
 to $\{ \hat u, \hat u + (v-u) \}$
where $\hat u\in \hat T$ projects to $u$.
The lifting is injective because we can recover the torus animal by projection.
See Figure~(figure:LTlift of the paper) for an example.

\end{enumerate}
title: Definition def:lift of arXiv:2412.05491

For a width n>=1 zero-bias tanh MLP with independent iid N(0,1/n) weight matrices across layers and one deterministic input with initial normalized squared norm q0 in [0,1], let h_j be its preactivations and let hbar_j be the corresponding independent centered Gaussian vectors with deterministic kernel variances qbar_0=q0 and qbar_(j+1)=E tanh(sqrt(qbar_j)Z)^2. For every integer depth L>=1, W2(h_L/sqrt(n),hbar_L/sqrt(n))^2<=1152/n, and W2((h_j/sqrt(n))_(j=1)^L,(hbar_j/sqrt(n))_(j=1)^L)^2<=1152 L/n in the product Euclidean metric. Including each layer postactivation increases the joint squared bound to at most 2304 L/n. This is only the one-input tanh chain family, not arbitrary Tensor Programs. Independent review and literature novelty assessment remain outstanding. Lean runtime was unverified.
One deterministic input; q0 in [0,1]
Constant integer width n>=1, finite integer depth L>=1
Fresh independent Gaussian weight matrices, variance 1/n
Zero biases and componentwise tanh
Product Euclidean metric on normalized layer trajectories

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:f6b365a8110df7488036122974bf083176e3928d6a071bb5045b9fe5ab493e31","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/f6/f6b365a8110df7488036122974bf083176e3928d6a071bb5045b9fe5ab493e31.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:2c90ba3792628fff09939e3da3b97f25ccc9b7c0b0727923e71bf717e0e9a145","bundle_entry_key":"tanh-depth-uniform","bundle_id":"population.t250-critical-tanh-depth-uniform-001","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w712/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.neural_networks:critical-tanh-mlp-one-input-depth-uniform-gp-rate-w712","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Critical tanh chain: depth-uniform one-input Gaussian approximation

Claim T250-w712-C002, version 2. Status: proof (unaudited).
Target 1. Scope: one input, tanh MLP, critical variance 1/n, no biases. This does not cover general Tensor Programs or a multi-input tanh chain.

Let n >= 1 and q_0 in [0,1]. Independently at every layer sample n standard Gaussians Z_li and put
q_(l+1) = n^(-1) sum_i tanh(sqrt(q_l) Z_li)^2.
Let F(q)=E tanh(sqrt(q) Z)^2, and qbar_(l+1)=F(qbar_l), qbar_0=q_0.
For a final independent Gaussian vector g in R^n, the layer-L preactivation has law sqrt(q_(L-1))g and its GP comparison has law sqrt(qbar_(L-1))g.

THEOREM. For every depth L>=1 and every n>=1,
W_2( sqrt(q_(L-1))g/sqrt(n), sqrt(qbar_(L-1))g/sqrt(n) )^2 <= 1152/n.
In particular this gives the target sqrt(L/n) rate and, more strongly, a depth-uniform n^(-1/2) rate for this critical non-ReLU chain. Constants are deliberately loose.

The hard step is bounding relative kernel error without multiplying absolute Lipschitz constants. The proof below uses conditional second moments, not products of marginal probability estimates.

1. Elementary tanh inequalities.
For t>=0, tanh t <= t, sinh t >= t, and therefore
 tanh(t)^2 = sinh(t)^2/(1+sinh(t)^2) >= t^2/(1+t^2).
Consequently
 t-tanh t = integral_0^t tanh(s)^2 ds >= t^3/[3(1+t^2)],
and multiplying by t+tanh t >= t gives
 t^2-tanh(t)^2 >= t^4/[3(1+t^2)].
These inequalities include t=0. Denominators are strictly positive.

2. Kernel shape.
For each fixed z, q -> tanh(sqrt(q)|z|)^2 is increasing and concave on [0,infinity). Indeed at q>0 its derivative is
 z^2 [tanh(t)/t] sech(t)^2, t=sqrt(q)|z|.
Both nonnegative factors are decreasing in t: sech(t)^2 is decreasing, and tanh(t)/t is decreasing since tanh is concave, vanishes at zero, and has derivative sech(t)^2. The z=0 case is constant. Continuous extension at zero proves concavity there too. Integrating preserves concavity and monotonicity. F(0)=0 and F(q)>0 for q>0.
The derivative argument is pointwise; no derivative is exchanged with an integral.

For 0<=q<=1, step 1 and Cauchy-Schwarz give
 q-F(q) >= (q^2/3) E[Z^4/(1+q Z^2)] >= q^2/[3(1+q)] >= q^2/6.
Cauchy-Schwarz uses E Z^2=1 and E(1+q Z^2)=1+q, with integrable nonnegative variables.
Also, using the probability measure with density Z^2 relative to Gaussian measure and Jensen for x -> 1/(1+q x),
 F(q) >= q E[Z^2/(1+q Z^2)] >= q/(1+3q) >= q/4.
The density integrates to one and its Z^2 mean is E Z^4=3.

3. Conditional sampling noise.
Set Y=tanh(sqrt(q) Z)^2. For 0<q<=1,
 E Y^2 <= q^2 E Z^4 =3q^2 <=48 F(q)^2.
Given the entire past, q_(l+1) is an average of n independent copies of Y with q=q_l. Hence
 E[q_(l+1)|past]=F(q_l),
 Var(q_(l+1)|past)<=48 F(q_l)^2/n.
No independence of q_l across layers is asserted. Since tanh^2<=1, all random and deterministic q_l lie in [0,1].

4. Relative error, before depth n/96.
Assume q_0>0. Every qbar_l>0. Set R_l=q_l/qbar_l, S_l=F(q_l)/F(qbar_l), v_l=E(R_l-1)^2.
Concavity, monotonicity and F(0)=0 imply that S_l lies between R_l and 1. This is valid also at q_l=0 by continuity. Thus
 (S_l-1)^2 <= (R_l-1)^2, S_l^2 <= 2(S_l-1)^2+2.
The conditional variance identity, with a deterministic denominator qbar_(l+1)>0, yields
 v_(l+1) = E(S_l-1)^2 + E Var(R_(l+1)|past)
 <= (1+96/n) v_l+96/n.
Starting at v_0=0, induction gives v_l <= (1+96/n)^l-1.
For 96l/n<=1, log(1+x)<=x and exp(x)-1<=2x on [0,1] imply
 v_l <=192l/n.
All moments used here are finite: for each fixed l, R_l<=1/qbar_l, a finite deterministic bound.

5. Signal decay.
Write mu_l=E q_l. Step 2 and E q_l^2>=mu_l^2 imply
 mu_(l+1)<=mu_l-mu_l^2/6.
The same inequality holds for qbar_l. For 0<a<=1, a-a^2/6>0 and
 1/[a(1-a/6)] >= 1/a+1/6.
Therefore, if a subsequent mean is positive, reciprocals increase by at least 1/6. A zero mean makes all subsequent signals zero. Thus
 mu_l, qbar_l <= 1/(q_0^(-1)+l/6) <= 6/l for l>=1.
The sharper first bound gives values <=1 at l=0 and avoids division by zero.

6. Coupling and splitting depths.
Use the same independent g for the two output vectors. Its mean squared normalized norm is one, so
 W_2^2 <= E(sqrt(q_l)-sqrt(qbar_l))^2,
where l=L-1.
For 1<=l<=n/96, using |sqrt(r)-1|<=|r-1| for all r>=0,
 E(sqrt(q_l)-sqrt(qbar_l))^2 <= qbar_l v_l <= (6/l)(192l/n)=1152/n.
For l>n/96, nonnegative square roots give (sqrt(a)-sqrt(b))^2<=a+b, hence
 E(sqrt(q_l)-sqrt(qbar_l))^2 <=mu_l+qbar_l <=12/l<1152/n.
At l=0 the error is zero. These cases exhaust every integer l, even when n<96 (the short positive-depth range is then empty). If q_0=0, both chains vanish identically. This proves the displayed uniform bound.

NETWORK INTERPRETATION.
Start with any deterministic activation vector a_0 of norm squared n q_0; let W_l have independent N(0,1/n) entries and set h_l=W_l a_(l-1), a_l=tanh(h_l). Fresh W_l implies the conditional law h_l=sqrt(q_(l-1))Z_l and q_l=||a_l||^2/n. Thus the scalar chain is exact, rather than an SDE or asymptotic surrogate. A scalar output readout has the identical bound without the vector normalization.

WHAT REMAINS.
This closes the dossier's one-input tanh absolute-rate obstruction if independently accepted. It does not prove the entire target for all critical chain programs. The next unpaid step is a multi-input tanh Gram estimate or a theorem covering a larger class of stable chains. Novelty relative to all literature is not yet established; source checks must accompany this result.


7. Joint Tensor Program trajectory (target 1).
Construct independent Gaussian vectors g_1,...,g_L on a single space. Recursively set h_j=sqrt(q_(j-1))g_j and q_j=||tanh(h_j)||^2/n. Simultaneously set hbar_j=sqrt(qbar_(j-1))g_j. The finite trajectory has the correct law by conditional Gaussianity of fresh weight matrices. The infinite-width trajectory has the correct joint law: its deterministic variances multiply independent Gaussian vectors. This independence is only across fresh layers; input correlations are not being modeled because there is just one input.

By the sum-of-squares Euclidean norm on the product of L normalized layer spaces,
 E sum_(j=1)^L ||h_j-hbar_j||^2/n <=1152 L/n.
Therefore W_2 of the joint normalized preactivation trajectories is at most sqrt(1152 L/n), uniformly for all L and n, including L<=n^(1-epsilon). If the program records postactivations as well, tanh is 1-Lipschitz, so the joint squared cost for pre- and postactivations is at most 2304 L/n. The initial deterministic input contributes zero cost.

This is a length-explicit quantitative forward Tensor Program statement on the one-input tanh chain family. It is a narrowed result, not a theorem for all critical chains or for transposed weights.

VERIFICATION RECORD.
Analytic side conditions have been checked in steps 1-6: q=0 separately, strict positivity of deterministic denominators, finiteness of relative moments at each finite depth, integrability in Cauchy-Schwarz/Jensen, and the integer depth split for n<96. scripts/verify_tanh.py independently checks Gaussian-integral inequalities numerically at q down to 1e-12 and verifies 54 finite/cutoff cases with exact rational arithmetic. These numerical integrals are diagnostics, not part of the proof. A convex counterexample F(q)=q^2 confirms that monotonicity without concavity would invalidate step 4. Full proof has not received independent review.

[Theorem of arXiv:2609.03988, 'A $p$-summability approach to the weak maximizing property'] Let $X$ and $Y$ be Banach spaces with $Y\neq{0}$. The following assertions are equivalent: \\
{\rm (1)} There exists $1\leq p<\infty$ such that every bounded linear operator $T:X\to Y$ with a maximizing sequence which is not weakly $p$-summable is norm-attaining. \\
{\rm (2)} For every $1\leq p<\infty$, every bounded linear operator $T:X\to Y$ admitting a maximizing sequence which is not weakly $p$-summable is norm-attaining. \\
{\rm (3)} Every bounded linear operator $T:X\to Y$ is norm-attaining.

    \]

[Theorem -m case of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] {SWB2024}}]
   
Suppose $\mathcal{X}$ is a smooth and separated Deligne--Mumford stack, and $\mathcal{E} \hookrightarrow \mathcal{X}$ is a Cartier divisor such that $\mathcal{E} \simeq \mathcal{P}(a_1, \ldots, a_r).$ 
Let $\mathcal{N} = \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{X}}(\mathcal{E})|_{\mathcal{E}}$, and set $\mathcal{X}_m := \mathcal{X}(\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{2}m]\mathcal{E})$ and $\mathcal{E}_m := \mathcal{C}(\sqrt[\leftroot{-2}\uproot{2}m]{\mathcal{N}}).$
Then, there exists a smooth and separated Deligne--Mumford stack $\mathcal{Z}_m$ completing the diagram below, and such that $\mathcal{X}_m$ can be recovered as a weighted blowup of $\mathcal{Z}_m$ at $B\mu_m$ with exceptional divisor $\mathcal{E}_m$.
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathcal{E}_m \arrow[rr, hook] \arrow[rd] \arrow[dd] &                                 & \mathcal{X}_m \arrow[rd] \arrow[dd, dotted] &     \\
                                             & \mathcal{E} \arrow[rr, hook] \arrow[dd] &                                     & \mathcal{X} \\
B\mu_m \arrow[rd] \arrow[rr, dotted, hook]   &                                 & \mathcal{Z}_m                               &     \\
                                             & p                               &                                     &    
\end{tikzcd}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Defn Radial meander Matrix of arXiv:2506.01306, 'Asymptotic of Coulomb gas integral, Temperley-Lieb type algebras and pure partition functi'] Let $LP(n,m)$ be the set of chordal link patterns on $n$ boundary points, consisting of $m$ non-crossing pairings of $n$ points on the real line. The \emph{meander matrix} $\mathcal{M}_{\kappa}(\alpha,\beta)$ is the Gram matrix associated with the bilinear form
\[ \langle \alpha \mid \beta \rangle_{n,m}
\]
where $\alpha, \beta \in LP(n,m)$, $a = n(\kappa)=-2\cos(\frac{4\pi}{\kappa})$ and $b=2$ are two loop weight parameters.

Let a_1,...,a_m be independent N(0,I_n) vectors, n>=1, x in R^n fixed, and Omega a fixed nonempty compact subset of the Euclidean unit ball. Let g:R^2->R and K:R^n->[0,infinity) be fixed measurable functions. Define ||Y||_psi_p=inf{s>0:E exp(|Y|^p/s^p)<=2}, p=1,2. Assume tau,eta>0, sup_{z in Omega}||g(a^T z,a^T x)||_psi_1<=tau for a~N(0,I_n), and ||K(a)||_psi_2<=eta. Assume also that almost surely, for every z,z0 in Omega, m^(-1)sum_i |g(a_i^T z,a_i^T x)-g(a_i^T z0,a_i^T x)|<=m^(-1)sum_i K(a_i)|a_i^T(z-z0)|. Then for every epsilon>0 there are C,c>0 depending only on epsilon,tau,eta such that m>=C n implies P(sup_{z in Omega}|m^(-1)sum_i g(a_i^T z,a_i^T x)-E g(a^T z,a^T x)|>epsilon)<=exp(-c m). This is Corollary2.2 p7 in an explicit unit-ball domain restriction, with its proof pp23-24; bounded sets of another fixed radius can first be rescaled. K(a_i) may depend on a_i.

[Corollary 22 (Every truncated Debye expansion) of arXiv:2609.01589, 'Uniform stability of expanding simple waves for Euler--Poisson--Boltzmann: a singular comp'] Assume the $M$th-order preparation in \cref{cor:expansion}.  For
$0\le L\le M$, set
\[
 n^{[L]}=\sum_{j=0}^L\eps^{2j}N_j,\qquad
 u^{[L]}=\sum_{j=0}^L\eps^{2j}U_j,\qquad
 \phi^{[L]}=\sum_{j=0}^L\eps^{2j}\Phi_j.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
 \sup_{t_0\le t\le T}\bigl(&
 \norm{n-n^{[L]}}_{H^s}+\norm{u-u^{[L]}}_{H^s}
 +\norm{\phi-\phi^{[L]}}_{H^s}\\
 &+\eps\norm{\nabla(\phi-\phi^{[L]})}_{H^s}\bigr)
 \le C_{L,M,t_0,T}\eps^{2L+2}.
 
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Thus the construction is an asymptotic expansion in the usual nested
sense, not only an estimate for the full $M$th-order sum.

Let independent iid walk increments on Z have P(X=0)=epsilon, P(X=+1)=(1-epsilon)p and P(X=-1)=(1-epsilon)(1-p), with 0<=epsilon<1 and 1/2<=p<=1; let S_0=0 and S_n=sum_{i=1}^n X_i. Independently let C_z be iid fair black/white scenery and Y_i=C_{S_i}. For n>=1 let CT_n be the set of k in {0,...,n-1} for which {S_0,...,S_k} and {S_{k+1},...,S_n} are disjoint AND S_k>=0. Define f(m)=sup_{n>=m}max_{y in {B,W}^n}max_{A subset {0,...,m-1}, |A|>=m/2} P(CT_n intersect A is empty | Y_1^n=y). There exists a neighborhood U of (1,0) in the allowed (p,epsilon) parameter rectangle such that for every (p,epsilon) in U, limsup_{m->infinity}(1/m)log f(m)<0, with log 0=-infinity. Thus even after conditioning on ANY future color word, the probability of avoiding every time in ANY deterministic set of at least m/2 candidate times decays exponentially, uniformly in the outer length n>=m. The neighborhood has not been identified with the entire p>4/5 region. This is a ONE-SIDED future-conditioned estimate. Source: A crossover for the bad configurations of random walk in random scenery, Definition 2.1 and equation (2.2), Lemma 2.4, PDF pages 6-7; proof Section 2.4, PDF pages 11-15.

[Lemma 4 (Bounded weak maximum principle) of arXiv:2608.30211, '2608.30211'] Let $D$ be a uniformly smooth domain, let $V\in L^\infty(D)$ be real, and
suppose
\[
 \lambda(-\Delta+V,D,\varrho)>0.
\]
If $w\in H^1_{\rm loc}(\overline D)\cap L^\infty(D)$ is a weak
supersolution of $(-\Delta+V)w\geq0$ with homogeneous $\cN_\varrho$
boundary condition, then $w\geq0$.  Here ``weak'' means the variational
inequality associated with the Robin form when $\varrho>0$; at
$\varrho=0$ we require the negative part of the trace to vanish and use
zero-trace test functions.

body:
[Corollary 5 of arXiv:2609.01965, 'A logarithmic Bogomolov--Sommese vanishing theorem on compact K\"ahler manifolds'] Let $X$ be a compact K\"ahler manifold of dimension $n$ and $L$ a pseudo-effective line bundle over $X$.
    Let $D$ be a reduced simple normal crossing divisor on $X$. 
    Assume that $\{\alpha\}$ is a pseudo-effective class on $X$ and $c_1(L)-\{\alpha\}=\{\theta+\frac{\ddbar\psi}{2\pi}\}$, where $\theta$ is a smooth real closed $(1,1)$-form and $\psi$
    is a function on $X$ such that $\theta+\frac{\ddbar\psi}{2\pi}\geq0$ in the sense of currents.
    Then
    $$H^n(X,\Omega^p_X(\log D)\otimes L\otimes\mathcal{O}_X(-D)\otimes\mathcal{I}(\psi))=0 \quad\text{for } p\geq n-\nd(\{\alpha\})+1.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 5 of arXiv:2609.01965

[Thm 7 of arXiv:2609.03054, 'The classes of bivariate Schur and Herglotz matrix-valued rational functions: realizations'] Let $F\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}(z_1,z_2)$ be a rational matrix function as in Theorem~\ref{thm:posReRHP}~{\rm(i)}.  
Then the following conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (i)]
\item function $F$ is symmetric;
\item the matrices $A,B,C,D,P_1,P_2$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:posReRHP}~{\rm(ii)} can be chosen in such a way that \eqref{eq:symre} is satisfied
for some unitary involution $U\in{\mathbb C}^{k\times k}$.
\end{enumerate}

Additionally, if $F\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}(z_1,z_2)$ then the matrices $A,B,C,D,P_1,P_2,U$ in {\rm (ii)} may be chosen as real matrices.

[Proposition prop:jointSurvival of arXiv:2608.13452, 'Wasserstein stability of the zero cell of a Poisson hyperplane tessellation under directio'] Given the coupling $(Z_0^{(1)},Z_0^{(2)})$ defined by (equation eq:couplingZeroCells of the paper),
    we have, for all $r_1, r_2 > 0$,
    \begin{align*} 
        \mathbb{P}\bigl[\rho_{Z_0^{(1)}}(u) \geq r_1, \rho_{Z_0^{(2)}}(u) \geq r_2\bigr]
        &= \exp( - \gamma F_u(r_1,r_2) ),
    \end{align*}
    where
    \begin{align} 
        F_u(r_1,r_2)= F_u^{\Phi}(r_1,r_2)
        := \frac{1}{2} \int_{(S^{d-1})^2} |\langle r_1 u , v_1\rangle|+ |\langle r_2 u, v_2 \rangle| + |\langle r_1 u , v_1\rangle - \langle r_2 u, v_2 \rangle| \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \Phi(v_1 , v_2) .
    \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:jointSurvival of arXiv:2608.13452

body: A probability law F on R is n-completely mixable with center mu if there exist n random variables X_1,...,X_n, all with law F, such that sum_i X_i=n*mu almost surely. No independence is required. If F is integrable, taking expectations forces mu=E[X]. Source: Wang, arXiv:1411.6190v3, Definition 3, p.4.

[Defin of arXiv:2605.31054, 'On the empirical spectral distribution of matrix perpetuities'] We say that the distribution of an $N\times N$ real random matrix ${\mathbf Y}$ is invariant under the action of the orthogonal group $O(N)$ if, for any orthogonal matrix ${\bf u}$, we have
    \[
    {\bf u}{\mathbf Y} {\bf u}^\top\stackrel{d}{=}{\mathbf Y}.
    \]    
More generally we say that a pair of random matrices $({\mathbf A},{\mathbf B})$ is orthogonally invariant if for every orthogonal matrix ${\mathbf u}$, we have
\[({\mathbf A},{\mathbf B})\stackrel{d}{=}\left({\mathbf u}{\mathbf A}{\mathbf u}^\top,{\mathbf u}{\mathbf B}{\mathbf u}^\top\right).\]
title: Unnumbered defin of arXiv:2605.31054, 'On the empirical spectral distribution of matrix perpetuitie'

body:
[Cor 14 of arXiv:2606.09691, '\textsc{Degenerate Diffusions on Continuum Percolation and Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Equatio'] Let $\mathcal C(\omega):=\bigcup_{y\in\omega} B_{1/2}(y)$ 
and as before assume $\mathcal C(\omega)$ has a unique unbounded connected component $\mathcal C_\infty(\omega)$. Let
$$
U=\mathcal C_\infty(\omega),
\qquad
\rho(x,\omega):=\rho_{\mathcal C_\infty(\omega)}(x).
$$
with $\rho$ being the function constructed in Lemma \ref{lemma}. 
Let $\theta\in C^\infty([0,\infty))$ satisfy
$\theta(0)=0$, $\theta(r)=r \quad \text{for }0\le r\le \frac12$, 
$\theta(r)=1 \quad \text{for }r\ge 1$, 
$0\le \theta(r)\le 1$, 
$\theta(r)>0 \text{ for } r>0$ and 
$|\theta'(r)|+|\theta''(r)|\le C$.
Define
$$
a(x,\omega):=
\begin{cases}
\theta(\rho(x,\omega)) I_{d\times d},
& x\in \mathcal C_\infty(\omega),\\
0,
& x\notin \mathcal C_\infty(\omega).
\end{cases}
$$
Then the following properties hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item For every $x\in \R^d$ and $\omega\in \Omega$, $a(x,\omega)=a(0,\tau_x \omega)$.
\item The function $\xi(x,\omega):=\theta(\rho(x,\omega))$  satisfies the following:  
for $x\in \mathcal C_\infty(\omega)$, $\xi(x,\omega)\in(0,1]$ and for any $x\in \R^d$ and $\omega\in \Omega$, $\langle a(x,\omega)v,v\rangle
=\xi(x,\omega)|v|^2$ and $\xi(x,\omega)=\xi(0,\tau_x\omega)$. 
\item $\R^d\ni x \mapsto a(x,\omega)$ is globally Lipschitz, 
\item The map 
$$
\mathcal C_\infty(\omega)\ni x \mapsto \sigma(x,\omega):=\sqrt{\theta(\rho(x,\omega))}\, I_{d\times d}
$$ 
is locally Lipschitz on every set $\{x\in \mathcal C_\infty(\omega): d(x,\partial \mathcal C_\infty(\omega))\ge \varepsilon\}$, 
\item The map $x \mapsto \operatorname{div}a(x,\omega)=\nabla\rho(x,\omega)$ 
is bounded and locally Lipschitz away from the boundary, because 
\[
|D^2\rho(x,\omega)|\le C\, d(x,\partial \mathcal C_\infty(\omega))^{-1}.
\]
So $\nabla\rho$ is locally Lipschitz on every region at positive distance from $\partial \mathcal C_\infty(\omega)$.
\end{itemize}

body:
[Lem 110 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $f:\R\to[0,\infty)$ be a smooth function which integrates to one and has compact support. Then the derivative of $f^{1/2}$ is uniformly bounded, that is,
	\[ \|(f^{1/2})'\|_\infty
	= \frac12 \bigg\|\frac{f'}{f^{1/2}}\bigg\|_\infty
	\le O(1)\,,\]
where $O(1)$ indicates a constant depending on $f$.

\begin{proof}
Since $f$ is smooth, we have $\|f''\|_\infty \le C$ where $C$ is a constant depending only on $f$. Assume without loss that $C$ is large. Now suppose $f(y)>0$ is small while $|f'|$ is large, say
$f'(y) \ge 2 C f(y)^{1/2}$. The bound on $f''$ implies $f'(x) \ge C f(y)^{1/2}$ for all $|x-y| \le f(y)^{1/2}$. It follows that
	\[
	f\Big(y-f(y)^{1/2}\Big)
	\le f(y) - Cf(y)^{1/2} \cdot f(y)^{1/2}
	< 0\,,
	\]
contradicting the assumption that $f\ge0$. The case $f'(y) \le - 2 C f(y)^{1/2}$ leads to a similar contradiction, so we conclude 
	\[\bigg\|\frac{f'}{f^{1/2}}\bigg\|_\infty
	\le 2C\,,
	\]
which proves the claim.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 110 of arXiv:2608.29416

[Definition Homological certificate of arXiv:2606.23025, 'Spectral-Capacitary Bounds for Homological Recovery from Reflected Brownian Trajectories'] Let
\(q \in \{ 0,\ldots,d\}\) and \(r > 0\). A finite family
\(\mathcal{A = \{}A_{1},\ldots,A_{m}\}\) of measurable subsets of \(M\)
is a \emph{degree-}\(q\)\emph{, radius-}\(r\) \emph{homological
certificate} for \(M\) if every continuous path
\(\gamma:\lbrack 0,T\rbrack \rightarrow M\) hitting all targets in
\(\mathcal{A}\) satisfies
\(H_{q}\left( \operatorname{Tr}(\gamma)^{r} \right) \cong H_{q}(M)\). If the
implication holds simultaneously for every \(q = 0,\ldots,d\), then
\(\mathcal{A}\) is a \emph{full} homological certificate at radius
\(r\).
title: Homological certificate

[Theorem thm:expLPPgeoconv of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Fix $\rho \in \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$. Either let $\mathcal{M}_n$ equal $\mathcal{L}_n$ in Theorem (thm:expconv of the paper), or else let $\mathcal{M}_n$ equal $H_{\epsilon_n}$ in Theorem (thm:colorTASEPconv of the paper) for a sequence $\epsilon_n \to 0$. Consider a coupling where $\mathcal{M}_n \to \mathcal{L}^\rho$ almost surely, uniformly on compact sets. Then there exists a set $\Omega$ of probability $1$ such that on $\Omega$, the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
	\item Consider a sequence $(x_n, s; y_n, t) \to (x, s; y, t) \in \mathbb H^2_\uparrow$ and a sequence of geodesics $\pi_n$ in $\mathcal{M}_n$ from $(x_n, s)$ to $(y_n, t)$. Then $\pi_n$ is precompact in the uniform topology and any subsequential limit of $\pi_n$ is a geodesic in $\mathcal{L}^\rho$ from $(x, s)$ to $(y, t)$.
	\item If $\mathcal{L}^\rho$ contains a unique geodesic $\pi$ from $(x, s)$ to $(y, t)$, then $\pi_n \to\pi$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem LemODE of arXiv:2608.25865, 'Instability of Böhm's Einstein metrics'] Let $X:\Omega\to \mathbb{R}^4$ be a $C^\infty$ function defined on an open subset $\Omega$ of $\mathbb{R}^4$. Let $s_-<0<s_+$ and 
    $Z_c:[s_-,s_+]\to \Omega$ be a solution of $Z'=X(Z)$.

Set $K=Z_c([s_-,s_+])$, which is a compact subset of $\Omega$. Let $\eta_0>0$ be such that $T:=\{x\in \Omega~|~d(x,K)\leqslant \eta_0\}$ is a compact subset of $\Omega$. Since $X$ is locally Lipschitz, it admits a Lipschitz constant $L$ on $T$.

Finally, let $P\in \mathbb{R}^4$ be such that $|P-Z_c(0)|<\eta_0 e^{-LS}$, where $S=\max(-s_-,s_+)$.

Then the maximal solution $Z_P$ of 

$$\begin{cases}
    Z'=X(Z)
    \\ Z(0)=P
\end{cases}$$
is defined on $[s_-,s_+]$ and \begin{equation}

    \sup_{[s_-,s_+]}|Z_P-Z_c|\leqslant |P-Z_c(0)|e^{LS}.
\end{equation}
title: Lem LemODE of arXiv:2608.25865

[Thm ABC of arXiv:2411.14090, '{\bf Exponential Ergodicity in $\W_1$ for SDEs with Distribution Dependent Noise and Parti'] Assume that for any $\mu\in\mathscr P_1(\mathbb R^d)$, there exists a unique invariant probability measure $\Gamma(\mu)\in\mathscr P_1(\mathbb R^d)$ to (equation GPS12 of the paper) such that $$\mathbb W_1((P_t^{\mu})^\ast\eta,\Gamma(\mu))\leq c_0\text{\rm{e}}^{-\lambda_0 t}\mathbb W_1(\eta,\Gamma(\mu)),\quad t\geq 0,\,\eta,\mu\in\mathscr P_1(\mathbb R^d)$$
for some constants $c_0\geq 1$ and $\lambda_0>0$ not depending on $\mu$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)]
Suppose 
that there exists a continuous function $G:[0,\infty)\rightarrow[0,\infty)$ satisfying
$$\inf_{t>\frac{\log c_0}{\lambda_0}}\frac{G(t)}{1-c_0\text{\rm{e}}^{-\lambda_0 t}}\in[0,1)$$
such that
$$\mathbb W_1((P_t^{\mu_1})^\ast\Gamma(\mu_2),\Gamma(\mu_2))\leq  G(t)\mathbb W_1(\mu_1,\mu_2),\quad t\geq 0,\,\mu_1,\mu_2\in\mathscr P_1(\mathbb R^d).$$

 Then
there exists a unique invariant probability
measure $\mu^\ast\in\mathscr P_1(\mathbb R^d)$ 
for
(equation GPS of the paper).
\item[(ii)] 
Let $\nu\in\mathscr P_1(\mathbb R^d)$ be an invariant probability measure for (equation GPS of the paper).   Assume that there exist a constant $t_1>0$ and a continuous function $H:[0,t_1]\rightarrow[0,\infty)$ with
$$H(t_1)+c_0\text{\rm{e}}^{-\lambda_0 t_1}<1$$
such that $$\mathbb W_1(P_{t}^\ast\eta,(P_{t}^{\nu})^\ast\eta)\leq H(t)\mathbb W_1(\eta,\nu),\quad \eta\in\mathscr P_1(\mathbb R^d),\ \ t\in[0,t_1].$$
Then there exist constants $c,\lambda>0$ such that
$$\mathbb W_1(P_t^\ast\eta,\nu)\leq c\text{\rm{e}}^{-\lambda t}\mathbb W(\eta,\nu), \quad t\geq0,\, \eta\in\mathbb P_1(\mathbb R^d).$$
\end{enumerate}
