[Proposition prop:pll-converse-four-frame-condition of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] Let $\mathfrak{F} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset)$ be a $\Box$-p f-frame.
  Then $\mathfrak{F} \vDash^e \Box \Box \varphi \to \Box \varphi$ for every $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_\Box$
  iff $\mathfrak{F}$ is weakly $\sqsubset$-dense.
  \begin{proof}
    Suppose first that $\mathfrak{F}$ is weakly $\sqsubset$-dense,
    and let $\mathfrak{M}$ be an f-model based on $\mathfrak{F}$.
    Fix $x,x' \in W$ and $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_\Box$ such that
    $x \leq x'$ and $x' \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box \Box \varphi$.
    To show that $x' \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box \varphi$, fix $y \in W$ such that $x' \sqsubset y$.
    By weak $\sqsubset$-density, there are $u,z \in W$ such that
    $x' \sqsubset u \sqsubset z \leq y$.
    Since $x' \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box \Box \varphi$, we have
    $u \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box \varphi$, and hence $z \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$.
    The extrinsic satisfaction relation is $\Box$-persistent on $\mathfrak{M}$
    by Proposition~(prop:extrinsic-persistency of the paper), so $z \leq y$ gives
    $y \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$.
    Thus $x' \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box \varphi$, and therefore
    $x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box \Box \varphi \to \Box \varphi$.

    Conversely, suppose that $\mathfrak{F}$ is not weakly $\sqsubset$-dense.
    Fix $x,y \in W$ such that $x \sqsubset y$ and there are no $u,z \in W$ satisfying
    $x \sqsubset u \sqsubset z \leq y$, and fix $p \in \mathord{\mathrm{PropVar}}$.
    Define a valuation $V$ by
    \[
      V(p) \coloneq
      \set*{ w \in W; \exists u,z \in W\, (x \sqsubset u \sqsubset z \leq w) },
      \qquad
      V(q) \coloneq \emptyset \quad (q \ne p).
    \]
    Each $V(q)$ is upward closed with respect to $\leq$, so
    $\mathfrak{M} = (\mathfrak{F},V)$ is an f-model.
    The definition of $V(p)$ gives $x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box \Box p$,
    while the choice of $x,y$ gives $y \nVdash^e_\mathfrak{M} p$ and hence
    $x \nVdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box p$.
    By the reflexivity of $\leq$,
    $x \nVdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box \Box p \to \Box p$.
    Therefore, $\mathfrak{F} \not\vDash^e \Box \Box p \to \Box p$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:pll-converse-four-frame-condition of arXiv:2608.29708

[Prop 5 of arXiv:2608.30415, 'On generalized complex projective product spaces'] Let $m_1\leq \cdots \leq m_k\leq n_1 \cdots \leq n_\ell$, and $p_j \geq 1, 1 \leq j \leq \ell$. Then,  
\begin{equation}
H^*(C_{(\overline{n}, \overline{p})(\ell),\overline{m}(k)}; \ZZ_2) \cong \ZZ_2[\alpha]/(\alpha^{m_1+1})\otimes\Lambda[\alpha_2, \ldots, \alpha_k, \beta_1,\ldots, \beta_\ell],
\end{equation} where $|\alpha|=2$, $|\alpha_i|=2m_i+1,$ for $2 \leq i \leq k $ and $|\beta_j|=2n_j+1,$ for $1 \leq j \leq \ell,$ $Sq(\alpha_i)=(1+\alpha)^{m_i+1}\alpha_i,$ and $Sq(\beta_j)=(1+\alpha)^{n_j+1-p_j} \beta_j$ .

Otherwise,  $\alpha_i^2 = \alpha^{m_i}\alpha_i$ for all 
$i \geq 2$ with $m_i = m_1$, and $\beta_j^2 = \alpha^{n_j} \beta_j $ for those $j$ with $p_j = 1$ and $n_j = m_1$.
title: Prop 5 of arXiv:2608.30415

[Proposition 38 of arXiv:2605.02002, 'Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI'] Let $p\geq 1,t\geq 0$, consider a subset $A\subseteq [p]$ and a tuple of vertices $u_1,\cdots,u_p\in G$. Then for any sequence of integers $(\ell_i)_{i\in A}$ where 
\begin{equation}
d(u_i,u_{i-1})\geq\ell_i,\quad i\in A,\quad\text{ and   }d(u_i,u_j)\geq 2(\ell_i+\ell_j),\quad i\neq j\in A
    ,\end{equation}we have the factorization
    \begin{equation}
  \mathbb{E}\left[\prod_{i\in A}\delta_t(u_i,\ell_i)\mid h\right]  \leq\prod_{i\in A}\left(\sum_{v\in B_{\ell_i}(u_i)}(1+\mathbf{1}_{v=u_i})\delta_0(v,\ell_i)\right).  
    \end{equation}Here the expectation $\mathbb{E}$ is taken with respect to the Brownian localization path $\operatorname{SL}$ only.

[Lem 29 of arXiv:2607.21759, 'Marchenko--Pastur law for tensor powers of exchangeable unconditional vectors'] For $0<k<\infty$, let $(X_1,\dotsc,X_n) \sim \Inv_k(R)$. Then \[
        \E(X_1^4\dotsm X_r^4 X_{r+1}^2\dotsm X_{2d - r}^2) = \frac{\Gamma(5/k)^r \,\Gamma(3/k)^{2d - 2r}}{\Gamma(1/k)^{2d - r}} \cdot \frac{\Gamma\bigl(\frac{n}{k}\bigr)}{\Gamma\bigl(\frac{n+4d}{k}\bigr)}\cdot \E(R^{4d}).
    \]
    Let $r = 0$ and replace $2d$ by $d$, we get \[
        \E(X_1^2\dotsm X_d^2) = \frac{\Gamma(3/k)^d}{\Gamma(1/k)^d} \cdot \frac{\Gamma\bigl(\frac{n}{k}\bigr)}{\Gamma\bigl(\frac{n+2d}{k}\bigr)}\cdot \E(R^{2d}),
    \] and taking $d = 1$ gives \[
        \E(X_1^2) = \frac{\Gamma(3/k)}{\Gamma(1/k)} \cdot \frac{\Gamma\bigl(\frac{n}{k}\bigr)}{\Gamma\bigl(\frac{n+2}{k}\bigr)}\cdot \E(R^{2}).
    \]

[Proposition 30 (Averaged lower bound under sparsity and edge-density control) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Fix \(u\in[0,1]\), \(\theta>0\), and let
\[
c_{\theta,u}:=1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}.
\]
Also define
\[
C_\theta:=
\begin{cases}
1, & \theta=1,\\[1ex]
\dfrac{\theta |\log \theta|}{|\theta-1|}, & \theta\neq 1.
\end{cases}
\]

Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite graph with \(|V|=n\), and assume that for some \(\eta,\varepsilon>0\),
\[
e_G(S)\le (1+\varepsilon)|S|
\qquad\text{for every }S\subset V\text{ with }|S|\le \eta n.
\]
Assume moreover that
\[
\frac{|E|}{n}\in [m_-,m_+]
\]
for some \(m_-,m_+>0\).

Then for every \(a\ge 0\) and every \(s>0\),
\[
\frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^G_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t
\ge
\frac{
m_- - c_{\theta,u}(1+\varepsilon)-C_\theta/s
}{
(1+\theta)m_+ - c_{\theta,u}(1+\varepsilon)
},
\]
provided the denominator is positive.

[Proposition 16 of arXiv:2609.03098, 'Standing waves for Schr\"odinger equations with Kato class potentials and $L^\infty$-bound'] Let $f:\mathbb{R}^N \times \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a mapping satisfying conditions $(f1)$, $(f2)$, and let 
$\mathcal{E} : H^1(\mathbb{R}^N) \to \mathbb{R}$ be the functional given by
\[
\mathcal{E}(v) := \frac{1}{2} \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} \big(|\nabla v(x)|^2+(V(x)-\lambda)v(x)^2\big)\, dx 
- \int_{\mathbb{R}^N} \mathcal{F}(x,v(x))\, dx, 
\quad v \in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N),
\]
where $\mathcal{F}: \mathbb{R}^N \times \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined by
\[
\mathcal{F}(x,v) := \int_0^{v} f(x,w)\,dw, \quad x\in\mathbb{R}^N, \ v\in\mathbb{R}.
\]
Then $\mathcal{E}$ is a well-defined continuous Lyapunov functional for equation \eqref{main-eq}. More precisely, if
$u:[t_0,t_1)\to H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ is a solution of \eqref{main-eq}, then
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\mathcal{E}(u(t)) = -\int_{\mathbb{R}^N} |\dot u(t)|^2\,dx, \quad t\in(t_0,t_1).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let N=N(n) with N/n->c in (0,infinity). For all n,i,j let X_ij^(n) be real independent identically distributed random variables with mean zero, variance one, and E|X_ij^(n)|^(4+epsilon)<infinity for some epsilon>0. Let sigma_ij(n) be deterministic real numbers uniformly bounded in absolute value. Let A_n be deterministic real N-by-n matrices whose row Euclidean norms and column Euclidean norms are uniformly bounded over all n and all rows and columns. Put (Y_n)_ij=sigma_ij(n) X_ij^(n)/sqrt(n) and Sigma_n=Y_n+A_n. For the relevant N,n, write A=A_n and sigma_ij=sigma_ij(n), D_j=diag(sigma_1j^2,...,sigma_Nj^2), and Dtilde_i=diag(sigma_i1^2,...,sigma_in^2). Let S_plus consist of the functions z->integral_[0,infinity) (lambda-z)^(-1) nu(dlambda) for probability measures nu on [0,infinity), analytically continued to C minus [0,infinity). Define the unique S_plus-valued solution psi_i,psitilde_j by psi_i(z)=-1/[z(1+tr(Dtilde_i Ttilde(z))/n)] and psitilde_j(z)=-1/[z(1+tr(D_j T(z))/n)], where Psi=diag(psi_i), Psitilde=diag(psitilde_j), T(z)=[Psi(z)^(-1)-z A Psitilde(z) A^T]^(-1), and Ttilde(z)=[Psitilde(z)^(-1)-z A^T Psi(z) A]^(-1). Both trace terms in these canonical equations use division by n. For fixed s>0, use natural logarithms and define C_n(s)=E[log det(I_N+Sigma_n Sigma_n^T/s)]/N and Cbar_n(s)=integral_s^infinity [1/omega-tr(T_n(-omega))/N] domega. Then C_n(s)-Cbar_n(s)->0 as n->infinity. Furthermore, evaluating all canonical matrices at -s, Cbar_n(s) equals (1/N)log det[Psi(-s)^(-1)/s+A_n Psitilde(-s) A_n^T]+(1/N)log det[Psitilde(-s)^(-1)/s]-(s/(n N)) sum_{i=1}^N sum_{j=1}^n sigma_ij(n)^2 (T_n(-s))_ii (Ttilde_n(-s))_jj. Both logarithmic determinants are divided by N, including the determinant of the n-by-n matrix. The first quantity C_n is an expectation, as defined in equation (4.1). Equivalently Cbar_n(s)=integral log(1+lambda/s) pi_n(dlambda), with pi_n specified by tr(T_n)/N.
N/n converges to a positive finite constant
real iid entries across the array, centered with variance one and a finite 4+epsilon moment
uniformly bounded deterministic variance profile sigma_ij
deterministic real means A_n with uniformly bounded Euclidean row AND column norms
noise normalization Y_ij=sigma_ij X_ij/sqrt(n)
fixed positive noise-variance parameter s
C_n uses an expectation and 1/N normalization
natural logarithms

[Proposition prop:tailrl-centered-target of arXiv:2609.02987, 'Tail Likelihood Reinforcement Learning'] For $N\geq2$, let
\begin{equation}
\bar\omega
:=
\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N\omega\bigl(r(x,z_i)\bigr),
\qquad
\hat g_{\mathrm{TailRL}}^{(N)}(x)
:=
\sum_{i=1}^N
\Bigl(\omega\bigl(r(x,z_i)\bigr)-\bar\omega\Bigr)\,S(x,z_i).

\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}_{z_{1:N}}\!\left[\hat g_{\mathrm{TailRL}}^{(N)}(x)\right]
=
\nabla_\theta J_{\mathrm{TailRL{}}}^{(N-1)}(\theta;x).

\end{equation}

body:
[Proposition 20 of arXiv:2605.17494, 'Generalized intersection exponents and local cut points for three-dimensional Brownian loo'] For all $j\ge4$, there exist constants $C_1,C_2,C_3,C_4 >0$
    depending only on $r$, $j$, and $\alpha$ such that, for any
    $n\ge m \ge j+4$ and any cube $D$ of side length $2^{-n}$,
    we have
    \begin{equation}
        C_1 2^{-n(1+\xi_{\alpha}(1,1))} \le \Pb(D \in K_{j,n}) \le C_2 2^{-n(1+\xi_{\alpha}(1,1))},
    \end{equation}
    and, for any pair of cubes $D,E$ of side length $2^{-n}$ with
    distance in $[2^{-m-1},2^{-m}]$,
    we have
    \begin{equation}
        \Pb(D,E \in K_{j,n})\le C_3 2^{(-2n+m)(\xi_{\alpha}(1,1)+1)}.
    \end{equation}
    Furthermore, 
    \begin{equation}
        \Pb(D\in F_{j,n}) \le C_4 2^{-n(2+\xi_{\alpha}(1,1))}.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 20 of arXiv:2605.17494

body:
Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, split B, full calibration, paired). The two-vertex blend of the transductive covariance penalty keeps the simplex's gain on EMIT and closes three quarters of its deficit to the pool's hand-tuned heuristic on OCO-2 (-0.27 there); the heuristic is itself label-free, so it was added as a third vertex with barycentric weights chosen by the same criterion. P26 (a) REFUTED: on OCO-2 the three-vertex blend reads -0.09 vs the pool best and +0.18 vs the two-vertex blend; (b) HELD: on EMIT it reads +4.78 vs the pool best and +0.05 vs the two-vertex blend; (c) HELD: mean weights (simplex, least squares, pool) are (0.09, 0.44, 0.47) on OCO-2 and (0.59, 0.24, 0.17) on EMIT; falsifier (three-vertex worse than two-vertex by more than 0.5 on either corpus) not triggered. Fresh-split replication (P27, split C, pre-registered before the split-B result was read): P27 (a) HELD: on split C OCO-2 the three-vertex blend reads -0.12 vs the pool best and +0.20 vs the two-vertex blend; (b) HELD: on EMIT +4.83 vs the pool best and +0.18 vs the two-vertex blend; (c) HELD: mean weights (simplex, least squares, pool) (0.11, 0.42, 0.48) on OCO-2 and (0.57, 0.26, 0.17) on EMIT; falsifier (three-vertex worse than two-vertex by more than 0.5 on either corpus) not triggered.
the three bases are fitted on the calibration rows only (simplex = long-only relative-metric stack; least squares = per-output ridge 1e-6; pool heuristic = per-output ridge with a GCV lambda shrunk toward the pooled convex weights by a 5-fold-CV amount); barycentric weights on the 0.1 grid (66 points); the criterion is the 5-fold cross-validated squared relative error on the calibration rows plus the excess pairs-bootstrap variance (B = 8) of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows; the two-vertex blend is the face with zero pool weight, so its comparison is exact
title: A Three-Vertex Blend of the Simplex, Least Squares and the Pool's Heuristic, Chosen by the Covariance Penalty at the Scored Rows

admissible domains
\(\left( M_{0}^{\varepsilon},M_{1}^{\varepsilon} \right)\),
coinciding outside a ball-like region
\(A_{\varepsilon} = B_{M}(x,\varepsilon)\) inside which the

[Prp 23 of arXiv:2608.30763, 'Ultracontractivity of heat semigroups with non-local Robin boundary conditions via two-sid'] Let $\phi$ be an eigenfunction of $L(A,-C)$ corresponding to an eigenvalue $\mu \in \R$, that is
$$
L(A,-C) \phi \ = \ \mu \phi.
$$
Suppose, in addition, that there exist constants $\delta, M > 0$ such that 
$$
0 \ < \ \delta \ \ \leq \ \phi \ \leq M \ < \ \infty
$$
almost everywhere in $\Omega$. Then the comparison semigroup $(\mathrm{e}^{-tL(A,-C)})_{t \geq 0}$
acts boundedly on $\mathrm{L}^{\infty}(\Omega)$ with
$$
\left\| \mathrm{e}^{-tL(A,-C)} \right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\infty} \to \mathrm{L}^{\infty}} \ \leq \ \frac{M}{\delta} \mathrm{e}^{-t\mu}.
$$
It follows directly from  (\ref{L^infty_continuity}) that $\mathrm{e}^{-tL(A,B)}$ acts boundedly on
$\mathrm{L}^{\infty}(\Omega)$ for every $t > 0$.\\

body:
[Thm 96 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Given any $\acute{b},\acute{\sigma},\acute{w},p,\acute{\zeta},
\acute{\zeta}^\Ising$, let  
\begin{align*}
    d Z(t) &= p'(t)^{1/2} \ab_t\,dt + s(t) \asig_t\,dB(t)\,,
    \\
    dZ^{\Ising}(t)
    &= \aw_t\,dW(t)\,,
    \end{align*}
on the time interval $q_0 \le t \le 1$, with $Z(q_0)\sim\acute{\zeta}$ and $Z^\Ising(q_0)\sim\acute{\zeta}^\Ising$. Assume the following:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item 
The coefficients
$\ab,\asig,\aw$ are 
progressively measurable processes on the time interval $[q_0,1]$;

\item 
$\bE[(\aw_t)^2]=1$ for all $t\in[q_0, 1]$;

\item  $p\in\incr([q_0,1];[0,1])$ with
$p(q_0)\ge 1/L$
and $\|p\|_{C^2([q_0,1])}\le L$;

\item 
The coefficients $\ab,\asig,\aw$ obey the budget constraints \eqref{eq:is-budget-constraint}, that is,
	\[
	\bE \bigg[(\ab_t)^2 + \frac{(tp)'(t)}{p(t)}(\asig_t-1)^2\bigg]
        \le \frac{(\bE \aw_t)^2 }{ \alpha}\,,\]
for all $t\in [q_0,1]$;

\item 
$|Z^{\Ising}(1)|=1$ almost surely;

\item 
$Z(q_0)=0$ almost surely, and $\bE[Z^{\Ising}(q_0)^2]=q_0$;

\item 
$\zeta^\Ising\in\cP([-1,1])$,
the space of Borel probability measures on $[-1,1]$.\footnote{We note that since $Z^\Ising$ is a martingale with $|Z^{\Ising}(1)|=1$ almost surely, the initial distribution cannot have support outside of $[-1,1]$.}
\end{enumerate}
Given any
$q_*,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta,\zeta^\Ising$
(same $p$ as above),
let $X,X^\Ising$ be given by \eqref{e:sde.x} and \eqref{e:sde.x.ising} on the time interval $[q_*,1]$, with $X(q_*)\sim\zeta$ and $X^\Ising(q_*)\sim\zeta^\Ising$.
Then for any $\epsilon>0$ there exist parameters $q_*,b,\sigma,w,\zeta,\zeta^\Ising$ such that the following hold: 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item 
$b_t= b(t,X_t)$, $\sigma_t=\sigma(t,X_t)$, and $w_t= w(t,X_t)$,
for $C$-Lipschitz functions
$b:[q_*,1]\times\R\to[-C,C]$
and $\sigma,w:[q_*,1]\times\R\to[0,C]$, for a constant $C=C(L,\epsilon)$.
 
\item 
 $|\bE[(w_t)^2] -1| \le\epsilon$
 for all $t\in[q_*,1]$. 
 
\item 
 $X$ and $X^{\Ising}$ approximately obey the budget constraints at each time $t$, that is,
	\[\bE \bigg[(b_t)^2 + \frac{(tp)'(t)}{p(t)}(\sigma_t-1)^2\bigg]
        \le \frac{(\bE w_t)^2 }{ \alpha}
        +\epsilon\]
for all $t\in[q_*,1]$.

\item  The initial distributions of $(X,X^\Ising)$ and $(Z,Z^\Ising)$ are close:
\[\begin{aligned}
\bbW_2(\zeta,\acute{\zeta}) &= 
\bbW_2(\Law(X(q_*)),\Law(Z(q_0)))
\leq \epsilon\,,\\
\bbW_2(\zeta^\Ising,\acute{\zeta}^\Ising)
&= \bbW_2(\Law(X^{\Ising}(q_*)),
        	\Law(Z^{\Ising}(q_0)))
\leq \epsilon\,.
\end{aligned}\]

\item  
The initial time $q_*$ lies in $[q_0,q_0+\epsilon]$.
\end{enumerate}
Lastly, we have
	\beq
    \begin{aligned}
	\bbW_2(\Law(X(1)),\Law(Z(1)))
	&\leq \epsilon\,,\\
	\bbW_2(\Law(X^{\Ising}(1)),
        	\Law(Z^{\Ising}(1)))
	&\leq \epsilon
    \end{aligned}
	\eeq
Thus the more general diffusions $(Z,Z^\Ising)$ are well approximated by the Markovian SDE solutions
$(X,X^\Ising)$. Finally, if $\Law(Z^{\Ising}(t))$ is even for each $t$, then we can take $w_t$ to be even for each $t$, that is, $w(t,x)=w(t,-x)$ for all $(t,x)\in [0,1]\times \bbR$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 96 of arXiv:2608.29416

[Proposition 18 of arXiv:2606.16164, 'A Low-Regularity Semigroup Sewing Lemma via Quotient Structures'] Let $\tau\in[0,T]$ and $\beta\in\mathbb R$. If $\gamma\in(0,1)$, then
\[
\Lambda_\tau^{\mathrm d}: ZC^{\gamma}(\Delta^3_\tau;B_\beta)\to C^{\gamma}(\Delta^2_\tau;B_\beta)
\]
is linear, satisfies $\delta\Lambda_\tau^{\mathrm d}h = h$ and obeys the estimate $\|\Lambda_\tau^{\mathrm d}h\|_{\gamma,\beta;\tau}\le C_\gamma\|h\|_{\gamma,\beta;\tau}$. 
If $\gamma=1$, then
\[
\Lambda_\tau^{\mathrm d}: ZC^{1}(\Delta^3_\tau;B_\beta)\to C^{1}_{\mathrm{log}}(\Delta^2_\tau;B_\beta)
\]
is linear, satisfies $\delta\Lambda_\tau^{\mathrm d}h = h$ and obeys the estimates $\|\Lambda_\tau^{\mathrm d}h\|_{1,\log;\tau,\beta} \le C_{1,T}\|h\|_{1,\beta;\tau}$, as well as, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$,  $\|\Lambda_\tau^{\mathrm d}h\|_{1-\varepsilon,\beta;\tau}\le C_{\varepsilon,T}\|h\|_{1,\beta;\tau}$.

[Lem le:paraproduct of arXiv:2411.03482, 'Ergodicity of 2D singular stochastic Navier--Stokes equations'] For $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbf{R}$ and $p, p_1, p_2, q, q_1, q_2 \in [1, \infty]$ such that 
	\begin{equ}
		\frac{1}{p} := \frac{1}{p_1} + \frac{1}{p_2}\;, \qquad \frac{1}{q} := \frac{1}{q_1} + \frac{1}{q_2}\;,
	\end{equ}
	the following bounds hold uniformly in $\varphi, \psi$.
	\begin{equs}
	
		\| \varphi \olessthan \psi \|_{\Besov{\alpha}{p, q}} & \lesssim \| \varphi
    \|_{L^{p_1}} \| \psi \|_{\Besov{\alpha}{p_2, q}} \;, & &  \\ 
    
    \| \varphi \olessthan \psi \|_{\Besov{\alpha+ \beta}{p, q}} &\lesssim \| \varphi
    \|_{\Besov{\alpha}{p_1, q_1}} \| \psi \|_{\Besov{\beta}{p_2, q_2}} \;, \ \ & &  \text{if} \ \ \alpha  <
    0 \;, \\
    
    \| \varphi \odot \psi \|_{\Besov{\alpha+ \beta}{p, q}} &\lesssim \| \varphi
    \|_{\Besov{\alpha}{p_1, q_1}} \| \psi \|_{\Besov{\beta}{p_2, q_2}}\;, \ \ & & \text{if} \ \ \alpha
    {+} \beta > 0 \;.
	\end{equs}
	We will call the first two inequalities high-low paraproduct estimate, and the third inequality resonance estimate. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop locality of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple C'] Let $\Gamma, D$ be the random variables appearing in the subsequential limits~(equation eq cv ball of the paper) and~(equation eq cv subsequence boundary of the paper). Let $V \subseteq \BD$ be a deterministic simply connected subdomain and $I \in \SCS$ a deterministic segment. Let $V^\star$ be the open set obtained by removing from $V$ the closure of the union of the domains encircled by the loops of $\Gamma$ which are not included in $V$. Let $V_j$ for $j\ge 1$ be the connected components of $V^\star$ in decreasing order of Lebesgue measure. For all $j\ge 1$, let $Z_j$ be an independent random point in $V_j$ sampled uniformly with respect to Lebesgue measure. Let $\phi_j$ be the unique conformal mapping from $\BD$ to $V_j$ sending $0$ to $Z_j$ and such that $\phi_j'(0)>0$.

	Then, there exist random distances $D_j$ on $\phi_j^{-1}(\Gamma\vert_{V_j})$, coupled with $(\Gamma, D)$, such that
	\begin{itemize}
		\item Conditionally on $\{ \SCL \in \Gamma: \SCL \not \subseteq V\}$, 
		$\{\SCB_t(\SCL): \SCL \in \Gamma, \  \SCL \not\subseteq V, t \in [0, D(\SCL, \partial V^{\star}))\}$ and $\{\SCB_t(I): t \in [0, D(I, \partial V^\star))\}$, the $(\phi_j^{-1}(\Gamma\vert_{V_j}), D_j)$'s are i.i.d.\ and their conditional law is that of $(\Gamma, D)$.
		\item For all $j$, for all $\SCL_1, \SCL_2 \in \Gamma\vert_{V_j}$, we have
		\[
		D(\SCL_1, \SCL_2) \le D_j(\phi_j^{-1}(\SCL_1), \phi_j^{-1}(\SCL_2)).
		\]
		\item For all $j$, for all $\SCL \in \Gamma\vert_{V_j}$, for all $t \in [0, D(\SCL, \partial V_j))$, the image under $\phi_j$ of the metric ball of radius $t$ for $D_j$ centered at $\phi_j^{-1}(\SCL)$ is $\SCB_t(\SCL)$.
	\end{itemize}

body:
[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2606.09121, 'Truncated Signature Information for Mixed Fractional Brownian Paths'] Let $\theta\in\mathcal P_K$, $t\ge0$, and $h>0$.  Then the expected signature of the local time-augmented path $Z_{t,h}^\theta$ has the following parameter-dependent expected-signature content up to level three.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item Level one is parameter-free:
\[
    \mathbb E_\theta[S^1(Z_{t,h}^\theta)]=(1,0).
\]
\item At level two, the only parameter-dependent expected coordinate is
\[
    2\mathbb E_\theta[\pi_{22}S(Z_{t,h}^\theta)]
    =q_\theta(h)
    =\sum_{r=1}^K v_rh^{\alpha_r}.
\]
\item At level three, the only additional parameter-dependent transform is
\[
    R_\theta(h)
    =\sum_{r=1}^K\frac{v_r}{\alpha_r+1}h^{\alpha_r},
\]
with
\begin{align*}
    \mathbb E_\theta[\pi_{122}S(Z_{t,h}^\theta)]
    &=\frac12R_\theta(h),\\
    \mathbb E_\theta[\pi_{221}S(Z_{t,h}^\theta)]
    &=\frac12R_\theta(h),\\
    \mathbb E_\theta[\pi_{212}S(Z_{t,h}^\theta)]
    &=\frac12q_\theta(h)-R_\theta(h).
\end{align*}
Every level-three coordinate with an odd number of stochastic letters has zero expectation, and $\pi_{111}$ is the deterministic constant $1/6$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, the parameter-dependent part of $\Phi_{2,\mathcal H}$ is $\Psi_{\mathcal H}$, while the parameter-dependent part of $\Phi_{3,\mathcal H}$ is generated by $\Gamma_{\mathcal H}$.

[Ppn 19 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recall $F=F^{\ri}$ from \eqref{e:freeprob.F.equals.F.ri} and $F^{\rii}$ from \eqref{e:F.rii}. 
    For sufficiently large $N$, for all $t\in \R$,
    \[
        \P(F \ge t) \le
        \P\bigg(F^{\rii}(k) +
        \frac{\epsilon'}{5} \ge t
        \bigg) + e^{-cN} \,.
    \]
That is, $F^{\rii}(k)$ approximately stochastically dominates $F$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary 10 (Stochastic Kessler Syndrome) of arXiv:2608.23491, 'Stochastic Dynamics of Low Earth Orbit Near Full Capacity'] The Feller diffusion has the explicit extinction probability
\[
\pr\big(z_F(\tau) = 0\big) = \exp\!\left( -\frac{\theta\, z_{F,0}}{\kappa_5\,\big(1 - e^{-\theta \tau}\big)} \right),
\]
which at exact criticality ($\theta = 0$) reduces to $\exp\!\big(-z_{F,0}/(\kappa_5 \tau)\big)$. Hence:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \emph{Exactly critical ($\theta = 0$):} the debris population goes extinct almost surely, but the time to extinction is heavy-tailed, $\pr(z_F(\tau) > 0) \sim z_{F,0}/(\kappa_5 \tau)$, and excursions scale like $\sqrt{\tau}$.
    \item \emph{Subcritical ($\theta < 0$):} extinction almost surely, at an exponential rate.
    \item \emph{Supercritical ($\theta > 0$):} survival with positive probability $1 - e^{-\theta z_{F,0}/\kappa_5}$, on which event $\E[z_F(\tau)] = z_{F,0}e^{\theta \tau}$ grows exponentially --- a stochastic Kessler runaway.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Stochastic Kessler Syndrome

independent copies of Brownian motion, we use the notation ${_1}B,{_2}B,{_3}B,\ldots$
(in particular, we use ${_i}B^{x_i}$ and ${_i}B^{x_i,y_i}_t$, $i\geq1$, to denote independent Brownian motions
started at $x_i$ and independent Brownian bridges from $x_i$ to $y_i$ on the time interval $[0,t]$).

[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2608.30898, 'Necessity of Ladyzhenskaya \& Ural'tseva's sufficient conditions in nonuniform ellipticity'] Let $q\in (1,2)$ be any number. There exist $\ell_{p}\equiv \ell_{p}(q)>0$, a cube $Q_{p}:=(-\ell_{p},\ell_{p})^{2}\subset \mathbb{R}^{2}$ and a function $u\in W^{1,\infty}(Q_{p})$ with $\sup_{(x,y)\in \bar{Q}_{p}}\snr{Du(x,y)}\le 1$, analytic in a neighborhood of $Q_{p}$, such that $u$ is a local maximizer of functional $\mathcal{J}_{q}(\ \cdot\ ;Q_{p})$ in \eqref{0.0}. Specifically, integral identity
\eqn{0.36}
$$
\int_{Q_{p}}\langle\partial J_{q}(Du),D\varphi\rangle\dx\dy=0\qquad \mbox{for all} \ \ \varphi\in W^{1,1}_{0}(Q_{p})\cap W^{1,\infty}(Q_{p}),
$$
holds true,
\eqn{0.37}
$$
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\ \partial J_{q}(Du)\in L^{\frac{q}{2(q-1)},\infty}(Q_{p},\mathbb{R}^{2})\vspace{1.5mm}\\
\displaystyle
\ [-\ell_{p},\ell_{p}]\times \{0\}\mbox{ is the only maximally extended light ray of }u,
\end{cases}
$$
that is $u(x,0)=x$ for all $x\in [-\ell_{p},\ell_{p}]$ and $\snr{Du(x,y)}<1$ for all $(x,y)\in Q_{p}\setminus \{y=0\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 6 of arXiv:2608.30898

\nabla_\theta J^{(T)}_{\mathrm{TailRL{}}}(\theta;x)
=

\end{equation}

[Theorem th:main of arXiv:2510.13733, 'Internal Diffusion Limited Aggregation \\ with Critical Branching Random Walks'] Let $(A(t))_{t\in \mathbb{N} }$ denote a BIDLA process on $\mathbb Z^d$ satisfying Assumption (equation assumption of the paper). 
\begin{itemize}
\item If $d=1,2$ then there exists $\varepsilon >0$ such that 
	\[ \mathbb{P} \big( A(t) \not\in \mathcal{S}_\varepsilon \mbox{ infinitely often} \big) =1 . \]
\item If $d\geq 3$ then $\forall \varepsilon >0$ 
	\[ \mathbb{P} \big( A(t) \in \mathcal{S}_\varepsilon \mbox{ eventually} \big) =1. \]
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary BPLumpedTrans of arXiv:2605.16244, 'Analysis of a twisted Bose--Einstein Markov chain with applications to sampling Catalan st'] Let $\overline K_{\mathrm{PF}}$ and $\overline\pi_{\mathrm{PF}}$ be the transition kernel and uniform stationary distribution of the lumped Burnside process on $\mathrm{IPF}_n$. 
For $u,v\in\mathrm{IPF}_n$, write $\bm{i}:=\mathrm{hist}(u)$ and $\bm{j}:=\mathrm{hist}(v)$. The lumped Burnside process on $\mathrm{IPF}_n$ has transition kernel
\begin{align}
 \overline K_{\mathrm{PF}}(u,v)
 &=(n+1)\overline K_{\mathrm{BE}}\bigl((\bm{i},0),(\bm{j},0)\bigr)\notag\\
 &=
 (n+1)
 \sum_{M=(m_{a,b})\in\mathcal{M}(\bm{i},\bm{j})}
 \prod_{a,b=1}^n
 \frac{(1/(n+1))_{(m_{a,b})}}{m_{a,b}!}.
 
\end{align}
Its stationary distribution is
\[
 \overline\pi_{\mathrm{PF}}(u)
 =(n+1)\overline\pi_{\mathrm{BE}}\bigl((\bm{i},0)\bigr)
 =\frac1{C_n}.
\]
title: Corollary BPLumpedTrans of arXiv:2605.16244

[Prop 1 of arXiv:2603.26228, 'A local limit theorem for nonlattice multidimensional random walks in cones'] \cite[Lemmas 3.6]{DW2019} {\rm Harmonic function for random walks killed at the boundary of $\cC$.} 
Assume hypotheses {\bf C},  {\bf M} and {\bf N}. Then,  the function $V : \mathcal C \rightarrow \bR^+$ defined by
\[
V({\bf x}) := \lim_{n \to \infty} {\bE}(u({\bf x} +S(n)); \tau({\bf x})>n)
\]
is well-defined,  finite and harmonic for $({\bf x} +S(n))_{n \geq 0}$ killed at leaving $\mathcal C$; in other words, 
\[
V({\bf x})= \bE(V({\bf x} +S(n)); \tau({\bf x})>n),  \quad {\bf x} \in \cC,  n \geq 1.
\]
Furthermore,  the function $V$ satisfies the following properties:
 	\begin{itemize}
	 		\item[(i)] (Positivity) The function 	$V$ is positive    on the set  $\mathcal C$.
			
		\item[(ii)] (``monotony" inside the cone)   If ${\bf x} \in \cC$ then $V({\bf x})\leq V({\bf x} +{\bf a})$ for  all  ${\bf a}\in \mathcal C$ such that ${\bf a} +\cC\subset \cC$.
		
		\item [(iii)]There exists $C_V>0$ such that $0\leq V({\bf x}) \leq C_V(1+\vert {\bf x}\vert^p)$ for any ${\bf x} \in \cC$.
				
		\item[(iv)] (Asymptotic behavior)  For any ${\bf x} \in   \Sigma, $
		\[V(t{\bf x})\sim t^p m_1({\bf x})\quad {\rm  as } \quad t \to \infty, \]
		the convergence being  uniform on compact set of $ \Sigma$.
		\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 1 of arXiv:2603.26228

[Proposition 28 of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $n,m \in \N$. Then, for any $Q \in \conbodo[m]$, and any compact set $K\subset \R^n$ with positive volume such that $o\in \operatorname{int}\operatorname{conv}(K)$,
\[\Vol(K^{\star,Q}) \vol(K^\circ)^{-m} \leq \Vol((\B)^{\star,Q}) \vol(\B)^{-m}.\]

 For a fixed $Q$, there is equality when $K=E$ for some centered ellipsoid $E\subset\R^n$ up to removal of null sets. For a fixed $K$, there is equality when $Q=[0,1]^m$.

Fix t>0, let X have density p(x)=(sqrt(2)/2) exp(-sqrt(2)|x|), and let G~N(0,1) be independent. Put Y=X+sqrt(t)G and a(y)=Var(X|Y=y). Then 0<=a(y)<=t and a(y) tends to t as y tends to positive infinity. For any nonzero smooth phi supported in (0,1), let f_L(x)=integral_{-infinity}^x phi(u-L)du and h_L(Y)=E[phi(X-L)^2|Y]. As L tends to positive infinity, E[a(Y)h_L(Y)]/(t E h_L(Y)) tends to 1. Consequently no fixed q<1 controls this ratio for every test function even for this one fixed isotropic log-concave measure.
X is the specified variance-one centered Laplace law
G independent standard Gaussian
t>0 fixed
phi nonzero smooth and supported in (0,1)
L tends to positive infinity

[Defi Def:Product-DW of arXiv:2608.29013, 'Weighted Homology and Cohomology of Weighted Polyhedra'] \ \vskip 0.1cm
  Let $(X,\lambda)$ be a descending type weighted polyhedron and $R$ be a commutative ring with unit.
  Then for any cochains $\phi\in \mathcal{W}^p(X,\lambda)$ and
  $\psi\in \mathcal{W}^q(X,\lambda)$, let $\phi \Cup \psi\in
  \mathcal{W}^{p+q}(X,\lambda)$
  be the cochain whose value on a
   weighted singular $(p+q)$-simplex
  $\theta: (|\Delta^{p+q}|,\lambda_{\xi}) \rightarrow (X,\lambda)$ is defined by
  \begin{align}  
   \phi\Cup \psi  (\theta)
   :=  \frac{\xi([v_0,\cdots,v_p]) \xi([v_p,\cdots,v_{p+q}])}{\xi([v_0,\cdots,v_{p+q}])} \, \phi(\theta|_{[v_0,\cdots,v_p]})
 \cdot \psi(\theta|_{[v_p,\cdots,v_{p+q}]}).
 \end{align}
 \normalsize
 The coefficient on the right hand side of~(equation Equ:Prod-Wt-Homol of the paper) is always integral because $\xi$ is descending.
  We call $\Cup$ the \emph{weighted cup product} on $(\mathcal{W}^*(X,\lambda),\delta^{\lambda})$.

[Definition defi_strong_sol of arXiv:2603.26307, '\LARGE The incompressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system with thermal noise'] Let Assumption (Ass:noise of the paper) hold, $(\Omega,\mathfrak{A},\mathbb{P})$ be a probability space equipped with a filtration $\mathscr{F}$ satisfying the usual conditions and $3$-dimensional standard $\mathscr{F}$-Brownian motions $(W_n)_{n\in \mathbb{Z}^3}$ and $3\times 3$-matrix valued $\mathscr{F}$-Brownian motions $(B_n)_{n\in \mathbb{Z}^3}$ with covariance structure (equation Eq_noise_matrix_covariation of the paper) be independent. Then a local strong solution to (equation Eq_new_var of the paper), defined up to a stopping time $\tau >0  $, is a tuple of continuous, adapted  processes $U \colon [0,\tau ) \to C^1(\mathbb{T}^3;\mathbb{R}^3)$ and $\Psi \colon [0,\tau ) \to C^1(\mathbb{T}^3)$, such that for a strictly increasing localizing sequence $0\le \tau_j\nearrow \tau $ the following holds for any $j\in \mathbb N$:
	\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
		\item  We have $\mathrm{inf_{(t,x) \in [0,\tau_j] \times \mathbb{T}^3}} \Psi(t,x)>0$, $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely.
		\item  For every divergence-free $\varphi\in C^{{\infty}}(\mathbb{T}^3;\mathbb{R}^3)$ it holds
		\begin{align}\begin{split}
				& \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}  U_t\cdot \varphi\,\mathrm{d} x \,-\, 
				\int_{\mathbb{T}^3} U_0 \cdot \varphi\,\mathrm{d} x
				\\&\quad=\,  \int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} -  \Bigl(\frac{1}{2}+ \frac{F_1}{4}\Bigr) \nabla U: \nabla  \varphi \,+\, U\otimes U:\nabla \varphi \,\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} s \,+\, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}^3}\int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}\Psi f_n \nabla \varphi\,\mathrm{d} x :\mathrm{d} B_{n,s},
			\end{split}
		\end{align}
		and $\nabla \cdot U_t = 0$  for all $t\in [0,\tau_j]$, $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely.
		\item 
		For every $\eta\in C^{{\infty}}( \mathbb{T}^3)$ it holds
		\begin{align}\begin{split}
				&\int_{\mathbb{T}^3} \Psi_t  \eta  \, \mathrm{d} x  \,-\, \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}
				\Psi_0 \eta
				\,\mathrm{d} x \,=\,  \int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}  \frac{\eta}{\Psi} \bigl(
				|\nabla \Psi|^2+|\nabla_\mathrm{sym} U|^2
				\bigr) \,\mathrm{d} x \, \mathrm{d} s
				\\&\qquad+\int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} - \bigl(1+ {F_1}/2 +G_1/2\bigr) \nabla \Psi\cdot \nabla  \eta \,+\,\Psi U\cdot \nabla \eta   \,-\, (F_2/2+G_2/8) \Psi \eta \,\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} s 
				\\&\qquad + \sum_{i=1}^3
				\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}^3}\int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} \Psi g_n \partial_i \eta  + \frac{1}{2} \Psi \eta \partial_ig_n   \,\mathrm{d} x \, \mathrm{d} W_{n,s}^i
				\,-\, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}^3}\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb{T}^3}\eta f_n \nabla U\,\mathrm{d} x :\mathrm{d} B_{n,s},
			\end{split}
		\end{align} for all $t\in [0,\tau_j ]$, $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely.
	\end{enumerate}

[Definition 25 (The density of the absolutely continuous part) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Let $\alpha : \XXA \to [0,\infty)$ be a finite measure and let
$\alpha = \alpha_{\acp{\pi}} + \alpha_{\sgp{\pi}}$ be its Lebesgue decomposition with
respect to $\pi$, as in Theorem \ref{thm:lebesgue} applied with $\mu := \pi$ and
$\nu := \alpha$, with $\alpha_{\sgp{\pi}}$ carried by a set $S \in \XXA$ with
$\pi(S) = 0$; both summands are finite, and
$\sing(\alpha\mid\pi) = \alpha_{\sgp{\pi}}(\XX)$ by \eqref{eq:singsg}. By the
Radon--Nikodym theorem we may fix a map
\[
  g_{\alpha} : \XX \longrightarrow [0,\infty),
  \qquad
  \alpha_{\acp{\pi}}(A) = \int_{A} g_{\alpha} \dd\pi \quad (A \in \XXA),
\]
finite at every point, and call it \emph{the density of the absolutely continuous part
of $\alpha$}; by \ref{conv:representative} it is a genuine map, and every statement
below about it is invariant under changing it on a $\pi$-null set.

Read with the pair $(\pi,\alpha)$ in place of $(\alpha,\beta)$, form
\eqref{eq:singdens} of Proposition \ref{prop:singforms} expresses the \emph{reversed}
singular mass through this same density:
\begin{equation}
  \sing(\pi\mid\alpha) \;=\; \pi\bigl( \{ g_{\alpha} = 0 \} \bigr) ,
  
\end{equation}
so that $\pi \ll \alpha$ if and only if $g_{\alpha} > 0$ $\aewhere$, by the last
sentence of Proposition \ref{prop:singforms}. The set on which
the density of the absolutely continuous part still vanishes is thus exactly the part
of the target that $\alpha$ does not see.
title: The density of the absolutely continuous part

body: [Question q:closed_form_critical_gauge of arXiv:2506.12171, 'The multinomial dimer model'] In Section~(sec:limit_shapes of the paper) we saw various examples of growing families of graphs where the critical gauge has an explicit (in fact rational) closed form in terms of $n$. What are the properties of these graphs? (Stated as a question by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

[Corollary 19 of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Fix $\kappa>1$ and $K_{\rm feat}>0$. For each $d$, let
	$W_1,\ldots,W_n\in\Ssym^d$ be i.i.d. copies of a
	$(K_{\rm feat},\tau_d)$-regular feature with covariance
	$\Sigma_\kappa$, and let $G_1,\ldots,G_n$ be independent Gaussian
	features with the same covariance. Write $W=(W_i)_{i\le n}$ and
	$G=(G_i)_{i\le n}$, and assume
	$n/d^2\to\alpha\in(0,\infty)$.
    Then, the following holds.
	\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
		\item Let $(\mathcal D_d,\mathcal B_d)$ be either
		$(\mathcal R_d^\circ,\mathcal B_+)$ or $(\mathcal R_d^{(m,M)},\mathcal B_{m,M})$ for fixed
		$0<m<1<M<\infty$,
		.
		For every deterministic sequence $0<\beta_d\le1$,
		\begin{equation}
			
			\left|\Phi_W(\mathcal D_d;\beta_d)
			-\Phi_G(\mathcal D_d;\beta_d)\right|
			=O_\P\left((1+\beta_d^{-1})^2
			\left(\tau_d+
			\left(\frac{\log d}{d}\right)^{1/3}\right)\right).
		\end{equation}

		\item If, in addition, $\tau_d\le C_0(\log d)^{-3}$ for some fixed
		$C_0>0$, then
		\[
			\Phi_W(\mathcal R_d^\circ)
			-\Phi_G(\mathcal R_d^\circ)\pto0.
		\]
	\end{enumerate}

[Defi of arXiv:2412.05999, 'Non-Archimedean GUE corners and Hecke modules'] For any $n\ge 1$, let
$$\Lambda_n=\mathbf{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]^{S_n}=\oplus_{k\ge 0}\Lambda_n^k$$denote the ring of symmetric polynomials in $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, here $\Lambda_n^k\subset\Lambda_n$ is the free $\mathbf{Z}$-submodule consisting of all homogeneous symmetric polynomials of degree $k$.

We form the inverse limit $\Lambda^k=\lim_\leftarrow\Lambda_n^k$ of the $\mathbf{Z}$-modules $\Lambda_n^k$ relative to the canonical homomorphisms, and $\Lambda=\oplus_{k\ge 0}\Lambda^k$ to be the graded \emph{ring of symmetric functions} in countably many independent variables $x_1,x_2,\ldots$.

[Defn def:flowblowdown of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $\Phi$ be a smooth flow on a closed $3$-manifold $M$. A \textbf{blowup} of $(M, \Phi)$ along a closed orbit $\gamma$ of $\Phi$ is a pair $(M^\circ,\Phi^\circ)$, where $M^\circ$ is a compact $3$-manifold with torus boundary and $\Phi^\circ$ is a flow on $M^\circ$ tangent to the boundary, together with a map $\pi:M^\circ \to M$ such that 
        \begin{enumerate}
        \item There exist smooth local coordinates $(r, \theta, \phi)$ around $\partial M^\circ$ (where $r$ parametrizes the normal direction, $\phi$ parametrizes the longitudinal direction, $\theta$ parametrizes the meridional direction) and cylindrical coordinates $(r,\theta,\phi)$ in a neighborhood of $\gamma$ (where $\gamma$ lies along $\{r=0\}$), such that $\pi$ has the form 
        $$\pi(r,\theta,\phi) = (f(r),\theta,\phi)$$
        for some smooth function $f:[0,1]\to [0,1]$. In particular, $\pi$ sends $\partial M^\circ$ to $\gamma$, collapsing leaves of a linear foliation on $\partial M$ to points.
        \item $\pi$ restricts to a smooth orbit equivalence between $(\interior M^\circ, \Phi^\circ\vert_{\interior M^\circ})$ and $(M, \Phi\vert_{M\setminus \gamma})$.
        \end{enumerate}
    We say that $(M, \Phi)$ is a \textbf{blowdown} of $(M^\circ, \Phi^\circ)$ along the slope $\phi=const$.
title: Defn def:flowblowdown of arXiv:2608.30031

[Lem almostflat of arXiv:2606.01627, 'The geometry of the giant component of random geometric graphs'] For each $z \in M$ and $\eta > 0$ there exists $\delta_0 \in (0,1)$
	such that for every $0<\delta \le \delta_0$,
	any ball $U = B_M(z,\delta)$ in $M$ of radius $\delta$ has the following properties. 
	Let
	\[
	u : U \to B_{\mathbb{R}^d}(0,\delta)
	\]
	be exponential normal coordinates. 
	Then $u$
	is a diffeomorphism with
	\[
	e^{-\eta} d_M(x,y) 
	\le d_{\mathbb{R}^d}( u(x), u(y) )
	\le e^{\eta}d_M(x,y)
	\]
	for all $x,y \in U$.
	Moreover if $\mathcal{L}$ is the Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$ then the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the pushforward $u_\ast dM$ of the Riemannian volume measure $dM$ satisfies $$e^{-\eta} \leq \frac{u_\ast dM}{d\mathcal{L}} \leq e^{\eta}$$ on $u(U)$.
title: Microscopic balls on $M$ are almost flat
Theorem th 5.6 of arXiv:2511.07173

[Lemma lem6.14 of arXiv:2508.12951, '\textbf{On the central limit question for strictly stationary, reversible Markov chains}'] Suppose $(E_1, E_2, E_3, \dots)$ is a sequence of independent events
on a probability space $(\Omega, \mathcal F, P)$, such that 
$\sum_{j=1}^\infty P(E_j^c) < \infty$ (where the superscript 
$c$ denotes complement).

   Suppose that on the same probability space, $(F_1, F_2, F_3, \dots)$ is a
sequence of independent events such that
(i) $P(F_j) > 0$ for each $j\in \mathbb N$, and 
(ii) $F_j = E_j$ (an equality of events) for all except at most finitely
many indices $j \in \mathbb N$.
Then $P(\bigcap_{j=1}^\infty F_j) = \prod_{j=1}^\infty P(F_j) > 0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem6.14 of arXiv:2508.12951

[Lemma lem:free-energy-typical-truncation of arXiv:2411.09075, 'Weak Poincar{\'e} Inequalities, Simulated Annealing, and Sampling from Spherical Spin Glas'] The following holds for sufficiently small $c>0$ depending on $\eps$.
    Let
    \[
        T = T(H_N) \coloneqq \lt\{
            \sigma \in S_N :
            \int_{S_N}
            \Ind[|R(\sigma,\tau)| \ge N^{-2/5}]
            e^{H_N(\tau)}
            \dif\rho(\tau)
            \le e^{N\xi(1)/2 - cN^{1/5}}
        \rt\}.
    \]
    Then, we have:
    \begin{align}
        
        \E \int_{S_N} \Ind[\sigma \not\in T] e^{H_N(\sigma)} \dif\rho(\sigma)
        &\le e^{N\xi(1)/2 - cN^{1/5}}, \\
        
        \E \int_{S_N} \Ind[\sigma \not\in T] e^{H_{N,2}(\sigma)} \dif\rho(\sigma)
        &\le e^{N\xi''(0)/4 - cN^{1/5}}, \\
        
        \E \int_{S_N} \Ind[\sigma^1 \not\in T, |R(\sigma^1,\sigma^2)| \le 3N^{-2/5}]
        e^{H_N(\sigma^1)+H_N(\sigma^2)} \dif\rho^{\otimes 2}(\sigma^1,\sigma^2)
        &\le e^{N\xi(1) - cN^{1/5}}, \\
        
        \E \int_{S_N} \Ind[\sigma^1 \not\in T, |R(\sigma^1,\sigma^2)| \le 3N^{-2/5}]
        e^{H_{N,2}(\sigma^1)+H_N(\sigma^2)} \dif\rho^{\otimes 2}(\sigma^1,\sigma^2)
        &\le e^{N\xi(1)/2 + N\xi''(0)/4 - cN^{1/5}}.
    \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:free-energy-typical-truncation of arXiv:2411.09075

body:
[Proposition 7 (Fixed-threshold almost-flat/torus-bundle alternative) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Let \(M\) be \(\TT^3\), a compact \(\Nil\) torus bundle with nontrivial
unipotent monodromy, or a compact \(\Sol\) torus bundle with hyperbolic
monodromy, and let \(g(t)\) be an immortal Ricci flow on \(M\).  Let \(K\) be
a Type-III constant supplied by Proposition~\ref{input:bamler-typeIII}.
Fix any \(c_0\in(0,1)\) such that
\begin{equation}
        Kc_0^2<\eps_{\mathrm{af}}.
\end{equation}
The parameter \(c_0\) is used only as the diameter threshold separating the two
geometric alternatives below; it is not an analytic smallness parameter and will not
be decreased later to meet compactness or stability tolerances.

There exist a finite time \(T_B(c_0)<\infty\) and a nonincreasing function
\[
        \eps_B^{c_0}:[T_B(c_0),\infty)\longrightarrow(0,\tfrac12],
        \qquad \eps_B^{c_0}(t)\longrightarrow0,
\]
with
\begin{equation}
        \eps_B^{c_0}(t)<c_0,
        \qquad t\geq T_B(c_0),
\end{equation}
such that every \(t\geq T_B(c_0)\) belongs to exactly one of the following
diameter-defined alternatives.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
If
\begin{equation}
        \diam(M,g(t))<c_0\sqrt t,
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}
 \bigl(\sup_M|\sec_{g(t)}|\bigr)\diam(M,g(t))^2
 <Kc_0^2<\eps_{\mathrm{af}}.
\end{equation}
Thus the slice is quantitatively almost flat.

\item
If
\begin{equation}
        \diam(M,g(t))\geq c_0\sqrt t,
\end{equation}
then there exist a torus fibration \(\pi_t^B:M\to S_t^1\) and an invariant metric \(g_t^B\), in the sense described in
Subsection~\ref{subsec:torus-bundle-conventions}, such that
\begin{equation}
        (1+\eps_B^{c_0}(t))^{-1}g_t^B\leq g(t)
        \leq(1+\eps_B^{c_0}(t))g_t^B.
\end{equation}
Moreover, for every integer \(m\) with
\(0\leq m<\bigl(\eps_B^{c_0}(t)\bigr)^{-1}\), the metric
\(t^{-1}g_t^B\) is \(\eps_B^{c_0}(t)\)-close to \(t^{-1}g(t)\) in
\(C^m\), relative to \(t^{-1}g(t)\), and every fiber has
\(g(t)\)-diameter at most \(\eps_B^{c_0}(t)\sqrt t\).
\end{enumerate}
Labels~(\ref{item:bamler-small-slice}) and~(\ref{item:bamler-large-slice})
refer only to the diameter inequalities.  A torus comparison
may also exist in the first alternative, but it is not used there.  In the
second alternative the fibration, quotient circle, and comparison metric may
depend on \(t\), with no asserted compatibility or uniqueness. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary cor:fpt-exponential of arXiv:2605.17082, 'Spectral Purification in Reversible Markov Chains: Hidden Parameters, Observable Equivalen'] Let $\tau_a$ be the first-passage time to an absorbing state $a$, and let $\nu_2$ be the dominant eigenvalue of the absorbing chain $P_a$. For any $\delta \in (0, 1/2)$ and any $k \ge T_{\mathrm{rigid}}(\delta)$,
\[
\left| \frac{\mathbb{P}(\tau_a > k)}{\alpha_2 \nu_2^k} - 1 \right|
\le C(\lambda_2, \lambda_3) \left( \delta + \frac{R_0}{|c_2|^2} \left(\frac{\lambda_3}{\lambda_2}\right)^{2k} \right),
\]
where $C(\lambda_2, \lambda_3) = (1-\lambda_3^2)/(\lambda_2^2 - \lambda_3^2)$ and $R_0 / |c_2|^2$ is the initial fast-to-slow energy ratio.

[Defn d:sharp-dperc of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] For a graph $\Psi = {\Psi(\cdot)}$ defined on the input process \( \mathcal{P} \), the {\em critical probability $q_c$ for  percolation} is defined as  
\begin{equation}
q_c := \sup\Bigl\{q \in [0,1] :  \forall p \in \mathbb{N} , \, 
\text{the function $\tilde{\mathfrak{a}}_{p,q}(r)$ is fast decreasing as $r\to\infty$}\Bigr\},
\end{equation}
where for $r > 0$
\begin{equation} \tilde{\mathfrak{a}}_{p,q}(r):=\sup_{n \geq 1} \sup_{x_1,\ldots,x_p\in W_n}
\mathbb{P}_{\bk x1p,q}\bigl( x_1 \stackrel{(\mathcal{P}_n\cap B_{r}(x))_{*q}}{\longleftrightarrow} \mathcal{P}_n \cap B_r(x_1)^c \bigr), \,
\end{equation}
where the underlying graph is $\Psi(\mathcal{P}_n)$ and recall that
\(
\{x \stackrel{{{\cal X }'}_{*q}}{\longleftrightarrow} \mathcal{Y}\} = \{x \stackrel{\perc{\Psi({\cal X })}{{\cal X }'}{q}}{\longleftrightarrow} \mathcal{Y} \}
\)
means that there exists an open path in~\(\Psi({\cal X })\) from~\(x\in{\cal X }'\subset{\cal X }\) to
\(\mathcal{Y}\subset {\cal X }\)  through vertices in ${\cal X }'_{*q}$, the thinned subset of ${\cal X }'$ where vertices in~\({\cal X }'\) are
independently open/retained with probability~\(q\), while all other vertices in ${\cal X }$ are
always open, and where \(\mathbb{P}_{\bk x1p,q}\) incorporates this additional percolation randomness on top of Palm distribution.

[Corollary Main Corollary of arXiv:2608.27248, 'Optimal Transport and the ABP Method in Higher Codimension'] Let $n\geq2$ and $1\leq m\leq4$.  Let
$X:\Sigma\to\mathbb{R}^{n+m}$ be a smooth immersion of a compact $n$-dimensional
manifold with smooth boundary, where the boundary may be empty, and let
$\mathcal E$ be a centered ellipsoid.  Then every positive
$f\in C^\infty(\Sigma)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \int_\Sigma h_{\mathcal E}(\nabla^\Sigma f+fH)\,\mathrm d\mu
 +\int_{\partial\Sigma}f h_{\mathcal E}(\eta)\,\mathrm d\sigma
 \geq nV_*(\mathcal E)^{\frac1n}
 \left(\int_\Sigma f^{\frac n{n-1}}\,\mathrm d\mu\right)^{\frac{n-1}{n}}.
\end{equation}
Equality holds if and only if $\Sigma$ is connected, $f$ is constant, and,
for some $n$-plane $P$ realizing $V_*(\mathcal E)$, $X$ is an embedding onto
$x_0+r\,\overline{\operatorname{proj}_P\mathcal E}$ for some
$x_0\in\mathbb{R}^{n+m}$ and $r>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm subcritical-blob-picture of arXiv:2607.21428, 'Subcritical percolation and network archaeology on random recursive tree substrate network'] Fix \(\gl>0\) and \(0<p<p_c(\gl)\). Then the following hold.
		\begin{enumeratea}
			\item For every \(\varepsilon>0\), there is a finite \(K=K(\varepsilon)\) such that
			\[
			\limsup_{n\to\infty}
			\mathbb P\left(
			\operatorname{rank}(\mathcal{B}_n(1))>K
			\right)
			<\varepsilon .
			\]
			Here \(\operatorname{rank}(\mathcal{B}_n(1))\) is the position of the root blob in the
			decreasing size order fixed in Section~(sec:model-notation of the paper).
			\item The normalized counts of retained recursive-tree blobs have a
			power-law tail. More precisely, if \(N_{n,k}\) denotes the number of blobs
			of size \(k\), then, for every fixed \(k\geqslant 1\),
			\[
			\frac{N_{n,k}}{n}
			\stackrel{\mathrm{P}}{\longrightarrow}
			q_k
			:=
			\frac{1-p}{p}\,B\left(k,1+\frac1p\right),
			\]
			where \(B(\cdot,\cdot)\) is the Beta function. Thus,
			\[
			\sum_{\ell\geqslant k} q_\ell
			\sim
			(1-p)\Gamma\left(1+\frac1p\right)k^{-1/p}.
			\]
			The size-biased blob seen from a uniformly chosen vertex has probabilities
			\[
			\mathbb P(W^\star=k)=kq_k,
			\]
			and, for \(p<1/2\),
			\[
			\mathbb E W^\star=\sum_{k\geqslant1}k^2q_k=\frac{1}{1-2p}.
			\]
			\item For each fixed \(K\), with probability tending to one, the \(K\) largest
			full percolation components are those containing the \(K\) largest
			backbone blobs, with their order determined by the tie rule above. Moreover,
			for every fixed \(i\),
			\[
			\left|
			|\mathcal{C}_{n,i}^{\operatorname{full}}|
			-
			\frac{W_{n,i}}{1-\rho(p,\gl)}
			\right|
			=
			o_{\mathbb P}(n^p),
			\]
			where \(\mathcal{C}_{n,i}^{\operatorname{full}}\) is the full percolation component containing
			\(\mathcal{B}_{n,i}\).
		\end{enumeratea} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Subcritical blob picture

body:
[Theorem Inverse transport theorem of arXiv:2608.27248, 'Optimal Transport and the ABP Method in Higher Codimension'] Let $m\geq1$, let $X:\Sigma^n\to\mathbb{R}^{n+m}$ be a smooth immersion of a
compact manifold, possibly with smooth boundary, and let
$\mathcal K\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+m}$ be a bounded open convex set.  Let
$u\in C^{2,\alpha}(\Sigma)$, understood up to the boundary, for some
$\alpha\in(0,1)$.  If $\partial\Sigma\ne\varnothing$, assume
$\langle\nabla^\Sigma u,\eta\rangle=h_{\mathcal K}(\eta)$ on
$\partial\Sigma$.  With $v$, $Q$, $\Phi$, $\mathcal{C}$, and $\vartheta$ defined
above, the following conclusions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item One has $Q_x(y)\geq0$ on $\mathcal{C}$ and, for every Borel function
$\varphi:\mathcal K\to[0,\infty]$,
\begin{equation}
 \int_{\mathcal{C}}\varphi(\Phi(x,y))\frac{\det Q_x(y)}{\vartheta(x)}
 \,\mathrm d\mu(x)\,\mathrm dy
 =\int_{\mathcal K}\varphi(\xi)\,\mathrm d\xi.
\end{equation}
Both sides are understood as extended nonnegative integrals.

\item Let $\rho$ be a nonnegative Borel function satisfying
$\int_{\mathcal K}\rho\,\mathrm d\xi=1$, and set
\[
 I_\rho(x)=\int_{\mathcal{C}_x}\rho(\Phi(x,y))\det Q_x(y)\,\mathrm dy,
 \qquad
 \mathrm d\lambda_{u,\rho}(x)=\frac{I_\rho(x)}{\vartheta(x)}\,\mathrm d\mu(x).
\]
By part \textup{(i)}, $I_\rho(x)<\infty$ for $\mu$-almost every $x$.
For $0<I_\rho(x)<\infty$, define
\begin{equation}
 \mathrm d\nu_{x,\rho}(y)
 =\frac{\rho(\Phi(x,y))\det Q_x(y)}{I_\rho(x)}
 \mathbf1_{\mathcal{C}_x}(y)\,\mathrm dy.
\end{equation}
On $\{I_\rho=0\}\cup\{I_\rho=\infty\}$ set
$\nu_{x,\rho}=\delta_0$.  Then $x\mapsto\nu_{x,\rho}$ is a Borel
probability kernel, $\lambda_{u,\rho}$ is a probability measure, and the plan
$\pi_{u,\rho}$ defined by
\begin{equation}
 \int \zeta\,\mathrm d\pi_{u,\rho}
 =\int_\Sigma\int_{N_x\Sigma}
 \zeta(x,v(x)+y)\,\mathrm d\nu_{x,\rho}(y)\,\mathrm d\lambda_{u,\rho}(x)
\end{equation}
for bounded Borel $\zeta$ has marginals $\lambda_{u,\rho}$ and
$\rho\,\mathrm d\xi$, and is optimal for
$c(x,\xi)=\frac12|X(x)-\xi|^2$.

\item Let
\begin{equation}
 \Psi(\xi)=\max_{z\in\Sigma}
 \{\langle X(z),\xi\rangle-u(z)\}.
\end{equation}
As a supremum of affine functions, $\Psi$ is convex and hence differentiable
almost everywhere.  Then $T=\nabla\Psi$ is the Brenier map from
$\rho\,\mathrm d\xi$ to $X_\#\lambda_{u,\rho}$ and
\begin{equation}
 T_\#(\rho\,\mathrm d\xi)=X_\#\lambda_{u,\rho}.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Inverse transport for the ABP map

[Lemma 25 (Block entropy bound for exchangeable laws) of arXiv:2608.28827, 'Quantitative Target Convergence and Uniform-in-Time\\ Propagation of Chaos for Langevin-Re'] Let \(P^N\) be an exchangeable probability measure on
\((\R^d)^N\), let \(\rho\in\mathcal P(\R^d)\), and let
\(1\le k\le N\). Then
\begin{equation}
    \KL(P^{N,k}\|\rho^{\otimes k})
    \le
    \frac{1}{\lfloor N/k\rfloor}
    \KL(P^N\|\rho^{\otimes N}),
\end{equation}
where \(P^{N,k}\) denotes the common \(k\)-coordinate marginal of
\(P^N\).

[Definition of arXiv:2412.07936, 'Simple Norm Bounds for Polynomial Random Matrices via Decoupling'] [Graph matrix, see e.g. [RT23] Definition 4.4]
Given a shape $\tau$, the associated graph matrix ${\bf M}$ : $\Omega \rightarrow {\mathbb R}^{d_1 \times d_2}$ is a matrix-valued function such that
$$
{\bf M} [I,J] = \sum_{\substack{\varphi \in {\mathcal T}^k_n: \\ \varphi(U_\tau) = I, \varphi(V_\tau) = J }} \prod _{(u,v) \in E(\tau)} G_{\varphi(u),\varphi(v)}.
$$
In other words, ${\bf M}$ maps an input graph $G \in \Omega$ to a $\frac{n!}{(n-|I|)!} \times \frac{n!}{(n-|J|)!}$ matrix whose rows and columns are indexed by $I$ and $J$ respectively.

The PDF (v2, 4 May 2021), printed p.8, states for H={sum_(i=1)^d alpha_i x_i^2}, Gaussian input, and orthogonally equivariant learners:
  N_star(A,P,epsilon) >= [d(d+3)/2](1-epsilon)-1.
The formula was visually checked in papers/theorem54_page.png; this is not inferred only from PDF text extraction. The definition directly above it normalizes mean square prediction error by E[y^2].

Counterexample to the literal lower bound: take d=2. Any symmetric quadratic x^T A x has only D=d(d+1)/2=3 coefficients. Given n=3 Gaussian observations, solve least squares over Sym(2) and select the minimum Frobenius-norm solution on rank-deficient samples. This algorithm is orthogonally equivariant on every dataset: conjugation A->R A R^T maps the least-squares solution sets into each other and preserves Frobenius norm, while the minimum-norm solution is unique. Hence predictions transform as required by source Definition 3.2.

For three generic Gaussian inputs, the 3 by 3 quadratic evaluation design is invertible almost surely. Its determinant is a polynomial that is not identically zero: inputs (1,0), (0,1), (1,1), with coefficient coordinates (A_11,A_12,A_22), give rows (1,0,0), (0,0,1), (1,2,1), with determinant -2. A nonzero polynomial vanishes on a Lebesgue-null set; independent Gaussian inputs are absolutely continuous. Thus the algorithm reconstructs EVERY symmetric A exactly almost surely, in particular every diagonal target in H, and has zero population squared error. For each fixed target, N_star<=3 at every epsilon>0, including the normalized definition. The zero target also has zero error and poses no division issue because the definition is an inequality against epsilon E[y^2].

At epsilon=1/10, the printed bound is 5*(9/10)-1=7/2>3, a contradiction. More generally, D Gaussian samples exactly reconstruct every symmetric d by d quadratic, so the printed expression cannot hold when it exceeds D.

The interpolation counterexample alone refutes the literal theorem constant, independently of those calculations.

[Defn Formal Jackson integral operator of arXiv:2609.01458, 'Confluence relations for $q$-analogues of multiple zeta values'] Define the $\mathbb{Q}$-linear map $S\colon\mathbb{Q}\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{z}\otimes\Omega\to\mathbb{Q}\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{z}$
by 
\[
S(\mathbb{L}_{k_{1},\dots,k_{d}}(q^{n_{1}},\dots,q^{n_{d-1}},zq^{n_{d}})\otimes e_{0})\coloneqq\mathbb{L}_{k_{1},\dots,k_{d-1},k_{d}+1}(q^{n_{1}},\dots,q^{n_{d-1}},zq^{n_{d}}),
\]
\[
S(\mathbb{L}_{k_{1},\dots,k_{d}}(q^{n_{1}},\dots,q^{n_{d-1}},zq^{n_{d}})\otimes e_{q^{-r}})\coloneqq-\mathbb{L}_{k_{1},\dots,k_{d},1}(q^{n_{1}},\dots,q^{n_{d-1}},q^{n_{d}-r},zq^{r}),
\]
\[
S(\mathbb{L}(\emptyset)\otimes e_{q^{-r}})\coloneqq-\mathbb{L}_{1}(zq^{r}),
\]
\[
S(\mathbb{L}(\emptyset)\otimes e_{0})\coloneqq0.
\]
The last assignment is made by convention, and this exceptional value
is not used in the recursive construction of $\varphi$ introduced
later.
title: Formal Jackson integral operator

[Definition of arXiv:2605.02226, 'Finitely Dependent Processes on Subshifts'] A process $(Y_g)_{g \in G} $ is an \textbf{r-block factor} of $ (X_g)_{g \in G} $, 
 if there exists a measurable function $ \psi: \mathcal{A}^{\mathbf{B}(r)} \rightarrow \mathcal{B}$ such that $ Y_g = \psi((X_h)_{h \in g \cdot \mathbf{B}(r)})$ for all $ g \in G$. $(Y_g)_{g \in G}$ is a \textbf{block factor} of $(X_g)_{g \in G}$ if it is an $r$-block factor of $ (X_g)_{g \in G}$ for some $ r \in \mathbb{N}$.

$G$. Let $E_{G}$ be an equivariant holomorphic principal $G$--bundle on $X$ equipped
with an equivariant holomorphic reduction of structure group of $E_{P}\,\subset\, E_{G}$, to some parabolic
subgroup $P\, \subset\, G$, that is equivariantly infinitesimally rigid. Take any equivariant holomorphic
Lie algebroid $(V,\,\phi)$ on $X$ that satisfies the condition that the anchor map $\phi$ is not
surjective. Then
the holomorphic principal $P$--bundle $E_{P}$ admits an equivariant holomorphic $(V,\,\phi)$--connection.

[Theorem thm_main_R of arXiv:2411.08846, 'On the Number of Crossings and Bouncings\\ of a Diffusion at a Sticky Threshold'] Let $X$ be the sticky-reflected Brownian motion of stickiness parameter $\rho>0 $, defined on the filtered probability space $(\Omega,\bF,(\bF_t)_{t\ge 0},\Prob_x) $ such that $\Prob_x$-a.s.: $X_0 = x \geq 0$ (in particular, $X$ is $(\bF_t)_{t\ge 0}$-adapted). 
Let also $\loct{X}{0}{} $ be the right local time at $0$ of $X$ 
and $\cB{0}{},\cB{1}{},\cB{2}{},\cD{1}{}, \cD{2}{} $ be the quantities defined in Section~(sec_intro of the paper)
for the process $X$.
Then, the following convergences holds, 
\begin{enumerate}
	[label={ (\roman*)}]
	\item  for every diverging sequence $u_n$, it holds that:  
	$ \cB{0}{n,\cdot}(X)/u_n  \convergence{\Prob_x\text{-}\mathrm{ucp}} 0 $, 
	\item $ \cB{1}{n,\cdot}(X)/\sqrt n \convergence{\Prob_x\text{-}\mathrm{ucp}}
	2 \sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}} \loct{X}{0}{} $, 
	\item $ \cB{2}{n,\cdot}(X)/n \convergence{\Prob_x\text{-}\mathrm{ucp}} \frac{\rho}{2} \loct{X}{0}{} $, 
	\item $ \cD{j}{n,\cdot}(X)/n^{j/2}$ has the same limit as $ \cB{j}{n,\cdot}(X)/n^{j/2}$ for $j=1,2$,
	
\end{enumerate}
where as per~(equation eq_SDE_X of the paper), $\frac{\rho}{2} \loct{X}{0}{t}= \int_{0}^{t} \mathbbm{1}_{\{X_s = 0\}} \,\mathrm{d} s $, for all $t\ge 0 $.
title: Theorem thm_main_R of arXiv:2411.08846

[Lemma lem.few_dropped of arXiv:2603.11043, 'An asymptotically optimal bound for the concentration function of a sum of independent int'] Let $k$ and $K$ be positive integers and let $\delta \in (0,1)$.
   Let $\alpha \in (0,1]^n$.
   Let $(Y_1, \dots, Y_n)$ be a standard extremal sequence for $\alpha$,
   and suppose that $\alpha_i \ge K^{-1}$ for $i \in \{1, \dots, k\}$.
   Write $S_n = \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i$.
   If 
   \[
        {\mathrm{Var}}\, S_n \ge V_{k, K, \delta} := \frac{70}{\delta^{3}} k K^2
   \]
   then
   \begin{equation}
        \mathcal{Q}(Y_1 + \dots + Y_n) \ge (1-\delta)\mathcal{Q}(Y_{k+1} + \dots + Y_n)
   \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem.few_dropped of arXiv:2603.11043

The system is exactly an M/G/1 queue of rate k*lambda and service duration M=min(B1,...,Bk), where the vector B is iid across jobs but may be correlated within each job. Its strict stability condition is k*lambda*E M<1. In the S-and-X case M=X*min_i S_i. Identical copies yield lambda<1/(k*E B); independent unit exponentials yield lambda<1. ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Explicit calculation or obstruction with source-specific scope Result: A fixed metric sphere and the union of spheres over all radii have different dimension behavior. In the Euclidean plane, each circle about the origin has Hausdorff dimension1 while their union over radii in[1,2] is an annulus of dimension2. Thus even a sharp dimension theorem for each outer boundary cannot be passed to the metric net by countable stability: the union is uncountable. Check: The annulus contains a nonempty open set, proving its dimension2; each positive-radius circle is a smooth one-dimensional manifold. Countable unions would preserve the supremum of dimensions, so the radii parameter cannot be silently replaced by a countable dense set. Obstruction: For LQG one needs joint control of the outer boundaries as radius varies, including the jumps created by swallowed components. The source non-constancy representation supplies a lower bound, but not the required upper covering or exact law. The dimension3 statement remains unproved here.

[campaign status: literature_result_rederived_with_scope_correction - author-checked proof text; no independent review; the law identity was already in Dhara et al. 2019, so novelty is not claimed] Let the weights theta_i be a Poisson point process of intensity rho(dx) = (tau - 1) c x^{-tau} dx on (0, infinity) with 3 < tau < 4 and c, mu > 0, and given the weights let T_i be independent exponential clocks of rate theta_i/mu. Put S(t) = sum_i theta_i (1{T_i <= t} - theta_i t/mu) with decreasing-weight summation, and let Z = lim_{eps -> 0} [ sum_{theta_i > eps} theta_i^2 - integral_{(eps, infinity)} x^2 rho(dx) ]. CLAIM: L(t) = S(t) + (t/mu) Z has independent, generally NONSTATIONARY increments; it is the compensated integral of marked Poisson points with intensity rho(dx) (x/mu) exp(-x s/mu) ds against the displayed deterministic compensator. THE SCOPE CORRECTION, which is the point: with a DETERMINISTIC drift in place of Z/mu the increments are DEPENDENT - S(mu) and S(2 mu) - S(mu) are dependent, shown by a mixed log-Laplace difference that is positive for small a. So the random drift is not a normalisation convenience; it is what buys independence. FULL CONSTRUCTION AND PROOF: the store already holds this as the lemma math:probability.stochastic:marked-poisson-random-drift-correction-thinned-levy, under a title that names neither the problem nor the campaign; this node is the identity and status record that makes it reachable from the problem.

exponential marks of rate theta_i/mu, conditionally independent given the weights

		\qquad\text{hence}\qquad
		\Bigl|\frac{t}{Np}\Bigr|\le\frac{B}{\delta N}<\tfrac12,
		\quad
		\Bigl|\frac{t}{Nq}\Bigr|<\tfrac12 .
	\]
	Consequently $Np/m$ and $\sqrt{q\,m/(p\,(N-m))}$ are bounded above and below by positive
	constants depending only on $K$ and $H$, and their logarithms have convergent expansions in
	$N^{-1}$ whose coefficients are bounded uniformly on $K\times H$.

[Thm 2 of arXiv:2605.07369, '2605.07369'] {\bf (Moderate deviation principle for weighted sums of  bounded martingale differences)}
Let $\{U_n, \FF_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of \ $\rr$-valued, bounded martingale differences, satisfying the conditions (\ref{sa-2}) and (\ref{sa-6}). Let $(b_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of positive numbers such that $b_n\rightarrow\infty$ and  $\frac{b_n}{\sqrt{n}}\rightarrow0$.
For any constants $b$ and $\alpha_1$ satisfying $b\alpha_1<-1$, and for any $r>0$, we have
\beq
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \frac{1}{b^2_n} \log \pp \left(h_n\left|b\sum_{k=0}^n \frac{1}{k+1}\beta_{k+1}^n\left(b\alpha_1\right)U_{k+1}\right|>r b_n\right)=-\frac{r^2}{2 \sigma^2},
\deq
where $h_n:=\left(b^2\sum_{k=0}^n \left(k+1\right)^{-2} \left(\beta_{k+1}^n(b \alpha_1)\right)^2\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}$ and $\beta_{k}^n\left(b \alpha_1\right):=\prod_{j=k}^n \left(1+\frac{b \alpha_1}{j+1}\right)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let G be an m x n matrix (m >= n) with independent standard Gaussian entries, and let s_max(G) >= s_min(G) denote its largest and smallest singular values (the extreme values of |G x| over unit vectors x in R^n). Then sqrt(m) - sqrt(n) <= E s_min(G) <= E s_max(G) <= sqrt(m) + sqrt(n). Both maps G |-> s_max(G) and G |-> s_min(G) are 1-Lipschitz in the Frobenius (Euclidean) norm, so Gaussian concentration gives, for every t >= 0, P( s_max(G) >= sqrt(m) + sqrt(n) + t ) <= exp(-t^2/2) and P( s_min(G) <= sqrt(m) - sqrt(n) - t ) <= exp(-t^2/2). In words: an m x n Gaussian matrix with m substantially larger than n is a well-conditioned near-isometry, with condition number about (sqrt(m) + sqrt(n)) / (sqrt(m) - sqrt(n)); for square matrices (m = n) the lower bound degenerates to 0 and the smallest singular value is of order n^{-1/2} (a separate theorem). The constants are sharp in the sense that both bounds match the Marchenko-Pastur edges (1 +- sqrt(n/m)) sqrt(m) to first order.
G has independent N(0,1) entries, m >= n
expectations are over the Gaussian matrix; the concentration statements use the 1-Lipschitz property of singular values in the Frobenius norm
the square case m = n is NOT covered by the lower bound (it gives 0); see the smallest-singular-value theorem for square matrices

\end{equation}
Consequently,
\[
\big|\Delta(z_0;\hat \theta,\rho,\mathbb P_1)-\Delta(z_0;\theta^\star,\rho,\mathbb P_1)\big|
\le\delta_{\rm inv}+o_p(1),
\]
and if $\delta_{\rm inv}=0$ then $\big|\Delta(z_0;\hat \theta,\rho,\mathbb P_1)-\Delta(z_0;\theta^\star,\rho,\mathbb P_1)\big|\xrightarrow{p}0$.

body: In statistics, the Neyman–Pearson lemma describes the existence and uniqueness of the likelihood ratio as a uniformly most powerful test in certain contexts. It was introduced by Jerzy Neyman and Egon Pearson in a paper in 1933. The Neyman–Pearson lemma is part of the Neyman–Pearson theory of statistical testing, which introduced concepts such as errors of the second kind, power function, and inductive behavior. The previous Fisherian theory of significance testing postulated only one hypothesis. By introducing a competing hypothesis, the Neyman–Pearsonian flavor of statistical testing allows investigating the two types of errors. The trivial cases where one always rejects or fails to reject the null hypothesis are of little interest but it does prove that one must not relinquish control over one type of error while calibrating the other. Neyman and Pearson accordingly proceeded to restrict their attention to the class of all $\alpha$ level tests while subsequently minimizing type II error, traditionally denoted by $\beta$. Their seminal 1933 paper, which includes the Neyman–Pearson lemma showed not only the existence of tests with the most power that retain a prespecified level of type I error ( $\alpha$), but also provided a way to construct such tests. The Karlin-Rubin theorem extended the Neyman–Pearson lemma to settings involving composite hypotheses with monotone likelihood ratios.

body: Cayley's formula: For every positive integer n, the number of labeled trees on the vertex set {1, 2, ..., n} (that is, trees whose vertices are distinguishable) is n^{n-2}. For example the count is 1 for n = 1 and n = 2, 3 for n = 3, and 16 for n = 4. Equivalently, the number of spanning trees of the complete graph K_n is n^{n-2}.

[Theorem mainthm1 of arXiv:2412.09471, 'On the moderate deviation principles in the sparse multi-type Erd\H{o}s R\'enyi random gra'] Suppose $\Sigma(\kappa, \mu)> 1$, then for any sequence $(a_n)$ such that $n^{1/4}\ll a_n\ll \sqrt{n}$ and $|\mu^n-\mu|=O(\frac{1}n)$, under the conditioning event 
\[
\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{N(Z_n n)}X_i^n=\mu^n n\right\},
\]
the sequence of random vectors
\[
\frac{1}{a_n\sqrt{n}}\left(\max_{1\leq i\leq N(nZ_n)}X_i^n-(\mu-c)n\right),
\]
satisfies the moderate deviation principle in ${\mathbb R}^{d}$ with speed $a_n^2$ and rate function $\mathcal{I}(x)$, where $\mathcal{I}(x)$ is given in Theorem~(thm1 of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Thm 1 of arXiv:2603.27433, 'The $k$-cycle shuffling with repeated cards'] Let $(n_N)_{N\ge 1},(k_N)_{N\ge 1}$, and $(t_N)_{N\ge 1}$ be sequences of positive integers, such that $\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}n_N=\infty$. For all $N\ge 1$, let $t'_N:=t_N-\frac{n_N\log n_N}{k_N}$. Also, let $P_{n_N,k_N}^{*t_N}$ be defined as in \Cref{defi: Pnk and its convolution}, and $\nu_{n_N,k_N}^{t_N}$ be defined as in \Cref{defi: construction of nu}. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item Suppose that 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $k_N\ge 2$ for all $N\ge 1$, and $\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{k_N\log n_N}{n_N}=0$.
\item $t_N'=cn_N/k_N$, where $c\in\R$ is an absolute constant.
\end{enumerate}
Then, we have
$$\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}d_{TV}(P_{n_N,k_N}^{*t_N},\nu_{n_N,k_N}^{t_N})=0.$$ 

\item Suppose that 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $k_N\ge 2$ for all $N\ge 1$, and $\limsup_{N\rightarrow\infty}\log_{n_N}k_N\le c_0$, where $c_0\in[0,1)$ is an absolute constant.
\item $\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\log\log n_N-|2k_Nt_N'/n_N|=+\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
Then, we have
$$\limsup_{N\rightarrow\infty}\log_{n_N}d_{TV}(P_{n_N,k_N}^{*t_N},\nu_{n_N,k_N}^{t_N})\le c_0-1.$$

\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 1 (Radial LRU extremality) of arXiv:2605.26107, 'Radial Extremality for LRU Caching and the Fill--Holst Conjecture'] Let $N\ge2$, let $1\le C<N$, and let $q\in\Delta_N^\circ$ be nonuniform.
Define
\[
        p(\theta)=u+\theta(q-u),\qquad 0\le\theta\le1.
\]
Then
\[
        \frac{\dd}{\dd\theta}H_C(p(\theta))>0,
        \qquad 0<\theta\le1.
\]
Consequently $\theta\mapsto H_C(p(\theta))$ is strictly increasing on
$(0,1]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Method: Sharp comparison of systematic and random Ising updates explicit structural calculation Result: At infinite temperature one deterministic sweep gives an exact independent fair-spin sample. Random scan has mixing time asymptotic to(N/2)*log N. The upper bound follows from Fourier eigenvalues1-|S|/N: chi-square distance is sum_(k>=1) binom(N,k)*(1-k/N)^(2t) <=(1+exp(-2t/N))^N-1. For the lower bound, magnetization from all plus has mean N*(1-1/N)^t and variance at most N, whereas stationary magnetization has variance N. Thus at t=(N/2)*(log N-C) the means are separated by order exp(C/2)*sqrt(N). Check: For distinct spins, E[sigma_i*sigma_j]=(1-2/N)^t <=(1-1/N)^(2t), so their covariance is nonpositive and the variance bound follows. Chebyshev separates the two magnetization laws as C grows. This independently recovers the factor log N between random updates and one sweep. Obstruction: The product case shows why the logarithmic allowance is necessary. Interacting conditional-expectation projections fail to commute, so their product cannot be replaced by the power of their average.

[Prop islandconfigs of arXiv:2604.12963, 'Shocks, instability, and the twenty networks\\ of infinite geodesics in the Directed Lands'] Let $\omega\in\Omega_0$ and $\theta\in\Theta^\omega$. Suppose that $\tau:[s,t]\to\mathbb{R}$ is the right boundary of a stability island, including its tip and bottom points. Then for $r\in[s,t]$, $\tau(r)\in\IG\theta$, and the following are the only possible $\theta$-directed geodesic configurations out of $\tau(r)$.  See the first and last configurations on the second row and the configurations on the third row in Figure (fig:geodesics of the paper).
    
    \begin{enumerate}[label={\rm(\alph*)}, ref={\rm\alph*}] \itemsep=1pt
        \item $r = t$, $\tau(t)$ is the tip of the island and is in $\IGpns\theta$. 
       \item $r=s$, $\tau(s)$ is the bottom of the island and is a snowbird shock. 
        \item $r\in(s,t)$, $\tau(r)$ is a $\theta+$ hugging shock, $\Gamma_{{\tau(r)}}\dir{L}{\theta}{-}\big|_{[r,t]}=\Gamma_{{\tau(r)}}\dir{L}{\theta}{+}\big|_{[r,t]}$,  exactly one of the following happens and each of the three types {\rm(}(prop:islandconfigs.ci of the paper)-(prop:islandconfigs.ciii of the paper){\rm)} occurs at a dense set of times $r\in(s,t)$.
         \vspace{5pt}
              
        \begin{enumerate}[label={{\rm(}(prop:islandconfigs.c of the paper).\rm\roman*)}, ref={(prop:islandconfigs.c of the paper).\rm\roman*}] \itemsep=1pt
            
        \item $\tau(r)\notin{\mathrm{NU}}_1^{\theta-}$ and $\Gamma_{{\tau(r)}}\dir{M}{\theta}{+} = \Gamma_{{\tau(r)}}\dir{R}{\theta}{+}$ {\rm(}i.e.\ no middle $W^{\theta+}$-geodesic{\rm)}.
        \item $\tau(r) \in {\mathrm{NU}}_1^{\theta-}$ and hence $\Gamma_{{\tau(r)}}\dir{L}{\theta}{-}$ and $\Gamma_{{\tau(r)}}\dir{R}{\theta}{-}$ are initially distinct. In this case, both geodesics go strictly left of $\tau$ on $(r,t)$ and coalesce strictly before $t$. Furthermore, $\Gamma_{{\tau(r)}}\dir{M}{\theta}{+}\big|_{[r,t]}=\Gamma_{{\tau(r)}}\dir{R}{\theta}{-}\big|_{[r,t]}$.
       \item $\tau(r)\notin{\mathrm{NU}}_1^{\theta-}$ and $\Gamma_{{\tau(r)}}\dir{M}{\theta}{+}$ is initially distinct from both $\Gamma_{{\tau(r)}}\dir{L}{\theta}{+}$ and $\Gamma_{{\tau(r)}}\dir{R}{\theta}{+}$. In this case, the middle geodesic coalesces with one of these strictly before the other. If it first coalesces with the left geodesic, this occurs strictly after time $t$.
        Moreover, there exists $r_0\in(s,t)$ such that for all $r\in(s,r_0)$ with $\tau(r)$ of type (equation prop:islandconfigs.ciii of the paper), $\Gamma_{{\tau(r)}}\dir{M}{\theta}{+}$ first coalesces with $\Gamma_{{\tau(r)}}\dir{R}{\theta}{+}$. There is a dense subset of $(r_0,t)$ consisting of points $r$ for which $\tau(r)$ is of type (equation prop:islandconfigs.ciii of the paper) and $\Gamma_{{\tau(r)}}\dir{M}{\theta}{+}$ again first coalesces with $\Gamma_{{\tau(r)}}\dir{R}{\theta}{+}$. 
     On the other hand, the set of points $r\in[r_0,t)$ for which $\tau(r)$ is of type (equation prop:islandconfigs.ciii of the paper) and $\Gamma_{{\tau(r)}}\dir{M}{\theta}{+}$ first coalesces with $\Gamma_{{\tau(r)}}\dir{L}{\theta}{+}$ contains $r_0$, consists of isolated points, and accumulates at $t$.
    \end{enumerate}
    \end{enumerate}

    The analogous statements hold upon exchanging left and right and swapping $+$ and $-$. See the fourth row in Figure (fig:geodesics of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop islandconfigs of arXiv:2604.12963

\(S\alpha S\) random measure on \(\Q_p\) with Haar control measure.  The \(p\)-adic linear fractional stable motion is defined as

  X(t)=\int_{\Q_p}

  \qquad t\in\Q_p .
\]

[Lemma lem: DPtobound of arXiv:2604.10446, 'Least singular values of shifted sparse random combinatorial matrices'] Let $1\leq m \leq n$, $\lambda>0$, and $N$ as in ((newN of the paper)). 
      Let $M$ be a nonnegative $m \times n$ matrix with all row and column sums bounded by $N$. Suppose that $M$ has  $DP(\delta, \kappa_1, \kappa_2)$ with $\delta=\lambda N/n$, $\kappa_1>1$, $\kappa_2 \geq 0$. Then for any $x \in \mathbb{S}^{m-1}, y \in \mathbb{S}_{0}^{n-1}$, we have 
      \[
     \left| \sum_{(i,j) \in \mathcal{H}(x,y)}M_{ij}x_iy_j\right| \leq \alpha \sqrt{N},
      \]
      where $\alpha=16+32\lambda (1+\kappa_1)+64 \kappa_2 \left( 1+ \frac{2}{\kappa_1 \log \kappa_1} \right)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem: DPtobound of arXiv:2604.10446

body: A Markov chain on a countable state space S with transition matrix P is reversible with respect to a probability distribution pi on S if the detailed-balance equations hold: pi(x) P(x,y) = pi(y) P(y,x) for every pair of states x, y in S. Detailed balance is sufficient but not necessary for pi to be a stationary distribution of P: summing the detailed-balance equation over x gives sum_x pi(x) P(x,y) = pi(y) sum_x P(y,x) = pi(y). [standard, e.g. Levin and Peres, Markov Chains and Mixing Times]
title: Reversible Markov Chain (Detailed-Balance Condition)

body:
[Theorema 3 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let \(k\) be a perfect field of characteristic \(p>0\).
\begin{enumerate}
\item
Let \(X\) be a smooth quasi-\(F\)-split \(k\)-variety, and let \(D\)
be a simple normal crossings divisor on \(X\).  Then \((X,D)\) is
log HT-split (\Cref{qFs-to-HT}).

\item
Let \(X\) be a smooth \(k\)-variety, and let \(D\)
be a simple normal crossings divisor on \(X\).
Let \((X,D)\) be a log HT-split pair, and let
\[
\pi\colon Y \defeq \operatorname{Bl}_Z(X) \to  X
\]
be the blow-up along a stratum \(Z\) of \(D\) and $D_Y \defeq (\pi^{-1}D)_{\red}$. 
Then \((Y,D_Y)\) is log HT-split.  In particular, \(Y\) is HT-split (\Cref{HT-ascent-stratum-blowup}).

\item
Let \(T\) be a toric variety with Cox ring \(S_T\).  
Suppose that a smooth
closed subvariety \(Z\subseteq T\) is defined by a homogeneous regular sequence.
Then \(Z\) is HT-split (\Cref{complete-intersection}).

\item Let $\pi \colon X \to Y$ be a morphism of smooth $k$-varieties.
If $\cO_Y \to R\pi_*\cO_X$ splits and $X$ is HT-split, then $Y$ is HT-split (\Cref{finite-cover}).
In particular, if $\pi$ is a linearly reductive good quotient and $X$ is HT-split, then $Y$ is HT-split.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorema 3 of arXiv:2609.00567

[Corollary BPTransition of arXiv:2605.16244, 'Analysis of a twisted Bose--Einstein Markov chain with applications to sampling Catalan st'] Let $K_{\mathrm{PF}}$ and $\pi_{\mathrm{PF}}$ be the transition kernel and stationary distribution of the Burnside process on $\mathrm{PF}_n$. Then for all $x,y\in \mathrm{PF}_n$,
\bal
K_{\mathrm{PF}}(x,y) = \frac{n+1}{\prod_{a=1}^n i_a(x)!} \prod_{a,b = 1}^n \left(\frac{1}{n+1}\right)_{(m_{a,b}(x,y))}
\eal
and
\bal
\pi_{\mathrm{PF}}(x) = \frac{\prod_{a=1}^n i_a(x)!}{n! C_n},
\eal
where $C_n$ is the $n$th Catalan number.

[Proposition 22 of arXiv:2604.24684, 'Waning Immunity Fails to Restore a Positive Epidemic Threshold on Power--Law Networks'] Fix $\delta\in(0,1)$ and set
$
\varepsilon:=\frac{\delta}{400\tau^3}.
$
Let $G=G(n,\tau)$ be a power-law random graph on $n$ vertices with exponent $\tau>2$. Then there exists a constant $c>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P\Bigl(
\text{$G$ contains at least $\lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil$ vertex-disjoint $(n^{\varepsilon},n^{\varepsilon})$-hierarchical-stars}
\Bigr)
\ge
1-c(\log n)^{\mathbf{1}\{\tau=3\}}\,n^{-\min\{\tau-2,1\}}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm intro2 of arXiv:2509.08659, 'Gap metrics for stationary point processes and quantitative convexity of the free energy'] Consider $\varphi(x)=|x|^{-s}$ for $s>1$ and the metric space $( X^{a}_{p},\mathscr W_{gap,p})$.
Every $\mathsf{P}\in X^{a}_{p}$ with  $\mathcal F_{\beta}(\mathsf{P})<\infty$    is the starting point of a curve of maximal slope
for $\mathcal F_{\beta}$ with respect to the local slope $\abs{\partial \mathcal F_{\beta}}$, given by  \[
    \abs{\partial \mathcal F_{\beta}}(\mathsf{P}):=\limsup_{X^{a}_{p}\ni \mathsf{P}'\to\mathsf{P}}\frac{(\mathcal F_{\beta}(\mathsf{P})-\mathcal F_{\beta}(\mathsf{P}'))^+}{\mathscr W_{gap,p}( \mathsf{gap}(\mathsf{P}'), \mathsf{gap}(\mathsf{P}))}.
    \] 
    Moreover, such a curve $(\mathsf{P}_t)_{t>0}$ satisfies the energy identity\begin{align}
    \frac{1}{2}\int_0^T\abs{\mathsf{P}'}^2(t)+\frac{1}{2}\int_0^T\abs{\partial \mathcal F_{\beta}}^2(\mathsf{P}(t))dt+\mathcal F_{\beta}(\mathsf{P}(T))=\mathcal F_{\beta}(\mathsf{P}(0)),\quad T>0.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm intro2 of arXiv:2509.08659
