body:
[Definition Singular graph of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] Let \(F_{\tau}(z)\) be a transverse facet relatively carried by \(\tau\) and \(T\) be a ladderpole tube.
We define the \emph{singular graph} \(G_{T}(F_{\tau}(z))\) associated to \(T\) and \(F_{\tau}(z)\) as follows.
The vertices of \(G_{T}(F_{\tau}(z))\) is the set of ladderpole curves \(\mathrm{ld}_{T}\) in \(T\). Two vertices are connected by an edge if they are boundaries of an annular component of \(F_{\tau}(z)\cap T\).

Because the combinatorial positions are not unique, we add parallel components to \(F_{\tau}(z)\) such that the singular graph to every tube is maximal.
We say that the resulting \(F_{\tau}(z)\) is \emph{maximal} with respect to the veering triangulation \(\tau\).

body: For a sign matrix B_n, E_n means that some two distinct rows or some two distinct columns agree up to a global sign. E_n implies singularity by a left or right kernel vector supported on two coordinates. The converse is false; E_n is a specified subset of singularity, not all singularity.

body:
[Proposition 5 of arXiv:2506.15159, 'Conditional central limit theorems for exponential random graphs'] Suppose $W$ and $Y$ are random variables satisfying the above assumptions \eqref{ua1}-\eqref{ua3}. For any $k$ such that $p_k:=\mathbb{P}(Y=k)>0$ and $p_{k-1}=\mathbb{P}(Y=k-1)>0$, we have, using $(W|Y=k)$ to denote a random variable having the conditional distribution of $W$ given $Y=k$,
\begin{align}
 
     d_{\mathcal{W}}((W\mid Y=k),Z)\leq& C(1+r_k)(\mathscr{A}_k+\mathscr{B}_k+\lambda^{-1} \mathscr{C}_k+Q^{-1}(\mathscr{D}_k+\mathscr{E}_k+\mathscr{F}_k)),
\end{align}
 where $d_{\mathcal{W}}$ denotes the Wasserstein distance, $C$ is a universal constant, $Z\sim N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable, $r_k=p_{k-1}/p_k$,
 \begin{align*}
     &\mathscr{A}_k=\IE(|R_{1,+}+R_{1,-}|\mid Y=k);\\ &\mathscr{B}_k=\IE(|R_{2,+}+R_{2,-}|\mid Y=k);\notag\\
      &\mathscr{C}_k=\IE(|\Delta W|^3\mid Y\in\{k-1,k\});\\
     &\mathscr{D}_k=\IE((1+|a_+|+|\IE R_{1,+}|)(|\Delta W|+|R_{0,+}|+|R_{0,-}|)\mid Y\in\{k-1,k\}),\\
     &\t R_{1,+}=R_{1,+}-\IE R_{1,+},\\
     &\mathscr{E}_k=\IE(|\t R_{1,+}\Delta W|+|\Delta (\t R_{1,+})|  \mid Y \in \{k-1,k\})+ \IE(|\t R_{1,+}|(|R_{0,+}|
        + |R_{0,-}|)\mid Y \in \{k-1,k\}),\\
      &\mathscr{F}_k=  \IE(| R_{2,+}\Delta W|+|\Delta ( R_{2,+})|  \mid Y \in \{k-1,k\})
        + \IE(| R_{2,+}|(|R_{0,+}|
        + |R_{0,-}|)\mid Y \in \{k-1,k\}),
 \end{align*}
 and $\Delta$ is the difference operator defined in \cref{Delta def}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 5 of arXiv:2506.15159

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] For the negative hypergeometric law of parameters $(N,m,r)$,
$$M_k=\sum_{\pi\in P(k)}\frac{m!}{(m-|\pi|)!}\cdot\frac{(r+|\pi|-1)!}{(r-1)!}\cdot\frac{(N-m)!}{(N-m+|\pi|)!}$$
where $|.|$ denotes as usual the number of blocks.

[u]^{2}_{H^{s}(\mathbb{S}^{1})}=\eta_{s}\Vert(-\Delta)^{\frac{s}{2}}u\Vert^{2}_{L^{2}},

body:
[Defn rootedtest of arXiv:2608.06500, 'Free energy of Ising models under a spectral condition'] A \emph{rooted test graph} is a connected test graph with a
    distinguished root vertex. If $G=(\text{\boldmath $A$},\text{\boldmath $h$}_1,\ldots,\text{\boldmath $h$}_k)$ is a
    weighted graph on $[N]$ and $X=(\text{\boldmath $W$},\text{\boldmath $d$}_1,\ldots,\text{\boldmath $d$}_k)$ is a
    rooted test graph on $[n]$ with root vertex $1$, then we define
    the \emph{weighted homomorphism density vector} $\text{\boldmath $t$}(X,G)\in\mathbb{R}^N$
    as the vector whose $m$th component is given by

    \begin{align*}
    t_m(X,G) :=\sum_{\substack{f:[n]\rightarrow[N]\\f(1)=m}} \left( \prod_{i\in[n]}
\prod_{\ell=1}^k h_{\ell,f(i)}^{d_{\ell,i}} \right) \left( \prod_{i\le
j\in[n]} a_{f(i)f(j)}^{w_{ij}} \right).
\end{align*}

    A \emph{local vector} 
     is a vector-valued function on weighted
    graphs $G$ that can be expressed as a finite linear combination of
    $\text{\boldmath $t$}(X,G)$ for some rooted test graphs $X$.
title: Defn rootedtest of arXiv:2608.06500

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2603.28226, '2603.28226'] Let $f\ge0$ belong to $L^1(\mathcal F_\infty)$ and let $\lambda>0$. Then one can write
\[
 f=g+h+k
\]
with $g,h,k\in L^1(\mathcal F_\infty)$ such that

\medskip
\noindent\textup{(a)}
\[
\mathbb P\Bigl(\sup_{n\ge1}|\mathbb E_n[g]|>0\Bigr)
\le \frac{\|f\|_1}{\lambda},
\qquad
\|g\|_1\le2\|f\|_1.
\]

\noindent\textup{(b)}
\[
\Bigl\|\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|\mathbb E_n[h]-\mathbb E_{n-1}[h]|\Bigr\|_1
\le2\|f\|_1.
\]
In particular, $\|h\|_1\le2\|f\|_1$.

\noindent\textup{(c)}
\[
0\le k\le \lambda\quad\text{a.s.},
\qquad
\|k\|_1\le \|f\|_1,
\qquad
\|k\|_2^2\le \lambda\|f\|_1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2603.28226

body:
[Lemma 17 (Parameter-retaining fixed-supercritical target bound) of arXiv:2607.13183, '2607.13183'] Fix $a>1$. Let $q=q(a)$ be the extinction probability of a $\Poi(a)$
Galton--Watson process, and put
\[
        \rho:=1-q,
        \qquad \mu:=aq,
        \qquad \delta:=1-\mu,
        \qquad \Lambda_0:=a-\mu=a\rho .
\]
Since $q=e^{-a(1-q)}$, we have
$\mu e^{-\mu}=ae^{-a}$ and $\mu\in(0,1)$. Thus this definition of $\mu$
agrees with the conjugate-parameter definition in
\eqref{eq:mu-conjugate}, with $a$ in place of $1+\eps$.

Let $H^{(a)}$ be the strictly supercritical contiguous model of
Ding--Lubetzky--Peres \cite[Theorem~1]{dlp-strict}. More precisely, first
sample
\[
        \widehat\Lambda_n\sim\mathcal N(\Lambda_0,1/n).
\]
On the event $\{\widehat\Lambda_n\le0\}$, define the output to be a fixed
two-vertex graph with one edge. Otherwise take independent
$D_u\sim\Poi(\widehat\Lambda_n)$ for $u\in[n]$, retain the vertices with
$D_u\ge3$, condition their total degree to be even, and pair their half-edges
uniformly to obtain the kernel. Replace its edges by independent geometric
paths with success parameter $\delta$, and attach independent $\PGW(\mu)$
trees to the core vertices.

There is an absolute constant $C_{\rm par}<\infty$ such that, for every fixed
$a>1$ and every $\eta>0$, there exists $n_0=n_0(a,\eta)$ for which, whenever
$n\ge n_0$,
\begin{equation}
 \Pbb\left(
 \sum_{u,v\in V(H^{(a)})}\pi(u)\pi(v)\Reff^{H^{(a)}}(u,v)
 \le \frac{C_{\rm par}}{\Lambda_0},
 \quad
 |E(H^{(a)})|\le C_{\rm par}\Lambda_0 n
 \right)\ge1-\eta .
\end{equation}
Consequently, on the same event,
$\Kemeny(H^{(a)})\le C_{\rm par}^2n$. In particular, the constant is uniform
in $a$, although the threshold $n_0(a,\eta)$ need not be.

Fix p in (0,1] and a probability law mu on R that is symmetric about zero, has mean zero and variance one, has finite moments of every order, and has no atoms anywhere. Write mu_4 for its fourth moment. For positive layer widths n_0,...,n_d, let W^(i) be n_i by n_(i-1) matrices with iid mu entries, let D^(i) be diagonal n_i by n_i matrices with iid Bernoulli(p) diagonal entries, and assume all these random objects are mutually independent. Put X^(i)=(p n_(i-1))^(-1/2) D^(i) W^(i), M=X^(d)...X^(1). For a deterministic unit vector u in R^n_0 define Z=(n_0/n_d)||Mu||_2^2, S_2=sum_(i=1)^d n_i^(-2), and beta=(3/p-1)sum_(i=1)^d n_i^(-1)+(mu_4-3)||u||_4^4/(p n_1). For beta in a fixed compact interval [b,B] contained in (0,infinity), the Kolmogorov distance between log Z and a normal law of mean -beta/2 and variance beta is O(S_2^(1/5)); for a possible Z=0 interpret log Z=-infinity and compare distribution functions at finite real arguments. The implicit constant may depend on mu,p,b,B, and is uniform over the widths, depth and unit vector. Moreover, for every fixed integer k>=0 with k(k-1)/2 < min_(1<=i<=d)n_i, E[Z^k]=exp(k(k-1)beta/2+O(S_2)), with an error constant depending on k,p and the moments of mu. In particular, if beta tends to beta_* in (0,infinity) and S_2 tends to zero, log Z converges in distribution to N(-beta_*/2,beta_*), and Z converges to the corresponding lognormal law. The distributional assertion is a separate quantitative CLT; it is not deduced from convergence of lognormal moments.
All W entries iid from a symmetric atomless mean-zero unit-variance law with all moments finite
All matrices and Bernoulli gates mutually independent; p fixed in (0,1]
u deterministic with Euclidean norm one; X^(i) normalized by (p n_(i-1))^(-1/2)
CLT bound: beta in a fixed compact subset of (0,infinity)
Moment statement: k fixed nonnegative integer and k(k-1)/2<min_i n_i

[Defn 1 of arXiv:2608.13976, 'Boundary Harnack principle for diffusion with jumps on metric measure spaces'] \rm
Suppose $U$ is an open subset of $\sX.$ A real-valued function $u$ defined on $\sX$ is said to be
\begin{itemize}
\item[\rm (i)]
 {\it  harmonic in   $U$ with respect to $X$}
if for every open set $B$  whose closure is a compact subset of $U,$
   $\E_x |u(X_{\tau_B})|<\infty$ and
 $u(x)=\E_x u(X_{\tau_B})$ for  each  $x\in B.$
  In particular, we say $u$  is   regular harmonic in   $U$ with respect to $X$
if    $\E_x |u(X_{\tau_U})|<\infty$ and
$u(x)=\E_x u(X_{\tau_U})$  for each  $x\in U.$

\item[\rm (ii)]
 {\it $\alpha$-excessive with respect to $X^U$ with $\alpha\geq 0$}
if $u$ is non-negative,
$ u(x)\geq e^{-\alpha t}\E_x u(X^U_t)$ and $u(x)=\lim_{t\downarrow 0} e^{-\alpha t}\E_x  \left[ u(X^U_t)\right]$
 for every $t>0$ and   $x\in U.$
 If $\alpha=0,$ we say $u$ is an excessive function with respect to $X^U.$

\end{itemize}

body: In mathematics, Itô's lemma or Itô's formula is an identity used in Itô calculus to find the differential of a time-dependent function of a stochastic process. It serves as the stochastic calculus counterpart of the chain rule. It can be heuristically derived by forming the Taylor series expansion of the function up to its second derivatives and retaining terms up to first order in the time increment and second order in the Wiener process increment. The lemma is widely employed in mathematical finance, and its best known application is in the derivation of the Black–Scholes equation for option values.
title: Itô's lemma

[Lem many_to_two of arXiv:2506.10623, 'Polynomial slowdown in an angle-dependent 2d branching Brownian motion'] [Many-to-two] 
	Let $t \geq s_0 \geq 0$ and $f,g \colon \mathcal{C}([s_0,t],\mathbb{R}^2) \to [0,\infty)$ be measurable functionals. Then, for any $x,y \in \mathbb{R}^2$,
	\begin{align}
	    &\mathbb{E}_{(s_0,x,y)} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft[ \sum_{u,v \in \mathcal{N}(t), u \neq v} f\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft((X_u(s),Y_u(s))_{s\in [s_0,t]} \aftergroup\egroup\originalright) g\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft((X_v(s),Y_v(s))_{s\in [s_0,t]} \aftergroup\egroup\originalright)\aftergroup\egroup\originalright] \nonumber \\ 
	    &= \int_{s_0}^t \mathbb{E}_{(s_0,x,y)} \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft[ f\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft((\xi^1_s)_{s\in [s_0,t]} \aftergroup\egroup\originalright) g\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft((\xi^{2,r}_s)_{s\in [s_0,t]} \aftergroup\egroup\originalright)
	    b(\xi_r^1)

body: In mathematics, especially group theory, two elements $a$ and $b$ of a group are conjugate if there is an element $g$ in the group such that $b=gag^{-1}.$ This is an equivalence relation whose equivalence classes are called conjugacy classes. In other words, each conjugacy class is closed under the maps $a\mapsto gag^{-1},$ with $g$ an element of the group.

body:
Let X be a Banach space with dual X*. The duality set of x ∈ X is J(x) = {x* ∈ X* : ⟨x, x*⟩ = ‖x‖² = ‖x*‖²}, which is nonempty by the Hahn-Banach theorem. A linear operator A: D(A) ⊂ X → X is dissipative if for every x ∈ D(A) there exists some j ∈ J(x) with Re⟨Ax, j⟩ ≤ 0. Equivalently (Lumer-Phillips lemma), ‖(λ − A)x‖ ≥ λ‖x‖ for all λ > 0 and all x ∈ D(A). In a Hilbert space (J(x) = {x}) this reads Re⟨Ax, x⟩ ≤ 0 for all x ∈ D(A). A is m-dissipative (maximal dissipative) if it is dissipative and Ran(λ − A) = X for some λ > 0 (then for every λ > 0). A is accretive (m-accretive) if −A is dissipative (m-dissipative). For a dissipative A, λ − A is injective for λ > 0 and its inverse on Ran(λ − A) has norm at most 1/λ.
X is a real or complex Banach space
A is linear on a subspace D(A)
title: Dissipative Operator

[Proposition 107 (Pure-power tensor law and faithful transfer) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] If $T$ is positive compact and
$s_N(T)\sim cN^{-\alpha}$, then for every $k\ge1$,
\begin{equation}
 N_{T^{\otimes k}}(u)
 \sim\frac{c^{k/\alpha}}{(k-1)!\alpha^{k-1}}
 u^{-1/\alpha}(\log(1/u))^{k-1}.
 
\end{equation}
If a selected coefficient sector has a separately established positive
counting density inside $T^{\otimes k}$, and a registered operator $R_k(T)$ is
asymptotically faithful to that sector after a fixed threshold rescaling, then
the same counting, Mellin, and Fredholm laws transfer with the induced
constant.  Neither the sector density nor analytic faithfulness follows from
algebraic homogeneity alone.
title: Pure-power tensor law and faithful transfer

[Corollary 10 of arXiv:2607.20646, 'The Independence-Preserving Property and Planar Web Geometry'] Let $(\mu_X,\mu_Y,\mu_U,\mu_V)$ be probability measures on $(0, \infty)$ having positive continuous density.
Then $\HIIp|_{(0,\infty)^2}$ preserves their independence if and only if there exist $p,q,r\in\R$ with $p,q,r>0$ such that
\begin{alignat*}{2}
    \mu_X(\dd x)
        &\propto (e^{-\alpha x})^p x^q (1+x)^{-r} \dd x/x
        & &\propto x^{q-1}(1+x)^{-r}e^{-p\alpha x}\,\dd x,\\
    \mu_Y(\dd y)
        &\propto (e^{-\beta y})^p (1+y)^{-q} y^r \dd y/y
        & &\propto y^{r-1}(1+y)^{-q}e^{-p\beta y}\,\dd y,\\
    \mu_U(\dd u)
        &\propto (e^{-\alpha u})^p (1+u)^{-q} u^r \dd u/u
        & &\propto u^{r-1}(1+u)^{-q}e^{-p\alpha u}\,\dd u,\\
    \mu_V(\dd v)
        &\propto (e^{-\beta v})^p v^q (1+v)^{-r} \dd v/v
        & &\propto v^{q-1}(1+v)^{-r}e^{-p\beta v}\,\dd v.
\end{alignat*}

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2608.11071, 'Scaling Laws for Majority-based Opinion Dynamics in the Presence of Stubborn Agents'] For each $\kappa_1,\kappa_2,\alpha, n>0$, there exists a non-negative function $\psi\in C^3[-n^{1/3}\kappa_1,n^{1/3}\kappa_2]$ such that the following properties hold:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The function $\psi$ solves the ODE (Stein's equation)
    \begin{equation}
        \psi''(z)+\alpha z^2 \psi'(z)=-1,
        
    \end{equation}
    with boundary conditions $\psi'(-n^{1/3}\kappa_1)=\psi(n^{1/3}\kappa_2)=0$.
     \item We have $\psi'(z)\leq 0$ for all $z\in [-n^{1/3}\kappa_1, n^{1/3}\kappa_2]$ and $\sup_{z\in [-n^{1/3}\kappa_1,n^{1/3}\kappa_2]}|\psi'(z)|<C_6$ for some positive constant $C_6$ independent of $n$.
    \item We have $\sup_{z\in [-n^{1/3}\kappa_1, n^{1/3}\kappa_2]}\psi(z)<C_7$ for some positive constant $C_7$ independent of $n$.
    \item  For all sufficiently large $n$ we have $\sup_{z\in [-n^{1/3}\kappa_1, n^{1/3}\kappa_2]}|\psi'''(z)|=n^{2/3}\alpha\kappa_1^2$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.24552, 'Asymptotic Rounding Laws for Optimal Thresholds in Secretary Problems'] Consider a family of single-threshold problems $\{ \mathcal F_n\}_{n \geq 1}$
where each \(\mathcal F_n\) has payoff function \(V_n\). Assume that, for each
\(n\), the finite sequence
$\{V_n(r)\}_{r=0}^{n}$
is unimodal. Suppose that there exists a sequence \(\{k_n\}_{n\geq1}\) of positive constants such that the rescaled increments 
\[
D_n(r)=k_n\Delta_n(r)
\]
satisfy the following uniform local asymptotic expansion: there exist constants \(A<0\), \( c, \ell \in(0,1)\), such that, 
\begin{equation}
\varepsilon_n
:=
\sup_{\substack{|u|<2\\ \ell n+u\in I_n^*}}
\left|
D_n(\ell n+u)-A(u-c)
\right|
\longrightarrow0
\qquad\text{as }n\to\infty.
\end{equation}

Let \((p_j,q_j)_{j\geq1}\) be a sequence of integer pairs such that \[ q_j\longrightarrow\infty, \qquad p_j-\ell q_j\longrightarrow0. \] 

Then \(p_j\) is the unique optimal threshold for \(\mathcal F_{q_j}\) for all sufficiently large \(j\).

[Lemma lem:percolation of arXiv:2607.08914, 'Linear spreading speed in non-monotone population models'] There exist constants  $\tilde C < \infty$, $\tilde \gamma>0$
  and $\tilde v > 0$ such that
  \begin{enumerate}[ref=\alph*]
    \item 
    $\mathbb{P}(\tilde \tau_\mathrm{ext}^A < \infty)
    \le (1-p_\nu)\wedge\tilde Ce^{-\tilde\gamma\abs A}$
    for every $A \subseteq \mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{space}}$, $A\neq \emptyset$;

    \item 
    $ \mathbb{P}(t< \tilde \tau_\mathrm{ext}^0 <\infty) \le \tilde Ce^{-\tilde \gamma t}$ for
    every $t \in \mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{time}}$;

    \item 
    $\mathbb{P}(\tilde \tau_\mathrm{hit}^0(z)>t, \tilde \tau_\mathrm{ext}^0=\infty) \le \tilde
    Ce^{-\tilde \gamma t}$ for every $(z,t) \in \mathbb{L}$ with
    $z \in B_{\tilde v t/T_\mathrm{bl}}^\mathrm{bl}(0)$;

    \item
    there is a coupling of $\tilde Z^\nu $ and $\tilde Z^0$ so that
    $\mathbb{P}(z \notin \tilde K_t^0, \tilde \tau_\mathrm{ext}^0=\infty) \le \tilde
    Ce^{-\tilde \gamma t}$
    for every $(z,t) \in \mathbb{L}$ with $z \in B_{\tilde v t/T_\mathrm{bl}}^\mathrm{bl}(0)$;

    \item
    letting
    $\tilde S_r^\nu(z,t) \coloneq \sum_{z' \in B_r^\mathrm{bl}(z)} \tilde Z_t^\nu(z')$,
    there exists $r_0>0$ such that
    \begin{equation*}
      \mathbb{P} \big( \tilde S_r^\nu(z,t) < p_\nu  V_r/2 \big)
      \le \tilde Ce^{-\tilde \gamma r} \quad
      \text{for every } r \ge r_0 \text{ and } (z,t) \in \mathbb{L};
    \end{equation*}

    \item
    for every $V=\{(z_i,t_i):i=1,\dots,k\}\subset \mathbb L$ with
    $0\le t_1<\dots < t_k$,
    \begin{equation*}
      \mathbb P(\tilde Z_{t}^\nu(z) = 0 \text{ for all } (z,t)\in V)
      \le (1-p_\nu)\wedge \tilde C e^{-\tilde \gamma k}.
    \end{equation*}
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Assume that, for each $t>0$, the operator $KS(t)Q^{1/2}$ takes values in $\Dom(Q^{-1/2})$ and that, for every $T>0$,
\begin{equation}
        \int_0^T\big\|Q^{-1/2}KS(t)Q^{1/2}\big\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2\,dt<\infty .
\end{equation}
Then the Gaussian Ornstein--Uhlenbeck laws satisfy
\[
        \mathcal{L}(Y_A(W))\sim\mathcal{L}(Y_{\widetilde A}(W))
        \quad\hbox{on }D_{H,T}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Definition of arXiv:2609.03755, 'The Scramble Number of Outerplanar Graphs'] A set of vertices is \emph{independent} if no two vertices share an edge with each other. The \emph{independence number} of a graph, $\alpha(G)$, is the size of the largest possible independent set in $G$.

[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2512.04807, 'Existence and uniqueness of the canonical Brownian motion in non-simple conformal loop ens'] Let $(\vertexset,w)$ be a weighted graph, let $x_0,y_0 \in \vertexset$ two distinct vertices, and let
 \[
  w'(x,y) =
  \begin{cases}
   w(x,y) ,& (x,y) \neq (x_0,y_0) ,\\
   \infty ,& (x,y) = (x_0,y_0) .
  \end{cases}
 \]
 (In other words, we consider the weighted graph $(\vertexset',w')$ obtained from $(\vertexset,w)$ by contracting $(x_0,y_0)$ to a single vertex.)
 Let $R$ (resp.\ $R'$) the effective resistance associated with $w$ (resp.\ $w'$).
 Then
 \[ R(x,y) \le R'(x,y)+\frac{1}{w(x_0,y_0)} \quad\text{for each } x,y \in \vertexset . \]
title: Lemma 19 of arXiv:2512.04807

[Lemma 18 (Explicit flat zero-diagonal endpoint) of arXiv:2608.07820, 'Linear Spectral Statistics for Entrywise-Transformed Spiked Wigner Matrices under Shifted '] Let
\(
 S_N^0=N^{-1}(\one\one^{\mathsf T}-I)
\)
and \(\sigma_N=1-N^{-1}\).  Let \(m_N^0(z)\) be the scalar Dyson solution
\begin{equation}
 -\frac{1}{m_N^0(z)}=z+\sigma_Nm_N^0(z),
 \qquad m_N^0(z)\sim-z^{-1}.
\end{equation}
Uniformly for \(z,w\in\Gamma\),
\begin{align}
 N\bigl(m_N^0(z)-m(z)\bigr)
 &\longrightarrow-\frac{m(z)^3}{1-m(z)^2},
 \\
 \Tr\!\left[(S_N^0)^2(I-m(z)^2S_N^0)^{-1}\right]
 &\longrightarrow\frac{1}{1-m(z)^2},
 \\
 \Tr\!\left[S_N^0(I-m(z)m(w)S_N^0)^{-2}\right]
 &\longrightarrow
 \frac{1}{(1-m(z)m(w))^2}-1.
 
\end{align}
Consequently, if the summed fourth cumulants converge to \(\kappa\), the
Li--Xu bias together with the finite-flat Dyson correction converges to
\(m_{\varphi,\Gamma}^{\rm base}(\kappa)\) in
\eqref{eq:base-mean-definition}, and the covariance kernel converges to
\(\mathcal K_{\rm Wig}^{(\kappa,0)}\) in
\eqref{eq:Wigner-kernel}.
title: Explicit flat zero-diagonal endpoint

Fix integers $m\geq3$ and $1\leq d<m-1$, and fix $\lambda>0$.  Determine
\[
  \max\left\{
    \mathbb E\exp\!\left(\lambda\max_{1\leq i\leq m}\xi_i\right):
    \xi\sim\mathcal N(0,G),\ G\text{ a correlation matrix},\ \rank G\leq d
  \right\},
\]
and characterize all maximizing covariance matrices.  In particular, determine
whether the maximizing configuration depends on $\lambda$. (Stated as a problem by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: The rank-constrained Gaussian maximum

body:
[Definition 54 of arXiv:2604.03777, 'Equilibrium fluctuations for a multi-species particle system with long jumps'] Let $\mathcal{Z} \in C (\mathbb{R}_+ ; \mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}))$ be a
  stochastic process and assume it is incompressible, i.e. $\sup_{t \leqslant
  T} | \mathbb{E} [F (\mathcal{Z}_t)] | \lesssim_T \| F \|_{L^2 (\mu)}$ for
  all $T > 0$ and $F \in \mathcal{C}$. We say that $\mathcal{Z}$ is a solution to the
  {\textit{martingale problem associated to $(\mathcal{L},\mathcal{D}_{\max} (\mathcal{L}))$ }} if, for all
  $F \in \mathcal{D}_{\max} (\mathcal{L})$, the process 
  \[ F (\mathcal{Z}_t) - F (\mathcal{Z}_0) - \int_0^t \mathcal{L} F
     (\mathcal{Z}_s) \; \dd s, \qquad t \geqslant 0, \]
  is a martingale w.r.t. the filtration generated by $\mathcal{Z}$.
title: Definition 54 of arXiv:2604.03777

Let K>=1 be an integer, let a,b,c>0, and let d_2,...,d_(K+1) be real numbers such that for every k=1,...,K, d_(k+1)<=a/k+b(1+log k)+c sum_(ell=2)^k d_ell/(k-ell+2), with the empty sum zero. Then for every such k, d_(k+1)<=[a/k+b(1+log k)] sum_(i=0)^(k-1)[2c(1+log k)]^i. In particular, if 2c(1+log K)<=1/2, the right-hand geometric factor is at most two for every k<=K. Source: Liu--Zhou Lemma E.2. The finite comparison also extends to zero coefficients by a positive perturbation and a limit.
K is a positive integer
a,b,c are positive constants
The displayed scalar recurrence holds for every k=1,...,K; no sign condition on d is needed

body:
[Theorem 41 (Qualitative and quantitative response consequences) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let $\mathcal R$ be a filtered response.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item Full support in every order is equivalent to strictness.  It gives
      valuation exchange and the flag reconstruction formula
      \eqref{rk:eq-flag-reconstruction}.
\item Coefficient-pure full support gives, for every nonzero probe of top
      depth $r$, at least one labelled native coordinate with a nonzero exact
      critical $r$-packet.  Its singular, Mellin, and Fredholm laws are those
      of \Cref{cc:thm-critical-packet-principle}.
\item Window-pure full support gives the corresponding family-valued
      finite-window lower profile.  It preserves the valuation but does not
      assert one full-tail extremizing realization.
\end{enumerate}
Full support alone need not imply a regularly varying equivalent: it records
nonvanishing in the analytic quotient, while coefficient-purity identifies a
specific critical boundary line.

Let X_0 have any probability law on R^d with finite second moment. Let X_u=e^{-u}X_0+sqrt(1-e^{-2u})G, where G is an independent N(0,I_d), and denote its density for u>0 by q_u. Fix T>0 and let the exact reverse diffusion satisfy Y_0~q_T and dY_t=(Y_t+2 grad log q_{T-t}(Y_t))dt+sqrt(2)dB_t for 0<=t<T, so Y_t~q_{T-t}. Set S_t=grad log q_{T-t}(Y_t) and H_t=Hess log q_{T-t}(Y_t). Then dS_t=-S_t dt+sqrt(2)H_t dB_t. In particular M_t=e^t S_t is a square-integrable martingale on every closed interval [0,T-delta] with delta>0, and E||M_t-M_s||_2^2=2 integral_s^t e^{2r} E||H_r||_F^2 dr for 0<=s<=t<T. The Gaussian smoothing and the finite-second-moment estimates in Lemma 6 ensure that this integral is finite on each such interval.

For n>=2 and any nonnegative q_v summing to one on each of the n antidiagonals of the n-vertex up/right path triangle, define B_n(t)=sum_v q_v^(1+tanh(t/2)) and J_n=int_0^infinity e^(-t)B_n(t)dt. Then J_n>=(n-1)/log n, and B_n(n^(-alpha))/n tends to one for each fixed alpha>0. Consequently this direct unweighted one-site hypercontractive upper certificate cannot establish an O(n^(1-epsilon)) variance bound for fixed epsilon>0. The result is no lower bound on actual path overlap or variance.

[Lemma cond indep of arXiv:2608.29390, 'The Test and Find Model'] 1. For any $\gamma\in\Gamma$ and $s\in\Sigma$, we have
$$
P(S=s|T=\gamma) = \prod_{i=1}^n P(S_i=s_i|T_i=\gamma_i).
$$
2. Fix $s\in\Sigma$ and $\gamma_i\in\{0,1\}$ and let $S_{-i}$ and $s_{-i}$ denote, respectively, the vectors $S$ and $s$ with the $i$th coordinate removed. We have
$$
P(S_{-i}=s_{-i}, S_i=s_i|T_i=\gamma_i) = P(S_{-i}=s_{-i}|T_i=\gamma_i) P(S_i=s_i|T_i=\gamma_i).
$$

[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2608.13687, 'Multiplicative chaos from random multiplicative functions'] Fix a compact interval $\cI\subset \R$ and $f\in\mathbf{M}$ satisfying \eqref{eq:TwistCondition}. As  $\min(N,1/\ep)\to\infty$, the random field 
$E_{N,\ep}^{(1)}(x) \coloneq |D_N(\alpha f, \frac12 + \ep + ix)|^2/\exp(2\Re S_{N,\ep}(x))$ converges almost surely to a continuous, nonnegative random function $E^{(1)}$, uniformly over  $x\in \mathcal{I}$. 
The zero set of $E^{(1)}$ is equal to the zero set of $D_{N_0}(\alpha f, \frac12+ix)$, 
where $N_0\in\N$ is a deterministic constant depending only on $f$. Moreover, for all $\lambda>0$, we have 
    \[
     \mathbb{E}\Big[\sup_{N, \ep \ge 0}\|E_{N,\ep}^{(1)}\|_{L^\infty(\cI)}^\lambda\Big]<\infty\,.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 3 (Concentration) of arXiv:2604.05234, 'Quantitative propagation of chaos and universality for asymmetric Langevin spin glass dyna'] Let $v\subseteq \{1,\dots,N\}$ with $|v|=k$. The following hold:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item There exist constants $C,\theta \in (0, \infty)$ such that for every function $f:\mC_T^k\to \R$ that is $1$-Lipschitz with respect to the supremum norm,
\[\bbE\bigg[\exp\bigg(\frac{\theta N}{k}\bigg|\int_{\mC^k_T}f(x)\,d\big(P^{N,v}_{[T]}(\bfJ)-\bbE\big[P^{N,v}_{[T]}(\bfJ)\big]\big)(x)
\bigg|^2\bigg)\bigg]\leq C.\]
\item There exists a constant $C \in (0, \infty)$ such that 
\[\bbE\Big[\bbW_1\Big(P_{t}^{N,v}(\bfJ), \bbE\big[P_{t}^{N,v}(\bfJ)\big]\Big)\Big] \leq \left \{ \begin{aligned}
    & \frac{C}{\sqrt N}, &\quad & k =1,\\
    & \frac{C\log N}{\sqrt N}, &\quad & k =2, \\
    &  \frac{Ck}{N^{1/k}}
    , &\quad &k \geq 3.
\end{aligned} \right. \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 25 of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] Let \(\sigma,\tau\in L^\infty(\mathbb R)\). Assume that
\(\check\sigma,\check\tau\in L^1(\mathbb R)\) and
\[
\int_0^\infty x\left(
|\check\sigma(x)|^2+|\check\sigma(-x)|^2
+|\check\tau(x)|^2+|\check\tau(-x)|^2
\right)\,\mathrm dx<\infty .
\]
Then, for every \(L>0\), \(W_L(\sigma\tau)-W_L(\sigma)W_L(\tau)\) is trace
class on \(L^2(0,L)\), and
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|W_L(\sigma\tau)-W_L(\sigma)W_L(\tau)\|_1
&\le
\left(\int_0^\infty x|\check\sigma(x)|^2\,\mathrm dx\right)^{1/2}
\left(\int_0^\infty x|\check\tau(-x)|^2\,\mathrm dx\right)^{1/2} \\
&\quad+
\left(\int_0^\infty x|\check\sigma(-x)|^2\,\mathrm dx\right)^{1/2}
\left(\int_0^\infty x|\check\tau(x)|^2\,\mathrm dx\right)^{1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\]

body:
[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2608.30138, 'High-frequency wave propagation for the viscoelastic wave equation with singular memory'] There exists $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that, for every $0\le \varepsilon\le \varepsilon_0$,
the eikonal equation \r{eik2} 
admits a solution $\psi\in C^\infty(B(0,R_T))$, which also depends smoothly on $\varepsilon \in [0,\varepsilon_0]$ and on $\omega$. Consequently, $\psi$ admits a Taylor expansion in $\varepsilon$,
\[
\psi(x,\eps)
\sim \sum_{j\ge0}\varepsilon^j\psi_j(x)
\qquad \text{in } C^\infty(B(0,R_T)),
\]
with
\[
\psi_0(x)=x\cdot\omega,
\qquad
\psi_j(x)=\frac1{j!}\,\partial_\varepsilon^j\psi(x,\eps)\big|_{\varepsilon=0},
\]
and the coefficients satisfy
\begin{equation}
2\,\omega\cdot\nabla \psi_j
=
(-1)^j\sigma_{\mathfrak{m}}^j
-
\sum_{\ell=1}^{j-1}\nabla\psi_\ell\cdot\nabla\psi_{j-\ell},
\qquad j\ge1,
\end{equation}
together with
\[
\psi_j(x)=0
\qquad \text{for } x\in B(0,R_T),\quad x\cdot\omega<-R.
\]

body:
[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2609.03946, 'The groups $\SL_2(\F_{13})$ and $\SL_2(\F_{19})$ are Galois over $\Q$'] Let $\ell\in\{13,19\}$. For $\ell=13$, let $f_\ell\in\Z[x]$ be the degree $14$ polynomial displayed in Example~\textup{\ref{ex:f13}}, and for $\ell=19$, let $f_\ell\in\Z[x]$ be the degree $20$ polynomial in
Appendix~\textup{\ref{app:f19}}.  Then $f_\ell$ is irreducible,
all $\ell+1$ of its roots are real, and its splitting field $L_\ell$
satisfies
\[
 \Gal(L_\ell/\Q)\cong\PSL_2(\F_\ell).
\]
This isomorphism carries the action on the roots of $f_\ell$ to the action of
$\PSL_2(\F_\ell)$ on $\PP^1(\F_\ell)$.  Moreover, for every odd rational prime $q$
whose ramification index $e(q)$ in $L_\ell$ is even, the residue degree
$f(q)$ satisfies
\[
 f(q)\ \text{is odd}
 \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
 q\equiv1\pmod4 .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2609.03946

body: [Defn ribbon of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Given a foliation $\mathcal{F}$ on $M$, a \textbf{ribbon} is a smoothly embedded strip $R =  [-T, T] \times [0,\varepsilon] \subset M$ transverse to $\mathcal{F}$ such that the arcs $\{\pm T\} \times [0,\varepsilon]$ lie on $\partial M$, $(-T,T)\times [0,\varepsilon]$ lies in $\interior M$, and the induced foliation $\mathcal{F}|_R$ is topologically isotopic rel.~boundary to the standard foliation by lines $[0,T]\times \{y\}$, $y\in [0,\varepsilon]$. We use parameters $T$ and $\varepsilon$ for the width and height to emphasize that ribbons are usually short and long.
title: Defn ribbon of arXiv:2608.30031

body:
[Corollary Point-incoherent frames of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[corollary]{cor:point-incoherent}
Let \(\overline\sigma_{N-1}\) denote normalized surface measure on
\(\mathbb S^{N-1}(1)\), and define
\[
 D_{N,L}=\left\{x\in\mathbb S^{N-1}(1):
 \left\lVertx\right\rVert_\infty\le L\sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}\right\},
 \qquad
 \widehat\mathcal O_{N,L}
 =\{(v_1,\ldots,v_n,x)\in\mathbb O(N):x\in D_{N,L}\}.
\]
Let \(\widehat\mathcal Z_{N,L}^J\) be defined by replacing \(\mathcal O_{N,L}\) with
\(\widehat\mathcal O_{N,L}\) in (equation eq:Z-def of the paper).  Every conclusion of
(thm:bulk-universality of the paper) remains valid for
\(\widehat\mathcal Z_{N,L}^J\), with the same quantitative bound.  For Gaussian
disorder, (equation eq:Gaussian-Z-exact of the paper) remains valid with
\(\nu_N(\mathcal O_{N,L})\) replaced by
\(\overline\sigma_{N-1}(D_{N,L})\).  In particular, for \(L>L_0\) the
set \(D_{N,L}\) has spherical measure tending to one, while for every
fixed \(L>0\) the Gaussian variational pressure limit is unchanged.

[Theorem T:general V of arXiv:2411.01364, 'Global Dynamics of Granular Media Equations via Stochastic Order'] Suppose Assumption (asp:potential of the paper) holds, and $V'$  has finite zeros and they are all simple. Then there exist $\theta_0>0, \ \sigma_0>0$  such that for all $\theta\geq \theta_0$ and $\overline{\sigma}\leq \sigma_0$,
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
\item \textnormal{(Total Orderedness)} there are exactly $(2n-1)$ invariant measures $\{\nu_k\}_{k=1}^{2n-1}$ with $\nu_1<_{\mathrm{st}}\nu_2<_{\mathrm{st}}\cdots<_{\mathrm{st}}\nu_{2n-1}$ for some integer $n\geq 1$;
\item \textnormal{(Connecting Orbits)} for all $k=1,2,\dots,n-1$, there are a decreasing connecting orbit $\{\nu^{k,\downarrow}_t\}_{t\in \mathbb R}$ from $\nu_{2k}$ to $\nu_{2k-1}$ and an increasing connecting orbit $\{\nu^{k,\uparrow}_t\}_{t\in \mathbb R}$ from $\nu_{2k}$ to $\nu_{2k+1}$;
\item \textnormal{(Locally Attracting)} there exist $r>0$ and $a_1<\cdots<a_k$ such that for all $1\leq k\leq n$, $\nu_{2k-1}\in B(\delta_{a_k},r)$  and
\[
\mathcal W_2(P_t^*B(\delta_{a_k},r),\nu_{2k-1})=\sup_{\mu\in B(\delta_{a_k},r)}\mathcal W_2(P_t^*\mu,\nu_{2k-1})\to0\text{ as }t\to\8;
\]
\item \textnormal{(Attracting Unbounded Open Neighbourhoods)}
if $\mu\leq_{\mathrm{st}}\nu$ for some $\nu\in B(\delta_{a_1},r)$, then
\[
\mathcal W_2(P_t^*\mu,\nu_1)\to0\text{ as }t\to\8.
\]
If $\mu\geq_{\mathrm{st}}\nu$ for some $\nu\in B(\delta_{a_n},r)$, then
\[
\mathcal W_2(P_t^*\mu,\nu_{2n-1})\to0\text{ as }t\to\8.
\]
In particular,
\[
\mathcal W_2(P_t^*\mu,\nu_1)\to0\text{ as }t\to\8\ \text{ for all $\mu\in\bigcup_{a\leq0}B(\delta_{a_1+a},r)$},
\]
\[
\mathcal W_2(P_t^*\mu,\nu_{2n-1})\to0\text{ as }t\to\8\ \text{ for all $\mu\in\bigcup_{a\geq0}B(\delta_{a_n+a},r)$}.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let X_1, \dots, X_n be i.i.d. random variables with \mathbb{E}[X_1] = 0, \text{Var}(X_1) = \sigma^2 > 0, and \rho = \mathbb{E}[|X_1|^3] < \infty. Let F_n(x) = \mathbb{P}(\frac{1}{\sigma \sqrt{n}} \sum_{k=1}^n X_k \le x) and \Phi(x) be the standard normal CDF. Then there exists a universal constant A < \infty such that for all x \in \mathbb{R} and all n \ge 1, |F_n(x) - \Phi(x)| \le \frac{A \rho}{\sigma^3 \sqrt{n} (1 + |x|^3)}.

body:
Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, paired). The per-output long-only stack on the relative-metric error covariance was shrunk toward the pooled simplex weights, $w_d \mapsto w_g + (1 - s)(w_d - w_g)$. The ceiling of the family - the amount chosen by five-fold cross-validation on the calibration rows - adds $+0.59$ percent on EMIT and $+0.20$ on OCO-2 at full calibration (28 of 40 and 26 of 30 cells). A positive-part James-Stein amount $s = \min(1, \sum_d \operatorname{tr} V_d / \sum_d \|w_d - w_g\|^2)$ with $V_d$ the naive $n$-out-of-$n$ bootstrap covariance of the long-only weights over 20 resamples recovers $+0.10$ / $+0.15$ (worst cells $-2.6$ / $-0.0$) with amounts $0.18$ against the cross-validated $0.14$ on EMIT: it overshoots, because the long-only weights have coordinates at the boundary and the naive bootstrap is inconsistent there (Andrews 2000; resampled fits flip members between zero and positive weight). The $m$-out-of-$n$ subsampling repair ($m = n/2$, variance scaled by $m/n$; Politis-Romano) gives amounts $0.11$ / $0.12$ against $0.14$ / $0.57$ and gains $+0.43$ / $+0.09$ (worst $-1.3$ / $-0.0$). Reading: the residual pooling amount is not recoverable from resampling to the accuracy the ceiling requires and remains the one cross-validated quantity in the neighbourhood of the long-only estimator, which alone sits within that ceiling

[Lemma l:shape of arXiv:2605.20587, 'Persistence and entropic repulsion of stationary Gaussian fields with spectral singularity'] Let $D$ be a compact domain. Then for every $\ell, \Delta > 0$, $\nu \in \mathcal{P}(D) \cap \mathcal{M}_{>0} \cap \mathcal{M}_{<\infty}$, and $\eta \in \mathcal{M}_{<\infty}$,
\begin{equation}
    
- \log \mathbb{P} \Big[  \inf_{x \in D} f(x) \ge \ell , | \langle f,\eta \rangle - \ell \langle h_\nu, \eta \rangle| \ge \ell \Delta  \Big]   \ge  \frac{\ell^2}{2} \Big( \frac{1}{E[\nu]}   + \min \Big\{ \frac{\Delta^2}{E[\eta]}, \frac{1}{E[\nu] }  \Big\} \Big)  .   
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Proof (unaudited), elementary route obstruction; no novelty claimed. Let K>=2 be even, N=Kn, and let a ReLU tree committee have independent standard Gaussian input blocks, spherical hidden weights of norm sqrt(n), fixed balanced readout signs and zero threshold. Labels are fixed independently of inputs. Restrict to classifiers in which every unit is inactive on every opposite-label pattern, but allow assignments to depend arbitrarily on all inputs and allow same-sign overlaps. Conditional on positive and negative label counts M_+,M_-, strict storage probability is at most q(M_-,n)^(K/2) q(M_+,n)^(K/2), where q(0,n)=1 and q(m,n)=2^(1-m) sum_{r=0}^{min(n-1,m-1)} binom(m-1,r) for m>=1. Uniformly in labels this is at most q(ceil(P/2),n)^(K/2), so for fixed K storage probability tends to zero when n tends to infinity and P/N tends to a>4/K. With balanced labels and P=4n the conditional bound is 2^-K. Thus positive sequential wide-limit load requires allowing wrong-sign active votes in this model; this is not an upper bound on unrestricted ReLU capacity.
Even fixed K>=2, N=Kn, n>=1, P>=1; independent Gaussian blocks and patterns
Hidden weights have norm sqrt(n), both readout signs occur K/2 times, threshold zero, ReLU hidden activation
Labels fixed or random independently of inputs; no balance or inter-label independence required for asymptotic exclusion
Every unit is inactive whenever its readout sign differs from the pattern label; arbitrary input-dependent assignments and same-sign overlaps are allowed

body: In mathematics, Parseval's theorem usually refers to the result that the Fourier transform is unitary; loosely, that the sum of the square of a function is equal to the sum of the square of its transform. It originates from a 1799 theorem about series by Marc-Antoine Parseval, which was later applied to the Fourier series. It is also known as Rayleigh's energy theorem, or Rayleigh's identity, after John William Strutt, Lord Rayleigh.
title: Parseval's theorem

body: Publication record. Problem 19.30 of S. Janson's survey (Probab. Surveys 9, 2012; 18.30 in arXiv v1) asks whether two consequences of his Theorem 19.7 remain true when the offspring variance is infinite: (ii) if n P(xi >= h(n)) -> 0 then Y_(1) < h(n) with high probability; (iii) if n P(xi >= h(n)) -> infinity then Y_(j) >= h(n) with high probability for every fixed j. Y. Shmalo, The second largest outdegree of conditioned Galton-Watson trees with infinite variance (October 2026) shows that (iii) can fail at lambda = nu with sigma^2 = infinity: along a sequence n_r one vertex has outdegree (r + 1/2) L_r and every other vertex has outdegree at most L_r/(64 (log n_r)^2), although n_r P(xi >= L_r) >= r. Part (ii) was answered negatively by Kortchemski and Richier (Ann. Appl. Probab. 29, 2019, Theorem 3); (iii) for j = 1 remains open. Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/second-largest-degree-infinite-variance (commit ba626a83fe32). Not refereed; an outside audit is owed.
title: Janson Problem 19.30 (arXiv 18.30) answered in part: the second largest outdegree of conditioned Galton-Watson trees with infinite variance (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/second-largest-degree-infinite-variance)

[Lemma Strict finite-support profile of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[lemma]{lem:strict-profile}
Let \(K\) be a compact neighborhood in \(\mathbb S^{N-1}(1)\), let \(x_0\) lie in its relative interior, and suppose a continuous function \(P\) satisfies
\[
 P(x_0)=\max_KP,
 \qquad
 \Delta:=P(x_0)-\max_{\partial K}P>0.
\]
If \(\left\lVertr\right\rVert_\infty\le M\) and \(b\Delta>2M\), then \(bP+r\) has a local maximum in the interior of \(K\), with value in
\[
 [bP(x_0)-M,bP(x_0)+M].
\]
If \(P,r\) are \(C^1\), this point is a spherical critical point.

[Proposition 5 of arXiv:2512.01483, 'Scaling Limits of Line Models in Degenerate Environment'] Define the rescaled random walk $(X^{(T)}(t))_{t \geq 0}$ as follows:
$$X^{(T)}_i(t) = T^{-a_i/2} X_i(Tt), \quad i=1,2$$ 
with $a_i, i =1,2$, two positive constants such that $a_i > \frac{1+ \varepsilon_i}{1- \varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_2}$, $i=1,2$. Then, for $\mathbb{P}$ a.e. $\omega \in \Omega$, for all $t>0$, and $i=1,2$, 
\[ \sup_{0 \leq s \leq t} X_i^{(T)}(s) \underset{T \to \infty}{\longrightarrow} 0 \]
in $P^{\omega}_0$-probability. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 13 (Control of the adaptive log-survival term) of arXiv:2605.04048, 'Catastrophe--dispersion models in random and varying environments across generations'] In Example~\ref{ex:RE-adaptive}, assume that $\psi_0$ has a continuous distribution on $(0,1)$ and
that $\mathbb E[|\log \psi_0|]<+\infty$. Let $\pi_p$ denote the invariant
distribution of the Markov chain $(p_n)$ defined by
\[
p_{n+1}=\min\{1,\;a p_n+(1-a)\psi_{n+1}\},\qquad a\in(0,1).
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textnormal{(i)}]
$\log p_0\in L^1(\pi_p)$ and
\[
-\infty < \mathbb E_{\pi_p}[\log p_0] < 0.
\]
\item[\textnormal{(ii)}]
The map $a\mapsto \mathbb E_{\pi_p}[\log p_0]$ is continuous and nondecreasing on
$(0,1)$.
\item[\textnormal{(iii)}]
The following bounds hold:
\[
\mathbb E[\log \psi_0]
\;\le\;
\mathbb E_{\pi_p}[\log p_0]
\;\le\;
\log\!\bigl(a+(1-a)\mathbb E[\psi_0]\bigr).
\]
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Prop 5 of arXiv:2603.26228, 'A local limit theorem for nonlattice multidimensional random walks in cones'] Let  ${\bf x},  {\bf y} \in \mathcal C$ and $\delta,  \tilde \delta>0$.
Then,  for any  ${\bf z} \in \llbracket {\bf x},  {\bf x}+\delta{\bf 1}\rrbracket\;\cap\;\cC$,  it holds
\begin{equation}
\bP\left( \tau({\bf z}) >n,  {\bf z}  +S(n) \in\llbracket {\bf y},  {\bf y}+\widetilde\delta{\bf 1}\rrbracket \right)
\leq
\bP\left( \widetilde{\tau}_{-\widetilde\delta}({\bf y}) >n,  {\bf y}-S(n) \in \llbracket {\bf x}-\tilde \delta{\bf 1}, {\bf x}+\delta{\bf 1}\rrbracket\right).
\end{equation}

Conversely,  when  $ \widetilde\delta >\delta$ and ${\bf y}\in \mathcal C_{\tilde \delta}$,  it holds 
\begin{equation}
\bP\left(\widetilde{\tau}_{\widetilde\delta}({\bf y})>n,  {\bf y}-S(n) \in \llbracket {\bf x}-(\widetilde\delta-\delta){\bf 1}, {\bf x} \rrbracket\right)
\leq
\bP\left(\tau({\bf x}) >n,  {\bf x}  +S(n) \in\llbracket {\by},  {\by}+\widetilde\delta{\bf 1}\rrbracket\right).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop diff_psi of arXiv:2603.29711, 'Strong Feller property, irreducibility,\\ and uniqueness of the invariant measure\\ for st'] Under the assumptions of Theorem~(th:wp of the paper),
for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$
the operator $\Psi_{\beta,\varepsilon}':H\rightarrow H$ is G\^ateaux-differentiable along directions of $H$, 
Fr\'echet-differentiable along directions of $L^4(\mathcal O)$, 
and $D\Psi'_{\beta,\varepsilon}:H\rightarrow\mathscr{L}(H,H)$
is given by
\[
  D\Psi'_{\beta,\varepsilon}(z)[h]=\Psi''_{\beta, \varepsilon}(z)h , 
  \quad z,h\in H.
\]
Furthermore, $D\Psi_{\beta,\varepsilon}'\in C^{0,1}_b(L^4(\mathcal O);\mathscr{L}(L^4(\mathcal O), H))\cap 
C^{0,1}_b(H;\mathscr{L}(L^{2+\eta}(\mathcal O), V^*))$ for every $\eta>0$,
and  it holds that 
\[
(D\Psi_{\beta,\varepsilon}'(z)h,h)_H=(\Psi_{\beta,\varepsilon}''(z)h,h)
\geq0\quad\forall\,z,h\in H,\quad \forall\,\varepsilon\in(0,1).
\]

[Theorem 162 of arXiv:2605.03236, 'Stochastic It\^o Equations and Parabolic Second-Order Equations with singular Drift'] Suppose that
$$
 \widehat {Da}_{p_{0},\rho_{0}}\leq 
e^{-1 }\widehat{Da},\quad \hat b_{p_{0} , \rho_{0} }
\leq e^{-1 }\hat b,
$$
where $\widehat{Da},\hat b$ are from Lemma
\ref{lemma 11.26,3} with $n=1$ there.
Then, as we know from Theorem \ref{theorem 12.6.02} and 
  Remark \ref{remark 11.28,1},
there exists a strong Markov, strong Feller 
 regular
diffusion process $X$ corresponding to
  $a,b$, for which  
estimate \eqref{11.22,4} holds
and its finite-dimensional distributions
are completely determined by $a,b$ (Theorem 
\ref{theorem 12.12.3}). For $s\geq t$ introduce
$$
T_{t,s}f(x)=E_{t,x}f(x_{s-t}).
$$

Then there are constants $N$ depending only 
on $d,\delta,q_{0},p_{0},\rho_{0},\beta$ such that
with $\lambda =\lambda_{0}\rho_{0}^{-2}$ from
Theorem \ref{theorem 5.8,20}

(i) For any $f\in E_{p,\beta }$  
we have
$$
 \| T_{t,s}f\|_{E_{p, \beta} }
\leq N \|f\|_{E_{p,\beta}}.
$$  

(ii) For any $f\in E_{p,\beta }$
and $s_{0}<s$, $e^{ \lambda\cdot}T_{\cdot,s}f\in E^{1,2}_{q,p,\beta}((-\infty,s_{0})\times\bR^{d })$ and
\begin{equation}
                    
\|e^{\lambda  \cdot} T_{\cdot,s}f
\|_{E^{1,2}_{q,p,\beta}((-\infty,s_{0})\times\bR^{d })}\leq
N(s-s_{0}) ^{-1}e^{\lambda s}\|f\|_{E_{p,\beta }}.
\end{equation}
 
(iii) For any $f\in E_{p,\beta }$
and $s-t\in (0,1]$,  
\begin{equation}
                       
 |T_{t,s}f|\leq N(s-t)^{-\beta/2}
\|f\|_{E_{p,\beta }},\quad |T_{t,s}f|\leq N
 \sup_{B\in\bB_{\sqrt{ s-t}}}\dashnorm f\|_{L_{p}(B)},
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
                       
 \|DT_{t,s}f\|_{E_{p,\beta }}\leq N(s-t)^{-(q+2)/(2q)}
\|f\|_{E_{p,\beta }}.
\end{equation}
Furthermore, $T_{t,s}f(x)$ is a continuous function of $(t,x)$ for $s>t$.

(iv) For any $f\in E_{p,\beta }$  
and $t>0$, (all derivatives are Sobolev derivatives)
\begin{equation}
                     
\partial_{t}T_{t,s}f=
 \cL T_{t,s}f.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 5 (Simultaneous rounding) of arXiv:2609.02080, 'Logarithmic basis number of graphs'] There is an absolute constant $c>0$ with the following property.  Let $M$ be a finite matroid on ground set $S$, let $x\in P_M$, and let $A_1,\dots,A_q\subseteq S$, where $q\ge2$.  If $x(A_i):=\sum_{s\in A_i}x_s\le L$ for every $i$, then $M$ has a base $B$ such that
\[
    |B\cap A_i|\le c\bigl(L+\ln q\bigr)
    \qquad(i=1,\dots,q).
\]

[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2608.27218, 'Mapping class groups have a unique Polish group structure'] Let \( H \) and \( K \) be Borel subgroups of a Polish group \( G \).
		If \( H \cap K = \{1\} \), then the set \( HK = \{ hk : h \in H, k \in K \} \) is Borel in \( G \).

[Proposition 31 (Total mass) of arXiv:2607.24561, 'Range convergence and sharp one-arm asymptotics\\for the critical percolation cluster in h'] The law of $\mu(\R^d)$ under $\bN$ is atomless, has infinite mean on
$\{\mu(\R^d)>\eps\}$ for every $\eps>0$, and $\bN$ is an infinite but
$\sigma$-finite measure. The explicit Laplace transform
$\bN\bigl[1-e^{-\theta\mu(\R^d)}\bigr]=\sqrt{2\theta/\gamma}$
($\theta>0$) holds, giving the tail
$\bN\bigl(\mu(\R^d)>\eps\bigr)=\sqrt{2/(\pi\gamma)}\,\eps^{-1/2}$; this
explicit form is used for the cluster-tail consistency check
(Remark~\ref{rem:tailknown}) and for the finiteness of the restricted masses
$\bN(\mu(\R^d)>\eps)$; the rest of the paper requires only atomlessness.

[Thm 5 of arXiv:2609.02686, 'The Bonnet-Myers theorem on Finsler manifolds with integral weighted Ricci curvature bound'] Let $(M, F, m)$ be an $n$-dimensional Finsler metric measure manifold. Assume that $\mathbf{S}\geq -\vartheta$ for some $\vartheta \geq 0$.
Then for $p>\frac{n}{2}$, $K \in \mathbb{R}$ and $0<r \leq R$ $(R \leq \frac{\pi}{2 \sqrt{K}}$ when $K>0)$, there exists a constant $C_{2}=C_{2}(n, p, \vartheta, K, R)>0$ such that
\be
\left(\frac{m\left(B_{R}^{+}(x_{0})\right)}{v(n, K, R, \vartheta)}\right)^{\frac{1}{2 p-1}}-\left(\frac{m\left(B_{r}^{+}(x_{0})\right)}{v(n, K, r, \vartheta)}\right)^{\frac{1}{2 p-1}} \leq C_{2} \left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{K}\right\|_{p, R, \vartheta}^{\frac{p}{2 p-1}}(x_{0}), 
\ee
where $C_{2}(n, p, \vartheta, K, R):=\left(\frac{n-1}{(2 p-1)(2 p-n)}\right)^{\frac{p-1}{2 p-1}} {\rm{Vol}}\left(\mathbb{S}^{n-1}\right) \int_{0}^{R} e^{\frac{2 p}{2 p-1}\vartheta t} s_{K}^{n-1}(t)\left(\frac{t}{v(n, K, t, \vartheta)}\right)^{\frac{2 p}{2 p-1}} d t$ is nondecreasing in $R$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For d>=2 and L>=1, iid continuous-label local-minimum anchor agreement defines a stationary ergodic (2L+2)-dependent site field with good density (2L-1)^d/((2L+1)^(d-1)(2L+1+2d)) tending to one, whose every nearest-neighbor good component has at most (2L+1)^d vertices.
d>=2 integer
L>=1 integer
iid uniform(0,1) labels
Good means equal local-minimum anchors at x and all nearest neighbors
metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:935bcd3a27467c3aab3ecdf6efc1380b9253179ecef7d2205846803a199af245","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/93/935bcd3a27467c3aab3ecdf6efc1380b9253179ecef7d2205846803a199af245.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:a2d91716a267a4d2811da38743a7f3612abef0f5d757c3818fd9c4cf7e0a145d","bundle_entry_key":"w429-l1","bundle_id":"population.critical-percolation-finite-range-bridge-w429-001-keyfix","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"w429/bundle_001_keyfix.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.percolation:local-anchor-high-density-finite-range-counterexample","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"lemma L1: a high-density finite-range counterexample

Fix integers d>=2 and L>=1. Let (U_z)_{z in Z^d} be independent uniform(0,1) labels. Almost surely every finite set has a unique minimum. Put W_x=x+[-L,L]^d (integer vertices), and a(x)=argmin_{z in W_x} U_z. Declare x good if a(y)=a(x) for every nearest neighbor y of x. Let X_x be its indicator.

The field X is stationary, ergodic, and r-dependent with r=2L+2 in the sup norm: X_x is determined by labels in the union of W_y over y=x and its neighbors, which lies in x+[-L-1,L+1]^d. For two sets at sup-norm distance greater than 2L+2, their determining label sets are disjoint; independence applies to the corresponding sigma-fields, not merely individual pairs. Ergodicity follows because X is a measurable translation-equivariant factor of the ergodic iid label field.

Every nearest-neighbor component of good vertices is finite. If x and y are adjacent good vertices, their anchors coincide. Hence all vertices of any connected good component share an anchor a. Each such vertex x satisfies a in W_x, so the component lies in a+[-L,L]^d and has at most (2L+1)^d vertices.

Its exact good density is

    q(d,L) = (2L-1)^d / [(2L+1)^(d-1) (2L+1+2d)].

Proof of the formula: write I=intersection_{y=x or y~x} W_y and J=union_{y=x or y~x} W_y. All anchors agree iff the unique minimum on J belongs to I. Necessity holds because a shared minimum belongs to every W_y and minimizes the union; sufficiency is immediate. Now |I|=(2L-1)^d. The union is W_x and 2d disjoint outer faces of size (2L+1)^(d-1), giving the denominator. The minimum is uniformly located on J by exchangeability of continuous iid labels.

Consequently q(d,L)->1 as L->infinity while every good component is finite. This refutes the inference that marginal good probabilities tending to one plus finite dependence at each scale suffice for percolation when the dependence range is allowed to grow. [Proposition prop:lattice_potts of arXiv:2506.10765, 'A General Coupling for Ising Models and Beyond'] Let $\Lambda_k$ be a collection of $k$-cells, $\Omega = \{0,1\}^{\Lambda_k}$, $\Sigma =\ker(\partial_k)$,  $x_{\mathbf{c}}\in (0,1)$ for all $\mathbf{c}\in \Lambda_k$,  $f:\Omega\to 2^{\Sigma}$ be defined by $f(\omega)= \Sigma^{\downarrow}(\omega):=\{\eta \in \Sigma\mid \operatorname{supp}(\eta) \subset \omega\}$  and
	\[\rho[\omega] \propto \prod_{\mathbf{c}\in \Lambda_k (\omega)} \frac{x_{\mathbf{c}}}{1-x_{\mathbf{c}}}, ~\forall \omega\in \Omega, ~\gamma[\eta]\propto 1, ~\forall \eta\in \Sigma. \]
    	Then, under the coupling measure $\mathscr{P}$ defined in Theorem (thm:generalcoupling of the paper), 
    \item[(a)] The marginal  $\mathscr{P}_\Sigma = \ell^q_{\Lambda_k,x}$.
          For $\omega\in\Omega,$ the  conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\;\cdot \mid \omega]$  is uniform on $\Sigma^{\downarrow}(\omega)$, i.e. a uniform divergence free $q$-coloring of $\omega$.
		\item[(b)] The marginal $\mathscr{P}_\Omega= \phi^q_{\Lambda_k,p}$, with $x_{\mathbf{c}}=\frac{p_{\mathbf{c}}}{p_{\mathbf{c}}+q(1-p_{\mathbf{c}})}$.
        For each $\eta\in\Sigma$, the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\;\cdot \mid \eta] = \mathbb{P}_x \cup \delta_{\operatorname{supp}(\eta)}$,  Bernoulli percolation on $\Lambda_k$ with parameter $(x_{\mathbf{c}})_{\mathbf{c}\in \Lambda_k}$ conditioned on all $k$-cells in $\operatorname{supp}(\eta)$ being open. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:kac-moment of arXiv:2608.08375, 'Algebraic formulas for first-passage times of Markov processes in the linear framework: ge'] Let $G$ be a strongly connected graph and choose $u \in \mathcal{V}(G)$. The $r$-th moment of the recurrence time to $u$ is given by,
\[
    \tau^{(r)}_u(G) = \frac{r!}{\left( \lambda_u(G) \, x_u^*(G) \right)^r} \sum_{(i_1, \dotsc, i_r) \in \mathcal{V}(G)^r}{\left( \prod_{j=0}^{r-1}{\psi_{i_{j+1}|i_j,u} \, x_{i_{j+1}}^*(G)} \right)} \,,
\]
where the exchange factor takes the form,
\begin{align*}
    & \psi_{i_{j+1}|i_j,u} = 1 \,\, + \\
    & \sum_{\substack{m \in \mathcal{V}(G) \setminus \{i_{j+1}\} \\ m \to_G u}}\left( \frac{w(\Phi_{\{u,i_{j+1}\} \to \{m,i_{j+1}\}}(G)) - w(\Phi_{\{i_j,i_{j+1}\} \to \{m,i_{j+1}\}}(G))}{w(\Phi_{\{i_{j+1}\}}(G))} \right) \ell(m \to_G u) \,.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Generalised Kac lemma

[Lemma 20 (Yule jump-time asymptotics) of arXiv:2606.29635, 'Extremality and Limit Laws for the Siblings of the Coupon Collector'] Let $\xi_r\sim\Exp(r)$ be independent, and put $S_\ell=\xi_1+\cdots+\xi_\ell$. Then there is a random variable $W\sim\Exp(1)$ such that
\[
        (\ell+1)\e^{-S_\ell}\to W
\]
almost surely and in $L^m$ for every fixed integer $m\ge1$. Consequently,
\[
        \frac{S_\ell}{\log\ell}\to1
\]
almost surely. Moreover, for every fixed $s>0$ and nonnegative integer $r$,
\begin{equation}
        \E\left[\e^{-sS_\ell}S_\ell^r\right]
        =(-1)^r\frac{\dd^r}{\dd s^r}\frac{\Gamma(\ell+1)\Gamma(s+1)}{\Gamma(\ell+s+1)}.
\end{equation}

[Definition 10 (Kac chaos) of arXiv:2604.14427, 'A criterion for proving entropy chaos on path space'] We say that $\rho_N^{(n)}(t)$ is \emph{$\bar{\rho}(t)$-chaotic} if, for any fixed $k\geq 1$,
\[
\rho_{N}^{(k)}(t) \xrightarrow[N \to \infty]{} \bar{\rho}^{\otimes k}(t),
\]
where $\rho_{N}^{(n)}(t)$ denotes the $k-$th marginal of $\rho_N(t)$, $\bar\rho^{\otimes k}$ denotes the $k-$th product measure, and the convergence is understood in the sense of weak convergence of probability measures.
title: Kac chaos

increasing continuous maps from $[0,1]$ onto $[0,1]$ that converges

on $[0,1]$.

[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked; tested by direct Monte Carlo simulation of the Poisson-weighted infinite tree (4000 replicates, k=2,5,10,12), agreeing with the recursion within about 1.5 standard errors] This is the campaign's branching-walk identification behind Conjecture 1 of H. Stepanyants, P. L. Krapivsky, H. Hartle and D. Krioukov, The rank and layer distributions in random recursive trees, arXiv:2608.04303. Let the Poisson-weighted infinite tree have root position zero, with children of each vertex at the points of an independent rate-one Poisson process on (0,infinity), translated by their parent's position. Let M_k be the minimum position of generation k, and set M_0=0. Define s_0(y)=1 for y>=0 and s_k(y)=1-exp(-integral_0^y s_{k-1}(z)dz) for k>=1. Put bar_ell_k=integral_0^infinity s_k(y)exp(-y)dy and ell_k=bar_ell_k-bar_ell_{k+1}. In the source, ell_k is the limiting fraction of vertices in layer k of a random recursive tree, formed by joining each new vertex j uniformly to one of vertices 1,...,j-1. Layer zero consists of the initial leaves, and subsequent layers are obtained by successive leaf removals. For every k>=0 and y>=0, s_k(y)=P(M_k<=y). Consequently bar_ell_k=E[exp(-M_k)] and ell_k=E[exp(-M_k)-exp(-M_{k+1})]. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
Independent rate-one Poisson offspring displacement processes.
The layer-tail recursion is the one stated in the source paper.

[Defn Capacity in $\mathbb{D}$ of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] For any compact subset $K$ of $\overline{\mathbb{D}}$ such that $\mathbb{D} \backslash K$ is simply connected and contains 0 , let $g_K$ be the unique conformal map $\mathbb{D} \backslash K \rightarrow \mathbb{D}$ such that $g_K(0)=0$ and $g_K^{\prime}(0)>0$ . The conformal radius of $\mathbb{D} \backslash K$ is
$$
\operatorname{CR}(\mathbb{D} \backslash K):=\left(g_K^{\prime}(0)\right)^{-1} .
$$

The capacity of $K$ is
$$
\operatorname{cap}(K)=\log g_K^{\prime}(0)=-\log \mathrm{CR}(\mathbb{D} \backslash K,0).
$$
title: Capacity in $\mathbb{D}$

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Sharp harmonic-mean characterization of meeting times structural calculation Result: For a two-state chain with rates a<=b, tau1=tau2=1/(a+b), and the only distinct pair meets after an exponential time of mean tau2. Direct stationary hitting calculations give J/tau2=b*(a+b)/(a^2+b^2)=(1+r)/(1+r^2), r=a/b. This ratio ranges up to(1+sqrt2)/2, attained at r=sqrt2-1. Thus the converse cannot hold with constant1 even for two states, although a universal larger constant is consistent with this control. Check: E_pi T0=a/[b(a+b)] and E_pi T1=b/[a(a+b)]. Substituting the two maxima into the harmonic mean gives the formula; differentiating(1+r)/(1+r^2) gives its exact maximum. Meeting occurs at the first jump of either distinct coordinate, total rate a+b. Obstruction: The two-state calculation does not bound J/max E M on arbitrary chains. Rare spatial bottlenecks can affect stationary hitting times and two-particle meeting differently.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0252-sharp-harmonic-mean-characterization-of-meeting-times

[Definition of arXiv:2509.10225, 'Phase Transitions for Elephant Random Walks \\ with Two memory Channels'] Suppose $\Sigma$ is a strictly positive random variable. We say that another random variable $Z$ is a variance mixture of Gaussian with random variance $\Sigma$ (and denote this by ${Z} \sim N\left(0,\Sigma\right)$) if the conditional characteristic function of ${Z}$ given $\Sigma$ is 
    \[
       \mathbb{E}\left(e^{\iota tZ} \mid \Sigma\right) = e^{-\frac{t^2\Sigma}{2}}, \quad t \in \mathbb{R}.
    \]

body:
Let N_r be the r-by-r nilpotent shift with ones on the superdiagonal, with N_1=0. For a real a, delta>=0 and t>=0, ||exp(t(a I_r+delta N_r))||_2<=exp((a+delta)t). For real a,b and C=[[a,-b],[b,a]], the real block J=I_r tensor C+delta N_r tensor I_2 obeys the same bound ||exp(tJ)||_2<=exp((a+delta)t). For delta>0, a diagonal change of basis with successive power weights changes a Jordan superdiagonal of 1 to delta; use repeated power weights for the real form of a conjugate pair. Consequently, let A be a real finite matrix with algebraically simple real eigenvalue lambda_1>max{Re(lambda_j):j>=2}. For any rho with max_{j>=2}Re(lambda_j)<rho<lambda_1, a real basis S can be chosen with S^-1 A S=diag(lambda_1,B) so that ||exp(t S^-1 A S)-exp(lambda_1 t)e_1 e_1^T||_2<=exp(rho t) for every t>=0. These constant-one bounds concern the chosen coordinates: in the original Euclidean norm the corresponding estimate carries ||S||_2||S^-1||_2.
Finite-dimensional real matrices and Euclidean operator norm
t>=0 and delta>=0 for block bounds; delta>0 for the similarity
For the final assertion the leading eigenvalue is real and algebraically simple and strictly dominates all other real parts
The norm-one estimate is in the rescaled real Jordan coordinates, not automatically the original coordinates

[Lem lem-max-principle of arXiv:2506.18827, 'Random walk reflected off of infinity, with applications to uniform spanning forests and s'] Let $\mathcal A\subset  \mathcal V\mathcal G$ be non-empty and finite. 
Let $\phi : \mathcal A\to\mathbbm R$ and let $h^\phi$ be the energy-minimizing function on $\mathcal G$ with $h^\phi|_{\mathcal A} = \phi$, as in Proposition~(prop-min-harmonic of the paper).  
Then 
\begin{equation} 
\max_{x\in\mathcal V\mathcal G} h^\phi(x) = \max_{y\in\mathcal A}  \phi(y)  
\end{equation} 
and the same holds with ``min'' in place of ``max''. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Maximum principle

[Mainthm thm:motion of arXiv:2608.24830, 'Motion helps the contact process: survival below\\ the percolation threshold on Poisson Br'] Let $d\ge2$ and $r>0$, and let $\eta<\eta_c^{\mathrm{B}}$, so that at every fixed time the Gilbert graph has
almost surely only finite components and the cluster of the seed is almost surely finite. For every
$\lambda\in(0,\infty)$ there is $\mu_*=\mu_*(\lambda;\eta,r,d)>0$ such that for every
$\mu\le\mu_*$ the infection started from a single particle at the origin survives with positive
probability and spreads at positive speed,
\[
  \mathbb{P}^{\lambda,\mu}_\eta\Big(\liminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{rad}(I_t)}{t}>0\Big)\ >\ 0 ,
\]
in the finite-rate model and, with $\mathbb{P}^{\infty,\mu}_\eta$ in place of
$\mathbb{P}^{\lambda,\mu}_\eta$, in the instantaneous model as well. Consequently there is
$\mu_\dagger=\mu_\dagger(r,d)\in(0,\infty]$ such that
\[
  \eta_c(\infty,\mu)\ <\ \eta_c^{\mathrm{B}}\quad\text{for every }\mu<\mu_\dagger ,
  \qquad
  \eta_c(\infty,\mu)\ =\ \eta_c^{\mathrm{B}}\quad\text{for every }\mu\in(\mu_\dagger,\infty) .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Survival below the static percolation threshold

	\[
	W_1\cup_{Z_1}W_2\cup_{Z_2}\cdots\cup_{Z_{n}}W_{n+1} \cong W\# \overline{\mathbb {CP}}^2.
	\]

[Proposition 6 (Conjugacy invariance of infinite radius) of arXiv:2607.26377, '\textbf{Entire Logarithmic Signatures\\ of Bounded-Variation Paths in Finite Dimensions}'] Let $X$ and $Y$ be based continuous bounded-variation paths. Then
\[
R\bigl(\log S(X)\bigr)=\infty
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
R\bigl(\log S(Y*X*\overleftarrow{Y})\bigr)=\infty.
\]
More precisely, if $l=\log S(X)$ and $a=S(Y)$, then
\[
\log S(Y*X*\overleftarrow{Y})=a l a^{-1}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Conjugacy invariance of infinite radius

Let X be a nearest-neighbor walk on Z^d, d>=1, started at 0, in a static environment with all transition probabilities at least kappa>0 under its original quenched or annealed law P. For any random time T in N union {infinity}, define R_T=sup_{0<=n<=T}||X_n||_infinity. For integers r,t>=0, m=r+1, P(T>t)<=P(R_T>r)+(1-kappa^m)^floor(t/m). For any event A with alpha=P(A)>0, P(T>t|A)<=P(R_T>r|A)+alpha^(-1)(1-kappa^m)^floor(t/m). The conditional walk is not asserted to retain uniform ellipticity.
d is an integer >=1; X starts at 0 on Z^d
nearest-neighbor transitions in a fixed or randomly sampled static environment
every transition probability is at least a deterministic kappa in (0,1/(2d)] under the original law P
T takes values in N union {infinity}; it need not be a stopping time
For the conditional statement, A has positive original-law probability alpha

[Theorem thm:intro-two of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Let $\boldsymbol\kappa=(\kappa_1,\kappa_2)$ satisfy
$\kappa_1>0>\kappa_2$, and let
$(\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})\in\Lambda_2(D)$
be a strict local minimum point of the corresponding Kirchhoff--Routh function
$W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}$ defined in (equation eq:intro-KR of the paper).  Fix
$M_i,R_i>0$ for $i=1,2$.  For each $\varepsilon>0$, let
$\mathbf a_{1,\varepsilon},\mathbf a_{2,\varepsilon}\in D$, and let
$\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}\in L^\infty(D)$ be nonnegative and satisfy
\[
  \int_D\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}\,\mathrm d\mathbf x=|\kappa_i|,
  \qquad
  \|\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}\|_\infty\leq M_i\varepsilon^{-2},
  \qquad
  \operatorname{supp}\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}
  \subset B_{R_i\varepsilon}(\mathbf a_{i,\varepsilon}),
  \qquad i=1,2.
 \]
Suppose that
\[
  (\mathbf a_{1,\varepsilon},\mathbf a_{2,\varepsilon})
  \longrightarrow
  (\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2}),
  \qquad
  \mathcal A(\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0})\longrightarrow0
  \quad(i=1,2)
\]
as $\varepsilon\to0$.  Set
$\omega_{\varepsilon,0}
:=\zeta_{1,\varepsilon,0}-\zeta_{2,\varepsilon,0}$.
Let $\omega_{\varepsilon,t}$, $t\in\mathbb R$, be the corresponding
Yudovich solution of (equation eq:euler-intro of the paper), and, for $i=1,2$, let
$\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,t}$ denote the transport of
$\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}$ by the associated Euler flow map
(so that
$\omega_{\varepsilon,t}
=\zeta_{1,\varepsilon,t}-\zeta_{2,\varepsilon,t}$
for every $t\in\mathbb R$; see (rk:decomvor of the paper)).
Then, as $\varepsilon\to0$,
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\mathcal A(\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,t})
  \longrightarrow0
  \qquad(i=1,2),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\ \sup_{(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)\in
  \mathsf C(\zeta_{1,\varepsilon,t})\times
  \mathsf C(\zeta_{2,\varepsilon,t})}
  |(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)
  -(\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})|
  \longrightarrow0.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Global persistence: two opposite-sign vortices

Let X_1, \dots, X_n be i.i.d. random variables with mean 0, variance 1, and cumulants \kappa_3, \kappa_4, \dots. [Defn 1 of arXiv:2607.21759, 'Marchenko--Pastur law for tensor powers of exchangeable unconditional vectors'] Let $\binom{[n]}{d}$ be the collection of subsets of $[n]$ with size $d$, and let $[n]^{d}=\{1,\dotsc,n\}^d$. These index sets have sizes $\binom{n}{d}$ and $n^d$, respectively. Further, let $\nu$ be a probability measure on $\R^n$ and let $\mathbf X = (X_1,\dotsc, X_n) \sim \nu$. We define the following random tensor models.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.]
    \item Set $p = \binom{n}{d}$ and index the coordinates of  $\R^p$ by $\binom{[n]}{d}$. We define a random vector $\mathbf x \in \R^p$ by
    \[
         \mathbf x = \biggl(\prod_{\alpha \in i} X_\alpha\biggr)_{i \in \binom{[n]}{d}}.
    \] In this case, we say $\mathbf x$ is a \df{principal tensor generated from the base distribution $\nu$}, and denote its law by $\PrincipalT(n,d,\nu)$.
   \item Set $q = n^d$, and index the coordinates of $\R^q$ by $[n]^d$. We define another random vector $\mathbf x \in \R^q$ by \[
       \mathbf x = \biggl(\prod_{j=1}^d X_{i_j}\biggr)_{i \in [n]^d},
    \]
    where $i=(i_1,\dots,i_d)\in[n]^d.$ In this case, we say $\mathbf x$ is a (full) \df{tensor power generated from the base distribution $\nu$}, and denote its law by  $\PowerT(n,d,\nu)$.
        \end{enumerate}
    With a slight abuse of notation, we will usually write $\mathbf X$ in place of $\nu$, or omit them completely when the context is clear. When we are discussing both models simultaneously, we will just call them the tensor power models.
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2607.21759

[Definition def:regular-process-convergence of arXiv:2608.15923, 'Universality of two-dimensional Markovian holonomy fields'] Let $({\mathbb{G}}_n)$ be universally stable. Let, for each $n$, $H_n$ be a holonomy process on ${\mathbb{G}}_n$\footnote{Which we recall is just a random element of $\mathrm{Hom}(L_o({\mathbb{G}}_n),G)$.}. Let $H$ be a holonomy process on $\Sigma$. We say that $H_n$ converges \emph{regularly} to $H$ if, for every finite regular based loop family $L=(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r)$ and every stable graph approximation $L_n=(\ell_{1,n},\ldots,\ell_{r,n})$ carried by $({\mathbb{G}}_n)$,
\[
 \bigl(H_n(\ell_{1,n}),\ldots,H_n(\ell_{r,n})\bigr)
 \Longrightarrow
 \bigl(H_{\ell_1},\ldots,H_{\ell_r}\bigr)
\]
as probability measures on $G^r$.
title: Definition def:regular-process-convergence of arXiv:2608.15923

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2605.21155, 'Asymptotic Probabilities of Attaining the Maximum in Heterogeneous Gaussian Samples'] For $\sigma>1$,  the sequence
  $\mathbb P (M^{(1)}_{n_1}>M^{(2)}_{n_2} )$
converges to a limit in $(0,1)$ if and only if \eqref{eq:N1N2} holds for some $C\in(0,\infty)$.  Moreover, in this case,
\begin{equation}
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb P\!\left(M^{(1)}_{n_1}>M^{(2)}_{n_2}\right)
=
\mathbb P\!\left(\Lambda_1>\sigma^2(\Lambda_2-\kappa(C,\sigma))\right)
=
\int_0^\infty \exp\left(-y - e^{-\kappa(C,\sigma)} y^{1/\sigma^2}\right) \mathrm dy,
\end{equation}
where $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ are independent Gumbel random variables, and
\begin{align}
 
 \kappa(C,\sigma)
=
\frac{1}{\sigma^2}\log\frac{C}{\sigma}
+\frac12\left(1-\frac{1}{\sigma^2}\right)\log(4\pi).
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 3 of arXiv:2605.21155

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.27433, 'Scalar curvature on K\"ahler blow-ups and systolic inequalities'] Let \(X^{m+r}\) be a compact K\"ahler manifold admitting an almost holomorphic fibration \(f:X^{m+r}\dashrightarrow Z^m\) onto a normal compact K\"ahler space \(Z\) which is not uniruled. Assume
that a general fibre of \(f\) is biholomorphic to \(\PP^r\). If \(\omega\) is a K\"ahler metric on \(X\) with positive scalar curvature, then, for every \(1\le q\le r\),
\begin{equation}
        \min_X S(\omega)\cdot\sys_{2q}(\omega)^{1/q}
        \le 2\pi r(r+1).
\end{equation}
Moreover, for a fixed \(q\), equality holds if and only if the universal cover
\[
        (\widetilde X,\widetilde\omega)
        \cong
        (\PP^r,a\omega_{FS})\times(Y,\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}),
\]
where \(a=[\omega]\cdot[L]\) for a line \(L\) in a general fibre,
\(\omega_{\mathrm{RF}}\) is Ricci-flat, and \(\sys_{2q}(\omega)\) is realized by a
fibrewise linear \(\PP^q\subset\PP^r\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.27433

Let X be a real random variable and let M(t) = E[e^{tX}] be its moment generating function. For every real a and every t > 0 with M(t) < infinity, P(X >= a) <= e^{-ta} M(t); hence P(X >= a) <= inf_{t > 0} e^{-ta} M(t). Likewise for every t < 0 with M(t) < infinity, P(X <= a) <= e^{-ta} M(t). For a sum X = X_1 + ... + X_n of independent variables, M(t) = prod E[e^{tX_i}], which gives the usual exponential tail bounds; for instance, if the X_i are independent Bernoulli with mu = E[X], then P(X >= (1+delta) mu) <= (e^{delta} / (1+delta)^{1+delta})^{mu} for every delta > 0.
M(t) finite at the value of t used
independence is needed only for the product form of M

[Lemma lem.proj_coeffs of arXiv:2603.11043, 'An asymptotically optimal bound for the concentration function of a sum of independent int'] For any integer $d$, $d \ge 2$ 
    and a positive $\gamma$
    
    
    
    there
    are positive reals $\delta_0 =\delta_0(d, \gamma)$,
    $R_1=R_1(d,\gamma)$
    and an integer 
    $L_0 = L_0(d, \gamma)$
    such that the following holds.

    Let ${\bf X}$ be a random vector in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and let $\round{{\bf X}}$ 

    be
    obtained by rounding each component of ${\bf X}$ to the nearest integer. 
    

    Let $q = \sup_{e: \|e\|=1} \mathcal{Q}(\langle e, {\bf X} \rangle, 1)$, that is $q$ is
    the supremum of the mass of ${\bf X}$ concentrated (strictly) between any two hyperplanes at distance one from each other.

    
    

    Let $R_0 >0$ and suppose that in the open ball $\{x: \|x\| < R_0\}$ the random vector ${\bf X}$ has
    a positive and differentiable density $f$ (that is $\mathbb P({\bf X} \in A) = \int_{A} f(x) d x_1 \dots d x_d > 0$ for any Borel set $A \subseteq \{x: \|x\| < R_0\}$) such that

    
    \begin{equation}
        \sup_{ \|x\| < R_0 } \|\nabla \ln f(x) \| \le \delta_0
        
    \end{equation}
    Then for any vector $a \in \mathbb{R}^d$ either
    \begin{equation}
        \mathcal{Q}(\langle a, \round{{\bf X}} \rangle) = \max_{x \in \mathbb{Z}} \mathbb P(\langle a, \round{{\bf X}} \rangle = x) \le \gamma q + \mathbb P\left(\|{\bf X}\| \ge R_0 - R_1\right)
    \end{equation}
    or there is $\kappa \in \mathbb{R}$, $\kappa \ne 0$ such that $\kappa a \in \{-L_0, \dots, L_0\}^d$.
title: Lemma lem.proj_coeffs of arXiv:2603.11043

Let U ⊂ R^n be open, let F = F(p,z,x) be C^1 on R^n × R × U, and let u ∈ C^2(U) satisfy F(Du(x), u(x), x) = 0 for all x ∈ U. Let x(·): I → U solve the ODE x'(s) = D_pF( p(s), z(s), x(s) ), where p(s) := Du(x(s)) and z(s) := u(x(s)). Then on I: z'(s) = D_pF(p(s),z(s),x(s))·p(s) and p'(s) = -D_xF(p(s),z(s),x(s)) - D_zF(p(s),z(s),x(s)) p(s). Thus (x(·),z(·),p(·)) solves the characteristic system x' = D_pF, z' = p·D_pF, p' = -D_xF - p D_zF, and F(p(s),z(s),x(s)) ≡ 0 along it. The curve x(·) is called a projected characteristic.

[Lemma lem:stoch.comp of arXiv:2411.02033, 'Two stochastic versions of the Arps curve decline'] \hspace{1cm}
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $X$ and $Y$ are two positive random variables defined on the same probability space such that $X \preceq_{st} Y$ and if $f$ is a one-to-one map defined on $\mathbb{R}^+$, then $f(X) \preceq_{st} f(Y)$.
\item If $f$ and $g$ are two functions such that that for any $t \in \mathbb{R}$ $f(t) \leqslant g(t)$, then for any random variable $X$ $f(X) \preceq_{st} g(X)$.
\item Let $f$ and $g$ two continuous functions defined on $\mathbb{R}^+$ such that:
$$
\forall t \geqslant 0 , \quad f(t) \geqslant g(t) ,
$$
with $g(0) \leqslant f(0) \leqslant 0$. Then $T_{B,f(\cdot)} \preceq_{st} T_{B,g(\cdot)}$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:stoch.comp of arXiv:2411.02033

[Theorem concentration of arXiv:2412.02087, 'The spectral distribution of random graphs with given degree sequences'] Consider the degree sequence $\{ d_1^{(n)}, d_2^{(n)}, \cdots, d_n^{(n)} \}$ for each $n\geq 1$. Suppose that $\min\{d_i^{(n)}\}_{i\in [n]} \gg \sqrt{D^{(n)}/n}$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$. Consider the normalized Laplacian matrix $M^{(n)}$ as defined in (equation e:defM of the paper).     $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem lowergeneral of arXiv:2412.06246, 'The smallest singular value for rectangular random matrices with Lévy entries'] Fix $\alpha\in(0,2),$ $\delta>1$, and let $N,n$ be integers such that $N\geq \delta n$. Let $(x_{ij})_{1\leq i\leq N,1\leq j\leq n}$ be i.i.d. random variables with a symmetric distribution and satisfy (equation stablelaw of the paper). Fix $0<A_1<A_2$ and let $(a_{ij})_{1\leq i\leq N,1\leq j\leq n}$ be fixed real numbers such that $$A_1\leq a_{ij}\leq A_2\quad \forall i=1,\cdots,N, j=1,\cdots,n.$$ 
    Let $A=(a_{ij}x_{ij})$ be an $N\times n$ random matrix
and let $B$ be any deterministic $N\times n$ matrix. We do not make any assumption on $B$.
Then for any $D>0$ we can find $C_3>0$ and $N_0\in\mathbb{N}_+$ such that,
whenever $N\geq N_0,$ 
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}(\sigma_{min}(A+B)\leq C_3N^\frac{1}{\alpha}(\log N)^\frac{2(\alpha-2)}{\alpha})\leq N^{-D},
\end{equation}
 where $C_3$ and $N_0$ depend only on $D,\delta,\alpha,C_\ell,C_u,A_1,A_2$, and notably do not depend on $B$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop 48 of arXiv:2511.10535, 'Eigenvalues of Brownian Motions on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$'] Let $a$ be an operator in a $W^\ast$-probability space $(\A,\tau)$, and for each $N\in\N$ let $A^N$ be a matrix in $\M_N(\C)$.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item If $A^N$ converges strongly to $a$, then for each $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $N\in\N$ the spectrum of $A^N$ is contained in the $\varepsilon$-neighborhood of the spectrum of $a$: $\sigma(A^N)\subset\sigma(a)+\varepsilon$.
    \item If the ESD $\mu_{A^N}$ of $A^N$ converges weakly to the Brown measure $\mu_a$ of $a$, then for each $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $N\in\N$ the support of $\mu_a$ is contained in the $\varepsilon$-neighborhood of the spectrum of $A^N$: $\supp\mu_a\subset \sigma(A^N)+\varepsilon$.
    \item Ergo: if $A^N\to a$ strongly and $\mu_{A^N}\to\mu_a$ weakly, and in addition $\supp\mu_a = \sigma(a)$, then $\sigma(A^N)\to\sigma(A)$ in Hausdorff distance.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition 1 (Completely monotone, Bernstein, and Stieltjes classes) of arXiv:2607.04467, 'Bernstein Functions at Work:\\ Coalescents, Copulas, and Subordination'] Let all functions below be defined on \((0,\infty)\) and take values in
\([0,\infty)\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.3em]
\item A function \(f\) is \emph{completely monotone}, written \(f\in\CM\), if
\(f\in C^\infty\) and
\((-1)^n f^{(n)}(x)\ge0\) for every \(n\ge0\) and \(x>0\). It is
\emph{strictly completely monotone} if all these inequalities are strict.

\item A function \(g\) is a \emph{Bernstein function}, written \(g\in\BF\), if
\(g\in C^\infty\) and \(g'\in\CM\).

\item A Bernstein function \(g\) is a \emph{special Bernstein function}, written
\(g\in\SBF\), if \(x/g(x)\in\BF\).

\item A Bernstein function \(g\) is a \emph{complete Bernstein function}, written
\(g\in\CBF\), if its L\'evy measure has a completely monotone density.

\item A function \(h\) is a \emph{Stieltjes function} if
\begin{equation}
h(x)=\frac{a}{x}+b+\int_{(0,\infty)}\frac{1}{x+t}\,\sigma(dt),\qquad x>0,
\end{equation}
where \(a,b\ge0\) and
\(\int_{(0,\infty)}(1+t)^{-1}\,\sigma(dt)<\infty\).
\end{enumerate}
title: Completely monotone, Bernstein, and Stieltjes classes

[Corollary cor:rough-seeds of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] Let the seed $g$ on rank space be of bounded variation with a jump,
		in the sense that its odd extension to the rank circle has a jump.
		Then for almost every $\tau$ the deformation
		$\rho_{|e^{-i\tau H_{0}}g|^{2}}[f]$ of any law $f$ whose density is
		continuously differentiable and bounded above and below on its
		support has graph dimension exactly $\tfrac32$ there, the
		differentiability being necessary, since a rough multiplier $f$ can
		dominate the oscillation of the product; for the canonical seed the constant of the
		law~(equation eq:mass-strong-law of the paper) on the rank circle is
		\begin{equation}
			\kappa_{\mathrm{can}} = \frac{4}{\pi^{2}},
			
		\end{equation}

		Talbot optics is fractal of dimension $\tfrac32$ at almost every
		time for \emph{arbitrary} grating profiles of bounded variation
		with a jump, at arbitrary, possibly irrational, positions; for
		rational step gratings this is the theorem of Chousionis,
		Erdo\u{g}an, and Tzirakis~[chousionis2015], and the general
		case had remained open. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lem 77 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $\gamma:[q_0,1]\to[q_0,1]$ be a monotone and absolutely continuous function, and define its generalized inverse
	\[
	\lambda:[q_0,\gamma(1)]\to[q_0,1]\,,\quad
	\lambda(s)
	\equiv\inf\Big\{
	t : \gamma(t)>s
	\Big\}\,.
	\]
Then the set $\{s : \gamma'(\lambda(s))=0 \}$ has zero Lebesgue measure.

\begin{proof}
It is straightforward to verify that $\lambda$ is a right-continuous function with $\gamma(\lambda(s))=s$ for all $s$. For any measurable set $A\subseteq\R$, consider the preimage $\lambda^{-1}(A)$: we have $s\in \lambda^{-1}(A)$ if and only if $\lambda(s)\in A$, which implies $s=\gamma(\lambda(s)) \in \gamma(A)$. This proves that 
	\[\lambda^{-1}(A)
	\subseteq \gamma(A)\]
(the converse need not hold). Let $A=\{t\in[q_0,1] : \gamma'(t)=0\}$: by absolute continuity of $\gamma$, we have
	\[|\gamma(A)|
	= \int_{q_0}^1 \gamma'(t)
	\ind\{t\in A\}
	\,dt = 0\,.\]
Since $\lambda^{-1}(A)\subseteq \gamma(A)$, it follows that
	\[
	|\lambda^{-1}(A)|
	=\bigg| \Big\{s : \gamma'(\lambda(s))=0
	\Big\}\bigg|=0\,,
	\]
as claimed.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 77 of arXiv:2608.29416
