body:
[Theorem eq:symm_4q_special of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] In $\mathbb{Z}_3$ and $\mathbb{Z}_{4q}$ with $2 \nmid q$, there exist symmetrization resistant random variables for which the minimum-entropy independent symmetrizer is not unique. 

\begin{proof}
In $\mathbb{Z}_3$, writing PMFs as $z = (z(-1),z(0),z(1))$, we see that $f = \frac{1}{3}(1,2,0)$ (which is symmetrization resistant by (thm:Z3 of the paper)) has $\frac{1}{3}(2,0,1)$ and $\frac{1}{3}(0,2,1)$ as symmetrizers. 

In $\mathbb{Z}_{4q}$,
$f = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbb{1}_{0} + \mathbb{1}_{q})$ 
has equal-entropy symmetrizers 
$f_{-} = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbb{1}_{0} + \mathbb{1}_{3q})$
and
$g = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbb{1}_{0} + \mathbb{1}_{2q})$. 

Note that $h \in \Sym(f)$ if and only if for all $s \in [4q]$
\begin{equation}
h(s) + h(s-q) = h(-s) + h(-s-q) 
\end{equation}
so that if $h(s) > \frac{1}{2}$ for some $s$, we have 
\[ \frac{1}{2} < h(s) \le h(-s) + h(-s-q) \]
and therefore 
\[ 1 < h(s) + h(-s) + h(-s-q) \]
so that either $s = -s$ (so $s = 0$) or $s = -s-q$ (so $2s = q$). 
Since $2$ does not divide $q$, the latter cannot happen and we need only consider $s=0$.
Evaluating (equation eq:symm_4q_special of the paper) at $s=q$ yields
\[ h(q) + h(0) = h(-q) + h(-2q) \]
so that 
\[ \frac{1}{2} < h(0) \le h(-q) + h(-2q) \]
and since $0$, $-q$, and $-2q$ are distinct modulo $4q$, we obtain 
\[ 1 < h(0) + h(-q) + h(-2q) \le \sum_x h(x) = 1 , \]
a contradiction. 
Thus $h \le \frac{1}{2}$ everywhere and
\[ H(h) = \sum_{x}h(x) \log_2\bigg(\frac{1}{h(x)}\bigg) \ge \sum_{x} h(x) = 1 = H(f), \]
so our $f$ is symmetrization resistant. 

\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem eq:symm_4q_special of arXiv:2607.29020

body:
On a finite connected ferromagnetic Ising graph at zero external field with positive couplings, let G_ij=<sigma_i sigma_j> and U4(x1,x2,x3,x4) be the fourth spin moment minus its three Gaussian pair products. Sample two independent random currents with parity source sets x1 triangle x2 and x3 triangle x4 (coincident endpoints cancel modulo two). Then -U4(x1,x2,x3,x4)=2 G_12 G_34 times the probability that the source components of x1 and x3 connect in the union of these two currents. This is the original two-current law; the one-sourced-plus-one-sourceless hitting identity uses a different law. A lower bound for an augmented four-current event alone does not lower-bound this original-current probability.
Finite connected graph with strictly positive ferromagnetic couplings
Zero external field and independent currents with the stated parity source sets
Repeated marked vertices are interpreted modulo two for source sets
title: Four-spin Ursell function under two original sourced currents

body:
[Proposition 19 (Occupation moment measures) of arXiv:2607.24561, 'Range convergence and sharp one-arm asymptotics\\for the critical percolation cluster in h'] For every $k\ge1$ and $\phi_1,\dots,\phi_k\in\Ccg$,
\begin{equation}
\bN\Bigl[\prod_{i=1}^k\mu(\phi_i)\Bigr]
=\gamma^{\,k-1}\sum_{T\in\T_k}\int_{(\R^d)^k}
I_T(z_1,\dots,z_k)\prod_{i=1}^k\phi_i(z_i)\,dz_i ,
\end{equation}
the integral converging absolutely. In particular the identity holds
for all $\phi_i\in\Ccg$, not only nonnegative ones.
Equivalently, as locally finite measures off the diagonals,
\[\bN\left[\mu(dz_1)\cdots\mu(dz_k)\right]
=\gamma^{k-1}\sum_{T\in\T_k}I_T(\vec z)\,d\vec z.\]

body:
[Prop 16 of arXiv:2603.28702, 'Distribution of the magnetization of the critical Ising model on sparse random graphs'] Let $\mu$ be a spin system on a $G\sim G_{n,d}$, with a finite spin set $\mathcal{X}$ and weights $(\overline{\psi},\psi)$. Assume that $\psi>0$. For a given vertex-empirical distribution $\bar{h}$ such that $\bar{h}(x)>0$ for any $x\in\mathcal{X}$, let 
$$B_{\bar{h}}=\left\{h\in[0,1]^{\R^{\mathcal{X}^2}}:h(x,y)=h(y,x)\ \forall x,y\ \ \text{and}\ \ \SL{y\in\mathcal{X}}h(x,y)=\bar{h}(x)\ \forall x\right\}$$ 
and $\Phi_{\bar{h}}:B_{\bar{h}}\to\R$ be the function
$$\Phi_{\bar{h}}(h):=H(h)+\langle h,\log\psi\rangle.$$
Then, the maximizer of $\Phi_{\bar{h}}$ is an edge-empirical distribution $h^*$ of the form
\begin{equation}
h^*(x,y)\varpropto q(x)q(y)\psi(x,y),
\end{equation}
for some $q:\mathcal{X}\to(0,\infty)$ such that $h^*\in B_{\overline{h}}$.

[Theorem 88 (Saturation amplification through the native kernel) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Assume that a replicable grade-one saturation source exists.  Then every
nonzero stable natural exact-layer family
$G^{\mathrm{Schur}}_{\lambda,n,r}$ has minimax-sharp spectral depth $r$ in
the sense of \Cref{cc:gen-definition-minimax-depth}.  The Hall template,
cut, compressions, marker increments, and algebraic coefficient are fixed by
the exact layer before the spectral window.  For each requested window only
the finite dimensions of the $r$ source cells are enlarged.

body:
[Theorem thm:covering-regularity of arXiv:2608.21805, 'Logarithmic derivatives of variational and singular stochastic partial differential equati'] Under Assumptions (ass:LR of the paper), (ass:diff2 of the paper), (ass:SC of the paper), and (ass:nondeg of the paper), the covering vector field $v_h$ belongs to $L^2(\Omega; H_W)$ and satisfies the covering condition (equation eq:covering-condition of the paper). Moreover, $v_h \in \operatorname{Dom}(\delta_U)$ in each of the following cases:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
  \item \textup{(Linear drift with state-independent diffusion)} $\mathcal{A}(t,u) = -Au$ is linear and $\mathcal{B}(t,u) = \mathcal{B}(t)$ does not depend on $u$. Then $Y(t,r) = S(t-r)$ is the (deterministic) semigroup generated by $A$, the Malliavin covariance $\gamma_t$ is deterministic, and $v_h(r) = \mathcal{B}(r)^*S(t-r)^*\gamma_t^{\dagger}h$ is a deterministic function of $r$, hence adapted. The Skorokhod integral reduces to the It\^o integral $\delta_U(v_h) = \int_0^t \ip{v_h(r)}{\mathrm{d}W(r)}_U$. This case requires no differentiability beyond what is needed for well-posedness.
  \item \textup{(Second-order differentiability + fixed-Tikhonov substitution regularity)} The full Assumption~(ass:nondeg of the paper) (including the Cameron--Martin compatibility clause~(iii)) holds with the exponent $q$ of clause~(ii) chosen in $(2, \infty]$, and Assumption~(ass:SC-raised of the paper) holds at target $q^* = q/(q-2)$ (with $q^* = 1$ when $q = \infty$), and the fixed-Tikhonov substitution regularity hypothesis~(hyp:iii-F-prime of the paper) of Theorem~(thm:tikhonov-trace of the paper) holds for the SPDE-side covering data $(\mathcal{T}, \gamma_F, h) = (\Phi, \gamma_t, h)$. SPDE-level sufficient conditions for~(hyp:iii-F-prime of the paper) (in particular, automatic verification via the symmetric H\"older estimate when $q \leq 3$ on the H\"older triangle) are recorded in Remark~(rem:covering-iiiF-SPDE of the paper).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 1 (Trail) of arXiv:2511.18216, 'Classical localization problem: a survey'] A \emph{trail} on $G$ is a finite sequence of edges
\[
  \gamma = (e_0,e_1,\dots,e_{\ell-1}), \qquad e_i\in E,
\]
such that:
\begin{itemize}
  \item the terminal vertex of $e_i$ equals the initial vertex of $e_{i+1}$ for
        $0\le i\le \ell-2$;
  \item no directed edge is traversed more than once, i.e.\ $e_i\neq e_j$ for
        $i\neq j$.
\end{itemize}
We call $\gamma$ a \emph{closed trail rooted at} $e$ if $e_0=e_{\ell-1}=e$, and an \emph{open trail from $e$ to $e'$} if $e_0=e$, $e_{\ell-1}=e'$ and $e_i\neq e_j$ for $0\le i<j\le \ell-1$.

body: In combinatorics, two Latin squares of the same size (order) are said to be orthogonal if when superimposed the ordered paired entries in the positions are all distinct. A set of Latin squares, all of the same order, all pairs of which are orthogonal is called a set of mutually orthogonal Latin squares. This concept of orthogonality in combinatorics is strongly related to the concept of blocking in statistics, which ensures that independent variables are truly independent with no hidden confounding correlations. "Orthogonal" is thus synonymous with "independent" in that knowing one variable's value gives no further information about another variable's likely value.
title: Mutually orthogonal Latin squares

[Proposition 38 (projective normal form) of arXiv:2609.03736, '2609.03736'] Let $K,L\succeq0$ on $\mathcal H$ and $\tr(K+L)=1$.  There are a Hilbert
space $\widetilde{\mathcal H}$ of dimension at most
$2\dim\mathcal H$, an isometry $V:\mathcal H\to\widetilde{\mathcal H}$,
a state $G$ on $\widetilde{\mathcal H}$, and an orthogonal projection $P$
such that
\begin{equation}
 VKV^*=G^{1/2}PG^{1/2},\qquad
 VLV^*=G^{1/2}(I-P)G^{1/2}.
 
\end{equation}

pair by the right side of Equation~\eqref{eq:projective-normal-form}.

Let the nonnegative stochastic sequence $X_n$ satisfy \eqref{1} and \eqref{2}, and, as $x\to\infty$,
\[

Then the stochastic sequence is recurrent. If instead for some $\theta>1$ and almost all large $x$,
\[
\underline{\mu}(x)\geq\frac{\theta\overline{v}(x)}{2x},
\]

Let S:{-1,1}^k->R^D be a deterministic finite-coin sampler, k>=1, with ||S(b)||<=B for every b, B>0. Let 0<a<1 and r>0. For independent standard Gaussians Z in R^k and W in R^D put h=a/k, c(z)=min(1,min_i |z_i|/h), F(z)=c(z)S(sign z), and M=Law(F(Z)+r W). On coordinate hyperplanes set F=0.

Then M has a positive smooth density,

TV(M,Law(S(Bits)+r W))<=a,
C_LS(M)<=B^2 k^2/a^2+r^2.

The convention is Ent(f^2)<=2 C_LS E||grad f||^2. If E[S(Bits)S(Bits)^T]<=K I, then Cov(M)<=(K+r^2)I. If S,k,B,1/a,1/r are polynomially computable/bounded in D and S runs in polynomial time, this is an explicit generative prior with a polynomial LSI certificate. The final Gaussian is a genuine Gaussian, not a finite-grid output.

## Proof

Within an orthant S(sign z) is constant and c is 1/h-Lipschitz, so F is B/h-Lipschitz. Across two orthants choose a sign-changing coordinate j. Then

||F(z)-F(z')||<=B(c(z)+c(z'))
 <=(B/h)(|z_j|+|z'_j|)
 <=(B/h)||z-z'||.

The bound c(z)<=|z_j|/h holds even when c(z)=1. Boundary points cause no exception because F=0. Thus the Lipschitz property is global across the decoder's discontinuities.

The map (z,w)->F(z)+r w is sqrt(B^2/h^2+r^2)-Lipschitz. Pulling a test function back to its standard Gaussian input and applying Gaussian LSI gives the claimed constant by the chain rule. Nondegenerate Gaussian convolution gives the positive smooth density.

The polynomial output bound B and coin count k are essential for the polynomial certificate. The multiplier must vanish whenever any coordinate crosses zero; separately smoothing individual Boolean bits does not control an arbitrary decoder S. [Thm commutation_relation_u of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] In the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$, let $n$ radial SLEs start at $e^{i\theta_1}, e^{i\theta_2}, \ldots, e^{i\theta_n} \in \partial \mathbb{D}$, with a marked interior point \( u \neq 0 \).

\begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] For \( u = e^{i v} \), let the infinitesimal diffusion generators be
    \[
    \mathcal{M}_i = \frac{\kappa}{2} \partial_{ii} + b_i(\boldsymbol{\theta}, u) \partial_i + \sum_{j \neq i} \cot\left(\frac{\theta_j - \theta_i}{2}\right) \partial_j + \cot\left(\frac{v - \theta_i}{2}\right) \partial_v + \cot\left(\frac{\overline{v} - \theta_i}{2}\right) \overline{\partial}_v.
    \]
    If the $n$ SLEs locally commute, the generators satisfy:
    \[
    [\mathcal{M}_i, \mathcal{M}_j] = \frac{1}{\sin^2\left(\frac{\theta_j - \theta_i}{2}\right)} (\mathcal{M}_j - \mathcal{M}_i).
    \]
    There exists a partition function \(\psi(\boldsymbol{\theta}, u)\) such that the drift term \( b_i(\boldsymbol{\theta}, u) \) is given by
    \[
    b_i(\boldsymbol{\theta}, u) = \kappa \partial_i \log \psi,
    \]
    and \(\psi\) satisfies the null vector equations:
    \[
    \frac{\kappa}{2} \partial_{ii} \psi + \sum_{j \neq i} \frac{2}{\theta_j - \theta_i} \partial_i \psi + \frac{2}{v - \theta_i} \partial_v \psi + \frac{2}{\overline{v} - \theta_i} \overline{\partial}_v \psi + \left[\left(1 - \frac{6}{\kappa}\right) \sum_{j \neq i} \frac{1}{(\theta_j - \theta_i)^2} + h_i(\theta_i, u)\right] \psi = 0.
    \]

    \item[(ii)] By analyzing the asymptotics of adjacent points \( \theta_i \) and \( \theta_{i+1} \), we deduce that \( h_i(\theta, u) = h_{i+1}(\theta, u) \). If all points are consecutive, there exists a common function \( h(\theta, u) \) such that
    \[
    h(\theta, u) = h_1(\theta, u) = \cdots = h_n(\theta, u).
    \]

\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Commutation Relations for \( u \in \mathbb{D} \)

For continuous F this is F(t)>=(n-1)(1-F(1-t)). If the density is continuous at both endpoints, f(0)>=(n-1)f(1). Reflect for the upper boundary, or rescale from [a,b].
As stated in the linked proof

Status: proof (unaudited). Elementary necessary condition; novelty not asserted.

Let n>=2, and let X have a probability law supported on [0,1] with mean 1/n. If it is n-completely mixable, there are X_1,...,X_n with this same marginal and sum 1 almost surely. For every 0<t<=1/2,

    (n-1) P(X>1-t) <= P(X<t).

Proof. Define A_i={X_i>1-t}. At most one A_i occurs: two such coordinates would have sum strictly greater than 2(1-t)>=1. On A_i, the sum of all remaining nonnegative coordinates is 1-X_i<t, so each of those n-1 coordinates is <t. Let H=sum_i 1_A_i and L=sum_i 1_{X_i<t}. The pathwise inequality L>=(n-1)H follows, including outcomes with H=0. Taking expectations and using identical marginals gives n P(X<t)>=(n-1)n P(X>1-t). Divide by n. No independence or exchangeability is required.

For a continuous CDF F this is F(t)>=(n-1)(1-F(1-t)). On [a,b] with mean a+(b-a)/n, substitute (X-a)/(b-a). At the upper boundary reflect first.

If the density is continuous at 0 and 1, divide by t and let t decrease to zero to obtain f(0)>=(n-1)f(1). More generally, if P(X<t)~A t^p and P(X>1-t)~B t^q with A,B,p,q positive, then p<=q, and p=q forces A>=(n-1)B. Indeed p>q makes the ratio of the left probability to the right tend to zero, contradicting the bound; equal exponents give the coefficient inequality.

Hardest unresolved piece: conditions sufficient for a general unimodal boundary-mean law. body: [Definition def:zero-crossing of arXiv:2411.01364, 'Global Dynamics of Granular Media Equations via Stochastic Order'] The zero-crossing number of a continuous function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, denoted by $Z(f)$, is the maximal integer $N$ such that, there exists an increasing sequence $x_1<x_2<\cdots<x_N<x_{N+1}$ satisfying $f(x_n)f(x_{n+1})<0$ for all $n=1,2,\dots,N$.

[Definition 3 (Jump Matrix) of arXiv:2606.25810, 'Spectral Collapse Under Geometric Alignment of Extreme Events'] Let there be \(m_n\) extreme events, each represented by a jump vector \(v_{n,k} \in \mathbb{R}^n\) with magnitude \(\theta_{n,k} \ge 0\). Define

\[
J_n = \sum_{k=1}^{m_n} \theta_{n,k} v_{n,k} v_{n,k}^\top, \quad \|v_{n,k}\| = 1.
\]

Each term \(\theta_{n,k} v_{n,k} v_{n,k}^\top\) is a rank-1 matrix. The sum \(J_n\) has rank at most \(m_n\).
title: Jump Matrix

For each fixed polynomial P(d)>=1 bounding queries per round and inverse-polynomial score tolerance e0>0, for sufficiently large d there is a sampler-independent distribution over full-dimensional axis-aligned boxes K^theta in the unit ball, and one jointly measurable fixed oracle per uniform box law, such that E||oracle_sigma-score_sigma||^2<=e0^2/sigma^2 at every sigma>0. Any randomized algorithm making at most P(d) queries per adaptive round, at arbitrary points and positive noise levels, with fewer than d rounds has TV(output,Unif(K^theta))>=0.9 on at least 0.9 of instances. Only the selected interval labels are hidden; all candidate intervals are public. The target here is the unsmoothed box law, and no pointwise oracle error promise is imposed.
Fixed polynomial per-round budget and inverse-polynomial accuracy
Distributional score-error model, all sigma>0
No supplied hidden-instance information beyond stated public parameters and oracle

Independently checked by w389; draft concept only. If all weights on Z^2 satisfy0<a<=t_e<=b<infinity, then global distances between any u,v in B_n equal distances computed in B_R, R=n+ceil(4bn/a). A coordinate path costs at most4bn; every no-dearer competitor has at most floor(4bn/a) edges and stays in B_R. The finitely many such paths attain the infimum. Thus global root-crossing E_n uses only edges in B_R. Computing in B_n itself can misclassify a geodesic: an explicit positive-weight example has a B_1 minimizing path through0 costing20, but an outside ten-edge detour costs10.
Deterministically bounded positive weights
Global distances
No iid or uniqueness requirement
title: Deterministic localization preserves global distances

body: [Definition LCK-def of arXiv:2608.30747, 'Compact homogeneous complex manifolds'] A Hermitian structure $(J,g)$ is called {\it locally conformally K\"ahler} (LCK for short) if  $d\omega=\theta\wedge\omega$ for some $1$-form $\theta$ such that $d\theta=0$.  If in addition, $\nabla^g\theta=0$, then $(J,g)$ is said to be {\it Vaisman}.
title: Definition LCK-def of arXiv:2608.30747

[Theorem thm:composition of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] $\rho_{v}\circ\rho_{w} = \rho_{(A_{v}\circ A_{w})'}$, the prime
		now denoting the derivative alone, so
		$w \mapsto A_{w}$ is an isomorphism from $(\{\rho_{w}\},\circ)$ onto
		the monoid of absolutely continuous nondecreasing surjections of
		$[0,1]$ under composition. In particular the $n$-fold iterate is again
		a derangetropy operator,
		\begin{equation}
			\rho_{w}^{\,n}[f]
			= \big(A_{w}^{\circ n}\big)'(F)\,f
			= f\prod_{j=0}^{n-1} w\big(A_{w}^{\circ j}(F)\big).
			
		\end{equation}

[Lemma 58 (Flattening bounds for the localized wave--Klein--Gordon kernel) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $L\sim N$, $Q\le c_{\mathrm{ap}}N$, and $M\lesssim N$.  If
$F_1,\ldots,F_4$ denote
the flattenings in \eqref{eq:flattening-orientations}, then for every
$2\le r_0<\infty$,
\begin{align}
 \|F_1\|_{\mathfrak S_{r_0}}
 &\lesssim |A_N|C_\kappa N^{3/2}Q^{3/2}M^{3/r_0},
 \\
 \|F_2\|_{\mathfrak S_{r_0}}
 &\lesssim |A_N|C_\kappa N^{3/2}M^{3/2}Q^{3/r_0},
 \\
 \|F_3\|_{\mathfrak S_{r_0}}+\|F_4\|_{\mathfrak S_{r_0}}
 &\lesssim |A_N|C_\kappa Q^{3/2}M^{3/2}N^{3/r_0},
 
\end{align}
where
\[
 C_\kappa:=\|\kappa_1\|_{L^1}
 \bigl(\|\kappa_2\|_{L^1}+\|\kappa_2\|_{L^2}\bigr).
\]
The estimates are uniform over all measurable amplitudes $\mathfrak m_z$ with
$|\mathfrak m_z|\le1$; no frequency-derivative bound on $\mathfrak m_z$ is required.

[Lemma l:stable.limit.thm.D of arXiv:2601.12677, 'Stable and Fréchet limit theorem for subgraph functionals in the hyperbolic random geometr'] $(i)$ If $\frac{1}{2} (k-1)<\alpha< k-1$, then as $n\to\infty$, it holds that 
$$
\sup_{0\le t\le 1}\bigg|  \frac{1}{a_{k,n}} \Big( \sum_{i=1}^{[N_n t]}\mathcal D_{k,n}(X_i) -[N_n t] \mathbb{E} \big[\mathcal D_{k,n}(X_1) \big]\Big) - \frac{1}{a_{k,n}} \Big( \sum_{i=1}^{[N_n t]}\mu_{k,n}(U_i) -[N_n t]  \mathbb{E} \big[  \mu_{k,n}(U_1) \big]\Big)\bigg| \stackrel{\mathbb{P}}{\to} 0. 
$$
$(ii)$ If $\frac{1}{2}<\alpha<\frac{1}{2} (k-1)$, then as $n\to\infty$, 
$$
\sup_{0\le t\le 1}\bigg|  \frac{1}{a_{k,n}}  \sum_{i=1}^{[N_n t]}\mathcal D_{k,n}(X_i) - \frac{1}{a_{k,n}} \sum_{i=1}^{[N_n t]}\mu_{k,n}(U_i) \bigg|\stackrel{\mathbb{P}}{\to} 0. 
$$

[Proposition limmeas of arXiv:2411.04795, 'Metastable Distributions of Semi-Markov Processes'] Suppose that conditions (a)-(f) are satisfied.
Let $x \in S_i$ where $1 \le i \le M.$ Consider the associated  sequence of time scales  $0  =  \mathfrak{t}_0^{\varepsilon}(i) \ll \mathfrak{t}_1^{\varepsilon}(i) \ll \mathfrak{t}_2^{\varepsilon}(i) \ll \dots  \ll \mathfrak{t}_{n(i)}^{\varepsilon}(i) = \infty $ introduced in Theorem~(prelimt2 of the paper). 
Suppose that either

(1) For each $i$, $T^\varepsilon(x, S_j)/\tau^\varepsilon_i$ converges weakly for some $x \in S_i$ and some $j$ (the limiting distribution does not have atoms due to (e) and does not depend on $x$ or $j$ due to (d)), or

(2)  For each $i$, 
 $\lim \limits_{\varepsilon \to 0 } ({ t(\varepsilon) }/\tau^\varepsilon_i) \in \{0, \infty\} $.
\\
Suppose that the function
$t(\varepsilon)$  satisfies, $$\lim \limits_{\varepsilon \to 0 } \dfrac{ t(\varepsilon) }{\mathfrak{t}_{k}^{\varepsilon}(i)} = C \in (0, \infty) $$ for some $k \geq 1$ (this is only possible with $k \geq 2$ if the second assumption holds). Then there exists a probability measure $\mu_{i,k,C}$ such that 
\begin{equation}

\lim \limits_{\varepsilon \to 0} \mathbb P \left({X_{t(\varepsilon)}^{x, \varepsilon} \in S_j }\right) = \mu_{i,k,C}(j)  
\end{equation}
uniformly in $x \in S_i$ for every $j \in \{1, \dots, M\}.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\mathbb{P}(\Lambda\in \{0,\star\}) = 0.

[Definition 2 (Finitary coding / finitary factor) of arXiv:2602.14618, 'Finitary coding and Gaussian concentration\\ for random fields'] With the notation introduced above, a coding map $\varphi$ is said to be
\emph{finitary} if $r\!_\varphi(x)<\infty$ for $\mu$-almost every $x$, or equivalently,
if $r\!_\varphi(X)<\infty$ almost surely.
In this case, $Y=\varphi(X)$ is called a \emph{finitary coding} of $X$,
and equivalently the shift dynamical system
$\big(B^{\Zd},(S^j)_{j\in\Zd},\nu\big)$ is called a \emph{finitary factor} of
$\big(A^{\Zd},(T^j)_{j\in\Zd},\mu\big)$.

[Theorem 11 (Bound on the log-pdf ratio) of arXiv:2606.16018, 'A non-asymptotic bound on the TV distance between a \\Wishart matrix and an appropriately '] Let \mA be a psd matrix.
    Let \(f_{\rm shifted}\) be the pdf associated with the shifted GOE matrix, and let \(f_{\rm wishart}\) be the Wishart pdf.
    Then, for any PSD matrix \(\mA \succeq \frac k2 \mI\), the log pdf ratio \(\alpha(\mA) \defeq \log(f_{\rm shifted}(\mA) / f_{\rm wishart}(\mA))\) satisfies
    \[
        \alpha(\mA)
        \lesssim \frac{n}{k}\tr(\mA-k\mI)
    	- \frac{n}{k^2}\tr((\mA-k\mI)^2)
    	- \frac{1}{k^2}\tr((\mA-k\mI)^3)
    	+ \frac{k}{k^4}\tr((\mA-k\mI)^4)
        + \frac{n^3}{k}.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:consecutive-pass of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Use the notation of (lem:typed-pass of the paper).  Let
$\mathsf V_1,\ldots,\mathsf V_s$ be typed passive singleton multipliers,
possibly with passive representation amplification, and put
\[
 B_j=\mathscr G^*\mathsf V_j\mathscr G.
\]
Then, with the same unit-circle parameter in every residual gap,
\[
 \boxed{
 \|XR_zB_1R_zB_2\cdots R_zB_sR_zY^*\|
 \le b_Xb_Y\left(\frac C{\sqrt n}\right)^s.}
\tag{3.2.10q$_{9}$}
\]
The estimate keeps the entire consecutive run and its shared resolvent
intact.  It is stable under ancillary amplification and prescribed-gate
terminal gluing.

[Proposition pure_diffusion_plaplace of arXiv:2604.25851, '{Non-uniqueness of nonlinear Markov processes in the sense of McKean associated with parab'] Let $p>2$. For every $z\in \mathbb{R}^d$, there exists a unique weak solution $X^{1,z}$ to the MV-SDE (equation p_lap_pure_diff_sde of the paper) with one-dimensional time marginals given by the Barenblatt solution (equation eq:barenblatt_solution_plaplace of the paper), i.e., $\mathcal{L}(X^{1,z}_t) = u^z(t,x)dx$, $t>0$, and $\mathcal{L}(X^{1,z}_0) = \delta_z$. 
        \\
        Furthermore, the corresponding family of solution path laws $\{\mathbb{V}^{1,z}\}_{z \in \mathbb{R}^d}$, $\mathbb{V}^{1,z} := \mathcal{L}(X^{1,z})$, is a nonlinear Markov core for $\{u^z\}_{z\in \mathbb{R}^d}$, which is uniquely determined by  $\{u^z\}_{z\in \mathbb{R}^d}$ and (equation p_lap_pure_diff_sde of the paper).
title: Proposition pure_diffusion_plaplace of arXiv:2604.25851

[Corollary 16 (Mean and variance for inversions) of arXiv:2606.18047, 'Analysis of the asymmetric shelf shuffle'] Fix $n, m \geq 1$ and $p\in (0, 1)$.
Let $\pi\sim\nu^{(p)}_{n,m}$ and set $I_n=\operatorname{inv}(\pi)$ and $\dd=2p-1$.  Then,
\[
\E[I_n]=\binom{n}{2}\left(\frac12-\frac{\dd}{2m}\right),
\]
and
\[
\Var(I_n)=\frac{n(n-1)(2n+5)}{72}
+\frac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{18m^2}
-\frac{\dd^2 n(n-1)(2n-1)}{24m^2}.
\]

body: [Proposition prop cv crossing segments of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple C'] The number $N^\kappa$ of crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^\kappa_A$ converges in law as $\kappa \uparrow 4$ to the number $N^4$ of crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^4_A$. More precisely, for all $\kappa_n \uparrow 4$ there exists an ordering $\eta_1^n, \ldots, \eta^n_{N^{\kappa_n}}$ of the crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^{\kappa_n}_A$ for which they converge in law to $\eta_1, \ldots, \eta_{N^4}$, which are the crossings of $A$ by loops in $\Gamma^4_A$, with respect to the Hausdorff topology.

Own-work draft. Status: proof (unaudited), T232-w704-C002 v2. No reviewer PASS and no established novelty/priority. Conditional dimension-two corollary: let C(P)=||PX-Y||_F^2/(2N), XX^T positive definite, min(input dimension,output dimension)=2 and rank of M=YX^T(XX^T)^(-1) equal to two. Assume arrival at a globally best rank-one critical product and the exact strong relative Gram alignment in C001. The selected canonical width-two local escape is a complete saddle-to-global-minimum connection: its factors have finite limits at both ends, and its forward product limit is M. Original factors converge to this path modulo one hidden orthogonal rotation per alpha on compact shifted-time intervals. Remaining gap/scope: Reviewer audit required. This is a conditional corollary from established ingredients; specialist novelty/priority is not established. Gaussian alignment and the general m,n>=3 second step remain open.
Full row rank X
min(m,n)=2; rank M=2; hidden width w>=2
Arrival Gram limit Z1 represents a globally best rank-one product
C001 strong alignment liminf (v^T Zalpha v)/||Zalpha-Z1||_F>0 at nonnegative arrival times
Existing Li-Luo-Lyu conditional local escape theorem; no Gaussian alignment claim

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:82d204866c9de546a5e644cda77c2c41837d0caad12cd981f4e6f519f060ff48","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/82/82d204866c9de546a5e644cda77c2c41837d0caad12cd981f4e6f519f060ff48.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:cdffb74e247ea38af9a95c8f87f6b93e9ec3c9eb3e821280b787574508c2e968","bundle_entry_key":"conditional-endpoint-two","bundle_id":"population.t232-conditional-endpoint-and-variational-transport-20261020","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"deep linear networks; saddle-to-saddle gradient flow","draft":"w704/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.deep_linear_networks:t232-conditional-dimension-two-endpoint","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T232 target 1: conditional complete second step when min(m,n)=2

Status: proof draft, independent review pending; a corollary of existing local escape theory. No novelty or unconditional Gaussian result is claimed.

## Statement
Let X in R^(n x N) have full row rank, Y in R^(m x N), and min(m,n)=2. Let C(P)=||PX-Y||_F^2/(2N), with its unique unconstrained minimizer M=YX^T(XX^T)^(-1) of rank two. Let w>=2 and the asymmetric factors obey B'=-G A^T, A'=-B^T G, G=grad C(BA). Let P1 be a globally best rank-at-most-one product, with a corresponding critical rank-one factor theta1=(b1,a1^T); put u1=(b1;a1), Z1=u1u1^T. Assume that this is the rank-one endpoint being approached by the given initialization family. Use the block lift, residual singular vector v, and the strong arrival-alignment hypothesis of C001. In particular there are nonnegative arrival times T_alpha with Z_alpha(T_alpha)->Z1 and
  liminf a_alpha/||Z_alpha(T_alpha)-Z1||_F>0,
where a_alpha=v^T Z_alpha(T_alpha)v. Then the known canonical local escape orbit selected at the time shift log(1/a_alpha)/(2s) has a width-two factor realization whose product tends to M as t->infinity. Its factor path tends to a finite critical width-two parameter theta2 representing M, hence a global (in particular width-two local) minimum. The original family converges to that width-two factor path after a hidden orthogonal rotation depending on alpha but fixed in time, on each fixed compact interval of shifted time.

No hypothesis that XX^T is isotropic or commutes with the target is used. No Gaussian arrival-alignment assertion is made. The theorem conditions on the rank-one arrival and exact strong Gram alignment, just as the existing local theorem does.

## The single hardest piece still open beyond this conditional statement
For the actual small Gaussian initialization, prove the required quantitative arrival alignment (or replace it by a weaker hypothesis proved to suffice). In dimensions at least three on both sides, identifying the forward rank-two local-minimum endpoint also needs more than the energy argument below.

## 1. Existing local result and nontriviality
C001 specializes Section 3 and Theorem G.2 of Li-Luo-Lyu, arXiv:2012.09839. Its local complete-extension argument handles the source's all-real-time convention. The selected Gram path Z*(t) has rank at most two and tends to Z1 as t->minus infinity. The canonical simple-top escape is nonconstant: the local estimates in Appendix E, Lemmas E.3-E.6, compare the shifted orbit at sufficiently negative t with a nonzero top eigenmode of size exp(2s t), with quadratic error. Thus that mode cannot disappear identically in the limit. This is the outgoing orbit, rather than the constant stationary solution.

For this data class s is automatically simple and positive when P1 is critical and nonglobal. Indeed G1 a1=0 and G1^T b1=0, with both b1 and a1 nonzero (M rank two excludes the zero product as a best rank-one solution). Consequently rank G1<=min(m-1,n-1)=1. Since XX^T is positive definite, G1=0 would imply P1=M, which contradicts their ranks. Thus rank G1=1 and its positive top singular value is simple. Every cancellation here uses nonzero b1,a1 and positive-definite XX^T.

## 2. A factor realization, strict descent and rank two
At any fixed time, factor the PSD matrix Z*(0)=U*(0)U*(0)^T using at most two columns. Solve U'=-H(Z)U, equivalently the asymmetric two-factor flow. Uniqueness of the induced Gram ODE identifies UU^T with Z*. Backwards on every finite interval the prescribed continuous H(Z*(t)) defines a linear factor ODE, so this realization covers the complete Gram orbit. The known rank-at-most-two Gram constraint is preserved. To check the backward PARAMETER endpoint as well, the canonical local estimates give ||Z*(t)-Z1||_F=O(exp(2s t)) as t->minus infinity. Let H1=H(Z1). The factor norm is bounded there since ||U||_F^2=tr Z*. Since H1 Z1=0,
  ||H1 U||_F^2=tr(H1^2 Z*)=tr(H1^2(Z*-Z1))=O(exp(2s t)).
Also H(Z*)-H1=O(exp(2s t)) because H is smooth. Therefore ||Uprime||_F=O(exp(s t)), integrable at minus infinity. Hence U*(t) converges to a finite factor Uminus with Uminus Uminus^T=Z1. This is precisely the width-one saddle inclusion up to a single hidden orthogonal rotation.

Along factor flow,
  d C(BA)/dt = -||GA^T||_F^2-||B^TG||_F^2.
A nonconstant gradient trajectory cannot have a stationary time, by uniqueness. Its loss is therefore strictly decreasing; as t->minus infinity it tends to C(P1). Hence C(B(t)A(t))<C(P1) for every finite t. Since P1 is globally best among all rank-at-most-one products, rank(B(t)A(t))>=2. Combining this with the width-two realization gives rank two at every finite time.

## 3. Forward boundedness, with the constants and dimensions shown
For any forward factor trajectory set P=B^TB, Q=AA^T, K=P-Q (these are w-by-w matrices). Differentiate to see K'=0. Exact trace expansion gives
  ||P||_F^2+||Q||_F^2=2||BA||_F^2+||K||_F^2.
By nonincreasing loss and the triangle inequality, ||BA X||_F is uniformly bounded forward. If lambda>0 is the smallest eigenvalue of XX^T, then
  lambda ||BA||_F^2 <= ||BA X||_F^2.
So BA is bounded. Cauchy-Schwarz on the 2w nonnegative eigenvalues of P,Q then yields
  ||B||_F^2+||A||_F^2 = tr(P)+tr(Q)
  <= sqrt(2w) sqrt(2||BA||_F^2+||K||_F^2).
This bounds both factors uniformly. The polynomial vector field cannot blow up in a finite positive time while its state is bounded, so the forward solution is global. This proof does not assume initial balance K=0.

## 4. Why boundedness gives a stationary limit here
The factor loss L(B,A)=C(BA) is polynomial, hence real analytic. We spell out the standard analytic-gradient argument rather than infer convergence from boundedness alone (compare the analytic argument in Li-Luo-Lyu, proof of Theorem 5.8, PDF p.32).

Since L decreases and is bounded below, L(t)->ell. Boundedness gives a cluster point z0, with L(z0)=ell. Moreover integral_0^infinity ||grad L||^2 dt=L(0)-ell is finite. On the compact forward orbit the Hessian and gradient are bounded, so ||grad L||^2 is uniformly continuous in time. A nonnegative uniformly continuous integrable function tends to zero (otherwise disjoint fixed-width intervals around its positive peaks force a divergent integral). Thus grad L(z0)=0.

The analytic gradient inequality supplies c>0, theta in [1/2,1) and a neighbourhood of z0 on which ||grad L(z)||>=c |L(z)-ell|^theta. Write e=L-ell>=0 along this trajectory. If e ever reaches zero, energy monotonicity makes the remaining trajectory stationary. Otherwise, while inside that neighbourhood,
  -d(e^(1-theta))/dt
  =(1-theta)e^(-theta)||grad L||^2
  >=c(1-theta)||grad L||.
Choose a sufficiently late cluster time with z(t_k) arbitrarily close to z0 and e(t_k) small enough that e(t_k)^(1-theta)/(c(1-theta)) is less than the distance to the boundary of a fixed smaller ball. The displayed length bound forbids exit from that ball, and bounds the remaining arc length. The trajectory is Cauchy and converges to z0. All uses of theta require theta<1, and no division by e is made in the e=0 case. Hence B(t)->B2, A(t)->A2, a finite stationary factor pair.

## 5. The endpoint is the global regression minimizer
Fix any finite t0. Monotonicity gives C(B2A2)<=C(B(t0)A(t0))<C(P1). Thus the ENDPOINT product also has rank two; the strict inequality is inherited from the fixed finite t0, not from taking a limit of merely pointwise strict inequalities without a uniform margin.

If m=2, rank(B2A2)=2 forces B2 to have full row rank two. Its transpose is injective, so stationarity B2^T G2=0 forces every column of G2 to be zero. If n=2, A2 has full column rank two, so stationarity G2 A2^T=0 forces G2=0 instead. Either case gives
  G2=(B2A2 XX^T-YX^T)/N=0,
and XX^T invertible yields B2A2=M. This is a global minimum of C and of the width-two factor loss.

## 6. Recovering parameters modulo one hidden rotation per alpha
Gram convergence alone must not be mistaken for convergence of the original factors. Here it suffices as follows. At shifted time zero, choose two linearly independent row vectors of the limiting rank-two Gram factor; their 2-by-2 Gram determinant is strictly positive. The corresponding rows of U_alpha remain independent for all sufficiently small alpha. Apply Gram-Schmidt to these two rows to obtain the first two columns of a hidden orthogonal basis Q_alpha, completing it arbitrarily. The coefficients of every other row on those first two basis vectors converge, because they are obtained from converging Gram inner products and strictly nonzero limiting pivot norms. The squared norm in the orthogonal complement is the Schur-complement residual and tends to zero, since the limiting Gram matrix has rank two. Therefore U_alpha(shift)Q_alpha converges to a width-two realization with zero extra columns.

Keep this SAME Q_alpha at all times. Right orthogonal equivariance of factor gradient flow and continuous dependence on its initial state give convergence to the corresponding width-two solution on every fixed compact time interval. Backward dependence is used only on finite intervals where the limiting path exists, and the positive shift tends to infinity so the original flow is defined there. Factors of the same Gram matrix differ by a right orthogonal transformation, so this limiting realization has the endpoint from Sections 3-5.

## Literature scope and novelty
Li-Luo-Lyu explicitly supply the asymmetric lift and conditional local theorem. Their Appendix H treats later endpoints as generic; the dimension-two endpoint conclusion here is an elementary corollary of their local result plus standard bounded analytic gradient convergence. Zhang-Saxe-Latham, arXiv:2512.20607, Sections 4-5, explicitly call the subsequent trajectory arguments heuristic; their Theorem 4 is about the LINEARIZED dynamics (10), not a full nonlinear second-phase limit. This check does not establish priority for the corollary; no claim of specialist novelty is made.

## Adversarial checks and scope boundary
scripts/check_endpoint_algebra.py checks exact stationarity implications in rectangular two-dimensional examples and a noncommuting covariance example. It also supplies a genuine boundary to THIS PROOF: in dimension three, a nonoptimal rank-two stationary product can have loss strictly below the best rank-one value. Take S=[[1,1,0],[0,1,0],[0,0,1]], D=diag(5,4,3), C(P)=||PS-D||_F^2/2 and P=diag(5,0,3)S^(-1). This P is stationary for rank-two factors, with loss 8<25/2 (best rank one), but the best rank-two loss is 9/2. It is not a counterexample to saddle-to-saddle dynamics; it shows why the dimension hypothesis cannot simply be omitted from the endpoint argument.

The full-row-rank data hypothesis is used to bound the product and to conclude its unique minimizer; rank(M)=2 makes the second step nonglobal at rank one; global best rank-one optimality is used to exclude all rank-one endpoints; width two and min(m,n)=2 are used in the injectivity step. None is silently discarded. The exact alignment remains an assumption, not something the endpoint proof derives.

Formal status: proofs/stationary_injective.lean addresses only injective cancellation of a zero image, the algebraic last step. The checker identifies that named theorem, binds the exact source hash, reports no axioms and FORMAL_TARGET_VERIFIED, conditional on its trusted core environment. This does not certify the rank argument, the analytic convergence theorem, local escape, or the full prose result. Full result remains proof (unaudited).","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:6a4577ebe6b264bbde99675f49f8bf7e67c2ed31c8a6fbc344b3a5fdeabcff20","revision_digest":"sha256:0a5c8728989d5a42c5f12907528216182b03292653ce22f6fcec88b2b0067601","source_id":"own-work:w704:T232-w704-C002:v2","source_revision":"v2-as-read-2026-10-20","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body:
On a FINITE measure space, uniform integrability plus convergence in measure gives L^1 convergence. On a general (for instance sigma-finite but infinite) measure space this is FALSE and a third hypothesis is needed. The correct statement: let (Omega, F, mu) be a measure space and f_n in L^1(mu) with f_n -> f in measure (or mu-a.e.). Then f_n -> f in L^1(mu) if and only if (i) {f_n} is uniformly integrable, meaning sup_n integral_{|f_n| > K} |f_n| dmu -> 0 as K -> infinity, AND (ii) {f_n} is uniformly tight, meaning for every eps > 0 there is a set A with mu(A) < infinity and sup_n integral_{Omega \ A} |f_n| dmu < eps. Counterexample showing (ii) is not implied by (i): on R with Lebesgue measure take f_n = 1_{[n, n+1]}. Then |f_n| <= 1 so the family is uniformly integrable and dominated, f_n -> 0 pointwise everywhere, yet ||f_n||_1 = 1 for every n. Mass escapes to infinity; on a finite measure space it has nowhere to go, which is exactly why the finite-measure statement can omit (ii). [standard; e.g. Bogachev, Measure Theory, Vol. I, Section 4.5]
f_n -> f in measure or mu-almost everywhere
uniform integrability of {f_n}
uniform tightness of {f_n}: on an infinite measure space this is an independent hypothesis

[Theorem ASASiid of arXiv:2603.12774, 'Synchronization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Browni'] There exists a sequence of deterministic values, called {Lyapunov exponents}
	\[
	\lambda_k < \cdots < \lambda_1, \qquad \lambda_i \in [-\infty, \infty),
	\]
	and a set of full measure $\tilde{\Omega} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathcal{B} \times \mathcal{B}$ with respect to $\mu \times \mathbf{P}$ such that 
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item The set $\tilde{\Omega}$ is $\Theta_t$-invariant for every $t \ge 0$.  
		For each $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$, define
		\[
		G_\lambda(\omega,x) := \left\{ z \in \mathbb{R}^d : 
		\limsup_{t \to \infty} \frac{1}{t} \log \big| \mathrm{D}_x \Phi^t_\omega(z) \big| \le \lambda \right\}.
		\]
		Then $G_{\lambda_1}(\omega, x) = \mathbb{R}^d$, and for every $1 \le i < k$,
		\[
		z \in G_{\lambda_i}(\omega,x) \setminus G_{\lambda_{i+1}}(\omega,x)
		\quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad
		\lim_{t \to \infty} \frac{1}{t} \log \big| \mathrm{D}_x \Phi^t_\omega(z) \big| = \lambda_i.
		\]
		Moreover, for all $z \in G_{\lambda_k}(\omega,x) \setminus \{0\}$,
		\[
		\lim_{t \to \infty} \frac{1}{t} \log \big| \mathrm{D}_x \Phi^t_\omega(z) \big| = \lambda_k.
		\]
		\item Suppose $\lambda_1 < 0$ and that for some $r \in (0,1]$ and all $y,z \in \mathbb{R}^d$ there exist constants $\overline{C}_F > 0$ and $p_1 \ge 1$ such that
		\begin{equation}
			\| \mathrm{D}_y F - \mathrm{D}_z F \|_{L(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathbb{R}^d)}
			\le \overline{C}_F (1 + |y| + |z|)^{p_1} |y-z|^r.
		\end{equation}
		Then there exists a full-measure set $\mathcal{M} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d \times \Omega$ such that, for every $0 < \nu < -\lambda_1$, there exists a positive random variable
		\begin{align}
			R^\nu : \mathcal{M} \to (0,\infty)
		\end{align}
		with the property that for all $(x,\omega) \in \mathcal{M}$ and all $y \in \mathbb{R}^d$ satisfying $|y| \le R^\nu(x,\omega)$,
		\[
		\sup_{t \ge 0} \exp(t\nu) \, \big| \Phi^t_\omega(x+y) - \Phi^t_\omega(x) \big| < \infty.
		\]
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem ASASiid of arXiv:2603.12774

$$

[Definition def:alternating-increasing of arXiv:2608.19050, 'Online Permutation Embedding: \\ Optimal Stopping and Scaling Laws'] For $m \ge 1$, define
\begin{align*}
    \mathrm{Alt}_{2m} &:=(2,1,4,3,\ldots,2m,2m-1)\in\Pi_{2m} \,,\\
    \mathrm{Alt}_{2m+1} &:=(2,1,4,3,\ldots,2m,2m-1,2m+1)\in\Pi_{2m+1} \,.
\end{align*}
By convention, set $\mathrm{Alt}_{1} := (1)$. Also, provided the following limit exists, define
\[
    c_{\mathrm{alt}}
    :=
    \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\beta(\mathrm{Alt}_n)}{n^2}\,.
\]

[Prop main-prop of arXiv:2411.10318, 'Polynomial Mixing of the critical Glauber Dynamics for the Ising Model'] Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a tree and let $(\sigma_v)_{v\in V(\mathcal{T})}$ be a configuration drawn from the Ising model on $\mathcal{T}$ with external field $h$ and inverse temperature $s$ (and let $\theta=\tanh(s)$). Denote by $\mathbb{E}_h$ the expectation under the Ising Model with external field $h$. Then, if $\rho$ is the root of $\mathcal{T}$, $v_1,...,v_k$ are vertices of $\mathcal{T}$ and $\mathbb{E}_h(\sigma_\rho)=0$, the following inequality holds:
$$\mathbb{E}_h\left(\sigma_\rho|\sigma_{v_1}=\cdots=\sigma_{v_k}=+\right)\le 50\cdot\sum\limits_{i=1}^k\mathbb{E}_0\left(\sigma_\rho|\sigma_{v_i}=+\right)=50\cdot\sum\limits_{i=1}^k\theta^{\text{dist}(\rho,v_i)}.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop main-prop of arXiv:2411.10318

body:
Let $E = \frac{1}{n} X^T X$ be the sample covariance of $n$ i.i.d. rows in $\mathbb{R}^p$ with population covariance $C$ (rows $C^{1/2} z_i$ with $z_i$ having i.i.d. entries of mean zero, variance one and finite twelfth moment), in the regime $p, n \to \infty$ with $q = p/n \to q_0 \in (0, \infty)$, and assume the spectral distribution of $C$ converges to a limit with bounded support. Let $\lambda_k, u_k$ be the sample eigenvalues and eigenvectors and let $g_E(z) = \frac{1}{p}\operatorname{tr}(z I - E)^{-1}$ be the Stieltjes transform of the sample spectrum, with $g(\lambda - i0) := \lim_{\eta \downarrow 0} g_E(\lambda - i\eta)$ inside the bulk. THEOREM (Ledoit and Peche, 2011, Theorem 4; in the form of Bun, Bouchaud and Potters 2017). The oracle eigenvalues $\xi_k^{\mathrm{or}} = u_k^T C u_k$ converge, uniformly in $k$ inside the bulk, to $$\xi(\lambda_k) = \frac{\lambda_k}{\big|\, 1 - q + q\, \lambda_k\, g_E(\lambda_k - i0) \,\big|^2}.$$ This limit depends on the population covariance $C$ only through the observable sample spectrum, so it is a consistent, computable estimator (the rotationally invariant estimator, RIE, or nonlinear shrinkage): replace each sample eigenvalue by $\xi(\lambda_k)$, keep the sample eigenvectors. In practice $g_E$ is evaluated at $\lambda_k - i\eta$ with a small $\eta$ of order $n^{-1/2}$ times the eigenvalue scale, and the result is floored at a small positive fraction of the bulk level. When $C = \sigma^2 I$ the formula returns $\sigma^2$ for every eigenvalue (the Marchenko-Pastur spread is entirely removed); for a spike above the bulk it returns approximately the debiased population spike. Applying the formula to a matrix whose largest eigenvalue is a signal one is trying to keep, and flooring relative to that top eigenvalue, destroys the small eigenvalues that the inverse depends on.
i.i.d. rows C^{1/2} z with z having i.i.d. mean-zero unit-variance entries and finite twelfth moment
p/n -> q_0 in (0, infinity)
the population spectral distribution converges to a limit with bounded support
the formula is used inside the bulk; isolated spikes are handled by the BBP correction

body:
[Theorem thm-hurewicz of arXiv:2412.03067, 'Geodesic Trees and Exceptional Directions in FPP on Hyperbolic Groups'] [engelking]
A separable metric space $X$ satisfies the inequality $\mathrm{ind}\, X \leq  n$ (for some $n\geq 0)$ if and only if there exists a closed surjective mapping $f: Z \to X$ of a zero-dimensional (in the sense of topological dimension)  separable $Z$ with fibers of cardinality
at most $n + 1$.  

Further,
\begin{enumerate}
	\item For every compact metric space $ X$ with  $\dim_t X \leq  n$ (for some $n\geq 0)$  there exists a continuous mapping $f: Z \to X$ of a closed subspace $Z$ of the  Cantor set  onto the space $X$ with fibers of cardinality at most $n+ 1$.
	\item If for a compact  metric space $X$ there exists a continuous mapping $f: Z \to X$ of a closed subspace $Z$ of the Cantor set  onto the space X with fibers of cardinality at most $n+ 1$, then  $\dim_t X \leq  n$.
\end{enumerate}

&\mathbb{P}(\tau=k)
\le C_1\frac{\mathbb{E}|S_\tau|}{k^{3/2}}(\mathbb{E}|X_1|^3)^2,\\

\le C_1\frac{\mathbb{E}|S_\tau|}{k^{3/2}}(\mathbb{E}|X_1|^3)^2

$$

[Corollary 94 (Terminal bracket versus covariance delivery) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Fix a deterministic terminal bracket $Q\in\mathcal S_1(H)_+$.  Among
revealed bracket paths with $R_T=Q$, the particle-two area covariance is
\begin{equation}
 C_{\alpha_A,T}^{\mathrm{loc}}
 =\frac14\left(\Lambda^2Q-
   \sum_{0<s\le T}\Lambda^2\Delta R_s\right).
 
\end{equation}
Consequently
\[
 0\le C_{\alpha_A,T}^{\mathrm{loc}}\le\frac14\Lambda^2Q.
\]
Continuous delivery attains the upper bound, one centered terminal jump with
covariance $Q$ attains zero, and every scalar level
$\theta\Lambda^2Q/4$, $0\le\theta\le1$, is attainable.  Thus the terminal
predictable bracket alone does not determine area covariance; its temporal
atomic structure is essential.

[Lemma 8 (Tightness criterion check for regularly-varying covariance) of arXiv:2606.04179, 'Functional Scaling Limits of Interpolated Correlated Random Walks in Hölder Topology'] If \(\abs{\rho(k)} =  \abs{k}^{-\alpha}\slowVar(k)\) for a slowly
    varying function \(\slowVar\), then for all \(p\in [2, \infty)\) and all
    \(\beta \in (\frac12 - \frac1p, \hurst - \frac1p)\) with \(\hurst = 1-\frac{\alpha \hermRank}{2}\)
    there exists a constant \(C_{\mathrm{tight}}\) and \(n_0 \in \nat\)
    such that 
    \[
        \norm{\hat\interpF_t^n-\hat\interpF_s^n}_{L^p(\Omega)}
        \le C_{\mathrm{tight}} \abs{t-s}^{\frac1p + \beta}
        \qquad \text{for all  \(n\ge n_0\)  and \(t,s \in [0,T]\)}.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let K be a compact convex subset of a locally convex Hausdorff topological vector space, and suppose K is metrizable. Then the set ext K of extreme points of K is a G_delta set, and for every x in K there is a Borel probability measure mu on K, concentrated on ext K, whose barycenter is x: phi(x) = integral phi dmu for every continuous linear functional phi. Without metrizability, the Bishop-de Leeuw theorem gives a probability measure that vanishes on every Baire set disjoint from ext K. The Krein-Milman theorem, that K is the closed convex hull of ext K, is the qualitative counterpart. Uniqueness of the representing measure for every x characterises the Choquet simplices.
K compact and convex in a locally convex Hausdorff space
K metrizable for the measure to live on ext K itself

body: The transitive closure of a set x, denoted \mathrm{TC}(x), is the unique smallest transitive set containing x as a subset. It is given by \mathrm{TC}(x) = \bigcup_{n < \omega} x_n, where x_0 = x and x_{n+1} = \bigcup x_n.

[Lemma 5 (Refined Ring Lemma for RCP) of arXiv:2608.03575, '2608.03575'] Let $(G,\Theta)$ be a tame ADT satisfying (Z1)--(Z4), and assume that (Z2) is strengthened to (Z2'). Let $r:V(G)\to(0,\infty)$ be the radius function of a regular circle-pattern realization of $(G, \Theta)$ in the plane. Then there exists a constant $C=C(\varepsilon_{0},\varepsilon_{1})>0$ such that, for every edge $u\sim v$,
\[
\frac{r(v)}{r(u)}>e^{-CS(u)}
\]
where $S(u)=\sum_{w\sim u}\deg_{G}(w)$ is the flower degree of $u$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Prop 1 (Proposition 2.5 and Lemma 2.8 in \cite{Geiss:Ylinen:21}) of arXiv:2506.10213, 'Coupling of forward-backward stochastic differential equations on the Wiener space, and ap'] Let \(X, X_1, \dots, X_n \in L^0(R\times\Omega^0)\), and let \(Y_i \in \cC(X_i)\) for \(i=1,\dots,n\).
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The joint distribution is preserved; i.e. one has the following
    $$(Y_1,\dots,Y_n) \stackrel{d}{=} (X_1,\dots,X_n).$$
    \item For all Borel functions \(g:\R^n\to\R\),
    $$g(Y_1,\dots,Y_n) \in \cC\bigl(g(X_1,\dots,X_n)\bigr).$$
    \item For \(Y\in L^0([0,T]\times\Omega^1)\), we have \(Y\in \cC_T(X)\)
    if and only if there exists a null set \(N\subset [0,T]\) such that for all \(r\in [0,T]\setminus N\),
    $$Y(r,\cdot) \in \cC_0\bigl(X(r,\cdot)\bigr).$$
    \item Let $M$ be the complete metric space that is locally $\sz$-compact.
    If $f:[0,T]\times\Oz^0\times M \to \R$ satisfies
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $(r,\oz) \to f(r,\oz,x)$ is measurable for all $x\in M$;
        \item $x\to f(r,\oz,x)$ is continuous for all $(r,\oz)\in [0,T]\times\Oz^0$.
    \end{itemize}
    Then there is a function $g:[0,T]\times\Oz^1\times M \to \R$ satisfying all the conditions above, and $g(\cdot,x)\in \cC_0(f(\cdot,x))$ for all $x\in M$.
    Moreover, for all $\wt{g}$ which satisfies the same properties with $g$, it holds true that 
    $$\wt{g} = g, \quad\quad \frac{\lambda}{T}\otimes\P^0-a.s.$$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 2.5 and Lemma 2.8 in \cite{Geiss:Ylinen:21}

[Proposition 6 (Kaimanovich end-space coding {\cite[Section~5) of arXiv:2606.23896, 'The one-point Schreier Poisson boundary of Thompson's group \(F\)'] {Kaimanovich2017}}]
The end space of
\(\Gamma\) decomposes as

\[
\partial\Gamma
=
\partial_-\Gamma
\sqcup
\partial_+\Gamma
\sqcup
\partial\overline\Gamma,
\]

where \(\partial_-\Gamma\) and \(\partial_+\Gamma\) are the countable families
of negative and positive ray ends, and \(\partial\overline\Gamma\) is the end
space of the skeleton. The skeleton end space is identified with the
odd 2-adic integers \(\mathbb Z_2^\times\). Under the grey-tree coding,

\[
(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2,\ldots)
\longmapsto
1+\sum_{j\ge 1}\varepsilon_j2^j .

OWNER RESULT DRAFT, proof (unaudited), C007 v1; no novelty claim.
Let a fixed zero-mean finite-rank Gaussian process have a supplied feature map phi with ||phi(x)||<=R, independent Gaussian observation noise of variance s>0, and at most n context observations. All context/query input locations and context length are jointly independent of the GP and all noises. Context labels may be correlated and are not bounded or conditioned. Put V=s+R^2. Given the full original context W, let P_W=N(m,v) be the exact noisy posterior predictive. Clip each context label to [-B,B], B>0, and recompute the mean m_B with the same design; v is unchanged. Suppose a Gaussian predictor h_B=N(mhat,vhat), depending only on clipped context and supplied features, has vhat>=s and KL(N(m_B,v)||h_B)<=eps_c for every possible context and design. Then on the ORIGINAL unconditioned task law,
E_W KL(P_W||h_B) <= 2 eps_c + (2 sqrt(2) n^2 R^4 V/s^3) exp(-B^2/(4V)).
In particular, for eps>0, eps_c=eps/4 and B=sqrt(4V log(max(e,4 sqrt(2) n^2 R^4 V/(s^3 eps)))) make the expected KL at most eps. If nR=0 the bias is zero. This does not assert that N(m_B,v) is the conditional law given clipped labels. The supplied-feature comparator exists by the separately audited C002 construction; this clipping lemma itself awaits independent review.
Zero-mean fixed finite-rank GP, supplied feature norms <=R, independent Gaussian noise variance s>0
At most n context labels; all input locations and context length jointly independent of latent GP and noises; iid tasks
Full original posterior is the target; only the predictor clips context labels at the explicit deterministic B

Claim T336-w727-C007 v1. Kind: bound. Target: none (the reviewer-authorized
generalization continuation). Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty is claimed.
The hardest step is retaining the original conditional target after clipping
the observed context. The comparison below keeps that target unchanged.

## 1. Task law and clipping comparator

Fix a zero-mean finite-rank GP with supplied feature map phi into R^p,
k(x,x')=<phi(x),phi(x')>, ||phi(x)||<=R, and independent observation
noise of variance s>0. Each task has at most n context observations and one
query observation. The joint law of all input locations and the context
length is independent of the latent GP and all observation noises. Locations
within a task need not be independent. Tasks are iid, with fresh GP/noise
draws. Write W for the FULL context labels, locations and query location.
Thus P_W, the query law given W, is the exact Gaussian posterior predictive.
No label-based selection, rejection, or conditioning of tasks is made.

Put V=s+R^2. Conditional on the input design alone, every observed label
is centered Gaussian of variance at most V. The context labels can be
correlated. Given W, the posterior variance v is in [s,V].

For B>0, replace each context label y_i by c_B(y_i)=max(-B,min(B,y_i)).
Let m and m_B be the posterior means computed from the original and clipped
labels. Their computed predictive variances are the same v, since that
variance depends only on the input design. The Gaussian N(m_B,v) is an
auxiliary predictive; it is NOT asserted to be the conditional law given
clipped labels.

Set A=s I_p+sum_i phi_i phi_i^T. The coefficient of y_i in the predictive
mean is phi_*^T A^{-1} phi_i, whose absolute value is at most R^2/s.
For r_i=y_i-c_B(y_i), Cauchy-Schwarz therefore gives, for any context
length l<=n,

    |m-m_B|^2 <= (R^4/s^2) l sum_i r_i^2.                 (1)

For a centered Gaussian G of variance tau<=V,

    E[G^2 exp(G^2/(4V))]
       = tau (1-tau/(2V))^(-3/2) <= 2 sqrt(2) V.

This follows by differentiating the elementary Gaussian square-mgf;
it also holds for tau=0. Since r_i^2<=y_i^2 1{|y_i|>B}, conditioning
on the design and then averaging yields

    E|m-m_B|^2 <= 2 sqrt(2) n^2 R^4 V/s^2
                         * exp(-B^2/(4V)).              (2)

Only a sum of marginal expectations was used, not independence of labels.

Apply the independently checked C002 v1 construction to clipped context
labels with its pointwise accuracy eps_c>0. Let its output be
h_B=N(mhat,vhat), with vhat>=s. Pointwise in every full W, C002 gives

    KL(N(m_B,v) || h_B) <= eps_c.

The variance part d_v=(log(vhat/v)+v/vhat-1)/2 is nonnegative. Splitting
m-mhat=(m-m_B)+(m_B-mhat) and using (a+b)^2<=2a^2+2b^2 gives

    KL(P_W || h_B) <= 2 KL(N(m_B,v) || h_B)+(m-m_B)^2/s.

Consequently, on the ORIGINAL task law,

    E_W KL(P_W || h_B) <= 2 eps_c+Ctail exp(-B^2/(4V)),
    Ctail=2 sqrt(2) n^2 R^4 V/s^3.                       (3)

For any eps>0 choose

    eps_c=eps/4,
    B=sqrt(4V log(max(e,2 Ctail/eps))).                  (4)

Then (3) is at most eps. This formula also makes sense when Ctail=0:
the bias vanishes. If R=0 or n=0, the exact constant predictive N(0,v)
can alternatively be used. [Lemma 1 (Criterion for $\Xstar_T$ {\cite[Lemma~4.1) of arXiv:2608.24294, 'Existence of densities and atoms for the running maximum of time-inhomogeneous jump diffus'] {NakagawaSuzuki2024}}]
Fix $p>1$ and $\Theta=(h,v)\in \Hb_{\infty-}\times \Vb_{\infty-}$.
For each $n\ge1$, let $\{X^{(n)}_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ be a right-continuous real-valued process, and let $\{X_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ be a right-continuous real-valued process.
Write
\[
\Xstarn_T:=\sup_{0\le s\le T}X^{(n)}_s,
\qquad
\Xstar_T:=\sup_{0\le s\le T}X_s.
\]

Assume that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.4em]
\item $\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\E[|\Xstarn_T|^p]<\infty$, and for every $t\in[0,T]$ we have $X^{(n)}_t\in W^{1,p}_\Theta$ with
\[
\sup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\E\Big[\sup_{0\le s\le T}|D_\Theta X^{(n)}_s|^p\Big]<\infty;
\]
\item for each $n\ge1$, the process $\{D_\Theta X^{(n)}_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ admits a right-continuous version;
\item $\displaystyle \lim_{n\to\infty}\E\Big[\sup_{0\le s\le T}|X^{(n)}_s-X_s|^p\Big]=0$.
\end{enumerate}
Assume moreover that $D_\Theta X$ admits a right-continuous version and satisfies
\[
\Pbb\big(D_\Theta X_t\neq 0 \text{ on }\{t\in(0,T]: X_t=\Xstar_T\}\big)=1.
\]
Then the law of $\Xstar_T$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure on $\R$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def_pointwise_multiplier of arXiv:2609.01984, 'Instantaneous shrinking of supports for stochastic PDEs\footnote{JY was supported by a KIA'] Fix $\eta\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\alpha\in[0,1)$ such that $\alpha=0$ if
$\eta\in\mathbb{Z}$, and $\alpha>0$ if $|\eta|+\alpha$ is not an integer. Define
\[
B^{|\eta|+\alpha}
=
\begin{cases}
B(\mathbb{R}), & \eta=0,\\
C^{|\eta|-1,1}(\mathbb{R}), & \eta\text{ is a nonzero integer},\\
C^{|\eta|+\alpha}(\mathbb{R}), & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
and
\[
B^{|\eta|+\alpha}(\ell_2)
=
\begin{cases}
B(\mathbb{R};\ell_2), & \eta=0,\\
C^{|\eta|-1,1}(\mathbb{R};\ell_2), & \eta\text{ is a nonzero integer},\\
C^{|\eta|+\alpha}(\mathbb{R};\ell_2), & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Here $B(\mathbb{R})$ denotes the space of bounded Borel functions,
$C^{|\eta|-1,1}$ denotes the space of $|\eta|-1$ times continuously differentiable
functions whose derivatives of order $|\eta|-1$ are Lipschitz continuous, and
$C^{|\eta|+\alpha}$ denotes the usual H\"older space.

Let n>=2, K>=2 and d>=1. Let each f_i:R^d->R be convex C1 with globally L_i-Lipschitz gradient, L_i>0. Let psi:R^d->R union {+infinity} be proper closed convex. Set f=(1/n)sum_i f_i, F=f+psi, and suppose x* minimizes F with F(x*) finite. Start at x_1 in dom psi. Write D=||x_1-x*||, Lbar=(1/n)sum_i L_i, Lmax=max_i L_i, s=1+log K, sigma_any^2=(1/n)sum_i ||grad f_i(x*)||^2 and sigma_rand^2=sigma_any^2+n||grad f(x*)||^2. Use a fixed positive step eta<=1/[4n sqrt(2 Lbar Lmax s)]. In epoch k, set z_0=x_k, take z_i=z_(i-1)-eta grad f_(sigma_i)(z_(i-1)) for i=1,...,n along a permutation sigma, and set x_(k+1)=prox_(n eta psi)(z_n), where prox_(n eta psi)(z) minimizes psi(x)+||x-z||^2/(2n eta). There is an absolute constant C such that, for every sequence of permutations, F(x_(K+1))-F(x*)<=C[D^2/(n eta K)+(n eta)^2 Lbar sigma_any^2 s]. If fresh independent uniform permutations are used in each epoch, E[F(x_(K+1))-F(x*)]<=C[D^2/(n eta K)+n eta^2 Lbar sigma_rand^2 s]. These are bounds for the last epoch iterate, with no strong-convexity assumption. For D>0, balancing eta under the stated cap gives respectively O(D^2 sqrt(Lbar Lmax s)/K+D^(4/3)(Lbar sigma_any^2 s)^(1/3)/K^(2/3)) and O(D^2 sqrt(Lbar Lmax s)/K+D^(4/3)(Lbar sigma_rand^2 s)^(1/3)/(n^(1/3) K^(2/3))). The fixed-step bounds also cover D=0. All norms are Euclidean. Source: Zijian Liu and Zhengyuan Zhou, On the Last-Iterate Convergence of Shuffling Gradient Methods, Theorem 4.4 and its full version Theorem C.1.
Finite-dimensional Euclidean space; n>=2 components and K>=2 epochs
Convex C1 f_i with globally L_i-Lipschitz gradients, L_i>0
Proper closed convex psi and an attained finite minimum of F=f+psi
x_1 is in dom psi; eta is constant, positive, and satisfies the displayed K-dependent cap
For the expected random-reshuffling bound, use fresh independent uniform permutations
For the optimized-rate corollaries assume D>0; the fixed-step inequalities do not require D>0

Equivalently for all x, y, z, w ∈X , d(x, z) + d(y, w) ≤ (3.1) max {d(x, y) + d(z, w), d(y, z) + d(x, w)} + 2δ, which is called the 4-point condition. such that for any

body: Exact rank three for the bounded-density conjecture: what is proved and what is open. (1) The step 'a rank-three coarea bound ||p_S||_inf <= K ||rho||_inf^{2/3} for S = sum_{j<=3} lambda_j Y_j^2' is false for general bounded densities rho on R^3: a density rho <= B that puts mass 2hB A(s) on the shell {|S - s| < h} gives p_S about B A(s) near s, where A(s) = d/ds vol{S <= s} = 2 pi s^{1/2}/sqrt(lambda_1 lambda_2 lambda_3) for a definite form, unbounded as s grows; a bound needs regularity of rho beyond its supremum. (2) Orthonormal 3D projections of product densities have that regularity on spheres: their spherical means satisfy M_{y0}(r) <= 6/(pi r) uniformly in the centre, and definite rank-three forms have density <= 82 for every linear term. (3) The marginal bound is sharp and law-free: the projection onto a k-dimensional subspace of a vector with independent coordinates of densities <= 1 has density <= min{(n/(n-k))^{(n-k)/2}, 2^{k/2}} (Livshyts, Paouris and Pivovarov 2016); Ball's cube slicing is the uniform case and Rudelson-Vershynin give (CK)^d with an unspecified absolute C. (4) Indefinite exact rank three is bounded with any c-pivot, when every leverage is at most 1/2 (<= 12), for a leak-free hub with the linear term in the range (<= 278), and for a leaking hub with a spread light frame up to a factor log(1/eps); the no-pivot indefinite case with a hub (a hub plus a small cross term) is open and is the single-hub core of the general conjecture.

body:
Random variables X_n converge in distribution to X if and only if their characteristic functions converge pointwise, phi_{X_n}(t) -> phi_X(t) for every t. More usefully: if phi_{X_n}(t) -> psi(t) pointwise and psi is continuous at t = 0, then psi is the characteristic function of some random variable X and X_n -> X in distribution. This is the engine that turns the characteristic-function computation in the Central Limit Theorem into convergence in distribution.

body:
[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2608.13687, 'Multiplicative chaos from random multiplicative functions'] Fix constants $C',c', K>0$. 
Let $X$ be a nonnegative random variable such that $\E X \leq r$ and, for some $\sigma \in (0,K]$, 
\[
\P(X>u ) \leq C' e^{- c' u^2/\sigma^2}\,.
\]
Then for each $\lambda>0$, there exist constants $C_\lambda, c_\lambda>0$ (depending also on $c',C'$, and $K$) such that
\[
  \E e^{\lambda X}-1 \leq C_\lambda r + C_\lambda e^{-c_\lambda/\sigma}\,.
\]
\begin{proof}
On the event $\{X \leq \sigma^{1/2}\}$, the mean value theorem yields
\[
  \E[(e^{\lambda X} - 1) \ind{X \leq \sigma^{1/2}}] \leq \E[\lambda e^{\lambda \sigma^{1/2}} X \ind{X \leq \sigma^{1/2}}] \leq C_\lambda r\,,
\]
where the $\sigma$ independence in the last bound comes from $\sigma\leq K$.
On  $\{X > \sigma^{1/2}\}$, we write
\begin{multline}
  \E [(e^{\lambda X}-1) \ind{X > \sigma^{1/2}}] - (e^{\lambda \sigma^{1/2}}-1)\P(X>\sigma^{1/2})
  \\
  = \int_{\sigma^{1/2}}^{\infty} \int_0^x \partial_u (e^{\lambda u}) \d u ~\d \P_X(x)  
  = \int_{\sigma^{1/2}}^{\infty} \P(X>u) \lambda e^{\lambda u} \d  u  \leq C_\lambda \int_{\sigma^{1/2}}^{\infty} e^{-c'\frac{u^2}{\sigma^2} + \lambda u} \d u\,.
\end{multline}
Now, for $u\geq \sigma^{1/2}$ and $\lambda>0$, there exists $\sigma_\lambda>0$ such that for all $\sigma \in (0,\sigma_\lambda]$, we have 
$
  \lambda u \leq \tfrac{c' u^2}{2\sigma^2}$.
For such $\sigma$, it follows from \eqref{eq:layer-cake} that
$
  \E [(e^{\lambda X}-1) \ind{X > \sigma^{1/2}}] \leq C_\lambda e^{-c_\lambda/\sigma}\,.
$
For $\sigma >\sigma_\lambda$, note that the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:layer-cake} can be bounded by a constant $C_\lambda'>0$ times the Laplace transform of a Gaussian with variance $K^2/2c'$
to get 
$\E [(e^{\lambda X}-1) \ind{X > \sigma^{1/2}}] \leq C_\lambda$,
possibly enlarging $C_\lambda$ from before.
We finish by multiplying by $e^{-c_\lambda/\sigma} e^{c_\lambda/\sigma_\lambda}$, which is larger than $1$. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 8 of arXiv:2608.13687

[Lemma gaussian-IBP of arXiv:2606.19763, 'Optimal Sparsification of Gaussian Processes'] Suppose $f: \R \to \R$ is a differentiable function such that $f'\in L^1(\gamma_1) $. 
	Then 
	\[
		\Ex_{\bg\sim N(0,1)}\sbra{\bg\, f(\bg)} = \Ex_{\bg\sim N(0,1)}\sbra{f'(\bg)}\,.
	\]
	Consequently, for $F : \R^n \to \R$ with $F \in C^1$ and $F, \frac{\partial}{\partial x_i} F(x) \in L^1(\gamma_n)$ for $1 \leq i \leq n$, we have   
	\[
		\Ex_{\bg\sim N(0, I_n)}\sbra{\bg_j F(\bg)}
		=
		\Ex_{\bg\sim N(0, I_n)}\sbra{\frac{\partial}{\partial \bg_j} F(\bg)}
	\]
	for each coordinate $1 \leq j \leq n$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition 14 (Admissible metrics of type II) of arXiv:2608.29427, '\small Positive mass and rigidity \\ for asymptotically flat tangent bundles'] A tubular interpolating metric \(\widetilde g\) is called an \emph{admissible metric of type II} if it satisfies \hyperref[item:admI-1]{condition~\ref{item:admI-1}} of \hyperref[defn:adms-1]{Definition~\ref{defn:adms-1}} and the following additional conditions.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item
		The function
		\[
		\xi=\xi(x,\y)
		\]
		is compactly supported in the fiber variable and satisfies
		\[
		\xi_{,s}\le0.
		\]
		Thus, for each \(x\in U_\infty\), the function \(\xi(x,\cdot)\) is radially non-increasing cut-off function on the fiber.
		\item
		The vertical metric \(h\) is conformally flat:
		\[
		h_{ij}=e^{H(x)}\delta_{ij},
		\]
		where \(H\) is non-negative and radially non-increasing.
		\item
		The decay assumptions are
		\[
		g_{ij}-\delta_{ij}
		\in
		\mathcal O_2(r^{-(n-2)}),
		\]
		\[
		a^c_{ij}
		\in
		\mathcal O_1(\rho^{-\lambda^c}),
		\qquad \text{where} \quad 
		\lambda^c>2n-1,
		\]
		and
		\[
		H\in\mathcal O_1(r^{-\sigma^v}),
		\qquad
		\xi\in\mathcal O_1(\rho^{-\tau^v}),
		\]
		where
		\[
		\tau^v\ge1,
		\qquad
		\sigma^v+\tau^v\ge n-1.
		\]
	\end{enumerate}
title: Admissible metrics of type II

Let f: [t_0-a,t_0+a] x B(y_0,b) -> R^n be continuous, where B(y_0,b) subset R^n is the closed ball of radius b around y_0, and suppose f is Lipschitz in its second argument uniformly in the first: there is L >= 0 with |f(t,y_1)-f(t,y_2)| <= L|y_1-y_2| for all t in the interval and y_1,y_2 in B(y_0,b). Let M = max|f(t,y)| over this compact domain and h = min(a, b/M). Then the initial value problem y'(t) = f(t,y(t)), y(t_0)=y_0, has a unique solution y on [t_0-h, t_0+h]. (When M = 0, read b/M as infinity, so h = a.) Continuity alone does not give uniqueness: y' = 2 sqrt(|y|), y(0) = 0 has infinitely many solutions. If f is continuous and locally Lipschitz in y on an open domain D, the local solutions through (t_0, y_0) patch together into a unique maximal solution, which leaves every compact subset of D as t approaches either end of its interval.
f is continuous on a closed cylinder around (t_0,y_0)
f is Lipschitz in y, uniformly in t, on that cylinder

body:
[Definition eq:third_renormalisation of arXiv:2607.18011, 'From local giants to locality in long-range percolation'] For $i \geq 0$ and for $c_{\mathrm{vor}}{}$ as in \thref{prop:tile_and_cell_volume_bounds}, we let 
    
    \begin{equation}
        
        \rho_i 
        = 
       
            1 - (i+s)^{-3/2}/2
      
        ,
        \quad
        \xi_i
        = 
        (i +1+ s)^{-3/2}/4,
        \quad
        \text{and}
        \quad
        C_i
        =
        c_{\mathrm{vor}}{}
        (m_i/2)^d.
    \end{equation}
    
    We say that a level-$0$ tile $\Tile{0}{j}$ is \textbf{good} if it contains a cluster $\mathcal{C}_{0,j}$ satisfying
    
    \begin{equation}
        \# 
        \left(
            \mathcal{C}_{0,j}
            \cap
            B(x_{0,j},r_0/4)
        \right)
        \geq 
        \nu 
        \# B(r_0/2),
    \end{equation}
    
    where $\nu$ is as in \thref{prop:biskup}.
    
    For a good level-$0$ tile $\Tile{0}{j}$, the \textbf{good part} is $\mathcal{C}_{0,j}
            \cap
            B(x_{0,j},r_0/4)$.
    
    We say that a level-$1$ tile $\Tile{1}{j}$ is \textbf{good} if at least a $\rho_1$ proportion of its level-$0$ subtiles are good, and their good parts are connected to each other inside $\Tile{1}{j}$.
    
    For a good level-$1$ tile $\Tile{1}{j}$, we choose $C_1$ of its good level-$0$ subtiles and the \textbf{good part} of $\Tile{1}{j}$ is the union of the good parts of these subtiles, denoted by $\mathcal{C}_{1,j}$.
    
    For $i \geq 2$, we say that level-$i$ tile $\Tile{i}{j}$ is \textbf{good} if at least a $\rho_i$ proportion of its level-$i-1$ subtiles are good, and additionally: 
    
    if $\Tile{i-2}{j}$ is a good level-$i-2$ subtile in a good level-$i-1$ subtile of $\Tile{i}{j}$, 
    
    and $\Tile{i-2}{k}$ is a good level-$i-2$ subtile in some other good level-$i-1$ subtile of $\Tile{i}{j}$, 
    
    then the good parts of $\Tile{i-2}{j}$ and $\Tile{i-2}{k}$ are connected in $\Tile{i}{j}$.
    
    For a good level-$i$ tile $\Tile{i}{j}$, we choose $C_i$ of its good level-$i-1$ subtiles and the \textbf{good part} of $\Tile{i}{j}$ is the union of the good parts of these subtiles, denoted by $\mathcal{C}_{i,j}$.
    
    When choosing the good part of $\Tile{i}{j}$, if the subtile containing the origin $o$ is good, we choose it to be part of the good part.
title: Definition eq:third_renormalisation of arXiv:2607.18011

body: [Theorem T:half-KPZ-horizon of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. body:
[Lemma Lem:pathcounting of arXiv:2411.13030, 'Classification of the limit shape for 1+1-dimensional FPP'] Given integers  $M \ge k \ge 1$, let $S(M,k)$  be the number of distinct $k$-tuples $(a_1,...,a_k)$ of integers whose absolute values sum up to $M$. We then have that
\[
S(M,k)= \sum_{\rho=0}^{M-1} \binom{k}{\rho}\binom{M-1}{\rho}2^{\rho}+\binom{k}{M}2^{M}
\]

body: Corollary 5. Let t >= 2 be an integer and G = {G_i | i in [1, t]} be a multiset of simple graphs of order at least 2. Then we have the following. (i) If G_j is discrete for some j in [1, t], then r(G) = min{|V(G_i)| | G_i is discrete and i in [1, t]}. (ii) If G_1, ..., G_t are non-discrete graphs and r(G_{I_00}) = r(G) - 1, then r(G) = max{|V(G_j)| | delta(G_j) = 0 and j in [1, t]} > max{|V(G_j)| | delta(G_j) >= 1 and j in [1, t]}. Here r(G) = r(G_1, ..., G_t) is the multicolour Ramsey number; a graph is discrete if chi(G) = 1, that is, if it has no edges; delta is the minimum degree; I_0 := {i in [1, t] | delta(G_i) = 0} and I_00 := {i in I_0 | |V(G_i)| = r(G)}; and for J in [1, t] the paper's multiset G'_J replaces G_i, for i in J, by G_i with one isolated vertex removed (by G_i itself when delta(G_i) >= 1).

body: For a sign fibre A subset {+-1}^r the entropy defect is ell(A) = r - log_2|A|. d_cb(A) is the minimum signed-selector residual rank after optimizing over ALL coordinate bases drawn from the full dual of A: pick a coordinate basis, pick for each full-dual form a signed basis selector, require all assignment residuals to lie in one common space R, and minimize dim R over basis and selector choices. Notes: S6 uses ell and d_cb throughout without re-deriving them; the quantifier 'optimizing over all coordinate bases in the full dual' is the load-bearing part (it is what makes d_cb weaker than a fixed-basis d(H)).

[Theorem 37 (Cutoff profile for colored top-\texorpdfstring{$m$}{m}-to-random) of arXiv:2604.09933, 'Explicit cutoff profiles for colored top-\texorpdfstring{$m$}{m}-to-random shuffles'] Fix \(c\in\R\) and integers \(p\ge1\) and \(m\ge1\), with \(m\) independent of \(n\). Let \(k=k_n(c)\).
Then
\[
\bigl\|(Q^{(m)})^{*k}-U\bigr\|_{\TV}
=f_p(c)+o(1)
\qquad(n\to\infty),
\]
where \(f_p(c)\) is the function from Theorem~\ref{prop:DFP3.1-colored}. In particular, the colored top-\(m\)-to-random shuffle has total-variation cutoff at time \(\frac{n}{m}\log n\) with window \(\frac{n}{m}\).

[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2609.02017, 'Optimal girth-dependent bounds for the Bethe approximation of the permanent'] Let $G=(L\sqcup R,E)$ be a bipartite graph of girth at least $g$, with
$|L|=|R|=n$. Let $\mu$ be a probability distribution on the perfect
matchings of $G$, and let $
  p_e:=\P_{M\sim\mu}(e\in M)$, $\bs{p}:=(p_e)_{e\in E}$.
Then
\[
  H(\mu)\leq\Phi_G(\bs{p}).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
  H(\mu)-H_{\mr B}(\bs{p})
  \leq\frac2g\sum_{v\in V}F(\bs{p}_v).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 11 of arXiv:2609.02017
