Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). Given that the long-only gain is the estimation variance the constraint removes at the rows the stack is scored on, the amount of constraint was chosen with the evaluation inputs: a blend w(t) between the simplex and least-squares stacks with t minimising the cross-validated calibration error plus the excess bootstrap variance of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows, and a per-row version t_i = 1/(1 + kappa v_i/median v) that leans to the simplex where least squares is uncertain. P24 (a) HELD: on EMIT the per-cell blend reads +0.08 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 39 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 t* is at or above 0.5 on 30 of 30 cells and the blend reads +0.66 vs least squares; (c) REFUTED: the per-row blend vs the per-cell blend is +0.70 on Y2 and -0.14 on EMIT overall; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Fresh-split replication (P25, split C, SPLIT_SEED 11, the criterion uses no evaluation targets): P25 (a) HELD: on split C the EMIT blend reads +0.63 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 35 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend reads +0.84 vs the simplex (wins 30 of 30) and +0.65 vs least squares; (c) HELD: t* averages 0.34 on EMIT and 0.67 on OCO-2; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Bootstrap-size stability (P28, B = 16 against B = 8 on split B): P28 (a) HELD: t*(16) equals t*(8) on 86 pct of the 70 cells and is within 0.2 on 100 pct; (b) HELD: the blend's mean gain against the simplex moves from +0.08 to +0.06 on EMIT and from +0.83 to +0.83 on OCO-2, and the both-endpoints win count on OCO-2 is 30 of 30 at B = 16; falsifier (agreement below 50 pct or a gain moving by more than 0.5) not triggered. Break test: a fixed midpoint t = 0.5 matches the criterion on OCO-2 (+0.96 / +1.01 against +0.83 / +0.84 on the two splits) but loses 1.6 and 4.4 pct on EMIT where the criterion stays at +0.08 and +0.63 - the criterion's value is knowing, without labels, when not to leave the simplex; the EMIT shortfall against the hindsight-best t is the bias-shift term of the risk identity. Scarce calibration (P30, 240 of the calibration rows per cell, split B): P30 (a) HELD: at n = 240 the simplex beats least squares by +14.10 on EMIT (full calibration +8.83); (b) REFUTED: t* averages 0.22 on EMIT and the blend reads -2.61 vs the simplex; (c) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells and the simplex reads +2.27 vs least squares (full calibration -0.18); falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT) TRIGGERED. The observable part of the bias shift (P31): adding t^2 (D_ev - D_cal), the shift in the two bases' mean squared disagreement between the evaluation and calibration rows, to the criterion - P31 (a) REFUTED: the R'-blend reads -0.71 vs the simplex on EMIT split B (R-blend +0.08) and +0.71 on split C (R-blend +0.63); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R'-blend is -0.11 vs the R-blend on split B and -0.12 on split C; (c) REFUTED: mean t** 0.39 against t* 0.33 on EMIT, share of the hindsight optimum 0.07 -> -0.62; falsifier (R'-blend worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 on any corpus or split) TRIGGERED. Per-output mixing weights (P34, the criterion decoupled across outputs): P34 (a) REFUTED: the per-output blend reads -0.41 vs the per-cell blend on EMIT split B and -0.53 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.02 and -0.08 on split C; (c) REFUTED: on Y2 the share of outputs at t_d = 0 is 0.20 and at t_d >= 0.5 is 0.34; falsifier (per-output worse than per-cell by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED. A nearest-neighbour proxy for the bias shift (P35, the simplex's out-of-fold residuals at the nearest calibration rows standing in for its bias at the scored rows): P35 (a) REFUTED: the full-shift blend reads -0.69 vs the R-blend on EMIT split B and -0.12 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.08 and -0.14 on split C; (c) REFUTED: cross-only vs full on EMIT -0.05 vs -0.62 (split B); falsifier (either variant worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED. Scarce calibration, the ratio-metric criterion (P41, 240 calibration rows, split B, three-vertex form, registered and R_1 choices side by side): P41 (a) HELD: at n_cal = 240 the R_1 blend reads +1.17 vs the simplex on EMIT (within 1.0; the registered three-vertex blend reads -1.83); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R_1 blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells (at least 25); (c) HELD: R_1 vs the registered blend on EMIT +1.38 (at least +1.0); falsifier (R_1 worse than the simplex by more than 2.0 on EMIT) not triggered. So the P30 caveat is confined to the squared-loss criterion; the criterion in the score's own metric keeps the simplex where it should at scarce calibration. P44: the shipped tool against the driver (P44): P44 (a) REFUTED: the tool's mixing weight is within 0.2 of the driver's on 14 (squared) and 11 (ratio) of 14 cells; (b) HELD: the tool's blend scores within 1 pct of the driver's on 12 / 12 of 14; (c) HELD by the clause's wording (worse than both endpoints by more than 1 pct while the driver beats one: none); under the stricter test the analyzer was first written with (worse than the better endpoint by more than 1 pct): one cell, emit s102 Y3 (ratio); falsifier not triggered by the clause's wording, TRIGGERED under the stricter test. P55: the seed-102 diagnostic (P55): P55 (a) REFUTED: with the target norms at the scored rows the tool's ratio choice is within 0.2 of the driver's on 0 of 3 cells; (b) REFUTED: with the shipped convention at B = 32 on 2 of 3 (at most one); (c) REFUTED: on Y3 arm A stays at the least-squares endpoint; falsifier TRIGGERED (the draw decides - raise B before the ratio metric is the default). P49: scarce calibration on the held-out split (P49): P49 (a) HELD: on split D at 240 rows the R_1 blend reads +0.56 vs the simplex on EMIT (within 1.0; the registered blend -0.52); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 it beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells; (c) HELD: R_1 vs the registered blend on EMIT +1.00 (at least +1.0); falsifier (R_1 worse than the simplex by more than 2.0 on EMIT) not triggered.
the members' predictions on the rows to be scored are available (transductive setting); their targets are not
the blend w(t) = (1 - t) w_simplex + t w_leastsquares is linear in t, so the cross-validated and bootstrap predictions of every t come from the two base estimators' predictions; the criterion is the 5-fold cross-validated squared relative error on the calibration rows plus the excess pairs-bootstrap variance (B = 8) of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows

[Theorem t:DeGiorgiNashMoser of arXiv:2511.12692, 'A stochastic flow approach to De Giorgi--Nash--Moser estimates for SPDE\lowercase{s} with '] Let Assumption (ass:DeGiorgi_Nash_Moser of the paper) be satisfied, and let $\tau \le T$ be a stopping time. Suppose that for some $\delta\in (0,1)$ 
	and $R_b<\infty$ we have a.s.
	\[\|b^i(t,\cdot)\|_{C^{3+\delta}(\mathbb{T}^d;\ell^2)}\leq R_b,\qquad t\in [0,T], \,i\in \{1,\ldots, d\}.\]
	Moreover, assume that there exist $\gamma_0>0$ and $p,q\in (2,\infty)$ such that $\frac{2}{p}+\frac{d}{q}<1$ and $f^0, \ldots, f^d,g$ are progressively measurable satisfying a.s.\
	\begin{equation}
	f^0\in L^{p/2}(0,\tau;L^{q/2}(\mathbb{T}^d)),\quad \quad
	f^1, \ldots, f^d \in L^p(0,\tau;L^q(\mathbb{T}^d)) \ \ \text{and} \ \  g\in L^p(0,\tau;L^q(\mathbb{T}^d;\ell^2)),\end{equation}
	and $u_0\in C^{\gamma_0}({\mathbb{T}^d})$ a.s.\ is strongly ${\mathscr F}_0$-measurable. 
	Then, there exists a sequence of $(\overline{\gamma}_m)_m\subset (0,\infty)$ depending only on $(d, M,\nu,p,q)$ for which the  solution $u$ to (equation eq:SPDE_lin of the paper) satisfies the following with $\gamma_m:={(\overline{\gamma}_m\wedge\gamma_0)}/{3}$: 
    
    There exist stopping times $(\tau_m)_m$ depending only on $\tau$ and $b$ such that $\lim_{m\to \infty}	{\mathbb P}(\tau_m=\tau)=1$ and
	\begin{equation}
    
	u\in C^{ \gamma_m }((0,\tau_m)\times \mathbb{T}^d)\ \ \text{ a.s.\ for all } m\ge 1.
	\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Stochastic De Giorgi--Nash--Moser estimates -- qualitative version

body:
[Definition def:push-forward of arXiv:2505.02685, 'On the Spectral Expansion of Monotone Subsets of the Hypercube'] Let $\varphi_{X}:\mathbb{R}\rightarrow[0,1]$ be the Borel-measurable map defined by $a\mapsto \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}} \left[ X\geq a \right]$, and then for each Borel set $E\subseteq [0,1]$, let $\alpha(E)$ be the Lebesgue measure of the inverse image $\varphi_{X}^{-1}(E)$. The countable additivity of $\alpha$ easily follows from the countable additivity of the Lebesgue measure.

The measure $\alpha$ is referred to as the push-forward of the Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}$ by the map $a\mapsto \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}} \left[ X\geq a \right]$. Similarly define the Borel measure $\beta$ on $[0,1]$ to be the push-forward of the Lebesgue measure by the map $b\mapsto \ensuremath{\mathbb{P}} \left[ Y\geq b \right]$.
title: Definition def:push-forward of arXiv:2505.02685

body: In commutative algebra and algebraic geometry, localization is a formal way to introduce the "denominators" to a given ring or module. That is, it introduces a new ring/module out of an existing ring/module R, so that it consists of fractions ${\frac {m}{s}},$ such that the denominator s belongs to a given subset S of R. If S is the set of the non-zero elements of an integral domain, then the localization is the field of fractions: this case generalizes the construction of the field $\mathbb {Q}$ of rational numbers from the ring $\mathbb {Z}$ of integers.

body:
[Theo 22 (Explicit threshold, compact-support branch and onset amplitude) of arXiv:2608.30578, 'Compactly Supported Solutions near a Nehari Critical Value'] Let $0<\alpha<1$ and $n\ge2$. Consider the problem
\[
\begin{cases}
	-u''=\lambda u+m_n(x)u^\alpha,& -1<x<1,\\
	u(-1)=u(1)=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Define
\[
\lambda_{c,n}:=
\frac{\pi^2}
{\left((1-\alpha)+\dfrac{1+\alpha}{n}\right)^2}.
\]
Then
\[
\frac{\pi^2}{4}
<
\lambda_{c,n}
<
\lambda_n^*.
\]
At $\lambda=\lambda_{c,n}$ there exists an even positive flat solution
$u_{c,n}$ satisfying $u_{c,n}(\pm1)=u_{c,n}'(\pm1)=0$. For every
$\lambda\in(\lambda_{c,n},\lambda_n^*)$ there exists a unique even
non-negative solution in the above class whose connected support is
\[
\operatorname{supp}u_{\lambda,n}
=
[-b_{\lambda,n},b_{\lambda,n}]
\Subset(-1,1),
\]
where
\[
b_{\lambda,n}
=
\frac{1}{1-\alpha}
\left(
\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{\lambda}}
-\frac{1+\alpha}{n}
\right).
\]
For $x\ge0$ the solution is
\[
u_{\lambda,n}(x)
=
\begin{cases}
	A_{\lambda,n}\cos(\sqrt{\lambda}\,x),
	& 0\le x\le\dfrac1n,\\[2mm]
	\displaystyle
	\left(
	\frac{2}{(1+\alpha)\lambda}
	\right)^{\frac1{1-\alpha}}
	\sin^{\frac{2}{1-\alpha}}
	\left[
	\frac{1-\alpha}{2}\sqrt{\lambda}\,
	(b_{\lambda,n}-x)
	\right],
	& \dfrac1n\le x\le b_{\lambda,n},\\[3mm]
	0,
	& b_{\lambda,n}\le x\le1,
\end{cases}
\]
and it is extended evenly to $(-1,0)$. Moreover,
\[
A_{\lambda,n}
=
\|u_{\lambda,n}\|_{L^\infty(-1,1)}
=
\left(
\frac{2}{(1+\alpha)\lambda}
\right)^{\frac1{1-\alpha}}
\cos^{\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}}
\left(\frac{\sqrt{\lambda}}{n}\right).
\]
For each fixed $n$, the mapping $\lambda\longmapsto A_{\lambda,n}$
is strictly decreasing on $(\lambda_{c,n},\lambda_n^*)$, and
$A_{\lambda,n}\longrightarrow0\hbox{ as }\lambda\uparrow\lambda_n^*$. If
\[
A_n:=\|u_{c,n}\|_{L^\infty(-1,1)},
\]
then
\[
A_n=
\left[
\frac{2}{(1+\alpha)\pi^2}
\left(
(1-\alpha)+\frac{1+\alpha}{n}
\right)^2
\right]^{\frac1{1-\alpha}}
\cos^{\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}}
\left(
\frac{\pi}{n(1-\alpha)+(1+\alpha)}
\right),
\]
and
\[
\lambda_{c,n}\uparrow
\lambda_{c,\infty}:=
\frac{\pi^2}{(1-\alpha)^2},
\]
while
\[
A_n\longrightarrow
A_\infty:=
\left[
\frac{2(1-\alpha)^2}
{(1+\alpha)\pi^2}
\right]^{\frac1{1-\alpha}}
>0.
\]
Furthermore,
\[
\frac{\lambda_{c,n}}{\lambda_n^*}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Moreover, $H_\lambda(u_{\lambda,n})=M_n(u_{\lambda,n})<0$, and therefore
$E_\lambda(u_{\lambda,n})>0,\ E_\lambda''(u_{\lambda,n})<0$. Thus, these
explicit solutions have the variational character of the
branch $u_{\lambda,n}^-$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Explicit threshold, compact-support branch and onset amplitude

[Defn 2 of arXiv:2608.13976, 'Boundary Harnack principle for diffusion with jumps on metric measure spaces'] Let $B$ be a ball in $\sX$ with  $\overline B\subsetneq \sX.$
 For an open subset $U\subset B,$
  we say $G^B_U(x, y)$ is
the Green function of $X^B$ in $U$ (or equivalently $X^U$)  with respect to the measure $m_B$ if it is  not identically infinite and is  the potential kernel of $X^B$ in $U$. That is, the following conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item[\rm (i)]
 For any Borel bounded function  $f\geq 0$ on $U$,
$$
\E_x \int_0^{\tau_U} f(X_s) ds=\E_x \int_0^{\tau_U} f(X^B_s) ds = \int_U G^B_U (x, y) f(y) m_B(dy), \quad \hbox{for} \quad x\in U.
$$

\item[\rm (ii)]
For each fixed $y\in U,$ $x\mapsto G^B_U(x, y)$ is excessive with respect to $X^B$ in $U.$ For each fixed $x\in U,$  $y\mapsto G^B_U(x, y)$ is excessive with respect to $\wh X^{B, U}.$

 \end{enumerate}

  When   $U=B$,  we denote the Green function $G^B_U(x, y)$ by $G^B(x, y)$.
title: Definition 2 of arXiv:2608.13976

[Theorem 11 (An analog of the Borel theorem~\cite{Borel:1909:PDA} for binary representation) of arXiv:2607.29327, 'Fractal Random Variables\\ Defined by Probability Distributions of Digits\\ of Their $G_2$'] Let
  $B = \{x \colon \nu_0(x) = g_0\}$
  be a set of numbers $x$ from interval $[0;g_0]$ such that
  a frequency of digit $0$ in their $G_2$-representation is equal to $g_0$.
  Then the set $B$ is of full Lebesgue measure.

[Theorem Voiculescu of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] Let $A_1 = U_1 \text{} \ensuremath{\operatorname{diag}} (a^{(1)}_1, \ldots,
  a^{(1)}_N) U_1^{\ast}$ and $A_2 = U_2 \ensuremath{\operatorname{diag}} (a^{(2)}_1, \ldots,
  a^{(2)}_N) U_2^{\ast}$ be Hermitian random matrices of size $N$, where $U_1,
  U_2$ are chosen independently at random with respect to the Haar measure
  on the unitary group $U (N)$ and $\{ a_i^{(j)} \}_{i, j}$ are fixed and such
  that for $j = 1, 2$ the empirical distribution of $A_j$ converges weakly to
  a probability measure $\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_j$. Then the random empirical
  distribution of $A_1 + A_2$ converges weakly, in probability to a
  deterministic probability measure $\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_1 \boxplus
  \ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_2$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Voiculescu

[Corollary 2 of arXiv:2608.18075, '2608.18075'] Let $\lambda_1$ denote the top Lyapunov exponent of the derivative
      cocycle $U(t,s)$ over the stationary base law. Then $\lambda_1>-\infty$
      and
      \begin{align}
       \lambda_1
       =
       \int_{H^b\times\PP(H)}
       \left(
         -\nu\norm{\nabla\mathsf p}_2^2
         +\ip{w}{B(\mathsf p,\mathsf p)}_2
       \right)
       \widehat\mu(\dd w,\dd[\mathsf p]),
      \end{align}
      where $\mathsf p$ denotes either representative of $[\mathsf p]$ satisfying
      $\norm{\mathsf p}_2=1$. Moreover,
      \begin{align}
       \lim_{t\to\infty}
       \frac1t\log\norm{U(t,0)\mathsf p}_2
       =
       \lambda_1
      \end{align}
      for $\widehat\mu\otimes\mathbf P$ almost every stationary initial state
      $(w,[\mathsf p])$ and driving Wiener path. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 42 of arXiv:2605.02430, '\textbf{Scaling limit of the range of tree-valued branching random walks in random environ'] For all $n\ino \bbN$, let $(\cF_{n, k})_{k\in \bbN}$ be a filtration on $(\Omega, \ccF)$ and let $(D_{n, k})_{k\in \bbN^*}$ be a sequence of real valued r.v.s. Let $(s_n)_{n\in\bbN}$ be a sequence of integers and let $s\in\bbR_+$. We make the following assumptions. 
\begin{compactenum}
\item[$(a)$] For all $n,k$, $D_{n, k}$ is $\cF_{n,k}$-measurable, $\bE [ D_{n,k}^2] \leko \infty$ and $\bP$-a.s.~$\bE [D_{n, k} | \cF_{n, k-1}]\eqo 0$.
\item[$(b)$] 
There exists a filtration $(\mathcal G_j)_{j\in \bbN}$ on $(\Omega, \ccF)$ and a sequence of integers $(r_n)_{n\in \bbN}$ such that 
$\cF_{n, 0}\eqo \mathcal G_{r_n}$, $n\ino \bbN$. 
\item[$(c)$] For all $\epp \ino (0, 1)$, $\bP$-a.s.~$\lim_{n\to \infty} 
\sum_{1\leq k\leq s_n}\bE [D_{n,k}^2\un_{\{| D_{n, k}|>\epp  \}} | \cF_{n, k-1} ]= 0$. 
\item[$(d)$] $\bP$-a.s.~$\lim_{n\to \infty} \sum_{1\leq k\leq s_n}\bE [D_{n,k}^2 | \cF_{n, k-1} ]\eqo s$. 
\end{compactenum}

\smallskip
\noi
Then, we set $M_n\eqo \sum_{1\leq k\leq s_n}D_{n,k}$ and for all $\lambda \ino \bbR$, we get 
\begin{equation}

\textrm{$\bP$-a.s.~} \quad \lim_{n\to \infty}\bE \big[ e^{i\lambda M_n} \big| \cF_{n, 0} \big] = e^{-\frac{_1}{^2} s\lambda^2}\; .
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 42 of arXiv:2605.02430

body:
[Theorem thm:scaled-murmuration of arXiv:2609.00777, 'Universal murmuration and Hecke augmentation'] Let $k\geq 2$ be fixed.  Let $P\neq 2$ be a prime, and suppose that $P$, $X$, and $Y$ tend to infinity.
Assume that
\[
Y=(1+o(1))X^{1-\delta_1},
\qquad
P^k\ll X^{1+\delta_2},
\]
where
\[
0<2\delta_2<\delta_1<\frac18,
\qquad
(k-1)\delta_2<1.
\]
Put
\[
\eta=\frac{\delta_1}{2}-\delta_2,
\qquad
y=\frac{P^k}{X}.
\]
Let
\[
A=\prod_p\left(1+\frac{p}{(p+1)^2(p-1)}\right),
\]
\[
B=\prod_p\left(1-\frac{p}{(p^2-1)^2}\right),
\]
and
\[
C(r)=\prod_{p\mid r}
\left(1+\frac{p^2}{p^4-2p^2-p+1}\right).
\]
Then, for every $\varepsilon>0$,
\begin{multline*}
\frac{
\displaystyle
\sideset{}{'}\sum_{N\in[X,X+Y]}
\ \sum_{f\in H_{\mathrm{new}}(N)}
P^{k/2}\lambda_{\operatorname{sym}^k f}(P)\,\varepsilon(f)
}{
\displaystyle
\sideset{}{'}\sum_{N\in[X,X+Y]}
\ \sum_{f\in H_{\mathrm{new}}(N)}1
}
\\
=
\frac{12}{\pi D_0}
\left(
A\sqrt y
+
B\sum_{1\leq r\leq 2\sqrt y}
C(r)\sqrt{4y-r^2}
-\pi y
\right)
+
O_{k,\varepsilon}\left(
X^{-\eta+\varepsilon}
+X^\varepsilon\frac{\sqrt y}{P}
+\frac{1+y}{P}
\right).
\end{multline*}
Here the prime indicates that the sum is restricted to squarefree integers $N$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:scaled-murmuration of arXiv:2609.00777

[Thm Bennettinequality of arXiv:2604.10446, 'Least singular values of shifted sparse random combinatorial matrices'] Let $n, m\geq 1$.
Let $M$ be as in (lemma: Negas of the paper).
 Let $Q$ be an $m \times n$ deterministic matrix with all entries in $[0,K]$.
 Then for all $t \geq 0$,
     \[
     \max\{ \mathbb{P}(f_Q(M)-\mu \geq t), \, \mathbb{P}(f_Q(M)-\mu \leq -t)\}
     \leq \exp \left(-\frac{\sigma^2}{K^2} h \left( \frac{Kt}{\sigma^2} \right)\right) 
     \leq  \exp \left(-\frac{3t^2}{6\sigma^2 + 2Kt} \right),
     \]
     where $h(u)=(1+u) \log (1+u) -u $ for $ u \geq 0$.

body:
Let (M_n) be a martingale with respect to a filtration (F_n) and let tau be a stopping time for the same filtration. Then E[M_tau] = E[M_0] under any one of the sufficient conditions: (a) tau is bounded; (b) tau is almost surely finite and (M_n) is uniformly bounded; (c) E[tau] < infinity and the increments |M_n - M_{n-1}| are uniformly bounded. For a submartingale the equality becomes E[M_tau] >= E[M_0] (and <= for a supermartingale). Some integrability condition is essential - without one the martingale of a simple symmetric random walk stopped at first hitting of +1 has E[M_tau]=1 != 0.
(M_n) a martingale for (F_n)
tau a stopping time
one of the sufficient integrability conditions (a)/(b)/(c)

Viewed as a function of time $t \in [0, T]$, $S_R$ is a random element of $K = L^2([0, T])$.

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The even moments of the standard coordinates of $S^3_\mathbb R\subset\mathbb R^4$ are
$$\int_{S^3_\mathbb R}x_i^{2r}dx=\frac{1}{4^r}\cdot\frac{1}{r+1}\binom{2r}{r}$$
the odd moments vanish, and the doubled coordinates follow the Wigner law $\gamma_1$:
$$2x_i\sim\frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{4-x^2}\,dx$$
Moreover, in the standard picture of the group $SU_2$, which is as follows,
$$SU_2=\left\{\begin{pmatrix}x+iy&z+it\\ -z+it&x-iy\end{pmatrix}\Big|(x,y,z,t)\in S^3_\mathbb R\right\}$$ 
the main character is one of these doubled coordinates, $\chi=2x$, following $\gamma_1$.

[Lemma lem:abstract-coherent-fiber of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] Let
\[
 H_N:=\operatorname{span}\{e_1,\ldots,e_N\}\subsetH_{\mathrm{reg}},
\]
where $e_1,\ldots,e_N$ are linearly independent.  Put
$v_t:=\sum_{k=1}^Nt_ke_k$, and let
$t(x)$, $x^\perp$, and $\mathbb P_{H_N}^\perp$ be the corresponding slice
objects from (equation eq:abstract-slice-coordinates of the paper) and
Lemma~(lem:abstract-gaussian-disintegration of the paper).  Let
$\Omega_0\in\mathcal B(X)$ satisfy
$\Omega_0\subset\Omega_{\rm can}$ and $\mathbb P(\Omega_0)=1$; in the
applications below, $\Omega_0=\Omega_{\rm str}$.
For $\mathbb P_{H_N}^\perp$-almost every $x^\perp$, the set
\begin{equation}
 T_0(x^\perp)
 :=\{t\in\mathbb R^N:x^\perp+v_t\in\Omega_0\}
 
\end{equation}
satisfies
\[
 T_0(x^\perp)\in\mathcal B(\mathbb R^N),
 \qquad
 \mathcal L^N(\mathbb R^N\setminus T_0(x^\perp))=0.
\]
For such $x^\perp$ and any
$s\in T_0(x^\perp)$, define
\begin{equation}
 \mu_t^{\rm coh}
 :=e^{\kappa(v_t-v_s)}\mu_{x^\perp+v_s},
 \qquad t\in\mathbb R^N.
 
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{align}
 d\mu_t^{\rm coh}
 &=e^{\kappa(v_t-v_r)}\,d\mu_r^{\rm coh},
 &&r,t\in\mathbb R^N,
 \\
 \mu_t^{\rm coh}
 &=\mu_{x^\perp+v_t},
 &&t\in T_0(x^\perp).
 
\end{align}
If $\Omega_0\subset\Omega_{\rm str}$, then
\begin{equation}
 \mu_t^{\rm coh}\in\mathcal M_{\rm adm},
 \qquad t\in\mathbb R^N.
 
\end{equation}

body:
Let (X,d) be a compact metric space and T : X -> X continuous. Define the Bowen metric d_n(x,y) = max over 0 <= k < n of d(T^k x, T^k y). A set E is (n, eps)-SEPARATED if distinct points of E are at d_n-distance greater than eps; a set F is (n, eps)-SPANNING if every point of X is within d_n-distance eps of some point of F. Let s(n,eps) be the largest cardinality of an (n,eps)-separated set and r(n,eps) the smallest cardinality of an (n,eps)-spanning set. Then the topological entropy is h_top(T) = lim as eps -> 0 of limsup_n (1/n) log s(n,eps) = lim as eps -> 0 of limsup_n (1/n) log r(n,eps), and this agrees with the open-cover definition of Adler, Konheim and McAndrew. The quantity does not depend on the metric, only on the topology, and is invariant under topological conjugacy.
X compact, T continuous.
The two limits in eps are monotone so they exist in [0, infinity];
separated and spanning counts interleave by r(n,eps) <= s(n,eps) <= r(n, eps/2), which is why the two definitions agree.
title: Bowen-Dinaburg definition of topological entropy by spanning and separated sets

[Lemma sylvester_equation_weight_operator of arXiv:2608.23765, '\texorpdfstring{Tight Majorizations and Convergence Rates\\ of Nuclear Norm Minimization I'] Let $\mathbf{X} \in \R^{d_1 \times d_2}$ and $\varepsilon > 0$.
    Let the SVD of $\mathbf{X}$ be given by $\mathbf{X} = \mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}} \diag(\boldsymbol{\sigma}) \mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X}}^{\top}$,
    where $\boldsymbol{\sigma} = (\sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_d) \in \R^d$ are the singular values of $\mathbf{X}$ ordered in nonincreasing order.
    For $i \in [\max \left( d_1 , d_2 \right)]$,
    set
    $\lambda_i := \max \left( \sigma_i, \varepsilon \right)$ with the convention of $\sigma_i = 0$ for $i > d$.
    Define the vectors
    $\boldsymbol{\lambda}_1 := (\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_{d_1}) \in \R^{d_1}$
    and
    $\boldsymbol{\lambda}_2 := (\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_{d_2}) \in \R^{d_2}$.
    Then, 
    for any 
    $\mathbf{Z} \in \R^{d_1 \times d_2}$,
    its image via the harmonic-mean weight operator  $\W{\mathbf{X}}{\varepsilon} (\mathbf{Z})$ with core matrix (eq:harmonic:mean of the paper) is the unique solution of the Sylvester equation
    \begin{equation} 
        \mathbf{L}_{\mathbf{U}} \W{\mathbf{X}}{\varepsilon} (\mathbf{Z}) 
        + \W{\mathbf{X}}{\varepsilon} (\mathbf{Z}) \mathbf{L}_{\mathbf{V}} 
        = 2 \mathbf{Z},
    \end{equation}
    where $\mathbf{L}_{\mathbf{U}} = \mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}} \diag(\boldsymbol{\lambda}_1) \mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}}^{\top}$
    and
    $\mathbf{L}_{\mathbf{V}} = \mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X}} \diag(\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{2}) \mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X}}^{\top}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Sylvester Equation Characterization

[Defn 16 of arXiv:2608.26068, 'All once-extended 3D TQFTs are Reshetikhin--Turaev theories'] $\KV$ is the symmetric monoidal bicategory with 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item Objects: positive integers.
        \item 1-morphisms: matrices of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces.
        \item 2-morphisms: matrices of $k$-linear maps.
    \end{itemize}
    Composition of 1-morphisms and horizontal composition of 2-morphisms is given by matrix multiplication, with $\oplus$ and $\otimes$ playing the role of the usual addition and multiplication. Vertical composition of 2-morphisms is given by the entrywise composition.

    This has a symmetric monoidal structure given by multiplication on objects, and on the 1- and 2-morphisms, the pairwise tensor products of entries.
title: Definition 16 of arXiv:2608.26068

Own-work candidate T387-C006 v1, unaudited sketch; no final-learning or novelty claim. Let d>k>=2, y be a k-parity, and independent online x have law (1-rho) uniform signs plus rho product signs of mean mu. For f=m^(-1)sum a_r ReLU(w_r dot x+b_r), use exact simultaneous hinge-SGD with common step eta, h=eta/m, no neuron-specific randomness. Both initial groups a=+/-1/4 must be nonempty, with w=0,b=1/4. Each group stays internally identical. Group masses p,1-p enter f and its hinge indicator, but the per-neuron step remains h, not eta p. In the all-active regime hT(d+1)<=1/8, set A=(a_plus+a_minus)/2,D=(a_plus-a_minus)/2,U=(u_plus+u_minus)/2,V=(u_plus-u_minus)/2,u=(w,b),z=(x,1). Exact sample increments are Delta A=h y U dot z, Delta U=h y A z, Delta D=h y V dot z, Delta V=h y D z. With v=E[yz], conditional drifts replace yz by v without factorizing any state products. D has zero sample increment initially, so common output noise cancels from it at that step. Pathwise 3/14<=D<=2/7 gives support-ordering failure probability at most k(d-k)exp(-9Tg^2/128) for V, g=rho mu^(k-1)(1-mu^2). The predictor remains affine only in this regime: beta=p a_plus u_plus+(1-p)a_minus u_minus, H=p(u_plus u_plus^T+a_plus^2 I)+(1-p)(u_minus u_minus^T+a_minus^2 I), M=E[zz^T]. Its exact conditional drift is h H v+h^2 M beta; the second-order term comes from simultaneous multiplication of parameter increments. Full gated equations and exact polynomial formulas for the unconditional means of A,D,U,V are in proofs/two_group_drift.md. Means of beta cannot be obtained by multiplying those state means. Numerical evidence is limited to finite exact checks; final parity fitting after gate changes is open. Lean returned runtime UNVERIFIED, so no formal certificate exists.

[Theorem BEbound of arXiv:2605.16244, 'Analysis of a twisted Bose--Einstein Markov chain with applications to sampling Catalan st'] Fix integers $k,n \ge 2$. Let $K$ be the transition kernel of the twisted Bose-Einstein Markov chain on $[k]^n$ and let $\pi$ be its stationary distribution. Then $\lambda_2 = \lambda_2(K) = \frac{k-1}{k(\theta + 1)}$, and for all $t \geq 1$, 
\bal
 \max\left\{
 \frac{\max\{\theta + 1,\theta(k-1)\}}{k\theta + 1}\lambda_2^t,\,
 1-\frac{(\psi(\theta+1)-\psi(1))t+\log(2 + \theta^{-1})}{\log(\min\{n,k\})}
 \right\} 
 \le d_K(t) 
 \le
 \frac n2\sqrt{2k}\,\lambda_2^{t/2}.
\eal
Consequently, for every fixed $\theta>0$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$, if $k=k_n=n^{\beta+o(1)}$, where $\beta>0$ is a fixed constant and $o(1) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$, then
\[
 t_{\mathrm{mix},K}(\varepsilon)

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2609.00867, '2609.00867'] Assume that \(s=m=0\).  Let \(\tau>0\), and let \(\nu\) be a finite signed
measure satisfying
\[
 \nu(\mathbb R^d)=0,
 \qquad
 \int\log(2+\abs{x})\,\abs{\nu}(\dd x)<\infty.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \iint g_\tau(x-y)\,\nu(\dd x)\nu(\dd y)
 =\frac1{\Gamma(d/2)}\int_\tau^\infty
 t^{d/2-1}\norm{p_{t/2}*\nu}_2^2\dd t.
\end{equation}
Consequently, for the density \(\rho\) in
Assumption~\ref{ass:kernel-density}, \((g_\tau)_\rho^\circ\) is positive
semidefinite.

\]
In particular,
\[
        \nu_n(n)=\Theta_p\!\left(\frac{n!}{n^n}q^{n(n+1)/2}\right).
\]

[Proposition 1 of arXiv:2506.11707, 'Fluctuations of two-dimensional determinantal processes associated with Berezin--Toeplitz '] Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:V}, one has the pointwise asymptotics as $N\to\infty$:
\[
\Pi_N(x,x) \sim N \1\{V(x)<\mu\}, \qquad \forall x\in\C \setminus \{V= \mu\}. 
\]
For any $\delta>0$, these asymptotics holds uniformly in $ \{ |V
-\mu| \ge \delta\}$, with error $O(e^{-\alpha\sqrt{N}})$ for any $\alpha>0$. 
In particular, as $N\to +\infty$, the particle number satisfies  \[{\mathcal N}(\mu) \simeq N\bgamma(\mathcal{D}) = \frac N\pi |\{V<\mu\}|.\] 

Moreover,  for any function $f:\C \to\R_+$  with $ f \le e^{C|\cdot|}$
for some $C\ge 0$, the rescaled linear statistic converges: 
\[
N^{-1}\X(f) \to \int_{\mathcal{D}} f \d \bgamma \qquad\text{in $L^2$ as }N\to\infty .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

there exists $\delta>0$ such that for any path development $(\mathfrak{g},F)$ with $\|F\|_{\mathbb{C}^{2}\rightarrow{\cal M}}<\delta,$

setting $\tilde{L}(\gamma)\in{\cal D}(\hat{F})$  provided that the operator
norm of $F$ is small enough (recall that $\tilde{L}(\gamma)$ is the logarithmic signature
of $\gamma\sqcup\overleftarrow{{\rm e}_{1}}$).

body:
[Proposition 14 of arXiv:2608.15874, '2608.15874'] Let $X$ have distribution
\[
  \P{X=2}=\P{X=-2}=\frac1{36},\qquad \P{X=0}=\frac{17}{18}.
\]
Then $X$ is centred with $v:=\E X^2=2/9$, and satisfies the two-sided sub-Poisson condition with variance proxy $v$:
\[
  \log\E e^{sX}=\log\E e^{-sX}\leq v\psi_h(s),\qquad s\geq0.
\]
It therefore also satisfies the two-sided sub-gamma condition with the same variance proxy:
\[
  \log\E e^{sX}=\log\E e^{-sX}\leq v\psi_b(s),\qquad 0\leq s<3.
\]
Moreover, for each $f\in\curlyb{h,b}$,
\[
  \E U_\rho^f(X,v)=1+\frac{1}{54\rho^2}+O(\rho^{-3}),\qquad \rho\to\infty,
\]
so $\E U_\rho^f(X,v)>1$ for all sufficiently large $\rho$.

[Lemma lem:conditions_a_b of arXiv:2608.28169, 'characteristic polynomial of self-normalized random matrices'] Let $\{h_n \}_{n \geqslant 1}$ be a sequence of random elements in $\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$ and denote the coefficients of $h_n$ by $(\xi_k^{(n)} )_{k \geqslant 0}$ so that for all $z \in \mathbb{D}$, $h_n(z) = \sum_{k \geqslant 0} \xi_k^{(n)} z^k$. Suppose also that the following conditions hold.
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[$(a)$] The sequence $\{h_n \}_{n \geqslant 1}$ is
		a tight sequence of random elements of $\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$.
		\item[$(b)$] There exists a sequence $(\xi_k)_{k \geqslant 0}$ of random variables such that, for every $m \geqslant 0$, \\
		$\left(\xi_0^{(n)}, \dots, \xi_m^{(n)}\right) \stackrel{\rm d}{\rightarrow} (\xi_0, \dots, \xi_m)$.
	\end{itemize}
	Then, $h(z) = \sum_{k \geqslant 0} \xi_k z^k$ is a well-defined function in $\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$ and $h_n \stackrel{\rm d}{\rightarrow} h$ in $\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$ for the topology of local uniform convergence. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, A Levy random drift destroys compactness for every confining power (2026). Let V be a two-sided semi-selfsimilar Levy process of index alpha in (0,2) and L^{w+V} = (1/2)(Delta - grad(w+V).grad) on L^2(R; e^{-(w+V)} dx), with w_1 = |x|^delta and w_2 = -|x|^delta; the unperturbed semigroups are compact exactly when delta > 1. Shiozawa and Wang (arXiv:2607.07410, Proposition 5.2) proved the perturbed semigroups noncompact for delta <= 1/alpha and left delta > 1/alpha open (their Remark 5.3(ii)). For delta > 1/alpha: if the Levy measure of V on one of the two half-lines charges (-infinity,0), the bottom of the essential spectrum of -L^{w_1+V} is 0 almost surely, and if one charges (0,infinity) the same holds for -L^{w_2+V}; in either case the semigroup is noncompact. If V changes sign and either alpha < 1 or the jumps go both ways (for instance V symmetric), both semigroups are noncompact for every delta > 0. The case alpha in [1,2) with both Levy measures on the same half-line is left open for one of the two operators. The proof uses test functions with disjoint supports around large jumps of V. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/levy-drift-noncompact (commit f3a3d2c42394). Not refereed.
title: A Levy random drift destroys compactness of the diffusion semigroup for every confining power delta > 1/alpha, on a question of Shiozawa and Wang (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/levy-drift-noncompact)

body:
[Lemma 59 of arXiv:2606.11758, '2606.11758'] Let \(\eta\) be a nonzero finite Borel measure supported on \(\gamma([0,1])\).
Suppose that \(\sigma>0\) is an admissible Fourier decay exponent for
\(\eta\).  Then, for every
\(
    0<\tau<\min\{\sigma,1\},
\)
there exists \(C_{\tau,\gamma}<\infty\) such that, for every
\(x_0\in\operatorname{spt}\eta\) and all sufficiently small \(\rho>0\),
\[
    \eta(B(x_0,\rho))
    \le
    C_{\tau,\gamma}\rho^\tau.
\]
Consequently,
\(
    \alpha_{\min}(\eta)\ge\tau.
\)

body: Lemma (campaign status: proved): Assume affine spanning and coordinate-full homogenization; put $R=\dim\widehat W=m-2$, $M=m+1$. Then after a linear choice of intrinsic coordinates, $\widehat A_t$ becomes an antipodal spanning subset $A\subset\{\pm1\}^R$ (tag 6) which is full closed and whose projective full dual satisfies $|D(A)|=M=R+3$ (tag 7). Notes: Proof: choose $R$ independent full-dual members as a basis and let $\Phi(w)=(g_1(w),\dots,g_R(w))$ (tag 8), a linear isomorphism mapping $\widehat A_t$ into the intrinsic cube. The $M$ displayed homogenized coordinate forms are projectively distinct (if $\widehat f_i=\pm h$ on $\widehat W$, restriction to $U=\ker h=\ker C\times\{0\}$ would give $f_i=0$ on $\ker C$, contradicting old projective simplicity). Closure: if $y\in\operatorname{cl}(A)$ and $w=\Phi^{-1}(y)$, every displayed coordinate of $w$ is a sign, so $w\in\widehat W\cap\{\pm1\}^M=\widehat A_t$.

\[
  \pr_{z_{F,0}}\bigl(T_L < T_0\bigr)
  \;=\; \frac{1 - e^{-\theta z_{F,0}/\kappa_5}}{1 - e^{-\theta L/\kappa_5}},
\]
which at exact criticality $(\theta = 0)$ reduces to $z_{F,0}/L$.

For nonempty compact sets A, B in R^n and their Minkowski sum A + B = {a + b}, the n-th roots of volumes satisfy vol(A + B)^{1/n} >= vol(A)^{1/n} + vol(B)^{1/n}, with equality for homothetic convex bodies. Equivalently vol((1-t)A + tB) >= (vol A)^{1-t} (vol B)^t; the inequality is the geometric root of the isoperimetric inequality and of concentration phenomena in convex geometry.

body: The Riemann–Roch theorem is an important theorem in mathematics, specifically in complex analysis and algebraic geometry, for the computation of the dimension of the space of meromorphic functions with prescribed zeros and allowed poles. It relates the complex analysis of a connected compact Riemann surface with the surface's purely topological genus g, in a way that can be carried over into purely algebraic settings.

body:
[Corollary of arXiv:2410.23509, 'Dynkin Games for L\'evy Processes'] The DG of Definition (def:dg of the paper) for the Brownian motion with drift in (equation eq:bm of the paper) and  payoff functions $G_1(x)=x-\delta,$ $G_2(x)=x+\delta,$ has an optimal stopping rules  given by hitting times of the levels
$$
\aligned
x_I&=-\delta-\dfrac1{r_I}-\dfrac{\sqrt{c^2+2r\sigma^2}}{r}\dfrac{e^{r_Iu}-1}{e^{(r_I+r_S)u}-1},\\
x_S&=\delta+\dfrac1{r_S}+\dfrac{\sqrt{c^2+2r\sigma^2}}{r}\dfrac{e^{r_Su}-1}{e^{(r_I+r_S)u}-1},
\endaligned
$$
where $r_I,r_S$ are the roots in (equation eq:roots_MB of the paper),
and $u$ is the unique positive solution of the equation
\begin{equation*}
u-2\delta=\dfrac{\sqrt{c^2+2r\sigma^2}}{r}
\frac{(e^{r_Su}-1)(e^{r_Iu}-1)}{e^{(r_I+r_S)u}-1},
\end{equation*}
and value function (equation eq:value of the paper)
with
$$
A_I=-\frac1{r_I}\frac{e^{r_Su}-1}{e^{(r_I+r_S)u}-1},
\quad
 A_S=\frac1{r_S}\frac{e^{r_Iu}-1}{e^{(r_I+r_S)u}-1}.
$$
\vskip1mm\par\noindent

Moreover, as a consequence of the discussion in Subsection (subsection:smooth of the paper), in view of the fact that
the infimum and supremum of the process have no atoms, the value function is everywhere differentiable, i.e. we have smooth pasting. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Examine the small parameter of the lace expansion and whether a different expansion parameter exists for d in {7,...,10}. Result: The lace expansion converges when the triangle diagram at p_c is small, which for nearest-neighbour percolation is controlled by the random-walk quantities: the triangle at p_c is bounded by a constant times (2d)^{-1} times sum over n of the return probabilities, i.e. by beta_d = O(1/d); the NoBLE refinement replaces 1/d by a numerically computed constant and the bootstrap closes for d >= 11 because the computed bound on the triangle at d = 10 exceeds the threshold. Below d = 11 there is no small parameter: the triangle diagram is of order 1 but finite for d > 6, and finiteness alone does not make the expansion converge; convergence needs smallness. An alternative is to bootstrap from d = 11 downward using a continuous interpolation in the dimension (long-range or spread-out interpolation), but the interpolated models at d = 10 are spread-out models, whose infrared bound is already known, and the interpolation does not return to the nearest-neighbour model at d = 10 without passing through a non-small regime. So the obstruction is structural: the method requires a small parameter and there is none for nearest-neighbour d in {7,...,10}. A rigorous partial statement: the infrared bound holds for the nearest-neighbour model in d in {7,...,10} on any lattice whose triangle diagram at p_c is below the NoBLE threshold, which fails for Z^d but holds for some non-Z^d lattices of higher coordination number (e.g. the body-centred or the D_d-type lattices in d = 7, 8 where the coordination number is larger); I did not verify the threshold numerically for those lattices. Obstruction: No small parameter for nearest-neighbour Z^d with 7 <= d <= 10.

[Proposition pro:face-crit of arXiv:2606.21391, 'Extreme points and faces in the moment problem'] Let $\mathcal{N}$ be a set of pairs $((A_i)_{i\in I},A)$ where $(A_i)_{i\in I}\subset\mathcal{F}$ 
is an increasing net upper bounded by $A\in\mathcal{F}$ (the directed set $I$ can 
depend on the pair). Then the set of probability measures $\mu\in P$ that satisfy

body: [Definition 4 of arXiv:2511.14740, 'Marking and re-marking'] Let $\mathbf X$ be a random variable taking values in $\mathbb N^d$. Let $\mathsf A = (a_{ij}) \in [0,1]^{c \times d}$ be a matrix where each column $\mathbf a_j \in [0,1]^c$ satisfies $|\mathbf a_j| \leq 1$. Define random variables $\mathbf Z^{(1)}, \dots, \mathbf Z^{(d)}$ as follows: the conditional distribution of $\mathbf Z^{(j)}$ given $\mathbf X$ is multinomial $\mathbf Z^{(j)} \sim \Multi(X_j, \mathbf a_j)$, and the $\mathbf Z^{(j)}$s are conditionally independent given $\mathbf X$. Write $\mathbf Y = \sum_{j=1}^d \mathbf Z^{(j)}$. Then $\mathbf Y$ is the \emph{multinomial re-marking} of $\mathbf X$ with parameters $\mathsf A$, written $\mathbf Y = \mathsf A \circ \mathbf X$.
title: Definition 4 of arXiv:2511.14740

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2604.08127, 'Asymptotics of Brownian occupation measures \\ with unusually large intersections'] Suppose $p \ge 2$ and $d(p-1) < 2p$. Conditioned on $\{ \alpha([0, t]^p) \ge t^p \}$, the tuple of occupation measures $L_t^{\otimes p} = (L_t^1 , \dots , L_t^p)$ satisfies
    \[  
    \lim_{t \to \infty} \widetilde{L}_t^{\otimes p} = \widetilde{\mu}_{d, p}^{\otimes p} \quad \text{in } \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_1^{\otimes p}(\mathbb{R}),
    \]
    where $\mu^{\otimes p}_{d, p} = (\mu_{d, p}^1 , \dots , \mu_{d, p}^p)$. Each $\mu_{d, p}^j$ has density $\psi_{d, p}^2$ where $(\psi_{d, p} , \dots , \psi_{d, p})$ uniquely solves \eqref{eq:mutual-var-problem} (up to diagonal shifts). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem Morph-Vertex of arXiv:2608.29013, 'Weighted Homology and Cohomology of Weighted Polyhedra'] Suppose $(K,\mu)$ and $(K',\mu')$ are two divisibly weighted simplicial complexes of the same type.  Then
   a simplicial map $\varphi: K\rightarrow K'$ is a morphism from $(K,\mu)$ to $(K',\mu')$ if and only if
   for every vertex $v$ of $K$,
   $$ \begin{cases}
   \mu'(\varphi(v)) \mid \mu(v),  &  \text{if $\mu$ and $\mu'$ are ascending}; \\
   \mu(v) \mid \mu'(\varphi(v)),  &  \text{if $\mu$ and $\mu'$ are descending}.
 \end{cases} $$    
 In particular, $\varphi$ is weight-preserving if and only if
 $\mu'(\varphi(v))=\mu(v)$ for every vertex $v$ of $K$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem Morph-Vertex of arXiv:2608.29013

body: [Proposition 9 (\cite{diaconiszhong}, Theorem 2) of arXiv:2511.01245, 'A curiously slowly mixing Markov chain'] The eigenvectors of the Markov chain $K^{\text{lumped}}_n$ are the discrete Chebyshev polynomials $T_n^m$ on $\{0, 1, \cdots, n\}$. The nonzero eigenvalues are $\beta_k = \frac{1}{2^{4k}} \binom{2k}{k}^2$ for $k = 0, 1, \cdots, \lfloor \frac{n}{2} \rfloor$, corresponding to the even-degree Chebyshev polynomials $T_n^{2k}$, respectively. All remaining eigenvalues are zero, corresponding to the odd-degree Chebyshev polynomials $T_n^m$ for odd $m \le n$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{diaconiszhong}, Theorem 2

[Theorem 15 (Candidate verification) of arXiv:2606.17517, 'Killed resolvents and measure-valued stopping gains for reflected optimal stopping with ma'] Let $h$ be a candidate boundary and define $U_h$ by \eqref{eq:Uh-def}. Assume:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(C1)}] $U_h$ is continuous and of polynomial growth.
\item[\textup{(C2)}] $U_h\ge G$ on $\R^2_+$.
\item[\textup{(C3)}] $U_h=G$ on $\mathcal D_h$.
\item[\textup{(C4)}] In $\mathcal C_h$, $(\mathcal L-r)U_h=c$ in the weak,
viscosity, or generalized It\^o sense required by
Theorem~\ref{thm:verification-measure}.
\item[\textup{(C5)}] $U_h$ satisfies the reflected Neumann condition on the
coordinate axes in the trace or reflected-viscosity sense.
\item[\textup{(C6)}] $U_h$ is globally measure-superharmonic relative to the
running cost: $(\mathcal L-r)U_h-c\le0$ as a signed measure in the interior, in
the sense required by Theorem~\ref{thm:verification-measure}.
\item[\textup{(C7)}] The localization, additive-functional, and
uniform-integrability hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:verification-measure} hold
for $U_h$ and $\tau_h$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $U_h=V$ on $\R^2_+$, and $\tau_h$ is optimal. If, in addition, the true
stopping set is known to be an epigraph
$\mathcal D=\{(x_1,x_2):x_2\ge b(x_1)\}$, then $h=b$ at every point where both
graph representatives are defined with the same convention.

regularity assumptions hold, and
\[
\int_\Omega m(x)\varphi_{1,\Omega}^{\alpha+1}\,dx<0.

Then the following assertions hold.

\item[i)]
Problem \eqref{OuyangRepeated} has a nonzero non-negative minimizer
\(\overline u\in H_0^1(\Omega)\). Moreover, $H_{\lambda^*}(\overline u)=0, M(\overline u)=0$.

\(\lambda^*=\lambda_{1,\Omega^0}\), and \(\overline u\) is a positive
multiple of \(\varphi_{1,\Omega^0}\), extended by zero outside
\(\Omega^0\).

\item[iii)]
If, in addition, condition \textbf{(M)} holds, then there exists
\(\tau>0\) such that \(\tau\overline u\) is a weak solution of
\eqref{Eq1} for \(\lambda=\lambda^*\), and $E_{\lambda^*}''(\tau\overline u)=0$.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact identities, finite controls and structural obstruction Result: Writing J_i=E[eta_i*(1-eta_(i+1))], stationarity of eta_i gives J_(i-1)-J_i=kappa*1_(i=0)*E eta_0. There is also an exact obstruction to any independent Bernoulli invariant law whose site densities r_i all lie strictly between0 and1. For adjacent sites, subtract the derivative of r_i*r_(i+1) from the generator derivative of E[eta_i*eta_(i+1)]. At a product law the covariance derivative equals J_i*(r_(i+1)-r_i), with killing terms cancelling. Stationarity therefore forces all adjacent densities equal. The one-site balance at0 then forces kappa*r_0=0, a contradiction. Check: The internal jump i to i+1 leaves eta_i*eta_(i+1) equal to0 both before and after, whereas it changes the two marginal means by -J_i and +J_i. Incoming and outgoing exterior jumps factor under the product law, giving the displayed covariance derivative. Independent killing at0 contributes the same product term in both expressions and cancels. Obstruction: Thus even a piecewise Bernoulli product with strictly interior densities cannot be the desired invariant law. The source matrix-product approach needs nontrivial correlations and a telescoping identity at the killing defect. Neither this obstruction nor the current-balance equation supplies that identity or classifies the correlated stationary measures.

body:
[Proposition 20 (Girsanov is not tight) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] Let $\Prob_{\mathrm{true}}$ and $\Prob_{\mathrm{dir}}$ be the laws of the full and the directed (single-parent-conditioned) systems on a time interval $[0,\tau]$. The Radon--Nikodym density is
\[
\log\frac{d\Prob_{\mathrm{true}}}{d\Prob_{\mathrm{dir}}}=\int_0^\tau\langle b^{-1}\Delta_t,dW_t\rangle-\frac12\int_0^\tau\|b^{-1}\Delta_t\|^2\,dt,
\]
where $\Delta_t=\gamma\,\sigma\big(s^{(v)}_t-\theta_{vu}\big)$ is the back-reaction drift. On the cascade timescale $\|\Delta_t\|=\Theta(1)$ whenever the child is active, so the quadratic-variation term is $\Theta(\tau)$ and the density is not tight toward $1$ as $G_n\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BS}}T$. Hence Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:red} cannot be obtained by a change of measure showing $d\Prob_{\mathrm{true}}/d\Prob_{\mathrm{dir}}\to1$.

[Theorem Thm_KC of arXiv:2511.12692, 'A stochastic flow approach to De Giorgi--Nash--Moser estimates for SPDE\lowercase{s} with '] Let $(M,d_M)$ be a metric space satisfying the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item \emph{(Finite diameter)}  We have $\mathrm{diam}_M \coloneqq \sup_{x,y \in M} d_M(x,y) <\infty$.
    \item \emph{(Finite Minkowski dimension)} There exist $D\in (0,\infty)$ and $C<\infty$ such that $M$ can be covered by no more than $C r^{-D}$ open balls in $(M,d_M)$  of radius $r$, for any $r\in (0,\mathrm{diam}_M]$.
    \item \emph{(Finite doubling number)} There exist $n\in {\mathbb N}$ such that any open ball in $(M,d_M)$ with radius $r$ can be covered by $n$ open balls in $(M,d_M)$ of radius $r/2$.
\end{enumerate}
    Then for $p \in (D,\infty) \cap [1,\infty)$, $\alpha\in (D/p,1)$ and $\beta \in (0,\alpha - D/p)$ and any measurable
    $Z \colon \Omega\times M \to {\mathbb R}^d$ with 
    \begin{equation} C_Z \,\coloneq\, 
    \sup_{x\in M} {\mathbb E}[|Z(x)|^p]^{1/p} \,+\,
    \sup_{x,y \in M} \frac{{\mathbb E} [ |Z(x) - Z(y)|^{\alpha p }]^{1/p} }{d_M(x,y)^\alpha  } \,<\, \infty,
    \end{equation}
    there exists a continuous modification $\widetilde{Z}$ of $Z$ satisfying the bound 
    \begin{equation}
    {\mathbb E}\biggl[ \sup_{x\in M} |Z(x)|^p \,+\, 
     \sup_{x,y \in M} \frac{|Z(x) - Z(y)|^p }{d_M(x,y)^{\beta p} }
    \biggr]^{1/p}\,
    \lesssim_{ (\alpha,\beta,p, M)}  \, C_Z.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition Def:limit_shape of arXiv:2411.13030, 'Classification of the limit shape for 1+1-dimensional FPP'] For $G\neq \delta_0$ and $0\le \theta \le \frac \pi 2$, we define the curve
\[
\mathcal B(\theta)=\frac 1 {\Lambda(\tan(\theta))\cos(\theta)}.
\]
The \emph{limit shape} $\mathcal B_G$ is the closed area embodied by the four symmetrical copies of the curve $\mathcal B(\theta)e^{i\theta}$, 
$\mathcal B(\theta)e^{-i\theta}, -\mathcal B(\theta)e^{i\theta}, -\mathcal B(\theta)e^{-i\theta}$. The union of the four curves then form the boundary of the limit shape $\partial \mathcal B_G$.

body:
[Prop countlayered of arXiv:2609.03081, 'Non-attacking rook placements on crossword grids'] Suppose $m_1, m_2 > 0$ and let $m = \min(m_1, m_2)$. For the layered permutation $w \in S_n$ of shape $(m_1, 1,1,\dots,1, m_2)$, the number of rook placements on $\operatorname{Grid}(w)$ is given by 
    \[
    \sum_{i = 0}^{m-1} S(m_1, m - i)S(m_2, m - i)\left((m-i)^{n - m_1 - m_2} \cdot (m-i)!\right)^2.
    \]
    In particular, if $m > 1$ then for the layered permutation in $S_n$ of shape $(m,1,1,\dots,1,m)$, the number of rook placements on $\operatorname{Grid}(w)$ is given by 
    \[
    \sum_{k = 1}^m \left[S(m, k) \cdot k^{n-2m} \cdot k!\right]^2.
    \]
title: Prop countlayered of arXiv:2609.03081

[Pro dadgty of arXiv:2411.07158, 'Markov chains on trees: almost lower and upper directed cases'] Let $\tau$ and $\tau'$ be two finite or infinite trees such that  $\tau'$ can be obtained from $\tau$ by the suppression of a leaf $\ell$, that is $\tau'=\tau \setminus\{\ell\}$.\par 
Assume that ${\sf U}$ and ${\sf U}'$ are two {\sf AUD}\xspace transition matrices on $\tau$ and $\tau'$, respectively, such that:\\
{\tiny $\blacksquare$ \normalsize } if $u\in \tau'$ and $v\in \tau'\setminus\{p(\ell)\}$ then  ${\sf U}_{u,v}'={\sf U}_{u,v}$,\\
{\tiny $\blacksquare$ \normalsize } if $u\in \tau'$ then  ${\sf U}_{u,p(\ell)}'={\sf U}_{u,p(\ell)}+{\sf U}_{u,\ell}$ ( the transitions in ${\sf U}$ toward $\ell$ are redirected toward $p(\ell)$ in ${\sf U}'$).\par
Then,\begin{itemize} \topsep0pt   \itemsep=0pt   \partopsep=0pt   \parsep=0pt \setcounter{c}{0}
\addtocounter{c}{1}\item[($\roman{c}$)] if $\rho'=(\rho'_u,u\in \tau')$ is a 1-left eigenvector of $\;{\sf U}'$, then   $\rho$  defined by
 \begin{eqnarray}
\bpar{ccl}\rho_u&=& \rho'_u,~~\textrm{if }u\neq \ell,\\
\rho_\ell&=& \displaystyle\sum_{v\in \cro{\varnothing,p(\ell)}} \rho'_v U_{v,\ell } /{\sf U}_{\ell,p(\ell)} \end{array}\right. \end{eqnarray}
is a 1-left eigenvector of ${\sf U}$.
\addtocounter{c}{1}\item[($\roman{c}$)] If $\rho'$ is the $h$-invariant measure $\pi'$ of $\;{\sf U}'$, then $\rho$ defined in \eref{eq:gtey} is the  $h$-invariant measure $\pi$ of $\;{\sf U}$.
\end{itemize}\vspace{-2em}~ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Pro dadgty of arXiv:2411.07158

[Proposition 18 (Differential formula) of arXiv:2609.03361, 'Grassmann--Pl\"ucker Parametrization of Convolutional Filter Subspaces:\ Regularity and Cl'] Under the natural isomorphisms
\[
  T_U\Gr(q,\cK)\cong\Hom(U,\cK/U)
\]
and
\[
  T_{\cC(U)}\Gr(q,H)
  \cong\Hom(\cC(U),H/\cC(U)),
\]
one has, for every $A\in\Hom(U,\cK/U)$,
\begin{equation}
  \dd\Gamma_{\cC}|_U(A)
  =\overline{\cC}_U\circ A\circ(\cC|_U)^{-1}.
\end{equation}

[Lemma lem:coupr of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Let $I=\llbracket a,b\rrbracket$ for some $-\infty \le a < b \le \infty$. 
Take real parameters $\gamma_0<\gamma_1$ and $\{\beta_i\}_{i\in I}$, such that $\gamma_0+\beta_i>0$ for each $i\in I$.

Let $\{A_i,B_i\}_{i\in I}$ be independent random variables with
$A_i\sim \operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(\gamma_0+\beta_i)$, $B_i\sim \operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(\gamma_1+\beta_i)$.
Similarly, let $\{C_i,D_i\}_{i\in I}$ be independent random variables with
$C_i\sim \operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(\gamma_1+\beta_i)$, $D_i\sim \operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(\gamma_0+\beta_i)$.

Then these two families of random variables can be coupled so that almost surely, for any $x\le y\in I$,
\begin{equation}
\sum_{j=x}^y \prod_{i=x}^j A_i \prod_{i=j}^y B_i
=
\sum_{j=x}^y \prod_{i=x}^j C_i \prod_{i=j}^y D_i .
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:coupr of arXiv:2604.10020

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The real probability measure having as moments the middle binomial coefficients, $E_k=\binom{k}{[k/2]}$, is the following law on $[-2,2]$,
$$\sigma_1=\frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{2+x}{2-x}}\,dx$$
called modified arcsine law on $[-2,2]$.

Known result, source-bound formulation of Blum-Dick-Manoj-Zhang (2020), Theorem 1.2 and Corollary B.3. Let d>=2, 2<=p<=infinity (1/infinity=0), B>0 and 0<delta<1. Let R_p(B,delta) be the supremum of radii r>=0 for which some fixed Borel probability law D on R^d satisfies E_D||Z||_2^2<=B and TV(D,D+v)<=delta for every v with ||v||_p<=r, with TV(P,Q)=sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|. Then (2*delta/9)*sqrt(B)*d^(1/p-1) <= R_p(B,delta) <= sqrt(800)*delta/sqrt(1-delta)*sqrt(B)*d^(1/p-1). In particular B=d*sigma^2 gives matching dimension exponent d^(1/p-1/2) at fixed delta and sigma. Arbitrary dependence and nonzero means are allowed for the upper bound; the lower construction is isotropic Gaussian. Fixed classifier accuracy alone does not imply the uniform-TV hypothesis. This does not settle input-dependent smoothing certificates.

0<delta<1 and B>0
One fixed Borel noise law; uniform TV over every shift in the l_p ball

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2607.25986, 'Asymptotics of a two-species particle system associated to the doubly parabolic Keller-Seg'] Fix $\rho_0 \in \Pp(\R^2)$, $c_0 \in L^\infty(\R^2)\cap L^1(\R^2)$, as well as $\chi>0$, $\lambda>0$, 
$\theta>0$, $N\geq 2$, $M>0$ and $\e\in (0,1]$. Consider the $(\rho_0,c_0,N,M,\e)$-2SKS system
with all the associated random objects. For all $\varphi \in C^{2}(\R_+\times\R^d)$, all $t\geq 0$,
\begin{align*}
\langle \nu^{1,N,M,\e}_t,\varphi(t,\cdot)\rangle=& \langle \nu^{1,N,M,\e}_0,\varphi(0,\cdot)\rangle
+\frac 1 \theta \int_0^t \langle \mu^{1,N,M,\e}_s,\varphi(s,\cdot)\rangle\dd s\\
&+ \int_0^t \Big\langle  \nu^{1,N,M,\e}_s, \partial_t\varphi(s,\cdot)+\frac1\theta(\Delta \varphi(s,\cdot)
-\lambda \varphi(s,\cdot))\Big\rangle \dd s\\
&+\frac1{(N-1)M}\sum_{a \in \Uu_{N,M},a_1\neq 1}\sqrt{\frac 2 \theta}\int_0^t \1_{\{s\in [\tau_a^{N,M},\zeta_a^{N,M})\}} 
\nabla\varphi(s,Y^{a,N,M,\e}_s) \dd W^a_s\\
&+\frac1{(N-1)M}\sum_{i\in I_N,i\neq 1}\int_0^t\varphi(s,X^{i,N,M,\e}_s) \dd \tilde \pi_s^{i,M}\\
&-\frac1{(N-1)M}\sum_{a \in \Uu_{N,M},a_1\neq 1}\int_0^t \1_{\{s\in (\tau_a^{N,M},\zeta_a^{N,M}]\}}
\varphi(s,Y^{a,N,M,\e}_\sm) \dd \tilde \Lambda^a_s,
\end{align*}
where $\tilde \pi_t^{i,M}=\pi^{i,M}_t-\frac M\theta t$ and $\tilde \Lambda^a_t= \Lambda^a_t- \frac\lambda \theta t$.
title: Lemma 5 of arXiv:2607.25986

[Proposition 5 (Triangular detector response) of arXiv:2609.02788, '\textbf{Quantized Einstein Metrics on \(S^7\) with \(SU(3)\)-Symmetry}'] At the $p_2$ sine cone, the differential of the reflection detector respects
the Weyl splitting.  The odd response contributes at first order only to
$F_1$, and its complex transfer coefficient is nonzero; equivalently, its
real $F_1$-response is a nontrivial sinusoid of the odd phase.  The regular
even mode contributes at first order only to $F_2$, and its transfer
coefficient is positive.  Thus, in parity-adapted coordinates, the response
has nonzero odd transfer and a positive even diagonal entry.

[Dfn 5 of arXiv:2604.01748, 'Largest-loop-first loop-erased random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^{4}$'] Let $\lambda = [\lambda(0), \lambda(1), \cdots, \lambda(m)]$ be a path of length $m$ in $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$. 
    \begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] Define
    $$ l_{1} = \max \big\{ k -j \ : \ 0 \le j \le k \le m, \ \lambda (j) = \lambda (k) \big\}. $$
This is the maximum length of loops in $\lambda$. Among the pairs $(j,k)$ that attain the maximum on the right-hand side of the definition of $l_{1}$ above, let $(j_{1},k_{1})$ be the one with the smallest $j$:
\begin{itemize}
\item let 
$$\Lambda (1) = \Big\{ (j, k) \, : \, 0 \le j \le k \le m, \ \ \lambda (j) = \lambda (k), \ \ k-j = l_{1} \Big\},$$
\item set 
$$ j_{1} = \min \big\{ 0 \le  j \le m \, : \, \exists k \in [j, m] \, \text{ such that } \, (j,k) \in \Lambda (1) \big\},$$
\item choose $k_{1}$ so that 
$(j_{1}, k_{1}) \in \Lambda (1). $
\end{itemize}
That is, $(j_{1},k_{1})$ is the leftmost pair $(j,k)$ such that $\lambda(j)=\lambda(k)$ and $k-j=l_{1}$.

\item[(ii)]
 We define $\lambda_{1}$ to be the path obtained from $\lambda$ by removing this maximal loop. That is, $\lambda_{1}$ is a path of length $m - k_{1} + j_{1}$ defined by 
$$ \lambda_{1} = [\lambda (0), \cdots, \lambda (j_{1}), \lambda (k_{1} +1), \cdots \lambda (m) ] = \lambda [0, j_{1}] \oplus \lambda [k_{1}, m]. $$
Note that $\lambda = \lambda_{1}$ if and only if $\lambda$ is a simple path. For notational convenience, we abbreviate $\lambda$ as $\lambda_0$.

\item[(iii)] Apply the procedures (i) and (ii) above to $\lambda_{1}$ in the same way. Denote the resulting path by $\lambda_{2}$. Repeating the same procedure, $\lambda_{3}, \lambda_{4}, \cdots$ are obtained.

\item[(iv)] Define $q$ by
$$ q = \min \Big\{ l \ge 0 \ : \ \text{ $\lambda_{l}$ is a simple path} \Big\}.$$
 The largest-loop-first (LLF) loop-erasure of $\lambda$ is given by 
 $$ \text{LE}^{\ast} (\lambda) = \lambda_{q}. $$

\end{itemize}

[Corollary 24 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $G$. 
Assume that the action of $G$ on $\wt B$ satisfies the moment condition \eqref{moment-assumption-01},
the action of $G$ on $B$ satisfies the contraction property \eqref{contraction-property-on-B}, 
and the continuous cocycle $\sigma_0: G \times B \to \bb R$ satisfies the integrability condition \eqref{moment-assumption-02}. 
Suppose that, for every $\wt b \in \wt B$ with $\eta(\wt b) \in \supp \nu$,  we have $\wt b M \subset \overline{\Gamma_{\mu} \wt b}$. 
Fix $\wt b_0 \in \wt B$ with $\eta(\wt b_0) \in \supp \nu$. 
Then, for every character $(\chi, t)$ of the group $(M \times \bb R)/ M_1^{\mu}$, the operator $P_{\mu, \chi, it}$ 
has a unique eigenvalue $\lambda_{\chi, t}$ of modulus one in the space $W_{\chi}^{0}$. 

Moreover, there exists a unique associated eigenvector $\varphi_{\chi, t} \in W_{\chi}^{0}$
such that $\varphi_{\chi, t}(\wt b_0) = 1$ and $\varphi_{\chi, t}$ is H\"older continuous on $\wt B$.  
Also, the generalized eigenspace associated with the eigenvalue $\lambda_{\chi, t}$ for the operator $P_{\mu, \chi, it}$ acting on the space $W_{\chi}^0$ 
is equal to $\bb C \varphi_{\chi, t}$, that is, this eigenvalue is multiplicity free. 

Finally, the restriction $\varphi_{\chi, t}|_{\eta^{-1}(\supp \nu)}$ is the unique continuous function on $\eta^{-1}(\supp \nu)$
such that $\varphi_{\chi, t}(\wt b_0) = 1$ and for every $m \in M$,  $g \in \supp \mu$ and $\wt b \in \eta^{-1}(\supp \nu)$, we have 
\begin{align*}
\varphi_{\chi, t}(\wt b m) = \chi(m)^{-1} \varphi_{\chi, t}(\wt b)
\quad \mbox{and} \quad
\varphi_{\chi, t}(g \wt b) = e^{-it\sigma_0(g, \eta(\wt b))} \lambda_{\chi, t} \varphi_{\chi, t}(\wt b). 
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 24 of arXiv:2607.19873

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2608.27166, 'Well-posedness and regularity of stochastic heat equations on moving domains'] Let $D\subset\R^n$ be bounded and $C^{1,1}$. Suppose $z$ solves
\begin{align*}
\partial_t z
&=
\operatorname{div}(A\nabla z)+c\cdot\nabla z+F+\operatorname{div} H
&&\text{in }(S,2T_0]\times D,
\\
z&=0
&&\text{on }(S,2T_0]\times\partial D,
\end{align*}
where $A$ is bounded and uniformly elliptic, and $c\in L^\infty((S,2T_0]\times D;\R^n)$. Assume
$$
z\in L^\infty((S,2T_0]\times D),
\qquad
F\in L^p((S,2T_0]\times D),
\qquad
H\in L^p((S,2T_0]\times D;\R^n)
$$
for some $p>n+2$. Then there are $\alpha_2\in(0,1)$ and $C>0$, depending only on $n,\lambda,p,T_0,D$ and $\|c\|_{L^\infty}$, such that
\begin{align*}
\|z\|_{C^{\alpha_2/2,\alpha_2}([T_0,2T_0]\times\overline D)}
&\leq
C
\left(
\|z\|_{L^\infty((S,2T_0]\times D)}
+
\|F\|_{L^p((S,2T_0]\times D)}
+
\|H\|_{L^p((S,2T_0]\times D)}
\right).
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 12 of arXiv:2608.27166

[Proposition 16 (Canonical approximation and compactness) of arXiv:2608.29726, '\LARGE A Priori Estimates for Singular Fractional Stochastic Burgers Equations'] Let \((\alpha,\gamma)\) satisfy \eqref{eq:admissible-alpha-gamma}, fix
\(T>0\), and let \(\eps_n\downarrow0\).  Let
\(\mathbb X^n_{\alpha,\gamma}\) be the canonical mollified enhancements of
\Cref{prop:fractional-enhancement}, and let
\(\mathbb X^n_{Q,\lambda}\) be the associated resolvent families from
\eqref{eq:resolvent-model-uniform}.  Suppose that \(u_0^n\in C^\infty(\T)\)
converges strongly to \(u_0\) in \(L^2(\T)\). After passage to a deterministic subsequence, not relabeled, there is an
event \(\Omega_T\) of probability one for which the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=*,nosep]
\item
On \(\Omega_T\), the model convergence of
\Cref{prop:fractional-enhancement} and the uniform resolvent-family
convergence in \eqref{eq:resolvent-model-uniform} hold along the chosen
subsequence.  For \(\omega\in\Omega_T\), use the local uniformity in
\Cref{prop:zvonkin} to choose one resolvent parameter
\(\lambda=\lambda(T,\omega)\) for the limiting and all approximate Zvonkin
maps. For each \(n\), let \(u^n\) be the smooth solution of
\eqref{eq:formal-sbe} driven by \(\xi^{\eps_n}\), with initial condition
\(u_0^n\).  Let \(\ell^n\) be its response, and let
\((\Psi^n,J^n)\) be the Zvonkin pair constructed with the common value of
\(\lambda\).  Define \(m^n\) by
\[
 u^n
 =X^n+X^{\zzone,n}+\ell^n+J^n(m^n)^{\Psi^n}.
\]
Let \((\ell,\Psi,J)\) be the corresponding limiting objects and define
\(a,Q_\lambda,R\) by \eqref{eq:coefficients}.  Then \(m^n(0)=u_0^n\), and the
bounds of \Cref{thm:main-result} hold uniformly in \(n\) for this fixed
realization.

\item
For each \(\omega\in\Omega_T\), there is a further subsequence, possibly
depending on \(\omega\), and a limit \(m\) such that
\begin{align}
 m^n&\longrightarrow m
 &&\text{strongly in }L^2(0,T;L^2),\\
 m^n&\rightharpoonup m
 &&\text{weakly in }L^2(0,T;H^{\gamma/2}),\notag\\
 m^n&\rightharpoonup^\ast m
 &&\text{in }L^\infty(0,T;L^2).\notag
\end{align}
The limit has a representative in \(C_{\mathrm w}([0,T];L^2)\) with
\(m(0)=u_0\), solves \eqref{eq:transformed-equation} in distributions on
\((0,T)\times\T\), with the flux \eqref{eq:Dflux} when \(1<\gamma<2\) and
\eqref{eq:local-check} when \(\gamma=2\), and inherits the bounds of
\Cref{thm:main-result}.  When \(\gamma=2\), this includes the Besov range
\(0<s<1/2\).
\end{enumerate}

[Corollary coro:fringe tree counts large of arXiv:2606.24465, 'History estimation in random recursive trees:\\Pointwise approach via iterated Jordan cent'] There exists a constant $C\ge 1$ such that for all  $t > 0$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$
	\begin{equation*}
		\mathbb{P} \left( \big| \big\{ v\in [n]  : \mathrm{Fr}_{n}(v)  > n/t \big\} \big| >  Ct \right) \leq  \exp \left( 1 -t^{1/4} \right).
	\end{equation*}
\begin{proof}
The statement is clear for $t\leq 1$. So let $t> 1$.
Every $v\in \{u\in [n]:\mathrm{Fr}_n(u)>n/t\}$ other than the root has a parent $u\in \mathcal{U}$ and a child-index $i$ such that $(u,i)\in A_n^\prime$ and $\mathrm{Fr}_n(u)\mathrm{Fr}_n((u,i))>\,(n/t)^2$. Thus
\[
|\{v\in [n]:\mathrm{Fr}_n(v)>n/t\}\big|\le 1 + \big|\{(u,i)\in A_n^\prime:\ \mathrm{Fr}_n(u)\mathrm{Fr}_n((u,i)) > (n/t)^2\}\big|.
\]
Lemma (lem:mixed large of the paper) implies the probability that the right-hand term exceeds $Ct+1$ is at most $\exp(-t^{1/4})$, which yields the claim by increasing the constant $C$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm thm-cont-time-walk of arXiv:2506.18827, 'Random walk reflected off of infinity, with applications to uniform spanning forests and s'] There exists a function $\mathfrak w_* : \mathcal V\mathcal G \to (0,\infty)$ such that for each function $\mathfrak w : \mathcal V\mathcal G \to (0,\infty)$ with $\mathfrak w(x) \geq \mathfrak w_*(x) ,\, \forall x\in\mathcal V\mathcal G$ and for each possible starting point $z \in \mathcal V\mathcal G$, the following is true. There is a unique (in law) continuous-time stochastic process $X : [0,\infty) \to \mathcal V\mathcal G \cup \{\infty\}$ with $X_0 = z$, called the \textbf{continuous time random walk on $\mathcal G$ reflected off of infinity}, which satisfies the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[($i$)]
\item  \textit{(Almost everywhere defined).} For each $t\geq0$, a.s.\ $X_t \in \mathcal V\mathcal G$ and there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that $X_s = X_t$ for each $s\in (t-\varepsilon,t+\varepsilon)$. 
\item  \textit{(Right continuity).} Almost surely, for every $t\geq 0$ such that $X_t\in\mathcal V\mathcal G$, there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that $X_s = X_t$ for each $s\in [t,t+\varepsilon]$. 
\item  \textit{(Continuous time random walk).} If we let $\tau := \min\{t > 0:  X_t \not= z \}$, then $\tau$ and $X_\tau$ are independent, $\tau$ has the exponential distribution with rate $\mathfrak w(z)$, and $X_\tau$ has the law of a step of the random walk on $\mathcal G$ started at $z$ (i.e., for each $x \sim z$, $\mathbbm P[X_\tau = x] = \mathfrak c(z,x) / \pi(z)$). 
\item  \textit{(Markov property).} For every $t\geq 0$ and $x\in\mathcal V\mathcal G$, on the event $\{X_t = x\}$, the conditional law of $\{X_{s+t} \}_{s\geq 0}$ given $\{X_s\}_{s\leq t}$ is the same as the law of $\{X_s\}_{s\geq 0}$ started from $X_0=x$.  
\item  \textit{(Recurrence).} Almost surely, there exist arbitrarily large values of $t\geq 0$ for which $X_t = z$. 
\item  \textit{(Relation to harmonic functions).} Let $\mathcal A\subset \mathcal V\mathcal G$ be a non-empty finite set and let $\phi : \mathcal A\to\mathbbm R$. Let $h^\phi : \mathcal V\mathcal G\to\mathbbm R$ be the energy-minimizing discrete harmonic function as in Proposition~(prop-min-harmonic of the paper). If we let $\tau := \min\{t\geq 0 : X_t \in\mathcal A\}$, then for each choice of starting point $z\in\mathcal V\mathcal G$, 
\begin{equation*}
h^\phi(z) = \mathbbm E_z\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft[ \phi(X_\tau) \aftergroup\egroup\originalright] .
\end{equation*}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm thm-cont-time-walk of arXiv:2506.18827

[Proposition prop:harmonic-grad of arXiv:2609.02987, 'Tail Likelihood Reinforcement Learning'] Under (as:tailrl-smooth,as:tailrl-finite,as:tailrl-bounded of the paper), for every $\theta\in \Theta$ and every $T \ge 1$,
\begin{equation}
\nabla_\theta J^{(T)}_{\mathrm{TailRL{}}}(\theta;x)
=
\sum_{k=1}^{T} \frac{1}{k}\,\nabla_\theta\, \text{\emph{Best-of-}}k(\theta;x)
=
\int_0^1 \frac{1-\big(1-p_\theta(x,\tau)\big)^{T}}{p_\theta(x,\tau)}\,\nabla_\theta p_\theta(x,\tau)\,d\tau .

\end{equation}
title: Harmonic Best-of-$k$ expansion of the gradient

[Lemma devlim of arXiv:2602.08591, 'The Yang--Mills measure on compact surfaces as a \\ universal scaling limit of lattice gau'] Let $\delta>0$ be such that $\exp : B(1_G,\delta) \to \mathfrak{g}$ 
is a diffeomorphism on its image.
Let $p$ be an integer greater than $2$. There exists $C_p >0$ such that if  $\vert X\vert , \vert Y\vert \leqslant \delta$, 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item  there exists $\Lambda_{Y}\in \mathrm{End}(\mathfrak{g})$, such that 
   \[\left \vert \log(\exp X \exp Y)- X- Y - \Lambda_{Y}(X)\right \vert  \leqslant C_p\left( \vert X \vert ^2\vert Y \vert+\vert X \vert \vert Y\vert^{p}\right); \]
   \item we have $\left \vert  \log(\exp X \exp Y)- X- Y\right \vert \leqslant C_p \vert X \vert \vert Y\vert .$
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Lem 4 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any constant $\delta > 0$, there exists $c = c(\alpha, L, \delta) > 0$ such that with probability $1-e^{-cN}$,
    \begin{align}
        
        \bigg|\frac{\|\bar{\bx}\|^2}{N} - 1\bigg| &\le \delta\,,\\
    
        \bigg|\frac{\E[ \|\hat{\by}\|^2 | \bG]}{N} - 1\bigg| &\le
        \frac{\delta}{2}\,.
    \end{align} 
Moreover, conditional on any realization of $\bG$ satisfying \eqref{e:fp-y-cond-conc} the following holds. Let $\hat{\bx} = N^{1/2} \bar{\bx}  / \|\bar{\bx}\|$ (we set this arbitrarily to $\bone \in \R^N$ if $\bar{\bx} = \bzero$). Let $\bXi'$ be an independent copy of $\bXi$ and $\hat{\by}' = \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi')$. Then
    \beq
        
        \lt|\frac{\|\hat{\by}\|^2}{N} - 1\rt|\,,
        \frac{|(\hat{\bx},\hat{\by})|}{N},
        \frac{|(\hat{\by},\hat{\by}')|}{N} \le \delta
    \eeq
   with probability at least $1-e^{-cN}$.

\begin{proof}
    Since $\bG \mapsto \|\bar{\bx}\|$ is $L$-Lipschitz, $\|\bar{\bx}\|$ is $O(1)$-subgaussian by gaussian concentration of measure.
    Combined with $\E \|\bar{\bx}\|^2 = N$ this implies \eqref{e:fp-x-conc}.
    We next argue that the function
    \[
        f(\bG) = \E[ \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]^{1/2}
    \]
    is also $L$-Lipschitz. Indeed,
    \[
        \nabla f(\bG)
        = \frac{\E[ (\nabla_\bG \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi))(\bG,\bXi) \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi) | \bG]}{\E[ \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]^{1/2}}\,,
    \]
    and thus
    \[
        \|\nabla f(\bG)\|^2
        = \frac{\|\E[ (\nabla_\bG \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)) \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi) | \bG]\|^2}{\E[ \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]}
        \le \frac{\E[ \|\nabla_\bG \hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|_\op^2 \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]}{\E[ \|\hat{\by}(\bG,\bXi)\|^2 | \bG]}
        \le L^2\,.
    \]
    Thus $\E[ \|\hat{\by}\|^2 | \bG]^{1/2}$ is also $O(1)$-subgaussian.
    Combined with $\E \|\hat{\by}\|^2 = N$ this proves \eqref{e:fp-y-cond-conc}. 
    The first inequality of \eqref{e:fp-y-conc} follows similarly to \eqref{e:fp-x-conc}, applying gaussian concentration on $\bXi$ conditional on $\bG$.
    The second inequality of \eqref{e:fp-y-conc} holds by gaussian concentration because $\bXi \mapsto (\hat{\bx},\hat{\by}) / N$ is $L/N^{1/2}$-Lipschitz and $\E[\hat{\by} | \bG] = \bzero$. 
    The third inequality of \eqref{e:fp-y-conc} follows similarly, conditioning further on a realization of $\hat{\by}$ such that $\|\hat{\by}\| \le 2N^{1/2}$ (which holds with probability $1-e^{-cN}$).
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 4 of arXiv:2608.29416

body:
[Proposition prop:one-point-conditional-hessian of arXiv:2607.29330, 'Large deviations for the maximum of\\ the generalized TAP free energy'] Let \(f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)\) be regular, let \(\zeta=\zeta_f\), and let
		\(q\) be the first positive contact point of \(\zeta\). Let \(X\) be the
		corresponding Auffinger--Chen process. Suppose that
		\[
		1-\xi''(q)\mathbb{E}\left[
		\left(
		\partial_{xx}\Phi_\zeta(q,X_q)
		\right)^2
		\right]>0.
		\]
		Let \(\mathbf{m}\in (-1,1)^N\) satisfy \(q_\mathbf{m}=q\), and define \(b_i\) by
		\(m_i=\partial_x\Phi_\zeta(q,b_i)\). Assume that
		\[
		\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{b_i}
		\xrightarrow{W_2}\mathrm{Law}(X_q).
		\]
		Let \(f_N\to f\) and condition on
		\[
		\nabla F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})=0,
		\qquad
		F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})=Nf_N.
		\]
		Write \(\mathbb{P}_{\mathbf{m},f_N}\) and \(\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{m},f_N}\) for the corresponding
		conditional probability and expectation. For
		\(\sigma\in\{-,+\}\), the following conclusions hold.
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
			\item There is \(c>0\) such that
			\begin{equation}
				\mathbb{P}_{\mathbf{m},f_N}\left(
				\nabla_\sigma^2F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})\preceq-cI_N
				\right)\longrightarrow1.
			\end{equation}
			
			\item
			\begingroup
			There are \(\delta_0,\kappa>0\) such that, for every
			\(0<\delta<\delta_0\),
			\begin{equation}
				\mathbb{P}_{\mathbf{m},f_N}\left(
				\sup_{\substack{
						x\in(-1,1)^N,\\
						\|x-\mathbf{m}\|_2\le2\sqrt{\delta N}
				}}
				\lambda_{\max}\!\left(
				\nabla^2F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(x)
				\right)
				\le-\kappa
				\right)\longrightarrow1.
			\end{equation}
			If \(q_x\) is an atom of \(\zeta\), the two one-sided Hessians may
			differ. In (equation eq:one-point-local-spectral-gap of the paper),
			\(\nabla^2F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(x)\) denotes
			\(\nabla_-^2F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(x)\), obtained by approaching \(q_x\)
			through smaller self-overlaps.
			\endgroup
		\end{enumerate}
		The conclusion in \textup{(ii)} is uniform under
		\[
		|q_\mathbf{m}-q|\le\varepsilon,
		\qquad
		|f_N-f|\le\varepsilon,
		\qquad
		W_2\left(N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{b_i},\mathrm{Law}(X_q)\right)\le\varepsilon.
		\]
		The probability of the complementary event in
		(equation eq:one-point-local-spectral-gap of the paper) is
		\(o_\varepsilon(1)+o_N(1)\), with \(N\to\infty\) before \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:one-point-conditional-hessian of arXiv:2607.29330

[Lem disjoint-head of arXiv:2608.29018, 'Sharp Restricted Isometry Thresholds for\\ Global Minima of Rank-Restricted Matrix LASSO'] Suppose $0<t\le1$.  Condition $(\bm{T},\bm{S})$
on $\bm{T}\cap\bm{S}=\varnothing$.  The conditional marginals remain
uniform and 
\[
\bm{T}\cup\bm{S}\sim\operatorname{Unif}\{R\subseteq[r_{\star}]:|R|=\alpha+\beta\}.
\]
 Moreover, \begin{subequations}
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}\!\left[\normtwo{\sigma_{\bm{T}}+\sigma_{\bm{S}}}^{2}\,\middle|\,\bm{T}\cap\bm{S}=\varnothing\right] & =t\mathsf{H}^{2},\\
\mathbb{E}\!\left[\normtwo{\beta\sigma_{\bm{T}}-\alpha\sigma_{\bm{S}}}^{2}\,\middle|\,\bm{T}\cap\bm{S}=\varnothing\right] & =\alpha\beta t\mathsf{H}^{2}.
\end{align}
\end{subequations} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Disjoint head sampling

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2604.07579, 'Topology of Percolation Clusters: Central Limit Theorems beyond the Lattice'] Let $G$ be the Cayley graph of an amenable group $\Gamma$
    admitting a finite-index left-orderable subgroup $H$, with
    $n=[\Gamma:H]$. Consider Bernoulli bond percolation on $E(G)$ with parameter
    $p\in(0,1)$ and an exhaustive F{\o}lner sequence $(A_{r})$. Fix a local
    graph simplicial complex rule $\Delta$, and let $\beta_{n}^{r}$ denote the
    $n$-th Betti number of the simplicial complex $\Delta(G(\omega;A_{r}))$.

    Let $\preccurlyeq$ and $(\mathcal{F}_{e})_{e\in E(G)}$ be as in Theorem~\ref{TLC_func}.
    If $\beta_{n}^{r}>0$ a.s.\ for some $r$, then there exists a finite $H$-fundamental
    set of edges $\tilde{E}\subset E(G)$ such that:
    \begin{enumerate}
      \item $\displaystyle \lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{1}{|A_{r}|}\Var_{p}(\beta
        _{n}^{r})=\sigma^{2}$;

      \item $\displaystyle |A_{r}|^{-1/2}\Bigl(\beta_{n}^{r}-\E_{p}[\beta_{n}
        ^{r}]\Bigr)\ \overset{d}{\Longrightarrow}\ \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2}
        )$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Moreover, the asymptotic variance is given by
    \[
      \sigma^{2}=\frac{1}{2n}\sum_{e\in\tilde{E}}\E_{p}\!\left[\E_{p}\!\left
      ( D_{e}^{\infty}\,\middle|\, \mathcal{F}_{e}\right)^{2}\right ],
    \]
    where $D_{e}^{\infty}$ is the limit in probability, as $r\to\infty$, of
    the difference in $\beta_{n}^{r}$ caused by perturbing the state of $e$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 4 of arXiv:2604.07579

[Proposition Btor of arXiv:2608.30747, 'Compact homogeneous complex manifolds'] For any $A,B\in\ag^c$ and $\alpha,\beta\in\Delta_\qg$, $\alpha+\beta\ne 0$, 
$$
T^b(A,B)=0, \qquad T^b(A,E_\alpha)=\tfrac{g_\ag(A,A_\alpha)}{x_\alpha} E_\alpha, \qquad 
T^b(E_\alpha,E_{-\alpha})=-A_\alpha, 
$$
$$
T^b(E_\alpha,E_\beta)=\left\{\begin{array}{cl}
\tfrac{-\epsilon_\alpha\epsilon_\beta\epsilon_{\alpha+\beta} N_{\alpha,\beta}(\epsilon_\alpha x_\alpha+\epsilon_\beta x_\beta-\epsilon_{\alpha+\beta} x_{\alpha+\beta})}{x_{\alpha+\beta}} E_{{\alpha+\beta}}, &\quad \alpha+\beta\in\Delta_\qg, \\ 
0,&\quad \alpha+\beta\notin\Delta_\qg.
\end{array}\right.
$$
In particular, 
$$
T^b(E_\alpha,E_\beta)
=\tfrac{N_{\alpha,\beta}(x_{\alpha+\beta}-x_\alpha-x_\beta)}{x_{\alpha+\beta}} E_{{\alpha+\beta}}, 
\qquad\forall\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta\in\Delta_\qg^{\pm}.  
$$

body:
[Lemma 3 (Radial order-statistic representation) of arXiv:2608.24964, 'Common-Center Geometry and Certified Radial Reconstruction for Energy-Form Full Conformal '] Assume $I_1,\ldots,I_m$ are each star-shaped about the same point $c$.  For
\[
u\in\mathbb S^{d-1},
\]
define
\[
R_j(u)=\sup\{r\ge0:c+ru\in I_j\}\in[0,\infty].
\]
Let
\[
R_{(1)}(u)\le\cdots\le R_{(m)}(u)
\]
be the ascending order statistics.  For $0\le\varepsilon<1$ and
\[
1\le k=\lfloor(m+1)\varepsilon\rfloor\le m,
\]
the radial function of $\Gamma^\varepsilon$ about $c$ is
\[
R_\varepsilon(u)
=
\sup\{r\ge0:c+ru\in\Gamma^\varepsilon\},
\]
and satisfies
\[
R_\varepsilon(u)=R_{(m-k+1)}(u).
\]
If $k=0$, then
\[
\Gamma^\varepsilon=\mathbb R^d,
\qquad
R_\varepsilon(u)=+\infty.
\]
At $\varepsilon=1$, the prediction set is empty.  For the power-distance specialization with $m=1$, one has
\[
I_1=\mathbb R^d,
\qquad
R_1\equiv+\infty.
\]
Thus finite power-distance radial reconstruction begins at $m\ge2$.

[Theorem 3 (Centered Gaussian relative entropy) of arXiv:2607.10769, '\fontsize{14}{17}\selectfont\bfseries Sharp Poincar\'e interpolation along Wasserstein geo'] Let $\mu_0$ and $\mu_1$ be $1$-strongly log-concave, and let
$(\mu_t)_{0\leq t\leq1}$ be their quadratic Wasserstein geodesic.  Then
$0\leq W_{\rm c}^2\leq2n$, and
$\mathcal D_t=\mathcal D(\mu_t)$ satisfies the following distortion
inequality along the whole geodesic:
\begin{equation}
 e^{-\mathcal D_t/n}
 \geq
 \frac{\sin((1-t)\omega)}{\sin\omega}
 e^{-\mathcal D_0/n}
 +\frac{\sin(t\omega)}{\sin\omega}
 e^{-\mathcal D_1/n},\qquad \omega=\sqrt{\frac{2}{n}}\,W_{\rm c}.
\end{equation}
The sine quotients are understood by continuity when $\omega=0$, in
which case they equal $1-t$ and $t$, respectively.
Moreover, equality in \eqref{eq:intro-entropy-distortion} at some
$t\in(0,1)$ holds if and only if $\mu_1$ is a translate of $\mu_0$.
In this case, equality holds for every $t\in[0,1]$. 

In particular, if the endpoints have the same barycenter, then the same statements
hold with $\Ent_\gamma(\mu_t)$ in place of $\mathcal D_t$ and with
$W_2(\mu_0,\mu_1)$ in place of $W_{\rm c}$. In this case, equality at
an interior time holds if and only if $\mu_0=\mu_1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let K_n converge weakly to K in the Hausdorff space of nonempty compact subsets of compact metric S. For nonempty closed A, closed A_m obey N_r_m(A) subset A_m subset N_R_m(A), with 0<r_m<=R_m tending to zero. If every fixed-m avoidance probability has limit q_m and q_m tends to q, then P(K avoids A)=q, even with positive contact mass.
S compact metric; all random sets nonempty compact
A nonempty closed
A_m closed
Both radii positive and tend to zero
First take n to infinity for each fixed m; q_m exists
Then take m to infinity; q_m tends to q
