body:
[Defn 1 (Log-concavity, PF$_2$, and TP$_2$) of arXiv:2605.18751, '\mytitle'] A positive function \(a:J\to(0,\infty)\) on an interval \(J\subseteq E\) is \emph{log-concave} if \(\log a\) is concave on \(J\). In the discrete case this is equivalent to \(\Delta^2\log a(k)\le0\) for every admissible \(k\in J\) and in the continuous case it is equivalent to \((\log a)''(x)\le0\) wherever the second derivative exists.

For a sequence \(b=(b_k)_{k\in\Z}\), we say that \(b\) is a \emph{P\'olya frequency sequence of order 2} (PF$_2$) if \(b_k\ge0\) for all \(k\), the support \(\{k:b_k>0\}\) is an interval in \(\Z\), and \(b\) is log-concave on its support.  A probability distribution \(F\) on \(\N_0\) is PF$_2$ if its mass sequence, extended by zero outside its support, is PF$_2$.

A nonnegative kernel \(M:I\times J\to[0,\infty)\) on two totally ordered sets is \emph{totally positive of order 2} (TP$_2$) if
\[
M(i,j)M(i',j')\ge M(i,j')M(i',j)
\]
whenever \(i\le i'\) and \(j\le j'\). See~\cite{Karlin1968} for the general total positivity theory.
title: Log-concavity, PF$_2$, and TP$_2$

[Lemma 19 (H\"older Continuity of Solutions) of arXiv:2603.26936, 'Sharp Riemannian heat kernel estimates on the cut locus and the Parabolic Anderson model'] Let $\alpha>{(d-2)}/{2}$ (equivalently, $\nu:=2\alpha+2-d>0$). Fix $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and $\varepsilon<T$. Then for every $p\ge 2$ there is a constant $C$ depending on $p,\varepsilon$ and $T$ such that for all
$s,t\in[\varepsilon,T]$ and $x,y\in M$,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}\big|u(t,x)-u(s,y)\big|^p
\le C\Big(|t-s|^{\frac{p\nu}{4}} + d(x,y)^{\frac{p\nu}{2}}\Big).
\end{equation}
Consequently, $u$ admits a modification that is jointly continuous on
$[\varepsilon,T]\times M$, and for any exponents
\[
\gamma_t\in\bigl(0,\min(\nu/4,1)\bigr),\qquad \gamma_x\in\bigl(0,\min(\nu/2,1)\bigr),
\]
the modification is H\"older of order $\gamma_t$ in time and $\gamma_x$ in space
(on $[\varepsilon,T]\times M$).
title: H\"older Continuity of Solutions

[Theorem 2 (Infinite lifetime regime) of arXiv:2505.06187, 'Preferential Attachment Trees with Vertex Death: Persistence of the Maximum Degree'] Consider the PAVD model in Definition~\ref{def:pavd}. Suppose that $b$ and $d$ are such that Assumption~\eqref{ass:A1} is satisfied and let $O\sim \mathrm{Geo}(\P{D=\infty})$. Then, 
		\be 
		O_n\longrightarrow O\qquad \mathbb P_\cS\mathrm{-a.s.}
		\ee 
		In particular, a persistent elder exists, in the sense of~\eqref{eq:persOn}, if and only if Assumption~\eqref{ass:A2} is not satisfied.
		
		Suppose Assumption~\eqref{ass:A1} is satisfied and Assumptions~\eqref{ass:A2} and~\eqref{ass:varphi2} are not satisfied. Then, for any $m\in\N$,   a persistent $m$-hub does not exist $ \mathbb P_\cS$-almost surely. 
		
		If  Assumptions~\eqref{ass:A1}, \eqref{ass:varphi2}, and~\eqref{ass:mufin} are satisfied and Assumption~\eqref{ass:A2} is not, then for any $m\in\N$ there exists an almost surely finite random variable $I^{(m)}$ such that 
		\be 
		I_n^{(m)}\longrightarrow I^{(m)}\qquad \mathbb P_\cS\mathrm{-a.s.} 
		\ee 
		That is, a \emph{persistent $m$-hub} exists $ \mathbb P_\cS$-almost surely, in the sense of~\eqref{eq:pershub}. Moreover, for any $m\geq 2$ there exists $n_0\in\N$ such that for all $n\geq n_0$, 
		\be 
		\deg_n(I_n^{(1)})>\deg_n(I_n^{(2)})>\cdots>\deg_n(I_n^{(m)})\quad\mathbb P_\cS\mathrm{-a.s}.
		\ee (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Publication record. Problem 19.9 of S. Janson's survey (Probab. Surveys 9, 2012; 18.9 in arXiv v1) asks whether the conclusion of his Theorem 19.7 at lambda = 0 also holds when m/n -> 0. Y. Shmalo, Poisson limits for large boxes in sparse random allocations (October 2026) answers it: it holds for every m -> infinity if and only if the support of the weights lies in aZ, a = min{k >= 1 : w_k > 0}; bounded m fails; for b coprime to a the sequences along which it holds are characterized by c_n = n P(xi = b) and m mod a, and for c_n -> c in (0, infinity) the number of boxes with at least b balls is asymptotically Poisson(c) conditioned on a residue class. Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/sparse-allocation-poisson-limits (commit e5851c841b58). Not refereed.
title: Janson Problem 19.9 (arXiv 18.9) answered: Poisson limits for large boxes in sparse random allocations (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/sparse-allocation-poisson-limits)

[Theorem thm:weakly-mixing-Bartlett-component of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] Let $\Gamma\leq\mathbb R^d$ be a lattice and let $(Z,\nu)$ be a
nontrivial weakly mixing probability-preserving Borel
$\Gamma$-space. Then the induced $\mathbb R^d$-space
$\operatorname{Ind}_\Gamma^{\mathbb R^d}(Z)$ admits a generating
stealthy Delone cross-section $Y$ for which
\[
    \sigma_Y
    =
    \sigma_Y^{\mathrm{tor}}
    +
    \sigma_Y^Z,
    \qquad
    \operatorname{supp}\sigma_Y^{\mathrm{tor}}
    \subset
    \Gamma^*\setminus\{0\},
\]
and
\[
    0\neq\sigma_Y^Z
    \ll
    \widetilde{\mathfrak m}_{Z,\nu}^0.
\]
In particular, $\sigma_Y$ has a nonzero continuous component. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:weakly-mixing-Bartlett-component of arXiv:2607.25616

body: A homeomorphism between topological spaces X and Y is a bijection f from X to Y such that both f and its inverse map f^(-1) are continuous. If such a map exists, X and Y are called homeomorphic. Homeomorphic spaces are indistinguishable by topological properties: any property expressed purely in terms of open sets (compactness, connectedness, Hausdorffness, and so on) holds for X if and only if it holds for Y. A continuous bijection need not be a homeomorphism in general; it is one, for example, whenever X is compact and Y is Hausdorff.
title: Homeomorphism

[Theorem thm:PWd of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] For $f\in PW_{\Omega}$ the Fourier inversion formula extends $f$ to an
entire function
$$
  F(z):=\frac{1}{(2\pi)^{d}}\int_{B_{\Omega}}
          \widehat f(\xi)\,e^{i\,\xi\cdot z}\,d\xi,
  \qquad z\in\mathbb{C}^{d},
$$
which satisfies the exponential–type bound
\begin{equation}
|F(z)| \le C e^{\Omega |\mathrm{Im} z|},
\qquad z\in\mathbb{C}^{d},
\end{equation}
for some constant $C$ depending only on $|f|_{L^{2}}$.  Conversely,
any entire $F$ obeying (equation eq:PWd-growth of the paper)

arises in this way from a
unique $f\in PW_{\Omega}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: d–Dimensional Paley–Wiener

	(i) Let $p_1, q_1\in [1,\infty]$ be such that $\frac{d}{p_1}+\frac{2}{q_1}<2$. Then for every $m\geq 1$, there exists a constant $N(c_0,c_1,c_2,\alpha,\beta,\theta,p,q,p_0,q_0,p_1,q_1,\bar{p},d)>0$ such that

	\de 
	
	(ii) Let $q_0=\infty$ and $p>1$. Let $\theta\in[0,1)$ be such that 
	\be 
	\theta<\frac{3}{2}-\frac{d}{2p}-\frac{2}{q}.
	\ee 
	Then for every $\bar{p}\in [1,p)$ and $n\geq 1$, there exists a constant $N$ depending on $C$ such that

	\de 
	
(iii) Assume furthermore that $\frac{d}{p}+\frac{4}{q}<1$ and that there exists a continuous control $\sW_0$ on $\Delta$ and a constant $\Pi\geq 0 $ such that 
	\be
	\|b-b^n\|_{\mH_{-1,p}^q([0,1])}\leq \Pi\sW_0(s,t)^{\frac{1}{q}}
	\ee 
	and 
		\be
	\|b-b^n\|_{\mL_{p}^q([0,1])}\leq \Pi\sW_0(s,t)^{\frac{1}{q}}
	\ee

body:
[Lemma 223 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Functions $\mathfrak{c}$ have the following properties (see also Table~\ref{table:sumf}):

\begin{itemize}
\item For each $g \in [H]$, the $H$-tuple of functions $\boldsymbol{\mathfrak{c}}^{\textnormal{1st}}_{\bullet;g}(z)$ satisfies the master Riemann--Hilbert problem with zero source. Besides, we have $\mathfrak{c}^{\textnormal{1st}}_{h;g}(z) = \frac{\delta_{h,g}}{z} + O(\frac{1}{z^2})$ as $z \rightarrow \infty$ for any $g,h \in [H]$; equivalently: $\oint_{\gamma_h} \frac{\dd z}{2\ii\pi} \mathfrak{c}^{\textnormal{1st}}_{h;g}(z) = \delta_{h,g}$. And, it is tame with exponent $1$.
\item For each $\boldsymbol{f}$, the $H$-tuple of functions $\boldsymbol{\mathfrak{F}}^{\textnormal{I}}[\boldsymbol{f}](z)$ satisfies the master Riemann--Hilbert problem with source
\[
\forall h \in [H]\qquad D_h^{\textnormal{I}}[\boldsymbol{f}](z) = - \oint_{\gamma_h} \frac{\dd\zeta}{2\ii\pi}\, \frac{f_h(\zeta)}{(z - \zeta)^2}.
\]
where $z$ is \emph{inside} the contour of integration. Besides, it behaves as $O(\frac{1}{z^2})$ as $z \rightarrow \infty$. And, it is tame with exponent $1$.
\item For each $\boldsymbol{f}$, the $H$-tuple of functions $\boldsymbol{\mathfrak{F}}^{\textnormal{II}}[\boldsymbol{f}](z)$ satisfies the master Riemann--Hilbert problem with zero source. Besides, it is $O(\frac{1}{z^2})$ as $z \rightarrow \infty$, and it becomes tame with exponent $1$ after subtraction of $(\frac{1}{2} \partial_z(\sigma_h(z)f_h(z)))_{h = 1}^H$.
\item For each $\boldsymbol{f}$, the $H$-tuple of functions $\boldsymbol{\mathfrak{F}}^{\textnormal{III}}[\boldsymbol{f}](z)$ satisfies the master Riemann--Hilbert problem with source
\[
\forall h \in [H] \qquad D_h^{\textnormal{III}}[\boldsymbol{f}](z) = \oint_{\gamma(\alpha_h)} \frac{\dd\zeta}{2\ii\pi}\,\frac{f_h(\zeta)}{(z - \zeta)^2}+\oint_{\gamma(\beta_h)} \frac{\dd\zeta}{2\ii\pi}\,\frac{f_h(\zeta)}{(z - \zeta)^2}.
\]
Besides, it is $O(\frac{1}{z^2})$ as $z \rightarrow \infty$, and it becomes tame with exponent $1$ after subtraction of $(\frac{1}{2\theta_{h,h}} \partial_z f_h(z))_{h = 1}^H$.
\item For each $g \in [H]$ and $\zeta \in \amsmathbb{C} \setminus \amsmathbb{B}$, the $H$-tuple of functions $\boldsymbol{\mathfrak{c}}^{\textnormal{3rd}}_{\bullet;g}(z;\zeta)$ satisfies the master Riemann--Hilbert problem with respect to $z$ and with source
\[
\forall h \in [H] \qquad D_{h;g}(z;\zeta) = -\frac{\delta_{h,g}}{z - \zeta}.
\]
Besides, it is $O(\frac{1}{z^2})$ as $z \rightarrow \infty$. If $\zeta$ is away from the endpoints $\alpha_g,\beta_g$ it is tame with exponent $1$. If $\zeta$ is located at $\alpha_g$ or $\beta_g$, it becomes tame (with respect to the variable $z$) with exponent $1$ after we subtract $\frac{1}{2\theta_{g,g}}\boldsymbol{D}_{\bullet;g}(z;\zeta)$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Thm 2 of arXiv:2606.13459, 'Symmetric Cooperative Motion in Higher Dimensions'] Let $d>1$, $m\geq 1$ and $(X^{n}, n \geq 0)$ be $\CM(m,d)$-distributed started from 0. Let $p(\cdot, n)$ be the PMF of $X^{n}$ (as in \eqref{e.pdef}). There exists $C = C(d,m) > 0$ such that,
	\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
		\item  For all $k \in \Z^{d}$ and $n \in \N$, $p(k,n) \leq Cn^{-d\beta},$
		\item  For all $r > 0$ and $n \in \N$, $\sum_{k\in \Z^{d}\cap B_{rn^{\beta}}^{c}}p(k,n) \leq C \exp(-r/C)$,
		\item  For all $r>0$ and $n \in \N$, $[p(\cdot,n)]_{\TV(B_{rn^{\beta}}\cap\Z^{d})} \leq C r^{d-1}n^{-\beta},$
	\end{enumerate}
	where $B_{rn^{\beta}}$ denotes the ball of radius $rn^{\beta}$ in $\R^{d}$, $B_{rn^{\beta}}^{c}$ denotes its complement, and the discrete total variation $[\cdot]_{\TV(B_{rn^{\beta}}\cap\Z^{d})}$ is defined in \eqref{e.dtv}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 2 of arXiv:2606.13459

body: [Definition def:admissible_path of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] Let $\Gamma$ be a collection of loops in $\mathbf{C}$. We say that a path $\gamma$ is \emph{admissible for $\Gamma$} if it does not cross any loop of $\Gamma$.\footnote{This means that for any subsegment $\ell \subseteq \mathcal {L}$ of a loop $\mathcal {L} \in \Gamma$, if we let $\varphi$ be a conformal transformation from the unbounded connected component of $\mathbf{C}\setminus\ell$ to $\mathbf{C}\setminus\overline{\mathbf{D}}$, then $\varphi(\gamma \setminus \operatorname{fill}(\ell))$ extends to a continuous path in $\mathbf{C}\setminus\mathbf{D}$ (where $\operatorname{fill}(\ell)$ denotes the complement of the unbounded component of $\mathbf{C} \setminus \ell$).}. For each $U \subseteq \mathbf{C}$, we let $\paths{x}{y}{U}{\Gamma}$ denote the set of admissible paths for $\Gamma$ from $x$ to $y$ within $U$.
title: Definition def:admissible_path of arXiv:2507.15589

[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] For the circle graph, having $N$ vertices, the number of length $k$ loops based at one of the vertices is approximately
$$L_k\simeq\frac{2^k}{N}$$
in the $k\to\infty$ limit, when $N$ is odd, and is approximately
$$L_k\simeq\begin{cases}
\frac{2^{k+1}}{N}&(k\ {\rm even})\\
0&(k\ {\rm odd})
\end{cases}$$
also with $k\to\infty$, when $N$ is even.

body:
[Lemma pushforward of arXiv:2603.12774, 'Synchronization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Browni'] Let \((X, \sigma(X))\) and \((Y, \sigma(Y))\) be two measurable spaces and let \(T: X \to Y\) be a measurable mapping.  
	Suppose that \(\tilde{\mu}\) is a Borel measure defined on \((X, \sigma(X))\).  
	The pushforward measure of \(\tilde{\mu}\) under \(T\), denoted by \(T_{\ast}\tilde{\mu}\), is defined on \(Y\) by
	\[
	T_{\ast}\tilde{\mu}(E) := \tilde{\mu}(T^{-1}(E)), \qquad \forall E \in \sigma(Y).
	\]
	Furthermore, for every measurable function \(f: Y \to \mathbb{R}^{+}\), the following identity holds
	\[
	\int_{X} f(T(x)) \, \tilde{\mu}(\mathrm{d}x) 
	= \int_{Y} f(y) \, T_{\ast}\tilde{\mu}(\mathrm{d}y).
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma pushforward of arXiv:2603.12774

[Corollary Scaling of mixing times under a feasible start of arXiv:2608.29657, 'Hypocoercivity of Tempered Bouncy Particle Samplers for Heavy-Tailed Targets'] Let $\{(\mu_0^{(d)},{\mathcal B}({\mathbb R}^d\times{\mathbb R}^d))\}_{d \in {{\mathbb N}\setminus \{0\}}}$ and $\{(\mu^{(d)},{\mathcal B}({\mathbb R}^d))\}_{d \in {\mathbb N}\setminus \{0\}}$ be sequences of probability measures. Also, let $\{\sigma_d : {\mathbb R}^d \rightarrow [1, \infty)\}$ be a sequence of smooth maps. For $d \in {\mathbb N}\setminus \{0\}$,
        define the joint target distribution 
        on ${\mathbb R}^d \times {\mathbb R}^d$ by
        $\mu_\sigma^{(d)} ({\mathrm d} x, {\mathrm d} v) \coloneqq  {(2\pi \sigma_d^2(x))^{-d/2}} \exp(-|v|^2/(2\sigma_d^2(x))) \,{\mathrm d} v\, {\mathrm d}\mu^{(d)}( x )$.\\
        
        (i) Assume that $\log \chi^2(\mu_0^{(d)} \| \mu_\sigma^{(d)}) =  O(d)$. \\
        (ii) Assume that $(\mu^{(d)}, \sigma_d)$ satisfies~(ass:wpi of the paper),~(ass:sigmabounds of the paper) and~(ass:curvature of the paper) with $m = \widetilde \Omega(d^{-l})$ (for some $l \in {\mathbb R}_+$), $M_D = O(1)$, $M_H = O(d^{1/2})$, $M_{U, \sigma} = O(d)$ and $K = O(d)$.\\
        Then we have that $t_\mathrm{mix}(1, \mu_0^{(d)}) =  O(d^{l+ 5})$.
        
        In particular, for $\mu^{(d)}({\mathrm d} x) \propto \langle x \rangle^{-d - r_d} {\mathrm d} x$ for $r_d > d$ or $\mu^{(d)}({\mathrm d} x) \propto \exp( -\langle x \rangle^{p}) \,{\mathrm d} x$ for $p \in (0, 1)$ with the tempering $\sigma_d = \langle x\rangle$ or $\langle x \rangle^{1 - p}$ respectively, assumption (ii) is satisfied for $l = 1$. Then, for initial distributions $\{\mu_0^{(d)}\}_{d \in {\mathbb N}\setminus \{0\}}$ satisfying assumption (i), we have that $t_\mathrm{mix}(1, \mu_0^{(d)}) =  O(d^{6})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Under the standing hypotheses for weak solutions ($U$ bounded open, $a^{ij}=a^{ji}$, $a^{ij},b^i,c\in L^\infty(U_T)$, uniform parabolicity with constant $\theta>0$, $f\in L^2(0,T;L^2(U))$, $g\in L^2(U)$), every weak solution $u$ of $u_t+Lu=f$ with zero lateral data and $u(0)=g$ satisfies $\max_{0\le t\le T}\|u(t)\|_{L^2(U)}+\|u\|_{L^2(0,T;H^1_0(U))}+\|u'\|_{L^2(0,T;H^{-1}(U))}\le C\big(\|f\|_{L^2(0,T;L^2(U))}+\|g\|_{L^2(U)}\big),$ with $C=C(U,T,\theta,\|a^{ij}\|_\infty,\|b^i\|_\infty,\|c\|_\infty)$. In particular the weak solution is unique, and it depends continuously on the data.
U bounded open, T > 0
a^{ij} = a^{ji}, a^{ij}, b^i, c in L^infty(U_T)
uniform parabolicity a^{ij} xi_i xi_j >= theta |xi|^2, theta > 0
f in L^2(0,T;L^2(U)), g in L^2(U)
u a weak solution in the class L^2(0,T;H^1_0) with u' in L^2(0,T;H^{-1})

[Theorem thm:lbound of arXiv:2512.06984, 'Infinite Dimensional Multifractal Analysis of the Wiener measure'] For every $ \bar{\omega} \in \Omega$, we have 
    \[ \underline{\mathsf{ord}}_{\mathrm{loc}} W ( \bar{\omega} ) \ge 2 \frac{1-q^+ ( \bar{\omega}) }{ q^- ( \bar{\omega} ) } \in [0, +\infty ] \; . \]  
    In particular, if $ \bar{\omega} \in \Omega $ admits its Orey exponent $ q(\bar\omega)=\alpha > 0 $, then
    \[  \underline{\mathsf{ord}}_{\mathrm{loc}} W ( \bar{\omega}) \ge 2 ( \alpha^{-1} - 1 ) \;. \]
title: Theorem thm:lbound of arXiv:2512.06984

[Lemma 7 (Stable-subordination normal form) of arXiv:2607.04467, 'Bernstein Functions at Work:\\ Coalescents, Copulas, and Subordination'] Let $P$ be a finite positive measure on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform
$F(u)=\int_0^\infty e^{-ur}\,dP(r)$, let $0<\alpha<1$ and $\lambda>0$, and let
$S_\alpha$ be the positive $\alpha$-stable variable with
$\E e^{-sS_\alpha}=e^{-s^\alpha}$. Define the finite measure
\begin{equation}
Q(A)=\int_{[0,\infty)}\Prob\{(\lambda r)^{1/\alpha}S_\alpha\in A\}\,dP(r).
\end{equation}
Then $\int_0^\infty e^{-xt}\,dQ(t)=F(\lambda x^\alpha)$ for all $x>0$.
title: Stable-subordination normal form

[Corollary cor: main of arXiv:2412.07690, 'A law of large numbers concerning the distribution of critical points of random Fourier se'] Suppose that $m\geq 2$. In white noise limit ($N\to\infty$) the \emph{random} measures $\frac{1}{N^m}\mathfrak{C}\big[\, -, F^N_\mathfrak{a}\,\big]$ converge vaguely a.s. and $L^2$ to the  \emph{deterministic} measure $C_m(\mathfrak{a}){\boldsymbol{\lambda}}$. In particular,  for any  bounded Borel subset $S\subset {\mathbb R}^m$ we have
  \[
\lim_{N\to \infty}  \frac{1}{N^m}\mathfrak{C}\big[\, S, F^N_\mathfrak{a}\,\big]= C_m(\mathfrak{a}){\boldsymbol{\lambda}} \big[\, S\,\big]
\]
a.s. and $L^2$.
\nobreak\hfill\penalty250 \hbox{}\nobreak\hfill$\rlap{$\sqcap$}\sqcup$\vskip\aline (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2607.09246, 'Scaling limit of 1+1 dimensional directed polymer with power-law tail and spatial correlat'] Fix \(C_0<\infty\).  There exists \(C<\infty\), depending only on \(C_0\) and
the tail bounds, such that the following holds for all large \(N\).  Let
\(a,u\in\mathbb R\) and \(b>0\) satisfy
\[
        C_0^{-1}|u|\le b\le C_0|u|,
        \qquad
        |a|\le C_0|u|,
        \qquad
        2bk_N\le1 .
\]
Define
\[
        \Delta^{(b)}
        :=
        \xi\mathbbm{1}_{\{|\xi|>k_N,\ 2b|\xi|\le1\}}
        -
        \mu_N,
        \qquad
        d\mathbb Q_a
        :=
        \frac{e^{a\bar\xi}}
        {\mathbb E_{\mathbb Q}[e^{a\bar\xi}]}\,d\mathbb Q .
\]
Then
\[
        \left|
        \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_a}
        [e^{u\Delta^{(b)}}]-1
        \right|
        \le Cu^2w_N,
\]
and
\[
        \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_a}
        \left[
        (e^{u\Delta^{(b)}}-1)^2
        \right]
        \le Cu^2w_N,
        \qquad
        \left|
        \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_a}
        [e^{2u\Delta^{(b)}}]-1
        \right|
        \le Cu^2w_N .
\]

for all 
$  \overline{b^{+}}\in (\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0})^j $

and for all $k\in [j]$ with $z'_k=0$,
$b^+_k = b_k$,
$\mathrm{hls}(\Psi, \overline{b^{+}},t) = \Psi'$.

[Proposition 23 of arXiv:2608.19832, 'Sharp Convex Concentration for Symmetric Random Tensors with Subgaussian Coordinates'] There are absolute constants $K_0,c,C>0$ such that the following holds.
Let $p$ be an integer such that
\[
 1\le p\le cn,
 \qquad
 dp\log(en/p)\le cn.
\]
There are independent centered variance-one random variables $X_i$ such that
\[
 \norm{X_i}_{\psi_2}\le K_0\qquad(1\le i\le n),
\]
and there is a convex one-Lipschitz function $f$ such that, for every
$m\in\R$,
\[
 \Pp\left\{
 \abs{f(X^{\otimes d})-m}
 \ge c n^{(d-1)/2}\sqrt{dp\log(en/p)}
 \right\}
 \ge e^{-Cp}.
\]

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact integral manipulation, Palm calculus, mass transport, limiting obstruction or conditional construction Result: The vertex graph has constant degree d+1. Under its stationary Palm law, rerooting at a uniformly selected neighbor preserves the marked-vertex marginal by mass transport: send f of the receiving marked vertex along every directed edge with weight 1/(d+1). Outgoing expectation is the neighbor average and incoming mass is f at the root. Thus the separation mark of a uniformly chosen neighbor also has the source Gamma(d+1) marginal. Any proposed joint neighbor formula must reproduce this law, not the Exp(1) law for a volume-typical point. Check: Constant degree makes the incoming weights sum to one. Without constant degree the stationary neighbor-rooted law would instead be degree-biased. The mass transport applies to the full marked configuration. Obstruction: Marginal preservation does not determine dependence between neighboring separation marks, lengths or angles. A joint Palm/Mecke calculation remains missing.

body: For n >= 1 let zeta_n = exp(2 pi i / n) be a primitive n-th root of unity. The n-th cyclotomic field is Q(zeta_n). Facts: (1) the minimal polynomial of zeta_n over Q is the n-th cyclotomic polynomial Phi_n(x) = prod over 1 <= k <= n with gcd(k, n) = 1 of (x - zeta_n^k), which has integer coefficients and is irreducible over Q (Gauss for n prime, Kronecker/Dedekind in general), so [Q(zeta_n) : Q] = phi(n), Euler's totient; (2) Q(zeta_n)/Q is a Galois extension with Galois group canonically isomorphic to (Z/nZ)^*, the automorphism sigma_a sending zeta_n to zeta_n^a; in particular it is abelian, and by the Kronecker-Weber theorem every finite abelian extension of Q lies in some cyclotomic field; (3) the ring of integers of Q(zeta_n) is Z[zeta_n]; (4) a prime p not dividing n is unramified and splits into phi(n)/f primes of residue degree f, where f is the order of p in (Z/nZ)^*; a prime p dividing n ramifies, totally so in Q(zeta_{p^k}) where p is the phi(p^k)-th power of a prime, and p O_K = (1 - zeta_{p^k})^{phi(p^k)}; the discriminant of Q(zeta_{p^k}) is +- p^{p^{k-1}(pk - k - 1)}, and in general the primes ramified in Q(zeta_n) are exactly the primes dividing n (for odd n; 2 ramifies only when 4 divides n); (5) Q(zeta_n) contains the quadratic field Q(sqrt(p^*)) with p^* = (-1)^{(p-1)/2} p for each odd prime p dividing n (Gauss sums), which is one route to quadratic reciprocity; (6) the maximal real subfield is Q(zeta_n + zeta_n^{-1}) of degree phi(n)/2 for n > 2; (7) the class number h_n of Q(zeta_p) is 1 exactly for the primes p <= 19; Kummer proved Fermat's last theorem for regular primes (p not dividing h_p) using the arithmetic of Z[zeta_p]. Cyclotomic fields are the class field theory of Q made explicit and the model case of Iwasawa theory.

For each 0<tau<T, continuous mapping at the positive continuous limit gives

    (n theta_floor(nt))_[tau,T] => (1/U_t)_[tau,T],
    (log theta_floor(nt)+log n)_[tau,T] => (-log U_t)_[tau,T].

    L^2(1-cos theta_L) => t^2/(2 U_t^2),

    Var(log U_t) = Var(log q_t)/4
                = Var(log integral_0^t exp(s+sqrt(2) W_s) ds).       (V)

This is the predicted centered log-angle variance. It is finite: the absolute
value of log(U_t/(a t)) in this equality-in-law representation is bounded by

There is a rigorous truncated network statement, but not an unqualified raw

    Var(g_R(U_n(L/n))) -> Var(g_R(U_t)),  L/n -> t.

Any extension on degenerate paths gives the same bounded-moment limit. Then
dominated convergence using the just-proved finite log moments gives

    lim_(R->infinity) lim_(n->infinity) Var(g_R(U_n(L/n)))
        = Var(log U_t).                                            (TV)

[Proposition prop:zero-cell-continuity of arXiv:2608.13452, 'Wasserstein stability of the zero cell of a Poisson hyperplane tessellation under directio'] Let \(\phi_n,\phi\in\mathcal{P}(S^{d-1})\) be even probability measures, and let \(\gamma_n,\gamma > 0\).
For each \(n\), let \(Z_0^n\) be the zero cell of the stationary Poisson hyperplane process \(\Psi_n\) with intensity measure
\(\Theta_n=(\phi_n \otimes \gamma_n \lambda)\circ \mathfrak{q}^{-1}\) and let \(Z_0\) be the zero cell of the stationary Poisson hyperplane process \(\Psi\) with intensity measure \(\Theta=(\phi \otimes \gamma \lambda)\circ \mathfrak{q}^{-1}\).
Then, \(\phi_n \Rightarrow \phi\) (weakly) and \(\gamma_n \to \gamma\) if and only if \(Z_0^n\) converges to \(Z_0\) in distribution as random convex bodies as $n \to \infty$.

Put F(t)=product_(i=1)^m(t-t_i). Let P_l be the degree-l polynomial orthogonal for weight (1-t^2)^((d-3)/2) on [-1,1], normalized by P_l(1)=1. Every coefficient of F in the basis P_0,...,P_m is strictly positive. This is strict positive definiteness in the coefficient sense used by Cohn-Kumar; it is not an assertion that every Gram matrix of F(<x,y>) is nonsingular. The case m=1 is included.

\begin{equation}
  \langle\mathbf M u,v\rangle
  :=\int_{\widehat B}
  \langle\xi_H,u\rangle\langle\xi_H,v\rangle\,\,d\xi
\end{equation}
commutes with $K_G$. Moreover, if the representation of $K_G$ on $V_1$ is
irreducible, then $$\mathbf M=m_G I,\qquad m_G = \frac{1}{k} \int_{\widehat B} |\xi_H|^2 \,d\xi, $$ and therefore
\[
  A_hf\longrightarrow\kappa_G\Delta_Hf,\qquad
  \kappa_G=\frac{m_G}{2\widehat V}
  ,\qquad
  \Delta_H=\sum_{i=1}^kX_i^2.
\]
This happens, in particular, when $K_G$ acts transitively on the unit
sphere.

For a deterministic K=1 NK-form landscape on 2m bits with F(x)=sum_i J_i 1{x_(2i-1)=x_(2i)}, J_i>0, there are 2^m strict single-bit local maxima, all global. Two distinct peaks differing on pair set D connect by a single-bit path inside {F>=max F-delta} exactly when delta>=max_{i in D} J_i. Label: proof for a deterministic K=1 block landscape, awaiting w346. This is not a typical-case statement about iid Gaussian NK fitness.

On 2m binary sites partition the coordinates into m disjoint pairs. For positive J_i define

F(x)=sum_(i=1)^m J_i * 1{x_(2i-1)=x_(2i)}.

This is a K=1 local NK-form landscape: assign each of the two sites in pair i the local term J_i/2 times the equality indicator, depending on itself and its partner. Its maximum is M=sum J_i, attained at all 2^m configurations whose pairs are each 00 or 11. All are strict single-bit local maxima.

For two such peaks u,v, let D be the pairs on which their 00/11 labels differ. If D is nonempty, the smallest deficit needed for a single-bit path from u to v inside {F>=M-delta} is max_(i in D) J_i.

Necessity: on every path changing the label of pair i from 00 to 11 or conversely, an intermediate configuration has a mismatched pair. Its deficit is at least J_i because all block deficits are nonnegative. Sufficiency: change the differing pairs one at a time, using two bit flips for each. Only the currently changing pair is mismatched, so the largest deficit equals max_(i in D) J_i.

The components of peaks at level delta are therefore exactly classified by the fixed labels of pairs with J_i>delta. There are 2^(number of such pairs) components. Every other vertex in the level set connects to a peak by repairing its mismatched pairs, which only increases fitness, so this is also the component count for the whole level set. In particular J_i=1 gives 2^m isolated peaks for delta<1 and a connected level set for delta>=1. Multiple peaks can therefore have bridges at a bounded deficit in this deterministic NK subclass; neighbor counts alone do not give the earlier proposed universal 'deficit must diverge' criterion. [Corollary 6 of arXiv:2608.29427, '\small Positive mass and rigidity \\ for asymptotically flat tangent bundles'] In the setting of the \hyperref[thm:main]{Main Theorem}:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item 	If $\widetilde g$ is a good metric. Then
		\[
		0\leq
		\underline{\m}(TM,\widetilde g,\zeta)
		\leq
		\overline{\m}(TM,\widetilde g,\zeta)
		<\infty.
		\]
		Moreover,
		\[
		\underline{\m}(TM,\widetilde g,\zeta)=0
		\]
		if and only if
		\[
		(M,g)\cong_{\mathrm{isom}}(\mathbb R^n,\delta)
		\qquad\text{and}\qquad
		(TM,\widetilde g)\cong_{\mathrm{isom}}(\mathbb R^{2n},\delta).
		\]
		\item If $g$ is weakly trace-rigid. Then 
		\[
		(M,g)\cong_{\mathrm{isom}}(\mathbb R^n,\delta)
		\] 
		if and only if there exists an admissible metric $\widetilde g$ on $TM$ with vanishing lower mass.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own-work draft: w720 T306 C17 v1, status sketch, independent review pending. This is a standard entropy-dissipation route obstruction, with no novelty claim. Let d>=1 and let P,Q be finite Gaussian mixtures on R^d, all component covariance matrices positive definite. For each initial law define its Ornstein-Uhlenbeck evolution as the law of exp(-t)X+sqrt(1-exp(-2t))Z, where Z is an independent standard Gaussian; the generator is L=Delta-x dot grad. Write p_t,q_t for the densities, s_p,t=grad log p_t, s_q,t=grad log q_t, M=(E_P||X||^2+E_Q||X||^2)/2 and delta=TV(P,Q)>0, with TV=half the L1 distance. Suppose epsilon>=0 and a jointly measurable field b(t,x) satisfy E_Pt||b(t,X)-s_p,t(X)||^2<=epsilon^2 and E_Qt||b(t,X)-s_q,t(X)||^2<=epsilon^2 for every t in [0,T], where T>0. For r=exp(-2T), the proposed obstruction is delta^2<=2 epsilon^2 T+r M+d[-r-log(1-r)]. All logarithms are natural. The source uses J_t=(KL(P_t||M_t)+KL(Q_t||M_t))/2, where M_t=(P_t+Q_t)/2, and Pinsker gives delta^2<=2J_0. The entropy-dissipation integration by parts and time differentiation remain explicitly pending independent review. The scope is one globally common accurate score field; this does not obstruct transcript-local agreement of instance-specific fields and does not settle T306 Target 2 or give a diffusion query lower bound.

One jointly measurable score field satisfies both absolute L2 error budgets at every time in [0,T]

body:
[Defn Screening Charge of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] Let $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ be a configuration of charges on the Riemann sphere, and let $C_{(b)}[\boldsymbol{\sigma}]$ denote the associated Coulomb gas correlation differential. The conformal dimension of a charge $\sigma \in \mathbb{C}$ inserted at a point $z_j$ is defined by
\begin{equation}
\lambda_b(\sigma) = \frac{\sigma^2}{2} - \sigma b.
\end{equation}
The condition $\lambda_b(\sigma) = 1$ characterizes special charges whose insertions yield integrands of weight $(1,0)$. Solving this quadratic equation yields two solutions:
\[
\sigma = -2a, \quad \sigma = 2(a + b).
\]

A charge $\tau \in \{-2a, \, 2(a + b)\}$ is called a \emph{screening charge}. Consider a divisor of the form
\begin{equation}
\boldsymbol{\sigma} = \sum_i \sigma_i \cdot z_i + \sum_j \tau_j \cdot \xi_j,
\end{equation}
where $\{\tau_j\}$ are screening charges inserted at positions $\{\xi_j\}$.

The resulting Coulomb gas differential on the Riemann sphere $\hat{\mathbb{C}}$ is given by
\begin{equation}
C_{(b)}[\boldsymbol{\sigma}] =
\prod_{i<j} (z_i - z_j)^{\sigma_i \sigma_j}
\prod_{i,k} (z_i - \xi_k)^{\sigma_i \tau_k}
\prod_{j<k} (\xi_j - \xi_k)^{\tau_j \tau_k},
\end{equation}
where the products range over all distinct pairs of points.

Since each $\tau_j$ satisfies $\lambda_b(\tau_j) = 1$, the differential $C_{(b)}[\boldsymbol{\sigma}] \, d\xi_j$ transforms as a holomorphic 1-form in each variable $\xi_j$. This allows for the definition of contour integrals of the form
\[
\int_\Gamma C_{(b)}[\boldsymbol{\sigma}] \, d\xi_1 \cdots d\xi_m,
\]
where $\Gamma$ is a suitable multidimensional integration cycle avoiding branch points.

This procedure is known as \emph{screening}, and it plays a fundamental role in the Coulomb gas formalism. By integrating out screening charges, one obtains new correlation functions that are conformally covariant and satisfy null vector differential equations, as required by conformal field theory.
title: Screening Charge

body:
[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] The ordinary generating function of $H$ is
  \[
    \phi_H(z) = (1-p)^m \binom{m/z - 1}{m}^{-1}.
  \]
  \begin{proof}
    We use the Laplace--Borel transform with $m$ applications of integration
    by parts:
    \begin{align*}
      \frac{\phi_H(x)}{(1-p)^m} &= \int_0^\infty
        \left( e^{xt/m} - 1 \right)^m
        e^{-t} \, dt\\
      &= \underbrace{\left. \left( e^{xt/m} - 1 \right)^m \left(-e^{-t}\right)
          \right|^{t=\infty}_{t=0}}_0\\
      &\quad + \int_0^\infty m\left( e^{xt/m} - 1 \right)^{m-1} \left(\frac{x}{m} \, e^{xt/m}\right)
      e^{-t} \, dt\\
      &= \frac{m\left(x/m\right)}{1} \int_0^\infty \left(e^{xt/m}-1\right)^{m-1}
            e^{-(1-x/m)t} \, dt\\
      &= \frac{m \left(m-1\right) (x/m)^2}{1-x/m} \int_0^\infty \left( e^{xt/m}-1\right)^{m-2}
            e^{-(1-2x/m)t} \, dt\\
      &\ \,\vdots\\
      &= \frac{m!\left(x/m\right)}{\left(m/x - 1\right)^{\underline{m-1}}} 
            \int_0^\infty e^{-(1-x)t} \, dt\\
      &= \frac{m!}{\left(m/x-1\right)^{\underline{m}}} = \binom{m/x - 1}{m}^{-1},
      \quad 0 < x < 1.
    \end{align*}
    The right-hand side is a rational function of $x$, say
    $f(x) / g(x)$ where $f(z)$ and $g(z)$ are real polynomials in $z$.
    Then $f(z) \, g(z)^{-1}$ is a well-defined object in the ring 
    of formal power series $\mathbb{R}[[z]]$ and we can
    restate our result for $\phi_H(z)$;
    see Section~\ref{language}.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 10 of arXiv:2605.14206

[Lemma 22 of arXiv:2604.01978, 'Homogenized Transformers'] Let $X\in(\S^{d-1})^{n}$ and let $R\in\R^{n\times n}$ be its Gram matrix.
Set
\(
R(\gamma)\coloneqq (1-\gamma)I_n+\gamma\,\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\sT}.
\)
Then there exists $L>0$ such that for all $\gamma\in(-1/(n-1),1)$,
\begin{equation*}
\max_{1\leq i\neq j\leq n}|\cD_{ij}(R)-b(\gamma)|
\leq L\max_{(i,j)\in[n]}|R_{ij}-R(\gamma)_{ij}|.
\end{equation*}
(Note that $\mathscr{D}_{ij}(R(\gamma))= b(\gamma)$.)
Moreover one can take $L=O(1+d\sigma_{\bA}^{4}\upbeta^{2}n)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 5 (Exact regenerative representation) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] Let $(C_{n,r},K_{n,r})_{r\ge1}$ be independent copies of $(C_n,K_n)$, with $C_{n,r}$ independent of $K_{n,r}$ for each $r$.  Let
\[
        G_n:=\inf\{r\ge1:C_{n,r}\le K_{n,r}\}.
\]
Then $G_n$ is geometric on $\{1,2,\ldots\}$ with success probability $s_n$, and
\[
        T_n\stackrel{d}=\sum_{r=1}^{G_n-1}(K_{n,r}+1)+C_{n,G_n},
\]
where the sum is empty if $G_n=1$.

body:
[Theorem 7 (Varying environment: interval bounds) of arXiv:2605.04048, 'Catastrophe--dispersion models in random and varying environments across generations'] Consider the Poissonian growth with binomial survival of Example~\ref{ex:poisson-binomial}. Let $(\mathcal E_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a deterministic environment sequence whose components satisfy, for all sufficiently large $n$,
\[
\theta_n\in[\theta_-,\theta_+],\quad
\lambda_n\in[\lambda_-,\lambda_+],\quad
p_n\in[p_-,p_+],\quad
d_n\in[d_-,d_+],
\]
with $0<\lambda_-\le\lambda_+<\theta_-\le\theta_+<+\infty$, $0<p_-\le p_+\le1$, and integers $1\le d_-\le d_+$. Then, for every dispersion mechanism $\Delta^{(j)}$, $j=1,2,3,4$:
\begin{itemize}
  \item if
  $\displaystyle p_+<\frac{\theta_-}{\theta_-+\lambda_+}$,
  the process becomes extinct almost surely;
  \item if
  \[
    \frac{d_-}{d_--1}\,\frac{1-p_-}{p_-}\,
    {}_2F_1\!\Bigl(1,1;d_-;-\frac{\lambda_-p_-}{\theta_+}\Bigr) + {}_2F_1\!\Bigl(1,1;d_-+1;-\frac{\lambda_-p_-}{\theta_+}\Bigr)< \frac{1}{p_-},
  \]
  where ${}_2F_1$ is the hypergeometric function, then the process survives with positive probability.
\end{itemize}

[Definition def:hypLP of arXiv:2412.03366, 'Regularity of Weighted Tensorized Fractional Brownian Fields and associated function space'] \begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] For any $\bar{j} = (j_1,j_2) \in \mathbb{N}^2$ and any
$\boldsymbol{\xi}=(\xi_1,\xi_2) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ set
$$
\theta_{\bar{j}}(\boldsymbol{\xi}) := \theta_{j_1}(\xi_1) \theta_{j_2}(\xi_2) \;.
$$
The function $\theta_{\bar{j}}$ belongs to $\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ for all $\bar{j} \in \mathbb{N}_0^2$ and is compactly supported
on a dyadic rectangle. Further $\sum_{\bar{j} \in \mathbb{N}^2}  \theta_{\bar{j}} = 1$ and
$(\theta_{\bar{j}})_{\bar{j} \in \mathbb{N}^2}$ is called a hyperbolic resolution of unity.
\item[(ii)] For $f \in \mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}^2)$ and $\bar{j} \in \mathbb{N}^2$ set
$$
\Delta_{\bar{j}}f :=  {\mathcal{F}}^{-1} (\theta_{\bar{j}} {\mathcal{F}}f )\;.
$$
The sequence $(\Delta_{\bar{j}}f)_{\bar{j}\in \mathbb{N}^2}$ is called a hyperbolic Littlewood-Paley analysis of $f$.
\end{itemize}

body:
[Lemma lemma-shape-potential-neck of arXiv:2609.00108, 'The double sphere solution in the liquid drop model'] Let \(\Sigma=\partial\Omega\), and let
		\[
		\Sigma_h
		=
		\{
		\hat x= x+h(x)\nu(x):
		x\in\Sigma
		\}
		\]
		be a sufficiently small normal graph enclosing $\Omega_h$. Then for $x \in \Sigma$
		\begin{equation}
			N_{\Omega_h} (\hat x)-N_\Omega (x)
			=
			m\varepsilon^3 \left(
			\int_\Sigma
			\frac{h(\sigma)}{|x-\sigma|}
			\,d\sigma
			+\nabla_x N_\Omega (x) \cdot \nu (x) \, h (x) \right) +
			\tilde  N_\varepsilon[h](x),
		\end{equation}
		where
		\(
		\tilde  N_\varepsilon [0]
		=
		0.
		\)
		Moreover, for any $\alpha \in (0,1)$
		\begin{equation}
			\begin{aligned}
				|\tilde  N_\varepsilon[h](x)|
				\lesssim{}&
				m\varepsilon^3 |h(x)|^{1+\alpha} + m\varepsilon^3 \int_\Sigma |h(\sigma)|^2 
				\sup_{|t|\le |h(\sigma)|}
				\frac{|A(\sigma)|}
				{|x-\sigma-t\nu(\sigma)|}
				d\sigma.
			\end{aligned}
		\end{equation}
		For two sufficiently small graphs \(h_1,h_2\), the remainder
		satisfies the corresponding quadratic Lipschitz estimate
		\begin{equation}
			\begin{aligned}
				&
				|\tilde   N_\varepsilon [h_1](x)
				-
				\tilde  N_\varepsilon [h_2](x)|
				\lesssim
				C \, m\varepsilon^3
				\bigl(
				\|h_1\|^\alpha_\infty+\|h_2\|^\alpha_\infty
				\bigr)
				\|h_1-h_2\|_\infty.

	where $\zeta$ is a constant such that $g(\zeta) \le -N_1$ for $\zeta \ge \zeta_0 $. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: A twin-prime pair consists of two positive prime integers p and p+2. Examples include (3,5), (5,7), (11,13), (17,19), and (41,43). Either member can be called a twin prime. The pair (2,3) is not a twin-prime pair because its gap is one. The twin-prime conjecture asserts that infinitely many such pairs exist; this definition supplies no proof of the conjecture.
title: Twin primes: definition and complete examples

body: Let X_1, X_2, ... be iid random variables in a Polish space X with common law mu, and let L_n = (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n delta_{X_i} be the empirical measure, an element of the space of probability measures on X with the weak topology. Sanov's theorem states that L_n satisfies a large deviation principle, as n -> infinity, with rate function I(nu) equal to the relative entropy D_KL(nu || mu) when nu is absolutely continuous with respect to mu, and I(nu) = +infinity otherwise: for Borel sets Gamma of measures, the log-probability (1/n) log P(L_n in Gamma) has upper limit at most -inf_{closure of Gamma} I and lower limit at least -inf_{interior of Gamma} I. Due to Ivan Sanov.
title: Sanov's theorem

body:
[Corollary cor:at-most-sampler of arXiv:2607.13990, 'Effective Resistance in Fixed-Rank External-Field Measures\\ and Constant-Stretch Correlat'] For every integer $n\ge1$ and every $k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}$, there
exists a jointly measurable map
\[
    B_{n,k}:\Delta^{\le}_{n,k}\times\Omega_{n+k}
\to
    \{S\subseteq[n]:|S|\le k\}
\]
such that
\[
    \left|B_{n,k}(x,\omega)\right|
\in
    \left\{\left\lfloor\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\right\rfloor,\left\lceil\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\right\rceil\right\}
\]
for every $x\in\Delta^{\le}_{n,k}$ and every $\omega\in\Omega_{n+k}$.
Moreover,
\[
    \mathbb P_\omega\bigl(i\in B_{n,k}(x,\omega)\bigr)
=
    x_i
\qquad
    \text{for every }x\in\Delta^{\le}_{n,k}
    \text{ and every }i\in[n],
\]
and
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb E_\omega\left[\left|B_{n,k}(x,\omega)\triangle B_{n,k}(y,\omega)\right|\right]
\le
    32\|x-y\|_1
\qquad
    \text{for every }x,y\in\Delta^{\le}_{n,k}.

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: At most $k$ elements

body:
[Corollary of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] $M$ has an eigenvalue $1$ with multiplicity $1$. $M$ has an eigenvalue $0$ with multiplicity $n/2$ if $n$ is even, and multiplicity $(n-1)/2$ if $n$ is odd.
    \begin{proof}
        By the Perron-Frobenius theorem, $M$ has an eigenvalue $1$ with multiplicity $1$. We also note that by Corollary $(stationary distribution of the paper)$, one can take $\vec{v}=[1,1,...,1]^T$ as the corresponding eigenvector. Note that $M_{ij}=M_{i,n-j+1}$ and $M_{ij}=0$ if and only if $i+1\leq j\leq n-i$, so the rank of $M$ is $n/2$ if $n$ is even and $(n-1)/2$ if $n$ is odd. This shows that $0$ is an eigenvalue with the desired multiplicity.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered corollary of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'

[Lemma 2 of arXiv:2606.23896, 'The one-point Schreier Poisson boundary of Thompson's group \(F\)'] Let \(R\) be a Markov kernel on a countable set \(A\), and

R^\circ(a,b)=\frac{R(a,b)}{1-R(a,a)}

Then

H^\infty(A,R)=H^\infty(A,R^\circ).
\]

In particular, \((A,R)\) and \((A,R^\circ)\) have the same Poisson boundary.

[Proposition prop:Bartlett-torus-base-decomposition of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] Let $(Z,\nu)$ be weakly mixing, and let $Y\subset X$ be a Delone

\[
    \sigma_Y
    =
    \sigma_Y^{\mathrm{tor}}
    +

\]

\[
    \sigma_Y^{\mathrm{tor}}

\]
and
\[

    \widetilde{\mathfrak m}_{Z,\nu}^0.
\]
In particular, $\sigma_Y^Z$ is atomless.

body:
[Definition 35 of arXiv:2605.11801, 'A non-local singular non-linear Fokker-Planck PDE'] Let $\Omega_T^d$ be the canonical space  $C([0,T];\R^d)$ equipped with
     its Borel $\sigma$-field $\shf_T$ and $Z$ be the canonical process. A probability measure $\P\in\shp(\Omega_T)$ is a solution to the rough martingale problem with distributional drift $B$ and initial condition
     $\nu$ 
      if and only if for every $f\in\shd_\shl$ 
    $$f(t,Z_t)-f(0,Z_0)-\int_0^t\mathcal{L}f(s,Z_s)ds$$
    is a local martingale under $\P$, and $\P\circ Z_0^{-1}=\nu$, i.e. $\mathcal{L}aw(Z_0)=\nu$. 
We will also say that $\P$ is a solution to rMP$(B,\nu)$.

body:
[Lemma 26 of arXiv:2608.29585, '2608.29585'] For $m\ge0$, let
\[
 \mathscr P_m
 =\{\lambda:\ell(\lambda)\le n,\ |\lambda|\le m\},
 \qquad
 E_m=\bigl(G_\lambda(p_\mu)\bigr)_
       {\mu,\lambda\in\mathscr P_m},
\]
where
\[
 p_\mu=(Q^{\mu_1+n-1},Q^{\mu_2+n-2},\ldots,Q^{\mu_n}),
\]
and the rows and columns are ordered by any linear extension of
inclusion.  Then $E_m$ is lower triangular and
\[
 G_\lambda(p_\lambda)
 =u_\lambda\prod_{\square\in\lambda}
       (1-Q^{h(\square)}),
 \qquad u_\lambda\in R_{\mathrm{ev}}^\times.
\]
In particular,
\[
 D_m:=\det E_m\in R_{\mathrm{ev}}\setminus\{0\}
\]
is a Laurent unit times a product of cyclotomic polynomials, and
\[
 D_mE_m^{-1}=\operatorname{adj}(E_m)
 \in\operatorname{Mat}_{\mathscr P_m}(R_{\mathrm{ev}}).
\]

If $F=\sum_\lambda b_\lambda G_\lambda\in
\Lambda_n^{\mathrm{pol}}$ and
\[
 \mathbf v_m(F)=\bigl(F(p_\mu)\bigr)_{\mu\in\mathscr P_m},
 \qquad
 \mathbf b_m(F)=\bigl(b_\lambda\bigr)_{\lambda\in\mathscr P_m},
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf v_m(F)=E_m\mathbf b_m(F).
\end{equation}
Consequently, for every ideal $J\subseteq R_{\mathrm{ev}}$,
\[
 F(p_\mu)\in J\quad(\mu\in\mathscr P_m)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 b_\lambda\in D_m^{-1}J
 \quad(\lambda\in\mathscr P_m).
\]

body:
[Proposition 23 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $G$. 
Assume that the action of $G$ on $\wt B$ satisfies the moment condition \eqref{moment-assumption-01},
the action of $G$ on $B$ satisfies the contraction property \eqref{contraction-property-on-B}, 
and the continuous cocycle $\sigma_0: G \times B \to \bb R$ satisfies the integrability condition \eqref{moment-assumption-02}. 
Suppose moreover that, for every $\wt b \in \wt B$ with $\eta(\wt b) \in \supp \nu$,   we have $\wt b M \subset \overline{\Gamma_{\mu} \wt b}$. 
Then, there exists a unique closed subgroup $M_1^{\mu}$ of $M \times \bb R$ with $[M, M] \times \{0\} \subset M_1^{\mu}$ such that,  
for any $x \in \wh M$ and $t \in \bb R$, the operator $P_{\mu, x, it}$ admits an eigenvalue with modulus one in $W^0_x$ if and only if  
$\rho_x$ is the one-dimensional representation associated with a character $\chi_x$ of $M$
such that, for any $(m, s) \in M_1^{\mu}$, one has $\chi_x(m) e^{i st} = 1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 23 of arXiv:2607.19873

body: Index of open problems answered in papers by Y. Shmalo posted in 2026, as public repositories under github.com/yspennstate (several also on arXiv and ResearchGate); none is refereed as of 14 October 2026. Answered in the negative: Aldous-Fill Open Problems 7.27 (arc-transitive-graphs-that-mimic-the-cycle), 4.49(ii) (flow-parameter-diameter), 4.30 (relaxation-time-normal-approximation) and 4.48(a) (variation-threshold-stationary-times); Ding-Lee-Peres Question 5.2 (cover-time-fluctuations); Ganikhodzhaev-Rozikov Problem 11 (strictly-nonvolterra-qso-fixed-points); Thévenin's 2020 conjecture on degree counts (non-gaussian-degree-counts); Janson Problems 19.41 (uniform-condensation-windows), 19.42 and 19.43 (condensation-two-giant-boxes) and 19.30(iii) (second-largest-degree-infinite-variance); Leskelä's form of Ross's second queueing conjecture (Ross-s-second-queueing-conjecture, arXiv:2609.25084); Hasebe-Ueda-Wang Problems 4.3, 4.7 and 4.11 (free-multiplicative-log-unimodality); Agresti-Veraar Problems 4 and 5 (critical-allen-cahn-noise); Pete's Question 13.2 for 0 < q < 1 (random-cluster-not-monotone); Aldous-Janson Open Problem 14, linear growth instead of n log^4 n (beta-splitting-drawn-length); Vu's Conjecture 9.5 (gaussian-integer-spectra); Lyons-Peres Question 17.18 (nonergodic-galton-watson-flow-rule); Holroyd-Levine-Meszaros-Peres-Propp-Wilson Question 6.2 for H >= -1 (sandpile-holes-corner-angles). Answered in the affirmative or proved: Hasebe-Ueda Problem 3.3 with the sharp constant (free-brownian-unimodality-sharp-constant) and Problem 3.11 (free-strong-unimodality); Lyons-Peres Question 6.20 for finite-faced regular tessellations (outer-vertex-isoperimetry); Bradley's Question 5 (phi-mixing-interlaced-rho-mixing-markov); Janson Problem 19.10 with its joint extension (joint-allocation-extremes), Conjecture 19.4 (sparse-allocation-largest-box), Problem 19.9 (sparse-allocation-poisson-limits) and Conjecture 21.1 (level-width-moments); Aldous-Fill 6.13, Kemeny half (maximal-kemeny-constant), and 4.48(b); Garban-Pete-Schramm Section 11 Question 1 and Kalai's Conjecture 8 for crossings (percolation-crossing-entropy, arXiv:2609.15388); the FEI inequality for every linear threshold function (fourier-entropy-threshold-functions, arXiv:2610.16069); Aldous's coagulation-fragmentation mixing item (linear-polymer-relaxation); Kosygina-Zerner Problem 5.3 (positive-cookie-ballisticity); the Krauth-Mézard capacity at zero margin (ising-perceptron-capacity, arXiv:2607.11010). Other results: exact Toeplitz and Hankel moments to order 14 (toeplitz-hankel-exact-moments); the Bubeck-Li-Nagaraj law of robustness up to one logarithm (arXiv:2607.07778); the Gaussian Balan-Wang phase-retrieval base 1/4 (arXiv:2607.06249); Matrix Spencer for Toeplitz and Hankel matrices (ResearchGate 407239961); a new proof of Atanassov's conjecture (arXiv:1708.07175, 2017). Of the 200 famous open problems on the owner's list of 14 October 2026 none is solved; its item T069, the Krauth-Mézard capacity, is the preprint arXiv:2607.11010. Each result has its own publication-record card; answers not yet posted are on the posting-queue card.

body:
CAUTION ON THE NAME: this is the other result commonly called 'Rosenblum's argument' - the contour-integral solution of the Sylvester equation; the scattering-theory Hilbert-Schmidt estimate is a different theorem of the same author, so a citation naming Rosenblum must be matched to its context. STATEMENT: let H and K be complex Banach spaces, A a bounded operator on H, B a bounded operator on K, and suppose their spectra are disjoint: sigma(A) intersect sigma(B) is empty. Then for every bounded operator C from K to H the equation A X - X B = C has a UNIQUE bounded solution X from K to H, and it is given by X = (1 / (2 pi i)) times the contour integral over Gamma of (A - z)^(-1) C (B - z)^(-1) dz, where Gamma is a finite union of positively oriented rectifiable Jordan curves lying in the resolvent set of B, encircling sigma(A) once and sigma(B) not at all. WHERE IT FAILS: (i) disjointness of the spectra is what gives both existence and uniqueness. With A = B and C = 0 the equation A X - X A = 0 is solved by every operator commuting with A, so uniqueness fails badly; and with A = B = 0 on a one-dimensional space the equation is unsolvable for nonzero C. (ii) It is the SPECTRA, not the norms, that matter: no smallness of C is assumed, the solution depends linearly on C, and the bound on X is controlled by the length of Gamma and by the size of the two resolvents on Gamma - a bound that blows up as the spectra approach each other, which is the quantitative content usually needed in perturbation arguments. (iii) The theorem as stated is for BOUNDED A and B; for unbounded operators the analogous statement requires separate hypotheses (sectoriality, semigroup generation), and the contour formula must be justified anew. (iv) Finite-dimensional corollary: for matrices, A X - X B = C is uniquely solvable precisely when A and B have no common eigenvalue.
H and K are complex Banach spaces
A and B are BOUNDED linear operators on H and K respectively
sigma(A) and sigma(B) are disjoint compact subsets of C
C is a bounded operator from K to H
Gamma is a cycle in the resolvent set of B winding once around sigma(A) and not at all around sigma(B)

 \[
(1+o(1))\frac{(\Delta \ell)^{\ell-1}}{\ell!}\, .
 \]

body:
[Theorem modcty of arXiv:2411.05204, '\Large\bf Sample Path Properties of the Fractional Wiener--Weierstrass Bridge'] Let $ Y $ be a fractional Wiener--Weierstrass  bridge with parameters $\alpha$, $b$, and $H$, and $K=\min\{1,({-\log_b\alpha})\}$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]

\item If $H<K$, then $\rho(u)=u^H\sqrt{\log\log(1/u)}$ is an exact local modulus of continuity for $Y$ at every $s\in[0,1]$.
\item If $H=K$, then $\rho(u)=u^H\sqrt{\log (1/u)\log\log(1/u)}$ is an exact local modulus of continuity for $Y$ at every $s\in[0,1]$.
\item If $H>K$, then there exist non-negative random variables $Z_s,~s\in[0,1]$, such that
\begin{align}
    {\mathbb P}\left(\limsup_{t\in[0,1],\,t\to s}\frac{|Y(t)-Y(s)|}{|t-s|^{K}}=Z_s\right)=1.
\end{align}
Moreover, if $\kappa$ is strictly increasing,\footnote{This is a technical assumption, which we expect can be removed.} the random variable $Z_s$ is non-constant, strictly positive, and unbounded for almost every $s\in[0,1]$. 
In particular, $Y$ does not have an exact local modulus of continuity at almost every $s\in[0,1]$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem modcty of arXiv:2411.05204

body: The conditional block bridge is not a proof of critical nonpercolation. Its unproved premise is a fixed, finite, deterministically compatible block construction from theta(p_c)>0 with error delta small enough for its actual sigma-field dependence range r. One self-contained sufficient condition is delta<64^(-(r+1)^2). Qualitative uniqueness and a sequence of high marginal densities with uncontrolled growing range do not supply this certificate: the local-anchor counterexample has densities tending to one and only finite good components. Peer w430 has supplied a coarsening criterion delta<64^(-4)/(r+1)^2, pending designated referee w431; it reduces the promising numerical hurdle but does not construct critical blocks.
title: C0023 compatible finite-block construction: the remaining gap

[Theorem th:crit:exp of arXiv:2506.15949, 'On the passage times of self-similar Gaussian processes on curved boundaries'] If $\nu=1$ and either $0<\beta<d$ or $\beta=d=1$, then
	\[
		\lambda_X(c) \leqslant \lambda_B(c/K_0)
		\qquad\forall c>0,
	\]
	where $B$ denotes an $\fBm$ with index $\alpha = \frac12 (1-\beta\gamma^{-1})$,
	and 
	\begin{align}
		K_0^2 = \frac{c(d\,,\beta)}{2(2\pi)^d} 
		\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left[ \left( 1-{\rm e}^{-\|\xi\|^\gamma} \right)^2  
		+\left( 1-{\rm e}^{-2\|\xi\|^\gamma} \right)  \right] 
		\frac{{\rm d} \xi}{\|\xi\|^{d+\gamma-\beta}}.
	\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm P exact Haus of arXiv:2608.25471, 'Exact Hausdorff measures and fine geometry of collisions of independent Markov processes'] [Exact Hausdorff measure for collision points] 
  Assume that $\hat{d}_{\mathrm{s}} > 2$.
  Then there exist a deterministic function
  $c_1\colon (0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ and a deterministic constant
  $c_2\in(0,\infty)$ such that,
  $\hat{P}_{\bm{\rho}}$-a.s., for all $t \in (0,\infty)$ and for every Borel subset $A$ of $M$,
  \begin{equation}
    c_1(t)\Pi_t(A)
    \leq
    \mathcal{H}_{\Psi_{\mathrm{cp}}}(A\cap\mathcal{P}_t)
    \leq
    c_2\Pi_t(A).
  \end{equation}
  In particular, 
  $0<\mathcal{H}_{\Psi_{\mathrm{cp}}}(\mathcal{P}_t)<\infty$ for all $t \in (0,\infty)$, 
  $\hat{P}_{\bm{\rho}}$-a.s. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Prover-written mathematical claim; independent review pending. Let Y_1,...,Y_n be independent Exp(1) variables, X_i=Y_i-1, and mu the law of X. For every n>=1 and d>=1, the operator f -> T_df=(1/d!)D^dF_f(0), from L2(mu) to the ordered-index Hilbert--Schmidt tensor space, has norm exactly sqrt(binom(2d-2,d-1)). Thus ||T_df||<=2^(d-1)||f||_2 and R=2 is the smallest base valid in ||T_df||<=R^d||f||_2 for all degrees in this family. Equality is attained by the normalized one-coordinate polynomial P_d(Y_1), where P_d(y)=y^d/d!-y^(d-1)/(d-1)!. The proof separates orthogonal coordinate supports before bounding each positive frame-operator trace. The law is isotropic and log-concave but nonsmooth, so this direct calculation does not invoke the regularity-dependent BKL criterion. It does not supply the input for arbitrary log-concave laws.

body:
[Theorem nef-positive-thm of arXiv:2609.00592, 'Bounded cohomology property on Jacobian elliptic surfaces with simplicial Mori cones'] Let $X$ be a smooth projective surface with $q(X)=0$ such that $\overline{\operatorname{NE}}(X)$ is rational polyhedral.
Let $\operatorname{Nef}(X)=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}[C_i]$  where each $C_i$ is an effective divisor on $X$.
Then the following statements holds.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] Suppose each $C_i$ has $\kappa(X,C_i)\ge1$.
Then $X$ satisfies the BCP.
\item[(b)] 
Suppose $\kappa(X)\ge 1$ and $K_X$ is nef. Then $X$ satisfies the BCP if and only if for any indices $i\neq j$ and any curve $D=a_iC_i+a_jC_j$ with $$a_i>0, \quad 0<2a_j(C_i\cdot C_j)<(K_X\cdot C_i),$$we have
$$
\liminf_{a_i\to+\infty}\frac{h^0(\mathcal O_X(a_iC_i+a_jC_j))}{a_i}>0.
$$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem nef-positive-thm of arXiv:2609.00592

body:
STATUS: proof (unaudited); own-work draft; no novelty assertion. Every period-dividing-two orbit of simultaneous joint-head factored-attention GD with nonzero key-query imbalance is a fixed point, at every eta>0. Every nonstationary nonbalanced finite periodic orbit of any period requires delta squared >=2 at some iterate, where delta=eta vG. These exact algebraic obstructions do not prove full-space convergence or exclude balanced cycles. For every eta>0 a distinct-example coupled factored logistic attention family has the exact balanced period-two orbit (2/eta,1,-1) <-> (2/eta,-1,1), with constant loss log 2 and transverse two-step multiplier 9. Thus excluding imbalance-zero points is essential in 014, and an every-initialization GD classification containing only fixed points and endpoint escapes is false; no positive-measure or almost-everywhere failure is claimed.

# Target 1: two-cycle exclusion and necessary overshoot for periodic GD

Version 1, proof unaudited. This excludes possible third fates; it does not
classify all factored-GD trajectories or prove convergence.

Consider the factored model of claim 010 with any eta>0. More generally the
argument applies to any real update
 v_+=v+eta F(v,kq),
 k_+=k+delta q, q_+=q+delta k,
 delta=eta v G(v,kq),
where G is strictly positive at every finite point and F(0,s) has a unique
zero p_bar. The softmax logistic model satisfies these conditions.

1. Every orbit of period dividing two with k^2-q^2!=0 is a fixed point.
   It lies on v=0,kq=p_bar. This holds at every fixed step size.
2. Every nonstationary finite periodic orbit with k^2-q^2!=0 at one (hence
   every) iterate must contain an iterate with delta^2>=2. Equivalently,
   any periodic orbit on which |eta vG|<sqrt(2) throughout is stationary.

Neither statement excludes balanced-plane cycles, long cycles with large
overshoot, unbounded nonconvergent orbits, or nonperiodic bounded invariant
sets. This is a special obstruction result, not a scored global classification.

## Proof of two-cycle exclusion

Let U=k+q and D=k-q. Their exact simultaneous updates are
 U_+=(1+delta)U, D_+=(1-delta)D.
The nonzero imbalance is C=UD, so U,D are both nonzero initially.
For a returning two-step orbit, with a=delta_0,b=delta_1,
 (1+a)(1+b)=1, (1-a)(1-b)=1.
Expansion and addition yield 2ab=0; subtraction yields 2(a+b)=0.
Over the reals this forces a=b=0. Since eta>0 and G>0, v_0=v_1=0.
The factors therefore do not move. The head update then forces
F(0,kq)=0, hence kq=p_bar. This is a fixed point, as claimed.

## Proof of the overshoot requirement

The exact imbalance update is C_+=(1-delta^2)C. If an r-step orbit returns
with C_0!=0, no intermediate C can vanish, and
 product_{t=0}^{r-1}(1-delta_t^2)=1.
If every delta_t^2<2, every absolute factor is <=1, strictly less than 1
whenever delta_t!=0. The product can have absolute value 1 only if every
delta_t=0. Then every v_t=0, the factors stay fixed, and F(0,kq)=0.
Thus any nonstationary periodic orbit requires at least one delta_t^2>=2.

## Relation to the remaining gap

The flow's invariant imbalance is unavailable in GD, but its multiplicative
replacement still excludes every nonbalanced two-cycle, including at steps
beyond the normal-stability threshold of claim 013. A loss of an attracting
normal multiplier therefore does not by itself provide a two-cycle witness.
The unresolved step is controlling general, possibly large factor updates
well enough to show eventual entry into one of claim 010's escaping regions,
or finding a third fate that persists off the balanced planes.


# Target 1: exact balanced two-cycle and its transverse multiplier

Version 1, proof unaudited. Boundary check for claim 014, not a positive-volume
counterexample to an almost-everywhere theorem.

Fix any n>=2 and any distinct positive kappa_i. Put
 b_i=2 cosh(kappa_i)^2/kappa_i,
 a_i=b_i tanh(kappa_i).
These satisfy 0<a_i<b_i. In the usual coupled factored model
h_i(s)=a_i+b_i tanh(kappa_i s), all links have
 h_i(-1)=0, h_i'(-1)=2.

For EVERY fixed eta>0, simultaneous Euclidean GD on the average logistic
loss has an exact two-cycle
 (v,k,q)=(2/eta,1,-1) <-> (2/eta,-1,1).
At both points the loss is log 2, the product is -1, and k^2-q^2=0.
The two-step Jacobian has a transverse multiplier 9 normal to k=-q.
Thus the nonzero-imbalance assumption in 014 is necessary. This cycle
does not establish a positive-measure basin or rule out almost-everywhere
endpoint convergence.

## Proof

At either displayed state every h_i(kq)=0, so g_i=1/2, F=0 and
G=mean_i g_i h_i'=1. The head therefore stays fixed and
delta=eta vG=2. The factor update sends
 (k,q)->(k+2q,q+2k).
It exchanges (1,-1) and (-1,1). The cycle is nonstationary and has exact
period two; the loss remains log(1+exp(0))=log 2. The construction uses
different nonlinear scales, rather than requiring repeated identical examples.

The full factor-sum identity is U_+=(1+delta)U, U=k+q. At U=0 its
linearization gives dU_+=(1+delta)dU=3dU; the term U d(delta) vanishes.
After two steps dU_{++}=9dU, an exact normal multiplier even when v and
the product vary in the perturbation. No stability assertion at a unit
multiplier is involved.

The same constructed family has finite stationary points at v=0,kq=-1,
whereas the displayed periodic points have v=2/eta>0. Hence a classification
of every finite initialization by stationary points and escaping selections
alone would be false at any positive constant step. The exceptional balanced
plane must be allowed, as it is in claim 012's flow statement (which is a
different dynamical system).
Updates v+=v+eta F(v,kq), k+=k+delta q, q+=q+delta k; eta>0, G(v,s)>0 at every finite point, delta=eta vG; F(0,s) uniquely zero at p_bar. Includes 010 logistic tanh family.
n>=2; arbitrary distinct kappa_i>0; b_i=2 cosh(kappa_i)^2/kappa_i, a_i=b_i tanh(kappa_i); h_i(s)=a_i+b_i tanh(kappa_i s); simultaneous Euclidean GD on average logistic loss in (v,k,q), p=kq, eta>0.

with C_0!=0, no intermediate C can vanish, and
 product_{t=0}^{r-1}(1-delta_t^2)=1.
If every delta_t^2<2, every absolute factor is <=1, strictly less than 1
whenever delta_t!=0. The product can have absolute value 1 only if every
delta_t=0. Then every v_t=0, the factors stay fixed, and F(0,kq)=0.
Thus any nonstationary periodic orbit requires at least one delta_t^2>=2.

## Relation to the remaining gap

The flow's invariant imbalance is unavailable in GD, but its multiplicative
replacement still excludes every nonbalanced two-cycle, including at steps
beyond the normal-stability threshold of claim 013. A loss of an attracting
normal multiplier therefore does not by itself provide a two-cycle witness.
The unresolved step is controlling general, possibly large factor updates
well enough to show eventual entry into one of claim 010's escaping regions,
or finding a third fate that persists off the balanced planes.


# Target 1: exact balanced two-cycle and its transverse multiplier

Version 1, proof unaudited. Boundary check for claim 014, not a positive-volume
counterexample to an almost-everywhere theorem.

Fix any n>=2 and any distinct positive kappa_i. Put
 b_i=2 cosh(kappa_i)^2/kappa_i,
 a_i=b_i tanh(kappa_i).
These satisfy 0<a_i<b_i. In the usual coupled factored model
h_i(s)=a_i+b_i tanh(kappa_i s), all links have
 h_i(-1)=0, h_i'(-1)=2.

For EVERY fixed eta>0, simultaneous Euclidean GD on the average logistic
loss has an exact two-cycle
 (v,k,q)=(2/eta,1,-1) <-> (2/eta,-1,1).
At both points the loss is log 2, the product is -1, and k^2-q^2=0.
The two-step Jacobian has a transverse multiplier 9 normal to k=-q.
Thus the nonzero-imbalance assumption in 014 is necessary. This cycle
does not establish a positive-measure basin or rule out almost-everywhere
endpoint convergence.

## Proof

At either displayed state every h_i(kq)=0, so g_i=1/2, F=0 and
G=mean_i g_i h_i'=1. The head therefore stays fixed and
delta=eta vG=2. The factor update sends
 (k,q)->(k+2q,q+2k).
It exchanges (1,-1) and (-1,1). The cycle is nonstationary and has exact
period two; the loss remains log(1+exp(0))=log 2. The construction uses
different nonlinear scales, rather than requiring repeated identical examples.

The full factor-sum identity is U_+=(1+delta)U, U=k+q. At U=0 its
linearization gives dU_+=(1+delta)dU=3dU; the term U d(delta) vanishes.
After two steps dU_{++}=9dU, an exact normal multiplier even when v and
the product vary in the perturbation. No stability assertion at a unit
multiplier is involved.

The same constructed family has finite stationary points at v=0,kq=-1,
whereas the displayed periodic points have v=2/eta>0. Hence a classification
of every finite initialization by stationary points and escaping selections
alone would be false at any positive constant step. The exceptional balanced
plane must be allowed, as it is in claim 012's flow statement (which is a
different dynamical system).","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:e84cc72d2fbe6ab968d32d1b1555801822f794f495ba4dea4c8ed8457d5c1833","revision_digest":"sha256:0df68f50462dd56c31ee950483aeb7bd438f615b6d425e3e42b23d39a5ad9565","source_id":"owner:T328:w698:claims-014-015:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20; no independent PASS","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Theorem t:caccioppoli of arXiv:2607.15140, 'On the absence of blow-up in the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with transport noise'] Let $Q=I \times B$ be a parabolic cylinder with side length $\varrho\in (0,1/2]$. Fix $r\in (1,\infty)$ and $\eta\in (0,1)$.
Suppose that (equation eq:ass_caccioppoli1 of the paper)-(equation eq:ass_caccioppoli4 of the paper) hold. Then there is a constant $C>0$ depending only on $d,M,\varrho,\nu,\nu_0,r$ and $\eta$ for which the following estimates hold for all local solutions $(v,\pi,(\widetilde{\pi}_n)_n)$ to the stochastic Stokes system (equation eq:turbulent_stokes_caccioppoli of the paper) (see Definition (def:local_solutions_NSE of the paper)):
\begin{align*}
\Big({\mathbf E}\sup_{\eta I}\Big\|v- \fint_{\eta B}v\Big\|_{L^2(\eta B)}^r\Big)^{1/r}+
\big({\mathbf E}\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\eta Q)}^r\big)^{1/r}&\leq C\mathcal{E}_{  Q}^{\#}, \\
\big({\mathbf E}\| \pi\|_{L^{2}(\eta Q)}^r\big)^{1/r}&\leq C\mathcal{E}_{ Q}^{\#},\\
\big({\mathbf E}\|( \nabla\widetilde{\pi}_n)_n\|_{L^{2}( \eta Q;\ell^2)}^r\big)^{1/r}&\leq C\mathcal{E}_{ Q}^{\#},
\end{align*} 
where $\mathcal{E}^{\#}_{ Q}$ is the sharp energy of the local solution $(v,\pi,(\widetilde{\pi}_n)_n)$ in $ Q$, i.e., 
\begin{align}
\nonumber
\mathcal{E}_{ Q}^{\#}
=\Big( \max\Big\{
{\mathbf E} \Big\|v-\fint_B v \Big\|_{L^2( Q)}^r
,\,

{\mathbf E} \|\pi\|_{L^2(I;H^{-1}( B))}^r,\, 
{\mathbf E} \|( \widetilde{\pi}_{n} )_{n}\|_{L^{2}( Q;\ell^2)}^r,&\\
{\mathbf E} \|F \|_{L^2( Q)}^r,\,
{\mathbf E} \|(G_n)_n \|_{L^2( Q;\ell^2)}^r & \Big\}\Big)^{1/r}.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Stochastic Caccioppoli inequality -- Stochastic Stokes system

[Theorem thm.ctfemg of arXiv:2606.30517, '\textsc{Convergence towards Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations with a focus on Diestel--'] Let $E$ be the edge-measured graph corresponding to a bipartite graph $G$. Consider the measure $\alpha^{(n)}$ on $G^2$, defined above, and let $\lambda_n\downarrow 0$ such that $F(n)^{-1}\leq \lambda_n \leq F(n-1)^{-1}$. Then, $X^{(\lambda_n)}$ converges weakly (after a suitable shift) to a nonempty point process $(\Theta_i,\Delta_i)_{i\geq 1}$ on the extended boundary if and only if:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
			\item  $\restrict{F}{\mathbb N}$ is log-regularly-varying with positive index $b$,
			\item  the measure $\alpha^{(n)}$ converges weakly as $n\to\infty$ to a probability measure $\alpha$ on $(\partial G)^2$,
			\item  and $\lim_{n\to \infty} \lambda_n F(n) = e^{b\xi}$ for some $\xi$.
		\end{enumerate}
		If these conditions hold, then $(\Delta_i)_{i\geq 1}$ is a Poisson point process on $\mathbb R$ with intensity measure 
		$$
		\beta^{(\xi)}\coloneqq \sum_{j\in \mathbb Z} (p-1)p^{j+\xi} \mathrm{Leb}_{[j,j+1]} \; ,
		$$ where $p\coloneqq e^b$ and $\mathrm{Leb}_{[j,j+1]}$ is the Lebesgue measure on $[j,j+1]$.
		In addition, conditionally on $(\Delta_i)_{i\geq 1}$, the points $(\Theta_i)_{i\geq 1}$ are independent points on $\partial E$ such that $\Theta_i$ has distribution $\nu_{\{\Delta_i\}}$, where $\{\cdot\}$ denotes the fractional part and, for all $t\in[0,1)$, $\nu_t$ is a measure on $\partial E$ determined by $\alpha$. In addition, the corresponding Poisson--Voronoi diagrams also converge to the IPVT of $(\Theta_i,\Delta_i)_{i\geq 1}$, which we denote by ${\rm IPVT}_{\xi}(E)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \textsc{Full Convergence  for Edge-Measured Bipartite Graphs}

[Lemma lem:SSL-vanila of arXiv:2412.01645, 'Regularisation by Gaussian rough path lifts of fractional Brownian motions'] Let $p\in[2,\infty)$.   Let $(S,T)\in[0,1]_\leq^2$ and let
$(A_{s,t})_{(s,t)\in[S,T]_\leq^2}$ be a family of ${\mathbb{R}}^d$-valued random variables 

such that $A_{s,t}$ is $\mathcal{F}_t$-measurable for all $(s,t)\in[S,T]_{\leq}^2$.
Suppose that there exist constants $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2\in[0,\infty)$, $\beta_1>1/2$, and $\beta_2>1$ such that the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item $\|A_{s,t}\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\leq \Gamma_1|t-s|^{\beta_1}$, $(s,t)\in[S,T]_{\leq}^2$,
    \item $\|\mathbb{E}_s\delta A_{s,u,t}\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\leq \Gamma_2|t-s|^{\beta_2}$, $(s,u,t)\in[S,T]_{\leq}^3$. 
\end{enumerate}
  Then there exists a unique continuous $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t\in[S,T]}$-adapted process $\mathcal{A}:[S,T]\mapsto L^p(\Omega;{\mathbb{R}}^d)$  such that $\mathcal{A}_S=0$ and the following bounds hold for some constants $K_1,K_2, K>0$: $(s,t)\in[S,T]_{\leq}^2$,
  \begin{enumerate}[(I)]
      \item $\|\mathcal{A}_t-\mathcal{A}_s- A_{s,t}\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\leq K_1|t-s|^{\beta_1}+ K_2|t-s|^{\beta_2}$, 
      \item $\|\mathbb{E}_s(\mathcal{A}_t-\mathcal{A}_s- A_{s,t})\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\leq K_2|t-s|^{\beta_2}$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, there exists a constant $K=K(\beta_1,\beta_2,p,d)$ such that the above bounds hold with $K_1=K\Gamma_1$, $K_2=K\Gamma_2$, and  one has for all $(s,t)\in[S,T]_{\leq}^2$
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(III)]  $\|\mathcal{A}_t-\mathcal{A}_s\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\leq K\Gamma_1|t-s|^{\beta_1}+K\Gamma_2|t-s|^{\beta_2}$.
    
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:SSL-vanila of arXiv:2412.01645

[Proposition prop:int-ext-coincides of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] Let $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$ be a $\Box$-p and $\Diamond$-p model, then \\
  $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi \iff x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$ for any $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$ and $x \in W$.
  \begin{proof}
    We use an induction on the construction of $\varphi$.
    We shall consider the cases with modal operators, as the other cases are either trivial or easily proven with the induction hypothesis.
    We note that $\Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M}$ is persistent by the assumption and Proposition (prop:combined-persistency of the paper).

    ($\Box\Rightarrow$)
    Suppose $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$, then $\forall x',y'\, ((x \leq x' \sqsubset y') \mathrel{\Rightarrow} y' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi)$.
    Now take any $y$ such that $x \leq x \sqsubset y$, then it follows that $y \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$, so $y \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis.
    Therefore, $x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$.

    ($\Box\Leftarrow$)
    Suppose $x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$, then $\forall y\, (x \sqsubset y \mathrel{\Rightarrow} y \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi)$.
    Now take any $x', y'$ such that $x \leq x' \sqsubset y'$,
    then $x \leq x' \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$ by persistency,
    then $y' \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi$,
    so $y' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis.
    Therefore, $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi$.

    ($\Diamond\Rightarrow$)
    Suppose $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$, then $\forall x'\, (x \leq x' \mathrel{\Rightarrow} \exists y'\, (x' \sqsubset y' \mathrel{\text{\&}} y' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi))$.
    This and $x \leq x$ imply that there is $y$ such that $x \sqsubset y$ and $y \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$, then $y \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis.
    Therefore, $x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$.

    ($\Diamond\Leftarrow$)
    Suppose $x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$, then there is $y$ such that $x \sqsubset y$ and $y \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi$.
    Now take any $x'$ such that $x \leq x'$,
    then by $\Diamond$-p, $x' \geq x \sqsubset y$ implies that there is $y'$ such that $x' \sqsubset y' \geq y$.
    Here, $y \leq y' \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by persistency,
    so $y' \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi$ by the induction hypothesis.
    Therefore, $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:int-ext-coincides of arXiv:2608.29708

[Theorem thm-omni-BM24 of arXiv:2607.25567, 'Random Trees in Hyperbolic FPP'] The following hold for both forward and backward random trees for FPP on a hyperbolic group. 

	\begin{enumerate}
		\item If $G$ is not free (up to finite index), almost surely exceptional directions in ${\partial G}$ exist and are dense in ${\partial G}$.
		\item If ${\partial G}$ has topological dimension $\dim_t {\partial G}$ greater than 1, then almost surely there are 
		\emph{uncountably many} exceptional directions.
		\item If $G$ is a cocompact lattice in the hyperbolic plane, and the Cayley graph $\Gamma$ is planar, then  almost surely there are \emph{countably many} exceptional directions. 
		\item Let $G$ be a  hyperbolic group such that $\dim_t {\partial G} = n-1$. Then
		there exists an exceptional direction $z \in {\partial G}$ with multiplicity \emph{at least $n$}. Thus there exist hyperbolic groups with arbitrarily large
		multiplicity of an exceptional direction.
		\item Exceptional directions have measure zero with respect to the Patterson-Sullivan measure. In fact the set of exceptional directions has Hausdorff dimension (almost surely uniformly) smaller than that of ${\partial G}$.
		\item For any (fixed) $\Gamma$, there exists an almost sure uniform upper bound 
		on the  multiplicity of an exceptional direction.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm-omni-BM24 of arXiv:2607.25567

body: When $M$ predictors of the same target are trained on the same data, their error vectors are nearly collinear: the error covariance has a few large eigenvalues and a long tail of tiny ones. Its participation ratio $M_{\mathrm{eff}} = (\sum_k \lambda_k)^2 / \sum_k \lambda_k^2$ counts the independent error directions. Measured on the EMIT lookup-table pool (23 members, 932 calibration rows, seed 101): $M_{\mathrm{eff}} = 2.2$ to $3.4$, with spectra spanning sixteen decades (top / median / smallest eigenvalue $5.9 \times 10^{-4}$ / $6 \times 10^{-6}$ / $5 \times 10^{-20}$ on one component; condition numbers $10^5$ to $10^{16}$). Two consequences. First, the Marchenko-Pastur regime is not the relevant one: with $q_{\mathrm{eff}} = M_{\mathrm{eff}}/n$ between $0.002$ and $0.06$ the Pafka-Kondor inflation of the plug-in minimum-variance stack predicts gains of $0.1$ to $3$ percent from cleaning, while the measured gains of nonlinear shrinkage over least squares were $+4$, $+10$, $+14$, $+22$ percent at $n = 932, 240, 120, 60$ on the hardest component - an order of magnitude more. Second, the mechanism is different: the minimum-variance inverse $\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1}$ is dominated by the smallest eigenvalues, which are numerical noise around zero, so the plug-in stack wanders in the members' near-null space (the raw inverse is far worse than least squares at small $n$: $0.31$ against $0.058$ at 60 rows on one component), and any cleaning of that bottom of the spectrum is a large regularisation. Which cleaning matters depends on the component: where the gain is small (two of four components) a floor at the noise level, a cross-validated ridge and the Ledoit-Peche shrinkage agree within one percent; where the gain is large (the other two) the nonlinear shrinkage without any floor equals the shrinkage with the floor and beats every fixed floor by $4$ to $20$ percent and the cross-validated ridge by about $4$ percent, with no tuning. The number to compute before applying a random-matrix result to an ensemble is $M_{\mathrm{eff}}$, not $M$.

[Lemma 24 of arXiv:2609.01574, 'A linear bound for Fujita's freeness conjecture'] Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a pair with $X$ smooth projective, let $L$ be an ample Cartier divisor, and let $x\in X$ be a closed point. Assume either that $\Delta=0$, in which case let $W:=X$, or that $(X,\Delta)$ is log canonical near $x$ but not klt at $x$, in which case let $W:=W_x(X,\Delta)$. Let $d:=\dim W>0$. For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exist an effective $\mathbb Q$-divisor $D\sim_{\mathbb Q}L$ and a rational number $t:=\lct_x((X,\Delta);D)$ such that, for $\Delta':=\Delta+tD$, the pair $(X,\Delta')$ is log canonical near $x$, one has $W_x(X,\Delta')\subsetneq W$, and
$$
 b_x(X,\Delta')\leq b_x(X,\Delta)
 -t\left(\frac{L^d\cdot W}{\mult_xW}\right)^{1/d}+\varepsilon.
$$

[Lemma 25 of arXiv:2604.04267, 'On Sharpest Tail Bounds for Functions \\ of Tail Bounded Random Variables'] Mass retracts have the following properties. 
   \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   \item  If $\gamma$ is a mass retract of $U$, then $\forall$ measures $m, \gamma_\#(m)(U) = m(U)$.
   \item Preserve tail bounds: if $m \in \mathcal{T}^d(f)$, then $\gamma_\#(m) \in \mathcal{T}^d(f)$ too. 
   \item Closed under composition. Also, if $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ are mass retracts of $U$, then so is $\gamma_2 \circ \gamma_1$.
   \end{enumerate}

[Lemma lem:annular-amalgamation of arXiv:2608.28330, 'Realising atomless laws as distance distributions on metric measure spaces'] Let $R>0$ and $N\in\mathbb N$, and let
		$(X_i,d_i)$, $i=1,\ldots,N$, be metric spaces
		with \(\operatorname{diam} X_i\le R\).  We order the components by their indices and call $X_i$ earlier than
		$X_j$ if $i<j$. For \(i=1,\ldots,N-1\), let
		\(\phi_i:X_i\to[R,2R]\) be \(1\)-Lipschitz.  On the disjoint union
		\(X=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^N X_i\), retain \(d_i\) on each \(X_i\) and, for
		\(1\le i<j\le N\), set
		\[
		d(x,y)=d(y,x)=\phi_i(x),
		\qquad x\in X_i,\quad y\in X_j.
		\]
		Then \(d\) is a metric on \(X\).

DRAFT exact special case. For X=Y-1 with Y~Exp(1), define F_f(s)=E[f(X)exp(sX)]/E[exp(sX)]. The normalized tilt coefficient T_d f=F_f^(d)(0)/d! is E[f(X)q_d(Y)], where q_d(y)=y^d/d!-y^(d-1)/(d-1)! for d>=1. Its squared L2 operator norm is binomial(2d-2,d-1), attained by the normalized representer; its all-degree exponential rate is 2. Scalar cumulants of order m>=2 equal (m-1)!. Moreover q1=X, q2=(X^2-1)/2 have Gram entries 1, 2 and cross entry 1. Thus Var(q1+q2)=5, a diagonal sum gives 3, and E|(q1+q2)prime|^2=2. This does not prove a tensor bound for general laws.
