[Theorem 2 (Pathwise Convergence of the Modular-Poisson Algorithm) of arXiv:2603.26003, 'Pathwise Convergence of a Modular Simulation Scheme for Hybrid SDEs with Memory'] Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:main_construction}, \ref{ass:micro}, and \ref{ass:logHolder} hold. Let the approximated initial  path $\widehat{Y}^{(n)}$ on $(-\infty, 0]$ satisfy $\widehat{J}_s^{(n)} = J_s$ for all $s \le 0$ and
\[ \sup_{s \le 0} \|\widehat{X}_s^{(n)} - X_s\| \le (\log n)^{b_0} n^{-\gamma} \]
for a constant $b_0\ge 0$. Then for any $T>0$ and $\varepsilon_1 \in (0,\gamma)$,
\[
\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}\mathbb{P}\!\left(\sup_{0\le t \le T}\|\widehat{Y}^{(n)}_t-Y_t\| > n^{-\gamma+\varepsilon_1}\right)
\;=\; 0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2605.08345, '\vspace{-18mm}\textbf{Quantitative ergodicity for gene regulatory networks with transcript'] Given \( \nu^i(0) \) and \( \eta^i(0) \) for every \( i \in \{1, 2\} \) and set 
\[ w_0 = W_1(\nu^1(0), \nu^2(0)) + \widetilde{W}_1(\eta^1(0), \eta^2(0)) \quad \text{and} \quad p^* = p^*(w_0), \] 
where \( \widetilde{W}_1 \) stands for the Wasserstein metric on \( (\R^n, \weightnorm{\cdot}) \)
Then for all \( t \ge 0 \),
\[ W_1( \nu^1(t), \nu^2(t)) \le \left( w_0 \vee \roverdun + \gamma e^{-1}(w_0 + \tau (1 - p^*)) t \right) e^{- \gamma t} \]
where 
\[ \gamma = \frac{p^* \tau \mindun}{p^* \tau + \mindun}, \]
and \( \tau \) is defined at \eqref{eq_:_tau}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[
s_A \left(z\right)
\ = \

\]

[Proposition prop:gamma of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] As $D \to 0$ the rescaled energies
		$\mathcal{E}_{D}/\sqrt D$ Gamma-converge, on distribution functions
		supported in a fixed bounded interval, or along tight families, to
		$2/\pi^{2}$ times the number of jumps of the limit step
		function~[modica1987]; on laws the minimum is a single jump. The variational sharp-interface limit of the
		reaction--diffusion theory is therefore condensation onto one atom,
		and for the harmonic kernel $w_{k}$, whose potential
		$\Phi_{k}(u) = \sin^{2}(k\pi u)/(2\pi^{2}k^{2})$ has wells at the
		lattice $\{j/k\}$, the limiting configurations are the
		$k$-jump crystallized laws with per-interface tension
		$2\sqrt D/\pi^{2}k^{2}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 11 (Uniform inner--outer matching) of arXiv:2609.02788, '\textbf{Quantized Einstein Metrics on \(S^7\) with \(SU(3)\)-Symmetry}'] There is a function $\varepsilon(b)\to0$ such that, uniformly for
$|\mu|\le\mu_0$,
\begin{align}
 F_2(b,\mu)&=\mathcal E(\mu)+O(\varepsilon(b)),\\
 b^{-5/2}F_1(b,\mu)
 &=\Re\!\left(C_o(\mu)Qe^{i\omega\log(1/b)}\right)
   +O(\varepsilon(b)).
\end{align}
With $\delta_b=b^{1/2}$ one may take
\begin{equation}
 \varepsilon(b)
 =C\left[
   \kappa_b+\delta_b^\sigma+\delta_b^2
   +\left(\frac b{\delta_b}\right)^5
 \right](1+|\log\delta_b|).
\end{equation}
In particular \(\varepsilon(b)\to0\) as \(b\downarrow0\).  Indeed,
\(\beta_+=(-5+3\sqrt5)/2\in(0,2)\),
\(\rho(b)=O(b^{\beta_+/m})\), and with
\(\delta_b=b^{1/2}\), \(\tau_b=b^{-1/2}\), every power occurring in
\(\kappa_b\) and \((b/\delta_b)^5\) is strictly positive; multiplication by
\(1+|\log\delta_b|\) therefore still tends to zero.

body:
[Lemma 9 (Ridge oracle bound under feature reduction) of arXiv:2608.22179, '\bf Token-Level Likelihood-Array Regression for Membership Inference and AI-Generated Text'] Let \((Y,X)\) satisfy
\[
\Pp(Y=1\mid X)=\sigma\{\eta_0(X)\},
\]
and let \(Z=T(X)\) be a centered bounded Hilbert-space feature with covariance
operator \(\Gamma_Z\). Consider scores
\(f_{\alpha,\theta}(Z)=\alpha+\ip{\theta}{Z}\) in a fixed coefficient ball.
Assume that \(\eta_0(X)\) and all candidate scores are uniformly bounded. Let
\(\widehat f_\lambda=f_{\widehat\alpha,\widehat\theta}\) minimize
\[
P_n\ell_Y\{f_{\alpha,\theta}(Z)\}
+\frac{\lambda}{2}\norm{\theta}^2
\]
over this ball. Then, for every comparator
\(f^*(Z)=\alpha^*+\ip{\theta^*}{Z}\) in the same ball,
\begin{equation}
\E_{\mathcal D}
\norm{\widehat f_\lambda(Z)-\eta_0(X)}_{P_X}^2
\leq
C\left\{
\norm{f^*(Z)-\eta_0(X)}_{P_X}^2
+\lambda\norm{\theta^*}^2
+\frac{1+\mathcal N_{\Gamma_Z}(c\lambda)}{n}
\right\}.

\end{equation}
Here
\[
\norm{f(Z)-\eta_0(X)}_{P_X}^2
=
\E_X\left[\{f(T(X))-\eta_0(X)\}^2\right],
\]
and \(\E_{\mathcal D}\) is over the labeled training sample. The constants
\(C,c>0\) depend only on the fixed score and coefficient bounds.

    Let $X \sim \mathcal N(\mu, \Sigma)$ with $\mu \in \R^{N}$ and $\Sigma \in \R^{N}$ where $N = \binom{n}{2}$. Index the mean $\mu$, covariance $\Sigma$ and random vector $X$ by tuples $(i, j) \in [n]^2$ where $i < j$. We define a dependent Erdős-Rényi graph as a graph $G_{\mu, \Sigma}(X) := (V, E(X))$ where $V = [n]$ and $(i,j) \in E(X)$ if $\indicator{X_{(i,j)} \geq 0}$ .

[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2512.10686, 'Maximal rigidity of random measures and uniqueness pairs: stealthy processes, quasicrystal'] Let $ \X$ a strongly stationary field on $ \mathbb{Z} ^{d}$ taking values in a uniformly discrete set $  \U$. Assume the support of its spectral measure $ \S$ is contained in a simply connected set  of $  \mathbb  T  ^{ d}$. Then $ \X$ is a.s. periodic, with a possibly random period. In particular, $ \S$ is a purely atomic measure.

[Proposition prop:depinning of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] Along the phase family, the reaction
		$\varphi_{\alpha}(u)
		= -\big[\sin(2\pi(u+\alpha)) - \sin(2\pi\alpha)\big]/(2\pi)$ is
		bistable for $0 \le \alpha < \tfrac14$ and degenerates at the
		quarter phase:
		$\varphi_{1/4}(u) = \sin^{2}(\pi u)/\pi \ge 0$, with double zeros
		at the endpoints and no interior zero. In the angular variable the
		family is the tilted washboard
		$\partial_{t}v = D\,\partial_{xx}v - \sin v + \sin(2\pi\alpha)$,
		and the tilt attains its depinning magnitude exactly at the
		quarter phase and at its mirror $\alpha = \tfrac34$, the
		reflection $\alpha \mapsto 1 - \alpha$ exchanging the two and
		reversing the drift, so the depinning parameter is unique up to
		that symmetry: at these phases, and only there, the reaction is
		one-signed and every interior rank drifts in one direction, while
		for $\alpha \in (\tfrac14, \tfrac34)$ the washboard re-pins, the
		reaction regaining a stable interior zero at the rank
		$\tfrac32 - 2\alpha$, and, by the reflection
		$\varphi_{1-\alpha}(u) = -\varphi_{\alpha}(1-u)$, bistability
		returns for $\alpha \in (\tfrac34, 1)$: the pinning--sliding transition of the
		washboard
		occurs exactly on the second generator of the isotropy
		fields~(equation eq:isotropy-fields of the paper) of the exceptional orbit, whose
		first generator is the canonical flow itself.

[Proposition prop:Eproduct of arXiv:2507.10531, 'Quantitative central limit theorems for exponential random graphs'] For any fixed $k$, let $e_1, \dotsc, e_k \in \binom{[n]}{2}$ be distinct potential edges and suppose that
either of the following two conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
	\item The density $p$ is the unique global maximizer of $L_\beta$, i.e.\ $M_\beta = U_\beta = \{p\}$.
	\item The edges $e_1, \dotsc, e_k$ form a forest in $K_n$, the complete graph on $[n]$.
\end{enumerate}
Then we have
\begin{equation}
	\mleft| \mathbb{E}\mleft[ \prod_{j=1}^k X(e_j) \mright]
	- \mathbb{E}[X(e)]^k \mright| \lesssim \frac{1}{n},
\end{equation}
where $e$ is an arbitrary edge in $\binom{[n]}{2}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
For a least-squares predictor yhat(x) = x' beta_hat fitted on n rows, the textbook variance at a new point x is sigma^2 x'(X'SX)^(-1) x (sigma^2 times the leverage), and the hat matrix H = X(X'SX)^(-1)X'S has trace equal to the number of parameters. Both statements require X'SX to be invertible. On a design that is rank-deficient - here, an ensemble whose members include exact duplicates, so the member-prediction Gram of every output is singular by the number of duplicates - the leverage is undefined: the trace of the hat matrix drops to the rank (21 instead of 24 on the s104 Y1 cell of the EMIT pool), and inverting through a tiny ridge assigns any new point that leaves the duplicates' span an arbitrarily large leverage (a load 11.8 times the whole prediction error on that cell), which is a property of the ridge, not of the predictor actually used. The pairs bootstrap sidesteps this: resample the n rows with replacement B times, refit the predictor exactly as it is fitted in production (with its own ridge or pseudo-inverse and its own constraints), and take the empirical variance of the B predictions at x. Under Freedman's (1981) conditions for the pairs (correlation-model) bootstrap - independent rows, finite fourth moments of the regressors and errors, and a design whose empirical second-moment matrix converges - the bootstrap variance of a linear predictor is consistent for its sampling variance, and it remains well defined on a singular design because every resample is fitted by the same regularised map as the original. It is the right variance estimator when the estimator's regularisation, rather than an invertible Gram, determines its behaviour; it also applies unchanged to a constrained estimator (a long-only stack) for which no closed form exists. Cost: B refits per cell; B = 8 was enough to rank rows and cells in the RMT ensemble program (the ranking, not the level, was used).
rows independent and identically distributed (the pairs bootstrap resamples rows, not residuals, so heteroscedasticity is allowed)
finite fourth moments and a converging empirical second-moment matrix (Freedman 1981); the predictor is a fixed measurable map of the sample, applied identically to every resample

body: Let pi(x) denote the number of primes less than or equal to x. The prime number theorem states pi(x) is asymptotic to x / log(x) as x tends to infinity, meaning the ratio pi(x) / (x / log x) tends to 1; equivalently pi(x) is asymptotic to the logarithmic integral Li(x), a sharper approximation. Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, the error term satisfies pi(x) = Li(x) + O(sqrt(x) log x). First proved independently in 1896 by Jacques Hadamard and Charles Jean de la Vallee Poussin, using nonvanishing of the Riemann zeta function on the line Re(s) = 1.
title: Prime number theorem

body: For a household size h and contacts vector X = (X_G, X_L), let B(p) be the branching process approximating the early epidemic when each local contact is replaced by a global one independently with probability p. The extinction probability rho_p of B(p) is decreasing in p (Lemma 5.2). Proof: for 0 <= p < q <= 1, B(p) and B(q) are built on one probability space so that the i-th individual makes the same X_{G,i} + X_{L,i} attempted births and Y^(p)_{T,i} <= Y^(q)_{T,i} of its local contacts are converted to global ones; a lower-bound process B^(p, q), with the Y^(q) - Y^(p) extra contacts made 'ghost contacts', gives rho_q <= rho_p. Consequently the probability of a major outbreak increases in p for any distribution of X_L, while the limiting final size z increases in p when the pgf of X_L is log-convex and can fail to otherwise.

[Lem L4.1 of arXiv:2609.03848, 'The mean-field limit of the Schr\"{o}dinger-Lohe model\\ and emergent dynamics'] Let $Q^{0}_N$ be a coupling of $F^{0}_N$ and $(f^{0})^{\otimes N}$, and we set                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
\[
Q_N(t)=\mathcal T_N(t,0)\#Q_N^0\,.
\]
Then, the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
For each $t\ge 0$, the probability measure $Q_N(t)$ on $(\mathbf S\mathfrak H)^N\!\times\!C(\mathbb T^d)^N\!\times\!(\mathbf S\mathfrak H)^N\!\times\!C(\mathbb T^d)^N$ is a coupling
of $F_N(t)$ and $f(t)^{\otimes N}$.
\vspace{0.1cm}
\item
If $Q^{0}_N$ is a symmetric coupling of $F^{0}_N$ and $(f^{0})^{\otimes N}$, then $Q_N(t)$ is a symmetric coupling of $F_N(t)$ and $f(t)^{\otimes N}$.
\vspace{0.1cm}
\item
The time-dependent probability measure $Q_N(t)$ on $(\mathbf S\mathfrak H)^N\!\times\!C(\mathbb T^d)^N\!\times\!(\mathbf S\mathfrak H)^N\!\times\!C(\mathbb T^d)^N$ is a Lagrangian
weak solution of
\[
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle {\partial}_tQ_N+ \sum_{k=1}^N\operatorname{div}_{\phi_k}(Q_N(Y^f(t,\phi_k,V_k)+\tfrac12\kappa Y^i_k(t,\Phi_N))) \\
\displaystyle \hspace{0.5cm} +\sum_{k=1}^N\operatorname{div}_{\tilde\phi_k}(Q_N(Y^f(t,\tilde\phi_k,\tilde V_k)+\tfrac12 \kappa Y^{mf}[\rho_f](t,\tilde\phi_k)))=0, \\
\displaystyle Q_N{\big |}_{t=0}=Q^{0}_N.
\end{cases}
\]
\end{enumerate}
title: Lem L4.1 of arXiv:2609.03848

body: [Lemma lem:Hypercontractivity of arXiv:2410.23915, 'Asymptotic Bounds and Online Algorithms for Average-Case Matrix Discrepancy'] Let $X$ be a random vector in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with independent, centered and $\kappa$-hypercontractive entries, then $X$ satisfies the Khintchine anti-concentration inequality (equation eq:KhintchineAntiConcentration of the paper) with parameter $\eta = \Omega(\sigma\kappa^4)$, where $\sigma^2 = \min_i \E{X_i^2}$.
title: Lemma lem:Hypercontractivity of arXiv:2410.23915

body:
[Question Online universality of arXiv:2608.19050, 'Online Permutation Embedding: \\ Optimal Stopping and Scaling Laws'] For a fixed $k$,
consider a family of online algorithms $\mathrm{OA}(\Pi_k)$,
with each algorithm in $\mathrm{OA}(\Pi_k)$ producing
online order-isomorphic embeddings of all $k!$ permutations from $\Pi_k$
into the stream $\mathcal{S}$. For every $\mathcal{A}\in \mathrm{OA}(\Pi_k)$,
let $T_\mathcal{A}$ be the (random stopping) time of embedding all elements of $\Pi_k$. What are the asymptotics of 
$$\frac{1}{k^2}
\inf\limits_{\mathcal{A}\in \mathrm{OA}(\Pi_k)}\,\EE\,T_\mathcal{A}?$$ (Stated as a question by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Online universality

[Definition defi_solution_ep of arXiv:2603.26307, '\LARGE The incompressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system with thermal noise'] A  \emph{weak martingale solution 
		to (equation ep_approx of the paper)--(equation eqn354865865 of the paper)} 
	consists of a probability space $(\Omega,\mathfrak{A},\mathbb{P})$, a filtration $\mathscr{F}$ satisfying the usual conditions, independent $3$-dimensional standard $\mathscr{F}$-Brownian motions $(W_n)_{n\in \mathbb{Z}^3}$ and $3\times 3$-matrix valued $\mathscr{F}$-Brownian motions $(B_n)_{n\in \mathbb{Z}^3}$ with covariance structure (equation Eq_noise_matrix_covariation of the paper), a weakly continuous and adapted  $L^2(\mathbb{T}^3 ;\mathbb{R}^3)$-valued process
	$u_{\epsilon}$, as well as   progressively measurable   $\psi_{\epsilon} \in L^\infty(0,T;L^2( \mathbb{T}^3))$ and  $q_{\epsilon}\in \mathcal{M}_+([0,T]\times \mathbb{T}^3)$, such that the following holds:
	\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
		\item  We have the additional regularity {$u_{\epsilon}\in L^{2}(0,T;H^2(\mathbb{T}^3 ;\mathbb{R}^{3}))$ and $\psi_{\epsilon} \in  L^{2}(0,T;H^2(\mathbb{T}^3))$}, $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely.
		\item   It holds $\psi_{\epsilon}>0$, $\mathbb{P}\otimes \mathrm{d} t \otimes \mathrm{d} x$-a.e., and  $q_{\epsilon} \ge \frac{1}{\psi_{\epsilon}}(|\nabla \psi_{\epsilon}|^2 + |\nabla_\mathrm{sym} u_{\epsilon}|^2+\epsilon)$,  as measures  on $[0,T]\times \mathbb{T}^3$, $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely. 
		\item   For every divergence-free $\varphi\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{T}^3;\mathbb{R}^3)$ it holds
		\begin{align}\begin{split}
				& \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}  u_{\epsilon,t}\cdot \varphi\,\mathrm{d} x \,-\, 
				\int_{\mathbb{T}^3} u_0 \cdot \varphi\,\mathrm{d} x\,+\,\epsilon\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb{T}^3} u_{\epsilon}\Delta^2\varphi\,\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} s
				\\&\quad=\,  \int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} -  \Bigl(\frac{1}{2}+ \frac{F_1}{4}\Bigr) \nabla u_{\epsilon}: \nabla  \varphi \,+\, u_{\epsilon}\otimes u_{\epsilon}:\nabla \varphi \,\mathrm{d} x\, \mathrm{d} s \,+\, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}^3}\int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}\psi_{\epsilon} f_n \nabla \varphi\,\mathrm{d} x :\mathrm{d} B_{n,s},
			\end{split}
		\end{align}
		and $\nabla \cdot u_{\epsilon,t} = 0$ for all $t\in [0,T]$, $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely.
		\item  
		For every $\zeta\in C_c^{\infty}([0,T) \times \mathbb{T}^3)$ it holds
		\begin{align}\begin{split}
				&-\,
				\int_0^T \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} \psi_{\epsilon}  \partial_t \zeta  \, \mathrm{d} x\, \mathrm{d} t \,-\, \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}
				\psi_0 \zeta
				\,\mathrm{d} x\,+\,\epsilon\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb{T}^3} \psi_{\epsilon}\Delta^2\zeta\,\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} s 
				\\&\quad=\,  \int_0^T \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} - \bigl(1+ {F_1}/2 +G_1/2\bigr) \nabla \psi_{\epsilon}\cdot \nabla  \zeta \,+\,\psi_{\epsilon} u_{\epsilon}\cdot \nabla \zeta   \,-\, (F_2/2+G_2/8) \psi_{\epsilon} \zeta \,\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} t \,+\, \int_{[0,T]\times\mathbb{T}^3} \zeta \,\mathrm{d} q
				\\&\qquad + \sum_{i=1}^3
				\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}^3}\int_0^T \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} \psi_{\epsilon} g_n \partial_i \zeta  + \frac{1}{2} \psi_{\epsilon}  \zeta \partial_ig_n \,\mathrm{d} x \, \mathrm{d} W_{n,t}^i
				\, +\, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sum_{i,j =1}^3\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}^3}\int_0^T \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}u_{\epsilon,j}\partial_i (\zeta f_n) \,\mathrm{d} x \,\mathrm{d} B_{n,t}^{ji},
			\end{split}
		\end{align}  $\mathbb{P}$-almost surely.
	\end{enumerate}

body:
[Cor 15 of arXiv:2608.27249, 'Torus actions, almost non-negative curvature and fundamental groups'] Let \(M\) be a \((2n+4)\)-dimensional closed connected manifold with  a  metric of non-negative Ricci curvature.
  Assume that that there is no abelian subgroup with at most two generators and finite index in \(\pi_1(M)\).
  If \(M\) admits an effective action of a torus \(T\) of dimension \(n\) with fixed point, then there is a \(T\)-invariant metric of positive scalar curvature on \(M\).

[Corollary Recovery from sampled trajectories of arXiv:2606.23025, 'Spectral-Capacitary Bounds for Homological Recovery from Reflected Brownian Trajectories'] There
exist constants \(C,C_{low},C_{up},\varepsilon_{0},c > 0\) such
that if \(0 < \varepsilon < \varepsilon_{0}\),
\[T \geq C\left( s_{0} + \kappa_{d}(\varepsilon)^{- 1}\left( \log N_{\varepsilon}(M) + \log\frac{1}{\delta} \right) \right)\],
and \(\omega_{X}(\Delta) \leq c\varepsilon\), then with
probability at least \(1 - \delta\),

\begin{multline*}
H_{q}\left( \left( \Gamma_{T}^{\Delta} \right)^{r} \right) \cong H_{q}(M)\\
\text{for every }q = 0,\ldots,d\text{ and every }C_{low}\,\varepsilon \leq r \leq C_{up}\, \operatorname{reach}(M).
\end{multline*}

Blachère–den Hollander–Steif (2011), Theorem 1.3, restricted to zero holding probability: let iid increments X_n in {-1,+1}, n>=1, have P(X_n=+1)=p in [1/2,1], let S_0=0 and S_n=sum_{j=1}^n X_j, and let C_z be independent iid fair black/white scenery. Set Y_n=C_{S_n}. Badness and goodness refer to the conditional law of Y_0 given the ONE-SIDED future record (Y_n)_{n>=1}, using finite-cylinder tail-tampering discontinuity. (i) There exists p0<1 such that every future record is good when p0<p<=1. (ii) Every future record is bad when 1/2<p<4/5. (iii) At p=1/2 both good and bad future records exist. These conclusions do not classify two-sided exterior records. The paper's more general walk has holding probability epsilon; all three conclusions stated here assume epsilon=0. Locator: arXiv:1103.1780v3, Theorem 1.3, PDF page 5; one-sided restriction Section 1.1, PDF page 2.

body:
[Proposition prop:fast of arXiv:2607.14266, 'The Swapping Mechanism for Interacting Diffusions: Framework, Comparison with Switching, a'] Let $p_0(x,y,t)$ denote the product density appearing in
		Proposition~(prop:slow of the paper). As $st\to\infty$,
		$p(x,y,t)$ converges in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ to the symmetrised mixture
		\[
		p_\infty(x,y,t)=\frac12\bigl[p_0(x,y,t)+p_0(y,x,t)\bigr].
		\]
		Thus the rapid swapping makes the two configurations
		$(x,y)$ and $(y,x)$ equally probable, but the system still
		remembers the two possible initial assignments. Moreover, for all
		$st\ge 1$,
		\begin{equation}
			\|p(\,\cdot\,,\cdot\,,t)-p_\infty(\,\cdot\,,\cdot\,,t)\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)}
			\le C(t)(st)^{-1/2},
		\end{equation}
		where $C(t)>0$ depends continuously on $t$. The $O((st)^{-1/2})$ rate
		is dictated by the $z\to0$ edge of the Bessel integrals, where
		$I_\nu(u)\sim e^u/\sqrt{2\pi u}$, and is a signature of the underlying
		telegraph-type structure
		[goldstein1951,kac1974,tailleur2008,cates2012]. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Fast-swap regime

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2608.18557, 'Randomly Permuted Orthogonal Products and Fast Dimension Reduction'] Let \(X\subseteq \mathbb S^{d-1}\) with \(|X|=N\), let
	\(0<\eta<1/2\), and assume that \(1\le m\le d\). Set
	\begin{equation}
		\ell
		=

		\qquad
		L_d

		\log\left(\frac{8Nd}{\eta}\right),
		\qquad
		L_m
		=
		\log\left(\frac{8Nm}{\eta}\right).
	\end{equation}
	Suppose the admissibility condition
	\begin{equation}
		36\kappa_I(A)\Theta_B(X)\,mL_dL_m
		\le
		d.

	Then, with probability at least \(1-\eta\),
	\begin{equation}
		\sup_{x\in X}
		\left|
		\norm{\Phi x}_2-1
		\right|
		\le
		10\sqrt{\frac{\ell}{m}}.
	\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Own-work draft; C18 v1 status SKETCH, independent audit pending, no novelty claim; not a certified theorem. Proposed diagnostic: for a finite public Gaussian family N(mu_theta,v0 I_d), d>=1 and v0>0, every finite set of OU time-point pairs (t_j,x_j), t_j>=0, and epsilon>0 admit instance-specific jointly smooth estimated fields b_theta equal to zero on those pairs with E_{OU_t(P_theta)} ||b_theta-s_theta,t||^2 <= epsilon^2 for every t>=0. Each field has some finite global spatial Lipschitz constant uniform over t; no prescribed, polynomial, or efficient-computability bound is supplied. The fields need not be gradients or scores of an OU-consistent family. Construction: choose smooth time bumps h_j and small spatial bumps g_j, set chi=1-product_j(1-h_j g_j), and b_theta=(1-chi)s_theta. The Gaussian envelope and chi^2<=chi<=sum_j h_j g_j make the uniform error arbitrarily small. For a sampler with a uniform finite query cap Q and a selected finite set S of query-randomness seeds, form at most Q|S| query pairs from all-zero-reply adaptive paths. The resulting fields are fixed before drawing the realized seed and produce identical replies on every seed in S. If S has probability at least 1-eta, two output laws have TV at most eta, so for target separation delta one target has sampling TV error at least (delta-eta)/2. Independent continuous randomness after the query phase is allowed. Finite sets of individual continuously distributed query seeds can instead have zero probability. Smoothness without a quantitative modulus does not justify query discretization. Thus this does not prove a lower bound for continuously randomized diffusion samplers, a prescribed Lipschitz oracle class, or Target 2. The real missing step is continuous adaptive transcript indistinguishability, not finite path interpolation. Only finite mask algebra was checked; the construction and coupling await review.
Finite public Gaussian family with common positive spherical variance; d>=1
Finite prescribed set of nonnegative OU time-point pairs; epsilon>0
No prescribed Lipschitz constant, gradient constraint, or OU-consistency assumption for estimated fields
Adaptive application assumes identical public input, uniform finite query cap, and a finite selected set of query-randomness seeds
Finite-seed masking does not establish continuously randomized query hardness

[Lem lm:Duncan of arXiv:2604.12963, 'Shocks, instability, and the twenty networks\\ of infinite geodesics in the Directed Lands'] {\rm[\citenum{Dau-Ort-Vir-22}, Lemma 10.2(1-2) and \citenum{Dau-Pan-26-}, Lemma 8.1]}
There exists an event $\Omega_{13}\subset\Omega_{12}$ with $\mathbb{P}(\Omega_{13})=1$ and such that for any $\omega\in\Omega_{13}$ and any $x,\theta\in\mathbb{R}$ and $s\in\mathbb{Q}$, we have the following.
\begin{enumerate} [label={\rm(\alph*)}, ref={\rm\alph*}] \itemsep=1pt 
\item If $\gamma^L$ and $\gamma^R$ are two geodesics out of $(x,s)$ that are $\theta$-directed {\rm(}i.e.\ satisfy (equation geo:directed of the paper){\rm)} and the two geodesics separate immediately at $(x,s)$, then reunite at $(y,t)$, for the first time after time $s$, and then separate again at some later time $t'>t$, then there exists a $t''\in(t,t')$ such that $\gamma^L(r)=\gamma^R(r)$ for $r\in[t,t'']$. See Figure (fig:tail of the paper).
\item 
For any $\theta$-directed geodesic $\gamma$ out of $(x,s)$, there exists an $r>s$  such that either $\gamma|_{[s,r]}=\Gamma_{{(x,s)}}\dir{L}{\theta}{-}\big|_{[s,r]}$ or $\gamma|_{[s,r]}=\Gamma_{{(x,s)}}\dir{R}{\theta}{+}\big|_{[s,r]}$. In particular, 
there are no distinct middle $W^{\theta-}$ or $W^{\theta+}$ geodesics from $(x,s)$. 
In the notation of Remarks (rk:Mgeo of the paper) and (rk:Mgeostable of the paper), if $\theta \notin \Theta^\omega$, then $\Gamma_{{(x,s)}}\dir{M}{\theta}{} = \Gamma_{{(x,s)}}\dir{L}{\theta}{}$, while if $\theta \in \Theta^\omega$, then $\Gamma_{{(x,s)}}\dir{M}{\theta}{-} = \Gamma_{{(x,s)}}\dir{L}{\theta}{-}$ and $\Gamma_{{(x,s)}}\dir{M}{\theta}{+} = \Gamma_{{(x,s)}}\dir{R}{\theta}{+}$.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Mixing of the random-pair binary crossover chain structural calculation Result: The naive Hamming coupling in the source has exact one-column drift E(W_next|W=w)=w-w^2/[2(K-1)]. At the last possible disagreement w=2, the chance of removing it is1/(K-1), so this coupling itself requires order K further steps from that state. It therefore cannot prove logarithmic K mixing simply by improving its large-w drift estimate. Check: When w=2 there is one opposite mismatch of each sign. They coalesce only if paired, probability1/(K-1), and then the prescribed opposite-swap coupling agrees forever. Waiting is geometric. This is a limitation of the coupling, not a mixing-time lower bound. Obstruction: One needs a different coupling, entropy estimate or representation argument which does not insist on coordinatewise agreement at every generation. Marginal one-column mixing also does not automatically control joint mixing because pairings are shared across all columns.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0251-mixing-of-the-random-pair-binary-crossover-chain
No independent review
title: Attempt on Mixing of the random-pair binary crossover chain

[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2608.07879, 'Sharp Wasserstein Convergence Rates for Empirical Path Laws of It\^o Processes'] Let $N$ be a real-valued continuous local martingale. Fix deterministic
times $0\le u<v\le T$, and suppose that, for some deterministic $V>0$,
\begin{equation}
    \langle N\rangle_v-\langle N\rangle_u\le V
    \qquad\text{almost surely}.
\end{equation}
Then, for every $x>0$,
\begin{equation}
    \P\left(
        \sup_{u\le t\le v}|N_t-N_u|\ge x
        \,\middle|\,\Fc_u
    \right)
    \le
    2\exp\left(-\frac{x^2}{2V}\right)
    \qquad\text{almost surely}.
\end{equation}
title: Lemma 7 of arXiv:2608.07879

body: Let A be a real symmetric (or complex Hermitian) n by n matrix, and define its inertia as the triple (n_+, n_-, n_0) of the numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues of A, counted with multiplicity (n_+ + n_- + n_0 = n). If B = P* A P for some invertible n by n matrix P (a congruence transformation), then B has the same inertia as A. [standard, e.g. Horn and Johnson, Matrix Analysis]
title: Sylvester's Law of Inertia

body: Let G = (V, E) be a finite graph. A proper k-coloring of G is a function c: V -> {1, ..., k} such that c(u) is not equal to c(v) whenever {u,v} is in E. The chromatic number chi(G) is the smallest integer k for which a proper k-coloring of G exists. [standard, e.g. Diestel, Graph Theory]
title: Chromatic Number of a Graph

body: If a countable first-order theory, over a countable language, has an infinite model, then it has models of every infinite cardinality. The downward Lowenheim-Skolem theorem gives, for any infinite model, an elementary substructure of any smaller infinite cardinality down to that of the language; the upward part gives elementary extensions of every larger cardinality. Consequently no countable first-order theory with an infinite model can determine a unique infinite structure up to isomorphism, as illustrated by the Skolem paradox for axiomatic set theory. Proved by Leopold Lowenheim (1915) and Thoralf Skolem (1920, 1922).
title: Lowenheim-Skolem theorem

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2608.18075, '2608.18075'] Let $E$ be a separable Hilbert space, let $Q: H\to E$ be
Hilbert--Schmidt, and let
$Z_t=Z_0+V_t+QW_t$, where $V$ is continuous and of bounded variation
in $E$.  On each $[0,N]$ use the standard dyadic grid and restrict that
grid to subintervals with dyadic endpoints.  There is a probability one set,
depending only on $Q$, $W$, and these countably many grids, with the following
property.  On every such compact subinterval $I=[t_1,t_2]$, for every continuous
bounded variation path
$\ell:I\to E^*$, even when $\ell$ and $V$ are anticipative, and every
real Brownian coordinate $W^r$,
\begin{align}
 [\ell(Z),W^r]_t=\int_{t_1}^t\ell_u(Qe_r)\,\mathrm du .
\end{align}
Here the bracket is the limit along the fixed dyadic partitions.  In
particular, if $\ell(Z)$ is of bounded variation, then
$\ell_t(Qe_r)=0$ for every $t\in I$.
The same assertion holds after complexification by taking real and
imaginary parts.
title: Lemma 6 of arXiv:2608.18075

   \[\mathbb{E}_x\left(|\Phi(X_1)-\Phi(x)|^2\right)\leq R,\quad \forall x\in \Omega\]
   Then for any $x\in \Omega$ and $\epsilon\in (0,1)$,
   \[t_\text{mix}(\epsilon) \geq \frac{1}{2\log(1/\alpha)}\left[\log \left(\frac{(1-\alpha)\Phi(x)^2}{2R}\right) + \log\left(\frac{1-\epsilon}{\epsilon}\right)\right]\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Bootstrap thresholds on the line and the three-regular tree Result: On Z the one-neighbor bootstrap threshold is zero, whereas the two-neighbor threshold is one because any initially vacant adjacent pair stays vacant. On the three-regular tree with threshold two, the final vacant set is the two-core of the initial vacant percolation. If its density q<=1/2, all vacant clusters are finite almost surely and leaf pruning empties them. If q>1/2, with positive probability a vertex has two surviving vacant branches, giving a bi-infinite vacant path that remains vacant. Hence the complete-occupation threshold is p=1/2. Check: An infinite bi-infinite path supplies a stable set since each vertex has two vacant neighbors. Finite trees have an exposed leaf and are exhausted by the pruning process. Critical Binomial(2,1/2) clusters die out. Obstruction: This illustrates both the amenable endpoint behavior and a nonamenable interior threshold. It does not classify every generating set or every group.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0042-bootstrap-thresholds-as-a-characterization-of-amenable-groups

body:
[Theorem thm:VarY_exceeds_VarX of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] Let $X \sim \Bern(p,a,b)$ for some $p \ne \frac{1}{2}$. 
Then, any independent symmetrizer $Y$ of $X$ satisfies $\Var(Y) \ge \Var(X)$, with equality if and only if $f_Y = f_{-X}$. 

\begin{proof}
By (lem:affine_invariance of the paper) we may take $X \sim \Bern(p,-1,1)$. 

Let $f \in \Sym$, 
define $R_f$ as in (thm:Bernoulli_calY_representation of the paper), 
and define 
for each $r \in R_f$ constants $c_r \coloneqq \sum_{z \in S^r}f(z)$ and PMFs $g_r(\cdot) \coloneqq \frac{1}{c_r}f(\cdot)\mathds{1}_{S^r}(\cdot) \in \Sym^r$ as in (lem:Sr_restriction_of_symmetrizers_produces_symmetrizers of the paper). 

Then $f = \sum_{r \in R_f} c_r g_r$ and, by the concavity of the variance,
\begin{align}
\Var(f) 
\ge \sum_{r \in R_f} c_r \Var(g_r) \nonumber
&= \sum_{r \in R_f} c_r (M_2(g_r) - M_1(g_r)^2) \nonumber \\
 &\ge \sum_{r \in R_f} c_r (1 - (p-q)^2) \\

&= 1 - (p-q)^2 
= \Var(f_{-X}) \nonumber
\end{align}
where we have used (lem:calYr_min_M2s of the paper) in ((eq:varsymmres2 of the paper)). 

Note that by (lem:calYr_min_M2s of the paper), equality is attained 

in ((eq:varsymmres2 of the paper)) if and only if for all $r \in R_f$, $M_2(g_r) = 1$. 

In this case $R_f = \{1\}$ and $f = g_1 = \hat{f}_0^1$. 

\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Variance symmetrization resistance of Bernoulli

[Definition 8 (Equilibrium measure and branching capacity) of arXiv:2605.09459, 'Multipoint connectivity in the branching interlacement process'] Let $K$ be a finite subset of $\mathbb{Z}^d$. The \textbf{equilibrium measure} of $K$ is the measure defined by
  \[
    e_K(x) = \indic{x \in K}\ \P(\mathcal{T}_-^x \cap K = \emptyset),\quad x \in \mathbb{Z}^d.
  \]
  The \textbf{branching capacity} of $K$ is defined by
  \[
    \mathrm{BCap}(K) = \sum_{x \in K} e_K(x).
  \]
  We can normalize the equilibrium measure and define a probability measure $\widetilde{e}_K(x)$ by
  \[
    \widetilde{e}_K(x) = \frac{e_K(x)}{\mathrm{BCap}(K)},\quad x \in \mathbb{Z}^d.
  \]
title: Equilibrium measure and branching capacity

\(D_i^p\) be a Poisson random measure on
\[
\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R_+\times\{0,1\}^{N-1}
\]
with intensity
\[
\mathrm du\,\mathrm dz\,\nu_p(\mathrm d\theta),
\]
where \(\nu_p\) is the product measure of \(N-1\) independent Bernoulli
random variables with parameter \(p\).

For \(\theta=(\theta_m)_{m\neq i}\in\{0,1\}^{N-1}\), define
\[
\mu_i^p(\theta)
=
B\log_2\left(
1+
\frac{1}{1+\sum_{m\neq i}\theta_m l(d(i,m))}
\right).
\]
The random-environment system is defined, for each
\(i\in\{1,\dots,N\}\), by
\[
q_i^p(t)
=
q_i^p(0)
+
A_i[0,t]
-
\int_{\{0,1\}^{N-1}}\int_{\mathbb R_+}\int_0^t
\mathbf 1_{\{u\leq \mu_i^p(\theta)\}}
\mathbf 1_{\{q_i^p(z^-)>0\}}
\,D_i^p(\mathrm du,\mathrm dz,\mathrm d\theta).
\]

[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2606.15843, 'Long-time behaviour of DLRA for SDEs'] Suppose Assumptions  (H3), (H5), (H7) and (H8) hold for SDE~\eqref{eq.sec4}. Moreover, for some $p> 2$, suppose Assumption~\ref{AS:relation2} holds. Then, the strong DO solution~\eqref{eq:DO} to Eqn.~\eqref{eq.sec4} admits an invariant probability measure $\pi^*\in\scr P_2(V_r(\bb R^d)\times\bb R^r)$. Moreover, the second marginal $$\mu^*(A):=\int_{V_r(\bb R^d)}\pi^*(\rrm du, A), \quad\text{for any }A\in \scr B(\bb R^r),$$
        satisfies $\rrm{det}(C_{\mu^*}) \neq 0$, where $C_{\mu^*}=\int_{\bb R^r}xx^\top \, \mu^*(\rrm dx).$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 8 of arXiv:2606.15843

body: [Theorem 4 of arXiv:2608.27093, 'Soliton Solutions to the Curvature Flow on the 2-dimensional De Sitter Space and Applicati'] For any $v \in \mathbb{R}^{3}_1\setminus\{0\}$, there is a 2-parameter family of non-trivial timelike soliton solutions to the curvature flow on the 2-dimensional De Sitter space. There exists no non-trivial timelike complete soliton. The curvature function has at most one zero. Moreover, we have three cases: the curvature function has no zeros and is unbounded at both ends; the curvature function has a unique zero and is unbounded at both ends; and the curvature function has no zeros, is unbounded at one end, and converges to zero at the other. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 4 of arXiv:2608.27093

[Definition Quantile-based Risk Measure of arXiv:2609.03104, 'Occupancy-based Quantile Risk Control'] Let $\psi(p)$ denote a weighting function such that
\(\psi(p) \ge 0\) and \(\int_0^1 \psi(p)\,dp = 1\). 
The quantile-based risk measure parameterized by $\psi$ is expressed as
\[
R_{\psi}(F_X;\lambda) \coloneqq \int_0^1 \psi(p) F_X^{-1}(p)\,dp.
\]
title: Quantile-based Risk Measure

body: [Definition 2.17 of arXiv:2603.24423, 'First passage percolation preserves sublinearly Morse boundaries'] The topology on ∂sX is defined as follows: let β be a κ Morse sublinearly quasi-geodesic ray for some κ. [Defi 3 (Equivalent definition for the nested sequences $\mathcal{D}$) of arXiv:2607.28614, 'Tampered Memory Elephant Random Walk on one-dimensional integer lattice'] Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a collection of nested sequence generated by the chain $\{L_n\}_{n \ge 1}$. Consider the sequences of random variables $\{ \tau_k, \sigma_k \}_{k \geq 1}$ where $\tau_k, \sigma_k$ as defined above. Then the sets $D_n^c$ and $D_n$ can be expressed as follows:  
for $k \in [\mu_n, \mu_{n+1})$, with $\mu_0 \equiv 0$
\[ D^c_k = \begin{cases}

    D^c_{\mu_n} \cup \{ \mu_n + 1, \mu_n + 2, \ldots, k \},  & \text{ for } \mu_n < k \leq \mu_n+\tau_{n+1}, \\ 
    D^c_{\mu_n+ \tau_{n+1}} & \text{ for } \mu_n + \tau_{n+1} < k \leq     \mu_{n+1},
\end{cases}\]
and 
\[
D_k = \begin{cases}
    D_{\mu_n} & \text{ for } \mu_n < k \le \mu_n+\tau_{n+1}, \\
    D_{\mu_n} \cup \{ \mu_n + \tau_{n+1}+1, \mu_n + \tau_{n+1}+2, \ldots, k \} & \text{ for } \mu_n < k \leq \mu_{n+1}.
\end{cases}
\]

body: For a complex m by n matrix A, s_1(A) >= s_2(A) >= ... >= 0 are its singular values (padded with zeros to min(m, n) entries). For 1 <= p < infinity the Schatten p-norm is ||A||_{S_p} = (sum_i s_i(A)^p)^(1/p), and ||A||_{S_infinity} = s_1(A), the spectral norm. Zero singular values do not change the value. These norms are unitarily invariant, ||U A V||_{S_p} = ||A||_{S_p} for unitary U and V, and S_1 is the nuclear (trace) norm, S_2 the Frobenius norm and S_infinity the spectral norm.

body:
[Lemma eq:prob0 of arXiv:2607.29330, 'Large deviations for the maximum of\\ the generalized TAP free energy'] Let \(q\in(0,1)\) satisfy \(\xi'(q)>0\), let
		\(\zeta\in\mathcal P([q,1])\), and let \(\mathbf{m}\in B_N^\circ\) satisfy
		\(\|\mathbf{m}\|_2^2=Nq\). Let
		\[
		\lambda=-2\mathcal V'_\zeta(q)
		=\xi''(q)\widehat\zeta(q)+\frac1{\widehat\zeta(q)}.
		\]
		Then
		\begin{equation}
			\log p_{\nabla F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(\mathbf{m})}(0)
			=-\frac{Nq\lambda^2}{2(\xi'(q)+q\xi''(q))}
			-\frac{N-1}{2}\log(2\pi\xi'(q))
			-\frac12\log(2\pi(\xi'(q)+q\xi''(q))).
		\end{equation}
		If in addition \(\xi'(q)\widehat\zeta(q)^2=q\), then
		\begin{equation}
			\frac1N\log p_{\nabla F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(\mathbf{m})}(0)
			=-\frac12
			-\frac{q\xi''(q)}{2\xi'(q)}
			-\frac12\log(2\pi\xi'(q))
			+O\left(\frac1N\right).
		\end{equation}

Method: Synchronous contraction on convex domains Result: For two reflected motions driven by the same Brownian path, the noise cancels in their difference. With inward normals, d|X-Y|^2=2<X-Y,n(X)>dL_X-2<X-Y,n(Y)>dL_Y. Convexity makes both contributions nonpositive, so the distance is nonincreasing. Check: Each sign follows from the supporting half-space inequality at the boundary point. The calculation uses finite-variation reflection terms and has no missing quadratic-variation term. Obstruction: Nonincrease alone does not prove convergence to zero. Nonconvex domains can have both signs and require control of the long-run reflection geometry.

Method: Exact recurrence, conditional-law calculation, or source-specific limiting obstruction Result: For a fixed finite ball B and bounded time t, the chance of any lightning in B is at most |B|*lambda_n*t, which vanishes under the source scaling lambda_n->0. Yet nontrivial freezing must survive in the limiting process. Therefore all limiting freezing in a fixed ball must be transmitted from components extending outside every fixed ball, so simply coupling local clocks and discarding distant vertices cannot prove the result. Check: The bound follows from1-exp(-|B|*lambda_n*t)<=|B|*lambda_n*t. The simultaneous condition n*lambda_n->infinity allows giant components to freeze quickly while fixed neighborhoods see no direct marks. Obstruction: One needs quantitative control on mesoscopic component growth and transmitted freeze times. The local graph limit and vanishing local lightning do not determine the required boundary randomness.

body: In the localized FPP problem on a finite region of Z^2 (weights restricted to a finite edge set), define G as the set of edges lying in EVERY geodesic between two fixed points. Then membership is Borel outright: e belongs to G if and only if the passage time computed with e forbidden strictly exceeds the unrestricted passage time, and both are continuous functions of finitely many weights. No measurable selection of a geodesic is needed for any argument consuming G, and geodesic non-uniqueness only SHRINKS G (more geodesics means more constraints), so uniqueness assumptions are unnecessary for upper bounds on |G|. Confirmed in independent review (2026-08-10) of an entropy-method derivation that had carried a measurable-selection caveat it turned out not to need.

We split the proof into short and long averaging horizons.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Short averaging horizons: $0<T\le T_N$.}
By Kantorovich--Rubinstein duality,
\[
\begin{aligned}
        W_1(\overline\mu_T^N,\overline\mu_T)

body:
[Thm 1 of arXiv:2605.07050, 'Universality of the fluctuations of the free energy in generalized Sherrington--Kirkpatric'] Suppose that $\sqrt{N} W_{ij}$ $(1 \leq i<j \leq N)$ are i.i.d., symmetric, and strictly sub-Gaussian random variables with variance $1$. Suppose that $\sqrt{N} x_k$ $(1 \leq k \leq N)$ are i.i.d., symmetric, and strictly sub-Gaussian random variables with variance $1$, independent of $\sqrt{N} W_{ij}$. Let
\beq 
	Z_N \equiv Z_N(\beta) = \E_{\caX} \left[ \exp \left( \beta N \sum_{i<j} W_{ij} \frac{x_i x_j}{\| \bsx \|^2} \right) \right], \qquad F_N \equiv F_N(\beta) = \frac{1}{N} \log Z_N.
\eeq
(When $\| \bsx \| = 0$, we define $x_i x_j / \| \bsx \|^2 = 0$ for all $i, j$.) Then, for any $\beta \in (0, 1)$,
\[
	F_N(\beta) \to F(\beta) := \beta^2 /4
\]
and
\[
	N(F_N(\beta) - F(\beta) ) \Rightarrow \caN(m_F, V_F),
\]
as $N \to \infty$, i.e., $N(F_N(\beta) - F(\beta) )$ converges in distribution to the Gaussian with mean $m_F$ and the variance $V_F$ as $N \to \infty$. Here,
\[
	m_F = \frac{1}{4} \log (1- \beta^2) + \frac{\beta^2 (1-m_4)}{4} + \frac{\beta^4 (w_4-3)(m_4^2 -3)}{48}
\]
and
\[
	V_F = -\frac{1}{2} \left( \log (1- \beta^2) + \beta^2 - \frac{\beta^4 (w_4-3)}{4} \right),
\]
where we let $w_4 = N^2 \E[W_{ij}^4]$ and $m_4 = N^2 \E [x_1^4]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 22 of arXiv:2608.18557, 'Randomly Permuted Orthogonal Products and Fast Dimension Reduction'] There exist universal constants \(c,C>0\) such that the following
	holds. Let \(X\subseteq \mathbb S^{d-1}\) with \(|X|=N\geq d\),
	\(0<\eps<1\), \(0<\eta<1/2\), and
	\(I\subseteq [d]\) with \(|I|=m\). Let \(Q_T\) be a Kac walk with
	\(T\geq Cd\log(d/\eta)\), let \(D_\xi\) be an independent
	Rademacher diagonal, and let \(\pi\) be an independent uniform
	permutation on \(S_d\). Define
	\[
	\Phi=\sqrt{\frac dm}\,P_IQ_TD_\xi P_\pi.
	\]
	Assume the admissibility condition
	\[
	m\log\left(\frac d\eta\right)
	\log\left(\frac{Nd}{\eta}\right)
	\log\left(\frac{Nm}{\eta}\right)
	\leq c d.
	\]
	If $m\geq C\eps^{-2}\log(N/\eta)$,
	then, with probability at least \(1-\eta\),
	\[
	\sup_{x\in X}
	\left|
	\norm{\Phi x}_2-\norm{x}_2
	\right|
	\le
	\eps\norm{x}_2.
	\]

[Proposition 25 of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] Let $G_1,G_2$ be locally compact Hausdorff groups and $f$ a map from $G_1$ to $G_2$.
    Consider that $G_1$ and $G_2$ are equipped with LR-coarse structure.
    Then the following six assertions hold:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Assume that  $f$ is a continuous group-homomorphism. Then $f$ is controlled.
        \item Assume that  $f$ is a continuous anti-group-homomorphism. Then $f$ is controlled.
        \item Assume that  $f$ is a topological closed embedding group-homomorphism. Then $f$ is coarse. 
        \item Assume that  $f$ is a topological closed embedding anti-group-homomorphism. Then $f$ is coarse. 
        \item Assume that  $f$ is an isomorphism of topological groups. Then $f$ is a coarse equivalence. 
        \item Assume that  $f$ is an anti-isomorphism of topological groups. Then $f$ is a coarse equivalence. 
    \end{enumerate}
    In particular, for a group and its closed subgroup, the inclusion map is coarse. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own-work research draft; proof (unaudited), independent review and priority assessment pending. Fix k>=2, D>=1, 0<alpha<1, b>0, M,K>=0 and 0<lambda<=1<=Lambda. Let F:[0,1]^k->R^D extend C1 to a neighborhood with ||DF||<=b and Lip(DF)<=M, and let p be a probability density with lambda<=p<=Lambda and Lip(p)<=K. There are C,W0 depending only on these constants such that, for W>=W0, a common scalar-input ReLU feedforward DAG with at most W charged edge weights and biases and depth O(W) satisfies sup_(F,p) inf_theta W1((G_theta)#Unif[0,1], F#(p dx))<=C W^(-2(1+alpha)/k). Skip connections, unrestricted real precision and discontinuous target-to-weight assignments are allowed. All fixed coefficients, affine biases, output translations and scalar-source conversion edges are charged. The proof reflects p evenly to a 2-periodic positive density, invokes Caffarelli-Li periodic Monge-Ampere C2,alpha regularity and uniqueness, and derives uniform potential bounds by compactness and the mean-zero periodic Schauder implicit-function theorem. Reflection symmetry forces S=x+grad u to preserve every cube face; det DS=p implies its inverse R samples p exactly. F composed with R lies in a common C1,alpha ball; the Yarotsky-Zhevnerchuk function approximation theorem and a logarithmic-size tent-map scalar-source conversion give the rate. For (a,b)-bi-Lipschitz maps with Lip(DF)<=M, exactly uniform surface laws are included by lambda=(a/b)^k, Lambda=(b/a)^k, K=k b^(k-1) M/a^k. Thus every exponent 4/k-eta with fixed 0<eta<2/k is available, but no endpoint 4/k, bounded-bit upper or arbitrary closed-manifold-class upper is claimed. The least-trusted analytic step is uniformity of the mean-zero periodic Schauder/implicit-function argument, not certified by finite algebraic controls.

[Theorem thm:fullII of arXiv:2607.01463, 'Two Multi--Draw Coupon Collector models with different retention rules'] The full asymptotic expansion of the expectation of the random variable $T_{N,1}$ (of Theorem (result2 of the paper)) regarding the $d$ coupon collector problem, where we draw $d$ coupons each time, but keep the \textbf{least} collected coupon so far, is (as $N \rightarrow \infty$)
\[
\mathbb{E}[T_{N,1}]
\sim
\frac{N}{d}\log N
+\left(\frac{\gamma}{d}+
C_d\right)N
+
\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}
\bigl(\alpha_{j+1}(d)\log N+u_j(d)\bigr)N^{-j},
\]
where,
\begin{equation*}
C_d:
=
\int_0^1
\left(
\frac{1}{1-(1-x)^d}-\frac{1}{dx}
\right)\,dx,
\end{equation*}
\[
u_j(d)
=
\gamma\,a_{j+1}(d)
+
\int_0^1 h_{j+1}(x;d)\,dx
+
\frac{a_j(d)+h_j(1;d)-h_j(0;d)}{2}
\]
\[
\qquad
-
\sum_{r=1}^{\lfloor (j+1)/2\rfloor}
\frac{B_{2r}}{2r}\,a_{j+1-2r}(d)
+
\sum_{r=1}^{\lfloor (j+1)/2\rfloor}
\frac{B_{2r}}{(2r)!}
\bigl(
h_{j+1-2r}^{(2r-1)}(1;d)-h_{j+1-2r}^{(2r-1)}(0;d)
\bigr),
\]
and, as usual, $\lfloor x\rfloor$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$. The quantities $\alpha_j$ and $h_j$ are defined in the Appendix in relations ((a3 of the paper)) and ((a4 of the paper)). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let e be the normalized all-ones vector, P=I-ee*, and B a balanced diagonal matrix with entries plus/minus1. B strongly converges to the symmetric Bernoulli law.     \[
    Y_{-1}\xrightarrow{f_0}Y_0\xrightarrow{f_1}Y_1\xrightarrow{f_2}Y_2\to\ldots
    \]
    satisfies $f_n\simeq 0$ for $n\geq 0$. We call such an extended filtered object \textbf{split}.

body: In statistical mechanics, the Griffiths inequality, sometimes also called Griffiths–Kelly–Sherman inequality or GKS inequality, named after Robert B. Griffiths, is a correlation inequality for ferromagnetic spin systems. Informally, it says that in ferromagnetic spin systems, if the 'a-priori distribution' of the spin is invariant under spin flipping, the correlation of any monomial of the spins is non-negative; and the two point correlation of two monomial of the spins is non-negative.
title: Griffiths inequality

body: In Riemannian geometry, the sectional curvature is one of the ways to describe the curvature of Riemannian manifolds. The sectional curvature $K(\sigma _{p})$ depends on a two-dimensional linear subspace $\sigma _{p}$ of the tangent space at a point $p$ of the manifold. It can be defined geometrically as the Gaussian curvature of the surface which has the plane $\sigma _{p}$ as a tangent plane at $p$, obtained from geodesics which start at $p$ in the directions of $\sigma _{p}$ (in other words, the image of $\sigma _{p}$ under the exponential map at $p$). The sectional curvature is a real-valued function on the 2-Grassmannian bundle over the manifold.

Historical source result, superseded as a convergence-rate frontier by arXiv:2606.29593v1 Theorem 3.1. Let Delta_(t+1)=(I-M_t)Delta_t in finite-dimensional real space, where the random self-adjoint matrices M_t are independent, satisfy 0<=M_t<=I, and have a common mean Q. Let Delta_0 be deterministic (or independent of the matrix sequence with finite second moment). Dereziński and Dong prove that there exist absolute constants C>0 and theta>=0.001 such that E[Delta_t^T Q Delta_t]<=C E||Delta_0||^2/t^(3/4+theta), for t>=1. In particular, for a nonzero consistent matrix A with rows a_i^T, randomized Kaczmarz sampling nonzero row i with probability ||a_i||^2/||A||_F^2 satisfies E||A x_t-b||^2<=C ||A||_F^2||x_0-x_*||^2/t^(3/4+theta). Unit rows give uniform sampling. The rate is for the true last iterate and is independent of condition number; it does not establish inverse-time convergence.

\|(Q(x)^{j+1} - \Pi(x)) - (Q(y)^{j+1} - \Pi(y))\| \leq 2C^*\lambda^{j+1}.
\end{equation}

\emph{Lipschitz bound:} By telescoping $Q(x)^{j+1} - Q(y)^{j+1} = \sum_{\ell=0}^{j} Q(x)^\ell(Q(x) - Q(y))Q(y)^{j-\ell}$ and $\|Q(x)^\ell\| \leq 1$:
\[
\|Q(x)^{j+1} - Q(y)^{j+1}\| \leq (j+1)L_Q\|x - y\|.
\]

[Definition def:strong-solution of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] Let \((\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})\) be a complete probability space supporting a family of \(d\)-dimensional Wiener processes \((W(\cdot,\xi))_{\xi \in [0,1]}\) and a family of initial random variables \((X_0(\xi))_{\xi \in [0,1]}\) , along with a deterministic initial fibered probability-graphon \(q_0 \in \mathcal{P}_{\nu\otimes \nu}([-W,W]\times [0,1]^2)\). We shall say that a pair \((X(\cdot,\xi),q_\gamma^{\xi,\xi'})_{\xi,\xi'\in [0,1]}\) is a \emph{strong solution} of (equation eq:multi-agent-macroscopic-SDE of the paper) if the family of continuous stochastic processes \(X=(X(\cdot,\xi))_{\xi \in [0,1]}\) and the map \(q:[0,1]^2\times [0,T]\times \mathcal{C}_T^d\times \Omega \to \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R})\) verify:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
		\item For almost every \(\xi \in [0,1]\), the pathwise law of the state process satisfies \(\mu^{\xi} = \mathrm{Law}(X(\cdot,\xi)) \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_T^d)\), and the map \(\xi \mapsto \mu^{\xi}\) is measurable.
		\item For almost every \(\xi \in [0,1]\), the process \(X(\cdot,\xi)\) is adapted to the filtration generated by the Wiener process \(W(\cdot,\xi)\) and the initial condition \(X_0(\xi)\), and satisfies the following integral equation \(\mathbb{P}\)-a.s.:
		\[
			\begin{aligned}
            &\quad X(t,\xi) = X_0(\xi)\\
            &\qquad+ \int_{0}^{t} \int_0^1\int_{\mathcal{C}^d_s} \int_{\mathbb{R}} w \,q^{\xi,\xi'}_\gamma(s,dw)\,K(X(s,\xi),\gamma(s))\,d\mu_{[0,s]}^{\xi'}(\gamma)\,d\xi' \,ds + \sqrt{2\nu}W(t,\xi), \quad t \in [0,T].
            \end{aligned}
		\]
		\item \(\mathbb{P}\)-a.s. and for almost every \(\xi,\xi' \in [0,1]\), the map 
		\[
		(t,\gamma) \in [0,T]\times \mathcal{C}_T^d \mapsto q^{\xi,\xi'}_\gamma(t) \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R})
		\]
		is narrowly continuous. Moreover, for any fixed path \(\gamma \in \mathcal{C}_T^d\), the time-dependent measure \(t \in [0,T] \mapsto q^{\xi,\xi'}_\gamma(t) \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R})\) solves the transport equation \((equation eq:multi-agent-macroscopic-SDE of the paper)_2\) in the distributional sense, with initial condition \(q^{\xi,\xi'}_{\gamma}(0) = q_0^{\xi,\xi'}\).
		\item \(\mathbb{P}\)-a.s., for every \(t\in [0,T]\) and every \(\gamma\in \mathcal{C}_T^d\), the map \((\xi,\xi') \in [0,1]^2 \mapsto q^{\xi,\xi'}_\gamma(t) \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R})\) is measurable.
	\end{enumerate}
title: Strong solution to \eqref{eq:multi-agent-macroscopic-SDE}

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The paths on $\mathbb Z$ are counted by the binomial coefficients. In particular, the $2k$-paths based at $0$ are counted by the central binomial coefficients,
$$L_{2k}=\binom{2k}{k}$$
and $\mu$ is the centered measure having these numbers as even moments.

Let q be a prime power and 1 <= k <= q. Choose C_0, ..., C_{k-1} independent and uniform in F_q and let P(t) = C_0 + C_1 t + ... + C_{k-1} t^(k-1). Then the family (P(a))_{a in F_q} is k-wise independent and each P(a) is uniform on F_q. If k < q, no k + 1 of the evaluations are independent: for distinct a_1, ..., a_{k+1}, P(a_{k+1}) is a function of P(a_1), ..., P(a_k), and the (k+1)-tuple takes only q^k of the q^(k+1) possible values.

[Theorem T:inv-reflect of arXiv:2412.03521, 'On ergodic properties of stochastic PDEs'] Let $B_t$ be the standard Brownian motion in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Let $\nu$ be the
  probability measure of the 3-$d$ Bessel bridge, namely, the law of
  $\left\{\left|B_t\right|\right\}_{t \in [0,1]}$ conditioned to $B_1 = 0$.  The
  set $K_{0}$ is introduced in (equation E:def-Kalpha of the paper) with $\alpha=0$. We consider a
  measure $\nu^{G}$ on $K_0$ defined as follows: for all $\xi \in K_0$,
  \begin{align}
    \nu^G (\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} \xi) \coloneqq e^{2 G(\xi)} \nu(\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} \xi),
  \end{align}
  where $G$ is given by~(equation E:def-Gxi of the paper). Then, $\nu^G$ is an invariant measure
  for~(equation E:reflect of the paper) reflected at $0$.
title: Theorem~5 of~\cite{zambotti:01:reflected}

[Lem 13 of arXiv:2608.21090, 'Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process conditioned to have restricted $L_2$-norm'] Fix $x\in\R$ and define $M=(M_t)_{t\geq 0}$, with $h$ as in Lemma \ref{lem:ratiouniformasymptotics},
    \[M_t:=h\left(U_t,Z_t,t\right)=\exp\left(\left(x^2-U_t^2+t\right)\frac{1-2\gamma\theta}{4\theta}- Z_t\frac{1-4\gamma^2\theta^2}{8\theta^2}\right),\quad\forall t\geq 0.\]
    Then $M$ is a martingale and
    \[M_t=\exp\left(-\left(\frac{1}{2\theta}-\gamma\right)\int_0^tU_s\,d W_s-\frac12\left(\frac{1}{2\theta}-\gamma\right)^2Z_t\right),\quad\forall t\geq 0.\]
title: Lem 13 of arXiv:2608.21090

[Prop Prop_TransformToNormalForm of arXiv:2609.02848, 'The universal moduli space of non-degenerate $\Z/2\Z$~harmonic spinors'] {Donaldson2021}}]
  
  Let $\mathbf{Sl}$ be a slice.
  For every $({\mathbf{p}}_0,[{\mathfrak l}_0]) \in \mathbf{Sl}$ there is a \defined{local uniformiser};
  that is:
  an open neighbourhood $\mathscr{U} \subseteq \mathbf{Dir} \times \mathbf{Ram}$ of $({\mathbf{p}}_0,[{\mathfrak l}_0])$ and a tame smooth map
  \begin{equation*}
    u \mskip0.5mu\colon\thinspace \mathscr{U} \to \widehat\mathscr{G}(S)
  \end{equation*}
  such that for every $({\mathbf{p}},[{\mathfrak l}]) \in \mathscr{U}$
  \begin{equation*}
    u({\mathbf{p}},[{\mathfrak l}])^*({\mathbf{p}},[{\mathfrak l}]) \in \mathbf{Sl}.
  \end{equation*}
  Moreover, given a compact subset $K \subseteq X {\backslash} \mathrm{Br}({\mathfrak l}_0)$,
  the local uniformiser can be chosen such that 
  $u({\mathbf{p}},[{\mathfrak l}])|_K = \mathbf{1}_S$
  for every
  $({\mathbf{p}},[{\mathfrak l}]) \in \mathscr{U}$.

body: [Prop poincare of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Every Reebless $C^0$-foliation $\mathcal{G}$ on $\mathbb{T}^2$ of slope $s$ is monotone equivalent to a linear foliation $\mathcal{G}_s$ of slope $s$. When $s$ is irrational, the monotone equivalence can be taken to be a blowup along countably many leaves. When $s$ is rational, the monotone equivalence can be taken to be a blowup along countably many leaves, each inserting a $\sharp$ or $\flat$ annulus, followed by a blowdown of countably many $\natural$ annuli. The invariant measure on $\mathcal{G}_s$ pulls back to an invariant transverse measure on $\mathcal{G}$ whose support is the union of all minimal sets of $\mathcal{G}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop poincare of arXiv:2608.30031

body: In mathematics, Hall's marriage theorem, proved by Philip Hall, is a theorem with two equivalent formulations. In each case, the theorem gives a necessary and sufficient condition for an object to exist:The combinatorial formulation answers whether a finite collection of sets has a transversal—that is, whether an element can be chosen from each set without repetition. Hall's condition is that for any subset of sets from the collection, the total unique elements they contain is at least as large as the number of sets in the subset. The graph theoretic formulation answers whether a finite bipartite graph has a perfect matching—that is, a way to match each vertex from one group uniquely to an adjacent vertex from the other group. Hall's condition is that any subset of vertices from one group has a neighbourhood of equal or greater size.
title: Hall's marriage theorem

body:
[Proposition 26 of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $V$ be a strictly convex, $p$-homogeneous, $C^2$ function on $\R^n$, $p>1$, satisfying $V(o)=0$. Then, the geometric inequality
    \begin{equation}
    
        \vol(K)\vol\left(\nabla \mathcal{L}V(K^\circ)\right)^{p-1} \leq \vol\left(\left\{V\leq \frac{1}{p}\right\}\right)^p, \qquad \forall \,K \in \mathcal{C}^n,
    \end{equation}
    holds if and only if for every $f \in \mathcal{F}_n$ and all measurable functions $g:\R^n\to\R_+$ and $\Omega:\R_+\to\R_+$, where $\Omega$ is non-increasing, that satisfy the pointwise bound
    \[
        f(x)^{\frac{1}{p}}g(y)^{\frac{p-1}{p}} \leq \Omega\left(\frac{\langle x,y \rangle}{p}\right), \qquad \forall \,\,x, y \in \R^n \text{ with } \langle x,y \rangle>0,
    \]
    one has the functional inequality:
    \begin{equation}
    
        \left(\int_{\R^n}f(x)dx\right)\left(\int_{\R^n}g(\nabla V(z))dz\right)^{p-1} \leq \left(\int_{\R^n}\Omega(V(z))dz\right)^p.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 26 of arXiv:2609.01460

body:
[Definition eqn:SplittingMap of arXiv:2609.01464, 'Removability of non-isolated singularities for Einstein metrics and RCD spaces'] Let $n\geqslant 2$ be an integer. Let $(X,\mathrm{d},\mathcal{H}^n)$ be an $\mathrm{RCD}(-1,n)$ metric measure space, and let $1\leqslant k\leqslant n$. Let $\delta>0$, $r>0$. We say that $u=(u_1,\ldots,u_k):B_r(x)\to \mathbb R^k$ is a {\rm $\delta$-splitting map} if there is a constant $C=C(n)$ such that the following hold:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $u_i$ is harmonic on $B_r(x)$ for every $i=1,\ldots,k$.
        \item $|\nabla u_i|\leqslant C$ for every $i=1,\ldots,k$.
        \item We have, for every $i,j=1,\ldots,k$,
        \[
        \fint_{B_r(x)} |\nabla u_i\cdot \nabla u_j-\delta_{ij}|\ensuremath{\mathrm d}\mathcal{H}^n \leqslant \delta.
        \]
        \item We have, for every $i=1,\ldots,k$ 
        \[
        r^2\fint_{B_r(x)} |\operatorname{Hess} u_i|^2\ensuremath{\mathrm d}\mathcal{H}^n \leqslant \delta
        \]
    \end{enumerate}
title: Definition eqn:SplittingMap of arXiv:2609.01464

body: [Lemma lem:likeliness of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple C'] Fix distinct $x,y \in \partial \BD$ and let $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ be such that $\varepsilon < \min\{1/2, |x-y| / 3\}$. For each $n \in \BN$, let $\eta_n$ be a chordal $\SLE_{\kappa_n}(-1;-1)$ in $\BD$ starting from $x$ and targeting $y$, where the force points are located at $x^-$ and $x^+$ respectively. Then, there exists a universal constant $p \in (0,1)$ such that the following holds for all $n \in \BN$. With probability at least $p$, we have that $\eta_n$ hits $B_{\varepsilon}((1-2\varepsilon)x)$ before exiting $B_{2\varepsilon}(x)$.

[Theorem 29 of arXiv:2609.02105, 'Contact fundamental forms and \\ adjoint varieties'] For each simple Lie algebra $\fg$, there is a unique (up to isomorphism) graded Lie algebra structure of the form 
  $$\fg \ = \ \fg_{-2} \oplus \fg_{-1} \oplus \fg_0 \oplus \fg_1 \oplus  \fg_2$$ such that $\fg_-$ and $\fg_+$ are graded Heisenberg algebras. The  corresponding homogeneous space $G/P_+$ (in the notation of Theorem \ref{t.graded}), called the {\em adjoint variety} of $\fg$, has a natural $G$-invariant contact structure given by $\fg_{-1}$. Conversely, if a $G$-homogeneous projective variety has a $G$-invariant contact structure, then it is the adjoint variety of $\fg$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 29 of arXiv:2609.02105

[Lemma lower_bound_on_expected_total_size_of_animals_hitting_one_vertex_on_free_product of arXiv:2505.07145, 'Nonamenable Poisson zoo'] Consider a nonamenable graph $G$ that can be obtained as a free product $G_1 \star G_2$ of two transitive graphs, and let $\Gamma \leq \mathrm{Aut}(G)$ be such that it acts transitively and unimodularly on $G$.
Let $\nu_{o}$ be a $\Gamma$-rotation invariant measure on $\mathcal{H}_{o}$, then $\nu$ the measure on $Z$ induced from $\nu_{o}$ via (equation def:induced_measure_on_zoospace of the paper), and $\mathcal{X} = \sum_{i \in I} \delta_{(x,H)_i} \sim \mathcal{Q}_{\nu}^\lambda$.
Given any $R \in \mathbb{N}_{>0}$ and $x \in V(G)$, for the restriction of the process introduced in Definition (def:point_measure_restricted_to_hit_B_but_not_the_closure_of_A of the paper), depending on $\nu_{o}$ and maybe $R$, at least one of 
\begin{equation}
	
	\mathbb{E} \left[ \check{ \Sigma }_{\{x\}, \, \mathcal{N}_1(x) }^R \right] \geq \tfrac{\mathrm{h}(G)}{2} \cdot \lambda \cdot m_2^R
	\qquad \text{or} \qquad
	\mathbb{E} \left[ \check{ \Sigma }_{\{x\}, \, \mathcal{N}_2(x)}^R \right] \geq \tfrac{\mathrm{h}(G)}{2} \cdot \lambda \cdot m_2^R
\end{equation}
holds, where $\mathcal{N}_i(x)$ is the $G_i$-neighbourhood of $x$, as defined in~(equation def:free_product_term_neighbourhood of the paper).
title: Lemma lower_bound_on_expected_total_size_of_animals_hitting_one_vertex_on_free_product of arXiv:2505.07145

[Thm 9 of arXiv:2608.05185, '\large\bf ON THE HEAT FLOW CONJECTURE FOR RANDOM MATRICES'] Fix \(s>0\), \(u\in\C\) with \(\left|u\right|=1\), and
\(c_0\in\C\) with \(\left|c_0\right|\leq s\).  Put \(c_1=su^2\).
Let \(\mathbf{A}_N=\mathbf{A}_N^*\) be deterministic and satisfy
\[
 \sup_N\left\|\mathbf{A}_N\right\|<\infty,
 \qquad
 L_{\mathbf{A}_N}\overset{\mathrm{w}}{\longrightarrow}\mu_0,
\]
and let \((b_N)\) be a deterministic scalar sequence with
\(b_N\to b\in\C\).  Let
all the matrices \(\mathbf{Z}_N(s,c_j)\), \(N\geq1\), \(j=0,1\), be
defined on a common probability space.  Assume that, for each \(N\) and
\(j\), the entries of \(\mathbf{Z}_N(s,c_j)\) are centred and jointly
real-Gaussian, and satisfy
\[
 \E[(\mathbf{Z}_N(s,c_j))_{ab}
       \overline{(\mathbf{Z}_N(s,c_j))_{kl}}]
 =\frac{s}{N}\delta_{ak}\delta_{bl},
 \qquad
 \E[(\mathbf{Z}_N(s,c_j))_{ab}
       (\mathbf{Z}_N(s,c_j))_{kl}]
 =\frac{c_j}{N}\delta_{al}\delta_{bk}.
\]
The matrices may be coupled arbitrarily with each other and across \(N\).
Define
\[
 p_N(z)=\det\!\left(z\mathbf{I}-b_N\mathbf{I}
              -u\mathbf{A}_N-\mathbf{Z}_N(s,c_0)\right),
 \qquad
 q_N=\exp\!\left(-\frac{c_1-c_0}{2N}\partial_z^2\right)p_N.
\]
Then, almost surely,
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 \nu_{q_N}
 &\overset{\mathrm{w}}{\longrightarrow}
 (x\mapsto b+ux)_*(\mu_0\boxplus\mathfrak{sc}_s),\\
 L_{\,b_N\mathbf{I}+u\mathbf{A}_N+\mathbf{Z}_N(s,c_1)}
 &\overset{\mathrm{w}}{\longrightarrow}
 (x\mapsto b+ux)_*(\mu_0\boxplus\mathfrak{sc}_s).
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 9 of arXiv:2608.05185

body: In computational complexity theory, the Cook–Levin theorem, also known as Cook's theorem, states that the Boolean satisfiability problem is NP-complete. That is, it is in NP, and any problem in NP can be reduced in polynomial time by a deterministic Turing machine to the Boolean satisfiability problem.
title: Cook–Levin theorem

in the first variable, and invariant under simultaneous rotations:
\[
\psi(Oz,Ow)=\psi(z,w),\qquad O\in O(d).
\]
Then, for $d\ge2$ and every algebraic curvature tensor $R$ on $\R^d$,
\[
\int_{S^{d-1}}\int_{\R^d}\psi(z,w)R(z,w,z,w)\,dz\,d\sigma(w)
=\frac{\Scal(R)}{d(d-1)}
\int_{S^{d-1}}\int_{\R^d}\psi(z,w)
\bigl(|z|^2-(z\cdot w)^2\bigr)\,dz\,d\sigma(w).
\]

body: [Definition 21 (Iterative maximal independent set (IMIS) process) of arXiv:2608.07239, 'Unified framework for asymptotically uniform iterative construction of generalised random '] Consider a graph $G=(V,E)$. Start with the empty set $\boldsymbol{S}_0=\emptyset$. For $r=0$ onward, if $V\setminus\overline{N}(\boldsymbol{S}_r)$ is empty, let $\boldsymbol{S}_{r+1}=\boldsymbol{S}_r$. Otherwise, choose $v\in V\setminus\overline{N}(\boldsymbol{S}_r)$ uniformly at random, and let $\boldsymbol{S}_{r+1}=\boldsymbol{S}_r\cup\{v\}$. Finally, define $\boldsymbol{S}_{\infty}=\cup_{r=0}^{\infty}\boldsymbol{S}_r$.
title: Iterative maximal independent set (IMIS) process

[Definition of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] Given a constant \(W \geq 0\), we define the set of graphons with uniformly bounded weights in \([-W,W]\) as 
	\[
		\mathcal{G}_W := \left\{w \in L^{\infty}([0,1]^2) : \|w\|_{L^{\infty}} \leq W\right\}.
	\]
	For any two graphons \(w,\bar{w} \in \mathcal{G}_W\), the labeled cut distance is defined as 
	\[
		d_{\square}(w,\bar{w}) := \sup_{S,T\subset [0,1]} \left\vert \iint_{S\times T} (w(\xi,\xi')-\bar{w}(\xi,\xi')) d\xi d\xi' \right\vert,
	\]
	where the supremum is taken over all measurable sets \(S,T\subset [0,1]\). The unlabeled cut distance is defined as 
	\[
		\delta_{\square}(w,\bar{w}) := \inf_{\varphi \in S_{[0,1]}} d_{\square}(w,\bar{w}^{\varphi}),
	\]
	where \(\bar{w}^{\varphi}\) represents the rearrangement of \(\bar{w}\) by \(\varphi\), that is,
	\(\bar{w}^{\varphi}(\xi,\xi') = \bar{w}(\varphi(\xi),\varphi(\xi'))\).
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions '

body: [Theorem thm:RCDcodim3 of arXiv:2609.01464, 'Removability of non-isolated singularities for Einstein metrics and RCD spaces'] Let $n\geqslant 2$ be an integer and $K\in\mathbb R$. Suppose that $(M^n, g)$ is a closed $L^\infty$ Riemannian manifold, and $S\subset M$ is a closed subset of upper Minkowski codimension greater than $3-\frac{1}{n-1}$. Suppose that $\mathrm{Ric}(g) \geqslant Kg$ on $M\setminus S$. Then the metric completion of $(M\setminus S, g)$ is an $RCD(K,n)$-space. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm cty of arXiv:2507.09120, 'Chemical distance in graphs of polynomial growth'] Above criticality, the time constants associated to $D_p$ are Lipschitz continuous in $p$ in the following sense.
   For each $p_0 > p_c$, there exists $C(p_0)$ such that
   \[
      \limsup_{x \to \infty} \left| \frac{ \mathbb{E} D_p(o, x) }{ d_G(o,x) } - \frac{\mathbb{E} D_q(o,x) }{ d_G(o,x) } \right|
      \le C(p_0)|p-q|
   \]
   for all $p,q \in [p_0, 1]$.
   In particular, given any sequence $x_n \to \infty$ in $V$, if we define
   \begin{align*}
      \overline{d}(p) := \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{ \mathbb{E} D_p(o,x_n) }{ d_G(o, x_n) } & &

body:
[Definition defWellPoseHadmard of arXiv:2411.05534, 'Inverse problems for stochastic partial differential equations'] Consider the equation

\begin{equation}
F(u) = v, \qquad u\in U,\; v \in V.
\end{equation}

The equation (equation defWellPoseHadmard-eq1 of the paper) is called well-posed in the sense of Hadamard if the following three conditions are satisfied:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item For any $ v \in V $, there exists a solution $ u \in U$ such that $ F(u) = v $.
    \item This solution is unique.
    \item The solution $ v = F^{-1}(u) $ depends continuously on $ u $ in $U$.
\end{enumerate}
If at least one of these conditions is failed, the problem is called ill-posed.
title: Definition defWellPoseHadmard of arXiv:2411.05534

[Thm prop.convipvt of arXiv:2412.00822, '\textsc{Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations \\ beyond hyperbolic spaces}'] Let $\mathbf{X}^{(\lambda)}=(X_i^{(\lambda)} \, \,;\; \, i\geq 1 )$ be a PPP of intensity measure $\lambda \cdot \mathrm{Vol}_{ \mathcal{M}}$, where the points of $\mathbf{X}^{(\lambda)}$ are ranked by increasing values of $d(X_i^{(\lambda)},\mathbf{o})$. Then the following convergence in law holds
$$
\mathrm{Vor}(\mathbf{X}^{(\lambda)}) \underset{\lambda \downarrow 0}{\overset{\rm law}{\Longrightarrow}}\mathrm{Vor}( \boldsymbol{\Theta}, \boldsymbol{\Phi}, \mathbf{D}) \; ,
$$
where $\boldsymbol{\Theta}=(\Theta_{1},\ldots)$ and $\boldsymbol{\Phi}=(\Phi_{1},\ldots)$ are i.i.d.~uniform on $\partial\mathbb{H}_2 \times \partial\mathbb{H}_2$ and $\mathbf{D}=(D_{1},\ldots)$ is s.t.~$\left(\pi^{2}e^{D_{i}}\right)_{i\geq 1}$ is a rate-1 homogeneous PPP on $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$. The processes $\boldsymbol{\Theta}$,  $\boldsymbol{\Phi}$, $\mathbf{D}$ are all pairwise independent. We call $\mathrm{Vor}( \boldsymbol{\Theta}, \boldsymbol{\Phi}, \mathbf{D})$ the \textbf{\textit{ideal Poisson–Voronoi tessellation}} of $\mathcal{M}$ and denote it by $\text{\rm IPVT}(\mathcal{M})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \textsc{Convergence towards IPVT($\mathcal{M}$), extended version}

body:
[Proposition prop:weightedgap of arXiv:2608.30888, 'Three-term asymptotics for discrete\\ Hardy--Rellich constants in high dimension'] Fix $q,\gamma\in\mathbb N$.  Uniformly for smooth
$\phi\in\mathscr F_{q,N}$,
\begin{align}
 \int|\nabla\phi|^2\omega^\gamma
 &\geq(q-o(1))\int|\phi|^2\omega^\gamma,
 \\
 \int|\nabla\phi|^2\omega^\gamma
 &\geq\frac{qN}{2}(1-o(1))
 \int|\phi|^2\omega^{\gamma-1},
 \\
 \int|\Delta\phi|^2\omega^\gamma
 &\geq(q-o(1))\int|\nabla\phi|^2\omega^\gamma,
 \\
 \int|\Delta\phi|^2\omega^\gamma
 &\geq\frac{qN}{2}(1-o(1))
 \int|\nabla\phi|^2\omega^{\gamma-1}.
 
\end{align}
More precisely, there are constants $A_{q,\gamma}>0$ and
$N_{q,\gamma}$ such that, for $N\geq N_{q,\gamma}$, every occurrence of
$o(1)$ in these four inequalities may be replaced in absolute value by
$A_{q,\gamma}N^{-1/2}$.

    \[
        \MS(n,k)\ni\sum_{\ii\in\ms{[n]}{{k}}}\alpha_\ii\delta_\ii ~~~~\stackrel{\Psi_k}{\longmapsto}~~~~\sum_{\jj\in\ms{[n]}{{k+1}}}\beta_\jj\delta_\jj\in\MS(n,k+1),
    \]
    where $\delta_\ii\in\MS(n,k)$\marginpar{$\delta_\ii$} is the indicator vector of $\ii\in\ms{[n]}{k}$, and for $\jj=\{j_1,\ldots,j_{k+1}\}$ we have 
    \[
        \beta_\jj=\sum_{t=1}^{k+1} \alpha_{\jj\setminus\{j_t\}}.
    \]
    Denote by $\pure(n,k)$\marginpar{$\scriptstyle{\pure(n,k)}$} the orthogonal complement of $\Psi_{k-1}(\MS(n,k-1))$ in $\MS(n,k)$.\footnote{We use the standard inner product on $\MS(n,k)$ with respect to the basis given by $\{\delta_\ii\mid\ii\in\ms{[n]}{k}\}$.}

[Theorem thm:weak_sequential_compactness of arXiv:2606.11951, 'On Skorokhod Problems for Reflected and Singular Stochastic Heat Equations'] The families of (vector) measures $(\mu^{(a,\varepsilon)})_{\varepsilon\in (0,1]}$, $(\sigma^{(a,\varepsilon)})_{\varepsilon >0}$ and $(\nu_{\varepsilon})_{\varepsilon \in (0,1]}$ (and all non-empty subfamilies) are weak sequentially compact.
	
	Further, all weak limits of sequences in $(\mu^{(a,\varepsilon)})_{\varepsilon\in (0,1]}$, $(\sigma^{(a,\varepsilon)})_{\varepsilon >0}$ and $(\nu_{\varepsilon})_{\varepsilon \in (0,1]}$ are bounded by $(2\pi a(1-a))^{-1/2}$, bounded by $(2\pi a(1-a))^{-1/2}$ w.r.t.\ $\| \cdot \|$ and bounded w.r.t.\ $\| \cdot \|$, respectively.

[Theorem 23 of arXiv:2609.00209, 'Exit Times for Brownian Motion and Location Detection'] Let $D\subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ denote a bounded Lipschitz domain that is symmetric with respect to the $x$- and $y$-axes and let $u_k(x,y)=\mathbb{E}^{(x,y)}[\tau_D^k]$ for $k\geq 1$ denote the exit time moments from $D$. Denote
\[
D^+=\{(x,y)\in D:x,y\geq 0\}
\]
and assume that whenever $p,q\in D^+$ are distinct, there is some $\mu \in \textup{Spec}^{\ast}(D)$ where $\Phi_{\mu}(p)\neq \Phi_{\mu}(q)$. Then distinct points $p,q\in D$ have the same exit time moments if and only if $p$ and $q$ are obtained from each other by reflection across the $x$- and/or $y$-axes. Consequently, if $c_k$ for $k\geq 1$ are positive numbers such that the level curves $u_k=c_k$ intersect, then their intersection is either one, two, or four points determined by the values $c_k$.

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT; mathematical review pending; C0052 is not solved or refuted. Fix 0<gamma<3. Let G_x, x in Z^3, be a stationary centered unit-variance Gaussian field with covariance R_gamma(x-y)=(1+|x-y|^2)^(-gamma/2), and sigma_x=sign(G_x). These are stationary spin-flip symmetric positively associated +/-1 spins with E[sigma_0 sigma_x]=(2/pi)arcsin R_gamma(x), asymptotic to (2/pi)|x|^(-gamma), and on-site fourth cumulant -2. For every finite list of compactly supported smooth real tests f, N^(-3+gamma/2)sum_x f(x/N)sigma_x converges jointly to a Gaussian vector with covariance (2/pi)integral integral f(u)h(v)|u-v|^(-gamma)du dv. The nonlinear remainder after subtracting sqrt(2/pi) times the similarly scaled G-field has squared L2 norm O(N^(-2gamma)) for gamma<1, O(N^(-2)log N) at gamma=1, and O(N^(-(3-gamma))) for gamma>1; constants depend on fixed gamma and test. No nearest-neighbor Ising Gibbs, reflection-positivity, random-current, distribution-space tightness, or fourth-moment-convergence assertion is made.

[Lemma sumconvergestoexpectationas of arXiv:2506.10448, 'Hitting probabilities and the Ekstr\"om--Persson conjecture'] Let $(\widetilde\Omega,\widetilde\mathbb{P})$ be a probability space. Let $(A_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be 
a sequence of independent events in $\widetilde\Omega$, and let $(a_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be a 
bounded sequence of positive numbers. Suppose that $(N_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ is a strictly
increasing sequence of natural numbers such that 
\[
\sum_{n=1}^\infty E_n^{-1}<\infty,
\]
where $E_n:=\sum_{k=N_{n-1}+1}^{N_n}\widetilde\mathbb{P} (A_k)a_k> 0$. For all 
$\tilde\omega\in\widetilde\Omega$, define 
\[
S_n(\tilde\omega):=\sum_{k=N_{n-1}+1}^{N_n} \chi_{A_k}(\tilde\omega) a_k.
\]
Then $\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{S_n}{E_n}=1$ almost surely.

[Lemma 23 of arXiv:2608.16752, 'Absorption Probabilities for Random Convex Hulls: Distribution-Freeness via the Wall-Cross'] Let $N,d\geq1$ and  $q_1, \dots, q_N \in \R^d$.
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[(i)] $0 \notin \Conv(q_1, \dots, q_N)$ if and only if
        there is $v \in \R^d$ with $\langle q_m, v \rangle > 0$ for all
        $m$.
        \item[(ii)] $0 \in \Int \Conv(q_1, \dots, q_N)$ if and only if
        there is \emph{no} $v \neq 0$ with $\langle q_m, v \rangle \ge
        0$ for all $m$.
        \item[(iii)] If $q_1, \dots, q_N$ are in general linear position, then
        either $0 \notin \Conv(q_1, \dots, q_N)$ or $0 \in \Int
        \Conv(q_1, \dots, q_N)$.
        \item[(iv)] Let $N \ge d+1$ and $0 \in \partial \Conv(q_1, \dots, q_N)$.
        If there is exactly one $d$-element set $I\subseteq [N]$ such that
        the vectors $(q_i)_{i \in I}$ are linearly dependent, then the points $q_i$, $i \in I$,
        are affinely independent,
        $0 \in \relint \Conv(q_i : i \in I)$, and there is a unique unit
        vector $\nu$ such that $$\langle q_i, \nu \rangle = 0 \text{ for } i \in I
        \quad
        \text{and}
        \quad
        \langle q_m, \nu \rangle > 0 \text{ for }\, m \notin I.$$

    \end{itemize}

Proof (unaudited), target-2 extension. Consider scalar off-policy TD(0) on two states with feature 1, gamma=1/2, zero rewards, target always L, behavior L probabilities 1/2 and 1/4, and action-independent transition matrix P_p=[[p,1-p],[1-p,p]] for 0<=p<=1. The parameter is measured before fresh action/transition sampling conditional on the current state and whole past. Mean-square stability for every finite-second-moment initial joint law holds exactly for 0<alpha<r(p). For p<1, r(p) is the unique root in (1,2) of 4(1-p)+(7p-5)alpha+3(1-2p)alpha^2+(2p-1)alpha^3=0; r(1)=1. The function r is continuous and strictly decreasing on [0,1], with r(0) in (7/5,3/2), r(1/2)=4/3, and r(3/4) in (6/5,121/100). The trajectory mean threshold remains 4. Uniform stationary iid replay has mean-square threshold 4/3 for every p, so trajectory dependence improves the threshold below persistence 1/2 and worsens it above 1/2. Endpoints of all stability intervals are excluded.

[Lemma lem:linear-bound of arXiv:2507.09120, 'Chemical distance in graphs of polynomial growth'] Let $(X_e)_{e \in E}$ be a family of $\mathbb{N}$-valued random variables indexed by the
   edges of a transitive graph $G$ with polynomial growth of degree $d$.
   Suppose that for each $N \ge 1$ and each $2N$-separated
   subset $S$ of $E$, the family $\{X_e = N\}_{e \in S}$ is independent.
   Define $q_N := \sup_{e \in E} \mathbb{P}(X_e = N)$.
   Suppose that for some $B <\infty$
   we have $\sum_{N=0}^{\infty} N^{d+2} q_N \le B$.
   Then there exists $C$ depending only on $G$ and $B$ such that the following holds.
   For any random path $\pi$ starting from $o$ and any $L \in \mathbb{N}$ we have
   \[
      \mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{e \in \pi} X_e \right] \le CL + C \sum_{\ell \ge L} \ell \mathbb{P}( |\pi| = \ell )^{1/2}.
   \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own-work draft; F0124_C18 version 1; status: independently checked proof. For a two-sided nearest-neighbor iid walk with p in [1/2,1], q=1-p, independent iid fair sign scenery, and n>=4, prescribe Y_t=+1 at t=0 or 1 mod4 and -1 at t=2 or 3 mod4 for 0<|t|<=n; the t=0 color is NOT observed. Put A_n=p^(2n)+q^(2n) and D_n=16[p^(2n-2)q^2+q^(2n-2)p^2]. Then P(C0=+1 | this exterior)=A_n/(2A_n+D_n). For p=1/2 it equals 1/18 for every n>=4; for 1/2<p<1 its limit is 1/[2+16(q/p)^2], and at p=1 it is 1/2. Color inequality at time-distance two excludes every turn except possibly -1 and +1. A single turn at either conflicts with the exterior for n>=4. Straight paths allow either central color; paths with both turns require C0=-1 and save four distinct scenery sites, giving the factor 16. This is an exact finite-cylinder family, not a good/bad classification: arbitrary remote pattern changes remain uncontrolled. No novelty is asserted.
