{"artifact_digest":"sha256:f1a62227238ada58ac7f3867f52e37e36bf907ad6e27418a82a4593061dca15e","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/f1/f1a62227238ada58ac7f3867f52e37e36bf907ad6e27418a82a4593061dca15e.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:003ee7cd411bd14e46e167b8c6d8c2748dacb1466880217907ba41819bb91206","bundle_entry_key":"i0005-c23","bundle_id":"population.i0005-final-exploration-energy-and-charge-007","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"parking and interacting particle systems","draft":"w661/bundle_007.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.particle-hole:parking-unrevealed-hole-posterior-nearest-unexplored-reduction-draft","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# I0005-C23 v1: deferred holes and an exact unexplored-site reduction

Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty: KNOWN deferred-decision method;
UNCHECKED this exact parking posterior/reduction formulation. All statements
use the explicit exploration filtration below, which does not reveal
unvisited initial hole/empty labels.

For the sparse critical synchronous particle-hole process on Z^d, d>=1,
P(eta=1)=P(eta=-1)=p, P(eta=0)=1-2p, 0<p<1/2, put q=p/(1-p).
Let E_t be the information generated by the initial active-particle
indicators, active trajectories and actual arrivals/settlements through
round t. It includes A_t, but reveals an initial hole/empty label only
when an arrival tests that site. Define the E_t-measurable eligible field

    V_t(x)=1{A_0(x)=0 and no particle has arrived at x in rounds 1,...,t}.

Conditional on E_t, the surviving-hole indicators H_t(x) are independent
Bernoulli(q) coins on the set V_t=1, and are zero elsewhere. Consequently,

    h_t=q P(V_t(0)=1),
    P(H_t(0)=H_t(z)=1)=q^2 P(V_t(0)=V_t(z)=1), z!=0.

Let D_A be the graph distance from the origin to the nearest active site
at time t, and let

    N_t=number of V_t sites in B_(D_A-1)(0),

with an empty ball when D_A=0 and a limiting union when D_A=infinity.
Then the exact closer-hole probability is

    P(F_t)=E[1-(1-q)^N_t].

In particular

    q P(N_t>=1)<=P(F_t)<=P(N_t>=1).

For one fixed p, the closer-hole probability tends to zero if and only
if the probability of an eligible never-arrived site strictly nearer than
an active site tends to zero. This is an exact reduction; the unexplored
geometry remains unproved in d4.

## 1. Independent latent coins for the source initial law

Generate iid initial-particle indicators I_x with probability p. Independently
generate iid Bernoulli(q) coins B_x and all walks/tie randomness. Set eta(x)=1
when I_x=1. When I_x=0 set eta(x)=-1 if B_x=1 and eta(x)=0 otherwise.
This gives probabilities p,(1-p)q=p,(1-p)(1-q)=1-2p, exactly the source law.
Coins at initial particle sites are irrelevant.

Simulate by revealing B_x at the first arrival to a site with I_x=0.
If B_x=1, one arriving particle settles; otherwise none does. After that
first visit there is no unfilled hole there in either case. Before the
first arrival the coin has no effect on any trajectory or tie choice.
This is a law-equivalent deferred-decision construction.

## 2. Exact conditional distribution, including adaptive exploration

For a finite set S, the event that all its sites are eligible is determined
without reading any of their coins. To see this without assuming that
the explored set is independent of the coins, fix all initial indicators,
external coins and walk/tie randomness. Vary the coins at S. If no site
in S receives an arrival, the history through t is identical for every
choice. If some first arrival to S occurs, its occurrence is determined
before reading the first such coin, and the event that all S are eligible
is already false. Thus for any nonnegative E_t-measurable F,
F product_{x in S}V_t(x) is invariant under changing B_S.

Pointwise H_t(x)=B_x V_t(x). Integrating over the independent coins at S
therefore gives

    E[F product_{x in S}H_t(x)]
       =q^|S| E[F product_{x in S}V_t(x)].

This holds for all nonnegative F in the exploration sigma-field, and so
determines all conditional joint moments. Binary inclusion-exclusion
then identifies the conditional finite-dimensional law as independent
Bernoulli(q) on eligible sites, zero elsewhere. This proves the posterior
claim and its one- and two-site consequences. It does not condition on
the full initial eta configuration; doing so would reveal these coins.

## 3. Exact nearest-event formula

D_A and V_t are exploration-measurable. For each finite value D_A=k,
strictly nearer holes are exactly holes in the deterministic ball B_(k-1).
Conditional independence gives the probability that none of its N_t
eligible sites carries a hole as (1-q)^N_t. Partition by k to obtain
the formula. The k=0 case has N_t=0. For infinite D_A, take increasing
finite balls and use continuity of conditional probabilities; adopt
(1-q)^infinity=0. Thus no finite-nearest-distance assumption is necessary.

For each integer n>=1, q<=1-(1-q)^n<=1, and for n=0 the expression
vanishes. The bounds follow on averaging; fixed q>0 proves the stated
equivalence of zero limits. This does not hold uniformly if p is reselected
and q tends to zero.

## 4. Palm domination is now justified by a coupling

Given exploration, generate fresh independent Bernoulli(q) coins at all
eligible sites to realize the conditional hole field. It is coordinatewise
bounded by an iid Bernoulli(q) field on all sites. Mixing over exploration
preserves this domination even after conditioning on the final active
field. After conditioning additionally on H_t(0)=1, the origin is eligible
and its coin is fixed to one; all other remaining coins still have their
independent Bernoulli(q) law. Hence the other-hole Palm field is dominated
by iid Bernoulli(q), via this explicit coupling. This conclusion is not
inferred merely from C5's factorial-moment inequalities.

The moment consequences in C5/C8 become immediate from the displayed
identity. They do not constrain the geometry of V_t: for example the
two-hole upper bound q h_t reduces to the trivial bound
P(V_t(0)=V_t(z)=1)<=P(V_t(0)=1). A finite Palm count at mean spacing
still requires information about the actual unexplored set.

## Sources and remaining piece

Primary model: Bou-Rabee--Panagiotis arXiv:2609.02820v1, Sections 2 and
8.2, capacity-one sparse law. The latent-variable construction, adaptive
invariance argument and nearest-event reduction are explicitly proved
above. The unresolved task is the geometry of never-arrived eligible
sites relative to current active particles for one fixed d4 law.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:910b07332d3c65bdc4ce5cdeda4b2465d185fe70eef164a8962607b3724a5daf","revision_digest":"sha256:10667b77db602237787d0f4f48383239ddf147d74a90e24f5fd523c092a83032","source_id":"own-work:w661:I0005-C23:v1","source_revision":"v1; packaged 2026-10-14T07:46:54.3984460+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Corollary cor:charac-Y-reflexive of arXiv:2609.00794, 'On operators whose adjoints or second adjoints attain their norms'] Let $Y$ be a Banach space. Then the following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \itemsep0.25em
        \item $Y$ is reflexive.
        \item $\operatorname{QNA}(X,Y) = \operatorname{NA}_1(X,Y)$ for every Banach space $X$.
        \item $\operatorname{QNA}(\ell_1,Y) = \operatorname{NA}_1 (\ell_1,Y)$.
    \end{enumerate}
    If, moreover, $Y$ contains no isomorphic copy of $\ell_1$, then these conditions are also equivalent to 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*), start=4] 
\itemsep0.25em
        \item $\operatorname{NA}_1(X,Y) = \operatorname{NA}_2(X,Y)$ for every Banach space $X$.
        \item $\operatorname{NA}_1(\ell_1,Y) = \operatorname{NA}_2 (\ell_1,Y)$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary cor:charac-Y-reflexive of arXiv:2609.00794

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2607.26944, 'Improved bounds on the inradius and inverse inradius process of the convex hull of planar '] Let the exit time $\tau_{m,b}$ and opening angle $\alpha_m$ be defined as in~\eqref{eq:exit_time} and~\eqref{eq:opening_angle}, respectively, with parameters $m>0$ and $b>0$. Then for all powers $p\in\R$ and all starting points $(x,y)\in \mathbb{H}_{m,b}$, we have 
\[
\E _{(x,y)}[\tau_{m,b}^p]<\infty~\text{ if and only if }~p<\frac{\pi}{2\alpha_m}.
\]
In particular, $\E _{(x,y)}[\tau_{m,b}^p]<\infty$ for all $m>0$ when $p\leq\frac{1}{2}$, while for $p>\frac{1}{2}$, we have 
\[
\E _{(x,y)}[\tau_{m,b}^p]<\infty~\text{ if and only if }~m>\cot\left(\frac{\pi}{4p}\right).
\]

body:
[Lem 133 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $t\notin \oJ$ (recall Lemma~\ref{l:bad.J}) and parameters as in \eqref{eq:order-of-limits}: 
    \[\bE\Big[|tp'(t) - \trrr_t|\Big]
    \leq  
    o_{\trK}(1)
    \]
for $ \trrr_t\equiv \trrr(t,X^\plus(t))$. 

\begin{proof}
Let $\bar{P}(t)$ be the temporal smoothing of $tp'(t)$. Then for $t\notin\bar{J}$ we have
	\[
    \bE\Big[|tp'(t) - \trrr_t|\Big]
    =
    \bE\Big[|tp'(t) - \bar P(t)|\Big]
    +\bE\Big[|\bar P(t) - \trrr_t|\Big]
    = O(\lambda)
    +\bE\Big[|\bar P(t) - \trrr_t|
    \Big]\,.
    \]
Let $\bar{P}^N$ be the temporal smoothing of $t(p^N)'(t)$. It follows from Lemma~\ref{l:limit.coefs} that $\bar{P}^N$ converges pointwise to $\bar{P}$, and $\trrr^N$ converges pointwise to $\trrr$. It follows by the bounded convergence theorem that we also have convergence in expectation, so
	\[
	\bE\Big[|\bar P(t) - \trrr_t|\Big]
	=\bE\Big[|\bar P^N(t) - (\trrr^N)_t|\Big] + o_N(1)\,.
	\] 
We then note that $\bar{P}^N-\trrr^N$ is the smoothing (via Definitions~\ref{d:sp.smooth} and \ref{d:t.smooth}) of 
	\begin{align} \nonumber
	A^N(t,\vy)
	&\equiv t(p^N)'(t)-\rrr^{\plus,N}(t,\vy)
	= t(p^N)'(t)-\sum_{B^\frozen \subseteq B^{\frozen,\coarse}}
    \frac{|B|}{|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|}
    \rrr^{\trunc,N}(t,B) 
    \\
	&\qquad= \bigg(
	1-\frac{|B^{\frozen,\coarse} \cap [M]|}{|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|} 
	\bigg)
	t(p^N)'(t)
	+ \sum_{B^\frozen \subseteq B^{\frozen,\coarse}} \frac{|B|}{|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|}
	\bigg(
	t(p^N)'(t) -
	\rrr^{\trunc,N}(t,B)\bigg)\,,
	
	 \end{align}
where the correspondence between $\vy$ and $B^{\frozen,\coarse}$ is as described around \eqref{e:review.P}. For the first term in
\eqref{e:P.N.r.frozen.twoterms}, at any fixed time $t$, we have
\[\bE\bigg[ 1-\frac{|B^{\frozen,\coarse} \cap [M]|}{|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|} \bigg]
    = 1 - \sum_{B^{\frozen,\coarse}}
    \frac{|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|}{M^\frozen}
    \frac{|B^{\frozen,\coarse} \cap [M]|}{|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|}
    = 1 - \frac{M}{M^\frozen}
    = o_{\trK}(1)\,,
\]
by recalling the choice of $M^\frozen$ from Definition~\ref{d:froze}. For the second term in \eqref{e:P.N.r.frozen.twoterms},  we argued in the proof of Proposition~\ref{p:budget-constraints-without-frozen}\ref{it:Ising-budget-constraint} that the total fraction of particles ever frozen is with high probability at most $o_{\trK}(1)$, so this term is also small on average at any fixed time for the process $Y$. Altogether this shows
	\beq
	\bE\Big[ |A^N(t,\vY^{\frozen,N,\RomI:\RomIII}(t)) |\Big]
	= \int_{\R^3} |A^N(t,\vy)| \varrho_{N,t}(d\vy)
	\le o_{\trK}(1)\,.
	\eeq
Let $\tilde{A}^N$ be the spatial smoothing of $A^N$, via Definition~\ref{d:sp.smooth}. Let $\tvY^{\frozen,N}(t)\equiv \vY^{\frozen,N}(t)+\xxx$, and denote the projection onto the sum of the first three coordinates as
 $\tilde{Y}^{\frozen,N} = \tilde{Y}^{\frozen,N,\RomI}+\tilde{Y}^{\frozen,N,\RomII}+\tilde{Y}^{\frozen,N,\RomIII}$. Then
	\begin{align*} &\bE\Big[ |\tilde{A}^N(t, \tilde{Y}^{\frozen,N}(t)) |\Big]
	= \int_{\R} |\tilde{A}^N(t,y)| \overline{\varrho_{N,t}*\sphi}(y)\,dy \\
	&\qquad = \int_{\R} \bigg|
	\int_{H(y)} \int_{\R^3} \sphi(\vy-\vx) A^N(t,\vx)
		\,\rho_{N,t}(d\vx)\,d\vy \bigg| \,dy \\
	&\qquad\le  \int_{\R^3}
	|A^N(t,\vx)| \bigg( \int_{\R^3}
		 \sphi(\vy-\vx) \,d\vy\bigg)
		\,\rho_{N,t}(d\vx) =  \int_{\R^3}
	|A^N(t,\vx)|\rho_{N,t}(d\vx) \le o_{\trK}(1)\,,
	\end{align*}
using the previous estimate \eqref{e:AN.small.finiteN}. This shows that the bound \eqref{e:AN.small.finiteN} can be passed to the spatially smoothed quantity $A^N$. Similarly, let $\bar{A}^N$ be the temporal smoothing of $\tilde{A}^N$, via Definition~\ref{d:t.smooth}. Then
	\begin{align*}
	&\bE\Big[ |\bar{A}^N(t,\tilde{Y}^{\frozen,N}(t))| \Big]
	=\int_{\R} |\bar{A}^N(t,y)| \overline{\varrho_{N,t}*\sphi}(y)\,dy\\
	&\qquad\le \int_{\R}  
	\bigg( \int_{\R}\tphi(t-s) |  \tilde{A}^N(s) |\,ds  \bigg) \,
	 \overline{\varrho_{N,t}*\sphi}(y)\,dy \\
	&\qquad=
	\int_{\R} \tphi(t-s)
	\bigg[ \int_{\R} | \tilde{A}^N(s) | 
	 \overline{\varrho_{N,s}*\sphi}(y)
	 \,dy \bigg] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:Buse_basic_properties of arXiv:2605.26048, 'Classification of the eternal solutions and multiple coalescing shocks in the KPZ fixed po'] [Busa-Sepp-Sore-22a] 
On the space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb P)$, there exists a process
\[
\Bigl(W^{\xi}(x,s;y,t): \xi \in \mathfrak{X}, (x,s;y,t) \in \mathbb{R}^4\Bigr)
\]
such that for each fixed $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\xi \in \mathfrak{X}$, $\xi \in \Xi^c$, and $x \mapsto W^\xi(0,t;x,t)$ is a Brownian motion with diffusion coefficient $\sqrt 2$ and drift $2\mathcal P(\xi)$. Furthermore, the process satisfies the following properties on a single event of probability one:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), font=\normalfont]
\item{\rm(Continuity)}  The $\mathbb{R}^4 \times \mathfrak{X} \to \mathbb{R}$ function  $(x,s;y,t;\xi) \mapsto W^{\xi}(x,s;y,t)$ is  continuous. Furthermore, if $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^4$ is a compact set, then for all $\xi \in \mathfrak{X}$ and sequences $\xi_n \to \xi$, there exists $N \in \mathbb{N}$ so that for all $n \ge N$, we have 
\[
W^{\xi_n}(x,s;y,t) = W^{\xi}(x,s;y,t),\quad \text{for all }(x,s;y,t) \in K.
\]
 \item {\rm(Additivity)}  For all $\xi \in \mathfrak{X}$ and $p,q,r \in \mathbb{R}^2$, 
    $W^{\xi}(p;q) + W^{\xi}(q;r) = W^{\xi}(p;r)$.   In particular, \\ $W^{\xi}(p;q) = -W^{\xi}(q;p)$ and $W^{\xi}(p;p) = 0$.
    \item {\rm(Monotonicity along a horizontal line)}
     Whenever $\xi_1< \xi_2$ in $\mathfrak{X}$, $x < y$, and $t \in \mathbb{R}$,
    \[
  W^{\xi_1}(x,t;y,t) \le W^{\xi_2}(x,t;y,t).
    \]
    \item \rm{(Divergence to $\pm \infty$)} 
    For all $\xi_1 < \xi_2$ and $t \in \mathbb{R}$,
    \[
\lim_{x \to \pm \infty} W^{\xi_2} (0,0;x,t) -W^{\xi_1}(0,0;x,t) = \pm \infty.
\]
    \item {\rm(Eternal solution)} For 
    all $\xi \in \mathfrak{X}$, $x,y \in \mathbb{R}$, and $s < t$,
    \begin{equation}
    W^{\xi}(x,s;y,t) = \sup_{z \in \mathbb{R}}\{W^{\xi}(x,s;z,s) +
 \mathcal{L}(z,s;y,t)\}.
    \end{equation}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem thm:binomial of arXiv:2411.18155, 'Besov regularity of random wavelet series'] Let $n\in\mathds{N}$, $\rho\in (0,1)$, $\sigma\in (0,\infty)$, and $X\sim \mathrm{Bin}(n,\rho)$ a binomially distributed random variable.

[Lemma lem:poly-regression-learns of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] Fix $\sigma>0$, $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$. 
Let $\mu$ be a distribution over $\mathbb{R}^d \times \{\pm 1\}$. \

If for any target $f\in \cH(k)$, there exists a polynomial $P$ of degree $D_\varepsilon$ such that $\|T_\sigma f - P\|_{L^2(\mu)} \le \varepsilon/4$, 
then there exists a procedure that takes $n= O\big(\varepsilon^{-2}  d^{D_\varepsilon}\log(1/\delta)\big)$ training samples, operates in $\mathrm{poly}(n,d)$ time, and outputs a polynomial threshold classifier $\hath$ such that with probability at least $1-\delta$, 
\begin{align}
\mathbb{P}_{(x,y)\sim\mu}(h(x) \neq y) &\leq \mathrm{opt}_{\sigma,\cH(k)} + \varepsilon.  
\end{align}
title: Lemma lem:poly-regression-learns of arXiv:2512.04371

[Lem 8 of arXiv:2603.28702, 'Distribution of the magnetization of the critical Ising model on sparse random graphs'] Let $C>0$ and $m=m(n)$ be a sequence of positive integers with the same parity as $n$, with $|m|\le Cn^{3/4}$. Then,
$$\E(Z_m)\sim c_{d,n}\cdot\exp\left(-\dfrac{(d-1)(d-2)}{12d^2}\cdot \dfrac{m^4}{n^3}\right),$$
where 
$$c_{d,n}=\dfrac{2^{1/2}\sqrt{d-1}}{\sqrt{n}\sqrt{\pi d}}\cdot(2\cdot\cosh(\beta)^{d/2})^n,$$ 
and
$$\dfrac{\E(Z_m^2)}{\E(Z_m)^2}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\sqrt{\dfrac{d-1}{d-2}}.$$
Moreover, both of these convergences are uniform in $m$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Proposition 50 of arXiv:2609.01114, 'Unbalanced spectral Tur\'an problem for color-critical graphs with prescribed large maximu'] Let $G^{\star}\in\mathfrak U_n(\Delta,\zeta_F;F)$ be an upper-tail extremal graph and put $D=\Delta(G^{\star})$.  If $\left\lceil\frac{p}{p+1}n\right\rceil\le D<\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon^2}{200}\right)n$ and $n-D\ge\kappa_Fn^{s_F}$, then $G^{\star}\cong S_{n,D,p}$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

Let A be a complex m by n matrix of rank r, and let v_1, ..., v_n be an orthonormal eigenbasis of A*A with eigenvalues lambda_1 >= ... >= lambda_n >= 0. Put sigma_i = sqrt(lambda_i). Then sigma_i > 0 exactly for i <= r; the vectors u_i = A v_i / sigma_i (i <= r) are orthonormal and satisfy A v_i = sigma_i u_i and A* u_i = sigma_i v_i; ker A is spanned by v_{r+1}, ..., v_n; and extending u_1, ..., u_r to an orthonormal basis u_1, ..., u_m of C^m gives A = U Sigma V*, where U has columns u_j, V has columns v_j, and Sigma is the m by n matrix with Sigma_ii = sigma_i and zeros elsewhere.

body:
[Lemma 63 (Strong measurability of fixed dyadic blocks) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $H_Q$ and $H_M$ be the separable $L^2$ spaces of fixed input and output
shells.  Every centered dyadic kernel constructed above admits a strongly
measurable representative in
\[
 C\bigl(\Delta_T;\mathcal K(H_Q,H_M)\bigr).
\]
Its Volterraization is strongly measurable with values in
\[
 \mathcal L\bigl(C_TH_Q,\,C_TH_M\cap L_T^1H_M\bigr),
\]
and every finite dyadic sum is strongly measurable and separably valued in
the corresponding finite-block operator topology.

body:
An initial data set $(\Sigma, g, h)$ for the 3+1 Einstein equations is called asymptotically flat of order $\tau > 0$ if there exists a compact set $K \subset \Sigma$ such that $\Sigma \setminus K$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3 \setminus B_R(0)$, and in the corresponding asymptotic coordinates $x$, $g_{ij} - \delta_{ij} = O(|x|^{-\tau})$, $\partial_k g_{ij} = O(|x|^{-\tau-1})$, $h_{ij} = O(|x|^{-\tau-1})$, and $\partial_k h_{ij} = O(|x|^{-\tau-2})$ as $|x| \to \infty$.
\Sigma is a complete connected 3-manifold
g is a Riemannian metric, h is a symmetric (0,2)-tensor
\tau > 0 is the decay rate
title: Asymptotically Flat Cauchy Initial Data

body: [Conjecture conj:Schoen of arXiv:2609.01464, 'Removability of non-isolated singularities for Einstein metrics and RCD spaces'] Suppose that $(M^n, g)$ is an $L^\infty$-Riemannian manifold, and $S\subset M$ is a smooth closed embedded submanifold of codimension at least 3. Suppose that $g$ has non-negative scalar curvature on $M\setminus S$, and $M$ has non-positive Yamabe invariant. Then $g$ extends smoothly to $M$ as a metric with zero Ricci curvature. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Conjecture conj:Schoen of arXiv:2609.01464

body:
[Defn def: height of arXiv:2508.13827, 'Surface sums in two-dimensional large-$N$ lattice Yang--Mills: Cancellations and explicit '] Given a loop $\ell$, we define its \textbf{height} $h_{\ell}:\mathcal{P} \to \mathbb{Z}$ as follows (notice $\ell$ must be contained in $B= [-N,N]^2$ for some $N\in \mathbb{N}$):
    \begin{enumerate}
		\item $h_{\ell}(p)=0$ for $p\in \mathcal{P}^+\cap B^c$.
		\item If for $p\in \mathcal{P}^+$, we have that $h_{\ell}(p) = x$, then we define $h_{\ell}(q)$ for $q\in \mathcal{P}^+$ adjacent to $p$ as follows: If $\ell$ crosses the oriented line from the center of $p$ to the center of $q$ from right to left $n\geq 0$ times and crosses the line from the left to the right $m\geq 0$ times, set $h_{\ell}(q) = x+n-m$.
	\end{enumerate}
    For $p\in\mathcal{P}\setminus \mathcal{P}^+$, we define $h_{\ell}(p) = h_{\ell}(p^{-1})$.
    For a string $s=\{\ell_1,\dots,\ell_n\}$, we define $h_s(p) = \sum_{i\in [n]}h_{\ell_i}(p)$.
title: Defn def: height of arXiv:2508.13827

[Thm 1 of arXiv:2607.03360, 'Smoluchowski-Kramers Approximation Meets Khasminskii Averaging Principles in Nonequilibriu'] Suppose that \assmref{ass:mom-bdd} and \assmref{ass:gd-lip} hold. Let $(x^m,y^\e)$ be the solution of slow-fast stochastic system \eqref{fast-slow}. Suppose that $\la^{-1}\sg$ is independent of the fast variable $y$. Under the scaling $m=\e^2$, as $\e\to 0$, the process $x^m$ converges in probability to $\bar x$, where $\bar x$ is the unique strong solution of the following averaged equation:
\bea
d\bar x_t = \big[(\lbar{\la^{-1}b})(\bar x_t)+ \bar S(\bar x_t) \big]dt + (\la^{-1}\sg)(\bar x_t)dW_t, \quad 
\bar x_0 =x_0,
\eea
with effective coefficients defined in \eqref{bar-b-sg} and \eqref{bar-S}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 1 of arXiv:2607.03360

body:
Fix an integer d>=2 and normalized uniform surface measure sigma on S^(d-1). Let H_l be the real degree-l spherical harmonics, h_l=dim H_l, and Y_(l,1),...,Y_(l,h_l) any orthonormal basis in L2(sigma). Let P_l be the degree-l polynomial orthogonal to lower-degree polynomials for weight (1-t^2)^((d-3)/2) on [-1,1], normalized by P_l(1)=1. Then sum_(j=1)^(h_l) Y_(l,j)(x)Y_(l,j)(y)=h_l P_l(<x,y>). In particular P_l(<x,y>) is a positive semidefinite kernel: for any finite x_i on the sphere and real c_i, sum_(i,j)c_i c_j P_l(<x_i,x_j>)>=0. For a real polynomial u=sum_l a_l P_l, its zonal kernel u(<x,y>) is positive semidefinite if and only if every a_l>=0. The product of two such polynomials again has nonnegative P_l coefficients. If every coefficient through the respective degrees is strictly positive, the product also has every coefficient through its degree strictly positive. Here d=2 uses the normalized Chebyshev polynomials, and d>=3 the Gegenbauer polynomials rescaled to value 1 at 1. Positive semidefinite kernels allow zero quadratic forms; strictly positive coefficients do not mean strict positivity of every finite Gram matrix.
d>=2 integer; real harmonics orthonormal for probability surface measure
P_l(1)=1; fixed dimension throughout
polynomials have finitely many coefficients

Nonnegative coefficients therefore suffice. Conversely, integrate the quadratic form of the continuous zonal kernel against a degree-l spherical harmonic on both variables; its harmonic eigenvalue is a_l/h_l, forcing a_l>=0. Products of Gram kernels are Gram kernels by tensoring feature vectors, hence the polynomial coefficients of the product are nonnegative. Finally the coefficient of P_(i+j) in P_i P_j is positive by their positive leading coefficients. [Lemma lem:geodesic_intersects_loops of arXiv:2609.04140, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ III:\\ uniqueness'] Suppose that we have the same setup as in (cor:conditions_a_b_c of the paper),  so that in particular $R$ and $P$ are as fixed above.  Let $z \in \BD ,  k \in \BN$ be such that $\overline{B_{2^{-k}}(z)} \subseteq \BD$ and $E_{z,k}(\Psi)$ occurs.  Suppose also that the collection of loops in $\overline{\Gamma}$ with height in $\{-\lambda,\lambda\}$ which cross $B_{2^{-k-1}}(z) \setminus \overline{B_{2^{-k-R}}(z)}$ 

is non-empty and that there are at least two loops in $\overline{\Gamma}$ with height in $\{-\lambda,\lambda\}$ which cross $B_{2^{-k-1}}(z) \setminus \overline{B_{2^{-k-R}}(z)}$.  Let $\ell_1,\ell_2$ denote the elements of the above collection (recall that,  since $E_{z,k}(\Psi)$ occurs,  it consists of at most two loops; we use the letters $\ell_1,\ell_2$ rather than $\SCL_1,\SCL_2$ in order to avoid a clash with the chain of loops constructed in (subsec:constructing_chains of the paper)).  Then,  wherever the geodesic $P$ makes a crossing of $B_{2^{-k-1}}(z) \setminus \overline{B_{2^{-k-R}}(z)}$ (in particular,  whenever it makes a crossing of the larger annulus $B_{2^{-k}}(z) \setminus \overline{B_{2^{-k-R}}(z)}$),  the portion of $P$ which makes that crossing must intersect either $\ell_1$ or $\ell_2$.  More generally,  the same conclusion holds whenever $P$ crosses one of the connected components $U_j$ of the complement in $B_{2^{-k-1}}(z) \setminus \overline{B_{2^{-k-R}}(z)}$ of the crossings of that annulus made by loops in $\overline{\Gamma}$ with height in $\{-\lambda,\lambda\}$ together with the interiors of the excursions into it made by such loops (we use the notation of (prop:good_annulus_macroscopic_scale of the paper)),  between the two marked boundary arcs $I_j^3$ and $I_j^4$ of $\partial U_j$.

[Thm 3 of arXiv:2605.26669, '2605.26669'] Let $Y^1_0$ and $Y^2_0$ be non-negative integers such that $T_0:=Y^1_0+Y^2_0>0$. For any positive integers $a,b,c$ and any $p\in (0,1)$,
the total number of balls  after $n$ draws, denoted as $T_n$, satisfies
$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \frac{T_n}{n}= (a+b)p+c(1-p).
$$
Moreover, we have the convergence for the conditional expectation:
$$
\ee\left[\left(\frac{n+1}{T_{n+1}} \Delta M_{n+1}\right)^2\Bigg|\FF_{n} \right]\rightarrow \frac{p(a-b)^2+c^2(1-p)}{4\big((a+b)p+c(1-p)\big)^2}\ \ \ \ a.s.,
$$
where $\Delta M_{n+1}$ is defined in (\ref{M}). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Conjecture of arXiv:2507.01236, 'Disintegration theorem for multifunctions, \\ with applications to empirical Wasserstein d'] Let $\mathfrak{X}$ be any compact, connected, $D$-dimensional Riemannian manifold, $d$ its geodesic distance, and $\mu$ any probability measure that is absolutely continuous with respect to the volume measure, with density $f$ satisfying $0<c\leq f(x)\leq C<\infty$ for all $x\in\mathfrak{X}$. Then for any $\alpha\in(0,\infty)$, the space $(\mathfrak{X},d,\mu)$ is asymptotically disintegrable with rate $\left( O(n^{-\alpha}),O\!\left( \left( \frac{\ln n}{n} \right)^{1 / \max\{2,D\}} \right) \right)$. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

[Lemma Order of exponent when inducing graph is a tree of arXiv:2411.11341, 'Ultra high order cumulants and quantitative CLT for polynomials in Random Matrices'] Let $G_1,\dots,G_n$ be unoriented graphs and let $T=(V_T,E_T,\allowbreak\{V(e)\}_{e\in E_T})$ be a graph of the graphs $G_i$. Let $G=\cup_{i=1}^n G_i$ be the graph consisting of the union of the graphs $G_i$. If $T$ is a tree, then
$$t(G^T) = \sum_{i=1}^n t(G_i)-n+1.$$

[Proposition prop: affine of arXiv:2411.04238, 'Holomorphic jump-diffusions'] Let $X=(X_t)_{t\in[0,T]}$ be an affine process on $S\subseteq \mathbb R$.  Suppose that for each $x\in S$, $K(x,d\xi)=\nu_0(d\xi)+x\nu_1(d\xi)$ for some signed measure $\nu_0,\nu_1$ such that both $|\nu_0|$ and $|\nu_1|$ have bounded support.       Set
      \begin{align*}
    \mathcal V&:=\{h\in H(\mathbb C)\colon h,h',h''\text{ are bounded on }\mathbb R\},\\
    \mathcal V^*&:=\{\mathbf{u}\in \mathcal{S}^* \colon h_\mathbf{u}=h,  \ h\in \mathcal{V}\}.
\end{align*}
The following conditions hold true.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is an $S$-valued $\mathcal V$-holomorphic process.
    \item The process $N^h$ given in equation (equation eq:localmart of the paper) is a true martingale for each $h\in \mathcal V$.
    \item 
    Fix $\mathbf{u}\in \mathcal V^*$. Assume that $h_\mathbf{u}(x)=\int_{-\tau}^\tau \exp((\varepsilon+iu)x)g(u) du$ for some $g:[-\tau,\tau]\to \mathbb R$ with $\int_{-\tau}^\tau |g(u)|du<\infty$, $\varepsilon,\tau\in[0,\infty)$ and 
 $$\mathbb E[\exp((\varepsilon+iu)X_t)|X_0=x]=\exp(\phi(t,\varepsilon+iu)+\psi(t,\varepsilon+iu)x),$$
 for all $u\in [-\tau,\tau]$ and $t\in [0,T]$. Then there exists a $\mathcal{V}^*$-valued solution $(\mathbf{c}(t))_{t\in[0,T]}$ of (equation eq: ODE pointwise of the paper) with initial condition $\mathbf{u}$ which satisfies condition~(moment formula ii of the paper) and~(moment formula iii of the paper) of Theorem~(th: moment formula holomorphic of the paper). 
 
 In particular, the holomorphic formula holds true:
    \begin{align*}
    \mathbb E[h_\mathbf{u}(X_T)]=h_{\mathbf{c}(T)}(x_0).
\end{align*}

\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition D:asy-Feller of arXiv:2412.03521, 'On ergodic properties of stochastic PDEs'] A Markov transition semigroup $P_t$ on a Polish space $\mathcal{X}$ is called
  asymptotically strong Feller at $x$ if there exists a totally separating
  system of pseudo-metrics $\left\{d_n; n\ge1\right\}$ for $\mathcal{X}$ and a
  sequence $\left\{t_n; n\ge 1\right\}$ with $t_n>0$ such that
  \begin{align*}
    \liminf_{U\in \mathcal{U}_x}\: \limsup_{n\to\infty}\: \sup_{y\in U}\Norm{P_{t_n}(x,\cdot)-P_{t_n}(y,\cdot)}_{d_n}=0,
  \end{align*}
  where $\mathcal{U}_x$ is the collection of all open sets containing $x$. It is
  called asymptotically strong Feller if this property holds at every $x \in
  \mathcal{X}$.
title: Definition D:asy-Feller of arXiv:2412.03521

[Definition def:subdivided-graph of arXiv:2411.06195, 'Restrictions of some reinforced processes to subgraphs'] For $r\in{\mathbb N}_0$, the \emph{$2^r$-subdivision}
$G_r=(\Lambda_r,E_r)$ of $G$ is obtained by replacing every edge by a series
of $2^r$ edges as follows.
\begin{itemize}
\item $\Lambda_r$ is obtained from $\Lambda$ by adding $2^r-1$ new vertices $v_{e,2^{-r}j}$,
  $j=1,\ldots,2^r-1$ for
  any edge $e\in E$. We say that these new vertices are located on the edge $e$. 
  In particular, $\Lambda\subseteq \Lambda_r$. 
\item Every edge $e\in E$ is replaced by a series of $2^r$ edges $e_{1,r},\ldots,e_{2^r,r}$ as follows.
  For bookkeeping purposes only, we endow $e$ with a direction, and 
  call $v_{e,0}$ and $v_{e,1}$ the two vertices it consists of. Then, $e$ is
  replaced by the new edges $e_{j,r}=\{v_{e,2^{-r}(j-1)},v_{e,2^{-r}j}\}$, $1\le j\le 2^r$,
  which we view as being located on the edge $e$. Thus, 
  $E_r=\{e_{j,r}:e\in E, 1\le j\le 2^r\}$.
\end{itemize}
Note that $\Lambda_0=\Lambda$ and $\Lambda_r\subseteq\Lambda_{r+1}$. 
For technical convenience, we introduce also the set of
direct self-loops $\Delta_r:=\{\{i,i\}:i\in\Lambda_r\}$.

[Corollary cor:iid of arXiv:2411.07878, 'Bernstein-type and Bennett-type inequalities for unbounded matrix martingales'] Let $\mathbf{X}_1, \dots, \mathbf{X}_n \in \mathbb{H}(d)$ be i.i.d.\ random matrices and 
    \[
    \E \mathbf{X}_1 \preccurlyeq \bm{0},\quad 
    \lambda_{\max}(\E \mathbf{X}^2_1) \le \sigma^2,\quad
    \norm*{\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf{X}_1)_+}_{\psi_{\alpha}} \le K,\quad
    z \coloneqq \lr{4 \hspace{0.2em}\underline{\log}\hspace{0.2em} \frac{e K}{\sigma}}^{1/\alpha} .

    Then, with probability at least $1 - d e^{-\mathrm{x}}$,
    \[
    \lambda_{\max}\lr{\frac{1}{n} \sum_i \mathbf{X}_i}

    \]

[Lemma lem:rep-detail of arXiv:2605.03703, 'Scaling Limits of Bivariate Nearly-Unstable Hawkes Processes and Applications to Rough Vol'] Let $M^{T,i}_t=N^{T,i}_t-\int_0^t\lambda^{T,i}_s\,ds$ be the compensated counting
martingales. Then, with $\psi_T^i=\sum_{k\ge1}(a_T^i\phi^i)^{*k}$ and
$\Psi_T^{12}=(\delta_0+\psi_T^1)*(\delta_0+\psi_T^2)*\phi_T^{12}$,
\begin{align*}
\lambda^{T,1}_t&=\mu_T^1\Bigl(1+\int_0^t\psi_T^1(u)\,du\Bigr)+\int_0^t\psi_T^1(t-s)\,dM^{T,1}_s,\\
\lambda^{T,2}_t&=\mathbb{E}[\lambda^{T,2}_t]+\int_0^t\psi_T^2(t-s)\,dM^{T,2}_s+\int_0^t\Psi_T^{12}(t-s)\,dM^{T,1}_s,
\end{align*}
and $\langle M^{T,1},M^{T,2}\rangle\equiv0$. In particular
$\mathbb{E}[\lambda^{T,1}_t]=\mu_T^1(1+\int_0^t\psi_T^1)$.

[Defi Hecke algebra of arXiv:2412.05999, 'Non-Archimedean GUE corners and Hecke modules'] Let $L(G,K)$ (resp. $L(G^+,K)$) denote the space of all complex-valued continuous functions of compact support on $G$ (resp. $G^+$) which are bivariant with respect to $K$, i.e., such that $f(k_1xk_2)=f(x)$ for all $x\in G$ (resp. $G^+$) and $k_1,k_2\in K$. We define a multiplication on $L(G,K)$ as follows: for $f,g\in L(G,K)$,
$$(f*g)(x)=\int_Gf(xy^{-1})g(y)dy$$
where $dx$ is the unique Haar measure on $G$ such that $K$ has measure $1$. This product is associative and commutative, which makes $L(G^+,K)$ a subring of $L(G,K)$. Also, let $H(G,K)$ (resp. $H(G^+,K)$) denote the subspace of $L(G,K)$ (resp. $L(G^+,K)$) consisting of functions with integer values, which shall be called the \emph{Hecke ring} of $G$ (resp. $G^+$).
title: Defi Hecke algebra of arXiv:2412.05999

[Lemma 17 of arXiv:2506.15159, 'Conditional central limit theorems for exponential random graphs'] Denote the edge set of $H_l$, $1\leq l \leq m$, by $k_{l_1},\dots, k_{l_{e_l}}$.
    Denote by $s(H_l\backslash k_{l_j})$ and $t(H_l\backslash k_{l_j})$ the numbers of two stars and triangles in graph $H_l\backslash k_{l_j}$, respectively. We have $|\widetilde{p}-p-c^* n^{-1}|\leq C n^{-3/2}$ with
\begin{align*}
       c^*=\frac{p(1-p)}{1-\varphi^{\prime}(p)}&\bigg[\sum_{l=1}^m\beta_l\sum_{j=1}^{e_l}\left(4s(H_l\backslash k_{l_j})p^{e_l-3}\frac{q^2\sum_{r=2}^m\beta_rs_rp^{e_r}}{1-2\sum_{r=2}^m\beta_rs_rp^{e_r-1}q}\right.\\
       &\left.\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad+12t(H_l\backslash k_{l_j})p^{e_l-4}q^3\sum_{r=2}^m\beta_rs_rp^{e_r}\right)\\
        &+(1-2p)\left( \frac{8(\sum_{l=2}^m \beta_ls_l p^{e_l-2})^2pq}{(1-2\sum_{l=2}^m\beta_ls_lp^{e_l-1}q)}+36\big(\sum_{l=2}^m \beta_lt_l p^{e_l-2}\big)^2q^2\right)\\
        &-\sum_{l=2}^m\beta_le_lp^{e_l-1}\left(v_l-2\right)\left(v_l-3\right)\bigg].
    \end{align*}
title: Lemma 17 of arXiv:2506.15159

body:
[Lem 107 (spatial smoothing of domain constraint) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $\sV^N$ and $\sU^N$ be the spatially smoothed quantities from Definition~\ref{d:sp.smooth}. Then, analogously to \eqref{e:domain.plus.coarse}, with high probability we have
	\[
	\svvv^N(t,y)
	=\frac{\sV^N(t,y)}{p^N(t)}
	\ge
	\frac{\sU^N(t,y)^2}{p^N(t)
		\cdot  \srrr^N(t,y)}
	-\frac{\eta^2}{2}
	\ge 
	\frac{\sU^N(t,y)^2}{p^N(t)
		\cdot  t (p^N)'(t)}
	-\frac{\eta^2}{2}
	=\suuu^N(t,y)^2
	-\frac{\eta^2}{2}
	\]
for all $(t,y) \in[q_0,1]\times\R$.

\begin{proof}
We use the abbreviations introduced above. In particular, recall from Definition~\ref{d:disc.rescaled.coeffs} that we can regard $V$ as a function of $(t,\vy)$ for $\vy\in\R^3$. 
Using 
\eqref{e:discrete.ratio.occ.V}, we can rewrite
	\[
	\rho_{V,t}*\sphi(\vy)
	= \int_{\R^3} \sphi(\vy-\vx) V(t,\vx)\,\varrho_t(d\vx)\,.
	\]
It follows that we can express 
$\sV(t,y)\equiv 
\sE_{t,y} V(t,\xxx)$ where $\sE_{t,y}$ 
refers to expectation with respect to the law of $(\vy,\xxx)\sim\tilde{\bP}_{t,y}$ defined by
	\beq
	\tilde{\bP}_{t,y}(d\vy\,d\vx)
	= \frac{ 
		\varrho_t*\sphi(\vy)}
		{\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}
		(y)}
		\cdot 
		\frac{\sphi(\vy-\vx)\,
		\varrho_t(d\vx)}
		{\varrho_t*\sphi(\vy)} \, d\vy
	\eeq
for $\vx\in\R^3$ and $\vy\in H(y)$ where
	\beq
	H(y)
	\equiv \bigg\{\vy\in\R^3 : (\vI,\vy)=y\bigg\}\,.\eeq
Here $H(y)$ is equipped with the Hausdorff measure inherited from Lebesgue measure on $\R^3$, and in \eqref{e:tilde.bP} $d\vy$ denotes integration with respect to this measure. Similarly, $\sU(t,y) = \sE_{t,y} U(t,\xxx)$ and $\srrr(t,y)=\sE_{t,y} \rrr(t,\xxx)$. One can check that the function
	\[
	(u,r) \mapsto \begin{cases}
	 \frac{u^2}{r} & r>0\,,\\
	0 & u=r=0
	 \end{cases}
	\]
is convex on the domain $\{u\in\R,r>0\}  \cup\{u=r=0\}$, so Jensen's inequality gives
	\[
	\frac{\sV(t,y)}{p(t)}
	= \frac{\sE_{t,y} V(t,\xxx)}{p(t)}
	\stackrel{\eqref{e:domain.plus.rewrittten}}{\ge}
	\sE_{t,y} \bigg[
		\frac{U(t,\xxx)^2}{p(t) 
		\cdot \rrr(t,\xxx)}
		- \frac{\eta^2}{2}\bigg]
	\ge 
	\frac{\sU(t,y)^2}{p(t) 
	\cdot  \srrr(t,y)}
		- \frac{\eta^2}{2}\,,
	\]
as claimed.

Let Omega in R^n be bounded and open with C^2 boundary, and let Lu = -sum D_i(a^{ij} D_j u) + sum b^i D_i u + c u with a^{ij} = a^{ji} in C^1(closure of Omega), b^i, c in L^infinity(Omega), and uniform ellipticity sum a^{ij}(x) xi_i xi_j >= lambda |xi|^2 with lambda > 0. Let f in L^2(Omega) and let u in H^1_0(Omega) be a weak solution of Lu = f. Then u is in H^2(Omega), Lu = f holds almost everywhere (u is a strong solution), and ||u||_{H^2(Omega)} <= C ( ||f||_{L^2(Omega)} + ||u||_{L^2(Omega)} ) with C depending only on Omega and the coefficients; if the Dirichlet problem is uniquely solvable (for instance b = 0 and c >= 0), the term ||u||_{L^2} may be dropped. Interior H^2 regularity (u in H^2_loc with the corresponding estimate on compactly contained subsets) needs only a^{ij} in C^1(Omega) and no boundary hypothesis. The C^2 boundary hypothesis can be relaxed to C^{1,1}, and for L = -Laplacian to convexity of Omega, but it cannot be dropped: on a domain with a reentrant corner the conclusion is false.
Omega bounded open in R^n with C^2 (or C^{1,1}) boundary for the global statement
a^{ij} = a^{ji} in C^1(closure of Omega) (Lipschitz is enough); b, c in L^infinity
uniform ellipticity with lambda > 0
f in L^2(Omega) and u in H^1_0(Omega) a weak solution

[Theorem 2 (Leading eigenvalue) of arXiv:2606.20816, 'Spectral Properties of Dense Barab\'asi--Albert Graphs'] Let $M$ be the adjacency matrix of the Barab\'asi--Albert multigraph with $m = c n$ and fixed rational $c \in \left(0, \frac12\right)$ such that $n$ and $m$ are integers. Then the largest eigenvalue of the scaled adjacency matrix satisfies
\[
\lambda_{\max} \left(\frac{M}{\sqrt{m}}\right)
\ = \
\frac{\alpha \left(c\right)}{\sqrt{c}} \sqrt{n}
+
o_{\P} \left(\sqrt n\right),
\qquad n \to \infty,
\]
with
\[
\alpha \left(c\right)
\ = \
c + \frac{c}{2} \log \frac{2 - c}{c}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 14 (Maximal Solution) of arXiv:2606.07290, 'Boundary behaviour of the Volterra square-root process'] The mapping $u \longmapsto V_u(t)$ is nondecreasing for each $t > 0$. Define the maximal solution
    \[
        V_{\infty}(t) := \sup_{ u \geq 0} V_u(t).
    \]
    Then the following assertions hold:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] If $K$ is regularly varying of the form \eqref{eq: regularly varying} where $\alpha \in (1/2,1)$ and $\ell$ is slowly varying at zero, then for each $\eta \in (0,1)$ there exists $t_0 > 0$ such that
        \[
            V_{\infty}(t) \leq (1+\eta)\frac{2C_{\alpha}}{\sigma^2}\frac{t^{-\alpha}}{\ell(t)}, \qquad t \in (0,t_0),
        \]
        where the constant is given by
        \[
        C_{\alpha} = \frac{4^{\alpha}\sqrt{\pi}}{|\Gamma\left(\frac{1}{2} - \alpha\right)|} = \frac{\Gamma(1-\alpha)}{|\Gamma(1-2\alpha)|}.
        \]
        Moreover, the function $V_{\infty}$ satisfies the fractional Riccati differential equation
        \begin{equation} 
            (D_LV_{\infty})(t) = \beta V_{\infty}(t) - \frac{\sigma^2}{2}V_{\infty}(t)^2, \qquad t > 0.
        \end{equation}
        \item[(b)] For the pure fractional kernel $K(t) = \frac{t^{\alpha-1}}{\Gamma(\alpha)}$, we obtain 
        \[
            V_{\infty}(t) \leq \frac{2C_{\alpha}}{\sigma^2} t^{-\alpha} + \mathbbm{1}_{\beta > 0} \frac{2\beta}{\sigma^2}, \qquad t > 0.
        \]
        with equality when $\beta = 0$.
    \end{enumerate}

[Theorem 17 of arXiv:2604.13819, 'Convolution, cumulants and infinitesimal generators in the formal power series ring'] Let $\mathfrak{Q}=\{Q_s\}_{s\ge 0} \subset \mathcal{A}_r^{(t)}$ be a $\boxplus^t$-semigroup. Assume that there exists the following limit:
$$
\eta_\mathfrak{Q}(z)\coloneqq \lim_{s\to 0^+} \frac{\Phi_t(Q_s)(z)-1}{s}, \quad \text{for each } z\in \mathbb{D}_r.
$$
Then we have
$$
\mathcal{L}_r^{(t)}[\mathfrak{Q}] = \Phi_t^{\langle-1\rangle} \circ \mathbf{M}_{\eta_\mathfrak{Q}(z)} \circ \Phi_t
$$
and its domain is written by
$$
{\rm Dom}\big(\mathcal{L}_r^{(t)}[\mathfrak{Q}] \bigr)=\left\{ A\in \mathcal{A}_{r}^{(t)} : \eta_\mathfrak{Q}(\cdot) \Phi_t(A)\in \mathcal{A}_r\right\},
$$
where $\mathbf{M}_{c(z)}$ is the multiplication operator by $c(z)$, that is, $\bigl(\mathbf{M}_{c(z)} A\bigr)(z)\coloneqq  c(z)A(z)$.
title: Theorem 17 of arXiv:2604.13819

body:
[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The orthonormal polynomials for $L^2[-1,1]$, subject to
$$\int_{-1}^1P_k(x)P_l(x)\,dx=\delta_{kl}$$
and called Legendre polynomials, satisfy the following differential equation,
$$(1-x^2)P_k''(x)-2xP_k'(x)+k(k+1)P_k(x)=0$$
which is the Legendre equation from physics. Moreover, we have the formula
$$(k+1)P_{k+1}(x)=(2k+1)xP_k(x)-kP_{k-1}(x)$$
called Bonnet recurrence formula, as well as the formula
$$P_k(x)=\frac{1}{2^kk!}\cdot\frac{d^k}{dx^k}\left(1-x^2\right)^k$$
called Rodrigues formula for the Legendre polynomials.

[Proposition 2 (Spherical tangent-indicatrix characterization) of arXiv:2609.00673, '2609.00673'] Let \(T_0,\ldots,T_{n-1}\in S^2\) be the unit edge tangents of a polygon.
Then the polygon is a discrete general helix if and only if its tangent
indicatrix is contained in the intersection
\[
S^2\cap\{X\in\mathbb R^3:X\cdot U=c\}
\]
for some unit vector \(U\) and some \(c\in[-1,1]\).  If \(0<|c|<1\),
this intersection is a small circle on \(S^2\); if \(c=0\), it is a
great circle; and if $|c|=1$, it consists of the single point $\{cU\}$.  Under the standing assumptions $n\ge3$ and $0<\theta_i<\pi$, the last case cannot occur.

[Theorem 2 (Equality characterization) of arXiv:2607.10769, '\fontsize{14}{17}\selectfont\bfseries Sharp Poincar\'e interpolation along Wasserstein geo'] Fix $t\in(0,1)$ and denote $m_i=\int x\,\d\mu_i$. Then
\[
 C_P(\mu_t)
 =\left(\frac{1-t}{\sqrt{\kappa_0}}
        +\frac{t}{\sqrt{\kappa_1}}\right)^2
\]
if and only if there exists a unit
vector $e\in\R^n$ such that, under the orthogonal decomposition
$\R^n=\R e\oplus e^\perp$, the coordinate map
$\mathcal C_e(x)=(e\cdot x,P_{e^\perp}x)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 (\mathcal C_e)_\#\mu_i
 =N\!\left(\ip{e}{m_i},\kappa_i^{-1}\right)\otimes\nu_i, \qquad \nu_i\in\mathcal P(e^\perp)
 \qquad i=0,1.
\end{equation}
In this case the optimal transport splits along the same decomposition and
\[
 C_P(\mu_s)
 =\left(\frac{1-s}{\sqrt{\kappa_0}}
        +\frac{s}{\sqrt{\kappa_1}}\right)^2,
 \qquad\text{for every }s\in[0,1].
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm Thm_strict_monotonicity of arXiv:2606.22183, 'Expected loss of quasi-arithmetic means of exchangeable random variables'] Let $I\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a nonempty open interval, $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ be a continuous and strictly increasing function,
 and $(\xi_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of exchangeable random variables with values in $I$ such that
 $\mathbb{D}^2(f(\xi_1))\in(0,\infty)$.
Let $\mu\in\mathbb{R}_+$ and $L:I\to\mathbb{R}$ be a function such that the function $L\circ f^{-1}: f(I)\to\mathbb{R}$ is strongly convex with modulus $\mu$
 and $\operatorname{\mathbb{E}}(\vert L(\xi_1)\vert)<\infty$.
Then, for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, we have that $\operatorname{\mathbb{E}}\big(L\big( \mathscr{A}_n^{f}(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n) \big)\big)\in[-\infty,\infty)$ and the sequence
\[
  \bigg(\operatorname{\mathbb{E}}\big(L\big( \mathscr{A}_n^{f}(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n) \big)\big)-\frac{\mu(1-\varrho)}{n}\mathbb{D}^2(f(\xi_1))\bigg)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}
\]
is decreasing, where
 \[
   \varrho:=\frac{\operatorname{Cov}(f(\xi_1),f(\xi_2))}{\sqrt{ \mathbb{D}^2(f(\xi_1)) \mathbb{D}^2(f(\xi_2)) } }
           = \operatorname{Corr}(f(\xi_1),f(\xi_2)).
 \]

\(B \subseteq M\) be closed of positive capacity, let

every \(x \in M\) and every \(t \geq 0\),

\[\mathbb{P}_{x}\left( \tau_{B} > t \right) \geq \varphi_{B}(x)\, e^{- \lambda_{B}t}.\]

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2607.12384, '2607.12384'] Assume that $\sigma$ is Lipschitz continuous with Lipschitz
		constant \(L\). Then, for every $p\geq 2, T>0$
	and every $(t,x)\in [0,T]\times\mathbb R$, the mild solution
	$u(t,x)$ of \eqref{eq:main equation} belongs to $\mathbb D^{1,p}$. 
    
    Moreover, there exists a bounded predictable random field
		\[
		\Sigma=\{\Sigma(r,z):(r,z)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb R\},
		\qquad |\Sigma(r,z)|\le L,
		\quad
		\mathbb P\otimes dr\otimes dz\text{-a.e.},
		\]
		such that, for every \((t,x)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb R\), there exists a
		version of \(Du(t,x)\) satisfying, for almost every
		\((s,y)\in[0,t)\times\mathbb R\), \(\mathbb P\)-a.s.,
		\begin{equation}
			\begin{aligned}
				D_{s,y}u(t,x)
				&=
				G_{t-s}(x-y)\sigma(u(s,y))\\
				&\quad+
				\int_s^t\int_{\mathbb R}
				G_{t-r}(x-z)\Sigma(r,z)
				D_{s,y}u(r,z)\,W(dr,dz).
			\end{aligned}
		\end{equation}
        
		Moreover,
\(
D_{s,y}u(t,x)=0
\) for almost every \((s,y)\in(t,T]\times\mathbb R\),
\(\mathbb P\)-a.s. If, in addition, \(\sigma\in C^1(\mathbb R)\), then one may take
		\(\Sigma(r,z)=\sigma'(u(r,z))\).

[Proposition 27 (Maximum principle for particle-production Navier--Stokes flows) of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] Fix a Navier--Stokes triple $(\mathscr F,\chi,\mathscr B)$ that is admissible (\autoref{def-pot-admissible-triple}) and torus-adapted (\autoref{def-NS-torus-adapted}).
Let $(\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)$ be a sufficiently regular particle-production Einstein--Navier--Stokes areal flow $(\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)$ on $[t_0,t_1]\times\Tbb^3$.
If the density $\mu>0$ is positive throughout, in terms of the characteristic flow~\eqref{eq:section-8-characteristics} of $\velo$, one has
\bel{eq:pot-characteristic-contraction}
\aligned
\Gammaunpar_\chi\bigl(t,X(t;t_0,x)\bigr)&=\exp\left(-\int_{t_0}^t\frac{\mathfrak d_{\mathscr B}^{\rm ar}}{\rho_\chi}\bigl(r,X(r;t_0,x)\bigr)\,dr\right)\Gammaunpar_\chi(t_0,x),\\
\Gammazero\bigl(t,X(t;t_0,x)\bigr)&=\Gammazero(t_0,x),
\endaligned
\ee
hence the ranges of $\Gammaunpar_\chi(t,\cdot)$ and $\Gammazero(t,\cdot)$ obey
\bel{eq:pot-radial-hull}
\operatorname{Ran}\Gammaunpar_\chi(t,\cdot)\subset\left\{\lambda z\middle|\ 0\leq\lambda\leq1,\ z\in\operatorname{Ran}\Gammaunpar_\chi(t_0,\cdot)\right\},\qquad \operatorname{Ran}\Gammazero(t,\cdot)=\operatorname{Ran}\Gammazero(t_0,\cdot).
\ee
For flows including the vacuum $\mu=0$, a weaker statement holds: the convex hull of $\{0\}$ and the range of~$\Gammaunpar$ is contained in the same convex hull at initial time.

[Definition 5 ($s$-valid subsequences) of arXiv:2605.13107, 'Discrepancy and Fisher information'] Fix a sign sequence $\e = (\e_1, \ldots, \e_n) \in \{-1,1\}^n$ and an integer \(s\in [-T,T] \). We say that an index subsequence $1 \le i_1 < \cdots < i_m \le n$ is {\em \(s\)-valid} if  
	\[
	\max_{1\le k\le m}\left| s + 
	\sum_{r=1}^k \e_{i_r}
	\right|\le T .
	\]
	Denote by $\ell(\e,s)$ be the maximum length of an $s$-valid index subsequence.

[Lemma lem:appendix-fredholm-dual-weight of arXiv:2608.30904, 'Entire monotone solutions of the anisotropic Allen--Cahn equation in dimension 5'] Assume that
\[
  -\gamma\neq\beta_j^\pm
\]
for every $j$. Then
\begin{equation}
  J_{F,\Gamma}:C_\gamma^{2,\alpha}(\Gamma)
  \longrightarrow C_{\gamma+2}^{0,\alpha}(\Gamma)
  
\end{equation}
is Fredholm. If, in addition,
\[
  -(1-\gamma)=\gamma-1\neq\beta_j^\pm
\]
for every $j$, then the unweighted pairing
\[
  (f,v)\longmapsto\int_\Gamma fv\,d\mathcal H^3
\]
induces a canonical isomorphism
\begin{equation}
  \left(
    \operatorname{coker}
    \bigl(J_{F,\Gamma}\big|_{C_\gamma^{2,\alpha}}\bigr)
  \right)^*
  \simeq
  \ker\bigl(J_{F,\Gamma}\big|_{C_{1-\gamma}^{2,\alpha}}\bigr).
  
\end{equation}
Moreover, there are a compact set $K\Subset\Gamma$ and a constant $C$ such
that
\begin{equation}
  \|u\|_{C_\gamma^{2,\alpha}(\Gamma)}
  \leq C\left(
    \|J_{F,\Gamma}u\|_{C_{\gamma+2}^{0,\alpha}(\Gamma)}
    +\|u\|_{C^0(K)}
  \right).
  
\end{equation}

body:
[Proposition 9 (Feller boundary classification) of arXiv:2607.12365, 'Bernoulli--Doob representation, asymptotic limits and boundary behavior of bounded homogen'] Consider $dZ_t=\sigma(Z_t)\,dW_t$ on $[a,b]$ with $Z_0=z\in(a,b)$,
$\sigma\in C^2([a,b])$, $\sigma>0$ on $(a,b)$,
$\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=0$. Since the drift is zero, the diffusion is
in natural scale $s(x)=x$ with speed measure density
$m(x)=2/\sigma^2(x)$. Fix an interior reference point $z\in(a,b)$
and define
\[
N_a := \int_a^z(z-x)\sigma^{-2}(x)\,dx\,,\qquad
\Sigma_a := \int_a^z(x-a)\sigma^{-2}(x)\,dx\,,
\]
and analogously $N_b$, $\Sigma_b$ at the right boundary $b$. The
boundary type is determined by the following table.
\[
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.4}
\begin{array}{c|c|l}
N_a & \Sigma_a & \text{Boundary type of }a \\ \hline
<\infty & <\infty & \text{Regular: attainable and startable} \\
<\infty & =\infty & \text{Exit: attainable, not startable} \\
=\infty & <\infty & \text{Entrance: not attainable, startable} \\
=\infty & =\infty & \text{Natural: not attainable, not startable}
\end{array}
\]
Here $N_a<\infty$ means $\Pr_x(\tau_a<\infty)>0$ for all
$x\in(a,b)$; $N_a=\infty$ means $\tau_a=\infty$ a.s.
$\Sigma_a<\infty$ means $a$ is an admissible starting point in the
diffusion sense; $\Sigma_a=\infty$ means it is not. The same table
applies to the right boundary $b$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Feller boundary classification

body:
[Lemma lem:upper-box-to-requests of arXiv:2608.29561, 'Ball codes: A coding characterization of Hausdorff and packing dimensions'] Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and bounded, and let \(q>0\) satisfy
\[
\overline{\dim}_{\mathrm B}(F)<q.
\]
For every \(\eta>0\), there are \(r_0\in\omega\), closed balls
\(B_{r,i}\ (r\ge r_0, i<m_r)\), and natural numbers
\(\ell_{r,i}\ (r\ge r_0, i<m_r)\) such that, for every \(r\ge r_0\),
\[
F\subseteq\bigcup_{i<m_r}B_{r,i},
\qquad
\diam(B_{r,i})\le2^{-r},
\]
and, in total,
\[
\sum_{r\ge r_0}\sum_{i<m_r}2^{-\ell_{r,i}}<\eta,
\]
and
\[
\ell_{r,i}\le qr+2\log_2(r+1)+O(1)
\]
where the constant in \(O(1)\) may depend on \(F,q,\eta\), but not on
\(r\) or \(i\).  Thus a bounded set of upper box-counting dimension \(<q\) admits
descriptions at \emph{every sufficiently large scale} with rate \(q\), up to a
logarithmic overhead, and with arbitrarily small total Kraft weight.

Consider a finite simple graph with an FK(p,q) law, 0<p<1 and q>=1, with no imposed identification of vertices outside a chosen subgraph H. Suppose H has at least two distinct boundary vertices and boundary vertex v has k incident edges outside H. If xi is the partition of the boundary induced by open paths using only exterior edges, then P(xi is not the one-block wired partition)>=(1-p)^k. In a family of maximum degree D this is at least (1-p)^D>0. Therefore uniqueness of a giant component alone cannot justify an assertion that every fixed boundary vertex is wired together with probability tending to one.

body:
[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2609.02785, 'Characterization of Stanley-Reisner varieties by their automorphism group'] Let $\Delta$ be a simplicial complex on $[n]$ and let $\partial\neq0$ be a $\ZZ^n$-homogeneous
derivation of $\KK[\Delta]$ of degree $\alpha\in\ZZ^n$. Define $c_1,\dots,c_n\in\KK$ by
$\partial(\overline{x}_j)=c_j\,\overline{\mathbf{x}}^{\mathbf{e}_j+\alpha}$, with the
normalisation $c_j:=0$ when $\mathbf{e}_j+\alpha\notin\Lambda$, and put
$p:=\sum_{j}c_j\,e_j^*\in N_\KK$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
\item $\alpha\in\ZZ^n_{\geq0}\cup\mathcal{N}$, where
$\mathcal{N}:=\{\beta-\mathbf{e}_i\ :\ i\in[n],\ \beta\in\ZZ^n_{\geq0},\ \beta_i=0\}$;
\item $\partial=\partial_{\alpha,p}$, that is,
$\partial(\overline{\mathbf{x}}^a)=p(a)\,\overline{\mathbf{x}}^{a+\alpha}$ for every $a\in\Lambda$;
\item if $\alpha=\beta-\mathbf{e}_i$ with $\beta\in\ZZ^n_{\geq0}$ and $\beta_i=0$,
then $p\in\KK^{*}\!\cdot e_i^*$, so that
$\partial=\lambda\,\overline{\mathbf{x}}^{\beta}\,\partial/\partial\overline{x}_i$ for some
$\lambda\in\KK^{*}$.
\end{enumerate}

[Definition of arXiv:2510.13659, 'On the energy image density conjecture of Bouleau and Hirsch'] We say that a Borel function $g: \mathbb{R}^n \to [0,\infty]$ is an \emph{upper gradient} of $f: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ if 
		\[
		{\left\vert\kern-0.25ex f(\gamma(a)) - f(\gamma(b)) \kern-0.25ex\right\vert} \le \int_\gamma g\,ds,
		\]
		for all rectifiable curves $\gamma:[a,b] \to \mathbb{R}^n$.

[Theorem 6 (Wendel's formula: Probabilistic version) of arXiv:2608.16752, 'Absorption Probabilities for Random Convex Hulls: Distribution-Freeness via the Wall-Cross'] Let $\xi_1, \dots, \xi_n$ be random vectors in $\R^d$ whose joint distribution is invariant under sign flips, that is,
$$
(\xi_1, \dots, \xi_n) \stackrel{d}{=} (\eps_1 \xi_1, \dots, \eps_n \xi_n)
\qquad \text{for every } \eps \in \{\pm 1\}^n.
$$
Suppose additionally that the configuration $X := (\xi_1 \,|\, \dots \,|\, \xi_n)$ is regular almost surely, i.e.\ $\pr(X \in \mathcal D) = 0$. Then
\begin{align*}
    \pr\big( 0 \notin \Conv(\xi_1, \dots, \xi_n) \big)
    = \frac{1}{2^{\,n-1}} \sum_{j=0}^{d-1} \binom{n-1}{j}.
\end{align*}
Note that neither independence nor exchangeability of $\xi_1, \dots, \xi_n$ is assumed.

[Lemma 35 of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] For every $i\in[n]$ and
	$u=(u^\theta,u^b)\in\mathsf V\oplus\R$,
	\begin{equation}
		
		\langle u,H^{(i)}u\rangle
		\ge
		2\beta\left(
		\lambda_\Sigma\|u^\theta\|_2^2+(u^b)^2
		\right)
		+\gamma\|u^\theta\|_{\mathcal B,\theta^{(i)}}^2.
	\end{equation}
	In particular, writing
	\[
		(H^{(i)})^{-1}
		=
		\begin{pmatrix}
			Q^{(i)} & v^{(i)}\\
			(v^{(i)})^* & c^{(i)}
		\end{pmatrix}
	\]
	with respect to $\mathsf V\oplus\R$, where
	$Q^{(i)}:\mathsf V\to\mathsf V$, $v^{(i)}\in\mathsf V$, and
	$c^{(i)}\in\R$, we have
	\begin{equation}
		
		\|Q^{(i)}\|_{\op}
		\le C\beta^{-1}\lambda_\Sigma^{-1},
		\qquad
		\|v^{(i)}\|_2
		\le C\beta^{-1}\lambda_\Sigma^{-1/2},
		\qquad
		|c^{(i)}|
		\le C\beta^{-1},
	\end{equation}
	for a universal constant $C<\infty$.

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2511.16973, '2511.16973'] Suppose Condition \ref{cond noise} is satisfied.
Then there exist constants $C_0,C_1>0$ such that for any $t>s\ge0$ and $x,y>0$,
$$
W_V(P_{s,t}(x,\cdot),P_{s,t}(y,\cdot))\le C_0 d_V(x,y)\mathrm{exp}\left(-C_1\int_s^tb_0(r)\,\dd r\right),
$$
where $d_V$ and $W_V$ denote the metric defined in \eqref{metric of dv} and the Wasserstein distance introduced in \eqref{wasserstein dist}, respectively. In particular, if
$$
\limsup\limits_{t\rightarrow\infty}\left( t^{-1}\int_\cdot^tb_0(r)\,\dd r\right)>0,
$$
the process is exponentially contractive in the $W_V$-distance. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

PRIVATE CONDITIONAL RESOLUTION, author-recorded, sources not re-fetched. Procaccia, Rosenthal and Sapozhnikov (PTRF 2016) prove a quenched invariance principle for random walk on the infinite cluster of correlated percolation models satisfying a polynomial decoupling condition, local uniqueness and a density condition; for the vacant set these were known for u < u** at the time. Duminil-Copin, Goswami, Rodriguez, Severo and Teixeira (2023) prove u* = u** = bar u, so the inputs hold for every u < u*, and the conclusion of PRS should extend to the whole supercritical phase, answering Open Problem 16.7 of Heydenreich-van der Hofstad for the vacant set (the interlacement set itself was already covered for all u > 0). Verification owed: that the decoupling inequalities of the sharpness paper have exactly the PRS form and that constants may depend on u.
Random interlacements on Z^d, d >= 3
PRS 2016 hypotheses; DGRST 2023 equality of thresholds
title: Quenched invariance principle on the vacant set of random interlacements for every u < u* as a corollary of Procaccia-Rosenthal-Sapozhnikov plus the 2023 sharpness theorem (conditional)

[Definition 35 of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] A point $(t,x) \in L  \cdot (\Z_{\leq 0}\times\Z^d)$ is said to be $(L  ,\delta)$-good is the following three conditions are satisfied:
\begin{itemize}
\item  For all $r \in [-L  (t+1), -L  t]$, the two configurations $R^{\Lambda_{2n_L  }(v), -(t+1)n_L  , -r}(\tau^\pm )$ coincide on the space box $\Lambda_{n_L  }(v)$.
\item For all $-r \in [-L  (t+1), -L  t] $, there exists no $\om$-open cluster of $R^{\Lambda_{2n_L  }(v), -(t+1)n_L  , -r}(\tau^+ )$ crossing the space box $\Lambda_{L  }(v)$.
\item For all $-r \in [-L  (t+1), -L  t] $, there exists no $\eta$-open cluster of $R^{\Lambda_{2n_L  }(v), -(t+1)n_L  , -r}(\tau^+ )$ crossing the space box $\Lambda_{L  }(v)$.

If $(t,x)$ satisfies the first condition amongst those three, we still say that it is $(L  ,\delta)$-mixed.

[Corollary 23 (The Weighted Functional Santal\'o inequality) of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $q \in (0, n)$, let $a\in L^\frac{n}{q}(\s)$ be non-negative and define $$C_{n,q}(a) = \frac{n-q}{n\|a\|_{L^1(\s,\sigma_{n-1})}} \left(\frac{n}{n-q}\|a\|_{L^\frac{n}{q}(\s,\sigma_{n-1})}\right)^{\frac{n}{2n-q}}.$$ Then, for every function $f \in \mathcal{F}_n$ and any non-negative measurable function $g$ on $\R^n$ that satisfy the pointwise bound
    \[
        f(x)^{\frac{n-q}{2n-q}} g(y)^{\frac{n}{2n-q}} \leq \Omega(\langle x, y \rangle) \quad\forall \,x, y \in \R^n \text{ with } \langle x,y\rangle>0,
    \]
    where $\Omega: \R_+ \to \R_+$ is a measurable, non-increasing function, one has:
    \begin{equation}
        
        \left(\int_{\R^n} \!\!\!f(x) dx \right)^{\frac{n-q}{2n-q}} \left(\int_{\R^n} \!\!\!\!g(y) |y|^{-q}a\left(\frac{y}{|y|}\right) dy \right)^{\frac{n}{2n-q}} \leq C_{n,q}(a) \int_{\R^n}\!\!\! \Omega(|z|^\frac{2n-q}{n}) |z|^{-q}a\left(\frac{z}{|z|}\right) dz.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let (X_n) be a submartingale with sup_n E[X_n^+] < infinity. Then X_n converges almost surely to a limit X_infinity with E|X_infinity| < infinity. For a MARTINGALE the hypothesis is equivalent to sup_n E|X_n| < infinity, since E[X_n] is constant and E|X_n| = 2E[X_n^+] - E[X_n]. Convergence is ONLY almost sure: it need not hold in L^1, and E[X_infinity] need not equal E[X_0]. Standard failure: let (X_n) be the product of independent nonnegative mean-one factors, for instance X_n = prod_{k <= n} (1 + eps_k) with eps_k = +1 or -1 with probability 1/2 each - equivalently X_n = 2^n on the event that all signs were +1 and 0 otherwise. Then X_n is a nonnegative martingale with E X_n = 1 for every n, so it is L^1-bounded and converges a.s., but the limit is 0 almost surely and E X_infinity = 0 != 1 = E X_0. Nonnegative supermartingales always converge a.s. because X_n^+ = X_n has bounded expectation; upgrading to L^1 convergence is exactly what uniform integrability supplies. [standard; e.g. Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed., Theorem 4.2.11]
(X_n) a submartingale for a filtration (F_n)
sup_n E[X_n^+] < infinity (for a martingale: sup_n E|X_n| < infinity)
no uniform integrability is assumed, and without it convergence is only almost sure

The counts U_N[a,b] increase in N, so monotone convergence gives E[U_infinity[a,b]] < infinity and hence U_infinity[a,b] < infinity almost surely. [Lemma 9 of arXiv:2608.03497, 'Connective Constants on Nested Fractal Graphs'] Let
\[
  \eta=(x_0,\ldots,x_\ell),\qquad \ell\ge1,
\]
be a finite polygonal path in \(\R^d\), with consecutive vertices
distinct.  For \(y\in V_\infty\), let \(\mathscr E_y(\eta)\) be the set
of distinct
vertex sequences
\[
  (T(x_0),\ldots,T(x_\ell))
\]
such that \(T\) is a Euclidean isometry of \(\R^d\),
\(T(x_0)=y\), and
\[
  \{T(x_{j-1}),T(x_j)\}\in E(F_\infty),
  \qquad 1\le j\le\ell.
\]
Then
\[
  \#\mathscr E_y(\eta)\le D^d.
\]
The same estimate holds if \(T(x_\ell)=y\) is prescribed in place of
\(T(x_0)=y\).

[Proposition 23 (Skorokhod representation and generalized weak limit) of arXiv:2605.23529, 'Generalized Bessel-Dunkl diffusions'] Assume \ref{ass:cont}-\ref{ass:sigma}, and let $X^{(n)}$ be the approximating
sequence. Then, after passing to a subsequence, there exist a probability space, a
continuous $\Cc$-valued process $X$, a continuous local martingale
$M=(M_1,\ldots,M_N)$, and, for every $\alpha\in R_+$, a continuous increasing
process $A^\alpha$ on $[0,\zeta)$ with $A^\alpha(0)=0$, such that, for
\begin{equation*}
    \zeta
    :=
    \lim_{r\to\infty}
    \inf\{t\ge0:\ |X(t)|\ge r\},
\end{equation*}
we have, for every $t<\zeta$,
\begin{equation}
    
    X(t)
    =
    x_0
    +
    M(t)
    +
    \int_0^t b(s,X(s))\,ds
    +
    \sum_{\alpha\in R_+}\alpha\,A^\alpha(t),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
    
    \langle M_i,M_j\rangle(t)
    =
    \delta_{ij}
    \int_0^t \sigma_i^2(s,X(s))\,ds,
    \qquad i,j=1,\ldots,N.
\end{equation}
Consequently, possibly after enlarging the probability space, there exists an
$N$-dimensional Brownian motion $B$ such that
\begin{equation*}
    M(t)
    =
    \int_0^t \sigma(s,X(s))\,dB(s),
    \qquad t<\zeta.
\end{equation*}
In particular, $X$ is a generalized weak limit of the approximating sequence.

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The moments of complex hyperspherical variables are given by
$$\int_{S^{N-1}_\mathbb C}|z_i|^{2k}dz=\frac{(N-1)!k!}{(N+k-1)!}$$
with the other moments vanishing. The normalized complex hyperspherical variables 
$$w_i=\sqrt{N}z_i$$
become standard complex normal, following $G_1$, and independent with $N\to\infty$.

the identity
\begin{equation}

\int_0^t\Big[(a_s^{ij}D_j u_s+\mathfrak{f}_s^i(u_s),D_i \varphi)
+(u_{s(u_s)},\varphi)\Big]\,ds                              \\
&\quad
+\int_0^t\big(\gamma_s^{ki}D_i q_s^k+f_s(u_s,Du_s),\varphi\big)\,ds\\
&\quad
+\int_0^t\big(\sigma_s^{ik}D_i u_s+h_s^k(u_s),\varphi\big)\,dm_s^k
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
holds for $\mathbb P\otimes dt$-almost every
$(\omega,t)\in\Omega\times[0,T]$, 
and 
\begin{equation}
                                 
\nabla q_t^k=R\big(\sigma_t^{ik}D_i u_t+h_t^k(u_t)\big)

(\bP\otimes dt\otimes dx\text{-a.e.})\quad \text{for $k\in\bZ$}.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:3eb4c72118a0c98b85af5b199155f8951f52c2c3b4f0e70884c258772e8b604b","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/3e/3eb4c72118a0c98b85af5b199155f8951f52c2c3b4f0e70884c258772e8b604b.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:13469eb43ce2832dcdec7940e941823fddca997fdd31a9e3d4f7045f3065ea4d","bundle_entry_key":"core-double-graph-cover-st-numbering-index-bound-w718","bundle_id":"population.t287-general-core-cover-asymmetric-coefficients-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Graph cycle ranks and extensive-rank Gaussian-channel information","draft":"w718/bundle_011.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian_channels:core-double-graph-cover-st-numbering-index-bound-w718","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Core double covers and st-ordering: the bridge-free restriction is unnecessary

Target1 supporting graph lemma. Proof draft, UNAUDITED; novelty is
unestablished. This extends claim030 to local graphs with bridges. It
does not supply the analytic, size-uniform remainder required by Target1.

## 1. Abstract theorem

Let B be a finite connected loopless undirected multigraph, with q
vertices and e edges. Assign every edge two distinct labels from a set
of v>=2 labels, and let G be the label multigraph: its vertices are the
labels and its edges are the edges of B with those label endpoints.
For each label t let B_t be its edge-induced subgraph, without isolated
vertices. Suppose:

* G is connected and G-t is connected for every vertex t; the graph
  with one vertex is regarded as connected.
* Every B_t is nonempty, connected, and has minimum degree at least two.

Then q-e+v<=2. If at least one B_t has cycle rank at least two, then
q-e+v<=1. Degree counts include the multiplicities of parallel edges.

The statement does NOT assume that the B_t are bridgeless or Eulerian.
The proof below is self-contained; its st-ordering device is a standard
graph method, not a novelty assertion.

## 2. Adding a core subgraph increases cycle rank

Let A and H be finite connected subgraphs of a loopless multigraph.
Assume A meets H, H has minimum degree at least two, and H has an edge
not in A. Then

    b(A union H) >= b(A)+1,     b(J)=|E(J)|-|V(J)|+1.

Proof. Contract the entire connected A in A union H to a single root,
and discard the edges of A. Retain all edges outside A, including any
loops created by contraction. The resulting graph K is connected and

    b(K)=|E(H) minus E(A)|-|V(H) minus V(A)|
        =b(A union H)-b(A).

If b(K)=0, K is a tree. It has at least one edge. A nontrivial finite
tree has a leaf different from the root. This leaf corresponds to an
original vertex outside V(A), so all its incident edges in A union H
are edges of H, and none was altered or removed by the contraction.
Its degree in H is therefore one, contradicting the assumption. A
connected graph has nonnegative cycle rank, so b(K)>=1. QED.

This step uses a graph contraction and a leaf contradiction, not an
independence assertion about different local cycle spaces.

## 3. An st-order with any prescribed first vertex

Choose any vertex s of G and any neighbor z of s. There is a linear
ordering of the vertices starting at s and ending at z in which every
other vertex has both an earlier and a later neighbor. Here is a
construction, included to avoid assuming an unstated graph theorem.

Begin with the ordered set [s,z]. Suppose a proper vertex set S is
already ordered with that property. A component C of G-S has at least
two distinct neighbors in S. It has a neighbor since G is connected;
if its only neighbor were w, deleting w would disconnect C from the
nonempty S minus {w}, contradicting connectedness of G-w.

Choose distinct neighbors x,y in S and a simple path from x to y whose
internal vertices lie in C: join their adjacent vertices through the
connected component C, and simplify the resulting walk. Orient the
path so x precedes y in the current ordering. Insert its internal
vertices, in path order, immediately after x. Every new vertex has an
earlier and a later path neighbor, and the earlier/later neighbors of
old vertices keep their relative positions. The first and last vertices
stay s and z. At least one vertex is added. Iteration ends with the
required ordering. The construction also covers v=2 without iteration.

## 4. Proof of the theorem, including strictness

If there is a label s with b(B_s)>=2, choose it as the first vertex of
the preceding order. Otherwise choose any s. The last label z may be
any neighbor of s. Write the ordered labels t_1=s,...,t_v=z, and set

    A_j = union of B_(t_i) for i<=j.

All A_j are connected: each new label has an earlier neighbor, and the
edge of G to that neighbor is an edge common to the new B_t and the
previous union. For 2<=j<=v-1, label t_j also has a later neighbor.
The edge to that later neighbor is absent from A_(j-1), because its
only labels are t_j and that later label. Thus the lemma of Section2
gives b(A_j)>=b(A_(j-1))+1.

Every edge of B already lies in A_(v-1): its two labels are distinct,
so at least one is different from the last label. Therefore

    b(B) >= b(B_s)+(v-2).

A nonempty finite connected graph of minimum degree two has cycle
rank at least one. This proves b(B)>=v-1, equivalently q-e+v<=2.
If b(B_s)>=2, it proves b(B)>=v and hence q-e+v<=1. QED.

## 5. Exact application to raw cumulant diagrams

The entropy contraction graph G has v tensor vertices and e Wick edges;
by claim010's exact entropy cancellation it is loopless, connected and
has no articulation. The surviving terms have v>=2. At each tensor
vertex t, the raw cumulant expansion is indexed by row and column
partitions with connected join and no singleton blocks. Its local
bipartite graph H_t has the raw row and column blocks as vertices and
the incident tensor positions as edges. It is connected and has minimum
degree two; odd blocks and bridges are allowed.

Let B have one vertex per global row equality class and one per global
column equality class. Each Wick pair is a distinct edge joining its
row and column classes. Its labels are the two tensor vertices joined
by the Wick pair. Those labels are distinct because G is loopless.
For a fixed t, no two local tensor positions are identified as the
same Wick edge; otherwise that pair would be a self-loop at t. Thus
H_t maps edge-bijectively onto B_t, identifying only vertices of the
same row/column type. In particular B_t is connected and has minimum
degree two. Connectedness of G implies connectedness of the union B.

If a raw block has size>=3, H_t has a vertex of degree>=3 while all
degrees are>=2. For h vertices and d edges this implies 2d>=2h+1,
so integer d>=h+1 and b(H_t)=d-h+1>=2. Vertex identifications cannot
decrease cycle rank of a connected graph. Hence b(B_t)>=2 and the
strict form of the theorem applies.

As B has q=c_i+c_j vertices, this proves

    c_i+c_j-e+v<=1

whenever at least one higher raw block occurs. The weak bound<=2
holds for every term. This pays the previously open odd-block graph
step, including the two-cycle-plus-bridge local graph.

## 6. Audit boundaries

The abstract graph theorem is independent of probability. Its translation
uses the loopless/no-articulation entropy-graph reduction from claim010;
that statistical reduction remains independently unaudited. The next
coefficient theorem also needs the existing finite-dimensional Taylor
coefficient representation and moment hypotheses. None of this bounds
posterior connected cumulants uniformly in dimension at positive SNR.

Least trusted new application step: the edge-bijection from H_t to B_t
depends on excluding contraction self-loops BEFORE applying this lemma.
The proof does not apply to a graph with self-loop tensor contractions.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:5dc5e55fd52de17190c46ce82824b733f184b71e297dcfbd13ccb4dc60f2d10c","revision_digest":"sha256:1130e3377af7cbbff31fa89abc6abbdc189cea3af1b6c09a0ca864ad0a0d417b","source_id":"owner:w718:T287:core-double-graph-cover-st-numbering-index-bound-w718","source_revision":"2026-10-21-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Proposition prop:imported of arXiv:2604.20327, 'Persistent Homology of the Wiener Sausage II: A Central Limit Theorem for Drifted Planar B'] Fix a compact radius window $[r_0, r_1] \subset (0,\infty)$. Then the following hold.
  \begin{itemize}
  \item[\emph{(i)}] There exists a sequence of regeneration times $(\tau_n)_{n \geq 0}$ such
    that the associated recentered regeneration blocks are i.i.d.
  \item[\emph{(ii)}] The cycle lengths $(\eta_n)_{n \geq 0}$ are i.i.d.\ and admit
    exponential moments.
  \item[\emph{(iii)}] For every bounded Borel function $\psi$ supported in $[r_0, r_1]$,
    the regeneration-time increments
    \begin{equation}
      \Delta_n = \Phi_\psi(\tau_{n+1}) - \Phi_\psi(\tau_n)
    \end{equation}
    form a stationary $1$-dependent sequence.
  \item[\emph{(iv)}] All topological nonadditivity across a regeneration cut is localized to an
    interface region whose temporal extent is controlled by local forward and backward window
    times with exponential moments.
  \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemm l:difference-conditional-variances of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] Let $X_1,X_2$ be square-integrable random variables on a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$, and let $\mathcal{G}\subset \mathcal{F}$ be any sub-$\sigma$-algebra.
    Then
    \begin{align*}
        \Bigl|
            \mathbb{E}[\Var(X_1|\mathcal{G})] - \mathbb{E}[\Var(X_2|\mathcal{G})]
        \Bigr|
        \leqslant
        \bigl(\mathbb{E}[X_1^2]^{1/2} + \mathbb{E}[X_2^2]^{1/2}\bigr)\cdot\mathbb{E}\bigl[(X_1-X_2)^2\bigr]^{1/2}.
    \end{align*}

For a language model on a finite alphabet Sigma, a supported prefix t[1:i-1], and i<j, empirical substring entropy is H_e^[i:j)(t)=-ln P_Model(T[i:j-1]=t[i:j-1] | T[1:i-1]=t[1:i-1]); it equals the sum of the realized token surprisals along that substring. A watermark has PPT algorithms Setup,Wat,Detect and a polynomial output-length cap Lmax. Soundness bounds the key-averaged acceptance probability for every fixed key-independent word of length at most Lmax by a negligible function. Undetectability compares polynomially many oracle samples from one fixed watermark key with independent model samples. For a threshold beta, the high-entropy event for a length ell=j-i substring is H_e^[i:j)(t)>=beta(ell)*ln|Sigma|. CAUTION: the displayed Definition2.6 and LemmaC.6 Eq37 sample tprime from E(t), where t is the full watermarked text, and require negligible probability of detection failure together with existence of such a high-entropy interval. The following Definition2.6 prose and C.6 Step1 instead give the channel the selected substring, setting tprime=E(t[i:j-1]). These are distinct experiments when the edit budget is measured relative to the channel input length. This card records the distinction and does not silently replace the displayed definition or certify Theorems5.1-5.2.
All conditional token probabilities use the same language model and realized prefix; logarithms are natural.
Strings may be END-padded to Lmax for selecting intervals; the input actually given to the channel must be specified.
This is a source-definition record, not a watermark construction guarantee.

[Lem 64 of arXiv:2605.23308, 'Convergence rate estimates for semigroups and heat kernels associated with resistance form'] Fix $x,y\in F,\;y_n\in F_n,\;t>0,\;\kappa\in [1/2,1],\;p_0,p,q\in [1,\infty],$ and $\alpha\in (0,\alpha_0)$.
\begin{itemize}

  $\varepsilon\in (0,1],\;\rho\in (0,\infty),\;r\in [d_{\rm{H}}(F,F_n),\infty),\;\delta\in (0,r)$ that
\begin{align*}
  |p(t,x,y)-p_n(t,x_n,y_n)|
  \lesssim&
  \frac{1}{\mu(B(x,r))}\g{I}{totyuu}\\
  &+M(t)(c_1(\varepsilon,\kappa,p_0)\mu(B(x,r))^{\frac{1}{p_0}-1}+\mu(B(x,r))^{-1})d_{\BL^{\kappa}}(\mu,\mu_n)\\
  &+L(t)d(x,x_n).
\end{align*}
\item[$\rm{(ii)}$]Moreover, if the assumption $\rm{(A3)}$ is additionally satisfied, then it holds 
  for $\varepsilon,\rho\in (0,1),\;\xi\ge d_{\rm{H}}(F,F_n),$ and $0<r<\eta<1$ that
  \begin{align*}
   |p(t,x,y)-p_n(t,x_n,y_n)|
  \lesssim&
  \frac{1}{\mu(B(x,r))}\g{II}{totyuu}\\
  &+M(t)(c_1(\varepsilon,\kappa,p_0)\mu(B(x,r))^{\frac{1}{p_0}-1}+\mu(B(x,r))^{-1})d_{\BL^{\kappa}}(\mu,\mu_n)\\
  &+L(t)d(x,x_n).
  \end{align*}
\end{itemize}

PRIVATE REDUCTION, author-recorded. Barsky-Grimmett-Newman: at p_c(Z^d) the half-space N x Z^{d-1} has no infinite cluster. To conclude theta(p_c) = 0 in Z^d (open for 3 <= d <= 10) one would show that a unique infinite cluster (Burton-Keane) cannot be made of infinitely many finite half-space clusters connected through the boundary hyperplane. In d = 2 this works because the half-plane susceptibility at p_c is infinite. The reduction: theta(p_c) = 0 in Z^d follows from (i) infinite half-space susceptibility at p_c(Z^d), and (ii) a gluing lemma showing that finite half-space clusters linked across the hyperplane force an infinite half-space cluster on one side at a slightly larger parameter. Both (i) and (ii) are open for 3 <= d <= 10; (i) is a natural intermediate target because it is a statement about a single half-space cluster rather than about the full-space cluster.

body: In number theory, the sum of two squares theorem relates the prime decomposition of any integer n > 1 to whether it can be written as a sum of two squares, such that n = a^{2} + b^{2} for some integers a, b. An integer greater than one can be written as a sum of two squares if and only if its prime decomposition contains no factor p^{k}, where prime $p\equiv 3{\pmod {4}}$ and k is odd.

body: [Theorem 2.4 (Erdős–Rényi, SBMs and logistic RDPGs) in the first version of arXiv:2512.18592, 'Wavelet Latent Position Exponential Random Graphs'] Fix $c\in\mathbb{R}$ and a real symmetric Hilbert–Schmidt matrix $S=(s_{rs})_{r,s\geq 0}$, and let $G_{n}\sim\mathrm{WL\mbox{-}ERG}(c,S)$ be generated as in Definitions 2.1 – 2.3. 1. (Erdős–Rényi.) If $s_{rs}=0$ for all $(r,s)\neq(0,0)$, then $G_{n}$ is Erdős–Rényi $G(n,p)$ with $p=\sigma(c+s_{00})$. 2. (Haar/SBM special case.) Assume the underlying wavelet system is the Haar system and fix an integer $J\geq 0$. Let $\{I_{\ell,J}\}_{\ell=0}^{2^{J}-1}$ be the dyadic partition of $(0,1)$, define $\phi_{\ell,J}(x):=2^{J/2}\mathbf{1}_{I_{\ell,J}}(x)$, and let $V_{J}:=\mathrm{span}\{\phi_{\ell,J}:0\leq\ell\leq 2^{J}-1\}\subset L^{2}(0,1)$. If the logit satisfies $f_{S}\in V_{J}\otimes V_{J}$, equivalently if there exist real coefficients $\alpha_{\ell k}$ such that $f_{S}(x,y)=\sum_{\ell,k=0}^{2^{J}-1}\alpha_{\ell k}\,\phi_{\ell,J}(x)\phi_{k,J}(y)\quad\text{in }L^{2}\big((0,1)^{2}\big),$ then $G_{n}$ is a stochastic block model with $2^{J}$ blocks. In particular, there are constants $\beta_{\ell k}:=2^{J}\alpha_{\ell k}$ such that $f_{S}(x,y)=\beta_{\ell k}$ for a.e. $(x,y)\in I_{\ell,J}\times I_{k,J}$, and hence the block connectivity probabilities are $p_{\ell k}=\sigma(c+\beta_{\ell k})=\sigma(c+2^{J}\alpha_{\ell k}).$ Under $U_{i}\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1)$, the block proportions are $\pi_{\ell}=2^{-J}$. 3. (Finite-rank PSD $\Rightarrow$ logistic RDPG.) Assume $S$ is positive semidefinite as an operator on $\ell^{2}$ and has finite rank $d$. Then there exist functions $g_{1},\dots,g_{d}\in L^{2}(0,1)$ such that $f_{S}(x,y)=\sum_{k=1}^{d}g_{k}(x)g_{k}(y)\quad\text{in }L^{2}\big((0,1)^{2}\big).$ Consequently, for a measurable representative $\Phi(x):=(g_{1}(x),\dots,g_{d}(x))\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ (defined a.e.), $W_{c,S}(x,y)=\sigma\!\bigl(c+\Phi(x)^{\top}\Phi(y)\bigr)\quad\text{for a.e. }(x,y).$ Therefore $G_{n}$ is a logistic random dot product graph: with latent positions $X_{i}=\Phi(U_{i})\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$, the edges are independent conditional on $X$ and satisfy $\mathbb{P}(A_{ij}=1\mid X)=\sigma(c+X_{i}^{\top}X_{j})$ for all $i<j$.

For n >= 5 the general polynomial equation of degree n, x^n + a_1 x^{n-1} + ... + a_n = 0 with independent indeterminate coefficients over Q (the field Q(a_1, ..., a_n)), is not solvable by radicals: there is no formula for its roots built from the coefficients by field operations and extraction of k-th roots. Moreover specific polynomials over Q are not solvable by radicals, for instance x^5 - x - 1 and x^5 - 4x + 2, whose Galois groups over Q are S_5. For n <= 4 the general equation IS solvable by radicals (the quadratic formula; Cardano's formula for cubics, 1545; Ferrari's method for quartics). GALOIS'S CRITERION, which subsumes the theorem: a polynomial over a field of characteristic 0 is solvable by radicals if and only if its Galois group is a solvable group.
characteristic 0 (over Q or a field containing Q); the criterion needs the field to contain, or to be extended by, roots of unity
'general' means indeterminate coefficients; a particular polynomial of degree >= 5 may well be solvable (x^5 - 2 is)
