Let mu be a product probability measure on {0,1}^n (Harris 1960), or more generally a measure on a finite distributive lattice satisfying the FKG lattice condition mu(x v y) mu(x ^ y) >= mu(x) mu(y) (Fortuin, Kasteleyn, Ginibre 1971). If A and B are both increasing events, then mu(A and B) >= mu(A) mu(B); equivalently, for increasing functions f and g, E[f g] >= E[f] E[g]. The same holds when both are decreasing. If one event is increasing and the other decreasing, the inequality reverses: mu(A and B) <= mu(A) mu(B). The inequality says nothing about a pair of events that are neither increasing nor decreasing, and it fails for a general (non-FKG) measure.
mu is a product measure on {0,1}^n, or satisfies the FKG lattice condition (log-supermodular)
A and B are both increasing (or both decreasing) events; f and g both monotone in the same direction
the reversed inequality needs one increasing and one decreasing event
no conclusion for events that are not monotone, and none for a non-FKG measure

[Lemma lem:fold of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Let $\mathcal F$ be an enterable distance-hereditary one-front fold with
ordered formal ports $x_1,\ldots,x_p$ on its carrier arcs.  For an incoming
two-front state $\Xi$, its open tensor has an identity
\[
 \mathcal F(x_1,\ldots,x_p)[\Xi]
 =\sum_\nu a_\nu
 u_\nu(x_1,\ldots,x_p)\,\Xi\,
 v_\nu(x_1,\ldots,x_p),
\tag{2.4.3}
\]
where every port variable occurs exactly once, every fixed letter in
$u_\nu,v_\nu$ is a safe gate or signed isometry, and
$\sum_\nu|a_\nu|\le A^s$ for a fold with $s$ coefficient occurrences.
After substituting safe words $X_i$ for the ports,
\[
 \|\mathcal F(X_1,\ldots,X_p)[\Xi]\|_1
 \le A^sK^s\left(\prod_i\|X_i\|\right)\|\Xi\|_1.
\tag{2.4.4}
\]

[Proposition 17 of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $X$ and $Y$ be geodesic vector spaces, and let $c: X \times Y \to \R$ be a continuous cost function that is $1$-homogeneous in each variable. Let $1 < p, q < \infty$ such that $\frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{q} = 1$. Let $K \subset X$ and $L \subset Y$ be compact, geodesically convex sets containing the origin in their respective interiors. Then,
\[
\Ld c\left(\frac{\|\cdot\|_K^p}{p}\right)(y)=\frac{\|y\|_{K^{\circ, c}}^q}{q} \quad \text{and} \quad \Lu c\left(\frac{\|\cdot\|_L^q}{q}\right)(x)=\frac{\|x\|_{L^{\star, c}}^p}{p}.
\]
title: Proposition 17 of arXiv:2609.01460

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The number of partial fixed points of permutations,
$$\chi_t(\sigma)=\#\left\{i\in\{1,\ldots,[tN]\}\Big|\sigma(i)=i\right\}$$ 
when regarded as random variable $\chi_t:S_N\to\mathbb N$, satisfies the formula
$$\chi_t\sim p_t$$
that is, follows the Poisson law of parameter $t\in(0,1]$, in the $N\to\infty$ limit.

[Proposition 11 of arXiv:2605.08844, 'Signature Kernel and Schwinger-Dyson Kernel Equations as Two-Parameter Rough Differential '] Let $S$ be a finite-dimensional Banach space. Let $\mathbf{X}\in \Omega G_p([a,b],V)$ and $\mathbf{Y}\in \Omega G_q([c,d],W)$, and set $\kappa=\lfloor p\rfloor$ and $\lambda=\lfloor q\rfloor$. Let $g\colon F\to S$ be Fr\'echet smooth, and let $Z$ be a two-parameter $(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})$-controlled path.
Then the composition $g(Z)$ defines a two-parameter controlled path
\[
g(Z) \in \mathcal{D}^{p,q}_{\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y}}([a,b]\times[c,d], S).
\]
Moreover, $g(Z)$ is characterized by the identity
\[
g(Z)_{t,v}[\eta,\xi] = g\left(Z^{(0,0)}_{t,v}\right)[\eta,\xi],
\qquad
\text{for all } \eta \in V^{\otimes 0},\ \xi \in W^{\otimes 0}.
\]

The higher level components of $g(Z)$ are given as follows. For
$\xi_j \in V^{\otimes j}$ and $\eta_k \in W^{\otimes k}$, define
\[
g(Z_{t,v})[\xi_j,\eta_k] :=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\displaystyle
\sum_{m=1}^{\kappa-1} \frac{1}{m!}
D^m g\left(Z^{(0,0)}_{t,v}\right) \circ Z_{t,v}^{\otimes m}
\circ \left(\tilde{\Delta}^m \boxtimes \mathrm{id}_{T^{<\lambda(W)}}\right)
[\xi_j,\eta_k],
& j>0,\ k=0, \\[2ex]
\displaystyle
\sum_{n=1}^{\lambda-1} \frac{1}{n!}
D^n g\left(Z^{(0,0)}_{t,v}\right) \circ Z_{t,v}^{\otimes n}
\circ \left(\mathrm{id}_{T^{<\kappa(V)}} \boxtimes \tilde{\Delta}^n\right)
[\xi_j,\eta_k],
& j=0,\ k>0, \\[2ex]
\displaystyle
\sum_{\ell=1}^{\lambda+\kappa-2} \frac{1}{\ell!}
D^\ell g\left(Z^{(0,0)}_{t,v}\right) \circ Z_{t,v}^{\otimes \ell}
\circ \widetilde{(\Delta \boxtimes \Delta)}^{\ell}
[\xi_j,\eta_k],
& j>0,\ k>0 .
\end{cases}
\]
Here, $\Delta$ denotes the shuffle coproduct, $\tilde{\Delta}$
denotes the restriction $\pi_{\geq 1} \circ \Delta$ and $\Delta^m$ denotes the $m$-fold iterate of $\Delta$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:self_normal of arXiv:2609.00193, 'Provably Efficient Federated Reinforcement Learning with Linear Function Approximation and'] Let $\{\eta_t\}_{t \ge 1}$ be a real-valued martingale difference sequence
adapted to a filtration $\{\mathcal{F}_t\}$, such that $\eta_t$ is conditionally
$R$-sub-Gaussian, i.e.,
\[
\mathbb{E}\!\left[\exp(\lambda \eta_t)\mid \mathcal{F}_{t-1}\right]
\le \exp\!\left(\frac{\lambda^2 R^2}{2}\right)
\quad \text{for all } \lambda \in \mathbb{R}.
\]

Let $\{x_t\}_{t \ge 1}$ be an $\mathbb{R}^d$-valued predictable process
(i.e., $x_t$ is $\mathcal{F}_{t-1}$-measurable), and define
\[
V_t = \lambda I + \sum_{s=1}^t x_s x_s^\top,
\quad
S_t = \sum_{s=1}^t x_s \eta_s,
\]
for some $\lambda > 0$.

Then, for any $\delta \in (0,1)$, with probability at least $1-\delta$,
for all $t \ge 0$ simultaneously,
\[
\|S_t\|_{V_t^{-1}}^2
\;\le\;
2 R^2 \log\left(
\frac{\det(V_t)^{1/2}}{\det(\lambda I)^{1/2}\,\delta}
\right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let $X_1, \dots, X_n$ be i.i.d. with mean $\theta \ge 0$ and variance $\sigma^2$, and let the estimator respect the constraint: $\hat\theta_n = \max(0, \bar X_n)$. When the true parameter is interior ($\theta > 0$) the nonparametric bootstrap is consistent: the conditional law of $\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n^* - \hat\theta_n)$ converges to $N(0, \sigma^2)$, the law of $\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n - \theta)$. When the true parameter is on the boundary ($\theta = 0$) it is not: $\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n - \theta) \Rightarrow \max(0, Z)$ with $Z \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$, a law with an atom of mass $1/2$ at zero, whereas the bootstrap law of $\sqrt n(\hat\theta_n^* - \hat\theta_n)$ converges, conditionally on the data, to the law of $\max(0, Z + \zeta) - \max(0, \zeta)$ with $\zeta \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$ a random shift that does not vanish - so the bootstrap distribution is random in the limit and does not equal the sampling distribution (Andrews 2000, Theorem 1). The same failure holds for maximum-likelihood and least-squares estimators under inequality constraints whenever the true parameter has an active constraint, in particular for nonnegatively constrained regression and portfolio weights with coordinates at zero: the bootstrap replicates flip the constrained coordinates between zero and positive values, and the spread of the replicates is not the spread of the estimator. Consistent alternatives: the $m$-out-of-$n$ bootstrap with $m \to \infty$, $m/n \to 0$, and subsampling, both of which recover the limit law at the boundary.

[Definition 10 of arXiv:2604.01978, 'Homogenized Transformers'] A $\cF_t^{\mathsf W}$-adapted process $(\mu(t))_{t\in[0,T]}$ with values in $\mathcal \cP(\S^{d-1})$
is called a weak solution to \eqref{eq: the.spde} if for all $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb S^{d-1})$,
\begin{align*}
\langle \mu(t),\varphi\rangle
=
\langle \mu(0),\varphi\rangle
&+\int_0^t \langle \mathsf{L}_{\mu(s)}\varphi,\mu(s)\rangle\,\de s \nonumber\\
&+\int_0^t\int_{\Uptheta} \langle \nabla\varphi\cdot G_{\mu(s)}(\cdot,\bm{\theta}),\mu(s) \rangle\,\mathsf{W}(\de s,\de \bm{\theta}),
\end{align*}
where $\mathsf{L}_{\mu}$ is the generator
\[
\mathsf{L}_{\mu}\varphi(x)=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\Uptheta}\Hess \varphi(x)[G_{\mu}(x,\bm{\theta}),G_{\mu}(x,\bm{\theta})]\uprho_*(\de \bm{\theta})
\]
for all $\varphi \in C^{\infty}(\S^{d-1})$.

body: Let (X,Sigma,mu) be a probability space and T: X -> X a measure-preserving transformation. T is ergodic if every T-invariant measurable set has measure 0 or 1: whenever A in Sigma satisfies T^{-1}A = A up to a mu-null set, mu(A) is 0 or 1. Equivalently, T is ergodic iff every T-invariant measurable function f (f(Tx)=f(x) a.e.) is a.e. constant; equivalently, by the Birkhoff ergodic theorem, iff for every f in L^1(X,mu) the time averages (1/N) sum_{n=0}^{N-1} f(T^n x) converge a.e. to the constant integral_X f dmu.
title: Ergodicity

\]

Let H = (L, R, E) be a finite bipartite graph and take the network with a source s, a sink t, arcs s->u of capacity 1 for u in L, arcs u->v for each edge uv, and arcs v->t of capacity 1 for v in R, the middle arcs carrying positive integer capacities. In every feasible integral s-t flow, the middle arcs with positive flow carry exactly one unit each and form a matching whose size is the flow value; conversely, every matching gives an integral flow of the same value, one unit along each path s-u-v-t. The integrality is needed: in the network on K_{2,2}, flow 1/2 on each of the four middle arcs and 1 on each terminal arc is a maximum flow of value 2 whose support is not a matching. Integer capacities guarantee that some maximum flow is integral, not that every one is.

the network is layered s -> L -> R -> t, terminal capacities are 1, middle capacities are positive integers
the flow is integral

[Proposition deterministic convergence inversions of arXiv:2603.09008, 'On the statistics of random-to-top shuffles'] Let $R_i$ be independent discrete uniform random variables on $\{0,1,$ $\ldots,n-i\}$. Let $a_n$ be a deterministic sequence with $a_n\to a\in(0,1)$. Set 
    \[f(a_n)=\sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor a_n n\rfloor} (R_i-(n-i)/2).\] 
    We have
    \[\frac{f(a_n)}{n^{3/2}}\Rightarrow_d\,\mathcal{N}\left(0,\frac{1-(1-a)^3}{36}\right).\]

[Definition Strato of arXiv:2602.08591, 'The Yang--Mills measure on compact surfaces as a \\ universal scaling limit of lattice gau'] Let $r\in (0,1]$ and $0\leqslant \theta_1 \leqslant \theta_2 \leqslant 2\pi$. The parallel transport of $A$ along $\theta_1\xrightarrow r \theta_2$ is defined as the strong solution of the Stratonovich SDE 
      \[
  \begin{cases}
      \mathrm{d} X_t = X_t \circ \mathrm{d} \int_{\theta_1\xrightarrow{r}\theta_1 + t}A \\
      X_0 = 1
  \end{cases}
  \]
  at time $\theta_2-\theta_1$. It is denoted by 
  \[\mathrm{Hol}(A,\theta_1\xrightarrow r \theta_2).\]
title: Definition Strato of arXiv:2602.08591

[Lemma 9 (Generalized Laplace Method) of arXiv:2607.13273, 'Asymptotics of transition densities for L\'evy processes with stochastic resetting'] Let $-\infty<a<b<\infty$, and $f\in C^2((a,b))$ with unique global maximum at $x_0\in(a,b),$ $h(x)\in C((a,b))$ and $h(x)\geq 0$ for $x\in(a,b)$. If $e^{f(x)}h(x)$ is integrable on $(a,b)$, then
     \begin{equation*}
        \int_a^b h(x)e^{rf(x)} \dx \sim_r h(x_0)\sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{r|f^{\prime\prime}(x_0)|}} e^{rf(x_0)}.
    \end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\begin{enumerate}[(1)]

          K_u \mbox{ is $\cF_{t_{n-1}}$-measurable for } 
          u\in (t_{n-1},t_n]

\end{enumerate}

body:
[Definition 1 of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] Let $\{ C_n \}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be uniformly random elements of $[m]\coloneqq\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$, and let
$\{ U_n \}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be uniformly random elements of $(0, 1)$.
Assume the family $\{ U_n, C_n \}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is independent.
The random variable $C_n$ denotes the coupon type
obtained on day $n$.
Define the random variables
\[
  L(i, n) \coloneqq \sup\{ k \leqslant n \mid C_k = i \}, \quad i \in [m], \quad n > 0.
\]
Then $L(i, n)$ is the most recent day no later than $n$ that coupon
type $i$ was issued.
For clumsiness probability $p \in [0, 1)$, the 
clumsy coupon collection time can be defined by
\[
  T_{m, p} \coloneqq \inf \{ n > 0 \mid L(i, n) > 0 \ \text{and} \ U_{L(i, n)} \leq 1 - p \ 
    \text{for all $i \in [m]$} \},
\]
the first day that every coupon type has been updated, their most
recent updates all having been non-clumsy.
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2605.14206

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2606.20816, 'Spectral Properties of Dense Barab\'asi--Albert Graphs'] Let $c \in \left(0, \frac12\right)$ and $m = c n$. For indices $k > j$ with $k / n \to y \in \left(0, 1\right]$ and $j / n \to x \in \left(0, 1\right]$, set $t_0 = m + 1$ and $s_0 = \max\left\{j, t_0\right\}$. Then
\[
\E[M_{k j}]
\ = \
m \frac{\mu_j \left(k - 1\right)}{D_{k - 1}}
\ \to \
\frac{c}{\sqrt{\left(2 \max\left\{x, c\right\} - c\right) \left(2 y - c\right)}},
\qquad n \to \infty,
\]
where $D_t = 2 m t - m \left(m + 1\right)$ and $\mu_j \left(\cdot\right) = \E[d_j \left(\cdot\right)]$. Moreover, $\E[M_{k j}] = O(1)$ uniformly in $j,k,n$.

[Definition of arXiv:2604.22528, 'Malliavin calculus for signatures with applications to finance'] Fix $\vartheta \geq 0$ and a letter ${\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{i}}} \in A$. We define the operators 
    ${\bf J}_{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{i}}}}^\vartheta \colon \eTA[d+1] \to \eTA[d+1]$ 
    and 
    ${\bf \Lambda}_{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{i}}}} \colon \eTA[d+1] \to \eTA[d+1]$ 
    by
\begin{align*}
    &{\bf J}_{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{i}}}}^\vartheta\colon
    \sum_{n \ge 0}\sum_{|{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}| = n} \bm{\ell}^{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}} {\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}
    \mapsto 
    \sum_{n \ge 0}\sum_{|{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}| = n} 
        e^{-|{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}|_{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{i}}}}\,\vartheta}\,
        \bm{\ell}^{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}} {\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}, 
    \\
    &{\bf \Lambda}_{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{i}}}}\colon
    \sum_{n \ge 0}\sum_{|{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}| = n} \bm{\ell}^{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}} {\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}
    \mapsto 
    \sum_{n \ge 0}\sum_{|{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}| = n}
        |{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}|_{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{i}}}}\,
        \bm{\ell}^{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}} {\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}},
\end{align*}
where $|{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}|_{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{i}}}}$ denotes the number of occurrences of the letter ${\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{i}}}$ in the word ${\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}$.

body: Let L/K be a finite Galois extension with Galois group G = Gal(L/K). There is an inclusion-reversing bijection between subgroups H of G and intermediate fields K <= E <= L, given by H -> Fix(H) (the fixed field of H) and E -> Gal(L/E), and these two maps are mutually inverse. Under this correspondence [L:E] = |Gal(L/E)| and [E:K] equals the index [G : Gal(L/E)]. A subgroup H is normal in G if and only if the corresponding field E = Fix(H) is itself Galois over K, in which case Gal(E/K) is isomorphic to the quotient group G/H.
title: Fundamental theorem of Galois theory

[Proposition 10 of arXiv:2608.30859, 'Conservation Laws with Discontinuous Flux:\\ A First Application to Traffic Flow'] Let $f,g$ be as in Assumption \ref{assump}.
Let $u^\flat(t, x)$ and $u^\sharp(t, x)$ be the solutions to the Cauchy problems \eqref{eq:sys_ub}-\eqref{eq:sys_ud} with $\bar u(0+)=u^+$. Then, there exists a time $t_0>0$ and a constant $M>0$ such that, given any curve $x(t)$ satisfying \eqref{eq:propx}, denoting
\[
u^\flat(t)=u^\flat(t,x(t)), 
\qquad 
u^\sharp(t)=u^\sharp(t,x(t)) \quad \text{with} \quad x(t) \in \Gamma_M \quad \text{as} \quad \eqref{eq:gammaM},
\]
the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The functions $u^\flat(t)$ and $u^\sharp(t)$ have bounded variation on $[0, t_0]$:
\begin{equation}
    TV_{t \in [0, t_0]} (u^\flat(t))+TV_{t \in [0, t_0]} (u^\sharp(t)) \le C \cdot  TV(\bar u (x)),
\end{equation}
where $\bar u(x)$ is the initial data in \eqref{eq:sys_ub} and $\eqref{eq:sys_ud}$ and $C>0$ is a universal constant.
    \item There exists a constant $\mathfrak C=\mathfrak C (|u^+-u^-|)>0$ such that
    \[
|u^\flat(t)-u^\sharp(t)| \;\ge\; \mathfrak C
\qquad \text{for all } t\in[0,t_0].
\]
\item The function $H(t, x(t))$ in \eqref{eq:H}, associated to the Cauchy problem \eqref{eq:Yode}, has bounded variation on $[0,t_0]$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 11 (Local \(L^1\)-convergence) of arXiv:2608.16256, 'Error Distribution of the Local Linearization Method for Stochastic Differential Equations'] \label[lemma]{le:C1toconpro}
Let \(T>0\), and let \(Y^n\) and \(Y\) be measurable
\(\mathbb R^d\)-valued processes on \([0,T]\).  Let
\(h:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be continuous.  Assume that
\[
    \sup_{s\le T}|Y_s^n-Y_s|
    \xrightarrow{P}0
\]
and
\[
    \lim_{\rho\uparrow\infty}
    \limsup_{n\to\infty}
    \Prob*{P}{
        \sup_{s\le T}
        (|Y_s^n|\vee |Y_s|)>\rho
    }
    =
    0 .
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
    \int_0^T |h(Y_s^n)-h(Y_s)|\,ds
    \xrightarrow{P}0 .
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\[
    \sup_{t\le T}
    \left|
        \int_0^t h(Y_s^n)\,ds
        -
        \int_0^t h(Y_s)\,ds
    \right|
    \xrightarrow{P}0 .
\]
title: Local \(L^1\)-convergence

body:
[Proposition eq:residual-mixed-set of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[proposition]{prop:bulk-sparse-reduction}
Let \(V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be Borel measurable and bounded below, and let
\(0<r_N\le1\) and \(1\le k_N\le N\) be arbitrary deterministic
sequences.  Write
\[
 D_{N,r_N}
 =\{x\in\mathbb S^{N-1}(1):\left\lVertx\right\rVert_\infty\le r_N\}
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal A_N(k_N,\rho)
 =\left\{x\in\mathbb S^{N-1}(1):
 \text{some \(S\subset[N]\), \(\left\lvertS\right\rvert\le k_N\), satisfies }
 \norm{x_{S^c}}_2\le\rho\right\}.
\]
For \(\rho>0\), define the residual mixed-profile set
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal R_N(r_N,k_N,\rho)
 :=
 \left\{x\in\mathbb S^{N-1}(1):
 \left\lVertx\right\rVert_\infty>r_N,\ 
 \inf_{\substack{S\subset[N]\\|S|\le k_N}}
 \norm{x_{S^c}}_2>\rho\right\}.
\end{equation}
Then the disjoint decomposition
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb S^{N-1}(1)
 =D_{N,r_N}\,\dot\cup\,
  \bigl(\mathcal A_N(k_N,\rho)\setminus D_{N,r_N}\bigr)
  \,\dot\cup\,\mathcal R_N(r_N,k_N,\rho)
\end{equation}
holds.  Suppose only that the exact bulk slice satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
 \log\mathscr C_N^J(V;D_{N,r_N})
 =:\Phi\in\mathbb R.
\end{equation}
No independence, moment matching, tail, density, or nondegeneracy
condition is needed for the decomposition itself.
For \(\rho>0\), set
\begin{align*}
 \mathscr S_N(\rho)
 &:=
 \mathscr C_N^J\bigl(
 V;\mathcal A_N(k_N,\rho)\setminus D_{N,r_N}\bigr),\\
 \mathscr R_N(\rho)
 &:=
 \mathscr C_N^J\bigl(
 V;\mathcal R_N(r_N,k_N,\rho)\bigr),
\end{align*}
and define
\begin{align}
 \overline\Phi_{\rm sp}^J(V;r_\bullet,k_\bullet)
 &:=
 \lim_{\rho\downarrow0}\limsup_{N\to\infty}
 \frac1N\log\mathscr S_N(\rho),
 \\
 \overline\Phi_{\rm mix}^J(V;r_\bullet,k_\bullet)
 &:=
 \lim_{\rho\downarrow0}\limsup_{N\to\infty}
 \frac1N\log\mathscr R_N(\rho).
 
\end{align}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathscr C_N^J(V)
 =
 \max\left\{
 \Phi,\,
 \overline\Phi_{\rm sp}^J(V;r_\bullet,k_\bullet),\,
 \overline\Phi_{\rm mix}^J(V;r_\bullet,k_\bullet)
 \right\}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, exact universality holds if and only if both nonbulk
upper exponents are at most \(\Phi\).

If \(k_N=o(N)\), \(({\rm PT})_p\), and
(equation eq:critical-count-ceiling of the paper) also hold, then
\begin{equation}
 \overline\Phi_{\rm sp}^J(V;r_\bullet,k_\bullet)
 \le\Xi_p^{\rm sp}(V).
\end{equation}
In particular, whenever the explicit sparse-rate compatibility condition
\begin{equation}
 \Xi_p^{\rm sp}(V)\le\Phi
\end{equation}
holds, exact universality is equivalent to the single residual condition
\begin{equation}
 \overline\Phi_{\rm mix}^J(V;r_\bullet,k_\bullet)
 \le\Phi.
\end{equation}
When the disorder and \(V\) satisfy the hypotheses of
(thm:growing-point-cutoff of the paper), and
(equation eq:growing-Haar-zero-cost-condition of the paper) and
\(q_N^{\rm gr}\to0\) hold, that theorem supplies the corresponding
universal regularized bulk pressure.  Controlling its one-sided
de-regularization defects is one sufficient route to
(equation eq:exact-growing-bulk-slice of the paper), with
\(\Phi=\Phi_p^{\rm bulk}(V)\).

body: [Proposition prop:averagecasecounterexample of arXiv:2507.01236, 'Disintegration theorem for multifunctions, \\ with applications to empirical Wasserstein d'] Consider the example $(\mathfrak{X}, d, \mu)$ in Proposition (prop:counterexample of the paper). Then $(\mathfrak{X},d,\mu)$ is not $(n,\epsilon,r)$-average case approximable for any $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $r < 1-q$ and $\epsilon<1$. In particular, $(\mathfrak{X},d,\mu)$ is not asymptotically average-case approximable for any rate.

$C>0$ such that, for every $\va\in(0,\va_1)$ and every
$
u\in\mathcal D\cap\V(0,\ell,\delta;\va)
$
satisfying
$
\|\mathcal R_u-r_\infty\|_{C^0(\Omega)}<\va
$
and
$
\int_\Omega u^{\frac{2n}{n-2}}\,\ud x=1,
$
we have
\[
\begin{aligned}
&-C\mathfrak G(u)^2
-C\bm\Lambda
-C\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}\lambda_k^{2-n}\leq
Y_\Omega(u)-r_\infty\leq
C
\mathfrak G(u)^2
+C\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}\lambda_k^{2-n},
\end{aligned}
\]
where $\mathfrak G(u)$ is defined in \eqref{eq:Gu}. If, in addition, $Y_\Omega(u)\geq r_\infty$, then
\be
\begin{aligned}
\bm\Lambda + \|w\|^2
\leq{}&
C\mathfrak G(u)^2
+C\sum_{k=1}^{\ell}\lambda_k^{2-n}.
\end{aligned}
\ee

[Lem 2.7 of arXiv:2412.00708, 'Stochastic PDE approach to fluctuating interfaces'] The Sturm-Liouville operator is modified as $\mathcal{A} = -\big(\partial_z^2
+ c\partial_z+ f'(U_0(z))\big)$.  The function $U_0'(z)$ is the eigenfunction 
of $\mathcal{A}$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $0$,
and $\mathcal{A}$ is symmetric in the space $L^2({\mathbb{R}}, e^{cz}dz)$.
title: Lem 2.7 of arXiv:2412.00708

body:
[Lemma lem:GLPP-kernel of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] We have
\[
\mathbb{P}\Bigl(\bigcap_{i=1}^k
\{G(m_i, n) < a_i\}\Bigr)
= \det(I - K_{n, \mathbf{m}, \mathbf{a}})
_{\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})},
\]
where
\[
K_{n, \mathbf{m}, \mathbf{a}}(x, x')
= \sum_{1 \le j \le i \le k}
  \sum_{r \ge a_i} \sum_{r' \ge a_j}
   \psi_{n, m_i, r}(x)
  \bigl[\delta_{ij}\delta_{r,r'}
  + [B_{\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{m}}]_{ij}(r, r')\bigr]
  \phi_{n, m_j, r'}(x').
\]
This identifies $K_{n, \mathbf{m}, \mathbf{a}}$ with the
kernel~(equation eq:K-def of the paper) on the product graph
$\mathcal{G}^k$, with $\psi, \phi$ as the seed data and
$B_{\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{m}}$ as the propagator.

		\begin{description}
			\leftskip=0.3in
			\item[Kolmogorov-Chenstov criteria:] If $P \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^T)$ and \ \[\exists a,b,C \in \mathbb{R}_+^*, \forall (s,t) \in T^2, \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} |x-y|^b P^{s,t}(dx,dy) \leq C |t-s|^{1+a},\] then $P$ is concentrated on continuous paths.
			\item[Kolmogorov tightness criteria:] If $(P_n)_{n \geq 1} \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}(T,\mathbb{R}))^{\mathbb{N}^*}$ and \ \[\exists a,b,C \in \mathbb{R}_+^*, \forall (s,t) \in T^2, \sup_{n \geq 1} \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} |x-y|^b P_n^{s,t}(dx,dy) \leq C |t-s|^{1+a},\] then $(P_n)_{n \geq 1}$ is tight for the weak convergence.

## Printed statement and locator

Li-Zhang-Arora, Why Are Convolutional Nets More Sample-Efficient than Fully-Connected Nets?, arXiv:2010.08515v2 (4May2021), AppendixD.6, LemmaD.8, printed p21 (PDFpage21), states

    E_(x~N(0,I_d)) [(x^T M x)^2]
       = ||(M+M^T)/2||_F^2 + (tr M)^2.

The rendered page papers/lemmaD8_page.png was visually inspected, not just OCR: neither the displayed lemma nor the last proof line includes a factor2 multiplying the squared Frobenius term. The preceding expanded sum already contains the correct diagonal coefficient3.

## Smallest counterexample

Set d=1 and M=[1]. Then x^T M x=x^2, so the left side is E x^4=3. The printed right side is1+1=2. Every stated hypothesis is met: M is a real1-by-1 matrix and x is standard Gaussian. The mismatch also occurs in any d>=1 with M=e_1 e_1^T, so it does not depend on allowing d=1.

## Correct identity and proof

For every real d-by-d M and standard Gaussian x, put S=(M+M^T)/2. Since x^T(M-M^T)x=0 and trS=trM, diagonalize S=Q diag(lambda_i)Q^T. Rotational invariance makes z=Q^T x independent standard Gaussian coordinates. Therefore

    E (x^T M x)^2
      =3 sum_i lambda_i^2 +2 sum_(i<j) lambda_i lambda_j
      =2 sum_i lambda_i^2 +(sum_i lambda_i)^2
      =2||S||_F^2 +(trM)^2.

Only finite sums occur; E z_i^4=3 and E z_i^2 z_j^2=1 for i!=j. Gaussian moments can be obtained by integration by parts: E Z^4=3E Z^2=3, the boundary terms being polynomials times exp(-z^2/2), hence0. Skew M gives S=0 and both sides0; no denominator or nonzero-matrix assumption is used.

## Source normalization affected

The same page uses LemmaD.8 to assert, for M with d^2 IID standard Gaussian entries, E_M E_x (x^T M x)^2=d(d+3)/2. Directly conditioning on x instead gives

    E_M (x^T M x)^2 = sum_(i,j) x_i^2 x_j^2 =||x||^4,
    E_x ||x||^4 =3d+d(d-1)=d(d+2).

Thus the normalization calculation is affected as well, separately from the algebra/interpolation discrepancy already recorded in SOURCE-004. This note does NOT propose a replacement for the entire Theorem5.4 or assert that its remaining lower-bound proof is repaired. Its Omega(d^2) order may survive with corrected constants.

## Model assumptions for the previous counterexample

Theorem5.4 on the same page explicitly takes targets sum_i alpha_i x_i^2; its proof explicitly identifies the O(d) orbit with sum_(i,j) beta_ij x_i x_j. Neither introduces affine terms or a constant offset. Definition3.2 permits arbitrary function-valued orthogonally equivariant learners, so the minimum-Frobenius-norm least-squares learner of SOURCE-004 is within its quantified algorithm class. 		Let $A$ be an $H$-supralgebra on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$. Suppose $A$

body:
[Proposition 20 (\textsf{Exact four-moment counterexample}) of arXiv:2608.12451, '2608.12451'] Let $\eps_1, \eps_2, \eps_3$, $\eps_a$, $\eps_b$, $\eps_c$, and
$\eps_d$   be i.i.d. symmetric
Rademacher random variables. 
Define
\[
 Q_\triangle
 :=\eps_1\eps_2
 +\eps_1\eps_3
 +\eps_2\eps_3
 \AND
  Q_\square
 :=\eps_a\eps_b
 +\eps_b\eps_c
 +\eps_c\eps_d
 +\eps_d\eps_a.
\]
Take four independent copies of $Q_\triangle$ and three independent
copies of $Q_\square$, and set their independent sums to be
\noi
\begin{align}
 F:=\sum_{j=1}^4Q_{\triangle,j}
   +\sum_{j=1}^3Q_{\square,j}.
 \notag
\end{align}
Then, $F$ belongs to the second Rademacher chaos
and satisfies 

 
\noi
\begin{align}
 \frac{F+24}{2}\in\N_0
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \E[(F+24)^k]=\E[P_{24}^k],
 \qquad 1\leq k\leq4,
  \notag
\end{align}
where $P_{24}\sim\Pois(24)$.  Moreover,

\noi
\begin{align}
 \dTV\bigl(\cL(F+24),\Pois(24)\bigr)
 \geq\frac{1-e^{-48}}2.
 \notag
\end{align}

[Proposition of arXiv:2609.04101, 'Endpoint Estimates for Stein's Purely Quadratic Carleson Operator'] For large $M$ and $B\geq1$, define $\mathbf{A}(M,B,c)$ to be
	the union of Bohr sets over  $B$ many dyadic consequetive frequencies that are greater than $ M $ by the formula 
	\[ \mathbf{A}(M,B,c) \coloneqq \bigcup_{ k \in 2^{\mathbb{N}}, \; \log(k) \in [M,M+B)} \mathbf{B}\left (k,c\right ). \] Then, if $c \in (0,10^{-10})$ we have the following lower bound on $\mathbf{A}(M,B,c)$   \[\left| \mathbf{A}(M,B,c)\right|   \gtrsim \frac{(Bc)^2}{ (Bc)^2+Bc  }.\]   In particular, when  $c \gtrsim B^{-1}$ we have a uniform lower bound on $\mathbf{A}(M,B,c)$, namely $\left|\mathbf{A}(M,B,c) \right|\gtrsim 1.$

Li-Nica-Roy Proposition A.6 small-jump estimate, with conditional uniformity stated explicitly. Fix a dimension d, p,delta>0, h_n=n^(-2p), and a Markov transition increment Delta_n(y)=h_n*B_n(y)+sqrt(h_n)*sigma_n(y)*xi_n+h_n*n^(-delta)*R_n(y). The displayed random quantities refer to the one-step transition law conditional on the current state y; sigma_n(y) is deterministic. Fix q>2. For every radius R<infinity assume sup_{n,||y||<=R} (E[||B_n(y)||^q | y]+E[||xi_n||^q | y]+E[||R_n(y)||^q | y]+||sigma_n(y)||_op^q)<infinity. No independence between the within-step random terms is required for this estimate. Then, uniformly on ||y||<=R, h_n^(-1) E[||Delta_n(y)||^q | y] <= C_R,q h_n^(q/2-1). Consequently for every epsilon>0, h_n^(-1)*P(||Delta_n(y)||>epsilon | y) <= C_R,q*epsilon^(-q)*h_n^(q/2-1), and h_n^(-1)*E[||Delta_n(y)||^2*1_{||Delta_n(y)||>epsilon} | y] <= C_R,q*epsilon^(2-q)*h_n^(q/2-1). Both quantities tend to zero. This is the vanishing-large-jump/Lindeberg step of source AppendixA equationA.12, not a full path-convergence theorem.
Fixed dimension and p,delta>0; conditional one-step moments uniformly bounded on each compact set as stated.
Additional conditional mean/covariance and coefficient convergence assumptions appear explicitly in the characteristics lemma.

[Own-work draft: T407-JOINT-005 v1, proof (unaudited). Independent audit pending; priority unestablished.] Candidate joint-flow regime for q=2: a shared square-activation CNN with h=p(p+1)/2 spanning filters and patch-specific trainable readout learns every sum of k local quadratic forms from n=k h noiseless Gaussian samples, to any positive population squared error at finite data-dependent time, almost surely. Both layers are jointly trained with positive rates; the filter rate is explicitly data-dependent. Gaussian initialization of both layers is allowed, since the h rank-one filters span Sym(p) almost surely. Normalized squared-loss constant-risk/confidence lower bounds are Omega(kp^2) for arbitrary local learners and Omega((kp)^2) for equivariant learners, via the unit-sphere coefficient prior. Assumptions and scope: p,k>=1 integers, n>=k p(p+1)/2; independent standard Gaussian patches; noiseless arbitrary symmetric local quadratics; shared square-activation filters with spanning initialization; arbitrary finite readout initialization; positive data-dependent filter gradient-flow rate; no uniform runtime or discrete-SGD guarantee; lower class has unit L2 target norm and epsilon+4delta<1.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:7c7b624336aee0da6c2ac36239d4ba12095cf83c0c7ce2dd893abe4e5327d4d6","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/7c/7c7b624336aee0da6c2ac36239d4ba12095cf83c0c7ce2dd893abe4e5327d4d6.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:7ec281326ff9ffe04dd32578e791dbc62e6252a328dc7729dc70836c5629daa1","bundle_entry_key":"draft-joint-quadratic-flow","bundle_id":"population.t407-draft-quadratic-source-correction-and-joint-flow","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"statistical learning theory","draft":"w693/bundle_003.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.sample_complexity:draft-joint-quadratic-flow-w693","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Target 3: joint quadratic CNN gradient flow in a stated regime

Rung: proof (unaudited); priority unestablished. This is a concrete positive-filter-rate gradient-flow regime, not a theorem about equal learning rates, discrete SGD, or uniform running time. The source Theorem 5.4 printed constant is not used (see T407-SOURCE-004).

## Model and claim

Let p,k>=1 be integers, d=kp, h=p(p+1)/2 and D=kh. Inputs X=(x_1,...,x_k) have independent x_j~N(0,I_p). Targets are f_star(X)=sum_j x_j^T M_j x_j with arbitrary symmetric p by p matrices M_j. Consider the shared-filter square-activation CNN
  f_(W,A)(X)=sum_(j=1)^k sum_(r=1)^h A_(r,j)(w_r^T x_j)^2,
where W=(w_1,...,w_h) and ALL entries of W and A are trained jointly. Let W_0 have its rank-one matrices w_r w_r^T spanning Sym(p). This holds almost surely for h independent Gaussian filters; the explicit bank e_i and e_i+e_l (i<l) is a deterministic example. A_0 can be arbitrary finite, including independent Gaussian initialization.

There is an explicit strictly positive, sample-dependent filter learning rate eta, with readout learning rate one, such that joint gradient flow on half the squared empirical residual norm converges to the true function from n>=D noiseless Gaussian observations almost surely. A computable residual threshold gives any prescribed population squared error epsilon>0 in finite sample-dependent time. Thus at every stated confidence 1-delta, D=kp(p+1)/2=O(kp^2) samples suffice in this joint-flow regime. Setting eta=0 gives the simpler second-layer-only statement.

For L2-normalized target classes, any learner of local quadratics needs at least (1-epsilon-4delta)_+ D samples at confidence 1-delta and squared error epsilon. Any orthogonally equivariant learner needs at least (1-epsilon-4delta)_+ d(d+1)/2 samples for this same local target family. For example epsilon=1/4 and delta=1/16 give lower bounds D/2 and d(d+1)/4, respectively. These are matching orders at fixed risk/confidence: kp^2 versus (kp)^2 when p is fixed. The generic full-quadratic least-squares learner achieves the latter dimension order and is equivariant. Exact risk normalization is specified below.

## 1. Finite feature space and Gaussian rank

Use an orthonormal symmetric-matrix vectorization svec, so z(x)=svec(xx^T), theta_j=svec(M_j), and x^T M_j x=<theta_j,z(x)>. The local feature vector phi(X) concatenates k such z vectors and has dimension D. Let Phi be the n by D feature design.

For n>=D, Phi has full column rank almost surely. Its determinant for D rows is a polynomial not identically zero: use k blocks of h witness inputs, with only one patch nonzero in each block; in that patch use e_i and e_i+e_l. The local evaluation matrix has diagonal-coordinate pivots 1 and off-diagonal pivots sqrt(2), after subtracting diagonal rows. Its determinant is nonzero. Gaussian absolute continuity then makes a rank failure a null event. The same polynomial witness proves that h Gaussian filters give an invertible matrix
  B(W)=[svec(w_1w_1^T),...,svec(w_hw_h^T)]
almost surely. This is a rank argument, not a concentration assertion.

Write b(W)=I_k tensor B(W), and stack A to a vector a. The network coefficient vector is theta=b(W)a. Every network output lies in the same D-dimensional local quadratic space, for every W,A. Let S=||Phi||_op and sigma=sigma_min(Phi)>0.

## 2. Explicit positive filter rate

Put M=||W_0||_F, gamma=sigma_min(B(W_0))>0, L=2M+1,
  rho=min{1,gamma/(2L)}, beta=gamma/2, C_B=(M+1)^2, lambda=beta^2 sigma^2.
For ||W-W_0||_F<=rho, the identity
  ||ww^T-vv^T||_F <= (||w||+||v||)||w-v||
gives ||B(W)-B(W_0)||_op<=L||W-W_0||_F<=gamma/2. Therefore sigma_min B(W)>=beta, ||B(W)||_op<=C_B, and max_r||w_r||<=M+1 throughout that ball.

Let e_0=Phi b(W_0)a_0-y and E=||e_0||. If E=0, Phi's full rank implies theta_0=theta_star and all gradients vanish; population error is already zero. Set eta=1 in this trivial branch. Otherwise define
  C_A=||a_0||+C_B S E/lambda >0,
  eta=min{1, rho lambda/[4 S(M+1) C_A E]} >0.
All quantities depend only on observed inputs/labels and initial weights. There is no access to unknown target coefficients and no population-distance oracle.

## 3. Joint flow and bootstrap

For loss L_emp(W,a)=||e||^2/2, e=Phi b(W)a-y, use
  dot a=-gradient_a L_emp,
  dot W=-eta gradient_W L_emp.
Let J_a=Phi b(W), and let J_W be the output Jacobian with respect to W. Then
  d(||e||^2/2)/dt=-||J_a^T e||^2-eta||J_W^T e||^2.
Since e=Phi(theta-theta_star) lies in range(Phi), whenever W remains in the ball,
  ||J_a^T e||^2 >= beta^2||Phi^T e||^2 >= lambda||e||^2.
Thus ||e(t)||<=E exp(-lambda t).

Also ||dot a||<=C_B S||e||, so ||a(t)||<=C_A before any exit. For a perturbation Delta W, each patch coefficient perturbation is sum_r A_(r,j)(w_r Delta w_r^T+Delta w_r w_r^T); Cauchy-Schwarz yields
  ||D_W theta[Delta W]|| <=2(M+1)||a|| ||Delta W||_F.
Hence ||J_W||_op<=2S(M+1)||a||, and
  ||W(t)-W_0||_F <= eta 2S(M+1)C_A integral_0^t ||e(u)||du
  <=eta 2S(M+1)C_A E/lambda <=rho/2.
A first exit at radius rho is impossible, because the bound there would be only rho/2. The bounds therefore hold for all time. The polynomial vector field is locally Lipschitz and all parameters remain bounded, so its solution exists globally; no finite-time explosion is possible. Both parameter blocks use their actual gradients with strictly positive fixed learning rates. No conditional probabilities are multiplied in this deterministic bootstrap.

## 4. Population risk and stopping time

For block-diagonal Delta M formed from coefficient error Delta theta,
  E[(X^T Delta M X)^2]=2||Delta M||_F^2+(tr Delta M)^2
  <=(d+2)||Delta theta||^2.
The Gaussian moment identity uses E X_i^4=3, E X_i^2 X_l^2=1 for i!=l, and vanishing odd moments. Phi's full rank gives ||Delta theta||<=||e||/sigma. Therefore
  R_pop(t) <= (d+2)E^2 exp(-2lambda t)/sigma^2.
Stop when the observed empirical residual satisfies ||e(t)||^2<=epsilon sigma^2/(d+2), or at the explicit time max{0,log((d+2)E^2/(sigma^2 epsilon))/(2lambda)} when E>0. This is finite for every full-rank sample and spanning initial W. The theorem makes no uniform bound on this random time: rare ill-conditioned designs or initial filters can force a tiny eta and a long run. No simulation or model training is part of the proof.

## 5. Correct dimension lower bounds without the source's bad constant

For any finite-dimensional quadratic function space V of dimension q, equipped with its L2(Gaussian) inner product, choose an orthonormal basis psi_1,...,psi_q. For the local space q=D; for all homogeneous symmetric quadratics q=Q=d(d+1)/2. The covariance of the unwhitened symmetric coefficients is positive definite, because
  E (X^T M X)^2=2||M||_F^2+(tr M)^2>0 for M!=0,
so this orthonormal basis exists and all target coefficients below are valid quadratics.

Put a uniform prior on coefficient xi in the unit sphere S^(q-1). Every target f_xi=sum xi_i psi_i has L2 norm exactly one. Conditional on the input sample, its n noiseless labels reveal only the projection of xi on the row span of the evaluation matrix. That row span has rank r<=n and is independent of xi before seeing labels. By reflection symmetry on its orthogonal complement, the posterior mean is precisely the observed projection. Among arbitrary output functions, the posterior mean target minimizes squared prediction risk. Its Bayes risk, averaged over labels and inputs, is E||xi-P_row xi||^2=1-r/q>=1-n/q (and zero is the trivial bound for n>=q). This gives minimax expected squared risk >=(1-n/q)_+; it is a known spherical-prior dimension argument, not a new statistical principle.

For confidence bounds, postprocess any learner by projecting its output into V in L2 and then clipping its coefficient norm to the unit ball. This does not increase squared error against any unit-norm target and bounds that error by four. If an output is not in L2, map it to zero: it could not have finite error against a target in V on a successful event. A uniform guarantee risk<=epsilon with probability >=1-delta would thus imply average risk <=epsilon+4delta. Therefore n>=q(1-epsilon-4delta), whenever the factor is positive. This is an inequality for real n, so the actual integer sample requirement is its ceiling.

The local class includes all diagonal quadratics. Every full homogeneous quadratic is an orthogonal rotation of a diagonal one, and its L2 norm is preserved by Gaussian rotation. For an equivariant learner, a uniform guarantee on the normalized local class therefore implies the same guarantee on the entire normalized full quadratic class. Apply the preceding q=Q Bayes lower bound. For an arbitrary local learner use q=D. Conversely D or Q Gaussian observations give exact coefficient recovery by local or full least squares, respectively; full least squares with minimum Frobenius-norm tie-breaking is orthogonally equivariant even on singular datasets.

## Scope and audit points

This covers arbitrary p,k with a finite shared filter bank, Gaussian or explicit spanning initialization, both parameter blocks trained jointly, noiseless labels, and a sample-dependent strictly positive filter learning rate. It does not cover fixed equal learning rates, ordinary discrete SGD, noisy labels, or q>2. The case p=1 is included. E=0 is handled before any division by E. The full-rank event and gamma>0 hold almost surely but no deterministic lower bound on conditioning is claimed. Source 2006.15459, Section 2 Equation (1), fixes second-layer weights; 1712.09203 treats a PSD factorization teacher. [Lemma 38 of arXiv:2604.00630, 'The contact process on a bipartite spatial network'] Let
\begin{align*}
	\mathcal J = &\left\{(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,a): \gamma_1 \ge \frac12,\;\gamma_2 \le \frac{\gamma_1}{1+\gamma_1} \right\} \\
	&\cup \left\{ (\gamma_1,\gamma_2,a): \gamma_1 \ge \frac12,\;\frac{\gamma_1}{1+\gamma_1} \le \gamma_2 \le \frac12,\; a \le \frac{\gamma_1-\gamma_2}{\gamma_2-\gamma_1+\gamma_1\gamma_2}\right\}.
\end{align*}
We have
\[\mu_\star \le  1+ \bar{\gamma}_2 \nu_\star \quad \text{if }(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,a) \in \mathcal J\]
and
\[\mu_\star \ge  1+ \bar{\gamma}_2 \nu_\star\quad \text{if }(\gamma_1,\gamma_2,a) \in (\mathcal S \times (0,\infty)) \backslash \mathcal J.\]
title: Lemma 38 of arXiv:2604.00630

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.30073, 'A remark on the fourth order Q curvature on manifolds with dimension at least 5'] Let $\left( M^{n},g\right) $ be a smooth compact Riemannian
manifold with dimension $n\geq 5$ and $Y\left( g\right) >0$. Then we have

\begin{enumerate}
\item $Y_{4}\left( g\right) >0\Longleftrightarrow \exists \widetilde{g}\in 
\left[ g\right] $ s.t. $\widetilde{R}>0$ and $\widetilde{Q}>0.$

\item $Y_{4}\left( g\right) =0\Longleftrightarrow \exists \widetilde{g}\in 
\left[ g\right] $ s.t. $\widetilde{R}>0$ and $\widetilde{Q}=0.$

\item $Y_{4}\left( g\right) <0\Longleftrightarrow \exists \widetilde{g}\in 
\left[ g\right] $ s.t. $\widetilde{R}>0$ and $\widetilde{Q}<0.$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma l:holder-regularity of arXiv:2607.24640, 'The Yang-Mills measure on surfaces via Morse theory'] Let $\gamma$ be an admissible curve and let $\psi\in L^\infty(\Sigma,\mathbb{R})$ that is continuous on the support of $[\blacktriangle(\gamma([0,t]))]$. Then, the function
$$
t\in[0,1]\mapsto \int_{\Sigma}[\blacktriangle(\gamma([0,t]))]\psi\upsilon 
$$
is continuous and of class $\mathcal{C}^1$ outside finitely many points $t_1<t_2\ldots <t_M$ where $\gamma(t_m)\in W^u(a)$ for some critical point of index $1$. Moreover, near every $t_m$ with $1\leq m\leq M$, one has
$$
\partial_t\int_{\Sigma}[\blacktriangle(\gamma([0,t]))]\psi\upsilon=\mathcal{O}(|\ln |t-t_m||),\ \text{as}\ t\rightarrow t_m,
$$
where the constant in the remainder depends on $\psi$, $\gamma$, $\upsilon$ and $f$. Finally, if $\gamma$ is $V$-oriented and has no type $\operatorname{III}$ elementary curve, then there exists a constant $c_\gamma>0$ such that
$$
\forall t\in[0,1]\setminus\{t_1,\ldots,t_M\},\quad \left|\partial_t\int_{\Sigma}[\blacktriangle(\gamma([0,t]))]\upsilon\right|\geq c_\gamma
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma l:holder-regularity of arXiv:2607.24640

Then, for all $n\geq 0$ and for all non-negative functions $F$ and $G$, it holds that
 \[{\mathbf E}\bigg[\sum_{u\in \tau}{\mathbf 1}_{\left\{|u|=n\right\}}F(\operatorname{Cut}_u \tau,u)G(\theta_u\tau)\bigg]=m_\mu^n\, {\mathbf E}\big[F(\operatorname{Cut}_{U_n} \tau_\infty,U_n)\big]\, {\mathbf E}\big[G(\tau)\big].\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma l2 of arXiv:2412.04015, 'Linear fluctuation of interfaces in Glauber-Kawasaki dynamics'] Fix $1\le j\le d$. Then, there exists a finite constant
${\mathfrak c}({\boldsymbol u}^N)$ such that
\begin{equation*}
\begin{aligned}
& \int h \, [\omega_x - \omega_{x+e_j}]\, f\; d\nu^N
\;\leq\; \beta  \, I^E_{x,x+e_j}(f)
\;+\;  \frac{{\mathfrak c}({\boldsymbol u}^N)}{\beta}  \, \int h^2 \, f  \; d\nu^N 
\\
&\quad \;-\;
[{\boldsymbol u}^N(x+e_j) - {\boldsymbol u}^N(x)] \,
\int  h(\eta)  \, A_x(\eta)  \,  f(\eta)  \; d\nu^N
\;+\;  \beta\, {\mathfrak c} ({\boldsymbol u}^N)\, [{\boldsymbol u}^N(x+e_j) - {\boldsymbol u}^N(x)]^4
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
for all $\beta >0$, $x \in {\mathbb T}^d_N$, $h\colon \Omega_N \to {\mathbb R}$ such that
$h(T^{x,x+e_j}\eta) = h(\eta)$ for all $\eta \in \Omega_N$, and
density $f\colon \Omega_N \to [0,\infty)$ with respect to $\nu^N$.

[Theorem 3 (OU covariance of Gaussian density ratios) of arXiv:2607.07712, 'Parameter-Space Heat Flow, Gaussian Density Ratios, and Sharp Hermite Truncation Rates'] Let \(u\in\mathbb R^d\) and let \(S=S^T\) satisfy \(I+S>0\).
Interpreting \(T_t\) as the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck Markov semigroup acting on
density ratios with respect to \(\gamma_d\), one has
\begin{equation}
T_tK_{u,S}
=
K_{e^{-t}u,e^{-2t}S},
\qquad t\ge0,

\end{equation}
in \(L^1(\gamma_d)\). If in addition \(\|S\|_{\mathrm{op}}<1\), then the
identity also holds in \(L^2(\gamma_d)\) and agrees with the Hermite spectral
action of \(T_t=e^{-tN}\).

In particular, in the isotropic heating parametrization \(S=\sigma^2I\),
\[
T_tK_{u,\sigma}
=
K_{e^{-t}u,e^{-t}\sigma}.
\]

[Definition 8 of arXiv:2608.29972, '\bf Cram\'er transform, half-space depth and threshold phenomena for convex bodies'] \rm Let $K$ be a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and let $\Phi:\operatorname{int}(K)\to\mathbb{R}$. We say that $\Phi$ is a
barrier for $K$ if
$$\Phi(x)\longrightarrow+\infty,\qquad\text{as }\,x\longrightarrow\partial K.$$
If $\Phi$ is $C^3$, we say that it is self-concordant if, for every $x\in\operatorname{int}(K)$ and every $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$\left|\nabla^3\Phi(x)[v,v,v]\right|\leq 2\left\langle\nabla^2\Phi(x)v,v\right\rangle^{3/2}.$$
Furthermore, $\Phi$ is called $\alpha$-self-concordant if, in addition, for every $x\in\operatorname{int}(K)$ and every $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$\langle\nabla\Phi(x),v\rangle^2\leq\alpha\left\langle\nabla^2\Phi(x)v,v\right\rangle.$$

[Theorem 10 of arXiv:2608.18557, 'Randomly Permuted Orthogonal Products and Fast Dimension Reduction'] Let \(A,B\in O(d)\), let $D_\xi \in \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$  be a Rademacher
	diagonal, and let \(\pi\) be an independent uniform permutation on

	\[

	\]

	\[
	\log \E_{\xi,\pi} \left ( e^{\lambda\langle y,Ux\rangle} \right )
	\le
	\frac{3\lambda^2}{2d} \qquad \text{for } |\lambda| \leq \frac{1}{\norm{A^{\mathsf T}y}_\infty
		\norm{Bx}_\infty}.
	\]

body:
[Ppn 44 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any fixed $C_9$, and any fixed $\gamma \in [1/C_9,C_9]$, we have
    \[
        \sup \Big\{ V_\gamma(\by) :\|\by\|^2=N\Big\}
         \le g(\gamma) + \frac{\epsilon'}{20}\,.
    \]
with probability at least $1-e^{-cN}$, where $c$ depends on $C_9$ and the parameters in Remark~\ref{r:fp-rpr}. 

\begin{proof}In this proof, we will set constants $\upsilon, \upsilon_1, \delta > 0$, where $\upsilon$ is sufficiently small depending on $C_9$, $\upsilon_1$ sufficiently small depending on $\upsilon,C_9$, and $\delta$ sufficiently small depending on $\upsilon_1,\upsilon,C_9$. That is,
\beq
    \delta \ll \upsilon_1 \ll \upsilon \ll \frac1{C_9}\,.
\eeq
Note that $C_9, \upsilon, \upsilon_1, \delta$ nonetheless depend on only the parameters in Remark~\ref{r:fp-rpr}.

Consider any local maximizer $\by$, and recall that $\dbA_\beta \equiv (\beta I_N-\dbD)^{-1}$.
By Lemma~\ref{l:fp-g-prep2}, $\by$ is of the form \eqref{e:fp-g-prep2-stationarity}, which we expand as
    \[
    \by
    =\dbA_\beta\bigg(\gamma^{1/2}\dbg
        +\sum_{j=1}^{r'}
        \frac{\hx_j}{M}(\tbmeta^j,\by)
        \tbmeta^j
        \bigg)
    =\dbA_\beta\sum_{j=0}^{r'} c_j \tbmeta^j\,.
    \]
For the last equality, we have defined $c_0\equiv \gamma^{1/2}$, $\tbmeta^0\equiv\dbg$, and 
    \[c_j\equiv \frac{\hx_j(\tbmeta^j, \by)}{M}\]
    for $1\le j\le r'$. With probability at least  $1-e^{-cN}$ (with $c$ an absolute constant), we have $\|\tbmeta^j\| \le 2\sqrt{N}$ for all $j \in 1[r']$, which implies 
        \[|c_j| \le \frac{2 |\hx_j|}{\alpha}
        \stackrel{\eqref{e:reduced-normalization}}{\le} \frac{4\alpha}{\iota}
        \]
for all $j\in[r']$. On this event, we have
\[
    \|\vc\|_\infty \le \max\bigg\{
        \gamma^{1/2}, \max\bigg\{
            \frac{2 |\hx_j|}{\alpha} : j\in [r']

[Corollary 14 of arXiv:2609.03962, '$L^p$ isomorphisms for the fractional Laplacian on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and their application'] Applying Hardy's inequality to $Du$ for $s-1\in(0,1)$ and the Calder\'on--Zygmund theorem, the following holds for $u\in C_{\mathrm{c}}^\infty(\R^n\setminus B_1)$:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $\Big\|\dfrac{u}{\rho\lg}\Big\|_{L^n(\R^n)}\lesssim\|Du\|_{L^p(\R^n)}\lesssim\|(-\triangle)^{1/2}\,u\|_{L^p(\R^n)}$.
        \item If $1<s<2$, $1<p<\infty$, $sp=n$, then
        $$\Big\|\frac{u}{\rho^s\lg}\Big\|_{L^p(\R^n)}\lesssim\Big\|\frac{Du}{\rho^{s-1}}\Big\|_{L^p(\R^n)}\lesssim\|\flap u\|_{L^p(\R^n)}.$$
    \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 84 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $\acute{Y}$ be a continuous local martingale started from $\acute{Y}(0)=1$, and let $\theta$ be a stopping time with $\E\langle \acute{Y}\rangle_\theta<\infty$. If $\E [(|{{\acute{Y}}}_\theta|-1)^2] \le\epsilon$, then $\E\langle \acute{Y}\rangle_\theta \le 4\epsilon^{1/2}$.

\begin{proof}
The process
$\acute{M}(t)\equiv \acute{Y}^2(t)-\langle\acute{Y} \rangle_t$ is a continuous local martingale. It follows from e.g.\ \cite[Thm.~4.13]{MR3497465} that the stopped process $\acute{M}(t\wedge\theta)$ is a uniformly integrable true martingale, so the optional stopping theorem gives
    \[
    \E\langle \acute{Y}\rangle_\theta
    = \E\Big[ (\acute{Y}_\theta)^2-1\Big]\,.
    \]
Combining with Lemma~\ref{l:quadratic.ineq} and the hypothesis gives
    \[
    \E\langle \acute{Y}\rangle_\theta
    \le 2\epsilon^{1/2}
    + \frac{2\E[(|\acute{Y}_\theta|-1)^2]}{\epsilon^{1/2}}
    \le 4\epsilon^{1/2}\,,
    \]
as claimed.
\end{proof}

Method: Exact recurrence, conditional-law calculation, or source-specific limiting obstruction Result: The proposed transfer through a near-critical binary scaling limit cannot rely merely on convergence in distribution: deterministic measurable functions of richer input fields can converge jointly to a variable with extra randomness. After the conditional residual-line reduction, the fixed-apex pair estimate for bounded-density subgaussian row submatrices rests on a single inequality, which is OPEN as of 2026-09-14: for overlap parameter $D \ge 3$, $\mathbb{E}_A\big[\operatorname{tr}(M_A^2)\big] \le C/D$, where $M_A = \mathbb{E}[v v^{\top} \mid A]$ is the conditional second-moment matrix of the residual null line. Perfect conditional isotropy $M_A = I_D/D$ gives $\operatorname{tr}(M_A^2) = 1/D$ exactly, so the target asserts that the conditional law of the residual null line is isotropic up to a constant factor, a statement about one matrix with no pair and no angle left in it. Note also the shape of the reduction: the singular near-parallel edge, where $|\rho| \to 1$, was closed as a SEPARATE lemma, leaving only this bulk quadratic estimate. When a bound fails only at an integrable singularity, proving the bulk and the edge as different lemmas is what reduces the obligation to one clean line.

[Dfn 3. dfn: effective resistance between sets of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{Effective resistance between sets}]  
  Fix a resistance form $(\mathcal{E}, \mathcal{F})$ on $F$
  and write $R$ for the corresponding resistance metric.
  For sets $A, B \subseteq F$,
  we define
  \begin{equation}
    R(A,B)
    \coloneqq
    \left(
    \inf\{
    \mathcal{E}(f,f):
    f \in \mathcal{F},\
    f|_{A} \equiv 1,\
    f|_{B} \equiv 0
    \}
    \right)^{-1},
  \end{equation}
  which is defined to be zero if the infimum is taken over the empty set.
  Note that by (4. dfn cond: resistance forms condition 4 of the paper) 
  we clearly have $R( \{x\}, \{y\}) = R(x,y)$.

There exists a constant $C>0$  (depending only on parameters and defined norms) such that for all $\eps\in(0,1)$ and any periodic observable $\varphi\in\bC^\gamma(\mT^d)$,
\begin{equation}
\sup_{t\geq0}\sup_{x\in\mR^d}
\Big|
\mE\big[\varphi(X_t^\eps(x)-\bar b\,t/\eps)\big]
-
\mE\big[\varphi(x+\cF t+\sqrt{2\cG}W_t)\big]
\Big|
\leq C\,\eps\|\varphi\|_{\bC^\gamma(\mT^d)}.
\end{equation}

body:
[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2511.02725, 'Mixing of general biased adjacent transposition chains'] Let $A=[i+1,n-j]$ and $A^c=[n]\setminus A = [i]\cup[n-j+1,n] $. 
    Let $\vell$ be $n$-admissible.
            For $b:A^c\to [n]$ that is $\vell$-localized, define the relabeling map $r_{b}:[n-i-j]\to [n]\bs b(A^c)$ as the unique strictly increasing (one-to-one) map between those sets.
    Given $\si:A\to [n]$ (such that $\si\opl b\in S_n$\footnote{$\si\opl b$ denotes the function that takes values $\si(x)$ when $x\in A$ and $b(x)$ when $x\in A^c$.}), define the restriction $R_{b}\si\in S_{n-i-j}$ by
    \[
R_b\si(x) = r_b^{-1}(\si(i+x)) \qquad \text{for $x\in [n-i-j]$}\,.
    \]
    Then the following hold.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item 
        (Labels preserved (up to translation) away from boundary)
        Let $\si\in S_n$ and $b=\si(A^c)$. Then 
        $r_{b}(k) = k+i$ for $k\in [1+\ell_{\max}^-, n-i-j-\ell_{\max}^+]$.
                \item 
        (Locality maintained)
        Let $\si\in S_n$. 
        $\si\in \vloc$ if and only if letting $b=\si(A^c)$, $b$ is $\vell$-localized and  
        $R_b\si\in \vell'\loc$, where $\vec{\ell}'=R_b\vell$ is defined by 
        \begin{align*}
        \ell_{k}^{\prime-} &= 
                \min\{\ell_{r_b(k)}^- +k+i - r_b(k), k-1\}
        \\ 
        \ell_{k}^{\prime+} &=
        \min\{\ell_{r_b(k)}^+ + r_b(k)-k-i, n-i-j-k\}
        .
        \end{align*}
        Moreover, 
        $\vell'$ is $n-i-j$-admissible with $\ell_{\max}^{\prime\pm}\le \ell_{\max}^{\pm}$, respectively.
        \item (Measure on restriction)
        Let $\mu$ be the probability measure on $S_n$ given by $p_{k,k'}$, and let $\mu_{|b}$ be the measure conditioned on $\set{\si\in S_n}{\si({A^c})=b}$. 
        Then $(R_b)_* \mu_{|b}$\footnote{We use the notation $f_*\mu$ to denote the pushforward of the measure $\mu$ by the function $f$.} is the probability measure on $S_{n-i-j}$ given by~\eqref{eq:stationary-distribution} with $\vec{q}$ given by $q_{k,k'} = p_{r_b(k),r_b(k')}$. If $\vec{p}$ satisfies $\ep$-positive bias, then $\vec{q}$ satisfies $\ep$-positive bias. 
            \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 12 of arXiv:2511.02725

body:
[Lem 17 of arXiv:2608.13976, 'Boundary Harnack principle for diffusion with jumps on metric measure spaces'] Suppose that ${\rm \bf (\wh{Jt})}_{\leq, \bar r, \gamma}$ holds  with   $\bar r>0$ and $\gamma>0.$ Then there is a constant $C=C(\bar r, \gamma)\in  (0,\infty)$
such that for every ball $B$ with radius $\bar r$ and  $\overline B\subsetneq \sX$,
  every open $U\subset 2^{-1}B$ and every $W\subset \tfrac{1}{2}B\setminus \overline{U}$, we have
\begin{equation}
\P_x(\wh X^B_{\wh\tau^B_U}\in W)\leq C\frac{\E_x[\wh\tau^B_U]}{(d(U,W) \wedge\bar{r})^\gamma} \quad \hbox{ for every }x\in U.
\end{equation}
 Here $d(U, W)$ denotes the distance between two sets $U$ and $W$, that is,
$d(U, W)=\inf\{d(x, y): x\in U \hbox{ and } y\in W\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 17 of arXiv:2608.13976

body: [Prop of arXiv:2608.27939, 'Entropy and domination for quasi-Hitchin representations'] Let $\rho_0:\pi_1(S) \to \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ be a Fuchsian representation, corresponding to the hyperbolic surface $X$. Then for the one-parameter  family of representations $\rho_t:\pi_1(S)\to \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ obtained by bending $\rho_0$ along a measured geodesic lamination $t\lambda$ on $X$, we have that the entropy $H(\rho_t)$ increases monotonically as $t$ increases (from $0$ to the first value $t_0$ where $\rho_{t_0}$ is not quasi-Fuchsian).

[Theorem 2 (Markov chain tree theorem) of arXiv:2606.31596, 'The Invariant Measure of Multiscale Markov Chains via Fast Arborescence Factorization'] Let $X^N_t$ be a continuous-time Markov chain with transition graph $(V,E)$ and positive transition rates $r_N$.
	If $(V,E)$ is strongly connected, then $X^N_t$ admits a unique invariant measure $\pi_N$, which is strictly positive and given by
	\begin{equation}
		
		\pi_N(x)=\frac{r_N(\mathcal{T}_x)} {r_N(\mathcal{T})}\,,\quad x\in V\,.
	\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Markov chain tree theorem

[Proposition 19 of arXiv:2607.11283, 'Markov Properties of $k$-Record Processes via Order Statistics'] Let $F$ be continuous and define
\[
F_{1:k}(x)=1-(1-F(x))^k.
\]
Then the transition kernel $K_k$ in \eqref{eq:k-record-kernel} coincides with the transition kernel of the ordinary record process associated with the distribution function $F_{1:k}$.

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2606.15425, 'Well-posedness of stochastic parabolic equations with gradient nonlinearities and applicat'] Let the coefficients of \eqref{IntroABSModel} satisfy assumptions \ref{ass:ColeHopfGLipschitz} to \ref{ass:CriticalNemytskiiDispersion}. Let $W^Q$ take values in $H^{\sigma,q}$ for some arbitrary $\sigma > 0$ and $q \in (d,2d)$. Then, for suitable $p$ and $\mathcal F_0$-measurable $\log \phi_0, c_0 \in B^{d/q}_{q,2p}$ with $0 \leq \phi_0, c_0 \leq 1$ almost surely, there exists a unique global-in-time solution $(\phi, c)$ of \eqref{IntroABSModel} with initial data $\phi_0, c_0$, in the sense of Def. \ref{def:localsol}. In particular, $\mathbb P$-a.s.,
$$
\phi \in C([0,T];B^{d/q}_{q,2p}) \cap C((0,T];H^{1,q}),~ c \in L^4([0,T];H^{1,q})
$$
with $$\sup_{t\in (0,T]} t^{\frac12 - \frac{d}{2q}} \norm{\phi}_{H^{1,q}} < \infty$$ and
$0 \leq \phi_t, c_t \leq 1$ for all $t \in [0,T]$. Moreover, $(\phi,c)$ is the unique solution with these regularities. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2606.15425

[Definition 4 (Schur multiplier) of arXiv:2604.21113, 'Tail Bounds via Southwest Boundary'] Let \(\mathcal{M}_n\) denote the space of \(n \times n\) real matrices and \(E_{i,j}\) the elementary matrix whose only non-zero entry is in position \((i,j)\). 
Let \(d,n \in \mathbb{N}\) and let
\[
\mathfrak{m}(d) = \{m_{j_1,\dots,j_{d+1}}\}_{j_1,\dots,j_{d+1}=1}^n
\]
be a multi-dimensional matrix with real entries. The \(d\)-linear Schur multiplier \(\mathfrak{M}_{\mathfrak{m}(d)} : \mathcal{M}_n \times \cdots \times \mathcal{M}_n 
\to \mathcal{M}_n\) is
\begin{equation}
\mathfrak{M}_{\mathfrak{m}(d)}(X_1,\dots,X_d) = \sum_{j_1,\dots,j_{d+1}=1}^n m_{j_1,\dots,j_{d+1}} x^{(1)}_{j_1,j_2} \cdots x^{(d)}_{j_d,j_{d+1}} E_{j_1,j_{d+1}}.
\end{equation}
where $x_{ij}^{(k)}$ is the $(i,j)$ entry of $X_k$.
title: Schur multiplier

body: [Definition age_dependent_BP of arXiv:2412.03415, 'Critical first passage percolation on random graphs'] Fix distribution $F$ on $\mathbb{R}_+$ and probability mass function on $\mathbb{Z}_+$ with generating function $h$.  An age dependent branching process ${\sf BP}(F,h)$ is a branching process in continuous time,  starting with a single individual at time $t=0$ with individuals having random life-lengths with distribution function $F$ such that at death, an individual produces offspring of random size with probability generating function $h$. All life-lengths and family sizes are independent of each other. We assume that the process starts at time $t=0$ with one individual of age zero.
title: Age-dependent branching process

[Lemma corollary4.88 of arXiv:2504.15992, 'Repeated singular values of a random symmetric matrix and decoupled singular value estimat'] Given any $B>0$, a random variable $\zeta\in \Gamma_B$ that has a finite, $n$-independent log-Sobolev constant, and a random matrix $A_n\sim\operatorname{Sym}_n(\zeta)$. Fix $\kappa>0$. Then we can find constants $C_1,C_2,C_3>0$ depending only on $\kappa$, $B$ and the log-Sobolev constant (and not on $c_0$) such that, for any $c_0>0$ and  $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\in[-(2-\kappa)\sqrt{n},(2-\kappa)\sqrt{n}]$,
    \begin{equation}
   \mathbb{P}\left( \frac{C_1\sqrt{n}}{k}\leq 
   \mu_k(\lambda_i)\leq \frac{C_2\sqrt{n}}{k}\text{ for both $i\in\{1,2\}$ and all } c_0n\leq k\leq C_3n
   \right)\geq 1-e^{-\Omega(n)}.     
    \end{equation}

In particular, we can find $C_4>1$ depending only on $\kappa$, $B$ and the log-Sobolev constant such that for any $c_0>0$ and for each $\lambda_i$ in the given interval,
$$
\left(\mu_{\frac{k}{C_4}}(\lambda_i)\geq {10}\mu_k(\lambda_j) \text{ for all } c_0n\leq k\leq C_3n\text{ and  }\text{ for all } i,j\in\{1,2\}\right)\geq 1-e^{-\Omega(n)}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:Wg_for_R of arXiv:2510.21186, 'Weingarten Calculus with Virtual Isometries'] Let $X=(x_1,\dots,x_n)^{\mathtt{T}}$ be a uniform vector on the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^n$.
For $2n$ nonnegative integers $m_1,\dots, m_n, l_1,\dots, l_n$, the moment
\[
\mathbb{E}\bigl[x_1^{m_1} x_2^{m_2} \cdots x_n^{m_n} \overline{x_1^{l_1} x_2^{l_2} \cdots x_n^{l_n}} \bigr]
\]
 vanishes unless $m_j=l_j$ for all $1 \le j \le n$.
In this case, we have
\[
\mathbb{E} \bigl[|x_1|^{2m_1} |x_2|^{2m_2} \cdots |x_n|^{2m_n}\bigr]
= \frac{m_1! \, m_2! \, \cdots \, m_n!}{n^{\uparrow m}},
\]
where $m=m_1+ m_2+ \cdots+m_n$.

body:
[Theorem 4 (Frydman's $R_6$ test) of arXiv:2608.08242, 'Bang--bang representation of $3\times 3$ embeddable stochastic matrices'] Let $P$ be a $3\times 3$ row-stochastic matrix with $D>0$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item If $P$ has a zero entry, 
\[
P\in\T\Longleftrightarrow G(P)\geq 0.
\]
In that case $P\in R_5$, and $G(P)=0$ implies $P\in R_4$.

\item If $P>0$, then $P\in\V$ if and only if
$\max_{i,j}V_{ij}(P)\geq0$.  More generally,
\[
P\in\T\cup\V
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\max_{i,j}V_{ij}(P)\geq0.
\]

\item If $P\notin\T\cup\V$, then $P\in\NH$ if and only if, for some
ordered pair $(i,j)$, the quadratic $q_{ij}^P$ has a root in
$[0,\bar c_{ij}]$.

\item One has 
\[
R_6=\T\cup\V\cup\NH.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Frydman's $R_6$ test

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); T385-w737-C04 v2; no independent PASS. Let n tend to infinity, let X and W be n by n and a be in R^n. The entries of X are iid N(0,1/n); the entries of W and a are iid N(0,1), jointly independent and independent of X. For the bias-free scalar network f(x)=n^(-1/2) sum_j a_j ReLU(w_j dot x), include both W and a in the empirical NTK. Write H=ReLU(XW), G_ij=1{(XW)_ij>0}, D=(XX^T) elementwise-multiplied by (G diag(a_j^2)G^T/n), and K=HH^T/n+D. The recorded unaudited derivation asserts lambda_1(K)-n/(2pi) converges in distribution to Normal(3/2-1/(4pi),1/pi), where the second Normal parameter is variance, and lambda_2(K)=O_P(1). Thus it would identify only one diverging mean-induced eigenvalue, without excluding bounded outliers. No bounded-edge outlier theorem is claimed. No general ReLU bulk law or deeper-network result follows. No novelty claim is made, and independent review is pending.

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2512.00570, 'Makeenko--Migdal equations for lattice Yang--Mills--Higgs'] For any line $\ell \in \mL_{1}$ with both beginning and ending points $x \in \Lambda$,

\begin{align*}
	 -2c_0  \phi(\ell) 
	&=\kappa \sum_{\ell' \in \mE_{\text{ext},x}(\ell) }  \phi(\ell') 
	+\sum_{k=1}^n c_k
		\sum_{s \in \mE^k_{x}(\ell)}  \phi(s)
	+2q\sum_{\ell' \in \mG_x(\ell) }  \phi(\ell')\qquad (M\in \{\mR^N,\mC^N\})

\\
	2qN \phi(\ell) 
	&=\kappa \sum_{\ell' \in \mE_{\text{ext},x}(\ell) }  \phi(\ell')
	 -\kappa \sum_{s \in \mE_{x}(\ell) }  \phi(s)
	 +2q\sum_{\ell' \in \mG_x(\ell) }  \phi(\ell')\qquad\quad(M\in \{\mS^{N-1},\mS^{2N-1}\}).
\end{align*}
Here  $q=1$ in the real case and $q=2$ in the complex case as in Lemma~\ref{lem:DMx}.

[Corollary cor:sequential-price-inequalities of arXiv:2512.21026, 'Minimax Duality in Game-Theoretic Probability\thanks{Work in progress: mistakes are likely'] Let $(\mathcal{Y},\hat\mathcal{Z},\infty)$ be a sequentially normalized gamble space, and let $X:\mathcal{Y}^T\to{\mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}}$ be measurable and bounded below.

  where $\mathcal{Z}' = \mathrm{bb}(\mathcal{Z}_\infty) \cup \bigcup_{t\in\mathbb{N}} \mathcal{Z}_t$.
  If we further have $\Delta_0^\infty(\hat\mathcal{Z}) \neq \emptyset$, 
  then
  \begin{align}
    \underline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}} X
    \leq
    \underline{\mathbb{E}}_{\mathcal{Z}'} X
    \leq
    \underline{\mathbb{E}}^* X
    \leq 
    \overline{\mathbb{E}}^* X
    \leq
    \overline{\mathbb{E}}_{\mathcal{Z}'} X
    \leq
    \overline{\textsf{\textbf{E}}} X~.
  \end{align}

body:
[Definition def:covered of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix $\lambda \in (0,1),$ a send sequence~$\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$, and a positive integer~$j$.   
We consider three properties.
\begin{enumerate}[({Prop }1):]
\item $C_{\mathrm{F}} W_j j^{\phi}\le 
\exp(c_{\mathrm{NB}}\lambda\widetilde{W}[j]\,|\Upsilon_{j,\ge\widetilde{W}[j]}|) $.
\item  $|\Upsilon_{j,\geq j^2}| \geq  C_{\Upsilon} \mathrm{L}(j)/(2\lambda)$.
\item  $|\Upsilon_{j,\ge j^{\chi}}| \ge C_{\Upsilon} \mathrm{LL}(j)/\lambda$.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{itemize}
\item  We say that bin $j$ is \emph{many-covered} if 
(Prop~(cov-prop-1 of the paper)) holds. 
\item We say that bin $j$ is \emph{heavy-covered} if (Prop~(cov-prop-1 of the paper)) is false and  (Prop~(cov-prop-2 of the paper)) holds.
\item We say that bin $j$ is \emph{weakly exposed} if
(Prop~(cov-prop-1 of the paper)) is false,
(Prop~(cov-prop-2 of the paper)) is false, and
(Prop~(cov-prop-3 of the paper)) holds.
\item We say that bin $j$ is \emph{strongly exposed} 
if (Prop~(cov-prop-1 of the paper)) is false, 
(Prop~(cov-prop-2 of the paper)) is false, and
(Prop~(cov-prop-3 of the paper)) is false.
     
\end{itemize}

We say that bin $j$ is \emph{covered} if it is many-covered or heavy-covered -- that is, 
if (Prop~(cov-prop-1 of the paper)) or
(Prop~(cov-prop-2 of the paper)) holds.
We say that bin $j$ is \emph{exposed} if it is weakly exposed or strongly exposed -- that is, if 
(Prop~(cov-prop-1 of the paper)) is false and
(Prop~(cov-prop-2 of the paper)) is false.
title: Definition def:covered of arXiv:2602.21315

[Lemma 41 of arXiv:2605.02430, '\textbf{Scaling limit of the range of tree-valued branching random walks in random environ'] Let $\nu$ be a supercritical offspring distribution whose mean is denoted by $\ttm_\nu$. 
 Let $\ttb_0\ino (1, \infty)$. We assume that $\sum_{k\in \bbN} k^{2\ttb_0 +1}\nu(k) \leko \infty$. Let $(\bT, \boo)$ be an invariant GW($\nu$)-tree as in Definition \ref{definvRW}. 
Let the r.v.s $U_x$, $x\ino \bT$, be as in (\ref{welldefcoo}). Let $\overline{X}_n \eqo (\bT, X_n)$, $n\ino \bbN$, be a $\mathtt m_\nu$-biased RW on $\bT$ such that $X_0 \eqo \boo$, and recall that $P_{(\bT, \boo)}$ stands for the conditional law of $(X_n)_{n\in \bbN}$ given $(\bT, \boo)$. 
Then, for all $\ttb \ino (1, \ttb_0)$, there exists a $\bP$-a.s.~finite r.v. $K_\ttb (\bT)$ that is a measurable function of $\bT$ and $\ttb$ such that for all $m\ino \bbN$ and all $n\ino \bbN^*$,
\begin{equation}

\textrm{$\bP$-a.s.~}\qquad E_{\bT, \boo} \big[ |S_{X_{m+n}} \! \! -\! S_{X_m} |^{2\ttb}  \big] \leq K_\ttb (\bT)\,  n^{\ttb-1} (m+n) .

[Definition 1 (Control and $\omega$-$p$-variation) of arXiv:2605.08844, 'Signature Kernel and Schwinger-Dyson Kernel Equations as Two-Parameter Rough Differential '] A control on $[a,b]$ is a continuous, super-additive map
$\omega:\Delta_{[a,b]}\to[0,\infty)$ vanishing on the diagonal.

Given $p\ge 1$ and $f:\Delta_{[a,b]}\to F$ set
\[
\|f\|_{p,\omega}
:=
\inf\Big\{C>0:\ \|f_{s,t}\|_F\le C\,\omega(s,t)^{1/p}
\ \text{for all }(s,t)\in\Delta_{[a,b]}\Big\},
\]
with the convention $\inf\varnothing=\infty$, and define
\[
C_\omega^p(\Delta_{[a,b]},F)
:=
\{f:\Delta_{[a,b]}\to F:\ \|f\|_{p,\omega}<\infty\}.
\]

For a path $g:[a,b]\to F$, we write $g\in C_\omega^p([a,b],F)$ if its increment map
\(
(s,t)\mapsto g_{s,t}
\)
belongs to $C_\omega^p(\Delta_{[a,b]},F)$.
title: Control and $\omega$-$p$-variation

[Lemma 35 (Reversibility) of arXiv:2608.03575, '2608.03575'] Define the degree-biased law \(\widehat{\mathbb P}\) by
\begin{equation}
    \frac{d\widehat{\mathbb P}}{d\mathbb P}(G,\rho,\Theta)
    =
    \frac{\deg_G(\rho)}{\E[\deg_G(\rho)]}.
\end{equation}
Then, under \(\widehat{\mathbb P}\), the rooted marked graph is reversible
for simple random walk:
\[
    (G,\rho,X_1,\Theta)
    \overset{d}{=}
    (G,X_1,\rho,\Theta).
\]
Consequently, the bi-infinite walk \((X_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}\) is stationary
under time shifts.

Own-work draft, proof (unaudited), T326-w697-C10 v1; reviewer PASS pending. Bah-Rauhut-Terstiege-Westdickenberg arXiv:1910.05505v5 Theorem 4 (printed p.4) states that a bounded global negative-gradient trajectory of a real analytic function converges to a critical point. Applying it to C07's bounded polynomial augmented scalar-value/K^TQ loss proves convergence of the full parameter trajectory to a single critical point for every pool under C07's hypotheses. This resolves existence of the limit, not whether its loss is zero. The source's Theorem 39(b) (p.21), for two matrix layers and almost every ambient initialization with full-rank input covariance, does not justify a global-minimum conclusion for the exact deterministic scalar-plus-two-factor initialization here. The known analytic-gradient theorem requires a real analytic f on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and a bounded global solution x'=-grad f; it concludes one limiting critical point, not a global minimum. C07 supplies boundedness for the actual initialized polynomial loss, so the application is valid without full-rank input covariance. Theorem 39(b) has different hypotheses: two freely trained matrix layers, full-rank XX^T, almost every ambient initialization. It cannot certify the exact deterministic shared-scalar model. The related queued w696 compact-manifold convergence card was considered during dedup; this entry records the specific noncompact-Euclidean bounded-trajectory application, not a duplicate generic theorem card.

[Theorem theorem ethier kurtz path convergence of arXiv:2512.20338, 'Up-down chains and scaling limits: \\ application to permuton- and graphon-valued diffusio'] Let $ T_n $ be the transition operator of $ Y_n $ and $ \{ T( t ) \}_{ t \ge 0 } $ a Feller semigroup on $ C( E ) $.
    Suppose that the initial distributions of $ \{ \gamma_n( Y_n( 0 ) ) \} $ converge, say to $ \nu $, and that $ \{  \varepsilon _n \}_{ n \ge 1 } $ is a positive sequence converging to zero such that
    $$
    	T_n^{  \lfloor  t/ \varepsilon _n  \rfloor  }
    	\pi_n
    	f
    		\to
    			T( t ) f
    		,
    			\qquad
                \text{ for all }f \in C( E ),
    			\,
    			t \ge 0
    		.
    $$
    
    \noindent
    Then there exists a Markov process $ Y $ with initial distribution $ \nu $, transition semigroup $ \{ T( t ) \}_{ t \ge 0 } $, and sample paths in the Skorokhod space $ D( [ 0, \infty ), E )  $ such that the convergence
	$$
		\big(
			\gamma_n( Y_n (  \lfloor  t/ \varepsilon _n  \rfloor ) )
		\big)_{ t \ge 0 }
			\Longrightarrow
        		\big(
        				Y( t )
        		\big)_{ t \ge 0 }
	$$
    holds in distribution in $D( [ 0, \infty ), E )$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [campaign status: candidate_partial_counterexample - author-checked, unrefereed] Ansatz 20, stated inside Open Problem 8 of Aldous and Janson (arXiv:2303.02529), claims for nonnegative f with f(j) = O(j^k) that (i) if sum_i a(i) f(i) converges then sum_{i <= n} a(n,i) f(i) tends to it, and (ii) if it diverges then sum_{i <= n} a(n,i) f(i) is asymptotic to sum_{i <= n} a(i) f(i); here a(n,j) is the probability that the tagged harmonic descent chain started at n visits j and a(j) = 6 H_{j-1} / (pi^2 (j-1)) is its fixed-j limit. Our result (id P0341, 2026-09-08): BOTH parts are FALSE, on the single observation that a(n,n) = 1 exactly - the chain starts at n, so it visits n surely. For (i), take f(j) = 1{j = 2^r}: f is bounded (hence of polynomial growth) and a(2^r) = O(r 2^-r), so S = sum a(i) f(i) converges; but at n = 2^K the truncated sum contains the top term a(2^K, 2^K) = 1, forcing liminf >= 1 + S against the predicted S. For (ii), take g(j) = j 1{j = 2^r} (so g(j) <= j): since a(j) j ~ (6/pi^2) log j the truncated limiting sum at n = 2^K is of order K^2 while the actual sum is at least its root term 2^K, so the ratio diverges. The refutation is scoped to the displayed Ansatz, not to Open Problem 8 as a whole - explicit bounds on |a(n,m) - a(m)| remain open. Verification as the source words it: each piece re-derived (the asymptotics of a(j) and a(j) j, the summability of a(2^r), the polynomial-growth hypothesis for both test functions, and a(n,n) = 1 from the definition); no rate of convergence and no numerical evaluation is needed anywhere. Prior art not cleared. f nonnegative with f(j) = O(j^k) a(n,j) the visit probability of the tagged harmonic descent chain, a(j) = 6 H_{j-1}/(pi^2 (j-1))

[Lemm 17 of arXiv:2607.13849, 'Rearranged Stochastic Heat Equation with an Entropy Gradient Structure'] For fixed {$h \in T/{\mathbb N}^*$} and 
$\varepsilon >0$, let $E_\varepsilon$ be given by \eqref{eq:varepsilon}.
 Then,  for any $\delta >0$, 
\begin{align*}
	\lim_{h \searrow 0} \mathbb{P}\left\{\sup_{j\in\{1,\cdots, N\}}\sup_{\mathbf{x}\in \mathbb{S}} \sup_{0\leq t\leq h}\bigg| \frac{1}{E_\varepsilon(\mathbf{x})+[g\star D_{\mathbf{x}}F_{\mu_{j},t}^{-1}](\mathbf{x})} - \frac{1}{E_\varepsilon(\mathbf{x})+[g\star D_{\mathbf{x}}F_{\mu_{j,h}}^{-1}](\mathbf{x})} \bigg|\geq \delta\right\}  =0, 
\end{align*}
where $\mu_{j,h}$ is the value of $\mu_{j,t}$ at $t=h$ and $\mu_{j,t}=\mathrm{Leb}_{\mathbb{S}}\circ (X_{t_{j}^-}^{(h)})^{-1}\star \Gamma_t$.

Let Q denote the law of a two-sided, nontrivial, (r_0,alpha)-semi-selfsimilar Levy process V with cadlag paths and V(0)=0, where alpha is in (0,2), Q(V(1)>0)>0 and Q(V(1)<0)>0. Strictly alpha-stable processes are included. Let nu be its Levy measure and suppose nu((0,infinity)) > 0. Let delta > 1. Put w(x) = -|x|^delta + V(x) and mu^w(dx) = exp(-w(x))dx. Let L^w be the self-adjoint operator associated with the closure on L^2(R,mu^w) of E^w(f,f) = (1/2) integral_R |f'(x)|^2 exp(-w(x))dx, f in C_c^infinity(R). For fixed x_0 > 0 set B_r(x) = (integral_x^infinity exp(w(y))dy)(integral_{x_0}^x exp(-w(y))dy). Then, Q-almost surely: limsup_{x->infinity} B_r(x) = infinity; lambda_ess(-L^w) = 0; and exp(tL^w) is noncompact. The proof is the negative-jump calculation applied to -V, with the two Hardy factors interchanged. For 0 < delta <= 1/alpha the same conclusion is the paper's Proposition 5.2. The record's claim for alpha in (1,2) and 1/alpha < delta <= 1 is not covered by the written proof. This is an unrefereed campaign result.

body:
[Theorem q>1 of arXiv:2605.10452, 'A secretary for Messrs. Luce and Mallows'] Consider the secretary problem for a Mallows distribution with $q=q_n>1$ in the case that the largest number is  of highest rank.

\noindent i. Let $q_n=1+\frac cn$, where $c>0$. Then the asymptotically optimal strategy is $\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*)$, where
\begin{equation}
M_n^*\sim n\Big(\frac1c\log\big(1+\frac{1-e^{-c}}{e-1+e^{-c}}\big)\Big),
\end{equation}
 and the corresponding  limiting probability of success
is $\frac1e$:
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n^{\mathcal{M};q_n}(\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*))=\frac1e.
$$
Also, $\lim_{c\to\infty} \frac1c\log\big(1+\frac{1-e^{-c}}{e-1+e^{-c}}\big)=0$ and $\lim_{c\to0} \frac1c\log\big(1+\frac{1-e^{-c}}{e-1+e^{-c}}\big)=\frac1e$.

\noindent ii.
Let $q_n=1+\frac c{n^\alpha}$, where $c>0$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$. Then the asymptotically optimal strategy  is $\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*)$, where
$$
M_n^*\sim\frac1c\left(1-\log(e-1)\right)n^\alpha\approx0.459\frac{n^\alpha}c,
$$
 and the corresponding limiting probability of success
is $\frac1e$:
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n^{\mathcal{M};q_n}(\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M_n^*))=\frac1e.
$$
\noindent iii. Let $q>1$.  Then the asymptotically optimal strategy  is $\mathcal{S}^\uparrow(n,M^*)$, where
$$
M^*=\begin{cases}&\max\left\{M\ge1: \sum_{j=M}^\infty\frac1{q^j-1}\ge\frac q{q-1}\right\}, \ \text{if}\ \sum_{j=1}^\infty\frac1{q^j-1}\ge \frac q{q-1};\\
&0,\ \text{if}\ \sum_{j=1}^\infty\frac1{q^j-1}<\frac q{q-1}.\end{cases}
$$
(If  $\sum_{j=M^*}^\infty\frac1{q^j-1}=\frac q{q-1}$, then $M^*-1$ is also optimal.)

\noindent The corresponding limiting probability of success is given by
\begin{equation}
\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n^{\mathcal{M};q}(\mathcal{S}^\downarrow(n,M^*))=\begin{cases}&\frac{q-1}q(1-q^{-M^*})\sum_{j=M^*}^\infty\frac1{q^j-1}\ge\\
&(1-q^{-M^*}),\ \text{if}\ M^*\ge1;\\
&\frac{q-1}q>,\ \text{if}\ M^*=0.\end{cases}
\end{equation}
The limiting probability in (equation SuccessProbup of the paper) is always greater or equal to $\frac1e$ and is strictly greater than $\frac1e$ for all but at most a countable number of $q$ with no accumulation points in $(0,\infty)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem q>1 of arXiv:2605.10452

[Thm 9 (Theorem 16.8 of \cite{billingsley_convergence_1999}) of arXiv:2605.07341, 'A Scaling Limit of Random Walks in the Rational Adeles'] A sequence of probability measures $(P_n)_{n = 1}^\infty$ is tight in the $J_1$ topology if and only if:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item For each $T$,
        \[ \lim_{\lambda \to \infty} \limsup_n P_n(x : \sup_{s \leq T} |x(s)|_{\Omega}  \geq \lambda) = 0, \]
        
        and
        \item for each $T$ and $\lambda$, 
        \[ \lim_{\delta \to 0} \limsup_n P_n(x : w_T^\prime(x, \delta; \Omega) \geq \lambda) = 0.\]
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

AUDIT CORRECTION (w559, 2026-10-10; independent review pending) of the 2026-09-07 C0047-A001 spectral route. For independent Bernoulli bond percolation on an infinite connected d-regular simple Cayley graph G, let rho=||A_G||/d denote the normalized simple-random-walk spectral radius. Benjamini-Schramm 1996, Theorem 4, printed p.76 (bond extension in section 2), and Juschenko-Nagnibeda 2015, Theorem 2, give the sufficient condition d*rho*p_c(G)<1 for p_c(G)<p_u(G). The original p_c<1/rho quotation omitted d and is not that criterion: it is automatic when rho<1 and p_c<=1. Nonamenability does not imply the repaired criterion for a prescribed generating set. In the simple Cayley graph C_2*C_3 with generators {a,b,b^-1}, p_c=q is the root of 2q^2+2q^3-2q^4=1 in (0.63,0.64), p_u=1, and ||A||>=2, so d*rho*p_c>1.26. This counterexample refutes only the stronger universal spectral bridge. An existence theorem for a favorable generating multiset does not establish the result for every prescribed simple generating set. [Definition of arXiv:2605.22803, 'Persistence of asymptotic variance under transport:\\ from hyperfluctuation to stealthy hy'] Suppose that $\Phi$ is an invariant locally square-integrable simple point process and suppose that $\tau$ is an invariant allocation. We then call $(\Phi, \tau)$ an \textit{invariant random partition} if $\tau(x)\in\Phi$ for all $x\in\R^d$. Further, for $x\in\Phi$, we call $C(x):=\tau^{-1}(x)$ a \textit{cell} of $(\Phi,\tau)$. Finally, $V_0:= C(\tau(0))$ is called the \textit{zero-cell}.

Additionally, if $\lambda_d(C(x))=\gamma^{-1}$ for all $x\in\Phi$, where $\gamma$ is the intensity of $\Phi$, then we call $(\Phi,\tau)$ a \textit{random fair partition}; see~[Klatt_Last_Lotz_Yogeshwaran_2025].
