body:
[Theorem 11 (Finite reduction) of arXiv:2608.15805, 'Spectral duality structures and the Fisher--Rao geometry of reset distributions'] Assume \textup{(S2)--(S4)}, and let $\mathbf d_O$ be the orbit
directors of Lemma~\ref{lem:orbit-collapse}. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(i)}] \emph{Orbitwise decomposition.} Every normal
direction decomposes as
\[
\mathbf n_\nu=\sum_{O} w_\nu^{(O)}\,\mathbf d_O,
\qquad
w^{(O)}_\nu=\frac{[\mathbf n_\nu]_{z_O}}{\sqrt{\kappa(z_O)}},
\]
each $\mathbf d_O$ being supported on its own orbit. In particular
every $\mathbf n_\nu$ vanishes at every neutral site.
\item[\textup{(ii)}] \emph{Activation and independence.} The
coefficient matrix $\bigl(w^{(O)}_\nu\bigr)_{\nu,O}$ has full column
rank $n_{\mathrm{pair}}$; in particular no orbit is inactive.
\item[\textup{(iii)}] \emph{Finite reduction.}
$V=\bigoplus_{O}\mathbb R\,\mathbf d_O$, so that
$r=\dim V=n_{\mathrm{pair}}$, and
\begin{equation}
\psi(\gamma)=\sum_{O}\varphi_O(\gamma)\,\mathbf d_O,
\qquad
\varphi_O(\gamma):=\sum_\nu f_\nu(\gamma)\,w^{(O)}_\nu .

\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
Each orbit of $\sigma$ therefore contributes exactly one fixed
direction to $V$, neutral sites contribute none, and all
$\gamma$-dependence is carried by the orbit response scalars
$\varphi_O$.

Let $f(x)=c\prod_{i=1}^d(x-\alpha_i)$, where $c\in k$, $c\ne 0$. Let $g\in k[x]$ be a polynomial of degree $<d$, then

    $ holds.

body: The paper proving the Aldous-Fill spectral gap conjecture leaves conditional the claim that for every sufficiently large even order n, the slowest d-regular graph (maximising relaxation time tau_2) is cubic (d=3); the finite crossover point is n=8. The 2-regular cycle has tau_2 = 1/(1-cos(2 pi/n)) ~ n^2/(2 pi^2), one third of the cubic asymptotic 3n^2/(2 pi^2), so cubic graphs must eventually overtake the cycle but do not lead at first: the slowest-known regular graph by order is 2-regular (the cycle) at n=4 (tau_2=1.0000) and n=6 (2.0000), then becomes 3-regular at n=8 (3.9271, versus the cycle's 3.4142), n=10 (13.5414, cycle 5.2361), and n=12 (17.8846, cycle 7.4641). Separately, the extremal cubic maxima (0.75, 1.50, 3.93, 13.54, 17.88 for n=4,6,8,10,12) jump by a factor of 3.5 from n=8 to n=10, out of line with the surrounding steps; this is because the extremal cubic graph acquires a BRIDGE at n=10 and CANNOT do so at any earlier order. Proof that a bridged cubic graph needs n>=10: if a cubic graph has a bridge uv, deleting it leaves a component A containing u where every vertex has degree 3 except u (degree 2), so the degree sum 3|A|-1 must be even, forcing |A| odd; |A|=1 would need a loop and |A|=3 would need four edges among three vertices (both impossible for a simple cubic graph), so both sides of any bridge are odd and at least 5, giving n>=10. This matches exact enumeration: no bridged cubic graph exists at n=4, 6, or 8; at n=10 there is exactly one bridged cubic graph and it IS the extremal one (tau_2=13.5414, versus 6.8423 for the best bridgeless cubic graph on 10 vertices); at n=12 there are four bridged cubic graphs and the extremal one among them is a 5|7 split (17.8846, versus 10.3190 for the best bridgeless cubic graph), a 6|6 split being impossible by the same parity argument. So the crossover at n=8 (cubic first overtakes the cycle, still bridgeless there, via a narrow 2-edge 4|4 cut) and the jump at n=10 (the bridge becomes possible) are two DIFFERENT events. NOT CERTIFIED: whether any regular graph of degree d>=4 ever competes with the cubic extremal graphs at these orders - only suggested: a 4-regular graph would need a second eigenvalue of 0.944 to compete, and the best 4-regular graph seen has 0.890; and a parity fact (a d-regular graph has a cut of size c across a vertex subset A only if c = d|A| mod 2, checked on 8400 random cuts with zero violations) shows a bridge is impossible outright for any EVEN degree d, which is suggestive but not a proof that odd degrees d>=5 cannot compete either.

body: There are functions on (0, 1) with Lebesgue measure that converge to 0 pointwise while their integrals do not: f_n = n 1((0, 1/n)) has int f_n = 1 for every n. No integrable function dominates all f_n, since sup_n f_n(x) = floor(1/x) >= 1/x - 1, which is not integrable near 0. So the dominated convergence theorem cannot drop its common integrable dominator.

		$$\lim_{r\to \infty}  \limsup_{\|z\| \to \infty}  \sup_{y\in \partial B(z,r)} \frac{\mathbb P(\mathcal T^y \cap A \neq \emptyset, \mathcal T^y_-\cap (z+B)  \neq \emptyset)}{G(z)} = 0 . $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 4 of arXiv:2511.01424

[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2607.10102, 'Dynamical mean-field limit and replica-symmetric free energy for the orthogonally-invarian'] Suppose the conditions of Theorem \ref{thm:replica} hold.
Fix any sufficiently large $T_0,T>0$ and sufficiently small $\eps>0$.
Let $(\tilde c_g,\tilde r_g) \equiv (\tilde c_g^m,\tilde r_g^m)$ be
the kernels of Corollary \ref{cor:semigroupapprox} for this $\eps$. Let
$\{\tilde g^t\}_{t \in \R},\{\tilde b^t\}_{t \geq T_0},z$
be mutually independent such that
$\{\tilde g^t\}_{t \in \R} \sim \GP(0,\tilde c_g)$,
$\{\tilde b^t\}_{t \geq T_0}$ is a standard Brownian motion with $\tilde b^{T_0}=0$, and $z \sim \cN(0,q_*\cR_\Lambda'(v_*-q_*))$.

Then there is a coupling of
$(\{\tilde g^t\}_{t \in \R},\{\tilde b^t\}_{t \geq T_0},z)$
with the process $\{\theta^t\}_{t \geq 0}$ in \eqref{eq:dmft-theta} of
Definition \ref{def:DMFT} such that the following holds: Define the process
$\{\tilde \theta^t\}_{t \geq 0}$ by
\begin{align*}
\tilde\theta^t&=\theta^t \text{ for all } t \in [0,T_0],\\
\d\tilde \theta^t&=
\left[-U'(\tilde \theta^t)+\int_0^t \tilde r_g(t-s)
\tilde \theta^s ds+\tilde g^t+z\right]
\d t+\sqrt{2}\,\d \tilde b^t \text{ for } t \geq T_0.
\end{align*}
Then for some constants $C,c>0$ not depending on $T_0,T,\eps$,
\begin{equation}
\sup_{t \geq 0} \E(\theta^t)^4<C,
\qquad \sup_{t \geq 0} \E(\tilde \theta^t)^4<C,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
\sup_{t \in [T_0,T_0+T]} \E(\tilde \theta^t-\theta^t)^2
<C(\eps+T^{1/4}e^{-cT_0})^{2/3}.
\end{equation}

[Definition 11 of arXiv:2605.02002, 'Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI'] Consider the denoising process $(Y_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ for a measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$. Then the process $(Y_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ is said to be $\phi$-entropically stable with rate $C$ at $\theta\in[0,1]$ if for any given function $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$, denoting by $F=f(Y_1)$, then for any configuration $T$ with $\mathbb{P}(Y_\theta=T)>0$, we have
    $$
\lim_{h\to 0^+}\frac{1}{h}\operatorname{Ent}^\phi[\mathbb{E}[F\mid Y_{\theta+h}]\mid Y_\theta=T]
\leq\frac{C}{1-\theta}\operatorname{Ent}^\phi[F\mid Y_\theta=T].
    $$
title: Definition 11 of arXiv:2605.02002

[Definition Orbit equivalence of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] Let \(N_{1}\) and \(N_{2}\) be oriented compact 3-manifolds, which admit semiflows \(\varphi_{t}^{1}\) and \(\varphi_{t}^{2}\), respectively.
The semiflows \(\varphi_{t}^{1}\) and \(\varphi_{t}^{2}\) are \emph{orbit equivalent} if there exists a homeomorphism \(H:N_{1}\to N_{2}\) such that for every \(x_{1}\in N_{1}\), \(H\) sends the orbit \(\mathcal{O}^{1}(x_{1})\) homeomorphically onto the orbit \(\mathcal{O}^{2}(H(x_{1}))\), preserving the orientation of orbits.

If, in addition, \(N_{1}\) and \(N_{2}\) are sutured manifolds, we require that \(H\) preserves the suture structure.
title: Orbit equivalence

[Definition of arXiv:2412.04579, 'Solvable Families of Random Block Tridiagonal Matrices'] Suppose that $\mathbf{M}$ is an ${\mathbb{F}}$-Hermitian $rn\times rn$ matrix.
 We define the spectral measure of $\mathbf{M}$ with respect to $\mathbf{e}_{[\![r ]\!]}$ as the $r\times r$ matrix-valued measure
\begin{align*}
 \mu_{[\![r ]\!]}=\sum_{j=1}^{rn} \mathbf{v}_{j,[\![r ]\!]} \cdot \mathbf{v}_{j,[\![r ]\!]}^{\dag} \delta_{\lambda_j}.
\end{align*}
Here $\mathbf{v}_{j}$ is the normalized eigenvector corresponding to $\lambda_j$, and
$\mathbf{v}_{j,[\![r ]\!]}\in {\mathbb{F}}^r$ is the projection of~$\mathbf{v}_j$ to the first $r$ coordinates.
title: Unnumbered Definition of arXiv:2412.04579, 'Solvable Families of Random Block Tridiagonal Matrices'

body:
[Lemma 29 (Poisson--Dirichlet approximation of the one-step exponents) of arXiv:2604.25877, 'Asymptotic height of Plancherel random trees'] Fix $t>1$. For an integer $k\ge2$, let $(A^{(u)}_i)_{1\le i\le d(u)}$ be the multiset of block sizes in the
$\mathrm{Ewens}(k-1,\theta)$ partition at a node $u$ with $K(u)=k$. We define the 

one-step exponent:
\begin{equation*}
\kappa_k(t):=\log\,
\E\!\left[\sum_{i=1}^{d(u)}\left(\frac{A^{(u)}_i}{k-1}\right)^t\ \Big|\ K(u)=k\right].
\end{equation*}
Then as $k\to\infty$,
\begin{equation}
\kappa_k(t)\longrightarrow \kappa(t)=\log\beta_t(\theta).
\end{equation}
More precisely, there exists a constant $C=C(t,\theta)<\infty$,
$\gamma=\gamma(\theta)\in(0,1/2]$, and $m_0\ge 2$ such that for all $m\ge m_0$,
\[
\sup_{k\ge m}\,|\kappa_k(t)-\kappa(t)| \le C\,m^{-\gamma}.
\]

[Proposition prop:FKG of arXiv:2608.05089, 'Correlation decay in area-tilted line ensembles'] Let $\mathbf{Y} \sim \mathcal{L}^{\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y},\bm{\lambda}}_{n,\ell,r,\mathbf{f},\mathbf{g}}$, recalling Definition (def:extFLE of the paper)
of this measure with $n$ curves having boundary conditions $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y} \in \overline{\mathbb{A}_+^n}$
on $[\ell,r]$, Lipschitz floors and ceilings given by $\mathbf{f}, \mathbf{g} : [\ell,r] \to \mathbb{A}_+^n$ with $\mathbf{f} \prec \mathbf{g}$,
and varying area tilt strengths given by $\bm{\lambda} : [\ell,r] \to \mathbb{R}_+^n$. 
We may also consider the measure without floors or ceilings, or with floors but not ceilings, et cetera.
Consider any functions $f, g$ on the space of continuous curves $[\ell,r] \to \mathbb{A}_+^n$
which are continuous in the topology of uniform convergence, increasing
with respect to the ordering $\preceq$, and such that $\operatorname{Cov}[f(\mathbf{Y}),g(\mathbf{Y})]$ is well-defined.
Then $\operatorname{Cov} \mleft[ f(\mathbf{Y}), g(\mathbf{Y}) \mright] \geqslant 0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Pro 5.1 of arXiv:2608.00420, '{Weighted $L^p$ solutions of scalar BSDEs with general unbounded stochastic coefficients}\'] Assume that the generator $g$ satisfies assumption (A:H3 of the paper) (resp. (A:H1' of the paper)). For each $n\geq1$, define the function $g_n$ as follows: for $(\omega,t,y,z)\in \Omega\times [0,\tau]\times{\mathbb R}\times{\mathbb R}^d$,
$$
g_n(\omega,t,y,z):=\inf_{\bar{z}\in{\mathbb R}^d}\{g(\omega,t,y,\bar{z})
+\bar{\nu}_t^n(\omega)|z-\bar{z}|\}
$$
$$
({\rm resp.}\ \ g_n(\omega,t,y,z):=\inf_{(\bar y,\bar{z})\in {\mathbb R}\times {\mathbb R}^d}\{g(\omega,t,\bar y,\bar{z})+\bar\mu_t^n(\omega)|y-\bar y|
+\bar{\nu}_t^n(\omega)|z-\bar{z}|\})
$$
with
$$
\bar\mu_t^n:=\mu_t+ne^{-t}\ \ {\rm and}\ \  \bar{\nu}_t^n:=\sqrt{\nu_t^2 +ne^{-t}}.
$$
Then the sequence of function $g_n$ is well defined, and for each $n\geq1$, $g_n(\omega,t,y,z)$ is $(\mathcal{F}_t)$-progressively measurable for each $(y,z)\in{\mathbb R}\times{\mathbb R}^d$, and it satisfies, ${\rm d}\mathbb{P}\times{\rm d} t-a.e.$,
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] For each $z\in{\mathbb R}^d$, $g_n(\omega,t,\cdot,z)$ is continuous and $g_n$ satisfies (A:H3 of the paper)(ii)-(iii) (resp. (A:H1' of the paper)(ii));
\item[(ii)] Monotonicity in $n$: for each $(y,z)\in{\mathbb R}\times{\mathbb R}^d$, $g_n(\omega,t,y,z)$ nondecreases in $n$;
\item[(iii)] Stochastic Lipschitz condition: for each $(y,y_1,y_2,z_1,z_2)\in{\mathbb R}\times{\mathbb R}\times{\mathbb R}\times{\mathbb R}^d\times{\mathbb R}^d,$ we have
$$
\left|g_n(\omega,t,y,z_1)-g_n(\omega,t,y,z_2)\right|\leq \bar{\nu}_t^n(\omega)|z_1-z_2|
$$
$$
({\rm resp.}\ \ \left|g_n(\omega,t,y_1,z_1)-g_n(\omega,t,y_2,z_2)\right|\leq \bar{\mu}_t^n(\omega)|y_1-y_2|+\bar{\nu}_t^n(\omega)|z_1-z_2|);
$$

\item[(iv)] Convergence: If $(y_n,z_n)\rightarrow (y,z)$, then $g_n(\omega,t,y_n,z_n)\rightarrow g(\omega,t,y,z)$, as $n\rightarrow \infty$.\vspace{0.2cm}
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma l:embedding-classical-weighted of arXiv:2607.24640, 'The Yang-Mills measure on surfaces via Morse theory'] Let $(\kappa,p)\in \mathbb{R} _+\times \mathbb{Z} _+$ such that $0\leqslant\kappa\leqslant p$ and let $q\geqslant 0$. There exists a constant $C>0$ such that, for every $A \in H^{-\kappa}(\Sigma,T^*\Sigma\otimes\mathfrak{g})$,
$$
\psi\in H^{p,q}(\Sigma\setminus\{a_{2g+2}\},T^*\Sigma\otimes\mathfrak{g})\mapsto\langle A,\psi\rangle\in  \mathbb{R} 
$$
belongs to $H^{-p,-q}(\Sigma\setminus\{a_{2g+2}\},T^*\Sigma\otimes\mathfrak{g})$ and
$$
\left\|A\right\|_{H^{-p,-q}(\Sigma)}\leq C\| A\|_{H^{-\kappa}(\Sigma)}.
$$
More precisely, there exists a constant $C_1>0$ such that, for every $\chi\in\mathcal{C}^{\infty}(\Sigma, \mathbb{R} )$ and for every $A \in H^{-\kappa}(\Sigma,T^*\Sigma\otimes\mathfrak{g})$ that is supported in $\{\chi=1\}$, one has
$$
\left\|A\right\|_{H^{-p,-q}(\Sigma)}\leq C_1(1+\|\chi\|_{\mathcal{C}^p})\max\{d\left(a_{2g+2},x\right)^{q}:\chi(x)\neq 0\}\| A\|_{H^{-\kappa}(\Sigma)}
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma l:embedding-classical-weighted of arXiv:2607.24640

[Lemma 4 (Wave--Hodge reduction) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] Let $X=X(t,y)$ be smooth in spacetime, let $w:=X-\mathrm{id}$ and let
$\Kmat=(dX)^{-1}$.  Then the following statements hold.
 
\emph{(i) Algebraic pressure identity.}
Without using an evolution equation or the constraint $J=1$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal Q[dw]
 =-\tr \left(
   \Kmat\mathcal A^+(dw)\Kmat\mathcal A^-(dw)\right)
 =-\Kmat^a_i\Kmat^b_j
   Q_0(\partial_aw^j,\partial_bw^i).
\end{equation}
 
\emph{(ii) Smooth MHD reduction.}
Assume in addition that $X$ is the Lagrangian flow of a smooth solution of
\eqref{eq:mhd}, with $X(0)=\mathrm{id}$ and initial magnetic field $\Binf$.
If
$\mathcal Q[dw]\in L^{r_{\mathrm{HLS}}}(\mu)$ and the pressure is normalised so
that $(\nabla p)\circ X\in L^4(\mu)$ then
\[
 (\nabla p)\circ X=F[dw]=\mathcal{P}_{\gmetric[dw]}\mathcal Q[dw],
\]
and $(w,F[dw])$ satisfies \eqref{eq:auxiliary-system}. In particular, this holds when
$v,b\in C([0,T];H^\infty)$ decay together with all their derivatives and $p$ is
the Riesz pressure \eqref{eq:return-pressure}.

[Defn Basic properties of  \( {\rm Aut}(\mathbb{H}) \) of arXiv:2505.16093, 'Multiple chordal SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Moser system'] We summarize some basic properties of the conformal group \( {\rm Aut}(\mathbb{H}) \), 

\( {\rm Aut}(\mathbb{H}) \) is isomorphic to \( PSL_2(\mathbb{R}) \). By the well-known Iwasawa decomposition of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$, see [S85], every element \( \tau \in {\rm Aut}(\mathbb{H}) \) can be written as 
\[
\tau(z) = T_{a,n} \circ \rho_{\theta},
\]
where $$ \rho_\theta(z) = \frac{\cos \theta \cdot z + \sin\theta}{-\sin\theta \cdot z + \cos\theta} $$ and $$ T_{a,n}(z) = \frac{az}{nz+\frac{1}{a}} $$
where $a>0$, $n\in \mathbb{R}$ are two real constants.

Geometrically, this decomposition shows that \( {\rm Aut}(\mathbb{H}) \) is an \( S^1 \)-bundle over \( \mathbb{H} \).
title: Basic properties of  \( {\rm Aut}(\mathbb{H}) \)

[Definition def:bounded-noise of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] Consider a filtered probability space \((\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t\in[0,T]},\mathbb{P})\). A bounded noise consist in an adapted stochastic process $R:[0,T]\times \Omega\longrightarrow \mathbb{R}$ verifying the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item $R$ has continuous paths.
    \item $R(0)=0$ almost surely.
    \item We have $\mathbb{E}[R(t))]=0$ for every $0\leq t\leq T$.
    \item There exists some $M>0$ such that $\mathbb{P}\left[\max_{0\leq t\leq T}|R(t)|\leq M\right]=1$.
\end{enumerate}
We shall denote the pathwise law of such bounded noise by $\mathcal{R}_{[0,T]}={\rm Law} R_{[0,T]}\in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C}_T)$.
title: Bounded noise

Let $S=\{x_1,\dots,x_N\}$ be a finite subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$. The following are equivalent: (i) there is $y$ with $\langle y,x_i\rangle>0$ for every $i$; (ii) $0 \notin \operatorname{conv}(S)$. The frequently attempted substitute is FALSE: the condition that $\operatorname{conv}(S)$ have empty interior does NOT imply (i). Counterexample in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with $N=2$: take $x_1=e_1$ and $x_2=-e_1$. Their convex hull is a segment, which has empty interior, yet $0$ lies in it and no $y$ satisfies both inequalities. In particular, the observation that $N$ points in $\mathbb{R}^N$ span an affine hull of dimension at most $N-1$, and so have a hull with empty interior, proves nothing about separation. What does suffice is linear independence: if $N \le d$ and $x_1,\dots,x_N$ are linearly independent then (i) holds, and an explicit witness solves $\langle y,x_i\rangle = 1$ for every $i$.
S is a finite subset of R^d
for the final claim: N <= d and x_1,...,x_N are linearly independent

For 0<s<=1,

Proof. Consider z=4(n,m,l), n>=4, |m|,|l|<=floor(n/4), and f(t)=K_s(z+te) for -1<=t<=1. Throughout this interval the squared cosine with e is at least 9/11 and |z+te|<=6n. Thus

f''(t)=s |z+te|^{-s-2}[(s+2)(z_1+t)^2/|z+te|^2-1]
>= (7s/11)(6n)^{-s-2}.

The exact central-difference identity gives -I_s(z)=integral_{-1}^1 (1-|t|) f''(t)dt, so |I_s(z)|>=(7s/11)(6n)^{-s-2}. There are (2floor(n/4)+1)^2>=n^2/16 such centers for each n. Distinct n give distinct centers, and the total contribution at n is therefore at least 7s/(176*6^{s+2}) n^{-s}. The p-series diverges for 0<s<=1. This proves absolute divergence on an explicit separated set, not just an upper-bound failure or an angular heuristic. Conditional angular cancellation, renormalization, and collective screening remain possible; this is not a counterexample to crystallization.

$$
\lvert C(x,m)\lvert\leq K\left(1+\lvert x\lvert^r+\int_\R\lvert y\lvert^rm(dy)\right).
$$

Let  $\pi \in \Pi_S(\mu, \nu)$ be supermartingale $C$-monotone w.r.t. some $\Gamma$. Then $\pi$ is optimal for (WSOT).

[Definition 13 (Noncommutative differential of a trace polynomial) of arXiv:2604.03213, 'Asymptotic expansion for transport maps \\ between laws of multimatrix models'] We first set $ \partial : \C\la \cB\ra \to H_c\otimes \C\la \cB\ra^{\otimes 2} $ by
    $$ \partial P = \sum_{e\in\cB} e\otimes \partial_e P, $$
    and
    $$ \partial^{(s)} \coloneqq (\id_{H_c^{\otimes (s-1)}}\otimes \partial \otimes\id_{\C\la\cB\ra^{\otimes (s-1)}})\circ\cdots\circ (\id_{H_c}\otimes\partial\otimes\id_{\C\la\cB\ra})\circ \partial, $$
    and for $\ell\geq 1$, we define $\partial^{(s)}:\Tr^{\ell}(\cB)\to \Tr^{\ell+s}(\cB)$ by 
    \begin{align*}
        &\partial^{(s)} \left(h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_{\ell} \otimes P_1\otimes \cdots\otimes P_{\ell}\otimes \tr(R_1)\otimes \cdots\otimes \tr(R_m) \right)\\
        &\coloneqq h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_{\ell} \otimes (\partial^{(s)} P_1) \otimes P_2\otimes \cdots\otimes P_{\ell}\otimes \tr(R_1)\otimes \cdots\otimes \tr(R_m).
    \end{align*}
    We also define $\widetilde{\partial}$ by 
    \begin{align*}
        &\widetilde{\partial} \left(h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_{\ell} \otimes P_1\otimes \cdots\otimes P_{\ell}\otimes \tr(R_1)\otimes \cdots\otimes \tr(R_m) \right)\\
        &\coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^m h_1\otimes\cdots\otimes h_{\ell} \otimes \cD R_i \otimes P_1 \otimes P_2\otimes \cdots\otimes P_{\ell} \otimes \tr(R_1)\otimes \cdots \tr(R_{i-1})\otimes \tr(R_{i+1})\cdots\otimes \tr(R_m).
    \end{align*}
    And finally we set $\widetilde{\partial}^{(s)}\coloneqq \partial^{(s-1)}\circ\widetilde{\partial}$.

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2608.15914, 'Absorption cutoff and stationary singularities for rounded Gaussian random dynamical syste'] The map $V_A$ is strictly increasing on $[0,1]$ and strictly concave on
  $[0,1]$, with $V_A(0)=0$, $V_A'(0+)=A^2$, and $V_A(1)<1$. If
  $A\leq1$, then $0$ is its only fixed point. If $A>1$, then it has a unique
  nonzero fixed point $q_\ast\in(0,1)$ satisfying
  \begin{equation}
    q_\ast=V_A(q_\ast),
    \qquad
    \mu_A:=V_A'(q_\ast)\in(0,1).
  \end{equation}
  If $A>1$, every orbit of $V_A$ started from $(0,1]$ converges to $q_\ast$.
  In this case, for every $q_0\in(0,1]\setminus\{q_\ast\}$, there is a
  continuous function $C$ in a neighborhood of $q_0$, with $C(q_0)\neq0$,
  such that
  \begin{equation}
    V_A^t(q)-q_\ast
    =
    C(q)\mu_A^t+o(\mu_A^t)
  \end{equation}

[Lemma 5 (Kostlan) of arXiv:2608.20101, '\bfseries Largest bulk gap of the complex Ginibre ensemble'] Let \(z_1,\ldots,z_n\) be the eigenvalues of \(X_n\), with their labels
discarded.  The unordered multiset
\[
 \{n|z_1|^2,\ldots,n|z_n|^2\}
\]
has the same law as the unordered multiset
\(\{\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_n\}\), where the variables are independent and
\(\gamma_k\) has gamma density
\[
 \frac{x^{k-1}e^{-x}}{\Gamma(k)}\one_{\{x>0\}}\dd x.
\]
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 \Pp\{\xi_n(D_r)=0\}=\prod_{k=1}^nQ(k,nr^2).
\end{equation}

[Proposition 44 of arXiv:2609.01473, 'Keller sequences of exact $\infty$-categories'] Let $\cal{D}$ be an $\infty$-category equipped with an orthogonal factorisation system $(\cal{D}^l,\cal{D}^r)$, such that there is some object $0 \in \cal{D}$ which is initial for maps in $\cal{D}^r$.
    Let $p\colon\cal{E} \to \cal{D}$ be a functor satisfying the following:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Maps in $\cal{D}^l$ admit $p$-cocartesian lifts given any lift of their domain and maps in $\cal{D}^r$ admit $p$-cartesian lifts for any lift of their target.
        \item The fibre inclusion $\cal{F} := p^{-1}(0) \to \cal{E}$ admits a retraction $r\colon \cal{E} \to \cal{F}$. 
    \end{enumerate}
    Then the functor 
    \[ (r,p)\colon \cal{E} \to  \cal{F} \times \cal{D} \]
    is a weak homotopy equivalence.

[Theorem 79 (Commutative diagram) of arXiv:2605.14630, '2605.14630'] There exist linear maps $\W:\R[\bX]\to\R[\bX,\bY]$, 
and $\Theta_\tF: \spanF\to\spanF$ such that the following 
diagram commutes:
\begin{equation}  

\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large, row sep=large]
\R[\bX]
\arrow[r, "\cP"] 
\arrow[d, "\W"']
& \spanF
\arrow[d, "(\Pi_N\tilde{\cA}\otimes\id)\DeltaCK + \Theta_\tF"] 
\\
\displaystyle
\R[\bX,\bY]
\arrow[r, "\cP"] 
& \spanF
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
The map $\W$, called \emph{Wick map}, satisfies 
\begin{equation}
 \W(\bX^n) = H_n(\bX;-\beta\bY) \quad\forall n\geqs2
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 \W(\e^{-\alpha\bX}) = \e^{-\alpha\bX-\beta\bY}\;,
\end{equation} 
where $H_n$ is the $n$th scaled Hermite polynomial, 
while the map $\Theta_\tF$ satisfies 
\begin{equation}
 (\Pi_N\Theta_\tF\circ\cP)(\e^{-\alpha \bX})
 = - (\Pi_N\tilde\cA \circ \cP)(\e^{-\alpha \bX})
 = \gamma\;.
  
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In mathematics, Hodge theory, named after W. V. D. Hodge, is a method for studying the cohomology groups of a smooth manifold M using partial differential equations. The key observation is that, given a Riemannian metric on M, every cohomology class has a canonical representative, a differential form that vanishes under the Laplacian operator of the metric. Such forms are called harmonic.

[Theorem 15 (A priori bounds for the transformed equation) of arXiv:2608.29726, '\LARGE A Priori Estimates for Singular Fractional Stochastic Burgers Equations'] Let \(m\) be a smooth transformed solution.  When \(1<\gamma<2\), assume
that \(\Acal_\Psi^\gamma\) satisfies
\Cref{prop:transformed-operator-paralinearization,
prop:transformed-operator-coercivity}; when \(\gamma=2\), let it be the
Laplacian divergence-form operator in \eqref{eq:local-check}.  Assume also
that \eqref{eq:verified-coefficient-bounds} holds with
\[
 \rho>1-\frac\gamma2,
 \qquad
 1-\frac\gamma2<\beta<1.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\le T}\norm{m(t)}_{L^1}
  \lesssim_\Psi N_T<\infty.
\end{equation}
Moreover, there is a finite constant \(C_T\), depending only on \(T\), the
initial norms, and the coefficient, ellipticity, bi-Lipschitz, and operator
bounds in these assumptions, such that
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\le T}\norm{m(t)}_{L^2}^2
  +\int_0^T\norm{m(t)}_{H^{\gamma/2}}^2\dd t
  +Z_T^\beta(m)
  \le C_T.
\end{equation}
For every \(0<s<1/3\), there is a finite constant \(C_{T,s}\), with the
same dependence as \(C_T\) and additionally on \(s\), such that
\begin{equation}
  K_T^s(m)\le C_{T,s}<\infty.
\end{equation}

CANDIDATE APPLICATION, NOT INDEPENDENTLY REVIEWED; PRIOR-LITERATURE STATUS UNVERIFIED. Burdzy-Scheutzow (2014), Problem 7.5 asks whether a process with law equivalent to Wiener measure can receive a random finite prefix to become Brownian motion. Apply the forward filling lemma on two-sided Wiener paths with theta w(t)=w(t+1)-w(1) and density f equal to the desired future-law density. The selected future W(N+t)-W(N) has the desired law; prefixing W[0,N] recovers the original Wiener path. A standard Borel disintegration supplies the coupling for an already-given suffix process. Auxiliary randomness and non-stopping joining times are essential permitted scope; no independence of prefix and suffix is asserted. The construction actually uses absolute continuity only. Check earlier filling, shift-coupling, and Brownian embedding literature before any claim of novelty.

body: In mathematics, the Fortuin–Kasteleyn–Ginibre (FKG) inequality is a correlation inequality, a fundamental tool in statistical mechanics and probabilistic combinatorics, due to Cees M. Fortuin, Pieter W. Kasteleyn, and Jean Ginibre. Informally, it says that in many random systems, increasing events are positively correlated, while an increasing and a decreasing event are negatively correlated. It was obtained by studying the random cluster model.

In stationary ergodic strictly elliptic static nearest-neighbor RWRE let q=P_0^omega(A_l), p=E_P q, and f_n=d Law(tau_Xn omega)/dP. If 0<p<1, then B_epsilon={q<=epsilon or q>=1-epsilon} has b_epsilon=P(B_epsilon)->0 as epsilon decreases to zero, while a_n=integral_B_epsilon f_n dP->1. For r>1, E_P f_n^r>=a_n^r/b_epsilon^(r-1) whenever b_epsilon>0. Hence E_P f_n^r->infinity. No time-diverging subsequence of f_n or its Cesaro averages is uniformly integrable. [Prop existence of plus state extremal of arXiv:2608.18045, 'Supercritical sharpness for the random cluster representation of real-valued spin models'] Let $ eta_0,h_0\geq 0$. There exist $a_0,b_0>0$ such that the following properties hold for $ eta\leq  eta_0$ and $\mathsf{h}\in (\mathbb R^+)^{\mathbb Z^d}$ such that $\mathsf{h}\leq h_0$. 
 egin{enumerate}
    \item[$(i)$] The measures $
u_{\Lambda,  eta,\mathsf{h}}$ are $(a_0,b_0)$-regular for every finite $\Lambda\subset \mathbb Z^d$. In addition, they converge to a measure $
u_{ eta,\mathsf{h}}\in \mathcal{G}( eta,\mathsf{h})$ as $\Lambda
earrow \mathbb Z^d$. We call $
u_{ eta,\mathsf h}$ the infinite volume free measure at parameters $( eta, \mathsf h)$.
    \item[$(ii)$] There exists a measure $
u^+_{ eta,\mathsf{h}} \in \mathcal{G}( eta,\mathsf{h})$ which is maximal, extremal, and $(a_0,b_0)$-regular. We call $
u^+_{ eta,\mathsf{h}}$ the infinite volume plus measure at parameters $( eta,\mathsf{h})$.
\end{enumerate}

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Relate the intrinsic distance to the number of pivotals along the backbone plus the sizes of the intermediate sausages. Result: The intrinsic distance from 0 to x equals the sum over the backbone decomposition of the intrinsic distances through each 'sausage' between consecutive pivotal bonds; the number of pivotals is the object of Theorem 15.4, and the sausage lengths are i.i.d.-like with a fixed law in the mean-field picture (each sausage is a doubly connected piece of bounded expected size in d > 6 with exponential tails?). If the sausage intrinsic lengths were i.i.d. with finite mean m, then d(0,x) ~ m times the number of pivotals, and the intrinsic two-point function would follow from Theorem 15.4 by a renewal argument with n replaced by n/m. The obstruction is the dependence between sausage sizes and the backbone geometry, which is weak in high dimensions but not zero; the lace expansion with a memory of the intrinsic length would need a new expansion variable (a generating function in both the spatial variable and the intrinsic length), which is what the source suggests. A rigorous partial result: the intrinsic length is at least the number of pivotals plus one, so tau_n^{(in)} summed over n >= N is bounded by the pivotal-count two-point function summed over counts >= N... wait the direction: d(0,x) >= |Piv(0,x)| + 1 gives P(d >= N) >= P(|Piv| >= N - 1), a lower bound on the intrinsic tail from the pivotal tail, hence the intrinsic one-arm probability is at least the pivotal one-arm probability, consistent with both being of order 1/N. No asymptotic constant. Key identity: d_{C(0)}(0,x) >= |Piv(0,x)| + 1, so intrinsic tails dominate pivotal tails. Obstruction: Joint expansion in space and intrinsic length not available.

[Thm thm_gGE of arXiv:2411.17216, 'Large deviations of the empirical measures of a strong-Feller Markov process inside a subs'] Let $(\mathbb P_T)_{T>0}$ be a sequence of probability distribution on $\mathcal P(\mathscr S)$, such that:

\begin{enumerate}
\item For any potential $V\in b\mathcal B(\mathscr D)$,
\begin{equation}
\boldsymbol \Lambda(V)=\lim_{T\to +\infty} \frac{1}{T} \log \int_{\mathcal P(\mathscr D)} e^{T\beta(V)} \mathbb P_T (d\beta).
\end{equation}

  \item The mapping $V\mapsto \boldsymbol \Lambda(V)$ is Gateaux differentiable on $b\mathcal B(\mathscr D)$, i.e. the mapping $t\mapsto \boldsymbol \Lambda(V+t V_1)$ is differentiable  at $t=0$ for any potential $V,V_1\in b\mathcal B(\mathscr D)$.
  \item $\mathbb P_T$ is exponentially $*$-tight, namely,  $\forall L>0,\ \exists \mathbf K $ compact in $(\mathcal P(\mathscr D),\tau)$ such that for any measurable neighborhood $\mathcal{N}$ of $\mathbf K$,
  $$
  \limsup_{T\to +\infty} \frac{1}{T} \log \mathbb P_T [L_T\notin \mathcal{N}] \leqslant -L.
  $$
\end{enumerate}
Then, $\mathbb P_T$ satisfies the {\rm L.D.P.} on $(\mathcal P(\mathscr D), \tau)$ with speed $T$ and the rate function
$$
I(\beta)=\sup\left\{\beta(V)-\boldsymbol \Lambda (V),\ V\in \mathcal C_b(\mathscr D)\right\}, \ \beta\in \mathcal P(\mathscr D),
$$
which is the Legendre transform $\boldsymbol  \Lambda^*$ of the Cramer functional $\boldsymbol \Lambda$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 1 (The \JKL{} formulation of Einstein areal flows) of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] Consider four-dimensional spacetimes $(\Mcal,\guntrois)$ with spatial topology $\Tbb^3$ and two commuting spacelike Killing fields with closed orbits, admitting a foliation by the area~$|t|$ of the symmetry orbits. Consider a constitutive law $p=p(\mu)$ (pressure vs.\ mass-energy density) satisfying hyperbolicity and asymptotic conditions (stated in~\eqref{hyperbolic-eos-zero}, below). Then the following properties hold.
\bei

\item \textbf{Perfect-fluid matter model.} In the class of regular flows, the Einstein--Euler system 
\bel{equa-49F}
G^{\alpha\beta} = T^{\alpha\beta},
\qquad
\nabla_\alpha T^{\alpha\beta}=0
\ee
is equivalent to an \emph{evolution--constraint, first-order differential system} in terms of the variables \eqref{equa-phipsi}, as  given in \eqref{eq:T2-1234-def}--\eqref{equa-9385}, below, and referred to as the \JKL{} system. Its evolution subsystem has essentially \emph{quadratic nonlinearities} with a partial \emph{null structure} and, away from vacuum, is strongly hyperbolic.   All differential operators in the formulation 
remain defined on the full (closed) state space, including cavitation and near-light speed fluid propagation, although the hyperbolicity degenerates at non-zero null states.  

\item \textbf{Particle-production dissipative model.} Analogous properties hold for the following class of Einstein--Navier--Stokes systems
\bel{eq:pot-production-system0}
G^{\alpha\beta}=T_\chi^{\alpha\beta},
\qquad
\nabla_\alpha T_\chi^{\alpha\beta}=0,
\qquad
\nabla_\alpha A_\chi^{\alpha\beta\gamma}
=-\mathscr B^{\beta\gamma}, 
\ee
namely an extension of the Einstein--Euler system by adjoining to the fluid variables a symmetric two-tensor relaxation field~$\zeta$. The tensors $T_\chi$ and $A_\chi$ are defined from second-order derivatives
of a \emph{Navier--Stokes potential} denoted by~$\chi$, which is assumed to satisfy suitable equilibrium, dominant-energy, and causal-hyperbolicity conditions in \autoref{def-pot-hyperbolic}. The relaxation rate tensor~$\mathscr B$ is prescribed and satisfies suitable stable-equilibrium and positivity conditions in \autoref{def-pot-source}. In particular, the coupled evolution equations are symmetric hyperbolic in the interior of the state space, and both Einstein equations and Bianchi equations are satisfied.  The associated particle-number current~$\vNumb_\chi$ satisfies $\nabla_\alpha \vNumb_\chi^\alpha = \zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}\geq 0$.

\item \textbf{Dissipated-energy dissipative model.} 
Analogous properties also hold for the following class of Einstein--Navier--Stokes systems
\bel{eq:pot-dissipated-system0}
\begin{aligned}
G^{\alpha\beta}
&=T_\chi^{\alpha\beta}+T_{\rm aux}^{\alpha\beta}, \quad
&
\nabla_\alpha T_\chi^{\alpha\beta}
&=-\sigma n^\beta, \quad
&
\nabla_\alpha A_\chi^{\alpha\beta\gamma}
&=-\mathscr B^{\beta\gamma},
\end{aligned}
\ee 
with 
\be
\begin{aligned}
T_{\rm aux}^{\alpha\beta}
&=\sigma \underline\pi^{\alpha\beta},
&
\sigma & \coloneqq \frac{\zeta_{\alpha\beta} \mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}}{-n_\alpha\beta^\alpha} \geq 0. 
\end{aligned}
\ee 
Here $\underline\pi^{\alpha\beta}$ is the (rescaled) projection onto the symmetry orbits, $n_\alpha$ is the future-directed normal to the areal foliation, and $\beta$ is the rescaled fluid momentum.
The model includes an auxiliary stress tensor~$T_{\rm aux}$ (\autoref{def-diss-en}), which compensates the mass-energy dissipated by~$T_\chi$. In particular, the coupled evolution equations are symmetric hyperbolic in the interior of the state space, and both Einstein equations and Bianchi equations are satisfied.
The associated particle-number current~$\vNumb_\chi$ is divergence-free.
\eei
\noindent For all three systems, the Einstein constraints propagate from one areal hypersurface, and the metric variables are reconstructed from the transport, constraint, and periodicity equations. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The \JKL{} formulation of Einstein areal flows

body: Let X be a normed vector space over R or C, and let X* be its continuous dual space equipped with the weak-* topology (pointwise convergence on X). Then the closed unit ball B* = {f in X* : ||f|| <= 1} is compact in the weak-* topology. More generally, the polar of any neighborhood of 0 in X is weak-* compact. Completeness or separability of X is not required; the proof rests on Tychonoff's theorem, and if X is separable then B* with the weak-* topology is also metrizable.
title: Banach-Alaoglu theorem

body: Publication record. Question 17.18 of R. Lyons and Y. Peres, Probability on Trees and Networks (Question 3 of Section 10 of Lyons, Pemantle and Peres, Ergodic theory on Galton-Watson trees, 1995) asks whether a flow rule with a stationary measure equivalent to the Galton-Watson measure GW must give an ergodic chain. Y. Shmalo, A nonergodic flow rule with Galton-Watson stationary measure (October 2026) answers no: for the offspring law p_2 = 3/5, p_3 = 2/5 an AND/OR colouring is a function of the tree, the flow rule that spreads the flow evenly over the children of the root that share its colour has GW stationary, and the event that the root has colour 1, of probability 1/2, is invariant, so the chain is not ergodic; GW(.|C = 1) and GW(.|C = 0) are its ergodic components. Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/nonergodic-galton-watson-flow-rule (commit 837dd0c8da7d). Not refereed; an outside audit is owed.

[Theorem 30 of arXiv:2609.03831, 'On flows generated by square-integrable vector fields'] Let $I\subset \R$ be an open interval.
	Let $\v \in \boldsymbol{L}^2(\R^d)$ be a compactly supported divergence-free
	vector field and suppose that $\v$ has the renormalization property in $L^\infty(I; L^2(\R^d))$.
	Then for any $s\in \overline{I}$ and any $\rho_0 \in L^2(\R^d)$ the continuity
	equation has at most one weak solution $\rho \in L^\infty(I; L^2(\R^d))$
	such that $\rho|_s = \rho_0$.

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); independent mathematical, priority and scope audit pending. Let d>=1,N>=2d+1,K>=2,1<=r<K,F=K-r,gcd(r,F)=1. There are d unknown A/S context pairs with r arbitrary truths in A and all K truths in S, others known S. The source selects contexts uniformly then truths uniformly. Observe n iid untagged facts and independent uniform ell-subsets of truths in BOTH variable contexts, including S. Assume ceil(K/2)<=ell<=r and 0<=n<=r-ell. Each realized generator must have source Mis_infinity<=c in every compatible world at exact generator-score bins, 0<=c<1/(2NrK). Let h_i be the smaller observed-plus-certified truth union size in pair i,H=max_i h_i,b_h=[1/K+(r-h)/(r(K-h))]/(2N),tau_h=F/(2(K-h)). Every feasible generator has false mass at least sum_i F*b_hi-c*tau_H in EACH compatible world. Selecting h_i known truths from each sibling, pooling paired residuals, then moving c mass from a largest-h residual group to fixed S attains equality in all worlds. Thus the exact global expected robust minimax frontier is Gamma(c)=E[sum_i F*b_hi]-c*E[tau_H], with exact polynomial-time occupancy coefficient evaluation in the proof. For the same-data supplied-partition oracle, let a_i be the known union size in actual A context i. Its pointwise value is sum_i F*(r-a_i)/(Nr(K-a_i))-c*max({F/(K-a_i):a_i<r} union {0}). Its expectation is the exact global oracle O(c), and Gamma(c)-O(c) is the matching experiment-specific learning penalty. Zero-residual groups a_i=r must not supply a slope-one coefficient. The proof is pointwise weighted Cauchy-Schwarz on invariant-bin residual objects, not averaging conditional maxima. The class has VC dimension d. This is a fractional-verifier infinite family with n allowed to grow with K, but not a classical labeled ERM/PAC theorem or unrestricted longer-sample result.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:2c717d067c6da4462e3891f795f17fbed5873c863178801bd02b0ed6b1b8b79f","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/2c/2c717d067c6da4462e3891f795f17fbed5873c863178801bd02b0ed6b1b8b79f.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:7423c431828c9909c7b6bcba53f72350fd5e1df2022fcd1dc2a0e012065ced38","bundle_entry_key":"high-fraction-partial-verifier-global-frontier","bundle_id":"population.t379-high-fraction-partial-verifier-global-vc-frontier-20261020","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"calibrated generation; partial truth verification; global VC minimax","draft":"w709/bundle_015.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.calibration:kalai-vempala-high-fraction-partial-verifier-arbitrary-vc-global-frontier","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# High-fraction partial verification: arbitrary-VC global frontier

T379-C023 v2, proof (unaudited); exact checks PASS. Target1; secondary target2.

## Model and conditional theorem candidate

There are d>=1 independent A/S pairs and N-2d>=1 known S contexts, K
candidates per context, r arbitrary truths in A and K truths in S.
Put F=K-r and assume gcd(r,F)=1. Source p chooses contexts uniformly,
then truths uniformly. Observe actual untagged iid facts and independently
uniform ell-subsets of truths from BOTH variable contexts, including S.
For observed-plus-certified union sizes j_x, suppose ALL pairs remain
unresolved (every j_x<=r) and h_i=min(j_iL,j_iR)>=K/2.
Let H=max_i h_i and 0<=c<1/(2NrK). Every realized generator is required
to satisfy source Mis_infinity<=c in all compatible worlds.

Define
 b_h=[1/K+(r-h)/(r(K-h))]/(2N), tau_h=F/[2(K-h)].

Pointwise matching candidate theorem (unaudited):

 EVERY feasible g has H_theta(g)>=sum_i F*b_hi-c*tau_H
 in EACH compatible actual world theta. A causal pooling rule attains
 equality simultaneously in every world.                       (1)

This strengthens the C019 conditional worst-world assertion in the
high-known-count regime. It does not average a conditional maximum.

## Hardest step: a weighted cell inequality

C019's bin-mass lattice and coprime support expansion apply: every
score-bin source mass is world-invariant, and forgetting surplus known
truths down to the smaller count h_i preserves the same generator's
source bin masses and actual false-count vectors for every orientation.
Fix any actual world in the expanded balanced-minimum game. Write

 C=(K+r)/(2NrK), E=1/(Nr), q_i=2(K-h_i)/F.

Use its fair orientation mean only to COMPUTE common source bin masses;
do not substitute fair orientations for actual sampling likelihoods.
The invariant-bin classification gives the following components:

* A common residual bin of pair i peels k_i<=h_i known truths from each
  sibling. Its object has m=2(K-k_i) atoms, f=F actual false atoms, and
  source mass m*b_ki=C*m-E*f. Thus m>=f*q_i.
* If the two outside bins differ, each contains a whole context. The
  actual A context is an object m=K,f=F, source mass1/N. Since h_i>=K/2,
  m>=f*q_i. Its source mass is >=C*m-E*f, with excess F/(2Nr).
  The actual S context is safe with density lambda=1/(NK).
* Both saturated h_i=r,r may split outside atoms into balanced sub-bins.
  A balanced outside component has m=2v,f=v, source mass lambda*m/2
  =C*m-E*f, and q_i=2. Known truths in these bins are safe.
  A coprime unbalanced bin contains a whole context and uses the previous
  case. No assertion forces ALL saturated outside atoms into one bin.
* Remaining certified/fixed atoms are safe and have mean source density
  >=lambda; safe whole-S components have density lambda.

All risk-bearing objects have mean source density <=lambda. For a bin
containing them, analytically remove its safe components of density
>=lambda. This weakly lowers its mean source density and therefore its
actual false mass. This is a scalar inequality, not a new generator or
a data-dependent deletion. Let its remaining objects have sizes m_a,
false counts f_a>0 and targets q_a=q_i of the originating pair.
Put M=sum m_a, f=sum f_a. Its original false mass is at least

 f*(sum object_source)/M >= C*f-E*f^2/M
 >= C*f-E*sum_a(f_a/q_a)
 =sum_a f_a*b_hi.                                      (2)

Here M>=sum f_a*q_a and weighted Cauchy--Schwarz gives
f^2/(sum f_a*q_a)<=sum f_a/q_a.
Every pair has total actual false count F among its objects, so summing
bins proves H_theta(p0)>=sum_i F*b_hi for the common coarsened source p0.

The SAME component bounds give actual false fractions <=1/q_i=tau_hi:
common residual objects have k_i<=h_i, whole-A objects satisfy K>=2(K-h_i),
and saturated split objects have fraction1/2=tau_r. Safe atoms only lower
the fraction. Hence every actual score-bin risk is <=tau_H. Calibration
TV c reduces actual false mass by at most c*tau_H, proving (1).

Attain (1) by selecting h_i known truths in each sibling and pooling
their paired 2(K-h_i) residuals at their common source density. Remove
c mass from any count-H residual group and transfer it to fixed S.
Every group source mass is invariant and its actual false fraction is
tau_hi. The strict budget is smaller than every positive group mass.
Ties/selections may be randomized as policies; never average output laws.

## Actual iid global regime and exact frontier

Assume ceil(K/2)<=ell<=r<K and 0<=n<=r-ell. Then every possible data
outcome has j_x<=ell+n<=r and h_i>=ell>=K/2. Thus (1) applies to ALL
outcomes, and the exact global expected robust minimax is

 Gamma(c)=E[sum_i F*b_hi]-c*E[tau_H].                    (3)

Both bounds are pointwise in each world before expectation. The class has
VC dimension d. The estimator has polynomial arithmetic complexity in
n,NK. This is an experiment-specific expected robust frontier, not a
classical labeled-sample ERM/PAC theorem.

The expectation in (3) has a polynomial-time exact coefficient formula.
For m in {r,K} define the truth-union occupancy probability

 P_m(j|u)=binom(m-ell,j-ell)/m^u
           *sum_{a=0}^{j-ell}(-1)^a binom(j-ell,a)(j-a)^u,

using 0^0=1. All polynomials below are truncated after degree n.
For one actual A/S pair let

 B_h(z)=sum_{u+v<=n} z^(u+v)/(u!v!)
           *sum_{a=ell}^r sum_{b=ell}^K
                1_{min(a,b)=h} P_r(a|u) P_K(b|v).
 E_t(z)=sum_{h=ell}^t B_h(z).

Then E_r(z)=exp(2z) modulo z^(n+1). Set

 G_t=n!/N^n *[z^n] exp((N-2d)z)*E_t(z)^d.

This is the exact CDF P(H<=t); the coefficient handles multinomial
context counts without assuming independent learned counts. Therefore

 Gamma(c)=d*n!/N^n *[z^n] exp((N-2)z)*sum_h F*b_h*B_h(z)
   -c*(tau_ell+sum_{h=ell+1}^r(tau_h-tau_(h-1))*(1-G_(h-1))). (4)

This expression holds for every fixed world because support/certificate
permutations carry the full experiment to each other.

## Same-data supplied-partition oracle

Let a_i be the known union size in actual A context i. Its residual
source density is A_a=(r-a)/(Nr(K-a)), false fraction alpha_a=F/(K-a).
The pointwise oracle value in the same small-budget regime is

 O(D,c)=sum_i F*A_ai
          -c*max({alpha_ai:a_i<r} union {0}).             (5)

Groups with a_i=r have zero residual source mass, and must not contribute
a slope-one coefficient. Ordered residual-density/risk tails, or the
already saved C009 known-partition argument, prove (5); native residual
groups and transfer to fixed S attain it in every support.

For an explicit expectation define, for ell-1<=t<=r-1,

 A_t(z)=sum_{u=0}^n z^u/u! *
            sum_{j in ({ell,...,t} union {r})}P_r(j|u),
 F_t=n!/N^n *[z^n] exp((N-d)z)*A_t(z)^d.

Thus F_t is the probability that every A union is either saturated r or
<=t; F_(ell-1) is the probability all A unions are saturated.
Let

 T(z)=sum_{u=0}^n z^u/u!*sum_{j=ell}^r P_r(j|u)*F*A_j.

The exact global oracle is

 O(c)=d*n!/N^n*[z^n]exp((N-1)z)*T(z)
  -c*(alpha_ell*(1-F_(ell-1))
       +sum_{j=ell+1}^{r-1}(alpha_j-alpha_(j-1))*(1-F_(j-1))). (6)

Empty sums have value zero. The exact matching learning penalty is
Gamma(c)-O(c), with (4) and (6). It is not claimed equal to ordinary
binary classification error.

## Limits, source and pending verification

For ell<r this is a genuine fractional-verifier family, with arbitrary d
and n up to r-ell, not just an isolated sample size. E.g. r=K-1 is always
coprime, ell=ceil(K/2) permits n growing linearly with K. Lower verifier
fractions, longer samples with resolved pairs, noncoprime saturation and
larger calibration budgets remain open here. Full verifier ell=r with
arbitrary n was separately handled by C022.

Calibration statistic: Kalai--Vempala2311.14648v3 Definitions1--2 pp8--9.
Structural reduction: C019; occupancy: C021; weighted Cauchy--Schwarz is
standard. Exact finite/algebraic checks and independent audit pending.

## Exact verification and standard-method attribution

verifier twelve-atom experiments, 18190 exact pointwise TV-ball optima,

coefficient comparisons against independent full joint occupancy sums
covering18182 outcomes. There are36364 same-data oracle comparisons and

and Fraction. The old h=0,h=1 C015/C020 pointwise failure is reproduced

The weighted Cauchy step is STANDARD. Brain recall/walk006.txt supplies
claim_e2c9498384f7c85c7e0659ae49dcad0ef383c3b44e1c9c2e77befccd273596f1,
Schatten Hoelder at p=q=2, which applies to column vectors
sqrt(f_a*q_a) and sqrt(f_a/q_a). An entirely rational identity is

[Theorem 27 (Widom {\cite[Theorem~3) of arXiv:2608.17509, '2608.17509'] {Widom1982}}]

Let \(\sigma\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})\), and let \(W_L(\sigma)\) be the truncated Wiener--Hopf operator on \(L^2(0,L)\). Suppose that there exists a bounded determination \(\psi\) of \(\log\sigma\) whose inverse Fourier transform \(\check{\psi}\) satisfies
\[
\int_{\mathbb{R}}|x|\,|\check{\psi}(x)|^2\,\mathrm{d}x<\infty.
\]
Then \(W_L(\sigma)\exp(-W_L(\psi))\) is of determinant class, and
\[
\det\bigl(W_L(\sigma)\exp(-W_L(\psi))\bigr)
\to
\exp\left(
\int_0^{\infty}x\check{\psi}(x)\check{\psi}(-x)\,\mathrm{d}x
\right)
\]
as \(L\to\infty\). If, in addition, \(\psi\in L^1(\mathbb{R})\), then
\[
\det W_L(\sigma)
\exp\left(
-\frac{L}{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\psi(\xi)\,\mathrm{d}\xi
\right)
\to
\exp\left(
\int_0^{\infty}x\check{\psi}(x)\check{\psi}(-x)\,\mathrm{d}x
\right),
\]
where \(\det W_L(\sigma)\) denotes the Fredholm determinant of \(W_L(\sigma)=\operatorname{Id}+W_L(\sigma-1)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\begin{enumeratea}
\item 
Let $0<\alpha< d/3$ and $\alpha<\theta< 2\alpha$.
Then for $x\in\Lambda_n\setminus\{0\}$,
\begin{align}
	\pr(0 \connects x)
	\asymp
	\begin{cases}
		\zeta_n^{-1} \| x\|^{-\alpha}\, ,
		\ \ \text{ if }\ \ 0< \|x\| \leq \diam(\Lambda_n)^{a_0} \, ,
		\\[4pt]
		|\Lambda_n|^{-(d+\alpha - \theta)/d}\, , 
		\text{ if }\ \  \diam(\Lambda_n)^{a_0} < \|x\| \leq \diam(\Lambda_n) \, ,
	\end{cases}
\end{align}
where $a_0 := 2 - \theta\alpha^{-1}$.

\vskip2pt

\item
Let $0 < \alpha < d/3$ and $2\alpha\leq \theta < \alpha + d/3$.
Then
\[
\pr(0 \connects x)
\asymp
|\Lambda_n|^{-(d+\alpha - \theta)/d} 
\ \text{ for }\ x\in\Lambda_n\setminus\{ 0 \}\, .
\]

\item 
Let $d/3\leq \alpha\leq 5d/6$ and $\alpha<\theta<\alpha + d/3$.
Then \eqref{eqn:788-a} continues to hold.

\vskip2pt

\item 
Let $5d/6 < \alpha < d$ and $\alpha < \theta < 2d - \alpha$.

\end{enumeratea} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:raw-velocity-decay of arXiv:2605.20697, 'Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for \\ Second-Order Consensus-Based Optimization'] Under the assumptions of (thm:exp-decay-centered-moments of the paper) for \(p\geqslant 2\), 
    assume in addition that \(\mathbf{E}|V_0^j|^p<\infty\). 
    Set $\eta_p := \frac{p\gamma}{2m}.$
    Then there exists a constant \(C_V>0\) such that, for all \(t\geqslant 0\),
    \[
        \mathbf{E}|V_t^j|^p
        \leqslant
        \begin{cases}
            C_V \e^{-\lambda_{p} t},
            & \text{if } \lambda_{p} < \eta_p, \\[0.4em]
            C_V(1+t)\e^{-\eta_p t},
            & \text{if } \lambda_{p} = \eta_p, \\[0.4em]
            C_V \e^{-\eta_p t},
            & \text{if } \lambda_{p} > \eta_p.
        \end{cases}
    \]
    Equivalently, away from the critical case \(\lambda_{p}=\eta_p\), the raw velocity decays at rate
    \[
        \lambda_{p}^*:= \min\left\{\lambda_{p},\eta_p\right\}
        =
        \min\left\{\lambda_{p},\frac{p\gamma}{2m}\right\}.
    \]
title: Exponential Decay of Raw Velocity

\[

STATEMENT
Fix eta,epsilon>0 and a positive two-coordinate diagonal quadratic.
Use ordinary separately bias-corrected Adam with b=.9,d=.999,
epsilon OUTSIDE sqrt and standard m0=v0=0. Let
theta_h=eta*lambda_h/epsilon>38 and theta_l=eta*lambda_l/epsilon=38.
Assume x_l,0 is nonzero. If BOTH physical coordinates approach their
origins, then x_l,t is eventually nonzero and

 x_l,t+1/x_l,t -> -1 OR -b,
 g_h,t/g_l,t ->0,
 A_t=eta*C_active,t ->38, S_t=eta*S_top,t ->theta_h>38.

The alternatives concern the actual nonzero scalar solution; neither
root is asserted to occur generically. No existence or size of a
nonzero-high origin basin is claimed.

Combining this result with012v2 and024v2 gives the following sharper
critical-line classification for the SAME standard initialization,
under the explicit hypothesis x_l,0 != 0:

 x_l,0 != 0: [A_t->38 and liminf S_t>38] IFF [x_h,t->0]. (1)

Thus the gradient-alignment condition in022v2's critical origin type
is automatic once both coordinates converge to zero and the critical
coordinate's initial position is nonzero. This covers every high cap
theta_h>38, including cycle-neutral and stable-cycle cap parameters;
it is not an origin-basin avoidance or generic-tracking theorem.

PRIOR WORK AND HARDEST STEP
The recurrence theorem used below is CLASSICAL, not a new method:
Borcea--Friedland--Shapiro, arXiv0909.1216v1, actual version title
"On Asymptotic Ratio of a Sequence of Functions Obeying a Finite
Recurrence Relation", Theorem3 (headed Poincare--Perron), printed p4. The ratio-convergence
part used here is Poincare's theorem (1885).
The paragraph before it states the discrete version. Coefficient limits
and characteristic roots of distinct absolute values give the ratio
limit for each nontrivial, not-eventually-zero solution. Here every
last recurrence coefficient is nonzero and the position pair never
vanishes. There is no need for summable coefficient convergence or an
assumed generic coefficient of the dominant root. Perron's additional
root-attainment conclusion for nonvanishing last coefficients is not
used: we do not claim that either root occurs for a standard Adam start.

The new Adam step is to combine this pointwise scalar conclusion with
the supercritical origin rate q<b in025v1. The earlier inverse-Lyapunov
pair bound gave only a dominating SUBSEQUENCE of scalar positions.

1. CHECK THE ACTUAL SCALAR RECURRENCE
For either coordinate put
P_t=sqrt(v_(t+1)/(1-d^(t+1)))+epsilon,
a_t=eta/[(1-b^(t+1))*P_t]>0.
Eliminate raw momentum from x_(t+1)=x_t-a_t*m_(t+1) and
m_(t+1)=b*m_t+(1-b)*lambda*x_t. For t>=1,

 x_(t+1)=[1+b*a_t/a_(t-1)-(1-b)*lambda*a_t]*x_t
                         -b*a_t/a_(t-1)*x_(t-1).       (2)

Along any fixed actual trajectory these are a particular scalar linear
recurrence's coefficient sequences. Their dependence on the trajectory
does not obstruct applying a deterministic recurrence theorem after
the trajectory is fixed.

If x_t->0, the stable raw variance recursion gives v_t->0, so P_t->epsilon,
a_t->eta/epsilon and a_t/a_(t-1)->1. At cap theta_l=38 the limiting
characteristic polynomial is

 r^2-[1+b-(1-b)*38]*r+b = (r+1)*(r+b).                  (3)

At every finite t the last coefficient in(2) is nonzero. Since
(x_l,1,x_l,0) is nonzero, the invertible position-pair recurrence shows
no later pair can be zero. In particular the solution cannot be
eventually zero. Poincare's ratio theorem applies to(2): its limiting roots
-1 and-b have distinct moduli because0<b<1. Therefore the low scalar
position is eventually nonzero and its ratio converges to one of those
roots. This is a statement about EVERY such nontrivial solution, not
only the dominant-root solutions.

2. UPGRADE SUBSEQUENCE DOMINANCE TO POINTWISE DOMINANCE
For the high coordinate tending to its origin,025v1 Section2 supplies
some q<b and C<infinity with |x_h,t|<=C*q^t. Its Green contraction
does not depend on any low-coordinate rate. If that coordinate starts
at zero it stays zero and the same bound is trivial.

Choose nu with q<nu<b. The ratio conclusion for the low coordinate
gives |x_l,t+1|>=nu*|x_l,t| at all sufficiently large t. Iteration
from a sufficiently late nonzero position gives c>0 such that
|x_l,t|>=c*nu^t for every sufficiently large t. Thus

 |g_h,t/g_l,t| <= (lambda_h*C)/(lambda_l*c)*(q/nu)^t ->0. (4)

Both variance denominators tend to epsilon, and the nonzero low
gradient dominates their weights. Consequently A_t->theta_l=38.
The two preconditioned curvatures tend to theta_h and38, respectively,
so S_t->theta_h>38. The active quotient is eventually defined.

3. SHARPER CRITICAL-LINE CLASSIFICATION
For the reverse implication in(1),012v2 gives x_l,t->0 for every
standard initial position at cap38. Hence x_h,t->0 implies both origins,
and Sections1--2 give the left side of(1).

For the forward implication in(1),024v2 gives that, under A_t->38,
the high coordinate approaches its origin or its exact alternating
cycle. In the cycle alternative its denominator tends to eta*lambda_h/38;
the critical denominator tends to epsilon. Both scaled curvatures
then tend to38, contradicting liminf S_t>38. Only the high-origin
alternative remains. This proves(1), with x_l,0 != 0 as stated.
The dependencies012v2,024v2 and025v1 now all have reviewer PASS;
Section1--2 use025's high-origin rate and Poincare's ratio theorem.

ZERO CRITICAL INITIALIZATION IS EXCLUDED FOR A REASON
If x_l,0=0, that coordinate remains zero and cannot dominate the active
gradient. A nonzero high gradient converging to zero would give active
limit theta_h>38, even while both coordinates tend to zero. The
nonzero-low assumption cannot be discarded. This result makes no
claim for complex equal-modulus limiting roots on other low caps.

[Definition Distinguished orbit of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] Let \(\gamma\) be a closed orbit of \(\varphi\) and let \(P\) be a prong of \(\gamma\).
Then \(\gamma\) is said to be \(z\)-\emph{distinguished} in \(P\)-direction if there exists a surface \(S\) with \([S]=z\) such that \(P\cap S\) contains a closed curve component.
Equivalently, according to \autocite[Lemma 8.3]{LandryMinskyTaylor2022_FlowsGrowthRatesAndTheVeeringPolynomial_PUB}, a power of \(\gamma\) is homotopic to a closed leaf of either \(W_{S}^{s}\) or \(W_{S}^{u}\), where \(W_{S}^{s/u}= W^{s/u}\cap S\) on \(S\).
title: Distinguished orbit

[Theorem 20 (Convergence theorem \cite{Yakymiv}) of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] Let $X$ and $X_1, X_2, \dots$ be random variables with moment-generating
  functions $M_X$ and $M_{X_1}, M_{X_2}, \dots$ respectively.
  Assume these \textsc{mgf}s are finite
  on some interval $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ that is bounded, open and non-empty.
  Then $M_{X_m}$ converges pointwise to $M_X$ on $I$
  if and only if
  \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item $X_m$ converges weakly to $X$; and
    \item $\sup_m M_{X_m}(t) < \infty$ for all $t \in I$.
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Convergence theorem \cite{Yakymiv}

[Lemat 13 of arXiv:2609.03054, 'The classes of bivariate Schur and Herglotz matrix-valued rational functions: realizations'] Given a contraction 
  \begin{equation}\begin{bmatrix} A_1 & A_2\cr A_2 & A_1\end{bmatrix},\end{equation}
  there exists an orthogonal projection
  $P={\tiny \begin{bmatrix} P_1 & P_2\cr P_2 & P_1\end{bmatrix}}$ and a contraction $B={\tiny \begin{bmatrix} B_1 & B_2\cr B_2 & B_1\end{bmatrix}}$ with $1\not\in \sigma(B)$, so that $PB=0=BP$ and
  $$\begin{bmatrix} A_1 & A_2\cr A_2 & A_1\end{bmatrix}= \begin{bmatrix} P_1 & P_2\cr P_2 & P_1\end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} B_1 & B_2\cr B_2 & B_1\end{bmatrix} .$$

  In case \eqref{A} is a real matrix, $B$ and $P$ can be chosen to be real as well.

Let a Poisson(lambda) Galton-Watson process have lambda>1 and extinction probability q in (0,1), satisfying q=exp(-lambda(1-q)). Conditional on extinction its offspring law is Poisson(lambda q). If I(a)=a-1-log a, then I(lambda q)=I(lambda) exactly. For lambda=1+epsilon with epsilon decreasing to zero, lambda q=1-epsilon+(2/3)epsilon^2+O(epsilon^3). This is a branching-process mechanism for discrete duality; it does not prove that hypercube clusters after deleting the giant have this law.

body: [Theorem 11 of arXiv:2512.19063, 'Sharp Decoupling Inequalities for the Variances and Second Moments of Sums of Dependent Ra'] With the same setting as Theorem 6, we have a Chebyshev-type inequality for any $t>0$, $\mathbb{P}\left(|S_{n}-\mathbb{E} S_{n}|>t\right)\leq\frac{2\operatorname{Var}(S^{\prime}_{n})}{t^{2}}.$ (15) If in addition $S_{n}\geq 0$ a.s., we have a Paley-Zygmund-type inequality for any $0<\theta<1$, $\mathbb{P}(S_{n}>\theta\,\mathbb{E} S_{n})\geq(1-\theta)^{2}\,\frac{(\mathbb{E} S_{n})^{2}}{2\mathbb{E}{S^{\prime}}_{n}^{2}-(\mathbb{E} S_{n})^{2}}=(1-\theta)^{2}\,\frac{1}{\frac{2\mathbb{E}{S^{\prime}}_{n}^{2}}{(\mathbb{E} S_{n})^{2}}-1}.$

body:
[Theorem 19 of arXiv:2605.06556, 'Probability of Quota Violations in Divisor Apportionment Methods with Nonzero Allocations'] (Asymptotic Quota Stabilization) Let $\bm\tau$ be a nonexceptional parameter vector for which Theorem~\ref{lim_1_nstates} holds. Then there exists $x_{\bm{\tau}}$ such that for all $x\ge x_{\bm\tau}$

$$
A(1,x,y_1(x,\tau_1),\dots,y_{n-2}(x,\tau_{n-2}))
= \tilde A_1(\tilde q_2,\dots,\tilde q_n).
$$

Consequently the quota behavior stabilizes: for sufficiently large $x$, the apportionment is always either quota compliant, a quota violation caused by nonzero allocation, a quota violation worsened by nonzero allocation, or an upper quota violation. Moreover, this behavior depends only on $\bm{\tau}$. If $A(\tilde q_2,\dots,\tilde q_n)=(\tilde a_2,\dots,\tilde a_n)$ is the apportionment of $M$ seats among states $2,\dots,n$ and state $i$ receive the last seat then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $A(\tilde q_2,\dots,\tilde q_n)$ is not a quota violation and $\tilde a_i=\lfloor\tilde q_i\rfloor$, then the asymptotic apportionment is a quota violation caused by nonzero allocation.
\item If $A(\tilde q_2,\dots,\tilde q_n)$ is not a quota violation and $\tilde a_i=\lceil\tilde q_i\rceil$, then the asymptotic apportionment is not a quota violation.
\item If $A(\tilde q_2,\dots,\tilde q_n)$ is an upper quota violation where state $i$ is the only state assigned more than its upper quota and $\tilde{a}_i = \lceil\tilde q_i\rceil +1$, then the asymptotic apportionment is not a quota violation.
\item If $A(\tilde q_2,\dots,\tilde q_n)$ is an upper quota violation and case (3) does not apply, then the asymptotic apportionment is an upper quota violation.
\item If $A(\tilde q_2,\dots,\tilde q_n)$ is a lower quota violation, then the asymptotic apportionment is a quota violation worsened by nonzero allocation.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let D = {z in C : |z| < 1} and let f : D → D be holomorphic with f(0) = 0. Then |f(z)| ≤ |z| for every z in D, and |f'(0)| ≤ 1. Moreover, if |f(z0)| = |z0| for some z0 in D with z0 ≠ 0, or if |f'(0)| = 1, then f is a rotation: f(z) = λz for a constant λ with |λ| = 1. (The hypothesis f(D) ⊂ D may be weakened to |f| ≤ 1 on D, since a nonconstant such f maps D into D by the open mapping theorem and the constant must be 0.) Without f(0) = 0 the correct statement is the Schwarz–Pick theorem.

body:
[Lemma 2 of arXiv:2605.11264, 'Uniform sampling of multitype continuous-time Bienaym\'e-Galton-Watson trees'] Let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be two probability measures on a $\sigma$-algebra $\F$ and $\G\subseteq \F$ is also a $\sigma$-algebra with Radon-Nikodym derivatives
\[
\left.\frac{{\rm d}\mu}{{\rm d}\nu}\right|_{\F}=:Y\qquad \mbox{ and }\qquad \left.\frac{{\rm d}\mu}{{\rm d}\nu}\right|_{\G}=:Z.
\]
Then for any non-negative random variable $X$, $\F$-measurable, we have
\[
Z\mu[X |\, \G]=\nu[XY|\, \G]\qquad \nu-a.s.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 2 of arXiv:2605.11264

body:
[Theorem thm:berry-esseen-transfer of arXiv:2507.12502, 'Quantitative Edge Eigenvector Universality for Random Regular Graphs: Berry-Esseen Bounds '] For any deterministic unit vector $\mathbf{q} \perp \mathbf{e}$:
\[
\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} \left|\mathbb{P}\left(X_2^{(\mathbf{q})}(t_*) \leq x\right) - \Phi(x)\right| \leq C_{\text{GOE}}N^{-1/2} + CN^{-1/3+2\varepsilon}
\]
where the first term comes from the GOE approximation and the second from the cumulant comparison.
title: Berry-Esseen Transfer to Time $t_*$

[Prop 9 of arXiv:2609.03653, 'The derived set of multiple star polylogarithms'] All limits below are locally uniform on $\mathcal{D}$.

$(i)$
\[
\lim_{r\rightarrow+\infty}H_{\{1\}^{r}}(z)=\frac1{1-z}.
\]

$(ii)$ For a finite nonempty index $(k_1,\ldots,k_s)$,
\[
\lim_{r\rightarrow+\infty}
H_{k_1,\ldots,k_{s-1},k_s+1,\{1\}^{r}}(z)
=H_{k_1,\ldots,k_s}(z).
\]

$(iii)$ For a finite nonempty index ${\bf k}$,
\[
\lim_{q\rightarrow+\infty}H_{{\bf k},q}(z)=H_{\bf k}(z).
\]

body:
[Proposition 10 of arXiv:2604.07207, 'Mixing times of step-reinforced random walks'] Let $S$ be as in Proposition \ref{consSRRWRRT} and assume that $G$ is finite.   For $n\geq 1$, one has 
    $$
\|\PP(S_{n} = \cdot \mid \F_n, (g_j)_{j \in [n]\backslash \mathscr{I}_n}) -  U\|_{\mathrm{TV}} = \| \delta_{e_G}\prod_{k=1}^nP_k-U\prod_{k=1}^nP_k  \|_{\mathrm{TV}}, 
    $$
    where $\delta_{e_G}$ and $U$ are viewed as row vectors. In particular, 
   $$
\|\PP(S_{n}=\cdot)- U\|_{\mathrm{TV}} \leq \EE \| \delta_{e_G}\prod_{k=1}^nP_k-U\prod_{k=1}^nP_k  \|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
   $$
title: Proposition 10 of arXiv:2604.07207

[Lemma lem:hetero_vk_self_normalized of arXiv:2609.00193, 'Provably Efficient Federated Reinforcement Learning with Linear Function Approximation and'] Fix $\bar p\in(0,1)$ and set $\lambda=1$. Suppose the optimistic estimates are formed with bonus parameter
\[
\beta
=
c_\beta^\prime Hd\sqrt{\log\Bigl(1+\frac{dMHT}{\bar p}\Bigr)}
+2H\xi\sqrt{dMT},
\]
where $c_\beta^\prime > 0$ is a sufficiently large positive constant.
Then there exists an absolute constant $C>0$ such that, if we define an event $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{het}}$ as, simultaneously for all steps $h\in[H]$ and rounds $k\in[K]$,
\begin{align*}
    \Biggl\|
\sum_{m=1}^M\sum_{t=1}^{\tau_k-1}
\phi(x_h^{m,t},a_h^{m,t})
&\Bigl[
V_{h+1}^{k}(x_{h+1}^{m,t})-
\mathbb P_{m,h}V_{h+1}^{k}(x_h^{m,t},a_h^{m,t})
\Bigr]
\Biggr\|_{(\Lambda_h^k)^{-1}}
\\
&\quad \le CHd\sqrt{\log\Bigl(1+\frac{(c_\beta^\prime+1)dMHT}{\bar p}\Bigr)}.
\end{align*}
 Then $\mathbb P(\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{het}})\geq 1-\bar p$.

[Prop of arXiv:2411.09988, 'A Study in Markov Chains, Loop-Erased Random Walk and Loop Soups'] Suppose $X_j,j = 0, 1,\ldots$, is an irreducible Markov chain on $\overline{A} = A \cup \partial A$ where $A = \{x_1, ..., x_n\}$ is finite and $\partial A \neq \emptyset$. Let $P_A = [p(x, y)]_{x,y \in A}$ denote the transition matrix restricted to $A$ and $G_A = (I - P_A)^{-1}$ the Green's function. Suppose $V = \{x_1, ..., x_k\}$. We will consider the Markov chain that corresponds to the original chain “viewed only when visiting points in $V$”. The transition matrix $\tilde{P}  = [\tilde{p}(x, y)]_{x,y \in V}$ is given by
    \[\tilde{p} = \sum_{\omega: x \rightarrow y}p(\omega),\]
    where the sum is over all paths $\omega = [\omega_0,...,\omega_r]$ with $r \geq 1$; $\omega_0 = x,\omega_r =y$; and $\omega_1,...,\omega_{r-1} \in A\backslash V$. Then\\
    (1)the Green's function $\tilde{G}_V := (I-\tilde{P})^{-1}$ is the same as $G_A$ restricted to rows and columns indexed by vertices in $V$ and\\
    (2)\[F_V(A) = \det \tilde{G}_V.\]

[Defn 14 ({{\bf Sub/Super-harmonicity}}) of arXiv:2506.17979, '\large\bf A remark on subharmonicity for symmetric Dirichlet forms'] {\rm Let $D$ be an open set in $E$. We say that a nearly Borel
$\overline{\R}$-valued function $u$ defined on $E$ is
\emph{subharmonic {\rm(}resp.~superharmonic{\rm)} in $D$} if 
for any open subset $U$ of $D$ with $U\Subset D$, $t\mapsto u(X_{t\wedge\tau_U})$ is a uniformly integrable right continuous $\mathbb{P}_x$-submartingale (resp.~$\mathbb{P}_x$-supermartingale) for q.e.~$x\in E$. A nearly Borel $\overline{\R}$-valued function $u$ on $E$ is said to be
\emph{harmonic in $D$} if $u$ is  both superharmonic and subharmonic in $D$.
If $t\mapsto u(X_{t\wedge\tau_U})$ is a uniformly integrable right
continuous $\mathbb{P}_x$-submartingale for all $x\in E$, $u$ is called \emph{subharmonic in $D$ without exceptional set}. 
The \emph{subharmonicity/harmonicity in $D$ without exceptional set} is
analogously defined.
}
title: {{\bf Sub/Super-harmonicity}}

[Definition def:j-jammed of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a positive integer~$j$. Fix a send sequence~$\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$, a non-negative integer~$\tau$, and a $\lambda\in (0,1)$. 
Fix a $j$-tuple $\overline{a} \in (\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0})^j$.
A \emph{$j$-jammed} process~$Y$ with send sequence~$\overline{p}$, start time~$\tau$, birth rate~$\lambda$, 
and initial population size tuple~$\overline{a}$   
is a generalised backoff process~$Y$ with

Fix a sufficiently small $\lambda \in (0,1/3)$.
Let $j$ be a sufficiently large integer. Fix an integer $\tau \ge 0$ and a tuple $\overline{a} \in (\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0})^j$.
Let $E^+$ be a constant-escape process on $[j]$ with send sequence~$\overline{p}$, start time $\tau$, end-of-step arrival rate $\nu_j^\mathrm{hi}$, and $\overline{\mathrm{arr}}_{[j]}^{E^+}(\tau) = \overline{a}$. 
Fix real numbers~$d$ and~$\theta$

Fix $t$ in the range $\tau + j^{17} \leq t \leq \tau + (4/\lambda)^{2j}$. Then,  with probability at least $1-\exp(-(\log j)^2)$, $\mathcal{N}_S^{E^+}(t+1) \le \lambda |S|/160$.

body:
[Lem 38 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] There exists a constant $C_8=C_8(\alpha,\iota)$ such that the following holds with probability at least $1-e^{-cN}$ over $\dot{\bg}_+, \hat{\bg}_+$, where $c$ is an absolute constant. 
    For any $\|\by\|^2=N$, the function
    \[
        \btheta_+ \mapsto
        \frac{2(\hbg_+,\btheta_+)}{M}
        + \frac{2\|\btheta_+\|(\dbg_+,\by)}{M\sqrt{N}}
        - \frac{((\hbD_+)^{-1} \btheta_+, \btheta_+)}{M}
    \]
    attains its supremum over $\R^{B_+}$ at some $\btheta_+$ satisfying
    $\|\btheta_+\| \le C_8N^{1/2}$.
    (We take the assertion to be vacuously true if $B_+ = \emptyset$.)

\begin{proof}
    Since the function tends to $-\infty$ as $\|\btheta_+\| \to +\infty$, the supremum is attained at a local maximizer $\btheta_+$.
    The function is differentiable everywhere except possibly at $\btheta_+=\bzero$, so the only possible local maximizer are $\btheta_+=\bzero$ and stationary points $\btheta_+$. 
    The stationarity condition gives
    \[
      \btheta_+
     =\hbD_+\bigg(   \hbg_+
        + \frac{(\dbg_+,\by) \btheta_+}{N^{1/2} \|\btheta_+\|}
        \bigg) \,.
    \]
With probability $1-e^{-cN}$, we have $\|\hbg_+\| \le 2 M^{1/2}$, $\|\dbg_+\| \le 2 N^{1/2}$, and consequently $|(\dbg_+,\by)| \le 2N$. Since the operator norm of $\hbD_+$ is at most $\hv_1$, it follows that any stationary point $\btheta_+$ must satisfy
    \[
        \|\btheta_+\|
        \le\hv_1 \bigg(
            \|\hbg_+\|
            + \bigg|
            \frac{(\dbg_+,\by) }{N^{1/2} }
            \bigg|
        \bigg)
        \le
        2\hv_1\Big( M^{1/2} + N^{1/2}
         \Big)
        \stackrel{\eqref{e:reduced-normalization}}{\le}
        \frac{4(\alpha^{1/2}+1)}{\iota} N^{1/2}\,.
    \]
This proves the claim.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 38 of arXiv:2608.29416

[Theorem thm:intro-one of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Let $\mathbf a_*\in D$ be a strict local minimum point of $H$.  Fix
$\kappa,M,R>0$.  For each $\varepsilon>0$, let
$\mathbf a_\varepsilon\in D$ and let
$\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\in L^\infty(D)$ be nonnegative and satisfy
\begin{equation}
  \int_D\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\,\mathrm d\mathbf x=\kappa,
  \qquad
  \|\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\|_\infty\leq M\varepsilon^{-2},
  \qquad
  \operatorname{supp}\omega_{\varepsilon,0}
  \subset B_{R\varepsilon}(\mathbf a_\varepsilon).
\end{equation}
Suppose that
\begin{equation*}
  \mathbf a_\varepsilon\longrightarrow\mathbf a_*,
  \qquad
  \mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,0})\longrightarrow0
  \qquad\text{as }\varepsilon\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation*}
Let $\omega_{\varepsilon,t}$, $t\in\mathbb R$, denote the corresponding
Yudovich solution of (equation eq:euler-intro of the paper).
Then, as $\varepsilon\to0$,
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})\longrightarrow0,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\ \sup_{\mathbf b\in
  \mathsf C(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})}
  |\mathbf b-\mathbf a_*|\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop 26 of arXiv:2606.11271, '\LARGE The $K$-th nearest neighbor random walk on a Poisson point process gets trapped'] Let $(Y^L_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be the Markov chain on $\{0,1,\ldots,3L\}$ with $Y^L_0=0$ and transition probabilities:
\[
\P(Y^L_{n+1}=j \mid Y^L_n=i) = \begin{cases} 
(1-p)\mathbf{1}_{j=1}+p\mathbf{1}_{j=2} & \text{if } i=0 \\
(1-p)\mathbf{1}_{j=i+1}+p\mathbf{1}_{j=i-1} & \text{if } i\equiv 0 \pmod 3 \text{ and } 0<i<3L \\
(1-p)\mathbf{1}_{j=i-1}+p\mathbf{1}_{j=i+1}  & \text{if } i\not\equiv 0 \pmod 3 \text{ and } 0<i<3L \\
(1-p)\mathbf{1}_{j=3L-1}+p\mathbf{1}_{j=3L-2}  & \text{if } i=3L.
\end{cases}
\]
If $\mu = \mu_0$, then on the event $\cH_L$, the walk $(X_n)_{n\ge 0}$ has the law of $(x_{Y^L_n})_{n\ge 0}$.

[Corollary cor:saturation of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] Let $L \supseteq \textbf{FIK}$ and let $(\Gamma, \Delta)$ be a maximal $L$-consistent theory.
  \begin{itemize}
    \item If $L \vdash \varphi$, then $\varphi \in \Gamma$.
    \item If $\varphi \in \Gamma$ and $\varphi \to \psi \in \Gamma$, then $\psi \in \Gamma$.
    \item $\bot \notin \Gamma$.
    \item $\varphi \land \psi \in \Gamma$ iff $(\varphi \in \Gamma \mathrel{\text{\&}} \psi \in \Gamma)$.
    \item $\varphi \lor \psi \in \Gamma$ iff $(\varphi \in \Gamma \mathrel{\text{or}} \psi \in \Gamma)$.
  \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Defn $\sharp$ and $\flat$ modifications of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a cooriented $C^0$-foliation on the $2$-torus $\mathbb{T}^2$, and $p \in \mathbb{T}^2$. We choose a smooth closed arc $c$ transverse to $\mathcal{G}$ and containing $p$ in its interior. After some arbitrarily small $C^0$ isotopy, we may assume that $\mathcal{G}$ is smooth in a neighborhood of $c$, and we choose coordinates $N(c) \cong (-\varepsilon, \varepsilon)_x \times (-2,2)_y$ near $c$, in which $c$ is identified with $\{0\} \times [-1,1]$, $p=(0,0)$, and $\mathcal{G}$ is tangent to $\partial_x$. 

    Let $h : [-1,1] \rightarrow [-1,1]$ be a smooth diffeomorphism satisfying 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $h \geq \mathrm{id}$ (resp.~$h \leq \mathrm{id}$),
        \item $h = \mathrm{id}$ near $\partial [-1,1]$,
        \item $h > \mathrm{id}$ (resp.~$h < \mathrm{id}$) on $[-1/2, 1/2]$.
    \end{itemize}

    We modify $\mathcal{G}$ in $(-\varepsilon/2, \varepsilon/2) \times (-2,2) \subset N(c)$ so that the parallel transport along the leaves of $\mathcal{G}$ from left to right is $h$, and moreover the new $C^0$-foliation $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}$ is everywhere either tangent or positively (resp.~negatively) transverse to $\partial_x$ in $N(c)$. Choosing $h$ sufficiently $C^0$-close to $\mathrm{id}$, we can further arrange that $T\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}$ is $C^0$-close to $T\mathcal{G}$. 
    
    We call the resulting $C^0$-foliation a $\sharp$ (resp.~$\flat$) modification of $\mathcal{G}$ near the point $p$. This modification can be made arbitrarily $C^0$-small and close to $p$.
title: $\sharp$ and $\flat$ modifications

[Proposition 16 of arXiv:2606.07839, 'Bounds on Spectral Gaps for Non-Reversible Markov Chains with Applications to Temporal Dif'] Say that all eigenvalues of $F$ have magnitude less and $1$ and  the pair $(F,G)$ is controllable. Let $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n$ denote the eigenvalues of $F$ (which may not be distinct). The following statements hold:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item  If $\gamma \in\spec(P)\setminus\{0,1\}$ then $\gamma = \prod_{j=1}^k\lambda_{i_j}$ for some sequence of numbers $i_j\in \{1,\ldots,n\}$.

[Theorem thm:wobbling of arXiv:2607.04620, 'The Exact Ville Identity\\ \large From the Absorbing Case to the General Law\\ with an App'] Let $\{M_n,\mathcal{F}_n\}$ be a mean-zero martingale and fix a level $r\ge0$. Let $T_r$ be the first $n\ge1$ with $M_n>r$, and $\infty$ if no such $n$ exists. Suppose
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item (sufficient wobbling)
\[
  \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\limsup_{k\to\infty}
  \mathbb{P}\left(\sup_{n\ge k}|M_n-M_k|>\varepsilon\right)=1,
\]
\item (bounded expected overshoot) there is $B<\infty$ with $\mathbb{E}[M_n\mid T_r=n]\le r+B$ a.s. for every $n\ge1$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathbb{P}(T_r<\infty)=1$ and $\mathbb{E}[M_{T_r}]\le r+B$; moreover $\limsup_{n\to\infty}M_n=+\infty$ almost surely. Condition (i) ensures the martingale wobbles arbitrarily far out; condition (ii) bounds the overshoot of $M_{T_r}$ beyond $r$. Dropping either condition can make $\mathbb{P}(T_r=\infty)>0$, as the counterexamples of [klass2026beyond] demonstrate. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Wobbling and bounded overshoot force crossing \cite{klass2026beyond}

[Theorem Thm:BesovLog of arXiv:2412.03366, 'Regularity of Weighted Tensorized Fractional Brownian Fields and associated function space'] Let $s, \beta \in \mathbb{R}$ and $0 < p,q\leq \infty$ and $p'$ the conjugate exponent of $p$. We have the following embeddings
\begin{itemize}
\item if $q<+\infty$
\begin{equation}
\widetilde{B}^s_{p,q,\vert \log \vert^{\beta - r_1/q}}(\mathbb{R}^2) \hookrightarrow B^s_{p,q,\vert \log \vert^{\beta}}(\mathbb{R}^2) \hookrightarrow \widetilde{B}^s_{p,q,\vert \log \vert^{\beta +r_2/q}}(\mathbb{R}^2)
\end{equation}
where $$r_1 = \begin{cases}q(\frac{1}{p}-1)+ \max(q-1,0) & \text{ if } p \le 1 \\ 
\max( \frac{q}{\min(p,p')}-1,0) & \text{ if }p>1 \end{cases}$$
and
$$
r_2 = \begin{cases}1  & \text{ if } p < 1 \\ 
\max(1- \frac{q}{\max(p,p')}-1,0) & \text{ if }p\ge 1 .\end{cases}$$

\item if $q=+\infty$
\begin{equation}
\widetilde{B}^s_{p,\infty,\vert \log \vert^{\beta - \max(1/p-1,0) -1}}(\mathbb{R}^2) \hookrightarrow B^s_{p,\infty,\vert \log \vert^{\beta}}(\mathbb{R}^2) \hookrightarrow \widetilde{B}^s_{p,\infty,\vert \log \vert^{\beta }}(\mathbb{R}^2)
\end{equation}

\item if $q=2$, the Sobolev spaces $H^{s}_{2,\vert \log \vert^{\beta}}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ coincide with the classical Besov spaces $B^{s}_{2,2,\vert \log \vert^{\beta}}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ and with the hyperbolic Besov spaces $\widetilde{B}^{s}_{2,2,\vert \log \vert^{\beta}}(\mathbb{R}^2) $.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem Thm:BesovLog of arXiv:2412.03366

Method: Explicit stationary law of the leftmost Hammersley drift-jump particles structural calculation Result: The established rank representation can be expanded into a convergent combinatorial density series. Let B=(1=b1<...<bk) be the limiting first-row labels of the insertion tableau, and let q_B be its probability. The first b=bk labels form a uniform permutation, so q_B=(1/b!)*sum over partitions lambda of b with first row length k of f^lambda times the number of standard tableaux of shape lambda with first row B. Independent unit-rate Poisson spacings then give density exp(-xk)*sum_B q_B*product_(i=2..k)[(x_i-x_(i-1))^(b_i-b_(i-1)-1)/(b_i-b_(i-1)-1)!]. Check: Restriction of an insertion tableau to labels at most b is the tableau of the corresponding restricted subword. The last specified first-row entry b pins the first k labels, irrespective of later larger labels. Conditional on B, the Poisson arrival times have independent gamma increments, so every term is a normalized conditional density and nonnegative summation is valid. For k1 this gives Exp(1); known Poissonized LIS formulas give P(X2>x)=exp(-x)*I0(2sqrt(x)) and E X2=e. Obstruction: This repackages a known representation into explicit but rapidly growing finite-tableau coefficients and an infinite sum. It does not establish a new tractable closed joint law or its novelty, and should not be promoted as a full solution to the source request.
