[Definition Pathwise solution of arXiv:2604.07497, 'The Three-Dimensional Stochastic EMHD System: Local Well-Posedness and Maximal Pathwise So'] Given ${\mathcal F}_0$-measurable initial data $B_0 \in L^2(\Omega;H^s)$, we say that: \\
\begin{enumerate}
\item A pair $\left(B, \eta \right)$ is a local pathwise solution to the system (equation eq:EMHD_Ito of the paper) if $\eta$ is a strictly positive ${\mathbb F}$-stopping time and $B(\cdot \wedge \eta)$ is a progressively measurable stochastic process such that, ${\mathbb P}$-almost surely,
\[
B(\cdot \wedge \eta) \in L^2(\Omega; C([0,\infty); H^s) \cap L^2([0,\infty);H^{s+\frac{\alpha}{2}})).
\]
Additionally, for every $t \geq 0$, the following identity holds:
\begin{align*}
&\left < B(t\wedge \eta),\phi \right > + \int_0^{t\wedge \eta} \left < \nabla \times \bigl( (\nabla \times B ) \times B \bigr) + \varLambda^\alpha B, \phi \right > ds \\
=\ &\left < B(0),\phi \right > + {\frac{1}{2}} \sum_{k=1}^\infty \int_0^{t\wedge \eta} \Ltwoinner{{\mathcal T}^2_k \widetilde{B},\phi} ds + \sum_{k=1}^\infty \int_0^{t\wedge \eta}  \Ltwoinner{{\mathcal T}_k \widetilde{B}, \phi} d\widetilde{W}^k_s ,
\end{align*}
for all $\phi \in H$.\\
\item A triplet $(B,(\eta_k)_{k \geq 1},\xi)$ is a maximal pathwise solution if for each pair $(B,\eta_k)$ it holds that: \\
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $(B,\eta_k)$ is a local pathwise solution. \\
\item $\eta_k$
 is an increasing sequence of stopping times such that $\lim_{k \to \infty} \eta_k = \xi$. \\
\item $\sup_{t \in [0,\eta_k]} \VertB(t)\Vert_{H^s({\mathbb T}^3)} \geq k $ on the set $\{\xi < \infty \}$.
 \end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
title: Pathwise solution

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2609.01920, 'Isospectral and not strongly isospectral spherical space forms with non-cyclic fundamental'] Let $\Gamma=\Gamma_2(m,4,m-1)$, for some prime integer $m\geq13$, and set $p=\frac{m-5}{2}$. 
Let $T=\{\alpha,\beta\}$ and
$T'=\{\alpha',\beta'\}$ be two-element subsets of $U_m:= \{1,2,\ldots,\frac{m-1}{2}\}$ satisfying 
$2\alpha\not\equiv\pm\beta\pmod m$, 
$\alpha\not\equiv\pm2\beta\pmod m$,
$2\alpha'\not\equiv\pm\beta'\pmod m$, and
$\alpha'\not\equiv\pm2\beta'\pmod m$. 
Write 
\begin{align}
U_m\smallsetminus T &=\{k_1,\dots,k_p\},&
U_m\smallsetminus T' &=\{k_1',\dots,k_p'\},
\end{align}
and set $\rho=\rho_{k_1}\oplus \dots\oplus \rho_{k_p}$ and $\rho'=\rho_{k_1'}\oplus \dots\oplus \rho_{k_p'}$.

The spherical space forms $S^{2m-11}/\rho(\Gamma)$ and $S^{2m-11}/\rho'(\Gamma)$ are isospectral. 
Moreover, they are not strongly isospectral (and consequently non-isometric) if the lens spaces $L_\rho$ and $L_{\rho'}$ (see (equation eq:lens-space-m of the paper)) are not isometric.
title: Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2609.01920

[Lemma chaining-edge-sets of arXiv:2412.08400, '\vspace{-1.0cm} Characterization of Exponential Families of \\ Lumpable Stochastic Matrice'] Let $\mathcal{E}, \mathcal{E}' \in \mathcal{Y}^2$ be such that $\mathcal{E} \subset \mathcal{E}'$, and $\mathcal{W}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{E})$ and $\mathcal{W}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{E}')$ are non-vacuous families of lumpable stochastic matrices. Then,
 there exists $L \in \mathbb{N}$ and a finite sequence of edge sets $\mathcal{E}_0, \mathcal{E}_1, \dots, \mathcal{E}_L \subset \mathcal{Y}^2$, such that
 \begin{enumerate}
     \item[(i)\xspace] $\mathcal{E}_0 = \mathcal{E}$, $\mathcal{E}_L = \mathcal{E}'$.
     \item[(ii)\xspace] The sequence $\{\mathcal{E}_\ell \}_{\ell = 0, \dots, L }$ is strictly monotone increasing, that is, for any $\ell \in \left\{ 0, \dots, L - 1 \right\}$, $\mathcal{E}_\ell \subsetneq \mathcal{E}_{\ell+1}$.
     \item[(iii)\xspace] The sequence $\{\mathcal{E}_\ell \}_{\ell = 0, \dots, L }$ is consecutive, in the sense where for any $\ell \in \left\{ 0, \dots, L -1 \right\}$, it holds that for any $\mathcal{E}'' \subset \mathcal{Y}^2$ such that $\mathcal{E}_\ell \subset \mathcal{E}'' \subset \mathcal{E}_{\ell+1}$ either $\mathcal{E}'' = \mathcal{E}_\ell, \mathcal{E}'' = \mathcal{E}_{\ell+1}$ or $\mathcal{W}_{\kappa}(\mathcal{Y} ,\mathcal{E}'') = \emptyset$.
     \item[(iv)\xspace] For any $\ell \in \left\{ 0, \dots, L \right\}$, $\mathcal{W}_\kappa(\mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{E}_\ell)$ is non-vacuous.
     \item[(v)\xspace] For any $\ell \in \left\{ 0, 1\dots, L - 1 \right\}$, $\mathcal{E}_\ell$ and $\mathcal{E}_{\ell+1}$ only differ either on an edge-link or a block-link:
     \begin{description}
         \item[Edge-link:] We say that $(y_\star, y_\star') \in \mathcal{E}_{\ell+1}$ is an edge-link between $\mathcal{E}_{\ell}$ and $\mathcal{E}_{\ell+1}$ whenever             $$\kappa_2(\mathcal{E}_{\ell+1}) = \kappa_2(\mathcal{E}_{\ell}), \text{ and } \mathcal{E}_{\ell+1} \setminus \mathcal{E}_{\ell} = \left\{ (y_\star, y_\star') \right\}.$$
 \item[Block-link:] We say that $(x_\star, x'_\star) \in \kappa_2(\mathcal{E}_{\ell+1})$ is a block-link between $\mathcal{E}_\ell$ and $\mathcal{E}_{\ell+1}$ whenever
 $$\kappa_2(\mathcal{E}_{\ell+1}) \neq \kappa_2(\mathcal{E}_{\ell}), \mathcal{E}_{\ell+1} \setminus \mathcal{E}_{\ell} \subset \mathcal{S}_{x_\star} \times \mathcal{S}_{x_\star'} \text{, and } (x_\star, x'_\star) \text{ is non-merging}.$$
     \end{description}
 \end{enumerate}
title: Chaining

body: In mathematics, the ideal class group of an algebraic number field is the quotient group where is the group of fractional ideals of the ring of integers of , and is its subgroup of principal ideals. The class group is a measure of the extent to which unique factorization fails in the ring of integers of . The order of the group, which is finite, is called the class number of .

Let X be a topological space (no separation or countability axiom is needed) and let (f_i), i in I, be a nonempty family of functions f_i : X -> [-infinity, +infinity], each upper semicontinuous; in particular each f_i may be continuous. The index set I is arbitrary: finite, countable, or uncountable. Put f(x) = inf over i in I of f_i(x). Then f is upper semicontinuous: the set {x : f(x) < c} is open for every real c, equivalently limsup_{y -> x} f(y) <= f(x) at every point x. The standard consequence: an upper semicontinuous function on a nonempty compact space attains its supremum, so a variational problem whose objective is an infimum of continuous quantities always has a maximiser. WHERE IT FAILS: (i) the direction is not symmetric. A SUPREMUM of continuous functions is lower semicontinuous, not upper: on R, sup over n >= 1 of min(1, n|x|) is the indicator of {x nonzero}, which is lower but not upper semicontinuous at 0. Quoting this result for a supremum is the common misuse. (ii) The infimum of an INFINITE family of continuous functions is in general not continuous: on [0,1], inf over n of x^n equals 0 for x < 1 and 1 at x = 1. Only finite infima of continuous functions are continuous, so upper semicontinuity is the most one can claim. (iii) Upper semicontinuity of each member is exactly what is used; an infimum of merely lower semicontinuous functions has no semicontinuity property at all. (iv) The pointwise version localises: if each f_i is merely continuous AT a point x, the same proof gives limsup_{y -> x} f(y) <= f(x), i.e. upper semicontinuity at that one point, which is the form most often needed in practice.
X is a topological space; no metrisability, compactness or separation axiom is required
each f_i is upper semicontinuous as a map into the extended reals (continuity is the special case used most often)
the family is nonempty; the index set may be uncountable
the infimum is taken pointwise, and values -infinity and +infinity are allowed

[Definition 3 of arXiv:2606.06193, 'Peng's Maximum Principle for McKean-Vlasov Stochastic Differential Equations with Common N'] For $\varphi:\R^d\times\cP_2(\R^d)\to \R^m $ we say $\varphi\in C_b^{2,1}(\R^d\times\cP_2(\R^d),\R^m)$ if
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item $\varphi(\cdot ,\mu)\in C^2_b(\R^d,\R^m)$ for all $\mu\in\cP_2(\R^d)$,
        \item $\varphi(x,\cdot)\in C^{2,1}_b(\cP_2(\R^d),\R^m)$ and $\partial_x\varphi(x,\cdot)\in C^{1,1}_b(\cP_2(\R^d),\R^{m\times d})$ for all $x\in\R^d$,
        \item $\partial_\mu\varphi(\cdot ,\mu)(\cdot)\in C^1_b(\R^d\times \R^d,\R^{m\times d})$ for all $\mu\in\cP_2(\R^d)$ and
        \item $\varphi$ and all first and second-order derivatives of $\varphi$ are bounded and Lipschitz continuous in all variables.
    \end{enumerate}
title: Definition 3 of arXiv:2606.06193

body: [Lemma 54 of arXiv:2608.26084, 'Localic Esakia Duality\\via Conic Frames'] In a category with finite limits, let~$q=(s,t)\colon Q\rightarrowtail Z\times Y$ be a regular monomorphism, and~$f\colon X\to Z$ any morphism. If~$P:=X\times_Z Q$ is the pullback of~$s$ and~$f$ with projections~$\pi_X,\pi_Q$, then~$j:=(\pi_X,t\circ\pi_Q)$ is a regular monomorphism.

Let X = (X_1, ..., X_n) have independent coordinates with finite ranges, f a real function of X, and f = sum over S of f_S its Hoeffding (ANOVA) decomposition over subsets S of {1, ..., n}: f_S depends only on X_S, f_empty = E f, and E[f_S | X_T] = 0 unless S is inside T. Put w_S = E[f_S^2] and W_k = sum over |S| = k of w_S, the variance at interaction order k. For 0 <= t <= n let A_t f be the average over t-element sets T of E[f | X_T], and for 0 <= k <= n put P_k = binom(n, k) sum_{t=0}^k (-1)^(k - t) binom(k, t) A_t. Then P_k f = sum over |S| = k of f_S: P_k is the orthogonal projector onto the order-k part, so P_j P_k = 0 for j != k, P_k^2 = P_k, sum_k P_k = I and ||P_k f||_2^2 = W_k. If K_r f(x) is the average over |A| = r of E[f(X^(A)) | X = x], with X^(A) redrawing X_A independently, then K_r = A_{n - r}, so the same alternating combination of the K_{n - t} recovers each order.

body: In algebraic geometry, a projective variety is an algebraic variety that is a closed subvariety of a projective space. That is, it is the zero-locus in $\mathbb {P} ^{n}$ of some finite family of homogeneous polynomials that generate a prime ideal, the defining ideal of the variety.

[Theorem 6 (Estimate of Extinction Time) of arXiv:2608.04716, 'Extinction Time Estimate for Subcritical (Binary) Homogeneous Crump-Mode-Jagers Processes'] Consider a birth death process with non-lattice lifetime random variable $\tau $.  Assume that $\lambda \E[\tau ]<1$ (subcritical case) and \linebreak $\lambda\E[\tau e^{-\alpha  \tau }]\neq 1$. 
Assume Malthusian parameter $\alpha<0$ exists.  We consider a sequence of initial configurations  indexed by $k\in \N$. For each configuration $k$, the initial population is given by a  non-negative, random integer-valued measure $Z_k$ on $\R_+$, where $Z_k(r)$ represents the number of individuals with age in the interval $[0,r]$ at time zero.   
Assume that the total number of individuals at time zero, $M_k:=Z_k(\infty)$, tends to infinity almost surely as $k\to \infty$. Furthermore, assume that
\begin{equation}
U:=\sup_{x\geq 0}\E[e^{-\alpha(\tau -x)}\mid \tau >x]<\infty
\end{equation}
and 
 the functions  $Z_k/M_k$ converge almost surely in  total variation distance  to  a non-decreasing random distribution  function  $B$, i.e. 
\[\lVert Z_k/M_k-B\rVert_{TV}:=\int_0^\infty \lvert  \d Z_k(  x)/M_k - \d B( x) \rvert \]
converges to zero almost surely  as $k\to \infty$.
Let
\[D:=\frac{1-\lambda \E[\tau]}{\lambda\E[\tau e^{-\alpha  \tau }]-1}\cdot\int_0^\infty\E\left[e^{-\alpha  (\tau -x)}-1\mid \tau >x\right] \d B(x)<\infty.\]
Let $T_k$ be the extinction time for configuration $k$. Then, as $k\to \infty$, the random variables $$-\alpha  T_k-\log( M_k)-\log(D)$$ converges in distribution to a Gumbel random variable $Z$ with distribution function $\P(Z\leq r)=e^{-e^{-r}}$. In other words, 
\[\lim_{k\to \infty}\P(-\alpha  T_k-\log( M_k)-\log(D)\leq r)=e^{-e^{-r}}.\]

[Lemma lemma-neck-refined of arXiv:2609.00108, 'The double sphere solution in the liquid drop model'] Let $\mathcal T_C$ be the inverse from
		Lemma~(lemma-linear-neck of the paper).
		
		\smallskip
		
		\noindent
		{\rm (i)}
		Set
		\[
		\zeta_\varepsilon
		=
		\mathcal T_C[1].
		\]
		Then
		$$
		\|\zeta_\varepsilon\|_*
		\le
		C,
		$$
		and for
		\(
		2<r<\varepsilon^{-1+b}
		\)
		one has
		\begin{equation}
			|\zeta_\varepsilon(r)|
			\le
			Cr^2,
			\qquad
			|\zeta_\varepsilon'(r)|
			\le
			Cr,
			\qquad
			|\zeta_\varepsilon''(r)|
			\le

		\end{equation}
		Consequently, for every constant $\gamma\in\mathbb R$,
		\begin{equation}

				|\mathcal T_C[\gamma](r)|
				&\le
				C|\gamma|r^2,
				\quad
				|(\mathcal T_C[\gamma])'(r)|
				\le
				C|\gamma|r,
				\quad
				|(\mathcal T_C[\gamma])''(r)|
				\le
				C|\gamma|.
			\end{aligned}
		\end{equation}
		
		\smallskip
		
		\noindent
		{\rm (ii)}
		Assume
		\(
		g_0\in L^\infty(1,\varepsilon^{-1+b})
		\)
		and $\operatorname{supp}g_0
		\subset
		(1,L_\varepsilon).$
		If
		\(
		u_0=\mathcal T_C[g_0],
		\)
		then
		$$
		\|u_0\|_*
		\le
		C\|g_0\|_\infty,
		$$
		and for
		\[
		2L_\varepsilon<r<\varepsilon^{-1+b}
		\]
		we have
		\begin{equation}
			\begin{aligned}
				|u_0(r)|
				&\le
				C L_\varepsilon^2\|g_0\|_\infty
				\left(
				1+\log\frac r{L_\varepsilon}
				\right),
				\quad
				|u_0'(r)|
				\le
				C L_\varepsilon^2\|g_0\|_\infty\frac1r,
				\\
				|u_0''(r)|
				&\le
				C L_\varepsilon^2\|g_0\|_\infty\frac1{r^2}.
			\end{aligned}
		\end{equation}
		In particular, if
		\begin{equation}
			\|g_0\|_\infty
			\le
			C\varepsilon^{3/2},
		\end{equation}
		then for
		\(
		2L_\varepsilon<r<\varepsilon^{-1+b}
		\)
		\begin{equation}
			\begin{aligned}
				|u_0(r)|
				&\le
				C_\delta
				\left(
				1+
				\left|
				\log(\varepsilon^{3/4}r)
				\right|
				\right),
				\quad
				|u_0'(r)|
				\le
				\frac{C_\delta}{r},
				\quad
				|u_0''(r)|
				\le
				\frac{C_\delta}{r^2}.
			\end{aligned}
		\end{equation}

Own-work draft; STATUS: sketch. Independent review and novelty assessment pending. Let 0<e<1/4, x_(s,t)=(1,e s,e^2 t)/sqrt(1+e^2+e^4), s,t in {-1,1}. Test input is uniform on these four points and the training design contains each point exactly once. The single-index teacher is LINEAR: g(x_(s,t))=(s+t)/4. Each label has independent noise uniformly plus or minus 1/2. Train f_m(x)=m^(-1/2) sum_j a_j ReLU(w_j^T x) by simultaneous full-batch GD with step 1/2 on squared residual norm divided by 8; w_j(0) are iid N(0,I_3) and a_j(0)=0. Both layers are updated with ReLU derivative 1_{z>0}. Q_(m,e)(k) is clean test MSE AVERAGED OVER ALL SIXTEEN TRAINING-NOISE VECTORS, conditional on hidden initialization. For each sufficiently small fixed e, as m tends to infinity, the probability over hidden initialization of four ordered integers k0<k1<k2<k3 with Q(k0)>Q(k1)<Q(k2)>Q(k3) tends to one. A self-contained draft gives explicit witness times, a finite-horizon nonlinear GD error recurrence, and central peak time asymptotic 8 e^(-2) log(1/e), taking width to infinity before e tends to zero. This does not assert exactly two extrema, generic iid sampling, a nonlinear teacher, random nonzero readout, high probability over label noise, macroscopic feature learning, practical width, or completion of Target 1. All qualifications and analytic derivations are in the linked proof draft.

[Lemma 11 (Gauss--Laguerre quadrature) of arXiv:2608.29143, 'Least Variability in a Polynomial-Square Class\\ of Rational Kernels'] For each $n\geq1$, there are positive weights
$w_{1,n},\ldots,w_{n,n}$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \int_0^\infty p(t)\e^{-t}\dd t
 =
 \sum_{r=1}^n w_{r,n}p(x_{r,n})
\end{equation}
for every $p \in \Pcal_{2n-1}$.
Moreover, for every
$p\in\Pcal_{2n}$,
\begin{equation}
 \int_0^\infty p(t)\e^{-t}\dd t
 =
 \sum_{r=1}^n w_{r,n}p(x_{r,n})
 +(n!)^2[t^{2n}]p.
\end{equation}
Here $[t^{2n}]p$ denotes the coefficient of $t^{2n}$ in $p$, which is zero whenever $\deg p<2n$.
Finally, the weights are
\begin{equation}
 w_{r,n}
 =
 \frac{1}{x_{r,n}\Lag_n'(x_{r,n})^2},
 \qquad r=1,\ldots,n.
\end{equation}

[Proposition prop:tailrl-closed-form-weights of arXiv:2609.02987, 'Tail Likelihood Reinforcement Learning'] For every $i=1,\ldots,N$,
\begin{equation}
\omega\bigl(r_{(i)}\bigr)
=
\sum_{k=1}^{i}
\frac{r_{(k)}-r_{(k-1)}}{N-k+1}.

\end{equation}
Equivalently, all weights follow the recurrence
\begin{equation}
\omega\bigl(r_{(i)}\bigr)
=
\omega\bigl(r_{(i-1)}\bigr)
+
\frac{r_{(i)}-r_{(i-1)}}{N-i+1},
\qquad
\omega\bigl(r_{(0)}\bigr)=0.

\end{equation}

body:
Let (X, M) be a measurable space and let mu and nu be SIGMA-FINITE positive measures on M. Then nu can be written as nu = nu_a + nu_s with nu_a absolutely continuous with respect to mu (nu_a << mu) and nu_s mutually singular with mu (nu_s perp mu), and this decomposition is unique. Combined with the Radon-Nikodym theorem, nu_a has a density: there is an M-measurable f >= 0, unique up to mu-null sets, with nu_a(E) = integral_E f dmu for all E in M; f is in L^1(mu) exactly when nu_a is a finite measure. The statement extends to nu a signed or complex measure of finite total variation with mu sigma-finite. WHERE IT FAILS: (a) sigma-finiteness of nu is essential for existence of the decomposition. Take X = [0,1] with the Borel sets, mu = Lebesgue measure and nu = counting measure. If nu = nu_a + nu_s with nu_a << mu and nu_s perp mu, pick E with mu(E) = 0 and nu_s(X minus E) = 0. For any x outside E we get nu({x}) = nu_a({x}), and mu({x}) = 0 forces nu_a({x}) = 0, contradicting nu({x}) = 1. So X minus E is empty, i.e. E = X, contradicting mu(X) = 1 > 0. (b) sigma-finiteness of mu is essential for the DENSITY. With mu = counting measure on [0,1] and nu = Lebesgue measure one has nu << mu, yet no f satisfies nu(E) = integral_E f dmu (evaluating on singletons forces f = 0). The decomposition itself survives here (nu_s = 0), but the Radon-Nikodym half does not. (c) Uniqueness is uniqueness of the pair of measures; the density f is only mu-almost everywhere unique.
(X, M) is a measurable space
mu is sigma-finite (needed for the Radon-Nikodym density)
nu is sigma-finite (needed for existence of the decomposition); for signed or complex nu, finite total variation
absolute continuity and mutual singularity are with respect to the same sigma-algebra M

body: In mathematics, in the areas of order theory and combinatorics, Dilworth's theorem states that, in any finite partially ordered set, the maximum size of an antichain of incomparable elements equals the minimum number of chains needed to cover all elements. This number is called the width of the partial order. The theorem is named for the mathematician Robert P. Dilworth, who published it in 1950.
title: Dilworth's theorem

DRAFT, proof (unaudited): source correction to Bai, Chen, Wang, Xiong and Mei, arXiv:2306.04637, Lemma 14, PDF pages 11-12. The printed lemma assumes convex differentiable f:R^d->R, a minimizer w*, R>=2||w*||, an L_f-Lipschitz gradient on the radius-R ball, zero initial exact and perturbed GD iterates, errors of norm at most epsilon, step 0<=eta<=2/L_f, and integer horizon L<=R/(2 epsilon). Its claimed bound ||hat w_L||<=R/2+L epsilon<=R is false even for a globally smooth scalar quadratic: f(w)=(w-1)^2/2, w*=1, R=2, L_f=1, eta=2, epsilon=1/10, and first perturbation 1/10 give exact first iterate 2 and perturbed first iterate 21/10, exceeding the claimed norm upper 11/10 and radius 2. Under only the printed local smoothness assumption even the comparison bound ||hat w_L-w_L^GD||<=L epsilon can fail. Take f(w)=(w-1)^2/2+(400/3)max(w-2,0)^3, w*=1, R=2, L_f=1, eta=39/20, epsilon=1/10, horizon L=2, perturbation 1/10 at step zero and zero thereafter. This f is globally C2 and convex, with second derivative 1+800 max(w-2,0), and its gradient is exactly w-1 on [-2,2]. Exact iterates are 39/20 and 39/400; perturbed iterates are 41/20 and -779/400. The step-two comparison error is 409/200>1/5=2 epsilon, and all stated hypotheses hold. The first perturbed iterate left the ball on which the Lipschitz constant is controlled. Both witnesses use exact rational arithmetic; source fidelity and the calculations are saved for independent review. No novelty or independent audit is claimed.
Interpret smoothness on the radius-R ball as the stated gradient Lipschitz bound; both examples also have convex C2 functions.

body:
[Definition 2 (Large deviations principle) of arXiv:2607.12666, 'Sample-path Large deviations for \\Scheduled Arrival Processes with Unpunctuality'] Let $(E,\mathcal{T})$ be a topological space. A sequence of random elements $\{X^{(n)}\}$ taking values in $E$ satisfies a large deviations principle with speed $n$ and rate function $I:E\to[0,\infty]$ if:
\begin{itemize}
\item for every closed set $F\subset E$,
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\log \Pbb(X^{(n)}\in F)
\le -\inf_{x\in F} I(x),
\]
\item for every open set $G\subset E$,
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\log \Pbb(X^{(n)}\in G)
\ge -\inf_{x\in G} I(x).
\]
\end{itemize}
The rate function $I$ is called {\it good} if its level sets $\{x: I(x)\le M\}$ are compact for all $M<\infty$.
title: Large deviations principle

[Lemma 2nd_spectral_derivative of arXiv:2608.23765, '\texorpdfstring{Tight Majorizations and Convergence Rates\\ of Nuclear Norm Minimization I'] Let $f:\R_{\geq 0} \to \R$ be a differentiable function 
	with $L$-Lipschitz first derivative $f'$ such that $f'$ is right differentiable at $0$ and $f'(0)=0$.
	Then the spectral function $F: \R^{d_1 \times d_2} \to \R$, $F(\mathbf{X})= \sum_{i=1}^d f(\sigma_i(\mathbf{X}))$ is differentiable with $L$-Lipschitz gradients $\nabla F(\mathbf{X}) \in \R^{d_1 \times d_2}$ and furthermore almost everywhere twice differentiable.
    Moreover, 
	$F$ is twice differentiable at $\mathbf{X} \in \R^{d_1 \times d_2}$ 
	if and only if $f$ is twice differentiable at all $\sigma_{1}(\mathbf{X}),\ldots, \sigma_{d}(\mathbf{X})$. 
	In that case, if additionally $d_1 \leq d_2$, 
	the Hessian $\nabla^2 F(\mathbf{X})$ of $F$ at $\mathbf{X}$ is given by
	\begin{equation} 
		\nabla^2 F(\mathbf{X})(\mathbf{Z}) = \mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}} \begin{bmatrix}\mathbf{H}_1 \circ S( \mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}}^\top \mathbf{Z} \mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X},1})
			+ 	
			\mathbf{H}_2 \circ T(\mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}}^\top \mathbf{Z} \mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X},1})
			& \mathbf{H}_3 \circ (\mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}}^\top \mathbf{Z} \mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X},2})\end{bmatrix}
		\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X}}^\top
	\end{equation}
	for any $\mathbf{Z} \in \R^{d_1 \times d_2}$, 
	where $\mathbf{X}$ has the SVD $\mathbf{X} = \mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}} \diag(\boldsymbol{\sigma}) \mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X}}^\top$ 
	with $\mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}} \in \R^{d_1 \times d_1}$, 
	$\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X}}= \begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X},1} & \mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X},2} \end{bmatrix} 
	\in \R^{d_2 \times d_2}$, $\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X},1} \in \R^{d_2 \times d}$, $\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X},2} \in \R^{d_2 \times (d_2-d)}$, 
	$T$ and $S$ are as in (equation eq:sym_and_antisym of the paper), and $\mathbf{H}_1 \in \R^{d \times d}$ is such that for $i,j \in [d]$,
	\[
	(\mathbf{H}_1)_{ij} =
	\begin{cases}
		\frac{f'(\sigma_i) - f'(\sigma_j)}{\sigma_i - \sigma_j} & \text{ if } \sigma_i \neq \sigma_j, \\
		f''(\sigma_i) & \text{ if } \sigma_i = \sigma_j,
	\end{cases}
	\]
	the matrix $\mathbf{H}_2 \in \R^{d \times d}$ is such that for $i,j \in [d]$,
	\[
	(\mathbf{H}_2)_{ij} =
	\begin{cases}
		\frac{f'(\sigma_i) + f'(\sigma_j)}{\sigma_i + \sigma_j} & \text{ if } \sigma_i + \sigma_j \neq 0 , \\
		f''(\sigma_i) & \text{ if } \sigma_i = \sigma_j = 0,
	\end{cases}
	\]
	and $\mathbf{H}_3 \in \R^{d_1 \times (d_2-d)}$ is such that for $i \in [d_1], j \in [d_2-d]$,
	\[
	(\mathbf{H}_3)_{ij} =
	\begin{cases}
		f'(\sigma_i)/ \sigma_i & \text{ if } \sigma_i \neq 0 , \\
		f''(\sigma_i) & \text{ if } \sigma_i = 0.	
	\end{cases}
	\]

[Theorem 1 (Intermediate singular values away from the upper edge) of arXiv:2608.30722, 'Intermediate Singular Values of Random Matrices\\ under Second-Moment and Anti-Concentrati'] Let $A=(\xi_{ij})_{i,j=1}^n$ be a real $n \times n$ random matrix with
independent entries satisfying \textnormal{(A1)--(A2)}. For every
$\delta\in(0,1)$,
there exist constants $c,C>0$, depending only on $a,b,\delta$, such that
\begin{equation}
  \mathbb{P}\!\left(
    s_{n+1-l}(A) > C t\frac{l}{\sqrt{n}}
  \right)
  \;\le\;
  \exp\!\left(-c\min\!\left\{tl,n\right\}\right)
\end{equation}
for every $t \ge 1$ and every integer $l$ satisfying
\[
  1 \le l \le (1-\delta)n.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:fk_density of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Let $V : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ be a bounded measurable function
and $k \in \mathbb{R}$.
The \emph{Feynman-Kac semigroup} associated with $V$
is the family of operators $(P_t^{k,\rho})_{t \geq 0}$
on $L^2(\mu)$ defined by
\begin{align}
  \bigl(P_t^{k,\rho} f\bigr)(x)
  \equiv
  \E^x\left[
    f(X_t)
    \exp\left(k \int_0^t V(X_s)\mathrm{d} s\right)
  \right],
  
\end{align}
for $f \in L^2(\mu)$, $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, $t \geq 0$.
title: Feynman-Kac semigroup for density observables

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.25971, 'Positive \texorpdfstring{$\tau$}{tau}-bi-Ricci curvature and Mean curvature flow with surg'] Let $n\geq3$ and $0\leq\tau\leq2$.  Let
$X_0:M^n\to\Hh^{n+1}$ be a smooth closed connected immersion whose induced
metric has positive $\tau$-bi-Ricci curvature.  Then there is a mean curvature
flow with surgery starting from $X_0$ which has only finitely many surgery
times and terminates.  When $n=3$ and $\tau=2$, the flow
may be taken to be smooth and it converges to a round point.  Moreover,
\begin{equation*}
 M\cong\Sph^n
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 M\cong\mathop{\#}_{j=1}^{k}
       \bigl(\Sph^{n-1}\times\Sph^1\bigr)
\end{equation*}
for some $k\geq1$.  If $X_0$ is embedded and bounds a compact domain
$\Omega_0$, the surgery flow may be chosen embedded and $\Omega_0$ is a
one-handlebody, namely a ball with finitely many one-handles attached. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.25971

\partial_r P_{\rho,r}^\gamma[v^\gamma(r,\cdot)](x)

w_{\rho,r}^\gamma(x),

[Lemma 23 of arXiv:2607.18862, 'Tamed Euler Schemes for Singular SDEs with Multiplicative L\'{e}vy Noise'] Let  $\widetilde{X}^n$ satisfy (\ref{formula1+12+1}) and suppose $f\in \mL_{p}^{q}([0,1])$ for some $p\in (d/\beta\vee 1,\infty)$, $q\in [1,\infty]$ saisfying $\frac{d}{p}+\frac{2}{q}<2$. Then, for any $(s,t)\in \Delta$ and any $m\geq 1$, we have 
		\be 
		\|\int_{s}^{t}f(r,\widetilde{X}_r^{n})dr\|_{L_m(\Omega|\sF_s)}\leq N_m\|f\|_{\mL_{p}^{q}([s,t])}(t-s)^{1-\frac{d}{2p}-\frac{1}{q}},
		\ee 
		where $N_m$ depends on $d,\alpha,\beta, p,q,c_0,c_1,m$, and
		\be 
		\mE_s\exp\bigg(\int_{s}^{t}f(r,\widetilde{X}_r^{n})dr\bigg)\leq 2\exp(N\|f\|_{\mL_{p}^{q}([0,1])}^{1/(1-\frac{d}{2p})}),
		\ee 
		where $N$ depends on $d,\alpha,\beta, p,q,c_0,c_1$.
		
		Furthermore, assume additionally that there exists a continuous control $\sW_0$ on $\Delta$ and positive constants $M$, $\gamma_0$ such that 
		\be 
		(1/n)^{1-\frac{1}{q}}\|f\|_{\mL_{\infty}^q([s,t])}\leq \sW_0^{\gamma_0},~\forall 0\leq t-s\leq 1/n
		\ee
		and 
		\ce 
		\|f\|_{\mL_p^q([0,1])}+\sW(0,1)\leq M.
		\de  
		Then there exists a finite constant $N_0$, which depends only on  $d,\alpha,\beta, p,q,c_0,c_1,M,\gamma_0$, such that
		\be

body: In mathematics, especially in the study of dynamical systems and differential equations, the stable manifold theorem is an important result about the structure of the set of orbits approaching a given hyperbolic fixed point. It roughly states that the existence of a local diffeomorphism near a fixed point implies the existence of a local stable center manifold containing that fixed point. This manifold has dimension equal to the number of eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix of the fixed point that are less than 1.
title: Stable manifold theorem

body: Let sum_(n=0 to infinity) a_n x^n be a real power series with finite radius of convergence R > 0, and suppose the series also converges at the boundary point x = R, to the value S = sum_(n=0 to infinity) a_n R^n. Let f(x) = sum a_n x^n for |x| < R. Then the limit of f(x) as x approaches R from below (x -> R^-, or more generally as x -> R while staying inside a Stolz angle at R) equals S. In particular, f extends continuously to x = R, and this continuous value agrees with the boundary series' sum.
title: Abel's theorem

body: Let X be a complex Banach space and T a bounded linear operator on X, with spectrum sigma(T) (a nonempty compact subset of C) and spectral radius r(T) = sup{|lambda| : lambda in sigma(T)}. Then the limit lim_{n -> infinity} ||T^n||^{1/n} exists and equals r(T), and moreover r(T) = inf_{n >= 1} ||T^n||^{1/n}, by subadditivity of n -> log||T^n|| and Fekete's lemma; the sequence ||T^n||^{1/n} need not itself be monotonic, only its limit is pinned down as the infimum. [Gelfand (1941); see Conway, A Course in Functional Analysis]
title: Gelfand's Spectral Radius Formula

[Thm 5 of arXiv:2608.13976, 'Boundary Harnack principle for diffusion with jumps on metric measure spaces'] Suppose that assumptions (A1) and (A2)-(A4)  hold for some $R_0>0$.
Let $D$ be an  open set in $\sX$.
Then for each  $z_0\in \partial D$ and $R\in (0,  R_0/16 ) $  so that $\overline{B(z_0, 2R)}\subsetneq \sX$,
 there exists a constant
$C=C( z_0, R)>0$,
 which depends on the constants in assumptions (A2)-(A4)  for the ball $B(z_0,  2R)$ and is independent of the geometry of $D$,
   such that   for any  nonnegative
 regular harmonic functions $f$ and $g$
on $D\cap B(z_0, R)$   vanishing  on  $  (D^c)^r \cap B(z_0, R),$
\begin{equation}
f(x)g(y)\leq Cf(y)g(x)  \quad \hbox{for } x, y\in D\cap B(z_0, R/32).
\end{equation}
 Furthermore, assume  that the assumptions (A1), (A2'), (A3'), (A4') and (A5) hold for  $R_0>0$.
 Then the constant in \eqref{e:1} depends only on $R,$ that is,  for each $R\in (0, R_0/16)$, the BHP \eqref{e:1} holds
  with $C=C(R)\geq 1$ uniformly for $z_0\in \partial D.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorema 1 (\cite{KSC}) of arXiv:2604.15152, 'The Multinomial Allocation Model and the Random Box Load'] Assume that, as $n \to \infty$, there exist positive constants $C_1$ and $C_2$, independent of $n$, such that
\begin{equation}
C_1 \le \alpha \le \beta \le C_2.
\end{equation}
For all non-negative integers $r$, define
\[
p_{r}(x) := \frac{x^r}{r!} e^{-x}.
\]
Then, for any fixed $r \ne t$,
\begin{align*}
\rE[\hat q_r] &= \rE[p_{r}(\xi)] + O(n^{-1}),\\
\rV[\hat q_r] &= n^{-1}\alpha \rE\!\left[p_{r}(\xi)\bigl(1 - p_{r}(\xi)\bigr)\right]
               - n^{-1}\!\left(\rE\!\left[p_{r}(\xi)(\xi - r)\right]\right)^2
               + O(n^{-2}),\\
\rC[\hat q_r,\hat q_t] &= -n^{-1}\alpha \rE[p_{r}(\xi)p_{t}(\xi)]
                         - n^{-1}\rE[p_{r}(\xi)(\xi - r)]\,
                           \rE[p_{t}(\xi)(\xi - t)]
                         + O(n^{-2}).
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

& \hphantom{\sum}{} \times a_k(\sigma_k, \tau_{k-1}) a_{k-1}(\tau_{k-1}, \tau_{k-2}) \cdots a_2(\tau_{2}, e_1)

summed over all sequences of permutations

body:
[Definition 13 (Admissible metrics of type I) of arXiv:2608.29427, '\small Positive mass and rigidity \\ for asymptotically flat tangent bundles'] A tubular interpolating metric \(\widetilde g\) is called an \emph{admissible metric of type I} if the following conditions hold.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item
		The function
		\[
		\psi=\psi(\y) \not\equiv 0
		\]
		depends only on the fiber variable, is compactly supported, and satisfies
		\[
		\psi_{,s}\le0.
		\]
		Thus \(\psi\) is a radially non-increasing cutoff function in the fiber variable.
		\item
		The base metric, cross term, and vertical component satisfy
		\[
		g_{ij}-\delta_{ij}
		\in
		\mathcal O_2(r^{-(n-2)}),
		\]
		\[
		a^c_{ij}
		\in
		\mathcal O_1(\rho^{-\lambda^c}),
		\qquad \text{where} \quad 
		\lambda^c>2n-1,
		\]
		and
		\[
		h_{ij}
		\in
		\mathcal O_1(r^{-\sigma^v}),
		\qquad
		\xi\in\mathcal O_1(\rho^{-\tau^v}),
		\]
		where
		\[
		\sigma^v+\tau^v>2n-1,
		\qquad
		\tau^v\ge2n-1.
		\]
	\end{enumerate}
title: Admissible metrics of type I

[Proposition 4 of arXiv:2604.06645, '2604.06645'] Fix $i\in \{1,...,m\}$ and $k\in \{1,...r\}$ and let $Z_{ik}$ be the stochastic convolution
\begin{equation}
Z_{ik} := \int_0^t\int_D G_i(t-s,x,y)g_{ik}(s,y)W_k(dyds),
\end{equation}
where $g_{ik}:\mathbb R\rightarrow \mathbb R$ is bounded and adapted and $G_i$ is the heat kernel corresponding to the operator $d_i\Delta$. Then, for every $t\in [0,T]$,
\[
\mathbb E\sup_{t\in [0,T]}||Z_{ik}(t)||^p_{W^{\varepsilon,p}(D)}\leq C_{i,k,p,\varepsilon,T}||g_{ik}||_{L^{\infty}(D)}^p,
\]
for $\varepsilon<1-\eta$, where $\eta$ is given in Assumption \ref{assump: convolution singularity}, and for sufficiently large $p$ depending on $\varepsilon$ and $\eta$.

body:
Let A be an irreducible 0-1 transition matrix and let X_A be the associated one-sided or two-sided subshift of finite type with the shift sigma. Let lambda be the Perron-Frobenius eigenvalue of A with positive left and right eigenvectors u and v normalised so that the inner product of u and v is 1. Then the topological entropy of the shift is log lambda, and there is a UNIQUE measure of maximal entropy - the Parry measure - given by the Markov chain with transition probabilities P(i,j) = A(i,j) v_j / (lambda v_i) and stationary vector p_i = u_i v_i. It is the Markov measure whose entropy equals log lambda, and it is ergodic; it is mixing exactly when A is aperiodic (primitive).
IRREDUCIBILITY of A gives existence and uniqueness;
primitivity (irreducible plus aperiodic) is what upgrades ergodicity to mixing.
For a reducible matrix the maximal measure may be supported on a proper irreducible component and uniqueness can fail.

body:
[Thm 1 of arXiv:2608.22514, 'Diffusion limits of cyclic finite-velocity random motions\\ along vector fields'] Suppose that assumptions
$\mathbf{A}_V$,
$\mathbf{A}_\tau$,
$\mathbf{A}_{V,\mu}$ and
$\mathbf{A}_\varkappa$ hold. Then, for any initial values $x\in\bR^d$ and $\iota\in \{1,\dots,p\}$,
the flight evolutions $\{X^{\e,\delta}\}$ converge weakly in $C(\bR_+,\bR^d)$
to a diffusion $X$ starting at $x$ with the generator
\ba

Af
= \frac{\varkappa^2}{2\mu}  \sum_{i} \sigma_{i}^2 \langle \nabla^2 f  V_i, V_i\rangle
+ \frac{\varkappa^2}{\mu} \sum_{j< i} \mu_i\mu_j \langle \nabla f , D V_i [ V_j] \rangle,\quad f\in C^3_b(\bR^d,\bR).
\ea
The diffusion $X$ is a solution to an It\^o-SDE
\ba

\di X_t= \frac{\varkappa}{\sqrt\mu}  \sum_{i} \sigma_{i} V_i(X_t)\,\di W^i_t +
\frac{\varkappa^2}{\mu} \sum_{j< i} \mu_i\mu_j  D V_i [ V_j](X_t)\,\di t,
\ea
where $W^1,\dots,W^p$ are independent standard one-dimensional Brownian motions.
The SDE \eqref{e:SDEX} can be rewritten in the Stratonovich form
as
\ba

\di X_t= \frac{\varkappa}{\sqrt\mu}  \sum_{i} \sigma_{i} V_i(X_t)\circ\di W^i_t
-\frac{\varkappa^2}{2\mu} \Big(
\sum_{i} \lambda_i^2  D V_i [ V_i](X_t)
+\sum_{j< i} \mu_i\mu_j  [ V_i,V_j](X_t)
\Big)\,\di t.
\ea (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 1 of arXiv:2608.22514

[Lemma Lemma_cadlag of arXiv:2603.26307, '\LARGE The incompressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system with thermal noise'] Let Assumption (Ass:noise of the paper) hold and $(\Omega,\mathfrak{A},\mathbb{P})$, $\mathscr{F}$, $(W_n)_{n\in \mathbb{Z}^3}$, $(B_n)_{n\in \mathbb{Z}^3}$, 
	$(u,\psi ,q)  $ be a weak martingale solution to (equation Eq_new_var of the paper) with divergence-free initial value 
	$u_0 \in L^2(\mathbb{T}^3; \mathbb{R}^3)$ and $\psi_0\in L^2(\mathbb{T}^3)$ non-negative. Then there exists a $\mathbb{P}\otimes \mathrm{d} t $ version $\psi^+$ of $\psi$ which is c\`adl\`ag in the weak topology of $L^2(\mathbb{T}^3)$. Denoting the process of left limits by 
	\begin{equation}\psi^-(t)\,=\,
		\begin{cases}
			\psi_0,& t = 0 ,\\
			\lim_{s\nearrow t}  \psi^+(s), & t\in (0,T],
		\end{cases}
	\end{equation}
	this version satisfies moreover, $\mathbb{P}$-a.s.,
	\begin{align}
		\int_{\mathbb{T}^3}	\eta \bigl(\psi_{t}^{+}   - \psi_{t}^{-} \bigr) \,\mathrm{d} x \,=\, \int_{\{t\}\times \mathbb{T}^3} \eta  \,\mathrm{d} q,
	\end{align} and 
	\begin{align} \begin{split}&
			\int_{\mathbb{T}^3} \psi^+_t \eta   \, \mathrm{d} x \,-\, \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}
			\psi_0 \eta 
			\,\mathrm{d} x 
			\\&\quad=\, \int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{T}^3} -  \bigl(1+ {F_1}/2 +G_1/2\bigr) \nabla \psi \cdot \nabla  \eta \,+\,\psi u\cdot \nabla \eta   \,-\, (F_2/2+G_2/8) \psi \eta \,\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} s \,+\, \int_{[0,t]\times\mathbb{T}^3} \eta \,\mathrm{d} q
			\\&\qquad + \sum_{i=1}^3
			\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}^3}\int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}\psi g_n \partial_i \eta  + \frac{1}{2} \psi  \eta \partial_ig_n  \,\mathrm{d} x\,  \mathrm{d} W_{n,s}^i
			\, +\, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sum_{i,j =1}^3\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}^3}\int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{T}^3}u_j\partial_i (\eta f_n) \,\mathrm{d} x \,\mathrm{d} B_{n,s}^{ji},
		\end{split}
	\end{align}
	for all $\eta \in C^{{\infty}}(\mathbb{T}^3)$ and  $t\in [0,T)$.

body:
[Lem trace power bfL-n-R asymp of arXiv:2608.23156, 'Disc counting statistics of the real Ginibre ensemble'] Let $N=2n$ be a positive even integer. Suppose that
$r\in(0,\infty)$ and
\begin{equation}
    R
    =
    r-\frac{s}{\sqrt{2N}}
    +
    o\bigl(N^{-1/2}\bigr)
 
 \end{equation}
as $N\to\infty$, for some fixed $s\in\mathbb{R}$. Then, for every fixed
positive integer $m$,
\begin{equation} 
    \operatorname{Tr}\big[\mathbf{L}_N(R)^m\big]
    =
    (r^2\wedge1)n
    +
    \alpha_{m,r,s}\sqrt n
    +
    o(\sqrt n),
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
    \alpha_{m,r,s}
    :=
    \begin{cases}
    \displaystyle
    r\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}
    \bigg[
        \bigg(\frac{\operatorname{erfc}(x)}{2}\bigg)^m
        -
        \mathbbm{1}_{\{x<s\}}
    \bigg]\,dx,
    & 0<r<1,
    \\[3mm]
    \displaystyle
    \int_{-\infty}^{s}
    \bigg[
        \bigg(\frac{\operatorname{erfc}(x)}{2}\bigg)^m
        -
        1
    \bigg]\,dx,
    & r=1,
    \\[3mm]
    0,
    & 1<r<\infty.
    \end{cases}
\end{equation}
If $R\to\infty$, the same conclusion holds with
$(r^2\wedge1)n$ interpreted as $n$ and
$\alpha_{m,\infty,s}:=0$.
title: Lem trace power bfL-n-R asymp of arXiv:2608.23156

[Proposition T:Upper-t of arXiv:2602.05317, 'Strong local nondeterminism for stochastic time-fractional\\ slow and fast diffusion equat'] Under the setting of Theorem~(T:main-holder of the paper), for all positive constants
  $S$ and $T$ with $S<T$, there exists a positive constant $C = C_{S,T}$, such
  that the following statements hold with $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ defined as
  in~(equation E:rho1-rho2 of the paper).

  \begin{enumerate}[\rm (i)]

    \item If either a) $\beta \in (0,2)$; or b) $\beta = 2$ and $\gamma > 2$; or
          c) $\beta = 2$, $\gamma \in (0,2]$ and $\ell < \alpha (\gamma + 1/2)$\footnote{This condition is required to apply part (ii) of Lemma~(L:intml of the paper) on $E_{2,2 + \gamma - 1}$.}, then for all $(t,s,x)\in [S,T]^2 \times \mathbb{R}^d$ it
          holds that
          \begin{align*} 
            \mathbb{E}\left[\left(u(t, x) - u(s, x)\right)^2\right]
            \le C
            \begin{dcases}
              |t-s|^{2 (\rho_1 \wedge 1)},                    & \ell \neq \alpha(\gamma + 1) - 2, \\
              |t-s|^2 \big(1 + \big| \log(|t-s|) \big| \big), & \ell = \alpha(\gamma + 1) - 2.
            \end{dcases}
          \end{align*}

    \item If $\beta = 2$ and $\gamma = 0$, then for all $(t,s,x)\in [S,T]^2
            \times \mathbb{R}^d$ it holds that
          \begin{align*} 
            \mathbb{E}\left[\left(u(t, x) - u(s, x)\right)^2\right]
            \le C
            \begin{dcases}
              |t-s|^{2(\rho_2 \wedge 1)},                     & \rho_2 \neq 1, \\
              |t-s|^2 \big(1 + \big| \log(|t-s|) \big| \big), & \rho_2 = 1.
            \end{dcases}
          \end{align*}

  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Theorem 3 (Estimating the number of communities). Assume that the average degree satisfies d >= 2 and Assumption 1 holds. For any epsilon > 0 small enough, the following holds with high probability for sufficiently large n: N_eps(sqrt d) = N(sqrt d + eps) = r_+ and N_eps(-sqrt d) = N(-sqrt d - eps) = r_-. The above is also valid when taking eps = eps_n = log(n)^{-c} for any c > 0. Here, for a stochastic block model with r communities, proportions pi and connectivity P: d := sum_j P_ij pi_j > 1 for all i is the average degree; Assumption 1 says pi_i, P_ij (and hence d, r and r_0) do not depend on n; r_+ and r_- count the positive and negative informative eigenvalues of the signal matrix Q = P diag(pi) (those mu with mu^2 > d); H(t) := t^2 - tA + (D - I) is the Bethe-Hessian of the graph (A its adjacency matrix, D its degree matrix); N_eps(t) is the number of eigenvalues of H(t) below -eps and N(t) the number of negative eigenvalues of H(t).

body: Skolem's Paradox is the apparent contradiction arising from Downward Löwenheim-Skolem: if ZFC has a model, it has a countable model M, yet M proves the existence of uncountable sets (such as \mathbb{R}). The resolution is that 'uncountable' is not absolute: the bijection between \mathbb{R}^M and \omega exists outside M but is not an element of M.
title: Skolem's Paradox

[Theorem thm:counterexample:leftsided:weight:operator of arXiv:2608.23765, '\texorpdfstring{Tight Majorizations and Convergence Rates\\ of Nuclear Norm Minimization I'] For any\\ $r,d \in \mathbb{N}$ with $d \ge 220 r$, there exists a measurement operator $\mathcal{A}: \mathbb{R}^{d \times d} \rightarrow \R^m$ satisfying the NSP of order $r$ with constant $\eta_r = 1/10$ and of order $1$ with $\eta_1 = 1/(11r -1)$, a rank-$r$ matrix $\mathbf{X}_\star \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}$ and a matrix $\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}$ such that $\mathbf{X} - \mathbf{X}_\star \in \ker(\mathcal{A})$ and $\nucnorm{\mathbf{X} - \mathbf{X}_\star} \le \frac{ \sigma_r \left( \mathbf{X}_\star \right) }{ \max \left( \eta_1 \sqrt{ d}, 2 \right)  }$, but also
\begin{equation*}
\innerproduct{ \mathbf{X}_\star - \mathbf{X}, \W{\mathbf{X}}{\varepsilon} (\mathbf{X}_\star - \mathbf{X} ) }
\ge
\frac{d}{220 r}\nucnorm{ \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{X}_\star},
\end{equation*}
if $\W{\mathbf{X}}{\varepsilon}(\cdot)$ is the weight operator (eq:W:operator:action of the paper) with left-sided core matrix (eq:leftsided:mean of the paper) and the smoothing parameter $\varepsilon$ satisfies $\varepsilon = \frac{\besterrNuc{\mathbf{X}}{r} }{d}$.

Furthermore, in this case, the subsequent IRLS iterate 
\[
\mathbf{X}^+ = \argmin_{ \mathbf{Z} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d} } \innerproduct{ \mathbf{Z}, \W{\mathbf{X}}{\varepsilon} (\mathbf{Z}) } \text{ subject to } \mathcal{A}(\mathbf{Z}) = \mathcal{A}(\mathbf{X}_\star)
\] 
satisfies
\[
	\nucnorm{\mathbf{X}^+-\mathbf{X}_\star}
	\geq \left(1-\frac{220 r}{d}\right)\nucnorm{\mathbf{X}-\mathbf{X}_\star}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] Let $X\sim N(0,1)$.

If $c<\tfrac14$, then the $L_2(N(0,1))$ expansion of $e^{c X^2}$ into orthonormal polynomials is
\[
e^{c X^2}
=(1-2c)^{-\tfrac12}\sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{\sqrt{(2k)!}}{k!}
\left(\frac{c}{1-2c}\right)^{\!k}\, h_{2k}(X),
\]
with no odd terms (i.e.\ the coefficients of $h_{2k+1}$ vanish).

body:
Let mu be a probability measure on {0,1}^{E(Z^d)} that is (i) invariant under the lattice translations, (ii) ERGODIC with respect to them, and (iii) has the FINITE ENERGY property: for every edge e, the conditional probability that e is open given the states of all other edges lies almost surely strictly between 0 and 1. Then the number of infinite open clusters is almost surely a constant taking the value 0 or 1. Each of the three hypotheses does work. Ergodicity is what makes the number a constant rather than a random variable; without it a mixture of two percolation measures is a counterexample. Finite energy is what rules out infinitely many infinite clusters, by allowing local modifications; a measure that deterministically forbids certain local patterns can have infinitely many. And the argument uses AMENABILITY of Z^d - on a regular tree or another nonamenable transitive graph there is genuinely a regime with infinitely many infinite clusters, so the theorem is false there. Bernoulli percolation satisfies all three hypotheses for every p, so its infinite cluster is unique whenever it exists. [Burton and Keane (1989), Comm. Math. Phys. 121; see Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed., Theorem 8.1]
translation invariance
ergodicity under the translations
finite energy
an amenable transitive graph such as Z^d; the theorem FAILS on nonamenable graphs

Step 1: rule out 2 <= N = k < infinity. If exactly k infinite clusters exist with k >= 2, choose a box large enough that with positive probability it meets at least two of them. Finite energy allows one to open all edges inside that box with positive conditional probability, which merges those two clusters into one and leaves at most k - 1 infinite clusters on an event of positive probability - contradicting that N is almost surely the constant k. Step 2: rule out N = infinity. Call a vertex x a TRIFURCATION if x lies in an infinite cluster, x has exactly three open incident edges, and deleting x splits its infinite cluster into exactly three infinite pieces. If N = infinity then by the same finite-energy local modification - take a box meeting three distinct infinite clusters and rewire its interior to join them through a single vertex of degree three - the probability that the origin is a trifurcation is strictly positive, say delta > 0. By translation invariance the expected number of trifurcations in a box of side 2n + 1 is delta (2n+1)^d. But a purely combinatorial fact about trees bounds the number of trifurcations inside a box by the size of its BOUNDARY: contracting each cluster gives a forest in which the trifurcations are branch vertices of degree at least three and the distinct infinite branches must exit through distinct boundary vertices, so the number of trifurcations in the box is at most the number of boundary vertices, of order n^{d-1}. For large n, delta (2n+1)^d exceeds C n^{d-1}, a contradiction. This step is exactly where amenability - the fact that boundary is of smaller order than volume - is used.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:0a10dca57c02792c802de68a722e918c5119beec63f791aa1a02a4d2b2b22ace","revision_digest":"sha256:19571635c9811ef2c4fa9bf7413abff7ada34807a8dc3b1fc48636004a01b663","source_id":"rederived:urn:mb-agent:dc73dee333054e1d-M9","source_revision":"re-derived-2026-08-22; statement, the role of each hypothesis and the two-step trifurcation proof were written and checked by the author; textbook cross-reference in the statement, source not fetched this session","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body:
[Definition def:covering of arXiv:2608.21805, 'Logarithmic derivatives of variational and singular stochastic partial differential equati'] For $h \in H$ satisfying clauses~\textup{(i)}--\textup{(ii)} of Assumption~(ass:nondeg of the paper), set $\tilde{h} := \gamma_t^{\dagger}h \in H$ (well-defined a.s.). The \emph{covering vector field} is the $U$-valued process
\begin{equation}
  v_h(r) \;:=\; \Phi_r^{*}\,\tilde{h} \;\in\; U, \qquad r \in [0, t],
\end{equation}
where $\Phi_r := D_r X(t) \in L_2(U, H)$ and $\Phi_r^{*} \in L_2(H, U)$ its adjoint. The representation
\[
  \Phi_r \;=\; Y(t,r)\,\mathcal{B}(r, X(r))
\]
of Proposition~(prop:D-Xt of the paper) is understood as an identity for the Hilbert--Schmidt composite $\Phi_r \in L_2(U,H)$. In the general variational framework we retain the intrinsic formula
\[
  v_h(r) \;=\; \Phi_r^{*}\,\gamma_t^{\dagger}h
\]
and do not require a pathwise adjoint $Y(t,r)^{*}$.
title: Covering vector field

body:
TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). Given a Markov chain with kernel P and a nonnegative P-harmonic function h, the Doob h-transform defines a new Markov chain with kernel P^h(x,y) = P(x,y) h(y)/h(x), representing the law of the original chain conditioned, in an appropriate limiting sense such as conditioning to survive forever or on an asymptotic event, to respect the weighting given by h. Applied to a critical or subcritical Galton-Watson branching process conditioned to survive forever, or, for critical trees, conditioned to have total size n with n -> infinity, the Kesten tree construction realizes the limiting law as an explicit infinite random tree: a single infinite spine, with each spine vertex additionally carrying an independent number of extra children distributed according to the size-biased-minus-one offspring law, each extra child then supporting an ordinary, unconditioned Galton-Watson subtree. This gives the exact local weak limit of large conditioned critical or subcritical branching trees and underlies scaling-limit results, such as convergence to the continuum random tree, that first pass through this explicit infinite-tree description. It does not directly give scaling limits of the whole tree's metric structure, which requires an additional contour or height-function argument, and the exact form of the spine's offspring law is specific to the conditioning event used, since conditioning on survival forever and conditioning on total size n give related but generally distinct limiting infinite trees. Typical failure: Confusing the different conditioning regimes for the conditioned Galton-Watson tree, such as conditioning on survival to infinity versus conditioning on total progeny exactly n as n -> infinity versus conditioning on height n, as if they all give the identical Kesten tree limit; they give related but generally distinct limiting infinite trees, differing in the spine's offspring bias and finer distributional details, and using one variant's known properties for a computation set up under a different conditioning is a frequent, easy-to-miss error. Canonical reference: Doob, 1957, Annales de l'Institut Fourier; Kesten, 1986, Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincare, Probabilites et Statistiques; Lyons, Pemantle and Peres, 1995, Annals of Probability.
a Markov chain, here a Galton-Watson branching process, with an identified P-harmonic function h appropriate to the conditioning event
for Kesten's tree specifically: finite-mean offspring distribution with criticality or subcriticality correctly identified, and a precisely specified conditioning event
existence of the relevant weak-convergence limit of the conditioned law to the h-transformed law, which must be checked rather than assumed
correct identification of the size-biased offspring law along the spine, which differs from the original offspring law

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2608.22534, 'Entropy power inequalities in compact groups'] Let $G$ be a connected compact abelian group, let $\mu$ be its Haar 
probability measure, and let $\chi \in \widehat G$ be a nontrivial 
continuous character. For a measurable set $S \subset G$ with 
$\mu(S)\in(0,1],$ write $g_S:=\frac{ \mathbb{I}_S}{\mu(S)}.
$
Then:
$$ 
\bigl|\widehat{g_S}(\chi)\bigr|
=
\left|
\frac{1}{\mu(S)}\int_G   \mathbb{I}_S(x)\,\overline{\chi(x)}\,d\mu(x)
\right|
\leq
\frac{\sin(\pi\mu(S))}{\pi\mu(S)}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: A Poisson process of rate lambda > 0 is a counting process {N(t) : t >= 0} with N(0) = 0, independent increments, and N(t+s) - N(s) distributed Poisson(lambda t) for all s, t >= 0 (stationary increments). Equivalently: the inter-arrival times are i.i.d. Exponential(lambda). Equivalently: increments are independent, N(t) has a.s. jumps of size 1, and P(N(h) = 1) = lambda h + o(h), P(N(h) >= 2) = o(h).

body: The quadratic variation [X]_t of a process X is the limit in probability of sum (X_{t_{i+1}} - X_{t_i})^2 over partitions of [0, t] with mesh tending to zero. For Brownian motion [W]_t = t; for continuous martingales the quadratic variation is the increasing process making X^2 - [X] a martingale, and it is the object that makes second-order terms survive in stochastic calculus.
title: Quadratic Variation

[Theorem 35 of arXiv:2604.03213, 'Asymptotic expansion for transport maps \\ between laws of multimatrix models'] Let $\cX$ be a Banach space, $\cU \subseteq \cX$ be an open set, and $a \in \R$.
If $f \colon [a,\infty) \times \cU \to \cX$ is locally Lipschitz in space, locally uniformly in time and $c \in C([a,\infty);\cX)$ is such that $c(a) \in \cU$, then there exists a time $T_{\infty} \in (a,\infty]$ and a continuous function $y_{\infty} \colon [a,T_{\infty}) \to \cU$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),font=\normalfont]
    \item $y_{\infty} = c + \int_a^{\boldsymbol{\cdot}} f(t,y_{\infty}(t))\,\d t$ on $[a,T_{\infty})$;
    \item If $T \in (a,\infty]$ and $y \colon [a,T) \to \cU$ is a continuous function such that $y = c + \int_a^{\boldsymbol{\cdot}} f(t,y(t))\,\d t$ on $[a,T)$, then $T \leq T_{\infty}$, and $y_{\infty}|_{[a,T)} = y$.
\end{enumerate}
The function $y_{\infty}$ is the \textbf{maximal solution} to $y = c + \int_a^{\boldsymbol{\cdot}} f(t,y(t))\,\d t$, and $T_{\infty}$ is its \textbf{lifetime}.

body:
[Definition def:hill of arXiv:2608.08375, 'Algebraic formulas for first-passage times of Markov processes in the linear framework: ge'] The vertices of $\mathcal{H}_u[G]$ are the non-terminal vertices of $G$, $\mathcal{V}(\mathcal{H}_u[G]) = \overline{Z}$. The edges and labels of $\mathcal{H}_u[G]$ are acquired from those of $G$ through the following rules.
\begin{enumerate}[topsep=1em]
    \item If $j, k \in \overline{Z}$ are non-terminal vertices with $k \neq u$ ($j = u$ is allowed) and there is an edge $j \to_G k$, then there is an edge $j \to_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} k$ with, 
    \[
        \ell(j \to_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} k) = \ell(j \to_G k) \,.
    \]
    \item If $j \in \overline{Z}$ is a non-terminal vertex and there is an edge $j \rightarrow_G u$, then there is an edge $j \to_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} u$ with, 
    \[
        \ell(j \to_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} u) = \ell(j \to_G u) + \sum_{j \rightarrow_G z ,\, z \in Z} \ell(j \rightarrow_G z) \,.
    \]
    \item If $j \in \overline{Z}$ is a non-terminal vertex other than $u$ ($j \neq u$) without an edge to $u$ ($j \not\to_G u$) but with at least one edge, $j \to_G z$, to some $z \in Z$, then there is an edge $j \rightarrow_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} u$ with, 
    \[
        \ell(j \rightarrow_{\mathcal{H}_u[G]} u) = \sum_{j \rightarrow_G z ,\, z \in Z} \ell(j \rightarrow_G z) \,.
    \]
\end{enumerate}
There are no other edges in $\mathcal{H}_u[G]$.
title: Definition def:hill of arXiv:2608.08375

For geometric offspring with pgf f(s)=1/(2-s), iteration gives f_l(s)=(l-(l-1)*s)/(l+1-l*s). Thus survival has probability 1/(l+1), and the conditional positive population is geometric with success 1/(l+1). Its mass on {1,...,M} tends to zero for each fixed M, while Z_l/l conditioned on survival converges to Exp(1). This is a single-type diagnostic, not the EWT. Check: Direct substitution verifies f(f_l(s))=f_(l+1)(s); subtract f_l(0), divide by survival probability and expand the geometric series. The conditional tail at floor(l*x) is (l/(l+1))^floor(l*x), tending to exp(-x). Obstruction: No EWT Yaglom or Q-process theorem is proved. A size-biased spine law is not automatically the law conditioned on nonextinction.

[Thm criterion-spc-T of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $T$ be a small $\infty$-category with a terminal object $1$, and let ${\mathcal{C}}\colon T^{\textup{op}}\to\CAT_\infty$ be a $T$-$\infty$-category. Assume the following:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item ${\mathcal{C}}$ has a fiberwise finite limits, and every restriction functor $f^*\colon{\mathcal{C}}(B)\to{\mathcal{C}}(A)$ admits a left adjoint $f_!$.
        \item For every $a\colon A\to 1$ in $T$, the functor ${\mathcal{C}}(A)\simeq{\mathcal{C}}(A)_{/1}\to{\mathcal{C}}(1)_{/a_!1}$ induced by $a_!$ is an equivalence.
        \item For every $f\colon A\to B$ in $T$ and every $X\in{\mathcal{C}}(B)$ the diagram
        \[
            f_!f^*1\xleftarrow{\;f_!f^*x\;}f_!f^*X\xrightarrow{\;\varepsilon\;}X
        \]
        exhibits $f_!f^*X$ as a product, where $x\colon X\to 1$ denotes the unique map and $\varepsilon$ denotes the counit of $f_!\dashv f^*$ as usual.
        \item The functor $\Upsilon\colon T\to{\mathcal{C}}(1)$ extends to an equivalence $\PSh(T)\to{\mathcal{C}}(1)$.
    \end{enumerate}

[Definition Properly norm-minimizing of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] Let \(M\) be a compact 3-manifold whose boundary is a collection of tori.
An oriented surface \(S\) is called \emph{properly norm-minimizing} if \(S\) is norm-minimizing and on each boundary \(P\) of \(M\), components of \(\partial S\cap P\) have the same orientation.

When \(M\) is closed, there is no difference between norm-minimizing and properly norm-minimizing.
title: Properly norm-minimizing

body:
Read the ladder result (every consistent cleaner ties inside the long-only stack; floors and linear shrinkage lose) through the entrywise bound. Unconstrained minimum variance depends on $\hat\Sigma^{-1}$, so its error is governed by the SPECTRUM of $\hat\Sigma$: the ratio $q = M/n$, the bulk edge, the near-null directions - the territory of random-matrix cleaning, where the Ledoit-Peche oracle, its analytical estimate and NERCOME differ from the sample covariance by design. The long-only plug-in's excess risk is bounded by twice the ENTRYWISE error $\varepsilon = \max_{ij}|\hat\Sigma_{ij} - \Sigma_{ij}|$, which is $O(\sqrt{\log M/n})$ for the sample covariance and of the same order for every consistent estimator (a consistent nonlinear shrinkage moves the eigenvalues by $O(n^{-1/2})$ relative, hence the entries by the same order) - so all of them obey the same bound and, on the well-conditioned active submatrix, produce the same weights. A fixed floor $f\sigma^2$ on the small eigenvalues, or a linear shrinkage $\rho(\mu I - \hat\Sigma)$, is a BIAS of size $f\sigma^2$ (or $\rho|\mu - \Sigma_{ii}|$) in the entries spanned by those directions that does not vanish with $n$; it cannot tighten the bound and it displaces the plug-in wherever an active member has weight in a floored direction. With case weights $s_i$ (the per-sample relative metric $s_i = 1/\|y_i\|^2$) the bound holds with $n$ replaced by the effective sample size $n_{\mathrm{eff}} = (\sum_i s_i)^2/\sum_i s_i^2$, which a few tiny-norm cases can make much smaller than $n$: that is why the relative-metric fit overfits without the constraint and why the long-only form still pays a little at very small $n$. Measured on the EMIT pool (2026-09-05, seed 101, diag_entrywise.py): the bound holds on every output of Y1/Y2/Y4 at $n = 932$ and of Y2/Y4 at $n = 60$, and is loose by one to three orders of magnitude (median $2\varepsilon$ over the oracle risk 10 to 1000 against a realised excess of 0.02 to 0.5 at full calibration) - it delivers finiteness and the right dependence, not a tight number; the unconstrained plug-in on the same matrices carries weights of median absolute size 68,000 on Y1 and 1,800 on Y2; the effective sample size of the $1/\|y\|^2$ weighting is 150 of 932 rows on Y2 (615 on Y1, 634 on Y4) and 8.7 of 60 in the $n = 60$ arm.
the cleaners compared are consistent for the population covariance (sample, eta-RIE without floor, LW2020, NERCOME)
the ensemble error covariance is rank-deficient in practice (members near-collinear), so the unconstrained plug-in has near-null sample directions

[Dfn 186 (discrete quadratic variation processes) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $\vY$ and $\vY^\frozen$ be the spatial rerandomization processes from Definitions~\ref{d:rerand} and \ref{d:rerand.Ising}. Let $\vD$ and $\vD^\frozen$ be the associated drift processes from Definition~\ref{d:D}.
We now let 
	\begin{align*}
	\vZ &\equiv \vY-\vD\,,\\
	\vZ^\frozen 
		&\equiv \vY^\frozen-\vD^\frozen\,,
	\end{align*}
so these are martingales with respect to the filtration $\cG(q_d)$ from \eqref{e:gaus.filt}. In this subsection we consider the ``quadratic variations'' (and ``covariations'') for the $Z$ processes. To this end, for $\sigma,\tau\in\{\RomI,\RomII,\RomIII,\Ising\}$, define 
$Q^{\sigma,\tau}$ to be the piecewise linear process with increments
	\beq
	\Delta Q^{\sigma,\tau}(q_d) 
	=  \bE \bigg[
		\Big( \Delta Z^\sigma(q_d)\Big)
		\Big(\Delta Z^\tau(q_d)\Big)
		\,\bigg|\, \cG(q_d)
		\bigg]\,,\eeq
started from $Q^{\sigma,\tau}(q_0)=0$. Clearly $Q^{\sigma,\tau}=Q^{\tau,\sigma}$; and we will also abbreviate $Q^{\sigma}\equiv Q^{\sigma,\sigma}$. We define likewise $Q^{\frozen,\sigma,\tau}$.
title: discrete quadratic variation processes

For a normal n by n matrix A, sigma_min(zI - A) = dist(z, spec A) for every z, so Lambda_epsilon(A) is the union of the closed disks of radius epsilon about the eigenvalues. Every eigenvalue of A + E lies within ||E|| of spec A, and if A and A + E are both normal, the Hausdorff distance between their spectra is at most ||E||. If moreover rho = min |lambda| over the eigenvalues of A is positive, every eigenvalue mu of A + E has an eigenvalue lambda of A with |mu - lambda| / |lambda| <= ||E|| / rho.

[Proposition 26 (Uniform logarithmic envelopes) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let \(r\ge1\), let \(T\) be compact, and suppose
\begin{equation}
 \|T\|_{\mathfrak W^{[r]}}\le b.
 
\end{equation}
Then \(T\in\mathcal S_2\), and there is a constant \(C_r\), depending
only on \(r\), such that for \(a\ge0\) and \(0<\varepsilon\le1\),
\begin{align}
 \mathfrak F_T(a)
 &\le C_r(ab)\bigl(\log(e+ab)\bigr)^{r-1},
 \\
 \zeta_T(1+\varepsilon)
 &\le C_r b^{1+\varepsilon}\varepsilon^{-r}.
 
\end{align}
The same bounds hold for every flattening of a tensor whose
multi-flattening \(\mathfrak W^{[r]}\)-norm is at most \(b\).  Thus, once a
Rees coefficient has been placed in grade \(r\), all upper Mellin and
Fredholm consequences are automatic.

[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2606.07290, 'Boundary behaviour of the Volterra square-root process'] Let $\alpha, \beta \in (0,1)$ with $\alpha + \beta \neq 1$, and let $f,g: (0,T] \longrightarrow \mathbb{R}_+$ be given by
    \[
        f(t) = t^{\alpha - 1}\ell_f(t) \quad \text{and} \quad g(t) = t^{\beta - 1}\ell_g(t), \qquad t > 0,
    \]
    where $\ell_f, \ell_g: (0,T] \longrightarrow \mathbb{R}$ are measurable and smoothly varying at $t = 0$. Then as $t \searrow 0$,
    \[
    \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t} \int_0^t f(t-s)g(s)\, \mathrm{d}s \sim (\alpha+\beta-1) B(\alpha, \beta) t^{\alpha+\beta-2} \ell_f(t) \ell_g(t) \quad \text{as } t \searrow 0,
    \]
title: Lemma 19 of arXiv:2606.07290

body: Let X_1, ..., X_n be independent, f non-negative and (a, b)-self-bounding with a >= 1/3, and Z = f(X_1, ..., X_n) with finite mean; put c = (3a - 1)/6. Then for t > 0, P(Z - E[Z] >= t) <= exp(-t^2 / (2(a E[Z] + b + c t))) (Theorem 1 of arXiv:2509.22375, after Boucheron, Lugosi and Massart). For the lower tail, P(Z - E[Z] <= -t) <= exp(-t^2 / (2(a E[Z] + b + t/3))) for t > 0 (Theorem 2 there); and when the X_i take values in {0,1}, P(Z <= E[Z] - t) <= exp(-t^2 / (2(a E[Z] + b))) for 0 < t <= E[Z] (Theorem 3.3 of arXiv:1005.2791). With b = 0 and a = 1 the upper tail is exp(-t^2 / (2 E[Z] + 2t/3)).

[Lemma 17 of arXiv:2511.04938, 'Uniform dimension theorems for parabolic SPDEs'] Choose and fix some $T>0$.
	If there exists $L>0$ such that $\mathcal{H}_k(h)\le L\sqrt{k}$ for all $k\in[2\,,\infty)$, 
	then there exists $c=c(L\,,\mathcal{M}(b)\,,\mathcal{M}(\sigma)\,,T)>0$
	such that
	\[
		\E\left[\exp\left( c 
		\sup_{\substack{(t,x),(s,z)\in[0,T]\times\T\\ (t,x)\neq (s,z)}}
		\left| \frac{\|u(t\,,x) - u(s\,,z)\|}{
		\rho( (t\,,x)\,,(s\,,z) ) \sqrt{\log_+  
		(1/\rho( (t\,,x)\,,(s\,,z)) ) |}}
		\right|^2 \right)\right]<\infty,
	\]
	where $\rho$ was  defined in \eqref{def:rho}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 17 of arXiv:2511.04938

[Corollary 50 of arXiv:2608.09700, 'A general paracontrolled ansatz for singular SPDEs'] For any tree $\tau\in\mcT$, we have the identity
		$$
			\frac{\Upsilon_F[\tau](v_*)}{S(\tau)} =  \sum_{\substack{ |\mu|<\gamma- r_\tau}} \frac{1}{S(\mu) S(\tau)}\P\Big(  \Upsilon_F[\mu \star \tau](v_*)  \, ,Z_\mu\Big)  + u_\tau^\#
		$$
		where  $r_\tau=\lfloor |\mcI(\tau)| \rfloor$, and $u_\tau^\# \in C^{\gamma-r_\tau}$.

body:
[Proposition prop:HB of arXiv:2608.25279, 'Provable Non-Acceleration of Standard Strang\\ Splittings of Kinetic Langevin Dynamics'] Let $(X_k,V_k)_{k\ge0}$ be the OBABO chain (equation eq:obabo1 of the paper)-(equation eq:obabo5 of the paper). Let $\xi_0^{(2)}$ be a $\mathcal N(0,\mathrm{Id}_d)$ variable independent of the pairs $(\xi_k^{(1)},\xi_k^{(2)})_{k\ge1}$ driving the chain. Alternatively, let $\xi_0^{(2)}$ be the zero vector. Define the auxiliary variable $X_{-1}$ by
\begin{equation}
 V_0=r\left(\frac{X_0-X_{-1}}h-\frac h2\nabla U(X_0)\right)
      +\sigma\xi_0^{(2)}.
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 X_{k+1}=X_k+\beta(X_k-X_{k-1})
 -s\nabla U(X_k)+\zeta_{k+1},
 \qquad
 s=\frac{h^2}{2}(1+\beta),
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
 \zeta_{k+1}=h\sigma\bigl(r\xi_k^{(2)}+\xi_{k+1}^{(1)}\bigr).
\end{equation}
Distinct $\zeta_k$ depend on disjoint noises and are therefore
independent centered Gaussians. If
$\xi_0^{(2)}\sim\mathcal N(0,\mathrm{Id}_d)$, they are identically distributed
with covariance
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[\zeta_k\zeta_k^\top]
 =h^2(1-\beta^2)\mathrm{Id}_d.
\end{equation}
If $\xi_0^{(2)}=0$, then
\[
 \zeta_1=h\sigma\xi_1^{(1)},\qquad
 \mathbb E[\zeta_1\zeta_1^\top]=h^2(1-\beta)\mathrm{Id}_d,
\]
while (equation eq:zetacov of the paper) holds for every $k\ge2$.

[Theo 61 of arXiv:2602.14618, 'Finitary coding and Gaussian concentration\\ for random fields'] Let $d\geq 2$ and $q>1$.\newline
If $p<p_c(q)$, then $\phi_{p,q}$ satisfies Gaussian concentration. \newline
If $p>p_c(q)$, then neither $\phi^{\mathrm{free}}_{p,q}$ nor $\phi^{\mathrm{wired}}_{p,q}$ satisfies Gaussian concentration.

[Corollary 5 of arXiv:2605.03851, 'The Relay Random Tree:\\A stochastic geometry approach of multihop relay in an urban visib'] \textbf{Increase of information.}\\
    Let $(x, y)$ be a point of $\Half$ and $\landsc$ be a landscape of buildings. Then the angle formed by $(x, y)$ and its blocking building $\tau(x, y)$ is greater than that formed by $\tau(x, y)$ and its own blocking building $\tau (\tau (x, y))$. [Thm exact_Wn_plugin of arXiv:2604.07183, 'Stopping on the last success with unknown odds: asymptotic minimax optimality of the plug-'] For any~$n\ge 2$ and $p\in(0,1)$, the win probability of the plug-in rule is 
\begin{equation}

W_n(p)
=
p
\sum_{t=\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil+1}^n (1-p)^{n-t}
\sum_{k=1}^{b_t} u_{t-1,k-1}
,
\end{equation}
where the quantities~$u_{t,k}$ can be computed via the recursion~(equation eq:u_recursion of the paper)
(the corresponding stopping probabilities are then
$
\mathbb P_p[\hat{\tau}_n=t]
=
p
\sum_{k=1}^{b_t} u_{t-1,k-1}$,
for $
t=1,\ldots,n
$). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm exact_Wn_plugin of arXiv:2604.07183

[Corollary 16 of arXiv:2608.08242, 'Bang--bang representation of $3\times 3$ embeddable stochastic matrices'] Let $A\in \mathcal M_+$.  Suppose that $A\in R_n\setminus\bigl(R_{n-1}\cup\V\bigr)$
 and $n\geq 6$.
	Then $A$ has a minimal representation
	\[
	A=(X_n\cdots X_6)(X_5\cdots X_1),
	\]
	where each $X_\ell$ is a homogeneous elementary matrix and
	\[
	A'=X_5\cdots X_1\in\V
	\]
	satisfies exactly one vestibule equality. Moreover, in any such
	representation, if the unique vestibule equality is
	$V_{ij}(A')=0$ and $k$ is the remaining state, then, read in the order in which the moves are applied, the move types of
	$X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are, successively,
	\[
	(i,k),\ (k,j),\ (j,i),\ (i,k),\ (k,j),\ (j,i),\ldots .
	\]

[Lemma 5 (Logarithmic integrability) of arXiv:2607.20823, 'Fluctuation impossibility results for stochastic burst networks'] Let $\pi$ be any full-support probability distribution on
$S=\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^N$ satisfying $\E_\pi[s(X)^2]<\infty$.
If, in addition, $\pi$ is stationary for a continuous-time Markov chain
whose total exit rate satisfies Assumption~\ref{ass:S-standing}\textnormal{(A3)},
then
\begin{equation}
        \sum_{x\in S}
        \pi(x)(1+s(x))|\log\pi(x)|
        <\infty,
        
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
        \sum_{x\in S}\pi(x)
        \sum_{y\ne x}q(x,y)
        \bigl(
        |\log\pi(x)|+|\log\pi(y)|
        \bigr)
        <\infty.
        
\end{equation}
In particular, for $g(x):=-\log\pi(x)$, we have
$Lg\in L^1(\pi)$ and
\[
        \E_\pi[(Lg)(X)]=0.
\]

[Lemma 5.13 of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186'] Let $t>0$ and $x_1,x_2\in\mbb R^2$ be fixed.
Suppose that the pair $(Z_1,Z_2)$ is either $({_1}B^{x_1},{_2}B^{x_2})$
or $({_1}B^{x_1,x_1}_t,{_2}B^{x_2,x_2}_t)$.
Given a positive $\theta>0$,
let us denote the event
\[\mf O_{t,\theta}(Z_1,Z_2)=\left\{\inf_{(r_1,r_2)\in[0,t]^2}\|Z_1(r_1)-Z_2(r_2)\|\geq\theta\right\}.\]
Almost surely, $\al_t(Z_1,Z_2)\mbf 1_{\mf O_{t,\theta}(Z_1,Z_2)}=0.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

paths, hence for their union. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 18 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $G$. 
Assume that the action of $G$ on $\wt B$ satisfies the moment condition \eqref{moment-assumption-01} and 
that the action of $G$ on $B$ satisfies the contraction property \eqref{contraction-property-on-B}.  
Suppose that, for every $\wt b \in \wt B$ with $\eta(\wt b) \in \supp \nu$,   we have $\wt b M \subset \overline{\Gamma_{\mu} \wt b}$. 
Then, there exists a unique closed coabelian normal subgroup $M_0^{\mu}$ of $M$ 
such that, 
for any $x \in \wh M$, the operator $P_{\mu, x}$ admits an eigenvalue with modulus one in $W^0_x$ if and only if 
$\rho_x$ is the one-dimensional representation associated with a character $\chi_x$ of $M$ which is trivial on $M_0^{\mu}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:band-limited-orbit-coding of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] Fix
\[
    \frac12<\sigma<1.
\]
There exist $\tau\in(\frac12,\sigma)$ and a real entire function
$\psi$ such that
\[
    \psi(n)
    =
    \begin{cases}
        1,&n=0,\\
        0,&n\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\},
    \end{cases}
\]
and, for every $j,N\geq0$,
\[
    \left|\psi^{(j)}(x+iy)\right|
    \leq
    C_{j,N}
    e^{2\pi\sigma|y|}
    (1+|x|)^{-N}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
    \operatorname{supp}\widehat\psi
    \subset[-\tau,\tau].
\]

Let $b:Z\to[-1,1]$ be a Borel injection and define
\[
    H_z(w)
    :=
    \sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}
    b(T^nz)\psi(w-n).
\]
The series and all its derivatives converge locally uniformly on
$\mathbb C$. The map
\[
    z\longmapsto H_z
\]
is Borel for the topology of locally uniform convergence, and
\[
    H_z(n)=b(T^nz),
    \qquad
    H_{Tz}(w)=H_z(w+1).
\]
For every $j\geq0$,
\[
    \left|H_z^{(j)}(x+iy)\right|
    \leq
    C_j e^{2\pi\sigma|y|}
\]
uniformly in $z\in Z$ and $x,y\in\mathbb R$. Finally,
\[
    \operatorname{supp}\widehat H_z
    \subset[-\tau,\tau]
    \qquad
    (z\in Z).
\]

body:
[Lem 168 (errors from spatial rerandomization) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $\vY$ be the spatial rerandomization of $\vX^\trunc$, defined by \eqref{e:def.Y}
with indices $(a(q_0), \ldots, a(\dmax))$ sampled according to Definition~\ref{d:rerand}. Then we have
	\begin{align*} 
	\max\bigg\{
	\Big|\Delta Y^{\sigma}(q_d)
		-\Delta X^{\trunc,\sigma}(q_d, a(q_{d+1}))\Big|
		: \sigma\in\{
		\RomI,\RomII,\RomIII
		\}
		\bigg\}
		&\le 2\eta\,,\\
	\bigg|
	\Delta Y^{\Ising}(q_d)
	-\Delta X^{\trunc,\Ising}(q_d,i(q_{d+1}))
	\bigg|
	&\le2\eta\,.
	\end{align*}
for all $0\le d\le \dmax-1$. The same holds with $(\vY^\frozen,\vX^\frozen)$ in place of $(\vY,\vX^\trunc)$.

\begin{proof}
We prove the estimate for
$Y^{\RomI}$ versus $X^{\trunc,\RomI}$; the other bounds follow by the same argument. It follows from the definition~\eqref{e:def.Y} that
	\[
	\Delta Y^{\RomI}(q_d)
	= \sum_{a\in B(q_{d+1},a(q_{d+1}))}
	\frac{X^{\trunc,\RomI}(q_{d+1},a)}{|B(q_{d+1},a(q_{d+1}))|}
	-\sum_{a\in B(q_d,a(q_d))}
	\frac{X^{\trunc,\RomI}(q_d,a)}{|B(q_d,a(q_d))|}\,.
	\]
Marginally, $a(q_d)$ is a uniformly random index from $[M]$. Conditional on $\cG(q_d)$, the index $a(q_{d+1})$ is sampled uniformly at random from  $B=B(q_d,a(q_d))$, the bucket at time $q_d$ that contains $a(q_d)$. 
It follows from the definitions of the buckets (see~\eqref{e:bucket}) that
	\begin{align*}
	\max\bigg\{ \Big|X^{\trunc,\RomI}(q_{d+1},a)
	-X^{\trunc,\RomI}(q_{d+1},a(q_{d+1}))\Big|
	: a\in B(q_{d+1},a(q_{d+1}))
	\bigg\} &\le \eta\,,\\
	\max\bigg\{ \Big|X^{\trunc,\RomI}(q_d,a)
	-X^{\trunc,\RomI}(q_d,a(q_{d+1}))\Big|
	: a\in B(q_d,a(q_{d+1}))
	\bigg\} &\le \eta\,,
	\end{align*}
where the second bound uses that
$a(q_{d+1})$ and $a(q_d)$ are in the same bucket $B$ at time $q_d$.
Since $\vY(q_d)$ is obtained by averaging $\vX^\trunc(q_d,a)$ over $a\in B$, we immediately obtain
	\[
	\max\bigg\{
	\Big|Y^{\RomI}(q_d)
	- X^{\trunc,\RomI}(q_d,a(q_d))\Big|,
	\Big|Y^{\RomI}(q_d)
	- X^{\trunc,\RomI}(q_d,a(q_{d+1}))\Big|
	\bigg\} \le\eta\,.
	\]
Likewise, since $\vY(q_{d+1})$ is obtained by averaging 
$\vX^\trunc(q_{d+1},a')$ over $a'\in B'=B(q_{d+1},a(q_{d+1}))$, we have
	\beq
	\Big|Y^{\RomI}(q_{d+1})
	- X^{\trunc,\RomI}(q_{d+1},a(q_{d+1}))\Big| \le\eta\,.
	\eeq
Combining these gives the claimed bound.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: errors from spatial rerandomization

[Lemma 49 (Two-spine continuation bound) of arXiv:2604.25877, 'Asymptotic height of Plancherel random trees'] Under the assumptions \ref{hyp_A1}, \ref{hyp_A2} and \ref{hyp_A3}, choose
    \(0<\alpha<\rho\) and 
let $w$ be a vertex at depth $r\in\{0,\dots,h-1\}$, and write
\[
m:=h-r, \qquad \ell:=L_r(w):=ar-S_r(w)\ge0.
\]
Thus, if two depth-$h$ descendants have MRCA (most recent common ancestor) equal to $w$, then each continuation from $w$
to generation $h$ has length $m$, including the split step from generation $r$ to generation $r+1$.
\medskip

For $j\in\{0,\dots,m\}$, define the translated continuation barrier event
\[
E_{m,\ell}:=
\left\{
Y^{\mathrm{cont}}_j\le \ell,\ \forall\,0\le j\le m,\ 
-\omega_n-1+\ell\le Y^{\mathrm{cont}}_m\le -\omega_n+\ell
\right\},
\]
where
\[
Y^{\mathrm{cont}}_j:=\sum_{i=1}^j (X_i-a),\qquad Y^{\mathrm{cont}}_0:=0,
\]
and $(X_i)_{i\ge1}$ denotes the descendant increment process under the spine law $\Q_t$
along a continuation issued from $w$, with the first increment corresponding to the split step
from generation $r$ to generation $r+1$.
Let
\[
q_m(\ell):=\Q_t(E_{m,\ell}\cap \mathcal G^{\mathrm{cont}}_{n,\alpha}),
\]
where \(\mathcal G^{\mathrm{cont}}_{n,\alpha}\) denotes the event that the starting mass
\(K(w)\) and all masses subsequently encountered along the continuation are at
least \(n^\alpha\).
\medskip

Then there exists a constant $C<\infty$ such that the following holds for all large $n$, uniformly
for those values of $\ell=L_r(w)$ with $\ell+\omega_n=o(\sqrt m)$ (in the application to Lemma~\ref{lem:critical_barrier_second_moment}, this estimate will only be used in the regime \(m\ge (\omega_n)^3\), so that \(\omega_n=o(\sqrt m)\) holds uniformly there):

\smallskip

\noindent{\rm (i)} One-spine continuation bound:
\begin{equation}
q_m(\ell)\le C\,\frac{(1+\ell)(1+\omega_n)}{m^{3/2}}.

\end{equation}

\smallskip

\noindent{\rm (ii)} Two-spine product bound:
let $\mathcal G_r(w)$ be the $\sigma$-field generated by $\widetilde{\mathcal F}_r$ together with the full offspring
configuration of $w$. Conditionally on $\mathcal G_r(w)$, consider two descendant spines
issued from two \emph{distinct} children of $w$, each evolved below its initial child according to the tilted spine law $\Q_t$ in the corresponding subtree. Let $E^{(1)}_{m,\ell}$ and $E^{(2)}_{m,\ell}$
be the two corresponding continuation events. Then
\begin{equation}
\Q_t\otimes \Q_t\left(
E^{(1)}_{m,\ell}\cap \mathcal G^{(1),\mathrm{cont}}_{n,\alpha},
\ 
E^{(2)}_{m,\ell}\cap \mathcal G^{(2),\mathrm{cont}}_{n,\alpha}
\ \middle|\ \mathcal G_r(w)
\right)
\le
C\,\frac{(1+\ell)^2(1+\omega_n)^2}{m^3}.

\end{equation}

body: [Definition 92 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mf A$ be an HTM and $\mu$ be an $\mf A$-valued map. Given a set $A$, we say that $\mu$ is $A$-exhaustive and write $\ex{\mf A}{A}\mu$ if $\mu(\mb A(n))\to 0$ in $\mf A$ as $n\to\infty$ whenever $\mb A\colon\N\to D_\mu$ is a disjoint family such that $\mb A(n)\subset A$ for every $n\in\N$. We call $\mu$ weakly exhaustive if $\ex{\mf A}{A}\mu$ for every $A\in D_\mu$.
title: Definition 92 of arXiv:2609.03875

body:
Let f : {-1,1}^n -> R with the uniform product measure and let Delta_i f (x) = ( f(x) - f(x^{(i)}) ) / 2, where x^{(i)} flips coordinate i. Then there is a UNIVERSAL constant C with Var(f) <= C sum_{i=1}^n || Delta_i f ||_2^2 / ( 1 + log( || Delta_i f ||_2 / || Delta_i f ||_1 ) ), with the convention that a term is 0 when Delta_i f = 0. The unimproved bound Var(f) <= sum_i ||Delta_i f||_2^2 is the Efron-Stein inequality on the cube; Talagrand's refinement gains a LOGARITHMIC factor for every coordinate whose influence is spread out, that is whose L2 and L1 norms are far apart, and gains nothing for a coordinate whose discrete derivative is essentially an indicator. This is precisely the inequality Benjamini, Kalai and Schramm apply to first-passage percolation with two-valued weights to obtain Var <= C n / log n, and the reason their theorem carries a two-point weight hypothesis is that the L1-L2 comparison must be run on that specific cube structure. The p-biased and Gaussian analogues exist with modified constants; the Gaussian version replaces the log ratio by an entropy term (Falik-Samorodnitsky). [Talagrand (1994), 'On Russo's approximate zero-one law', Ann. Probab. 22; used in Benjamini-Kalai-Schramm (2003)]
uniform product measure on the discrete cube {-1,1}^n
f real-valued and square integrable on the cube
C is a universal constant, in particular independent of n and of f

[Lemma sphere_coupling_moments of arXiv:2607.22480, 'Distinguishability threshold for random geometric graphs'] Let $t\in \mathbb R$ and $m\ge 1$ be such that $|t|<m^{1/8}$. Let $X$ be distributed as the first coordinate of a uniform point on $\mathbb{S}^{m-1}$, conditioned on being at least $t/\sqrt{m}$, and let $Y\sim \mathcal{N}(0,1/m)$ conditioned on being at least $t/\sqrt{m}$. Then
\[ \big|\mathbb{E}[X]-\mathbb{E}[Y]\big| \le O\Big(\frac{|t|^{5}+1}{m^{3/2}}\Big)\quad \text{ and }\quad \big|\mathbb{E}[X^2]-\mathbb{E}[Y^2]\big| \le O\Big(\frac{|t|^{6}+1}{m^{2}}\Big)\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma sphere_coupling_moments of arXiv:2607.22480
