body:
[Thm1 13 of arXiv:2608.29797, 'Mean-field branching SDEs: propagation of chaos, scaling limits and phase transitions'] Suppose that Condition \ref{con2} holds.
 Let $\xi_1,\xi_2,\ldots$ be i.i.d. with law $\mu_0$. Set $Z_0^{i,n,N}=\lfloor n\xi_i\rfloor$ and $X_0^{i,n,N}=\frac{Z_0^{i,n,N}}n.$
Let $Z^{n,N}$ be the chain defined by
\eqref{eq:discrete-birth-rate}--\eqref{eq:discrete-death-rate} and let
$X^{n,N}=Z^{n,N}/n$.  Then, for every fixed $T<\infty$, the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] For each fixed $N$,
\[
X^{n,N}\Rightarrow X^N\qquad\text{in }\D([0,T],\R_+^N),\qquad n\to\infty,
\]
where $X^N=(X^{1,N},\ldots,X^{N,N})$ solves \eqref{Xi} with initial state
$(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N)$.
\item[(ii)] The iterated limit satisfies
\[
\lim_{N\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{Law}(X^{1,n,N})
=\operatorname{Law}(X)
\]
weakly on $\D([0,T],\R_+)$, where $X$ solves \eqref{X} with initial law $\mu_0$.
\item[(iii)] There is a deterministic sequence $N_T(n)\to\infty$ such that
\[
X^{1,n,N_T(n)}\Rightarrow X\qquad\text{in }\D([0,T],\R_+),\qquad n\to\infty.
\]
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem eq:second-largest-in-theorem of arXiv:2607.18011, 'From local giants to locality in long-range percolation'] \thlabel{prop:second_largest}
    Let $G$ be a transitive graph of polynomial growth with $d \geq 1$, and suppose that $J : V \times V \to \mathbf{R}_+$ is a transitive kernel satisfying $J(x,y) = \Omega(d_G(x,y)^{-d \alpha})$ with $\alpha \in (0,2)$. 
    
    Let $\beta > \beta_c$.
    
    Then there exists $A=A(G,J) > 0$ such that for all $r \in \mathbf{N}$ and $k \in \mathbf{N}$
    
    \begin{equation}
        \mathbf{P}_{\beta}
        \left( 
            \# K_{r}^{\scriptscriptstyle (2)}
            > 
            k
        \right)
        \leq 
        \frac{\#B(r)}{k}
        \exp
        \left(
            -
            \beta 
            k^{\min(2-\alpha,1)}/A
        \right).
    \end{equation} 
    In particular, $ \# K_{r}^{\scriptscriptstyle (2)}=O_{\mathbf{P}}((\log r)^{\max(1, 1/(2-\alpha))})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Uniqueness of the giant

[Prop cocycles into Aut(N) reduce to lattice stabiliser, baby case of arXiv:2605.16921, '${\ASL_n}(\mathbb Z)$ invariant random subsets of $\mathbb Z^n$'] Let $N$ be a nilpotent Lie group of the form $\mathbb{Z}^d \ltimes N_0$ with $d \geq 3$ and $N_0$ connected simply connected, and let $\Gamma \subset N$ be a lattice. Let $\Delta \subset \Aut(N)$ be a subgroup such that $\delta(\Gamma)$ is commensurable with $\Gamma$ for every $\delta \in \Delta$. Let $(X, \nu)$ be an ergodic $\SL_d(\mathbb{Z})$-system and $\alpha: \SL_d(\mathbb{Z}) \times X \to \Delta$ a cocycle.

    Then there exist a finite group extension $\pi: \tilde{X} \to X$ and a lattice $\Gamma' \subset N$ such that the lifted cocycle $\tilde{\alpha} := \alpha \circ (\id \times \pi)$ is cohomologous in $\Delta$ to a cocycle taking values in $\{\delta \in \Delta : \delta(\Gamma') = \Gamma'\}$.

[Theorem thm:limitTheorems of arXiv:2609.03094, 'Discrete Gromov--Wasserstein Duality: Algorithms and Isomorphism Testing'] Fix $(\mu_0,\mu_1)\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X_0)\times\mathcal P(\mathcal X_1)$ with full support. If the sequence $(\mu_{0,n},\mu_{1,n})_{n\in\mathbb N}\subset \mathcal P(\mathcal X_0)\times  \mathcal P(\mathcal X_1)$ is such that   
    $\sqrt n ( (w_{\mu_{0,n}},w_{\mu_{1,n}})-(w_{ \mu_{0}},w_{ \mu_{1}}))\stackrel{d}{\to}(G_{\mu_0},G_{\mu_1})$, 
    \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*]
        \item   
        $\sqrt n\left({\mathsf{GW}_p(\mu_{0,n},\mu_{1,n})^p- \mathsf{GW}_p(\mu_{0},\mu_{1})^p}\right)
     \stackrel{d}{\to}  \inf_{\pi^{\star}\in\Pi^{\star}(\mu_0,\mu_1)}\sup_{(\varphi_0,\varphi_1)\in\mathcal D_{\pi^{\star}}}\left\{v_{ \varphi_0}^{\intercal}G_{\mu_0}+v_{ \varphi_1}^{\intercal}G_{\mu_1}\right\}$, where $\Pi^{\star}(\mu_0,\mu_1)$ is the set of optimal plans for $\mathsf{GW}_p(\mu_{0},\mu_{1})$ and $\mathcal D_{\pi^{\star}}$ is the set of OT potentials for $\mathsf{OT}_{c_{\pi^{\star}}}(\mu_0,\mu_1)$ for $c_{\pi^{\star}}(x,y)=2\int \Delta(x,y,x',y')d\pi^{\star}(x',y')$.    
    \item If $\varepsilon >0 $, 
   $     \sqrt n\left({\mathsf{EGW}^{\varepsilon}_p(\mu_{0,n},\mu_{1,n})- \mathsf{EGW}_p^{\varepsilon}(\mu_{0},\mu_{1})}\right)
     \stackrel{d}{\to}  \inf_{\pi^{\star}\in\Pi^{\star}(\mu_0,\mu_1)}\left\{v_{ \varphi_0^{\pi^{\star}}}^{\intercal}G_{\mu_0}+v_{ \varphi_1^{\pi^{\star}}}^{\intercal}G_{\mu_1}\right\},
   $ 
    where $\Pi^{\star}(\mu_0,\mu_1)$ is the set of optimal plans for $\mathsf{EGW}_p^{\varepsilon}(\mu_{0},\mu_{1})$ and $(\varphi_0^{\pi^{\star}},\varphi_1^{\pi^{\star}})$ is the unique (up to constants) pair of EOT potentials for $\mathsf{EOT}^{\varepsilon}_{c_{\pi^{\star}}}(\mu_0,\mu_1)$
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Limit theorems

[Lemma 13 (Offspring tail bounds, Lemmas $5.3$ and $5.4$ in~\cite{HeyLod25}) of arXiv:2505.06187, 'Preferential Attachment Trees with Vertex Death: Persistence of the Maximum Degree'] Let $D$ be as in~\eqref{eq:D}. Then,
		\be 
		\P{D\geq k}\leq \e^{-\rho_1(k)-\frac12 \rho_2(k)}. 
		\ee 
		In particular, $\P{D=\infty}=0$ if and only if Assumption~\eqref{ass:A2} is satisfied. Furthermore, assume that $b$ and $d$ are such that Assumption~\eqref{ass:A2} is satisfied. When $\rho_2$ diverges and $d=o(b)$, 
		\be 
		\P{D\geq k}=\e^{-\rho_1(k)-(\frac12+o(1))\rho_2(k)}.
		\ee 
		If, instead, $\lim_{k\to\infty}\rho_2(k)$ exists, 
		\be 
		\P{D\geq k}=\e^{-\rho_1(k) -\cO(1)}.
		\ee (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Offspring tail bounds, Lemmas $5.3$ and $5.4$ in~\cite{HeyLod25}

[Definition def:susy-state of arXiv:2607.29330, 'Large deviations for the maximum of\\ the generalized TAP free energy'] Fix a regular \(f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)\), write \(\theta=\theta_f\) and
		\(\zeta=\zeta_f\), and let \(q\) be the first positive contact point of
		\(\zeta\). Let \(X\) be the Auffinger--Chen process associated with
		\(\zeta\).
		
		For \(\varepsilon>0\), an \(\varepsilon\)-SUSY state at level \(f\) is a
		critical point \(\mathbf{m}\in(-1,1)^N\) of \(F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}\) satisfying
		\[
		|q_\mathbf{m}-q|\le\varepsilon,
		\qquad
		\left|\frac1N F_{\mathrm{TAP},\zeta}(\mathbf{m})-f\right|\le\varepsilon,
		\qquad
		\left|\frac1N F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(\mathbf{m})-f\right|\le\varepsilon.
		\]
		Define \(b_i\) by
		\[
		m_i=\partial_x\Phi_\zeta(q,b_i),
		\qquad 1\le i\le N,
		\]
		and require
		\[
		W_2\left(
		\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{b_i},
		\mathrm{Law}(X_q)
		\right)\le\varepsilon.
		\]
		Let \(\mathsf N_\varepsilon\) denote the number of
		\(\varepsilon\)-SUSY states at level \(f\).
title: SUSY states

[Lem 4 of arXiv:2606.27078, 'Semimartingale Optimal Transport with Jumps: A General Framework and Equivalent Formulatio'] Let $\Theta \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{S}_+^d \times \mathcal{L}$ be closed, convex and satisfy Assumptions~\ref{B} and~\ref{J}, and let $\Gamma_0,\,\Gamma_1\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ be compact. Moreover, let the cost function $L$ satisfy Assumption~\ref{L}. Then the following statements hold true:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(1)] The set $\overline{\mathfrak{P}}_{\Theta}(\Gamma_0, \Gamma_1):=\{\overline{\mathbb{P}}\in\overline{\mathfrak{P}}_{\Theta}\mid \overline{\mathbb{P}}\circ \overline{X}_{0}^{-1}\in\Gamma_0,\,\overline{\mathbb{P}}\circ \overline{X}_{1}^{-1}\in\Gamma_1\}$ is a compact convex set under the weak convergence topology.
\item[(2)] For any $\mu_0,\mu_1\in\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and any $\mathbb{P}\in{\mathfrak{P}}_{\Theta}(\mu_0, \mu_1)$, we can construct $\overline{\mathbb{P}}:=
\mathbb{P}\circ(\Psi^{\mathbb{P}})^{-1}\in\overline{\mathfrak{P}}_{\Theta}(\mu_0,\mu_1)$ such that $J(\mathbb{P})=\overline{J}(\overline{\mathbb{P}})$.
\item[(3)] Conversely, for any $\mu_0,\mu_1\in\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and any $\overline{\mathbb{P}}\in\overline{\mathfrak{P}}_{\Theta}(\mu_0, \mu_1)$, we can construct $\mathbb{P}:=
\overline{\mathbb{P}}\circ\overline{X}^{-1}\in{\mathfrak{P}}_{\Theta}(\mu_0, \mu_1)$ such that $J(\mathbb{P})\le \overline{J}(\overline{\mathbb{P}})$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 4 of arXiv:2606.27078

[Thm 62 of arXiv:2609.02561, 'NON-NEF LOCI IN MIXED CHARACTERISTIC'] Let $S$ be a Dedekind scheme of characteristic zero, and let $f:X \rightarrow S$ be a projective surjective morphism from a normal integral scheme.
Suppose that every non-closed point $x\in X$ satisfies one of the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $(x\in X)$ is of equal characteristic zero and of klt type.
\item $(x\in X)$ is of mixed characteristic and of BCM-regular type.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[ \NNef(D/S)=\Bm(D/S) \]
for every $\R$-Cartier $\R$-divisor $D$ on $X$.

[Corollary 10 of arXiv:2608.26618, 'A Unified Descriptive-Complexity Framework for Model Selection under Correlated Designs'] Consider the multi-class selection setting in
Section~\ref{sub:example_family}
with \(\eta_n=\log n\).
Assume there exists a unique true pair \((m^*,S^*)\in\widetilde{\mathcal M}_n\), and $g^* \leq p^\gamma$ for $0<\gamma<1$.
Assume that the following conditions hold:

\noindent
(\romannumeral 1) There exists an absolute constant $K_{\max}$ such that
$K \le K_{\max}$ for every candidate in the ordered families and
$|I_j| \le K_{\max}$ for every $j \in G$ in each Haar candidate.

\noindent
(\romannumeral 2) There exists a sufficiently large constant \(c_1>0\) such that, for every
\((m,S)\in\widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathrm{sub}}\),
\[
\mathrm{APP}(m,S)\ge c_1\bigl(s^*-s_{(m,S)}\bigr)(\log n+\lambda\log p);
\]

\noindent
(\romannumeral 3) There exist sufficiently large constants $\kappa>0$ and
$c_2>1$ such that, for every
\((m,S)\in\widetilde{\mathcal M}_{\mathrm{w}}\) with
$
s_{(m,S)}\le (1+\kappa)s^*,
$
we have
\[
\mathrm{APP}(m,S)\ge
c_2\Bigl\{
\bigl(s^*-s_{(m,S)}\bigr)_+\log n+\lambda s^*\log p+\log\log n
\Bigr\}.
\]
Then there exists a constant \(\lambda_{\rm basis}\), depending on \(\zeta\) and \(\gamma\), such that, for every \(\lambda\ge\lambda_{\rm basis}\), 
\[
\Pr\bigl\{(\hat m,\hat S)=(m^*,S^*)\bigr\}\to 1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 10 of arXiv:2608.26618

OWNER RESULT DRAFT: proof (unaudited), T336-w727-C016 v1, no novelty claim. For d>=1,n>=0,ell,s,epsilon>0, a zero-mean Gaussian process with unit-diagonal Gaussian kernel exp(-||x-z||^2/(2ell^2)) on [0,1]^d and independent N(0,s) observation noises, take iid tasks with fresh GP/noises, <=n context labels and a noisy query, with joint input design and context length independent of GP/noises. Within-task independence is not required. Let W be the FULL original context and query location, and P_W its exact noisy posterior. C016 specifies finite raw-input normalized-ReLU-attention-plus-residual-MLP dimensions D,H,L, parameter count P=L(15D^2+2DH)+2D, entrywise radius W_max=(n+1)max(4,s,2/s,1/ell), clipped-label input bound K0=max(1,B,s), output mean clip [-U,U] and variance clip [s,1+2s], all independent of training data. For eps_c=epsilon/4, V=s+1, C_tail=2sqrt(2)n^2 V/s^3 and B=sqrt(4V log(max(e,2C_tail/epsilon))), the C013/C015 comparator belongs to this class and has original-task expected forward KL <=epsilon. The finite-Gram ridge coefficient bound |a_i|<=1/s extends context-clipping control to the full kernel without a supplied-feature oracle. For any m>=1, confidence alpha in (0,1), gamma>0 and measurable xi-approximate empirical minimizer xi>=0 of Gaussian log loss on this fixed bounded class, with probability >=1-alpha, E_fresh W KL(P_W||h_theta_hat(c_B(W)))<=epsilon+2E_m+xi. E_m, the C014 cover recurrence and every size/tail constant are explicitly given in the attached proof; only the predictor encoding clips context, not the target posterior or task law. For fixed approximation parameters and alpha, gamma=1/m gives E_m=O(sqrt(log(m)/m)+log(m)/m). Statistical C007 and approximation/cover C013-C015 dependencies remain unaudited. This is an approximate-global-ERM statistical theorem, not efficient optimization, SGD, latent noiseless prediction, adaptive input selection, finite precision or softmax attention.

Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty, efficient-training or independent-audit claim.

## 1. Task law and theorem
Fix d>=1, n>=0, ell,s,epsilon>0. On X=[0,1]^d let f be a zero-mean GP with kernel k(x,z)=exp(-||x-z||^2/(2 ell^2)). Observations are f(x) plus independent N(0,s) noises. Each task consists of at most n context observations and one fresh noisy query. The joint law of context length and all input locations is independent of f and the noises. Within-task locations and labels need not be independent. Tasks are iid with fresh GP/noise draws. There is no label-based rejection or input selection. Let W denote the FULL, unclipped context, its locations and the query location; P_W denotes the exact noisy query posterior given W.

For m>=1 training tasks, confidence alpha in (0,1), output cover tolerance gamma>0 and empirical optimization error xi>=0, define the explicit architecture and constants below. Let theta_hat be any measurable xi-approximate empirical minimizer over that bounded parameter cube for the displayed Gaussian loss. With probability at least 1-alpha over the training tasks,

    E_fresh W KL(P_W || h_theta_hat(c_B(W))) <= epsilon + 2 E_m + xi.    (1)

The expectation is over a fresh ORIGINAL task, conditional on training. Only the predictor's encoding uses clipped context labels. Its input is raw coordinates, clipped labels and fixed flags/constants, with no supplied kernel-feature oracle. The deterministic approximation and cover lemmas invoked below, and this composition, remain unaudited. In particular (1) is not an additional independently checked MOVE.

## 2. Completely specified architecture and class
Put V=s+1 and

    C_tail=2 sqrt(2) n^2 V/s^3,
    eps_c=epsilon/4,
    B=sqrt(4 V log(max(e,2 C_tail/epsilon))).

Use C013 v1 with tolerance eps_c and this B. For convenience its explicit size recipe is restated, without re-proving that saved construction:

    b_mu=sqrt(s eps_c), b_v=min(s/2,s sqrt(eps_c)),
    C_mu=nB/s+n^2 B/s^2, C_v=1+2n/s+n^2/s^2,
    tau=min(1/2,b_mu/[3(1+C_mu)],b_v/[3C_v]),
    a=d/ell^2, t=ceil(max(1,2e a,log(1/tau)/log(2))),
    p=binomial(d+t-1,d),
    E_mu=nB(3/s+6n/s^2), E_v=3+12n/s,
    rho=min(1,b_mu/[3(1+E_mu)],b_v/[3E_v]),
    g=max(1,ceil(d sqrt(p)/(ell rho))), J=(g+1)^d,
    eps0=min(eps_c/9,1/36), kappa=1+4max(1,n)/s, M=4nB/s,
    delta0=min(1/2,s/8,sqrt(s eps0)/(1+M),s sqrt(eps0)/4),
    T_c=ceil(sqrt(kappa) log(2/delta0)/2),
    N=n+1, D=7p+6+d+Jd+pJ,
    H=2Jd+pJ+4p+1, L=T_c+5+ceil(log(J)/log(2)).

The class has L attention-then-residual-MLP layers, five normalized ReLU attention heads per layer (zero padding unused heads), token width D, MLP hidden width H, and a two-output linear readout on the query token. All layer and readout matrix entries range over [-W_max,W_max], where C015 v1 supplies

    W_max=N max(4,s,2/s,1/ell), K0=max(1,B,s),
    P=L(15D^2+2DH)+2D.

The fixed, parameter-independent input placement has bound K0; encoder coefficients are counted as trainable parameters. The exact clipping map c_B clips each observed context label to [-B,B]. Fixed output clips impose

    mu_theta in [-U,U], U=nB/s+sqrt(s eps_c)+1,
    v_theta in [v0,v1], v0=s, v1=1+2s.

C015 proves those clips leave the C013 comparator unchanged. No general monotonicity of Gaussian KL under variance clipping is required. Fixed label/output clips and affine input placement are excluded from the trainable count, as in C004/C013.

## 3. Explicit cover and statistical constants
Use the saved C014 recurrence, starting K_0=K0,F_0=0:

    Kbar_j=K_j+5D^4 W_max^3 K_j^3,
    Fbar_j=(1+15D^4 W_max^3 K_j^2)F_j+15D^4 W_max^2 K_j^3,
    K_(j+1)=(1+HD W_max^2)Kbar_j,
    F_(j+1)=(1+HD W_max^2)Fbar_j+2HD W_max Kbar_j,
    Lambda=D W_max F_L+D K_L.

Here F is the sensitivity recurrence, renamed to avoid confusion with E_m. Set

    q=max(1,ceil(2W_max Lambda/gamma)), J_cover=(q+1)^P,
    C=0.5 log(v1/v0)+U^2/v0, A=V/v0, K_loss=4(C+A),
    u=log(4 J_cover/alpha), t_query=log(4m/alpha),
    T_query=sqrt(2V t_query),
    Q=1/(2v0)+(U+sqrt(V))/v0+(U^2+V)/v0^2,
    L_query=1/(2v0)+(T_query+U)/v0+(T_query+U)^2/(2v0^2),
    beta=4sqrt(2) K_loss sqrt(u/m)+2K_loss u/m,
    E_m=beta+gamma(Q+L_query).                              (2)

These are finite explicit real constants, not an efficient numerical prescription. One may evaluate u using P log(q+1), without materializing an enormous cover. For fixed approximation parameters and alpha, taking gamma=1/m gives E_m=O(sqrt(log(m)/m)+log(m)/m) as m tends to infinity (m>=2). Constants depend on d,n,ell,s,epsilon and alpha through the displayed formulas. This rate describes estimation above the fixed approximation error epsilon; it does not assert efficient dependence on dimension or on epsilon.

Use normalized Gaussian log loss

    loss_theta(W,Y)=0.5 log(v_theta/v0)+(Y-mu_theta)^2/(2v_theta).

An xi-approximate empirical minimizer has empirical risk at most infimum empirical risk plus xi. No algorithm for finding it is asserted.

## 4. New bridge: clipping bias for the full Gaussian kernel
We extend the saved C007 finite-feature clipping argument to the non-finite-rank kernel, rather than asserting that an infinite-dimensional feature input was supplied.

Fix a deterministic context of length l<=n and its query. Their (l+1)-point real positive-semidefinite Gram matrix admits a finite Gram realization by vectors z_1,...,z_l,z_* in R^(l+1). Each vector has norm one because the kernel diagonal is one. Let F have rows z_i^T, let K_ctx=F F^T, and set A_ctx=sI+F^T F. Both ridge matrices are positive definite. The identity

    A_ctx F^T = F^T(sI+K_ctx)

implies F^T(sI+K_ctx)^(-1)=A_ctx^(-1)F^T. Therefore the coefficient a_i of y_i in the exact posterior mean satisfies

    a_i=z_*^T A_ctx^(-1) z_i,   |a_i|<=1/s.              (3)

The last inequality uses ||A_ctx^(-1)||_op<=1/s and unit vector norms. This is a pointwise finite-matrix argument for each design; a globally selected Gram factor is not needed as a measurable input to the predictor.

Let mu and mu_B be the exact-kernel posterior formulas evaluated at full and clipped labels respectively. The computed variance v is identical for the two formulas. N(mu_B,v) is an auxiliary Gaussian, NOT the conditional law given clipped labels. For r_i=y_i-c_B(y_i), Cauchy-Schwarz and (3) give

    |mu-mu_B|^2 <= (l/s^2) sum_i r_i^2.

Conditional on the input design, each y_i is centered Gaussian with variance at most V (in fact V for this kernel). For G of variance tau<=V the elementary square-mgf identity gives

    E[G^2 exp(G^2/(4V))]=tau(1-tau/(2V))^(-3/2)<=2sqrt(2)V.

Since r_i^2<=y_i^2 1{|y_i|>B}, multiplication by the indicator and the positive exponential yields

    E|mu-mu_B|^2 <= 2sqrt(2) n^2 V/s^2 exp(-B^2/(4V)).  (4)

This uses a sum of marginal expectations, not independence of correlated context labels. The Gaussian square-mgf needs tau<=V and the argument 1/(4V)<1/(2tau); it is available from the exogenous Gaussian task law, not from a mere second-moment bound.

C013 at eps_c gives a raw-input comparator h_B=N(muhat,vhat) with vhat>=s and KL(N(mu_B,v)||h_B)<=eps_c for every clipped context. C015 places it in the bounded class and preserves it through the fixed output clips.

Writing d_v=0.5(log(vhat/v)+v/vhat-1)>=0, the scalar inequality (a+b)^2<=2a^2+2b^2 gives

    KL(P_W||h_B)
      <= 2 KL(N(mu_B,v)||h_B)+(mu-mu_B)^2/s.

The direction uses vhat>=s and nonnegativity of d_v. By (4),

    E_W KL(P_W||h_B) <= 2eps_c+C_tail exp(-B^2/(4V)) <= epsilon. (5)

If C_tail=0 the tail term vanishes; otherwise the definition of B gives exp(-B^2/(4V))<=epsilon/(2C_tail). Empty contexts are included. All expectations in (4)-(5) retain the original task law.

## 5. Apply the saved concentration result with the new cover
C007 Section 3 is a uniform concentration statement whose predictor dependence enters only through bounded output intervals and a fixed gamma-cover. Its attention-only cover is replaced here by C014, not used for an architecture containing uncounted MLPs. C015 supplies the comparator radius and intervals. The query marginal conditional on exogenous design is centered Gaussian with variance <=V even though its conditional mean given W need not be bounded.

For clarity the hypotheses and directions of the invoked tail argument are explicit. The pointwise loss envelope is 0<=loss<=C+Y^2/v0. Its finite exponential moment satisfies E exp(loss/K_loss)<2; no independence of Y and the predictor is used. C007's moment expansion gives, for |z|<1/(2K_loss),

    log E exp(z(loss-E loss)) <= 8K_loss^2 z^2/(1-2K_loss|z|).

IID tasks allow multiplication of their mgfs. The Chernoff exponential-Markov argument then gives two-sided tail at most 2exp(-u) at threshold beta in (2). This is an exponential-moment argument, not Chebyshev's second-moment inequality. Union over the fixed J_cover predictors costs alpha/2. The Gaussian marginal query bound 2exp(-T_query^2/(2V)), unioned over m tasks, costs alpha/2. No within-task independence is used.

The loss derivatives on the output rectangle give the output-distance bound gamma L(Y), where

    L(Y)=1/(2v0)+(|Y|+U)/v0+(|Y|+U)^2/(2v0^2).

C007 proves E L(Y)<=Q from E|Y|<=sqrt(V), EY^2<=V and (|Y|+U)^2<=2Y^2+2U^2. On the query-tail event L(Y_i)<=L_query. The fixed cover therefore yields, with probability >=1-alpha,

    sup_theta |R(theta)-Rhat(theta)| <= E_m.

This is precisely the saved statistical lemma applied to the correct architecture and original task law; it is not a fresh independent audit of C007. An empirical xi-minimizer then obeys R(theta_hat)<=inf_theta R(theta)+2E_m+xi.

Finally, conditional Gaussian entropy is integrable because s<=v(W)<=V. For every fixed predictor,

    R(theta)=E_W KL(P_W||h_theta(c_B(W)))
                  +0.5 E_W log(v(W)/s)+0.5.

Subtract the same finite constant from the risk comparison and insert (5). This proves (1), including data-dependent theta_hat on the uniform event.

## 6. Sources, status and limitation
Dependencies: C007 Sections 1 and 3-4 (saved original-task loss concentration and clipping template); C013 (raw-coordinate Gaussian-kernel approximation); C014 (trainable attention-plus-MLP cover); C015 (explicit coefficient and output bounds). Accepted C002/C004 are not re-audited. C013 uses the Taylor feature facts in Cotter, Keshet and Srebro, arXiv:1109.4603v1, Section 3 equations (6)-(11), PDF pages 4-5; those facts are known, not new here. Bai et al., arXiv:2306.04637v2, Section 5.1 Theorem 20, PDF pages 14-15, is the related square-loss ERM framework, not a cited Gaussian-log-loss theorem. The main new composition step here is (3)-(5) for the full raw-input kernel and the fully specified bounded hypothesis class.

No novelty is claimed. Independent review is required for C007 and C013-C016. This is noisy predictive forward KL averaged over the prior and original exogenous task law. It is not a guarantee for latent noiseless prediction, adaptive data acquisition, SGD convergence, finite precision, causal/softmax attention, or a practical architecture size.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:771b7b618cfcbfb038543863f534f27b901b7a1e9265fa3d9be740e1dcdf6f02","revision_digest":"sha256:1cd1bf37aa08246ca2f0b2197064d7f12d41ccb7274dce3101743c2fc91a262f","source_id":"owner:T336-w727-C016-v1","source_revision":"T336-w727-C016-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

\[
  \ldc(G)=
  \begin{cases}
    3, & \text{if } \ell_k=1,\\[2pt]

    \bigl\lfloor \ell_3/2\bigr\rfloor+2, & \text{if } k=3 \text{ and } \ell_1\ge2,\\[2pt]
    \bigl\lceil \ell_k/2\bigr\rceil+2, & \text{if } k\ge4,\ \ell_1=1

body:
If a set S of natural numbers contains 0 (or 1) and contains n+1 whenever it contains n, then S is all of N. Equivalently (strong induction) if S contains n whenever it contains all m < n, then S = N. Both are equivalent to the well-ordering principle (every nonempty subset of N has a least element).

[Proposition 7 (A law-weighted Brownian error with sublinear spatial growth) of arXiv:2608.17540, 'Pathwise stability for one-dimensional SDEs driven by Brownian motion and a symmetric stab'] Let $\wt\eta\in(1/\alpha,1)$, $0<\lambda<1$, $\kappa\ne0$, and let $0<\theta<\alpha/2$. Put
\[
  \phi_\theta(x):=(1+x^2)^{\theta/2},\qquad x\in\R,
\]
and let $r\in L^2(0,T)$ be deterministic. Consider
\[
  b(t,x)=\wt b(t,x)\equiv0,
  \qquad
  a(t,x)\equiv\kappa,
  \qquad
  \wt a(t,x)=\kappa+r(t)\phi_\theta(x),
\]
and
\[
  \sigma(t,x)=\wt\sigma(t,x)=1+\lambda\bigl(|x|^{\wt\eta}\wedge1\bigr).
\]
Then the stable coefficient is bounded, bounded away from zero, and H\"older while failing to be Lipschitz at the origin. The perturbed Brownian coefficient is spatially Lipschitz. For any coupled solution pair satisfying Assumption~\ref{ass:solutions},
\[
  B=0,
  \qquad
  A^2=\int_0^T |r(t)|^2\,\E \phi_\theta(X_t)^2\dd t,
  \qquad
  S=0.
\]
Moreover, $A<\infty$ and
\[
  A^2\le C_{\theta,T}\|r\|_{L^2(0,T)}^2,
\]
where $C_{\theta,T}$ depends on the baseline moment $\sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t|^{2\theta}$, which is finite by Proposition~\ref{prop:baseline-moments}. Consequently, for every $R>0$ there exists $C_R>0$ such that, whenever $\|r\|_{L^2(0,T)}\le R$, $x_0=\wt x_0$, and $A<1$ (for instance, for sufficiently small $\|r\|_{L^2(0,T)}$),
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^{\alpha-1}
  \le C_R\|r\|_{L^2(0,T)}^{\frac{2(\alpha\wt\eta-1)}{\alpha\wt\eta-\alpha+2}}.
\]

body: In mathematics, and in particular linear algebra, the Moore–Penrose inverse ⁠⁠ of a matrix ⁠⁠, often called the pseudoinverse, is the most widely known generalization of the inverse matrix. It was independently described by E. H. Moore in 1920, Arne Bjerhammar in 1951, and Roger Penrose in 1955. Earlier, Erik Ivar Fredholm had introduced the concept of a pseudoinverse of integral operators in 1903. The terms pseudoinverse and generalized inverse are sometimes used as synonyms for the Moore–Penrose inverse of a matrix, but sometimes applied to other elements of algebraic structures which share some but not all properties expected for an inverse element.
title: Moore–Penrose inverse

[Theorem Nkq>1 of arXiv:2509.24452, 'A family of non-uniform distributions on the set of parking functions generated by random '] Consider $N^{(n)}_k$ as in (equation Nk of the paper)  under the measure $\mathcal{P}_n^{(q)}$ with $q>1$.

\noindent i. For $k$ fixed, $N^{(n)}_k$ converges in distribution  to the distribution of
$\sum_{j=k}^\infty Z_{j;k}$, where $\{Z_{j;k}\}_{j=k}^\infty$ are independent random variables and $Z_{j;k}$ has the Bernoulli distribution with parameter $\frac{(q-1)q^{k-1}}{q^j-1}$.
The distribution is supported on $\mathbb{Z}^+$;
\

\noindent ii. For $\{k_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ satisfying $\lim_{n\to\infty} k_n=\infty$ and $\lim_{n\to\infty}(n-k_n)=\infty$, $N^{(n)}_{k_n}$ converges in distribution to the distribution of
$\sum_{i=0}^\infty Y_i$, where $\{Y_i\}_{i=0}^\infty$ are independent and $Y_i$ has the
Bernoulli distribution with parameter $\frac{q-1}{q^{i+1}}$. The distribution is supported on $\mathbb{Z}^+$;
\

\noindent iii. For $k$ fixed, $N^{(n)}_{n-k}$ converges in distribution to the distribution of $\sum_{i=0}^k Y_i$. The distribution is supported on $\{0,1,\cdots, k+1\}$.
\

\noindent iv. $\sum_{i=0}^\infty Y_i\stackrel{\text{dist}}{=}\lim_{k\to\infty}\sum_{i=0}^kY_i\stackrel{\text{dist}}{=}\lim_{k\to\infty}\sum_{j=k}^\infty Z_{j;k}$.
Thus,
$$
\lim_{k\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}N^{(n)}_{n-k}\stackrel{\text{dist}}{=}\lim_{k\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}N^{(n)}_k=\sum_{i=0}^\infty Y_i.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Lemma lem:det_lemma of arXiv:2510.06891, 'Multivariate CLT for L\'evy processes: convergence rates without moment assumptions'] Let $\bm{M}(t)$ be a $d \times d$ positive definite matrix (i.e. with strictly positive eigenvalues), such that $\bm{M}(t) \to \bm{I}_d$ as $t\to\infty$. Let $\bm{M}(s,t)\coloneqq s\bm{I}_d +(1-s)\bm{M}(t)$ and $D_t(s)\coloneqq\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} s}[\det(\bm{M}(s,t))^{-1}]$ for $s \in [0,1]$ (with the derivatives at $s\in\{0,1\}$ being one-sided) and $t \geqslant 1$. Then, for every $t\geqslant 1$, the function $s\mapsto D_t(s)$ is well-defined, continuous and finite on $[0,1]$. Moreover, $\det(\bm{M}(s,t))\sim 1$ and $D_t(s) \sim -\mathrm{tr}(\bm{I}_d-\bm{M}(t))$ uniformly in $s\in [0,1]$ as $t \to \infty$.

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2607.04012, 'Hölder regularity for backward stochastic Volterra integral equations and applications to '] Suppose that $\Psi^\pi \in L^{p}\big(\Omega; L^2(0,T) \big)$, that $G^{\pi,0} \in \mathcal{H}_{\Delta}^{p}(0,T)$, and that $G^\pi$ is uniformly Lipschitz in $(y,z)$, with Lipschitz constant $[G^\pi]_{L}$. Then the BSDE system \eqref{def:BSDE-app-BSVIE} admits a unique solution $(Y^\pi, Z^\pi )$ with
    \begin{gather*}
         \big(Y^\pi(t_k, \cdot), Z^\pi(t_k, \cdot) \big) \in \mathcal{H}^{p}(t_k,T) \times \mathcal{H}^p(t_k, T)
    \end{gather*}
    for each $k\in\{0,\dots,N-1\}$. Moreover, there exists a constant $C>0$, depending only on $p$, $T$ and $[G^\pi]_L$, such that 
    \begin{flalign*}
       \mathbb{E}\Bigg[ 
        \sup_{s\in[0,T]}
        \bigg(
        \sum_{k:t_k\leq s}
        \Delta_k &
        |Y^\pi(t_k,s)|^2
        \bigg)^{\frac p2} + 
        \bigg(  
        \int_{0}^{T}
        |Y^\pi(\tau(r),r)|^2\,dr
        \bigg)^{\frac p2}
         \\ &+
        \bigg(
        \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} \Delta_k
        \int_{t_{k+1}}^T
        |Z^\pi(t_k,s)|^2\,ds 
        \bigg)^{\frac p2}
        \Bigg]
        \leq
        C\bigg(
        \norm{\Psi^\pi}_{2,p}^p
        +
  \norm{G^{\pi,0}}_{\mathcal{H}_{\Delta}^p}^{p}

[Proposition 9 of arXiv:2609.03951, 'Generalized Semi-Riemannian Submersions and Foliations'] Let $U$ be an irrotational observer field in a spacetime, and $\mathcal{F}$ be a regular foliation such that $\mathcal{V}^{\mathcal{F}}\cap U^{\perp}$ is an integrable regular distribution. Then $\mathcal{F}$ is $U$-stationary if and only if the distribution
\[
(\mathcal{V}^{\mathcal{F}}\cap U^{\perp}) \;\oplus\; \mathrm{span}\{U\}
\]
is integrable.

body:
[Definition 22 (Admissible stage start) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Fix a torus structure and constants \(\Lambda,\eta,\theta>0\).  We call the
pair \((q_0,r_0)\), where \(r_0=\overline{q_0}\), an \emph{admissible stage
start with constants \(\Lambda,\eta,\theta\)} if \(r_0\) is Riemannian and
\begin{equation}
 \BG_N(r_0;\Lambda),\qquad
 \|q_0-r_0\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,r_0)}<\eta,\qquad
 d_{\TT^2}(r_0)<\theta.
\end{equation}
The Riemannian condition and the first two displayed conditions are the
\emph{analytic start conditions}; the last displayed condition is the
\emph{geometric start condition}.  Stage preparation and positive-time
smoothing reproduce bounded geometry and control the endpoint error;
finite-time decay and averaging contract that error, while fibration comparison
reproduces the geometric condition.  No quotient-length condition is part of
an admissible stage start; the required lower bound is reconstructed from the
large-diameter hypothesis inside each block.
title: Admissible stage start

REFUTED ROUTE, author-checked and pending w425: the proposed inference from uniformly bounded conditional pivotal moments at p_c to bounded pivotal cost on one fixed interval below p_c is false on general locally finite graphs. Even all conditional exponential moments at the endpoint and uniqueness of the infinite critical cluster do not suffice. The explicit chain of parallel-path blocks provides the obstruction. Whether Z^d geometry supplies the missing interval estimate is not settled by this refutation.

Let a<b and let f:[a,b]->R be continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b). Then there is c in (a,b) with f'(c)=(f(b)-f(a))/(b-a). In particular if f(a)=f(b), some c has f'(c)=0 (Rolle's theorem). For a continuous f:[a,b]->V into a real or complex normed vector space, differentiable on (a,b) in norm, a single-point vector equality need not hold; however ||f(b)-f(a)|| <= (b-a) sup_{x in (a,b)}||f'(x)|| whenever the supremum is finite (and the estimate is vacuous if it is infinite). Complex-valued functions use the usual complex modulus as norm.

body:
[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2606.17381, 'Large deviation principle for friendship-biases\\ in Galton--Watson trees'] {\bf [LDP for type fractions along a random path]}

Under the joint law of the Galton--Watson tree $\mathcal{T}_\infty$ and the random exploration path, the family of random variables $\{\Upsilon_j\}_{j\in\N_4}$ satisfies the LDP in the Polish space $(0,\infty) \times \mathcal{S}_2$ with rate $j$ and with good rate function $J$ given by
\[
J(x,s) = \inf_{\nu \in \Phi(x,s)} I(\nu), \qquad x \in (0,\infty),\, s \in \mathcal{S}_2.
\]
Here,
\begin{itemize}
\item 
$I\colon\,\mathcal{P}(E) \to [0,\infty]$ is the good rate function given by
\[
I(\nu) =
\begin{cases}
H\left(\nu\,\middle\|\, \pi_{1,2}\nu \otimes \zeta^{\otimes 2}\right), & \text{if } \pi_{1,2}\nu=\pi_{2,3}\nu,\\[1ex]
\infty, & \text{otherwise,}
\end{cases}
\]
where $H(\cdot\, \|\, \cdot)$ denotes relative entropy and $\pi_{1,2}$, $\pi_{2,3}$ denote the projection onto the first two, respectively, the last two of the three coordinates.
\item
The constraint on $\nu$ is to the subset of $\mathcal{P}(E)$ given by
\[
\Phi(x,s) = \big\{\nu \in \mathcal{P}(E)\colon\,\|G(\nu)\|_1 = x,\,G(\nu)/\|G(\nu)\|_1 = s\big\},
\qquad x \in (0,\infty),\,s \in \mathcal{S}_2,
\]
where $G = (G^\chi)_{\chi \in S}$ with $G^\chi\colon\,\mathcal{P}(E) \to [0,\infty]$ is given by
\[
G^\chi(\nu) = \int_{E} h^\chi\,\mathrm{d}\nu
\]
with $h^\chi\colon\,E \to \N_0$ given by
\[
\begin{aligned}
h^{-}\big((a,a^\prime),(b,b^\prime),(c,c^\prime)\big)
&= \mathbbm{1}_{\{c>0\}}
+ \mathbbm{1}_{\{b=0,\, c>0\}}
+ \mathbbm{1}_{\{b=0,\,c=0,\, c^\prime>0\}}, \\[6pt]
h^{0}\big((a,a^\prime),(b,b^\prime),(c,c^\prime)\big)
&= c-\mathbbm{1}_{\{c>0\}}-\mathbbm{1}_{\{c>1\}}
+ \mathbbm{1}_{\{b=0,\,c=0,\,c^\prime=0\}}, \\[6pt]
h^{+}\big((a,a^\prime),(b,b^\prime),(c,c^\prime)\big)
&= \mathbbm{1}_{\{c>0\}} + \mathbbm{1}_{\{c>1\}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let (X_n)_{n=1}^\infty be independent real random variables, and fix c > 0. Define the truncated variables Y_n = X_n \mathbf{1}_{\{|X_n| \le c\}}. Then the series \sum_{n=1}^\infty X_n converges almost surely if and only if all three of the following series converge: (1) \sum_{n=1}^\infty \mathbb{P}(|X_n| > c) < \infty; (2) \sum_{n=1}^\infty \mathbb{E}[Y_n] \text{ converges in } \mathbb{R}; (3) \sum_{n=1}^\infty \text{Var}(Y_n) < \infty.

Preserved duplicate statement and commentary:
Let X_1, X_2, ... be independent random variables and fix a constant c > 0. For each i define the truncation Y_i = X_i 1(|X_i| <= c). Then the series sum_{i=1}^infinity X_i converges almost surely if and only if all three of the following series converge: sum_i P(|X_i| > c), sum_i E[Y_i], and sum_i Var(Y_i). If one of the three series diverges, the partial sums of sum X_i do not converge almost surely. [Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples]

c > 0 constant

[Lemma 2-l01 of arXiv:2412.04015, 'Linear fluctuation of interfaces in Glauber-Kawasaki dynamics'] Fix a finite subset $D$ of ${\mathbb Z}^d$. Then, there exists a finite constant
$C_0$, depending only on $D$ and the bounds (equation 2-38b of the paper),
(equation 2-84 of the paper) on the density profile, such that
\begin{equation*}
{\mathbb E}_{\nu^N} \Big[ \, \Big|\, \sum_{x\in {\mathbb T}^d_N} G(x) \,
\omega_{x+D}(t) \,\Big|^\alpha\,\Big] \;\le\; C_0 \,
N^{\alpha d/2} \, \Vert G\Vert^\alpha _\infty \, \big( \, 1 \,+\,
H_N(f^N_t)\,\big)^{\alpha /2} 
\end{equation*}
for all $1\le \alpha\le 2$, $t>0$, $G:{\mathbb T}^d_N \to{\mathbb R}$ and
$N \ge 1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. Let S_k=max_{j<=k} X_j and a_n=sqrt(n) log(n). If for every finite T, max_{k<=floor(nT)} |S_k-X_k|/a_n tends to zero in probability, and S_floor(nt)/a_n converges in the Skorokhod J1 topology to a continuous process Y, then X_floor(nt)/a_n also converges to Y. The identity time change bounds their J1 distance by the displayed uniform norm. A uniform O_P(sqrt(n)) backtracking estimate suffices; a fixed-time estimate alone does not establish this hypothesis. No such estimate under the weaker ERW cookie assumptions is claimed.
Uniform backtracking hypothesis on every compact time interval
Continuous J1 limit of the rescaled maximum

Label: proof of an elementary inversion and a conditional process-transfer lemma, not a solution of Problem 6.4. Current literature status is unverified offline.

The earlier C0135-A001 says both that a clock has size m^2 log(m) and that its inverse is sqrt(t)/log(t), and later uses the different scale sqrt(t) log(t). These cannot be equivalent scales.

Let f(x)=x^2 log(x), x>=1. It is strictly increasing for x>1. If a deterministic increasing clock T_m is asymptotic to m^2 log(m), its generalized inverse is asymptotic to sqrt(2t/log(t)). Indeed put u(t)=sqrt(2t/log(t)). Then log(u(t))=0.5(log(t)+log(2)-log(log(t))), so f(u(t))/t tends to one. For every fixed eps>0, T_floor((1-eps)u(t))/t tends to (1-eps)^2<1 and T_ceil((1+eps)u(t))/t tends to (1+eps)^2>1, which brackets the inverse. Thus neither of the two scales in A001 follows from that clock. This is an arithmetic correction; it does not assert that the ERW clock has this asymptotic behavior.

For the actual process question, define S_k=max_{j<=k} X_j and a_n=sqrt(n) log(n). If for every finite T,

max_{k<=floor(nT)} |S_k-X_k| / a_n -> 0 in probability,

and S_floor(nt)/a_n converges in distribution in the Skorokhod J1 topology to a continuous process Y, then X_floor(nt)/a_n converges to Y in J1. The uniform norm bounds their J1 distance by using the identity time change; convergence in probability of this distance and the metric-space Slutsky lemma give the result. A uniform O_P(sqrt(n)) backtracking bound would suffice, since sqrt(n)/a_n=1/log(n) tends to zero.

The missing mathematical work is to establish the maximum limit and this UNIFORM backtracking bound under the precise weaker cookie assumptions. body: Let l <= r be integers, [l..r] := [l, r] intersected with Z, a = (a_l, ..., a_r) in {L, R}^[l..r] an LR-sequence and b = (b_l, ..., b_r) in {+, -}^[l..r] a sign sequence. The rail-yard graph RYG(l, r, a, b) is the bipartite graph with vertex set [2l - 1..2r + 1] x (Z + 1/2); a vertex is even or odd with its abscissa. Each even vertex (2m, y), m in [l..r], is incident to three edges: the horizontal edges to (2m - 1, y) and (2m + 1, y), and one diagonal edge, to (2m - 1, y + 1) if (a_m, b_m) = (L, +), to (2m - 1, y - 1) if (L, -), to (2m + 1, y + 1) if (R, +), and to (2m + 1, y - 1) if (R, -). The odd vertices with abscissa 2l - 1 (resp. 2r + 1) form the left (resp. right) boundary. Every horizontal edge has weight 1 and each diagonal edge at an even vertex of abscissa 2i has weight x_i. The paper encodes the graph's perfect matchings (dimer coverings) by interlacing sequences of partitions (its Section 3.1).

body:
[Corollary co-ultra-two-CRSM-2 of arXiv:2411.12623, 'Random signed measures'] Let $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$ be two independent atomless random measures on $S\times T$ with independent $S$-increments and with driving Poisson processes $\Psi_1$ and $\Psi_2$, respectively. Then, $\Psi_1$ and $\Psi_2$ are independent. 
	
	Moreover, let $\xi$ be given by $\xi(B)=\eta_1(B)-\eta_2(B)$, $B\in\hat{\mathcal{S}}\otimes\hat{\mathcal{T}}$. Then, $\xi$ is an atomless random signed measure on $S\times T$ with independent $S$-increments with Jordan decomposition $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$. In particular, if $F_1$ and $F_2$ are the L\'{e}vy measures of $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$, respectively, then the L\'{e}vy measure $F$ of $\xi$ is given by $F_1$ on $S\times(\mathcal{M}_T\setminus\{0\})$ and by $F_2$ on $S\times(-\mathcal{M}_T\setminus\{0\})$, precisely for every $B\in\hat{\mathcal{S}}$ and $A\in\mathfrak{B}_{\mathcal{M}_T\cup-\mathcal{M}_T\setminus\{0\}}$ we have $F(B\times A)=F_1(B\times (A\cap\mathcal{M}_T))+F_2(B\times -(A\cap-\mathcal{M}_T))$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary co-ultra-two-CRSM-2 of arXiv:2411.12623

[Theorem thm:suffc of arXiv:2510.13572, 'Coalescence in Markov chains'] Let $P\in\mathcal{P}_S$ have (unique) invariant distribution ${\boldsymbol\pi}$.
\begin{letlist}
\item Let $m\in \mathbb N$, and suppose there exists $s\in S$ with $\pi_s>1/m$. Then
$k_{\text{\rm max}}< m$.
\item
Let $m\in \mathbb N$, and suppose there exists $s\in S$ such that $p_{i,s} > 1/m$ for all $i\in S$.
Then $k_{\text{\rm max}}< m$.
\end{letlist}

of \Cref{prop:fractional-enhancement} together with its resolvent family
\eqref{eq:resolvent-model-uniform}.  For all sufficiently large \(\lambda\),
equation \eqref{eq:zvonkin-equation} has a unique
paracontrolled solution.  The solutions built from smooth enhanced
approximations
converge in \(C([t_0,T];C^{1+\beta})\) to a map
\(\Psi=x+\psi\), and
\begin{equation}
 0<J_*\le J(t,x)\le J^*<\infty
\end{equation}
uniformly on finite time intervals.  In particular, \(\Psi\) and
\(\Phi\) are uniformly bi-Lipschitz.  The convergence
\begin{equation}
 \norm{\psi}_{C([t_0,T];C^{1+\beta})}
 +\norm{J-1}_{C([t_0,T];C^\beta)}
\longrightarrow0
\qquad\text{as }\lambda\to\infty
\end{equation}
is locally uniform on sets where the enhanced-model norm and the uniform
resolvent-family norm are bounded.
Consequently \(\lambda\) may be chosen so that
\(\norm{J-1}_{L^\infty}\le1/2\), which implies \eqref{eq:J-bounds}; alternatively,
with \(\lambda=0\), the same smallness is obtained on a sufficiently short
restarted interval.

body:
[Theorem thm:realization of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] Let $U \in C^{0}(0,1)$. The following are equivalent.
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\normalfont(\roman*), leftmargin=*]
			\item $U = U_{f}$ for some $f \in \mathcal{D}_{+}^{2}$.
			\item The Hill equation $\psi'' + \tfrac12 U\psi = 0$ has a positive
			solution on $(0,1)$.
			\item The Hill equation is disconjugate on $(0,1)$; equivalently,
			\begin{equation*}
				\int_{0}^{1}(\chi')^{2}\,dz
				\;\ge\; \tfrac12\int_{0}^{1}U\chi^{2}\,dz
				\qquad\text{for all } \chi \in C_{c}^{\infty}(0,1).
			\end{equation*}
		\end{enumerate}
		When these hold, every positive solution $\psi$ and base point
		$z_{0} \in (0,1)$ determine a law by
		\begin{equation}
			Q(z) = \int_{z_{0}}^{z}\frac{ds}{\psi(s)^{2}},
			\qquad
			F = Q^{-1},
			\qquad
			f = \psi^{2}\circ F
			\quad\text{on } J := Q\big((0,1)\big),
			
		\end{equation}
		and this $f$ has unit total mass automatically; conversely, every law
		with potential $U$ arises in this way. We call
		$\mathcal{C} := \{U : \textup{(iii) holds}\}$ the \emph{probability
			cone}.

[Theorem thm:root-comparison of arXiv:2607.08551, 'Weighted-threshold Coupon Collection'] Fix $\theta\in(0,1)$ and $0<\delta<t_{N,\theta}$. Define
\[
\Delta_{N,\theta}(\delta):=
\min\Bigl\{
\theta-m_N(t_{N,\theta}-\delta),
\,
m_N(t_{N,\theta}+\delta)-\theta
\Bigr\}.
\]
Then $\Delta_{N,\theta}(\delta)>0$ and
\[
\mathbb{P}\bigl(|\tau_{N,\theta}-t_{N,\theta}| > \delta\bigr)
\le
4\exp\!\left(
-\frac{\Delta_{N,\theta}(\delta)^2}
{2w_N^\ast+\frac23 w_N^\ast \Delta_{N,\theta}(\delta)}
\right).
\]

Consider the autonomous system y'=f(y) on an open set U subset R^n containing an equilibrium y* (f(y*)=0), with f locally Lipschitz. Suppose there is a continuously differentiable V: W -> R on a neighborhood W of y* with V(y*)=0, V(y)>0 for y in W\{y*} (V positive definite), and V_dot(y) = grad V(y).f(y) <= 0 for all y in W (V is a Lyapunov function). Then y* is stable: for every epsilon>0 there is delta>0 such that |y(0)-y*|<delta implies |y(t)-y*|<epsilon for all t>=0. If in addition V_dot(y)<0 for y in W\{y*}, then y* is asymptotically stable: stable, and y(t) -> y* as t -> infinity for all initial conditions sufficiently close to y*.
f is locally Lipschitz near the equilibrium y*
V is C^1, positive definite at y*, with V_dot <= 0 (resp. < 0) near y*

[Proposition 17 of arXiv:2605.11279, 'Flocking with Multiple Types: Competition, Fluid Limits and Traveling Waves'] There exists a solution $\parens*{G_+, G_-}$ to \eqref{sysFluid1} that satisfies the following two conditions:
    \begin{enumerate}[label = (\alph*)]
        \item First, $G_+$ and $G_-$ are non-increasing in time.

        \item In addition, $\lim_{t\to-\infty} G_\pm(t) = 1$, $\lim_{t\to\infty} G_\pm(t) = 0$. Moreover, $G_+(t) \geq G_-(t)$ for each $t\in\real$, and furthermore,
        \begin{align*}
            &\lim_{t\to\infty} \dfrac{\log G_\pm(t)}{t} = -\dfrac{v_+-\gamma+\alpha^+ +\alpha^- +\rho^+-\rho^-}{2\gamma} \\
            &\qquad+\dfrac{1}{2} \sqrt{\parens*{\!\dfrac{v_+ - \gamma +\alpha^+ - \alpha^- -1}{\gamma}\!}^2 + \dfrac{4\parens*{\alpha\displaystyle^+ -\rho\displaystyle^-} \parens*{\rho\displaystyle^+ +\alpha\displaystyle^-+\gamma}}{\gamma\displaystyle^2}\!},
        \end{align*}
        where the quantity on the right-hand side is the larger eigenvalue of $J(0, 0)$. Lastly, 
        \begin{align*}
            \lim_{t\to-\infty} \dfrac{\log \sqbr*{1-G_\pm(t)}}{t} &= -\dfrac{v_+-\gamma+\alpha^+ +\alpha^-}{2\gamma} + \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{\parens*{\!\dfrac{v_+ - \gamma +\alpha^+ - \alpha^-}{\gamma}\!}^2 + \dfrac{4\alpha\displaystyle^+ \parens*{\alpha\displaystyle^-+\gamma}}{\gamma\displaystyle^2}},
        \end{align*}
        where the quantity on the right-hand side is $\lambda_u$, the positive eigenvalue of $J(1, 1)$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 48 of arXiv:2604.22159, 'Adapted optimal transport between filtered Gaussian processes'] Let $N=2$ and $d=1$, and suppose that $\mu=\cN(0,A) \in \cP_2(\bR^2)$ for some diagonal matrix $A$. Let $X\sim \mu$ and $\epsilon^X=L^{-1}X$, where $L=\mathcal{C}_{\min}(A)$. Assume that
\[
\bE[\epsilon_2^X\mid X_1]\ne 0, \quad \mathrm{a.s.}
\]
 and admits a density. Then there exists a centered Gaussian
distribution $\nu$ such that
\[
\AW_2^2(\mu,\nu)
<
\AW_2^2(\cN_2(0,A),\nu).
\]
In particular, if the adapted Gelbrich bound holds for every centered Gaussian target,
then necessarily
\[
\bE[\epsilon_2^X\mid X_1]=0,
\quad\mathrm{a.s.}
\]

[Corollary 33 of arXiv:2609.01473, 'Keller sequences of exact $\infty$-categories'] Let $p\colon \cal{C} \hookrightarrow \cal{B}$ be a Keller projection and $\cal{E}$ some $\infty$-category which admits small colimits. 
Then the square
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep = 50pt]
\cal{C} \ar[r,"p"]\ar[d,"j_{\cal{C}}"'] & \cal{B} \ar[d,"j_{\cal{B}}"] \\
\pst(\cal{C}) \ar[r,"\pst(p)"] & \pst(\cal{B}) 
\end{tikzcd}
\]
satisfies the following Beck-Chevalley properties:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*]
\item
For every functor $\vphi\colon \cal{B} \to \cal{E}$ the Beck-Chevalley transformation
\[ (j_{\cal{C}})_!p^*\vphi \Rightarrow \pst(p)^*(j_{\cal{B}})_!\vphi  \]
is an equivalence. 
\item
For every presheaf $\vphi\colon \pst(\cal{C})^{\op} \to \cal{E}$ the Beck-Chevalley transformation
\[ p_!j_{\cal{C}}^*\vphi \Rightarrow j_{\cal{B}}^*\pst(p)_!\vphi \]
is an equivalence. 
\end{enumerate}

[Defn def-le-infty of arXiv:2506.18827, 'Random walk reflected off of infinity, with applications to uniform spanning forests and s'] Let $X$ be the (continuous time) random walk reflected off of $\infty$ on $\mathcal G$. Let $a , b \geq 0$ with $a < b$ and $X_a\not=\infty$. 
The \textbf{loop erasure} of $X|_{[a,b]}$ is the path $\operatorname{LE}  : \mathbbm N_0 \to \mathcal V\mathcal G$ defined inductively as follows. 
Let $\operatorname{LE}(0) = X_a$. Inductively, suppose $k\geq 1$ and $\operatorname{LE} (k-1)$ has been defined.  
If $\operatorname{LE} (k-1) = X_b$, we set $\operatorname{LE} (k) = X_b$. 
Otherwise, let $t_k$ be the supremum of the times $t \in [a,b]$ for which $X_t = \operatorname{LE}(k-1)$ (note that this set is a finite union of left-closed, right-open intervals by Lemma~(lem-to-infty of the paper)). Let $\operatorname{LE}(k) :=  X_{t_k}$ be the vertex which $X$ jumps to at time $t_k$.

[Definition def:invariant of arXiv:2605.22787, 'Invariant measures for half-space geometric LPP: classification and the one force--one sol'] A probability measure $\nu$ on the space of functions $f:\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ is called \textbf{invariant} if, whenever $f \sim \nu$, independent of the weights on or above level $1$: $(\omega_{(i,j)})_{i \ge j \ge 1}$, then for all $n \ge 1$, 
    \[
    \Bigl(G_f(n + k,n) - G_f(n,n)\Bigr)_{k \in \mathbb{N}} \sim \nu.
    \]
Here, we take the convention that $\mathbb{N} =\{1,2,\ldots\}$.

Let L/K be a finite Galois extension and G=Gal(L/K). The assignments H->L^H={x in L:sigma(x)=x for every sigma in H} and E->Gal(L/E) are inverse inclusion-reversing bijections between subgroups H of G and intermediate fields K subseteq E subseteq L. They satisfy [L:L^H]=|H| and [L^H:K]=[G:H]; moreover, H is normal in G exactly when L^H/K is Galois, in which case Gal(L^H/K) is isomorphic to G/H.

[Proposition thm:adaptive-distance-CS of arXiv:2608.25551, 'Beyond Optimal Rates in Stochastic Optimization: Trajectory-Adaptive Stopping Rules'] Suppose Assumptions~(assump:strong-convexity of the paper)--(assump:stepsize-bound of the paper) hold. Then, for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$, the process
\begin{equation}

    U^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t+1}(\alpha)
    \coloneqq
    \frac{1}{A_t}
    \left[
        Z_{t_0}
        +
        \sum_{s = t_0}^t
        A_s \eta_s^2 \left\| g_s \right\|^2
        +
        4\, \mathfrak H_\alpha \left( V_t^{\mathrm{dist}} \right)
    \right],
    \qquad
    t \ge t_0,
\end{equation}
is an upper confidence sequence for the last-iterate squared distance to the optimizer, in the sense that
\[
    \mathbb{P}\left(
        \forall t \ge t_0:\
        Z_{t+1}
        \le
        U^{\mathrm{dist}}_{t+1}(\alpha)
    \right)
    \ge
    1-\alpha.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Confidence sequence for $\norm{x_{t+1}-x^\star}^2$

\[
(\overline{\omega}\otimes_{\overline{\tau}(\overline{\omega})}\tilde{\omega})_u := 
\begin{cases}
\overline{\omega}_u, & 0\le u < \overline{\tau}(\overline{\omega}),\\
\overline{\omega}_{\overline{\tau}(\overline{\omega})} + \tilde{\omega}_{u-\overline{\tau}(\overline{\omega})}, & u \geq \overline{\tau}(\overline{\omega}).
\end{cases}
\]

body:
[Lemma 22 (\textsf{Zero-set bound}) of arXiv:2608.12451, '2608.12451'] Let
$
 P\in\bigoplus_{j=0}^s\cC_j^{\mathsf{R}}
$
be nonzero with $s\in\N_0$, and let $r:=\deg(P)\leq s$.
Then, for every
$(i_1,\ldots,i_r)\in\Delta_r$ such that
$
 D_{i_r}\cdots D_{i_1}P\not\equiv 0,
$
one has

\noi
\begin{align}
 \PP(P\ne0)
 \geq
 \prod_{\ell=1}^r
 \min\{p_{i_\ell},q_{i_\ell}\}.
 
\end{align}
Consequently, if, for some
$\eps\in(0,\frac12]$,
\[
 \eps\leq p_k\leq1-\eps
\]
for every coordinate on which $P$ depends, then
\noi
\begin{align}
 \PP(P\ne0)
 \geq\eps^r
 \geq\eps^s.
 
\end{align}

[Theorem poisson_convergence of arXiv:2606.09386, 'High-degree vertices in uniform recursive directed acyclic graphs with freezing'] Fix $m\in\mathbb{N}$ and a choice sequence $\mathbf x$ such that Assumption~$\hyperref[ass:A]{\mathbf{x}}$ is satisfied for some $\varepsilon<1-1/((m+1)\log\theta)$ in Part~(item:hI of the paper) and some $\eta<1-1/((m+1)\log\theta)$ in Part~(item:Jn of the paper). Fix $\varepsilon^\mathrm{a},\varepsilon^\mathrm{f}\in[0,1]$ and let $\mathcal{P}_\mathrm{a}\overset \mathrm{d}=\mathcal{P}^{\varepsilon^\mathrm{a}}$ and $\mathcal{P}_\mathrm{f}\overset \mathrm{d}= \mathcal{P}^{\varepsilon^\mathrm{f}}$ be independent point processes. Let $(n_\ell)_{\ell\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a subsequence of integers such that $n_\ell\to\infty$ and $\varepsilon_{n_\ell}^\square\to\varepsilon^\square$ as $\ell\to\infty$ for $\square\in\{\mathrm{a},\mathrm{f}\}$. Then, $\mathcal{P}_\mathrm{a}^{(n_\ell)}$ and $\mathcal{P}_\mathrm{f}^{(n_\ell)}$ jointly converge weakly to $\mathcal{P}_\mathrm{a}$ and $\mathcal{P}_\mathrm{f}$ as $\ell\to\infty$  in $\mathcal{M}^\#_{\mathbb{Z}^*}$, respectively. Equivalently, for any $i<i^\prime\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $j<j'\in\mathbb{Z}$, jointly as $\ell\to\infty$,
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
({}&X_i^{(n_\ell)},\ldots,X_{i^\prime-1}^{(n_\ell)},X_{\geq i^\prime}^{(n_\ell)},Y_j^{(n_\ell)},\ldots,Y_{j^\prime-1}^{(n_\ell)},Y_{\geq j^\prime}^{(n_\ell)})\\ 
&\buildrel {\mathrm{d}}\over{\longrightarrow}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{a}}\{i\},\ldots,\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{a}}\{i^\prime -1\},\mathcal{P}_\mathrm{a}[i^\prime,\infty),\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{f}}\{j\},\ldots,\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{f}}\{j^\prime -1\},\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{f}}[j^\prime,\infty)).
\end{aligned}\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:m1-sup of arXiv:2605.10617, 'Logarithmic scaling of selective sweep curves:\\ from tents to houses'] For $I= [\alpha, \beta]$, $t\in I$ and $f\in \mathcal D_I$ let 
    $$
      \overline f(t)
        := \max_{\alpha \le t'\le t} f(t'), \qquad
      \widetilde f(t)
        := \max_{\beta +\alpha  -t \le r\le \beta} f(r)
    $$
    be the running maximum of $f$ and of its time-reversal, respectively.
    Then
    $${\rm a)} \quad d_{M_1}(f,\overline f)\le \sup_{t\in I} | \overline f(t)-f(t) |, \qquad  \quad {\rm b)}\quad  d_{M_1}(f,\widetilde f)\le \sup_{t\in I} | \widetilde f(t)-f(t) |. $$

Let (X_{n, k})_{1 \le k \le r_n} be a triangular array of row-wise independent random variables with \mathbb{E}[X_{n, k}] = 0, \sum_{k=1}^{r_n} \text{Var}(X_{n, k}) = 1, and the uniform asymptotic negligibility (UAN) condition \lim_{n \to \infty} \max_{1 \le k \le r_n} \text{Var}(X_{n, k}) = 0.         \([\underline{t},\overline{t}]\), so that \(t_0=\underline{t}\) and \(t_K=\overline{t}\).
        Let \(x\colon [\underline{t}, \overline{t}] \to \banachSpace[X]\)
        be a function such that for all \(k\in \set{0, \dots, K-1}\) we have
        \[
            \holder{x}_{\alpha, [t_k, t_{k+1}]} \le \eta
        \]
        for some \(\eta > 0\). Then \(x\) is \(\alpha\)-Hölder continuous
        on \([\underline{t}, \overline{t}]\), specifically
        \[
            \holder{x}_{\alpha, [\underline{t}, \overline{t}]}
            \le \eta K^{1-\alpha}.
        \]
title: Hölder glue

[Theorem 33 of arXiv:2609.03070, 'Variants of order semicontinuity in Banach lattices'] Assume that $F$ is $r$-demicontinuous. Then:
\item[(i)] $F^{L}$ is an $r$-monotonically complete Banach lattice.
\item[(ii)] The norm of $F$ has an $r^{2}$-demicontinuous extension to $F^{L}$, equivalent to $\|\cdot\|_{L}$.
\item[(iii)] The norm completion of $F$ is $r^{2}$-demicontinuous.
\item[(iv)] If $T:F\to E$ is a contractive order continuous homomorphism into a demicontinuous normed lattice, then there is a unique order continuous extension $T^{L}:F^{L}\to E^{L}$ of $T$. Moreover, $T^{L}$ is a contractive homomorphism.
\item[(v)] If $G$ is a normed lattice which isomorphically contains $F$ as an order dense sublattice, then there is a unique injective order continuous homomorphism $J:G\to F^{L}$ which leaves $F$ in place.
\item[(vi)] If $F$ is $r$-semicontinuous, then so is $F^{L}$. In particular, the Lorentz completion preserves topological semicontinuity.

\Prob{T((0,0),(n,{\lceil v n \rceil}))\le n (\Lambda(v)-\varepsilon)}\le A \exp(-Bn). 
\]
The same holds for the SJ model when $G$ corresponds to a Bernoulli distribution. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 12 of arXiv:2605.26664, 'Mixing times for Glauber dynamics of lozenge tilings of the hexagon'] Let $S=(S_1,\dots,S_n)$ and $S'=(S'_1,\dots,S'_n)$ be two 
    Bernoulli path ensembles with  endpoints $(p_1=(x_p,y_{p_1}),\dots,p_n=(x_p,y_{p_n})),(q_1=(x_q,y_{q_1}),\dots,q_n=(x_q,y_{q_n}))$ for $S$,  and $(p'_1=(x_p,y'_{p'_1}),\dots,p'_n=(x_p,y'_{p'_n})),(q'_1=(x_q,y'_{q'_1}),\dots,q'_n=(x_q,y'_{q'_n}))$ for $S'$. Assume that $y_{p_i}\ge y'_{p'_i}$ and $y_{q_i}\ge y'_{q'_i}$
    for every $i=1,\dots,n$. Then, we can couple $S,S'$ in such a way that, almost surely, the $S_i$ is weakly above $S'_i$ for every $i=1,\dots,n$.

	More generally, fix functions $V^\pm_i,W^\pm_i:(x_p,x_q)\mapsto \mathbb R$  such that $V_i^\pm \ge W_i^\pm$. Condition  $S$ to the event that $S_i$ is above $V^-_i$ and below $V^+_i$ for every $i=1,\dots, n$, and condition $S'$ to the event that $S'_i$ is above $W^{-}_i$ and below $W^+_i$ for every $i=1,\dots,n$ (we assume that $(V_i^\pm , W_i^\pm)_{i=1,\dots,n}$ are such that these events are nonempty). Then, we can couple $S,S'$ in such a way that, almost surely, the $S_i$ is weakly above $S'_i$ for every $i=1,\dots,n$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, Partition quadratic stochastic operators converge to the empty body (2026). An F-quadratic stochastic operator acts on the simplex over types {0, 1, ..., m}, where 0 is the empty body: parents of the same sex, or a pair containing 0, produce 0; Rozikov and Zhamilov proved that every such operator has the unique fixed point e_0 and that every trajectory converges to it exponentially fast. Problem 10 of Ganikhodzhaev, Mukhamedov and Rozikov, Quadratic stochastic operators and processes: results and open problems (arXiv:0902.4207), asks whether the same holds when the two sexes are replaced by the blocks E_1, ..., E_q of an arbitrary partition of {1, ..., m}, with same-block pairs producing the empty body. The answer is yes: with y = 1 - x_0, every such operator V satisfies y(V(x)) <= (1 - 1/q) y(x)^2, so e_0 is the unique fixed point and y(V^n(x)) <= c^{-1} (c y(x))^{2^n} with c = 1 - 1/q, and the inequality is an equality at every step along some trajectories for each q. Without the rule that pairs containing 0 produce 0 the statement fails: (x_0, x_1) -> (x_0^2 + x_1^2, 2 x_0 x_1) has a second, attracting fixed point (1/2, 1/2). Exact rational checks and a Lean 4 file accompany the paper. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/partition-qso-empty-body (commit f3a2991ab8c5). Not refereed.
title: Partition quadratic stochastic operators converge doubly exponentially to the empty body, answering Problem 10 of Ganikhodzhaev, Mukhamedov and Rozikov (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/partition-qso-empty-body)

[Definition of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] Let $L \supseteq \textbf{FIK}$ and $\Gamma, \Delta \subseteq \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$.
  \begin{itemize}
    \item We let $\Box \Gamma \coloneq \set{ \Box \varphi; \varphi \in \Gamma }$ and $\Diamond \Gamma \coloneq \set{ \Diamond \varphi; \varphi \in \Gamma }$.\\
          We also let $\Box^{-1} \Gamma \coloneq \set{ \varphi; \Box \varphi \in \Gamma }$ and $\Diamond^{-1} \Gamma \coloneq \set{ \varphi; \Diamond \varphi \in \Gamma }$.
    \item A tuple $(\Gamma, \Delta)$ is said to be a \emph{theory}.
    \item A theory $(\Gamma, \Delta)$ is said to be \emph{maximal} if $\Gamma \cup \Delta = \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$.
    \item A theory $(\Gamma, \Delta)$ is said to be \emph{$L$-consistent} if $L \nvdash \bigwedge \Gamma_0 \to \bigvee \Delta_0$ for any finite $\Gamma_0 \subseteq \Gamma$ and any finite $\Delta_0 \subseteq \Delta$.
          We note that $\bigwedge \emptyset = \top$ and $\bigvee \emptyset = \bot$.
    \item A theory $(\Gamma, \Delta)$ is said to be \emph{$L$-final} if it is $L$-consistent and
          $(\Gamma \cup \Pi, \Delta \setminus \Pi)$ is not $L$-consistent for any nonempty $\Pi \subseteq \Delta$.
  \end{itemize}
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical M'

[Theorem thm:conva of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Let $\Phi_D$ be a zero boundary GFF on a bounded simply-connected domain $D$ and $\tilde \phi_m$ be a sequence of zero boundary metric graph GFFs on $\widetilde D_m$ that are coupled with the GFF $\Phi_D$ such that a.s., 
$\tilde \phi_m \to \Phi$ in $H^{-\varepsilon}(\mathbb{C})$, for some $\varepsilon>0$.
Further, take 
$(\widetilde C_k^m,  \tilde\nu_k^m,\tilde s_k^m)
_{k \geq 1}$ 
the excursion decomposition of $\tilde \phi_m$, where 
$\widetilde C_k^m$ are the connected components of 
$\{\tilde \phi_m \neq 0\}$, 
$\tilde \nu_k^m$ are given by $|\tilde \phi_m|$ restricted to $\widetilde C_k^m$, and $\tilde s_k^m$ are the sign of 
$\phi_m$ on $\widetilde C_k^m$. 
Moreover, the clusters are ordered by decreasing size of diameter.

For every $k>0$,  we have the joint convergence in probability of $ \widetilde C_k^{(m)}\to C_k$, 
$\tilde\nu_k^{(m)}\to \nu_k$ and $\tilde s_k^{(m)}\to s_k$ as $m\to \infty$, in the Hausdorff topology\footnote{This is the topology on closed sets given by the Hausdorff distance.} for the first component, and in the weak topology of measures for the second component. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Convergence of the excursion decomposition

body:
[Corollary 13 (Gaussian relative-energy decay) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] Under Proposition~\ref{thm:linear-gaussian-guidance}, the prior score is
\[
s_t^{\rm prior}(x)=-B_t^{-1}x.
\]
Then, under \(X_t\sim p_t\),
\begin{equation}

\frac1d\E\|s_t^{\rm prior}(X_t)\|^2
=\frac1d\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(B_t^{-1}\right)
=\frac1d\sum_{i=1}^d\frac{1}{a_t^2\lambda_i+\Delta_t},
\end{equation}
where \(\{\lambda_i\}\) are the eigenvalues of \(\Sigma\).  Under the schedule
\eqref{eq:forward-marginal}, \(\Delta_t\to1\) as \(a_t\to0\), so this converges
to \(1\) and the prior-score energy is \(\Theta(1)\); the same conclusion holds
for any VP schedule with \(\Delta_t\to\Delta_\infty>0\).  In fixed
dimension, the likelihood-force energy has the leading-order expansion
\begin{equation}

\frac1d\E\|g_t(X_t,R)\|^2
=\frac{a_t^2}{\Delta_t^2}\,\frac1d\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\Sigma A^\top Q^{-1}A\Sigma\right)
+O(a_t^4),
\end{equation}
and therefore
\begin{equation}

\rho_t^{\rm global}
:=
\frac{\E\|g_t(X_t,R)\|^2}
{\E\|s_t^{\rm prior}(X_t)\|^2}
=O(a_t^2).
\end{equation}
In the isotropic case \(\Sigma=\sigma_x^2\Id_d\), \(A=\Id_d\),
\(\Gamma=\sigma_y^2\Id_d\),
\(\rho_t^{\rm global}\sim a_t^2\sigma_x^4/(\sigma_x^2+\sigma_y^2)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Gaussian relative-energy decay

[Proposition 18 (Fixed-time moment formula) of arXiv:2607.24561, 'Range convergence and sharp one-arm asymptotics\\for the critical percolation cluster in h'] For $k\ge1$, $t_1,\dots,t_k>0$ and $\phi_1,\dots,\phi_k\in\Cc$,
\begin{equation}
\bN\Bigl[\prod_{i=1}^k X_{t_i}(\phi_i)\Bigr]
=\gamma^{\,k-1}\sum_{T\in\T_k}
\int
\prod_{\{a,b\}\in E(T)} p_{\,s_b-s_a}\bigl(y_b-y_a\bigr)
\prod_{v\in V_{\mathrm{int}}(T)} ds_v\,dy_v\,
\prod_{i=1}^k\phi_i(z_i)\,dz_i ,
\end{equation}
where each vertex $a$ of $T$ carries a space-time point $(s_a,y_a)$; the
root is pinned at $(0,0)$, the leaf $i$ at $(t_i,z_i)$; the edges
$\{a,b\}$ are written with $a$ the endpoint closer to the root; internal
vertices are integrated over $(0,\infty)\times\R^d$; and $p_s\equiv0$ for
$s\le0$ (which enforces the genealogical time-ordering). Here $\gamma$ is the branching parameter of \eqref{eq:laplace} (Section~\ref{sec:SBM}) and $p_s(x)=(2\pi s)^{-d/2}e^{-|x|^2/2s}$ is the heat kernel of Section~\ref{sec:notation}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Fixed-time moment formula

[Lemma 31 of arXiv:2605.31471, 'Convergence Rates of Continuous-Time Random Walks to Time-Fractional Diffusions with Unbou'] Let $\alpha,\beta\in\R$ and $k\in\N_0$.
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item If $u\in\cC^k_{\alpha,\infty}(\cX)$ and
            $v\in\cC^k_{\beta,\infty}(\cX)$, then
            $uv\in\cC^k_{\alpha+\beta,\infty}(\cX)$ and
            \[
                \|uv\|_{\alpha+\beta,k}
                \le C_{\alpha,\beta,k}\|u\|_{\alpha,k}\|v\|_{\beta,k}.
            \]
            The same estimate holds for contractions of tensor-valued
            functions.
            \item Let
            \[
                \eta_h(x)=h b(x)+\sqrt h\sum_{\ell=1}^d\sigma_\ell(x)\xi_\ell
            \]
            and let Assumptions~\ref{asm:weighted-regular} and
            \ref{asm:rw-bounded} hold.  Then, for $0<h\le h_0$ and
            $0\le\theta\le1$,
            \[
                C^{-1}w_\gamma(x)\le
                w_\gamma(x+\theta\eta_h(x))
                \le Cw_\gamma(x),
                \qquad \gamma\in\R,
            \]
            and, for $1\le j\le k+4$,
            \[
                \|\DD^j\eta_h(x)\|
                \le C\sqrt h\,w_{1-j}(x).
            \]
            Moreover, if $\varphi_h^\theta(x):=x+\theta\eta_h(x)$, then
            \[
                \|\DD\varphi_h^\theta(x)\|\le C,
                \qquad
                \|\DD^j\varphi_h^\theta(x)\|
                \le C\sqrt h\,w_{1-j}(x),
                \quad j\ge2.
            \]
            \item If $g\in\cC^k_{\alpha,\infty}(\cX)$, then
            $x\mapsto \E g(x+\eta_h(x))$ belongs to
            $\cC^k_{\alpha,\infty}(\cX)$.
        \end{enumerate}

body:
[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2506.16259, 'Two-dimensional Rademacher walk'] Let $C>0$ and $z\in\Z^2$ with $\norm{z}\le C$, and $b'$ and $b''$ are positive integers which are coprime. Then there exist three positive integers $c',c'', N_0$  such that $N_0$ depends on $c',c''$ and~$C$ only and
$$
\P(T_m=z\text{ for some }m\le N_0)\ge 1/2
$$
where
$$
T_m=\sum_{i=1}^m \tilde Z_i    \text{     with }
\tilde Z_i=b'(\xi_{i,1}'+\dots+\xi_{i,c'}')+b''(\xi_{i,1}''+\dots+\xi_{i,c''}'')
$$
and $\xi'_{i,k},\xi''_{i,k},$  are i.i.d.\ two-dimensional Rademacher random variables.

Let X and Y be Banach spaces, I ⊆ R an interval, and K : I × I → B(X,Y) a kernel that is continuous in the operator norm. Let 1 ≤ p < q ≤ ∞ and suppose the (untruncated) operator T f(t) = ∫_I K(t,s) f(s) ds satisfies ‖T f‖_{L^q(I;Y)} ≤ A ‖f‖_{L^p(I;X)} for all f ∈ L^p(I;X). Then the retarded (causal) truncation T̃ f(t) = ∫_{s ∈ I, s < t} K(t,s) f(s) ds satisfies ‖T̃ f‖_{L^q(I;Y)} ≤ C(p,q) A ‖f‖_{L^p(I;X)}, with C(p,q) depending only on p and q (it blows up as q ↓ p). The strict inequality p < q is necessary: the conclusion is false for p = q.
X, Y Banach spaces; K continuous in operator norm on I × I
1 ≤ p < q ≤ ∞, strictly
the untruncated operator is bounded L^p(I;X) → L^q(I;Y)

		& \eqdef \upepsilon_{iab} \partial_a V^b,
	\end{align}
	where $\upepsilon_{iab}$ is the fully antisymmetric symbol normalized by $\upepsilon_{123} = 1$.

Method: Explicit model calculation, comparison identities and remaining hypothesis obstruction Result: Continuous state alone cannot guarantee1/N weak accuracy for arbitrary observables. If X_i are iid standard normal and their empirical mean is M_N, then E|M_N|=sqrt(2/(pi*N)), whereas the limiting observable is0. The nonsmooth absolute value loses a power of sqrtN. In contrast, a twice differentiable test has its centered first Taylor term vanish and its expected second term of order1/N under a covariance bound. This locates the regularity input a weak-error proof needs. Check: The Gaussian example is exact because M_N has variance1/N. In the queue model, the observable mean workload is linear, but the routing mechanism and the empty-workload boundary create nonsmooth dynamics; smoothness of the observable does not automatically make its Poisson solution smooth. Obstruction: One needs uniform stationary moment bounds, quantitative propagation of chaos and a sufficiently regular Poisson equation or semigroup derivative estimate for the unbounded workload state. The source simulations and the discrete-state refined theorem do not provide those estimates. No matching general continuous-workload proof is supplied.

  \Pr\left\{
    \left|\eta_0(Y)-\frac12\right|\le t
  \right\}
  \le Ct,
  \qquad 0<t\le t_0.
\]
Thus the Tsybakov margin condition holds with exponent \(\alpha=1\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Margin exponent for regular two-component mixtures

[Corollary 21 (Several frequencies) of arXiv:2608.22342, 'Completely Positive Entropy and Fourier Central Limit Theorems for Stationary Random Measu'] Let $\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_q\in E_Y$ satisfy
\begin{equation}

    2\theta_a\neq0,
    \qquad
    \theta_a\neq\theta_b,
    \qquad
    \theta_a+\theta_b\neq0
    \quad (a\neq b).
\end{equation}
For each $a$, let
$h_{a,1},\ldots,h_{a,m_a}\in C_c^\infty(\bR^d;\bC)$. Then
\begin{equation}

    \bigl(V_R(h_{a,j},\theta_a)\bigr)_{a,j}
    \dto
    \bigl(G_{\theta_a}(h_{a,j})\bigr)_{a,j}
\end{equation}
in the finite product $\prod_{a=1}^q H^{m_a}$. The joint limit is complex Gaussian with mean zero. For each fixed $a$ its
covariance is given by
\eqref{eq:lattice-limit-covariance} with $\theta=\theta_a$. If $a\neq b$,
then for all $u,v\in H$ and all relevant $j,\ell$,
\begin{align}

    \E\!\left[
      \langle G_{\theta_a}(h_{a,j}),u\rangle_H
      \overline{\langle G_{\theta_b}(h_{b,\ell}),v\rangle_H}
    \right]&=0,\\

    \E\!\left[
      \langle G_{\theta_a}(h_{a,j}),u\rangle_H
      \langle G_{\theta_b}(h_{b,\ell}),v\rangle_H
    \right]&=0.
\end{align}
Consequently, the random vectors associated with distinct frequencies are
independent.

[Theorem multilinear:intro of arXiv:2412.07936, 'Simple Norm Bounds for Polynomial Random Matrices via Decoupling'] [Restatement of (homo multilinear recursion of the paper)]

Let ${\bf x} = \{x_i\}_{i = 1}^n$ be a sequence of i.i.d random variables with ${\mathbb E} x_i= 0$,  ${\mathbb E} x_i^2= 1$ and $|x_i| \leq L$ for all $1\leq i \leq n$. Let $\{{\bf A}_{{\bf i}}\}_{{\bf i} \in {\mathcal T}^d_n}$ be a multi-indexed sequence of deterministic matrices of the same dimension. Define a permutation symmetric, homogeneous multilinear polynomial random matrix of degree $d$ as
$$
{\bf F}({\bf x}) =  \sum_{{\bf i} \in {\mathcal T}^d_n} \left( {\bf A}_{{\bf i}} \cdot \prod_{j \in \{i_1,\dots, i_d \}} x_j\right).
$$
Let $a,b,c\in {\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0}$ and $d = a+b+c$. Then for $2 \leq t \leq \infty,$
$$
{\mathbb E} \ensuremath{\left\lVert {\bf F}({\bf x}) \right\rVert}_{4t}^{4t} ~\leq~ \sum_{\substack{a,b,c: \\ a+b+c=d}} (48dt)^{4dt} \cdot L^{4ct} \norm{{\bf F}_{a,b,c}}_{4t}^{4t}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem multilinear:intro of arXiv:2412.07936

body: [Dfn 17 (Strong lumping) of arXiv:2604.12853, 'Coupling Markov Chains \\with a Common Image Chain'] Let $f: A \twoheadrightarrow C$ be a surjective map between countable sets. We say that a stochastic matrix $P\in\SM(A)$ \textbf{lumps strongly} under $f$ if there exists a stochastic matrix $Q\in\SM(C)$ such that for all $\upalpha\in\PM(A)$, the chain $\MC(\upalpha,P)$ lumps weakly to $\MC(f_*(\upalpha),Q)$. In this case, we say that $P$ lumps strongly under $f$ to $Q$.

[Definition 8 of arXiv:2512.04807, 'Existence and uniqueness of the canonical Brownian motion in non-simple conformal loop ens'] Let $D \subsetneq \C$ be a simply connected domain.  Fix $N \in \N_0$ and let $\ul{x} = (x_1,\ldots,x_{2N})$ be a collection of distinct prime ends which are ordered counterclockwise.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item We call $(D;\ul{x})$ a \emph{marked domain}. Let $\markeddomain{2N}$ be the collection of marked domains with $2N$ marked points.
\item Suppose that $(D;\ul{x}) \in \markeddomain{2N}$, and we have a non-crossing collection of paths $\ul{\gamma} = (\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_N)$ outside of $D$ where each $\gamma_i$ connects a distinct pair of marked points. The paths $\ul{\gamma}$ induce a planar link pattern $\beta$ on the exterior of $D$, formally described by a partition of the marked points into pairs $\beta = \{\{a_1,b_1\},\ldots,\{a_N,b_N\}\}$ where $\{a_1,b_1,\ldots,a_N,b_N\} = \{1,\ldots,2N\}$, $a_r<b_r$, and such that the configuration $a_r<a_s<b_r<b_s$ does not occur. We let $\eldomain{2N}$ be the collection of exterior link pattern decorated marked domains.
\item Suppose that $(D;\ul{x}) \in \markeddomain{2N}$, and we have a non-crossing collection of paths $\ul{\eta} = (\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_N)$ in $D$ where each $\eta_i$ connects a distinct pair of marked points. We will also consider the planar link pattern $\alpha$ on the interior of $D$ induced by the paths $\ul{\eta}$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition 8 of arXiv:2512.04807

body:
[Lem 57 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any $\star$ as in \eqref{e:star.options} and $\mu \in \sM^\star(\alpha,q_0)$, we have
        \[\|\mu\|_{L^2}^2 \le
    \frac{10}{\alpha}
    +6 + O(\epsilon)\,.\]
\begin{proof}
Let $X$ be given by \eqref{e:formal.sde.main}. Let us write
$X(1)= X(q_*)+\textup{(a)}+\textup{(b)}$ where (a) denotes the drift term and (b) denotes the martingale term.
We have $\bbE[X(q_*)^2] \le \epsilon$ under either of the initialization conditions \ref{it:6.1} or \ref{it:6.2}. Next, using the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, we have
    \begin{align*}
    \E[\textup{(a)}^2]
    &= \E\bigg[
    \bigg(\int_{q_*}^1
    p'(t)^{1/2} b_t\,dt\bigg)^2
    \bigg]
    \le \E\bigg[
    \bigg(\int_{q_*}^1 p'(t)\,dt\bigg)
    \bigg(\int_{q_*}^1 (b_t)^2 \,dt
        \bigg)\bigg]
    \le
    \int_{q_*}^1 \E[(b_t)^2] \,dt\\
    &\le \int_{q_*}^1 \Cost(t)\,dt
    \le \int_{q_*}^1 \budget(t;\alpha)\,dt + \epsilon
    \le \frac{1+\epsilon}{\alpha} + \epsilon\,,
    \end{align*}
where the last two inequalities hold under any of the budget conditions
\ref{it:4.1}, \ref{it:4.2}, or \ref{it:4.3}
combined with either condition
\ref{it:2.1} or \ref{it:2.2}. Lastly, we have from \eqref{e:loc.mg.L2.bounded} that 
    \[
    \E[\textup{(b)}^2]
    \le \int_{q_*}^1 s(t)^2
    \E[(\sigma_t)^2] \,dt
    \le 2\bigg\{ \frac{1+\epsilon}{\alpha}
        + \epsilon + 1\bigg\}\,.\]
Combining the above bounds gives altogether
    \[
    \E[X(1)^2]
    \le 3\bigg\{
    \E[X(q_*)^2]
    +\E[\textup{(a)}^2]
    +\E[\textup{(b)}^2]\bigg\}
    \le 3\bigg\{
    \frac{3(1+\epsilon)}{\alpha}
    +2 + 4\epsilon\bigg\}\,,
    \]
proving the claim.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 57 of arXiv:2608.29416

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.30752, '2608.30752'] Assume that \(u_0\) satisfies the filling hypothesis.  Then there exists
\(K_E\ge1\), depending only on \(M,g,u_0,\mathfrak F\), and \(S\), such
that, for every Teichm\"uller geodesic
\(\gamma\colon I\to\mathcal T(S)\) and every

  \max\bigl\{
    \mathcal E_{u_0}(\gamma(s)),
    \mathcal E_{u_0}(\gamma(r))
  \bigr\}.
  
\end{equation}
Equivalently, \(\log\mathcal E_{u_0}\) is additively quasi-convex along
Teichm\"uller geodesics. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop analytic of arXiv:2411.12149, 'Airy limit for $\beta$-additions through Dunkl operators'] For integers $1\le i\le N$, let $x^N_i \in \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $x^N_i\ge x^N_{i+1}$ for each $1\le i \le N-1$.
Suppose there exists an increasing sequence of positive integers $N_1<N_2<\cdots$, such that for any $\alpha\in\mathbb{N}$ or $\alpha^{-1}\in\mathbb{N}$, as $k\to\infty$, the sum $\sum_{i=1}^{N_k} M[x_i^{N_k},\alpha,N_k]$ converges to a limit in $\mathbb{R}$, and $\sum_{i=1}^{N_k} M_+[x_i^{N_k},\alpha,N_k]$ is bounded by a constant independent of $k$ (but might depend on $\alpha$).
Then for each $i\in\mathbb{N}$, as $k\rightarrow\infty$, $x_i^{N_k}$ converges in $\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}$ to some limit $x_{i}$, and 
for any $\alpha>0$,
$$\sum_{i=1}^{N_k} M[x_i^{N_k},\alpha,N_k]\to \sum_{i=1}^\infty \exp(\alpha x_i).$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop analytic of arXiv:2411.12149

[Lemma 10 (Ambient equivalence for the localized integral) of arXiv:2606.07931, 'Pointwise Complexity for Gaussian Fields:\\Upper Envelopes, Algorithmic Lower Bounds, and '] Let \((T,d)\) be a finite metric space and let \(H\subseteq T\). Let \(p:T\to H\) be a nearest-point selector, so that \(d(y,p(y))=\min_{h\in H}d(y,h)\), and let \(\mu_H=p_\#\mu\) be the pushforward of an ambient prior \(\mu\in\Delta(T)\). Then, for every \(x\in H\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
\mu_H(B_d(x,2\varepsilon))\ge \mu(B_d(x,\varepsilon)).
\]
Consequently, for the localized functional \(\Phi\) in \eqref{eq:pointwise-phi-def},
\begin{equation}
\Phi_{\mu_H}(x)\le 2\Phi_\mu(x),
\qquad x\in H.
\end{equation}

Let $S_R$ be the spatial statistic of the stochastic heat equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d \in \{1, 2\}$) with flat initial data $u(0, x) \equiv 1$, smooth $g \in C_b^2(\mathbb{R})$, and Gaussian noise. Let $X$ be the limiting Gaussian process in $K = L^2([0, T])$ with covariance $Q(s, t) = \lim_{R \to \infty} \operatorname{Cov}(S_R(s), S_R(t))$. Then $d_2(S_R, X) \le C R^{-d/2}$ as $R \to \infty$.

[Proposition prop:remainder of arXiv:2608.27828, 'Scaling limit of the 3D abelian Yang--Mills Langevin dynamics'] Fix $T>0$ and $M,r\ge1$.
Suppose that, almost surely,
\begin{equ}
  \|\theta^\varepsilon(0)\|_{\mathcal C^\eta_\varepsilon}
  \le M,
 \qquad
  -\frac23+\frac53\kappa < \eta.
\end{equ}
There exist constants $C_{M,T}<\infty$ and
$\varepsilon_0=\varepsilon_0(M,T, r)>0$ such that for every
$\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$, on the event $\Omega_{r,\varepsilon}(T)$ from (equation eq:GoodEvent of the paper) we have
\begin{equ}[e:no-exit]
  \widehat\tau_\varepsilon>T
\end{equ}
and
\begin{equ}[eq:v-apriori-final]
  \|\widehat v^\varepsilon\|_
  {\mathcal C^{4\kappa,T}_{0,\varepsilon}}
  \le
  C_{M,T}\varepsilon^{\kappa/2}r^5.
\end{equ}
Consequently,
$\widehat \theta^\varepsilon$ agrees with the original
Langevin process $\theta^\varepsilon$ on $[0,T]$ and $\tau_\varepsilon>T$ on $\Omega_{r,\varepsilon}(T)$.

[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] Let $S,T \in \Sym(\Hcal)$ be compact, with eigenvalues $\{\alpha_k\}_{k \in \Nbb}$, $\{\beta_k\}_{k \in \Nbb}$
	and corresponding orthonormal eigenvectors $\{\phi_k\}_{k \in \Nbb}$, $\{\psi_k\}_{k \in \Nbb}$, respectively.
	Let $A \in \Sym(\Hcal)$.
	Then $\forall u,v \in \Hcal$,
	\begin{align}
		\la Su, ATv\ra = \sum_{k,j=1}^{\infty}\alpha_k\beta_j \la u,\phi_k\ra\la v, \psi_j\ra \la \phi_k, A\psi_j\ra.
	\end{align}
title: Lemma 21 of arXiv:2506.10494

body: Let (X_n)_{n=0}^N be a submartingale with respect to a filtration (F_n), and for real numbers a < b let U_N[a,b] denote the number of upcrossings of the interval [a,b] by X_0, ..., X_N, that is, the number of disjoint time intervals during which the process passes from at or below a to at or above b. Then E[U_N[a,b]] <= E[(X_N - a)^+] / (b - a), where x^+ = max(x, 0). This bound is the key step in the proof of the martingale convergence theorem. [Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples]
title: Doob's Upcrossing Inequality
