[Lemma lem:necessary of arXiv:2608.23765, '\texorpdfstring{Tight Majorizations and Convergence Rates\\ of Nuclear Norm Minimization I'] Let $\varepsilon > 0$ and let $\mathbf{X}\in\R^{d_1\times d_2}$ have the full singular value decomposition $\mathbf{X}=\mathbf{U}_{\mathbf{X}} \diag(\boldsymbol{\sigma}) \mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{X}}^\top$ of (def:optimalweightoperator of the paper),
	with singular values
	$\sigma_1 \geq \ldots \geq \sigma_d \geq 0$.
	Let $Q_\varepsilon(\cdot\mid \mathbf{X})$ be the quadratic model
	\begin{equation*}
	Q_\varepsilon(\mathbf{X}+\mathbf{\Delta}\mid \mathbf{X})
	=
	\mathcal{J}_{\varepsilon}(\mathbf{X})
	+\langle \nabla \mathcal{J}_{\varepsilon}(\mathbf{X}),\mathbf{\Delta}\rangle_F
	+\tfrac12\langle \mathbf{\Delta}, \W{\mathbf{X}}{\varepsilon} (\mathbf{\Delta}) \rangle_F,
	\end{equation*}
	where $\W{\mathbf{X}}{\varepsilon}$ is the weight operator (eq:W:operator:action of the paper) associated to a
	weight operator core matrix $\mathbf{H}_{\boldsymbol{\sigma}, \varepsilon} \in \R^{d_1 \times d_2}$ that is symmetric in the sense that
	$(\mathbf{H}_{\boldsymbol{\sigma}, \varepsilon})_{ij} = (\mathbf{H}_{\boldsymbol{\sigma}, \varepsilon})_{ji}$ for all $i,j \in [d]$.
	Assume that $Q_\varepsilon(\cdot\mid \mathbf{X})$ majorizes $\mathcal{J}_{\varepsilon}$ locally around $\mathbf{X}$,
	i.e.,
	there exists $\delta>0$ such that
	\begin{equation} 
	\mathcal{J}_{\varepsilon}(\mathbf{X}+\mathbf{\Delta})\le Q_\varepsilon(\mathbf{X}+\mathbf{\Delta}\mid \mathbf{X})
	\end{equation}
	for all $\mathbf{\Delta}\in\R^{d_1\times d_2}$ with
	$\left\lVert \mathbf{\Delta} \right\rVert_{F} \le \delta$.
	Then for all $i,j \in [d]$
	such that $i \neq j$, $\sigma_i>\varepsilon$ and $\sigma_j>\varepsilon$,
	it holds that
	\begin{equation} 
		(\mathbf{H}_{\boldsymbol{\sigma}, \varepsilon})_{ij}\ge  \frac{ 2}{\sigma_i+\sigma_j}.
	\end{equation}

body: Publication record. V. Vu conjectured (Conjecture 9.5 in Recent progress in combinatorial random matrix theory) that the probability that an n x n random sign matrix M_n has all its eigenvalues in the Gaussian integers Z[i] is 2^{-(1+o(1))n^2}. Y. Shmalo, Gaussian-integer spectra of random sign matrices (2026) constructs for every n >= 1 a family F_n of sign matrices with eigenvalues in Z[i] and |F_n| = 2^{ceil(n^2/2)} 3^{floor(n/2)}, so P(Spec(M_n) in Z[i]) >= 3^{floor(n/2)} 2^{-floor(n^2/2)}, which contradicts Conjecture 9.5. A matching upper bound remains open, and the adjacent conjecture for symmetric sign matrices is not settled. Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/gaussian-integer-spectra (commit ab366902fb67). Not refereed.

body:
[Theorem thm:no_symmetrizers_in_interior of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] Let $G$ be a compact group with Haar measure $\mu$ and let $f$ be a probability density with respect to $\mu$. 
If $\inf_{x \in G} f(x) > 0$, 
then $f$ is \emph{not} symmetrization resistant in $G$. 

\begin{proof}
By (lem:f_- and u are symmetrizers of the paper), $f_-$ and the uniform $u$ are both in $\Sym(f)$. 
Without loss of generality we take $\mu(G)=1$. 

In the case $h(f) = h(u)$, we have $h(u) - h(f) = D_{KL}\infdivx{f}{u} \ge 0$, with equality if and only if $f = u$ $\mu$-a.e.. 
Thus $f * g = u * g = u$ for any probability density $g$ on $G$, so this $f$ is not symmetrization resistant. 
Thus we assume $h(f) < h(u)$. 

Define $\varepsilon \coloneqq \inf f_- = \inf f  \in (0,1)$ and $b = \frac{f_- - \varepsilon u}{1-\varepsilon}$. 
Since $b \ge 0$, $b$ is a probability measure, and since the symmetry equations are linear, $b \in \Sym(f)$. 
Thus $f_- = (1-\varepsilon)b + \varepsilon u$. 
Applying concavity of entropy, 
\begin{align*} h(f) 
= h(f_-) 
= h(\varepsilon u + (1-\varepsilon) b)
&\ge \varepsilon h(u) + (1-\varepsilon) h(b) \\
&> \varepsilon h(f) + (1-\varepsilon) h(b) 
\end{align*}
so that $h(f) > h(b)$. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:no_symmetrizers_in_interior of arXiv:2607.29020

[Theorem 21 of arXiv:2609.00448, 'Equivariant formality and representation theory'] Let $G$ be a compact connected Lie group of rank $n$, $S$ a torus subgroup of dimension being $n-1$, $T$ a maximal torus of $G$ containing $S$, $\mu\in \chi(T)$ a primitive character of $T$ such that $S=\text{ker }\mu$, $L$ a primitive weight in the weight lattice $\mathfrak{t}^*_\mathbb{Z}$ corresponding to $\mu$ after exponentiation, and $W$ the Weyl group of $G$. Define
	\[\Phi_L:=\left(\prod_{w\in W/W_{[L]}} wL\right)^{n(L)}\in \text{Sym}^*(\mathfrak{t}^*)^W,\]
	where $W_{[L]}$ is the stabilizer of $[L]:=\{\pm L\}\in \mathfrak{t}^*/\{\pm 1\}$, $n(L)=1$ or 2 depending on whether $\displaystyle\prod_{w\in W/W_{[L]}}wL$ is $W$-invariant or $W$-anti-invariant, i.e. 
	\[\displaystyle w'(\prod_{w\in W/W_{[L]}}wL)=\text{sgn}(w')\prod_{w\in W/W_{[L]}}wL\text{ for all }w'\in W.\] 
	Then $(G, S)$ is isotropy formal if and only if $\Phi_L\notin (f_1, \cdots, f_n)^2$, where $f_1, \cdots, f_n$ are the fundamental $W$-invariant homogeneous polynomials on $\mathfrak{t}$, i.e. $\text{Sym}^*(\mathfrak{t}^*)^W=\mathbb{R}[f_1, \cdots, f_n]$.
title: Theorem 21 of arXiv:2609.00448

Let n >= 5 and let K = Q(a_0, ..., a_{n-1}) be the field of rational functions in independent indeterminates. The general polynomial x^n + a_{n-1} x^{n-1} + ... + a_1 x + a_0 over K is not solvable by radicals: no root of it lies in any radical extension of K (a tower K = K_0 < K_1 < ... < K_m in which each K_{i+1} = K_i(r) with r^{k} in K_i for some k >= 1). The reason is Galois' criterion: a polynomial is solvable by radicals exactly when its Galois group is a solvable group, and the general polynomial has Galois group the full symmetric group S_n over K, which is not solvable for n >= 5. For n <= 4 such formulas exist.

By Galois' criterion (characteristic zero), a polynomial is solvable by radicals if and only if the Galois group of its splitting field is a solvable group. For n >= 5 the alternating group A_n is simple and non-abelian, so S_n has the composition series S_n > A_n > 1 with a non-abelian factor and is not solvable. Hence no radical tower over K contains the splitting field, and no root can lie in a radical extension either, since the normal closure of a radical extension is again radical and would contain the whole splitting field.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:7b09312016e49880ce80485d30f216c41aada6801fe2cca944c4c57a2fc6f66b","revision_digest":"sha256:2256ca4481d9e0acf08c9c091382001ee523cf5d05e7ef315770d80b729f7390","source_id":"wikipedia:Abel–Ruffini theorem","source_revision":"statement authored 2026-08-29 replacing the lead read 2026-08-02","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":["claim_251e809882969d5de60b1b0a4c71da5adc7bc007853471bf362b72b5eb232139"],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body:
[Theorem 35 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let \(Z\) be a connected normal complex space whose dense analytic
regular locus \(\cR\) carries a K\"ahler structure \((g,J)\).  Assume
that the analytic and metric topologies agree, that \(d|_{\cR}\) is the
intrinsic length distance, and that \((Z,d)\) is a complete locally
compact length space equal to the metric completion of \((\cR,g)\).
Assume also that \(Z\) is klt, that \(\omega_g\) extends locally as a
positive current with bounded potential, and that every point has a
local closed holomorphic embedding
\(V\hookrightarrow\Omega_V\subset\C^L\) for which
\begin{equation}
                     \omega_g\ge c_V\omega_{\C^L}
                     \quad\text{on }V\cap\cR.
\end{equation}
Let $G:Z\to\C^r$ be continuous and holomorphic, and
assume on $\cR$ that
\begin{equation}
 \nabla dG^a=0,\qquad
 \left[\langle dG^a,d\overline{G^b}\rangle_{g^{-1}}\right]_{a,b=1}^r
 \text{ is positive definite}.
\end{equation}
Then, after composing \(G\) with an element of
\(\mathrm{GL}(r,\C)\), without translating the target, there is a global
biholomorphic isometry
\begin{equation}
                         Z\cong\C^r\times Z'
\end{equation}
under which $G$ is the projection.  The factor $Z'$ is connected, complete,
normal, and klt; write \(g'\) for its induced regular K\"ahler metric.
It inherits the bounded-local-potential K\"ahler current
and the local ambient metric lower bound of $Z$, and
\begin{equation}
                         \Sing Z=\C^r\times\Sing Z'.
\end{equation}

If, in addition, $f$ is locally Lipschitz on $Z$, smooth on $\cR$, and
satisfies \(\Rc+\nabla^2f=g/2\) on $\cR$, then
\[
                 f(z,y)=\frac{|z|^2}{4}+\ell(z)+f'(y),
\]
where $\ell$ is real affine-linear and $f'$ is locally Lipschitz; if $f$
is proper, then $f'$ is proper.  If also
\begin{equation}
                         \int_{\cR}e^{-f}\,dV_g<\infty,
\end{equation}
then \(\int_{\Reg Z'}e^{-f'}\,dV_{g'}<\infty\).  Finally, assume that
the flow of \(\nabla f\) is complete and preserves \(\cR\), and that its
canonical self-similar maps extend to the metric completions.  Then the
same Euclidean factor is static on every negative-time slice in that
canonical gauge. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
PRIVATE MECHANISM NOTE, author-recorded. On the torus T_{n,d} with volume V, a critical cluster of size V^{2/3} has intrinsic geometry of a critical tree embedded four-dimensionally, so its Euclidean diameter is of order (V^{2/3})^{1/4} = V^{1/6}, while the torus side is V^{1/d}. Since V^{1/6} > V^{1/d} iff d > 6, above six dimensions the window clusters wrap around the torus many times and see the torus uniformly; this is why the exploration process should have the same global (mass-proportional) depletion as in G(n,p), which is what the multiplicative-coalescent scaling limit (Heydenreich-van der Hofstad Open Problems 13.3 and 13.5) needs. The torus plateau theorem (Hutchcroft-Michta-Slade) is the two-point version of this uniformity; the open step is the exploration-level (higher-point) version. Same reason makes eps >> V^{-1/3} lie above the correlation-length crossover eps >> V^{-2/d} for d > 6 (Open Problem 13.2).
Bernoulli percolation on the discrete torus, d > 6
Mean-field cluster geometry (intrinsic diameter m^{1/2}, Euclidean diameter m^{1/4})

body: [Proposition 2.4.3 (Euler 1736) of arXiv:2308.04512, 'An introduction to graph theory'] Let G be a simple graph. Then, the sum of the degrees of all vertices of G equals twice the number of edges of G. In other words, ∑ v∈V(G) deg v = 2 · |E (G)| .

body:
[Lemma 2 of arXiv:2606.08884, 'A Poincar\'e Inequality and Exponential Decay for the Elephant Random Walk'] Conditionally on the event $\{X_t=k\}\cap A_t$, the transition probabilities of the Poissonized elephant random walk satisfy
\[
Q_t^k(1)
=
\frac12+\frac{k\rho}{2a(t)}
\]
and
\[
Q_t^k(-1)
=
\frac12-\frac{k\rho}{2a(t)},
\]
where
\[
\frac1{a(t)}
:=
\sum_{n=\lfloor (1-\varepsilon)\rfloor }^{\lfloor(1+\varepsilon)t\rfloor}
\frac1n
\frac{\mathbb P(n(t)=n,A_t,X_t=k)}
{\mathbb P(A_t,X_t=k)} .
\]
Moreover,
\[
\frac1{\lfloor(1+\varepsilon)t\rfloor}
\le
\frac1{a(t)}
\le
\frac1{\lfloor(1-\varepsilon)t\rfloor},\]
where $\lfloor x \rfloor$ is the integer part of $x$.
title: Lemma 2 of arXiv:2606.08884

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.06317, 'Sharp Tail Bounds Beyond Twice the Mean'] Let $n\in\N$, and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent non-negative random
    variables satisfying $\EE{X_i}\le1$. Then, for every $t\ge2n+1$,
    \[
\PP{\sum_{i=1}^n X_i\ge t} \le 1-\left(1-\frac{1}{t}\right)^n.
\]

Equality is attained by i.i.d.~random variables satisfying
$\PP{X_i=0}=1-1/t$ and $\PP{X_i=t}=1/t$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.06317

[Corollary 6 of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186'] Suppose that the hypotheses in Theorem \ref{Theorem: Main}
hold, and that $\msf T_0(t)$ has the asymptotic expansion in \eqref{Equation: Smooth Heat Trace}.
Let $t_1>t_2>\cdots>0$ be a vanishing sequence of positive numbers.
The following holds for any fixed $\ka>0$:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item If $t_n\leq cn^{-1/2-\eps}$ for some fixed $c,\eps>0$, then
\[\lim_{n\to\infty}2\pi t_n\,\msf T_\ka(t_n)=\msf{A}(D)\qquad\text{almost surely}.\]
\item If $t_n\leq cn^{-1-\eps}$ for some fixed $c,\eps>0$, then
\[\lim_{n\to\infty}4\sqrt{2\pi t_n}\left(\tfrac{\msf{A}(D)}{2\pi}t_n^{-1}-\msf T_\ka(t_n)\right)=\msf{L}(\partial D)\qquad\text{almost surely}.\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 6 of arXiv:2507.06186

[Theorem thm:cox2charac of arXiv:2412.04589, 'Inverting the Markovian projection for pure jump processes'] Let $X$, $\mathbb{G}$, $(J_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}^*}$, $(\tau_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ and $(\lambda^k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}^*}$ be given by Theorem~(thm:cox of the paper). Furthermore, suppose that each $\lambda^k$ is predictable with respect to $\mathbb{G}$. Let $h: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a truncation function. Then, $X$ is a $\mathbb{G}$-It\^o semimartingale whose differential characteristics associated with $h$ are
	\begin{equation*}
		\beta_t = \mathbb{E}[h(J_1)] \lambda_t,\quad
		\alpha_t = 0,\quad
		\kappa_t(d\xi) = \lambda_t \nu(d\xi),
	\end{equation*}
	where $\nu$ is the law of $J_1$ and $\lambda_t \coloneqq \sum_{k=1}^\infty \bm{1}_{\{\tau_{k-1} < t \leq \tau_k\}} \lambda^k_t$.
title: Theorem thm:cox2charac of arXiv:2412.04589

[Theorem main of arXiv:2411.07737, 'On Asymptotic Behavior of Extinction Moment of Critical Bisexual Branching Process in Rand'] Let $N_n$ be a critical BBPRE with $N_0 = N$ pairs satisfying Conditions~(cond:mating-superadditive of the paper)~--~(cond:bbpre-criticality of the paper).
    Then, the extinction moment 
    $
        \tau = \min\{ n \in \mathbb{N} \ \left| \ N_n = 0 \right. \}
    $
    satisfies the relation
    \[
        \frac{ \tau }{ \ln^2 N } \xrightarrow[N \rightarrow \infty]{\mathrm{D}} \chi,
    \]
    where $\chi$ is a r.v. with the density
    \[
        p_{\chi}(t) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \pi \sigma^2 t^3}} \exp\left( -\frac{1}{2 \sigma^2 t} \right) I\{ t \geq 0 \}.
    \]

[Proposition prop:minima-versus-infima-unlabeled-distance of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] Consider a distance \(d\) in \(\mathcal{P}_{\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times [0,1])\) which is:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
		\item Invariant under rearrangements: for every \(\mu,\bar{\mu} \in \mathcal{P}_{\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times [0,1])\) and every \(\varphi \in S_{[0,1]}\), we have that \(d(\mu,\bar{\mu})=d(\mu^{\varphi},\bar{\mu}^{\varphi})\). 
		\item Smooth: for every \((\mu_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\), \(\mu\) in \(\mathcal{P}_{\nu}(\mathcal{X}\times [0,1])\), if \(\mu_n^\xi\to \mu^{\xi}\) narrowly for a.e. \(\xi \in [0,1]\), then \(d(\mu_n,\mu)\to 0\).   
	\end{enumerate}
	Then, the unlabeled version of \(d\) can be equivalently reformulated as
	\[
		\delta(\mu,\bar{\mu})=\inf_{\varphi \in S_{[0,1]}} d(\mu,\bar{\mu}^{\varphi})=\min_{\varphi, \psi \in \bar{S}_{[0,1]}} d(\mu^{\varphi},\bar{\mu}^{\psi}).
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a compactly supported function $f:\mathbb R^N\to\mathbb C$, if we set
$$I_k(f)=\frac{1}{2^{Nk}}\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z^N/2^k}f(x)$$
with $\mathbb Z^N/2^k\subset\mathbb R^N$ being the points having as coordinates integer multiples of $1/2^k$, then
$$I(f)=\lim_{k\to\infty}I_k(f)$$
converges, and $f\to I(f)$ satisfies the assumptions of the Riesz theorem.

body:
Own-work draft, independently checked proof, T326-w697-C03 v1; reviewer urn:mb-agent:d6ca7a10ae76247b PASS on this exact version recorded in AUDITS_FROM_REVIEWER.tsv. Let C be a finite p by p positive semidefinite matrix, J a fixed m by p matrix, and L(v,U)=||(vU-J)C^(1/2)||_F^2/2. Train the scalar v and matrix U by Euclidean gradient flow with v_0>0 and delta=v_0^2-||U_0||_F^2. Assume delta>0, or delta=0 with the strict loss gap L(v_0,U_0)<L(0,0). If P projects onto range C and Q=I-P, put D=delta+||U_0Q||_F^2 and A=||JP||_F^2. Then the flow is global and converges to zero loss with v_infinity=sqrt((D+sqrt(D^2+4A))/2) and effective map G_infinity=JP+v_infinity U_0Q. The case C=0 is constant flow with the same formula. The invariants are v^2-||U||_F^2=delta and UQ=U_0Q. When delta=0, the strict loss gap Delta gives v^2>=Delta/||JC||_F>0; a PL estimate on the positive spectrum of C then proves exponential loss decay. In the square proxy J=I_d, z(w)=w, or augmented proxy J=[I_d,0], z(w)=(w,||w||^2/d+rho), C=(1/M)sum z(w_i)z(w_i)^T, use balanced isotropic initialization v_0=epsilon, U_0=epsilon J/sqrt(d), 0<epsilon<1. The initial effective map is epsilon^2 J/sqrt(d), giving the strict loss gap almost surely for iid Gaussian tasks. The selected map is JP+a_eff JQ, where a_eff=(epsilon/sqrt(d))*sqrt((D+sqrt(D^2+4A))/2), D=epsilon^2(1-A/d). For fixed epsilon and rho>=0, with Gaussian tasks and an independent fresh Gaussian task, M/d->kappa yields normalized new-task excess risk ->(1-kappa)_+; the small-epsilon limit is taken after training. Exactly zero factors are stationary. Balanced factors alone do not ensure convergence: for C=J=1, v_0=epsilon>0 and U_0=-epsilon, the invariant line U=-v gives v'=-v(1+v^2) and converges to the zero saddle. This is a scalar-times-matrix parameterization, not a claim about unrestricted raw K,Q,V training. The proof applies prior balanced-flow ideas and has 413 exact-rational checks plus 31 rational root brackets; no Lean certificate or broad novelty claim is asserted.
Finite-dimensional PSD C; stated Euclidean scalar and matrix coordinates
v_0>0; either positive delta, or balanced delta=0 and a strict initial loss gap
For the task-diversity law: fixed epsilon in (0,1), fixed rho>=0, iid Gaussian task pool and independent fresh Gaussian task, infinite context
Training time tends to infinity before dimension or vanishing initialization

body:
[Lemma 10 (Mixed factorial moments) of arXiv:2604.25877, 'Asymptotic height of Plancherel random trees'] Let $(C_1,\dots,C_m)\sim \mathrm{Ewens}(m,\theta)$.
Fix distinct indices $j_1,\dots,j_r\in\{1,\dots,m\}$ and integers $a_1,\dots,a_r\ge 1$ such that
$
L=\sum_{\ell=1}^r a_\ell j_\ell \le m.
$
Then,
\begin{equation*}
\E\left[\prod_{\ell=1}^r (C_{j_\ell})_{a_\ell}\right]
=
\left(\prod_{\ell=1}^r \left(\tfrac{\theta}{j_\ell}\right)^{a_\ell}\right)\,
\frac{m!}{(m-L)!}\, \frac{\theta^{(m-L)}}{\theta^{(m)}}.
\end{equation*}
In particular, for each $1\le j\le m$,
\begin{align}
    \E[C_j]&=\frac{\theta}{j}\, \frac{m!}{(m-j)!}\,
\frac{\theta^{(m-j)}}{\theta^{(m)}}; \\ 
    \E[(C_j)_2]&=\left(\frac{\theta}{j}\right)^2\, \frac{m!}{(m-2j)!}\,
    \frac{\theta^{(m-2j)}}{\theta^{(m)}},\nonumber
\end{align}
with the convention that the second expression is $0$ if $2j>m$.

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2606.00586, 'Stein's Method for Convergence Rates of Invariant Measures in the Nonlocal-to-Local Limit'] Let $\varphi$ be a non-negative function on $[0,1]$ such that for each $0\leq s<t\leq 1$, $\varphi$ satisfies 
    \[
    \varphi(s)\leq \theta \varphi(t) + \frac{A}{(t-s)^\beta}+B,

    \[
    \varphi(s)\leq C \left[ \frac{A}{(t-s)^\beta}+B \right], \quad 0\leq s<t\leq 1, 
    \]
    where $C$ only depends on $\theta$ and $\beta$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Method: Explicit model calculation, comparison identities and remaining hypothesis obstruction Result: A necessary condition follows by comparing a finite lag with the infinite-lag independent limit: Cov(g(X0),h(Xt))>=0 for every bounded increasing g,h and every t>=0. A simple nonmonotone candidate fails decisively. For the stationary clockwise three-cycle with rate-one jumps and state values0,1,2, the centered state observable has covariance (2/3)*exp(-3t/2)*cos(sqrt3*t/2). At t=2pi/sqrt3 this is negative, so that chain cannot be the desired example. Check: The two nonconstant eigenvalues of the three-cycle generator are -3/2 plus or minus i*sqrt3/2. The centered observable has variance2/3 and equal conjugate Fourier weights; this independently yields the displayed covariance and sign. Obstruction: Positive pairwise association would still be weaker than the required all-dimensional supermodular order. No nonmonotone chain satisfying the full order, or proof that none exists, has been found. Reset chains do satisfy the order but are already stochastically monotone and therefore do not answer the source question.

[Theorem 61 of arXiv:2609.03403, 'Hyperpositive functions, sector bounded functions and a trace formula'] Let $0\le T\le I_m$, and let $F$ be a $\mathbb C^{m\times m}$-valued function analytic in $\mathbb C_r$. The kernel
\[
      K_{T,-1}(z,w)=\frac{F(z)+F(w)^*-T-F(z)TF(w)^*}{z+\overline{w}},
\]
is positive definite in $\mathbb C_r$ if and only if $\det (I_m+F(z))\not= 0$ in $\mathbb C_r$ and the $\mathbb C^{m\times 2m}$-valued function
\begin{equation}
  
  (F(z)+I_m)^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}F(z)&I_m\end{pmatrix}\sqrt{I_m+T}.
\end{equation}
is bounded.

[Theorem 25 (Isserlis) of arXiv:2605.14630, '2605.14630'] For any $1\leqs k\leqs \frac{N}2$, we have 
 \begin{align}
  \bigexpec{X_1\dots X_{2k}} &= 
  \sum_{\cP}
  \;\prod_{\set{i,j}\in\cP} \bigexpec{X_iX_j}\;, \\
  \bigexpec{X_1\dots X_{2k-1}} &= 0\;,
 \end{align} 
where the sum runs over all \emph{perfect matchings} $\cP$ 
of $\intset{1,2k}$, meaning that each $\cP$ is a partition 
$\cP=\set{\set{i_1,j_1},\dots,\set{i_k,j_k}}$ of this set into disjoint subsets 
of two elements.

body:
[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The loops on $\mathbb N$ are counted by the Catalan numbers,
$$L_{2k}=\frac{1}{k+1}\binom{2k}{k}$$
and $\mu$ is the centered measure having these numbers as even moments.

body:
[Proposition 4 of arXiv:2606.07839, 'Bounds on Spectral Gaps for Non-Reversible Markov Chains with Applications to Temporal Dif'] Let $P$ be a Markov kernel with invariant probability distribution $\mu$. 
   Let $\phi_i\in L^2(\mu)$ for $i=1,\ldots,n$ and define the matrices $A$ and $S\in\bbC^{n\times n}$ by:
  \begin{align*}
    A_{ij}&=\langle \phi_i,(P^{(\lambda)}-I)\phi_j\rangle.
  \end{align*}

  
  If the following conditions hold:
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item  $P$ is irreducible,
  \item  
    the functions $\{\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_n\}$ are linearly independent,
  \item  
    the constant function, $\ones$, is not in the span of $\{\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_n\}$,
  \end{enumerate}
  then $A+A^\star$ is negative definite. In particular, $A$ is Hurwitz. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 4 of arXiv:2606.07839

body:
[Theorem thm:phase-transition of arXiv:2509.16541, 'Two-stage Bootstrap Percolation'] For the standard variant, if $q \ll p^2/(\log(1/p))^2$, then
    \[
    \mathbb{P}(\text{the origin is eventually in state 2}\, ) \to 1,
    \]
    and if $q\gg p^2$, then
    \[
    \mathbb{P}(\text{the origin remains forever in state 0}\, ) \to 1.
    \]
    For the modified variant, if $q \ll p^2/(\log(1/p))^2$, then
    \[
    \mathbb{P}(\text{the origin is eventually in state 1}\, ) \to 1,
    \]
    and if $q\gg p^2/\log(1/p)$, then
    \[
    \mathbb{P}(\text{the origin remains forever in state 0}\, ) \to 1.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

    Define also the operator $\mathcal{N}(\phi):= \mathcal{N}(\phi, \Delta \phi)$. Then continuously $\mathcal{N}: V^2\rightarrow V^{-2}$.

[Lemma lem:dgt4-weighted-last-visits of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] Let $X$ be simple random walk started at the origin. For integers
	$0\leq i\leq j$, let
	\[
		I_{i,j}(X)
		\coloneqq
	\mathbf{1}_{\{X_i\ne X_r\text{ for every }r\text{ with }i<r\leq j\}}\, .
	\]
	Then, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, as $n\to\infty$,
	\[
		\max_{0\leq j\leq\lfloor(1-\varepsilon)n\rfloor}
		\mathbf E_0\left|
		G(0,0)\sum_{i=0}^j\frac{I_{i,j}(X)}{n-i}
		+\log\left(1-\frac jn\right)
		\right|\longrightarrow0\, .
	\]

[Lemma 4 (Graph-dependent input bound) of arXiv:2608.16701, 'Order-Sensitive Fast-Synapse Limits in Sparse Excitatory--Inhibitory Threshold--Reset Netw'] Let $M_1,\dots,M_N$ be arbitrary firing counts satisfying
\eqref{eq:firing-bound} through $T$, and set
$H_j=k_{\tau(q_j^N)}*dM_j$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\int_0^T
 \left|
 \sum_{j=1}^N J_{\tau(q_j^N)}
 \left(\frac{a_{ij}^N}{\lambda_N}-\frac1N\right)H_j(t)
 \right|dt
 \le C_{T,\mathrm{data}}\Delta_N,
 
\end{equation}
where the constant may depend on the fixed class, kernel, coupling, and
refractory data, but is independent of the graph and firing histories.

[Definizione 2 of arXiv:2506.11937, 'Random rotational invariance of integration by parts formulas within a Bismut-type approac'] Let $\mu,\sigma$ be previsible path functionals and $ x \in \mathbb{R}^n.$ We say that $ X$ is a solution to the martingale problem $\ (\mu,\sigma\sigma^T)$ starting at $ x$ if $P^x(X_0=x)=1$ and for any $ f \in C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}_+)$
\[ f(X_t,t)-f(x,0)-\int_0^t L_t(f(X_s,s))ds\]
is a martingale w.r.t. $\mathcal{H}^n_t=\sigma(X_s, s \leq t)$, where
\[ L_t= \partial_t + L= \partial_t + \mu \partial + \frac{1}{2} \sigma \sigma^T \partial^2.\]

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:e4633521e14d6567a6da281ce58e450fab7d5e0adf26e189c18d3a7d8dfb73d8","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/e4/e4633521e14d6567a6da281ce58e450fab7d5e0adf26e189c18d3a7d8dfb73d8.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:c59f27348d2e0aa9f0f054c5157629be2c3a81bc165c7cd266472265ac588e4a","bundle_entry_key":"fredholm_alternative","bundle_id":"population.pivot3f-2","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"functional analysis, Riesz–Schauder theory, compact operators","draft":"claude-pivot3f-2/bundle_pivot3f-2.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:analysis.functional.spectral:fredholm-alternative","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"(a) On ker T the operator K is the identity; the identity of a normed space is compact only in finite dimension.
(b) Let Tu_n = f_n → f. Replacing u_n by its component orthogonal to ker T does not change Tu_n. If ||u_n|| were unbounded, pass to a subsequence with ||u_n|| → ∞ and set v_n = u_n/||u_n||: then ||v_n|| = 1, v_n ⊥ ker T and Tv_n → 0; compactness gives Kv_{n_j} → w, so v_{n_j} = Tv_{n_j} + Kv_{n_j} → w, with ||w|| = 1, Tw = 0, w ⊥ ker T - a contradiction. Hence (u_n) is bounded, Ku_{n_j} → z for a subsequence, u_{n_j} = Tu_{n_j} + Ku_{n_j} → f + z =: u, and Tu = f. So range T is closed. For any bounded operator (range T)^⊥ = ker T*; for closed range this gives range T = (ker T*)^⊥, and symmetrically for T*.
(c) Suppose T is injective but not surjective. The subspaces H_m = range(T^m) are closed (T^m = I − compact by the ideal property) and strictly decreasing: H_{m+1} ⊊ H_m, since T is injective and H_1 ⊊ H_0 = H. Choose unit vectors e_m ∈ H_m ∩ H_{m+1}^⊥. For m < l, Ke_m − Ke_l = e_m − (Te_m + e_l − Te_l), and the bracket lies in H_{m+1}, so ||Ke_m − Ke_l|| ≥ 1, contradicting the compactness of K. Conversely if T is surjective then ker T* = (range T)^⊥ = {0}, so T* is injective, hence bijective by what was just proved applied to K*, hence T = (T*)* is bijective. The inverse is bounded by the open mapping theorem (or directly from the closed-range argument).
(d) By (b), codim range T = dim ker T*. Suppose dim ker T > dim ker T*. Choose a bounded finite-rank operator F that vanishes on (ker T)^⊥ and maps ker T ONTO ker T* = (range T)^⊥ (possible because dim ker T ≥ dim ker T*); F is compact, so T + F = I − (K − F) is again identity minus compact. body:
[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The volume and area of the unit sphere in $\mathbb R^N$, given by
$$V=\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)^{[N/2]}\frac{2^N}{(N+1)!!}\quad,\quad 
A=\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)^{[N/2]}\frac{2^N}{(N-1)!!}$$
can be expressed in terms of the gamma function, the formulae being
$$V=\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)^{[N/2]}\frac{2^{(N-1)/2}c}{\Gamma(N/2+1)}\quad,\quad 
A=\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)^{[N/2]}\frac{2^{(N+1)/2}c}{\Gamma(N/2)}$$
with $c=\sqrt{2},\sqrt{\pi}$ for $N$ even, odd, as before.

    of probability measures $\mu$ on $[0,1]$ such that
    $\mu\geq (1-\epsilon)\cdot\diffi x$ (the Lebesgue measure on $[0,1]$)

    Then all distributions in $\calM$ can be coupled together in such a way that:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item If $\mu$ is stochastically dominated by $\nu$, then $X_\mu\leq X_\nu$,
        \item With probability $1-\epsilon$, all the random variables $(X_\mu)_{\mu\in\calM}$ are equal.
    \end{itemize}

body:
[Theorem 4 (Non-equilibrium fluctuations) of arXiv:2607.23640, '{\sl Non-equilibrium fluctuations of a two-species exclusion process with slow boundary }'] Assume that the initial distributions
 	\(\{\mu^n\}_{n\in \mathbb{N}}\) satisfy Assumptions
 	\ref{ass1}--\ref{ass4}.
 	Then the sequence \(\{\mathbb Q_n\}_{n \in \mathbb{N} }\) is tight in
 	\( \mathcal D([0,T],(\mathscr S^\dagger)')\). Moreover, every limit point \(\mathbb Q\) is
 	concentrated on paths \(\{\bm Y_t:0\le t\le T\}\) satisfying the following
 	property.
 	
 	For every \(\bm f\in\mathscr S^\dagger\) and every \(t\in[0,T]\),
 	\[
 	\bm Y_t(\bm f)
 	=
 	\bm Y_0(S_t\bm f)
 	+
 	\mathcal W_t(\bm f),
 	\]
 	where \((S_t)_{t\ge0}\) is the semigroup generated by $ \mathcal A^\dagger =\Delta \mathrm I_2+M^\top $
    on \(\mathscr S^\dagger \), and $ \mathcal W_t(\bm f) $ is a mean zero Gaussian variable of variance
    \[
    \int_0^t
    Q_r\left(
    S_{t-r}\bm f,
    S_{t-r}\bm f
    \right)\,dr.
    \]
 	Moreover, $ \bm Y_0 $ and $ \mathcal W_t $ are uncorrelated in the sense that $ \mathbb{E}  \left[ \bm Y_0(\bm f)\mathcal W_t(\bm g)  \right] = 0 $ for all $ \bm f,\bm g \in \mathscr{S}^{\dagger } $. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\mathcal{H}^{(t)} \begin{bmatrix}
\bm{b}\\
\bm{a}

$$

[Lemma 32 of arXiv:2609.02105, 'Contact fundamental forms and \\ adjoint varieties'] Let $(M,H\subset TM)$ be a contact manifold, and let
$\fc$ be the Lie algebra of all contactomorphic  vector fields.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] If $\psi:M\to M$ is a contact automorphism, then
$\psi_*:H^0(M,TM)\to H^0(M,TM)$ induces a Lie algebra automorphism of
$\fc$.
\item[(ii)] Under the isomorphism $\fc \simeq H^0(M,TM/H)$ in Theorem \ref{t.Ko}, the
subalgebra of contactomorphic vector fields vanishing at $z\in M$ corresponds to
$H^0(M,(TM/H)\otimes\mathbf m_z^2),$
where $\mathbf m_z^2$ is the weighted ideal from Definition \ref{d.CF}.
\end{itemize}

Then the second observation leaves the conditional mean and covariance of X unchanged for every compatible value exactly when D = 0, which in the jointly Gaussian model is exactly conditional independence of X and Y2 given Y1.

body: [Lemma lem:bubble-cle of arXiv:2603.28161, 'Boundary four-point connectivities of conformal loop ensembles'] Suppose $z\in\mathbbm{H}$, and $\Gamma$ is a $\CLE_\kappa$ on $\mathbbm{H}$. [Theorem 1 of arXiv:2604.10891, '2604.10891'] The PGF $q_n^*(z)$ ($n=1,2,\ldots$) satisfies

\begin{equation}
q_n^*(z) 
= 
q_0^*(\psi_n^H(z)) \prod_{k=1}^n \psi_k^V(z)
-
\sum_{j=1}^n 
q_{n-j}^*(0) \big( 1 - \psi_j^H(z) \big) \prod_{k=1}^j \psi_k^V(z),
\quad 
n=1,2,\ldots,

\end{equation}

where $\psi_n^H(z)$ and $\psi_n^V(z)$ ($n=1,2,\ldots$) are defined
recursively as

\begin{align}
\psi_1^H(z) 
&=
a_H^*(z),
\qquad
\psi_n^H(z) 
= 
a_H^*\big(\psi_{n-1}^H(z)\big)
=
\psi_{n-1}^H\big(a_H^*(z)\big),
\quad 
n=2,3,\ldots,

\\
\psi_1^V(z) 
&=
a_V^*(z), 
\qquad 
\psi_n^V(z) = a_V^*\big(\psi_{n-1}^H(z)\big),
\quad 
n=2,3,\ldots.

\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2604.10891

body:
[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2605.02771, 'Universality in Deep Neural Networks:\\ An approach via the Lindeberg exchange principle'] Fix \(\alpha\in\{1,2,3,4\}\) and \(x\in\R^{n_0}\).
Assume that the infinite-width covariances are non-degenerate on the singleton input set \(\{x\}\) in the sense of \cite{trevisan2023widedeepneuralnetworks}.
Let
\[
\Phi_\alpha(u_1,\dots,u_\alpha):=\prod_{r=1}^\alpha \sigma(u_r)^2.
\]
Then there exists a constant \(C_{\alpha,x}<\infty\), independent of the widths \(n_1,\dots,n_{L-1}\), such that for every \(\alpha\)-tuple \((i_1,\dots,i_\alpha)\) of pairwise distinct indices in \(\{1,\dots,n_L\}\),
\begin{equation}
\left|
\E\Bigl[\Phi_\alpha\bigl(z^{(L;1)}_{i_1}(x),\dots,z^{(L;1)}_{i_\alpha}(x)\bigr)\Bigr]
-
\E\Bigl[\Phi_\alpha(G_1,\dots,G_\alpha)\Bigr]
\right|
\le
C_{\alpha,x}\sum_{k=1}^{L-1}\frac{1}{n_k},
\end{equation}
where \(G_1,\dots,G_\alpha\) are i.i.d. centered Gaussian random variables with variance \(\Kcal^{(L)}(x)\).
metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:6766910bb4e936f09b9cb681da2c7391359a15e283f1531baf36973446281222","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/67/6766910bb4e936f09b9cb681da2c7391359a15e283f1531baf36973446281222.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:9fc897373b66a14c7407af418096e5cc44adf40ba811f2ddc5341de03a994166","bundle_entry_key":"2605-02771-lemma-13-gaussian-hidden-layer-to-gp","bundle_id":"population.tex-extract-s3_025","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"tex-extract-20260907/bundle_s3_025.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:harvest.arxiv.mathematics:arxiv-2605-02771-lemma-13-gaussian-hidden-layer-to-gp","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Paper's own proof, opening: Since \(\sigma\in C_b^{3\cdot 2^{L-1}}(\R;\R)\), the function \(\Phi_\alpha\) is bounded and Lipschitz on \(\R^\alpha\).
Fix pairwise distinct indices \(i_1,\dots,i_\alpha\), and consider the random vector
\[
U_I(x):=\bigl(z^{(L;1)}_{i_1}(x),\dots,z^{(L;1)}_{i_\alpha}(x)\bigr).
\]
Because the rows of each Gaussian weight matrix are i.i.d., \(U_I(x)\) has the same law as the output at layer \(L\) of a fully Gaussian network of depth \(L\), evaluated at the single input \(x\), with output dimension \(\alpha\).
The corresponding Gaussian-process limit is the vector \((G_1,\dots,G_\alpha)\), whose coordinates are independent and distributed as \(\mathcal N(0,\Kcal^{(L)}(x))\).

body: The variance of X is Var(X) = E[(X - E[X])^2] = E[X^2] - E[X]^2, the mean squared deviation; its square root is the standard deviation. Var(aX + b) = a^2 Var(X). The covariance Cov(X,Y) = E[(X-EX)(Y-EY)] = E[XY] - E[X]E[Y] measures joint variation; Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) + 2Cov(X,Y), so variances add for uncorrelated (in particular independent) variables. The correlation is Cov(X,Y)/(sd(X) sd(Y)) in [-1, 1].
title: Variance and Covariance

body:
Lyons and Peres, Probability on Trees and Networks (version 19 August 2026), Question 17.18 (p. 575) asks whether a consistent equivariant flow rule admitting a stationary measure EQUIVALENT to Galton-Watson measure must induce an ergodic Markov chain; their Proposition 17.17 proves it when all child weights are strictly positive, and Exercise 17.22 gives a non-ergodic example whose stationary measure is only absolutely continuous, so equivalence is the point of the question. Our result (id P0033, 2026-09-08): NO. Take Galton-Watson with P(D=2) = 3/5, P(D=3) = 2/5 (mean 12/5) and an isomorphism-invariant colour in {0,1} defined by AND at two-child vertices and OR at three-child vertices; both preserve unanimity, so every vertex has at least one child of its own colour, and the flow chooses uniformly among those. Galton-Watson measure is stationary, the root colour is invariant along the chain and takes each value with probability 1/2 - a non-constant invariant function, hence no ergodicity - and the stationary measure equals Galton-Watson measure, trivially equivalent to it. The colour exists because F(p) = (3/5) p^2 + (2/5)[1 - (1-p)^3] fixes 1/2, and r_n = E[q_n^2] satisfies r_{n+1} = 3/10 + (3/5) r^2 + (2/5) r^3 whose increment factors as (r - 1/2)[(2/5) r^2 + (4/5) r - 3/5], driving r_n from r_0 = 1/4 up to 1/2 and giving E[q(1-q)] = 0. Verification as the source words it: the step the proof leaves implicit, and which was checked, is that Galton-Watson really is stationary - it holds because, conditioned on the children's colours, the child subtrees are independent, each distributed as Galton-Watson conditioned on its own colour, so the chosen subtree is exactly GW given colour = c, the uniform choice adds no bias, and mixing over c returns GW. Prior art unchecked; the tree-automaton and factor-of-iid literature is where to look.

consistent equivariant flow rule choosing uniformly among same-coloured children

body:
[Proposition 20 of arXiv:2607.11756, 'Full replica symmetry breaking in the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model'] Let $\nu$ be a Borel probability measure on $[0,1]$, and write
\[
 \alpha_\nu(s)=\nu([0,s]),\qquad u=u_\nu.
\]
Let $X^\nu$ be the optimal diffusion
\[
 \dd X_s^\nu
 =\beta^2\alpha_\nu(s)u_x(s,X_s^\nu)\dd s+\beta\dd W_s,
 \qquad X_0^\nu=0.
\]
For every $s>0$, the law of $X_s^\nu$ has a strictly positive
$C^\infty$ density $p_\nu(s,\cdot)$. Define
\begin{equation}
 r_\nu(s,x)
 =\exp\{-\alpha_\nu(s)u(s,x)\}p_\nu(s,x),
 \qquad
 V_\nu(s,x)=-\log r_\nu(s,x).
\end{equation}
Then, for every $s>0$,
\begin{equation}
 r_\nu(s,x)
 =g_{\beta^2s}(x)
 \E_{\mathrm{br}}\exp\left\{
 -\int_{[0,s]}
 u\left(t,\frac tsx+\beta\mathfrak b_t^{\,s}\right)
 \nu(\dd t)
 \right\}.
\end{equation}
If $\alpha_\nu\equiv m$ on an open interval $(a,b)$, then
\begin{equation}
 (r_\nu)_s=\frac{\beta^2}{2}(r_\nu)_{xx}
 \qquad\text{on }(a,b)\times\R.
\end{equation}
If $q\in(0,1]$ is an atom of $\nu$ of size $c=\nu(\{q\})$, then
\begin{equation}
 r_\nu(q,x)=\e^{-cu(q,x)}r_\nu(q-,x),
\end{equation}
where
\[
 r_\nu(q-,x)
 =\e^{-\alpha_\nu(q-)u(q,x)}p_\nu(q,x).
\]
Finally, $r_\nu(s,\cdot)$ is even and log-concave, and
\begin{equation}
 (V_\nu)_x(s,x)\ge0,
 \qquad
 (V_\nu)_{xx}(s,x)\ge0,
 \qquad
 (V_\nu)_{xxx}(s,x)\le0,
 \qquad x>0.
\end{equation}
By parity,
\[
 (V_\nu)_x(s,0)=(V_\nu)_{xxx}(s,0)=0.
\]

Let G be an infinite countable vertex-transitive graph of bounded degree with Bernoulli bond percolation, adjacency operator A on l2(V), a=||A||>0, and critical threshold p_c<1. If the two-point kernel T_{p_c}(x,y)=P_{p_c}(x connected to y) defines a bounded l2 operator with norm M<infinity, then for p_c<=q<min(1,p_c+1/(aM)), ||T_q||<=M/[1-aM(q-p_c)]. Consequently p_c<p_{2->2}<=p_u.

[Defn 4 of arXiv:2604.12233, 'An upper bound on the smallest singular value of dense random combinatorial matrices'] For parameters $\delta, \rho \in (0,1)$, let $\mbox{Cons}_{\delta, \rho}\subset \S^{n-1}$  be the set of vectors 
    $v\in \S^{n-1}$ for which there exists a real number $\lambda$ such that $|v_i-\lambda|\leq \rho/\sqrt{n}$ holds for 
    at least $(1-\delta)n$ coordinates $i\in [n]$. A vector $v\in \S^{n-1}$ is called non-almost constant if it does 
    not belong to $\mbox{Cons}_{\delta, \rho}$.

body:
[Lem lemma:free-energy-random-ferro of arXiv:2608.06500, 'Free energy of Ising models under a spectral condition'] Let $G_N^{(r)}=(\text{\boldmath $A$}_N^{(r)},{\boldsymbol 0})$ be a sequence of random
$k$-regular graphs ($k\ge 3$) distributed according to the
configuration model, with constant edge weight $\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, and let
$F^{(r)}_N(\gamma)$ be the free energy density of the shifted graph
$G_N^{(r)}(\gamma)$. If $|\beta|<1/(4\sqrt{k-1})$, then there exists
$\eta=\eta(\beta,k)>0$ such that

\begin{align}
|\gamma-k\beta|<\eta\;\; \Rightarrow\;\;
\lim_{N\to\infty}F^{(r)}_{N}(\gamma)= \phi(\beta) \mbox{ a.s.}\, .
\end{align}

If $\beta\ge0$, then we may take $\eta=1/(4\sqrt{k-1})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem lemma:free-energy-random-ferro of arXiv:2608.06500

body: In mathematics, the concept of a measure is a generalization and formalization of geometrical measures and other common notions, such as magnitude, mass, and probability of events. These seemingly distinct concepts have many similarities and can often be treated together in a single mathematical context. Measures are foundational in probability theory, integration theory, and can be generalized to assume negative values, as with electrical charge. Far-reaching generalizations of measure are widely used in quantum physics and physics in general.

[Definition def:trajectory of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a positive integer~$j$. Fix a send sequence~$\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$, a non-negative integer~$\tau$, and a $\lambda\in (0,1)$. 
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a distribution with support $(\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0})^j$.
Let $Y$ be a $j$-jammed process with send sequence~$\overline{p}$, start time~$\tau$, birth rate~$\lambda$, and initial population size distribution~$\mathcal{P}$.
Let $t\geq\tau$ be an integer.

A \emph{ball trajectory} up to time~$t$ is a 
tuple \newsym{tr}{ball trajectory up to time $t$}{\overline{\mathrm{tr}}  := ({\mathrm{tr}}_\tau,\ldots,{\mathrm{tr}}_t)} of integers in $\{0, \ldots, j+1\}$ 
such that
$\mathrm{tr}_\tau \leq j$ and, for all $t' \in \{\tau+1,\ldots,t\}$,
$\mathrm{tr}_{t'} \in 
\{\mathrm{tr}_{t'-1}, \mathrm{tr}_{t'-1} + 1\}$.  
 

For any $t'\in \{\tau,\ldots,t\}$ such that ${\mathrm{tr}}_{t'} \in [j]$, a ball following trajectory~$\overline{\mathrm{tr}}$ is in  $\mathbf{b}_{{\mathrm{tr}}_{t'}}^Y(t')$.
If  ${\mathrm{tr}}_{t'} = 0$, then the ball is born after time~$t'$ -- that is, there is a $t''>t'$ such that the ball is in $\mathbf{n}^Y(t'')$.
If ${\mathrm{tr}}_{t'} = j+1$, then the ball sends from bin~$j$ (and leaves the system) by time~$t'$ -- that is, there is a $t'' \leq t'$ such that the ball is in $\mathbf{s}_j^Y(t'')$.

 
 
For every   integer~$t\geq \tau$ and every
$x\in \{0,\ldots,j+1\}$, let 
\newsym{T-x-t}{set of ball trajectories ending in bin $x$}{\mathcal{T}^Y(x,t)} be the set of all ball trajectories up to time~$t$ 
with ${\mathrm{tr}}_t = x$. 
Let 
\newsym{T-x}{set of ball trajectories}{\mathcal{T}^Y(t)} be the set of all ball trajectories up to time~$t$, that is $\mathcal{T}^Y(t) = \cup_{x\in \{0,\ldots,j+1\}} \mathcal{T}^Y(x,t)$.
For $\mathrm{tr} \in \mathcal{T}^Y(t)$, let 
\newsym{b-tr}{set of balls following a trajectory}{\mathbf{b}^Y_\mathrm{tr}} be the set of balls that follow trajectory~$\mathrm{tr}$ and let 
\newsym{b-tr-2}{$|\mathbf{b}^Y_\mathrm{tr}|$}{b^Y_\mathrm{tr}} be  $|\mathbf{b}^Y_\mathrm{tr}|$.
title: Definition def:trajectory of arXiv:2602.21315

[Thrm 2 of arXiv:2604.17732, 'Exact Simulation from Tempered Stable Distributions with Infinite Variation ($\alpha\ge1$)'] Fix $\epsilon\in(0,1)$ and set
$$
m_\epsilon^* = (\ell\epsilon)^{-(\alpha-1)} \frac{\alpha}{|\cos(\pi\alpha/2)|} \ \  \mbox{and} \ \  m_\epsilon^\sharp = \max\{m_\epsilon^*,1\}.
$$
1. For $x\le m^\sharp_\epsilon$ and $- \frac{\pi}{2}<\theta\le \frac{\pi}{2}$, we have
$$
g^*(x,\theta) \le C_{1} f^*(x,\theta),
$$
where
$$
C_{1}  = C e^{m_\epsilon^\sharp/\ell}.
$$
2.  For $x\ge m_\epsilon^\sharp$ and $-\theta_0<\theta\le \frac{\pi}{2}$, we have
$$
g^*(x,\theta) \le C_{2} \frac{\alpha}{\pi} e^{-\xi_\epsilon(\theta)(x-m_\epsilon(\theta))^2/2}\sqrt{\frac{2\xi_\epsilon(\theta)}{\pi}} ,
$$
where
$$
m_\epsilon(\theta) = \left(\frac{\alpha-1}{\ell \epsilon V(\theta)\alpha}\right)^{\alpha-1}, \ \ \ 
\xi_\epsilon(\theta) = (V(\theta))^{\alpha-1} \frac{(\epsilon\alpha)^{\alpha-1}}{(\alpha-1)^\alpha}\ell^{-(2-\alpha)},
$$
and
$$
C_{2} = C^{1-\epsilon^{1-\alpha}}  \sqrt \pi \frac{(\epsilon\alpha)^{(1-\alpha)/2}}{(\alpha-1)^{1-\alpha/2}} \left(\frac{3-\alpha}{e(1-\epsilon)}\right)^{\frac{3-\alpha}{2}} \ell^{1-\alpha/2} 2^{-(4-\alpha)/2}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 9 (The Haar law on a fixed-degree distinguished-factor component) of arXiv:2608.06576, 'The Resultant Distribution Method: Universality for $p$-adic Random Matrices and Polynomia'] Fix $i\in\Z_{>0}$ and $r\geq 0$. Let
$$
\mathcal{C}_{i,r}
:=
\left\{
Q\in\Z_p[x]:
Q\text{ is monic},
\deg Q=rd_i,
\bar Q=F_i^r
\right\},
$$
and let $\mu_{i,r}$ denote the normalized Haar probability measure on
$\mathcal{C}_{i,r}$ under the natural coefficient identification
$$
\mathcal{C}_{i,r}\cong F_i^r+p\Z_p^{rd_i}.
$$
Then, for every $n\geq 1$, the restriction of the law of
$P_n^{\Haar,\{i\}}$ to $\mathcal{C}_{i,r}$ on the event
${\bar P_n^{\Haar}\neq 0}$ is a constant multiple of $\mu_{i,r}$.
More precisely, for every Borel set $\mathcal{A}\subset\mathcal{C}_{i,r}$,
$$
\mathbf{P}\left(
P_n^{\Haar,\{i\}}\in A,
\bar P_n^{\Haar}\neq 0
\right)=
\mathbf{P}\left(
P_n^{\Haar,\{i\}}\in\mathcal{C}_{i,r},
\bar P_n^{\Haar}\neq 0
\right)
\mu_{i,r}(\mathcal{A}).
$$

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.27374, '\Large \bf Distribution-constrained optimal multiple stopping: the Root-type solution'] Let $\boldsymbol{\mu}_n=(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_n)$ be continuous probability measures on $\R_+$ with finite first moments and in stochastic order.
     Then
$$
(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_n)\, \mbox{solves}\,\mbox{ConsStop}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_n).
$$
Moreover, for $k=1,\dots,n$,
$$
u^k(t,x)=\P(\sigma_k>t,\;X_t>x),
\qquad (t,x)\in [0,\infty)\times\R.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.27374

[Corollary cor:one-dimensional-induced-space of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] The family $(Q_z)_{z\in Z}$ is Borel, $\Gamma$-equivariant and
uniformly Delone. It satisfies
\[
    \widehat{\delta}_{Q_z}
    =
    \frac{4}{a}\delta_0
    \qquad\text{on }
    \left(-\frac1a,\frac1a\right),
\]
and
\[
    Q_w=Q_z-u
    \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
    u\in\Gamma
    \ \text{ and }\
    w=u.z.
\]
Consequently, $(\operatorname{Ind}_{\Gamma}^{\mathbb R}(Z),\mu_{\Gamma,Z})$
admits a generating stealthy Delone cross-section.

[Theorem 2 (Gaussian bounded-differences inequality) of arXiv:2605.27563, '\textbf{On the Subgaussianity of Quantized Linear Maps: \\ An AI-Assisted Note}'] Let $X\sim\mathcal N(\mu,\Sigma)$ be an $n$-dimensional Gaussian vector with non-singular covariance matrix $\Sigma$. Let $f:\R^n\to\R$ have
bounded-differences constants $b=(b_1,\ldots,b_n)$. Then,
\[
\|f(X) - \E f(X)\|_{\psi_2} \le C \sqrt{\kappa(\Sigma)}\|b\|_2,
\]
where $C>0$ is an absolute constant. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 46 (Score-density sufficient condition) of arXiv:2608.07820, 'Linear Spectral Statistics for Entrywise-Transformed Spiked Wigner Matrices under Shifted '] Assume \(f\in L^4(\nu)\), \(\E_\nu f=0\),
\(\E_\nu f^2=1\), and that \(p\) is twice weakly differentiable.  In the
weighted norms
\[
        \|u\|_{f,1}:=\E_\nu |f(\zeta)|\,|u(\zeta)|,
        \qquad
        \|u\|_{f^2,1}:=\E_\nu |f(\zeta)|^2|u(\zeta)|,
\]
one has
\[
        \left\|\frac{p(\cdot-s)}{p(\cdot)}-1+s\frac{p'}{p}\right\|_{f,1}=o(|s|)
\]
and
\[
        \left\|\frac{p(\cdot-s)}{p(\cdot)}-1+s\frac{p'}{p}-\frac{s^2}{2}\frac{p''}{p}\right\|_{f^2,1}=o(s^2).
\]
Assume also \(\sup_{|s|\le s_0}\int |f(y)|^4p(y-s)\,dy<\infty\), with uniform integrability as \(s\to0\).  Then the weighted likelihood-ratio criterion applies with
\[
        \ell_1=-\frac{p'}{p},\qquad \ell_2=\frac{p''}{p}.
\]
For the Gaussian density, \(\ell_1(y)=y\) and \(\ell_2(y)=y^2-1\).

Let A be a real m x n matrix and b a vector in R^m. Exactly one of the following holds: (i) there is x in R^n with x >= 0 (componentwise) and A x = b; (ii) there is y in R^m with A^T y >= 0 (componentwise) and b^T y < 0. Equivalent form: b lies in the cone C = { A x : x >= 0 } if and only if b^T y >= 0 for every y with A^T y >= 0. The lemma is the finite-dimensional theorem of the alternative behind linear-programming duality; the nontrivial ingredient is that a finitely generated cone in R^m is closed.

[Corollary cor:spec of arXiv:2512.06984, 'Infinite Dimensional Multifractal Analysis of the Wiener measure'] Let $ \mu$ and $\nu$ be two Borel measures on  a separable metric space $ (X,d) $ and let $ \mathsf{scl} $  be a scaling. 
    \begin{itemize}
    \item[{\rm (1)}] If $\underline{\mathsf{scl}}_{\mathrm{loc}}\mu(x) = \alpha$ $\nu$-a.e., then
    $$
      \mathsf{scl}_H \{x \in X: \underline{\mathsf{scl}}_{\mathrm{loc}}\mu(x) =\alpha\} \ge \mathsf{scl}_H^*\nu . 
    $$
    \item[{\rm (2)}] If $\overline{\mathsf{scl}}_{\mathrm{loc}}\mu(x) = \alpha$ $\nu$-a.e., then
    $$
      \mathsf{scl}_P \{x \in X: \overline{\mathsf{scl}}_{\mathrm{loc}}\mu(x) =\alpha\} \ge \mathsf{scl}_P^*\nu.
    $$
    \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition1 triangulation_with_holes of arXiv:2603.05491, '\textbf{Local limits of uniform triangulations with boundaries in high genus}'] A triangulation with holes is a finite map $t$ with:
\begin{itemize}
	\item[$\bullet$] A set of distinguished faces, called the boundaries (or external faces) $\partial_1,\dots,\partial_{\ell}$, of degrees $p_1,\dots,p_{\ell} \ge 1$, which are vertex-simple (that is, all vertices of $\partial_i$ are distinct) and share no vertices. Each boundary $\partial_i$ is equipped with a distinguished edge $e_i$ such that $\partial_i$ lies to the right of $e_i$.
	\item[$\bullet$] A set of distinguished faces $h_1,\dots,h_{r}$ of degrees $q_1,\dots,q_r \ge 1$, called the holes, which are edge-simple (each $h_i$ is composed of $q_i$ edges) and share no edges.
	\item[$\bullet$] Faces that are neither boundaries nor holes have degree~$3$.
	\item[$\bullet$] The dual $t^{*}$ remains connected when removing the boundaries.
\end{itemize} 
The perimeter of $t$ is the tuple $\mathbf{p} =(p_1,\dots,p_{\ell})$, and the boundary length or total perimeter is $|\mathbf{p}| = p_1+\cdots+p_{\ell}$. Note that in the above definition, boundaries and holes may share vertices and edges. The internal faces of $t$ are the faces that are not boundaries. In particular, holes are internal faces. Similarly, the internal vertices (resp. edges) are the vertices (resp. edges) that do not lie on a boundary.
title: Definition1 triangulation_with_holes of arXiv:2603.05491

[Defn Local sets of arXiv:2602.06011, 'Excursion decomposition of the XOR-Ising model'] A coupling $(\phi,A,\phi_A)$ between a GFF $\phi$ in $D$, a random closed set $A \subset \bar{D}$ and a distribution $\phi_A$ is called a \emph{local set (coupling)} if
\begin{itemize}
    \item the restriction of $\phi_A$ to $D\setminus A$ is almost surely harmonic,
    \item conditionally on $\mathcal F_A := \sigma(A,\phi_A)$, the field
    \[
        \phi^A := \phi - \phi_A
    \]
    is a GFF with zero boundary conditions in $D \setminus A$.
\end{itemize}
title: Local sets

body:
[Prop 8 of arXiv:2509.09589, 'Geometry of critical discrete structures: long-range percolation on the hierarchical latti'] Fix $0< \alpha <d$. 
	For $t>-1$, let
	$
	r_{t}^{\sss(n)}(x, y)
	:=
	(1+t) \cdot \zeta_n^{-1} \cdot J(x, y)
	$, 
	$x, y\in\bT_n^d$.
\begin{enumeratea}
		\item 
		Purely subcritical regime:
		There exists $C>0$ depending only on $d$ such that for any $\eps\in(0, 1)$,
		\begin{align*}
			\pr\big(\hskip0.2pt
			\big| \cC_1^{\sss(n)}\big( r^{\sss(n)}_{-\eps} \big)  \big|
			\leq
			C \eps^{-2}\log n
			\big)
			\to 1 \ \ \text{ as }\ \ n\to\infty.
		\end{align*}
		
		
		
		\item
		Purely supercritical regime:
		Fix $\eps>0$. 
		Then there exists $C>0$ depending only on $\eps,$ $\alpha,$ $A_1, A_2$, and $d$ such that
		\begin{align*}
			\pr\big(\hskip0.2pt
			\big| \cC_1^{\sss(n)}\big( r^{\sss(n)}_{\eps} \big)  \big|
			\geq
			C n^d
			\big)
			\to 1 \ \ \text{ as }\ \ n\to\infty.
		\end{align*}
		
		
		
		
		
		
\end{enumeratea} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 8 of arXiv:2509.09589

body:
[Definition eq:v-grad of arXiv:2505.02685, 'On the Spectral Expansion of Monotone Subsets of the Hypercube'] We say that $F : L^2(V) \to \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ is \emph{Fréchet differentiable} at $f \in L^2(V)$ if there
    exists a bounded linear operator $A : L^2(V) \to \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ such that
    \[
        \lim_{\|h\|_{2} \to 0} \frac{\abs*{F(f+h) - F(f) - Ah}}{\|h\|_{2}} = 0 \,.
    \]
    In this case, we call $DF(f) \vcentcolon= A$ the \emph{Fréchet derivative} of $F$ at $f$. Moreover,
    by the Riesz representation theorem there exists a unique vector $v \in L^2(V)$ satisfying
    \begin{equation}
        
        Ah = \inp{h}{v}
    \end{equation}
    for all $h \in L^2(V)$. We call $\nabla F(f) \vcentcolon= v$ the \emph{gradient} of $F$ at $f$.
    Finally, we say that $F$ is (Fréchet) $C^1$ if it is Fréchet differentiable at every $f \in
    L^2(V)$ and the map $f \mapsto DF(f)$ (from $L^2(V)$ to the space of bounded linear operators
    $L^2(V) \to \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$) is continuous.
title: Fréchet derivative and gradient

[Thm toro of arXiv:2609.03033, 'An Overview of Einstein $4$-Manifolds'] Let  $T^4= S^1 \times S^1 \times S^1\times S^1$ denote  the $4$-torus, just considered   as  a smooth compact $4$-manifold. 
Then every  Einstein metric 
$g$ on $T^4$ is flat. Consequently  every such $(T^4,g)$ is  isometric to   Euclidean $4$-space
${\mathbb R}^4$ divided by a lattice $\Lambda \cong {\mathbb Z}^{\oplus 4}$ of translations, and   the 
moduli space $\mathscr{E}(T^4)$ of Einstein metrics on $T^4$ is therefore   connected. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 39 (Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup) of arXiv:2605.14630, '2605.14630'] The Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup is the one-parameter semigroup 
$\setsuch{T_t}{t\geqs0}$ of contraction operators on $\cH$ defined by 
\begin{equation}
 
 T_t(F) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \e^{-nt}P_n F
\end{equation} 
for any $F\in\cH$, where $P_n:\cH\to\cH_n$ denotes the orthogonal 
projection on the $n$th Wiener chaos.
title: Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup

[Lemma 20 of arXiv:2606.11994, 'Sample Path Properties of the\\ Fractional Wiener--Weierstrass Bridge II'] Let $L\in\N$ be such that $\beta=b^L\ge3$.  Put
$     D_L=\{1,2,\ldots,\beta-2\}
$,
and
\[     S_L=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}\xi_i \beta^{-i}:     \xi_i\in D_L\text{ for every }i\ge1\right\}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}     S_L\subset T_{2L},     
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}     \dimH S_L=\frac{\log(\beta-2)}{\log \beta}.     
\end{equation}
Moreover, for every
\begin{equation}     0<\eta<\frac{\log(\beta-2)}{\log \beta},     
\end{equation}
there is an atomless Borel probability measure $\mu_L$ supported on $S_L$
such that
\begin{equation}     \iint |t-s|^{-\eta}\,\mu_L(\dd t)\mu_L(\dd s)<\infty.     
\end{equation}

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2506.13913, '2506.13913'] {Connection between Brownian motion and the Heat equation}{Conexion-one-dim}
Let \(\{W_t\}_{t \geq 0}\) be a Brownian motion starting at \(x\) defined on a probability space \((\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})\), and assume that \(f \in C(\mathbb{R})\cap L^{\infty}( \mathbb{R})\). Furthermore, consider the heat equation
\begin{equation}
   \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}, \quad x \in \mathbb{R}, \, t > 0,
\end{equation}
with initial condition \(u(x, 0) = f(x)\). Then, it holds that:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item There exists a classical solution \(u \in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R} \times (0, \infty))\) given by
    \[
    u(x, t) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{4\pi t}} \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(y) \exp\left(-\frac{(y - x)^2}{4t}\right) \, dy, \quad t > 0.
    \]
    \item The solution \(u(x, t)\) admits a stochastic representation in terms of Brownian motion:
    \[
    u(x, t) = \mathbb{E}[f(W_t) \mid W_0 = x],
    \]
    where \(\mathbb{E}\) denotes the expectation with respect to the probability measure induced by the Brownian motion \(\{W_t\}_{t \geq 0}\).
\end{enumerate}

[Conj conj-scaling-limit of arXiv:2506.18827, 'Random walk reflected off of infinity, with applications to uniform spanning forests and s'] Let $(\mathcal M_k , \mathcal L_k)$ and $(\Phi,\Gamma)$ be as above. 
For $k\in \mathbbm N$, let $\mathbbm y_k$ be sampled uniformly from $\partial\mathcal M_k$ and let $\mathbbm x_k$ be a point sampled uniformly from the outermost gasket of $(\mathcal M_k , \mathcal L_k)$. Let $H_k : \mathcal V\mathcal M_k \to \overline{\mathbbm D}$ be the Tutte embedding of $(\mathcal M_k , \mathbbm x_k , \mathbbm y_k)$, as in Section~(sec-tutte of the paper). We have the following joint convergence in law as $k\to\infty$. 
\begin{itemize}
\item The counting measure on vertices of $\partial\mathcal M_k$, re-scaled by $1/(2k)$, converges weakly to the LQG length measure $\nu_\Phi$ on $\partial\mathbbm D$. 
\item The loop ensembles $H_k(\mathcal L_k)$ converge to the CLE$_4$ $\Gamma$ with respect to, e.g., the Hausdorff distance on countable collections of loops in $\mathbbm D$ viewed modulo time parametrization (see, e.g.,~[shef-cle]). 
\item  There are deterministic scaling factors $\{\mathfrak b_k\}_{k\geq 1}$ with $\mathfrak b_k = k^{\xi Q / 2 + o(1)}$ such that the graph distance on $H(\mathcal M_k)$, re-scaled by $\mathfrak b_k^{-1}$, converges to the LQG metric $D_\Phi$ with respect to the topology on lower semicontinuous functions\footnote{In order to view the graph distance on $d_k : H_k(\mathcal M_k)$ as a lower semincontinuous function $d_k : \overline{\mathbbm D} \times \overline{\mathbbm D} \to [0,\infty]$, instead of as a function $H_k(\mathcal V\mathcal G_k) \times H_k(\mathcal V\mathcal G_k) \to [0,\infty)$, we can, e.g., proceed as follows. 
Recall the definition of the set $H_k(f) \subset \overline{\mathbbm D}$ for a face $f$ of $\mathcal M_k$ from Section~(sec-tutte of the paper).
For $z,w\in \overline{\mathbbm D}$, we define 
\[
d_k(z,w) = \inf_{f , f' : z \in H_k(f) , w \in H_k(f')} \inf_{x \in \partial f , y \in \partial f'} d_{\mathcal M_k}(x,y) , 
\]
where $d_{\mathcal M_k}$ denotes graph distance and the infimum is over all faces $f,f'$ of $\mathcal M_k$ such that $z \in H_k(f)$ and $w \in H_k(f')$ and all vertices $x$ and $y$ lying on the boundaries of $f$ and $f'$, respectively. Note that the infimum is infinite if one of $z$ or $w$ does not lie in $H_k(f)$ for any face $f$ of $\mathcal M_k$. 
} 
$\overline{\mathbbm D} \times \overline{\mathbbm D} \to [0,\infty]$ (see, e.g.,~[beer-usc] or~[dg-supercritical-lfpp]).  
\item Let $X^k$ be the continuous time random walk on $\mathcal M_k$ reflected off of $\infty$ started from $\mathbbm x_k$ and stopped when it first hits $\partial \mathcal M_k$ (with any choice of rate function satisfying the condition of Theorem~(thm-cont-time-walk of the paper)). Then $H_k(X^k)$ converges with respect to the topology on curves viewed modulo time parametrization~[ab-random-curves] to standard planar Brownian motion started from 0 sampled independently from $(\Phi,\Gamma)$ and stopped when it first hits $\partial\mathbbm D$.  
\item Let $\Psi_k$ be the discrete GFF on $\mathcal M_k$ with zero boundary condition on $\partial\mathcal M_k$ and free boundary condition at $\infty$ (Definition~(def-gff of the paper)). Then $\sum_{x\in\mathcal V\mathcal M_k} \Psi_k(x) \mathbbm 1_{H_k(x)}(\cdot)$ converges in the distributional sense to a zero-boundary GFF on $\mathbbm D$ sampled independently from $(\Phi, \Gamma)$. 
\end{itemize} (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

[Theorem simplified-construction of arXiv:2412.09087, 'General Markovian randomized equilibrium existence and construction in zero-sum Dynkin gam'] Suppose ${B^{f\leq g<h}}\cup {B^{h<f\leq g}} = \emptyset$, i.e., if $f(x)\leq g(x)$ then $f(x) \leq h(x)\leq g(x)$ for all $x \in {\cal I}$. Then, the equilibrium $(\tau_{\Psi^{(1)}},\tau_{\Psi^{(2)}})$ of Theorem (thm:construction of the paper) can be attained with $\epsilon=0$, i.e., a global Markovian randomized  Nash equilibrium exists. More precisely, the global Markovian randomized Nash equilibrium can be attained with explicit randomization according to (equation Ne-stretegy of the paper) and 
\begin{align}
A_t^{(1)}:=& \int_0^t \frac{1}{f(X_s)-g(X_s)}\mathbb{I}_{\{X_s\in {B^{h<g<f}}\}}dC_s^{-}(g)\\
A_t^{(2)}:=& \int_0^t \frac{1}{f(X_s)-g(X_s)}\mathbb{I}_{\{X_s\in {B^{g<f<h}}\}}dC_s^{+}(f), 
\end{align}
where $C_t^{+}(f), t \geq 0$ is defined in (equation Cfplusminus1 of the paper) and $C_t^{-}(g), t \geq 0$ is defined as in (equation Cfplusminus2 of the paper) with $g$ instead of $f$ (note that both are non-decreasing processes). 

Furthermore, suppose that $f$ and $g$ are twice continuously differentiable except on countable sets of separated points, denoted by $x_i \in {\cal I}, i \in I$ and $x_j \in {\cal I}, j \in J$ (where $I$ and $J$ are index sets), respectively. Then (equation simplified-construction:eq1 of the paper)--(equation simplified-construction:eq2 of the paper) can be written as
\begin{align*}
A_t^{(1)}= \int_0^t\left(\frac{(\mathbb{L}_X-r)g(X_s)}{g(X_s)-f(X_s)}\right)_+\mathbb{I}_{\{X_s\in {B^{h<g<f}}, X_s \neq x_j, \forall j\}}ds + \frac{1}{2}\sum_{j}  \mathbb{I}_{\{x_j \in {B^{h<g<f}}\}}\left(\frac{g'(x_j+)-g'(x_j-)}{{g(x_j)-f(x_j)}}\right)_+l_t^{x_j}\\
A_t^{(2)}= \int_0^t\left(\frac{(\mathbb{L}_X-r)f(X_s)}{f(X_s)-g(X_s)}\right)_+\mathbb{I}_{\{X_s\in {B^{g<f<h}}, X_s \neq x_i,\forall i\}}ds + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i}  \mathbb{I}_{\{x_i \in {B^{g<f<h}}\}}\left(\frac{f'(x_i+)-f'(x_i-)}{{f(x_i)-g(x_i)}}\right)_+l_t^{x_i}.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Defn Matrix domination of arXiv:2608.27939, 'Entropy and domination for quasi-Hitchin representations'] Let $A$ be a $n\times n$ matrix with real and positive entries and $B$ be an $n\times n$ matrix with complex entries. Then we say that $A$ \emph{dominates} $\lvert B \rvert$, denoted by $A \geq \lvert B\rvert$ (or $\lvert B \rvert \leq A$), if each entry of $A$ is  at least the modulus of the corresponding entry of $B$.
title: Matrix domination

body: Let P be the transition matrix of an irreducible, aperiodic Markov chain on a finite state space S. Then P has a unique stationary distribution pi, pi(x) > 0 for every x in S, and there exist constants C > 0 and rho in (0,1) such that max_{x in S} ||P^n(x, .) - pi||_TV <= C rho^n for every n >= 1; in particular P^n(x,y) converges to pi(y) as n tends to infinity for every x, y in S, regardless of the initial distribution. [Levin and Peres, Markov Chains and Mixing Times]
title: Convergence Theorem for Irreducible Aperiodic Finite Markov Chains

body:
[Lemma 35 of arXiv:2608.03497, 'Connective Constants on Nested Fractal Graphs'] Consider
\[
  \mathcal G(x,y)
  =
  \bigl(y^2(1+x^3),y^2x(1+x)\bigr),
  \qquad x,y>0.
\]
Its unique positive fixed point is \((\theta_*,\phi_*)\), where
\[
  \theta_*^5+2\theta_*^4=1,
  \qquad
  \phi_*=\frac1{\theta_*(1+\theta_*)}.
\]
If a nonempty compact set \(L\subset(0,\infty)^2\) satisfies
\(\mathcal G(L)=L\), then
\[
  L=\{(\theta_*,\phi_*)\}.
\]

body: [Corollary workload-optimality of arXiv:2505.04942, '\textbf{Randomized Routing to Remote Queues}'] Assume the conditions of Theorem~(theorem:load-balancing of the paper) hold for a sequence of GBC systems where the customers' origins are known. If $\{ w_{k}(i) : i\in\mathbb{N} ; k = 1, \ldots, s \}$ is a sequence of i.i.d.\ random variables, the workload in the GBC system can be asymptotically minimized by the RJSQ policy, in the sense that for $T > 0$, $ \sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} \tilde{\Gamma}^{\dagger}_{n}(t) \Rightarrow 0 $ as $ n \to \infty $. If conditions~(equation eq:fourth-moments of the paper) and (equation eq:log-log-n-bound of the paper) also hold, then by taking $ \chi_{n} = C'' n^{-1/4}\sqrt{\log n} $ for $ C'' > 0 $, the RJSQ policy attains $ \sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} \tilde{\Gamma}^{\dagger}_{n}(t) = O\big(n^{-1/4}\sqrt{\log n}\big) $. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\]
where $C_5 = 10d^2\varepsilon^{-9}$.

[Lemma lem:subcriticalproj of arXiv:2601.20502, 'Optimal matching under size priority'] Define the families of truncated decorated trees $\left(\mathbb{T}_H,o,i_{-}^{H},i_{+}^{H}\right)_{H \geq 0}$ as follows:
    Sample $(\mathbb{T},o)$ an unweighted Bienaymé-Galton-Watson tree of reproduction law $\pi$, set $\mathbb{T}_H=B_H(\mathbb{T},o)$ and   $(i_{-}^{H})(u,v)=0$ for every edge of $\mathbb{T}_H$ pointing towards the $H-$boundary. Then use Recursion~(equation eq:systemrecursionzoombis of the paper) to define $i_{-}^{H}$ on the remainder of $\mathbb{T}_H$. Proceed similarly for $i_{+}^{H}$ by setting $i_{+}^{H}=1$ on the boundary instead of $0$.

    Then under assuming that $t \mapsto \hat{\phi}(1-\hat{\phi}(1-t))$ possesses a unique fixed point, both families $(i_{+}^{H}(o,v))_{v \sim o}$ and $(i_{-}^{H}(o,v))_{v \sim o}$ converges almost surely to a family $(i_l)_{l \leq N}$ where $(i_l)$ have i.i.d distribution $\gamma\delta_0+(1-\gamma)\delta_1$ and independent of $N$ of distribution $\pi$.

   \bigl(\mathcal{I}_{Y/Z}^{m}\bigr)_w\ge 2.

body: [Corollary cor:generaldetection of arXiv:2608.26564, 'Real ideal points, Conway spheres, and left-orderable Dehn fillings'] Let $M = T_1 \cup_CT_2$ be a knot complement in $S^3$ where $T_i$ are torus- or twist-trivial tangles. For every pair of real roots of $P_n$ or $\Lambda_{2m-1}$, there is a distinct real ideal point detecting the Conway sphere, with the corresponding limiting characters and two-sided real branch. If $T_i$ are both torus-trivial tangles, there are $nm$ such ideal points. The number of admissible data in the mixed twist-torus case is the parameter of the torus-trivial side. If $T_i$ are both twist-trivial tangles, there is one such ideal point.

[Lemma le:a_priori_int_fl of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] Fix $q>0$, $M,p > 0$. Let $w_1,w_2 \in B(0,\delta/4)$, and let $E$ denote the event that the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item Let $\eta_{w_1}^{\theta_1+\pi}$, $\eta_{w_1}^{\theta_1}$ (resp.\ $\eta_{w_2}^{\theta_2}$, $\eta_{w_2}^{\theta_2-\pi}$) be the flow lines with respective angles starting at $w_1$ (resp.\ $w_2$) and stopped upon exiting $B(0,3\delta/4)$. Then
\begin{itemize}
\item The right side of $\eta_{w_1}^{\theta_1}$ intersects the left side of $\eta_{w_2}^{\theta_2}$ with angle difference $\theta_1-\theta_2$, and they do not intersect in any other way.
\item $\eta_{w_1}^{\theta_1+\pi}$ does not intersect $\eta_{w_2}^{\theta_2}$, $\eta_{w_2}^{\theta_2-\pi}$; and $\eta_{w_2}^{\theta_2-\pi}$ does not intersect $\eta_{w_1}^{\theta_1+\pi}$, $\eta_{w_1}^{\theta_1}$.
\item Sample the internal metrics in the regions bounded between $\eta_{w_1}^{\theta_1}, \eta_{w_2}^{\theta_2}$. There exist $x',x,y,y' \in \eta_{w_1}^{\theta_1} \cap \eta_{w_2}^{\theta_2}$ such that $(x,y) \in \intptsapproxbubble{U_{x',y'}}{\epsilon}$ as in~(equation eq:intpts_bubble of the paper) and
\[ \metapproxres{\epsilon}{U_{x',y'}}{x}{y}{\Gamma} > \quant{q}{\epsilon} . \] 
\end{itemize}
\item The event $G_{0,\delta}$ from the statement of Lemma~(le:good_scales_merging of the paper) occurs for $h_\delta$.
\end{itemize}
Then
\[ \mathbf{P}[E] = O(\delta^{{d_{{\mathrm{dbl}}}}+o(1)}) \]
uniformly in the choice of $w_1,w_2$.

Let $p_1(x) = P(Y(1)=1 \mid X=x)$ and $p_0(x) = P(Y(0)=1 \mid X=x)$. For any fixed impression budget constraint $P(\pi(X)=1) \le B$, the policy maximizing incremental consumption per impression under monotonicity ($Y(1) \ge Y(0)$) is a level set of the uplift ratio $\frac{p_1(x) - p_0(x)}{c(x)}$, and the dual-threshold policy $\pi(x) = \mathbb{I}(p_1(x) \ge \theta_1 \land p_0(x) \le \theta_0)$ forms a conservative, robust approximation that provably purges always-takers whose $p_0(x) > \theta_0$.

p_1(x) and p_0(x) are well-calibrated

body:
Let k be an algebraically closed field and R = k[x_1, ..., x_n]. Weak form: every proper ideal of R has a common zero in k^n; equivalently, every maximal ideal of R is (x_1 - a_1, ..., x_n - a_n) for some a in k^n. Strong form: for every ideal I of R, the ideal of polynomials vanishing on V(I) is the radical of I, I(V(I)) = sqrt(I). Hence V and I are inclusion-reversing inverse bijections between the radical ideals of R and the algebraic subsets of k^n. Algebraic closure is needed: over the reals x^2 + 1 has no zero.

[Proposition 12 of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Consider a random vector $x\in \R^d$ such that $\E[x]=0$ and $\Cov(x)=I_d$. Assume that $x$ satisfies approximate tensorization of variance~\eqref{eq:approximate-variance-tensorization} with constant
	$C>0$, and that $\max_{j\le d}\E|x_j|^8\le M,$ where $M$ is independent of $d$. Set
	\[
	W:=\frac{xx^\top-I_d}{\sqrt d},
	\]
	and suppose that
	$\Cov(\operatornorm{vec}W)=\Sigma_\kappa$ for some fixed
	$\kappa>1$. Then there exists
	$C_{\rm reg}=C_{\rm reg}(C,M,\kappa)<\infty$ such that $W$ is a
	$(K_{\rm feat},\tau_d)$-regular feature with
	\[
	K_{\rm feat}\le C_{\rm reg},
	\qquad
	\tau_d\le C_{\rm reg}d^{-1/2}.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 6 of arXiv:2608.24549, 'Persistent Cross Entropy'] The \textbf{persistent cross entropy} of $D_X$ relative to $D_Y$ is
$$
H(p_X,p_X^Y)
=
-\sum\limits_{u\in D_X}p_X(u)\log p_X^Y(u).
$$
Its \textbf{entropy excess} is
$\Delta H_X^Y=H(p_X,p_X^Y)-H(p_X)$.

SETTING: X a compact metric space; T : X -> X a continuous, topologically exact map which is a local homeomorphism with finite fibres (so that the operator below sends continuous functions to continuous functions); w : X -> (0, infinity) a continuous weight. Define the transfer (Ruelle) operator on complex continuous functions by (L f)(x) = the sum of w(y) f(y) over the finitely many y with T(y) = x; L is a bounded positive operator on C(X). Assume the Perron data exist: a number lambda > 0 and a strictly positive h in C(X) with L h = lambda h, together with a Borel probability measure nu with L* nu = lambda nu, i.e. the integral of L f with respect to nu equals lambda times the integral of f with respect to nu for all f in C(X). CONCLUSION: (1) if f in C(X) is complex-valued and L f = z f with |z| = lambda, then z = lambda and f is a constant multiple of h - so lambda is the only eigenvalue of modulus lambda in C(X) and its eigenspace is one dimensional; (2) lambda is ALGEBRAICALLY simple: there is no f in C(X) with L f - lambda f = h, hence no Jordan block at lambda. WHERE THE HYPOTHESES BITE: (i) exactness cannot be weakened to minimality, unique ergodicity or transitivity. Take X the circle, T an irrational rotation and w identically 1, so that L f = f composed with T^{-1}: every character exp(2 pi i n x) is an eigenfunction with an eigenvalue of modulus 1, so the peripheral spectrum is infinite - and the system is minimal and uniquely ergodic but not exact (it is invertible, hence never exact). (ii) Strict positivity of the weight is essential. If w may vanish, the irreducibility can become periodic: in the finite-state model, where L is a nonnegative matrix, the statement above is the PRIMITIVE case of the Perron-Frobenius theorem, and an irreducible matrix of period p > 1 has exactly p eigenvalues of modulus equal to its spectral radius, so simplicity of the peripheral eigenvalue genuinely fails. (iii) The conclusion concerns the peripheral eigenvalue only and gives NO spectral gap: to place the rest of the spectrum in a strictly smaller disc one needs quasi-compactness (a Lasota-Yorke or Ionescu-Tulcea-Marinescu inequality on a Holder or bounded-variation space), a separate hypothesis on the regularity of w and the expansion of T. (iv) The existence of h and nu is assumed here, not proved; producing them is the other half of the Ruelle-Perron-Frobenius theorem and needs its own hypotheses.
X compact metric, T continuous and topologically exact
T is a local homeomorphism with finite fibres, so that L maps C(X) into C(X)
the weight w is continuous and strictly positive everywhere
there exist lambda > 0 and h in C(X) with h > 0 everywhere and L h = lambda h
there exists a Borel probability measure nu with L* nu = lambda nu (used only for algebraic simplicity)
the conclusion is about the eigenvalues of L acting on C(X); no Banach space of Holder or bounded-variation functions and no quasi-compactness is assumed

[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2609.02193, 'State-law dynamics of McKean-Vlasov stochastic reaction-diffusion equations on $\mathbb R^'] Let $Y$ be a separable Banach space compactly embedded into $X$, let $q>2$, and identify $Y$ with its Borel image in $X$. For $R>0$, set
	\begin{align*}
		\mathcal C_R
		=
		\Big\{
		\mu\in\mathcal P_2(X):
		\mu(Y)=1,
		\int_Y\|y\|_Y^q\,\mu(dy)\leq R
		\Big\}.
	\end{align*}
	Then $\mathcal C_R$ is relatively compact in $(\mathcal P_2(X),\mathcal W_{2,X})$. Consequently, every set $\mathcal B\subset Y\times\mathcal P_2(X)$ satisfying
	\begin{align*}
		\sup_{(x,\mu)\in\mathcal B}
		\Big(
		\|x\|_Y^q+
		\int_Y\|y\|_Y^q\,\mu(dy)
		\Big)<\infty,
		\qquad
		\mu(Y)=1
		\quad\text{for every }(x,\mu)\in\mathcal B,
	\end{align*}
	is relatively compact in $X\times\mathcal P_2(X)$.

Let A be a finite subset of R^n with N = |A| >= 2 elements, and let r = max_{a in A} ||a||_2. Let sigma_1, ..., sigma_n be independent Rademacher signs (uniform on {-1, +1}). Then E_sigma [ max_{a in A} sum_{i=1}^{n} sigma_i a_i ] <= r sqrt(2 log N), and consequently E_sigma [ max_{a in A} (1/n) sum_i sigma_i a_i ] <= r sqrt(2 log N) / n. Two consequences used constantly in learning theory: (1) for a finite class F of functions bounded by B on a sample x_1, ..., x_n, the empirical Rademacher complexity satisfies R_hat_S(F) = E_sigma sup_{f in F} (1/n) sum_i sigma_i f(x_i) <= B sqrt(2 log |F| / n), since each vector (f(x_1), ..., f(x_n)) has Euclidean norm at most B sqrt(n); (2) for a class C of sets of VC dimension d, restricting to the sample leaves at most s(C, n) <= (e n / d)^d distinct indicator vectors (Sauer-Shelah), each of norm at most sqrt(n), so R_hat_S(C) <= sqrt(2 d log(e n / d) / n) for n >= d. The logarithm cannot be removed at this generality: for A = {-1, +1}^n (N = 2^n, r = sqrt(n)) the maximum is exactly n while the bound reads n sqrt(2 log 2), so the lemma is sharp up to the constant sqrt(2 log 2) = 1.18; for VC classes Dudley's chaining removes the logarithm, R_hat_S(C) <= C sqrt(d / n).
A finite with at least two elements (for N = 1 the maximum has mean 0)
the signs are independent and symmetric; the bound is on the expectation over the signs only, the vectors are fixed

body:
[Lemm 14 of arXiv:2609.01105, 'Obstruction to quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures under transport flows on Riemannian M'] With the above notations, the operator
\[
    \theta_0 P^{-\mez} \theta_1 \left(S\theta_2 P \theta_2 S^{-1} -  \theta_3 P\theta_3 \right) \theta_1 P^{-1/2} \theta_0
\]
is Hilbert--Schmidt on~\(L^2(M)\). This translates into
\[
    P_{0,1}^{-\mez} \left(S_\kappa P_{2,2} S_\kappa^{-1}  - P_{3,3}\right)P^{-\mez}_{1,0}
\]
is Hilbert--Schmidt on~\(L^2(V_2)\), where~\(S_\kappa\) and~\(S_\kappa^{-1}\) are respectively the compositions with~\(\chi^{-1}\) and~\(\chi\).

body:
[Theorem thm:inter lln of arXiv:2512.17747, 'On exponentially height-penalized random trees'] Let $\mu=\mu_n$ be such that $1/\sqrt{n}\ll\mu\ll n$.
    Let $\mathbf{T}_n$ be a $\mu$-height-biased tree of size $n$.
    Then
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{h(\mathbf{T}_n)}{\left(\frac{2\pi^2n}{\mu}\right)^{1/3}}\overset{\mathbb P}{\longrightarrow} 1\,.
    \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Asymptotic height in the intermediate regime

body: [Proposition proposition_no_LDP_for_bounded_observables of arXiv:2605.26804, '\Large Large Deviation Principle for the Empirical Measures of Simple Random Walks on $\ov'] Let $(S_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a simple random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$ with constant transition probability function $p \equiv \overline{p} \neq \frac{1}{2}$. Then there exists a bounded function $f : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that the sequence $\big(\ell_n(f)\big)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ does not satisfy a LDP. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition proposition_no_LDP_for_bounded_observables of arXiv:2605.26804

[Problem prob:iml-cube-decidability of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] Are $\textbf{IK4}$, $\textbf{IK5}$, $\textbf{IK45}$, $\textbf{IKD4}$, $\textbf{IKD45}$, and $\textbf{IKB5}$ decidable?

[Lem integrabilidad_distance_vertex of arXiv:2606.15339, 'Uniform integrability of the distance to the nearest leaf in random trees'] For every $p\ge 0$, we have that $\sup_{n\ge n_0}\mathbf{E}\bigl[\partial(\mathcal{T}_n,v_n)^{p}\bigr]<+\infty$,
and the family $\{\partial(\mathcal{T}_n,v_n)\}_{n\ge 1}$ is uniformly integrable of every order.

identically distributed.

body:
[Lem 17 of arXiv:2609.00758, 'Deformations of Compact Calabi--Yau and Fano Varieties with Isolated Singularities'] \l{lem: Sard}
Let $X,Y$ be non-singular complex spaces and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism. Let $K\sb X$ be a closed subset which contains all the critical points of $f$ and such that $f|_K:K\to Y$ is a proper map. Then the set of critical values of $f$ is an analytic subset of $Y$ of positive codimension. \qed (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 17 of arXiv:2609.00758

Let E be a locally compact separable metric space and m a positive Radon measure on E with full support. An m-symmetric Hunt process M = (Omega, {X_t}, {P_x}, F, {F_t}, {theta_t}, zeta) is associated with a Dirichlet form (E, F) on L^2(E; m) if (E, F) is regular and the transition semigroup p_t f(x) = E_x[f(X_t); t < zeta] satisfies E(u,v) = lim_{t->0} t^{-1}(u - p_t u, v)_{L^2(E;m)}.
E locally compact separable metric space
m Radon measure with full support
title: Hunt Process Associated with Regular Dirichlet Form

[Lemma integ of arXiv:2602.08591, 'The Yang--Mills measure on compact surfaces as a \\ universal scaling limit of lattice gau'] Let $G\subset U(N)$ be a compact Lie group with lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$.  Let $U$ be a neighborhood of $1_G$ of diameter less than $1$, for which $\log$ is a diffeomorphism on its image. Then, there exists a constant $C$ such that for any positive bounded measurable function $f:U\subset G\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$,
    \[\left\vert \int_U f(g)\mathrm{d} g - \int_{\log U} f(\exp X)dX\right\vert \leqslant C \int_{\mathfrak{g}}\vert X\vert ^2 f(\exp X)dX. \]

[Definition 19 (Complete and incomplete scales) of arXiv:2609.01436, '2609.01436'] Let $k\geq k_0$ and $t\geq t_0$.  We say that scale $k$ is
\emph{$h$-complete at time $t$} if
\(
 e^{c_0(t-t_0)}U_k(t)\geq h,
\)
or equivalently, if $Z_k(t)\geq\Lambda_k(h)$.  Otherwise, scale $k$ is
\emph{$h$-incomplete at time $t$}.

[Theorem thm:G0 of arXiv:2412.05503, 'Critical scaling profile for trees and connected subgraphs \\ on the complete graph'] For both trees and connected subgraphs, for all $s \ge 0$, and for all sequences
$p_V$ with $p_V \le 1+sV^{-1/2}$ and $\lim_{V\to\infty}p_V=p\in [0,1]$,
\begin{align}

    \lim_{V\to\infty} G_{V,0}(p_V)
    &=
    \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{ n^{n-1} }{n!} \Big( \frac{p}{e} \Big)^{n-1}
    =
    -\frac{e}{p}W_0\Big(\!\!-\frac{p}{e} \Big)
    .
\end{align}
In particular, if $p=1$ then
$\lim_{V\to\infty} G_{V,0}(p_V) = e$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:G0 of arXiv:2412.05503

[Lem 6 of arXiv:2607.03360, 'Smoluchowski-Kramers Approximation Meets Khasminskii Averaging Principles in Nonequilibriu'] Fix $R>0$. For each $x\in \rr^{d_1}$ and $y \in \rr^{d_2}$, let $M_{R,n}(x,y)$ and $\Dl_{R,n}(x,y)$ be defined in \eqref{M-mat} and \eqref{Dl-xy}, respectively. Then 
\beq{M-I}
|M_{R,n}^{-1}(x,y)-I| \leq \frac{\sqrt{m} |\Dl_{R,n}(x,y)|}{1-\sqrt{m}|\Dl_{R,n}(x,y)|}.
\eeq
Moreover, for any fixed $R>0$, the estimate
\beq{MRn-bdd}
|M_{R,n}^{-1}(x,y)|\leq 2,
\eeq
hold for all sufficiently small $\e$ (equivalently, for all sufficiently small m).
