[Definition 16 (Viscosity sub/supersolutions) of arXiv:2606.09691, '\textsc{Degenerate Diffusions on Continuum Percolation and Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Equatio'] Let $V\subset \R_+\times\R^d$.

\begin{itemize}

\item
A locally bounded function
$u:\overline V\to\R$
is called a viscosity subsolution of
\begin{equation}
\partial_t u
=
\mathcal H(x,\nabla u,\mathrm{Hess}_x u)
\qquad
\text{in }V
\end{equation}
if, for every $(t_0,x_0)\in V$ and every smooth test function $\phi$ defined in a neighborhood of $(t_0,x_0)$ such that
\[
u^*-\phi
\]
has a local maximum at $(t_0,x_0)$, one has
\[
\partial_t\phi(t_0,x_0)
-
\mathcal H(
x_0,
\nabla\phi(t_0,x_0),
\mathrm{Hess}_x\phi(t_0,x_0)
)
\leq0.
\]

\item
A locally bounded function
$u:\overline V\to\R$
is called a viscosity supersolution of \eqref{eq-visc-sub} if, for every $(t_0,x_0)\in V$ and every smooth test function $\phi$ defined in a neighborhood of $(t_0,x_0)$ such that
\[
u_*-\phi
\]
has a local minimum at $(t_0,x_0)$, one has
\[
\partial_t\phi(t_0,x_0)
-
\mathcal H(
x_0,
\nabla\phi(t_0,x_0),
\mathrm{Hess}_x\phi(t_0,x_0)
)
\geq0.
\]

\item
A function is called a viscosity solution if it is both a viscosity subsolution and a viscosity supersolution.

\end{itemize}
title: Viscosity sub/supersolutions

Let $S$ be the sample covariance of $n$ i.i.d. Gaussian rows in $\mathbb{R}^p$ with population covariance $\Sigma = \sigma^2 (I_p + \theta u u^T)$, $\|u\| = 1$, $\theta > 0$, in the regime $p/n \to \gamma \in (0, 1]$. Let $\hat\lambda$ be the largest eigenvalue of $S$ and $\hat u$ its unit eigenvector. THEOREM (Baik, Ben Arous, Peche 2005 for the eigenvalue in the complex case; Paul 2007 for real Gaussian data, eigenvalue and eigenvector; Baik-Silverstein 2006 in general). (i) If $\theta \le \sqrt{\gamma}$ then $\hat\lambda \to \sigma^2 (1 + \sqrt{\gamma})^2$ almost surely, the bulk edge of the Marchenko-Pastur law, and $|\langle \hat u, u \rangle|^2 \to 0$: the spike is invisible. (ii) If $\theta > \sqrt{\gamma}$ then $\hat\lambda \to \sigma^2 (1 + \theta)(1 + \gamma / \theta)$, which exceeds the bulk edge, and $|\langle \hat u, u \rangle|^2 \to \frac{1 - \gamma / \theta^2}{1 + \gamma / \theta}$. The limit $\sigma^2 (1 + \theta)(1 + \gamma/\theta) = \sigma^2 (1 + \theta + \gamma + \gamma/\theta)$ is strictly larger than the population eigenvalue $\sigma^2 (1 + \theta)$: a detected sample spike always overstates its population value, by $\sigma^2 \gamma (1 + 1/\theta)$. The same statements hold spike by spike for $r$ fixed spikes with distinct $\theta_k$, each compared with the threshold $\sqrt{\gamma}$.
rows are i.i.d. Gaussian with covariance sigma^2 (I + theta u u^T)
p/n -> gamma in (0, 1]
the spike rank r is fixed as p, n -> infinity

Let f ∈ C(R; R^n) be the flux and u0 ∈ L^∞(R^n). A function u ∈ L^∞(R^n × (0,∞)) is a weak (integral) solution of the Cauchy problem u_t + div_x f(u) = 0 in R^n × (0,∞), u(·,0) = u0, if for every test function φ ∈ C_c^1(R^n × [0,∞)) (compactly supported, but NOT required to vanish at t = 0): ∫_0^∞ ∫_{R^n} ( u φ_t + f(u)·∇_x φ ) dx dt + ∫_{R^n} u0(x) φ(x,0) dx = 0. Equivalently, u_t + div f(u) = 0 in the sense of distributions on R^n × (0,∞) together with the attainment of the initial datum encoded by the boundary term. Every classical (C^1) solution is a weak solution, and a weak solution that is C^1 on an open set is a classical solution there. Weak solutions are in general NOT unique: an additional admissibility (entropy) condition is required.

[Proposition prop:hypercontractivity of arXiv:2602.11129, 'Information-Theoretic Thresholds for Bipartite Latent-Space Graphs Under Noisy Observation'] There are constants $C > 0, 1 > c > 0$ such that for every polynomial $f$ of degree $k \ge 1$ in i.i.d. standard Gaussian inputs $\mathbf{x}$ with $\Expectedsub{\mathbf{x}}{f(\mathbf{x})} = 0$, we have 
    $$
        \Pr{ |f(\mathbf{x})| \ge t \sigma(f)  } \le C\exp( - c t^{2/k})
    $$ where $\sigma = \sqrt{ \mathrm{Var}{f(\mathbf{x})}}$.
title: Concentration from Hypercontractivity

[Proposition P:vidotto of arXiv:2606.23865, 'Uniform-in-time Gaussian fluctuations for multiscale nonlinear stochastic systems via Mall'] [vido_2020]
Let ${F} \in \mathbb{D}^{2,4}$ be such that $\mathbb{E}(F) = 0$ and
$\operatorname{Var}(F) = \tilde{\sigma}^2$, and let $N \sim
\mathscr{N}(0,\tilde{\sigma}^2)$. Then,
\begin{align*}
d_W(F,N) &\leq \frac{\sqrt{10}}{2 \tilde{\sigma}^2 }\mathbb{E} \left[\|D^2 F \otimes D^2 F  \|_{\mathscr{H}^{\otimes 2}}^2 \right]^{\frac{1}{4}}\mathbb{E} \left[\|DF\|_{\mathscr{H}}^4 \right]^{\frac{1}{4}} ,
\end{align*}
where the Malliavin operators $D$ and $D^2$ are the ones defined in
Subsection (S:MD of the paper), and $\otimes$ is the convolution operator defined as follows: for any two function $\mathsf{f}$, $\mathsf{g} \in \mathscr{H},$ 
\begin{equation}
[\mathsf{f} \otimes \mathsf{g}] \triangleq \int_0^t \mathsf{f}(x,z) \thinspace \mathsf{g}(y,z)\thinspace dz.

body:
[Theorem LCK-intro of arXiv:2608.30747, 'Compact homogeneous complex manifolds'] Any Hermitian C-space which is LCK can be constructed according to the following recipe, whose only ingredients are a flag manifold $F=G_f/H_f$, a regular element $W\in\zg(\hg_f)$ (i.e., $\alpha(\im W)\ne 0$ for any $\alpha\in\Delta_\qg$) and real numbers $a,b,c,t$ such that $b\ne 0$, $c,t>0$: 
\begin{enumerate}[{\rm (i)}]
\item The C-space is $M=G/K=G_f/K\times S^1$, where $K$ is defined by  
$$
\zg(\hg_f)=\zg(\kg)\oplus\RR W, \quad \kg=[\hg_f,\hg_f]\oplus\zg(\kg), \quad \zg(\ggo)=\RR Z_0, \quad \ag=\RR Z_0\oplus\RR W, \quad \ag_f=\RR W,
$$
provided that $K\subset H_f$ is closed, and $\left\{Z_0,W\right\}$ is a $Q$-orthonormal basis of $\ag$. 

\item The complex structure is given by $J=(J_\ag,J_\qg)$, where $J_\qg$ is attached to the invariant ordering $\Delta_\qg^+:=\{\alpha\in\Delta_\qg:\alpha(\im W)>0\}$ and $J_\ag$ is defined by   
$$
[J_\ag]_{\left\{Z_0,W\right\}} = 
\left[\begin{matrix} a&-\tfrac{a^2+1}{b} \\ b& -a\end{matrix}\right].  
$$ 
\item As a compatible metric $g=g_\ag+g_\qg$, consider 
$$
g_\qg:=t g_W, \quad g_W=(x_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\Delta_\qg^+}, \quad x_\alpha:=\alpha(\im W)>0; \qquad     
[g_{\ag}]_{\{ Z_0,W\}} = c\left[\begin{matrix} b^2&-ab \\ -ab& a^2+1\end{matrix}\right].
$$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem LCK-intro of arXiv:2608.30747

[Lemma 48 of arXiv:2511.07350, 'Decoupling of clusters in independent sets in a percolated hypercube'] For every fixed $m \geq 1$, let 
	\[
		f(p) \coloneq \inf_{s \in (0, 1)} ms + H_p(s), \quad p \in (0, 1).
	\]
	Then $f$ is continuous and strictly increasing in $p$, and
	\[
		f\Rnd{\tfrac{1}{2}} = m + 1 - \log_2\Rnd{2^{m} + 1}.
	\]
title: Lemma 48 of arXiv:2511.07350

[Corollary 6 (Expected number of fixed points) of arXiv:2606.18047, 'Analysis of the asymmetric shelf shuffle'] The expected number of fixed points in $\pi\sim\nu_{n, m}^{(p)}$ is
\begin{equation*}
\E_{\nu^{(p)}_{n,m}}[N_1(\pi)]
=\sum_{r=1}^{n}m^{1-r}\bigl(p^r-(-q)^r\bigr)
=\frac{p(1-(p/m)^n)}{1-p/m}+\frac{q(1-(-q/m)^n)}{1+q/m}.

\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Expected number of fixed points

body:
[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2511.14379, 'Stability of storage processes with general release rates'] \begin{itemize}
		\item [(i)] Assume $\textbf{(C1)-(C3)}$ (or $\textbf{(\={C}1)-(\={C}2)}$ and  $\textbf{(C3)}$ in the case when $\bar\upnu(0)<\infty$), that $\process{X}$ is  $\uppsi$-irreducible and aperiodic, and that every compact set is petite for $\process{X}$.  If
	\begin{equation}\limsup_{u\to\infty}\frac{\int_0^\infty\frac{\varphi(\V(u+v))}{r(u+v)}\bar\upnu(v)\D v}{\varphi(\V(u))}<1,\end{equation}
	then $\process{X}$ admits a unique invariant measure $\uppi\in\mathcal{P}$ satisfying 
	$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(t))\lVert p(t,x,\D y)-\uppi(\D y)\rVert_{{\rm TV}}=0,\qquad x\ge0.$$ Moreover, the invariant measure $\uppi$ satisfies \begin{equation}\limsup_{u\to\infty}(\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(u))\vee\varphi(\V(u)) )\bar\uppi(u)<\infty.\end{equation}
	\item[(ii)] Assume that $\bar\upnu(u)>0$ for all $u\in(0,\infty)$   and $u\mapsto 1/\bar\upnu(u)$ is differentiable, increasing and submultiplicative\footnote{A function $f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ is submultiplicative if $f(u+v)\le cf(u)f(v)$ for some $c>0$ and all $u,v\in(0,\infty)$.}. Assume also that  $u\mapsto r(u)/u$ is decreasing with $\lim_{u\to\infty} r(u)/u = 0$. Then, if $\process{X}$ is ergodic with an invariant measure $\uppi\in\mathcal{P}$, for any $\epsilon>0$ there exists $c_\epsilon>0$ satisfying 
	$$
	\bar\uppi(u)\ge c_\epsilon \frac{\bar\upnu(u)}{r(u)}u^{1-\varepsilon}\qquad u\ge1.
	$$
Denote $L_\epsilon(u)\df c_\epsilon u^{1-\varepsilon}\bar\upnu(u)/r(u)$. If there exists increasing $h:[1,\infty)\to[1,\infty)$ such that $\mathbb{E}^x [h(X(t))]\leq h(x) + ct$ (for some $c\in(0,\infty)$ and all $x\ge0$ and $t\geq 1$) and $F(u)\coloneqq uL_\epsilon(h^{-1}(u))$ is increasing with $\lim_{u\to\infty} F(u) = \infty$, then the following lower bound holds
	$$
	\| p(t,x,\D y)-\uppi(\D y)\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\ge \frac{1}{2}L_\epsilon\circ h^{-1}\circ F^{-1}(2(h(x) + ct)).
	$$
	\item[(iii)] Assume that $\bar\upnu(u)>0$ for all $u\in(0,\infty)$   and $u\mapsto 1/\bar\upnu(\exp(u))$ is differentiable, increasing and submultiplicative. Assume also that  $u\mapsto r(u)/(u\log u)$ is decreasing eventually with $\lim_{u\to\infty} r(u)/(u \log u) = 0$. Then, if $\process{X}$ is ergodic with an invariant measure $\uppi\in\mathcal{P}$, for any $\epsilon>0$ there exists $c_\epsilon>0$ satisfying 
	$$
	\bar\uppi(u)\ge c_\epsilon \frac{\bar\upnu(u)}{u^{\varepsilon}}\qquad u\ge1.
	$$
Denote $L_\epsilon(u)\df c_\epsilon u^{-\varepsilon}\bar\upnu(u)$. If there exists increasing $h:[1,\infty)\to[1,\infty)$ such that $\mathbb{E}^x [h(X(t))]\leq h(x) + ct$ (for some $c\in(0,\infty)$ and all $x\ge0$ and $t\geq 1$) and $F(u)\coloneqq uL_\epsilon(h^{-1}(u))$ is increasing with $\lim_{u\to\infty} F(u) = \infty$, then the following lower bound holds
	$$
	\| p(t,x,\D y)-\uppi(\D y)\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\ge \frac{1}{2}L_\epsilon\circ h^{-1}\circ F^{-1}(2(h(x) + ct)).
	$$
	\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2511.14379

[Lemma 30 (Tanaka-type Formula) of arXiv:2605.04359, 'Well-posedness of reflected BSDEs with default time and irregular barrier: An application '] Let $Y$ be an adapted process of the form \eqref{form of the process for Ito} and $\Phi : \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a convex function. Then, $\Phi(Y)$ is an $\mathbb{F}$-optional semimartingale. Moreover, denoting by $\Phi^{\prime}$ the left-hand derivative of the convex function $F$. Then, we have
	$$
	\Phi(Y_t)=\Phi(Y_0)+\int_{0}^{t} \Phi^{\prime}(Y_{s-}) dY^{\ast}_s+\mathcal{L}_t,
	$$
	where $\mathcal{L}$ is a non-decreasing $\mathbb{F}$-adapted process with regulated trajectories (which is in general neither left-continuous nor right-continuous) such that
	$$
	\Delta_{-}\mathcal{L}_{t}=\Delta_{-}\Phi(Y_t)-\Phi^{\prime}(Y_{s-})\Delta_{-}Y_t,\quad \text{ and } \quad\Delta_{+} \mathcal{L}_{t}=\Phi(Y_{t+})-\Phi(Y_t).
	$$

Method: Exact small-grid count and an orientation reformulation Result: On the 2-by-2 grid (a four-cycle), exactly two peaks must be opposite and carry labels 3 and 4. There are two choices of diagonal, two orders of the top labels, and two orders of the bottom labels: eight of the 24 labelings. Their graph distance is always two. More generally orient each edge toward its larger label. Two peaks means precisely two sinks of the induced acyclic orientation; the number of labelings yielding a fixed orientation is its number of linear extensions. Check: Adjacent vertices cannot both be peaks. In the four-cycle, a proposed peak with label 2 would have to exceed both other nonpeak labels, which is impossible; this checks the count without enumeration software. Obstruction: The small-grid calculation gives no large-n scale. The orientation sum requires sharp weighted counts of acyclic orientations with two prescribed sinks. The source title says repel while its displayed question asks distance/n -> 0; that wording discrepancy is retained, not silently corrected.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0029-separation-of-two-peaks-in-random-square-grid-labelings

body: [Definition 4 of arXiv:2608.30875, 'A Decomposition Theorem for Topological Semi-small Maps'] Let $f:X \longrightarrow Y$ be an almost covering where $X$ is a closed $n$-manifold, $Y$ is a closed $n$-pseudomanifold. Let the filtration $Y \supset Y_{n_{R}}(=R) \supset Y_{n_{R}-1} \supset \cdots$ be the refined stratification on $Y$ obtained by Proposition~\ref{RefinedStra}, where $R$ is the fibered set and $n_{R}:= \dim(R)$. The almost covering $f:X \longrightarrow Y$ is called a \textbf{topologically semi-small map} if for each point $r \in S_{k}(:=Y_{k} \setminus Y_{k-1})$ and for each $0 \leq k \leq n_{R}$, the condition $2 \dim(f^{-1}(r))+\dim(S_{k}) \leq n$ is satisfied. Furthermore, we the set $R_{\operatorname{rel}}:=\{S_{k} \ \vert \  2 \dim(f^{-1}(r))+\dim(S_{k}) = n \ \forall \ r \in f^{-1}(S_{k})\}$ is referred to as the set of relevant strata.
title: Definition 4 of arXiv:2608.30875

body: A sequence of nonnegative integers d_1 >= d_2 >= ... >= d_n is the degree sequence of some finite simple graph on n vertices if and only if the sum d_1 + ... + d_n is even and, for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n, sum_{i=1}^k d_i <= k(k-1) + sum_{i=k+1}^n min(d_i, k). [Erdos and Gallai (1960); see West, Introduction to Graph Theory]

body:
[Lemma integration-type-gronwall of arXiv:2609.00627, 'Global well-posedness of radially symmetric strong solutions to two-dimensional compressib'] Let $I=[a, b]$ and $\alpha(t), \beta(t), u(t)$ be a real-valued continuous function defined on $I$. 
    Moreover, $\alpha(t)$ is  a nondecreasing function and $\beta(t)$ is a nonnegative function. 
    if 
    \begin{equation}
        \begin{aligned}
            v(t) \le \alpha(t)+\int_{a}^{t} \beta(s) v(s) ds, \enspace t \in I, 
        \end{aligned}
    \end{equation}
    then, 
    \begin{equation}
        \begin{aligned}
            v(t) \le 2\alpha(t)e^{\int_{a}^{t} \beta(s) ds}. 
        \end{aligned}
    \end{equation}
    \begin{proof}
        Define a function 
        \[
        g(s)=e^{-\int_{a}^{s} \beta(r) dr}\int_{a}^{s}\beta(r)v(r)dr, s \in I. 
        \]
        Differentiating $g(s)$ gives
        \[
        g'(s) = (v(s)-\int_{a}^{s} \beta(r)v(r) dr)\beta(s)e^{-\int_{a}^{s} \beta(r) dr}, 
        \] 
        so we have that
        \[
        g'(s) \le  \alpha(s) \beta(s)e^{-\int_{a}^{s} \beta(r) dr}, 
        \]
        Due to $g(a)=0$, integrating above inequality on $[a, t]$, we have that
        \[
        g(t) \le \int_{a}^{t} \alpha(s) \beta(s)e^{-\int_{a}^{s} \beta(r) dr} ds. 
        \]
        Using the defination of $g(t)$, we have that
        \[
        \int_{a}^{t} \beta(s)v(s) ds = e^{\int_{a}^{t} \beta(r)dr } g(t) \le  \int_{a}^{t} \alpha(s) \beta(s)e^{\int_{s}^{t} \beta(r) dr} ds. 
        \]
        Because $\alpha(t)$ is a nondecreasing function, so we have 
        \begin{equation}
            \begin{aligned}
                v(t) &\le \alpha(t) + \int_{a}^{t} \alpha(s) \beta(s)e^{\int_{s}^{t} \beta(r) dr} ds\\
                & \le \alpha(t)+ \alpha(t) \int_{a}^{t} \beta(s)e^{\int_{s}^{t} \beta(r) dr} ds \le \alpha(t)+ \alpha(t) [ -e^{\int_{s}^{t} \beta(r)dr } ]_{s=a}^{s=t}\\
                & \le \alpha(t)+ \alpha(t) e^{\int_{a}^{t} \beta(r)dr } \le 2\alpha(t) e^{\int_{a}^{t} \beta(r)dr }. 
            \end{aligned}
        \end{equation}
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma integration-type-gronwall of arXiv:2609.00627

[Lem apenlem of arXiv:2608.30518, 'Grow-up rates of inhomogeneous semilinear heat equations in the critical dimension'] Let $g(r)\in L^1(B_1)$.
Assume that $g_1:=r^2(-\log (r/e))^{-5/2}g(r)\in L^{\infty}(B_{1}^2)$ and $V(r)\in L^{\infty}(B_{1}^2)$. Let $w\in C^{1}_{0}(\overline{B_1})$  
be a radial solution of 
\[
-\Delta w= g(r)+V(r)w\quad \text{in $B_{1}^{2}$}.
\]
Then, 
\[
\lVert w\rVert_{L^{\infty}(B_{1}^2)}\le C(\lVert V\rVert_{L^{\infty}(B_{1}^2)}\lVert w\rVert_{L^2(B_{1}^2)}+\lVert g_1\rVert_{L^{\infty}(B_{1}^2)}),
\]

	\end{enumerate}

body:
[Lemma lem:hs_geodesics of arXiv:2605.22787, 'Invariant measures for half-space geometric LPP: classification and the one force--one sol'] Assume that $b$ is an eternal solution. For each $(m,n)$, define the following backwards infinite path $\gamma_{(m,n)} = (\gamma_{(m,n)}(-k): k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0})$: start at $\gamma_{(m,n)}(0) = (m,n)$, and define the path inductively as follows: if $\gamma_{(m,n)}(-k) = (i,j)$, then 
    \begin{equation} 
    \gamma_{(m,n)}(-(k+1)) = \begin{cases}
        (i,j-1),&i = j, \text{ or } i > j \text{ and }b(i,j-1) \ge b(i-1,j), \\
    (i-1,j), &i > j \text{ and } b(i-1,j) > b(i,j-1).
    \end{cases}
    \end{equation}
    Then, the following hold:
    \begin{enumerate} [label=(\roman*), font=\normalfont]
        \item For each $(m,n) \in \mathbb{Z}^2_{\mathrm{HS}}$, the path $\gamma_{(m,n)}$ is a semi-infinite geodesic rooted at $(m,n)$.
         \item  For $p \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, define $(m_{-p},n_{-p}) := \gamma_{(m,n)}(-p)$. Then, for every $k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$,
        \[
        G\bigl((m_k,n_k),(m,n)\bigr) = b(m,n) - b(m_{k+1},n_{k+1}).
        \]
        \item  For every $k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, the path $\bigl(\gamma_{(m,n)}(-k),\gamma_{(m,n)}(-(k-1)),\ldots, \gamma_{(m,n)}(0)\bigr)$ is the rightmost geodesic between the points $\gamma_{(m,n)}(-k)$ and $(m,n)$. 
        \item If $(m,n),(m',n') \in \mathbb{Z}^2_{\mathrm{HS}}$ are such that $\gamma_{(m,n)}(-k) =\gamma_{(m',n')}(-k')$ for some $k,k' \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, then for every $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$,
        \[
        \gamma_{(m,n)}(-k - \ell) =  \gamma_{(m',n')}(-k' - \ell).
        \]
        That is, if the paths from two different points ever meet, they stay together \rm{(}when moving backwards\rm{)}.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:hs_geodesics of arXiv:2605.22787

[Proposition 3 of arXiv:2605.14254, '2605.14254'] The process $(B_{t\wedge\sigma_z^{\lambda}}, t\geq 0)$ is not a martingale stopped at $\sigma_z^{\lambda}$ with respect to $\mathbb{F}^{\xi^{\lambda,z}}$. Moreover, we have
		\begin{multline}
			\mathbb{E}[B_{t\wedge\sigma_z^{\lambda}}\vert \mathcal{F}_{s}^{\xi^{\lambda,z}}]=B_{s\wedge\sigma_z^{\lambda}}-\biggl\{2\bigg(\lambda(t-s)-\dfrac{1}{2\lambda}+z-\xi^{\lambda,z}_s\bigg)\exp(2\lambda\,(z-\xi^{\lambda,z}_s))\\
			\times\Phi\bigg(-\lambda\sqrt{t-s}- \dfrac{ z-\xi^{\lambda,z}_s}{\sqrt{t-s}}\bigg)
			+\dfrac{1}{\lambda}\Phi\bigg(\lambda\sqrt{t-s}-\dfrac{ z-\xi^{\lambda,z}_s }{\sqrt{t-s}}\bigg)\\
			-2(t-s)p(t-s,z-\xi^{\lambda,z}_s,\lambda\,(t-s))\biggr\}\mathbb{I}_{\{\xi^{\lambda,z}_s< z\}}\\
			+\biggl\{2\bigg(\lambda(t-s)-\dfrac{1}{2\lambda}+z-\xi^{\lambda,z}_s\bigg)\Phi\bigg(\lambda\sqrt{t-s}+\dfrac{z-\xi^{\lambda,z}_s }{\sqrt{t-s}}\bigg)-2\lambda\,(t-s)\\
			+\dfrac{1}{\lambda}\exp(-2\lambda\,(z-\xi^{\lambda,z}_s))\Phi\bigg(-\lambda\sqrt{t-s}+ \dfrac{ z-\xi^{\lambda,z}_s}{\sqrt{t-s}}\bigg)-2z\\
			+2(t-s)\exp(-2\lambda\, (z-\xi^{\lambda,z}_{s}))p(t-s,z-\xi^{\lambda,z}_s,\lambda\,(t-s))\biggr\}\mathbb{I}_{\{\xi^{\lambda,z}_s> z\}}.
		\end{multline}
		for every $0\leq s\leq t$.

body:
[Proposition prop:uni_energy_estimate of arXiv:2604.07497, 'The Three-Dimensional Stochastic EMHD System: Local Well-Posedness and Maximal Pathwise So'] Given $p \geq 2$, $T \geq 0$, $\alpha \in (1,2]$, $s > \frac{5}{2}$ and $B_0 \in L^\infty(\Omega,H^s)$ be ${\mathcal F}_0$-measurable, suppose that $B_n$ is the solution to the Galerkin approximated equations (equation eq:EMHD_Ito_Galerkin of the paper), then there exists a universal constant $C := C(p,s,r,T)$ independent of $n$ such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item  We have the uniform energy estimate in $n \in {\mathbb N}$:
\begin{equation*}
    {\mathbb E} \Bigl( \sup_{t \in [0,T]} \left\lVertB_n(t)\right \rVert_{H^s({\mathbb T}^3)}^p +\int_0^T \VertB_n(t)\Vert_{H^s({\mathbb T}^3)}^{p-2} \left\lVertB_n(t)\right \rVert_{H^{s+\frac{\alpha}{2}}({\mathbb T}^3)}^2 dt \Bigr) \leq C \bigl( 1+ {\mathbb E} \VertB_0\Vert_{H^s({\mathbb T}^3)}^p \bigr). 
\end{equation*}
\item  For any $\gamma \in \left[0,{\frac{1}{2}} \right)$ and any $\beta \in (1,2]$, there is 
\[
{\mathbb E} \Big \lVert\int_0^\cdot \sum_{k=1}^\infty {\mathcal P}_n {\mathcal T}_k B_n dW^k_t \Big \rVert^p_{W^{\gamma,p}(0,T;H^{s-2+\frac{\beta}{2}})} \leq C \bigl( 1+ {\mathbb E} \VertB_0\Vert_{H^s({\mathbb T}^3)}^p \bigr ).
\]
\item  It holds that 
\[
{\mathbb E} \Big \lVert B_n - \int_0^\cdot \sum_{k=1}^\infty {\mathcal P}_n {\mathcal T}_k B_n dW^k_t \Big \rVert^2_{W^{1,2}(0,T;H^{s-2+\frac{\alpha}{2}})} \leq C \bigl(1+ {\mathbb E} \VertB_0\Vert_{H^s({\mathbb T}^3)}^4\bigr).
\]
\item   In addition, we have that for $\gamma \in \left[0,{\frac{1}{2}} \right)$:
\[
{\mathbb E} \left \lVert B_n\right \rVert^2_{W^{\gamma,2}(0,T;H^{s-2+\frac{\alpha}{2}})} \leq C \bigl(1+ {\mathbb E} \VertB_0\Vert_{H^s({\mathbb T}^3)}^4\bigr).
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Uniform energy estimate

body: In complex analysis, the residue theorem, sometimes called Cauchy's residue theorem, is a powerful tool to evaluate line integrals of analytic functions over closed curves; it can often be used to compute real integrals and infinite series as well. It generalizes the Cauchy integral theorem and Cauchy's integral formula. The residue theorem should not be confused with special cases of the generalized Stokes' theorem; however, the latter can be used as a component of its proof.
title: Residue theorem

[Lemma lem:regularity of arXiv:2609.00889, 'Dominant-Degree Conditions for Ramsey--Tur\'an Factors of Non-Directed Cycle Orientations'] For every real number $0<\varepsilon<1$, every real number $0\le d<1$, and all integers $M_0,q\ge1$, there exist integers
$M=M(\varepsilon,d,M_0,q)\ge M_0$ and
$n_{\rm reg}=n_{\rm reg}(\varepsilon,d,M_0,q)$
such that the following holds. Let $D$ be a digraph of order $n\ge n_{\rm reg}$, and let $\mathcal Q$ be a partition of $V(D)$ into at most $q$ nonempty parts. Then there are a partition
\[
V(D)=V_0\mathbin{\cup}V_1\mathbin{\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\cup}V_k
\]
refining $\mathcal Q$, and a spanning subdigraph $D'\subseteq D$, such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=\rm(\roman*)]
\item $M_0\le k\le M$, $|V_0|\le\varepsilon n$, and $|V_1|=\cdots=|V_k|=:m$;
\item $D'[V_i]$ is empty for every $i\in[k]$, and $V_0$ is isolated in $D'$;
\item for every $v\in V(D)$,
$d_{D'}^+(v)\ge d_D^+(v)-(d+2\varepsilon)n$ and $d_{D'}^-(v)\ge d_D^-(v)-(d+2\varepsilon)n;$
\item for every distinct $i,j\in[k]$, the pair $(V_i,V_j)$ in $D'$ is $\varepsilon$-regular and has density either $0$ or at least $d$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Degree-form diregularity

[Theorem 22 of arXiv:2608.29152, 'Uniform Statistical Convergence of Empirical Sinkhorn Potentials\\ with Exponential and Po'] Let \(A_0,L_0>0\), let \(\kappa\) be as above, and let
\(\mathcal M_{\eps}^{\mathrm{bin}}(\kappa)\) be the binary
bounded-interaction class. There exist constants
\(c_\kappa>0\) and \(n_\kappa\in\mathbb N\), depending only on
\(\kappa\), such that, for every \(0<\eps\le1\) and
\(n\ge n_\kappa\),
\[
    \inf_{\widehat f}
    \sup_{|t|\le1/4}
    \E_t
    d_\infty\bigl([\widehat f],[f_{\eps,t}]\bigr)
      \ge c_\kappa\frac{\eps}{\sqrt n}.
\]
Moreover, after possibly decreasing \(c_\kappa\),
\[
    \inf_{\widehat f}
    \sup_{|t|\le1/4}
    \Prob_t^{(n)}
    \left(
      d_\infty\bigl([\widehat f],[f_{\eps,t}]\bigr)
        \ge c_\kappa\frac{\eps}{\sqrt n}
    \right)
      \ge \frac38.
\]
The infima are over all measurable estimators based on the two

body:
[Theor thm:weighted-local-sparse of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] Let $M^{(k)}$, $k\geq 1$, be a deterministic sequence of $k\times n_k$ matrices with
$n_k/k\to\infty$. We assume the following:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item (Column support) The average column support size is of constant order:
  \[
  \frac1{n_k}\sum_{j=1}^{n_k}
  |\operatorname{supp}M^{(k)}_{\cdot j}|
  = O(1).
  \]
  \item (Average magnitude) The average magnitude of {\bf nonzero} entries
  is of constant order:
  \[
  \frac{
  1
  }{
     |\operatorname{supp}M^{(k)}|
    } 
    \sum_{i=1 }^k \sum_{j =1}^{n_k} |M^{(k)}_{ij}|
  =O(1).
  \]
  \item (Column overlaps)
  The total number of pairs of columns of $M^{(k)}$ whose supports overlap
  on two or more indices, is of order
  $$
  o\Big(\frac{n_k^2}{k}\Big).
  $$  
\end{enumerate}
Then for every $\varepsilon>0$, if
$\Omega_k\subset[n_k]$ are chosen uniformly at random with
$|\Omega_k|=\lfloor \varepsilon  k\rfloor$, we have \[
s_{\min}\bigl(M^{(k)}_{\Omega_k}\bigr)=o(1)
\]
with probability $1-o(1)$. Equivalently, a uniformly chosen proportional-size
column subset is well-invertible with asymptotically vanishing probability. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Main result: well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare

[Theo of arXiv:2510.23430, 'On the Martin boundary for discrete TASEP'] Assume that for a Borel probability measure $\nu$ on $\mathcal F$ and $\Psi\in\mathcal F$ we have

[Lemma LEM:Young of arXiv:2412.09790, 'Critical threshold for weakly interacting log-correlated focusing Gibbs measures'] Let $f$ be a strictly increasing function on $\mathbb{R}_+$
	such that   $f(0) = 0$ and its inverse $f^{-1}$ is also strictly increasing.
	Then, for any $a, b \ge 0$, we have
	\begin{align}
		ab \le \int_0^a f(x) dx   +  \int_0^b f^{-1}(x) dx 
		
	\end{align}
	
	\noindent
	with equality if and only if $b = f(a)$.
	In particular, applying (equation Young1 of the paper)
	to  $f(x) = e^x - 1$ and $f^{-1}(x) = \log(1+x)$
	\textup{(}with $b$ replaced by $b-1$\textup{)}, 
	we have 
	\begin{align}
		ab \le e^{a} + b \log b - b
		
	\end{align}
	
	\noindent
	for any $a \ge  0$ and $b \ge 1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.04045, 'Heat content and spectrum for subordinated sub-Laplacians'] We study heat content and spectral properties of subordinated sub-Laplacians on arbitrary Carnot groups. We consider restrictions of such operators to bounded open sets with zero Dirichlet boundary condition and study their spectral properties. In particular, for a large class of subordinators we give explicit eigenvalue estimates in terms of the subordinator and the eigenvalues of the sub-Laplacian. We also provide large-time asymptotics of the heat content for the subordinated sub-Laplacian in terms of its spectral gap. For fractional sub-Laplacians we prove short-time asymptotics for the corresponding heat content and relative heat content. Our approach combines semigroup methods, probabilistic techniques, geometric measure theory, and heat kernel estimates.
title: Abstract of arXiv:2609.04045: Heat content and spectrum for subordinated sub-Laplacians

[Corollary 40 (Convergence with an atom, stated with a reference measure) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Let $(\XX,\XXA)$ be a measurable space and $\lambda$ a $\sigma$-finite measure on
it. Let $p : \XX \to [0,\infty)$ be measurable with $\int_{\XX} p \dd\lambda = 1$, put
$\pi(A) := \int_{A} p \dd\lambda$ and $\Xp := \{p > 0\} \in \XXA$. Let
\[
  \kappa : \XX \times \XX \longrightarrow [0,\infty), \qquad (x,y) \longmapsto \kappa(y \mid x),
\]
be $\XXA\otimes\XXA$-measurable, put
$\theta(x) := \int_{\XX}\kappa(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y)$, assume $\theta(x) \le 1$
for every $x \in \XX$, so that
\[
  T(A \mid x) := \int_{A} \kappa(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y) + \bigl(1-\theta(x)\bigr)\,\ind_{A}(x)
  \qquad (A \in \XXA,\ x \in \XX)
\]
defines a Markov kernel $T$ on $(\XX,\XXA)$. Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep,topsep=3pt]
  \item \emph{(the chain can move)} $\theta(x) > 0$ for every $x \in \XX$;
  \item \emph{(invariance)} $\displaystyle\int_{\XX} \kappa(y \mid x)\,p(x)\,\lambda(\dd x) = \theta(y)\,p(y)$ for $\lambda$-almost every $y \in \XX$;
  \item \emph{(the support is not left)} for every $x \in \XX$: $\ \kappa(y \mid x) = 0$ for $\lambda$-almost every $y \in \XX \setminus \Xp$;
  \item \emph{(positivity)} $\kappa(y \mid x) > 0$ for $(\lambda\otimes\lambda)$-almost every $(x,y) \in \Xp\times\Xp$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\pi$ is the unique invariant probability measure of $T$, and
$\tv{T^{n}\circ\mu - \pi} \to 0$ for every $\mu \in \Prob$. If $p > 0$
$\lambda$-almost everywhere, hypothesis (iii) is vacuous.

[Def 40 (Convergence of one-parameter subgroups) of arXiv:2608.30990, 'Convergence of symmetries: nilpotency, dimension, and perfectness'] Given a sequence $\vv _i \in \mathfrak{g}_i$ with $\vert \vv _i \vert _{B_i} \leq 1 $ for each $i$, we say the sequence of one-parameter subgroups  $\gamma_i : \mathbb{R} \to G_i $ given by  
\[            \gamma_i (t) : =   \exp (t \vv _i )     \]
\emph{converges} to a one-parameter subgroup $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to G$ if for any $T > 0 $ and any identity neighborhood $ U \subset G $, for $i$ large enough one has 
\[     \phi_i (  \gamma _i (t)   ) ^{-1} \gamma (t)     \in U    \]
for all $t \in [-T,T]$.
title: Convergence of one-parameter subgroups

body: A square matrix with strictly positive entries has a unique eigenvalue of largest modulus; that eigenvalue is real, positive, simple, and possesses strictly positive left and right eigenvectors (Perron). For irreducible nonnegative matrices the largest eigenvalue is still positive and simple with positive eigenvectors, though other eigenvalues may share its modulus when the matrix is periodic (Frobenius). It governs stationary distributions of Markov chains, spectral ranking, and population models.
title: Perron-Frobenius Theorem

Let epsilon>0 and H,Htilde:R^d->R be C1 potentials with positive finite Gibbs normalizers. Set mu(dx)=Z^(-1)exp(-H/epsilon)dx,nu(dx)=Ztilde^(-1)exp(-Htilde/epsilon)dx,and D=Htilde-H. Suppose osc(D)=esssup D-essinf D is finite. If Ent_mu(f^2)<=2*C_mu*integral||grad f||^2 dmu for smooth test functions,then nu satisfies this gradient log-Sobolev inequality with C_nu<=exp(osc(D)/epsilon)*C_mu. In the inverse rate convention alpha=1/C_mu,an admissible rate is alpha_nu>=alpha*exp(-osc(D)/epsilon). No bound on grad D or preservation of convexity is required. This is the gradient LSI,not a discrete modified LSI or a Poincare-only bound. Draft,independent review pending.
d>=1,epsilon>0,C1 potentials,and positive finite Gibbs normalizers.
Bounded essential oscillation of the potential difference;the base gradient LSI with coefficient2*C_mu is assumed.

[Thm \cite{R1961} of arXiv:2411.02141, '\bf Uniqueness of Maximum Scores in Countable-Outcome Round-Robin Tournaments'] Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent discrete random variables, and let $p_j = \sup_{x} \mathbb{P}\left(X_j = x\right).$
Then
$
\sup_{x} \mathbb{P}(\sum_{j=1}^{n}X_j = x) \le \frac{A}{\sqrt{\sum_{j=1}^{n} (1 - p_j)}},
$
for some constant $A$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary cor:E_i of arXiv:2605.01444, 'From second moments to pairwise negative correlation: \\applications to minimal and unifor'] Suppose $G=(V,E)$ is a finite, connected, regular graph with degree $d\;\geqslant\; 3$. Set $M\coloneq \lfloor \log_3d \rfloor$. For $i=1,\ldots,M$, set $\epsilon_i\coloneq \frac{3^i}{d}$ and set $\epsilon_{M+1}\coloneq 1$. Let $E_0$ be the set of edges $e$ such that $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{eff}}(e)\;\leqslant\; \frac{3}{d}$. For $i=1,\ldots,M$, let $E_i$ be the set of edges $e$ with $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{eff}}(e)\in (\epsilon_i,\epsilon_{i+1}]$. Then $E=\bigcup_{i=0}^{M}E_i$ and for each $i\in[1,M]$,
	\[
	|E_i|\;\leqslant\; \frac{|V|}{3^i-2}\;\leqslant\; \frac{|V|}{3^{i-1}}\,.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary cor:E_i of arXiv:2605.01444

[Theorem thm:NMP_2D of arXiv:2604.25851, '{Non-uniqueness of nonlinear Markov processes in the sense of McKean associated with parab'] Let $\mathcal P_0 \subseteq \mathcal P$, and $\{\mathbb{P}^\zeta\}_{\zeta \in \mathcal P_0}$, $\{\mathbb{Q}^\zeta\}_{\zeta \in \mathcal P_0}$ be nonlinear Markov processes such that
    $$\mathbb{P}^\zeta_{s,t} = \mathbb{Q}^\zeta_{s,t},\quad \forall \zeta \in \mathcal P_0, \, 0\leq s \leq t.$$
    Then $\mathbb{P}^\zeta = \mathbb{Q}^\zeta$ for all $\zeta \in \mathcal P_0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 12 (\textsf{Lemma 2.2 and Proposition 2.3 in \cite{Zhe19}}) of arXiv:2608.12451, '2608.12451'] Let $F=Q_d(f;Y)\in L^4(\PP)$ and define $F_t$ as above.
 Then $(F,F_t)$ is exchangeable and

\noi
\begin{align}
 \frac1t\E[F_t-F | \cG]
 &\xrightarrow{t\downarrow 0}   -dF   \quad  \text{in $L^4(\PP)$}
\notag
 \\
 \frac1t\E[(F_t-F)^2 | \cG]
  &\xrightarrow{t\downarrow 0}     2\Gamma(F,F)
\quad  \text{in $L^2(\PP)$},
\notag
  \\
 \frac1t\E[(F_t-F)^4]
 &\xrightarrow{t\downarrow 0}      -4d\,m_4(F)+12\E[F^2\Gamma(F,F)]
 \geq  0.
\notag
\end{align}

\noi
Moreover, $\E[F_t-F | \cG]=-(1-e^{-dt})F$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 21 of arXiv:2606.09904, 'Non-explosion principles for branched rough differential equations with unbounded coeffici'] Suppose that \ref{eq:kappa_n} holds for all \(n = 0, \dots, N\). For all \(n + |f| \le N\), we have that
  \begin{equation}
    \|D^n [\partial^f_X \phi(\mathbf{Y})]\|_{\infty; B_r} \lesssim l(r)^{((|f| + 1)\theta - (|f| + n)\kappa)\gamma}.
  \end{equation}
  Consequently, \(C_{I}^f \lesssim l(R(k + 1))^{((|f| + 1)\theta - N\kappa)\gamma}\)
  and for all \(\tau \in \CT^+_{N - 1}\), 
  \[\|\partial^\tau_X Y\|_{\infty; I} \lesssim l(R(k + 1))^{(|\tau|\theta - (|\tau| - 1)\kappa)\gamma}.\]

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2603.26003, 'Pathwise Convergence of a Modular Simulation Scheme for Hybrid SDEs with Memory'] Let $t \ge 0$ and $y, \hat{y} \in D_E((-\infty, t))$ be two trajectories with identical discrete components. For $U$ uniformly distributed on $[0, \lambda)$, the disagreement probability satisfies
\[
\mathbb{P}\big(\mathfrak{h}(t, U, y) \neq \mathfrak{h}(t, U, \hat{y})\big) \le \frac{1}{\lambda} \sup_{i\in\mathbb{Z}}\sum_{j\neq i} \mathfrak{m}\Big(\big(\Delta_{ij}(t,y) \triangle \Delta_{ij}(t,\hat{y})\big)\Big).
\]
By Assumption~\ref{ass:logHolder}, this yields the bound
\[
\mathbb{P}\big(\mathfrak{h}(t, U, y) \neq \mathfrak{h}(t, U, \hat{y})\big) \le \frac{K_H}{\lambda}\cdot\frac{1}{-\log\big(\|y-\hat{y}\|_t\big)}.

PROOF (UNAUDITED); novelty unverified. For each n>=2 and Z~N(0,1), let f_n(z)=min(1,max(0,z-n)), c_n^2=E[(1+f_n(Z))^2], and X_n(z)=(1,(1+f_n(z))/c_n)^T. The uncentered Gram G_n=E[X_nX_n^T] is positive definite with unit diagonal; each feature coordinate is bounded by 2 and 1-Lipschitz. For the empirical Gram S_n of n iid rows, let s be the second-coordinate Schur complement given the first. Then E[(sqrt(s(S_n)/s(G_n))-1)^2]>=1-1/n. The relative mean-square error is at least 1-1/n. Thus bounded Lipschitz Gaussian-derived features and unit marginal moments do not alone yield a uniform relative Schur sampling rate or a uniform kappa bound in the companion lemma. The feature threshold varies with n and the population conditional variance may vanish: this is not failure of a fixed program or a theorem with a uniform innovation floor.
Z standard normal; n independent rows; n>=2
Uncentered empirical Gram; Schur complement given the first constant coordinate
Feature threshold varies with n; population conditional variance need not be uniformly bounded below
No failure for a fixed activation, fixed program or realized critical-chain rate is claimed
metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:dfc750496e9b0835124f4835970e1cf00845295a1bc65b9db93e2e19c848cf8d","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/df/dfc750496e9b0835124f4835970e1cf00845295a1bc65b9db93e2e19c848cf8d.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:a3ae660870fdea8f35c824f25dc15528839b10e28ddcb8627fdccfcc527d9ad7","bundle_entry_key":"t250_w712_c026","bundle_id":"population.w712-t250-c025-c026-relative-schur-and-rare-features","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability and Gaussian conditioning","draft":"w712/bundle_019.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.neural_networks:rare-gaussian-features-relative-schur-sampling-obstruction","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C026 v1: bounded Gaussian features do not give uniform relative Gram control

Kind: route-failure. Target: 4. Status: proof (unaudited); novelty unverified.
This is an exact obstruction to omitting the whitened-moment hypothesis of C025, not a fixed-program Tensor Program counterexample.

## Feature family and conclusion
For each integer n>=2, let Z be standard normal and define

f_n(z)=min(1,max(0,z-n)),
c_n^2=E[(1+f_n(Z))^2],
X_n(z)=(1,(1+f_n(z))/c_n)^T.

Take n iid rows X_n(Z_i), the uncentered empirical Gram S_n=n^(-1) sum X_n(Z_i)X_n(Z_i)^T, and G_n=E[X_n(Z)X_n(Z)^T]. Let s denote the Schur complement in the second coordinate given the first. Then

G_n is positive definite with both diagonal entries 1;
each feature coordinate is bounded in absolute value by 2 and is 1-Lipschitz (or better);
E[(sqrt(s(S_n)/s(G_n))-1)^2] >= 1-1/n.             (1)

In particular no uniform O(n^(-1/2)) relative square-root-Schur rate follows over this family from bounded Lipschitz feature coordinates, unit marginal second moments and Gaussian base rows alone. The empirical matrix can be singular; excluding that event without a probability bound would discard the obstruction.

## Proof
Write F=f_n(Z), mu=E F, and v=Var(F). We have 0<=F<=1 and 1<=c_n<=2. The positive Gaussian probability of Z<=n gives F=0 with positive probability, and the positive probability of n<Z<n+1 gives F>0 with positive probability. Thus v>0. Directly,

G_n=[[1,(1+mu)/c_n],[(1+mu)/c_n,1]],
s(G_n)=1-(1+mu)^2/c_n^2=v/c_n^2>0.

This proves positive definiteness and the stated diagonal entries. The first feature is constant. The clipped hinge f_n is 1-Lipschitz, so the second feature is 1/c_n-Lipschitz, at most 1; both coordinates are bounded by 2. These bounds do not depend on n. They also imply uniform bounded coordinate fourth moments, a fact that does not control whitened moments.

Let A_n be the event that all Z_i<=n. On A_n, every F_i=0 and

S_n=[[1,1/c_n],[1/c_n,1/c_n^2]].

Therefore S_n has rank one and s(S_n)=0. The random variable inside the expectation in (1) equals one on A_n. Since E Z^2=1, Markov's inequality gives P(Z>n)<=P(Z^2>=n^2)<=1/n^2. The union bound yields P(A_n)>=1-n/n^2=1-1/n. Nonnegativity on its complement proves (1).

## The exact unpaid implication
C025 controls relative Schur sampling through kappa=E[(X^TG^(-1)X)^2]. If a uniform kappa bound followed from the coordinate bounds just verified, C025 with d=2 would force the left side of (1) to tend to zero. Therefore that implication is false. This use does not refute C025; it locates the missing hypothesis. A rare transverse feature direction can have a much larger normalized fourth moment than the individual coordinates suggest.

The population conditional variance s(G_n) can tend to zero; no uniform lower bound for it is claimed. Thus this example also does not rule out a theorem with a separate uniform conditional-innovation lower bound. The threshold n changes with the sample size: it is a uniform-over-feature-families counterexample, NOT failure of convergence for a fixed activation or fixed program. It supplies no depth-to-width law, no realized growing-depth architecture lower bound, and no contradiction to arXiv:2607.06290, whose structural constants may depend on the activation and the Gram point.

## Strongest reason this might not obstruct the desired theorem
The actual critical chains may have additional analytic structure that prevents such rare standardized contrast directions, or an absolute-output coupling may remain accurate as s(G_n) tends to zero even while its relative error is large. Those alternatives remain open. A concrete check needed before extending this obstruction to the full target would be to realize comparable features in the stated fixed-activation critical chain with controlled stability constants; no such realization is supplied here.

The proof is analytic and uses only Gaussian positive density, E Z^2=1, Markov's inequality and a union bound. No Gaussian tail numerics or quadrature are used. The threshold-normalizing constant is an expectation defined exactly, not a floating estimate. C025 is an unaudited companion claim; equation (1) and the failure of uniform relative Schur control are proved independently above.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:aaabc5c893bde2a01d827bbf2481dfb9d080c5192eebb6167cd15af366f3bf1a","revision_digest":"sha256:2713a94d271ac41bb68aea63cf4fc481ed69431db0b826641b69a43eab17a95f","source_id":"own-work:T250-w712-C026:v1","source_revision":"C026 v1; proof (unaudited); source context Section 4.2 (4.9), not a claim that the paper states this result","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2607.16017, 'On large networks of integrate-and-fire neurons with short-term synaptic plasticity'] We have
	\begin{align*}
		J \int \frac{\d }{\d v} S^v_1(z) \nu_\infty(\d v) &= \frac{\widehat{\Xi_1}(z) - \widehat{\Xi_1}(z + 1/\tau)}{1-(1-U)\widehat{K}(z+1/\tau)} + \frac{\widehat{\Xi_1}(z)( \widehat{K}(z) - \widehat{K}(z+1/\tau))}{(1-\widehat{K}(z))(1 - (1-U) \widehat{K}(z+1/\tau)) } ,\\
		J \int_0^\infty \left[ \frac{\d }{\d v} S^2_t(v) \right] \frac{\nu_\infty(\d v)}{1+ \tau U f(v)} &= \frac{\widehat{\Xi_2}(z+1/\tau)}{1-(1-U) \widehat{K}(z+1/\tau)}.
	\end{align*}
		Therefore,
		\[ \widehat{\Theta}_\alpha (z)  = \frac{1}{1-(1-U)\widehat{K}(z+\tfrac{1}{\tau})} \left\{ \widehat{\Xi_1}(z) - \widehat{\Xi_1}(z + \tfrac{1}{\tau}) + \widehat{\Xi_2}(z+\tfrac{1}{\tau}) +  \frac{\widehat{\Xi_1}(z)( \widehat{K}(z) - \widehat{K}(z+\tfrac{1}{\tau}))}{1-\widehat{K}(z)}  \right\}. \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem t: univ pro of arXiv:2605.20587, 'Persistence and entropic repulsion of stationary Gaussian fields with spectral singularity'] Let $\alpha \in [0,d)$, let $f$ be an SGF on $\mathbb{R}^d$ or $\mathbb{Z}^d$, non-singular as per (equation e:sing of the paper), and suppose that one of the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[{\rm (i)}]
\item 
\[ \frac{K(x)}{k_\alpha(x)} \text{ is slowly varying, as } x\to\infty. \]
\item $\alpha>0$ and $\mu$ has density $\rho$ in a neighbourhood of the origin such that
\[ \frac{\rho(\lambda)}{\rho_\alpha(\lambda)} \text{ is slowly varying, as }\lambda \to 0.\] 

\item $\mu$ is radial (i.e.\ the field $f$ is isotropic), and
\[ \frac{\mu[B(\delta)]}{\mu_\alpha[B(\delta)]} \text{ is slowly varying, as } \delta\to 0. \]

\item $\alpha=0$ and $\mu$ has an atom at the origin.

\end{enumerate}
Then
\begin{equation}
\theta_\mu(T) \sim c_{\alpha,d}\, m(d-\alpha) \frac{\log T}{\mu[B(\tfrac 1 T)]}, \quad \text{ as }T\to\infty,
\end{equation}
where $m=\|\mu_{a.c.}\|$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 10 of arXiv:2609.02065, '\textbf{From Bowditch's question to Goldman's conjecture for type-preserving representatio'] \cite[Proposition 4.1, Theorem 4.3]{goldman}
    
        Let $\chi: \SL\times\SL\to \mathbb{R}^3$ be the character map, and let $\kappa: \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}$ 
        be the polynomial map defined by
        $$
        \kappa(x,y,z) := x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - xyz - 2 .
        $$
        Then 
        \begin{enumerate}[(1)]
            \item 
        For a pair $(A,B)$ in $\SL\times\SL$, $\kappa\big(\chi(A,B)\big) = \tr[A,B]$. Furthermore, if $A$ and $B$ are non-elliptic, 
        then $\kappa\big(\chi(A,B)\big) = 2$ if and only if the representation $\phi:\pi_1(\Sigma_{0,3})\to \SL$ determined by the pair $(A,B)$ is reducible.
        \item  If 
        $\kappa(x,y,z)\neq 2$
        and $\chi^{-1}(x,y,z)$ is non-empty, 
        $\chi^{-1}(x,y,z)$ in $\SL\times \SL$ 
        consists of one orbit of the $\GL$-conjugation, which is the union of two orbits of the $\SL$-conjugation.
        \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 10 of arXiv:2609.02065

body: Theorem (campaign status: conditional): S9 verdict. There is a rigorous linear-in-defect theorem for the part of the high-corank problem in which the weighted two-shadow batching has bounded entropy-normalized exposure congestion kappa. It is conditional, works on affine boundary fibres, uses the conditional defect that the dense-witness exchange leaves unused, and controls ALL unselected rows. In the original junction basis the constant is 2*kappa+1. If selected witnesses have private support at most s then kappa <= (s-1)/beta with beta = log_2(4/3), giving new quotient residual rank <= (1 + 2(s-1)/beta)*L (tag 1); insisting on the triangularly exchanged witness basis raises the constant by only beta^{-1}, to (1 + (2s-1)/beta)*L (tag 2). Notes: S9: 'This is a genuine residual-compression result, not the false inference that one residual direction is enough per selected witness.' Conditional on bounded kappa, which is precisely what the residual class (congestion >~ log n in every useful basis) denies.

[Lemma 9 (Last-occurrence occupancy bound) of arXiv:2604.26298, 'The Expiring Coupon Collector\\ Sliding-Window Surjection Flux and Rare-Entry Laws'] Let \(U\) be a uniform onto word of length \(m=M-1\) over an alphabet of size \(N=n-1\), and let \(R_u\) be the number of letters whose last occurrence in \(U\) is at most \(u\).  Assume
\[
        n\le M\le n\log n,
        \qquad
        \frac{\lambda_{n,M}}{(\log M)^2}\longrightarrow\infty,
        \qquad
        \lambda_{n,M}:=n\left(1-\frac1n\right)^M .
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
\sum_{u=1}^{M-1}
\Ebb\left[
        \frac{R_u}{n}\left(1-\frac1n\right)^{u-1}
        \exp\left\{-(R_u-1)_+\left(1-\frac1{n-1}\right)^{u-1}\right\}
\right]
        =O\left(\frac{\log M}{\lambda_{n,M}}\right).
\end{equation}
In particular the sum is \(o(1)\).

[Lemma 47 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] Let $\alpha,\gamma \in (0,1]$. Suppose $U : \T^d \to \R^d$ is a random field such that
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item almost surely, $U \in C^{\alpha-}(\T^d)$,
        \item and $\limsup_{r \to 0} \sup_{x \in \T^d} r^{-\gamma d} \P( |U(x)| \leq r)<\infty$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then almost surely, if $Z := \{ x \in \T^d : U(x) =0\}$, for any $\rho < \gamma \alpha$, 
    \[\lim_{r \to 0} r^{-\rho d} |\{x \in \T^d : d_{\T^d}(x,Z) \leq r\}| =0.\]

Fix -1<a<1 and sigma_a(t)=t for t>=0, sigma_a(t)=a*t for t<0, applied coordinatewise. A depth-L network has L affine layers, activation after the first L-1 layers, and an affine final output. Its squared parameter cost is sum_ell (||W_ell||_F^2+||b_ell||_2^2). For a function f and domain Omega, R_L is the infimum of this cost over all such finite-width networks equal to f on Omega; R_L=+infinity if the class is empty. Let Omega be a nonempty bounded open subset of R^d and f:R^d->R^m continuous finite piecewise-affine. Define rank_J(f;Omega)=max_(x in Omega, f differentiable at x) rank(Jf(x)). Define rank_BN(f;Omega) as the least integer k>=0 for which f=g composed with h on Omega with both h:R^d->R^k and g:R^k->R^m continuous finite piecewise-affine; k=0 means constant. Then rank_J(f;Omega)<=liminf_(L->infinity) R_L/L<=limsup_(L->infinity) R_L/L<=rank_BN(f;Omega). If the two ranks agree, the ordinary normalized-cost limit exists and equals their common value. If that ordinary limit exists in any other case, it lies between the two ranks. This card does not assert existence of the ordinary limit for every f solely from these two estimates.

[Definition of arXiv:2411.13430, 'Optimal subelliptic super-Poincar\'e and isoperimetric inequalities on stratified Lie grou'] For a Borel set $A \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, the surface measure $\mu^+(A)$ of $A$ is defined by 
    \[ \mu^+(A) = \liminf_{\epsilon \rightarrow 0^+} \frac{\mu(A_\epsilon) - \mu(A)}{\epsilon}, \quad A_\epsilon = \{y \in \mathbb{R}^n \mid d(y, A) < \epsilon\} \] 
    and the isoperimetric profile of $\mu$ by 
    \[ I_\mu(t) = \inf \{\mu^+(A) \mid A \text{ Borel and such that } \mu(A) = t\}. \]

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). Efron-Stein: for f(X_1,...,X_n) with independent coordinates, Var f <= (1/2) sum_i E[(f(X) - f(X^{(i)}))^2], where X^{(i)} resamples coordinate i; for a Boolean function under a product measure the right side is a constant times the total influence sum_i I_i(f). This bounds variance by total influence and needs no monotonicity. Benjamini-Kalai-Schramm (1999): if f_n : {0,1}^{m_n} -> {0,1} satisfy sum_i I_i(f_n)^2 -> 0 then (f_n) is noise sensitive, i.e. Cov(f_n(omega), f_n(omega^eps)) -> 0 for every fixed noise level eps > 0; for monotone functions the converse also holds. The quantitative engine is Talagrand's inequality Var f <= C sum_i I_i(f)/log(e/I_i(f)) (hypercontractivity), which for functions with all influences at most n^{-a} improves Efron-Stein by a factor log n; the same mechanism gives the BKS sublinear variance bound Var(first-passage time to distance n) <= C n/log n for first-passage percolation with suitable edge weights. What these do NOT give: a lower bound on any individual influence (that is Kahn-Kalai-Linial: max_i I_i >= c Var(f) log n / n), or a power improvement n^{1-eps} on the variance, which remains open outside integrable models. Typical failure: Using the plain Efron-Stein variance bound and mistaking it for the BKS lower bound on the maximal individual influence, which is a distinct and much sharper statement requiring monotonicity and a total-influence hypothesis; conflating the two leads to claiming individual-coordinate sensitivity conclusions, needed for noise-sensitivity theorems, from a tool that in its basic form only controls the aggregate variance. Canonical reference: Efron and Stein, 1981, The Annals of Statistics; Benjamini, Kalai and Schramm, 1999, Publications Mathematiques de l'IHES.
Independent coordinates (product measure)
BKS noise sensitivity criterion: sum of squared influences tends to zero
Talagrand's logarithmic improvement needs hypercontractivity of the product measure
title: Technique: Efron-Stein Inequality and the Benjamini-Kalai-Schramm Influence Bound

body: Lemma (campaign status: proved): One supported relation already uses one dimension of the rank-three global row space. By coordinate-fullness a genuinely new local full-dual form is represented by a displayed coordinate outside the forest endpoints; its equality with the local form gives a global row with a unique nonzero outside coordinate, so distinct extras give independent rows modulo the supported relation unless two local forms coincide on the global atom. Such a coincidence would be a second supported relation on the endpoints, which is excluded, so at most two local extras are possible. Notes: Exclusion of the second supported relation: with four or five endpoints, projective simplicity fails after two independent supported relations, so the only possible profile is six forms of rank four; normalizing $h=(1,1,1,1)$, the five old restrictions mod $h$ are five distinct nonzero vertices of $\{0,1\}^3$, any five of which contain two collinear signed pair differences, giving $d_{\rm geo}\le2$ and contradicting the standing $d_{\rm geo}=3$ hypothesis. S3 stresses the DEHOMOGENIZED reading: the relevant vectors are classes modulo $\mathbb Rh$, not the six sign rows in the unreduced four-space. This completes the bridge from the finite local table to the balanced support-four/six row.

[Proposition prop:variation_of_const of arXiv:2604.22528, 'Malliavin calculus for signatures with applications to finance'] Let $X = (X_t)_{t \in [0,T]}$ be a continuous $\mathbb{R}^d$-valued semimartingale with signature $\sigX$.  
    Suppose that each component $\bm{\sigma}^{{\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}}}$, ${\color{NavyBlue}{\mathbf{v}}} \in V$, is a continuous semimartingale.
    Then (equation eq:G_val_sde of the paper) admits a unique strong solution $\sigY$, and this solution admits the following representation:
    \begin{equation}
        \sigY[t] 
        = \sigY[s]\,\sigX[s,t] 
        + \int_s^t \circ d\bm{\sigma}_u \otimes \sigX[u,t].
    \end{equation}

[Lem 4 of arXiv:2609.02686, 'The Bonnet-Myers theorem on Finsler manifolds with integral weighted Ricci curvature bound'] Let $(M, F, m)$ be an $n$-dimensional $(n \geq 2)$ Finsler metric measure manifold. Assume that $\mathbf{S}\geq -\vartheta$ for some $\vartheta \geq 0$.
Further, for $p>\frac{n}{2}$ and  $R_{0}>0$, assume that $\overline{\left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{\Lambda_{F}^2}\right\|}_{p, R_{0}, \vartheta}(x_{0})\leq \left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)^{2-\frac{1}{p}}$. Then, for any $r \in \left[\frac{\pi}{\Lambda_{F}}, \frac{R_0}{\Lambda_{F}}\right]$, there exists a positive constant $C_{1}=C_{1}(n,p,\Lambda_{F},R_{0})$, such that
\beq
A(r) &\leq &  C_{1} e^{\vartheta r} \overline{\left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{\Lambda_{F}^2}\right\|}_{p, R_{0}, \vartheta}^{\frac{(n-1)p}{2p-1}}(x_{0}) m\left(B_{R_{0}}^{+}(x_{0})\right)\nonumber\\
&\leq &  C_{1} e^{\vartheta r} \left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)^{n-1} m\left(B_{R_{0}}^{+}(x_{0})\right), 
\eeq
where
$
C_{1}(n,p,\Lambda_{F},R_{0}):=\frac{3\cdot 2^{2p+n-3}\Lambda_{F}}{\pi} +\frac{\pi^{2p-1}}{4^{p}}\left(\frac{n-1}{(2p-1)(2 p-n)}\right)^{p-1} \Lambda_{F}^{-(2p-1)}R_{0}^{2p-1}.
$

[Lemma 12 (Minkowski inequality) of arXiv:2608.12070, 'Central limit theorems for a heavy-tailed subcritical Galton-Watson process with state-dep'] \cite[Theorem 9.2a]{bai}

Let $\{Z_n\}_{n\ge 0}$ be a sequence of random variables and $\alpha \ge 1$. If $\E[|Z_n|^\alpha] < \infty$ for every $n$ and the series $\sum\limits_{n=0}\limits^\infty \|Z_n\|_\alpha$ converges, then $\sum\limits_{n=0}\limits^\infty Z_n$ converges absolutely almost surely, and
\[
\Bigl\|\sum_{n=0}^\infty Z_n\Bigr\|_\alpha \le \sum_{n=0}^\infty \|Z_n\|_\alpha,
\]
where $\|Z\|_\alpha := (\E[|Z|^\alpha])^{1/\alpha}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Minkowski inequality

body:
[Definition def:well-behaved-backtracking of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] Let
\[
    \tau_t\cdot\tau_{t-1}\cdot\dots\cdot\tau_1,
    \qquad
    \tau_i\in\{\alpha,\beta, \frac{1}{d} I_m, M_D\},
\]
be a gadget record. We say that an adjacent pair
\(
    \tau_s\cdot\tau_{s-1}
\)
forms a \emph{well-behaved backtracking intersection} if
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \(\tau_s\) and \(\tau_{s-1}\) form one of the designated
    backtracking intersections: half-diamond, half-flat, or full-diamond;
    \item the vertices participating in this backtracking block have no
    additional vertex intersections with the earlier prefix
    \(
        \tau_{s-2}\cdot\dots\cdot\tau_1.
    \)
\end{enumerate}
If the first condition holds but the second fails, we call
\(\tau_s\cdot\tau_{s-1}\) a \emph{non-isolated backtracking pair}.
These are the three-way backtracking/diagonal intersections.
title: Well-Behaved Backtracking Intersections

[Defn 52378 of arXiv:2606.29143, 'Comonotonic and moment matching approximations for sums of lognormal random variables'] Let $A = (a_1, ..., a_m)^{'}$ and $Q = (q_1, ..., q_m)^{'}$ be two numerical vectors with $\min(a_1, ..., a_m) \geq 0, \max(a_1, ..., a_m) > 0$ and $0 = q_0 < q_1 < q_2 < ... < q_m = 1$. Let $X$ be a continuous random variable which means that the distribution function $F_X(x)$ of $X$ is continuous on $(-\infty, \infty)$. Then we call $\omega_{A, Q, X}(x)$ the step-weight function of the random variable $X$ associated with the numerical vectors $A$ and $Q$, abbreviated as $\omega_{A, Q}$ when there is no ambiguity, if it is defined by 
$$\omega_{A, Q, X}(x) = \begin{cases} a_1, & F^{-1+}_{X}(q_0) \leq x < F_X^{-1}(q_1), \\  
a_k, & F_X^{-1}(q_{k - 1}) \leq x < F_X^{-1}(q_k), \,\, k = 2, ..., m - 1, \\
a_m, & F_X^{-1}(q_{m - 1}) \leq x \leq F^{-1}_{X}(q_m), \\ 
0, & \text{otherwise}. 
\end{cases}$$
title: Defn 52378 of arXiv:2606.29143

[Definition 6 ($\mathrm{Ewens}(m,\theta)$ distribution) of arXiv:2604.25877, 'Asymptotic height of Plancherel random trees'] The $\mathrm{Ewens}(m,\theta)$ distribution on integer partitions of $m$ is the probability
measure on feasible count vectors
$(C_1,\dots,C_m)$ given by
\begin{equation}
\Pp\left((C_j)_{1\le j\le m}=(c_j)_{1\le j\le m}\right)
=\frac{m!}{\theta^{(m)}}\prod_{j=1}^m \frac{\theta^{c_j}}{j^{c_j}c_j!}~,
\end{equation}
for all $(c_j)_{1\le j\le m}$ such that $\sum_{j=1}^m j c_j=m$~.
title: $\mathrm{Ewens}(m,\theta)$ distribution

Let d,n>=1 be integers, lambda>0, and tau=n/d^2. Let H_mu be arbitrary real d by (d+1) matrices and y_mu arbitrary real labels, for mu=1,...,n. Set m=d(d+1), h_mu=vec_row(H_mu) in R^m, where vec_row stacks rows. The unique minimizer Gamma_star of sum_mu(y_mu-<Gamma,H_mu>_F)^2+(n/d)lambda||Gamma||_F^2 satisfies vec_row(Gamma_star)=G(0)v/d, where v=sum_mu y_mu h_mu. For a symmetric positive semidefinite m-square matrix Pi and pi>=0, define G(pi)=[sum_mu h_mu h_mu^T/d+pi Pi+tau lambda I_m]^(-1), q(pi)=G(pi)v/(d sqrt(d)), z_mu=[y_mu/d;h_mu/sqrt(d)], Pi_e=diag(0,Pi), and G_e(pi)=[sum_mu z_mu z_mu^T+pi Pi_e+tau lambda I_(m+1)]^(-1). Let c(pi) be the first diagonal entry of G_e(pi); it is strictly positive. Then 1/c(pi)=sum_mu y_mu^2/d^2+tau lambda-v^T G(pi)v/d^3, and G_e(pi) has blocks [[c,-c q^T],[-c q,G+c q q^T]]. For any A in R^(d x (d+1)), writing e_1=(1,0,...,0) in R^(m+1), (1/d)tr(Gamma_star A^T)=-[0,vec_row(A)^T]G_e(0)e_1/[c(0)sqrt(d)]. For any symmetric positive semidefinite B in R^((d+1) x (d+1)), choose Pi=I_d tensor B. Then (1/d)tr(Gamma_star B Gamma_star^T)=(d/dpi)[1/c(pi)] at pi=0, equivalently the right derivative at zero. These are exact finite identities of Appendix C (C2)-(C14), especially Lemma 2 (C12)-(C14), printed pp.21-22, of 2405.11751v3. They require no Gaussian assumptions, independence, asymptotic limit, or claim about unrestricted attention-factor training. Positive ridge is retained; no inverse formula at lambda=0 is asserted.

[Definition 73 of arXiv:2607.10486, 'Weak martingale solutions to stochastic Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system with transport '] Assume that  $(\Omega,\mathscr{F},\mathbb{P})$ is  a probability space with the right-continuous filtration of $\sigma$-fields $\mathbb{F}=(\mathscr{F}_t)_{t \in [0,T]}$. 
We denote by $\mathscr{P}(\mathbb{F})$ the $\sigma$-field of predictable subsets  of $[0,\infty) \times \Omega$,  with respect to $\mathbb{F}$, i.e. the  $\sigma$-field  generated by the following family of subsets of $[0,\infty) \times \Omega$:
\[
\bigcup_{0\leq s < t < \infty} \left\{ (s,t] \times A: A \in \mathscr{F}_s \right\},
\]
see \cite[Section 1.7]{Metivier+Pellaumail_1980}.\\
By $\mathcal{M}_{\loc}^{\rc}(\mathbb{F},\mathbb{P})$, we denote  the class of $\mathbb{R}$-valued local c\`adl\`ag martingales on the stochastic basis $(\Omega,\mathscr{F},\mathbb{F},\mathbb{P})$. 

A process $u:[0,\infty)\times \Omega \to \rU$ is called predictable, or more precisely $\mathbb{F}$-predictable, if and only if the map 
\[
u: [0,\infty)\times \Omega \to \rU
\]
is $\mathscr{P}(\mathbb{F})/\mathscr{B}(\rU)$ measurable.
title: Definition 73 of arXiv:2607.10486

body:
[Definition def:entangled of arXiv:2607.18070, 'The Brownian loop-catcher'] For $r\ge1$ and an ordered tuple of directed paths $\omega_i:a_i\to b_i$, $1\le i\le r$, put
\begin{equation}
 H_i=P(\omega_i),\qquad C_0=\varnothing,\qquad
 P_i=\Phi_{C_{i-1}}(H_i),\qquad
 C_i=C_{i-1}\cup\operatorname{supp}(P_i).
\end{equation}
Let $\gamma_i$ be the directed path corresponding to the record $P_i$ (equipped with the time parametrization).  We call $(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_r)$
the entangled multipath loop-erasure of $(\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_r)$, whose range is $C_r$.
title: entangled multipath loop-erasure

body: The Euler characteristic chi is a topological invariant. For a finite CW complex (in particular a convex polyhedron's surface) chi = V - E + F, the alternating count of cells by dimension; in general chi(X) is the alternating sum of Betti numbers when homology is finitely generated. Examples: chi of the sphere is 2, of a closed orientable surface of genus g is 2 - 2g, of the torus 0.
title: Euler characteristic

[Lem 8 (Compact critical bubbles) of arXiv:2609.02523, '\bf Strong Ill-Posedness in critical and subcritical regimes for the Hunter--Saxton equati'] There exist two constants $c>0$ and $C>0$ and a family $(\varphi_\varepsilon)_{0<\varepsilon<1}$ of functions in $C_c^\infty(\R)$ with the properties
\begin{gather}
  \supp\varphi_\varepsilon \subset[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon], \\ 
  
  \|\varphi_\varepsilon\|_{\dot H^{3/2}}  +\|\varphi_\varepsilon\|_{\dot H^1}  +\|\varphi_\varepsilon\|_{L^\infty}   \leqslant C \varepsilon^2, \\ 
  
  -\inf_{x\in\R}\varphi_\varepsilon'(x)   \geqslant -\varphi_\varepsilon'(0)\geqslant c \varepsilon^{-1},
\end{gather}
for all $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$.

body:
[Prop local_at_1k of arXiv:2604.07183, 'Stopping on the last success with unknown odds: asymptotic minimax optimality of the plug-'] Fix~$p_0\in(0,1)$ and~$\frac1k\in\mathcal B_{p_0}$. Then,
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] for every~$u\in\mathbb R$,
\begin{equation}

\lim_{n\to\infty}\sqrt n\,\bigl(V_n\bigl(p_{n,k}(u)\bigr)-W_n\bigl(p_{n,k}(u)\bigr)\bigr)
=
\gamma_k |u| \Phi(-|u|)
;
\end{equation}
in particular, this local profile is maximized exactly at~$|u|=u_\star$, where it
equals~$2\gamma_kC_\star$;
\item[(ii)] for every~$\rho>0$ and every sequence~$(\pi_n)$ of (possibly randomized) \mbox{$p$-blind} rules,
\begin{equation}

\lim_{\rho\to\infty}\ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\ \sup_{|u|\le\rho}\ \sqrt n\,\bigl(V_n\bigl(p_{n,k}(u)\bigr)-W_n^{\pi_n}\bigl(p_{n,k}(u)\bigr)\bigr)
 \ge
\gamma_k\sup_{u>0}u\Phi(-u)
=
2\gamma_kC_\star
,
\end{equation}
a bound that the plug-in rule attains: for that rule and any~$\rho\ge
u_\star$, the~$\liminf$ above is in fact a
limit and equals~$2\gamma_kC_\star$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop local_at_1k of arXiv:2604.07183

[Lemma lem:reg_vary_mu+finitemoment of arXiv:2510.06891, 'Multivariate CLT for L\'evy processes: convergence rates without moment assumptions'] Let the assumptions of Theorem~(thm:int-3_one-dim_version of the paper) hold. Define $\mu:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ and $\mu_t:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ via $\mu(x)\coloneqq -\log\varphi_{Y_1}(x)$ and $\mu_t(x)\coloneqq -\log\varphi_{\xi_t}(x)=t\mu(B(t)^{-1}x)$. Then, the following statements hold.
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=2.5em, nosep]
    \item[{\nf(a)}] The function $\mu$ is regularly varying at $0$ with index $2$. Hence the function $\ell$, given by $\ell(x)\coloneqq2\mu(x)x^{-2}=\Sigma_Y+4x^{-2}\int_{(0,\infty)}(1-\cos(x v))\nu_Y(\mathrm{d} v)$ for $x\in\mathbb{R}$, is slowly varying at $0$.
    \item[{\nf(b)}] The function $B$ is an asymptotic inverse of $x\mapsto 1/(2\mu(1/x))$ as $x\to\infty$, i.e. $1/(2\mu(1/B(t)))\sim t$ as $t\to\infty$, and is thus regularly varying at $\infty$ with index $1/2$.
    \item[{\nf(c)}] We have $\xi_t \coloneqq B(t)^{-1}Y_t\xrightarrow{d} Z$ as $t\to\infty$, that is, for any $x\in\mathbb{R}$, we have
    \begin{equation}
    
    \varphi_{\xi_t}(x)
    =\exp(-\mu_t(x))
    =\exp\big(-t\mu(B(t)^{-1}x)\big)
    \to e^{-x^2/2},
    \quad \text{as }t\to\infty.
    \end{equation}
    \item[{\nf(d)}] For any $p\in[0,2)$, the process $Y$ has a finite $p$-moment and $\sup_{t\geqslant 1}\mathds{E}[|\xi_t|^p]<\infty$.
    \item[{\nf(e)}] For any $p\geqslant 1$ we have $\sup_{t\geqslant 1}\int_\mathbb{R}|F_t(x)-\Phi(x)|^p\mathrm{d} x<\infty$.
\end{itemize}

[Definition 4 (Simultaneous profile completion) of arXiv:2607.16724, 'Algebraic Transfer for Operator-Valued Gaussian Chaoses: Oriented Schatten Profiles and Si'] For $1\le r<\infty$, let
\[
 \mathfrak T_{m,r}(\cH_1,\ldots,\cH_m;\cC,\cE)
\]
be the Banach completion of $\cK_m^{\mathrm{alg}}$ in the norm
$\Prof_{m,r}$.  For the same-field space, let $\cH$ be real, choose
labelled copies $\cH_\C^{(1)},\ldots,\cH_\C^{(m)}$ of its
complexification and unitary identifications
$J_\nu:\cH_\C\to\cH_\C^{(\nu)}$, and set
\[
 \operatorname{Dec}_m
 :=J_1\otimes\cdots\otimes J_m\otimes
   \Id_{\conj{\cC}}\otimes\Id_{\cE}.
\]
On symmetric algebraic kernels define
\[
 \norm K_{\mathfrak W_{m,r}}
 :=\Prof_{m,r}(\operatorname{Dec}_mK),
\]
and denote the resulting completion by
\[
 \mathfrak W_{m,r}(\cH;\cC,\cE).
\]
Different choices of labelled copies give canonically isometric spaces by
Proposition~\ref{prop:legwise-rule}.  At order zero and for
$1\le r<\infty$, set
\begin{equation}

 \mathfrak T_{0,r}(\cC,\cE)
 =\mathfrak W_{0,r}(\cC,\cE)
 :=\Sch_r(\cC,\cE).
\end{equation}
For every $1\le r\le\infty$, including the operator-norm endpoint, use the
algebraic convention
\begin{equation}

 \Prof_{0,r}(K):=\norm K_{\Sch_r},
 \qquad \Sch_\infty(\cC,\cE)=\cL(\cC,\cE).
\end{equation}

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2607.27082, '2607.27082'] Let \(X=(X_t)_{t\ge0}\) be a Brownian motion started from zero with variance
parameter \(\sigma^2>0\), that is,
\[
\E[X_t]=0,
\qquad
\E[X_t^2]=\sigma^2t,
\qquad t\ge0.
\]
For \(x>0\), set
\[
\tau_x^+(X):=\inf\{t\ge0:X_t\ge x\}.
\]
Then, for every \(q>0\),
\begin{equation}
\E\!\left[e^{-q\tau_x^+(X)}\right]
=
\exp\!\left(-\frac{x\sqrt{2q}}{\sigma}\right).
\end{equation}
For related Brownian first-hitting-time formulas, see also \cite[Part~II, Chapter~1, Section~2]{BorodinSalminen2002}.

body:
[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2609.00483, 'On Embedding Hamming Spheres with Applications to Positive Curvature'] Fix $\delta \in (0,\frac{p-1}{p})$. Suppose
$\rho : \mathbb{Z}_p^r \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}_p^m$
is injective and its image $C$ has minimum distance at least $\delta m$. Then
$$
r \le (1 - H_p(J_p(\delta)))m
+ \frac{1}{2}\log_p m
+ \frac{1}{2}\log_p\!\left(\frac{8(1-J_p(\delta))}{J_p(\delta)}\right)
+ \log_p(p-1)
+ \log_p\bigl(\kappa_p(\delta,m)\bigr),
$$
where
$\kappa_p(\delta,m) :=
\min\left\{(p-1)m+1,\gamma\!\left(p,\delta m,\lceil J_p(\delta)m\rceil-1,m\right)\right\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 11 of arXiv:2609.00483

[Lemma lem:sum of arXiv:2411.09381, 'On the well-posedness of SPDEs with locally Lipschitz coefficients'] Consider a function $f:(0\,,\infty)\to(0\,,\infty)$ and
	an increasing function $g:(0\,,\infty)\to(0\,,\infty)$. If
	there exists $\beta,T_0>0$ such that
	\[
		\sup_{t\in(0,T]}\left[ \mathrm{e}^{-\beta t}f(t)\right] \le \mathrm{e}^{-\beta T} g(T)
		\qquad\forall T\in(0\,,T_0),
	\]
	then $\sup_{(0,T]}f\le g(T)$ for every $T\in(0\,,T_0)$.

[Theorem 30 (Variance) of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] The second moment of $T_{m,p} - T_{m,0}$ is
  \begin{equation}
    
    \begin{aligned}
    \E\left[\left(T_{m,p} - T_{m,0}\right)^2 \right]
    &= 2\E\left[T_{m,p} - T_{m,0}\right]^2
    - \E\left[T_{m,p} - T_{m,0}\right]\\
      &\quad + 
      \frac{(1-p)^{-m}}{p} \Bigg\{ 2\,p^2\,m^3 \left(1-p\right)^{m-1}\\
      &\qquad +
      \int_0^1 p^3\, m^3 \left(m-1\right)
      \left(1 - p\,x\right)^{m-2} N(x) \, dx
      \Bigg\},
    \end{aligned}
  \end{equation}
  where $N(x) \coloneqq
  (\log^2(1-x) - 2\log(1-x) + 2)\,(x-1) + 2$.
  If $p = p_m$ is an $o(1/m)$ sequence
  then
  \[
    \Var\left(T_{m,p}\right)
    = \Var\left(T_{m,0}\right)
    + 2\,p\,m^3 - p\,m^2
    + \frac{5}{4} \, p^2\, m^4
    + O\left(p^3\,m^5\right)
    + O\left(p^2 \, m^3\right).
  \]
  If $p \sim c/m$ then
    \[
      \Var\left(T_{m,p}\right)
      = \Var\left(T_{m,0}\right)
      + \left(1+o(1)\right) m^2
      \left[2\,c + c^2\int_0^1
      e^{-cx} \left(L(x) + N(x)\right) dx\right]
    \]
  where $L$ is defined in Theorem~\ref{thm:first moment}.
  If $p = \omega(1/m)$ then
  \[
    \Var\left( T_{m, p} \right) =
    \Var\left( T_{m, 0} \right) + \frac{\left(1-p\right)^{-2m}}{p^2}
    \left( 1 + O\left(\frac{1}{p\,m} \right)\right).
  \]
  In particular, for $p > 0$ fixed,
  \begin{align*}
    \Var\left(T_{m,p}\right)
    - \Var\left(T_{m,0} \right)
    &= \frac{(1-p)^{-2m}}{p^2} \Bigg\{
      1 + \left(-12\,p + 10 + \frac{2}{p} \right) m^{-1}\\
    &\phantom{{}= \frac{(1-p)^{-2m}}{p^2} \Bigg\{}
      + \left(126\,p^2 - 184\,p + 29 + \frac{24}{p} + \frac{5}{p^2} \right) m^{-2}\\
    &\phantom{{}= \frac{(1-p)^{-2m}}{p^2} \Bigg\{}
      + O\left(m^{-3}\right)\Bigg\}.
  \end{align*}
  \begin{proof}
    This proof is akin to the previous one.
    By redefining $\Lambda \coloneqq 1/I_{m,p}$
    we can use the reasoning of
    \eqref{eq:mgf second deriv} to extract the second moment,
    \begin{equation}
      
      \E \left[ \left(T_{m,p} - T_{m,0}\right)^2 \right]
      = M_{T_{m,p}-T_{m,0}}''(0) =
      \left(\frac{1}{\Lambda}\right)''\left(0^-\right)
      = 2 \E\left[ T_{m,p} - T_{m,0} \right]^2
      - \Lambda''\left(0^-\right),
    \end{equation}
    where we have used $\Lambda(0^-) = \Lambda(0) = 1$. By
    \eqref{eq:one deriv}, the unknown term $\Lambda''(0^-)$ is
    \begin{align*}
      -\Lambda''\left(0^-\right)
      &= -\frac{\partial^2}{\partial t^2} \left\{ (1-p)^{-m}
      \left[1 - \int_0^1 p\, m \left(1-x\right)^{m\exp(-t)-m}
      \left(1 - p\,x\right)^{m-1} dx\right] \right\}_{t=0^-}\\
      &= \frac{\partial}{\partial t} \left\{ (1-p)^{-m}
      \int_0^1 p\, m^2 \, e^{-t} \left(1-x\right)^{m\exp(-t)-m}
      \left(1 - p\,x\right)^{m-1} \log\left(\frac{1}{1-x}\right) dx \right\}_{t=0^-}.
    \end{align*}
    Then, with the fact
    \[
      \frac{\partial}{\partial t} \left\{
        e^{-t} \left(1-x\right)^{m\exp(-t)-m} \right\}_{t=0^-}
        = \log\left(\frac{1}{1-x}\right) m - 1,
    \]
    we find
    \begin{align*}
      - \Lambda''\left(0^-\right)
      &= (1-p)^{-m}
      \int_0^1 p\, m^2 \,
      \left[\log\left(\frac{1}{1-x}\right) m - 1\right]
      \left(1 - p\,x\right)^{m-1} \log\left(\frac{1}{1-x}\right) dx\\
      &=
      - \E\left[T_{m,p} - T_{m,0}\right]
      + 
      (1-p)^{-m}
      \int_0^1 p\, m^3 \,
      \left(1 - p\,x\right)^{m-1} \log^2\left(\frac{1}{1-x}\right) dx,
    \end{align*}
    where we have recognised \eqref{eq:bad first moment}.
    To handle the integral, use integration by parts

body: [Definition rank_r_definition of arXiv:2411.04795, 'Metastable Distributions of Semi-Markov Processes'] For $ \varepsilon > 0, 0 \le r  <  R$, and $x \in S, $ let us define the Markov chain $\left({ {\bf X}_n^{x, r, \varepsilon}, {\bf T}_n^{x, r, \varepsilon} }\right)$ by  $$  {\bf X}_n^{x, r, \varepsilon} = {\bf X}_{ \theta_n(r) }^{x, \varepsilon},   \ {\rm for \ } n \ge 0,  $$ $$ \ {\bf T}_0^{x, r, \varepsilon} = 0, \    {\bf T}_n^{x, r, \varepsilon} = \sum_{ m =  \theta^{x, \varepsilon}_{n - 1}(r) + 1}^{ \theta^{x, \varepsilon}_{n}(r)  } {\bf T}_{ m }^{x, \varepsilon}, \ {\rm for \ } n \ge 1. $$  The semi-Markov process driven by the Markov chain $\left({ {\bf X}_n^{x, r, \varepsilon}, {\bf T}_n^{x, r, \varepsilon} }\right)$ will be denoted by ${ X}_t^{x, r, \varepsilon}$. For completeness, we restate the definition of the probability kernel $P^{r, \varepsilon}(x, \cdot)$. For $ A \in \mathcal B (S)$, $$ P^{r, \varepsilon}(x, A) = \mathbb P \left({ {\bf X}_1^{x, r, \varepsilon } \in A }\right).  $$ For $1 \le  j \le M_r$ and $r < R$, we define $T^{r, \varepsilon}(x, S_j^r)$ to be a random variable with distribution given by $$ \mathbb P \left({T^{r, \varepsilon}(x, S_j^r) \in I }\right) = \mathbb P \left({ {\bf T}_1^{x, r, \varepsilon} \in I \vert {\bf X}_1^{x, r, \varepsilon} \in S_j^r }\right) $$ whenever $ P^{r, \varepsilon}(x, S_j^r) > 0.$ Noting that there is only one cluster of rank $R$, we define $ { X}_t^{x, R, \varepsilon} = x$ for all $x \in S$ and $ t \ge 0$. We also put $ {\bf T}_1^{x, R, \varepsilon} = \infty$ for every $x \in S$.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Explicit calculation or obstruction with source-specific scope Result: The source switch-over variance absorption has a useful exact batch check. When the critical queue serves exactly k2 jobs per cycle, its batch time is sum of k2 iid B2 variables plus the total switch-over S. The batch variance divided by k2 is Var(B2)+Var(S)/k2. Assigning the same S/k2 to every effective job instead would give marginal variance Var(B2)+Var(S)/k2^2 but introduce correlations between those jobs. Ignoring those correlations would produce the wrong diffusion coefficient. Check: The variance of the sum of the correlated effective jobs contains k2*(k2-1) covariance terms Var(S)/k2^2 and exactly restores Var(S). The mean effective service is E B2+E S/k2, agreeing with the source. Obstruction: This verifies the proposed effective mean and variance but not the joint stationary limit. General renewal residual lives, the stable-queue vacation environment, asymptotic independence and stationary interchange still need a proof. The source simulation correlation near zero is not a proof of independence.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0302-one-critically-loaded-queue-under-general-k-limited-polling-inputs
No independent review

body: [Question q:always_smooth of arXiv:2506.12171, 'The multinomial dimer model'] Using the height function, we saw that multinomial limit shapes in 2D are smooth from the fact that they do not have facets (Corollary~(cor:2Dsmooth of the paper)). Is it true that multinomial limit shapes are smooth in any dimension? A positive answer to this question would mean that the $C^1$ condition in Theorem~(thm:critical_gauge_scaling_limit of the paper) is satisfied in any dimension. (Stated as a question by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Question q:always_smooth of arXiv:2506.12171

Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a compactly generated tensor-triangulated category. The homological cosupport induces a bijection between cohomological Bousfield classes $\langle E \rangle^*$ and subsets of $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathcal{T}^c)$ if and only if $\mathcal{T}$ is homologically stratified. Furthermore, stratification is equivalent to the classification of homological Bousfield classes together with the condition that every cohomological Bousfield class is homological.

[Lem 53 ({\cite[Lemma~7.2) of arXiv:2609.02561, 'NON-NEF LOCI IN MIXED CHARACTERISTIC'] {MST}}]
Suppose that $R$ is $\Q$-Gorenstein, $\dim R \geq 2$, and the residue field $k=R/\m$ is $F$-finite.
Let $\pi:Y\rightarrow X=\Spec R$ be a blow up of some $\m$-primary ideal $\mathcal{I}$.
Suppose that $\mathcal{I}\cdot\sO_{Y} =\sO_{Y}(-mE)$ for some $m\in\Z_{>0}$, where $E$ is a normal prime $\pi$-exceptional divisor.
Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a log $\Q$-Gorenstein pair.
Let $\Delta_E$ denote the different of $K_Y + E+\pi_{*}^{-1}\Delta$ along $E$.
Suppose that $(E,\Delta_E)$ is globally $F$-regular.
Then $(R,\Delta)$ is BCM-regular. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 6 (Canonical rough path for tfBm) of arXiv:2512.04646, '\textbf{Canonical Rough Path over Tempered Fractional Brownian Motion: Existence, Construc'] Let $H > 1/4$, $\lambda > 0$, and $B_{H,\lambda}$ be a
$d$-dimensional tfBm with independent components. Then there exists
a canonical geometric rough path
$\mathbf{B}_{H,\lambda} = (B_{H,\lambda}, \mathbb{B}_{H,\lambda})$
where
\begin{equation}

\mathbb{B}_{H,\lambda}(s,t)
= \lim_{|\mathcal{P}|\to 0}
  \sum_{[u,v]\in\mathcal{P}}
  B_{H,\lambda}(s,u)\otimes B_{H,\lambda}(u,v)
\quad\text{in }L^2(\Omega).
\end{equation}
Moreover, $\mathbf{B}_{H,\lambda}$ satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
  \item \textbf{Chen's relations:} For $s \le u \le t$,
    $\mathbb{B}_{H,\lambda}(s,t) = \mathbb{B}_{H,\lambda}(s,u)
    + \mathbb{B}_{H,\lambda}(u,t)
    + B_{H,\lambda}(s,u)\otimes B_{H,\lambda}(u,t)$.
  \item \textbf{Moment estimates:} For any $q \ge 1$,
    \begin{align}
    \mathbb{E}\bigl[|B_{H,\lambda}(s,t)|^q\bigr]
      &\le C_q(H,\lambda)\,|t-s|^{qH}, \\
    \mathbb{E}\bigl[|\mathbb{B}_{H,\lambda}(s,t)|^q\bigr]
      &\le C_q(H,\lambda)\,|t-s|^{2qH}. 
    \end{align}
  \item \textbf{$p$-variation:} Almost surely,
    $\mathbf{B}_{H,\lambda}\in\mathscr{C}^p([0,T],\mathbb{R}^d)$
    for every $p > 1/H$.
  \item \textbf{Continuity in parameters:}
    $(H,\lambda)\mapsto\mathbf{B}_{H,\lambda}$ is continuous in
    the $p$-variation rough path topology on compact subsets of
    $\{H>1/4,\,\lambda>0\}$.
  \item \textbf{Boundary case:} For $H=1/2$,
    $\mathbf{B}_{1/2,\lambda}$ is the Stratonovich rough path over
    the OU process; as $\lambda\to 0^+$, it converges to the
    standard Stratonovich rough path over Brownian motion.
\end{enumerate}

[Definition def:OGP of arXiv:2605.10911, 'The stochastic block model has the overlap graph property for modularity'] For a graph $G_n$ with planted partition~$\mathcal{P}$, the optimisation problem $\max_\mathcal{A} q_\mathcal{A}(G_n) $
exhibits OGP with values $\mu > 0$ and $0 \leq 
u_1 < 
u_2$ if the following holds: 
For any partition $\mathcal{B}$ for which $q_\mathcal{B}(G_n)\geq q^{\star}(G_n)-\mu$, it holds that either $d(\mathcal{B}, \mathcal{P})\leq 
u_1$, or that $d(\mathcal{B}, \mathcal{P})\geq
u_2$. Furthermore, $d(\mathcal{B}', \mathcal{P})\geq 
u_2$ does indeed occur for some partition $\mathcal{B}'$ with $q_{\mathcal{B}'}(G_n)\geq q^{\star}(G_n) - \mu$.
title: \bf Overlap gap property -- planted model

body:
Let (X_n)_{n=1}^\infty be independent real random variables with \mathbb{E}[X_n] = 0 for every n. For each n let \phi_n: [0, \infty) \to [0, \infty) be a function with \phi_n(0) = 0 and \phi_n(t) > 0 for t > 0 such that \phi_n(t)/t and t^2/\phi_n(t) are non-decreasing on (0, \infty). If \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\mathbb{E}[\phi_n(|X_n|)]}{\phi_n(n)} < \infty, then \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=1}^n X_k \to 0 almost surely. With one function \phi_n = \phi for every n, \phi(t) = t^2 gives Kolmogorov's criterion \sum_n \mathrm{Var}(X_n)/n^2 < \infty, and \phi(t) = t^p with 1 \le p \le 2 gives \sum_n \mathbb{E}|X_n|^p/n^p < \infty. The bound on growth (t^2/\phi_n(t) non-decreasing, so \phi_n grows at most quadratically) cannot be replaced by convexity with \phi(t)/t \uparrow \infty: for X_n = \sqrt{n}\,G_n with G_1, G_2, \dots independent standard normal and \phi(t) = t^4, \sum_n \mathbb{E}[\phi(|X_n|)]/\phi(n) = 3\sum_n n^{-2} < \infty, yet \frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^n X_k is normal with mean 0 and variance (n+1)/(2n) \to 1/2, so it does not tend to 0 even in probability. Convexity is not needed either: \phi(t) = t^2 for 0 \le t \le 1 and \phi(t) = t for t \ge 1 satisfies both conditions and is not convex.
