[Defn def:reg of arXiv:2606.30517, '\textsc{Convergence towards Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations with a focus on Diestel--'] A function $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R^+$ is \textbf{log-regularly-varying} if 
		$\lim_{n\to\infty} f(n+1)/f(n)$ exists and is positive. This clearly implies that $\forall r_0\in\mathbb Z: \lim_{n\to\infty} f(n+r_0)/f(n) = e^{br_0}$ for some $b\in\mathbb R$, which is called the \textbf{index} of $f$. We also use $p\coloneqq e^b$ in the formulas.\\
		Similarly, a measurable function $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^+$ is called \textbf{log-regularly-varying} (at $+\infty$) if $f\circ\log$ is regularly-varying; i.e., for every $r_0\in\mathbb R$, the limit $\lim_{r\to\infty} f(r+r_0)/f(r)$ exists and is positive. 
		By well-known results about regularly-varying functions,  the limit is equal to $e^{b r_0}$‌ for some $b\in\mathbb R$, which is called the \textbf{index} of $f$. Hence, $f(r)=l(r) e^{br}$, where $l$ is a \textbf{long-tail} function (see [bookFoKoZa11heavytail]); i.e., $\lim_{r\to\infty} l(r+r_0)/l(r)=1, \forall r_0$.
title: \textsc{Log-Regularly-Varying Functions}

body: In information theory, the entropy of a random variable quantifies the average level of uncertainty or information associated with the variable's potential states or possible outcomes. This measures the expected amount of information needed to describe the state of the variable, considering the distribution of probabilities across all potential states. Given a discrete random variable , which may be any member within the set and is distributed according to , the entropy is where denotes the sum over the variable's possible values. The choice of base for , the logarithm, varies for different applications. Base 2 gives the unit of bits, while base e gives "natural units" nat, and base 10 gives units of "dits", "bans", or "hartleys". An equivalent definition of entropy is the expected value of the self-information of a variable.
title: Entropy (information theory)

[Lemma 9 (Binary prefix extraction) of arXiv:2608.31157, 'Sharp Approximation Rates for Neural Networks with Affine Latent Parameterizations'] For every $D\in\N^+$, there exist a two-input architecture
$\Psi_D\in\Arch(20,4D+2)$ and a fixed parameter vector
$\bmtheta_D\in\R^{P_{\Psi_D}}$.  Denote the resulting function by
\[
 E_D:=(\Psi_D)_{\bmtheta_D}:\R^2\to\R.
\]
Then, for every $\bmnu\in\{0,1\}^D$,
\[
 E_D\bigl(\operatorname{bin}0.\nu_1\cdots\nu_D,k\bigr)
 =\sum_{i=1}^k\nu_i,
 \qquad k=0,1,\ldots,D,
\]
where the sum is understood to be zero when $k=0$.
The vector $\bmtheta_D$ depends on $D$, but none of its entries depends on
$\bmnu$.

Own-work draft; status proof (unaudited). If a nonzero even continuous Gaussian density obeys f(e^(i*(theta0+t)))/|t|^beta->c with beta>0 and 0<c<infinity, then rho-star mixing requires beta=2m for an integer m>=1. Helson-Sarason ordinary rho-mixing factorization gives f=|p|²w with all positive and negative powers of w integrable; the residual local exponent beta-2m must therefore be zero. Consequently f=(2-2cos theta)^d, d>=0, is rho-star mixing exactly when d is an integer, and then rho*(n)=0 for n>d. This does not decide theta²/log(1/|theta|).

body:
Use Frobenius inner products. Let f:R^(d by d)->R be C3, convex and transpose-invariant, f(W)=f(W^T). Put L(U)=f(U U^T)/2. Let 1<=r<=d and let U_0 in R^(d by r) have full column rank and be a second-order stationary point of L: grad L(U_0)=0 and D2L(U_0) is positive semidefinite. Set W_0=U_0 U_0^T and G_0=grad f(W_0), so G_0 U_0=0. On Sym_d consider g(W)=-W grad f(W)-grad f(W) W and J=Dg(W_0)|_(Sym_d). Then J[Delta]=-Delta G_0-G_0 Delta-W_0 D2f(W_0)[Delta]-D2f(W_0)[Delta]W_0. Choose orthonormal v_1,...,v_(d-r) spanning ker U_0^T and diagonalizing -G_0 there, with eigenvalues mu_i. In the factor Hessian -D2L(U_0), choose an orthonormal eigenbasis E_p with eigenvalues xi_p, arranging the r(r-1)/2 gauge directions U_0 R, R^T=-R, last; these gauge directions lie in its zero eigenspace. The complete spectrum of J on Sym_d consists of (i) mu_i+mu_j, 1<=i<=j<=d-r, and (ii) xi_p, 1<=p<=dr-r(r-1)/2. An associated left eigenmatrix in (i) is v_i v_j^T+v_j v_i^T, and an associated right eigenmatrix in (ii) is E_p U_0^T+U_0 E_p^T. All xi_p<=0. This is the symmetric-space restriction used in the paper, not an assertion about arbitrary nonsymmetric extensions of g; it does not assert that J is diagonalizable.

[Definition 2 (Classical history–dependent walk on $G$) of arXiv:2511.18216, 'Classical localization problem: a survey'] Fix a collection of node matrices $\{S^{(v)}\}_{v\in V}$ with $N_v=2$, and let
$G=(V,E)$ be a finite directed graph. A \emph{configuration} at time $n$ is a
pair $(\gamma_n,\eta_n)$, where
\begin{itemize}
  \item $\gamma_n=(e_0,\dots,e_n)$ is a directed path of length $n$ on $G$;
  \item $\eta_n$ records, for each node $v$, how many times each incident edge
        has been used by $\gamma_n$.
\end{itemize}
The process starts from some initial edge $e_0$ with configuration
$(\gamma_0,\eta_0)$. Given $(\gamma_n,\eta_n)$, let $v$ be the terminal vertex
of $e_n$, and let $j\in\{1,2\}$ be the label of the incoming channel at $v$
used by $e_n$. If $\gamma_n$ has never visited $v$ before, the walk chooses the
outgoing channel $i\in\{1,2\}$ with probability proportional to
$|S^{(v)}_{ij}|^2$, and sets $e_{n+1}$ to be the corresponding outgoing edge.
If $\gamma_n$ has already used some of the incident edges at $v$, the walk exits
along one of the remaining edges with probability~$1$ (if exactly one remains)
or according to the appropriate conditional weight derived from
\eqref{eq:node-weight}.
title: Classical history–dependent walk on $G$

[Theorem thm.uni of arXiv:2512.19897, 'On the convoy of the ASEP speed process'] The inhomogeneous random walk $Q_n$ converges in distribution to a q-independent limit after scaling. That is, for any $x\in\left(0,1\right)$, $c = x\left(1-x\right) \in \left(0, \frac{1}{4}\right)$, we have
    \begin{equation}
        \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{Q_{n+1}}{\sqrt{n}} \overset{\left(d\right)}{=} |\mathcal{N}\left(0,2c\right)|.
    \end{equation}
    Moreover, conditionally on the event $U_0 = u$ with $x = \tfrac{1+u}{2}$, the size of the convoy is asymptotically universal, 
    \[
    \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{\mathbb{E}_x \left[\mathcal{C}_0^{n}\right]}{\sqrt{n}} =  \sqrt{\frac{4c}{\pi}}. 
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma lem:defect-infinity of arXiv:2608.11931, '\texorpdfstring{Nonlinear parabolic characterizations of stochastic completeness at infini'] Assume that $G$ does not satisfy \hyperref[def:SC-infinity]{\textup{{(SC\textsubscript{$\infty$})}}}{}.  Then there exists $U\in\ell^\infty(X)$ such that
\[
    0\le U\le1,
    \qquad
    \sup_XU=1
    \qquad \text{and} \qquad
    (\Delta +1)U\le0.
\]
Consequently, the function $V:=2U-1$ satisfies
\[
    -1\le V\le1,
    \qquad
    \sup_XV=1
    \qquad \text{and} \qquad
    \Delta V\le -(V+1)-K.
\]
In particular, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, the super-level set $\{x \in X \mid V(x)>1-\varepsilon\}$ is nonempty and on it
\[
    -\Delta V\ge V+1+K>2-\varepsilon .
\]

  h^*(s) := \inf_{x>0} \{ sx - h(x) \}.
\]

body:
[Theorem 16 (Finite-fourth strong circular limit) of arXiv:2608.04824, 'Strong Convergence for a General Class of Random Matrix Models'] Let \(X_{1,n},\ldots,X_{d,n}\) satisfy
Definition~\ref{def:iid-entry-model}.  Let \(c_1,\ldots,c_d\) be a free
circular family in a tracial \(C^*\)-probability space with faithful trace,
with
\[
 \tau(c_\kappa c_\lambda^*)=\delta_{\kappa\lambda}\sigma_\kappa^2.
\]
Then \((X_{1,n},\ldots,X_{d,n})\) converges almost surely strongly in
\(*\)-distribution to \((c_1,\ldots,c_d)\).
Moreover, on the same probability-one event, for every \(q\geq1\) and every
\[
 Q\in M_q(\mathbb C)\otimes
 \mathbb C\langle x_1,\ldots,x_d,x_1^*,\ldots,x_d^*\rangle,
\]
one has
\begin{align*}
 \|Q(X_n,X_n^*)\|&\longrightarrow\|Q(c,c^*)\|,\\
 (\trn_q\otimes\trn_n)Q(X_n,X_n^*)
 &\longrightarrow(\trn_q\otimes\tau)Q(c,c^*).
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite-fourth strong circular limit

body:
[Thm t:def-YM-general of arXiv:2607.24640, 'The Yang-Mills measure on surfaces via Morse theory'] There exists a finitely additive functional 
$$
\mathbb{M}_{\operatorname{YM}}:\mathcal{B}_\infty^G\rightarrow \mathbb{R}_+
$$
such that the following holds
 \begin{enumerate}
  \item for all $n\geqslant 1$, $\mathbb{M}_{\operatorname{YM}}$ is a measure on $(\Omega\times G^{2g},\mathcal{B}_n^G)$;
  \item  for every continuous and piecewise $\mathcal{C}^1$ curve $\gamma:[0,1]\rightarrow \Sigma$ that is everywhere transverse to $V$, one can find a random variable $\mathbf{Hol}(\gamma)\in G$ such that, for every $n\geqslant 1$,  
  $$
  \gamma([0,1])\subset K_n\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathbf{Hol}(\gamma)\ \text{is}\ \mathcal{B}_{n}^G-\text{measurable}
  ,$$ 
  and, for every admissible disk $D$, the law of $\mathbf{Hol}(\partial D)$ is given by
  $$
  \boxed{\mathbb{M}_{\operatorname{YM}}\left(\mathbf{Hol}(\partial D)\in d\mathrm{g}\right)=\left(\sum_{\rho\in\widehat{G}}\frac{e^{-\frac{c_2(\rho)}{2}\upsilon(\Sigma\setminus D)}}{\left(\operatorname{dim} V_\rho\right)^{2g-1}}\chi_\rho(\mathrm{g})\right)\left(\sum_{\rho\in\widehat{G}}\operatorname{dim} V_\rho e^{-\frac{c_2(\rho)}{2}\upsilon(D)}\chi_\rho(\mathrm{g})\right)\mu_G(d\mathrm{g}),}
  $$
  where $\rho:G\rightarrow \operatorname{GL}(V_\rho)$ runs over the equivalent classes $\widehat{G}$ of unitary irreducible representations of $G$, $c_2(\rho)$ is the Casimir number of $\rho$ and $\chi_\rho$ is the character of $\rho$.
 \end{enumerate}
 In particular, the partition function is given by
  $$
  \boxed{Z_{\operatorname{YM}}:=\mathbb{M}_{\operatorname{YM}}(\Omega\times G^{2g})=\sum_{\rho\in\widehat{G}}e^{-\frac{c_2(\rho)}{2}\upsilon(\Sigma)}\left(\operatorname{dim} V_\rho\right)^{2-2g}.}
  $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let T be a piecewise C^2 map of the interval which is uniformly expanding, that is |T'| >= lambda > 1 wherever it is defined, with finitely many branches. Let L be its transfer (Perron-Frobenius) operator acting on functions of bounded variation. Then there are constants 0 < theta < 1 and C > 0 with Var(L^n g) <= C theta^n Var(g) + C ||g||_{L^1} for every g of bounded variation and every n. A uniform bound of this shape - contraction on the strong seminorm up to a compact-in-the-weak-norm remainder - is a Lasota-Yorke inequality. Combined with the Ionescu-Tulcea and Marinescu theorem (equivalently Hennion's theorem, which identifies the essential spectral radius as the limit of the n-th root of the contraction factor), it gives L a quasi-compact action on the bounded-variation space, hence a finite-dimensional peripheral spectrum, an invariant density of bounded variation, finitely many ergodic absolutely continuous invariant measures, and exponential decay of correlations when the peripheral eigenvalue 1 is simple - which topological exactness or mixing supplies.
UNIFORM expansion (or expansion after a fixed number of iterates), finitely many branches, and bounded distortion;
without uniform expansion the inequality fails and the invariant density may be infinite.
The conclusion of quasi-compactness needs the embedding of bounded variation into L^1 to be compact, which is Helly's theorem on the interval.

[Theorem thm:5.3 of arXiv:2608.27474, 'Nonlocality of Cover-Time Changes Under Edge Addition'] For \(n\ge3\) and \(P_n\to C_n\),
with \(N=n-1\) and start \(i\in\{0,\ldots,N\}\),

\[
t_{\mathrm{cov}}(P_n,i)=N^2+i(N-i),
\]

\[
t_{\mathrm{cov}}(C_n,i)=\frac{n(n-1)}2,
\]

so

\begin{equation}
\boxed{
\delta_i
=
-\frac{(n-1)(n-2)}2-i(n-1-i)<0.
}

\end{equation}

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2606.31455, 'Discrete time-multidimensional renewal theory and applications'] Let $a,b:\mathbb{N}^d\to\mathbb{R}$. Their (multi-time) convolution product $c=a*b$ is defined by

\begin{equation}
[a*b](k)
:=\sum_{\ell+\ell'=k} a(\ell)\,b(\ell')
=\sum_{\ell\le_d k} a(\ell)\,b(k-\ell),
\qquad k\in\mathbb{N}^d,
\end{equation}

where $\le_d$ denotes componentwise inequality.

[Definition of arXiv:2609.00592, 'Bounded cohomology property on Jacobian elliptic surfaces with simplicial Mori cones'] Let $X$ be a smooth projective surface.
Let $\pi: X \to B$ be a surjective morphism with connected fibres.
We call $\pi: X\to B$ a fibration on the surface $X$ with the base curve $B$.
We say $X$ is an \emph{elliptic surface} if the general fiber of $\pi$ is an elliptic curve, and $\pi$ is \emph{relatively minimal} if no fiber contains a $(-1)$-rational curve.

[Proposition 16 (Aldous' criterion, \cite{ref7}) of arXiv:2607.23640, '{\sl Non-equilibrium fluctuations of a two-species exclusion process with slow boundary }'] A sequence of real-valued processes $ \left\{X_t^n: 0\le t\le T\right\}_{n\in \mathbb{N}} $
	is tight in \(\mathcal D([0,T];\mathbb R)\) if the following two conditions hold:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item[(i)] $ \lim_{M\to\infty}
		\limsup_{n\to\infty}
		\mathbb P_{\mu^n}^n
		\left(
		\sup_{0\le t\le T}|X_t^n|>M
		\right)
		=0 $.
		
		\item[(ii)]
		For every \(\varepsilon>0\),
		\[
		\lim_{\delta\to 0}
		\limsup_{n\to\infty}
		\sup_{0<\lambda\le\delta}
		\sup_{\tau\in\mathcal T_T}
		\mathbb P_{\mu^n}^n
		\left(
		|X_{\tau+\lambda}^n-X_\tau^n|>\varepsilon
		\right)
		=0,
		\]
		where \(\mathcal T_T\) denotes the family of stopping times bounded by \(T\).
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Aldous' criterion, \cite{ref7}

[Df associated of arXiv:2605.14910, 'Sharp Phase Transition for the Formation of Infinite Tubes'] Let $w>0$.
  Associated with a configuration $\eta\in\Omega$ of the $k$-plaquette percolation model on $\mathbb{R}^d$, a directed graph $G_w=G_w(\eta)$ is defined as follows.
  The vertex set $V_w$ is given by
  \[
  V_w:=\{[\delta]\mid\text{$\delta$ is a $k$-collar based at some discrete $(k-1)$-sphere $S$ with $\diam(S)\le w$}\}.
  \]
  For distinct vertices $\Delta,\Delta'\in V_w$, we include the ordered pair $(\Delta,\Delta')$ as a directed edge in $E_w=E_w(\eta)$ if and only if there exist $k$-collars
  \[
  \delta\colon\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times I_\varepsilon\to|\mathcal{K}_k^d|
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  \delta'\colon\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times I_\varepsilon\to|\mathcal{K}_k^d|
  \]
  representing the equivalence classes $\Delta$ and $\Delta'$, respectively, and an open $k$-tube
  \[
  \gamma\colon\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}^d
  \quad\text{with $\width(\gamma)\le w$}
  \]
  such that the following conditions hold:
  \begin{itemize}
    \item (\emph{Initial compatibility}).
    For any $(p,h)\in\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times[0,\varepsilon]$,
    \[
    \gamma(p,a+h)=\delta(p,h);
    \]
    \item (\emph{Terminal compatibility}).
    For any $(p,h)\in\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times[-\varepsilon,0]$,
    \[
    \gamma(p,b+h)=\delta'(p,h);
    \]
    \item (\emph{Locality}).
    It holds that
    \[
    \diam(\im\gamma)\le2w+4.
    \]
  \end{itemize}

[Theorem thm:momentsP of arXiv:2510.21186, 'Weingarten Calculus with Virtual Isometries'] Let $m$, $l$ be nonnegative integers, and consider four sequences
\[
\bm{i}=(i_1,\dots, i_m), \qquad \bm{j} =(j_1,\dots, j_m), \qquad
\bm{i}'=(i_1',\dots, i_l'), \qquad \bm{j}' =(j_1',\dots, j_l').
\]
of positive integers in $\{1,\dots, n\}$.
Then the moment
\[
\mathbb{E} \bigl[ p_{i_1 j_1} \cdots p_{i_m j_m} \overline{p_{i_1' j_1'} \cdots p_{i_l' j_l'}} \bigr]
\]
vanishes unless $\bm{i} \sqcup \bm{j}'$ is a permutation of $\bm{j} \sqcup \bm{i}'$.
In this case, the moment is equal to
\[
\alpha_1! \cdots \alpha_{n-1}! \frac{n^{\uparrow \alpha_n}}{n^{\uparrow m}n^{\uparrow l}},
\]
where
\[
\alpha_k := \mathsf{m}_{k}(\bm{i}\sqcup \bm{j}') = \mathsf{m}_{k}(\bm{j} \sqcup \bm{i}'),
\qquad k=1,\dots,n.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:momentsP of arXiv:2510.21186

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2609.03506, 'Divergence of decreasing rearranged Fourier series\\ on every infinite compact abelian gro'] Fix \(N\geq1\) and any bijection \(r:\T_N\to\{1,\ldots,L\}\).
There exist an integer \(D\geq1\), an integer \(C\),
sets \(E_v\subseteq\R_p^D\) for \(|v|\leq N\), a function
\(k:\R_p^D\to\{1,\omega,\ldots,\omega^{p-1}\}\), and functions
\(P_v:\R_p^D\to\mathbb C\) for \(v\in\T_N\), each a character polynomial, with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item \(E_\varnothing=\R_p^D\). For every \(v\in\T_N\), the \(p\) sets
       \(E_{va}\), \(0\leq a\leq p-1\), partition \(E_v\). Moreover,
       \(\mu_D(E_v)=p^{-|v|}\) for every \(v\) with \(|v|\leq N\).
 \item For \(v\in\T_N\), the function
       \[
        h_v:\R_p^D\to\{0,\zeta_0,\ldots,\zeta_{p-1}\},\qquad
        h_v=\sum_{a=0}^{p-1}\zeta_a1_{E_{va}},
       \]
       vanishes outside \(E_v\) and equals \(\zeta_a\) on \(E_{va}\);
       and \(P_v=k\,h_v\).
 \item The Fourier supports of the \(P_v\) are pairwise disjoint.
 \item The exponents \(C+r(v)\) are nonnegative, and, for
       \(\xi\in\R_p^D\),
       \[
        |\widehat P_v(\xi)|\in\{0,p^{-(C+r(v))}\}.
       \]
       Moreover, \(\widehat P_v(0)=0\).
       Thus the nonzero coefficients have equal modulus within each
       node, while these moduli strictly decrease as \(r(v)\) increases.
\end{enumerate}

Let $M = (M_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a continuous local martingale vanishing at zero. Let A be a complex m by n matrix of rank r with singular triples (sigma_i, u_i, v_i), i <= r, so that A v_i = sigma_i u_i, A* u_i = sigma_i v_i, sigma_i > 0 and both families orthonormal, and let H(A) be the Hermitian (m + n) by (m + n) matrix [[0, A], [A*, 0]]. Then (u_i, v_i)/sqrt(2) and (u_i, -v_i)/sqrt(2) are eigenvectors of H(A) with eigenvalues sigma_i and -sigma_i, the kernel of H(A) is ker(A*) + ker(A) (a direct sum, the first summand in C^m and the second in C^n), and these 2r vectors together with an orthonormal basis of the kernel form an orthonormal eigenbasis. So the eigenvalues of H(A) are +-sigma_1, ..., +-sigma_r and 0 with multiplicity m + n - 2r.

[Defn def.Lp-stabilizing_marking-weak of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] In the setting of Definition~(def.Lp-stabilizing_marking of the paper), we say:
\begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),labelindent=0pt]
\item  
The marking function \(\xi\) is \emph{ \textnormal{BL}~cluster-localizing} on the point process~\(\tilde{\mathcal{P}}\) if  
there 
is an increasing-decreasing family of  
functions $\varphi_p: [0, \infty) \to [0,1]$,  $p \in \mathbb{N}$,
and constants $\alpha_p\in[0,\infty)$ such that the following two conditions hold:
\begin{align}

&\sup_{x_1,\ldots,x_p\in\mathbb{R}^d}
d_{\textnormal{BL},\bk{x}{1}{p}}
\bigl(\bk{\xi}{1}{p}(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}}),\bk{\xi^{\cup(r)}}{1}{p}(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}})\bigr)
\;\le\; 2\varphi_p(r),
\qquad r  \geq 0, 
\end{align}

and for all $p \geq 2$, $l\in\{1,\ldots,p-1\}$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_p \in\mathbb{R}^d$ such that $d(\bk{x}{1}{l},\bk{x}{l+1}{p}) > r^{\alpha_p}$  

we have 

\begin{align}

& 
d_{\textnormal{BL},\bk{x}{1}{p}}
\Bigl(\bk{\xi^{\cup(r)}}{1}{p}(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}}),
\bigl(
\bk{\xi^{\cup(r)}}{1}{l}(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}}),
\bk{\xi^{\cup(r)}}{l+1}{p}(\tilde{x},\tilde{\mathcal{P}})
\bigr)
\Bigr)
\;\le\; 2\varphi_p(r), \qquad r  \geq 0.
\end{align}
\end{enumerate}

(ii)~\emph{\textnormal{BL}~cluster-localization on finite windows},  
(iii)~\emph{fast \textnormal{BL}~cluster-localization},  
and (iv)~\emph{exponential \textnormal{BL}~cluster-localization}  
are defined \emph{mutatis mutandis} as in  
Definition~(def.Lp-stabilizing_marking of the paper).
title: \BL~cluster-localization of marks

body: [Theorem 7 (\cite{fEhRjS2019}*{Theorem 4.82}) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $(\mathcal{M},\Phi)$ be an MGHD for the quasilinear wave initial value problem \eqref{E:JANQNLW}--\eqref{E:JANQNLWDATA}. If $\mathcal{M}$ lies on one side of its boundary,\footnote{More precisely, for every $p \in \p \mathcal{M}$, there exists a neighborhood $U \subset \R^{1+d}$ of $p$ and a coordinate chart $f : U \to (-\epsilon,\epsilon)^{d+1}$, $\epsilon > 0$, and a continuous function $g : (-\epsilon,\epsilon)^d \to (-\epsilon,\epsilon)$ such that $\p \mathcal{M} \cap U = f^{-1}(\textnormal{graph $g$})$, all points \emph{below} the graph of $g$ are mapped into $\mathcal{M}$, and all points \emph{above} the graph of $g$ are mapped to $\R^{1+d} \setminus \mathcal{M}$.} then $(M,\Phi)$ is the unique MGHD of the data. [Thm lasso-vec of arXiv:2608.29018, 'Sharp Restricted Isometry Thresholds for\\ Global Minima of Rank-Restricted Matrix LASSO'] Fix integers $s_{\star}\ge1$ and $k\ge2$. Suppose
that $\normzero{x_{\star}}\les_{\star}$ and that $A\in\operatorname{rip}(\delta,k)$,
and let $\delta_{\mathrm{sharp}}$ be as in ((eq:threshold of the paper)). 
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{(Sufficiency)} If $\delta<\delta_{\mathrm{sharp}}(k/s_{\star})$, then every global
minimizer $x_{\lambda,s}$ of ((eq:vector-lasso of the paper)) with $\lambda>0$
satisfies 
\begin{equation}
s\ges_{\star},\;\;\lambda\gtrsim\norminf{A^{T}\xi}\implies\normtwo{x_{\lambda,s}-x_{\star}}\lesssim\sqrt{s_{\star}}\,\lambda,
\end{equation}
where the hidden constants depend only on $\delta$ and on the ratio
$k/s_{\star}$. 
\item \emph{(Necessity)} If $\delta\ge\delta_{\mathrm{sharp}}(k/s_{\star})+1/s_{\star}$, then there
exist $x_{\star}$ and $A$ with $\normzero{x_{\star}}\les_{\star}$ and
$A\in\operatorname{rip}(\delta,k)$ such that, even in the noiseless case $\xi=0$,
every global minimizer $x_{\lambda,s}$ of ((eq:vector-lasso of the paper))
satisfies 
\begin{equation}
s\gtrsims_{\star},\;\;\lambda>0\implies\normtwo{x_{\lambda,s}-x_{\star}}\ge\normtwo{x_{\star}},
\end{equation}
where the hidden constant depends only on the ratio $k/s_{\star}$. 
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Sparsity-restricted vector LASSO

[Lemm 15 of arXiv:2609.01105, 'Obstruction to quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures under transport flows on Riemannian M'] Let \(q_0  \in S^0\) be defined for all~\(y\in V_2\) and~\(\eta \in \Rr^d\) by 
\begin{equation}
    
    q_0(y,\eta) = \omega(\eta)\theta_0^2(\kappa^{-1}(y))\left( \frac{|\eta|^{2\alpha}_{y}}{|\Jac \chi(\chi^{-1}(y))^\top\eta|_{\chi^{-1}(y)}^{2\alpha}}-1\right), 
\end{equation}
where $|\eta|^2_{z}:=g^{ij}(\kappa^{-1}(z))\eta_i\eta_j$, and with $\omega$ which is a radial function such that $\omega = 0$ near $\eta =0$ and $\omega (\eta) = 1$ for $|\eta| \geq C$ for some constant $C>0$. 
There exists~\(\delta > 0\) and~\(r \in S^{-\delta}\) such that
\[
    P_{0,1}^{-\mez} (S_\kappa P_{2,2} S_\kappa^{-1}  - P_{3,3})P^{-\mez}_{1,0} = \Op(q_0) + \Op(r).
\]

[Corollaryen 8 (Expected bounded-domain clipped-FTRL bound) of arXiv:2608.18999, '2608.18999'] Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(W\subset H\) be nonempty, closed,
and convex, with diameter \(D<\infty\).  Fix \(1<p\le2\), let
\((\mathcal F_t)_{t\ge0}\) be a filtration, and let \((g_t)_{t\ge1}\) be
adapted to it with \(g_t\in L^p(\Omega;H)\).  For \(\eta,\tau>0\), put
\[
Y_t=C_\tau(g_t),
\qquad
M_t=\E[\norm{g_t}^p\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]<\infty,
\]
and define \(w_t\) as the unique quadratic-FTRL minimizer
\[
w_t\in\mathop{\arg\min}_{w\in W}
\left\{
  \sum_{s<t}\ip{Y_s}{w}+\frac{\norm{w}^2}{2\eta}
\right\}.
\]
For \(T\ge1\) and \(u\in W\), let
\(R_T(u)=\sum_{t=1}^T\ip{g_t}{w_t-u}\).  Then
\begin{equation}
\E R_T(u)
\le
\frac{\norm{u}^2}{2\eta}
+\sum_{t=1}^T
\E\!\left[
K_p\!\left(D,\frac{\eta\tau}{2}\right)
\tau^{1-p}M_t
\right].
\end{equation}

[Cor 11 (Local Martingale Criterion in Case  $\gamma<t_G<+\infty$ a.s.) of arXiv:2606.04245, 'Properties of a Special Type of Filtration and its Martingale Criteria'] Assume $t_G<+\infty$, $P(\gamma=t_G)=0$, $\EE[|L|]<+\infty$, and $\EE[\sup\limits_{t\leq t_G} |F(t)|]<+\infty$.
    Let $M$ be the process defined by Equation \ref{eq: M_t=F(t)1[t<g]+L1[t>=g]}.
    Then the following statements are equivalent: 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item The process $M$ is a local martingale on $\RRl_+$.
        \item The process $(M_t)_{t\in[0,t_G)}$ is a martingale.
    \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Local Martingale Criterion in Case  $\gamma<t_G<+\infty$ a.s.

[Theorem thm:growth-gadget of arXiv:2509.04333, 'The limiting law of the Discrete Gaussian level lines'] The following holds uniformly over all possible $Q$ as above. Let $\mathfrak{L}_n$ be the (unique) $(H+1-n)$ level line induced by $\xi$. Then, with $\pi^\xi_Q$-probability $1 - e^{-c\log L}$, $\mathfrak{L}_n$ lies below the point $X= (0, Y + \sigma(\log L)^a + \log L)$, where
		\begin{align}
			&Y = -\frac{N_n^{1/3}(\log L)^{2a}}{8(\tau_\beta(\theta) + \tau_\beta''(\theta))\cos(\theta)^3}\,,\\
			&\sigma^2 = \frac{N_n^{2/3}(\log L)^a}{4(\tau_\beta(\theta) + \tau_\beta''(\theta))\cos(\theta)^3}\,.\nonumber
		\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop potts_diffalpha of arXiv:2609.02682, 'LDP for tensor forms'] Consider the optimization problem (equation eq:potts_unconstrained_opt of the paper), under the assumption 
$$W_\infty>0\quad \lambda\text{-a.e.},\quad \text{  }\mathcal{V}[W_\infty](x)=1\quad\lambda\text{-a.e.}.$$ 
Then the following conclusions hold:
\begin{itemize}
  
		
		\item [(i)] For any ${\boldsymbol h} \in \mathbb{R}^c,$ define $\tilde{h}:=\max_{1\le r\le c} h_r - h_1$. Then, there exists $\eta=\eta(c,v,{\tilde{ h}})>0$, such that for any $\boldsymbol{\alpha}=(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\ldots,\alpha_c)$ with $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_c\geq 0$ and $\alpha_1 \ge \eta+ \max_{2\le r\le c} \alpha_r$, the optimization problem (equation eq:potts_unconstrained_opt of the paper) has a unique maximizer. Furthermore, denoting this maximizer by $ (x_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}, {\boldsymbol h} ,1},\ldots ,x_{ \boldsymbol{\alpha},{\boldsymbol h} ,c})$, we have $ x_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}, {\boldsymbol h} , 1}>\max_{2\le r\le c} x_{ \boldsymbol{\alpha},{\boldsymbol h} ,r}$, and the map ${(\boldsymbol{\alpha},\boldsymbol h}) \mapsto (x_{ \boldsymbol{\alpha},{\boldsymbol h} ,1},\ldots ,x_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}, {\boldsymbol h} ,c})$ is continuous.
        \item [(ii)] For any $\boldsymbol{\alpha} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq0}^c,$ define $\widetilde{\alpha}:=\max_{1\le r\le c} \alpha_r-\alpha_1$. Then, there exists $\eta=\eta(c,v,\widetilde{\alpha})>0$, such that for any ${\boldsymbol h}=(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$ with $h_1 \ge \eta+ \max_{2\le r\le c} h_r$, the optimization problem (equation eq:potts_unconstrained_opt of the paper) has a unique maximizer. Furthermore, denoting this maximizer by $ (x_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}, {\boldsymbol h} ,1},\ldots ,x_{ \boldsymbol{\alpha},{\boldsymbol h} ,c})$, we have $x_{{\boldsymbol{\alpha}},\boldsymbol{h},1}>\max_{2\le r\le c} x_{{\boldsymbol{\alpha}},\boldsymbol{h},r}$, and the map $({\boldsymbol{\alpha}},\boldsymbol{h})\mapsto  (x_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}, {\boldsymbol h} ,1},\ldots ,x_{ \boldsymbol{\alpha},{\boldsymbol h} ,c})$ is continuous.
        
        \item [(iii)] Assume $0\leq \alpha_r\leq \frac{1}{v(v-1)}$ for all $r\in [c]$ and ${\boldsymbol h} \in \mathbb{R}^c$.  Then the maximizer of the optimization problem (equation eq:potts_unconstrained_opt of the paper) is unique.
        \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop potts_diffalpha of arXiv:2609.02682

[Definition D:gamma of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Let $X:\mathbb{Z}^2_\ge \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\cup \{\infty\}$ be a field of independent random variables distributed as follows.
Take real parameters $\alpha$ and $\{\gamma_i\}_{i\in\mathbb{Z}}$.

For any $i\in \mathbb{Z}$, take $X(i,i)\sim \operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(\alpha+\gamma_i)$ if $\alpha+\gamma_i>0$, and $X(i,i)=\infty$ otherwise.

For any $i > j \in \mathbb{Z}$, take $X(i,j)\sim \operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(\gamma_i+\gamma_j)$ if $\gamma_i+\gamma_j>0$, and $X(i,j)=\infty$ otherwise. 
We extend the weights $X$ to all of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ by the symmetry condition $X(i,j)=X(j,i)$ for all $i,j$.

For any $u,v\in \mathbb{Z}^2$ with $u \le v$, define the \emph{partition function}
\[
Z_X(u;v)=\sum_{\pi}\prod_{(i,j)\in \pi}X(i,j),
\]
where the sum is over all up-right paths $\pi$ from $u$ to $v$, subject to the following condition:
\begin{equation}

\text{for any $(i,i)\in\pi$, necessarily $(i-1,i)\notin\pi$.}
\end{equation}
In words, paths may cross the diagonal at most once, moving from below the diagonal to above it.

[Proposition 21 (Equivalence with the multivariate Knothe--Rosenblatt coupling) of arXiv:2604.22159, 'Adapted optimal transport between filtered Gaussian processes'] Let $\mu = \cN_{Nd}(a, A)$ and $\nu = \cN_{Nd}(b, B)$ be Gaussian distributions on $\bR^{Nd}$. Let $L = \cC_{\min}(A)$ and $M = \cC_{\min}(B)$ be their respective minimal Cholesky factors in $\mathscr{L}_+(Nd)$. The Knothe--Rosenblatt coupling between $\mu$ and $\nu$, defined via their almost-surely unique quantile processes, coincides exactly with the synchronous bicausal coupling $\pi^I \in \Cpl_{\mathrm{bc}}(\bX^{a,L}, \bX^{b,M})$. More precisely,
$$
\pi_{\mathrm{KR}}= (\epsilon\mapsto (a+L\varepsilon,b+M\epsilon))_\#\pi^I
$$
title: Equivalence with the multivariate Knothe--Rosenblatt coupling

[Definition 19 of arXiv:2609.00285, 'Multicrossing complex of knot and secant classes'] Let $n\in\{2,3,4\}$ and a link $L$ be $n$-generic. The sum
\[
\sigma_n(L)=\sum_{s\in \mathcal S^{adm}_n(L)}\sgn(s)\cdot s
\]
is called the \emph{$n$-secant class} of the link $L$. The sum $\sigma_n(L)$ is considered as an element of $H_2(L,\Z)$ for $n=2$, an element of $H_3^-(L,\Z)$ for $n=3$, and an element of $H_4^+(L,\Z)$ for $n=4$.

$$L^\infty(X)\subset B(L^2(X))\quad,\quad

with the embedding being the above one, tensored with the identity.

[Theorem thm: discrete time profiles intro of arXiv:2509.23069, 'Every cutoff profile is possible'] Let $(t_n)$ be a sequence of positive integers and $(w_n)$ be a sequence of positive real numbers such that $w_n = o(t_n)$ as $n\to \infty$. Let $p{\ensuremath{\;:\;}} {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}}  \to [0,1]$ be a weakly decreasing function (but not necessarily continuous) such that $p(x) \xrightarrow[x\to -\infty]{} 1$ and  $p(x) \xrightarrow[x\to +\infty]{} 0$. There exists a sequence of discrete time Markov chains $((X_t^{(n)})_{t\in {\ensuremath{\mathbb N}} })_{n\geq 1}$ such that
\begin{equation}
    \sup_{c\in {\ensuremath{\mathbb R}}  {\ensuremath{\;:\;}} t_n + cw_n \in {\ensuremath{\mathbb N}} } \left| \mathrm{d}^{(n)}(t_n + c w_n) - p(c) \right| \xrightarrow[n\to \infty]{} 0.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 8 (Biased Random Transpositions) of arXiv:2605.19084, 'Limit Profiles for Separation Distance'] Let $P_{a,b}$ denote the biased random transpositions shuffle with $A$ of size $n-1$ and $B$ of size $1$, and set $\epsilon_n:=1/n!$. Put $t_n(c):=\frac n2(\ln n+c)$ and $\bar t_n(c):=\frac{n}{2(1-\epsilon_n)}(\ln n+c)$. Then, for every fixed $c\in\mathbb R$,
$$\left|s_*^{P_{1+\frac{\epsilon_n}{n-1},1-\epsilon_n}}\left(\bar t_n(c)\right)-s_*^{P_{1,1}}\left(t_n(c)\right)\right|\to0.$$
Consequently, any subsequential profile for one chain at these paired times is shared by the other. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let T be a densely defined symmetric operator on a complex Hilbert space H which is bounded below: ⟨Tx, x⟩ ≥ c‖x‖² for all x ∈ D(T), with c ∈ ℝ. Let q(x, y) = ⟨Tx, y⟩ on D(T) and let Q be the completion of D(T) in the norm ‖x‖_q² = ⟨Tx, x⟩ + (1 − c)‖x‖², which embeds injectively into H as a dense subspace. Then there is a self-adjoint extension T_F of T (the Friedrichs extension) with the same lower bound, ⟨T_F x, x⟩ ≥ c‖x‖² for all x ∈ D(T_F), given by the closed form obtained as the continuous extension of q to Q; its domain is D(T_F) = D(T*) ∩ Q and T_F = T* restricted to that domain. T_F is the unique self-adjoint extension of T whose operator domain is contained in Q, and it is the unique self-adjoint extension whose form domain is Q. In particular every densely defined semibounded symmetric operator has at least one self-adjoint extension, so its deficiency indices are equal; T_F is the largest semibounded self-adjoint extension in the sense of quadratic forms, and it is the only one when T is essentially self-adjoint (in which case T_F = T̄).
H is a complex Hilbert space
T is densely defined and symmetric
T is bounded below: ⟨Tx, x⟩ ≥ c‖x‖² on D(T)

[Proposition isotdec of arXiv:2608.30747, 'Compact homogeneous complex manifolds'] \hspace{1cm} 
\begin{enumerate}[{\rm (i)}] 
\item If $\dim{\mg_j}\geq 4$, then $\mg_j$ is $\Ad(K)$-irreducible.  

\item Two subspaces $\mg_j,\mg_k$, $j\ne k$ are equivalent as $\Ad(K)$-representations if and only if $\mg_j=\qg_{\alpha_j}$, $\mg_k=\qg_{\alpha_k}$ and $\alpha_j|_{\zg(\kg)}=\alpha_k|_{\zg(\kg)}$.  

\item The trivial $\Ad(K)$-subrepresentation of $\pg$ is given by 
$$
\pg_0=\ag\oplus \bigoplus_{j\in I_0} \qg_{\alpha_j}, \qquad I_0:=\{1\leq j\leq r :  \mg_j=\qg_{\alpha_j}, \;\alpha_j|_{\zg(\kg)}=0\}.  
$$
\item The subspaces $\mg_1,\dots,\mg_r$ in (equation isotrep of the paper) are all $\Ad(K)$-irreducible (in particular, nontrivial) and pairwise inequivalent as $\Ad(K)$-representations if and only if the subspace $\zg(\kg)\subset\zg(\hg_f)$ and all the central roots $\alpha_j$ such that $\mg_j=\qg_{\alpha_j}$ satisfy the following:  
\begin{equation}
\alpha_j|_{\zg(\kg)}\ne 0, \quad\mbox{and} \quad \alpha_j|_{\zg(\kg)}=\alpha_k|_{\zg(\kg)} \quad\mbox{if and only if}\quad \alpha_j=\alpha_k. 
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Every counterclockwise cell has contour defect 2i delta^2, tending uniformly to zero, but summing all n^2 cells gives the outer contour integral 2i. Let X be a continuous random vector in R^n with finite variance and let Z ~ N(0, I_n) be independent of X. Let X_t = X + sqrt(t) * Z. Let h(X_t) = - int p_t(x) log p_t(x) dx be the differential entropy of X_t. Then d/dt h(X_t) = (1/2) * J(X_t), where J(X_t) = int ||nabla log p_t(x)||^2 p_t(x) dx is the Fisher information of X_t.

[Theorem 6tmod4 of arXiv:2609.03926, 'Overcolored Partition $k$-tuples Restricted by Parity of the Parts'] We have
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item For all $n,r,s\ge1$ and $k$ even, $\bar{b}^k_{r,s}(n)\equiv 0\pmod{4}$.
		\item For all $n,r,s\ge 1$, some integer $\ell\ge1$, and $k$ odd,
		\[
		\bar{b}^k_{r,s}(n)\equiv
		\begin{cases}
			2s\pmod 4, & \text{if } n=\ell^2 \\[4pt]
			2(r+s)\pmod 4, & \text{if } n=2\ell^2\\[4pt]
			0 \pmod 4, & \text{otherwise }.
		\end{cases}
		\]
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\(\mathcal G:=\mathcal G_P(J)\).  The following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item \(\overline E=E\).
\item \(g^\vee\in J\) for every \(g\in\mathcal G\).
\item \(\NF_{\mathcal G}(g^\vee)=0\) for every \(g\in\mathcal G\), where
\(\NF_{\mathcal G}\) denotes the normal form with respect to
\(\mathcal G\).
\end{enumerate}

body: [Theorem thm:cle_partially_explored of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] Consider the setup described above. The conditional law of the remainder of $\Gamma$ given $\Gamma_{\mathrm{out}}^{*,V,U}$ is a multichordal ${\rm CLE}_{\kappa'}${} in $(V^{*,U};\underline{x}^*;\beta^*)$ with marked points $\underline{x}^*$ and exterior link pattern $\beta^*$ given as above. The family of multichordal ${\rm CLE}_{\kappa'}${} laws is conformally invariant in the sense that if $\Gamma$ is a multichordal ${\rm CLE}_{\kappa'}${} in $(D;\underline{x};\beta)$ and $\varphi\colon D \to \widetilde{D}$ is a conformal transformation, then $\varphi(\Gamma)$ is a multichordal ${\rm CLE}_{\kappa'}${} in $(\widetilde{D};\varphi(\underline{x});\beta)$. For each \emph{interior link pattern} $\alpha$, the probability that the chords of a multichordal ${\rm CLE}_{\kappa'}${} in $(\mathbf{D};\underline{x};\beta)$ induce the link pattern $\alpha$ is positive and depends continuously on $\underline{x}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:uniform-confinement of arXiv:2609.02710, 'Asymptotic Mean Value Laplacian\\ on equiregular sub-Riemannian manifolds'] Let $K\Subset O$, and let
$C\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a compact coordinate box such that
$0\in\operatorname{int}C$.  There exist bounded open boxes
$U_0\Subset U_1$, with $C\subset U_0$, and a constant $R<\infty$ with the
following property.  Let $h_0>0$, and let
$W^{x,h}=(W_1^{x,h},\ldots,W_k^{x,h})$, $x\in K$ and $h \in [0,h_0]$,
be a jointly smooth family on a neighborhood of
$K\times[0,h_0]\times\overline{U_1}$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
  W_i^{x,0}(\xi)=\widehat X_{i,x}(\xi),
  \qquad x\in K,\xi \in \overline{U_1},  \quad 1\le i\le k.
\end{equation}
Then there exists $h_*\in(0,h_0]$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The fields $W^{x,h}$ are
pointwise linearly independent and the family is uniformly two-generating
on $\overline{U_1}$ for any $h \in [0,h_*]$;
\item Every $W^{x,h}$-trajectory starting at
$0$ and controlled by $u \in L^2([0,1];\mathbb{R}^k)$ with $\|u\|_{L^2}\le R+1$ is defined on $[0,1]$
and remains in $U_0$;
\item For every  $x\in K$ and
$ h \in [0,h_*]$,
\begin{equation}
  d_{W^{x,h},U_1}(0,q)\le R,
  \qquad q\in C,
\end{equation}
where $d_{W^{x,h},U_1}$ denotes the distance obtained by restricting
trajectories to $U_1$;
\item For
$W^{x,h}=X^{x,h}$, the distance in (equation eq:centered-distance-bound of the paper) agrees with $d_{x,h}(0,q)$ for $q\in C$, where
$d_{x,0}:=\widehat d_x$.
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Definition 18 ($q$-labeling of $\lambda$) of arXiv:2606.12670, 'The censored stochastic six-vertex model and parabolic Kazhdan--Lusztig $R$-polynomials'] Given a partition $\lambda$, we will assign a number to each cell $(i,j)$ in $\lambda$. For each $k \in \Z$, we will label the cells in the $k$th diagonal according to the following rules:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item If $\lambda^k = \lambda$, we fill the $k$th diagonal with ones.
    \item If $\lambda^k > \lambda$, then we fill the $k$th diagonal with the values $(1-q)^{-1}, (1-q^2)^{-1},\dots$ starting with the box touching the bottom boundary.
    \item If $\lambda^k < \lambda$, we fill the $k$th diagonal with the values $(1-q),(1-q^2),\dots$, again starting with the box touching the bottom boundary.
\end{enumerate}
Let $w_\lambda(i,j)$ denote the value assigned to box $(i,j)$ by this labeling. See Figure \ref{fig:tiling} for an illustration of this labeling.
title: $q$-labeling of $\lambda$

body: [Definition def:sphere twist of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] For an embedded 2-sphere $S$ in $M$, define the \emph{sphere twist about $S$} as follows. Recall that $\pi_1(\SO(3)) \cong \mathbb{Z}/2$ is generated by a loop $\ell \colon [0, 1] \to \SO(3)$ which rotates $\mathbb{R}^3$ about an axis by a full turn. Identify $S$ with $S^2 \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ and define a diffeomorphism supported on a bicollar neighbourhood $S \times I \subseteq M$ by $r(s, t) = (\ell(s) \cdot t, t)$, to obtain the \emph{sphere twist about} $S$, denoted $T_S$.
title: Definition def:sphere twist of arXiv:2609.00233

[Theorem 3 (Exponential convergence in relative entropy) of arXiv:2607.19176, 'Exponential Convergence of the Sinkhorn Algorithm for the Schrödinger Bridge with Regime S'] Let Assumptions~ \ref{assum:reference_marginals}, \ref{assum:measures} and \ref{assum:map_c2} hold for \((\rho,\mu) \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)^2\) and the reference process $P \in \mathcal{P}(\Omega_T)$. Let $\pi^{\rho,\mu}$ be the unique optimal coupling, and let $\pi^{n+1,n}$ and $\pi^{n+1,n+1}$ be, respectively, the half-step and full-step couplings defined in \eqref{eq:half_step_coupling} and \eqref{eq:full_step_coupling}. Assume that $ H(\pi^{\rho,\mu} \mid \pi^{1,0}) < \infty$, $H(\pi^{\rho,\mu} \mid \pi^{1,1}) < \infty$. Then there exist constants $C > 0$ and $\theta \in (0, 1)$  depending on $ \rho, \mu, P $ and $ \pi^{1,0} $, $ \pi^{1,1} $ such that, for all $n \geq 0$,
\[
H(\pi^{\rho,\mu} \mid \pi^{n+1,n}) \leq C \theta^n,
\qquad
H(\pi^{\rho,\mu} \mid \pi^{n+1,n+1}) \leq C \theta^n .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Exponential convergence in relative entropy

[Corollary 3 of arXiv:2608.21663, '\bf Variance lower bounds for geometric functionals of rotationally invariant log-concave '] Let $p\geq1$ and $\mu_p$ be the rotationally invariant probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with density
$$
f_p(x)=c_{d,p}\exp\left(-\frac{\|x\|_2^p}{p}\right), \quad x\in \mathbb{R}^d.
$$
If $K_n^{(p)}$ is the convex hull of $n$ independent random vectors with distribution $\mu_p$, then for every $ n \geq d+1$
$$
\Var\bigl(V_\ell(K_n^{(p)})\bigr)
\geq C_1(p,d,\ell)\,
(\log n)^{\frac{2\ell}{p}-\frac{d+3}{2}},
\quad 1\leq\ell\leq d
$$
and for every $n \geq d+2$
$$
\Var\bigl(f_\ell(K_n^{(p)})\bigr)
\geq C_2(p,d,\ell)\,
(\log n)^{\frac{d-1}{2}},
\qquad 0\leq \ell\leq d-1,
$$
where $C_1(p,d,\ell),\,C_2(p,d,\ell)>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Lemma 5 of arXiv:2609.01681, 'Large induced subgraphs with $k$ vertices of maximum degree'] For every integer $k\ge 2$, there exists a constant $c_2 = c_2(k)$ such that the following holds. Let $H$ be a graph, let $b$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $X = \{x_1, \dots, x_k\}$ be a vertex set for which $H[X]$ is a regular graph. Suppose that for all $u, v \in X$, we have $|d_H(u) - d_H(v)| \le b$. Then there exists a set $U \subseteq V(H) \setminus X$ with $|U| \le c_2 b$ such that all vertices in $X$ have equal degree in $H - U$.

[Theorem 5 (Leading comparison with the local approximate equation) of arXiv:2608.30138, 'High-frequency wave propagation for the viscoelastic wave equation with singular memory'] Fix $0<\lambda_{\min}\le \lambda\le \lambda_{\max}<\infty$, $T>0$, and let
$u_{\rm in}$ denote the incoming branch of the solution of \eqref{1b},
\eqref{IC1}. Let $u_{\rm app}$ denote the corresponding incoming
geometric-optics solution of \eqref{approx_PDE}, with the same incoming
initial amplitude and phase. Then, for every $k\ge 0$,
\[
u_{\rm in}(t,x)-u_{\rm app}(t,x)
=
e^{i\lambda\phi(t,x,\eps)/h} r(t,x,h,\eps),
\]
where
\[
\|r\|_{C^k([0,T]\times\R^n)}
\le C_k h.
\]
 Equivalently,
\[
u_{\rm in}=u_{\rm app}+O(h)
\]
in the semiclassical $C^k_h$ norm.

DRAFT; independent review pending. A measure-preserving map T is dynamically mixing when mu(T^(-n)A intersect B) tends to mu(A)mu(B) for each fixed event pair. That condition supplies no rate, no growing-window size control, no planar Delaunay stabilization, and no empty-disk estimate. It cannot by itself be used as the quantitative point-process alpha hypothesis of a Delaunay covariance bridge. A Bernoulli shift illustrates the quantifier distinction: for an event B of probability 1/2 and A_n=T^nB, the unrestricted event covariance equals 1/4 for every n despite fixed-event mixing. This does not deny independence of separated finite Bernoulli windows.

Let T(X) be an estimator of g(theta) with E[T(X)^2] < infinity for all theta, and let S(X) be a sufficient statistic for theta. Define T*(X) = E[T(X) | S(X)]; this is a genuine statistic (computable without knowledge of theta) precisely because sufficiency of S makes the conditional distribution of X given S free of theta. Then E_theta[T*(X)] = E_theta[T(X)] for all theta (so T* is unbiased for g(theta) whenever T is), and Var_theta(T*(X)) <= Var_theta(T(X)) for all theta, with equality for a given theta if and only if T is almost surely equal to a function of S.
T has finite second moment under every theta
S is a sufficient statistic for theta

For the variance, the law of total variance gives Var(T(X)) = E[Var(T(X)|S(X))] + Var(E[T(X)|S(X)]) = E[Var(T(X)|S(X))] + Var(T*(X)). satisfies the finite-\(r\) witnessed hypothesis at exponent \(s\) if there exist \(r>1\) and \(\delta>0\) such that
\[
    \mathbb E[U^r]<\infty
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    2^{1-r}\mathbb E[U^r]\le 2^{-r(s+\delta)} .
\]

[Definition of arXiv:2412.00865, 'On the spectral problem and fractional diffusion limit for Fokker-Planck with(-out) drift '] \item 1.  We define the Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_\eta$ as being the completion of the space $C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{C})$ for the norm $\|\cdot\| _{\mathcal{H}_\eta}$ induced from the inner product $\langle \cdot,\cdot\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_\eta}$
$$
\mathcal{H}_\eta := \overline{\big\{ \psi \in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{C}) ; \ \| \psi \|_{\mathcal{H}_\eta}^2:= \langle \psi,\psi\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_\eta} < +\infty \big\} } ,
$$
where
$$
\langle \psi,\phi\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_\eta}:=  \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \nabla_v \bigg(\frac{\psi}{M}\bigg) \cdot \nabla_v \bigg(\frac{\bar\phi}{M}\bigg) \ M^2 \mathrm{d}v + \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}   \frac{\psi \bar \phi }{\langle v \rangle^2} \ \mathrm{d}v +  \eta \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} |v_1| \psi \bar \phi \ \mathrm{d}v .
$$

We have the embeddings
$$ \mathcal{H}_\eta \subseteq \mathcal{H}_{\eta^*} \subseteq \mathcal{H}_{0}  ,   \quad \forall \ 0 \leqslant \eta^* \leqslant \eta $$
since $\ \| \cdot \|_{\mathcal{H}_0} \leqslant \| \cdot \|_{\mathcal{H}_{\eta^*}} \leqslant \| \cdot \|_{\mathcal{H}_\eta} \ $  for all $\ 0\leqslant \eta^* \leqslant \eta$.   \smallskip

[Lem lemma for partial answer of arXiv:2505.11700, 'Distribution of the cokernels of determinantal row-sparse matrices'] Suppose that $k_n = O(n^{\frac{1}{7}-\delta})$ for some $\delta>0$. Then there exists $c>0$ such that the following holds for all $n> c$ and $1\le \ell \le r_n$. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item 
    $$
    \frac{n(k_n-1)_0}{n^{k_n-1}} =  \frac{n^{k_n-1}+ (n-2\ell)^{k_n-1}}{2n^{k_n-1}} \le 1 - \frac{\ell(k_n-1)}{2n} 
    $$
\item 
 $$
    \frac{n(k_n-1)_1}{n^{k_n-2}} =   \frac{n^{k_n-1} - (n-2\ell)^{k_n-1}}{2n^{k_n-2}} \le \ell(k_n-1)
    $$   
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2608.11637, '\bf Uniform Local Asymptotics for L\'evy Processes with Subexponential Jumps'] The following assertions hold.
 	\begin{enumerate}
 		\item[(1)] The following limit holds
 		\beqnn
 		\lim_{K\to\infty}\limsup_{t\to\infty} \mathbf{P}\Big( \frac{|M_t|}{b(t)}\geq K  \Big)  =0. 
 		\eeqnn
 		
 		\item[(2)] There exists a constant $t_0>0$ such that  
 		\beqnn
 		\sup_{t\geq t_0}\mathbf{E}\bigg[ \exp\Big\{ \frac{M_t}{b(t)}\Big\} \bigg] <\infty.
 		\eeqnn
 		
 		\item[(3)] For any $\eta>0$, there exist two constants $c_\eta,C_\eta  >0$ such that for all $t\geq 0$ and $y\geq \eta t$, 
 		\beqnn
 		\mathbf{P}\big(M_t>y\big) \leq C_\eta\cdot \exp\big\{-c_\eta\cdot y\big\}. 
 		\eeqnn
 		
 		\item[(4)] 	For any $T>0$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, we have  as $y\to\infty$,
 		\beqnn
 		\exp\{\varepsilon y\log y\}\cdot \sup_{0<s\leq T} 
 		\frac{ \mathbf P\big(M_s>y \big) }{ s } \to 0.
 		\eeqnn
 	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] [\cite{Minh:2020regularizedDiv}, Theorem 11 and Corollary 2]
	
	Let $\mu = \Ncal(m_1, Q)$, $\nu = \Ncal(m_2,R)$, with $m_2 - m_1 \in \range(Q^{1/2})$, $R = Q^{1/2}(I-S)Q^{1/2}$, $S \in \SymHS(\Hcal)_{<I}$.
	The Radon-Nikodym density $\frac{d\nu}{d\mu}$
	
	is given by
	\begin{align}
		
		\frac{d\nu}{d\mu}(x) = \exp\left[-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\Phi_k(x)\right]\exp\left[-\frac{1}{2}||(I-S)^{-1/2}Q^{-1/2}(m_2 - m_1)||^2\right],
		
	\end{align}
	where for each $k \in \Nbb$
	\begin{align}
		
		\Phi_k = \frac{\alpha_k}{1-\alpha_k}W^2_{\phi_k} - \frac{2}{1-\alpha_k}\la Q^{-1/2}(m_2-m_1), \phi_k\ra W_{\phi_k}+ \log(1-\alpha_k).
	\end{align}
	The series $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\Phi_k$ converges in 
	$\Lcal^2(\Hcal,\mu)$ and
	
	$s(x) = \exp\left[-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\Phi_k(x)\right] \in \Lcal^1(\Hcal, \mu)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2605.17296, 'Zero correlations and averaged fields of orthonormal Gaussian Functions'] Let $\{a_{n,N}\}$ be a triangular array of complex numbers, where
$N\ge 1$ and $0\le n\le N$. Assume that there exists a function
$f:[0,1]\to \C$ such that for every $t\in [0,1]$ and every sequence
$n_N$ with $0\le n_N\le N$ and $n_N/N\to t$, one has
\[
a_{n_N,N}\to f(t).
\]
Then $f$ is continuous on $[0,1]$ and
\[
\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1} a_{n,N}
\to
\int_0^1 f(t)\,dt.
\]

The points of an elliptic curve E over K, including O, form an abelian group with identity O: three points sum to O exactly when they are collinear (with tangency counting multiplicity). Addition is given by the chord-and-tangent construction - draw the line through P and Q, take its third intersection with E, and reflect in the x-axis - and the coordinates of P + Q are rational functions of those of P and Q over K.
E a smooth elliptic curve with base point O

There exists $g_0=g_0(C,\alpha,\Delta,\lambda^\star)$ such that for any family $\mathcal{G}$ of graphs of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ and girth at least $g_0$, if the hard-core model on $\mathcal{G}$ satisfies strong spatial mixing at $\lambda^\star$ with parameters $C,\alpha$, then there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that for each $G=(V,E)\in \mathcal{G}$ and $\Vec\lambda\in B(\lambda^\star,\varepsilon)^V$ we have $Z_G(\Vec \lambda)\neq 0$. [Lemma 6 of arXiv:2604.15152, 'The Multinomial Allocation Model and the Random Box Load'] For $n \ge 1$ and $0\le r\le n$, define $\delta_n(r,x)$ by
\[
\left(1-\frac{x}{n}\right)^{n-r} = e^{-x} + n^{-1}\delta_n(r,x).
\]
If $0 \le x \le \frac{n}{2}$, then
\begin{equation}
 -2 \le \delta_n(r,x) \le  r2^{r-1},
\end{equation}
and moreover, $\delta^*_n(r,x)$ defined by
\[\delta_n(r,x)=e^{-x}x(r-x/2)+n^{-1}\delta^*_n(r,x),
\]
satisfies 
\begin{equation}
-4-r\le \delta^*_n(r,x)\le x^2r(r+1) 2^{\,r+1}.
\end{equation}

[Def 8 of arXiv:2609.01389, 'K-stability and birational rigidity of Fano 3-fold weighted complete intersections'] Let $X$ be a closed subscheme of $\mbP$ defined by a homogeneous ideal $I \subset R$.
We set
\[
C_X \coloneq \Spec (R/I)
\]
and call it the \textit{affine cone} of $X$.
Let $\pi \colon \mbA^{N+1} \setminus \{O\} \to \mbP$ be the natural projection, where $O$ is the origin.
For a point $\msp \in X$, we say that $X$ is \textit{quasismooth at $\msp$} if $C_X$ is smooth along $\pi^{-1} (\msp)$.
We say that $X$ is \textit{quasismooth} if it is quasismooth at any point of $X$, that is, $C_X$ is smooth away from the origin.

[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2506.13913, '2506.13913'] {}{conexion-multi-dim}
Let \(\{W_t\}_{t \geq 0}\) be a \(d\)-dimensional Brownian motion starting at $x$ defined on a probability space \((\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})\), and and assume that \(f \in C(\mathbb{R}^d)\cap L^{\infty}( \mathbb{R}^d)\). Furthermore, Consider the \(d\)-dimensional heat equation
\[
\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = \Delta u, \quad x \in \mathbb{R}^d, \, t > 0,
\]
with initial condition \(u(x, 0) = f(x)\), where \(\Delta = \sum_{i=1}^d \frac{\partial^2}{\partial x_i^2}\) is the Laplace operator. Then:

\begin{enumerate}
    \item There exists a classical solution \(u\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d\times(0,\infty))\) given by
    \[
    u(x, t) = \frac{1}{(4\pi t)^{d/2}} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} f(y) \exp\left(-\frac{\|x - y\|^2}{4t}\right) \, dy, \quad t > 0.
    \]

    \item The solution \(u(x, t)\) admits a stochastic representation in terms of \(d\)-dimensional Brownian motion
    \[
    u(x, t) = \mathbb{E}[f(W_t) \mid W_0 = x],
    \]
    where \(\mathbb{E}\) denotes expectation with respect to the probability measure induced by the Brownian motion \(\{W_t\}_{t \geq 0}\).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 6 of arXiv:2506.13913

body: In geometric measure theory, Falconer's conjecture, named after Kenneth Falconer, is an unsolved problem concerning the sets of Euclidean distances between points in compact $d$ -dimensional spaces. Intuitively, it states that a set of points that is large in its Hausdorff dimension must determine a set of distances that is large in measure. More precisely, if $S$ is a compact set of points in $d$ -dimensional Euclidean space whose Hausdorff dimension is strictly greater than $d/2$, then the conjecture states that the set of distances between pairs of points in $S$ must have nonzero Lebesgue measure.

[Corollary 9 of arXiv:2608.21551, '\bf Sparse Separable Factor Analysis in the Complex Domain with an Application to Local Fi'] For $j=1,\ldots,d$, suppose that $\Sigmab_j\in\CC^{p_j\times p_j}$ is Hermitian positive definite with factor-analytic representation
\begin{align}
  \Sigmab_j
  &=
  \Lambdab_j\Lambdab_j^\star+\Psib_j,
  \qquad
  \Lambdab_j\in\CC^{p_j\times k_j},
  
\end{align}
where $\Psib_j$ is a real-valued diagonal matrix with positive diagonal entries. Let $(c_1,\ldots,c_d)$ be the rescaling constants in \eqref{eq:iden-c}, and define
\begin{align*}
  \widetilde{\Sigmab}_j
  &=
  c_j\Sigmab_j,
  \qquad
  j=1,\ldots,d.
\end{align*}
Each $\widetilde{\Sigmab}_j$ admits the factor-analytic representation
\begin{align}
  \widetilde{\Sigmab}_j
  &=
  \Lb_j\Lb_j^\star+\Db_j,
  \qquad
  \Lb_j
  =
  c_j^{1/2}\Lambdab_j,
  \qquad
  \Db_j
  =
  c_j\Psib_j,
  \qquad
  j=1,\ldots,d,
  
\end{align}
and the rescaled diagonal matrices satisfy
\begin{align}
  \min\left\{\diag(\Db_1)\right\}
  &=
  \cdots
  =
  \min\left\{\diag(\Db_d)\right\}.
  
\end{align}
Furthermore, $\widetilde{\Sigmab}_d \otimes\cdots\otimes \widetilde{\Sigmab}_1 = \Sigmab_d \otimes\cdots\otimes \Sigmab_1$. [Proposition 1 (Proposition  10 in Bertoin  \cite{B1996}, pp.~25) of arXiv:2605.18136, 'L\'evy processes with partially stochastic resetting'] The following assertions are equivalent:

			\[

		\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 13 of arXiv:2609.01770, 'Support of Dyson Brownian Motion'] Let \(z_0=u+\ri\eta\), \(w_0=u-\ri\eta\), and suppose that \(f\) is analytic in
neighborhoods of the closed discs \(B(z_0,\eta/2)\) and \(B(w_0,\eta/2)\). Define
\[
H_f(z,w):=\frac{f(z)-f(w)}{z-w}.
\]
For all integers \(a,b\geq0\),
\begin{equation}
\bigl|\partial_z^a\partial_w^bH_f(z_0,w_0)\bigr|
\leq C_{a,b}\eta^{-(a+b+1)}
\sup_{B(z_0,\eta/2)\cup B(w_0,\eta/2)}|f|,
\end{equation}
where
\[
C_{a,b}:=2^{a+b+1}a!b!\bigl(3^{-(a+1)}+3^{-(b+1)}\bigr).
\]
In particular,
\begin{equation}
\bigl|\partial_z^{k-1}\partial_w^kH_f(z_0,w_0)\bigr|
\leq\frac{2^{2k+2}}{3^{k+1}}(k-1)!k!\,\eta^{-2k}
\sup_{B(z_0,\eta/2)\cup B(w_0,\eta/2)}|f|.
\end{equation}

[Thm 5 of arXiv:2506.21829, 'Some notes on Lamperti's recurrence of stochastic sequences'] Assume that the states of the Markov chain $\mathscr{P}$ form connected domain, and $\sum_{j=1}^\infty jp_{0,j}<\infty$. Denote $e^-=\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}jp_{i+j-1,i-1}$ and $e_i^+=\sum_{j=1}^{i+1}jp_{i-j+1,i+1}$, $i\geq1$, assuming that $e_i^-<\infty$. Assume also that $1-p_{i,i}>\epsilon$ for all $i\geq0$, where $\epsilon$ is some positive value. Then the Markov chain $\mathscr{P}$ is recurrent if and only if
\[
\sum_{n=1}^\infty\prod_{i=1}^{n}\frac{e_i^-}{e_i^+}=\infty.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
For each n let M_n be an n by n random matrix with INDEPENDENT entries each uniform on {-1, +1}. Then P( M_n is singular ) = ( 1/2 + o_n(1) )^n. The matching lower bound is elementary: the probability that two rows are equal, or two rows are opposite, or two columns are equal, or two columns are opposite, is already of order n^2 2^{-n} = (1/2 + o(1))^n, and each such coincidence forces singularity. The content of the theorem is the UPPER bound, which settled a long-standing conjecture: Komlos (1967) proved the probability is o(1), Kahn, Komlos and Szemeredi (1995) obtained 0.999^n, and Tao-Vu and Bourgain-Vu-Wood improved the base to (1/sqrt(2) + o(1))^n before Tikhomirov reached the conjectured (1/2 + o(1))^n. Note precisely what is claimed: the ENTRIES are independent uniform signs, and the statement is asymptotic in n with an o(1) in the base, so it gives no numerical bound at any fixed n. The analogous question for a random symmetric sign matrix is a separate problem, resolved later and by different methods, and the result stated here must not be quoted for it. [Tikhomirov (2020), 'Singularity of random Bernoulli matrices', Ann. of Math. 191; arXiv:1812.09016]

[Theorem 1 (Pressure and exponential upper bounds) of arXiv:2607.07014, '2607.07014'] For every \(q\in\mathbb R\), the limit \[\Lambda(q):=\lim_{n\to\infty} n^{-1}\log\mathbb E[N_n^q]\]
exists. For \(q\ge0\), one has \(\Lambda(q)=\inf_{n\ge1} n^{-1}\log\mathbb E[N_n^q]\), while for \(q<0\), one has \(\Lambda(q)=\sup_{n\ge1} n^{-1}\log\mathbb E[N_n^q]\). 

	Moreover, \(\Lambda\) is finite and convex on \(\mathbb R\), and \(\min\{0,q\log 2\}\le \Lambda(q)\le \max\{0,q\log 2\}\). If \(I_+(x):=\sup_{q\ge0}\{qx-\Lambda(q)\}\) and \(I_-(x):=\sup_{q\le0}\{qx-\Lambda(q)\}\), then, for every \(x\in\mathbb R\),
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty} n^{-1}\log\mathbb P(X_n\ge x)\le -I_+(x)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\limsup_{n\to\infty} n^{-1}\log\mathbb P(X_n\le x)\le -I_-(x).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Pressure and exponential upper bounds

[Defn def:Sm of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $\gamma:[0,1]\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{2}$ be a weakly geometric
rough path. For each $m\geqslant1$, we define an analytic function
$S_{m}^{\gamma}:\mathbb{C}^{m}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ in the following
way. Given $a_{1},\cdots,a_{m}\in\mathbb{C}$, let $B:[0,1]\rightarrow\mathbb{C}^{m}$
be the path defined by 
\[
B_{t}\triangleq\sum_{j=1}^{m}\big(\int_{0}^{t}e^{a_{j}x_{s}}dy_{s}\big){\rm e}_{j}
\]
where $\{{\rm e}_{1},\cdots,{\rm e}_{m}\}$ denotes the standard basis
of $\mathbb{C}^{m}$. We define $S_{m}^{\gamma}(a_{1},\cdots,a_{m})$
to be the coefficient of the logarithmic signature of $B$ with respect
to the tensor ${\rm e}_{1}\otimes\cdots\otimes{\rm e}_{m}$, i.e.
\[
S_{m}^{\gamma}(a_{1},\cdots,a_{m})\triangleq\big(\log S(B)\big)^{(1,\cdots,m)}.
\]
title: Defn def:Sm of arXiv:2506.18207

[Lemma lem:ExpIneq of arXiv:2608.30848, '\huge \bf Limit Laws of the Iterated Logarithm Under Sub-linear Expectations'] Let $\{X_1,\ldots, X_n\}$ be independent random variables on $(\Omega, \mathscr{H}, \widehat{\mathbb E})$. Denote
$A_n(p,y)=\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat{\mathbb E}[(X_i^+\wedge y )^p]$,
$ \breve{B}_{n,y}=\sum_{i=1}^n \breve{\mathbb E}[(X_i\wedge y)^2]$. Then for any $p\ge 2$, $x,y>0$, $0<\delta\le 1$, we have
$$
  \widehat{\mathbb V}\Big( \max_{k\le n} \sum_{i=1}^k(X_i-\breve{\mathbb E}[X_i])\ge x\Big)
\le    \widehat{\mathbb V}\big(\max_{k\le n} X_k> y \big)
+\exp\bigg\{-\frac{x^2}{2(xy+\breve{B}_{n,y})   }\bigg\},
$$
\begin{align*}
& \widehat{\mathbb V}\Big( \max_{k\le n} \sum_{i=1}^k(X_i-\breve{\mathbb E}[X_i])\ge x\Big) \\
\le & \widehat{\mathbb V}\big(\max_{k\le n} X_k> y \big)
  +2\exp\{p^p\}\bigg\{\frac{A_n(p,y)}{y^p} \bigg\}^{\frac{\delta x}{10y}}
+\exp\bigg\{-\frac{x^2}{2\breve{B}_{n,y}(1+\delta)   }\bigg\}.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:ExpIneq of arXiv:2608.30848

[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2607.11756, 'Full replica symmetry breaking in the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model'] Let \(\nu\) be a probability measure on \([0,1]\). Suppose that, for
some \(0\le q_0<q_1\le1\) and \(\lambda\ge0\),
\[
 \nu([0,s])=\lambda,\qquad q_0\le s<q_1.
\]
If \(\lambda>0\), then
\begin{equation}
 u_\nu(q_0,\cdot)
 =
 T_{\lambda,\beta^2(q_1-q_0)}u_\nu(q_1,\cdot).
\end{equation}
If \(\lambda=0\), then
\begin{equation}
 u_\nu(q_0,\cdot)
 =
 P_{\beta^2(q_1-q_0)}u_\nu(q_1,\cdot).
\end{equation}
Consequently, every profile obtained by solving the Parisi PDE through
finitely many constant-mass intervals is a finite composition of
Cole--Hopf transforms and ordinary heat-semigroup evolutions.

[Theorem thm:generalized-mass-characterization of arXiv:2608.11931, '\texorpdfstring{Nonlinear parabolic characterizations of stochastic completeness at infini'] Let $\phi\in\mathcal{I}$ with $\phi^{-1}(\mathbb R_+)\neq\emptyset.$
Assume that either
\begin{equation*}
    \mu(X)<\infty
    \qquad\text{or}\qquad
    \phi\text{ satisfies }\hyperref[eq:LG]{\textup{(LG)}}{}.
\end{equation*}
The following statements are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[\rm(i)]
    \(G\) satisfies \hyperref[def:SC-infinity]{\textup{{(SC\textsubscript{$\infty$})}}}{}.

    \item[\rm(ii)]
    For every \(T>0\), every bounded positive pointwise solution \(u\) of the (eq:GPME of the paper) with initial datum \(u_0 \in \mathcal D_+\) satisfies \hyperref[eq:nonlinear-generalized-mass]{\textup{(MB)}}{} on \([0,T]\).

    \item[\rm(iii)]
    There exist \(T_0>0\) and a nonzero positive finitely supported
    \(u_*\) such that every bounded positive pointwise solution on
    \([0,T_0]\times X\) with initial datum \(u_*\)
    satisfies~\hyperref[eq:nonlinear-generalized-mass]{\textup{(MB)}}{}.

    \item[\rm(iv)]
    For some \(T_0>0\), every bounded positive pointwise solution on
    \([0,T_0]\times X\) with zero initial datum
    satisfies~\hyperref[eq:nonlinear-generalized-mass]{\textup{(MB)}}{}.
\end{enumerate}

If these conditions hold, then, for every solution \(u\) as in
\textup{(ii)}, the total mass \(\mathsf M_u\) is absolutely continuous
on \([0,T]\) and satisfies~(equation eq:differential-mass-balance of the paper) for
almost every \(t\in(0,T)\).

If \(G\) is not stochastically complete at infinity, then, for every
\(T>0\) and every \(u_0\in\mathcal D_+\), at least one bounded
positive pointwise solution with initial datum \(u_0\)
violates~\hyperref[eq:nonlinear-generalized-mass]{\textup{(MB)}}{}.  For \(u_0=0\), every
nontrivial bounded positive solution violates \hyperref[eq:nonlinear-generalized-mass]{\textup{(MB)}}{}.

When \(\mu(X)<\infty\), statement \textup{(iii)} may equivalently be
replaced by a constant-data test: There exist \(T_0>0\) and \(c_0 \in \mathbb R_+\)
such that every bounded positive solution with \(u_0= c_0\)
satisfies \hyperref[eq:nonlinear-generalized-mass]{\textup{(MB)}}{}.  Moreover, in the incomplete case, the violating
solution may be chosen for every constant datum \(u_0= c\), for
\(c\ge0\).

[Corollary 2 (\textsf{Zero terminal condition}) of arXiv:2609.02064, 'Coalescence and fluctuations of O'Connell--Yor polymers\\ via the free-energy correlation '] For $n\geq1$, $\be>0$, and $x\neq\wt x$,
  \begin{align}
    \rmP_{\wt x,x}^{\rfree,\be}(\tau\leq n-1)
    &=
    \frac{2}{\be^2}\sgn(\wt x-x)
    \frac{\partial}{\partial x}
    \EE\bigl[
      \log Z_{\wt x}^{\rfree,\be}\log Z_x^{\rfree,\be}
    \bigr]
    
    \\
    &=
    \frac{2}{\be^2}\sgn(\wt x-x)
    \frac{\partial}{\partial x}
    \Cov\bigl(
      \log Z_{\wt x}^{\rfree,\be},
      \log Z_x^{\rfree,\be}
    \bigr)
    \notag\\
    &=
    -\frac{1}{\be^2}\sgn(\wt x-x)
    \frac{\partial}{\partial x}
    \EE\left[
      \bigl(
        \log Z_{\wt x}^{\rfree,\be}
        -\log Z_x^{\rfree,\be}
      \bigr)^2
    \right].
    \notag
  \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:second_moment of arXiv:2510.24424, 'On the Fourier Coefficients of Critical Gaussian Multiplicative Chaos'] Let $A>0$ and $0<\delta<1/4$. Let $ r_n:=\delta\log n$.
For any $t\geq r_n$, consider the event
\[
    {E}_{n,t}{(A)}:=\big\{\forall \theta\in [0,1], \,\theta\in G_{n,t}{(A)}\big\},
\]
where 
\begin{align}
G_{n,t}{(A)}=\left\{ \theta \in [0,1]: \,\,
    X_s(\theta)\leq U(s)+A,\,\forall s\in [r_n,t] \right\}
\end{align}
and $U(t)$ is defined in Equation (equation eq:U(t) of the paper).
Then for any $\varepsilon>0$, there exists an integer $N>2$ such that for any $n\geq N$,
\[
  \limsup_{t\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\Big[|c_{n,t}|^2;{{E}_{n,t}{(A)}}\Big]\ll_A (\log n)^{-1/2+\varepsilon},
\]
where the implicit constant is uniform in $n$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:second_moment of arXiv:2510.24424

[Theorem thm:1-companion of arXiv:2509.04333, 'The limiting law of the Discrete Gaussian level lines'] Fix $\beta>0$ large enough and consider $\phi\sim \pi^0_\Lambda$, the $(2+1)$\textsc{d}  \ensuremath{\mathbb Z\textsc{gff}}\xspace model on $\Lambda=\llbracket 1,L\rrbracket^2$ 
        with a floor and zero boundary conditions. Set $H(L)$ and $N_n$ per (eq:H-def,eq:Nn-def of the paper).
For fixed $m$, let $\mathfrak{L}_n$ ($n=0,\ldots,m$) be the \texttt{large} $(H+1-n)$ level lines, where possibly $\mathfrak{L}_0$ does not exist. 
Let $I_n = \llbracket \frac{L}2- N_n^{2/3},\frac{L}2+N_n^{2/3}\rrbracket$, let $\rho_n(x) := \min\{y\geq 0 \,:\; (\frac{L}2+x,y)\in\mathfrak{L}_n\}$ be the vertical distance of~$\mathfrak{L}_n$ from $I_n$, and 
$Y_n(t) := N_n^{-1/3}\rho_n(t N_n^{2/3})$.
There exists a constant $\sigma>0$  such that:
\begin{enumerate}[1.,leftmargin=2em]
\item The law of $(Y_n(t))_{n=1}^m$ under $\pi_\Lambda^0$ converges weakly to the law of 
$m$ i.i.d.\ copies of the stationary Ferrari--Spohn diffusion $\mathsf{FS}_{\sigma}$ on~$[-1,1]$.
\item For $L$ with $\pi_\Lambda^0(\mathfrak{L}_0\mbox{ exists})>L^{-10}$, the law of $(Y_n(t))_{n=0}^m$ under $\pi_\Lambda^0(\cdot\mid\mathfrak{L}_0\mbox{ exists})$ converges weakly to that of $m+1$ i.i.d.\ copies of 
$\mathsf{FS}_{\sigma}$.
\item 
     For $L$ with $\pi_\Lambda^0(\mathfrak{L}_0\mbox{ does not exist}) > L^{-10}$, the law of $(Y_n(t))_{n=1}^m$ under $\pi_\Lambda^0(\cdot\mid \mathfrak{L}_0\mbox{ does not exist})$ converges weakly to that of $m$ i.i.d.\ copies of $\mathsf{FS}_{\sigma}$.

[Proposition 16 (cf.\ {\cite[Theorem~2.1.5) of arXiv:2511.09930, 'Martingale dimensions for a class of metric measure spaces'] {FOT11}}]
Let $U$ be a relatively compact open subset of $K$ and $A$ a subset of $U$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Suppose that $g\in\cF$ satisfies that $g\ge 1$ q.e.\ on $A$ and $g=0$ q.e.\ on $K\setminus U$.
Then, $\Cp(A;U)\le \cE(g,g)$.
\item There exists $f\in\cF$ such that $f=1$ q.e.\ on $A$, $f=0$ q.e.\ on $K\setminus U$, and $\cE(f,f)=\Cp(A;U)$.
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.27398, 'Strict Stability and Strict Minimality of Regular Area-Minimizing Hypercones: A Quantitati'] The following statements are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item The cone $\C$ is strictly stable in the sense of
\cite{caffarelli1984minimal} and strictly minimizing in the sense of
\cite{hardt1985area}.
\item There is a constant $c_\C>0$ such that, for every $R>0$ and every
set $F$ of locally finite perimeter satisfying
$F\mathbin\triangle E\Subset B_R$,
\begin{equation}
    D_R(F)\geq c_\C\mathcal W_R(F,E).
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Main result, in the authors' own words, arXiv:2609.03634, 'Joint Laws of Maximum Drawdown and Maximum Drawup for Spectrally Negative L\'{e}vy...'] The purpose of this paper is to express the laws of these components and to find distribution of maximum drawdowns and maximum drawups in each component directly through $W^{(\gamma)}$, $Z^{(\gamma)}$ scale functions, and their derivatives, then to assemble these conditional pieces into finding the joint distribution of $(M_T^-,M_T^+).$ Along the way of finding this joint distribution various other joint distributions are also proved such as the joint distribution of the infimum and the supremum together with the two orderings of these extrema, the maximum drawdown together with the case infimum occurs before the supremum and the maximum drawup where the supremum occurs before the infimum.

[Lemma Lemma_assumption_on_rho of arXiv:2608.08299, 'Non-linear optimal stopping with Bermudan strategies: the infinite horizon case'] Let $\rho$ satisfy the properties of knowledge preservation (iii), monotonicity (iv) and consistency (v). 
  \\ If $\rho$ does not depend on the second index 
   (that is, $\rho_{S,\tau}[\cdot]=\rho_{S}[\cdot]$), 
  we \textbf{assume} that: if $\eta \in L^+_0(\mathcal{F}_{\infty})$, then
  \begin{equation} 
   \limsup_{n \rightarrow +\infty} \rho_{\theta_n} [\eta] = \eta.
  \end{equation}
   If $\rho$ depends on both indices, 
  we \textbf{assume} that: if $\eta \in L^+_0(\mathcal{F}_{\infty})$, if 
  $(\tau_k)$ $\in \Theta^{\mathbb{N}}$ non-decreasing such that $\lim_{k \rightarrow +\infty} \tau_k  = +\infty$, then
  \begin{equation} 
  \limsup_{n \rightarrow +\infty} \limsup_{k \rightarrow +\infty} \rho_{\theta_n, \tau_k} [\eta] =  \eta.
  \end{equation}
When these conditions on $\rho$ are satisfied, we have:
   \begin{equation} 
      \limsup_{n\rightarrow\infty} V(\theta_n) = \limsup_{n\rightarrow\infty} \xi(\theta_n).
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 35 of arXiv:2609.02105, 'Contact fundamental forms and \\ adjoint varieties'] Let $\mathfrak q$ be a Lie algebra containing vector subspaces $V_i$, $i\ge-d$.
Assume that
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] $V_-\oplus V_0$, where $V_-:=\oplus_{i=-d}^{-1}V_i$, is a graded
Lie subalgebra isomorphic to $\fn_-\oplus\fn_0$;
\item[(ii)] $[V_i,V_{-k}]\subset V_{i-k}$ for $i\ge1$ and $1\le k\le d$,
where $V_r=0$ for $r<-d$; and
\item[(iii)] $\{X\in V_i\mid[X,V_-]=0\}=0$ for each $i\ge1$.
\end{itemize} Notice that the
spaces $V_i$ are not required to be closed under brackets with one another.
Then there are injective linear maps
$$
\jmath_i : \ V_i\hookrightarrow\operatorname{prol}(\fn_-,\fn_0)_i = \fn_i \qquad(i\ge1).
$$

\item If $h=1$, then $m\le40$, that is, $n\le41$.
\item If $h=2$, then $m\le41$, that is, $n\le42$.
\end{enumerate}

[Definition def: correlated initialization of arXiv:2609.03589, 'Correlated initialization of deep residual networks'] For a feature function \(\phi \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}\) we define
    \[
        v_l^i \coloneq \phi(\xi_l^i), \qquad i\in \set{1, \dots, r}, l \in \set{0, \dots, L -1},
    \]
    where \((\xi_l^{i})_{l \in \mathbb{N}_0}\) are stationary Gaussian
    sequences in \(\mathbb{R}\), independent over \(i\), with zero mean \(\mathsf{E}[\xi_k^i] = 0\), unit variance
    \(\var(\xi_k^i) = 1\) and regularly-varying correlation of index \(\alpha \in (0, 1)\)
    \[
        \rho(k) \coloneq \mathsf{E}[\xi_l^i \xi_{l+k}^i] = k^{-\alpha}\ell(k), \quad k\geq 1,l\geq 0,
    \]
    where \(\ell\) is a slowly varying function.

[Thm 7 (\cite{Bou}) of arXiv:2608.30967, 'B-Frames, B-Riesz basis, and Their tensor products'] For each $ i \in \{1,2\}$, let $\{ z^i_k \}_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \subset \mathcal{Z}_i$.

 $\{ z^1_j \otimes z^2_k\}_{j,k \in \mathcal{K}}$ is a frame (or Riesz basis) for $\mathcal{Z}_1 \otimes \mathcal{Z}_2$ if and only if $\{ z^i_k\}_{k \in \mathcal{K}}$ is a frame (or Riesz basis) for $\mathcal{Z}_i $ for each $ i \in \{1,2\}$.

In addition the frame bounds of a frame $\{ z^1_j \otimes z^2_k\}_{j,k \in \mathcal{K}}$ are $A_1A_2$ and $B_1B_2$ if, for each $ i \in \{1,2\}$, the frame bounds of the frame $\{ z^i_k \}_{k \in \mathcal{K}} $ are $A_i$ and $B_i$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2609.01413, 'Sharp Threshold for Universality of Rational Canonical Forms over a Finite Field'] Let $(\alpha_n)_{n\geq 1}$ be a sequence of positive real numbers
    satisfying
    \begin{equation}
        
        \liminf_{n\to\infty}
        \frac{n\alpha_n}{\log n}
        >1.
    \end{equation}
    For each $n$, let $A_n\in\Mat_n(\F_p)$ be an
    $\alpha_n$-balanced random matrix. For any tuple of distinct
    polynomials $F_{i_1},\ldots,F_{i_r}$,
    the joint distribution of
    $$
    \left(
    \lambda^{(F_{i_1})},\ldots,
    \lambda^{(F_{i_r})}
    \right)
    $$
    converges pointwise to the product measure $\prod_{j=1}^r\mu_{F_{i_j}}$
    on $\Y^r$ as $n\to\infty$, where
    \begin{equation}
        
        \mu_{F_i}(\lambda)
        =
        \frac{1}{\#\Aut_{F_i}(\lambda)}
        \prod_{\ell=1}^{\infty}
        \left(1-p^{-\ell\deg F_i}\right),
        \qquad
        \lambda\in\Y.
    \end{equation}
    Here $\Aut_{F_i}(\lambda)$ denotes the group of automorphisms of
    the $\F_p[t]$-module
    $$
    \bigoplus_{j\geq 1}
    \F_p[t]/\left(F_i^{\lambda_j}\right).
    $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 6 of arXiv:2609.01413

[Thm t:thm_q of arXiv:2504.07255, 'A Tail-Respecting Splitting Numerical Scheme\\ for L\'evy-Driven SDEs With Superlinear Dri'] Let assumptions
$\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{Lip}_+}_A$,
$\mathbf{H}_{A_x,A_{xx}}$,
$\mathbf{H}_{a,b,c}^{\mathrm{Lip}_b}$, and
$\mathbf{H}_{\nu,p}$
 hold. Then,
 for any $T\in[0,\infty)$ and $q\in (0,p)$ there is convergence
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
\sup_{t\in[0, T]} \mathbf{E} \|X_t^n-X_t\|^q \leq_C h_n^{\bar \delta}(1+\|x\|^p),\quad x\in\mathbb{R}^d,
\end{aligned}\end{equation}
with the convergence rate
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
\bar\delta=\frac{p-q}{\chi}\wedge\frac{q}{2}\wedge 1.
\end{aligned}\end{equation}
In particular, if $\chi=0$, i.e., if the drift $A$ has bounded first derivatives, the convergence rate reduces to
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
\bar\delta=\frac{q}{2}\wedge 1.
\end{aligned}\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm t:thm_q of arXiv:2504.07255

[Lemma 28 (Small-particle KMS comparison) of arXiv:2607.13183, '2607.13183'] Let $(X_t)_{t\ge0}$ be a finite irreducible reversible continuous-time chain
with at least two states and generator $\mathcal L=P-I$, where $P$ is an
irreducible reversible transition kernel. Let
$t_{\rm meet}^{\rm ct}$ be the worst-case expected meeting time of two
independent copies and let $t_{\rm mix}^{\rm ct}$ be its total-variation mixing
time. There are universal constants $a_0,c_0,C_0\in(0,\infty)$ such that the
following holds. Put
\[
        \alpha:=\frac{t_{\rm meet}^{\rm ct}}{t_{\rm mix}^{\rm ct}}.
\]
If $\alpha\ge a_0$, then the expected coalescence time of the process started
from any configuration with at most $c_0\alpha\log\alpha$ particles is at most
$C_0t_{\rm meet}^{\rm ct}$.
title: Small-particle KMS comparison

[Theorem 5 (Necessary Maximum Principle) of arXiv:2604.00937, 'Infinite Horizon Optimal Control of Forward-Backward Stochastic Volterra Equations with De'] Let $\hat{u} \in \mathcal{U}$ be an optimal control with corresponding solutions $\hat{X}(t)$, $(\hat{Y}(t),\hat{Z}(t,\cdot),\hat{K}(t,\cdot,\cdot))$, $\hat{p}(t)$, $\hat{q}(t,\cdot)$, $\hat{r}(t,\cdot,\cdot)$ and $\hat{\lambda}(t)$ of the state and adjoint equations respectively. Suppose the following transversality conditions hold:
\[
\varlimsup_{T\to\infty}\mathbb{E}[\hat{p}(T)\dot{X}(T)] = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \varlimsup_{T\to\infty}\mathbb{E}[\hat{\lambda}(T)\dot{Y}(T)] = 0.
\]

Then,
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[ \left.\frac{\partial H}{\partial u}(t)\right| \mathcal{G}_t \right]_{u=\hat{u}} = 0 \quad \text{for a.e. } t \geq 0.
\]

[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2608.31070, 'Sub-Laplacians on Compact Lie Groups: Heat Kernels, Distance, and Zeta Determinants'] For every $M>0$ there are $\eta_M,C_M>0$ with the following property. Let $v\in L^2([0,1];\pLie)$ satisfy $\|v\|_{L^2}\le M$, and let $\gamma_\eta:[0,1]\to G$ be the absolutely continuous curve solving
		\[
		\gamma_\eta^{-1}\dot\gamma_\eta=\eta v,
		\qquad
		\gamma_\eta(0)=e.
		\]
		If $|\eta|\le\eta_M$, then $\gamma_\eta(1)$ lies in a fixed exponential neighborhood of $e$, and
		\begin{equation}
			\log\gamma_\eta(1)
			=\eta X_v+\eta^2A_v+R_\eta(v),
		\end{equation}
		where
		\begin{equation*}
			X_v:=\int_0^1v(s)\,\mathrm ds,
			\qquad
			A_v:=\frac12\int_0^1[x_v(s),v(s)]\,\mathrm ds,
			\qquad
			x_v(s):=\int_0^s v(u)\,\mathrm du,
		\end{equation*}
		and
		\begin{equation}
			\left|\pr_{\pLie}R_\eta(v)\right|\le C_M|\eta|^3,
			\qquad
			\left|\pr_{\kLie}R_\eta(v)\right|\le C_M|\eta|^4.
		\end{equation}

[Proposition prop:passiveshear of arXiv:2608.16915, 'Exact mean--covariance dynamics of the Weber field in the stochastic Lagrangian representa'] Fix $t_0>0$, $\nu>0$ and $0<\alpha<1$. For $K=2\pi n$, $n\in\mathbb N$, let
$a_K:=\nu K^{1-\alpha}$ and $b_K(x,y,z):=a_K\sin(Ky)\,e_1$, a smooth divergence-free field

$\,\mathrm{d} X_t=b_K(X_t)\,\mathrm{d} t+\sqrt{2\nu}\,\mathrm{d} W_t$. There is a constant $C_\alpha$ independent of
$K$ such that
\[

\[
  \mathbb{E}\norm{\nabla A^K_{t_0}}_{L^\infty}\ \ge\ c\,\sqrt{\nu t_0}\;K^{1-\alpha}
  \ \xrightarrow[K\to\infty]{}\ \infty .
\]

[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2606.11068, '2606.11068'] Assume \eqref{eq:right-edge}. Consider the frog model on \(\mathbb Z\) in which activated particles perform
independent biased nearest-neighbour random walks with
\[
  \Pbb(X_1=1)=r,
  \qquad
  \Pbb(X_1=-1)=1-r,
\]
where \(r\in(0,1)\setminus\{1/2\}\). Set
\[
  \beta_c:=\frac1\gamma.
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If \(\E(\eta)<\infty\) and \(\beta>\beta_c\), then the frog model dies
out almost surely.
\item If \(\Pbb(\eta=0)<1\) and \(\beta<\beta_c\), then the frog model survives
with positive probability in the direction of the drift, that is, to the right
if \(r>1/2\) and to the left if \(r<1/2\).
\end{enumerate}

[Corollary 11 of arXiv:2609.03962, '$L^p$ isomorphisms for the fractional Laplacian on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and their application'] Applying the above Poincar\'e inequality to $Du$ for $s-1\in(0,1)$ and the Calder\'on--Zygmund theorem, passing to a rescaling if necessary, the following assertions hold:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item If $n<p<\infty$, then for $u\in C_{\mathrm{c}}^\infty(\R^n\setminus\{0\})$,
        $$\Big\|\frac{u}{|\cdot|}\Big\|_{L^p(\R^n)}\lesssim\|Du\|_{L^p(\R^n)}\lesssim\|(-\triangle)^{1/2}\,u\|_{L^p}.$$
        \item If $1<s<2$, $\frac{n}{s}<p<\infty$, $(s-1)p\neq n$, then for $u\in C_{\mathrm{c}}^\infty(\R^n\setminus\{0\})$,
        $$\Big\|\dfrac{u}{|\cdot|^s}\Big\|_{L^p(\R^n)}\lesssim\Big\|\dfrac{Du}{|\cdot|^{s-1}}\Big\|_{L^p(\R^n)}\lesssim\|(-\triangle)^{\tfrac{s-1}{2}}Du\|_{L^p(\R^n)}\lesssim\|\flap u\|_{L^p(\R^n)}.$$
        \item If $1<s<2$, $(s-1)p=n$, then for $u\in C_{\mathrm{c}}^\infty(\R^n\setminus B_1)$,
        $$\Big\|\frac{u}{\rho^s\lg}\Big\|_{L^p(\R^n)}\lesssim\Big\|\frac{Du}{\rho^{s-1}\lg}\Big\|_{L^p(\R^n)}\lesssim\|(-\triangle)^{\tfrac{s-1}{2}}Du\|_{L^p(\R^n)}\lesssim\|\flap u\|_{L^p(\R^n)}.$$
    \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition 9 of arXiv:2608.22534, 'Entropy power inequalities in compact groups'] Let $G$ be a compact and metrizable topological abelian group, equipped with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Let $X,Y$ be $G$-valued random variables with $h(X),h(Y) > -\infty$. 
    The {\em Ruzsa distance} between $X$ and $Y$ is 
    $$
    \dR(X,Y) =  h(X'-Y') - \frac{1}{2}h(X)-\frac{1}{2}h(Y),
    $$
    where $X',Y'$ are independent and have the same marginals as $X$ and $Y$,
	respectively.
    
    The {\em maximal Ruzsa distance} is
    $$
    \dstar(X,Y) = \sup h(X'-Y') - \frac{1}{2}h(X)-\frac{1}{2}h(Y)
    $$
    where the supremum is over all couplings $(X',Y')$ of $(X,Y)$, i.e.,
all jointly distributed random variables $(X',Y')$
with same marginals as $X$ and $Y$.
title: Definition 9 of arXiv:2608.22534
