[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2607.27150, 'Modelling Anomalous Diffusion: The Role of CTRWs and Non-Local Dynamics'] Let $(A(u), S(u))$, $u \geq 0$, be a general Feller process on $E \times \RR$ with the second coordinate strictly increasing, under the corresponding family of probability measures $\mathds{P}^{(x,v)}$, $(x,v)\in E\times \RR$. Denote its transition probabilities by $p_{u}(x,v;dy,dw)\coloneqq \PP^{(x,v)}(A(u)\in dy, S(u) \in dw) $.
		
		Then, for all $t\ge0$, there exist two Markov processes $\,^tZ^+=(^tA^+(u), \,^tS^+(u))$, $u\geq 0$, and $\,^tZ^-=(^tA^-(u), \,^tS^-(u))$, $u \geq 0$, on the canonical probability space with measures $\,^t\mathds{P}_\pm^{(x,v)}$, $(x,v)\in E\times [0,+\infty)$, with the transition probabilities 
		\begin{align*}
			\, ^t{p}_{u}^+(x,v;dy,dw) &\coloneqq \mathds{1}_{[0<w\leq v]}  p_{u}(x,t-v;dy,t-dw)+
			\delta_0(dw)\,^t\upvarpi_u^+(x,t-v,dy), \\
			\,^tp_{u}^-(x,v;dy,dw) &\coloneqq \mathds{1}_{[0<w\leq v]}  p_{u}(x,t-v;dy,t-dw)+\delta_0(dw)\,^t\upvarpi_u^-(x,t-v,dy),
		\end{align*}
		respectively, where $\,^t\upvarpi_u^+(x,t-v,dy)\coloneqq \mathds{P}^{(x,t-v)}\left( A(L(t))\in dy, S(u)\in[t,+\infty)\right)$ and $\,^t\upvarpi_u^-(x,t-v,dy)\coloneqq \mathds{P}^{(x,t-v)}\left( A(L(t)-)\in dy, 
		S(u)\in[t,+\infty)\right)$, such that 
		\begin{align}
			& \mathds{P}^{(x,0)} \left( A(L(t)) \in dy \right) =  \,^t\mathds{P}_+^{(x,t)} \left( \,^tA^+(\tau_0^+) \in dy \right), \\
			& \mathds{P}^{(x,0)} \left( A(L(t)-) \in dy \right) =  \,^t\mathds{P}_-^{(x,t)} \left( \,^tA^-(\tau_0^-) \in dy \right). 
		\end{align}
		where $\tau^{\pm}_0 \coloneqq \inf \{ u \geq 0 : \,^tZ^{\pm}(u) \in E \times \{ 0 \} \}$.
title: Theorem 11 of arXiv:2607.27150

Let 1<=k<=d, S subset {1,...,d} with |S|=k, and X have independent {-1,1} coordinates of common mean mu in (0,1). Put Y=chi_S(X)=product_{i in S} X_i and L_mu=mu^(k-1)-mu^(k+1). Then E[Y]=mu^k. For every fixed b in [-1,1], E[(Y-b)X_j]=mu^(k-1)-b*mu when j is in S, and mu^(k+1)-b*mu otherwise. In particular, b=mu^k gives L_mu on S and zero off S. If b is the mean of B>=1 iid labels from independent D_mu inputs, then P(|b-mu^k|>=zeta)<=2 exp(-B*zeta^2/2) for every zeta>0. Conditional on this independent centering batch, take a fresh X with the stated product law. On the event |b-mu^k|<=zeta, all its centered coordinate moments simultaneously differ from L_mu on S, or zero off S, by at most mu*zeta. For 0<delta<1, B>=2 log(2/delta)/zeta^2 makes that event have probability at least1-delta. This is the algebraic content of the source first-layer drift calculation; no assertion about jointly moving ReLU gates or batch-one training follows.
Independent product inputs with common mean0<mu<1; a fixed nonempty parity support.
For the probabilistic centering consequence, the B centering samples are iid and independent of the fresh input.
This is not a conditional-iid claim after arbitrary data-dependent filtering or sample reuse.

Partition Efron-Stein tensorization needs independence. Let X_1=X_2=B with B~Bernoulli(1/2), use the singleton partition {{1},{2}}, and let f(x_1,x_2)=x_1+x_2. Then Var(f)=1 but E Var(f|X_2)+E Var(f|X_1)=0. In the replace-one form, with each X_i resampled independently from its own law, (1/2)(E[(f - f^(1))^2] + E[(f - f^(2))^2]) = 1/2, since f - f^(i) = B - B' with B' an independent copy of B; so the classical Efron-Stein inequality Var(f) <= (1/2) sum_i E[(f - f^(i))^2] fails as well, 1 against 1/2. Thus the nontrivial partition tensorization inequality can fail completely without product-law independence, and the replace-one form fails by a factor of two.
joint law is the dependent law X_1=X_2=B with B Bernoulli(1/2)
partition is the singleton partition {{1},{2}}

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Explicit model calculation and hypothesis obstruction Result: A diagnostic linear calculation shows why a naive time-difference argument is insufficient. For du_k+lambda_k*u_k dt=x_k dW, a time increment includes fresh noise integral_t^(t+h) exp[-lambda_k*(t+h-s)]x_k dW_s. Its A^(1/2)-weighted second moment is (1/2)sum |x_k|^2*(1-exp[-2lambda_k*h]). Integrating h^(-1-2alpha) over h gives a term comparable to sum lambda_k^(2alpha)|x_k|^2. Thus even a constant-in-time coefficient needs additional spatial regularity to give W^(alpha,2) time regularity in D(A^(1/2)). Check: The change of variables z=lambda_k*h gives the lambda_k^(2alpha) factor, and the integral near zero is finite exactly when alpha<1/2. Agresti-Veraar2026, arXiv2509.07803, proves this precise obstruction for the linear problem. Obstruction: This known obstruction is not a counterexample to the full nonlinear bootstrap theorem, whose diffusion mapping assumptions may supply the missing spatial input. A proof must use those assumptions at the critical endpoint; interpolation with a positive exponent margin is unavailable.

[Lemma macro BBM, lower bound of arXiv:2606.19207, 'Extrema of cooling branching Brownian motion and related Gaussian fields'] Consider a BBM $\{Z_t^v\colon t\in[0,\mathbf{T}],\ v\in\mathcal{N}_t^Z\}$ with branching rate $1$, binary splitting, and variance profile
	\[
	\sigma(t)=\widetilde{\sigma}(t/\mathbf{T}),
	\qquad t\in[0,\mathbf{T}],
	\]
	where $\widetilde{\sigma}\in C^2([0,1];(0,\infty))$ is strictly decreasing and $\inf_{u\in[0,1]}\widetilde{\sigma}(u)>0$. Let
	\[
	\eta(t):=\alpha_1\lvert\sigma'(t)\rvert^{2/3}\sigma(t)^{1/3},
	\]
	where $\alpha_1$ is given in (equation eqA: Airy eigenvalues of the paper). Then, for any $\beta\in(0,1/3)$, there exists $c>0$ such that
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbb{P}\Bigl(
		\max_{v\in\mathcal{N}_T}Z_{\mathbf{T}}^v
		\le \int_0^{\mathbf{T}}
		\Bigl(\sqrt{2}\,\sigma(s)-\frac{\eta(s)}{\sqrt{2}}\Bigr)\,\text{d} s
		-\mathbf{T}^\beta
		\Bigr)
		\le \exp\{-c\mathbf{T}^\beta\},
	\end{equation}
	for all $\mathbf{T}$ large enough.
title: Lemma macro BBM, lower bound of arXiv:2606.19207

  \item $T^{N}(A \mid x) \ge \displaystyle\int_{A} u(y \mid x)\,\pi(\dd y)$ for every $x \in \XX$ and every $A \in \XXA$;
  \item $\displaystyle\int_{\XX} u(y \mid x)\,\pi(\dd y) \ge c$ for every $x \in \XX$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[
  \sing\bigl( T^{n}\circ\mu \bigm| \pi\bigr) \;\le\; (1-c)^{\lfloor n/N \rfloor}
  \qquad (\mu \in \Prob,\ n \in \Nz),
\]
and in particular \hyp{S}{S} holds, since $\delta_{x} \in \Prob$ for every
$x \in \XX$. The bound is uniform in $\mu$ and quantitative, so it gives considerably
more than \hyp{S}{S} asks.

body:
[Df $k$-tube of arXiv:2605.14910, 'Sharp Phase Transition for the Formation of Infinite Tubes'] Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^d$.
  A continuous map $\gamma\colon\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times[a,b]\to X$~(with $-\infty<a<b<\infty$) is called a \emph{$k$-tube} in $X$ if $\gamma$ is \emph{locally self-avoiding}; that is, for every $t\in[a,b]$, there exists a neighborhood $U\subset[a,b]$ of $t$ such that the restriction $\gamma|_{\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times U}$ is injective.
  If $\gamma$ itself is injective, then $\gamma$ is said to be \emph{self-avoiding}.
  The topological $(k-1)$-spheres $S=\gamma(\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times\{a\})$ and $S'=\gamma(\mathbb{S}^{k-1}\times\{b\})$ are called, respectively, the \emph{initial sphere} and the \emph{terminal sphere} of $\gamma$ (the \emph{initial loop} and the \emph{terminal loop} of $\gamma$ when $k=2$).
  In this case, we further say that $S$ and $S'$ are \emph{joined} in $X$, and denote this by $S\overset X{\approx}S'$.
  (See Figure~(fig:tube of the paper).)

 uniformly drawn from      $\cM_{n,d}$.

    \P\lr{s_n(M)\le \frac{\sqrt{d}}{\varepsilon^2 n}}\ge 1-C_p\lr{\varepsilon+\frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}}.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\begin{itemize} 
\item If $m>n+1$ we have $\mathcal{H}_{\overline\partial,P}^{m}(0)=0$,   and $\mathcal{H}_{\overline\partial,P}^{n+1}(0)\subset H^{n+1}(M)$. 
\item If $\mathcal{H}_{\overline\partial,P}^{m}(0)$ is nonzero

for some $m<n$, the first positive eigenvalue $\lambda_{1,m+1}$  satisfies
$$\lambda_{1,m+1}<4(n-m+1).$$
Also, we have 
$$\lambda_{1,m+2b}< 4(b+1)(n-m-b+1),$$

[Cor 9 of arXiv:2604.24189, 'Malliavin calculus and densities for chaos-driven stochastic differential equations'] Let $q \in \N$ and $f \in \mathfrak{H}^{\odot  q}$ be fixed, and set $F=I_q(f)$. For every $h \in \mathfrak{H}$, there exists an event $\Omega_h$ with $\mathbb{P}(\Omega_h)=1$ such that, for every $\omega \in \Omega_h$ and $0 \leq \ell \leq q$,
\[D^\ell F(\omega + j(h)) = \sum_{k=0}^{q-\ell} \frac{1}{k!} \langle D^{k+\ell} F(\omega),h^{\otimes k} \rangle_{\mathfrak{H}^{\otimes k}}. \]

body:
Fix a finite Netsor program. Its inputs are fixed real vectors of fixed dimensions and independent matrix variables W of shape n by m with independent N(0,1/m) entries. Its only instructions are MatMul g=W h and coordinatewise NonLin h=phi(h_1,...,h_k), with matching dimensions; a matrix variable may be reused, but transposition is not an instruction. Let n_hidden be the program collection of dimensions internal to chains of matrix contractions, and n_output the output dimensions; input dimensions remain fixed. Write h^ell in R^(n_ell) for the finite-width variable on line ell and bar_h^ell for the infinite-width execution. In the latter, every MatMul variable bar_g is centered Gaussian, all MatMul variables are jointly Gaussian, different matrix variables have zero cross-covariance, and two products using the same W, with parent variables bar_h,bar_h_prime in R^m, have cross-covariance [E(bar_h^T bar_h_prime)/m] I_n. NonLin instructions apply the same functions coordinatewise to this Gaussian execution. Assume every function phi used in a NonLin instruction is globally Lipschitz. For every p>=1 there is c<infinity depending only on p and the structural constants of the fixed program such that W_p((h^ell/sqrt(n_ell))_(ell=1)^L, (bar_h^ell/sqrt(n_ell))_(ell=1)^L) <= c sum_(m in n_hidden) m^(-1/2). W_p uses the Euclidean norm on the concatenated vector of all line variables. Structural constants include the fixed input vectors, input dimensions and activation functions; c is uniform in the hidden widths. The theorem does not give a polynomial dependence of c on program length L, and does not cover transpose instructions or arbitrary non-Lipschitz activations.

body:
[Proposition UB-ZW of arXiv:2411.13923, 'Harmonic analysis of multiplicative chaos \\ Part I: the proof of Garban-Vargas conjecture'] There exists a constant $C = C(\gamma, \tau, p, q)>0$ such that for any dyadic sub-interval $I\subset [0,1)$ of generation $k-1$ with $k\geq2$,  
	\[
	\mathbb{E}[\|Y_I\|_{\ell^q}^p] \le C |I|^{ 1 + \Theta(\gamma, \tau, p,q)}. 
	\]
In other words,   for each $k\ge 2$ and any $I\in \mathscr{D}_{k-1}$, 
\[
\mathbb{E}[\|Y_I\|_{\ell^q}^p] \lesssim  2^{-k \cdot \theta(\gamma, \tau, p, q)}
\]
with 
	\[
	\theta(\gamma, \tau, p, q) = 1+ \Theta(\gamma, \tau, p, q)  =  p-\frac{p(p-1)\gamma^2}{2}-\frac{\tau p}{2}-\frac{p}{q}. 
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition UB-ZW of arXiv:2411.13923

body:
[Proposition 10 (Trapezoid rule) of arXiv:2608.14143, 'Mod-$\phi$ convergence for random variables with cyclotomic generating functions'] Let $a<b$ and $f\in C^2[a,b]$ be a twice continuously differentiable function. Then, for any $n\in\N$,
	\[
	\int_a^b f(x)\,dx = A_{n}(f) + R_{n}(f),
	\]
	where
	\[
	A_{n}(f) = \frac{b-a}{n}\Big( \frac{f(a)+f(b)}{2} + \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} f\bigl(a + \frac{b-a}{n}i\bigr) \Big)
	\]
	and the remainder satisfies $|R_{n}(f)| \le \frac{(b-a)^3 \|f''\|_{\infty}}{12n^2}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Trapezoid rule

body:
[Thm 1 of arXiv:2607.24170, '\large\bf ON NON-MONOTONICITY OF LOGARITHMIC ENERGY\\ FOR RANDOM MATRICES'] Let $(\mathsf{W}_{ij})_{1\leq i\leq j<\infty}$ be independent with
common law $\sigma$, set
$\mathsf{W}_{ji}\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\mathsf{W}_{ij}$ for $i<j$,
and define
\[
 \mathbf{M}_n\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}(\mathsf{W}_{ij})_{1\leq i,j\leq n},
 \qquad
 \rho_n\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\E[\mu_{\mathbf{M}_n/\sqrt n}].
\]
Then $(\mathbf{M}_n)_{n\geq1}$ is a real symmetric Wigner sequence,
each $\rho_n$ has a compactly supported bounded density, and
\[
 m_2(\rho_n)=1,\qquad \cE(\rho_n)\in\R,\qquad n\geq1.
\]
Moreover, $\rho_1=\sigma$, $\rho_2((2,\infty))>0$, and, with
$\pentry_0\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\sigma((3/2,2))$,
\[
 \cF_{\R}(\rho_2)-\cF_{\R}(\rho_1)
 \geq\frac{\pentry_0^3}{2}\left(\frac34-\log2\right)>0,
 \qquad
 \cF_{\R}(\rho_1)=\cF_{\R}(\sigma)=\frac34.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 1 of arXiv:2607.24170

[Corollary 41 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let \(\xi\) be a fixed limiting point based at
\(q=q_\pi(\xi)\in Y^{\rm prod}\).  Let \(Z\) denote the underlying
time-\((-1)\) K\"ahler metric model of any tangent space at \(\xi\).
Then \(Z\) is globally smooth and is one of the following two models:
\begin{equation}
 Z\cong\C^{m+1}
 \qquad\text{or}\qquad
 Z\cong\C^m\times\PP^1.
\end{equation}
In the complex-linear normalization of
\cref{prop:local-coordinate-interface}, the limiting map is
\(G=\operatorname{pr}_{\C^m}\), its zero slice is respectively \(\C\) or \(\PP^1\),
and the ancient tangent flow has globally bounded curvature on every
compact negative-time interval.

$p_1(\tau)=-\phi_1(7\tau)$,

 $p_2(\tau)=\phi_2(7\tau)$,

and define
\begin{equation}
 X=
 1+p_1+p_2-\frac1{p_1p_2},
 \quad
 Y=
 \frac{(p_1+1)(p_2+1)(p_1p_2-1)}{p_1p_2}.

Then
\(
 X,Y\in\A_0(\G_0(49))
\),
and they satisfy
\begin{equation}
 Y^2+XY=X^3-X^2-2X-1.
\end{equation}
Furthermore,
\[
 \A_0(\G_0(49))=\C(X,Y).
\]
Thus \eqref{eq:X049-minimal} is a minimal Weierstrass model of
$X_0(49)$.

Those integrals are in turn named elliptic because they first were encountered for the calculation of the arc length of an ellipse.

body:
[Defi gs4 of arXiv:2507.20324, 'Non-existence of several random fractals in Brownian motion and Brownian loop soup'] Fix $\iota\in(0,1/2)$. Let
\begin{equation}
    \mu_{\iota}:=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{0}^{2\pi}\int_{\iota}^{1-\iota}\mu_{\mathcal{B}(0,r)}^{\mathrm{bub}}(re^{i\theta})(\cdot\,;\mathrm{diam}(\gamma)>\iota/2)\,r\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta, \quad \mu_{\iota}^{\#}:=\mu_{\iota}/|\mu_{\iota}|,
\end{equation}
where $\mu_{\mathcal{B}(0,r)}^{\mathrm{bub}}(re^{i\theta})(\cdot\, ;\mathrm{diam}(\gamma)>\iota/2)$ stands for the bubble measure restricted to loops with diameter greater than $\iota/2$. Note that the total mass $|\mu_{\iota}|$ is finite due to this restriction, and hence $\mu_{\iota}^{\#}$ is well defined. 
Let $\gamma$ be a (rooted) Brownian loop sampled according to $\mu_{\iota}^{\#}$, and let $t_{\gamma}$ be its duration. 

Let $N(\delta)$ be the smallest integer $n$ such that $2^{-n}<\delta/16$. For $n\geq N(\delta)$, let $\mathfrak{S}_{n}=\mathfrak{S}_{n}(\delta)$ be the collection of $\delta$-good boxes, i.e.\ the set of all $S\in\mathcal{S}_{n}$ with the following properties:
\par
(1) $S$ is visited twice by $\gamma$ and the path makes an excursion of distance at least $\delta-2^{-n-1/2}$ between visits. More precisely,
\[\tau_{\gamma}(S,\partial\mathcal{B}(S,\delta-2^{-n-1/2}),S)<t_{\gamma},\]
and we use $V_{\delta}^{\mathrm{BDP}}(S)$ to denote this event.
\par
(2) $S$ is not disconnected from infinity by $\widetilde{\gamma}$ (the cluster of $\{\gamma\}\cup\Gamma_{0}$ which contains $\gamma$).
title: Defi gs4 of arXiv:2507.20324

For the population loss (1/2)||BA-Delta||_F^2 with Delta an m-by-n rank-r matrix, rotate the two factors by the left and right singular vectors of Delta. Write R,T for the r-by-r principal blocks of the rotated B and A transpose, and J,K for the complementary blocks. Define S=(R+T)/2 and D=(R-T)/2, P=Sigma-SS^T+DD^T, and Q=SD^T-DS^T, with Sigma the positive diagonal r-by-r singular-value matrix. Then the principal error is P+Q, P is symmetric, Q is skew-symmetric, and its squared Frobenius norm is ||P||_F^2+||Q||_F^2. Ye and Du's proof grows the smallest singular value of S while controlling D,J,K in a warm-up phase, then uses a local geometric convergence phase. Their Theorem 1.1 assumes nondegenerate independent Gaussian entries in both factor matrices; its theorem statement does not directly cover B0=0. This is an optimization symmetrization of factor matrices, distinct from empirical-process symmetrization. Source: arXiv:2106.14289, sections 2.1-2.3 and 3.1-3.3.

body: Theorem (campaign status: proved): The real full-dual matroid on $D_n$ is genuinely three-connected. A dual representation is $t=\sum_i e_i$, $p_i=e_i$, $q_i=e_i+e_{i+1}$. A run-count proof shows every partition $(X,Y)$ with $|X|,|Y|\ge2$ satisfies $r(X)+r(Y)-n\ge2$; every dual column is nonzero and deleting any one column leaves rank $n$, ruling out singleton one-separations. Notes: Run-count proof lives in rigidity_attack_report.md, not reproduced here. This object exists to certify that the family below is genuinely three-connected, which is what makes it a counterexample rather than a degenerate case.

[Theorem thm:E[multi-edges] of arXiv:2604.05921, 'Simplicity of random hypergraphs'] Let $\forall e \in E: \delta_e \leq \frac{1}{2} n \mathds{E}[d_U]$ and let $R(\cdot)$ be as in (equation def:B of the paper). Then the expected number of multi-hyperedge pairs in a uniformly random undirected hypergraph with degree sequence $\vb*{d}$ is
    \begin{align}
    
        \mathds{E}[M_n]&= \frac{1}{2} \sum_{e \in E} \sum_{\substack{e' \in E\backslash\{e\}:\\\delta_{e'}=\delta_e}}\frac{(n\mathds{E}[d_U]-2\delta_e)!}{(n \mathds{E}[d_U])!}\sum_{\substack{\vb*{a} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_e}:\\\sum_{i=1}^{\delta_e} ia_i = \delta_e}}  \frac{\delta_e!^2}{\prod_{k=1}^{\delta_e} k!^{2a_k} }\sum_{\alpha(\cdot) \in R(\vb*{a})} (-1)^{\sum_{\vb*{x} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_e}} (\sum_{i=1}^{\delta_e} x_i - 1)\alpha(\vb*{x})} \\
     &\hspace{1cm}\times 
    \prod_{\vb*{y} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_e}} \Bigg( \frac{1}{\alpha(\vb*{y})!} \Big(\frac{n\mathds{E}\big[\prod_{i=1}^{\delta_e} (\mathds{1}_{\{d_U \geq 2i\}}\frac{d_U!}{(d_U-2i)!})^{y_i} \big]\big(\sum_{i=1}^{\delta_e} y_i-1 \big)!}{\prod_{i=1}^{\delta_e} y_i!} \Big)^{\alpha(\vb*{y})} \Bigg). \nonumber
    \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:E[multi-edges] of arXiv:2604.05921

[Theo 20 of arXiv:2608.00811, 'Comparison of Dirichlet forms for stable-like random walks on groups of polynomial volume '] Let $\Xi_0 = (\xi_1,\ldots, \xi_n)$ be a set of $N$
such that 
$$\Xi := \left(\bigsqcup_{i=1}^{m} \Xi_{u_i}\right) \sqcup \Xi_0$$
generates $N$, and  for $i=1,\ldots, n$, take $a_i > \frac{1}{2}$ with $a_i \le \mathfrak{u}(\xi_i)$. Construct 
\begin{align*}
 \mathbf{u} &:= \left(\bigsqcup_{i=1}^{m} \underbrace{(u_i,\ldots, u_i)}_{|\Xi_{u_i}|-times}  \right) \sqcup (a_1,\ldots,a_n) 
\end{align*}
If $(S,\mathbf{v})$ 
is a tuple with $S$ generating $N$ and  $\mbox{Red}(\mathcal{N}_{S,\mathbf{v}}) = \mathcal{I}$, then 
$$\mathcal{E}_{\mu_{S,\mathbf{v}}} =  \mathcal{E}_{\mu_{\Xi, \mathbf{u}}}$$

[Lemma lem:translate of arXiv:2608.23638, 'Replicable Conformal Prediction'] Fix an integer $N\ge1$, $\alpha\in(0,1)$,
$0<\varepsilon<\min\{\alpha,1-\alpha\}$,
$0<\delta<1/2$, and $c>0$.  Let
$Q_t:=\operatorname{Unif}[t,t+c]$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$,
with distribution function $F_t$.  Let $\nu$ be a fixed probability
law on a measurable seed space $\mathsf R$.  There is no single
measurable procedure $\mathcal{A}:\mathbb{R}^N\times\mathsf R\to\mathbb{R}$ for which, for
every $t\in\mathbb{R}$, both
\[
\text{there exists }v_t\in\mathbb{R}\text{ such that }
\mathbb{P}_t\{\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{D};R)=v_t\}\ge1-\delta
\]
and
\[
\mathbb{P}_t\!\left\{
F_t\bigl(\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{D};R)\bigr)
\in[1-\alpha-\varepsilon,1-\alpha+\varepsilon]
\right\}\ge1-\delta
\]
hold, where
$\mathbb{P}_t:=Q_t^{\otimes N}\otimes\nu$ is the joint law of
$\mathcal{D}$ and an independent seed $R$.

[Lemma lem:inequalities_FV of arXiv:2412.01645, 'Regularisation by Gaussian rough path lifts of fractional Brownian motions'] Let $F \in \mathcal{C}^2$ and set $\rho=1/H_-$. There exists a constant $C=C(\|F\|_{\mathcal{C}^2}$, $\|\sigma\|_{\mathcal{C}^2},H_-)$ such that for all $x \in {\mathbb{R}}^d$, $s\in [0,1]$ and ${\color{blue}M}=(M, M') \in \mathcal{D}^{2H_-}_B([s,1])$, if $V$ is a solution of (equation eq:general_equation_Jacobian of the paper), then for all $(u,v) \in [s,1]_{\leq}$ we have 
    \begin{equs}
     \,    [R^{\blue{F(\phi^{s,x}) V}}]_{\mathcal{V}^{\rho/2}_2([u,v])}  \leq& C \big(  [R^{\color{blue}V}]_{\mathcal{V}^{\rho/2}_2([u,v])} + \|V\|_{\mathcal{C}^0([u,v])} [R^{\blue{F(\phi^{s,x})}}]_{\mathcal{V}^{\rho/2}_2([u,v])} \big) 
  \\  & +C[B]_{\mathcal{V}^{\rho}([u,v])}\Big([R^{\color{blue}V}]_{\mathcal{V}^{\rho/2}_2([u,v])}+(\|V\|_{\mathcal{C}^0([u,v])}\\  &\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad+ \|M\|_{\mathcal{C}^0([u,v])})[B]_{\mathcal{V}^{\rho}([u,v])} \Big),
    \\
   \,  [(F(\phi^{s,x}) V)']_{\mathcal{V}^{\rho}([u,v])}\leq &C \Big( [R^{\color{blue}V}]_{\mathcal{V}^{\rho/2}_2([u,v])} + (\|V\|_{\mathcal{C}^0([u,v])}+\|M\|_{\mathcal{C}^0([u,v])})
   \\

 \|(F(\phi^{s,x}) V)'\|_{\mathcal{C}^0([u,v])}  \leq   & C ( \|V\|_{\mathcal{C}^0([u,v])}+\|M\|_{\mathcal{C}^0([u,v])}).
     \end{equs}

[Defn ofn of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $\gamma:[0,T]\to\mathbb{R}^{2}$ be a BV path and let $s<t$ be two fixed times such that $\gamma_{s}\neq\gamma_{t}$. We define
the associated
\textit{normalisation operator} $\mathcal{A}_{s,t}$ by 
\[
\mathcal{A}_{s,t}(x)\triangleq\frac{1}{|\gamma_{t}-\gamma_{s}|}R_{s,t}\left(x-\gamma_{s}\right),\ \ \ x\in\mathbb{R}^{2}.
\]
Here $R_{s,t}:\mathbb{R}^{2}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{2}$ denotes the rotation
that maps $\gamma_{t}-\gamma_{s}$ to $\left(\left|\gamma_{t}-\gamma_{s}\right|,0\right)$. We use $\mathcal{A}_{s,t}\gamma$ to denote the path $[s,t]\ni u\mapsto{\cal A}_{s,t}(\gamma_{u})$.
title: Defn ofn of arXiv:2506.18207

[Theorem thm: main BRW of arXiv:2607.20097, 'Phase transition for the asymptotic entropy of branching random walks on groups'] Assuming (ass: finite entropy of the paper), (ass: almost sure survival of the paper), and (ass: sec mom GW of the paper), the following holds.
\begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]
\item Assume $\rho\leq\mathsf{e}^{\textsf{h}(\mu)}$. Then for every $c > 0$ there exists $\delta_0>0$ such that, for all $\delta\leq \delta_0$, it holds that
$$
\lim_{K\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\big(\lim_{n\to\infty}\widehat{M}_n^{\text{typ}}\big(\mathcal{G}_{n,\delta,K,c}^{(1)}\big) = 1\big) = 1.
$$
\item Assume $\rho> \mathsf{e}^{\textsf{h}(\mu)}$. Then for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta_0>0$ such that, for all $\delta\leq \delta_0$, it holds that
$$
\lim_{K\to\infty}\mathbb{P}\big(\lim_{n\to\infty}\widehat{M}_n^{\text{typ}}\big(\mathcal{G}_{n,\delta,K,\varepsilon}^{(2)}\big) = 1\big) = 1.
$$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm: main BRW of arXiv:2607.20097

body:
[Proposition prop:born-binomial-starts of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] Suppose the symmetric urn starts from $\mathrm{Binomial}(n,p_0)$, where
$p_0=\cos^{2}(\theta_0/2)$ and $\theta_0\in[0,\pi]$. Then its law at time $t$ is the
Born distribution of the coherent state

\begin{equation}
e^{-i\theta(t)J_x}\lvert m=+\tfrac n2\rangle,\qquad
\theta(t)=\arccos\bigl(\cos\theta_0\,e^{-2t}\bigr).

\end{equation}

Equivalently, the initial coherent state at angle $\theta_0$ is rotated through
the additional angle $\theta(t)-\theta_0$ about the same axis.

[Lem 20 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $C$ be as in \eqref{e:wishart.bound.repeated}.
    Fix any realization of $\bG$ satisfying
    \beq
    
    \max\bigg\{
       \frac{ \|\bG\|_{\op}}{C},
       \frac{\|\bar{\bx}\|}{2}
      \bigg\} \le N^{1/2}\,.
    \eeq
For such $\bG$, we have the following:
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
        \item  Under the additional constraint that $\bXi$ satisfies
        \beq
            
            \frac{\|\bXi\|_{\op}}{N^{1/2}}
             \le C\,,
        \eeq
        the function
$\by \mapsto F^{\ri}(\bG,\bXi,\by)$,
        restricted to the domain $\{\|\by\| \le 2 N^{1/2}\}$, is $O(N^{-1/2})$-Lipschitz.
        \item 
Restricted to the (convex) domain \eqref{e:fp-F-kirszbraun-bXi-event},
the function
        \beq
        
            \bXi \mapsto F^{\ri}(\bG,\bXi,\ytrunc(\bG,\bXi))\,,
        \eeq
         is $O(N^{-1/2})$-Lipschitz.
    \end{enumerate}
Consequently, for any realization of $\bG$ satisfying \eqref{e:fp-F-kirszbraun-bG-event}, there exists a function $\tilde{F}(\bXi;\bG)$ which is $O(N^{-1/2})$-Lipschitz in $\bXi$, and agrees with the function
\eqref{e:fp-F-kirszbraun-fn-bXi} on the set of $\bXi$ satisfying \eqref{e:fp-F-kirszbraun-bXi-event}.

\begin{proof}
Fix $\bG$, $\bXi$ satisfying \eqref{e:fp-F-kirszbraun-bG-event}, \eqref{e:fp-F-kirszbraun-bXi-event}. Recalling \eqref{e:F.B}--\eqref{e:F.w}, we calculate
    \begin{align*}
    \nabla_\by F_B(\bG,\bXi,\by)
    &=
    \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{2\hB_j}{MN|B_j|}
        \bigg(\sum_{a\in B_j} \bmeta^a, \by \bigg)
        \bigg(\sum_{a\in B_j} \bmeta^a \bigg)\,,\\
            \nabla_\by F_v(\bG,\bXi,\by)
    &=\sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{2\hv_j}{M}
        \sum_{a\in B_j}
        \frac{(\barbg^a,\by) \barbg^a}{N}
    \\
            \nabla_\by F_U(\bG,\bXi,\by)
    &=
    \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{2\hU_j}{M|B_j|}
        \bigg(
            \sum_{a\in B_j}
            \frac{(\bmeta^a,\bar{\bx})(\barbg^a,\by)}{N}
        \bigg)\bigg(
            \sum_{a\in B_j}
            \frac{(\bmeta^a,\bar{\bx})\barbg^a}{N}
        \bigg)\\
            \nabla_\by F_w(\by)
    &=\sum_{j=1}^s\frac{2\hw_j}{N} \Pi_j \by\,.
    \end{align*}
Let $\bG^{B_j} \in \R^{B_j\times N}$ denote the restriction of $\bG$ to the rows indexed by $B_j$, and similarly denote $\bXi^{B_j}$.
Let $\ind_{B_j}\in\R^M$ denote the indicator of the $B_j$ coordinates.
Then we can bound
    \begin{align*}
    \Big| \nabla_\by F_B(\bG,\bXi,\by) \Big|
    &= \bigg| \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{2\hB_j}{MN|B_j|}
    (\ind_{B_j})^\st \bXi \by
    \cdot \bXi^\st\ind_{B_j} \bigg|
    \le  \bigg| \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{2\hB_j}{MN}
            (\|\bXi\|_\op)^2 \|\by\|  \bigg|
    \lesssim \frac{1}{N^{1/2}}\,,\\
    \Big| \nabla_\by F_v(\bG,\bXi,\by) \Big|
    &=\bigg| \sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{2\hv_j}{MN}
        (\bG^{B_j})^\st\bG^{B_j} \by \bigg|
            \le
    \bigg|\sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{2\hv_j}{MN}
    (\|\bG\|_\op)^2 \|\by\|
    \bigg|\lesssim \frac{1}{N^{1/2}}\,,\\
    \Big| \nabla_\by F_U(\bG,\bXi,\by) \Big|
    &=\bigg|\sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{2\hU_j}{MN^2|B_j|}
        (\bXi^{B_j}\bar{\bx},\bG^{B_j}\by)
        \cdot
            (\bG^{B_j})^\st \bXi^{B_j}\bar{\bx}\bigg| \\
    &\le \bigg|\sum_{j=1}^r
        \frac{2\hU_j}{MN^2|B_j|}
        (\|\bXi\|_\op\|\bG\|_\op)^2
        \|\bar{\bx}\|^2 \|\by\|
        \bigg|
        \lesssim \frac{1}{N^{1/2}}\,,\\
        \bigg|\nabla_\by F_w(\by)\bigg|
    &\le \bigg|
    \sum_{j=1}^s\frac{2\hw_j}{N} \|\by\|\bigg|
           \lesssim \frac{1}{N^{1/2}}\,.
    \end{align*}
Here, all factors of $\hB_j, \hv_j, \hU_j, \hw_j$ can be absorbed in the $\lesssim$ notation, as indicated by Remark~\ref{r:fp-implicit-constants}. Combining these estimates proves part \eqref{i:fp-F-kirszbraun-yLip}.

[Definition def:ncP of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] A non-commutative probability space consists of a unital algebra
  $\mathcal{A}$ over $\mathbb{C}$ and a linear functional $\varphi :
  \mathcal{A} \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$, such that $\varphi (1_{\mathcal{A}}) =
  1$. The elements of $\mathcal{A}$ are called non-commutative random
  variables. The non-commutative distribution of $a \in \mathcal{A}$ is the
  linear functional $\mu_a : \mathbb{C} \langle \mathbf{x} \rangle \rightarrow
  \mathbb{C}$, defined by
  \[ \mu_a (P) := \varphi (P (a)) \text{, \quad for every ploynomial } P \in
     \mathbb{C} \langle \mathbf{x} \rangle . \]
  For $(a_1, \ldots, a_n) \in \mathcal{A}^n$ the values $\varphi (a_1 \ldots
  a_n)$ are called moments.
title: Non-commutative probability

Let (G_n)_{n >= 0} be a DECREASING family of sub-sigma-algebras, G_0 containing G_1 containing G_2 and so on, and let G_infinity be their intersection. For Y in L^1, E[Y | G_n] converges almost surely and in L^1 to E[Y | G_infinity]. More generally a BACKWARD MARTINGALE, a family (X_n) with X_n G_n-measurable and E[X_n | G_{n+1}] = X_{n+1}, converges almost surely and in L^1 - and unlike the forward case NO extra hypothesis is required, because a backward martingale is automatically uniformly integrable: X_n = E[X_0 | G_n] is a family of conditional expectations of one integrable variable. This asymmetry with the forward theorem is the point: forward martingales need an L^1 bound for almost sure convergence and uniform integrability for L^1 convergence, backward martingales need neither. The classical application is the strong law of large numbers: with S_n the partial sums of an i.i.d. integrable sequence and G_n the exchangeable sigma-algebra generated by S_n, S_{n+1}, ..., one has E[X_1 | G_n] = S_n/n, so S_n/n converges almost surely and in L^1, and the Hewitt-Savage 0-1 law identifies the limit as E[X_1]. [standard; e.g. Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed., Theorem 4.6.1]

body:
[Thm main of arXiv:2608.30847, 'An Almgren-type formula for planar $p$-harmonic functions'] Let $u$ be a nonconstant $p$-harmonic function in a planar domain $\Omega$, and let $x_0\in\Omega$.  Put $v=u-u(x_0)$.  For all sufficiently small $r>0$, define
$$
  D(x_0,r)=\int_{B_r(x_0)} |D u|^p\,dx,
\quad 
  H(x_0,r)=\int_{\partial B_r(x_0)} |D u|^{p-2}v^2\,dS,
$$
and
$$
  N_*(x_0,r)=\frac{rD(x_0,r)}{H(x_0,r)}.
$$
If $u$ is not locally constant near $x_0$, then $H(x_0,r)>0$ for all sufficiently small $r$ and the limit
$$
  N_*(x_0,0+)=\lim_{r\to0}N_*(x_0,r)
$$
exists.

If $D u(x_0)\ne0$, then $ N_*(x_0,0+)=1.$
If $D u(x_0)=0$ and the Aronsson order of $x_0$ is $N\ge1$, then
$$
  N_*(x_0,0+)=\lambda_N(p),
$$
where
$$
  \lambda_N(p)=\frac{\beta_{N+1}(p)}{\beta_{N+1}(p)-1}
$$
and
$$
  \beta_{N+1}(p)
  =
  \frac{\sqrt{(p-2)^2+4(p-1)((N+1)/N)^2}-(p-2)}{2}.
$$
Moreover, in both cases there are constants $C>0$, $\delta>0$, and $r_0>0$ such that
$$
  |N_*(x_0,r)-N_*(x_0,0+)|\le Cr^\delta
  \qquad 0<r<r_0.
$$

In addition, the obstruction $\Theta$ defined as (equation eq:theta-defn of the paper) in Proposition~(thm:exact-identity of the paper) belongs to $L^1(0,r_0)$, and the gauge-corrected frequency (equation eq:gauge-frequency of the paper) in Corollary (cor:gauge-formal of the paper) is nondecreasing. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Unreviewed campaign concept; independent referee w461 pending. On a path with L>=1 edges, q>1 and 0<p<1, put alpha=p/[p+q*(1-p)]. Free random-cluster edges are iid Bernoulli(alpha). Wiring the two endpoints tilts that law by 1+(q-1)*1_{all edges open}. Therefore the wired minus free marginal gap at each edge is (q-1)*(1-alpha)*alpha^L/[1+(q-1)*alpha^L], positive at every finite L and tending to zero. For q=3,p=1/2 it is 1/4 at L=1 and 1/172 at L=4. Finite-size positivity alone cannot establish an infinite-volume gap. This d=1 example refutes the inference, not C0048 for d>=3.

body: [Thm main of arXiv:2606.01627, 'The geometry of the giant component of random geometric graphs'] Let $M$ be a connected compact $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold with $d \geq 2$ and let $\Delta_c = \Delta_c(d)$ be the critical average degree for having a giant component.  For each fixed $\Delta_0 > \Delta_c$,  $\beta \in (0,1)$, $\varepsilon > 0$, there is a $c = c(M,\Delta_0,\beta,\varepsilon) > 0$ and $n_0 = n_0(M,\Delta_0,\beta,\varepsilon)$ so that the following holds.  Let $G = G_M^n(r)$ be the Poisson random geometric graph on $M$ with expected average degree $\Delta \in [\Delta_0,n^{1-\beta}].$  Let $\mathring{G}_M^n(r)$ be the  component of $G$ with largest diameter and $d_G$ the graph metric on $G$. Then for all $n \geq n_0$ we have $$\mathbb{P}\left(d_{{\mathrm{GH}}}\left(\left(\mathring{G}_M^n(r),  \frac{r}{\overline{\mu}(\Delta)} d_G\right),(M,  d_M) \right) > \varepsilon\right) \leq \exp(-c \log^2 n)\,.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 6 (Dirichlet bounds) of arXiv:2604.00642, 'Quantitative central limit theorem for an integrated periodogram via the fourth moment the'] There exists $C<\infty$ such that for all $n\ge1$ and $\lambda\in(-\pi,\pi)$, we have
\[
\abs{D_n(\lambda)}\le C\min\Big(\sqrt n,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,\abs{\lambda}}\Big)
\le C H_n(\lambda),
\qquad
\Phi_n(\lambda):=\abs{D_n(\lambda)}^2 \le H_n^2(\lambda).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\Phi_n(\lambda)\dd\lambda=1,
\qquad
\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}D_n(\lambda-\omega)D_n(\omega-\mu)\dd\omega
=\sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{n}}\,D_n(\lambda-\mu),
\]
\begin{align*}
\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}|D_n(\lambda-\omega)D_n(\omega-\mu)|\dd\omega \leq C\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}|H_n(\lambda-\omega)H_n(\omega-\mu)|\dd\omega \leq C_{\eta}n^{\eta-1/2}H_n(\lambda-\mu).
\end{align*}

[Proposition prop:tangent_curvature of arXiv:2605.03896, 'Dimer models on astroidal zig-zag graphs'] Let \(\zeta_0\in \Sigma(\mathbb{R})\). Then:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The point \(\zeta_0\) is a critical point of
    \(\Omega^{-1}\big|_{\Sigma(\mathbb{R})}\) if and only if
    \(\Omega^{-1}(\zeta_0)\) is one of the four types of cusps in Definition~(def:regions_in_limit_shape of the paper) and Definition~(def:tp_cusp of the paper). 
    
    \item Each of these cusps is an ordinary cusp in the geometric sense, \emph{i.e.} after a smooth change of coordinates, it is locally given by $y^2=x^3$.
    
    \item The tangent line to the branch of \(\mathscr{A}\) at \( \Omega^{-1}(\zeta_0) \)
    determined by \(\zeta_0\) has slope
    \[
    -\frac{1}{\gamma(\zeta_0)}=-\frac{f_1(\zeta_0)}{f_2(\zeta_0)}.
    \]
    In particular, if $\zeta_0 = \alpha \in \bm \alpha$, then the tangent line is $\bm l_{e(\alpha)}$.
\end{enumerate}

(Thm 8) There is an absolute constant C such that for every polynomial p: R^n -> X of degree at most d with values in a Banach space X, every 0 < q < infinity, every log-concave probability measure mu on R^n and every alpha > 0: (int ||p||^{q/d} dmu)^{1/q} * alpha^{-1/d} * mu{x: ||p(x)|| <= alpha} <= C q. Taking q = 2d and real p: mu{|p| <= eps (int p^2 dmu)^{1/2}} <= 2C d eps^{1/d} for all eps > 0. (Thm 7) For 0 < r <= q < infinity: (int ||p||^{q/d} dmu)^{1/q} <= C (max(q,1)/max(r,1)) (int ||p||^{r/d} dmu)^{1/r}. A log-concave measure is supported on an affine subspace with density e^{-g} there, g convex; uniform measures on convex bodies and Gaussian measures qualify.

Assumes: mu log-concave; p a polynomial of degree <= d (real or Banach-valued)

Then, for \(h=0\),
\[
        G_{L,0}^{(\kappa)}
        \stackrel{d}{=}
        \sum_{r=1}^R Y_{L,r},
\]
where the \(Y_{L,r}\)'s are independent negative-binomial random variables. 
Moreover,
\[

        V_L
        \mathbf P

            G_{L,0}^{(\kappa)}=n
        \right)
        <\infty ,
\]
and, uniformly for \(n/V_L\) in compact subsets of \((0,\infty)\),
\[

            G_{L,0}^{(\kappa)}=n
        \right)
  -

        \left(
            \frac n{V_L}
        \right)\to 0,
\]
where
$       f_0^{(\kappa)}
        =
        g_1*\cdots*g_R$ and $g_r$ is the Gamma density
\[

        =
        \frac{\alpha_r^{\theta_r}}{\Gamma(\theta_r)}

        \mathbf 1_{\{x>0\}} .
\]

body:
[Df 27 of arXiv:2609.03836, 'Koszul Orlik--Solomon Algebras from Non-supersolvable Arrangements'] Let $m, r$ be positive integers. Let $\eta$ be a primitive $m$-th root of unity. The \textbf{cyclic Dowling arrangement} of order $m$ and rank $r$, denoted $Q_r(m)$, is the arrangement in $\mathbb{C}^r$
    \[
        Q_r(m) = \{ x_i \mid 1 \leq i \leq r\} \cup \{x_i - \eta^k x_j \mid 1 \leq i < j \leq r, \; 0 \leq k < m\}.
    \]
    The \textbf{cyclic Dowling geometry} of order $m$ and rank $r$ is the matroid $MQ_r(m) \deq M(Q_r(m))$.
    For a subset $Z$ of $\{1,\dots,m\}$, the \textbf{Dowling subarrangement} induced by $Z$ is the subarrangement 
    \[
        Q_Z(m) \deq \{x_i \mid i \in Z\} \cup \{x_i - \eta^k x_j \mid i, j \in Z,\; i < j,\; 0 \leq k < m\}.
    \]
    The corresponding submatroid $MQ_Z(m) \deq M(Q_Z(m))$ of $MQ_r(m)$ is the \textbf{Dowling subgeometry} induced by $Z$. It is isomorphic to 
    $Q_{\abs{Z}}(m)$ and its ground set is a flat of $Q_r(m)$. We also call ``Dowling subgeometry'' the flat $E(M(Q_Z(m )))$ of any submatroid of $MQ_r(m)$ containing it.
title: Definition 27 of arXiv:2609.03836

Let A_1, ..., A_m be pairwise independent with S = sum_i P(A_i) > 0. Then P(A_1 or ... or A_m) >= S/(1 + S(1 - 1/m)), with equality if and only if all P(A_i) are equal and the number N of events that occur is constant on the union. If every P(A_i) = p > 0 the bound reads mp/(1 + (m - 1)p), with equality if and only if N takes only the values 0 and r = 1 + (m - 1)p; so equality is impossible unless 1 + (m - 1)p is an integer. For the three even-parity events on {000, 011, 101, 110}, p = 1/2, r = 2 and the bound 3/4 is attained.

[Definition def:dominating of arXiv:2605.26048, 'Classification of the eternal solutions and multiple coalescing shocks in the KPZ fixed po'] For $\varphi \in \Phi$, we call a point $\xi\in\operatorname{supp}(\varphi)$ a (left) dominating color if there exists $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that for every $\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0$
\begin{align}
     \varphi(\xi')& <\varphi(\xi), \qquad \forall \xi'\in I_\varepsilon(\xi),\xi'< \xi\\
      \varphi(\xi')& \leq \varphi(\xi), \qquad \forall \xi'\in I_\varepsilon(\xi),\xi'\geq \xi
\end{align}
Note that (equation eq:o17 of the paper) (resp. (equation eq:o18 of the paper)) is vacuously true for points in $\Xi^+$ (resp. $\Xi^-$).
We denote by $\operatorname{Dom}(\varphi)$  the set of dominating colors.  See Figure (fig:function of the paper).

[Corollary 6 (Integrated head start) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] Suppose that $P_0(\cdot\mid r)\ll P_0$,
$\KL(P_0(\cdot\mid r)\|P_0)<\infty$, and the endpoint limits of
Theorem~\ref{thm:fixed-r-entropy-dissipation} hold.  Then
\begin{equation}

\int_0^\infty
\E_{X_t\mid r}\|g_t(X_t,r)\|^2\,\dd t
=
\KL\!\left(P_0(\cdot\mid r)\middle\|P_0\right).
\end{equation}
For the uniform empirical prior on pairwise distinct points,
\begin{equation}

\int_0^\infty
\E_{X_t\mid r}\|g_t(X_t,r)\|^2\,\dd t
=
\sum_{i=1}^n w_i(r)\log\{n w_i(r)\}
=
\log n-H(I\mid r).
\end{equation}
At fixed \(r\), the information supplied by the measurement before reverse
denoising is therefore the accumulated force energy along the full noising
path. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2608.04853, 'Minimal-Norm Extensions of Stationary Kernels on Subgroups of Locally Compact Abelian Grou'] Given a locally compact abelian group $G$ and a closed subgroup $H\subseteq G$, there exist measures on $\hat{G}/H^\perp$ and $H^\perp$ such that for all $f \in L^1(G)$ with $\hat{f} \in C_c(\hat{G})$ we have for almost all $x \in G$
\begin{align*}
f(x)
    =\int_{\hat{G}} \hat{f}(\xi) \cdot \xi(x) \d \xi 
    &= \int_{\hat{G}/H^\perp} \int_{H^\perp} \hat{f}(\xi_H+\xi^\perp) \cdot (\xi_H+\xi^\perp)(x) \d \xi^\perp \d \xi_H \\
    &= \int_{H^\perp} \int_{\hat{G}/H^\perp} \hat{f}(\xi_H+\xi^\perp) \cdot (\xi_H+\xi^\perp)(x) \d \xi_H \d \xi^\perp.
\end{align*}

Moreover, if $f \in L^2(G)$ we have 
\begin{align*}
    f
    =\int_{\hat{G}} \hat{f}(\xi) \cdot \xi \d \xi 
    &= \int_{\hat{G}/H^\perp} \int_{H^\perp} \hat{f}(\xi_H+\xi^\perp) \cdot (\xi_H+\xi^\perp) \d \xi^\perp \d \xi_H \\
    &= \int_{H^\perp} \int_{\hat{G}/H^\perp} \hat{f}(\xi_H+\xi^\perp) \cdot (\xi_H+\xi^\perp) \d \xi_H \d \xi^\perp.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 4 of arXiv:2608.04853

[Lem f-bounded-distortion of arXiv:2606.01627, 'The geometry of the giant component of random geometric graphs'] Let $M$ be a connected compact $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold of volume $1$ with $d \geq 2$.  For each fixed $\lambda_0 > \lambda_c$, $\beta \in (0,1), \varepsilon > 0$, let $X$ be a finite $(\varepsilon/5)$-net of $M$.  Then there are constants $c = c(M,\lambda_0,\beta,\varepsilon,X) > 0$ and $n_0 = n_0(M,\lambda_0,\beta,\varepsilon,X)$ so that {if $r \le n^{-\beta}$ and $\lambda \ge \lambda_0$} we have
        $$\mathbb{P}\left(\sup_{x, x' \in X}
        |\mu(\lambda)d_M(x,x') - r d^\lambda_r(f_r(x),f_r(x'))| > \varepsilon/2\right) \leq  \exp(-c \log^2 n) $$
        for $n \geq n_0$.
title: Lem f-bounded-distortion of arXiv:2606.01627

[Lemma Functional one-step inequality of arXiv:2608.24731, 'Optimal Alternating Regret for Online Learning and Games\thanks{Authors are alphabetically'] \label[lemma]{lem:functional}
Let $P$ be a probability measure on an arbitrary measurable space. Let $\xi,\zeta$ be measurable functions with values in $[-2,2]$ such that $\mathbb E_P[\xi]=0$, and define $Q(\,\mathrm d u):=(1-\xi(u)/2)P(\,\mathrm d u)$. If $\eta\le1/8$ and $\beta=\eta/4$, then
\[
\log\mathbb E_P\exp\!\left\{
\eta\bigl(\mathbb E_Q[\xi+\zeta]-\xi-\zeta\bigr)
+\beta(\xi^2-\zeta^2)
\right\}\le0.
\]

[Definition 9 (Gradient) of arXiv:2605.18198, 'Large deviations of crowding in finite $\beta$-ensembles'] The gradient of $Q$ is the vector-valued function on the plane
	\(
	\nabla Q : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2
	\)
	defined by
	\[
	\nabla Q(x)
	=
	\left(
	\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x_1}(x),
	\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x_2}(x)
	\right),
	\qquad x=(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2 .
	\]

[Proposition 37 of arXiv:2608.07239, 'Unified framework for asymptotically uniform iterative construction of generalised random '] Consider the quantity $\mathscr{Q}(T,U)$ from Theorem~\ref{theorem_space}.
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item We have
			\begin{align}
				\mathscr{Q}(T,U)&=\left(\frac{2}{\ell}\right)^{|T|}\frac{(\alpha')!}{\alpha!}\exp\left(-P'|U|+O\left(\frac{|T|M'}{\alpha'}\right)\right)
				\\&=P^{|T|}\exp\left(-P|U|+O\left(\frac{|T|^2+|T|M'}{\alpha'}\right)\right).
			\end{align}
			\item If $\b(v)=\frac12P|R^*(v)|$ for all $v\in V$, then
			\begin{align}
				\mathscr{Q}(T,U)&=\exp\Bigg(P|F|-P'|F\cap V'|-P'|R^*(T)\cap V'|-P'|U|\Bigg.
				\\&\quad\Bigg.+\tfrac12P^2\sum_{v\in V}|R^*(v)|-\tfrac12(P')^2\sum_{v\in V'}|R^*(v)\cap V'|\Bigg)\prod_{t=\alpha'+1}^{\alpha}\frac{t}{n_t}.
			\end{align}
			Therefore, a uniformly random FMIS of $G$ contains $T$ and is disjoint from $U$ with probability $(1+O(\mathscr{E}(\alpha',M')))\mathscr{Q}(T,U)$.
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 60 (Ising model at criticality) of arXiv:2602.14618, 'Finitary coding and Gaussian concentration\\ for random fields'] Let \(d\ge 2\). For the ferromagnetic Ising model at \(\beta=\beta_c(d)\), the unique Gibbs measure does not satisfy Gaussian concentration.
Nevertheless, it satisfies the blowing-up property, since it admits a finitary coding from an i.i.d. random field. Moreover, any finitary coding of this random field by an i.i.d. random field necessarily has infinite expected coding volume.

[Definition 21 of arXiv:2512.04807, 'Existence and uniqueness of the canonical Brownian motion in non-simple conformal loop ens'] Let $F$ be a non-empty set.  A pair $(\CE,\CF)$ is called a \emph{resistance form} if the following are true:
\begin{enumerate}[(RF1)]
\item $\CF$ is a linear subspace of the space of $\R$-valued functions on $F$ that contains the constant functions, and $\CE$ is a non-negative symmetric quadratic form on $\CF$.  Moreover, $\CE(f,f) = 0$ if and only if $f \in \CF$ is a constant function.
\item Let $\sim$ be the equivalence relation on $\CF$ given by $f \sim g$ if and only if $f-g$ is constant.  Then $(\CF/{\sim}, \CE)$ is a Hilbert space.
\item For each $x \neq y$ there exists $f \in \CF$ such that $f(x) \neq f(y)$.
\item For each $x,y \in F$, we have
\begin{equation}
 R(x,y) \defeq \sup \left\{ \frac{| f(x) - f(y)|^2}{\CE(f,f)} : f \in \CF,\, \CE(f,f) > 0 \right\} < \infty .
\end{equation}
\item We have $\ol{f} \in \CF$ and $\CE(\ol{f},\ol{f}) \leq \CE(f,f)$ for each $f \in \CF$ where $\ol{f} = (f \vee 0) \wedge 1$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition 21 of arXiv:2512.04807

[Proposition prop:wheel-geodesics of arXiv:2609.02544, 'A finiteness theorem for geodesic Leech wheels'] Every geodesic of $W_{m+1}$ belongs to exactly one of the following four classes.
\begin{align*}
&uv_i, &&\text{weight }a_i;\\
&v_iv_{i+1}, &&\text{weight }b_i;\\
&v_iv_{i+1}v_{i+2}, &&\text{weight }b_i+b_{i+1};\\
&v_i u v_j\quad(0\le i<j<m,\ \{i,j\}\notin E(C_m)),
&&\text{weight }a_i+a_j.
\end{align*}
Consequently
\[
  t_{gp}(W_{m+1})=\frac{m(m+3)}2.
\]
Equivalently, for $n\ge5$,
\[
  t_{gp}(W_n)=\frac{(n-1)(n+2)}2.
\]

body:
[Corollary multilinear reursion of arXiv:2412.07936, 'Simple Norm Bounds for Polynomial Random Matrices via Decoupling'] Let ${\bf x} = \{x_i\}_{i = 1}^n$ be a sequences of i.i.d random variables with ${\mathbb E} x_i= 0$,  ${\mathbb E} x_i^2= 1$ and $|x_i| \leq L$ for all $1\leq i \leq n$. Let $\{{\bf A}_{{\bf i}}\}_{{\bf i} \in {\mathcal T}^d_n}$ be multi-indexed sequences of deterministic matrices of the same dimension. Define a degree-$D$ multilinear polynomial random matrix as
$$
{\bf F}({\bf x}) =  \sum_{d=1}^D ~ \sum_{{\bf i} \in {\mathcal T}^d_n} \left( {\bf A}_{{\bf i}} \cdot \prod_{j \in \{i_1,\dots, i_d \}} x_j\right).
$$
Suppose ${\bf F}^{=d}({\bf x})$ is permutation symmetric for $1\leq d \leq D$. Let $a,b,c\in {\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0}$ and $d = a+b+c$. Then for $2 \leq t \leq \infty,$
$$
{\mathbb E} \norm{{\bf F}({\bf x}) - {\mathbb E} {\bf F}({\bf x})}_{4t}^{4t} ~\leq~ \sum_{d=1}^D  D^{4t} (48dt)^{4dt} \left( \sum_{\substack{a,b,c: \\a+b+c=d }} L^{4ct} \norm{{\bf F}_{a,b,c}^{=d}}_{4t}^{4t} \right).
$$

body:
[Cor one-environment-transience of arXiv:2507.09421, 'Stability of randomly switching stochastic reaction networks with asymptotically linear tr'] Suppose that $M$ is a $d\times d$ matrix which is associated to a CRN in the sense of equation (equation eq:associated CRN of the paper); suppose further that the CRN is endowed with mass-action kinetics and has at-most-monomolecular reactions. Suppose that there exists a vector $v\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^d$ such that $(vM)_m>0$ for each $m$ such that $v_m>0$, where as above $(vM)_m$ is the $m$-th entry of the vector $vM$. Then $x$ is a evanescent state for the CRN for each $x\in\mathbb Z^d_{\ge0}$ such that $\operatorname{supp}(v)\cap\operatorname{supp}(x)\ne\varnothing$.
\begin{proof}
    Fix $x\in\mathbb Z^d_{\ge0}$ such that $\operatorname{supp}(v)\cap\operatorname{supp}(x)\ne\varnothing$. We can view the CRN as a mixed process in one environment with $M_1=M$ and switching matrix $Q=(0)$. So if we consider the mixed process with matrix $\kappa Q$, then Theorem (thm:slow-switching-transience of the paper) says that $x$ is evanescent for the process if $\kappa$ is small enough and Theorem (thm:fast-switching-transience of the paper) says that $x$ is evanescent for the process if $\kappa$ is large enough. But $\kappa Q=Q$ in this case, so either theorem is enough to conclude the claimed result.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Dfn 202 (buckets for spherical perceptron) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] We now define $\vX^\trunc$ and $\vX^\frozen$, which may be regarded as the processes $\vX^\trstar$ and $\vX^\frstar$ with \textbf{small spatial buckets frozen}. For the spherical perceptron, initialize $\vX^\trunc(q_0)\equiv\vX^\trstar(q_0)$
and $\vX^\frozen(q_0)\equiv\vX^\frstar(q_0)$, and suppose inductively that $\vX^\trunc(q_\ell)$
and $\vX^\frozen(q_\ell)$
have been defined for $0\le\ell\le d$. Then let
    \begin{align}
    B(q_d, J(q_{0:d})) 
    &\equiv \Big\{ a\in[M]:
    \vX^\trunc(q_\ell,a)
    \in J(q_\ell)
    \textup{ for each }0\le\ell\le d
    \Big\}\,,\\
    B^\frozen(q_d, J(q_{0:d})) 
    &\equiv \Big\{ a\in[M^\frozen]:
    \vX^\frozen(q_\ell,a)
    \in J(q_\ell)
    \textup{ for each }0\le\ell\le d
    \Big\}\,.\end{align}
We emphasize that in both \eqref{e:bucket} and \eqref{e:bucket.fr}, the $J$ blocks are restricted to within $[-\trK,\trK)^3$. We then let
    \begin{align*}
    B(q_d,a)
    &= \begin{cases}
    B(q_d, J(q_{0:d}))
    &\textup{if $a\in B(q_d, J(q_{0:d}))$,}\\
    \{a\}
    &\textup{otherwise, meaning 
    $\vX^\trunc(q_d, a)
    \notin[-\trK,\trK)^3$;}
    \end{cases} \\
    B^\frozen(q_d,a)
    &= \begin{cases}
    B^\frozen(q_d, J(q_{0:d}))
    &\textup{if }a\in B(q_d, J(q_{0:d}))\,,\\
    \{a\}
    &\textup{otherwise, meaning }\vX^\frozen(q_d, a)\notin[-\trK,\trK)^3\,.
    \end{cases}
    \end{align*}
The sets $\mathcal{B}(q_d)\equiv\{B(q_d,a) : a\in[M]\}$ partition $[M]$, and the partition is progressive in the sense that each $\mathcal{B}(q_{d+1})$ refines the previous partition $\mathcal{B}(q_d)$.  Similarly, the sets
$\mathcal{B}^\frozen(q_d)\equiv\{B^\frozen(q_d,a) : a\in[M^\frozen]\}$ progressively partition $[M^\frozen]$. In either case we call these the \textbf{buckets} at time $q_d$.  We define the quantity
    \beq
    \BUCKETS
    \equiv \bigg(\frac{8\trK}{\eta}\bigg)^{6\dmax}\,,\eeq
so that $\BUCKETS$ upper bounds the total number of buckets within $[-\trK,\trK)^3$ over all times. We then let
    \begin{align}
    
    \vX^\trunc(q_{d+1},a)
    &=\begin{cases}
    \vX^\trstar(q_{d+1},a)
    &\textup{if } |B(q_d,a)| 
        \ge M/\BUCKETS^2\,,\\
    \vX^\trunc(q_d,a)
    &\textup{otherwise}\,.
    \end{cases}\\
    
    \vX^\frozen(q_{d+1},a)
    &=\begin{cases}
    \vX^\frstar(q_{d+1},a)
    &\textup{if } |B^\frozen(q_d,a)  \cap[M]  | 
        \ge M/\BUCKETS^2\,,\\
    \vX^\frozen(q_d,a)
    &\textup{otherwise}\,.
    \end{cases}
    \end{align}
Note that because the partitions $\mathcal{B}(q_d)$ and $\mathcal{B}^\frozen(q_d)$ are progressive, particles that are frozen in step $d+1$ (i.e. such that the second case of \eqref{e:small-bucket-freezing-trunc} or \eqref{e:small-bucket-freezing-frozen} holds) stay frozen in all future steps. Note also that when determining whether buckets for the $\vX^\frozen$ process are too small we only look at particle indices in $[M]$, that is, we ignore the added particles from Definition~\ref{d:froze} when determining bucket size. With this definition, one can verify by induction that the set of buckets $B\in \mathcal{B}(q_d)$ can be obtained by taking $B=B^\frozen\cap[M]$ for each $B^\frozen\in\mathcal{B}^\frozen(q_d)$.
title: buckets for spherical perceptron

body: Maximum modulus principle: Let D be a nonempty connected open subset of C (a domain) and let f be holomorphic on D. If |f| attains a local maximum at some point of D, then f is constant on D. Equivalently, if f is holomorphic and non-constant on D, then |f| has no local maximum at any point of D. Consequently, if D is bounded and f is continuous on the closure of D and holomorphic on D, then the maximum of |f| over the closure of D is attained on the boundary of D.
title: Maximum modulus principle

  Let $R_0 \subset \R^d$ be the set of roots of a non-trivial $d$-variate polynomial.

body: The interlacement (crossing) graph G_x(pi) of a pair partition pi does not determine the Toeplitz moment-polytope volume p_T(pi). Through order 8 every graph class carries one volume (K_3 gives 1/2, K_4 gives 2/5, matching p_T(w_r) = 2/(r+1) for G_x(w_r) = K_r; the empty graph gives 1). At order 10 exactly one of 34 classes is impure: the graph on five vertices with two disjoint edges and an isolated vertex carries 9/20 (aabcbcdede) and 4/9 (ababcdedec). Connected graphs are pure through order 10, but not at order 12: of 110 connected classes, 42 are realised by more than one inequivalent diagram and 10 of those are impure, every split being 19/90 against 22/105 (abacdbefcdfe and abacdecbfdef, two diagrams of the connected graph {01,02,03,04,12,13,14,25}). Adding the nesting number does not repair it (8 of the 10 still collide, both witnesses having nesting number 1), and the crossing number does not either. Exact rational arithmetic; orders 6, 8 and 10 enumerated completely.

PRIVATE REDUCTION, author-recorded. For a filled-in peeling exploration of the infinite Boltzmann map with critical weight sequence q, every boundary vertex is eventually swallowed almost surely iff sum_n q_{S_n} = infinity a.s., where S_n is the half-perimeter process (an h-transform of the step walk with law nu) and q_l is the probability that a peeling step at perimeter l swallows at least half of the boundary on a given side. For type a in [3/2, 5/2] the source proves divergence from q_l asymp l^{1-a} and the scaling limit S_n asymp n^{1/(a-1)}. Without a type, the criterion is a recurrence-type statement for the positive test function q along the h-transformed walk; it holds whenever liminf n q_{S_n} is bounded below in probability, so the question reduces to the growth of the h-transformed perimeter walk for non-regularly-varying critical nu. The reduction is rigorous (conditional Borel-Cantelli); the growth control is the open part.

body: Lemma (campaign status: audited-pass): psi(u) = min{3/4, 2^{1-u}*C(u, floor(u/2))} <= min{3/4, 2/sqrt(u)} (tag 12). For u = 2 the 3/4 bound is the nondegenerate-parallelogram bound; for u >= 3 it is the ordinary two-atom Littlewood-Offord bound. Over F_p invoke the finite-group one-point Littlewood-Offord theorem: when u < p and all coefficients are nonzero, each atom is at most the central-binomial mass; a union bound over the two targets gives the same psi. Notes: The bound must be uniform in the target center b, in the coefficients, and in all earlier block values - all three quantifiers are used by the reverse-exposure argument.

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); T385-w737-C06 v1; no independent PASS and no novelty claim. Let X,W be n by n and a in R^n, with X_ij iid N(0,1/n), W_ij and a_j iid N(0,1), jointly independent of X and each other. Let H=ReLU(XW), G_ij=1{(XW)_ij>0}, S=XX^T and D=S elementwise-multiplied by (G diag(a_j^2)G^T/n). For the bias-free scalar network f(x)=n^(-1/2) sum_j a_j ReLU(w_j dot x), its all-weights empirical NTK is K=HH^T/n+D. The recorded unaudited derivation asserts ||D-[S/4+I_n/4+(1/(2pi))1_n1_n^T/n]||_op ->0 in probability as n=d=m tends to infinity. Hence K has all its ordered eigenvalues within o_P(1) of HH^T/n+S/4+I_n/4+(1/(2pi))1_n1_n^T/n. The proof combines conditional matrix Bernstein after truncating Gaussian output squares with El Karoui's quadratic-kernel approximation and uniform row-radius control. It retains the quadratic rank-one term. It does not establish a full NTK bulk law, a bounded spectral edge, anisotropic resolvent limits, or a Marchenko-Pastur bulk. Independent review is pending.

[Lemma le:mixture-given-beta-I of arXiv:2411.06195, 'Restrictions of some reinforced processes to subgraphs'] Let $\Lambda=I\cup J$ be finite with $I\cap J=\emptyset$, $\rho\in J$, and
  $W\in[0,\infty)^{\Lambda\times\Lambda}$. 
  For $\beta=(\beta_I,\beta_J)\in{\mathbb R}^\Lambda$ such that $[H_\beta^W]_{\Lambda_-\Lambda_-}$
  is positive definite, let 
  $e^{u_{\Lambda_-}(\beta)}=([H_\beta^W]_{\Lambda_-\Lambda_-})^{-1}W_{\Lambda_-\rho}$
  and $u_\rho(\beta)=0$.
  Let $H_{\beta_J}^{W^J(\beta_I)}$ and $H_{\beta^{J\neq}}^{W^{J\neq}(\beta_I)}$
  denote the $J\times J$ matrices obtained
  from $H_\beta^W$ defined in (equation eq:def-H-beta of the paper) with $(\beta,W)$
  replaced by $(\beta_J,W^J(\beta_I))$ and $(\beta^{J\neq},W^{J\neq}(\beta_I))$,
  respectively, with $\beta^{J\neq}:=(\beta_j-\frac12W^J_{jj}(\beta_I))_{j\in J}$,
  $W^J(\beta_I)$ from (equation def:W-J of the paper), and 
  $W^{J\neq}(\beta_I)$ from (equation eq:def-W-J-neq of the paper). 
  Then, one has the following restriction property
  \begin{align}
    
    e^{u_{J_-}(\beta)}=([H_{\beta_J}^{W^J(\beta_I)}]_{J_-J_-})^{-1}W_{J_-\rho}^J(\beta_I)
    =([H_{\beta^{J\neq}}^{W^{J\neq}(\beta_I)}]_{J_-J_-})^{-1}W_{J_-\rho}^{J\neq}(\beta_I). 
  \end{align}
  As a consequence, $u_{J_-}(\beta)$ depends only on $W^J(\beta_I)$ and $\beta_J$.
  We write $u_J(W^J(\beta_I),\beta_J)=u_J(W^{J\neq}(\beta_I),\beta^{J\neq})$
  instead of $u_J(\beta)$.
  
  As an application of (equation eq:exp-u-J-in-volume-J of the paper) for fixed $\beta_I$, 
  vrjp on $J$ with parameters $W^J(\beta_I)$ and $W^{J\neq}(\beta_I)$, respectively, are
  mixtures of reversible Markov jump processes with weights 
  \begin{align}
    
     C^J_{ij}(\beta_I,e^{u_J})
    =W^J_{ij}(\beta_I)e^{u_i+u_j} \quad\text{and}\quad
    C^{J\neq}_{ij}(\beta_I,e^{u_J})
    =W^{J\neq}_{ij}(\beta_I)e^{u_i+u_j}, 
    \quad i,j\in J,
  \end{align}
  and the same reversible measure $\pi(u_J)=(2e^{2u_i})_{i\in J}$ 
  with $u_J=u_J(W^J(\beta_I),\beta_J)$ in both cases, where
  $\beta_J$ is a $\nu_J^{W^J(\beta_I)}$-distributed random variable.
  In other words, for any event $A\subseteq J^{{\mathbb N}_0}\times{\mathbb R}_+^{{\mathbb N}_0}$, one has
  \begin{align}

  \int_{{\mathbb R}^J}Q^{C^{J\neq}(\beta_I,e^{u_J(W^{J\neq}(\beta_I),\tilde\beta_J)}),J}_{\rho,\pi(u_J(W^{J\neq}(\beta_I),\tilde\beta_J))}((X,T)\in A)\,
  \nu_J^{W^{J\neq}(\beta_I)}(d\tilde\beta_J)
  \end{align}
  and the same formula with ``$J{\neq}$'' replaced by ``$J$'' at all five
  occurrences. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let $X \sim N(\theta, \sigma^2 I_k)$ in $\mathbb{R}^k$ with $k \ge 3$ and $\sigma^2$ known, and let $\mu_0 \in \mathbb{R}^k$ be any fixed target. Define $$\hat\theta_{\mathrm{JS}} = \mu_0 + \Big(1 - \frac{(k - 2)\sigma^2}{\|X - \mu_0\|^2}\Big)(X - \mu_0), \qquad \hat\theta_{\mathrm{JS}+} = \mu_0 + \Big(1 - \frac{(k-2)\sigma^2}{\|X - \mu_0\|^2}\Big)_+ (X - \mu_0).$$ Then for every $\theta$: (i) $E\|\hat\theta_{\mathrm{JS}} - \theta\|^2 = k\sigma^2 - (k-2)^2\sigma^4\, E\big[\|X - \mu_0\|^{-2}\big] < k\sigma^2 = E\|X - \theta\|^2$, so the shrunk estimator strictly dominates the observation itself in total squared error, with the largest gain when $\theta$ is near $\mu_0$ (risk $\to 2\sigma^2$ at $\theta = \mu_0$); (ii) the positive-part version dominates the plain one, $E\|\hat\theta_{\mathrm{JS}+} - \theta\|^2 \le E\|\hat\theta_{\mathrm{JS}} - \theta\|^2$ with strict inequality. The shrinkage amount $s = (k-2)\sigma^2/\|X - \mu_0\|^2$ is the ratio of the expected squared noise norm to the observed squared distance from the target; it is small exactly when the observation sits far from the target relative to its noise. When the noise covariance is a known $\Sigma$ rather than $\sigma^2 I$, apply the lemma to $\Sigma^{-1/2}(X - \mu_0)$ (so $s = (k - 2)/\big((X - \mu_0)^T \Sigma^{-1}(X - \mu_0)\big)$) - the Mahalanobis form; a mis-specified $\Sigma$ that understates the noise gives an $s$ that is too small.

Suppose that for each $z\in \mathbb{C},r>0$, we have events $E_r(z) \in \sigma(h)$ and additionally for any points $\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z} ,  \text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}w} \in \mathbb{C}$, and any simple path $\eta$ from $\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z}$ to $\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}w}$, we have events $\mathfrak{C}_r^{\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z},\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}w},\eta}(z) \in \sigma(h)$, satisfying, for a deterministic constant $\Lambda > 1$, the following properties.

\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item 
  For all $z \in \mathbb{C}$ and all $r >0$,  the event $E_r(z)$ is determined by $(h-h_{\lambda_5 r}(z))|_{\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}A}_{\lambda_1 r ,  \lambda_4 r}(z)}$,  and for all $\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z},\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}w} \in \mathbb{C}$,  the event $\mathfrak{C}_r^{\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z},\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}w},\eta}(z)$ is determined by $h|_{B_{\lambda_4 r}(z)}$ and the path $\eta$ stopped at the last time that it exits $B_{\lambda_4 r}(z)$.
\item 
For all $z \in \mathbb{C}$ and all $r >0$, we have $\mathbb{P}(E_r(z)) \geq \mathbbm{p}$.
\item 
For all points $z \in \mathbb{C},r >0$ and $\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z},\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}w}$ satisfying $\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z},\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}w}\notin B_{\lambda_4 r}(z)$, we have
\begin{align*}
\Lambda^{-1} \mathbb{P}(E_r(z) \cap \{\Gamma_{\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z},\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}w}} \cap B_{\lambda_2 r}(z) \neq \emptyset\} \lvert h|_{\mathbb{C} \setminus B_{\lambda_3r}(z)}) \leq \mathbb{P}(\mathfrak{C}_r^{\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z},\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}w},\Gamma_{\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z},\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}w}}}(z) \cap \{\Gamma_{\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z},\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}w}} \cap B_{\lambda_2 r}(z) \neq \emptyset\} \lvert h|_{\mathbb{C} \setminus B_{\lambda_3r}(z)}).
\end{align*}
\end{enumerate}

Under the above hypotheses, for all $q>0,  \ell \in (0,1)$,  and for each bounded open set $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$,  it holds with probability tending to $1$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$,  at a rate depending only on $U,q,\ell,\nu,  \{\lambda_i\}_{i=1,\cdots,5},  \Lambda$,  that for all $\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z},\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}w} \in (\varepsilon^q \mathbb{Z}^2) \cap U$ with $\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}w}\notin \mathcal{B}_{\tau_{4\ell}(\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z})}^\bullet(\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z})$,  there exist $z \in \mathbb{C},  r \in [\varepsilon^{1+\nu} ,  \varepsilon]$ such that $\Gamma_{\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z},\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}w}} \cap B_{\lambda_2 r}(z) \neq \emptyset$ and $\mathfrak{C}_r^{\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z},\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}w},\Gamma_{\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}z},\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}w}}}(z)$ occurs. [Defn 7 of arXiv:2605.25762, 'Brownian Convergence of Planar Domains and Stability of the Planar Skorokhod Embedding Pro'] Let $f$ be analytic on the unit disc $\mathbb{D}$ and $p>0$. The
$p$-th Hardy norm of $f$ is 
\begin{equation}
\Vert f\Vert_{\mathbf{H}^{p}(\mathbb{D})}:=\sup_{0\le r<1}\Big\{\frac{1}{2\pi}\int^{2\pi}_{0}\big|f(re^{i\theta})\big|^{p}\,d\theta\Big\}^{\frac{1}{p}}.
\end{equation}
The supremum is well-defined\cite{Rudin2001}. The Hardy space, denoted
by $\mathbf{H}^{p}(\mathbb{D})$, consists of analytic $f$ with $\Vert f\Vert_{\mathbf{H}^{p}(\mathbb{D})}<+\infty$.
A key fact of Hardy spaces is the boundary trace: if $\Vert f\Vert_{\mathbf{H}^{p}(\mathbb{D})}<+\infty$,
then the radial boundary values $f^{*}(e^{i\theta}):=\lim_{r\to1}f(re^{i\theta})$
exists a.e.\ on $\mathbb{S}$. Moreover 
\[
\|f^{*}\|_{L^{p}(\mathbb{S})}=\Vert f\Vert_{\mathbf{H}^{p}(\mathbb{D})}.
\]
When $p>1$, $\mathbf{H}^{p}(\mathbb{D})$ identifies with $L^{p}_{2\pi}$
in the following way: if $\xi\in L^{p}_{2\pi}$ then the map
\begin{equation}
\Psi(re^{\theta i})=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int^{2\pi}_{0}\frac{1+re^{(\theta-t)i}}{1-re^{(\theta-t)i}}\xi(t)dt
\end{equation}
belongs to $\mathbf{H}^{p}(\mathbb{D})$ and $\Re(\Psi^{*})=\xi$.
When $p=1$, $\Psi$ is analytic in the unit disc but not necessarily
an element of $\mathbf{H}^{1}(\mathbb{D})$. We recommend \cite{duren2000theory,butzer1971hilbert,king2009hilbert,mcgovern1980hilbert,pandey2011hilbert}
for a concise background on Hardy spaces as well as their connections
with the Hilbert transform. The following result illustrates a deep
connection between Hardy spaces and planar Brownian motion.

[Theorem 12 of arXiv:2506.13913, '2506.13913'] {Itô's Formula}{}
    Let \(\{X_t\}_{t \geq 0}\) be a \(d\)-dimensional Itô process given by
\[
\mathrm{d}X_t = \mu(t, X_t) \, \mathrm{d}t + \sigma(t, X_t) \, \mathrm{d}W_t,
\]
Let \(f(t,x)=(f_1(t,x),\cdots f_p(t,x))\in C^{2}([0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^d,\,\mathbb{R}^p)\), i.e., twice continuously differentiable on $[0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^d)$. Then $Y_t=f(t, X_t)$ is again an Itô process, and
\[
\mathrm{d}Y_t
= \frac{\partial f}{\partial t}(t, X_t) \, \mathrm{d}t 
+ \nabla f(t, X_t)^\top \, \mathrm{d}X_t 
+ \frac{1}{2} \operatorname{Tr}\left( \sigma(t, X_t) \sigma(t, X_t)^\top \nabla^2 f(t, X_t) \right) \, \mathrm{d}t,
\]
where \(\nabla f(t, X_t) \in \mathbb{R}^d\) and \(\nabla^2 f(t, X_t) \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}\) is Gradient and Hessian matrix of \(f\) with respect to \(x\), respectively. Therefore, expanding \(\mathrm{d}X_t\) gives
\[
\mathrm{d}Y_t = \left[\frac{\partial f}{\partial t} + \nabla f^\top \mu + \frac{1}{2} \operatorname{Tr}\left(\sigma \sigma^\top \nabla^2 f\right)\right] \, \mathrm{d}t
+ \nabla f^\top \sigma \, \mathrm{d}W_t.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2608.13687, 'Multiplicative chaos from random multiplicative functions'] Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a collection of disjoint finite subsets of primes. 
Let $H^1$ denote $H^1(\cI; \mathbb{K})$ with $\mathbb{K} = \R$ or $\C$. Fix  $(f_p)_{p}\subset H^1$. If $\mathbb{K} = \R$, let  $(A_p)_{p}$ satisfy Case \caseR, and if $\mathbb{K} = \C$, let $(A_p)_p$ satisfy Case \caseS.
For each $B \in \mathcal{B}$, fix an enumeration $B = \{p_1, \dots, p_{|B|}\}$. 
If the block summability~condition  
\begin{align}
    \sum_{B \in \mathcal{B}} \Big(\sum_{p\in B} \|f_p\|_{H^1}^2 \Big)^{1/2}<\infty
\end{align}
holds, then for every $\lambda >0$,
\[
    \E\exp\bigg(\lambda \sum_{B \in \mathcal{B}} \max_{1\leq k\leq|B|} \Big\|\sum_{j=1}^k A_{p_j} f_{p_j} \Big\|_\infty \bigg)<\infty \,.
\]
In particular,  $\sum_{B\in\mathcal{B}} \sum_{p\in B} A_p f_p$ converges uniformly over $\cI$, almost surely. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

  \max\!\left\{0,\frac{m_\nu-\tau}{1-\tau}\right\}
  \le
  \nu\!\left(\{x\in S:\, r(x)\ge \tau M\}\right)
  \le
  \min\!\left\{1,\frac{m_\nu}{\tau}\right\},
\]
and equivalently,
\[
  \max\!\left\{0,1-\frac{m_\nu}{\tau}\right\}
  \le
  \nu\!\left(\{x\in S:\, r(x)\le \tau M\}\right)
  \le
  \min\!\left\{1,\frac{1-m_\nu}{1-\tau}\right\}.
\]
These bounds are sharp: given only $m_\nu$ and $M$, no stronger universal
tail bounds can be obtained. Depending on weak versus strict threshold
conventions, the extremal constants are either attained or approached by
two-point laws supported at endpoint/threshold values.

Own-work C012 v1, proof (unaudited), novelty unestablished. Literal leaky ReLU phi(v)=max(v,lambda*v), 0<lambda<1, f=m^-1 sum_j a_j phi(w_j.x), both-layer simultaneous GD with actual step m*eta, average logistic loss L and G=average (1+exp(y_i*f_i))^-1. Finite data ||x_i||<=1, z_i=y_i*x_i, z_i.z_l>=kappa>0, rank>=2, and a unit u with u.z_i>=gamma>0. Suppose one neuron initially has a and every w.z_i nonzero of the same sign. Put c=lambda*sqrt(kappa), 0<eta<=c, h0=min(|a0|,min_i|w0.z_i|/sqrt(kappa)), B=h0^2/m, r0=||theta0||^2/m, zeta=2*eta*c/(1+eta*c)-eta^2>0. Then for every T>=1, sum_{t<T}G_t<=log((r0+4*eta*T)/B)/zeta. This follows by comparing r_T>=B*exp(2*eta*c*sum G/(1+eta*c)) from a persistent aligned neuron against r_T<=(r0+4*eta*T)*exp(eta^2*sum G), using the exact degree-two Euler identity. If Q_T=log((r0+4*eta*T)/B)/(zeta*T) and n*Q_T<1, some s<T satisfies L_s<=Q_T/(1-n*Q_T). Thus liminf loss is zero and best-iterate loss is O(log T/T); no last-iterate rate or permanent burn-in is claimed. For epsilon>0, q=zeta*epsilon/(1+n*epsilon), H=max(1,(r0+4*eta)/B), T=ceil(max(1,2*log(H)/q,4/q^2)) is a sufficient epsilon-hitting horizon. For iid coordinate N(0,sigma^2), define b=(gamma/sqrt(2*pi*d))^d exp(-(1+gamma/2)^2/2), p=2*exp(-2)*b/sqrt(2*pi). At width m>=log(2/delta)/p, with probability >=1-delta one can replace B by (sigma^2/m)*min(1,gamma^2/(4*kappa)) and r0 by 2*(d+1)*sigma^2/delta, uniformly in T and 0<eta<=c. This uses independent neuron initializations plus a union bound with the initial energy event, not independent trajectory events. Constants may be poor in dimension. Exact finite controls passed 9939 assertions but do not certify the full theorem; no independent audit or Lean certificate. The Euler identity is specific to positively homogeneous literal leaky ReLU; C011 smooth centered activations generally fail it. The remaining TARGET is permanent trained-output burn-in and arbitrary large steps.
Literal positively homogeneous leaky ReLU, mean-field scaling, actual GD step m*eta, no biases.
Strict signed-Gram positivity, normalized bounded data and rank>=2; one aligned neuron, or stated Gaussian sufficient-width event.
0<eta<=lambda*sqrt(kappa); best iterate and finite first entry only, not permanent burn-in.
Own unaudited work; novelty unestablished.

[Lemma 68 of arXiv:2607.18104, '2607.18104'] Fix some $M,K\in \N$ and let  $n\in \N$. Assume that for all $i\in \lbr M\rbr$ and $\varepsilon>0$, we have some $\hfix^{\per,(i),\varepsilon}_0$ in $\UCp$ so that the associated particle configurations satisfy \eqref{eq:DominationAssumption} at time $0$, and such that the rescaled height functions $\hfix^{\textup{patch},n^{-1},\varepsilon}(\hfix^{\per,(i),\varepsilon}_0;\cdot,0)$ of the $(n^{-1},N)$-patched ASEP at time $0$ converge to $\hfix^{\per,(i)}_0 \colon \mathbb{T}\rightarrow \R$ as $\varepsilon \rightarrow 0$ with respect to the UC topology. 
Then there exist $c,C>0$, not depending on $n$ or $\varepsilon$,  such that for any $ t_1 <t_2<\dots<t_{K}$ in $\mathcal{T}$,
with probability $1-C \exp(-c n^{1/2})$, we find a coupling between $\hfix^{\textup{patch},n^{-1},\varepsilon}$ and $\hfixpa$ so that
\begin{equation}
  \max_{i \in \lbr M \rbr} \max_{\ell \in \lbr K \rbr}  \sup_{y\in \mathbb{T}} \left|\hfix^{\textup{patch},n^{-1},\varepsilon}(\mathfrak{h}^{\per,(i),\varepsilon}_0;y,t_\ell)- \hfixpa(\mathfrak{h}^{\per,(i)}_0;y,t_\ell) \right|   \leq (2n+1) 2^{-n}
\end{equation} for all $\varepsilon>0$ sufficiently small.
Here, the functions on the left-hand side are coupled according to the patched coupling $\Ppatch$ for the underlying ASEPs in the definition of the patched ASEPs, while the functions on the right-hand side are coupled as in Definition~\ref{def:PeriodicKPZfixed} with respect to the same patched directed landscape $\Lpa$, taking values in $\mathcal{T}$ for the time component.

N^{-1}\Pi_N(x,x)\to \1\{V(x)<\mu\} , \qquad\text{ as $N\to +\infty$}.

[Proposition 5 (Probabilistic Schur-complement factorization) of arXiv:2607.13210, 'Punctured Wilson--Evolving Sets and Root Identities for Massive Kirchhoff Forests'] Let $k\geq 1$ and fix $x_1,\ldots,x_k$ distinct vertices of $V$. Let $A=\{x_1,\ldots,x_k\}$ and for $i\in [[1,k]]$, let $D_{i-1}=V\setminus\{x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1}\}$. Then
\begin{equation}
  \Pp(A\subset\Root)
  =\det K_q[A]
  =\prod_{i=1}^k q(qI+L_{D_{i-1}})^{-1}(x_i,x_i).
\end{equation}
Equivalently, the Wilson--evolving-set factorization is a probabilistic decomposition of
the principal minor $\det K_q[A]$ into successive Schur-complement pivots. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Probabilistic Schur-complement factorization

body: [Defn connected of arXiv:2411.11676, 'Surface sums for lattice Yang--Mills in the large-$N$ limit'] Let $K : \mathcal{P}_\Lambda \rightarrow \mathbb{N}$ be a plaquette assignment. We say that $K$ is {\bf connected} if its support $\mathrm{supp}(K) := \{p \in \mathcal{P}_\Lambda^+ : K(p) \text{ or } K(p^{-1}) \neq 0\}$ is connected, in the sense that any two plaquettes $p, p'$ in $\mathrm{supp}(K)$ are connected by a sequence $p = p_0, \ldots, p_n = p'$ such that $p_{j-1}$ and $p_j$ share an edge for all $j \in [n]$.
title: Defn connected of arXiv:2411.11676

body: [Conjecture 9 (A continuum of Maxwell--Poincar\'{e}--Borel laws for curvature measures) of arXiv:2605.11995, 'Intrinsic volumes of \(\ell_p\)-balls and a continuum of Maxwell--Poincar\'e--Borel laws f'] Consider a  ``sufficiently regular'' sequence of convex bodies $(K_n)_{n\geq 1}$ such that $\dim K_n = n$ for every $n$ and $\frac 1n \log \Vol_n K_n \to c\in \R$ as $n\to\infty$. \]
Then $\Pr\big(\hat t_{\rm alarm}\le t^\star\big)\to1$.

[Lemma logfluc1 of arXiv:2605.10617, 'Logarithmic scaling of selective sweep curves:\\ from tents to houses'] For $p> 1/2$ and $\ell \in \mathbb{N}_0$ write $\mathbb{P}_\ell^{p,+}$ for the probability measure $\mathbb{P}_\ell^p$ on $\mathbb W$ conditioned under the event $\{\tau_0^+(W) = \infty\}$. \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Theorem 3.2 of arXiv:1908.07093, 'Uniform Reliability of Self-Join-Free Conjunctive Queries'] Let Q be a CQ without self-joins. If Q is hierarchical, then UR(Q) is solvable in polynomial time. Otherwise, UR(Q) is #P-complete. As said above, the hardness side of Theorem 3.2 is essentially the statement that when Q is non-hierarchical, PQE(Q) is #P-hard even when every fact has the probability 1 2, and this is what we need to prove.
title: Theorem 3.2 of arXiv:1908.07093: Uniform Reliability of Self-Join-Free Conjunctive Queries

[Corollary 9 of arXiv:2606.31455, 'Discrete time-multidimensional renewal theory and applications'] Assume $f(0_d)<1$ so that $(\ez-f)(0_d)=1-f(0_d)\neq 0$ and $(\ez-f)$ is convolutionally invertible.
Then the renewal function admits the explicit representation
\begin{equation}
M=(\ez-f)^{(-1)}*F.
\end{equation}
If in addition $f(0_d)=0$, then $(\ez-f)^{(-1)}=\sum_{n\ge 0} f^{(n)}$ coefficientwise and
\[
M(k)=\sum_{n\ge 1} F_n(k)=\sum_{n\ge 1}\mathbb{P}(S_n\le_d k),
\qquad k\in\mathbb{N}^d,
\]
where the sum is finite for each fixed $k$.
title: Corollary 9 of arXiv:2606.31455

body:
[Definition 14 (Interlacing \cite{Brouwer-Haemers}) of arXiv:2609.01114, 'Unbalanced spectral Tur\'an problem for color-critical graphs with prescribed large maximu'] Let $\theta_1\ge\cdots\ge\theta_n$ and
	$\eta_1\ge\cdots\ge\eta_m$ be real sequences with $m<n$.  We say that
	$(\eta_j)_{j=1}^m$ interlaces $(\theta_i)_{i=1}^n$ if
	\begin{equation*}
		\theta_i\ge\eta_i\ge\theta_{n-m+i}
		\quad
		\text{for all } i\in[m].
	\end{equation*}
	The interlacing is tight if there exists $k\in\{0,1,\dots,m\}$ such that
	$\eta_i=\theta_i$ for $i\le k$ and
	$\eta_i=\theta_{n-m+i}$ for $i>k$.
title: Interlacing \cite{Brouwer-Haemers}

body:
[Lemma 22 (Endpoint Laplace asymptotics) of arXiv:2605.11995, 'Intrinsic volumes of \(\ell_p\)-balls and a continuum of Maxwell--Poincar\'e--Borel laws f'] Let $\delta>0$ and $\alpha>0$. Let $F:[0,\delta]\to (0,\infty)$ and
$H:[0,\delta]\to \mathbb C$ be continuous functions. Assume that
\begin{itemize}
\item $F(x)<F(0)$ for all $x\in (0,\delta]$;
\item the right derivative $F'(0)$ exists and satisfies $F'(0)<0$;
\item $H(0)\neq 0$.
\end{itemize}
Then, as $N\to\infty$,
\[
\int_0^\delta x^{\alpha-1}F(x)^N H(x)\,dx
\sim
H(0)\,\Gamma(\alpha)
\left(\frac{F(0)}{-F'(0)}\right)^\alpha
F(0)^N\,N^{-\alpha}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Endpoint Laplace asymptotics

[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2609.00415, 'Separation for Schr\"odinger operators. A counterexample to Simon's conjecture'] Let $d\ge 3$, and let $u$ be the solution of
$$-\left(r^{d-1}u'(r)\right)'=r^{d-1},\qquad 1\le r\le 2,$$
subject to the initial conditions $u(1)=cU(1)$, $u'(1)=cU'(1)$, where $c,\,U(1),\,U'(1)$ are given real constants. Then
$$u(2)+\frac{2}{d-2}u'(2)=c\left(U(1)+\frac{U'(1)}{d-2}\right)-\frac{3}{2(d-2)}.$$

body:
[Lem 12 of arXiv:2606.04636, 'A Thomson-type variational principle for diffusion coefficients'] For almost any $\omega\in\Omega$, $\omega(0)\neq\omega(1)$,
there exists a path $\omega_{1},\dots,\omega_{N}$, for $N=N(\omega)\in2\N$,
and a sequence of sites $x_{1},\dots,x_{N-1}$ in $[0,X(\omega)]$,
such that $\omega_{N}=\omega^{0,1}$, $\omega_{i+1}=\omega_{i}^{x_{i},x_{i}+1}\neq\omega_{i}$,
and $c(x_{i},x_{i+1};\omega_{i})=1$ for any $i\in\{1,\dots,N-1\}$.
Moreover, the following properties are satisfied:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $x_{1},\dots,x_{N/2-1}$ are all in $[2,X(\omega)],$ $x_{N/2}=0$,
and $x_{i}=x_{N-i}$ for any $i\ge N/2+1$.
\item $\omega_{j}(0)-\omega_{j}(1)=\omega(0)-\omega(1)$ for $j\le N/2$
and $\omega_{j}(0)-\omega_{j}(1)=\omega(1)-\omega(0)$ for $j>N/2$.
\item For all $i\in\{1,\dots,N-1\}$, $\omega_{i}(x)=\omega(x)$ if $x\notin[0,X(\omega)+1]$.
\item For all $i\in\{1,\dots,N-1\}$, $X_{-}(\omega)=X_{-}(\omega_{i})$.
\item For all $i\in\{1,\dots,N-1\}$, $X_{+}(\omega)\le\min\{x\ge x_{i}+4:\omega_{i}(x)=\omega_{i}(x+1)=0\}$.
\item Let $\eta\in\Omega$, and assume that there exists $i\in\{1,\dots,N-1\}$
such that $\tau_{x_{i}}\eta=\omega_{i}$. Then 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X_{-}(\omega)=X_{-}(\eta)+x_{i}$;
\item $X_{+}(\omega)\le X_{4}(\eta)+x_{i}\le X_{4}(\eta)-X_{-}(\eta)$.
\end{enumerate}
\item Let $\eta\in\Omega$, $x,x'\in\Z$, $\zeta=\pm1$. Then there is at
most one possible configuration $\omega$ and one possible $i\in\{1,\dots,N(\omega)\}$
such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $x=x_{i}$ and $\eta=\eta_{i}$,
\item $X(\omega)=x'$, and
\item $\omega(0)-\omega(1)=\zeta$.
\end{enumerate}
\item For $\omega'=\omega^{0,1}$, the path $\omega'_{1},\dots,\omega_{N}'$
beginning with $\omega'$ is given by the reversed path $\omega'_{k}=\omega_{N-k}$;
and the associated sites $x_{1}',\dots,x_{N-1}'$ are the same as
$x_{N-1},\dots,x_{1}$, which are also the same as $x_{1},\dots,x_{N-1}$.
\end{enumerate}

[Lem 38 (Following the paths leading to the two marked leaves) of arXiv:2506.19123, 'The longest increasing subsequence of Brownian separable permutons'] The following properties hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The two processes $Z^k$ and $\widetilde{Z}^k$ have the same law.
\item The process $(Z^k_h,\widetilde{Z}^k_h)_{h\geq 0}$ is  a Markov chain.
\item The divergence height $\stdivv$ is a stopping time for the Markov chain $(Z^k_h,\widetilde{Z}^k_h)_{h\geq 0}$. 
\item Whenever $L^k\neq \widetilde{L}^k$, the two leaves $L^k$ and $\widetilde{L}^k$ belong respectively to one and the other subtree above $v_{\stdivv-1}$ so that 
\begin{align*}
(\Mst{\stdivv},W_{\stdivv}) = (\widetilde{W}_{\stdivv},\widetilde{M}^*_{\stdivv}).
\end{align*}
\item Conditionally on $(Z^k_{h},\widetilde{Z}^k_{h})_{0\leq h \leq \stdivv}$, the two processes $(Z^k_{\stdivv+h})_{h\geq 0}$ and $(\widetilde{Z}^k_{\stdivv+h})_{h\geq 0}$ are independent. 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Following the paths leading to the two marked leaves

[Lemma lem:dirty-evacuation of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Fix a fresh plane $i$ and let $\mathbb T_i$ be its coordinate circle.
Let
$\mathcal S_i(\mathbf X):V_{\rm in}\to V_{\rm out}$ be a complete
same-time physical supernode made from current deposits, their centered
pure-Weyl gates, normalized Brauer maps, and physical root/pass maps, with
all non-current pieces retained once as typed gaps
$X_j:V_j^-\to V_j^+$.  Put
\[
 \delta_iX_j=d\rho_{V_j^+}(a_i)X_j-X_jd\rho_{V_j^-}(a_i).
\]
Then the exact identity
\[
 \boxed{
 d\rho_{V_{\rm out}}(a_i)\mathcal S_i(\mathbf X)
 -\mathcal S_i(\mathbf X)d\rho_{V_{\rm in}}(a_i)
 =\sum_j\mathcal S_i(X_1,\ldots,\delta_iX_j,\ldots,X_g)}
\tag{3.3.1u}
\]
holds before the plane sum and before either replica is estimated.
Therefore a marked action entering the supernode exits at one named
external leg or gap, or vanishes at $a_i$ or after complete scalar
closure; it is never duplicated.  If it passes immediately through
$W_i^\circ$, it acquires the exact scalar
\[
 b_n=-\frac{n-3}{(n-1)(n-2)},
 \qquad
 A_iW_i^\circ=W_i^\circ A_i=b_nA_i.
\tag{3.3.1v}
\]
The identity is stable under every gap substitution allowed by
(lem:bridge-consequences of the paper).
