body:
[Lem 159 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}\ref{i:IAMP-main-chaotic}, in the limiting regime \eqref{eq:eta-delta-eps} we have
  \[
    \sup_{\upp \in [0,1]}
    \lt|
      \lim_{N\to\infty} \chi_{\breve{\cA}_N}(\upp) - \plim_{N\to\infty} \frac{(\hat{\by}^{\ubl},\tilde{\by}^{\ubl})}{N}
    \rt| \le \iota'\,,
  \]
  where $\hat{\by}^{\ubl},\tilde{\by}^{\ubl}$ are the outputs of $\IAMP_{\chaos,N}(p,\sigma,b,w,\delta,\eta)$ on $\upp$-correlated $\bz, \tilde{\bz}$.
\begin{proof}
  For each $\upp \in [0,1]$, we have
  \[
    \chi_{\breve{\cA}_N}(\upp)
    = \frac{\bbE (\breve{\cA}_N(\bz), \breve{\cA}_N(\tilde \bz) )}{N}
    = \frac{N}{\bbE_{\bz'}[\|\bar\cA_N(\bz')\|^2]} \cdot \frac{\bbE (\bar{\cA}_N(\bz), \bar{\cA}_N(\tilde \bz) )}{N}\,.
  \]
  As argued in the \hyperlink{proof:t.IAMP.main.main}{proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}\ref{i:IAMP-main-main}},
  \[
    \bigg|\frac{N}{\bbE_{\bz'}[\|\bar\cA_N(\bz')\|^2]} - 1\bigg| \le \iota'\,.
  \]
  We can write
  \[
    \frac{(\bar{\cA}_N(\bz), \bar{\cA}_N(\tilde \bz))}{N}
    = \frac{\|\bar{\cA}_N(\bz) + \bar{\cA}_N(\tilde \bz)\|^2}{2N} 
    - \frac{\|\bar{\cA}_N(\bz)\|^2}{2N} 
    - \frac{\|\bar{\cA}_N(\tilde\bz)\|^2}{2N}
  \]
  Since $\bar{\cA}$ is a $C(L,\epsilon)$-Lipschitz function of standard gaussians, each of the terms on the right-hand side has variance $O(1/N)$.
  Thus $(\bar{\cA}_N(\bz), \bar{\cA}_N(\tilde \bz)) / N$ has variance $O(1/N)$, which implies
  \[
    \lim_{N\to\infty} \frac{\bbE (\bar{\cA}_N(\bz), \bar{\cA}_N(\tilde \bz) )}{N}
    = \plim_{N\to\infty} \frac{(\bar{\cA}_N(\bz), \bar{\cA}_N(\tilde \bz) )}{N}\,.
  \]
  Finally, because $\bar{\cA}_N(\bz)$ agrees with $\tilde{\cA}_N(\bz)$ with probability $1-e^{-cN}$,
  \[
    \plim_{N\to\infty} \frac{(\bar{\cA}_N(\bz), \bar{\cA}_N(\tilde \bz) )}{N}
    = \plim_{N\to\infty} \frac{(\tilde{\cA}_N(\bz), \tilde{\cA}_N(\tilde \bz) )}{N}
    = \plim_{N\to\infty} \frac{(\hat{\by}^{\ubl},\tilde{\by}^{\ubl})}{N}\,. 
  \]
  This concludes the proof.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 20 of arXiv:2608.19976, 'Random valuations'] Let $\Phi$ be a non-trivial $\sigma$-continuous non-negative ID valuation with
  independent increments and vanishing deterministic part. Assume that
  the distribution of $\Phi$ is determined by the measure $\nu$ on
  $\sC\times(0,\infty)$, see Theorem~\ref{thr:2}.
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item[(i)] $\Phi$ is $\alpha$-stable in argument if and only if
    \begin{equation}
      
      \nu(t^{1/\alpha}\sM\times A)=t \nu(\sM\times A)

    \end{equation}
    for all rational $t>0$, measurable $\sM\subset\sC$ and Borel
    $A\subset(0,\infty)$, and then $\alpha\in(0,\infty)$. Here the
    scaling of $\sM$ is applied to all its elements. 
  \item[(ii)] $\Phi$ is $\alpha$-stable in value if and only if 
    \begin{equation}
      
      \nu(\sM\times tA)=t^{-\alpha}\nu(\sM\times A)
    \end{equation}
    for all $t>0$, measurable $\sM\subset\sC$ and Borel
    $A\subset(0,\infty)$,
    and then $\alpha\in(0,1)$.
  \item[(iii)] $\Phi$ is $\beta$-homogeneous if and only if 
    $\nu(t\sM\times A)=\nu(\sM\times (t^{-\beta} A))$ for all $t>0$,
    measurable $\sM\subset\sC$ and Borel $A\subset(0,\infty)$.
  \end{enumerate}
  In each assertion, it suffices to verify the corresponding identity for 
  $\sM=\sC_L$, where $L$ ranges over finite unions of compact convex sets
  and $A\subset[\eps,\infty)$ for any $\eps>0$.
title: Proposition 20 of arXiv:2608.19976

[Prop rodl1995threshold of arXiv:2609.02588, 'Ramsey-type results for Maker-Breaker games'] Let $r\geq 2$ and let $H$ be a graph with a cycle. Then there exist a constant $C$ such that for $m=Cn^{2-1/m_2(G)}$ and any $t\geq 0$ the random graph $G(n,m)$ contains a subgraph $F'$ that satisfies the following with probability tending to $1$ as $n$ tends to infinity:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item Every subgraph $G\subseteq F'$ with $v(G)\leq t$ satisfies $m_2(G)\leq m_2(H)$
        \item $F'\rightarrow_r H$
    \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary $4$(c) in ~\cite{rodl1995threshold}

[Lemma SYNCH of arXiv:2603.12774, 'Synchronization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Browni'] Let \( \eta > 0 \) and suppose that 
	\begin{align}
		\lim_{n \to \infty} \chi_{B(0,\eta)}\!\left(\mathcal{R}\!\left(P_n(\omega^-, \omega^+)\right)\right) = 1, 
		\quad \mathbb{P}\text{-a.s.}.
	\end{align}
	Then
	\[
	\mathbf{P}\big(\mathcal{R}(\omega^-) < \eta\big) = 1.
	\]
	In particular, weak synchronization follows if (equation ASA85sd of the paper) holds for every \( \eta > 0 \). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lem lyapunovg of arXiv:2605.06488, 'Continuous-state branching processes with L\'evy-Khintchine drift-interaction: Laplace dua'] Consider a (sub)critical branching mechanism $\Sigma$ and a supercritical one, $\hat{\Psi}=\hat{\Sigma}-\hat{\Phi}$, such that $\int_0^1\frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\hat\Phi(u)}<\infty$. Set $g(x):=\int_0^{x}\frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\hat\Phi(u)}$ for $x\in [0,\infty)$. The function $g$ takes the following Bernstein form
	\begin{equation}g(x)=\int_0^{\infty}(1-e^{-xz})\frac{\hat{U}(\mathrm{d} z)}{z}, \ x\in [0,\infty),\end{equation} and denoting by $\mathcal{X}$ the generator of the minimal $\mathrm{CBDI}(\Sigma,\hat\Psi)$, see (equation genX of the paper), one has
\begin{equation} \mathcal{X}g(x)=1-xG(x)-\eta(x), \ x\in [0,\infty),
\end{equation}
where $G$ is given by (equation eq:G of the paper) and $\eta(x):=\frac{\hat{\Sigma}(x)}{\hat{\Phi}(x)}\underset{x\rightarrow 0}{\longrightarrow} 0$.

[Definition d:functionalspaces of arXiv:2609.03589, 'Correlated initialization of deep residual networks'] Let \(\banachSpace[W]\) be a Banach space, let
    \(T = [\underline{t}, \overline{t}]\subseteq [0, \infty)\) be a compact interval, and let
    \(\beta\in(0,1]\). We denote by
    \[
        C^\beta(T,\banachSpace[W])
        \coloneq
        \left\{
            w\colon T\to\banachSpace[W]
            \,:\,
            \norm{w}_{\beta}<\infty
        \right\}
    \]
    the space of \(\beta\)-Hölder continuous functions from \(T\) to
    \(\banachSpace[W]\), equipped with the Hölder norm
    \(\norm{\cdot}_{\beta}\) defined above.
title: Functional spaces

body:
Let M>=1 finite linear-regression tasks have matrices X_m in R^(n_m by d) and labels y_m. Suppose X_m*w_star=y_m for every m, put R=max_m||X_m||_2>0, and define L(w;m)=||X_m*w-y_m||^2/2 and L(w)=M^(-1)*sum_m L(w;m). Initialize w_0=0 and sample tau_1,...,tau_k independently and uniformly from{1,...,M}, with replacement. Scheme1 performs the exact update w_t=argmin_w {L(w;tau_t)+(lambda_t/2)*||w-w_(t-1)||^2}. Write D2=||w_0-w_star||^2. For a known integer horizon k>=2, use lambda_t=(13*R^2/3)*(k+1)/(k-t+2), t=1,...,k. Then E L(w_k)<=20*D2*R^2/(k+1). The regularizer penalizes movement from the preceding iterate; its coefficient grows through the run. The bound concerns the full-collection population loss L defined above.
Finite jointly realizable linear tasks; R is the largest task-matrix operator norm and R>0.
Independent uniform task indices sampled with replacement; exact Scheme1 updates; w_0=0.
Known horizon k>=2 and the displayed increasing coefficient schedule.

body:
[Prop 7 of arXiv:2606.30349, 'Attenuated Poisson Dirichlet approximations for divisibility configurations'] Let $\vec{C}(n)=(\alpha_p(H_n):p\le n)$ and $\vec{\xi}(n)=(\xi_p:p\le n)$. Then for all $n\geq  21$
\begin{align}
\PP[A_n]
  &=
\mathfrak{l}_n\prod_{p\le n}(1-p^{-1})\ge \frac12 , 
\\
\mathcal{L}(\vec{C}(n))
  &=\mathcal{L}(\vec{\xi}(n)\mid A_n).

\end{align}
In particular, for any additive arithmetic function $\psi$,
\begin{align}
\mathcal{L}(\psi(H_n))
=
\mathcal{L}\big(
\sum_{p\le n}\psi(p^{\xi_p}) \,\big|\, A_n
\big).
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 7 of arXiv:2606.30349

[Lemma lem:phase-pair of arXiv:2609.02544, 'A finiteness theorem for geodesic Leech wheels'] Let $\alpha,\beta,\Gamma,V>0$ with $\Gamma>V$, and set
\[
  \tau=\frac{\alpha}{2\sqrt{\Gamma-V}}.
\]
Assume also
\[
  0<\tau<\beta,
  \qquad
  \Gamma(\beta-\tau)\ge V(2\beta-\tau).
\]
If complex numbers $z,w$ satisfy
\[
  |z^2-w|\le \Gamma,
  \qquad
  |w|\le V,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
  \alpha\operatorname{Im}z+
  \beta\operatorname{Re}w
  \le
  \alpha\sqrt{\Gamma-V}+\beta V.
\end{equation}

[Lemma prop:hook-prop of arXiv:2410.23944, 'Hitting time mixing for the random transposition walk'] Let $\lambda\vdash n$. Then,
\begin{itemize}
\item \[d_{\lambda} \leq \binom{n}{\lambda_1}\cdot \sqrt{(n-\lambda_1)!};\]

\item for $\lambda_1 = n-x$ with $x \leq (\log n)^2$,
\[d_\lambda = \binom{n}{\lambda}\cdot d_{\lambda^{\ast}}\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(1 - \frac{x}{n} + O(n^{-2 + o(1)}) \aftergroup\egroup\originalright).\]
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma prop:hook-prop of arXiv:2410.23944

body: [Lemma 6 of arXiv:2609.01190, 'Rough differential equations on manifolds via natural bundles'] The jet-rough velocity composition is associative. That is, for $k,\ell, m,n\in\Nsf$, jets $a\in L^2_{k\ell}$, $b\in L^2_{\ell m}$, and a rough velocity $f\in F_{mn}^2$, we have the equality $(ab)f = a(bf)$.
title: Lemma 6 of arXiv:2609.01190

[Definition 7 (Canonical version of $W^\ell$) of arXiv:2511.09517, 'From Cannings model to Brownian motion conditioned on local time profile'] Let $\ell$ be a continuous profile with $h(\ell)<\infty$.
Set
\[
\tilde{\ell}(s):= I(\ell)^{-\frac12}\,\ell\big(I(\ell)^{\frac12}s\big),\qquad s\ge 0,
\]
so that \(I(\tilde{\ell})=1\).  
Let \(W^{\tilde{\ell}}\) denote the version of the conditioned reflected Brownian motion associated with the normalized profile \(\tilde{\ell}\) constructed above.  
We then define
\[
W^\ell_t:= I(\ell)^{\frac12}\, W^{\tilde{\ell}}_{I(\ell)^{-1}t}\,,\qquad 0\le t\le I(\ell).
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:scale}, this defines a version of conditional law, which will serve as our \emph{canonical version} of \(W^\ell\) throughout the paper.
title: Canonical version of $W^\ell$

body:
[Lem 72 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For all $q_0 \in [0,1)$, we have 
\begin{align*}
\sM^{\sx}(\alpha,q_0) 
&\subseteq \sM^{\sxii}(\alpha,q_0)\,,\\
\sM^{\six}(\alpha,q_0) 
&\subseteq \sM^{\sidealast}(\alpha,q_0)\,.
\end{align*}

\begin{proof}
We repeat the most relevant part of Definition~\ref{d:SDE.classification} for this proof:
	\begin{center}
	\begin{tabular}[h]{r|cccccccc}
	\MSRheader\\
	\hline
	\PRFTWOdefn\\
	\PRFFOURdefn\\
	\PRFONEHALFdefn\\
	\SUPERPERFECTASTdefn
	\end{tabular}
	\end{center}
The classes only differ in the conditions on the function $p$.

    Consider any $\mu \in \cM^{\sx}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)$ where $\epsilon < 1/2$. 
    Then $\mu$ is of the form $\mu = \mu(q_*=q_0,b,\sigma,p,\zeta = \delta_0)$ for some $(q_*=q_0,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta = \delta_0,\zeta^\Ising) \in \Adm^{\sx}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)$.
    Since $p$ satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.1}, $p$ is twice differentiable and therefore continuous, and further satisfies $p(q_0) \le \epsilon$.
    So we can find $q' \in (q_0,1)$ such that $p(q') = 2\epsilon$, and define $\tilde p \in \incr([q_0,1];[0,1])$ by
    \[
        \tilde p(t) = \begin{cases}
            2\epsilon (t - q_0) / (q' - q_0) & t \in [q_0,q')\,, \\
            p(t) & t \in [q',1]\,.
        \end{cases}
    \]
    In particular $\tilde p(q_0) = 0$, so $\tilde p$ satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.5withzero}, as required for the $\sxii$ class.
    Since $p$ and $\tilde p$ agree on $[q',1]$, we have
    \[
        \|p'-\tilde p'\|_1
        = \int_{q_0}^{q'} |p'(t) - \tilde p'(t)|\,dt
        \le \int_{q_0}^{q'} (p'(t) + \tilde p'(t))\,dt
        \le p(q') + \tilde p(q')
        = 4\epsilon\,.
    \]
Recalling Definition~\ref{d:X.adm}, we have $\mu \in \cM(q_0;p,f)$ for budget function
$f(t) = (\E w_t)^2 / \alpha$. Applying
    Proposition~\ref{p:continuity.in.p} gives the existence of a measure
    \[
        \tilde\mu \in \cM(q_0;\tilde p,f)
        \subseteq \cM^{\sxii}(\alpha,q_0)
    \]
    with $\bbW_2(\mu,\tilde \mu)^2 \le 6(1+1/\alpha) \cdot 4\epsilon$.
    Since this holds for all $\mu \in \cM^{\sx}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)$ with $\epsilon < 1/2$, we conclude
    \[
        \cM^{\sx}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon) \subseteq \cB_{\tilde\epsilon}\Big(\cM^{\sxii}(\alpha,q_0)\Big)
    \]
    for some $\tilde\epsilon$ tending to $0$ with $\epsilon$.
    By adjusting $\tilde\epsilon$ we can also ensure
    \[
        \cB_{\epsilon}\Big(\cM^{\sx}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)\Big) \subseteq \cB_{\tilde\epsilon}\Big(\cM^{\sxii}(\alpha,q_0)\Big)\,.
    \]
 Recall \eqref{e:measure.classes.simplification.without.L0}: taking a union over $L$ and an intersection over $\epsilon$ proves the first assertion, $\sM^{\sx}(\alpha,q_0) \subseteq \sM^{\sxii}(\alpha,q_0)$.

    The proof of the second assertion $\sM^{\six}(\alpha,q_0) \subseteq \sM^{\sidealast}(\alpha,q_0)$ is very similar, so we only describe the differences.
    Consider any $\mu \in \cM^{\six}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)$ where $\epsilon < 1/2$, realized by controls $(q_*=q_0,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta = \delta_0,\zeta^\Ising) \in \Adm^{\six}(\alpha,q_0;L,\epsilon)$.
    In this case $p$ satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.1concave}, so $p$ is concave in addition to the properties of condition~\ref{it:3.1} used above.
    Let $q'$ and $\tilde p$ be defined as above.
    Since $p(q_0) \ge 0$ and $p(q') = 2\epsilon$, the concavity of $p$ implies $p(t) \ge \tilde p(t)$ for all $t\in [0,q']$.
    Thus $\tilde p$ is also concave, and in particular satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.3}, as required for the $\sidealast$ class.
Then, arguing identically as above completes the proof.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 16 (Conditional occupation after a small-$r$ boundary hit) of arXiv:2607.19752, 'Weak Equilibrium Measures and Capacity--Hitting Identities\\ for the Hypoelliptic Third-Or'] Let $\Sigma\in\{\partial A,\partial B,\partial\calD\}$ and let
$\tau=\tau_\Sigma$.  There exist constants $c,q,C>0$ such that, for all
sufficiently small $b\in(0,1)$, on the event
$\{\tau<\infty,\ |r_\tau|\le b\}$,
\[
    \Pbb_z\left(
    Z_{\tau+s}\in
    \{y:\dist(y,\Sigma)\le Cb^2,\ |r(y)|\le2b\}
    \text{ for all }0\le s\le cb^2
    \middle|\mathcal F_\tau
    \right)\ge q .
\]
On the same event one may also require
\[
    \sup_{0\le s\le cb^2}
    \left(|p_{\tau+s}-p_\tau|+|\theta_{\tau+s}-\theta_\tau|\right)
    \le Cb^2 .
\]
For the regularized process, the same statement holds uniformly whenever
$0<\delta\le b^2$.  The constants are common to the three boundary components,
the forward and adjoint processes, the hitting point, and
$0\le\delta\le b^2$.

body:
[Theorem of arXiv:2411.19433, 'Singular mean-field backward stochastic Volterra integral equations in infinite dimensiona'] Assume condition \((A_{1})\) holds. Then for any \(\Psi(\cdot) \in L^2_{\mathcal{F}_T}(0, b; H)\), equation (equation r3 of the paper) has a unique adapted \(M\)-solution within \(H^2[0, b]\). Additionally, the subsequent bound is satisfied:

\[
\mathbb{E} \left\{ \int_0^b |X(t)|_H^2 \, dt + \int_0^b \int_0^b |\aleph(t,s)|_{L^2_0}^2 \, ds \, dt \right\} \leq C \mathbb{E} \int_0^b |\Psi(t)|_H^2 \, dt.
\]

Assume $\bar{F}$ also meets condition $(A_{1})$, and let $\bar{\Psi}(\cdot) \in L^2_{\mathcal{F}_{b}}(0, b; H)$. If \((\bar{Y}(\cdot), \bar{\aleph}(\cdot, \cdot)) \in H^2[0, b]\) represents the adapted \(M\)-solution of (equation r3 of the paper) with \(F\) and \(\Psi(\cdot)\) replaced by \(\bar{F}\) and \(\bar{\Psi}(\cdot)\), respectively, then the subsequent stability estimate is valid:

\begin{align*}
&\quad\mathbb{E} \left\{ \int_0^b |X(t) - \bar{X}(t)|_H^2 \, dt + \int_0^b \int_0^b |\aleph(t,s) - \bar{\aleph}(t,s)|_{L^2_0}^2 \, ds \, dt \right\} \\
&\leq C \bigg\{ \mathbb{E} \int_0^b |\Psi(t) - \bar{\Psi}(t)|_H^2 \, dt \\
& + \mathbb{E} \int_0^b \int_t^b |P(t,s, \bar{X}(s), \bar{\aleph}(t,s), \bar{\aleph}(s,t), \mathbb{E}\bar{X}(s), \mathbb{E}\bar{\aleph}(t,s), \mathbb{E}\bar{\aleph}(s,t)) \\
& - \bar{F}(t,s, \bar{X}(s), \bar{\aleph}(t,s), \bar{\aleph}(s,t), \mathbb{E}\bar{X}(s), \mathbb{E}\bar{\aleph}(t,s), \mathbb{E}\bar{\aleph}(s,t))|_H^2 \, ds \, dt \bigg\}.
\end{align*}

[Corollary 9 of arXiv:2606.11068, '2606.11068'] Assume \eqref{eq:right-edge} and let \(\beta=1/\gamma\). Set
 \(v:=|2r-1|\).
 \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item If \(\E(\eta)<\infty\) and
 \[
   \Gamma(1/\gamma)v\,
   \limsup_{n\to\infty} L(n^\gamma)
   <
   \frac{1}{2\E(\eta)},
 \]
 then the frog model dies out almost surely.
 \item If \(\Pbb(\eta=0)<1\) and
 \[
   \Gamma(1/\gamma)v\,
   \liminf_{n\to\infty} L(n^\gamma)
   >
   \frac{1}{\E(\eta)},
 \]
 where \(1/\E(\eta):=0\) when \(\E(\eta)=\infty\), then the frog model survives
 with positive probability in the direction of the drift. More precisely, the
 survival occurs to the right if \(r>1/2\), and to the left if \(r<1/2\).
 \end{enumerate}

multiplicity is $\nu(1-\mu)$.

body: Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem: every bounded sequence in R^n has a convergent subsequence. Equivalently, a subset of R^n is sequentially compact exactly when it is closed and bounded. body:
[Theorem thm:main-simple of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Let $D$ be a simply-connected domain and $z_1 \neq z_2 \in D$. Let $E^{\rm simp}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}(z_1,z_2)$ denote the event that the  CLE$_4$ gasket comes $\varepsilon_1$-close to $z_1$ and $\varepsilon_2$-close to $z_2$. Then we have
$$
\lim_{\max(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)\to 0}
\varepsilon_1^{-1/8}\varepsilon_2^{-1/8}
\mathbb{P}(E^{\rm simp}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}(z_1,z_2))
=
C_1\CR(z_1,D)^{-1/8}\CR(z_2,D)^{-1/8}
\sqrt{\frac{\theta_3(q^{1/4})}{\theta_2(q^{1/4})}},
$$
where $C_1$ is an absolute constant, and the nome $q$ is uniquely determined by
$$
\exp\!\left(\pi G_D(z_1,z_2)\right)
=
\frac{\theta_3(q^{1/2})}{\theta_2(q^{1/2})}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Two-point correlations of the simple CLE$_4$

body: [Theorem 5 of arXiv:2609.00448, 'Equivariant formality and representation theory'] Let $G$ be a compact connected Lie group and $S$ a torus subgroup, and $\pi: G/S\to\text{pt}$ be the collapsing map. Denote by $A$ the subring of $K_S^*(G/S)\otimes\mathbb{Q}$ generated by $S$-equivariant line bundles $G\times_S\mathbb{C}_\mu$ where $\mu\in\mathfrak{s}^*$. Define $\mathcal{L}_S$ to be the $R(S; \mathbb{Q})$-submodule of $K_S^*(G/S)\otimes\mathbb{Q}$ generated by the odd equivariant $K$-theory classes of $G/S$ defined by the $\delta$-construction (see Definitions \ref{deltaconstruction} and \ref{equivsamelson}). Then $(G, S)$ is isotropy formal if and only if there exist $a\in A$ and $b\in\bigwedge\nolimits_{R(S; \mathbb{Q})}^{\text{rank }G-\text{rank }S}\mathcal{L}_S$ such that $\pi_*(ab)\notin I(S; \mathbb{Q})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 5 of arXiv:2609.00448

[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] Let $\mathcal B$ be a field of characteristic $0$. Let $\mathcal C$ be a $\mathcal B[H]$-module. Then the following statement are equivalent.

\medskip
{\bf (1)} The  $\mathcal B[H]$-module $\mathcal C$ is rational.

\smallskip
{\bf (2)} The monic characteristic polynomial of the $\mathcal B$-linear map $\tau:\mathcal C\rightarrow \mathcal C$ belongs to $\mathbb Q[x]$.

\smallskip
{\bf (3)} For each $i\in\llbracket1,p^s\rrbracket$, the trace of  the $\mathcal B$-linear map $\tau^i:\mathcal C\rightarrow \mathcal C$ is a rational number.

\smallskip
{\bf (4)} For each $i\in\llbracket1,p^s-1\rrbracket$, the trace of  the $\mathcal B$-linear map $\tau^i:\mathcal C\rightarrow \mathcal C$ is a rational number.

body: A function f : U -> C on an open set U in C is holomorphic if the complex derivative f'(z) = lim_{h->0} (f(z+h) - f(z))/h exists at every z in U (the limit taken over complex h). Writing f = u + iv, differentiability at z implies the Cauchy-Riemann equations u_x = v_y and u_y = -v_x; conversely continuous partials satisfying Cauchy-Riemann on U give holomorphy.

body:
[Theorem 224 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Consider the master Riemann--Hilbert problem with sources $(D_h(z))_{h = 1}^H$. In addition, choose $\boldsymbol{\kappa} \in \amsmathbb{C}$ and rational functions $(L_h(z))_{h=1}^H$ that can have poles at $z = \alpha_h,\beta_h$ and such that $L_h(z) = O(\frac{1}{z})$ as $z \rightarrow \infty$ for each $h\in[H]$.

Then there exists a unique solution $(F_h(z))_{h = 1}^H$ to the master Riemann--Hilbert problem such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\displaystyle \left(F_h(z) - \sigma_h^{-1}(z) L_h(z) - \frac{1}{2\theta_{h,h}}D_h(z)\right)_{h = 1}^H$ is tame with exponent $1$; and
\item $\displaystyle\oint_{\gamma_h} \frac{\dd z}{2\ii\pi}\,F_h(z) = \kappa_h$ for all $h\in[H]$.
\end{enumerate}
The solution is given by the formula:
\[
F_h(z) = \sum_{g = 1}^H \big(\kappa_g \mathfrak{c}^{\textnormal{1st}}_{h;g}(z) - r(\alpha_g)\mathfrak{c}_{h;g}^{\textnormal{3rd}}(z;\alpha_g) - r(\beta_g)\mathfrak{c}^{\textnormal{3rd}}_{h;g}(\z;\beta_g)\big) - \sum_{\textnormal{J} \in \{\textnormal{I},\textnormal{II},\textnormal{III}\}} \mathfrak{F}_h^{\textnormal{J}}[\boldsymbol{f}^{\textnormal{J}}](z).
\]
The $H$-tuple of functions $\boldsymbol{f}^{\textnormal{J}}$ and the constants $(r(\alpha_g),r(\beta_g))_{g = 1}^{H}$ are determined by
\[
\forall g \in [H]\qquad f_g^{\textnormal{II}}(z) = \frac{2}{\sigma_g(z)} \int_{z}^{\infty} \frac{L_g(\zeta)}{\sigma_g(\zeta)}\dd \zeta,
\]
and the (unique up to addition of a constant to $f^{\textnormal{I}}_g$) decomposition of the source
\begin{equation}

\forall g \in [H]\qquad D_g(z) = \partial_z f^{\textnormal{I}}_g(z) + \frac{r(\alpha_g)}{z - \alpha_g} + \frac{r(\beta_g)}{z -\beta_g} + \partial_z f^{\textnormal{III}}_g(z),
\end{equation}
where the function $f_g^{\textnormal{I}}(z)$ is holomorphic in a complex neighborhood of $\overline{\amsmathbb{B}}_g$ and $f^{\textnormal{III}}_g(z)$ is a rational function with possible poles at $\alpha_g,\beta_g$ and such that $f^{\textnormal{III}}_g(z) = O(\frac{1}{z})$ as $z \rightarrow \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

        \varphi_p(x):=|x|^{p-2}x,
        \qquad
        \ell_p:=p\,\mb E[B^{p-1}(1-B)] .

\begin{equation*}

        \frac{m(p)}2(|a|^p+|b|^p)
        +
        \ell_p\{\varphi_p(a)b+\varphi_p(b)a\}
        +
        K_p|ab|^{p/2}.
\end{equation*}

[Lemma 1 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mathcal Q$ be a $\delta$-ring. Then the following statements hold:
  \begin{itemize}
  \item [(i)] Let $B\in\mathcal Q$ and $\mb A\colon I\to \mathcal Q$ be a countable family such that $\mb A(i)\subset B$ for all $i\in I$. Then $\bigcup_{i\in I} \mb A(i) \in \mathcal Q$.
  \item [(ii)] $\sigma(\mathcal Q) = \sigma_0(\mathcal{Q})$.
  \item [(iii)] If $A\in \sigma(\mathcal Q)$ and $A\subset B$ for some $B\in \mathcal Q$, then $A\in \mathcal Q$.
  \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 43 (Simultaneous finite compression of the four flattenings) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $2\le r<\infty$ and suppose that the four flattenings of $\mathbf H$
belong to $\Sch_r$.  Let
$P_{\mathcal A}^{(m)},P_{\mathcal C_1}^{(m)},
 P_{\mathcal C_0}^{(m)},P_{\mathcal E}^{(m)}$
be increasing finite-rank orthogonal projections converging strongly to the
identity on the corresponding Hilbert spaces, and define
\[
 \mathbf H_m(x,y,z,w)
 :=\mathbf H(P_{\mathcal A}^{(m)}x,
 P_{\mathcal C_1}^{(m)}y,
 P_{\mathcal C_0}^{(m)}z,
 P_{\mathcal E}^{(m)}w).
\]
Then the four flattenings of $\mathbf H_m$ are
\begin{align*}
 F_{1,m}&=P_{\mathcal E}^{(m)}F_1
 (P_{\mathcal A}^{(m)}\otimes P_{\mathcal C_1}^{(m)}
 \otimes P_{\mathcal C_0}^{(m)}),\\
 F_{2,m}&=P_{\mathcal C_0}^{(m)}F_2
 (P_{\mathcal A}^{(m)}\otimes P_{\mathcal C_1}^{(m)}
 \otimes P_{\mathcal E}^{(m)}),\\
 F_{3,m}&=(P_{\mathcal C_1}^{(m)}\otimes P_{\mathcal E}^{(m)})F_3
 (P_{\mathcal A}^{(m)}\otimes P_{\mathcal C_0}^{(m)}),\\
 F_{4,m}&=(P_{\mathcal A}^{(m)}\otimes P_{\mathcal E}^{(m)})F_4
 (P_{\mathcal C_1}^{(m)}\otimes P_{\mathcal C_0}^{(m)}).
\end{align*}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \|F_{\varkappa,m}-F_{\varkappa}\|_{\Sch_r}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad 1\le\varkappa\le4.
\end{equation}
The same conclusion holds for a difference of two forms.

[Prop log-concave of arXiv:2605.10908, 'On Talagrand's Convexity Conjecture'] Let $\mu=\sum\limits_{i=1}^{m} p_i \delta_{x_i}$ be a finitely supported centered probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $\nu$ be a centered  probability measure  on $\mathbb{R}^n$ absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure, and with finite first moments. Assume that $\mu\preceq_{\text{cx}}\nu$.
    Then there exists a natural bijection between the set of martingale couplings $(X,Y)$ of $\mu$ and $\nu$, and the collection $\mathcal{C}$ of tuples of nonnegative functions $(f_1,\ldots, f_m)$ (defined up to $\nu$-null sets) where the $f_{i} \colon \mathbb{R}^{n} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $$ \sum\limits_{i=1}^{m}p_if_i(x)=1,\ \mathbb{E}\left[f_i(Y)\right]=1,\ \mathbb{E} \left[Yf_i(Y)\right]=x_i.$$ 

 Moreover, we have $X\preceq_{\text{cx}}(1-\varepsilon) Y$ for some $\varepsilon>0$ if and only if there exist $(f_1^*,\ldots, f_m^*)$ in $\mathcal{C}$ such that each $f_i^*$ is of the form
 $$f_i^*(x)=\dfrac{e^{U_i+\langle V_i,x\rangle}}{\sum\limits_{j=1}^{m} p_j e^{U_j+\langle V_j,x\rangle}}$$
 for some $U_i\in \mathbb{R},\ V_i\in \mathbb{R}^n$. Note that each $f_i^*$ is log-concave. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop log-concave of arXiv:2605.10908

[Proposition 44 (The tower) of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] There are closed regular neighborhoods $V_j\subset\operatorname{int}B$ of
embedded rank-two roses $\Gamma_j$ whose petals are oriented and labeled
$a$ and $b$, a common wedge point
$x\in\bigcap_j\operatorname{int}V_j$, finite ball families
$\mathcal{U}_j=\{U_{j,\ell}\}$, and markings
$\mathfrak{m}_j:F_2\xrightarrow{\cong}\pi_1(V_j,x)$ such that for all
$j\ge1$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $V_{j+1}\Subset\operatorname{int}V_j$;
\item $\operatorname{cap}(V_j)<2^{-j}$;
\item $V_j\subset\bigcup_\ell U_{j,\ell}$ with
$\operatorname{diam}U_{j,\ell}<2^{-j}$ and
$\sum_\ell(\operatorname{diam}U_{j,\ell})^{1+1/j}<2^{-j}$;
\item $(i_j)_*\circ\mathfrak{m}_{j+1}=\mathfrak{m}_j\circ\omega$ for
$i_j:V_{j+1}\hookrightarrow V_j$;
\item $\mathfrak{m}_j(a)$ and $\mathfrak{m}_j(b)$ are represented by the
corresponding oriented petal loops of $\Gamma_j$ based at $x$;
\item there are a triangulation $\mathcal{T}_j$ of $S^n$ in which
$\Gamma_j$ is the polyhedron of a nonempty, proper, full subcomplex, the simplicial map
$f_j:|\mathcal{T}_j|\to[0,1]$ taking value $0$ on the vertices of this
subcomplex and value $1$ on all other vertices, and a number
$t_j\in(0,1)$ such that
\[
f_j^{-1}(0)=\Gamma_j,\qquad V_j=f_j^{-1}([0,t_j]),
\]
and, for every $c\in(0,1)$, $f_j^{-1}([0,c])$ is a closed regular
neighborhood of $\Gamma_j$ with
\[
\partial\bigl(f_j^{-1}([0,c])\bigr)=f_j^{-1}(c).
\]
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, for $k>j$ the inclusion $V_k\hookrightarrow V_j$
induces $\mathfrak{m}_j\circ\omega^{\,k-j}\circ\mathfrak{m}_k^{-1}$ on $\pi_1$; in
particular it is injective. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The tower

[Proposition 148 (Homeomorphism and diffeomorphism properties of $\Upsilon$) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] The change of variables map $\Upsilon(t,u,x^2,x^3) = (t,x^1,x^2,x^3)$
		is \textbf{injective} on the compact set
		$\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot]}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}$
		and satisfies: 
		\begin{align} 
		\| \Upsilon \|_{C_{\textnormal{geo}}^{3,1}\left(\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot]}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]} \right)}
		\leq C.
		\end{align}
		In particular, $\Upsilon$ is a homeomorphism from 
		$\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot]}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}$
		onto its image.
		
		Moreover, with $d_{\textnormal{geo}} \Upsilon$ denoting the Jacobian matrix of $\Upsilon$,
		we have:
		\begin{align} 
			\mydet d_{\textnormal{geo}} \Upsilon
			& = 
				  \frac{\upmu  X^1}{1 - \Yvfsmallcoeff{A} X^A} 
				\approx
				- 
				\upmu.
		\end{align}
		
		In addition, if $\ubarboot < 0$, then $\Upsilon$ is a diffeomorphism from
		$\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot]}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}$ onto its image.

body: [Prop 2 of arXiv:2411.06571, 'Moment-based approach for two erratic KPZ scaling limits'] Let $\tilde Z_{s,t}(x,y)$ be the continuous modification from Proposition (mr0 of the paper). Fix some $x,s\in \Bbb R$. Then for all $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\Bbb R)$ the process $$M_t(\phi) := (\tilde Z_{s,t}(x,\bullet),\phi)_{L^2(\Bbb R)}-\frac12 \int_s^t (\tilde Z_{s,u}(x,\bullet),\phi'')_{L^2(\Bbb R)}du,\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\; t\ge s$$ is a continuous martingale in the filtration $(\mathcal F_{s,t})_{t\ge s}$ where $\mathcal F_{s,t}:=\sigma(\tilde Z_{a,b}(x,y): s<a<b<t,x,y\in\Bbb R\}$. The quadratic variations are furthermore given by $$\langle M(\phi)\rangle_t = \int_s^t (\tilde Z_{s,u}(x,\bullet)^2 , \phi^2)_{L^2(\Bbb R)} du.$$

body: TYPEWRITER (L^p convergence does not imply almost-everywhere convergence). On [0,1] write n = 2^k + j with 0 <= j < 2^k and let f_n be the indicator of [j 2^{-k}, (j+1) 2^{-k}). Then ||f_n||_p^p = 2^{-k} -> 0, so f_n -> 0 in L^p for every p < infinity and in measure. But for every x in [0,1) and every k there is exactly one j with f_{2^k + j}(x) = 1, so f_n(x) equals 1 for infinitely many n and 0 for infinitely many n: the sequence converges at NO point. This is why one extracts an a.e. convergent subsequence rather than hoping for the full sequence. SLIDING BUMP (pointwise convergence does not imply L^1 convergence). On [0,1] let g_n = n 1_{(0, 1/n)}. Then g_n(x) -> 0 for every x in (0,1], indeed the convergence is pointwise everywhere on (0,1], yet integral g_n = 1 for every n. The mass does not disappear, it concentrates. The dominated convergence theorem excludes exactly this: no integrable g dominates all g_n, since any such g would satisfy g >= n on (0,1/n) for every n, forcing integral_{(0,1/n)} g >= 1 for all n and contradicting absolute continuity of the integral. ESCAPING MASS is the third, distinct failure and lives on infinite measure spaces: h_n = 1_{[n, n+1]} on R is uniformly bounded, converges to 0 everywhere, and has ||h_n||_1 = 1. Three different mechanisms, three different repairs: a subsequence, a dominating function, and a tightness condition. [standard; the typewriter sequence is sometimes attributed to Kolmogorov]

\begin{align*}

 \zeta \log K)=\underline n\big)
-e^{-p\,\lambda_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}\, \zeta \log K} \; u_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(\underline m)\;\nu_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(\underline n)
\right|\\
&= \sup_{\underline m\in\mathds Z^d_{+}\backslash\{{\ushort{0}}\}}\sum_{\underline n\in\mathds Z^d_{+}\backslash\{{\ushort{0}}\}}\left|P^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}_{p \zeta \log
  K}(\underline m,\underline n)
-e^{-p\,\lambda_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}\, \zeta \log K} \; u_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(\underline m)\;\nu_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(\underline n)
\right|\\
&
\le \Gamma( \zeta \log K,\,K)^{p}\;.
\end{align*}

(ii) It follows that for any $K$ large enough
$$
\sup_{\underline m\in\mathds Z^d_{+}\backslash\{{\ushort{0}}\}}\sum_{\underline n\in\mathds Z^d_{+}\backslash\{{\ushort{0}}\}}\left|{{\mathds P}}^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}_{\underline m}\big({\underline N^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}}(

\right|\le \lambda_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}\;.
$$

For complex matrices A (n by n) and B (m by m), S(X) = AX - XB on n by m matrices X, and the Frobenius separation is sep_F(A, B) = min over ||X||_F = 1 of ||AX - XB||_F. If A and B are normal, sep_F(A, B) = min over lambda in spec A and mu in spec B of |lambda - mu|. Repeated eigenvalues within A or within B are allowed; only overlap between the two spectra makes the separation vanish.
A is n by n and B is m by m, complex

[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2606.31455, 'Discrete time-multidimensional renewal theory and applications'] The renewal function $M$ satisfies the discrete multi-time renewal equation
\begin{equation}
M = F + f*M,
\end{equation}
i.e.\ for all $k\in\mathbb{N}^d$,
\[
M(k)=F(k)+\sum_{\ell\le_d k} f(\ell)\,M(k-\ell).
\]

$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Conservation, explicit coupling reduction, exact law comparison or spectral calculation Result: For a stationary occupation field with covariance c(z), $\mathrm{Var}(S_B)=\sum_z c(z)|B\cap(B-z)|$. If $\sum_z c(z)=0$ and $\sum_z |z|_1|c(z)|<\infty$, a cube of side L satisfies $\mathrm{Var}(S_B)\le C_d L^{d-1}\sum_z|z|_1|c(z)|$. Subtract |B| times the zero sum, then bound the lost overlap by $C_d L^{d-1}\min(|z|_1,L)$. This would give the desired exponent d-1, including bounded variance when d=1. Check: Expand the variance as a double sum of covariances and count ordered pairs with displacement z. For a cube the overlap equals the product of (L-|z_i|)_+, verifying the geometric bound directly. Obstruction: Neither the infinite-volume covariance cancellation nor the weighted absolute summability is proved for ARW. Finite-torus conservation gives a zero sum at each size but does not justify interchanging that sum with the infinite-volume limit.

\]

[Proposition 23 of arXiv:2511.04938, 'Uniform dimension theorems for parabolic SPDEs'] Suppose $p \ge 4$, $\mathcal{M}(b) < \infty$, $\mathcal{M}(\sigma)<\infty$ 
	and $\inf_{v\in\R^p}\lambda(v)>0$.
	Fix $T > 0$ and $\delta \in (0\,,1)$.
	Then, there exists $L = L(p\,,\delta\,, T\,, b\,,\sigma\,, u_0) > 0$ such that
	\[
		\P\left\{\mathcal{N}^\delta_n(t\,, B(\nu\,, 2^{-n})) \ge 2^{2np\delta}\right\} 
		\le L^n n^{3pn} 2^{-\delta pn^2},
	\]
	uniformly for all $\nu \in \R^p$, $t \in (0\,, T]$ and $n \in \Z_+$ 
	such that $2^{-n} \le t/2$.
title: Proposition 23 of arXiv:2511.04938

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2605.17296, 'Zero correlations and averaged fields of orthonormal Gaussian Functions'] Fix $z_0 \in \C$ and a compact set $K \subset \C$. Then
\[
\cG_N^{(z_0)} \inlawto \cG
\qquad
\text{in } C(K),
\]
where $\cG$ is a centered real Gaussian process on $\C$ with covariance
\[
\E\bigl[\cG(\xi)\cG(\eta)\bigr] = \kappa(|\xi-\eta|).
\]
The limit covariance is the normalized overlap area of two unit
disks,
\[
\kappa(r) := \frac{|B(0,1)\cap B(r,1)|}{\pi},
\qquad
r\ge 0,
\]
where $B(z, \rho)$ is the disk of radius $\rho \ge 0$
centered at $z \in \C$. Equivalently,
\[
\kappa(r)=
\begin{cases}
\disp \frac{2}{\pi}\arccos \frac{r}{2}
-
\frac{r}{\pi}\sqrt{1-\frac{r^2}{4}},
&
0\le r\le 2,
\\[1ex]
0,
&
r\ge 2.
\end{cases}
\]
Moreover, for every $0<\alpha<\frac{1}{2}$, the family
$\{\cG_N^{(z_0)}\}_{N\ge 1}$ is tight in $C^{0,\alpha}(K)$, and $\cG$ admits a
version with sample paths in $C^{0,\alpha}(K)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 4 of arXiv:2605.17296

[Definition maindefi of arXiv:2412.06701, 'Matsumoto-Yor processes on Jordan algebras'] Let $(w_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a sequence of i.i.d. random variables on $E_+$ distributed according to $\mathrm{GIG}_{E_+}\left( p ; e, e \right)$. 

Let on the one hand, $L := (L_n \ ; \ n\ge 0)$ be the Markov chain defined by 
$$L_{n+1}=\mathrm{P}(w_{n+1})(L_n)+w_{n+1}, \, n\ge 0,$$
and $L_0=0$. 

On the other hand, the random process $\Lambda := (\Lambda_n \ ; \ n\ge 1)$ is defined by
$$ \Lambda_{n+1}=\mathrm{P}(w_{n+1}+L_n^{-1})(\Lambda_{n}), \, n\ge 1, $$
and $\Lambda_1=e$.
title: Definition maindefi of arXiv:2412.06701

[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2609.00680, 'Sharp embeddings between quasi-Banach Besov spaces and shallow ReLU Variation spaces'] Let $0<p,q\leq\infty$ and $s>0$, with the convention $d/\infty=0$.
There exist $x_0\in\Omega$ and
$\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ such that, for all sufficiently small
$h>0$, define
\[
\psi_h(x):=\psi\left(\frac{x-x_0}{h}\right).
\]
The following two-sided estimates hold:
\begin{equation}
\|\psi_h\|_{B_{p,q}^s(\mathbb R^d)}\simeq h^{d/p-s},\qquad
\|\psi_h\|_{\mathcal L_1(\D)}\simeq h^{-k}.
\end{equation}

[Proposition 3 (\cite{Li}) of arXiv:2605.15781, 'Mean-Field Backward Stochastic Differential Equations with Nonlinear Resistance and Double'] Suppose that $(l^i,r^i)$ satisfy Assumption $\ref{asslr}$, $i=1,2$.
Given  $s^i\in C[0,T]$, let $(x^i,K^i)$ be the solution to the Skorokhod problem $\mathbb{SP}_{l^i}^{r^i}(s^i)$. Then, we have

[Definition Convexity gap of arXiv:2606.27073, 'Retention Profiles and KL Contraction Bounds in Finite Markov Chains'] For a distribution $\mu$ on $S$, define
\[
  \Delta(\mu)
  := \sum_{x\in S}\mu(x)\,D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P(x,\cdot)\|\pi)
     - D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu P\|\pi).
\]
By the convexity of $\nu\mapstoD_{\mathrm{KL}}(\nu\|\pi)$ (Jensen's inequality),
$\Delta(\mu)\ge 0$.
title: Convexity gap

[Theorem thm:multiclass-destruction of arXiv:2608.20480, 'When Clean Data Hurts: Learning with Monotone \\ Corruptions Beyond Binary Classification'] There are countable discrete spaces $\mathcal{X},\mathcal{Y}$ and a countable class
$\mathcal{H}\subseteq\mathcal{Y}^{\mathcal{X}}$ with $d_{\mathrm{DS}}(\mathcal{H})=2$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2em]
    \item A deterministic proper learner satisfies, for every clean sample
    size $N\ge2$,
    \[
        \Pr[L_D(\widehat h,h^\star)>\varepsilon]
        \le
        N^2e^{-\varepsilon(N-2)}.
    \]
    In particular, $\mathcal{H}$ is properly PAC learnable from clean i.i.d.\ data
    with sample complexity
    $O((\log(1/\varepsilon)+\log(1/\delta))/\varepsilon)$.

    \item For every $n\ge1$ and every learner $A_n$, permitted to be
    randomized and/or improper, there are a target $h^\star\in\mathcal{H}$, a
    finitely supported marginal $D$, and a deterministic adaptive monotone
    adversary adding exactly $n$ examples such that
    \[
        \mathbb{E} L_D(A_n(T),h^\star)\ge\frac14,
        \qquad
        \Pr\!\left[
            L_D(A_n(T),h^\star)>\frac18
        \right]
        \ge
        \frac17.
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:multiclass-destruction of arXiv:2608.20480

[Theorem thm:dependency_encoding of arXiv:2604.18558, 'Uniform analyticity of local observables in FK-percolation and analyticity of the Ising sp'] Let $(d,p,q) \in \mathcal G_{\mathsf{FK}}$. 
Then there exists $L_0 > 0$ such that for any $L \geq L_0$, there exists a probability measure $\mathbb P$ on $  \{0,1\}^{E(\mathbb T_N)} \times (\mathsf{P}^L_N)^{\mathbb T_N^L}$ satisfying the following properties.
When $(\omega, (\mathcal C_x)_{x \in \mathbb T_N^L})  \sim \mathbb P$, then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\omega$ is distributed according to $\phi_{\mathbb T_N,p}$.
\item For any $x\in\mathbb T_N^L$, $\mathcal C_x$ contains $x$. 
\item For any $\Delta_1, \Delta_2 \subset \mathbb T_N^L$, any $F,G$ functions of $\omega$ supported on $\Delta_1$ and $\Delta_2$ respectively and any $C_1 \supset \Delta_1, C_2 \supset \Delta_2$ such that $C_1 \cap C_2 = \emptyset$, then
\[
\mathbb P[F(\omega)G(\omega) \ind{\mathcal C_{\Delta_1} = C_1} \ind{\mathcal C_{\Delta_2 = C_2}} ] = \mathbb P[F(\omega)\ind{\mathcal C_{\Delta_1} = C_1} ] \mathbb P[G(\omega)\ind{\mathcal C_{\Delta_2 = C_2}} ],
\]
where we call $\mathcal C_\Delta \coloneqq  \bigcup_{x\in\Delta}\mathcal C_x$. 
\item There exist two sequences $\tilde c_L, c_L > 0$ going to infinity when $L$ goes to infinity such that, for any $x \in \mathbb T_N^L$ and any $n \in \mathbb Z_{> 0}$, 
\[  \mathbb P[|\mathcal C_x| \geq n] \leq \tilde c_L\exp(-c_L n). \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] For every $i$ choose a collar neighbourhood $T_i \times [0, 1]$ as above, and define $\iota_i$. By choosing small enough neighbourhoods, we can assume that they are pairwise disjoint, and then the elements in the images of different $\iota_i$ maps will commute with each other. Hence we obtain a map $\sum_i \iota_i \colon \bigoplus_i \pi_1 \Diff^+(T_i) \rightarrow \pi_0 \overline{\Diff}^+(M,(B_h),(T_i),(M_j))$. It follows from Lemma (lem:iota-properties of the paper) (b) that $\Image(\sum_i \iota_i)$ is a normal subgroup. We will denote the cokernel of $\sum_i \iota_i$ by
\[
\pi_0 \overline{\Diff}^+(M,(B_h),(T_i),(M_j)) \Big/ \bigoplus_i \pi_1 \Diff^+(T_i).
\]

body: In statistics, Gibbs sampling or a Gibbs sampler, also known in statistical mechanics as the heat bath algorithm, is a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm for sampling from a specified multivariate probability distribution when direct sampling from the joint distribution is difficult, but sampling from the conditional distribution is more practical. This sequence can be used to approximate the joint distribution ; to approximate the marginal distribution of one of the variables, or some subset of the variables ; or to compute an integral. Typically, some of the variables correspond to observations whose values are known, and hence do not need to be sampled.
title: Gibbs sampling

Let G be a finite undirected loopless multigraph on n vertices with positive edge weights w_e, L its weighted Laplacian, and t > 0. A spanning rooted forest is a spanning forest with one chosen root in each tree; its weight is t^|E(F)| prod_{e in F} w_e (so an unrooted forest with trees T_1, ..., T_k counts prod |T_i| times). Z(t) is the total weight of spanning rooted forests, and Q_t = (I + tL)^-1. Draw a spanning rooted forest with probability proportional to its weight. Then tr Q_t is the expected number of trees, and t (d/dt) log Z(t) is the expected number of edges, which equals n - tr Q_t.

body:
Let X be a normed space with dual X* carrying the weak-star topology sigma(X*, X). Then the closed unit ball B of X* is metrizable in the relative weak-star topology if and only if X is separable; in that case every bounded subset of X* is weak-star metrizable, and a compatible metric is d(f,g) = sum over n of 2^(-n) min(1, |f(x_n) - g(x_n)|) for any dense sequence (x_n) of the unit sphere of X. Combined with Banach-Alaoglu (B is weak-star compact), separability of X gives that B is weak-star compact and metrizable, hence weak-star SEQUENTIALLY compact: every bounded sequence in X* has a weak-star convergent subsequence. The dual statement also holds: for a Banach space X, the closed unit ball of X is metrizable in the weak topology sigma(X, X*) if and only if X* is separable. WHERE IT FAILS: (a) 'bounded' is essential - the weak-star topology on ALL of X* is metrizable only when X is finite dimensional; indeed if it were metrizable with countable base (U_m) at 0 and X is infinite dimensional, each U_m contains a nonzero subspace (it is cut out by finitely many functionals), so one can pick f_m in U_m with ||f_m|| >= m, and then f_m converges weak-star to 0 while being unbounded, contradicting the uniform boundedness principle; (b) the two directions are not interchangeable - separability of X does not imply separability of X*: X = l^1 is separable, so B of (l^1)* = l^infinity is weak-star metrizable, but (l^1)* = l^infinity is not separable, so the unit ball of l^1 is NOT weakly metrizable; (c) the metric above is not translation-invariantly compatible on the whole of X* and the equivalence is genuinely a statement about the relative topology on bounded sets; (d) for X = l^infinity, which is not separable, the unit ball of (l^infinity)* is weak-star compact but not weak-star metrizable, and weak-star compactness there is not sequential compactness.
X is a normed space (Banach for the uniform boundedness step in the failure remark and for the dual statement)
X* is the topological dual with the weak-star topology sigma(X*, X)
B is the closed unit ball of X*, or any bounded weak-star closed subset - the equivalence concerns bounded sets only
for the dual statement (weak metrizability of the ball of X iff X* separable), X is Banach

[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2605.06556, 'Probability of Quota Violations in Divisor Apportionment Methods with Nonzero Allocations'] \parencite{Self} \textit{(Lower Quota Violation Criteria Test)} Let $A$ be Adams's, Dean's, or the Huntington-Hill method, with divisor function $\delta(s)$. Order the populations such that $p_1 <p_2 < p_3$ and calculate the standard quotas $q_i$. Then the apportionment $A(p_1, p_2, p_3)$ on $M$ seats has a lower quota violation if and only if all three of the following statements are true: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $q_3 \delta(\lfloor q_1 \rfloor) < q_1 \delta( \lfloor q_3 \rfloor - 1)$
\item $q_3 \delta(\lfloor q_2 \rfloor) < q_2 \delta( \lfloor q_3 \rfloor - 1)$
\item $\lceil q_1 \rceil + \lceil q_2 \rceil + \lfloor q_3 \rfloor = M+1 $ (equivalently for $q_1, q_2 \notin \mathbb{Z}$, $\lfloor q_1 \rfloor + \lfloor q_2 \rfloor + \lfloor q_3 \rfloor = M-1) $.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own work draft; proof (unaudited), initialization-only special case, no novelty claim. For distinct parity subsets S_t of uniform d-dimensional Rademacher skill inputs and one-hot task controls, use f(e_t,x)=m^(-1/2)*sum_j a_j ReLU(w_j dot x+v_jt+b_j). Initialize all a_j=0 and all hidden data weights, control weights and biases independently N(0,sigma^2), sigma>0. For conditional half squared losses with labels product_{l in S_t} x_l, let g_t be the full parameter gradient. Then for t!=u, E_init<g_t,g_u>=0 and E_init|<g_t,g_u>|^2<=3*(d+2)^2*sigma^4/(2*m). A union bound gives failure probability at most binom(n,2)*3*(d+2)^2*sigma^4/(2*m*epsilon^2) for any cross-gradient magnitude exceeding epsilon. This is not a trained-trajectory or nonzero-output-initialization theorem.

[Theorem thm:duality of arXiv:2602.19192, 'Bakry--\'Emery Curvature of the Fractional Laplacian\\ via Fractional Brownian Covariance'] For $\gamma \in (0,2)$ and all $\xi, \eta \in \mathbb{R}$ with
$\xi\eta \geq 0$ (same-sign frequencies):
\begin{equation}
  \Psi_\gamma(\xi,\eta)
  = \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(|\xi|^\gamma + |\eta|^\gamma
  - |\xi - \eta|^\gamma\bigr)
  = R_{\gamma/2}(|\xi|, |\eta|).
\end{equation}
The carr\'e du champ of the $\gamma$-stable generator, evaluated
on same-sign Fourier modes, is the covariance of fBM with $H = \gamma/2$.

For opposite-sign frequencies ($\xi\eta < 0$), the carr\'e du champ
$\Psi_\gamma(\xi,\eta) = \frac{1}{2}(|\xi|^\gamma + |\eta|^\gamma
- |\xi-\eta|^\gamma)$ differs from $R_{\gamma/2}(|\xi|,|\eta|)
= \frac{1}{2}(|\xi|^\gamma + |\eta|^\gamma - \bigl||\xi|-|\eta|\bigr|^\gamma)$
since $|\xi - \eta| \neq \bigl||\xi|-|\eta|\bigr|$ when $\xi\eta < 0$.
The cross-sign kernel is treated separately in
Section~(sec:cross-sign of the paper).

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2609.01574, 'A linear bound for Fujita's freeness conjecture'] Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety of dimension $n$, let $\Delta\geq0$ be a $\mathbb Q$-divisor, and let $x\in X$ be a closed point. Assume that $(X,\Delta)$ is log canonical near $x$ and is not klt at $x$. Let $W$ be the positive-dimensional minimal lc center through $x$, then 
$$
2\ebarone(\m_{W,x})\leq\bigl(\dim W-b_x(X,\Delta)\bigr)\mult_xW,
$$
where $\ebarone(\m_{W,x})$ is the first normal Hilbert coefficient of the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{W,x}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 5 of arXiv:2609.01574

[Definition 5 of arXiv:2606.02036, 'Self-intersection local times for Volterra Gaussian processes in stochastic flows with int'] A centred Gaussian process $\{u(t) : t\in[0,1]\}$ is called a Volterra Gaussian process, if  it admits the representation

u(t) =

$ for each $t\in(0,1]$,

$

$

body: A probability distribution \mu with characteristic function \phi is said to be self-decomposable (or belonging to Lévy's class L) if for every c \in (0, 1), there exists a characteristic function \phi_c such that \phi(t) = \phi(ct) \phi_c(t) for all t \in \mathbb{R}. Class L distributions coincide with the class of all limit distributions of normalized sums \frac{1}{a_n} \sum_{k=1}^n X_k - b_n of independent (not necessarily identically distributed) random variables under the infinitesimal condition.
title: Self-Decomposable Distribution (Class L)

[Corollary cor:rho-intro of arXiv:2605.03703, 'Scaling Limits of Bivariate Nearly-Unstable Hawkes Processes and Applications to Rough Vol'] Under the assumptions of Theorem~(thm:main-intro of the paper) and in the
zero-start scaling regime,
the functional correlation satisfies
\[
\varrho(t)\sim C_\varrho\,t^{(3\alpha_1-\alpha_2)/2},
\qquad t\downarrow0.
\]
Since $\alpha_1>1/2$ and $\alpha_2<1$, the exponent is strictly positive.
In the homogeneous case $\alpha_1=\alpha_2$, it reduces to $\alpha_1$.
In particular $\varrho(t)\to 0$ as $t\downarrow 0$: the two components are decorrelated
at short time scales.
The explicit constant $C_\varrho$ and its proof are in Corollary~(cor:rho of the paper).
A stationary comparison, where the mean profiles are locally constant near
zero, gives the exponent $\alpha_1$; this is not the zero-start regime used
in the main theorem. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Short-time decorrelation, informal preview

body:
[Lem 149 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Fix $(b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta,\zeta^\Ising)$ satisfying the conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}\ref{i:IAMP-main-centered}. 
Fix any vectors $\bx^{\dagger,0},\prxbx^{\dagger,0}\in\bbR^M$, and let $\tilde{\cA}^\dagger$ be the centered IAMP specified by Definition~\ref{d:centered.iamp}. 
Then, for $C\equiv C(L,\epsilon,\delta)$, 
there exists a $C$-Lipschitz map $\cA^\dagger$ which agrees
with $\tilde{\cA}^\dagger$ with probability $1-\exp(-cN)$, and satisfies
	    \[
    \cA(-\bG,-\bg^\aux)
    =
    -\cA(\bG,\bg^\aux)\,.
    \]
In particular, it follows that $\bbE[\cA(\bG,\bg^{\aux})~|~\bx^{\dagger,0},\prxbx^{\dagger,0}]=\bzero\in\bbR^N$.
\begin{proof}
    Let $(\hat\by^{\dagger,k},\hat\prxby^{\dagger,k},\hat\bx^{\dagger,k},\hat\prxbx^{\dagger,k})$ be the IAMP iterates corresponding to $(-\bG,- \bg^{\aux})$.
    We claim that for all $0\leq k\leq \ubl$ we have
    \begin{align*}
    (\hat\prxby,\hat\by,\hat\bu,\hat\bw)^{\dagger,k}
    &=
    (-\prxby,-\by,-\bu,\bw)^{\dagger,k}
      \,\\
    (\hat\prxbx,\hat\bx,\hat\bv,
    \hat\bm,\hat\bsig,\hat\bb)^{\dagger,k}
    &=
    (\prxbx,\bx,\bv,
    \bm,\bsig,\bb)^{\dagger,k}\,.
    \end{align*}
Indeed, the base case for the first statement above holds easily since
$w$ is even by the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main} \eqref{i:IAMP-main-centered}, the functions
 $\psi$ and $\prxpsi$ are odd (Lemma~\ref{lem:even-manual-init}), 
the vectors $(\by,\prxby,\hat{\by},\hat{\prxby})^{\dagger,0}$ are defined by \eqref{eq:mean-0-initialization},  and  we defined $\bu^{\dagger,0}=\hat{\bu}^{\dagger,0}=\bzero\in\R^M$.
The remaining statements follow by 
induction, using the formulas \eqref{eq:proxy-y-amp-def}--\eqref{eq:x-amp-def}. 

The above shows the desired symmetry for the mapping $\tilde{\cA}^\dagger$, and we must now transfer it to $\cA^\dagger$. This proceeds similarly as in the \hyperlink{proof:t.IAMP.main.main}{proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}\ref{i:IAMP-main-main}}, using the Kirzsbraun extension theorem, except that we now need to ensure that the symmetry requirement is satisfied. 
First, we have by easy induction that $\tilde{\cA}^\dagger$ is $C$-Lipschitz on a subset $\mathcal{U}^{\dagger}\subseteq \bbR^{MN+N_{\aux}}$, similarly to the \hyperlink{proof:t.IAMP.main.main}{proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}\ref{i:IAMP-main-main}}. To be precise, 
    \[\mathcal{U}^{\dagger}
    =\bigg\{
    \begin{array}{c}
    (\bG,\bg^\aux) : 
    \textup{$\bG_\circ$
    satisfies \eqref{eq:Brownian-bridge-condition},
    $\|\bG\|_\textup{op}\le C_0
    (M^{1/2}+N^{1/2})$,}\\
    \textup{$\|\bar\bg^{\ell}\|\leq 2\sqrt{N}$
    for all $0\le\ell\le\ubl$, and
    $\|\bar\bg^{\init}\|\leq 2\sqrt{N}$}
    \end{array}
    \bigg\}\,.
    \]
In particular, this choice of $\mathcal{U}^{\dagger}$ is origin-symmetric. 
(Again, see e.g.\ the discussion on ``standard optimization algorithms'' in \cite{HuangSellke2021} for the Lipschitz bound on such a domain.)

Thus, let $S=\{\bg_1,\bg_2,\dots\}$ be a countable dense set in $\bbR^{MN+N_{\aux}}$.
    For each $\bg_i$, we assume $\tilde\cA^{\dagger}$ has been extended to a $C$-Lipschitz function on $\mathcal{U}^{\dagger,i}\equiv \mathcal{U}^{\dagger}\cup \{\bg_1,-\bg_1,\dots,\bg_i,-\bg_i\}$.
    Then by the Kirzsbraun extension theorem, there exists a $C$-Lipschitz extension to $\mathcal{U}^{\dagger,i}\cup \{\bg_{i+1}\}$.
    Since 
  $\mathcal{U}^{\dagger,i}$ is symmetric,  
the unique odd extension to $\mathcal{U}^{\dagger,i+1}$ is still $C$-Lipschitz. Continuing in this way yields a $C$-Lipschitz extension to $ \mathcal{U}^\dagger\cup S\cup -S$. This set is dense by definition of $S$, so the result follows by continuously extending to all of $\R^{MN+N_{\aux}}$.

[Theorem 18 of arXiv:2605.06556, 'Probability of Quota Violations in Divisor Apportionment Methods with Nonzero Allocations'] (Asymptotic Apportionment) Let $(1,x,y_1(x,\tau_1),\ldots,y_{n-2}(x,\tau_{n-2}))$ be a reduced population vector with $\bm\tau=(\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_{n-2})$. Let $A$ be a divisor method that guarantees nonzero allocations on $M$ seats. Then for almost every $\bm\tau$ satisfying $-\tfrac13 < \tau_1 < \cdots < \tau_{n-2} < \tfrac13,$

$$\lim_{x\to\infty}A(1,x,y_1(x,\tau_1),\dots,y_{n-2}(x,\tau_{n-2}))=\tilde A_1(\tilde q_2,\dots,\tilde q_n).$$

The limiting quotas are 
$$\tilde q_2=\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{Mx}{P(x)},\qquad\tilde q_{i+2}
=\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{M y_i(x,\tau_i)}{P(x)},$$
where $P(x) = 1+x+y_1(x,\tau_1)+\cdots+y_{n-2}(x,\tau_{n-2}).$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

	iff the temperature $\Theta = \Psi^2/2$ satisfies the following for any $j\in \mathbb N$:
	\begin{enumerate}[(i)']
		\setcounter{enumi}{2}
		\item 
		For every $\eta\in C^{{\infty}}( \mathbb{T}^3)$ it holds
		\begin{align}\begin{split}
				&

[Definition 16 of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] A \textbf{Navier--Stokes triple} \((\mathscr F,\chi,\mathscr B)\) is called \textbf{admissible} provided the following \textbf{invariant-domain property} holds for each of the two associated Einstein--Navier--Stokes models 
\eqref{eq:pot-production-system} and \eqref{eq:pot-dissipated-system}, as follows. 

Let \(\{\Sigma_t\}_{t_0\leq t<t_1}\) be a spacelike foliation of a compact spacetime slab, and let \((g,\beta,\zeta)\) be a regular solution of the corresponding hyperbolic evolution-constraint system\footnote{A gauge must be chosen to deal with the spacetime metric and formulate a well-posed initial value problem; this is a standard topic, not reviewed here \cite{Choquet-book}.} on \([t_0,t_1)\). Assume that
\be
\zeta(t_0,\Sigma_{t_0})\subset\mathcal K_0
\qquad\text{for some closed fiber subset }\mathcal K_0\Subset\mathscr F.
\ee
Then one has
\be
\zeta(t,\Sigma_t)\subset\mathscr F
\qquad\text{for every }t_0\leq t<t_1.
\ee
Moreover, if the fields admit a continuous limit in the ambient bundles as \(t\uparrow t_1\), while the nonsingular coefficients in the equation for~\(\zeta\) remain bounded, then the terminal relaxing field satisfies
\be
\zeta(t_1,\Sigma_{t_1})\subset\mathscr F,
\ee
rather than merely taking its values in~\(\overline{\mathscr F}\). Equivalently, the constitutive boundary~\(\del\mathscr F\) cannot be the first cause of breakdown of a regular solution.

[Theorem 3 (Ruelle) of arXiv:2605.29030, 'Preferential relocations enhance survival \\ for Markov chains with killing'] Suppose that the defective kernel $\kk\in \mathcal{H}_{>0}(\S)$. Then there exist a unique probability measure $\boldsymbol{\mu}\in \calP(\S)$ --often called the quasi-stationary distribution-- and a unique functional
$\mathbf{h}\in \mathcal{H}_{>0}(\S)$  such that
\[\Kk \mathbf{h}= \mathbf{r}  \mathbf{h}, \quad \Kk^{*} \boldsymbol{\mu}= \mathbf{r}  \boldsymbol{\mu}, \quad \text{and} \quad \int_{\S}\boldsymbol{\mu}(\d \s) \mathbf{h}(\s)=1.
\]
Moreover, for any $\mathbf{f}\in \calC(\S)$, there is the convergence in $\calC(\S)$
\[ \lim_{n\to \infty} \mathbf{r}^{-n}\Kk^n \mathbf{f} =   \boldsymbol{\mu}( \mathbf{f}) \mathbf{h} , \qquad \text{where} \  \boldsymbol{\mu}( \mathbf{f})=\int_{\S}\boldsymbol{\mu}(\d \s) \mathbf{f}(\s).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Prop cor:explicitcondforXe of arXiv:2605.06488, 'Continuous-state branching processes with L\'evy-Khintchine drift-interaction: Laplace dua'] Let $\Psi$ and $\hat{\Psi}$ be mechanisms, and denote by $\pi$ the L\'evy measure associated with $\Psi$. Assume that $\hat{\Psi} = \hat{\Sigma} - \hat{\Phi}$ with $\hat{\Sigma} \not\equiv 0$. Then the following statements hold:
\begin{enumerate}[1)]
\item Assume $\Hone$ and $\hatHone$. Then the process $X^{\mathrm{m}}$ admits a $[0,\infty]$-valued Feller extension at $\infty$, denoted by $X^{\mathrm{e}\infty}$, which satisfies (equation def:Xeinftyviamonotonicity of the paper) and the $(0^{+}\cdot \infty, \infty^-\cdot 0)$ Laplace duality relation (equation eq:laplaceduality1 of the paper). Moreover, $0$ is absorbing for $X^{\mathrm{e}\infty}$, and $\infty$ is inaccessible for $Y^{\mathrm{m}}$.

\item If $\hat{\Phi}'(0+) \in (0,\infty)$ (which in particular implies $\hatHone$) and
\begin{equation}
\exists \,\kappa \in (0,\infty) \text{ such that } \int_{\kappa}^{\infty} \frac{1 + u \bar{\pi}(u)}{\hat{\Psi}(u)} \mathrm{d}u < \infty,
\end{equation}
then the extension $X^{\mathrm{e}\infty}$ exists and satisfies all the properties listed in (1). Moreover, $\infty$ is an instantaneous entrance boundary and $0$ is accessible for $Y^{\mathrm{m}}$.
\item If $\hat{\Phi}'(0+) \in (0,\infty)$, $\Phi'(0+) \in [0,\infty)$, and $\neg \hatHtwo$, that is,
$\int_1^{\infty} \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\hat{\Sigma}(u)} < \infty$,
then (equation eq:JI of the paper) holds. Consequently, the extension $X^{\mathrm{e}\infty}$ exists and satisfies all the properties listed in (1) and (2).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop cor:explicitcondforXe of arXiv:2605.06488

[Cor 83 of arXiv:2509.01797, 'Relation between Wick powers and excursion clusters of the 2D GFF'] Let $j\geq 0$.
Let $n\geq 1$
and let $\alpha_{n}>\alpha_{n-1}>\dots >\alpha_{1}>\alpha_{0}=1$.
Let $(c_{0}, c_{1}, \dots, c_{n})$
be the unique solution to the linear system
\begin{displaymath}
\forall k\in \{0,\dots, n-1\},
\sum_{i=0}^{n} c_{i} \alpha_{i}^{-(k+1/2)} = 0,
\qquad
\sum_{i=0}^{n} c_{i} \alpha_{i}^{-(n+1/2)} = 1.
\end{displaymath}
Then
\begin{displaymath}
\psi_{2n+1, j} = \lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} (-1)^{n}\dfrac{2^{n} n! (n+1/2)}{(2\pi)^{n}}\vert\log\varepsilon\vert^{n+1/2}
\sum_{i=0}^{n} c_{i} \ind_{\Ns_{\varepsilon^{\alpha_{i}}}(\clus_j)},
\end{displaymath}
with convergence in $L^{2}(d\PP,\sigma(\Phi),H^{-\eta}(\C))$ for $\eta>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor 83 of arXiv:2509.01797

[Lemma 9 (Descent closure) of arXiv:2609.01882, '\textbf{Coxeter Descents and Parabolic Homotopy Colimits}\\[2mm] \large A Hochster-type de'] If $L_{\mathcal K,D}\ne\varnothing$, the map
\[
  c_D:Q_{\mathcal K,D}\longrightarrow Q_{\mathcal K,D},
  \qquad c_D(I)=I\cap D,
\]
is a descending closure operator. Its image is the poset of nonempty faces of $\mathcal K_D$. Consequently
\[
  L_{\mathcal K,D}\searrow \sd\mathcal K_D
\]
by a sequence of unit simplicial collapses.

body: [Lem enoughholo of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $\mathcal{F}$ be as in the setup of \zcref{def:enoughholo}. Moreover, assume that $\mathcal{F}$ is not semi-conjugate to an irrational foliation on $\mathbb{T}^2 \times I$. Then $\mathcal{F}$ can be $C^0$-approximated by $C^0$-foliations with enough holonomy, and whose boundary foliations are monotone-equivalent to $\partial \mathcal{F}$.

body:
[Theorem 14 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Consider an off-critical ensemble \eqref{eq_measure_general_intro} with fixed filling fractions. There exists functions $\mathcal{F}_{h_1,h_2}(z_1,z_2)$ indexed by $h_1,h_2 \in [H]$ depending only on $\boldsymbol{\Theta}$ and the endpoints of the bands, and having the following properties. First $\mathcal{F}_{h_1,h_2}(z_1,z_2) = \mathcal{F}_{h_2,h_1}(z_2,z_1)$. Second, for any $h_1,h_2 \in [H]$, any $x_1$ in bands of $[\hat{a}_{h_1},\hat{b}_{h_1}]$ and $z_2$ away from bands, we have
\[
\theta_{h_1,h_1}\big(\mathcal{F}_{h_1,h_2}(x_1^+,z_2) + \mathcal{F}_{h_1,h_2}(x_1^-,z_2)\big) + \sum_{g \neq h_1} 2\theta_{h_1,g}\,\mathcal{F}_{g,h_2}(x_1,z_2) = - \frac{\delta_{h_1,h_2}}{(x_1 - z_2)^2}.
\]
Third, for an analytic function $f$ near the bands, we have as $\N \rightarrow \infty$
\[
\amsmathbb{E}\big[(\Delta\textnormal{\textsf{Lin}}[f])^2\big] = \sum_{h_1,h_2 = 1}^{H} \oint_{\gamma_{h_1}}\oint_{\gamma_{h_2}} \frac{\dd z_1 \dd z_2}{(2\ii\pi)^2} \,\mathcal{F}_{h_1,h_2}(z_1,z_2)\,f(z_1)f(z_2) + o(1).
\]
where the contour $\gamma_h$ surrounds the $h$-th band. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 14 of arXiv:2601.16377

body:
[Lemma 20 (Time extension, causality, and restricted operator norms) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $0<T\le T_0$.  There is a bounded linear extension
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak E_{T,T_0}:E_T^{2,\sigma}\longrightarrow E_{T_0}^{2,\sigma},
 \qquad
 \mathfrak R_T\mathfrak E_{T,T_0}=I,
\end{equation}
whose norm is bounded by an absolute constant independently of $T$ and $T_0$.
The analogous assertion holds after translating the interval.

Call an operator $\mathcal A$ on $E_{T_0}^{2,\sigma}$ causal if inputs that
agree on $[0,t]$ have outputs that agree on $[0,t]$, for every $t\le T_0$.
For a causal operator, define
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal A_{[0,T]}:=\mathfrak R_T\mathcal A\mathfrak E_{T,T_0}.
\end{equation}
This restriction is independent of the chosen bounded extension.  More
generally, if $I=[t_0,t_1]$ and $w\in E_{I,0}^{2,\sigma}$, extend $w$ by zero on
$[0,t_0]$ and by any bounded extension after $t_1$; the restriction of
$\mathcal A$ to $I$ is again independent of the extension after $t_1$.  We
denote this zero-history operator by $\mathcal A_I$.

 \mathcal L_{\mathrm{mode}}(S_W,T)
 <\mathcal L_{\mathrm{mode}}(S_G,T),
 \qquad
 \sum_i\Phi_V(\chi_i^W)
 \le\sum_i\Phi_V(\chi_i^G).
 
\end{equation}

Let Omega in R^n be open and u in L^1_loc(Omega) satisfy integral_Omega u (Laplacian of phi) dx = 0 for every phi in C_c^infinity(Omega). Then u agrees almost everywhere with a function that is harmonic, hence real-analytic, in Omega. More generally, if P is a linear differential operator with smooth coefficients that is elliptic (nonvanishing principal symbol), then every distributional solution of Pu = f with f smooth is smooth; ellipticity, not any a priori regularity of u, is what does the work.
Omega open in R^n
u in L^1_loc(Omega)
integral u times Laplacian of phi vanishes for all phi in C_c^infinity(Omega) (u is harmonic in the sense of distributions)

Letting eps tend to 0, u_eps converges to u in L^1_loc, while the right-hand side converges locally uniformly to u_delta; hence u = u_delta a.e. on each compact subset of Omega_delta. body: Bayes' theorem, named after Thomas Bayes, gives a mathematical rule for inverting conditional probabilities, allowing the probability of a cause to be found given its effect. For example, with Bayes' theorem, the probability that a patient has a disease given that they tested positive for that disease can be found using the probability that the test yields a positive result when the disease is present. The theorem was developed in the 18th century by Bayes and independently by Pierre-Simon Laplace.

body:
[Lem 6. lem: Prohorov distance estimate of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] Let $X$ and $Y$ be random elements of a separable metric space $(S, d^{S})$ defined on a common probability space with probability measure $P$.
  Suppose that on an event $E$, we have that $d^{S}(X, Y) \leq \varepsilon$ almost surely.
  Then, it holds that 
  \begin{equation}
    d_{P}^{S}
    \bigl(
      P(X \in \cdot), P(Y \in \cdot)
    \bigr)
    \leq 
    P(E^{c}) + \varepsilon.
  \end{equation}

[Lemma 17 of arXiv:2607.18862, 'Tamed Euler Schemes for Singular SDEs with Multiplicative L\'{e}vy Noise'] Let $K>0$ be a constant and let $B,\widetilde{B}$ be symmetric invertible matrices such that $K^{-1}I\leq B\widetilde{B}^{-1}\leq KI$. Then, for all $x\in\mR^d$, we have the following bound
	\be
	|(p_B-p_{\widetilde{B}})(x)|\leq N\|I-B\widetilde{B}^{-1}\|(p_{\frac{B}{2}}+p_{\frac{\widetilde{B}}{2}})(x)
	\ee 
	where $p_B(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{(2\pi)^d\det{(B)}}}\exp{\bigg(-\frac{1}{2}x^TB^{-1}x\bigg)}$ and $N$ is a constant that depends only on $d,K$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 5 (Time-uniform probability estimate for the mixed example) of arXiv:2608.17540, 'Pathwise stability for one-dimensional SDEs driven by Brownian motion and a symmetric stab'] In the setting of Proposition~\ref{prop:mixed-brownian-error}, assume $x_0=\wt x_0$ and $\|r\|_{L^2(0,T)}<1$. Then, for every $h>0$,
\[
  \mathbb P\left(\sup_{0\le t\le T}|X_t-\wt X_t|>h\right)
  \le
  \frac{C}{h^{\alpha-1}}
  \|r\|_{L^2(0,T)}^{\frac{2(\alpha\wt\eta-1)}{\alpha\wt\eta-\alpha+2}}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
  \mathbb P\left(\sup_{0\le t\le T}|X_t-\wt X_t|^{\alpha-1}>h\right)
  \le
  \frac{C}{h}
  \|r\|_{L^2(0,T)}^{\frac{2(\alpha\wt\eta-1)}{\alpha\wt\eta-\alpha+2}}.
\]
The constant is independent of $h$ and $r$; for $0<\lambda<1$ it can be chosen uniformly in $\lambda$.

For iid Exp(1) edge weights on undirected nearest-neighbor Z^2, let T_n be the passage time from (0,0) to (n,0), n>=1, and sigma_n^2=Var(T_n)>0. Enumerate all edges, let F_k be the first-k-edge sigma-field with trivial F_0, M_{n,k}=E[T_n|F_k]-E T_n, D_{n,k}=M_{n,k}-M_{n,k-1}, and Q_{n,k}=sum_{j<=k} D_{n,j}^2. Uniform boundedness of E|T_n-E T_n|^4/sigma_n^4 is equivalent up to factor 81 to uniform boundedness of E Q_{n,k}^2/sigma_n^4 over n,k. If V_{n,k}=sum_{j<=k} E[D_{n,j}^2|F_{j-1}] satisfies E V_{n,k}^2<=a sigma_n^4 and sum_{j<=k} E D_{n,j}^4<=b sigma_n^4 uniformly for finite a,b>=0, then E|T_n-E T_n|^4<=81(sqrt(a)+sqrt(b))^2 sigma_n^4. These lattice estimates are hypotheses, not established facts.
The precise undirected lattice Exp(1) model in the statement
Countable full edge enumeration and corresponding exposure filtration
For the sufficient criterion, the two displayed uniform moment budgets are assumed

Exact remaining lattice condition and a predictable criterion

In the original specialization, T_n is the undirected nearest-neighbor passage time from (0,0) to (n,0) in Z^2 with iid Exp(1) edge weights. Enumerate the countably many edges, let F_k be the sigma-field generated by the first k weights, and set

    M_{n,k}=E[T_n | F_k]-E T_n,
    D_{n,k}=M_{n,k}-M_{n,k-1},
    sigma_n^2=Var(T_n),
    Q_{n,k}=sum_{j<=k} D_{n,j}^2.

Use a trivial F_0. T_n has finite fourth moment, since it is nonnegative and bounded above by the weight of the straight n-edge path. Its variance is positive: the minimum of the four weights incident to the starting vertex is a lower bound with unbounded support, while the straight-path upper bound is finite. Thus T_n cannot be almost surely constant. The endpoint is distinct for n>=1.

The following two conditions are equivalent up to universal constants:

    G: sup_n E|T_n-E T_n|^4 / sigma_n^4 < infinity;
    Q: sup_{n,k} E Q_{n,k}^2 / sigma_n^4 < infinity.

If G holds with constant K, conditional Jensen and the reverse inequality in L6 give Q with constant 81K. If Q holds with constant C, the forward inequality in L6 gives E M_{n,k}^4<=81C sigma_n^4. Moreover M_{n,k} converges to T_n-E T_n in the L^4 norm. To justify this step, cylinder random variables measurable with respect to some F_j are dense in L^4(F_infinity); conditional expectation is an L^4 contraction. Approximating T_n-E T_n by such a variable X gives, for k>=j,

    ||E[T_n-E T_n | F_k]-(T_n-E T_n)||_4
      <= 2 ||X-(T_n-E T_n)||_4.

T_n is F_infinity-measurable because it is an infimum over a countable collection of finite-path sums. The displayed approximation therefore proves the asserted convergence. Taking k to infinity yields G with constant 81C.

For a concrete sufficient criterion put

    v_{n,j}=E[D_{n,j}^2 | F_{j-1}],
    V_{n,k}=sum_{j<=k} v_{n,j}.

Suppose fixed finite constants a,b>=0 satisfy, uniformly in n,k,

    E V_{n,k}^2 <= a sigma_n^4,
    sum_{j<=k} E D_{n,j}^4 <= b sigma_n^4.

Then G holds with constant 81(sqrt(a)+sqrt(b))^2. Proof: the differences D_{n,j}^2-v_{n,j} form an L^2 martingale difference sequence. Orthogonality and conditional expectation give the exact identity

    E(Q_{n,k}-V_{n,k})^2
      = sum_{j<=k} (E D_{n,j}^4-E v_{n,j}^2)
      <= sum_{j<=k} E D_{n,j}^4.

Minkowski now bounds ||Q_{n,k}||_2 by ||V_{n,k}||_2 plus the square root of the jump-fourth-moment sum. Apply L6 and L^4 convergence. All uses of orthogonality concern actual martingale differences; no conditional probabilities are multiplied.

This criterion has not been verified for lattice FPP. The comparison Q<=>G is a reformulation of the missing moment estimate, not a proof that it holds. Unconditional identities E Q_{n,k}=E V_{n,k}=E M_{n,k}^2<=sigma_n^2 are insufficient to bound the required second moments of Q or V. The variance denominator here is that of the full T_n, not that of a truncated martingale.

## Counterexample to replacing the square-function second moment by its mean

Let 0<p<=1, B be Bernoulli(p), and epsilon be an independent symmetric sign. Use F_0 trivial, F_1=sigma(B), F_2=sigma(B,epsilon), and M_0=M_1=0, M_2=B epsilon/sqrt(p). This is a martingale with variance 1. Nonetheless

    Q_2=V_2=B/p,
    E Q_2=E V_2=1,
    E Q_2^2=E V_2^2=E M_2^4=1/p.

Thus the needed bound can fail arbitrarily badly even for two independent input variables and a two-step Doob martingale. Independence of the inputs does not make the conditional variance budget deterministic. This example is not a lattice FPP construction.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:4c443e3f19a14e2142010af75166771eee39e52faebda433bed243ebd82895f2","revision_digest":"sha256:30c98b020468f1e4b98809331bad26665eb077939fd4d38faa57f4e51075426c","source_id":"urn:mb-source:79d6d23859a360a4:w369:l7","source_revision":"author-proof-awaiting-independent-review-20261010","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Definition 1 (Progress-aware exploitation score) of arXiv:2608.25116, '\method: Gradient Refinement and Progress-Aware Exploitation for Query-Efficient High-Dime'] Let $\gamma_\bv=\mu_\bv/\sigma_\bv$ denote the standardized directional
mean. The progress-aware exploitation score of direction $\bv$ at $\bx$ is
\begin{align}
\mathcal{P}(\bv) &:= \mathbb{E}\bigl[-\nabla_\bv f(\bx)\mid \nabla_\bv f(\bx)<0\bigr] \notag \\
&= \sigma_\bv\!\left[\frac{\phi(\gamma_\bv)}{\Phi(-\gamma_\bv)} - \gamma_\bv\right],

\end{align}
where $\phi$ and $\Phi$ are the standard normal PDF and CDF.
title: Progress-aware exploitation score

body:
[Lemma prop:geodesics_intersect of arXiv:2512.09219, 'Strong confluence of geodesics in Liouville quantum gravity'] It is almost surely the case that the following is true. Let $P_n\colon [0,T_n]\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ be a sequence of $D_h$-geodesics converging to some $D_h$-geodesic $P \colon [ 0 , T]\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ as $n \to \infty$ in the Hausdorff sense with respect to $D_h$. Let $0<s<t<T$. Then, given $\varepsilon>0$, for all $n$ large enough, we have at least one of the following:
  \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
  \item  $d_H^1(P\lvert_{[s,t]},P_n\lvert_{[s,t]})\leq \varepsilon$,
  \item  $P\lvert_{[s,t]}\cap P_n\lvert_{[s,t]} \neq \emptyset$.
  \end{enumerate}
title: Lemma prop:geodesics_intersect of arXiv:2512.09219

body:
[Lemma 2 of arXiv:2608.25221, 'Representing MAX functions using two-hidden-layer ReLU networks'] Fix a natural number $k\geq 1$. For any atom pattern $P$ of degree $k$, there exist $\eta_L, \eta_R \in \Z^N_+$ such that $\|\eta_L\|_1 = \|\eta_R\|_1 = k$ such that $$\mathcal{A}_P(x) = \max\{\langle \eta_L, x\rangle, \langle \eta_R, x\rangle\}$$ for all $x \in \mathcal{C}$. $\eta_L$ and $\eta_R$ are given by the closed-form formulas: $$(\eta_L)_i = \sum_{j=1}^k \mathbf{1}_{\min(p_j) = i} \qquad \forall i = 1, \ldots, N,$$
$$(\eta_R)_i = \sum_{j=1}^k \mathbf{1}_{\min(q_j) = i} \qquad \forall i = 1, \ldots, N,$$ where $\min(p_j)$ and $\min(q_j)$ denote the minimum of the pair of numbers in $p_j$ and $q_j$, respectively.

body:
[Proposition 28 of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] For any $r > 0$, the tail event $\{ T_{m, p} \geq r \}$ has the following
  upper bound:
  \begin{align*}
      \PP(T_{m, p} \geq r)
      &\leq 2 - 2 
      \binom{m\exp(1/r)}{m}^{-1}
      (1-p)^m\\
      &\phantom{{} \leq 2 - 2} \times
      \left[
      1 - \int_0^1 p \, m
      \left(1-x\right)^{m\exp(1/r)-m}
      \left(1-p\,x\right)^{m-1} dx
      \right]^{-1}.
  \end{align*}
  \begin{proof}
    Since $T_{m, p}$ is non-negative,
    we can invoke a common bound from \cite[p.~126]{kallenberg2021probability},
    namely $\PP(T_{m,p} \geq r) \leq 2\left(1 - M_{T_{m,p}}(-1/r)\right)$.
    Substitute Lemma \ref{thm:factored mgf}.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 28 of arXiv:2605.14206

Own work draft, proof (unaudited); no independent review. For any fixed r>0, ReLU spiked random features with iid unit-sphere (or Gaussian N(0,I_d/d)) bulk rows and per-neuron spike r(v^T x), normalized by 1/sqrt(m), fail the ordinary Montanari-Saeed Gaussian projection condition along theta=1_m/sqrt(m). Matched full Gaussian features have a strictly positive bounded-Lipschitz negative-tail discrepancy. Singleton-readout ERM with that negative-tail loss gives minimum limits 0 and c_r>0. Scope: This refutes only the ordinary Gaussian reduction including this readout direction, not conditional Gaussian equivalence or ridge equivalence. Constant per-neuron spike has norm r sqrt(m), not a bounded-operator spike. No novelty claim for the conditional structure already identified in Cui et al.

[Theorem 16 (Full convergence of a fixed anchored finite-time Hopf profile) of arXiv:2609.00501, 'Uniqueness of Finite-Time Varifold Limits for the M\"obius-Invariant Willmore Flow'] Under the hypotheses of Corollary~\ref{cor:hopf}, fix the oriented
normal gauge and the material anchor introduced above, and let
\(\widetilde\gamma_t\) be the anchored constant-speed profile
\eqref{eq:anchored-gauge}.  Set
\begin{equation}
 
 C_{\mathrm g}:=\left(\frac2\pi+64\right)^{1/2}.
\end{equation}
Then, for \(0\leq s<t<T\),
\begin{equation}
 
 \|\widetilde\gamma_t-\widetilde\gamma_s\|_{L^2(\Sph^1)}
 \leq
 \frac{C_{\mathrm g}}{\sqrt\pi}
 \sqrt{(t-s)\bigl(W(s)-W(t)\bigr)} .
\end{equation}
There are an embedded regular constant-speed curve
\(\gamma_T\in W^{2,2}(\Sph^1,\Sph^2)\cap C^1(\Sph^1,\Sph^2)\)
and a number \(L_T\in[\pi,8]\) such that, as \(t\nearrow T\),
\begin{align}
 \widetilde\gamma_t&\rightharpoonup\gamma_T
 &&\text{weakly in }W^{2,2}(\Sph^1,\R^3),\\
 \widetilde\gamma_t&\longrightarrow\gamma_T
 &&\text{strongly in }W^{1,2}(\Sph^1,\R^3),\\
 \widetilde\gamma_t&\longrightarrow\gamma_T
 &&\text{strongly in }C^{1,\alpha}(\Sph^1,\R^3),
   \quad 0<\alpha<\tfrac12,\\
 L(\widetilde\gamma_t)&\longrightarrow L_T=L(\gamma_T),
 \qquad |\partial_x\gamma_T|=L_T .
\end{align}
The trace of \(\gamma_T\) is the embedded \(C^1\) profile
\(\pi(\spt\Var_T)\) of the unique limiting Hopf torus.
title: Full convergence of a fixed anchored finite-time Hopf profile

Suppose one-way functions exist. For any measurement count m>d^0.01, Gupta et al. establish a family of 10-well-modeled distributions over R^d and normalized linear measurement models Y=A X+eta with m measurements, ||A||_op<=1 and independent eta~N(0,beta^2 I_m), beta=Theta(1/(log d)^2), for which (1/10,1/10)-posterior sampling requires superpolynomial time in d. Well-modeled and posterior sampling have exactly the meanings of the two companion definition cards. In particular the approximation guarantee is a typical-measurement coupling guarantee; the shrinking noise parameter is a standard deviation, not a variance. The result supplies priors with efficient approximate smoothed-score representations despite computationally hard posterior sampling. It does not assert this lower bound under a dimension-independent noise level or under log-concavity, and gives no general unit-cost exact-score-oracle lower bound.

Own-work draft. Status: proof (unaudited), C023 v2; independent audit and novelty assessment pending. Gaussian input, unit teacher u, fixed positive outer weights, activation sigma=sqrt(A)He2/sqrt(2)+sqrt(B)He3/sqrt(6), and zero temperature. For d>=4, 1/2<=a<1, 0<=p<1, define n=d-1, ell=1-p, q=1-a^2, J=n(1+a^3)-3aq, D=aJ+q, A=3D/(3D+2dq), B=1-A, s=q/J. The law rho*=p delta_u+ell times the uniform latitude u.w=-a has an attracting basin among axial laws with fixed pole mass p. Put W=-na(1+a^2+4a^3-2a^5)+6a^2q^2, Lf=ell*q*(6BJ/n)*(s-a), Lc=ell*(6B/n)*W, gamma=min(-Lf,-Lc)>0. For initial ring overlap -a+h, set N0=|Eh|+||h-Eh||infinity. If N0<=min((1-a)/2,gamma/(3072ell)), then Nt<=N0 exp(-gamma*t/2), and the spherical laws converge in W2 to rho*. The collective rate Lc includes the changing moment feedback; Lf is only the frozen-field rate. The exact factorization W=-(n-3)a(1+a^2+4a^3-2a^5)-3a[(1-a)^2+4a^3(2-a^2)] proves negativity. A polynomial Frechet remainder gives Dini derivative N'<=-gamma*N+1536ell*N^2. This is a local zero-temperature basin with fixed pole mass. It supplies neither uniform-start reachability nor a noisy escape-time lower bound, and does not assert a local risk minimum in unrestricted W2 topology. Exact algebra checks are supplemental; the Lean attempt is runtime-unverified.
