measurable functions $f:\Gamma\to \IR$, which are local, in that $\exists n\in \IN$ such that $f(\xi)=f(\xi\cap \Lambda_n)$, $\forall \xi\in \Gamma$, and tame, in that $\left\lvertf(\xi)\right\rvert\leq c(1+\xi(\Lambda_n))$ for $n\in \IN$, a constant $c\in \IR$ and any $\xi\in \Gamma$. The topology $\mathcal T_{\mathcal L}$ is defined as the coarsest topology on $\mathcal P_{s,1}(\Gamma)$ such that the mappings $\mathsf{P}\mapsto \IE_{\mathsf{P}}[f]$ are continuous for any $f\in L$. We note that the topology $\mathcal T_{\mathcal L}$ is finer than the weak topology on $\mathcal P_{s,1}(\Gamma)$ which is induced by the vague topology on $\Gamma$.

Let (X_n)_{n=1}^\infty be i.i.d. strictly positive inter-arrival times with finite mean \mu = \mathbb{E}[X_1] \in (0, \infty). Let S_n = \sum_{k=1}^n X_k with S_0 = 0, and define the renewal counting process N(t) = \sup\{n \ge 0 : S_n \le t\}. Let m(t) = \mathbb{E}[N(t)] be the renewal function. Then \lim_{t \to \infty} \frac{m(t)}{t} = \frac{1}{\mu}.
(X_n) i.i.d., X_n > 0
0 < \mu = \mathbb{E}[X_1] < \infty

[Proposition prop:4D-cov of arXiv:2507.19554, 'Full extremal process in four-dimensional membrane model'] The covariance of the 4D membrane models $h_v$ satisfies
	\begin{itemize}
		\item
		There exists constant $\alpha_0'$ such that for $u, v \in V_N$, one has
		\bequ
			\begin{aligned}
				\Var\lp h_v^{N} \rp & \leq \frac{8}{\pi^2}\log N + \alpha_0; 		\\
				\mbE\lb \lp h_u^{N} - h_v^{N} \rp^2 \rb & \leq \frac{8}{\pi^2}\lp 2\log \lp 1 + \lv u - v \rv \rp - \lv \Var\lp h_v^{N} \rp - \Var\lp h_u^{N} \rp \rv + 4\alpha_0 \rp.
			\end{aligned}
		\eequ
		\item
		For any $\delta > 0$ there is a constant $\alpha^{\delta} > 0$ such that for all $u, v \in V_N$ with $\min\lp d_N\lp u \rp, d_N\lp v \rp \rp \geq \delta N$, one has
		\bequ
			\lv \Cov\lp h_v^{N}, h_u^{N}\rp - \log\frac{N}{1 + \lv u - v \rv} \rv \leq \alpha^{\delta}.
		\eequ 
	Here	$d_N\lp v \rp := \dist\lp v, \p V_N \rp$
		\item 
		There are a constant $\theta_0 > 0$, a continuous function $f_1: \lp 0, 1 \rp^4
		\rightarrow \mbR $ and a function $f_2: \mbZ^4 \times \mbZ^4 \rightarrow \mbR$
		such that the following holds. For all $L, \epsilon > 0, \theta > \theta_0$ there
		exists $N_0' = N_0'\lp L, \epsilon, \theta \rp$ such that for all
		$x \in \lb 0, 1 \rb^4, N \geq N_0', Nx \in \mbZ^4$ and
		$d\lp x \rp \geq \frac{\lp \log N \rp^{\theta}}{N}$ and for all
		$u, v \in \lb 0, L \rb^4 \cap \mbZ^4$, 
		\bequ
			\lv \Cov\lp h^{N}_{Nx + v}, h^{N}_{Nx + u} \rp - \frac{8}{\pi^2}\log N - f_1\lp x \rp - f_2\lp u, v \rp \rv < \epsilon.
		\eequ
		\item 
		There are a constant $\theta_1 > 0$ and a continuous function $f_3: D^4 \rightarrow \mbR$, where $D^4 := \lbb \lp x, y \rp, x, y \in \lp 0, 1 \rp^4, x \neq y \rbb$ such that the following holds: for all $L, \epsilon > 0, \theta > \theta_1$ there exists $N_1' = N_1'\lp L, \epsilon, \theta \rp$ such for all $x, y \in \lb 0, 1 \rb^4, Nx, Ny \in \mbZ^4$ and $d\lp x \rp \geq \frac{\lp \log N \rp^{\theta}}{N}$, $\min\lp d\lp x \rp, d\lp y \rp \rp \geq \frac{\lp \log N \rp^{\theta}}{N}$ and $\lv x - y \rv \geq \frac{1}{L}$ we have	
		\bequ
			\lv \Cov\lp  h^{N}_{Nx},  h^{N}_{Ny} \rp - f_3\lp x, y \rp \rv < \epsilon.
		\eequ
	\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Covariance of 4D membrane models \cite{schweiger2020maximum}

\begin{enumerate}
  \item[\textnormal{(1)}] Let $D$ be an invertible $n \times n$ matrix with columns $v_k = De_k$. Define $v_k^* = (D^{-1})^* e_k$. Then
  $(v_k, v_k^*)_{k=1}^n$ is a complete biorthogonal system in

body: [Lemma lma:essential of arXiv:2608.26564, 'Real ideal points, Conway spheres, and left-orderable Dehn fillings'] Let $T$ be a torus- or twist-trivial tangle variant, and let $C' \subset \partial T$ be its Conway boundary. body: FIRES WHEN a paper states a clean iff and credits it to an earlier short note, especially one in another language, and you are about to record the problem as resolved in the literature. WHAT HAPPENED: Ganikhodjaev and Zanin, arXiv:1205.3841 (2012, Russian), state as Theorem 1 that the Volterra operator on S^2 is non-ergodic if and only if a, b, c are nonzero and of one sign, attributing the condition to their 2004 note (Russian Math. Surveys 59:3, 571-572) whose TITLE announces only a necessary condition. An intermediate pass of this campaign recorded the problem as RESOLVED IN THE LITERATURE on that basis. Reading the 2004 note in full (Mathnet) shows it proves ONLY the necessary condition; the sufficiency was not there and had to be proved - see the E0061 result node. CONDITION OF FAILURE: an attribution chain read from the citing paper rather than from the cited one. The circumstantial warning was already visible and was not acted on: the 2009 source POSED the question five years AFTER the note it is attributed to, which is close to impossible if the note contained the answer.

[Lemma two Killing vector fields of arXiv:2609.02073, 'Existence of closed non-planar $p$-elasticae'] Let $k$ be a solution to (equation eq:EL for k of the paper) for $C^2> 0$ on $[0,L]$. By (equation eq:EL for k and tau of the paper), set $\tau =C k^{2-2p}$. Let $\gamma:[0,L]\to \R^3$ be an associated curve with tangent $T$, normal $N$ and binormal $B$. 
  Then the vector fields 
  \begin{equation*}
    J_0 = T ((p-1)k^p - \lambda) + N (p(p-1)k^{p-2}k') + B(pk^{p-1}\tau)\qquad \text{and} \qquad I = k^{p-1}B 
  \end{equation*}
  are Killing vector fields along $\gamma$.
  Moreover, $|J_0|^2 = (p-1-\lambda)^2 + p^2C^2$.

body:
[Lem FT_of_const._1_fn of arXiv:2606.29829, ''] Recall that $\widehat{G}$ is the set of equivalence classes of irreducible representations of the finite group $G$. Let $\mathbf{1}:G\rightarrow\{0,1\}$ be defined by $\mathbf{1}(g)=1$ for all $g\in G$, and $\delta_{*,*}$ denotes the Kronecker delta. Then
	\[\widehat{\mathbf{1}}(\sigma)=\frac{|G|}{d_{\sigma}}\;\delta_{\sigma,\trivial}\;I_{\sigma},\quad\sigma\in\widehat{G}.\]
	Here, $I_{\sigma}$ denotes the identity operator on the irreducible $G$-module indexed by $\sigma$, and $d_{\sigma}$ denotes its dimension.

body:
[Theorem 27 of arXiv:2511.06414, 'Non-uniform Edgeworth expansions for weakly dependent random variables and their applicati'] (i) Suppose that $\|f_n\|_{L^\infty}=O(n^{-\be})$ for some $\be\in(0,1/2)$. Then  Assumption \ref{DerAss} holds true when $r:=m-2<\frac1{1-2\be}$, and therefore the  non-uniform Edgeworth expansions of order $r$ and the  Edgeworth expansions in transport distances of order $r$ (as in Theorems \ref{Edge2} and \ref{Edge1}) and the expansions of the expectations as in Corollary \ref{Cor} (ii) hold true (with such $m$). In particular, if $\|f_n\|_{L^\infty}=O(n^{-1/2})$ then $S_n$ obeys expansions of all orders (in all of the above senses).

Moreover, the condition $r=m-2<\frac1{1-2\be}$ is optimal even for independent summands.
\vskip0.12cm
(ii) Suppose that $\cX$ is a compact Riemannian manifold, and that $f_n$ are uniformly H\"older continuous with some exponent $\al$. Additionally, assume that all the measures $\mathfrak{m_j}$ coincide with the volume measure and the transition densities $p_j$ which are (uniformly) bounded and bounded away from the origin. Then the non-uniform Edgeworth expansions of order $r=m-2$, 
the Edgeworth expansions in transport distances of order $r$, and the  expansions of the expectations as in Corollary \ref{Cor}(ii) hold true for every $m$ so that $r=m-2<\frac{1+\al}{1-\al}$, where for $\al=1$ we set $\frac{1+\al}{1-\al}=\infty$ (in particular, for Lipschitz continuous functions we get expansions of all orders in all of the above senses).

Moreover, the condition $r=m-2<\frac{1+\al}{1-\al}$ is optimal even in the iid case.

[Lem 2 of arXiv:2608.30763, 'Ultracontractivity of heat semigroups with non-local Robin boundary conditions via two-sid'] The boundary operator $C$ is  $\mathrm{L}^{\infty}$-continuous with 
$$
\left\| C \right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\infty} \to \mathrm{L}^{\infty}} \ = \ \left\| C {\bf 1}\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\infty}(\partial \Omega)}.
$$
In particular, 
$$
\left| Cu \right| \ \leq \ \left\| u \right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\infty}(\partial \Omega)} C {\bf 1}
$$ 
holds pointwise almost everywhere in $\partial \Omega$ for every $u \in \mathrm{L}^{\infty}(\partial \Omega)$. Furthermore
$C$ acts boundedly on $\mathrm{L}^{p}(\partial \Omega)$ for every $p \in [2,\infty)$ with
$$
\left\| C \right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{p} \to \mathrm{L}^{p}} \ \leq \ 
\max\left\{ \left\| C \right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{2} \to \mathrm{L}^{2}}, \left\| C {\bf 1}\right\|_{\mathrm{L}^{\infty}(\partial \Omega)} 
\right\} 
$$

body: In probability theory, statistics and related fields, a Poisson point process is a type of mathematical object that consists of points randomly located on a mathematical space with the essential feature that the points occur independently of one another. The process's name derives from the fact that the number of points in any given finite region follows a Poisson distribution. The process and the distribution are named after French mathematician Siméon Denis Poisson. The process itself was discovered independently and repeatedly in several settings, including experiments on radioactive decay, telephone call arrivals and actuarial science.
title: Poisson point process

[Definition def:BST of arXiv:2608.19050, 'Online Permutation Embedding: \\ Optimal Stopping and Scaling Laws'] Let $\pi \in \Pi_k$ be a permutation. The binary search tree 
$\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{BST},\pi}$ is constructed by inserting nodes labeled $1,\dots,k$ (containing keys
$\pi(1),\pi(2),\dots,\pi(k)$, respectively) sequentially into an initially empty binary search tree. The first node, labeled 1, is inserted as the root. Each remaining node $i$ is sequentially inserted as follows. Start at the root; descend to the left if the key $\pi(i)$ is smaller 
than the key of the current node, and descend to the right otherwise. Repeat this descent until an empty position is reached, and insert the current node at this empty position. If $\pi$ was drawn uniformly at random from $\Pi_k$, then we further say that $\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{BST},\pi}$ is a \textit{random} BST on $[k]$.
title: BST

    For $\landsc$ a landscape and $(x, y)\in \Half$ a point, we call (first) blocking building of $(x, y)$ in $\landsc$ the following quantity when it is well defined:
    \[\tau(x, y, \landsc) = (x_b, y_b) := \underset{\substack{(a, b) \in \landsc \\a>x}}{\text{argmax}} \frac{b-y}{a-x}.\]
    When the blocking building of $(x, y)$ is well defined, we further introduce its blockage angle as:

[-\log q_{B_p^n}]
\geq
C_p n\log n-c_p n.

exhibits a sharp threshold for random convex hulls. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2609.03819, 'Stochastic damped wave and Euler-Bernoulli equations with singular locally H\"older contin'] Assume \ref{H0}, \ref{H1} and \ref{H3} hold. Hence, there exist constants $M_0\geq 1$ and $b>0$, independent of $t\in(0,\infty)$ and $n\in\N$, such that, for every $n\in\N$ and $t\in (0,\infty)$, we have 
\begin{align}
&\|e^{tA_n}\mathcal{V}_n\|_{\mathcal{L}(U,H_n)}\leq \frac{M_0e^{-b\zeta t}}{t^{\gamma_1}},\\
&\|\Gamma_{t,n}\mathcal{V}_n\|_{\mathcal{L}(U,H_n)}\leq \frac{M_0}{t^{\gamma_2}},\\
&\|\Gamma_{t,n}\mathcal{G}_n\|_{\mathcal{L}(U,H_n)}\leq \frac{M_0}{t^{1/2}},\\
&\|\Gamma_{t,n}\|_{\mathcal{L}(H_n)}\leq \frac{M_0}{t^{\gamma_3}},
\end{align}
where, if $\alpha\in\left(0,\frac12\right]$, then $\zeta=\mu_1^\alpha$ and 
\begin{align}
&\gamma_1= \frac{\beta}{\alpha},
\\
&\gamma_2=\frac12+\frac{\beta+\delta}{\alpha},\\
&\gamma_3=\frac12+\max\left\{\frac\delta\alpha, 1\right\}, 
\end{align}
while, if $\alpha\in\left[\frac12,1\right)$, then $\zeta=\mu_1^{1-\alpha}$ and
\begin{align}
&\gamma_1= 
\max\left\{\frac{\beta}{\alpha},\frac{\beta+\frac12-\alpha}{1-\alpha}\right\}, 
\\
&\gamma_2=\frac12+\frac{\beta+\delta}{1-\alpha},\\
&\gamma_3=\frac12+\max\left\{\frac{\delta+\alpha-\frac12}{1-\alpha}, 1\right\}, 
\end{align}

body: In mathematics, Schur's lemma is an elementary but useful statement in representation theory of groups and algebras. In the group case it says that if M and N are two finite-dimensional irreducible representations of a group G and φ is a linear map from M to N that commutes with the action of the group, then either φ is invertible, or φ = 0. An important special case occurs when M = N, i.e. φ is a self-map; in particular, for representations over an algebraically closed field, any element of the center of a group must act as a scalar operator on M. The lemma is named after Issai Schur who used it to prove the Schur orthogonality relations and develop the basics of the representation theory of finite groups. Schur's lemma admits generalisations to Lie groups and Lie algebras, the most common of which are due to Jacques Dixmier and Daniel Quillen.
title: Schur's lemma

[Proposition 18 (Uniform BMO--Girsanov package) of arXiv:2608.06393, 'Intrinsic Tangential Hadamard Differentiability of Rough-BSDE Solution Maps'] Let \(\{N^\theta\}_{\theta\in\Theta}\) be continuous martingales on \(I\)
such that
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}
 \|N^\theta\|_{\mathrm{BMO}_2(\mathbb P;I)}\leq n_*.
\]
For \(u\leq t\leq v\), set
\[
 L_t^\theta
 :=\exp\left(
  N_t^\theta-N_u^\theta
  -\frac12(\langle N^\theta\rangle_t-
              \langle N^\theta\rangle_u)
 \right),
\]
so that \(L_u^\theta=1\), and define
\(d\mathbb Q^\theta/d\mathbb P=L_v^\theta\) on \(\mathcal F_v\).
There exist exponents \(r_+,r_->1\) and constants
\(C_+,C_-,C_{\mathrm{eq}}<\infty\), depending only on \(n_*\), such that,
uniformly in \(\theta\) and \(\tau\in\mathcal T_I\),
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E_\tau^{\mathbb P}
 \left[\left(\frac{L_v^\theta}{L_\tau^\theta}\right)^{r_+}\right]
 &\leq C_+,
 \\
 \mathbb E_\tau^{\mathbb Q^\theta}
 \left[\left(\frac{L_\tau^\theta}{L_v^\theta}\right)^{r_-}\right]
 &\leq C_-.
 
\end{align}
Moreover, if \(X\) is a continuous \(\mathbb P\)-local martingale and
\[
 \widetilde X^\theta
 :=X-\langle X,N^\theta\rangle,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 C_{\mathrm{eq}}^{-1}\|X\|_{\mathrm{BMO}_2(\mathbb P;I)}
 \leq
 \|\widetilde X^\theta\|_{\mathrm{BMO}_2(\mathbb Q^\theta;I)}
 \leq
 C_{\mathrm{eq}}\|X\|_{\mathrm{BMO}_2(\mathbb P;I)}.
 
\end{equation}
The exponents are selected after the budget \(n_*\) is fixed.  The
proposition does not assert \(r_+=r_-=2\), nor does it prescribe the same
exponent under the two measures. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Uniform BMO--Girsanov package

body:
[Conjecture conj:global of arXiv:2607.10717, 'Separatrix structure and the geometry of reset distributions'] Under assumptions \textnormal{(S1)--(S4)}, the sign of
$\partial_\gamma C(\pi,\gamma)$ is globally determined by
\[
\operatorname{sgn}\bigl(\partial_\gamma C(\pi,\gamma)\bigr)
= \operatorname{sgn}\langle\pi - \pi^*, \psi(\gamma)\rangle
\]
for all $\pi\in\Delta_{m-1}^\circ$ and all $\gamma\in(0,1)$.
In particular, $\Sigma$ acts as a global orientation boundary
for the reset response: every distribution on one side of
$\Sigma$ responds monotonically to changes in $\gamma$, with
the sign determined by the side. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Global orientation principle

$$ d_{BL} ( \cL  ( \bar V_t^{ \mu}, \bar X_t^{ \mu } ), \mu_\infty ) \le C_\lambda e^{ - \lambda t } d_{BL}  ( \mu, \mu_\infty ) + C_T d_{BL} ( \mu, \mu_\infty)^2. $$

body:
[Lemma lem:rn_derivative of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] Fix $M > 0$ and let $h$ (resp.\ $h_0$) be a GFF on $\mathbf{D}$ with boundary conditions bounded by $M$ (resp.\ zero boundary conditions).  Fix $r \in (0,1)$ and let $\mathcal {Z}_r$ be the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the law of $h|_{B(0,r)}$ with respect to $h_0|_{B(0,r)}$.  For each $q \in \mathbf{R}$ there exists a constant $C \in (0,\infty)$ depending only on $q$, $r$, and $M$ so that
\[ \mathbf{E}[ \mathcal {Z}_r^q] \leq C.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:rn_derivative of arXiv:2507.15589

body: [campaign status: author_checked_candidate - author-checked, unrefereed] Agresti and Veraar (journal version 2025, p. 130), Problem 5 asks: if u_0^n tends to u_0 in L^2(Omega; H), does u^n tend to u in L^2(Omega; L^2(0,T;V) intersect C([0,T];H))? Our result (id P0267, 2026-09-08): NO, from the same critical Allen-Cahn example as P0266. Take u_0^n = 1/n tending to 0; the limit solution is identically zero, and convergence in L^2(Omega; C([0,T];H)) would require E sup ||u^n||^2 to tend to 0, but that quantity is infinite for every n by the P0266 result (the constant-data solution's supremum has tail index one, coming from a four-dimensional Bessel process's capacity estimate). Verification as the source words it: uses the same construction and checks as Problem 4; of the six problems attacked in that session the memo states these two have the best odds of being genuinely new, since the source is a year old. Prior art not cleared. Allen-Cahn on the 1-d torus with 1-d quadratic noise, critical gamma^2 = 2 u_0^n = 1/n tending to 0

body:
[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2609.03506, 'Divergence of decreasing rearranged Fourier series\\ on every infinite compact abelian gro'] With the coefficients \(a_v\) defined above, let
\[
 \tau=\min\{\ell\in\{1,\ldots,N\}:|S_\ell|>\beta-1\},
 \qquad \min\varnothing=\infty,
\]
at each point of the underlying product group. Then
\[
 \sum_{v\in\T_N}a_vh_v=S_{\tau\wedge N}
\]
and, at every point,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\sum_{v\in\T_N}a_vh_v\right|\leq \beta.
\end{equation}

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:b01c32f421ba245e97b7deb6ace9f4ccfcec550037d1b24bf89b4e993b068f47","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/b0/b01c32f421ba245e97b7deb6ace9f4ccfcec550037d1b24bf89b4e993b068f47.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:47c1899e037c7f4cff115325d76967f95fbf4386c2eb4bee2497da0874e150da","bundle_entry_key":"2609-03506-lemma-7-stopping","bundle_id":"population.tex-extract-s3_161","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"tex-extract-20260907/bundle_s3_161.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:harvest.arxiv.mathematics:arxiv-2609-03506-lemma-7-stopping","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Paper's own proof, opening: Fix a point \(x\), and let \(v_0=\varnothing,v_1,\ldots,v_{N-1}\) be
its ancestors, so that \(h_{v_j}=Z_{j+1}\) at \(x\). Because \(v_j\)'s
own labels are exactly \(x\)'s first \(j\) increments,
\(S_\ell(v_j)=S_\ell\) at \(x\) for every \(\ell\leq j\), and hence
\[
 a_{v_j}=1
 \iff \max_{0\leq \ell\leq j}|S_\ell|\leq\beta-1
 \iff j<\tau.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \sum_{v\in\T_N}a_vh_v
 =\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}a_{v_j}Z_{j+1}
 =\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}1_{\{j<\tau\}}Z_{j+1}
 =\sum_{k=1}^{\tau\wedge N}Z_k
 =S_{\tau\wedge N},

[Theorem 14 of arXiv:2604.01701, '\bf Chung-type laws of the iterated logarithm for $m$-fold weighted integrated fractional '] Let $m\ge 0$, $\gamma\ge 0$, $\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_i<H+i+\gamma$, $i=1,\ldots,m$,  $\tau=H+m+\gamma$. Suppose  $q\ge 1$, $\frac{1}{r}=H+m+\gamma+\frac{1}{q}$, and  $\|w\|_{r,\tau,q}<\infty$. Then
\begin{align}
 &\lim_{\epsilon\to 0}  \epsilon^{1/\tau}\log \pr\left(\left\|w(t)t^{\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_m}  J_{m,\bm\alpha}(I_{\gamma}B_H)(t) \right\|_{L^q(0,\infty)}<a_H \epsilon\right)\nonumber\\
 =&\lim_{\epsilon\to 0}  \epsilon^{1/\tau}\log \pr\left(\left\|w(t)t^{\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_m}  J_{m,\bm\alpha}(W_{H+\gamma})(t) \right\|_{L^q(0,\infty)}< \epsilon\right)\nonumber\\
=& \lim_{\epsilon\to 0} \epsilon^{1/\tau}\log \pr\left(\left\|wW_{\tau}\right\|_{L^q(0,\infty)}< \epsilon\right) 
= -\kappa(\tau,q)\|w\|_{L^r(0,\infty)}^{1/\tau}, 
\end{align}
where $\kappa(\lambda,q)$ is defined as \eqref{eq:constant:2}.  When $q=\infty$, we assume that $w$  is almost everywhere continuous. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 14 of arXiv:2604.01701

[Definition def:flow of arXiv:2606.12143, 'Continuous stochastic flows driven by white noise and their duals'] A \textbf{stochastic flow} driven by $\mathcal W$ is a family of processes 
$$
\mathcal S = \left\{\bigl(\mathcal S_{r,x}(a),\, x \ge r\bigr)\right\}_{(a,r) \in {\mathbb R}^2}
$$
such that, for each $(a,r) \in {\mathbb R}^2$, the process $(\mathcal S_{r,x}(a),\, x \ge r)$ is the almost sure unique strong solution to~(equation eq:SDE_gener of the paper), and the following properties hold almost surely:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(R\arabic*)}, nosep]
    \item $\mathcal S_{r,r}(a) = a$ for all $(a,r) \in {\mathbb R}^2$. 
    \item For every $r \le x$, $a \mapsto \mathcal S_{r,x}(a)$ is c\`adl\`ag. 
    \item For any $(a_1,r_1), (a_2,r_2) \in {\mathbb R}^2$ and any $z \ge y \ge \max\{r_1,r_2\}$,
    $$
        \mathcal S_{r_1,y}(a_1) < \mathcal S_{r_2,y}(a_2) 
        \ \Longrightarrow\ 
        \mathcal S_{r_1,z}(a_1) \le \mathcal S_{r_2,z}(a_2).
    $$ 
\end{enumerate}

\vspace{-1.2em} 
A stochastic flow is said to be \textbf{continuous} if, almost surely, all flow lines are continuous. 
It is said to be \textbf{unique} if any other stochastic flow associated with~(equation eq:SDE_gener of the paper) satisfying the above properties is equal to $\mathcal S$ almost surely.
title: Definition def:flow of arXiv:2606.12143

Let P be an input probability law on X and let f,g:X->R be measurable functions with finite means E_P[f] and E_P[g]. Define c_P(f,g;x)=(f(x)-E_P[f])*(g(x)-E_P[g]) and L_cov(f,g;x,P)=max{0,1-c_P(f,g;x)}. Both centers use the same law P. In a curriculum, changing the sampling law therefore changes these centers. This is the population-centered covariance-loss definition used by Cornacchia-Mossel; their Remark1 describes estimating the two inner expectations and gradients with batches.
The input law P and both finite function means are specified.
For a finite Boolean input space, all real-valued network functions have finite means.
title: Cornacchia-Mossel covariance loss: population-centered product inside a hinge

body:
[Lem polyhom of arXiv:2608.06500, 'Free energy of Ising models under a spectral condition'] Let $p\in\mathbb{R}[x]$ be a polynomial. For all test graphs $X$, there
    exist test graphs $X_1,\ldots,X_r$ and constants
    $c_1,\ldots,c_r\in\mathbb{R}$ (depending on $p$ and $X$)
    such that for all weighted graphs
    $G=(\text{\boldmath $A$},\text{\boldmath $h$})$, we have that

    \begin{align*}
t(X,(p(\text{\boldmath $A$}),\text{\boldmath $h$}))=\sum_{i=1}^rc_it(X_i,G).
\end{align*}

    In other words, weighted homomorphism densities into the graph
    defined by a polynomial of the adjacency matrix of $G$ can be
    written as \emph{fixed} linear combinations of other weighted
    homomorphism densities into $G$. Consequently, local functions of
    $(p(\text{\boldmath $A$}),\text{\boldmath $h$})$ are also local functions of $G$.

Under the assumptions of unconfoundedness $(Y(1), Y(0)) \perp T \mid X$ and positivity $0 < P(T = 1 \mid X) < 1$, the CATE function $\tau(x) = \mathbb{E}[Y(1) - Y(0) \mid X = x]$ is nonparametrically identified from observational data by $\tau(x) = \mathbb{E}[Y \mid T = 1, X = x] - \mathbb{E}[Y \mid T = 0, X = x]$.
Unconfoundedness: (Y(1), Y(0)) \perp T | X

[Theorem thm:width of arXiv:2512.17747, 'On exponentially height-penalized random trees'] Let $\mu=\mu_n$ be such that $\mu\gg (\log n)^{3/2}/\sqrt{n}$.
Let $\mathbf{T}_n$ be a $\mu$-height-biased tree of size $n$.
Then for any $\epsilon>0$, we can find $K=K(\epsilon)>0$ large enough, such that
        \begin{align*}
            \liminf_{n \to \infty} \Prob{K^{-1}\leq\frac{w(\mathbf{T}_n)}{n\wedge\left((\mu n^2)^{1/3}\right)}\leq K}\geq 1-\epsilon\,.
        \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Prop 12 (\cite{Voiculescu1991}; \cite{Speicher1993}) of arXiv:2511.10535, 'Eigenvalues of Brownian Motions on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$'] Let $A_0^N,A_1^N$ be random matrix ensembles, i.e.\ random elements in the $W^\ast$-probability space $(\M_N(\C),\ts_N)$.  Let $(\A,\tau)$ be a $W^\ast$-probability space, with elements $a_0,a_1\in\A$ such that $A_0^N\to a_0$ a.s.\ in $\ast$-distribution and $A_1^N\to a_1$ a.s.\ in $\ast$-distribution.  For each $N\in\N$, let $U^N$ be a Haar Unitary Ensemble independent from $\{A_0^N,A_1^N\}$, and let $u$ be a Haar unitary operator in $\A$ freely independent from $\{a_0,a_1\}$.  Then $(A_0^N,U^NA_1^NU^{N\,\ast})$ converges a.s.\ in joint $\ast$-distribution to $(a_0,ua_1u^\ast)$; $ua_1u^\ast$ has the same distribution as $a_1$; and $a_0,ua_1u^\ast$ are freeely independent.  I.e.\ $A_0^N$ and $U^N A_1^N U^{N\,\ast}$ are a.s.\ asymptotically free. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{Voiculescu1991}; \cite{Speicher1993}

body: Fitting a per-output affine stack directly in the per-sample relative metric - weighted least squares with case weights $1/\|y_i\|^2$, or a per-output simplex fit with the same weights - overfits badly: the weights concentrate the effective sample on the handful of smallest-norm cases and $M + 1$ coefficients fitted to them are unusable out of sample (measured on the EMIT pool, seed 101: 0.1236 against 0.0465 for ordinary least squares on Y1, 0.1591 against 0.1292 on Y2; cross-validation on the weighted fit chooses to discard it entirely). The same objective becomes the best available estimator when it is reached through the error covariance rather than through the regression: form the error covariance in the relative metric, replace its sample eigenvalues by the Ledoit-Peche nonlinear-shrinkage values (floored at a small fraction of the bulk level), and take the sum-to-one minimum-variance weights with the intercept closing the weighted mean error, with no cross-validation anywhere. Measured on the same three cells (Y1, Y2, Y4): 0.0451 / 0.1190 / 1.799 against ordinary least squares 0.0465 / 0.1292 / 1.898 (+3.0 / +7.9 / +5.2 percent), matching the cross-validated best heuristic of the pool twice and beating it once; with the residual shrink toward the pooled simplex weights on top (cross-validated amount 0.2-0.4) it is the best estimator on all three cells, +4.1 / +11.7 / +6.7 percent over least squares and +3.4 to +3.9 percent over the pool's best. Two ingredients do the work: the nonlinear shrinkage tames the heavy-tailed spectrum that the small-norm cases create, and the sum-to-one constraint removes the scale and intercept freedom those cases exploit. In this metric the random-matrix cleaning is not a small correction on top of least squares; it is the difference between an unusable fit and the best one. Three cells of one seed at the time of writing; the seventy-cell population test on both corpora was running.

[Proposition 47 of arXiv:2512.07202, 'Hitting Probabilities for Hypoelliptic Differential Equations Driven by Fractional Brownia'] There exists a smooth random variable $\Psi$ such that
    $$
    \lambda_{\max}((\mathbf{J}^{\varepsilon,o}_1(\mathbf{J}^{\varepsilon,o}_1)^*)^{-1})\leqslant\Psi,
    $$
    for any $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$.
    \begin{proof}
     It is enough to prove that each entry of $(\mathbf{J}^{\varepsilon,o}_1)^{-1}$ is bounded by certain smooth random variable $\Psi$. 
     Note that 
     $
     \mathbf{U}^{\varepsilon,x}_t = x~\star~\mathbf{U}^{\varepsilon,o}_t
     $
     where $\star$ is the group law induced from $G^{(l)}(\mathbb{R}^d)$. Since the inverse of $x~\mapsto~x~\star~\mathbf{U}^{\varepsilon,o}_1$ is $y~\mapsto~y~\star~(\mathbf{U}^{\varepsilon,o}_1)^{-1}=: H(y)$, it follows that 
     $$
     (\mathbf{J}^{\varepsilon,o}_1)^{-1} = \frac{H(y)}{\partial y}\Big|_{y=\mathbf{U}^{\varepsilon,o}_1}
     $$
    Observe that every component of $\mathbf{U}^{\varepsilon,o}_1$ and $(\mathbf{U}^{\varepsilon,o}_1)^{-1}$ is a polynomial of
    $$
    \varepsilon^{Hm}\int_{0< t_1<\cdots< t_m< 1}d B^{i_1}_{t_1}\cdots d B^{i_d}_{t_m}.
    $$
    As in the argument of Lemma \ref{logsig1}, this can be bounded above by the random variable
\(\exp( \eta \left( \mathcal{N}^{0,1}_{\gamma,2q}(\mathbf{B}) \right)^{1/q})\) 
for some \(q \geqslant 1\), \(\eta \in (0, \eta_0]\) and \(\gamma < H\).
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 47 of arXiv:2512.07202

Let X_n and Y_n be random vectors in R^p. The Kolmogorov distance between their coordinate-wise maxima is rho(X_n, Y_n) = sup_{z >= 0} |P(max_{1 <= i <= p} |X_n(i)| <= z) - P(max_{1 <= i <= p} |Y_n(i)| <= z)|. In particular, rho_n = rho(X_n, bold_X_n) and rho_n^* = rho(X_n^*, bold_X_n) denote the distances to a centered Gaussian vector bold_X_n with matching covariances.
bold_X_n is Gaussian with matching covariance structure
title: Kolmogorov Distance Between Maxima of High-Dimensional Processes

[Lemma Campanato of arXiv:2509.04155, 'An Approach to Sub-Gaussian Heat Kernel Estimates via Analysis on Metric Spaces'] Let $p \geq 1, \, f \in L^p(X,\mu)$, $R > 0$ and $\delta > 0$.
    Let $M : X \to \mathbb{R}$ be the sharp maximal type function
    \[
        M(x) := \sup_{x \in B(y,r)} r^{-\delta} \vint_{B(y,r)} \abs{f - f_{B(y,r)}}^p \, d\mu
    \]
    where the supremum is taken over all $y \in X$ and $0 < r \leq R$ such that $x \in B(y,r)$.
    Then, there is a constant $C \geq 1$ such that for $\mu$-almost every $x \in X$ the two-point estimate
    \[
        \abs{f(x) - f(y)} \leq C d(x,y)^{\frac{\delta}{p}}(M(x)^{\frac{1}{p}} + M(y)^{\frac{1}{p}})
    \]
    holds for $\mu$-almost every $y \in B(x,R/4)$.
    This result is quantitative in the sense that $C$ depends only on the doubling constant of $\mu$ in (equation eq:muDoubling of the paper), $\delta$ and $p$.
title: Lemma Campanato of arXiv:2509.04155

body: [Lemma BC of arXiv:2505.11721, 'Variational principles for Hausdorff and packing dimensions of fractal percolation on self'] Let $\rho$ be a positive and finite Borel measure on $\mathcal{I}^{\mathbb{N}^+}$. Let $(\mathcal F_N)_{N\in\mathbb{\mathbb{N}^+}}$ be a sequence of partitions of $\Sigma$. For $\boldsymbol{i}\in \Sigma$ and $N\in\mathbb{\mathbb{N}^+}$, denote by $B_N(\boldsymbol{i})$ the  element of $\mathcal F_N$ which contains $\boldsymbol{i}$. Also let $(v_N)_{N\in\mathbb{\mathbb{N}^+}}\in \mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}^+}$. Suppose that for all $\eta> 0$ there exists $q > 1$ such that  $\sum_{N \geq 1} e^{N(q-1)(v_N-\eta)} \sum_{B\in\mathcal F_N} \rho(B)^q < +\infty$. Then $\liminf_{N \rightarrow \infty} \left(\frac{\log(\rho(B_N(\boldsymbol{i})))}{-N} - v_N \right) \geq 0$ for $\rho$-almost every $\boldsymbol{i}$. Similarly, if for all $\eta> 0$ there exists $0 < q < 1$ such that $\sum_{N \geq 1} e^{N(q-1)(v_N+\eta)} \sum_{B\in\mathcal F_N} \rho(B)^q < +\infty$. Then $\limsup_{N \rightarrow \infty} \left(\frac{\log(\rho(B_N(\boldsymbol{i})))}{-N} - v_N \right) \leq 0$ for $\rho$-almost every $\boldsymbol{i}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma BC of arXiv:2505.11721

[Definition 5 (Finite-\(r\) witnessed hypothesis) of arXiv:2606.08703, '2606.08703'] Let \(0<s<1\).  A nonnegative random variable \(U\) with \(\E U=1\) satisfies
the finite-\(r\) witnessed hypothesis at exponent \(s\) if there exist \(r>1\)
and \(\delta>0\) such that
\begin{equation}
        \E[U^r]<\infty,
        \qquad
        2^{1-r}\E[U^r]\le 2^{-r(s+\delta)}.
\end{equation}
title: Finite-\(r\) witnessed hypothesis

body: The abc conjecture is a conjecture in number theory that arose out of a discussion of Joseph Oesterlé and David Masser in 1985. It is stated in terms of three positive integers and that are relatively prime and satisfy . The conjecture essentially states that the product of the distinct prime factors of cannot often be much smaller than . A number of famous conjectures and theorems in number theory would follow immediately from the abc conjecture or its versions. Mathematician Dorian Goldfeld described the abc conjecture as "The most important unsolved problem in Diophantine analysis".
title: Abc conjecture

body:
[Corollary cor:Bernoulli-Bartlett-component of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] Let $\Gamma\leq\mathbb R^d$ be a lattice and let $(Z,\nu)$ be a
nontrivial Bernoulli $\Gamma$-space. Then the induced space
$\smash{\operatorname{Ind}_\Gamma^{\mathbb R^d}(Z)}$ admits a generating
stealthy Delone cross-section $Y$ whose Bartlett spectrum has the
form
\[
    \sigma_Y
    =
    \sigma_Y^{\mathrm{tor}}
    +
    h\,d\lambda_d,
    \qquad
    \operatorname{supp}\sigma_Y^{\mathrm{tor}}
    \subset\Gamma^*\setminus\{0\},
\]
where $h\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^d)$ is nonnegative and
not identically zero. Moreover, $h$ vanishes almost everywhere on
a neighborhood of the origin.

body: An inner product space is a vector space H over the real or complex numbers with an inner product <x, y> that is linear in its first argument, conjugate-symmetric (<y, x> equals the complex conjugate of <x, y>; symmetric in the real case), and positive definite (<x, x> > 0 for x nonzero). The inner product induces the norm ||x|| = sqrt(<x, x>), and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality |<x, y>| <= ||x|| ||y|| holds. A Hilbert space is an inner product space that is complete with respect to this norm; in particular every Hilbert space is a Banach space. Vectors x and y are orthogonal when <x, y> = 0. Examples: R^n and C^n with the dot product, l^2, and L^2 spaces.
title: Hilbert space

[Lem 13 of arXiv:2608.28355, 'About the contractibility of the walking coinductive equivalence'] Let $\cM$ be a model category, let $F\colon\cM\to\cM$ be a functor, and let $c_0$ be an initial object of $\cM$. If $F$ induces a Quillen adjunction
\begin{equation}

F\colon
\cM
\simeq
{}^{c_0/}\cM
\rightleftarrows
{}^{F(c_0)/}\cM
\noloc G,
\end{equation}
then for all $\ell\geq0$ there is a Quillen adjunction
\[
F^\ell\colon\cM\simeq {}^{c_0/}\cM
\rightleftarrows
{}^{F(c_0)/}\cM
\rightleftarrows
{}^{F^2(c_0)/}\cM
\rightleftarrows
\cdots
\rightleftarrows
{}^{F^\ell(c_0)/}\cM\noloc G^\ell.
\]
where, for $\ell\geq0$, the undercategory ${}^{F^\ell(c_0)/}\cM$ is equipped with the induced model structure of \cite{HirschhornOvercategories}.

[Theorem 4 (\textsf{Local bias bound and finite coordinate support}) of arXiv:2608.12451, '2608.12451'] Let $F\in\cC_d^{\mathsf{R}}$ satisfy the lattice condition \eqref{cond_La}
with shift $\theta\in\R$.
 Assume that, for some
$\eps\in(0,\frac12]$,

\noi
\begin{align}
 \eps\leq p_k\leq1-\eps
 \qquad
 \text{for every $k$ with $\Inf_k(F) > 0$}.
 
\end{align}
Then every  coordinate  $k$ with positive influence
satisfies

\noi
\begin{align}
 d\,d!\Inf_k(F)
 \geq\eps^d(1-\eps),
 
\end{align}
and $F$ depends on at most
$
 \frac{d\,m_2(F)}
 {\eps^d(1-\eps)}
 $
coordinates.  In the symmetric case,
$
 \Inf_k(F)\geq \frac{2^{-(d+1)}}{d\,d!}
$
for every   coordinate $k$ with positive influence.  

Consequently, no sequence of integer-valued shifts
$F_n+\theta_n$ satisfying \eqref{bias_compact}, with fixed $d$,
a common $\eps>0$, and uniformly bounded variances, can converge to a
nondegenerate Poisson law. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Proof (unaudited), standard criterion derived locally. Let s_t take finitely many states, a_t finitely many actions, and e_t in R^d obey e_{t+1}=B(i,a,j)e_t. Given all past variables and s_t=i, assume (a_t,s_{t+1}) has fixed law mu(a|i)P(j|i,a), with deterministic finite matrices B. On tuples of real symmetric matrices define (L X)_j=sum_{i,a} mu(a|i)P(j|i,a) B(i,a,j)X_i B(i,a,j)^T. Then E||e_t||^2 tends to zero for every initial joint law of (s_0,e_0) with finite second moment iff the ordinary spectral radius of L is less than one. This is not an arbitrary-switching joint-spectral-radius condition.

Finite deterministic update matrices
Conditional joint sampling law stated above

[Definition 15 of arXiv:2608.29157, 'Dilator-based analysis of $\KP$'] Let $\alpha,\beta$ be ordinals and $f\colon \alpha\to\beta$ be an increasing function.
    Suppose that $\Gamma$ is a sequent in $\calL_\beta$ such that every ordinal constant symbol occurring in $\Gamma$ takes the form $\overline{f(\xi)}$ for some $\xi\in\alpha$. 
    We define the new $\calL_\alpha$-sequent $\sfm_f(\Gamma)$ obtained from $\Gamma$ by replacing every constant symbol of the form $\overline{f(\xi)}$ with $\overline{\xi}$.
    
    For an $\LK_\beta$-proof $\pi$ of $\Gamma$, let us define its \emph{mutilation} ${}^f\pi$ obtained from $\pi$ by replacing every sequent $\Delta$ occurring in $\pi$ with $\sfm_f(\Delta)$. If the replacement is impossible, remove the corresponding sequent from the proof accordingly.
title: Definition 15 of arXiv:2608.29157

[Theorem 5 (Brenier's Theorem) of arXiv:2608.22746, 'Generative Neural Networks for Sinkhorn Distributionally Robust Hypothesis Testing'] Let $\mu,\nu$ be two finite-second-moment probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$, and assume that $\mu$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure. Then there exists a proper convex function $\varphi:~\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $(\nabla\varphi)_{\#}\mu=\nu$.
In addition, $\nabla\varphi$ is the unique solution to
\[
\inf_{T:~T_{\#}\mu=\nu}\mathbb{E}_{\mu}\|\boldsymbol{x} - T(\boldsymbol{x})\|_2^2,
\]
and $\gamma_{\text{opt}}\sim (\mathrm{Id},\nabla\varphi)_{\#}\mu$ is the unique solution to 
\[
\inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma(\mu,\nu)}~\mathbb{E}_{\gamma}\|\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{y}\|_2^2.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Brenier's Theorem

body:
[Definition def:shape-concate of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] Given shapes $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ that are composable, we take the concatenation $\tau_1 \circ \tau_2$ of $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ to be the shape such that:
\begin{enumerate}
		\item $V(\tau_1 \circ \tau_2) = V(\tau_1) \cup V(\tau_2)$ where the vertices in $V_{\tau_1}$ are identified with the vertices in $U_{\tau_2}$.
        \item $U_{\tau_1 \circ \tau_2} = U_{\tau_1}$ and $V_{\tau_1 \circ \tau_2} = V_{\tau_2}$.
		\item $E(\tau_1 \circ \tau_2) = E(\tau_1) \cup E(\tau_2)$. 
\end{enumerate}

	
This definition extends naturally to a sequence of $k$ shapes $\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_k$ such that for each $j \in [k-1]$, $|V_{\tau_j}| = |U_{\tau_{j+1}}|$. We call this a $k$-way (or $k$-fold) concatenation.  We can obtain the concatenation $\tau_1 \circ \cdots \circ \tau_k$ by concatenating these shapes together one by one (it is not hard to check that the order of the concatenations does not matter).
title: Proper Shape Concatenation

The following table classifies the isotropy formality of $(G, S)$ in terms of $L$. Here $\omega_i$ is the $i$-th fundamental weight of the relevant simple Lie group following the Bourbaki convention.
		\begin{center}
		\begin{tabular}{|c|c|}
		\hline
		$G$&$L$\\
		\hline
		$A_n, n\geq 2, n\neq 3$& $L\in W\cdot \omega_1$\\
		\hline
		$A_3$&$L\in W\cdot \omega_1\cup W\cdot \omega_2$\\
		\hline
		$B_2, C_2$&$\text{Any primitive weight}$\\
		\hline
		$B_n, C_n, n=3, 4$&$L\in W\cdot \omega_1\cup W\cdot \omega_n$\\
		\hline
		$B_n, C_n, n\geq 5$&$L\in W\cdot \omega_1$\\

		$D_4$&$L\in W\cdot\omega_1\cup W\cdot \omega_3\cup W\cdot \omega_4$\\

[Thm t:thm_q of arXiv:2504.07255, 'A Tail-Respecting Splitting Numerical Scheme\\ for L\'evy-Driven SDEs With Superlinear Dri'] Let assumptions
$\mathbf{H}^{\mathrm{Lip}_+}_A$,
$\mathbf{H}_{A_x,A_{xx}}$,
$\mathbf{H}_{a,b,c}^{\mathrm{Lip}_b}$, and
$\mathbf{H}_{\nu,p}$
 hold. Then,
 for any $T\in[0,\infty)$ and $q\in (0,p)$ there is convergence
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
\sup_{t\in[0, T]} \mathbf{E} \|X_t^n-X_t\|^q \leq_C h_n^{\bar \delta}(1+\|x\|^p),\quad x\in\mathbb{R}^d,
\end{aligned}\end{equation}
with the convergence rate
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
\bar\delta=\frac{p-q}{\chi}\wedge\frac{q}{2}\wedge 1.
\end{aligned}\end{equation}
In particular, if $\chi=0$, i.e., if the drift $A$ has bounded first derivatives, the convergence rate reduces to
\begin{equation}\begin{aligned}
\bar\delta=\frac{q}{2}\wedge 1.
\end{aligned}\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm t:thm_q of arXiv:2504.07255

[Thm 2 of arXiv:2511.02763, 'The Cayley-Moser problem with Poissonian arrival of offers'] (1) Let $F,F_0$ be a pair of distributions satisfying \eqref{fm},\eqref{fm0},\eqref{mM}, and $\lambda>0$.
		Then the corresponding optimal policy $\mu: [0,\infty)\rightarrow [0,\infty)$ has the following properties:
		\begin{itemize}
			\item[(i)] $\mu(0)=\mu_0=\int_{-\infty}^\infty xdF_0(x)$ and  $\lim_{t\rightarrow +\infty}\mu(t)=M$, where $M$ is defined by
			\eqref{def_M}.
			
			\item[(ii)] $\mu$ is continuously differentiable.
			
			\item[(iii)] $\mu'$ is absolutely continuous and satisfies $\mu'(t)>0$ for all $t\geq 0$. In particular $\mu$ is strictly monotone increasing.
			
			\item[(iv)] $\mu(t)$ is strictly concave.
			
			\item[(v)] The function \begin{equation}h(t)=-\frac{\mu''(t)}{\mu'(t)}
			\end{equation}
			(which, by (iii),(iv) is defined and positive {\it{a.e.}} on $[0,\infty)$) is a monotone decreasing function.
			
			\item[(vi)] The function $h$ satisfies
			\begin{equation}h(0+)\doteq\lim_{t\rightarrow 0+}h(t)\leq \lambda.
			\end{equation}
		\end{itemize}
		
		(2) Conversely, let $\mu:[0,\infty)\rightarrow [0,\infty)$ be any function
		satisfying (ii),(iii),(iv),(v) and let $\lambda$ satisfy \eqref{h_cond}.  Then, defining
		$M=\lim_{t\rightarrow \infty}\mu(t),$ there 
		exists a distribution $F$ satisfying 
		\eqref{fm}, such that for any distribution $F_0$ satisfying \eqref{fm0} with $E[X_0]=\mu(0)$, we have that 
		$\mu(t)$ is the optimal policy corresponding to $F,F_0$, and $\lambda$.

body: Let (M,g) be a Riemannian manifold with Levi-Civita connection nabla. A smooth curve gamma: I -> M on an interval I subset R is a geodesic if its velocity field is parallel along itself: nabla_{gamma'(t)} gamma'(t) = 0 for every t in I. Equivalently, in local coordinates x^1,...,x^n a curve gamma(t) = (x^1(t),...,x^n(t)) is a geodesic iff it satisfies the second-order ODE system d^2x^k/dt^2 + sum_{i,j} Gamma^k_{ij}(gamma(t)) (dx^i/dt)(dx^j/dt) = 0 for k=1,...,n, where Gamma^k_{ij} are the Christoffel symbols of g. Geodesics are the critical points of the energy functional among curves with fixed endpoints, and, when locally minimizing, are the locally shortest paths between nearby points.
title: Geodesic

[Prop 78 of arXiv:2604.00635, 'Large deviations of the periodic Toda chain'] Let $p \geq 1$, $U\in \mc{C}^0(\R)$ be such that  $\Int{\mathbb{R}}{}\mathrm{e}^{-U(x)} \, \mathrm{d}x = 1$.
 Then, upon fixing the notation $\mc{L}n_0(x)= \ln \big( x  \wedge 1\big) $ for $x \geq 0$, one has that the $N$-fold integral

$$

C_N^{(p)} [U] = \Int{\mathbb{R}^N }{}

\varpi_p(\bs{x}_N)

\pl{k=1}{N} \mathrm{e}^{- U(x_k)}\, \mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{x}_N \;, \quad

\varpi_p(\bs{x}_N) \, = \, \pl{j=1}{N} \bigg\{ 1 + \frac{1}{ N^{\frac{5}{4}}} \sum_{\substack{i=1 \\ i \neq j}}^N \mc{L}n_0^2|x_i - x_j| \bigg\}^p

$$

admits the upper bound $C_N^{(p)} [U] \leq \mathrm{e}^{C N^{\frac{3}{4}}\ln^2 N}$ for some $C>0$ and any $N$ large enough. $C$ may depend on $p$ and $U$.

body: In mathematics, Schur's lemma is an elementary but useful statement in representation theory of groups and algebras. In the group case it says that if M and N are two finite-dimensional irreducible representations of a group G and φ is a linear map from M to N that commutes with the action of the group, then either φ is invertible, or φ = 0. An important special case occurs when M = N, i.e. φ is a self-map; in particular, for representations over an algebraically closed field (e.g. $\mathbb {C}$), any element of the center of a group must act as a scalar operator (a scalar multiple of the identity) on M. The lemma is named after Issai Schur who used it to prove the Schur orthogonality relations and develop the basics of the representation theory of finite groups. Schur's lemma admits generalisations to Lie groups and Lie algebras, the most common of which are due to Jacques Dixmier and Daniel Quillen.

[Definition def:pll-extrinsic-frames of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] An f-frame $\mathfrak{F} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset)$ is \emph{weakly $\sqsubset$-dense} if
  ${\sqsubset} \subseteq (\sqsubset \cdot \sqsubset \cdot \leq)$,
  that is, for any $x \sqsubset y$, there are $u, z \in W$ such that
  $x \sqsubset u \sqsubset z \leq y$.
  We say $\mathfrak{F}$ is a \emph{$\textbf{PLL}$-frame} if it is $\Box$-p, $\sqsubset$-strong,
  and weakly $\sqsubset$-dense.

$$\sup_{0\leq s\leq t\leq 1}\|\delta A_{s,t}\|_{L_p(\Omega|\sF_s)}\leq N.$$
Then we have

(ii) For every $\bar{p}\in (0,p)$, there exists a constant $c_{\bar{p},p}$ such that 
$$\|\sup_{t\in[0,1]}|A_t|\|_{L_{\bar{p}}(\Omega)}\leq c_{\bar{p},p}N.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 3 (Regularity in the solvable model classes) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] The regularity conditions of
Theorem~\ref{thm:fixed-r-entropy-dissipation}, together with the endpoint
limits used below, hold in either of the following settings.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(P_0=\sum_{i=1}^n\pi_i\delta_{x_i}\) has finite support with
\(\pi_i>0\), and \(P_0(\cdot\mid r)=\sum_iw_i(r)\delta_{x_i}\).
If the support points are pairwise distinct, then
\[
\lim_{t\to0^+}\mathcal K_t(r)
=\sum_{i=1}^n w_i(r)\log\frac{w_i(r)}{\pi_i}.
\]
\item \(P_0=\calN(\mu,\Sigma)\) and
\(P_0(\cdot\mid r)=\calN(\mu_r,S_r)\), with
\(\Sigma\succ0\) and \(S_r\succ0\).
\end{enumerate}
In both cases \(\lim_{t\to\infty}\mathcal K_t(r)=0\).  On every compact
interval \(0<s<t<\infty\), the reverse path laws below have finite relative
entropy. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Regularity in the solvable model classes

\]

[Lemma lem GRR inequality of arXiv:2604.10509, 'Nonequilibrium fluctuations and moderate deviations for the occupation time of the SSEP wi'] Assume that $g: [0,T] \rightarrow \mathbb R$ is continuous and $g(0) = 0$, and that $\varphi (u), p(u)$ are strictly increasing functions such that
	\[\varphi (0) = p(0) = 0, \quad \lim_{u \rightarrow + \infty} \varphi (u) = + \infty.\]
	Then,
	\[\sup_{0 \leq t \leq T} |g(t)| \leq 8 \int_0^T \varphi^{-1} \big(4B/u^2\big) p(du),\]
	where
	\[B= \int_0^T ds \int_0^T dt \varphi \Big(\frac{|g(t)-g(s)|}{p(|t-s|)}\Big).\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2609.02017, 'Optimal girth-dependent bounds for the Bethe approximation of the permanent'] Let $g\geq4$ be even, and let
$A\in\R_{\geq0}^{n\times n}$ be a nonnegative matrix whose support
graph has girth at least $g$. Then
\[
  \on{Bethe}(A)
  \leq\on{per}(A)
  \leq2^{2n/g}\on{Bethe}(A).
\]
Moreover, whenever $g\mid2n$, the upper bound is attained by the
$0$--$1$ matrices whose support graphs are disjoint unions of cycles
of length $g$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2609.02017

[Proposition pr:moments of arXiv:2411.09381, 'On the well-posedness of SPDEs with locally Lipschitz coefficients'] If $L_{\sigma}>0$, then
	\[
		\sup_{N>0}\sup_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\mathrm{E}\left( |u_N(t\,,x)|^k\right) \le
		4^k(\|u_0\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb{R})}+ 1)^k\mathrm{e}^{128 L_{\sigma}^4 k^3t}.
	\]
	uniformly for all $t>0$ and $k\ge \max(2\,, L_b^{1/2} L_{\sigma}^{-2})$.

[Proposition prop:sc-scalar-HM of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] Let $(c_k, \lambda_k)$ be a scalar solution of the
semi-discrete diamond equations
(equation eq:sc-diamond-C of the paper)--(equation eq:sc-diamond-mixed of the paper) and
the fully discrete diamond equations of
Proposition~\textup{(prop:CL-gen-system of the paper)},
and let $F(u) = \det_H(I - zK(u))$ be as in
Corollary~\textup{(cor:sc-Woodbury of the paper)}.
Assume the boundary
conditions\footnote{These boundary conditions are natural in
the probabilistic applications of Chapter~(ch:semi-discrete-model-verifications of the paper).}
$\lim_{\ell \to -\infty} F(T^\ell v) = 1$ and
$\lim_{\ell \to -\infty} \partial_1 F(T^\ell v) = 0$ for all
$v \in \mathcal{V}$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}, leftmargin=*]
\item For each pair $i, j \geq 2$, assume
$\alpha_{ij}(u) \neq 0$ and
$\alpha_{ij}(u) \neq \alpha_{ji}(u)$ for all
$u \in \mathcal{V}$ and $i \neq j$, with the same
conditions holding for the limits
$\lim_{\ell \to -\infty} \alpha_{ij}(T^\ell v)$, which are
assumed to exist.  Then the fully discrete
mixed diamond equation reduces
to the scalar Hirota--Miwa equation with variable coefficients:
\begin{equation}
\alpha_{ij}(u)F(S_i u)F(TS_j u)
- \alpha_{ji}(u)F(S_j u)F(TS_i u)
- \bigl(\alpha_{ij}(u) - \alpha_{ji}(u)\bigr)
  F(Tu)F(S_i S_j u) = 0.
\end{equation}

\item For each $j \geq 2$, assume that $c_j(u) \neq 0$,
$F$ is $C^1$ in the continuous variable, and that
$\lim_{\ell \to -\infty} \alpha_j(T^\ell u)$ exists and is
finite, for all $u \in \mathcal{V}$.  Then the
semi-discrete mixed
diamond equation (equation eq:sc-diamond-mixed of the paper) reduces to the
bilinear differential-difference equation:
\begin{equation}
F(Tu)\partial_1 F(S_j u)
- F(S_j u)\partial_1 F(Tu)
+ \alpha_j(u)
\bigl[F(Tu)F(S_j u) - F(u)F(TS_j u)\bigr] = 0.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 3.3 of arXiv:2110.05374, 'When Janson meets McDiarmid: Bounded difference inequalities under graph-dependence'] (A step in the proof of Theorem 2.1; setting as in Lemma 3.2.) For i ∈ [n−1] let Ω-valued random vectors Y^{(i)}, Z^{(i)} be jointly distributed so that (C1) Y^{(i)}_{[i]} = x_{[i]}; (C2) Y^{(i)}_{[i+1,n]} has the conditional law of X_{[i+1,n]} given X_{[i]} = x_{[i]}; (C3) Z^{(i)}_{[i]} = x^{(i)}_{[i]} and Z^{(i)}_{S_i} = Y^{(i)}_{S_i}; (C4) given Z^{(i)}_{S_i} = ω_{S_i}, Z^{(i)}_{p_i} has the conditional law of X_{p_i} given X_{[i]} = x^{(i)}_{[i]} and X_{S_i} = ω_{S_i}. Then for every i ∈ [n−1] and ω_{[i+1,n]} ∈ Ω_{[i+1,n]}: (A1) P(Y^{(i)}_{[i+1,n]} = ω_{[i+1,n]}) = P(X_{[i+1,n]} = ω_{[i+1,n]} | X_{[i]} = x_{[i]}); (A2) P(Z^{(i)}_{[i+1,n]} = ω_{[i+1,n]}) = P(X_{[i+1,n]} = ω_{[i+1,n]} | X_{[i]} = x^{(i)}_{[i]}). So (Y^{(i)}, Z^{(i)}) is a coupling (Marton-type) of the two conditional laws of X in which the two vectors differ at most in coordinates i and p_i; (A2) uses Lemma 3.2.
G-dependent (Definition 1.3 of the paper): X = (X_i)_{i∈V(G)} is G-dependent when for all disjoint S, T ⊂ V(G) with no edge of G between S and T, the families (X_i)_{i∈S} and (X_j)_{j∈T} are independent; this is stronger than pairwise independence of non-adjacent coordinates.
Proof setting (Section 3 of the paper): G is a dependency tree on [n] that is Rooted (rooted at vertex n, with c_n = c_min) and Ordered (j is a descendant of i only if j < i), which a topological sort always provides; p_i is the parent of a non-root vertex i, S_i := [i+1, n] \ {p_i}, and for x ∈ Ω and x'_i ∈ Ω_i, x^{(i)} := (x_1, ..., x_{i−1}, x'_i, x_{i+1}, ..., x_n). The paper writes conditional probabilities of point events; for non-discrete Ω_i read them as conditional distributions.

[Theorem 13 (Pointwise macroscopic-loop criterion) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Let \(G_n\) be a random simple graph on \([n]\). Fix \(u\in[0,1]\) and
\(\theta\in\mathbb N\) with \(\theta>1\). Assume that \((G_n)_n\) satisfies
Assumption~\ref{ass:sparse-random-graph}, with limiting edge density \(\alpha\), and that $\alpha>c_{\theta,u}$.
Then for every \(\delta>0\) there exist \(\eta>0\) and \(c>0\) such that for every
\[
t\ge \frac{\theta\log\theta}{(\theta-1)(\alpha-c_{\theta,u})}+\delta,
\]
one has
\[
\Pbb\!\left(
\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\ge c
\right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Pointwise macroscopic-loop criterion

PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. Let T_a(x1,...,xr)=sum_j a_j product_k xk_j, with every xk in the l_p unit ball. Its multilinear norm is ||a||_infinity for p<=r and ||a||_q for p>r, q=p/(p-r), with q=1 at p=infinity. For the homogeneous polynomial using one repeated vector, the same identities hold for p<=r and for odd r. For even r and p>r the polynomial norm is max(||a_+||_q,||a_-||_q), so it is within factor 2^(1/q) of the multilinear norm. Explicit Holder optimizers prove all identities; the mixed-sign example r=2,p=infinity,a=(1,-1) has norms two and one.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:18e77ca7ea95c10287bd55798f7f5c8d7fc3f215443bead62d473b79b41b4a1d","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/18/18e77ca7ea95c10287bd55798f7f5c8d7fc3f215443bead62d473b79b41b4a1d.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:ca8e01022fc1ce72db5fc3e7129e770ab9870b7ba760aec7214981549babe3f3","bundle_entry_key":"diagonal-tensor-multilinear-and-polynomial-norm-identities","bundle_id":"population.w340-ten-problem-scoped-progress-20261010","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"w340/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian:diagonal-tensor-multilinear-and-polynomial-norm-identities","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# P0012: diagonal multilinear tensors, all p>=2

Label: proof for diagonal tensors in both the multilinear and homogeneous polynomial conventions, awaiting w346. The cached source defines I_p using one repeated vector; the last paragraph below covers that convention. No assertion about all symmetric tensors is made.

Let r>=2 be an integer and T_a(x1,...,xr)=sum_(j=1)^d a_j product_(k=1)^r xk_j. Define ||T||_(I_p)=sup {|T(x1,...,xr)|: ||xk||_p<=1 for every k}, with p in [2,infinity]. This is a multilinear norm; it must not be confused with the same-vector polynomial norm for even degree and mixed signs.

If p<=r, ||T_a||_(I_p)=||a||_infinity: Holder with r equal exponents bounds the sum of products by product ||xk||_r<=1, and a coordinate vector attains the largest coefficient. If p>r, let q=p/(p-r) (q=1 at p=infinity). Generalized Holder gives ||T_a||_(I_p)=||a||_q. For finite p equality is attained by choosing all coordinate magnitudes proportional to |a_j|^(1/(p-r)) and putting each coefficient's sign in the first vector. For p=infinity choose every magnitude one and signs in the first vector.

For diagonal tensors T_i=T_(a_i) and independent standard Gaussians g_i, put Z_j=sum_i g_i a_(i,j) and sigma_j^2=sum_i a_(i,j)^2. The coordinate Gaussians can be correlated; independence across j is not needed.

If p<=r, the Gaussian exponential-moment union bound gives

E||sum_i g_i T_i||_(I_p) <= sqrt(2 log(2d)) [sum_i ||T_i||_(I_p)^2]^(1/2).

If p>r and q>=2, Jensen and Gaussian moments give E||Z||_q <= c_q ||sigma||_q, where c_q=(E|g|^q)^(1/q). Minkowski in l_(q/2) gives ||sigma||_q <= [sum_i ||a_i||_q^2]^(1/2).

If p>r and 1<=q<2, use ||Z||_q<=d^(1/q-1/2)||Z||_2, E||Z||_2 <= [sum_i ||a_i||_2^2]^(1/2), and ||a_i||_2<=||a_i||_q. The result is

E||sum_i g_i T_i||_(I_p) <= d^(1/2-r/p) [sum_i ||T_i||_(I_p)^2]^(1/2),

with 1/p=0 at infinity. At q=2 the dimension factor is one. The exponent max(1/2-r/p,0) is no larger than the target 1/2-1/p, so this proves the desired dimension bound throughout the diagonal multilinear family, extending the old diagonal p<=r calculation. It leaves off-diagonal tensors unresolved.

The homogeneous polynomial convention can also be covered explicitly. Define P_p(a)=sup_(||x||_p<=1) |sum_j a_j x_j^r|. For p<=r it is again ||a||_infinity. For p>r, with q as above, odd r permits each sign to be selected in x, so P_p(a)=||a||_q. For even r, P_p(a)=max(||a_+||_q,||a_-||_q), because x_j^r is nonnegative and each sign-support optimization is Holder duality. Hence ||a||_q<=2^(1/q) P_p(a), while P_p(Z)<=||Z||_q. Applying the multilinear Gaussian estimates yields the same type-2 bounds for diagonal homogeneous forms, with an additional factor at most two for even r and p>r. This avoids importing an incorrect mixed-sign polynomial norm identity. For example r=2,p=infinity,a=(1,-1) has multilinear norm two and polynomial norm one.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:531a5ddd276062b8b8612e5e597231bc49324742e8374f26aff0274068818a3d","revision_digest":"sha256:31f11c32e33972a0c67c36c26fe8e97f3ddf7be6388d2f088c5184987719fea8","source_id":"own-work:w340:diagonal-tensor-multilinear-and-polynomial-norm-identities","source_revision":"2026-10-10-source-convention-confirmed-draft-awaiting-w346","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body:
[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2609.01681, 'Large induced subgraphs with $k$ vertices of maximum degree'] Let \(G\) be a graph on \(n\) vertices and let \(t\) be an integer with
\(0<t<n\). Choose an \((n-t)\)-vertex subset \(S\subseteq V(G)\) that
minimizes \(e(G[S])\), and set \(D=V(G)\setminus S\). For every integer
\(k\ge2\) there exists a constant \(c_3=c_3(k)\) such that the following
holds: if for some integer \(x\) the set
\(\{v\in D : d_S(v)=x\}\)
contains an independent set $D'$ of order at least \(c_3\), then
\(s_k(G)\le |D|+2k(k-1)\).
title: Lemma 7 of arXiv:2609.01681

[Proposition 2ndOrDerSph of arXiv:2507.08692, 'Some notes on higher order concentration of measure'] The intrinsic second derivative of $f$ at each $\theta \in {\mathbb S}^{n-1}$ is the symmetric matrix which is given by the orthogonal projection
	\[
	f_S''(\theta) = P_{\theta^\perp} B, \qquad B = f''(\theta) - \langle \theta, \nabla f(\theta)\rangle I_n,
	\]
	to the orthogonal complement of the linear subspace $L = L_\theta$ of all symmetric matrices $C$ in $\mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ such that $\langle Cx, x \rangle = 0$ for all $x \in T_\theta$. Equivalently,
	\[
	f_S''(\theta) = P_{\theta^\perp} B P_{\theta^\perp}.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem Burkholder-Davis-Gundy of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] For any \(1\leq p<\infty\), there exist two positive constants \(c_p\) and \(C_p\) such that for any continuous local martingale \(M\) with \(M_0=0\),
	\[
		c_p \mathbb{E}\left[ [M]_t^{p/2} \right] \leq \mathbb{E}\Vert M \Vert^p_{\ast, t}  \leq C_p \mathbb{E} \left[[M]_{t}^{p/2}\right],
	\]
	where \([M]_t\) denotes the quadratic variation of \(M\) at time \(t\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Burkholder-Davis-Gundy

Then the following conditions are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (1)]
\item The stratum $\Lambda_{I}$ is $\bm{w}$-bounded below.
\item The linear functional $\bm{\omega}=B^{T}\bm{w}$ is nonnegative on the recession cone $R_{\Lambda,I}$.
\item The stratum $\Lambda_{I}$ has a unique $\bm{w}$-minimum.
\end{enumerate}

	\begin{subequations}

			& \eqdef \{ (t,u,x^2,x^3) \in \R\times\R\times\T^2 \ | \ \timefunction(t,u,x^2,x^3) 
			= 
			\timefunction', \ u \in J \},
			\\
			\twoargroughtori{\timefunction',u}{0}
			& 
			\eqdef 
			\{ (t,u,x^2,x^3) \ | \ 
			(t,x^2,x^3) \in \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{T}^2,
			\,
			\timefunction(t,u,x^2,x^3) 
			= 
			\timefunction' 
			\},
			
			\\
			\nullhypthreearg{0}{u}{I} 
			& 
			\eqdef 
			\bigcup_{\timefunction' \in I} \twoargroughtori{\timefunction',u}{0},
			 
			\\
			\twoargMrough{I,J}{0} 
			& 
			\eqdef \bigcup_{\timefunction' \in I} \hypthreearg{\timefunction'}{J}{0} 
			= 
			\bigcup_{u' \in J} \nullhypthreearg{0}{u'}{I}.
			
		\end{align}
	\end{subequations}

body:
[Theorem 10 of arXiv:2607.28215, 'Almost stochastic dominance via optimal transport'] Assume that $\gamma\in [0,1]$, $X\le_{\gamma,g} Y$ for $X,Y\in \mathcal{L}_{c,g}(E)$ with $\E[g(X)]< \E[g(Y)]$, and that there exists a metric $d$ on $E$ such that $c\le d$ and
\[
|\E[g(\hat X)]-\E[g(\hat Y)]|\le \mathrm{OT}_d(\hat X,\hat Y)\quad \text{ for all } \hat X,\hat Y\in \mathcal{L}_g(E).
\]
If $\mathrm{OT}_d(Y,\tilde Y)\le \epsilon \le \E[g(Y)]-\E[g(X)]$ for some $\tilde{Y}\in \mathcal{L}_{c,g}(E)$, then we have
\begin{align*}
\gamma^\ast(X,\tilde Y;g)\le  \tilde{\gamma} :=  \gamma+\frac{(1-\gamma)\epsilon}{\E[g(Y)]-\E[g(X)]}.
\end{align*}
Analogously, if $\mathrm{OT}_d(X,\tilde X)\le \epsilon \le \E[g(Y)]-\E[g(X)]$ for some $\tilde X\in \mathcal{L}_{c,g}(E)$, then we have $\gamma^\ast(\tilde X, Y;g)\le  \tilde{\gamma}$ for the same $\tilde{\gamma}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 10 of arXiv:2607.28215

body: [Lemma giant of arXiv:2606.27844, 'Critical percolation on preferential attachment graphs with infinite variance'] Let $(m_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be a sequence of integers such that $m_n\le n$ for all $n$ and $m_n\to\infty$. body:
[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2608.22693, 'Uniformity of extremal behaviour along geodesics in Liouville quantum gravity'] Fix $\gamma \in (0,2)$ and $\alpha \in [-2,2]$, and let $h$ be a whole-plane GFF. Then, there exist deterministic constants $\Delta^{\mathrm{Euc}},\Delta_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{Euc}},\Delta_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{LQG}},\chi,\chi',\alpha_{\mathrm{min}}$, and $\alpha_{\mathrm{max}}$, such that we have the following. Fix $\bz\in \CC$ and let $P: [0,T] \to \CC$ be any $D_h$-geodesic starting from $\bz$ and parametrised to have unit speed with respect to its $D_h$-length. Then the following hold almost surely.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item 
  $\dim_{\mathrm{Euc}}(P)=\Delta^{\mathrm{Euc}}$,
  \item 
  $\dim_{\mathrm{Euc}}(P\cap \cT_h^{\alpha})= \Delta^{\mathrm{Euc}}_{\alpha}$ and $\dim_{\mathrm{LQG}}(P\cap \cT^\alpha_h)= \Delta^{\mathrm{LQG}}_{\alpha}$,
  \item 
  $\chi(P)=\chi$ and $\chi(P)=\chi'$,
  \item 
  $\alpha_{\mathrm{max}}(P)=\alpha_{\mathrm{max}}$ and $\alpha_{\mathrm{min}}(P)=\alpha_{\mathrm{min}}$.
 \end{enumerate}

[Lemma theo3lemm2_2 of arXiv:2607.19651, 'Metastability and phase transition in a social network model with multiple opinions'] For any $t>0$, for any $o \in \mathcal{O}$, the following holds for any $0<\alpha<\frac{1}{M-1}$.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item For any $l\in \mathcal{L}^{o}_{\alpha}$,
    $$
    {\mathbb P}(R^{\alpha,\beta,l}(\mathcal{C}^{-o}_{\alpha})>t) \geq  e^{-2tN^3(M+1)^3e^{-\frac{\beta}{2}\gamma}}.
    $$
    \item For any $u\in \mathcal{C}^{o}_{\alpha}$,
    $$
    {\mathbb P}(R^{\alpha,\beta,u}(\mathcal{C}^{-o}_{\alpha})\leq t) \leq (N^2M+2tN^3(M+1)^3)e^{-\frac{\beta}{2}\gamma}.
    $$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, Supermodular ordering of speeded-up Markov chains without stochastic monotonicity (October 2026). For a stationary continuous-time Markov chain with real values, let the chain run at speed c. Leskela (Queueing Systems 100 (2022), 213-215, Problem 3) asked whether some stationary ergodic chain that is not stochastically monotone becomes smaller in the supermodular order of processes as it is speeded up. The paper shows that such chains exist on three states: a chain that leaves its smallest value for either of the other two values at any positive rates and returns from both at a common rate has this property and is not stochastically monotone. If the largest value returns faster than the middle one, the property fails already for pairs of sampling times. For reversible three-state chains with two distinct nonzero eigenvalues, the pairs are ordered exactly when the slow left eigenvector does not have the same strict sign at the two extreme states. Exact certificate identities, symbolic spectral formulas, linear programs over supermodular functions and a Lean 4 file accompany the paper. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/supermodular-speed-ordering (commit e1afd4de9728). Not refereed.
title: A three-state Markov chain that is not stochastically monotone yet becomes smaller in the supermodular order when speeded up, answering Leskela's Problem 3 (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/supermodular-speed-ordering)

	\begin{equation}
		
		\mathbb{E} \left[ \sum_{i \in I} f((x,H)_i) \right] =
		\lambda \cdot \sum_{ x \in V } \sum_{H \in \mathcal{H}_x}  f \left( (x,H) \right) \cdot \nu \left( (x,H) \right).
	\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: A partition P = {V_1, ..., V_k} of the vertex set V of a graph G is epsilon-regular if the sum of |V_i||V_j| over the pairs (V_i, V_j) that are not epsilon-regular is at most epsilon |V(G)|^2.

[Prop one row and one column cores of arXiv:2607.19658, 'Hitting time mixing for random $k$-cycles'] Suppose that $r=o(n^{1/2})$. Then
$$
\sum_{\substack{\lambda\vdash n,\ \lambda\neq(n),(1^n)\\
\lambda/(r)\text{ is a rim hook of size }n-r}}
\frac{1}{d_\lambda^2}=O\left(\frac{r^2}{n}\right)=o(1).
$$
Similarly,
$$
\sum_{\substack{\lambda\vdash n,\ \lambda\neq(n),(1^n)\\
\lambda/(1^r)\text{ is a rim hook of size }n-r}}\frac{1}{d_\lambda^2}=O\left(\frac{r^2}{n}\right)=o(1).
$$
title: Prop one row and one column cores of arXiv:2607.19658

[Lemma 17 of arXiv:2604.25877, 'Asymptotic height of Plancherel random trees'] Fix $n\ge 2$ and $h\ge 0$, and let $M:=M_{r_n}$ with $r_n$ as in \eqref{eq:rn}.
Then, we have
\begin{align}
q_n(h)&\le \frac{\mathbb E[q_{M+1}(h)]}{\mathbb P(M\le n-1)};\\
q_n(h)&\ge \frac{\mathbb E[q_{M+1}(h)]-\mathbb P(M\le n-2)}{\mathbb P(M\ge n-1)}.
\end{align}
Consequently, for any sequence of integers $(h(n))_{n \geq 0}$, 
\begin{align}

\left(\mathbb E[q_{M_{r_n}+1}(h(n))]\to_{n \to \infty} 0\right) \ 
&\Longrightarrow\
\left(q_n(h(n))\to_{n \to \infty} 0\right),
\\
\left(\mathbb E[q_{M_{r_n}+1}(h(n))]\to_{n \to \infty} 1\right) \
&\Longrightarrow\ \left( q_n(h(n))\to_{n \to \infty}  1\right).\nonumber
\end{align}

[Lem gauss_cond of arXiv:2412.10001, 'On the Markov transformation of Gaussian processes'] Let $(m,n)$ be in ${\mathbb{N}^*} \times \mathbb{N}^*$. 
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item Fix  $\pi \in\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^{m+n})$ a Gaussian measure and set $\mu := {\textnormal{proj}^{1, \cdots,m}}_\# \pi$, $\nu := {\textnormal{proj}^{m+1, \cdots,m+n}}_\# \pi$, $\Sigma_{\pi} := \Sigma_{\pi}^{m,n} \in \mathcal{M}_{m,n}(\mathbb{R})$. If $\mu \in \mathcal{G}_m^*$ and $k : \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is a probability kernel such that $\pi(dx,dy) = \mu(dx)k_x(dy)$, then \[\mu(dx)-\textnormal{a.s.} , \ k_x = \mathcal{N}\left(\Sigma_{\pi}^t \Sigma_\mu^{-1}x, \Sigma_\nu- \Sigma_{\pi}^t \Sigma_\mu^{-1}\Sigma_{\pi}\right).\]
			\item Consider $\mu \in \mathcal{G}_m^*$, $(A,\Gamma) \in \mathcal{M}_{n,m}(\mathbb{R}) \times \mathcal{M}_n(\mathbb{R})$ and $k : x \in \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathcal{N}(Ax,\Gamma) \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^n)$. Then, writing $\pi(dx,dy) = \mu(dx)k_x(dy)$, we have \[ \pi = \mathcal{N}\left( 0_{\mathbb{R}^{m+n}},\begin{pmatrix}
				\Sigma_\mu & \Sigma_\mu A^t \\ A \Sigma_\mu & \Gamma + A \Sigma_\mu A^t
			\end{pmatrix}\right) \in \mathcal{G}_{m+n}.\]
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 45 of arXiv:2609.02065, '\textbf{From Bowditch's question to Goldman's conjecture for type-preserving representatio'] For $m_1, n_1, m_2, n_2 \in \mathbb{Z}$, let $\mathbb{B}_{m_1}\times \mathbb{B}_{n_1}$ and $\mathbb{B}_{m_2}\times \mathbb{B}_{n_2}$ be adjacent blocks. Let $\widetilde{C}\in \univcover$. Assume that the fiber $P^{-1}(\widetilde{C})$ intersects both the blocks. 
  \begin{enumerate}[(1)]
      \item If the blocks are edge-adjacent, then $P^{-1}(\widetilde{C})$ intersects their common edge.

      \item If the blocks are vertex-adjacent, then $P^{-1}(\widetilde{C})$ intersects either their common vertex or an edge incident to the common vertex.
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

    We first prove the claim for a fixed $(\lambda,\mu) \in \Lambda$, where $\epsilon'$ for now is permitted to depend on $(\lambda,\mu)$.

    where $\overline{S}$ denotes the closure of $S$ relative to the topology of $\cD_\mu$. This forms a nested family of nonempty compact sets indexed by $\epsilon' > 0$, so the intersection

        S_\star(\lambda,\mu)[\epsilon'] \cap \overline{S_\star\bigg(\lambda,\mu;
        	\frac\epsilon5, \frac\epsilon{3}\bigg)^c}\bigg\}
        = S_\star(\lambda,\mu) \cap

	\[

	+ \frac\epsilon5 \alpha^2\iota^3 (\|\vBBb\|_2)^2

	\]
This proves that for any fixed $(\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda$, the claim holds for some $\epsilon'>0$ that may depend on $(\lambda,\mu)$.

fix $(\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda$ and abbreviate $\epsilon'=\epsilon'(\lambda,\mu)$, so that we have

	\]

[Definition eq:sibling-reduced-PDE of arXiv:2607.29330, 'Large deviations for the maximum of\\ the generalized TAP free energy'] Fix \(r\in(0,q)\). For \(\mathbf{m}\in(-1,1)^N\), define \(b_i\) by
		\[
		m_i=\partial_x\Phi_\zeta(q,b_i),
		\qquad 1\le i\le N.
		\]
		Let \(\rho\) be a finite-step probability measure on \([r,q]\), and write
		\[
		\bar x_\rho(t)
		=
		\theta+(1-\theta)\rho([r,t]),
		\qquad r\le t<q.
		\]
		Let \(\phi_\rho\) solve on \([r,q]\)
		\begin{equation}
			\begin{aligned}
				\partial_t\phi_\rho
				+\frac{\xi''(t)}2
				\left(
				\partial_{xx}\phi_\rho
				+\bar x_\rho(t)(\partial_x\phi_\rho)^2
				\right)&=0,\\
				\phi_\rho(q,x)&=\Phi_\zeta(q,x).
			\end{aligned}
		\end{equation}
		For
		\[
		Z\sim\mathcal N\left(
		0,\xi'(r)-\frac{\xi'(r)^2}{\xi'(q)}
		\right),
		\]
		define
		\[
		\begin{aligned}
			\mathcal J_{N,\mathbf{m},q,r}(\rho)
			:={}&
			\theta\bigl[\xi(r)-r\xi'(r)-\xi(q)+q\xi'(q)\bigr]
			-\frac1N\sum_i\Phi_\zeta(q,b_i)\\
			&+\frac1N\sum_i
			\mathbb{E}_Z\phi_\rho\left(
			r,Z+\frac{\xi'(r)}{\xi'(q)}b_i
			\right)
			-\frac12\int_r^q t\xi''(t)\bar x_\rho(t)\,\mathrm{d} t.
		\end{aligned}
		\]
title: Definition eq:sibling-reduced-PDE of arXiv:2607.29330

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.22597, 'Scale-invariant Optimal Sampling for Rare-events Data with Sparse Models'] Under Assumptions~\ref{asm:a1}-\ref{asm:a3},~\ref{asm:a4}, and~\ref{asm:a6}, if
$\alpha_{\rt}\geq C\log\{\max\{s_{N},\log p_{N}\}/N\}$, where $C$ is a
constant, the
IPW adaptive lasso estimator in~\eqref{eq:w-las} has the
following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[1.]
\item Consistency in variable selection: The estimated active set
  $\hat{\cA}_{\rw}:=\{j:\hat{\beta}_{\rw(j)}^{\radp}\neq0\}$ satisfies that
  $\lim_{N\to\infty}\Pr(\hat{\cA}_{\rw}=\cA)=1$.
\item 
  Asymptotic normality: If $(\sqrt{s_{N}}\lambda_{N})/\sqrt{N_{1}}\to0$, the
  estimator of the active parameter vector satisfies that for any
  $s_{N}$-dimensional vector $\bm{e}_{N}$ with $\|\bm{e}_{N}\|=1$,
\begin{equation*}
\sqrt{N_1}\bm{e}_{N}\tp\V_{\rw(\cA)}^{-1/2}(\htheta_{\rw(\cA)}^{\radp}-\btheta_{\rt(\cA)})\cvd
\Nor(0,1),
\end{equation*}
where
$\V_{\rw(\cA)}=\Exp\left\{e^{f(\x;\bbeta_{\rt})}\right\}\M_{(\cA)}^{-1}\M_{\rw(\cA)}\M_{(\cA)}^{-1}
=\Exp\left\{e^{f(\x;\bbeta_{\rt})}\right\}\left\{\M_{(\cA)}^{-1}+c\V_{\mathrm{sub}(\cA)}\right\}$,
$\M_{(\cA)}=\Exp\left\{e^{f(\x;\bbeta_{\rt})}\dg_{(\cA)}^{\otimes2}(\x;\btheta_{\rt})\right\}$,
$\V_{\mathrm{sub}(\cA)}=\M_{(\cA)}^{-1}
\Exp\left\{\frac{e^{2f(\x;\bbeta_{\rt})}}{\varphi(\x)}
\dg_{(\cA)}^{\otimes2}(\x;\btheta_{\rt})\right\}\M_{(\cA)}^{-1}$, $c=\lim_{N\to\infty}e^{\alpha_{\rt}}/\rho<\infty$, and $\dg_{(\cA)}(\x;\btheta_{\rt})$ consists of the elements of gradient
vector $\dg(\x;\btheta_{\rt})$ with indexes in the active set $\cA$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.22597

[Theorem 3 ($\ell^p$ matrix deviation inequality) of arXiv:2506.09333, 'On the Dimension-Free Concentration of Simple Tensors via Matrix Deviation'] Let $p\ge 2$. Let $A \in \R^{N\times d}$ be a random matrix whose rows are i.i.d. copies of a mean-zero isotropic subgaussian random vector $Z \in \mathbb{R}^d$. Consider the stochastic process
    \begin{equation*}
        Z_v
        \coloneqq \abs*{\norm{Av}_{p}-N^{1/p}\norm{\ip{Z}{v}}_{L^p}}, \quad v \in \R^d.
    \end{equation*}
Then $Z_v$ has Lipschitz subgaussian increments:
    \begin{equation*}
        \norm{Z_v-Z_u}_\psitwo 
        \lesssim_{K,p} \norm{u-v}_2
        \quad \text{for every } u,v \in \R^d.
    \end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: $\ell^p$ matrix deviation inequality

body:
[Lemma 6 (Signed transport and one-side-fixed composition) of arXiv:2608.31157, 'Sharp Approximation Rates for Neural Networks with Affine Latent Parameterizations'] The following operations preserve affine dependence of network parameters on a
common code vector.
\begin{enumerate}[label={\textup{(\roman*)}}]
 \item A signed scalar $u$ may be transported through any number of hidden
 layers as the nonnegative pair
 $(u_+,u_-)=(\varrho(u),\varrho(-u))$, with the fixed identity update
 $(u_+,u_-)\mapsto(u_+,u_-)$ and recovery $u=u_+-u_-$.
 \item Finitely many networks may be copied or run in parallel.  Their widths
 add.  A $q$-dimensional state is transported coordinatewise by $2q$
 nonnegative channels, so shorter branches can be extended to a common
 depth by fixed signed transport.  If a branch already terminates in a
 nonnegative state or a signed pair, its existing depth gap is filled by fixed
 identity layers.  If only a signed scalar affine readout
 $u=\bmw(\bmxi)^\ts\bmh+b(\bmxi)$ is available, compose that readout with the
 fixed split map $u\mapsto(u,-u)$, whose matrix is $[1,-1]^\ts$, and merge the
 two adjacent affine maps.  The resulting hidden layer produces
 $(\varrho(u),\varrho(-u))$; its two affine
 rows are sign copies of $(\bmw(\bmxi),b(\bmxi))$, so affine code dependence
 is preserved.  This split layer must be included in the interface depth
 ledger.
 \item Two adjacent affine layers with no intervening activation may be
 merged without losing affine code dependence whenever at least one of the
 two layers is fixed.
 \item Repeating an affine slot assignment in copied branches and padding
 unused slots by fixed zeros preserve affine code dependence.  Zero padding
 changes the dense parameter count but not the realized function.
\end{enumerate}
By contrast, merging two code-dependent affine layers need not preserve affine

body:
[Theorem 10 of arXiv:2609.02444, 'The Hasse norm principle for $A_4$-quartic extensions of global function fields'] Let \(k\) be a finite field of characteristic \(\neq 2,3\).
  Let \((C, B_1, B_2,  C \xrightarrow{f} \PP^1_k)\) be an \(A_4\)-quartic cover of \(\PP^1\) over \(k\).
  The Hasse norm principle fails for \(f\) if and only if the \(k\)-point of \(H(n_1,n_2)\) represented by \(f\) lies in the image of a \(k\)-point of \(H^{\rm fail}(n_1,n_2)\).

body:
[Corollary ATRTASs of arXiv:2603.12774, 'Synchronization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Browni'] Assume the hypotheses of the second statement of 
	Theorem~(ASASiid of the paper) together with Proposition~(POINT of the paper) hold. Then there exists an integer \( p \) and a collection of random variables \( \{ b_i \}_{1 \leq i \leq p} \), where each \( b_i : \tilde{\mathcal{B}} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^d \), such that: 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[1)] The family \( \overline{\mathcal{A}} = \{ \overline{\mathcal{A}}(\omega^-) \}_{\omega^- \in \mathcal{B}} \) is given by
		\[
		\overline{\mathcal{A}}(\omega^-) =
		\begin{cases}
			\left\{ b_i(\omega^-)\right\}_{1 \leq i \leq p}, & \text{if } \omega^- \in \tilde{\mathcal{B}}, \\
			\{0\}, & \text{otherwise}.
		\end{cases}
		\]
		Moreover, for every $\omega^-\in \tilde{\mathcal{B}}$
		\[
		\mu_{\omega^-} = \frac{1}{p} \sum_{i=1}^{p} \delta_{\{ b_i(\omega^-) \}}.
		\]    
		\item[2)] For every \( \epsilon > 0 \) and every \( x_0 \in \mathbb{R}^d \),
		\begin{align*}
			\lim_{t \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{t} \int_0^t \mathbf{P}\left( d\left( \varphi^s_{\omega^-}(x_0), \overline{\mathcal{A}}(\omega^-) \right) \geq \epsilon \right) \, \mathrm{d}s = 0.
		\end{align*}
		
		\item[3)] {For the constant $C$ given in Lemma (JHJHJH of the paper), we have } 
		\[
		\max_{1\leq i \neq j\leq p} \left| b_i(\omega^-) - b_j(\omega^-) \right| \leq C, \quad \mathbf{P}\text{-a.s.}
		\]
	\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 5 (inverse-clock rate) of arXiv:2605.31471, 'Convergence Rates of Continuous-Time Random Walks to Time-Fractional Diffusions with Unbou'] Under Assumption~\ref{asm:heavy-tail}, for every terminal time
        $T>0$ and all $h>0$,
        \begin{equation} 
            \int_0^\infty
            \bigl|
                P(\hat\sigma_T>s)-P(N_T^h>s)
            \bigr|\,ds
            \le
            C_{\mathrm{clock}}(T)\,h^{\chi(\beta)},
        \end{equation}
        with $C_{\mathrm{clock}}(T):=(1+T+T^{-1})C(\beta)$, where $C(\beta)$
        and $\chi(\beta)$ are the constants of Theorem~\ref{theo:frac1}.

[Lemma 39 of arXiv:2609.00245, 'Higher-order Gaussian bounds for maximally subelliptic boundary value problems'] Fix \(c_0>0\).
    Let \(I\subseteq \R\) be an open interval and \(V\subseteq U\)
    be open.
    \(\forall \phi_1,\phi_2\in \CinftycptSpace[I\times V]\)
    with \(\phi_1\prec \phi_2\), \(\forall L\in \Zgeq\), \(\exists C\geq 0\),
    \(\forall u\in \LtlocSpace[I][\DomainL]\) with 
    \(\partial_t \left( u\big|_{I\times V} \right) = -c_0 \opL u\big|_{I\times V} \),
    
    \begin{equation}
        \CbjNorm{\phi_1 u}{L}
        \leq C \LtNorm*{\phi_2 u}[\R\times \ManifoldN],
    \end{equation}
    and, moreover,  \(u\in \CinftySpace[I\times V][\C^M]\).
    The same holds with \(\opL\) replaced by \(\opL^*\), throughout.
    Here the equivalence class of the norm \(\CbjNorm{\cdot}{L}\) is well-defined
    since \(\phi_1 u\) is supported in a fixed compact set (and one can use any choice of the norm
    from the equivalence class).

body: [Definition def:saturated of arXiv:2504.19367, 'Reduced Random Walks in the Hyperbolic Plane\textinterrobang'] Let $a \leq b$ be real numbers, let $T \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, and let $f \colon T \to \mathbb{R}$. For $\epsilon > 0$, we say that $f$ is \textcolor{blue}{\emph{$\epsilon$-saturated}} on $[a, b]$ if there exist $x_0, \ldots, x_n \in T$ such that \[a = x_0 < \cdots < x_n = b\] and $\abs{f(x_{i + 1}) - f(x_{i})} < \epsilon$ for $0 \leq i < n$.
title: Definition def:saturated of arXiv:2504.19367

[Lem lower prob of arXiv:2411.09640, 'Random Lipschitz functions on graphs with weak expansion'] There exists a constant $C$ for which the following holds. Let positive integers $M$ and $r$ be given. Let $B = B_{r}(v)$ be a ball of exact radius $r$ and $v_0 \notin B$. Let $g_0 \in \mbox{\rm{Lip}}_{v_0}(G[V \setminus B_{r-1}(v)]; M)$ be an $M$-Lipschitz function that can be extended to an $M$-Lipschitz function in $\mbox{\rm{Lip}}_{v_0}(G;M).$ Define
        \[\mathcal{G}  = \{g \in \mbox{\rm{Lip}}_{v_0}(G[B]; M): g|_{\Gamma} = g_0|_{\Gamma}\};\]
        and
        \[\mathcal{G} ' = \{g \in \mbox{\rm{Lip}}_{v_0}(G[B]; M):\max(g)-\min(g|_\Gamma) \geq \frac{Mr}{2} \text{ and } g|_{\Gamma} = g_0|_{\Gamma}\}.\]
        Then, for $m = m(G, r)$ the maximum size of a ball of radius $r-1$ in $G$, 
        \begin{equation}\label{height.lb} \frac{|\mathcal{G} '|}{|\mathcal{G} |} \geq C^{-m}.\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem lower prob of arXiv:2411.09640
