[Theorem thm:backward_flow_SDE of arXiv:2606.12143, 'Continuous stochastic flows driven by white noise and their duals'] Suppose that $(\sigma,b)$ satisfy Assumption~(assu:H of the paper) and conditions~(item:1a of the paper)--(item:1d of the paper), and let $\mathcal S$ be the associated stochastic flow. Then, for any $(a,r) \in {\mathbb R}^2$, $\mathcal S^*_{-r,-\cdot}(a)$ is the almost sure unique strong solution to
\begin{align}
    \nonumber \mathcal S^*_{-r,-x}(a) 
    = a 
  &- \int_r^x\!\! \int_{{\mathbb R}} \sigma\big( \mathcal S^*_{-r,-u}(a), -u, s \big) \mathcal W^*(\ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} s, \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} u) 
  - \int_r^x b\big( \mathcal S^*_{-r,-u}(a), -u \big) \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} u \\
  &
  + \frac{1}{2} \int_r^x 
   \partial_x \bar\sigma \big( \mathcal S^*_{-r,-u}(a), -u \big) \ensuremath{\mathrm{d}} u, 
  \qquad x \ge r,
\end{align}
where $\mathcal W^*$ is the image of $\mathcal W$ under the map $(a, r) \mapsto(a,-r)$. Moreover, the collection
$\{(\mathcal S^*_{-r,-x}(a),\, x \ge r)\}_{(a,r) \in {\mathbb R}^2}$ forms a stochastic flow. In particular, $(\mathcal S^*)^*=\mathcal S$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\alpha_i(s) = \mathrm E[\alpha^-(x,K)|S=s] = \sum_{k=0}^n \alpha^-(x,k)\pi_K'(k|s).
$$
If $s_i=1$, then $x\in\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$ and
$$
\alpha_i(s) = \mathrm E[\alpha^+(x,K)|S=s] = \sum_{k=0}^n \alpha^+(x,k)\pi_K'(k|s).
$$

[Definition of arXiv:2411.10296, 'Parking on a random rooted binary tree'] We say that a subset $t \subseteq \mathds{V}$ is a \emph{rooted binary tree} if
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\emptyset \in t$
        \item $v \in t \implies p(v) \in t$
        \item for every $v \in t$, there exists $0 \leq c(v) \leq 2$ such that if $c(v)= 0$ then $v1, v2 \notin t$, and if $c(v) > 0$ then $vi \in t$ if and only if $1 \leq i \leq c(v)$.
    \end{enumerate}
We take the edges of $t$ to be directed from $v$ to $p(v)$.
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2411.10296, 'Parking on a random rooted binary tree'

CAMPAIGN RESULT [independently checked proof; E0095-BIP v1; no novelty claim]. Let G be a finite connected bipartite unweighted d-regular graph, d>=2, with both bipartition classes of even size and lambda_2(L_G)>=2. Among perfect matchings of new edges, the optimal non-lazy absolute SRW gap on the (d+1)-regular augmentation is 2/(d+1). A matching attains it if and only if every matching edge lies within a bipartition class. This includes Q_d for d>=2 and K_{m,m} for even m>=2. It does not assert total-variation mixing-time optimality, and the spectral threshold is needed for the sufficiency argument.

Consider i.i.d. first-passage percolation on Z^d with weight law F. EXISTENCE of a finite geodesic between every pair of vertices, almost surely and simultaneously over all pairs, is known in each of the following cases, and the case division matters. (a) d = 2 and F ARBITRARY: Wierman and Reh proved that for any passage time distribution, with probability one there is a geodesic between any two points of Z^2. (b) Any d, with F(0) < p_c(d): existence follows from standard subcritical estimates. (c) Any d, with F(0) > p_c(d) and E[tau_e] < infinity: existence was proved by Zhang. (d) The remaining case F(0) = p_c(d) with d > 2 is STILL UNRESOLVED in general, though existence is known for distributions with F(0) = F(delta) = p_c for some delta > 0 in sufficiently high dimensions. So it is WRONG to say that geodesics need F(0) < p_c; that condition is sufficient and convenient, not necessary, and supercritical zero-weight percolation does not by itself destroy existence. UNIQUENESS is a separate matter: a continuous F is a SUFFICIENT condition for the model to be uniquely geodesic, since two distinct finite paths then have equal passage time with probability zero and there are countably many pairs of paths. With atoms - a two-valued weight law, say - ties are genuine and multiple geodesics occur with positive probability. All of the above is about FINITE geodesics; the existence, direction, uniqueness and coalescence of semi-infinite geodesics is a separate and largely open subject whose known results require differentiability or curvature assumptions on the limit shape. [Wierman and Reh (1978); Kesten, Aspects of First Passage Percolation, (9.23); Zhang; verified against Auffinger, Damron and Hanson, 50 Years of First-Passage Percolation, Section 4.1]

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a graph $X$, with adjacency matrix $d\in M_N(0,1)$, and with a distinguished vertex $*$, the number $L_k$ of loops of length $k$ based at $*$ is given by:
$$L_k=(d^k)_{**}$$
When writing $d=U\lambda U^{-1}$ with $U\in O_N$ and $\lambda=diag(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_N)$ with $\lambda_i\in\mathbb R$, we have
$$L_k=\sum_iU_{*i}^2\lambda_i^k$$
and the real probability measure $\mu$ having these numbers as moments is given by
$$\mu=\sum_iU_{*i}^2\delta_{\lambda_i}$$
with the delta symbols standing as usual for Dirac masses.

body:
[Lemma lem:expectation-taylor of arXiv:2608.23742, 'Second-order fusion asymptotics for $\Sine_\beta$ correlation functions'] Let $d\ge1$, $\gamma>0$, and put $D=d\gamma$. Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact. Suppose that real random variables $X,Y,M$ satisfy, for some $p,q$,
\begin{equation}
p>\max\{2,D\},\qquad q>\max\{1,D\},\qquad
2q\left(1-\frac1p\right)>1,
\end{equation}
and $X\in L^p$, $Y,M\in L^q$. Suppose, uniformly for $b\in K$ and $1\le j\le d$,
\begin{equation}
U_j(t,b)=tb_jX+\frac{t^2b_j^2}{2}Y+R_j(t,b),
\qquad |R_j(t,b)|\le C_K|t|^3M.
\end{equation}
Then, with
\[
F(u):=\prod_{j=1}^d|1+u_j|^\gamma,
\qquad A(b):=\sum_jb_j,
\qquad B(b):=\sum_jb_j^2,
\]
one has, uniformly for $b\in K$,
\begin{align}
\mathbb E F(U(t,b))
&=1+\gamma tA(b)\mathbb E X\\
&\quad+\frac{t^2}{2}\left\{\gamma B(b)\mathbb E Y+
\left[\gamma(\gamma-1)B(b)+\gamma^2(A(b)^2-B(b))\right]\mathbb E X^2\right\}
+o(t^2).\notag
\end{align}

body:
[Lemma 23 (Cone of influence; pathwise echo decay) of arXiv:2608.15987, 'Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees: a conditional bra'] Assume the saturated regime and $\kappa<1$. Couple the true system $s$ and the directed system $\tilde s$ (all back-reaction and non-genealogical couplings replaced by their saturated idealisations) synchronously, edge by edge, using the same Brownian motions. Let $D^{(v)}_t:=s^{(v)}_t-\tilde s^{(v)}_t$. Then, pathwise,
\[
\sup_{t\le\tau}\big|D^{(v)}_t\big|\le\frac{\gamma_{\max}\,\varepsilon(\delta)}{\alpha_{\min}(1-\kappa)}\sum_{u\in S_\tau}\kappa^{d(u,v)},
\]
where $S_\tau$ is the set of vertices failed by time $\tau$ and $d(\cdot,\cdot)$ is graph distance: the influence of an echo source decays geometrically, at rate $\kappa$, in graph distance.

body:
[Corollary 4 (Basis-independent geometric quantities) of arXiv:2608.30589, 'Vector-Valued Wavelet Bases as Hilbert $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-Module Bases: A Construc'] Let $U\in \mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$ be constant and $f\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)$. Then

\[
\langle Uf,Uf\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}
=U\,\langle f,f\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}\,U^{\top}.
\]

If $U\in O(m)$, then $\langle f,f\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}$ and $\langle Uf,Uf\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}$ have the same spectrum, and hence
\[
\mathrm{tr}\big(\langle Uf,Uf\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}\big)
=\mathrm{tr}\big(\langle f,f\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}\big).
\]

h_\ell(\mz_1,\ldots,\mz_\ell;\P_{\mZ})
:=
\E\Big[
h(\mz_1,\ldots,\mz_\ell,\mZ_{\ell+1},\ldots,\mZ_m)
\Big].
\]

body: [Lemma lem:XYsample of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] Let $\Omega'$, $\Omega''$ be  Polish spaces and $\mathcal{F}$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra on $\Omega'\times\Omega''$. On a measurable space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F})$, suppose $(X,Y)\to\Omega'\times\Omega''$ are random variables with distribution $m_x(dy)\mu_X(dx)$, where $\mu_X$ is a $\sigma$-finite measure and for each $x\in\Omega'$, $m_x$ is a probability measure on $(\Omega'',\mathcal{F})$. Further assume that $m_x$ is a kernel, in the sense that for any measurable set $A\subset \Omega''$, the function $x\mapsto m_x(A)$ is measurable on $\Omega'$. Then there exist $\sigma$-finite measures $(\tilde m_y)_{y\in\Omega''}, \nu$ (which are not necessarily finite), such that $(X,Y)$ can be sampled from the measure $\tilde m_y(dx)\nu(dy)$.
title: Lemma lem:XYsample of arXiv:2411.19810

body:
[Lemma 2 of arXiv:2604.04848, '\bf Addendum to:\\ Bounds for survival probabilities in \\ supercritical Galton-Watson pro'] The following representation holds:
\begin{equation}
	\tilde g_{\rm NB}(u;r,\ze) = \sum_{k=1}^{r-1}\sum_{n=0}^{2r-3-k} u^k \ze^n \cgt(r,k,n) \,,
\end{equation}
where
\begin{subnumcases}
	{\cgt(r,k,n)  = } \textstyle
		k \binom{n+k+2}{k+2}  & if $0\le n \le r-1-k$\,, \vspace{2mm}  \\
		\textstyle
		\binom{r}{k+1}\frac{(2r-k)(k+1)-(n+1)(k+2)}{k+2} & if $r-k \le n \le r-1$\,, \vspace{2mm}  \\
		\textstyle
		\binom{r}{k+1}\frac{(2r-k)(k+1)-(n+1)(k+2)}{k+2} \vspace{2mm} \notag \\
		\textstyle
		\quad+ \binom{k+(n-r)+1}{k+1}\frac{(2r-k)(k+1)-(n+1)k}{k+2} & if $r \le n \le 2r-3-k$ \,.  
\end{subnumcases} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lem 14 of arXiv:2512.05687, '$L^p$-Boltzmann-Gibbs principle \\ via Littlewood-Paley-Stein inequality'] (One-block estimate, cf.\ Lemma 5.4 of \cite{BFS})
Let $f=f(\eta)$ be a local $L^{p'}(\mu_{N,m})$ function on $\mathcal{X}_{N,m}$
with $p'>p$ depending 
only on $\eta_{\La_{\ell_0}} = (\eta(x))_{x\in \La_{\ell_0}}$.  
Then, there exists $C>0$, uniform in $N, m, \ell$ and $\ga$,
such that, for $\ell\ge \ell_0$ and $p\ge 2$, we have
\begin{align}  
E_{\mu_{N,m}} & \Bigg[ \sup_{0\le t \le T} \Big| \int_0^t \sum_{x\in \T_N}
h(s,x) \Big\{ f(\t_x \eta_s^N)- E_{\mu_{N,m}} [f(\t_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)]\Big\} ds
\Big|^p \Bigg] \\
& \le C T ^{(p-2)/2} N^{-p/2} \ell^{3p/2} \|f\|_{L^{p'}(\mu_{N,m})}^p 
\int_0^T \frac1N \sum_{x\in \T_N}|h(t,x)|^p dt.  \notag
\end{align}
From the uniformity of $C$ in $m$, we also have for a local $L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})$
function $f$ on $\mathcal{X}_{N}$ depending only on $\eta_{\La_{\ell_0}}$,
\begin{align}  
E_{\mu_{u_0}} & \Bigg[ \sup_{0\le t \le T} \Big| \int_0^t \sum_{x\in \T_N}
h(s,x) \Big\{ f(\t_x \eta_s^N)- E_{\mu_{u_0}} [f(\t_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)]\Big\} ds
\Big|^p \Bigg] \\
& \le C T ^{(p-2)/2} N^{-p/2} \ell^{3p/2} \|f\|_{L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})}^p 
\int_0^T \frac1N \sum_{x\in \T_N}|h(t,x)|^p dt.  \notag
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:7842 of arXiv:2605.26048, 'Classification of the eternal solutions and multiple coalescing shocks in the KPZ fixed po'] With probability one, for all $\xi_1 < \xi_2$ in $\mathfrak{X}$ and $t \in \mathbb{R}$, the function $x \mapsto W^{\xi_2}(0,0;x,t) - W^{\xi_1}(0,0;x,t)$ is nondecreasing and satisfies
    \[
    \lim_{x \to \pm \infty} W^{\xi_2} (0,0;x,t) -W^{\xi_1}(0,0;x,t) = \pm \infty,
    \]
    In particular, $\tau_t^{L/R,c,\xi_1,\xi_2} \in \mathbb{R}$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and $c = (c_1,c_2) \in \mathbb{R}^2$. Furthermore, for all $x >\tau_t^{R,c,\xi_1,\xi_2}$, we have 
    \[
    W^{\xi_1}(0,0;x,t) + c_1 < W^{\xi_2}(0,0;x,t) + c_2,
    \]
    while for $x < \tau_t^{L,c,\xi_1,\xi_2}$,
    \[
    W^{\xi_1}(0,0;x,t) + c_1 > W^{\xi_2}(0,0;x,t) + c_2.
    \]

body:
[Lemma lem:stayin of arXiv:2608.05089, 'Correlation decay in area-tilted line ensembles'] If $\mathbf{W}_1, \mathbf{W}_2 \in \mathcal{W}_N$, then $\mathbf{W}_1 \wedge \mathbf{W}_2, \mathbf{W}_1 \vee \mathbf{W}_2 \in \mathcal{W}_N$ as well.
Moreover, we also have
\begin{equation}
    \widetilde{\mathbf{W}_1 \wedge \mathbf{W}_2} = \widetilde{\mathbf{W}}_1 \wedge \widetilde{\mathbf{W}}_2
    \qquad \text{and}  \qquad
    \widetilde{\mathbf{W}_1 \vee \mathbf{W}_2} = \widetilde{\mathbf{W}}_1 \vee \widetilde{\mathbf{W}}_2,
\end{equation}
i.e.\ the maximum or minimum can be taken before or after linear interpolation.

Let E be a Banach space and v_1, ..., v_n in E. Let eps_1, ..., eps_n be independent Rademacher random variables. E is a Banach space

body:
[Lemma lem:OnejVolumeAnalysisAdvancing of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] There exists a real number $\lambda_0 \in (0,1/2)$ such that the following holds. Consider any $\lambda \in (0,\lambda_0)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ such that $p_0=1$ and, for all $i \ge 1$, $W_i \le (4/\lambda)^i$. Suppose that $\overline{p}$ has finitely many bins which are strongly exposed. 
Let $j_0$ be a sufficiently large positive integer
where  all strongly-exposed bins are in $[j_0-1]$.
Let $\tau_0$ be a non-negative integer. Let $\Psi_0$ be the   initialising high-level state with  $\tau^{\Psi_0} = \tau_0$ and $j^{\Psi_0} = j_0$. 
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be the $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule from Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-rule of the paper).  
Let $V$ be a volume process from $\Psi_0$ with transition rule $\mathrm{hls}$, 
 send sequence~$\overline{p}$, and birth rate~$\lambda$  (Definition~(def:volume-process of the paper)).
For any
$t \ge \tau_0$, 
let   $T(t) = \{\tau_0,\ldots,t\}$.
Then  the following statement holds  for
every $t > \tau_0$ and
every tuple
$ 
\overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)} = (\psi_{\tau_0},\dots,\psi_{t-1})$  of high-level states 
such that  
$\mathbb{P}( \overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}) > 0$, 
$\psi_{t-1}$ is a $j$-advancing state, and 
$\tau^{\psi_{t-1}} = t-1$.
Conditioned on $\overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)} $,
with 
probability at least $1-\exp(-\lambda j/500)
 $,  
the following events occur, where  
\[
\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}} = \min\{t'  \geq t \colon \textup{type}^{\Psi(t')} = \textup{failure} \mbox{ or }j^{\Psi(t')} = j+1\}.\]
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $\Psi(\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}})$ is $(j+1)$-filling or $(j+1)$-advancing
and $z_{j+1}^{\Psi(\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}})}=0$.
\item $\tau_{j,\mathrm{full}} \leq t+ 12 j^{\phi+1} W_j 
$.
\end{enumerate}

Suppose that, for any $T>0$, there exist constants $C(T),\epsilon>0$ and $p>0$ such that

		\sup\limits_n \mathbb{E}\left[d (X_s^{(n)},X_t^{(n)})^p\right]\leq C(T)\vert t-s\vert^{1+\epsilon},0\leq s\leq t \leq T.	
		$$

[Lemma cont of arXiv:2411.11393, '\fontsize{16}{19} \selectfont On differentiability of reward functionals corresponding to '] Let $\tau^{D,\lambda}\in \mathcal{Z}$, $A:=A^{D,\lambda}$ the corresponding additive functional given by (equation func of the paper), $\tilde \lambda \in \rm(D)$, $\tilde A:= A^{D,\tilde \lambda}$ the functional corresponding to $D,\lambda$ given by (equation func of the paper), $J\subset D$ an open interval, $\tau:=\tau^J$ and $h:I\to \mathbb{R}$ a bounded measurable function. Additionally, we set $\tilde A_{t-}:= \lim_{s\nearrow t} \tilde A_s$ with convention $\tilde A_{0-}:=0$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item  If $\tau<\infty$ $\mathbb{P}_x$-a.s.\ for all $x\in J$, then the function $f:I \to \mathbb{R}$,
\begin{align*}
    x\mapsto \mathbb{E}_x[e^{-A_\tau}h(X_\tau)]
\end{align*} is continuous on the closure $\overline{J}$ of $J$ (in $I$).
\item  If $\mathbb{E}_x[\tau]<\infty$ for all $x\in J$, $\mu\vert_J$, $\sigma\vert_J$ are bounded and $\tilde \lambda (J)<\infty$, then the function $F: I \to \mathbb{R}$,
\begin{align*}
    x\mapsto \mathbb{E}_x\left[ \int_0^\tau e^{-A_t} h(X_t) d\tilde A_t \right]
\end{align*} is continuous on $I$. We use the convention $\int_0^\tau:=\int_{[0,\tau)}$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemma cont of arXiv:2411.11393

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2608.30752, '2608.30752'] Let \(u_0\colon\Sigma\to(S,h)\) be an orientation-preserving 
covering map and let
\(Y=(\Sigma,u_0^*h)\).  Then there are constants depending only on \(Y\) such
that
\begin{equation}
  \frac{\eta_Y}{2}e^{2d_{\mathrm T}(X,Y)}
  \le
  E_{u_0}(X)
  \le
  A_Ye^{2d_{\mathrm T}(X,Y)}
  
\end{equation}
for every \(X\in\mathcal T(\Sigma)\), where
\(
  \eta_Y
  :=
  \min_{[\lambda]\in\mathbb P\mathcal{ML}(\Sigma)}
  \frac{\ell_Y(\lambda)^2}{\operatorname{Ext}_Y(\lambda)}
  >0.
\)

Consequently, there exists \(K_E\ge1\) such that, whenever
\(X_a,X_b,X_c\) occur in this order on a Teichm\"uller geodesic in
\(\mathcal T(\Sigma)\),
\begin{equation}
  E_{u_0}(X_b)
  \le
  K_E\max\{E_{u_0}(X_a),E_{u_0}(X_c)\}.
  
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
  \frac12\log E_{u_0}(X)
  =
  d_{\mathrm T}(X,Y)+O_Y(1).
  
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 4 of arXiv:2608.30752

[Definition def:function_a of arXiv:2510.21186, 'Weingarten Calculus with Virtual Isometries'] Let $k$ and $n$ be positive integers.
We define the \emph{ascension function} $\Raise_{k,n}$ in~$\mathbb{C}[S_k]$ by
 \[
\Raise_{k,n}(\sigma)= \sum_{t=0}^{\mathsf{f}(\sigma)} (-1)^{k-t} \binom{\mathsf{f}(\sigma)}{t} \frac{1}{n^{\uparrow (k-t)}},
\qquad \sigma \in S_k,
 \]
 where $\mathsf{f}(\sigma)$ is the number of fixed points in $\sigma$:
 \[
 \mathsf{f}(\sigma) =|\{i \in \{1,2,\dots,k\} \mid \sigma(i)=i\}|.
 \]
title: Definition def:function_a of arXiv:2510.21186

[Defn cor:conditional-ldp of arXiv:2609.02682, 'LDP for tensor forms'] (Conditional LDP)

Assume $Q_n$ is a sequence of random symmetric zero-diagonal $v$-tensors.
We say that $ N_n(Q_n,\phi,{{\bf X}})$ satisfies a \emph{conditional LDP} with speed $n$ and a deterministic good rate function $J(\cdot):\mathbb{R} \to [0,\infty]$, if the level sets of $J(\cdot)$ are compact, and for any Borel set $F\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ and every $\varepsilon>0$,
\begin{align}
\mathbb{P}_{Q_n} \Bigg(
 - \inf_{x \in F^\circ} J(x) - \varepsilon 
 \le \frac{1}{n} \log \mathbb{P}\big( N_n(Q_n,\phi,{{\bf X}}) \in F \big|\, Q_n\big)
 \le - \inf_{x \in \overline{F}} J(x) + \varepsilon
\Bigg)\xrightarrow{n\to\infty} 1,
\end{align}
where $\mathbb{P}_{Q_n}$ denotes the probability
over the randomness of $Q_n$. Moreover, $F^\circ$ and $\overline{F}$ denote the interior and the closure of $F$, respectively.
title: Defn cor:conditional-ldp of arXiv:2609.02682

[Theorem 1 (Finite Gaussian orbit reconstruction and stability) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Let \(d,m\geq1\).  For \(P,Q\in\cP_{d,m}\), the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \(Q=P\circ U\) for some \(U\in O(d)\);
\item for every \(r\leq r_*(d,m)\) and every \(\Sigma\in\cS_r\),
\[
  \Law\bigl(P(X_1),\ldots,P(X_r)\bigr)
  =
  \Law\bigl(Q(X_1),\ldots,Q(X_r)\bigr);
\]
\item \(\mathbf J_{d,m}(P)=\mathbf J_{d,m}(Q)\).
\end{enumerate}
Every matrix in \(\cS_r\) is rational and satisfies
\begin{equation}
  \frac12I_r\preceq\Sigma\preceq\frac32I_r,
  \qquad
  |\cS_r|=\binom{D_r+n_r}{n_r}.
  
\end{equation}
All Wick contractions are recovered from \(\mathbf J_{d,m}(P)\) by an
explicit rational finite-difference transform.  In particular the number of
scalar observations is
\begin{equation}
  N_{\mathrm{probe}}(d,m)
  =
  \sum_{r=1}^{r_*(d,m)}
  \binom{\lfloor rm/2\rfloor+r(r+1)/2}{r(r+1)/2}.
  
\end{equation}

Equip \(\cP_{d,m}\) with the invariant tensor norm \(\|\cdot\|_V\), and write
\[
  \delta_{\mathrm{orb}}(P,Q)
  =
  \min_{U\in O(d)}\|Q-P\circ U\|_V.
\]
If
\[
  A_{d,m}
  =
  r_*(d,m)\bigl(6r_*(d,m)-3\bigr)^{2N_{d,m}-1},
\]
then there is \(c_{d,m}>0\) such that
\[
  \|\mathbf J_{d,m}(P)-\mathbf J_{d,m}(Q)\|
  \geq
  c_{d,m}
  \left(
    \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{orb}}(P,Q)}
    {\sqrt2(1+\|P\|_V^2+\|Q\|_V^2)}
  \right)^{A_{d,m}}.
\]
Conversely, on every coefficient ball of radius \(R\), the map
\(\mathbf J_{d,m}\) is Lipschitz with respect to
\(\delta_{\mathrm{orb}}\).  Hence the probe metric and orbit metric are
bi-H\"older on coefficient balls. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite Gaussian orbit reconstruction and stability

[Theorem thm:mixing-upper of arXiv:2606.27073, 'Retention Profiles and KL Contraction Bounds in Finite Markov Chains'] For any ergodic chain and any $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, if
$0<\eta_{\mathrm{KL}}(P)<1$, then
\[
  t_{\mathrm{mix}}(\varepsilon)
  \;\le\;
  \max\left\{0,\,
  \left\lceil
  \frac{\log\!\bigl(\frac{1}{2\varepsilon^2}\log(1/\pi_{\min})\bigr)}{-\log \eta_{\mathrm{KL}}(P)}
  \right\rceil
  \right\}.
\]
If $\eta_{\mathrm{KL}}(P)=0$, then $t_{\mathrm{mix}}(\varepsilon)\le1$.

body:
[Ppn 216 (constraints on $(\bbb,\vvv,\uuu,\rrr,\www)^{\frozen,\coarse,N}$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For the coefficients defined by \eqref{e:b.plus.coarse}--\eqref{e:w.plus.coarse},
with high probability,
the following hold simultaneously for all $0\leq d\leq d_{\max}-1$:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item 
     
    The ``domain constraint'': for all 
    $B^{\frozen,\coarse} \in \mathcal{C}^\frozen(q_d)$,
    \beq
    \vvv^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d,B^{\frozen,\coarse}) 
    \ge 
    q_d p'(q_d)
    \frac{\uuu^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d,B^{\frozen,\coarse})^2 }
    {\rrr^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d,B^{\frozen,\coarse})}
    - \frac{\eta^2}{2}\,.
    \eeq
(If $\uuu^{\frozen,\coarse,N}$ and $\rrr^{\frozen,\coarse,N}$ are both zero, we interpret the ratio on the right-hand side as zero.)
 \item
 
The ``budget constraint'' for the spherical perceptron:
    \beq
    
    \bE_{\bG^N}
    \bigg[ \Cost\Big(
        \bbb^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d),
        \vvv^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d),
            \uuu^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d)
        \Big) \bigg]
    \le \frac{1}{\alpha} 
    + \epsilon^\circ
 .
    \eeq
\item 
The ``budget constraint'' for the Ising perceptron:
    \beq
    
    \bE_{\bG^N}\bigg[ \Cost\Big(
        \bbb^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d),
        \vvv^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d),
        \uuu^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d)
        \Big) \bigg]
    \le \frac{\bE_{\bG^N}[
    \www^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d)^{1/2}]^2}{\alpha} 
    + \epsilon^\circ\,.
    \eeq
\item  The ``diffusivity'' for the Ising perceptron:
    \[\Big|\bE(\www^{\frozen,\coarse,N}(q_d)) -1\Big|
    \le\epsilon^\circ\,.\]
\end{enumerate}

\begin{proof}
Assertions
\eqref{it:spherical-budget-constraint-plus-coarse}--\eqref{it:Ising-w-constraint-plus-coarse} follow straightforwardly from Jensen's inequality. For assertion \eqref{it:domain-constraint-plus-coarse}, note 
from \eqref{e:indicator.qd.less.than.qT},
 \eqref{e:def.r}, and \eqref{e:P.plus.hist}
that Proposition~\ref{p:budget-constraints-HIST}\ref{it:domain-constraint-plus-HIST} can be rewritten as
	\[
	\vvv^{\frozen,N}(q_d,B^\frozen) 
    \ge  q_d p'(q_d) 
    I(B^\frozen)
	\frac{\uuu^{\frozen,N}(q_d,B^\frozen)^2}
		{\rrr^{\frozen,N}(q_d,B^\frozen)}
    - \frac{\eta^2}{2}\,,
	\]
where we again interpret a $0/0$ ratio as zero, and
	\[I(B^\frozen)\equiv \ind\bigg\{|B^\frozen \cap[M]| \ge 
		\frac{M}{\BUCKETS^2}
		\bigg\}\,.\]
If $I(B^\frozen)=0$ for all $B^\frozen\in B^{\frozen,\coarse}$,
then the bound \eqref{e:domain.plus.coarse} follows.
Otherwise, consider a discrete probability measure $\pi$, and random variables $v_j,u_j,r_j$ which are zero on a set of indices $Z$, and otherwise satisfy
	\[
	v_j \ge A' \frac{(u_j)^2}{r_j} - a'\]
Assume $\pi_+ \equiv 1-\pi(Z)\in(0,1]$. Then Jensen's inequality gives
	\[
	\frac{\sum_j \pi_j v_j}{\pi_+}
	\ge \frac{1}{\pi_+}
	\sum_{j\notin Z} \pi_j \bigg\{
	A' \frac{(u_j)^2}{r_j} - a'\bigg\}
	\ge A'
	\bigg(\frac{1}{\pi_+}\sum_j \pi_j u_j\bigg)^2\bigg/
	\bigg(
	\frac{1}{\pi_+}\sum_j \pi_j r_j
	\bigg) - a'
	\]
and rearranging gives
	\[
	\sum_j \pi_j v_j
	\ge
	A' \bigg(\sum_j \pi_j u_j\bigg)^2\bigg/
	\bigg(\sum_j \pi_j r_j
	\bigg)
	-a'\pi_+\,.
	\]
If we apply the above inequality with the probability measure $\pi$
over buckets $B^\frozen\in B^{\frozen,\coarse}$ with probabilities 
$\pi(B^\frozen)=|B^\frozen|/|B^{\frozen,\coarse}|$, then we obtain the desired conclusion.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: constraints on $(\bbb,\vvv,\uuu,\rrr,\www)^{\frozen,\coarse,N}$

body:
[Corollary 2 (Admissible coefficient errors) of arXiv:2608.17540, 'Pathwise stability for one-dimensional SDEs driven by Brownian motion and a symmetric stab'] Assume Assumptions~\ref{ass:baseline} and~\ref{ass:perturbed}, and let $X$ solve \eqref{eq:X}. Suppose that there exist measurable functions
\[
  h_b\in L^1(0,T),\qquad h_a\in L^2(0,T),\qquad h_\sigma\in L^\alpha(0,T)
\]
and exponents
\[
  \theta_b\in[0,1],\qquad \theta_a\in[0,\alpha/2),\qquad \theta_\sigma\in[0,1)
\]
such that, for all $(s,y)$,
\begin{align*}
|b(s,y)-\wt b(s,y)|&\le h_b(s)(1+|y|^{\theta_b}),\\
|a(s,y)-\wt a(s,y)|&\le h_a(s)(1+|y|^{\theta_a}),\\
|\sigma(s,y)-\wt\sigma(s,y)|&\le h_\sigma(s)(1+|y|^{\theta_\sigma}).
\end{align*}
Then $B,A,S<\infty$. More precisely, if $m_r:=\sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t|^r$ for $r<\alpha$, then
\[
B\le \|h_b\|_{L^1(0,T)}(1+m_{\theta_b}),\quad
A^2\le 2\|h_a\|_{L^2(0,T)}^2(1+m_{2\theta_a}),\quad
S^\alpha\le 2^{\alpha-1}\|h_\sigma\|_{L^\alpha(0,T)}^\alpha(1+m_{\alpha\theta_\sigma}).
\]

  H(z)={\rm Tr}_q^{q^2}\!\left(\frac{z^{2q}+z}{z^2+z}\right).

body:
[Proposition ppn:deg2-subgaussianity of arXiv:2411.09075, 'Weak Poincar{\'e} Inequalities, Simulated Annealing, and Sampling from Spherical Spin Glas'] With probability $1-e^{-cN}$ over $H_{N,2}$, the following holds.
    Let $\sigma,\sigma^1,\sigma^2 \sim \mu_{H_{N,2}}$, and let $W = \la \sigma,v_i \ra$ for any $i\in [N]$, or $W = \la \sigma^1,\sigma^2\ra / \sqrt{N}$.
    Then:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item  For any $0\le t\le N^{1/5}$, $\bbP(|W| \ge t) \le 3e^{-ct^2}$.
        \item  For any $k\in 2\mathbb{N}$, there exists $C_k > 0$ independent of $N$ such that $\la W^k \ra_2 \le C_k$.
    \end{enumerate}
    In particular, part (equation it:deg2-subgaussianity-mmt of the paper) implies $\|\la \sigma \sigma^\top \ra_2\|_{\op} \le C$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition ppn:deg2-subgaussianity of arXiv:2411.09075

    &\mathbb{E}\left\{\left(\sum_{i = 1}^{n}a^{2}_{i\pi(i)} - \mathbb{E}\left\{\sum_{i = 1}^{n}a^{2}_{i\pi(i)}\right\}\right)^2e^{tW_n}\right\} \leq  C(n\delta^4+n^2\delta^6t^2)h(t),\\
    &\mathbb{E}\left\{\left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i \neq j}a^{2}_{i\pi(j)} - \mathbb{E}\left\{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i \neq j}a^{2}_{i\pi(j)}\right\}\right)^2e^{tW_n}\right\} \leq  C(n\delta^4+n^2\delta^6t^2)h(t),\\
    &\mathbb{E}\left\{\left(\sum_{i\neq j}b^{2}_{ij\pi(i)\pi(j)} - \mathbb{E}\left\{\sum_{i\neq j}b^{2}_{ij\pi(i)\pi(j)}\right\}\right)^2e^{tW_n}\right\} \leq  C(n\delta^4+n^2\delta^6t^2)h(t),\\
    &\mathbb{E}\left\{\left(\sum_{i\neq j}b_{ij\pi(i)\pi(j)}b_{ji\pi(j)\pi(i)} - \mathbb{E}\left\{\sum_{i\neq j}b_{ij\pi(i)\pi(j)}b_{ji\pi(j)\pi(i)}\right\}\right)^2e^{tW_n}\right\} \leq  C(n\delta^4+n^2\delta^6t^2)h(t),
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2506.10817, 'On the Weak Error for Local Stochastic Volatility Models'] Let $t\in[0,T)$, $Y^{t,x}$ be the solution of \eqref{Eq:target} started at time $t$ with $Y_t^{t,x}=x$. Assume that $\sigma$ is four times continuously differentiable with bounded derivatives and uniformly elliptic. Then the law of $Y_T^{t,x}$ admits a density $p(y;t,x)$ with respect to the Lebesgue measure. Furthermore, if $0\le n+m \le 4$ there are constants $0<C<\infty$ such that
    \begin{align*}
       \frac{d^m}{dy^m}\frac{d^n}{dx^n} p(y+x;t,x) \le C \frac{1}{(T-t)^{(m+1)/2}} \exp\Bigl( - \frac{y^2}{C(T-t)}\Bigr).
    \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma adj4 of arXiv:2609.03988, 'A $p$-summability approach to the weak maximizing property'] Let $X$ be a Banach space such that $B_X$ is relatively weakly $p$-precompact with $1\leq p\leq \infty$, let $Y$ be a Banach space, and let $T:X\to Y$ be a nonzero bounded linear operator.\\
{\rm (1)} If $Y$ has the $\mathrm{sDPP}_{(p,q)}$ with $1\leq q<\infty$, then every maximizing sequence for $T^*:Y^*\to X^*$ is weakly $q$-singular. \\
{\rm (2)} If $Y$ has the $\mathrm{DP}^*\mathrm{P}_p$, then every maximizing sequence for $T^*:Y^*\to X^*$ is non-weak$^*$ null.
title: Lemma adj4 of arXiv:2609.03988

body:
[Theorem thm: coupling time of arXiv:2411.02917, '\hspace*{2mm}\\[-16mm] Stein's Method for Spatial Random Graphs'] Assume that $\lambda$ fulfils (equation eq: stability cond of the paper).
For all $(\xi,\sigma),(\eta,\tau)\in \mathbb{G}$ the coupling time $\tau_{(\xi,\sigma),(\eta,\tau)}$ is integrable. In particular, if $\norm{\xi-\eta} = 1$, we have for any $n^*\in\N\cup\{\infty\}$
\begin{align*}
    \E(\tau_{(\xi,\sigma),(\eta,\tau)}) \leq (n^*-1)! \,\bigg(\frac{\varepsilon}{c}\bigg)^{n^*-1} \bigg(\frac{1}{c} \sum_{i=n^*}^{\infty} \frac{c^i}{i!} + \int_0^c \frac{1}{s}\sum_{i=n^*}^{\infty} \frac{s^i}{i!}\diff s\bigg) + \frac{1+\varepsilon}{\varepsilon}\sum_{i=1}^{n^*-1} \frac{\varepsilon^i}{i} =: B^{*},
\end{align*}
where
$$\varepsilon = \sup_{\norm{\tilde{\xi}-\tilde{\eta}} \, = \, 1}\int_{\mathcal{X}} \abs{\lambda(x\,|\,\tilde{\xi}) - \lambda(x\,|\, \tilde{\eta})} \, \alpha(\diff x)$$
and
$$c = c(n^*) = \sup_{\abs{\tilde{\xi} \cup \tilde{\eta}} \, \geq \, n^*}\int_{\mathcal{X}}\abs{\lambda(x\,|\,\tilde{\xi}) - \lambda(x\,|\,\tilde{\eta})} \, \alpha(\diff x).$$

For $n^* = \infty$, the bound is interpreted as $\E(\tau_{(\xi,\sigma),(\eta,\tau)}) \leq \frac{1+\varepsilon}{\varepsilon} (e^{\varepsilon}-1)$. If any of $\varepsilon$ and $c$ are zero, the bound is to be understood as the corresponding limit. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm: coupling time of arXiv:2411.02917

[Lemma 1 (Admissible configurations and regular strata) of arXiv:2607.20680, 'Exact Scale--Shape Factorization of the Typical Poisson--Voronoi Cell Volume in Arbitrary '] Fix \(d\geq1\) and \(k\geq1\), and identify \((\R^d)^k\) with \(\R^{dk}\). The admissible configuration set \(\mathcal A_{d,k}\) is semialgebraic, and hence Borel. Moreover, there exists a Lebesgue-null semialgebraic set \(\mathcal N_{d,k}\subset\mathcal A_{d,k}\) such that
  \[
    \mathcal A_{d,k}^{\rm reg}
    :=
    \mathcal A_{d,k}\setminus\mathcal N_{d,k}
    =
    \bigsqcup_{\ell=1}^{L_{d,k}}\mathcal S_\ell
  \]
is a finite disjoint union of connected smooth semialgebraic strata. The sets \(\mathcal N_{d,k}\), \(\mathcal A_{d,k}^{\rm reg}\), and \(\mathcal S_\ell\) may be chosen invariant under positive scaling. On every stratum \(\mathcal S_\ell\), the face lattice of \(P(\bfx)\) is fixed, every vertex of \(P(\bfx)\) depends smoothly on \(\bfx\), and \(\bfx\mapsto G(\bfx)\) is smooth.

body:
[Theorem thm:endpoint-spectrum of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] For every fixed integer $k\geq4$, there are constants
$0<\alpha_k<\beta_k$ such that, as $h\to\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\mathcal R(h,k)\cap
 [\alpha_kh^{k-1},\beta_kh^{k-1}]\right|
 \geq
 h^{k-1}\exp\!\left(
  -O_k\!\left(\frac{\log h}{\log\log h}\right)\right).
\end{equation}
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{h\to\infty}\frac{\log|\mathcal R(h,k)|}{\log h}=k-1,
 \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
 |\mathcal R(h,k)|=h^{k-1+o_k(1)}.
\end{equation}
Here $o_k(1)\to0$ as $h\to\infty$; the subscript records that $k$ is fixed.
Together with the elementary cases, the complete fixed-cardinality exponent
law is
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{h\to\infty}\frac{\log|\mathcal R(h,k)|}{\log h}=
 \begin{cases}
  0,&k=1,2,\\
  1,&k=3,\\
  k-1,&k\geq4.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Complete fixed-cardinality exponent law

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.03922, 'Absolute continuity of two-dimensional polynomial random vectors'] Let $M,R>0$ and let $d\in\mathbb N$, $d\ge2$.
There exists a constant $C(M,R,d)>0$ such that, for every
$\mu=\bigotimes_{j=1}^{\infty}\mu_j$
with $\mu_j\in\mathcal M_d(M,R)$ and every $f=(f_1,f_2)$ with
$f_1,f_2\in\mathcal P_d(\mu)$, one has
\[
[[f]]_{\mu,\infty}^{\frac1{2d-1}}\mu(f\in A)
\le
C(M,R,d)\bigl(\lambda_2(A)\bigr)^{\frac1{2d-1}}
\]
for every Borel set $A\subset\mathbb R^2$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 30 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] We use \Cref{notation:log-dR}.
Then the following conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $F^{\dR}_{(X,D)}$ splits in $\mcalD_{\qcoh}(X')$.
\item We have an isomorphism
\[
F_{X/k,*}\Omega_{X/k}^{\bullet}(\log D) \simeq \bigoplus_{i=0}^d \Omega_{X'/k}^i(\log D')[-i]
\]
in $\mcalD_{\qcoh}(X')$.
\item We have an isomorphism
\[
\tau_{\leq d-1}F_{X/k,*}\Omega_{X/k}^{\bullet}(\log D) \simeq \bigoplus^{d-1}_{i=0} \Omega_{X'/k}^i(\log D')[-i].
\]
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Theorem 10 of arXiv:2605.29030, 'Preferential relocations enhance survival \\ for Markov chains with killing'] For any probability measure $\boldsymbol{\nu}$ on $\S$, the following assertions hold:
  \begin{enumerate}
   \item[(i)] We always have
   $$\liminf_{n\to \infty} \frac{1}{n} \log  \P_{\boldsymbol{\nu}}(\z>n) \geq \log r. $$

  \item[(ii)] Suppose that $\tau$ is not a Dirac point mass and furthermore, either that \eqref{E:tauf1} holds, or that all the entries $\sigma(s,t)$ are positive 
  and \eqref{E:tauf2} holds. Then there is the strict inequality
   $$\liminf_{n\to \infty} \frac{1}{n} \log  \P_{\boldsymbol{\nu}}(\z>n)> \log r. $$
   
   
  \item [(iii)] If  $\tau$ is  a Dirac point mass, then 
$$ \lim_{n\to \infty} r^{-n} \P_{\boldsymbol{\nu}}(\z>n) = c(\boldsymbol{\nu})$$
for some $0<c(\boldsymbol{\nu})<\infty$. 

  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 10 of arXiv:2605.29030

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2609.01020, '2609.01020'] Let $F$ be a perverse sheaf on a complex manifold $X$. 
Then for a complex analytic Whitney stratification $\mathcal{S}$ of $X$ the 
following two conditions are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm{(i)}] 
$\msupp(F) \subset \bigsqcup_{S\in \mathcal{S}} T_S^\ast X.$
\item[\rm{(ii)}] 
$F\in \Perv(\CC_X) \text{ is adapted to } \mathcal{S}$ i.e. 
$H^jF|_S$ is locally constant for any $S\in \mathcal{S}$ and $j\in \ZZ$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemma 14 of arXiv:2609.01020

[Lemma final of arXiv:2508.02416, 'On the surjectivity of the conditional expectation\\ given a real random variable'] Let $\eta$ be a diffuse probability measure. Let $(f_y)_{y\in \mathcal{Y}}$ be a family of non-negative measurable functions from $\mathbb{R}$ to $\mathbb{R}$ such that the mapping
$
(x,y) \mapsto f_y(x)
$
is measurable and
\[
\nu(dy)\text{-a.e.,}\quad\int_{x \in \mathbb{R}} f_y(x)\, \eta(dx)>0.
\]
Then for each $\widehat{A} \in \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R})$ such that $\eta(\widehat{A})>0$, there exists a Borel set $A \subset \widehat{A}$ such that $\eta(A)>0$ and $\nu(dy)$-a.e.,
\[
\int_{x \in A} f_y(x)\, \eta(dx) < \int_{x \in \mathbb{R}} f_y(x)\, \eta(dx).
\]

Own-work draft, proof (unaudited), T385-w737-C03 v1; standard finite-dimensional algebra, no novelty claim. Let n,m>=1, H be any real n by m matrix, D any real symmetric PSD n by n matrix, and mu any vector in R^n. Set H0=H-mu 1_m^T, v=H0 1_m/m, B=H0 H0^T/m+D and K=H H^T/m+D. With U=[mu,v] and A=[[1,1],[1,0]], K=B+UAU^T. Outside spec(B), det(lambda I-K)=det(lambda I-B) det(I_2-AU^T(lambda I-B)^(-1)U). Also C=B-vv^T=H0(I_m-1_m 1_m^T/m)H0^T/m+D is PSD and K=C+(mu+v)(mu+v)^T. Therefore at most one eigenvalue of K exceeds the largest eigenvalue of C, and at most one exceeds the largest eigenvalue of B. For a bias-free two-layer scalar Gaussian ReLU NTK, H=ReLU(XW), mu_i=||x_i||/sqrt(2pi), and D is the PSD hidden-weight derivative Gram. The exact spike vectors depend on the centered bulk, so replacing their matrix-valued resolvent by its normalized trace is an additional unproved isotropy assumption. This statement does not extend Fan-Wang to ReLU.
Finite n,m>=1
H real n by m
D symmetric PSD
mu arbitrary; no independence from H or D assumed
For determinant formula lambda lies outside spec(B)

[OPEN PROBLEM - not a proved fact. Stated in arXiv:2509.01797, 'Relation between Wick powers and excursion clusters of the 2D GFF' (conj environment labelled Conj expansion c).] Fix $c\in (0,1)$.
The hypothetical fractional powers $:\fld_{c} \Theta_{\LL^{c}_{D}}^{n-1}:$ admit restriction to clusters of 
$\LL^{c}_{D}$.
That is to say, given a cluster $\clus$ of $\LL^{c}_{D}$, the field
\begin{displaymath}
\ind_{d(z,\clus)<\delta}\, :\fld_{c} \Theta_{\LL^{c}_{D}}^{n-1}:
\end{displaymath}
converges as $\delta\to 0$, in an appropriate sense (conditional $L^2$), towards a well defined generalized function
supported of $\overline{\clus}$,
which we will denote by $:\fld_{c} \Theta_{\LL^{c}_{D}}^{n-1}:_{\vert \overline{\clus}}$.
By contrast, the renormalized intersection local times $:\Theta_{\LL^{c}_{D}}^{n}:$
do not admit restrictions to clusters.
More precisely the integral
\begin{displaymath}
\int_{d(z,\clus)<\delta}:\Theta_{\LL^{c}_{D}}^{n}:
\end{displaymath}
converges in probability,
as $\delta\to 0$, to $\sigma(\clus)(-1)^{n-1}\infty$.

The $\varepsilon$-neighborhood of a cluster $\clus$ of $\LL^{c}_{D}$,
both for the Euclidean distance and conformal radius,
admits an asymptotic expansion in the $L^2$ sense, as $\varepsilon\to 0$,
into the powers $(\vert \log\varepsilon\vert^{-(n-c/2)})_{n\geq 1}$
of $\vert \log\varepsilon\vert$.
The coefficient of $\vert \log\varepsilon\vert^{-(n-c/2)}$
is a linear combination of fields
$\sigma(\clus):\fld_{c} \Theta_{\LL^{c}_{D}}^{k-1}:_{\vert \overline{\clus}}$
for $k\in\{1,\dots, n\}$.
By contrast, the renormalized intersection local times $:\Theta_{\LL^{c}_{D}}^{n}:$
do not appear in the expansion.
The expansion for the Euclidean distance and that for the conformal radius are related
through the expectations
\begin{displaymath}
\hat{\mu}^{\rm loop}_{\text{SLE}_{\kappa}}
\Big(
\log\Big(
\dfrac{\CR(0,\inter(\Gamma))}{d(0,\Gamma)}
\Big)^{k}
\Big)
\end{displaymath}
w.r.t. the MKS measure $\hat{\mu}^{\rm loop}_{\text{SLE}_{\kappa}}$,
where $\kappa$ and $c$ are related by (Eq rel kappa c). (Verbatim from the paper's TeX; symbols are the source paper's. Stated as open/conjectural; no resolution of it was found in the paper's own text by the rules of problem_index.py - a paper may still prove special cases of a conjecture it states.)

[Thm SNoverN of arXiv:2601.09537, 'Gene genealogies in haploid populations evolving according to sweepstakes reproduction'] Let $B^{\rm WF}(n, N)$ denote the random tree size of
a sample of size $n\ge 2$ from a haploid  population of size $N$ evolving according to the
Wright-Fisher model    with time measured in generations.  Then, with
$B^{\rm WF}(N,N)$ denoting the total tree length of the entire
population when it evolves according to the Wright-Fisher model, 
\begin{equation}

\limsup_{N\to \infty}\frac{1}{N\log(N)} \EE{B^{\rm WF}(N,N)} < \infty
\end{equation}

[Thm 8 of arXiv:2511.02763, 'The Cayley-Moser problem with Poissonian arrival of offers'] The cumulative distribution function of $T_t$ is given by
\begin{equation}H_t(r)=P(T_t\leq r)=\begin{cases}
		1-\frac{\phi(\mu(t))}{\phi(\mu(t-r))} & r<t\\
		1 & r\geq t
	\end{cases}.
\end{equation}
In particular, the 
probability that a sale is not made 
up to the deadline is given by
$$P(T_t=t)=H_t(t+)-H_t(t-)=\frac{\phi(\mu(t))}{\phi(\mu_0)}.$$

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For one-dimensional nearest-neighbor random walk in an i.i.d. random environment in the subballistic or intermediate regime, parametrized by an index kappa solving E[rho^kappa]=1 for rho the local odds ratio of the environment, hitting times of successive integers admit a classical Kesten construction as a branching process with migration: individuals reproduce according to an environment-dependent offspring law with an added immigration/emigration term reflecting the local environment. The Kesten-Kozlov-Spitzer theorem shows that for kappa in the relevant range below 2, the hitting time of level n, normalized by n^{1/kappa}, converges to a kappa-stable distribution, via a result on the total population size of the associated branching-with-migration process, which itself has heavy-tailed, stable-scaling behavior. This gives the precise non-Gaussian scaling limits characterizing anomalous, subdiffusive or index-dependent, behavior in one-dimensional random walk in random environment, a phenomenon absent for simple random walk. It does not extend to higher dimensions, since the explicit branching correspondence is a genuinely one-dimensional, nearest-neighbor phenomenon, and it requires the environment to be i.i.d. with a moment condition admitting a solution kappa in the relevant range. Typical failure: Extending the branching-process-with-migration correspondence and its kappa-stable scaling conclusion to multi-dimensional random walk in random environment, or to environments with dependence rather than i.i.d. structure, where no analogous exact combinatorial bijection to a branching process is known; the Kesten construction is a special, essentially exact identity in one dimension that does not generalize by analogy, so claiming kappa-stable scaling outside the one-dimensional i.i.d. setting requires an entirely separate justification. Canonical reference: Kesten, Kozlov and Spitzer, 1975, Compositio Mathematica.
one-dimensional, nearest-neighbor random walk in an i.i.d. random environment
existence of kappa in (0,2) solving E[rho^kappa]=1 for the environment's local odds ratio rho
transience of the walk, or the appropriate directional condition for the regime under study
technical non-lattice or non-degeneracy conditions on the environment law needed for the stable-law convergence
title: Technique: Kesten-Kozlov-Spitzer Branching Process with Migration

[Theorem thm3.3 of arXiv:2411.03528, '\textbf{On a boundary of the central limit theorem for strictly stationary, reversible Mar'] Suppose $(\zeta_1, \zeta_2, \zeta_3 \dots)$ is a sequence
of positive numbers such that \hfil\break
(a) $\lim_{n \to \infty} \zeta_n = 0$, and \hfil\break
(b) for every $c > 0$, 
$\lim_{n \to \infty} [\, \zeta_n/e^{-cn}] = \infty$. 

   Then there exists a (real) strictly stationary, countable-state
Markov chain $X := (X_k, k \in \mathbb Z)$ which is reversible, such that 
the following four conditions hold: \hfil\break
(i) eq.\ ((eq3.11 of the paper)) holds: $E(X_0^2) < \infty$ and $EX_0 = 0$; \hfil\break
(ii) $\alpha_X(n)\ \leq\ \beta_X(n)\  \leq\ \zeta_n$ for\ every $n \in \mathbb N$; \hfil\break
(iii) eqs.\ ((eq3.12 of the paper)) and ((eq3.13 of the paper)) hold; and \hfil\break
(iv) there exists a strictly increasing sequence 
$\bigl(J(1), J(2), J(3), \dots\bigl)$ of positive integers, 
and a sequence of positive constants
$(b_1, b_2, b_3, \dots)$ satisfying $b_n \to \infty$
as $n \to \infty$, such that
\begin{equation}

b_n^{-1} \sum_{k=1}^{J(n)}X_k\ \to\ \mu_{\rm P1sL}\ \
{\rm in\ distribution\ as}\ n \to \infty. 
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm3.3 of arXiv:2411.03528

Let (M, g) be a complete Riemannian manifold with weighted measure dmu = exp(-V) dvol satisfying the Bakry-Emery condition CD(K, infinity) for K in R. For any probability measure nu = f * mu, the relative entropy H = D_{KL}(nu || mu), quadratic Wasserstein distance W = W_2(nu, mu), and relative Fisher information I = int ||nabla f||^2 / f dmu satisfy H <= W * sqrt(I) - (K / 2) * W^2.

[Definition of arXiv:2412.08886, 'On domination for (non-symmetric) Dirichlet forms'] A Dirichlet form $({\mathscr E},{\mathscr F})$ on $L^2(E,m)$ is called \emph{quasi-regular} if the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(1)] There exists an ${\mathscr E}$-nest $\{K_n:n\geq 1\}$ consisting of compact sets.
\item[(2)] There exists an ${\mathscr E}_1$-dense subset of ${\mathscr F}$ whose elements have ${\mathscr E}$-quasi-continuous $m$-versions.
\item[(3)] There exists $\{f_k:k\geq 1\}\subset {\mathscr F}$ having ${\mathscr E}$-quasi-continuous $m$-versions $\{\tilde{f}_k:k\geq 1\}$ and an ${\mathscr E}$-polar set $N$ such that $\{\tilde{f}_k:k\geq 1\}$ separates the points of $E\setminus N$.
\end{itemize}
It is called \emph{regular} if $E$ is a locally compact separable metric space,  $m$ is a fully supported Radon measure on $E$,  and ${\mathscr F}\cap C_c(E)$ is ${\mathscr E}_1$-dense in ${\mathscr F}$ as well as uniformly dense in $C_c(E)$.  It is noteworthy that a regular Dirichlet form is always quasi-regular.

[campaign status: proved - the campaign's own proof, author-checked, unrefereed; the prior-art search was not completed] Let B_{m,n} be the balls-in-boxes model with a weight sequence (w_j), partition function Z(m,n), radius of convergence rho > 0 and w_0, w_1 > 0, and let Y(1) be the largest box occupancy. CLAIM (Janson, Conjecture 18.4): if m = o(n) then Y(1) = o_p(log n). Quantitatively, for m <= n/4, with gamma = min(1, w_1/w_0) and any r < rho, Y(1) <= (1 + delta) log n / log(gamma r n / (2m)) with high probability, i.e. Y(1) = O_p(log n / log(n/m)). The case w_1 = 0 (span 1) follows by the same comparison, writing j as a fixed sum of parts from a finite allowed set F by Frobenius, with constant max F / log(gamma_F r^{max F} n / (2m)); span d > 1 reduces to span 1 by dividing box counts by d. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: the finer multinomial asymptotics log n / log(n log n / m) of Gonnet and of Raab and Steger have no general-weight analogue here.

		$\mu_i = \Ncal(m_i, C_i) \in \Gauss(\Hcal)$, $i=0,1$. Let $\gamma>0, \gamma \in \R$ be fixed. Let $0 \leq \alpha \leq 1$ be fixed. Let $C_{\alpha,\gamma}$, $m_{\alpha,\gamma}$ be as defined in Eqs.\eqref{equation:C-alpha-gamma},
		\eqref{equation:m-alpha-gamma}, respectively.
		The regularized geometric Jensen-Shannon divergence between $\mu_0$ and $\mu_1$ is defined to be
		\begin{align}
			&\JS_{G_{\alpha}}^{\gamma}(\mu_0||\mu_1) = 
			\frac{1-\alpha}{2}||C_{\alpha, \gamma}^{-1/2}(m_0 - m_{\alpha,\gamma})||^2 + \frac{\alpha}{2}||C_{\alpha, \gamma}^{-1/2}(m_1 - m_{\alpha,\gamma})||^2 
			\nonumber
			\\
			&\quad +\frac{(1-\alpha)}{2}d^1_{\logdet}[(C_0+\gamma I), C_{\alpha,\gamma}]
			
			
			
			+ \frac{\alpha}{2} d^1_{\logdet}[(C_1+\gamma I), C_{\alpha,\gamma}].
		\end{align}

	\begin{align}

	\end{align}
	for all $\mu,\nu\in P$. In addition, $(t,\mu)\mapsto\varphi^\epsilon_P(t)\mu$ is continuous from $[0,\infty)\times P$ to $P$.

body: FIRES WHEN you plan to prove a balls-in-boxes statement by adding one ball and coupling B_{m,n} to B_{m+1,n}. THE ROUTE: for the multinomial weights w_k = 1/k! a ball-by-ball coupling shows the largest occupancy Y(1) is stochastically nondecreasing in m, and the monotonicity then sandwiches m/n -> 0 below every fixed lambda. WHY IT FAILS FOR A GENERAL WEIGHT SEQUENCE: there is no coupling of B_{m,n} and B_{m+1,n} that moves only one ball, because the conditional law of the extra ball's box depends on the WHOLE configuration through the ratios w_{Y_i + 1}/w_{Y_i}. With multinomial weights that ratio is 1/(Y_i + 1) and the dependence collapses; with any other weight sequence it does not. CONDITION OF FAILURE: w_{k+1}/w_k not of the multinomial form. The source itself names this as the missing piece. What worked instead was a direct partition-function comparison, which uses no coupling at all - see the F0055 result node.

\[
    \begin{tabular}{c|ccccccccc}
    $\otimes_{\mathcal{R}_1}$   & $C$   & $S_h$   & $S_v$ & $L$ \\

    $L$   & $0$   & $0$   & $0$   & $0$ \\

\]
In words, a tensor product of two standard complexes is $\sim$ equivalent to a standard complex, a product of a standard complex and a horizontal snake complex is $\sim$ equivalent to a horizontal snake complex, and so on.

[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2608.12804, 'Scaling Limits for Ising Models on Inhomogeneous Random Graphs and Applications'] Suppose that the entries of $\bs \coloneqq (\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_N)$ are i.i.d. Rademacher with mean $0$. Let $K:[0,1]^2\to\mathbb R$ be symmetric and Riemann
integrable, and suppose that
\(
    \|T_{|K|}\|_{\mathrm{op}}<1.
\)
    Then there exists $\delta >0$ such that
    \begin{equation}
        \limsup_{N \to \infty} \E \left[\exp\left(\frac{1+\delta}{2N}\sum_{i\neq j}K\left(\frac{i}{N},\frac{j}{N}\right)\sigma_i \sigma_j\right)\right] < \infty.
    \end{equation}
    Consequently,
    \[
        \exp \left(\frac{1}{2 N} \sum_{i \neq j} K\left(\frac{i}{N}, \frac{j}{N}\right) \sigma_{i} \sigma_j\right)
    \]
    is uniformly integrable.
title: Lemma 18 of arXiv:2608.12804

[Lemma of arXiv:2607.29020, 'Entropic Symmetrization Resistance'] \label[lemma]{large_median_at_zero}
Let $f \in \Sym$ with $\@ifstar{\oldabs}{\oldabs*}{\supp(f)} \ge 3$. 
Then, $H(f) > H(X)$ or $f(0) > p$. 
\begin{proof}
If $f < \frac{1}{2}$ everywhere,
\[
H(f) = \sum_{y} f(y) \log_2(1/f(y)) 
\ge \sum_y f(y) = 1 > H(X). 
\]
Otherwise, we apply (unique_large_mass of the paper). 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 26 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $G$. 
Assume that the action of $G$ on $\wt B$ satisfies the moment condition \eqref{moment-assumption-01},
the action of $G$ on $B$ satisfies the contraction property \eqref{contraction-property-on-B}, 
and the continuous cocycle $\sigma_0: G \times B \to \bb R$ satisfies the integrability condition \eqref{moment-assumption-02} 
and $M_1^{\mu} = M_0^{\mu} \times \bb R$. 
Suppose that, for every $\wt b \in \wt B$ with $\eta(\wt b) \in \supp \nu$,   
we have $\wt b M \subset \overline{\Gamma_{\mu} \wt b}$. 
Then, there exists $\gamma \in (0,1]$ with the following property.  
Let $h$ be a Schwartz function on $\bb R$ whose Fourier transform has compact support. 

(1) If $x \in \wh M$ is not the one-dimensional representation associated with a character vanishing on $M_0^{\mu}$, then,
for any $f \in V_x^*$ and $\psi \in W_x^{\gamma}$, 
we have, uniformly in $\wt b \in \wt B$ and in $w_n \in \bb R$ with $|w_n| = o(\sqrt{n})$,  
\begin{align*}
\upsilon_{\mu} \sqrt{2 \pi n} \,  \bb E  \left[ \langle f, \psi \rangle(g_n \cdots g_1 \wt b)  \,  h \left( \sigma_0(g_n \cdots g_1, \eta(\wt b)) - n \lambda_{\mu} - w_n \right)  \right]  
\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}  0. 
\end{align*}

(2) For any character $\chi$ of $M/M_0^{\mu}$, for any $\psi \in W_{\chi}^{\gamma}$, 
we have, uniformly in $\wt b \in \wt B$ and in $w_n \in \bb R$ with $|w_n| = o(\sqrt{n})$,  
\begin{align*}
&  \upsilon_{\mu} \sqrt{2 \pi n} \,  \bb E  \left[ \psi(g_n \cdots g_1 \wt b)  \,  h \left( \sigma_0(g_n \cdots g_1, \eta(\wt b)) - n \lambda_{\mu} - w_n \right)  \right]  \notag\\
& \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\quad
- \zeta_{\chi}(\psi)  \varphi_{\chi}(\wt b)  \chi(m_0^{\mu})^n  \int_{\bb R} h(u) du 
 \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}  0. 
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 26 of arXiv:2607.19873

[Prop of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The symmetric monoidal structure on $\CAT_T^\textup{$S$-cc}$ given by the parametrized Lurie tensor product restricts to a symmetric monoidal structure on the full subcategory $\textup{Pr}^S_T$.
    \begin{proof}
        It is clear that $\textup{Pr}^S_T$ contains the unit. To see that it is closed under the tensor product, note that a fiberwise cocomplete $T$-$\infty$-category ${\mathcal{E}}$ is fiberwise presentable if and only if each ${\mathcal{E}}(A)$ is presentable; in particular, an $S$-cocomplete $T$-$\infty$-category is $S$-presentable if and only its underlying $S$-$\infty$-category is $S$-presentable. It will therefore suffice to show that for any ${\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}}\in\textup{Pr}^S_T$ the $S$-$\infty$-category $i^*({\mathcal{C}}\otimes{\mathcal{D}})$ is $S$-presentable. By the previous lemma, $i^*({\mathcal{C}}\otimes{\mathcal{D}})\simeq (i^*{\mathcal{C}})\otimes (i^*{\mathcal{D}})$, which is then indeed $S$-presentable by [martiniwolf2022presentable]*{Proposition 2.6.2.9}.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma L:Int-9 of arXiv:2606.23865, 'Uniform-in-time Gaussian fluctuations for multiscale nonlinear stochastic systems via Mall'] For $0 \le u \le s \le w \le r \le t$, let the term $\mathcal{J}_9(t;\varepsilon,\eta)$ be defined as follows:
$$\mathcal{J}_9(t;\varepsilon,\eta)  \triangleq K  \int_{u=0}^t \int_{s=u}^t \int_{w=s}^t \int_{r=w}^t(\varepsilon+ \eta + \sqrt{\varepsilon \eta})^3 e^{-\alpha (t-u)} e^{-\alpha(t-s)} e^{- \alpha(t-w)} e^{- \alpha(t-r)}  e^{-\frac{\lambda}{\eta} (r-u)} dr \thinspace dw \thinspace ds \thinspace du.$$
Then, there exists a time-independent positive constant $K$ such that
$$ \mathcal{J}_9(t;\varepsilon,\eta) \le K \thinspace \eta^2 \thinspace  (\varepsilon+ \eta + \sqrt{\varepsilon \eta})^3.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary 9 of arXiv:2609.01166, 'Nonparametric inference for density-dependent McKean--Vlasov diffusions'] The rates above can be transferred to the case of finite-time observations, provided that exponential ergodicity holds.
To observe that, let \(\V\) be a potential for which the corresponding nonlinear dynamics satisfy
\begin{equation}
\chi^2(P_t\Vert\Pi_0)
\leq
\eta_t
:=
C_{t_0}e^{-\rho_\chi(t-t_0)},
\qquad t\geq t_0,
\end{equation}
for some \(t_0\geq0\), \(C_{t_0}<\infty\), and \(\rho_\chi>0\), where \(P_t\) and \(\Pi_0\) denote the laws with densities \(p_t\) and \(\pi_0\), respectively. For the OU potential~\eqref{eq:ou-potential}, the inequality~\eqref{eq:chi2-transfer-assumption} holds under the assumptions of~\cite{belomestny-morozova-ou}, with
\(
C_{t_0}=\chi^2(P_{t_0}\Vert\Pi_0).
\)
Let \(X_1^{T_n},\ldots,X_n^{T_n}\) be independent observations from \(P_{T_n}\) for some \(T_n>0\), and let \(G_{M_n}\) be the event on which~\eqref{eq:full-mle-oracle-transfer} holds. Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:oracle}, it holds that
\[
P_{T_n}^{\otimes n}(G_{M_n}^c)
\leq
\delta+n\tau_0(M_n)
+
\frac12\sqrt{(1+\eta_{T_n})^n-1}.
\]
Indeed,
\[
1+\chi^2(P_t^{\otimes n}\Vert\Pi_0^{\otimes n})
=
\left(1+\chi^2(P_t\Vert\Pi_0)\right)^{n}
\leq
(1+\eta_t)^n,
\]
and therefore
\(
\TV(P_t^{\otimes n},\Pi_0^{\otimes n})
\leq
0.5\sqrt{(1+\eta_t)^n-1}.
\)
The claimed bound follows from
\(
P_{T_n}^{\otimes n}(G_{M_n}^c)
\leq
\Pi_0^{\otimes n}(G_{M_n}^c)
+
\TV(P_{T_n}^{\otimes n},\Pi_0^{\otimes n})
\)
and
\(
\Pi_0^{\otimes n}(G_{M_n}^c)
\leq\delta+n\tau_0(M_n).
\)
Consequently, if
\(
n\eta_{T_n}\longrightarrow0
\)
and
\(
n\tau_0(M_n)\longrightarrow0,
\)
then the stationary oracle inequality and the rates in~\eqref{eq:kl-rate} remain valid for observations from \(P_{T_n}\). Under~\eqref{eq:chi2-transfer-assumption}, it is sufficient to choose, for any \(\varepsilon>0\),
\(
T_n
\geq
t_0+(1+\varepsilon)\rho_\chi^{-1}\log n,
\)
which guarantees
\(
n\eta_{T_n}
\leq
C_{t_0}n^{-\varepsilon}
\longrightarrow0
\)
as \(n\to\infty\).
Since by Lemma~\ref{lem:explicit-tails}
it holds that
\(
\tau_0(M)\lesssim e^{-c_a(M-v_\star)},
\)
taking
\(
M_n=v_\star+C_{\mathrm{tr}}\log n
\)
with \(c_aC_{\mathrm{tr}}>1\) yields the overall error \(\delta+o(1)\) and hence the desired rate. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem betac-unique of arXiv:2609.00110, 'Phase Transition and Fluctuation Results for First-Passage Percolation on Spread-Out Cycle'] Let $\gf(\beta)=(\sinh\beta)/\beta=\E e^{\beta\xi}$ with $\xi\sim\mathrm{Unif}[-1,1]$ and
$\gk_\theta(\beta)=\gf(\beta)^{1/\theta}$. Then $\beta\mapsto\gk_\theta(\beta)/\beta$
attains its infimum over $(0,\infty)$ at a unique point $\beta_{\mathsf{c}}\in(0,\infty)$,
$\mathsf{v}^\star=\gk_\theta(\beta_{\mathsf{c}})/\beta_{\mathsf{c}}\in(0,\infty)$, and
\begin{align}
 \beta_{\mathsf{c}}\gf'(\beta_{\mathsf{c}})=\theta\gf(\beta_{\mathsf{c}}),
 \qquad
 \mathsf{v}^\star=\gk_\theta'(\beta_{\mathsf{c}}).
\end{align}

[Lemma lem:main_event_high_prob of arXiv:2512.09219, 'Strong confluence of geodesics in Liouville quantum gravity'] We can choose the parameters $\delta,\Delta,\zeta,\alpha \in (0,\frac{\delta_3\rho}{4A^2}),\theta \in (0,\zeta/100),M,\Lambda_0 , B>1$ in a manner depending only on $b,\mathbbm{p},\delta_1,\delta_2,\delta_3,A$ and $\rho$ in such a way that the following hold.
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item 
    We have $\mathbb{P}(E_r(0)) \geq \mathbbm{p}$ for all $r>0$.
  \item The event $E_r(0)$ is measurable with respect to $\sigma( (h - h_{5r}(0))\lvert_{\text{\usefont{U}{bboldx}{m}{n}A}_{r/4,4r}(0)})$.
  \item 
   For all $x,y\in \partial B_{2r}(0)$ with $|x-y|\geq \delta r$, and any $z\in J_{x,y}\cap \mathcal{Z}$, the corresponding sets $\mathcal{A}_{u_+},\mathcal{A}_{u_-},\mathcal{M},\mathcal{A}_{v_-},\mathcal{A}_{v_+}$ and tubes $\mathcal{D}_u,\mathcal{D}_v$  have the following properties.  
Set $\mathcal{C} = B_{2 \zeta r}(U_r^{x,y} \cup W_r^x \cup W_r^y)$ and suppose that $z = z_k$ for some $k \in [\![k_x ,  k_y]\!]$.  Then the following conditions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item 
Any path in $\mathcal{C}$ connecting $B_{2 \zeta r}(L_k)$ to $B_{2\zeta r}(L_{k+1})$ has to intersect all of the sets $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{D}_u),  B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{D}_v)$ and $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{M} \setminus (S_u \cup S_v))$. 
\item 
Any path in $\mathcal{C}$ from $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{D}_u)$ to $B_{2\zeta  r}(\mathcal{A}_{u_+} \cup \mathcal{A}_{u_-})$ (resp.\  $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{D}_v)$ to $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{A}_{v_+} \cup \mathcal{A}_{v_-})$) has to intersect $B_{2\zeta r}(S_u)$ (resp.\  $B_{2\zeta r}(S_v)$).
\item 
Any path in $\mathcal{C}$ from $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{D}_u)$ to $B_{2\zeta r}(V_{\rho r / A^2}(z) \setminus (\mathcal{A}_{u_+} \cup S_u \cup \mathcal{A}_{u_-}))$ (resp.\  $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{D}_v)$ to $B_{2\zeta r}(V_{\rho r / A^2}(z) \setminus (\mathcal{A}_{v_+} \cup S_v \cup \mathcal{A}_{v_-}))$) has to intersect $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{A}_{u_+} \cup \mathcal{A}_{u_-})$ (resp.\  $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{A}_{v_+} \cup \mathcal{A}_{v_-})$). 
\item 
  Any path in $\mathcal{C}$ from $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{A}_{u_+} \cup \mathcal{A}_{u_-})$ to $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{M} \setminus S_u)$ (resp.\  $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{A}_{v_+} \cup \mathcal{A}_{v_-})$ to $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{M} \setminus S_v)$) has to intersect $B_{2\zeta r}(S_u)$ (resp.\  $B_{2\zeta r}(S_v)$).
    \item  
    Any path in $\mathcal{C}$ from $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{A}_{u_+}\cup \mathcal{A}_{u_-})$ (resp.\ $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{A}_{v_+}\cup \mathcal{A}_{v_-}))$ to $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{A}_{v_+}\cup S_v\cup \mathcal{A}_{v_-})$ (resp.\ $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{A}_{u_+}\cup S_u\cup \mathcal{A}_{u_-})$) necessarily intersects $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{M}\setminus S_u)$ (resp.\ $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{M}\setminus S_v)$).
    \item 
    Any path in $\mathcal{C}$ from $B_{2\zeta r}(L_k)$ (resp.\ $B_{2\zeta r}(L_{k+1})$) to $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{A}_{u_+} \cup \mathcal{A}_{u_-})$ (resp.\ $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{A}_{v_+} \cup \mathcal{A}_{v_-})$) intersects $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{D}_u)$ (resp.\ $B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{D}_v)$).
\end{enumerate}     
  \item 
    We have $B_{\frac{b\rho r}{2A^2}}(\{u_-,u_+\})\cap B_{2\zeta r}(U_r^{x,y}\cup W_r^x \cup W_r^y) = B_{2\zeta r}(\mathcal{A}_{u_-}\cup\mathcal{A}_{u_+}) \cap B_{\frac{b\rho r}{2A^2}}(\{u_-,u_+\})$.
  \item

  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] Let $\beta \in [1/2,1)$ and $\alpha = 1 - \beta$, and let $f \in \mathcal S_{\alpha}$ be an element of Schwartz space with Hermite polynomial expansion
 \[
   f(x)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_{n}\,h_{n}(x)
 \]
 in $L_2(N(0,1))$. 
The following two conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $f \in \mathcal S_{\alpha}^{\beta}$, the two-sided Gelfand--Shilov space.
    \item  The Hermite polynomial coefficients $a_n$ decay at an exponential rate in $n^{1/2\beta}$, i.e. there exists $t > 0$ such that
    \[ |a_n| = O(\exp(-tn^{1/2\beta})) \]
\end{enumerate}
Either of the equivalent conditions implies\footnote{Again, the one-sided condition $f \in \mathcal S^{\beta}$ is sufficient here without requiring $f \in \mathcal S_{\alpha}$.} that
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[3.]  For any $r$-strictly-sub-exponential probability measure $\mu$, there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that the following is true. For any $\epsilon \in (0,1/2)$, there exists a polynomial $P$ of degree at most $C \log^{2\beta r}(1/\epsilon)$ such that
    \[ \|f - P\|_{L_2(\mu)} \le \epsilon. \]
\end{enumerate}

body: Lagrange's theorem (group theory): If G is a finite group and H is a subgroup of G, then the order |H| divides the order |G|. More precisely, |G| = [G : H] |H|, where the index [G : H] is the number of distinct left cosets of H in G; this follows because the left cosets of H partition G and each has exactly |H| elements. In particular, the order of every element of G (the order of the cyclic subgroup it generates) divides |G|.
title: Lagrange's theorem (group theory)

[Lemma 15 of arXiv:2606.08776, 'Approximation of certain stochastic integrals with anticipating integrands'] Assume $\theta \in (0,1]$ and for $N>M$ Borel measurable $A_N:[0,1]\times[0,1] \to [-C,C]$ for some $C>0$
and an $A:[0,1] \to \R$  such that for the nets $\sigma_N^{\theta}$ from \cref{def:time_nets} the following conditions
are satisfied:
\begin{enumerate}[{\rm (1)}]
\item  For a.a. $s\in (0,1)$  it holds
       $\lim\limits_{N\to\infty} \sup\limits_{l_N(s) < t<s} |A^N(t,s) -A^N(s,s)| =0$.
\item $\lim_{N \to \infty} A^N(s,s) = A(s)$ for a.a. $s\in (0,1),$
\item 
      $A$ is left-continuous with right limits and has at most a finite number of discontinuities.
\end{enumerate}
Then one has that
\[   \lim_{N\to \infty} N \int_0^1\int_{l_N(s)}^s A^N(t,s) dtds
   = \frac{1}{2\theta} \int_0^1 (1-s)^{1-\theta} A(s)  ds. \]

Own-work draft, proof (unaudited), claim T280-w716-C1 v2; independent review pending. For d>=3, uniform probability inputs on S^(d-1), square loss and all-parameter characteristic mean-field gradient flow of f_t(x)=E[a_t ReLU(w_t.x+b_t)], assume continuous L2 residual and locally integrable second parameter moments. Let the initial law be invariant under (a,w,b)->(a,Qw,b) for every Q in O(d), S0=sqrt(a0^2+|w0|^2+b0^2), |w0|>0 almost surely, M2=E[S0^2]<infinity, Mgate=E[a0^2 S0/|w0|]<infinity. For r_t=f_t-y (or centered output minus y), R=||r_0||2>0, c=sqrt(2)R, Cd=Gamma(d/2)/(sqrt(pi)Gamma((d-1)/2)), and initial tangent operator K0, the draft proves ||r_t-exp(-tK0)r_0||2 <= (R/c)[4M2(exp(ct)-1)^2+8sqrt(2)Cd Mgate(exp(ct)-1-ct)] on every finite interval where the characteristic flow exists. The same bound holds for ||P_k r_t-exp(-mu_k t)P_k r_0||2 in each harmonic degree, since K0 is rotationally invariant. The error is O(t^2). For nonzero initial components and mu_j>mu_k it yields strict ordering of their normalized residual norms on an explicit positive short interval. It does not imply ordered half-energy hitting times or settle long-time feature learning. R=0 gives stationary flow. Gaussian a,b,w with nondegenerate isotropic w satisfy the moments. Core step: E[a0^2 |1_{w_t.x+b_t>0}-1_{w0.x+b0>0}|] <=2sqrt(2)Cd Mgate(exp(ct)-1), uniformly in unit x. The bound conditions on initial a,b,|w|; later trajectories need not remain isotropic. No novelty, PDE existence/uniqueness, Lean certification or independent audit is asserted.

[Theorem 5 (Exactness of the multi-judge $N$-vote acceptance rule) of arXiv:2609.00905, 'When Metropolis and Hastings Meet Bradley and Terry: Exact MCMC From Preference Voting'] Under the multi-judge BT parametric assumptions from
Section~\ref{sec:multi-judge}, for every integer \(N\ge 1\), the multi-judge
$N$-vote acceptance rule in Eq.~\eqref{eq:multi-n-vote-main}, combined with a
valid proposal kernel \(q\), defines a Markov transition kernel that satisfies
detailed balance with respect to the composite target \(\pi_m\). Consequently,
the resulting chain is reversible and has \(\pi_m\) as a stationary
distribution.

[Corollary thm:main of arXiv:2411.16572, 'Optimal decay of eigenvector overlap for non-Hermitian random matrices'] Consider an i.i.d. matrix $X$ satisfying Assumption (ass:mainass of the paper). Furthermore, we assume that $\chi$ has a 
bounded density $g$ and  in the complex case $\mathrm{Re}\,\chi, \mathrm{Im}\, \chi$ are independent. 
Fix any small constants $\tau, \epsilon,\xi>0$  with $\xi\le \epsilon/10$
and any large constant $D>0$. Set $\mathcal{D}^{\xi}_{z}\subset {\mathbb C}$ to be the disk centered at $z\in {\mathbb C}$ with radius $n^{-1/2+\xi}$.  Then for any $z_i\in {\mathbb C} ~(i=1,2)$ with $|z_i|\leq 1+n^{-1/2+\tau}$ and $|z_1-z_2| \geq n^{-1/2+\epsilon}$, there is an event $\Xi$ with very high probability, i.e. ${\boldsymbol{P}}(\Xi)\ge 1-n^{-D}$,
  such that
\begin{align}
 {\boldsymbol{E} } \Big(\sum_{\sigma_i\in \mathcal{D}^\xi_{z_1},\sigma_j\in \mathcal{D}^{\xi}_{z_2}} |\mathcal{O}_{ij}|\cdot {\bf 1}_\Xi \Big) &\lesssim \frac{ n^{8\xi}}{|z_1-z_2|^2}, \qquad \mbox{[Complex case]} \\

{\boldsymbol{E} } \Big(\sum_{\sigma_i\in \mathcal{D}^\xi_{z_1},\sigma_j\in \mathcal{D}^{\xi}_{z_2}} |\mathcal{O}_{ij}|\cdot {\bf 1}_\Xi \Big) &\lesssim \frac{ n^{8\xi}}{|z_1-z_2|^2} \cdot \frac{1}{|\mathrm{Im}\, z_1|\wedge |\mathrm{Im}\, z_2|}, \qquad \mbox{[Real case]}
\end{align}

 

Furthermore, in the complex case 
in the bulk regime, i.e if $|z_1|, |z_2|\le 1-\tau$,
 the event $\Xi$ is trivial, i.e. (equation Oij of the paper) holds without
${\bf 1}_\Xi$.  In the real case we have a special bound for the real eigenvalues $\sigma_i, \sigma_j$ 
near $z_1, z_2$:
\begin{equation}
   {\boldsymbol{E} } \Big(\sum_{\substack{\sigma_i\in \mathcal{D}^\xi_{z_1}\cap {\mathbb R }\\\sigma_j\in \mathcal{D}^{\xi}_{z_2}\cap {\mathbb R }}} |\mathcal{O}_{ij}|^{1/2} 
 \Big) \lesssim \frac{ n^{4\xi}}{|z_1-z_2|}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary thm:main of arXiv:2411.16572

[Theorem 19 of arXiv:2604.24392, 'Numerical approximation of Markovian BSDEs in infinite horizon and elliptic PDEs'] {Assume \eqref{as:generatorf}, \eqref{as:b:sigma}, \eqref{as:int:X:nablaX} and \eqref{as:suprho}, $a>\theta$ and $\ta>\ttheta$.\\
 
 We set $r'\geqslant 2$ such that $r'>r$ where $r$ comes from \eqref{prop:representationBSDEinfinitehorizon:growth}. We also assume that $\kappa_{\infty}<1$, $\norm{ v}_{{\rho}_r} \leqslant B <+\infty$ and $v \in C^2(\bR^{d},\bR^{d'}\times \bR^{d' \times d})$ with the growth $\norm{\nabla^2 v(x)} \leqslant C(1+|x|^{r'})$.
 
Then there exist some constants $\varepsilon \in (0,\kappa_{\infty}^{-1}-1)$ and $\delta_0>0$ such that the following holds for $M \in \bN^*$, $\tilde{N} \in \bN$, $n \in \bN$ and $\delta \leqslant \delta_0$.
 
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item If $\sigma$ is constant, $\ta-\ttheta-(1+r)K_b>0$ and ${a}-{\theta}-r K_b>0$, then 
  $$\Exp{ \sup_{x \in \bR^d} \norm{\frac{ Pv^{n}_M(x) -v(x)}{\rho_{r'}(x)}} } = O\left( \delta^2+\frac{(\ln (2+\tilde{N}))^{1/(r+1)}}{\sqrt{M}} + |1 \vee (\tilde{N}\delta)|^{r-r'}+ \left(\kappa_{\infty}(1+\varepsilon)\right)^n \right).$$
  \item If $f(x,y,z)=f(x,y)$ and $a-{\theta}-r K_b>0$, then
  $$\Exp{ \sup_{x \in \bR^d} \norm{\frac{ Pv^{n}_M(x) -v(x)}{\rho_{r'}(x)}}} = O\left( \delta^2+\frac{(\ln (2+\tilde{N}))^{1/(r\vee 1)}}{\sqrt{M}} + |1 \vee (\tilde{N}\delta)|^{r-r'} +\left(\kappa_{\infty}(1+\varepsilon)\right)^n \right).$$
  \item If $\beta \geqslant 2$,  $\ta-(r+1)K_b-\frac{2\beta-1}{2} K_{\sigma}^2-\frac{\beta-1}{\beta} \ttheta>0$ and $a-rK_b-\frac{\beta-1}{\beta} {\theta}>0$, then 
  $$\Exp{ \sup_{x \in \bR^d} \norm{\frac{ Pv^{n}_M(x) -v(x)}{\rho_{r'}(x)}}} = O\left( \delta^2+\frac{(1+2\tilde{N})^{d/\beta}}{\sqrt{M}} + |1 \vee (\tilde{N}\delta)|^{r-r'} +\left(\kappa_{\infty}(1+\varepsilon)\right)^n \right).$$
 \end{enumerate}
}

[Corollary 49 of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] Let $0 \leq \alpha \leq 1$.
	Let $\beta \in \R$ be fixed but arbitrary. Let $S_0, S_1$, $\{S_0^k\}_{k\in \Nbb}$, $\{S_1^k\}_{k \in \Nbb} \in \SymHS(\Hcal)_{< I}$.
	Assume that $\lim_{k \approach \infty}||S_0^k - S_0||_{\HS} = 0$, $\lim_{k \approach \infty}||S_1^k - S_1||_{\HS} = 0$.
	Let $A= (I-S_1)^{-1/2}(S_1-S_0)(I-S_1)^{-1/2}$, $A^k = (I-S_1^k)^{-1/2}(S_1^k-S_0^k)(I-S^k_1)^{-1/2}$.
	Then
	\begin{align}
		&\lim_{k \approach \infty}\det[(1-\alpha)(I+A^k)^{-\alpha} + \alpha (I+A^k)^{1-\alpha}]^{\beta}
		\nonumber
		\\
		& = \det[(1-\alpha)(I+A)^{-\alpha} + \alpha (I+A)^{1-\alpha}]^{\beta}.

body:
[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] Within our coupling of the collection times (Definition~\ref{def:coupling}),
  $T_{m,0}$ is independent of $T_{m,p} - T_{m,0}$ and this difference
  has \textsc{mgf}
  \[
    M_{T_{m, p} - T_{m, 0}}(t) = I_{m, p}(t), \quad t \leqslant 0.
  \]
  \begin{proof}
    If $T_{m, 0} = k$, then the value of $T_{m, p} - T_{m, 0}$
    is a deterministic function of the initial clumsiness $\{ U_{L(i,k)} \}_{i \in [m]}$,
    the future updates $\{ C_n \}_{n > k}$,
    and the future clumsiness $\{ U_n \}_{n > k}$. Call this function $f$.
    We will make $f$ explicit. Consider an initial clumsiness vector
    $\mathbf{x} = (x_1, \dots, x_m)^\top \in [0, 1]^m$,
    coupon updates $\mathbf{y} = (y_n)_{n > 0} \in [m]^\mathbb{N}$,
    and future clumsiness $\mathbf{z} = (z_n)_{n > 0} \in [0, 1]^\mathbb{N}$.
    Then define
    $L'(i, n; \mathbf{y})$ as the most recent update of coupon $i$
    no later than $n$,
    \[
      L'(i, n; \mathbf{y}) \coloneqq
      \sup\{ k \leqslant n \mid y_k = i \}, \quad
      i \in [m], \quad n \geqslant 0,
    \]
    where naturally $\sup\emptyset = -\infty$ and $L'(i, 0; \mathbf{y}) = -\infty$.
    Define
    \begin{align*}
      f(\mathbf{x}; \mathbf{y}; \mathbf{z})
      \coloneqq \inf \{ n \geqslant 0 \mid {} &\text{for all $i \in [m]$,}\\
          &\text{if $x_i > 1-p$ or $L'(i, n; \mathbf{y}) > 0$,}\\
          &\text{then $L'(i, n; \mathbf{y}) > 0$
          and $z_{L'(i, n; \mathbf{y})} \leq 1-p$}
          \}.
    \end{align*}
    Thus, for any integers $\ell \geqslant m$ and $x \geqslant 0$,
    \begin{align*}
      \PP\left( T_{m,p} - T_{m,0} = x \right)
      &= \sum_{k \geqslant m}
        \PP\left( T_{m,p} - T_{m,0} = x \mid T_{m,0} = k\right)
        \PP(T_{m,0} = k)\\
      &= \sum_{k \geqslant m} \PP\left(f(U_{L(1, k)}, \dots, U_{L(m, k)};
      C_{k+1}, C_{k+2}, \dots;
      U_{k+1}, U_{k+2}, \dots) = x\right)\\
      &\qquad \qquad \qquad \times \PP\left(T_{m,0} = k\right)\\
      &= \sum_{k \geqslant m} \PP\left(f(U_{L(1, \ell)}, \dots, U_{L(m, \ell)};
      C_{\ell+1}, C_{\ell+2}, \dots;
      U_{\ell+1}, U_{\ell+2}, \dots) = x\right)\\
      &\qquad \qquad \qquad \times \PP\left(T_{m,0} = k\right)\\
      &= \PP\left(f(U_{L(1, \ell)}, \dots, U_{L(m, \ell)};
      C_{\ell+1}, C_{\ell+2}, \dots;
      U_{\ell+1}, U_{\ell+2}, \dots) = x\right)\\
      &\qquad \qquad \qquad \times \underbrace{
        \sum_{k \geqslant m} \PP\left(T_{m,0} = k\right)
      }_1\\
      &= \PP\left(T_{m,p} - T_{m,0} = x \mid T_{m,0} = \ell\right).
    \end{align*}
    The third line uses our i.i.d.~assumptions from
    Definition~\ref{def:coupling}.
    This proves the independence of $T_{m,0}$ and $T_{m,p} - T_{m, 0}$.
    Hence the factorisation
    $M_{T_{m,0}}(t)\,M_{T_{m,p} - T_{m,0}}(t) = M_{T_{m,0}}\,I_{m,p}(t)$.
    These quantities are non-zero; divide both sides to conclude the proof.
    
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 19 of arXiv:2605.14206

[Proposition 41 (Gauss--Chebyshev quadrature) of arXiv:2609.03736, '2609.03736'] For every $N\geq2$, there is, up to relabeling, exactly one positive
$N$-point Gaussian quadrature rule for the arcsine measure.  It is the pair
$(\eta_N,\gamma_N)$ in Equation~\eqref{eq:Chebyshev-parameters}.
Its node polynomial is a scalar normalization of $T_N$, and its critical
points are $\cos(k\pi/N)$, $1\leq k<N$.  Here $T_N$ and $U_{N-1}$ are the
Chebyshev polynomials defined by
\begin{equation}
 T_N(\cos\theta)=\cos(N\theta),\qquad
 U_{N-1}(\cos\theta)=\frac{\sin(N\theta)}{\sin\theta};
 
\end{equation}
in particular, $T_N'=NU_{N-1}$.  No positive measure supported on $N$ points is exact on
all polynomials of degree $2N$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Gauss--Chebyshev quadrature

(0 < lambda <= Lambda), and |b| + |c| <= K. Let u in W^{2,n}_loc(Omega) satisfy Lu = 0 a.e. and u >= 0 in Omega. Then for every ball with B_{2R}(y) contained in Omega and R <= R_0, sup over B_R(y) of u <= C inf over B_R(y) of u, with C depending only on n, Lambda/lambda, K/lambda and R_0 (and only on n and Lambda/lambda when b = c = 0). Consequently strong solutions of Lu = 0 with measurable uniformly elliptic coefficients are locally Hoelder continuous, with the corresponding interior estimate; for b = c = 0 the exponent is alpha = alpha(n, Lambda/lambda), and in general it depends in addition on K/lambda and on the scale R_0. This is the nondivergence-form counterpart of the De Giorgi-Nash-Moser theory; neither theorem implies the other, because a nondivergence operator with measurable coefficients has no variational structure.

[Definition of arXiv:2512.18435, 'Indistinguishability for recurrent clusters'] A \textbf{tail component property} is a component property $\mathscr A$ such that if $\omega$ and $\omega'$ are two percolation configurations with environments $\eta$ and $\eta'$ such that $\eta$ and $\eta'$ differ only at finitely many sites or edges, and the clusters of $o$ in $\omega$ and $\omega'$ are infinite and have a finite symmetric difference, then either $o$ has type $\mathscr A$ in both $\omega$ and $\omega'$, or in neither.

    We call a component property $\mathscr A$ \textbf{essentially tail} if there exists a tail component property $\mathscr A'$ with $\mathbb P(\{(\eta,x)\in\mathscr A\}\bigtriangleup\{(\eta,x)\in\mathscr A'\})=0$.
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2512.18435, 'Indistinguishability for recurrent clusters'

We have

\de R_{ij}(t)

\de M_{ij}(t)
+

\end{equation}
where the local martingale part is
\begin{equation}
\de M_{ij}(t)
=
\int_\Uptheta
\left(\langle G_i(t,\bm{\theta}),x_j(t)\rangle+\langle x_i(t),G_j(t,\bm{\theta})\rangle\right)
\,\mathsf{W}(\de\bm{\theta},\de t),
\end{equation}
and the drift is
\begin{align}
\cD_{ij}(t)
&=
\frac1d\left(d-2+R_{ij}(t)^2\right)\,s_{\mu(t)}(x_i(t),x_j(t))\nonumber\\
&-
\frac{(d-1)}{2d}\,R_{ij}(t)\left(s_{\mu(t)}(x_i(t))+s_{\mu(t)}(x_j(t))\right),
\end{align} 
where $\mu(t) = \mu_{X(t)}$ and 
\begin{align*}
s_\mu(x)&\coloneqq \E\left\|\mathsf{m}_{\upbeta,\bA}[\mu](x)\right\|^2,\nonumber\\
s_\mu(x,x')&\coloneqq \E\left\langle \mathsf{m}_{\upbeta,\bA}[\mu](x),\mathsf{m}_{\upbeta,\bA}[\mu](x')\right\rangle.
\end{align*}

Consider the coexistence equilibrium K_3 = (N*, P*) with m > c and k*(m - c) > c. The Jacobian matrix J(K_3) has positive determinant. Its trace satisfies (1 + N*)*Trace(J(K_3)) = (2*N*/k)*((k - 1)/2 - N*). Consequently, K_3 is a locally asymptotically stable sink if k < (m + c)/(m - c), undergoes a supercritical Hopf bifurcation at k = (m + c)/(m - c), and becomes an unstable source surrounded by a unique stable limit cycle for k > (m + c)/(m - c).
m > c and k*(m - c) > c

body: [Lemma lem:VHStheorem of arXiv:2411.02030, 'Finite ergodic components for upper probabilities'] Let $(\Omega, \mathcal{F})$ be a measurable space, and $\{P_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence  of probabilities. Suppose that  for each $A\in \mathcal{F}$, the  limit  $\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} P_n(A)$ exists, denoted by $Q(A)$. Then $Q$ is a probability on $(\Omega,\mathcal{F})$. If we further suppose that each $P_n$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the probability $Q$, then the absolute continuity of  $P_n$ with respect to $Q$ is uniform in $n\in\mathbb{N}$, that is, for any $\epsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that for  any $A\in\mathcal{F}$, if  $Q(A)<\delta$ then $ P_n(A)<\epsilon$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Fluctuations of shortest routes in Poisson proximity networks structural calculation Result: A deterministic route of length D connecting points at distance r and reaching perpendicular deviation T must satisfy D>=sqrt(r^2+4*T^2). To see this, split at a point of maximal deviation and minimize the sum of its distances to the two endpoints over the longitudinal coordinate; the minimum occurs above the midpoint. Hence T<=sqrt(D^2-r^2)/2. Check: When D/r tends to a stretch constant mu>1, the bound gives only T/r<=sqrt(mu^2-1)/2 asymptotically. It does not force sublinear wandering. This explicitly explains why the existing route-length shape theorem does not already identify a transversal exponent. Obstruction: A KPZ-type prediction needs estimates for centered route excess and correlations of competing near-geodesics. The deterministic Euclidean inequality leaves an order-r allowance whenever the limiting stretch exceeds1.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0214-fluctuations-of-shortest-routes-in-poisson-proximity-networks
No independent review

 E_k(L)=P_k(U)\mathfrak a\Lambda,
 \qquad
 \PP(E_k(L))=P_k(U)\mathfrak a
 \qquad(1\le k<\ell),
\]
whereas
\[
 E_\ell(L)=\bigl(P_\ell(U)\bigr)\subset\Lambda,
 \qquad
 \PP(E_\ell(L))=\bigl(P_\ell(U)\bigr)\subset P.
\]
