[Lemma lem:one-step-descent-convex-nonconvex of arXiv:2608.29507, 'Denoising as Projection: Constrained Optimization with Gradient-Guided Diffusion'] Let $\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be nonempty, compact, and convex. Suppose that $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ is $L$-smooth on a convex neighborhood containing the iterates and $\mathcal{X}$. Consider the backward update as in (equation eq:projected-gradient-guidance-relaxed of the paper)
with ~$ \epsilon\eta L<2.$
Assume that, for every $z$,
~~ $\widehat\pi_t(z)\in\mathcal{X},
~~
\|\widehat\pi_t(z)-\pi_{\mathcal{X}}(z)\|\le E_t.$ Let
~~$p_t:=\pi_{\mathcal{X}}(x_t),
n_t:=x_t-p_t.$
Define the following constants
\begin{align*}
&\textstyle \alpha_{\eta,\epsilon}:=\epsilon\eta\left(1-\frac{\epsilon\eta L}{2}\right),
~~A_{\eta,\epsilon}:=1+\epsilon\eta L,~~
G:=\textstyle\sup_{x\in\mathcal{X}}\|\nabla f(x)\|,
~~
\Gamma_1:=GA_{\eta,\epsilon},
~~
\Gamma_2:=LA_{\eta,\epsilon}^2.
\end{align*}
Then, with $\mathcal G_\eta(p_t)$ defined in (equation eq:def-G-eta of the paper), we have
\begin{align*}
f(p_{t-1})
&\le
f(p_t)
-
\alpha_{\eta,\epsilon}\|\mathcal G_\eta(p_t)\|^2
+
\Gamma_1\|n_t\|
+
\Gamma_2\|n_t\|^2\
+
\epsilon GE_t
+
\epsilon^2LE_t^2.
\end{align*}
Moreover, the normal component satisfies
~~ $\|n_{t-1}\|\le (1-\epsilon)\|n_t\|.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: One-step descent for nonconvex objectives over a convex region

body: [Dfn 15 (Weak lumping) of arXiv:2604.12853, 'Coupling Markov Chains \\with a Common Image Chain'] We say that a stochastic matrix $P\in\SM(A)$ is \textbf{weakly lumpable} with respect to a surjective map $f: A \twoheadrightarrow B$ if there exists $\upalpha\in\PM(A)$ such that $f(\MC(\upalpha,P))$ is a homogeneous Markov chain taking values in $B$. In this case, we say that $\MC(\upalpha,P)$ \textbf{lumps weakly} under $f$, and that $f$ is a \textbf{weak lumping} of $\MC(\upalpha,P)$. If the transition matrix of $f(\MC(\upalpha,P))$ is $Q$ then we say that $P$ is weakly lumpable to $Q$ under $f$, and we say that $\MC(\upalpha,P)$ lumps weakly to $\MC(f_*(\upalpha),Q)$ under $f$.
title: Weak lumping

[Theorem thm-omni-intro of arXiv:2412.03067, 'Geodesic Trees and Exceptional Directions in FPP on Hyperbolic Groups'] $ $
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $G$ is not free (up to finite index), almost surely exceptional directions in ${\partial G}$ exist and are dense ${\partial G}$ (Theorem~(thm-nonfreedense of the paper)).
\item If ${\partial G}$ has topological dimension $\dim_t {\partial G}$ greater than 1, then almost surely there are 
\emph{uncountably many} exceptional directions (Theorem~(thm-uncountable of the paper)).
\item If $G$ is a cocompact lattice in the hyperbolic plane, and the Cayley graph $\Gamma$ is planar, then  almost surely there are \emph{countably many} exceptional directions (Theorem~(thm-countable of the paper)). 
\item Let $G$ be a  hyperbolic group such that $\dim_t {\partial G} = n-1$. Then
there exists an exceptional direction $z \in {\partial G}$ with multiplicity at \emph{at least $n$}. Thus there exist hyperbolic groups with arbitrarily large
multiplicity of an exceptional direction (in the sense of Question~(qn-exceptionaldirn of the paper)(3)).
\item Exceptional directions have measure zero with respect to the Patterson-Sullivan measure (Theorem~(t:exceptional of the paper)). In fact the set of exceptional directions has Hausdorff dimension (almost surely uniformly) smaller than that of ${\partial G}$.
\item For any (fixed) $\Gamma$, there exists an almost sure uniform upper bound 
on the  multiplicity of an exceptional direction (in the sense of Question~(qn-exceptionaldirn of the paper)(3)) (Theorem~(t:finite of the paper)).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm-omni-intro of arXiv:2412.03067

body:
[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2608.19744, 'Conditioned Brownian motion and local equivalence of path ensembles'] Let $X$ be an $\R^d$-valued conservative Markov process reversible with respect to a
probability measure $\mu$, and let $Q$ be a nonnegative, nonconstant
observable.  Suppose that conditions \textbf{(I)}-\textbf{(V)} above
hold.  Let
\[
    \theta\in\lambda'((0,\infty)),
    \qquad
    \lambda'(\beta_\theta)=\theta,
\]
and put
\[
    v_\theta=-\lambda''(\beta_\theta)>0,
    \qquad
    I_Q(\theta)
       =\lambda(\beta_\theta)-\beta_\theta\theta.
\]
Then, for every fixed initial state $x$ and every fixed $z\in\mathbb R$,
\[
    \bbP_x(A_T\leq\theta T+z)
    \sim
    \frac{
      \psi_{\beta_\theta}(x)
      \langle\psi_{\beta_\theta},\mathbf 1\rangle_{L^2(\mu)}
    }{
      \beta_\theta\sqrt{2\pi v_\theta T}
    }
    \exp\!\left(
       -I_Q(\theta)T+\beta_\theta z
    \right).
\]
Whenever the estimates in \textbf{(III)} are locally uniform in the
initial state, this asymptotic is locally uniform in $(x,z)$.

Moreover, for every $S<\infty$,
\[
    \mathcal L_{\bbP_x}
       \bigl((X_t)_{0\leq t\leq S}\mid A_T\leq\theta T\bigr)
    \longrightarrow
    \mathcal L_{\bbP_x^{(\beta_\theta)}}
       \bigl((X_t)_{0\leq t\leq S}\bigr)
\]
in total variation.  The corresponding fixed-width conclusion of
Corollary~\ref{cor:fixed-width-window} holds as well.

[Prop 8 of arXiv:2608.30554, 'Strong law of large numbers for generalized operator means II'] Let $X_1, X_2, ... $ be a sequence of i.i.d. real-valued random variables, and let $h \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a non-decreasing function such that
 $$ \mathbb{E}[|h(X_1 - r)|\log^+ |h(X_1 - r)|] < \infty$$ for every real $r$.
Assume that the equation $$\mathbb{E}h(X_1 - x) = 0$$ has the unique solution $x=0$.
 For arbitrary initial values $s_1,\hat{s}_1  \in \mathbb{R}$, consider the implicit stochastic approximations
$$\frac1n h(X_n - s_n) + s_{n-1} = s_n $$
and
$$
\frac1n h(X_n - \hat{s}_n) + h(\hat{s}_{n-1}-\hat{s}_n) = 0.
$$
The resulting sequences $\{s_n\}_{n \geq 1}$ and $\{\hat{s}\}_{n \geq 1}$ both converge to $0$ almost surely, given that in the case of the second iteration $\{\hat{s}\}_{n \geq 1}$, we additionally have that $h^{-1}$ exists and satisfies $$h^{-1}(x)=x+O(x^2)$$ in a neighborhood of $0$.
title: Prop 8 of arXiv:2608.30554

body:
[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2608.13358, 'Extreme points of sets of probability measures and $\phi$-divergences'] Assume that $\cI=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ for some $n\in \N$. Then, for $p\in \cM$, the following statements are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $p$ is an extreme point of $\cM$.
    \item There exist $m\in \N$, coefficients $\alpha_1,\ldots, \alpha_m>0$, and pairwise disjoint $p$-atoms $A_1,\ldots, A_m\in \cF$ such that
    \[
    p=\sum_{j=1}^m\alpha_j\, p_{A_j}
    \]
    and the matrix
    \[
    \left(\begin{matrix}
    1 & \dots & 1 \\
    f_1(A_1) & \dots & f_1(A_m) \\
    \vdots & & \vdots \\
    f_n(A_1) & \dots & f_n(A_m)
    \end{matrix}\right)
    \]
    has rank $m$, i.e., the vectors
    \[
    v_j:=\big(1,f_1(A_j),\ldots,f_n(A_j)\big)^\top\in\R^{n+1},
    \qquad j=1,\ldots,m,
    \]
    are linearly independent. In particular, extremality forces $m\leq n+1$.
    \item $p$ is $\ll$-minimal in $\cM$.
    \item For every $p'\in\cM\setminus\{p\}$, every $q\in\cM$ with $p\ll q$ and $p'\ll q$, and every convex function $\varphi\colon[0,\infty)\to\R$ satisfying \eqref{eq:phi:blowup},
    one has
    \[
    \lim_{\lambda\uparrow 1}\frac{\Div{\varphi}{\lambda p+(1-\lambda)p'}{q}-\Div{\varphi}{p}{q}}{1-\lambda}=-\infty.
    \]
    In particular, $\lambda=1$ is a strict local maximizer of the map
    \begin{equation*}
        [0,1]\to[0,\infty),\quad \lambda\mapsto\Div{\varphi}{\lambda p+(1-\lambda)p'}{q}.
    \end{equation*}
\end{enumerate}

For n>=3, let A_n={(a,b_1,...,b_n) in {-1,1}^{n+1}: a+b_i+b_(i+1) is in {-1,1} for every cyclic index i}, with b_(n+1)=b_1. Choose an independent dominating vertex set U of C_n with d=|U|=ceil(n/3) and every cyclic gap between consecutive vertices of U of length 2 or 3 (the singleton case n=3 has gap length 3). For u in U define L_u(a,b)=a+b_u and Z_u=1_{L_u!=0}. For z in {0,1}^U write (A_n)_z={x in A_n: Z(x)=z} and |z|=sum_u z_u. Then |(A_n)_z|<=2^(n+1-d-|z|) for every z. Consequently |A_n|/2^(n+1)<=(3/4)^d and, defining ell(A_n)=n+1-log_2|A_n|, d<=ell(A_n)/log_2(4/3). This is the activation-cell estimate for this particular certificate, not for an arbitrary vertex set U. On a=1, the vertices with b_i=1 form an independent set; gap lengths 2 and 3 have completion counts (2,1,1) and (3,2,1) according to the endpoint sum (0,1,2), each at most 2^(g-1-(s+t)/2). Antipodality supplies the factor 2.
n>=3 and A_n is the explicitly defined rooted NAE cycle sign fibre
U is an independent dominating set of size ceil(n/3) with cyclic gaps 2 or 3

  Consider the following rule and axiom schemes:
  \begin{align*}
    \textsf{N}_a  &: \quad \frac{\varphi \to \psi}{\varphi \lewis \psi}, \\
    \textsf{Tr}   &: \quad (\varphi \lewis \psi) \to ((\psi \lewis \chi) \to (\varphi \lewis \chi)), \\
    \textsf{K}_a  &: \quad (\varphi \lewis \psi) \to ((\varphi \lewis \chi) \to (\varphi \lewis (\psi \land \chi))), \\
    \textsf{Di}   &: \quad (\varphi \lewis \chi) \to ((\psi \lewis \chi) \to ((\varphi \lor \psi) \lewis \chi)), \\
    \textsf{Box}  &: \quad (\varphi \lewis \psi) \to \Box(\varphi \to \psi).
  \end{align*}
  We define:
  \begin{align*}
    \textbf{HLC}^\flat  &\coloneq \textbf{Int} + \textsf{N}_a + \textsf{Tr} + \textsf{K}_a, &
    \textbf{HLC}^\sharp &\coloneq \textbf{HLC}^\flat + \textsf{Di}, \quad \\
    \textbf{i-Box}      &\coloneq \textbf{HLC}^\sharp + \textsf{Box}.
  \end{align*}
  Following the notation in [visser_lewis_2024,groot_relational_2026],
  a $\textsf{Di}$-free logic is generally marked with a superscript $\flat$,
  and its extension by $\textsf{Di}$ with a superscript $\sharp$.\footnote{
    Litak and Visser [litak_lewis_2018] denote $\textbf{HLC}^\flat$ and $\textbf{HLC}^\sharp$
    by $\textbf{iA}^-$ and $\textbf{iA}$, respectively.

    while their sharp versions carry no superscript.}

[Lemma 13 of arXiv:2608.27398, 'Strict Stability and Strict Minimality of Regular Area-Minimizing Hypercones: A Quantitati'] Assume that $\C$ is strictly stable and strictly minimizing.  There is
\[
    \mathcal X
    \in C^0(\R^{n+1}\setminus\{0\};\mathbb S^n),
\]
smooth in $U_+\cup U_-$, such that
\begin{align}
    \mathcal X&=\nu_E
      &&\text{on }\C\setminus\{0\},
      \\
    \diver\mathcal X&\geq c_\C q_\C
      &&\text{in }U_+,
      \\
    \diver\mathcal X&\leq-c_\C q_\C
      &&\text{in }U_-,
      \\
       |\diver \mathcal X|
    &\leq C_\C q_\C
      &&\text{in }U_+\cup U_-.
      
\end{align}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}

    \diver \mathcal X
    =
    g
    \qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\R^{n+1}),
\end{equation}
where
\[
    g(x)
    =
    \begin{cases}
    \diver \mathcal X,
       &x\in U_+\cup U_-,\\[2ex]
    0,
       &x\in\C,
    \end{cases}
\]
and $g
    \in
    C^0(\R^{n+1}\setminus\{0\})
    \cap
    L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R^{n+1}).$

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.02682, 'LDP for tensor forms'] In this paper, we study the large deviation principle (LDP) for a tensor-weighted functional of i.i.d. random variables, when the sequence of tensors converges under a variant of the \enquote{bad} cut norm. Using the LDP, we analyze a Gibbs measure with a tensor-valued Hamiltonian, and characterize the optimizers of the limiting variational problem in terms of a functional fixed point equation. As applications, we focus on several concrete examples, which include monochromatic subgraph counts in sparse random graphs, Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi hypergraphs, and a generalized Potts statistic of order $v\ge 2$. Studying the optimization problem, we give sufficient conditions for uniqueness of the optimizer, as well as for existence of constant optimizers (replica symmetry). Our results demonstrate universal weak laws for a large class of tensor Gibbs models with approximately regular tensors.
title: Abstract of arXiv:2609.02682: LDP for tensor forms

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2506.13913, '2506.13913'] {Fundamental Properties of the Itô Integral}{}
Let \(f, g \in L^2([0, T] \times \Omega)\) be processes adapted to \(\mathcal{F}_t\), and let \(a, b \in \mathbb{R}\). Then

   \begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Linearity.} The Itô integral is linear, i.e., 
    \[
    \int_0^T \big(a f(t) + b g(t)\big) \, \mathrm{d}W_t = a \int_0^T f(t) \, \mathrm{d}W_t + b \int_0^T g(t) \, \mathrm{d}W_t.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Isometry.} The Itô integral satisfies the isometry property, i.e., 
    \[
    \mathbb{E}\left[\left(\int_0^T f(t) \, \mathrm{d}W_t\right)^2\right] = \mathbb{E}\left[\int_0^T f(t)^2 \, \mathrm{d}t\right].
    \]

    \item \textbf{Martingale Property.} The process
    \[
    M_t = \int_0^t f(s) \, \mathrm{d}W_s, \quad t \in [0, T],
    \]
    is a martingale with respect to the filtration \((\mathcal{F}_t)\).

    \item \textbf{Quadratic Variation.} The quadratic variation of the Itô integral is given by
    \[
    \left[\int_0^t f(s) \, \mathrm{d}W_s\right]_t = \int_0^t f(s)^2 \, \mathrm{d}s.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Zero-Mean Property.} The expectation of the Itô integral is zero, i.e., 
    \[
    \mathbb{E}\left[\int_0^T f(t) \, \mathrm{d}W_t\right] = 0.
    \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 9 of arXiv:2506.13913

[Definition of arXiv:2607.24640, 'The Yang-Mills measure on surfaces via Morse theory'] The free boundary Yang-Mills measure is defined as
$$
\int_{\Omega\times G^{2g}} \Phi(\omega,\mathrm{b}) \mathbb{P}_{\operatorname{YM}}^{{\rm free}}(d\omega,d\mathrm{b}) :=\int_{\Omega\times G^{2g}}\Phi\left(\omega,(\mathrm{b}_a)_{\operatorname{ind}(a)=1})\right)\mathbb{P}(d\omega)\mu_G^{\otimes 2g}(d\mathrm{b}),
$$
where $\mathbb{P}$ is the white noise probability measure, $\Omega$ is the probability space of the white noise, and $\Phi:\Omega\times G^{2g}\rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ is an integrable function with respect to the $\sigma$-algebra induced by the product of the one on $\Omega$ and the Borel sets of $G^{2g}$.
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2607.24640, 'The Yang-Mills measure on surfaces via Morse theory'

body:
[Definition def:density_profiles of arXiv:2607.08914, 'Linear spreading speed in non-monotone population models'] For given $\varepsilon, \delta  >0$ and $k_0 \in \mathbb{N}$, \emph{comparison
    density profiles} are deterministic functions
  $\xi_k^{-}, \xi_k^{+} : \mathbb{Z} \to [0,\infty)$, $k=0,1,\dots,k_0$, satisfying:
  \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item 
    For every $k=0,\dots,k_0$ and all $x \in \mathbb{Z}$,
    $(1+\delta )\xi_k^{-}(x) \le (1-\delta ) \xi_k^{+}(x)$.

    \item 
    For every $k=0,\dots,k_0$,
    $\Supp(\xi_k^-) \coloneq \{x\in \mathbb Z: \xi_k^-(x) > 0\}$ is finite, and
    $\xi_k^-(x)\ge \varepsilon $ for
    every $x\in \Supp(\xi_k^-)$.

    \item 
    For every $k = 0,\dots,k_0-1$, and $x\in \Supp(\xi_{k+1}^-)$ it holds
    that if $\zeta : B_R(x) \to \mathbb R$ satisfies $\zeta (y) \in
    [\xi_k^{-}(y), \xi_k^{+}(y)]$ for all $y\in B_R(x)$, then
    \begin{equation}
      
      (1+\delta) \xi_{k+1}^{-}(x)
      \le V_R^{-1} \sum_{y \in B_R(x)} \varphi_\mu ( \zeta(y))
      \le (1-\delta) \xi_{k+1}^{+}(x).
    \end{equation}
  \end{enumerate}
title: Definition def:density_profiles of arXiv:2607.08914

[Thm Power-law bounds of arXiv:2606.19583, 'Power-law hypothesis and (un)fairness of PageRank on undirected multi-type PAMs'] Consider the undirected multi-type PAM $(G_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with finite set of colors $S=\{1,2,\ldots,q\}$ with $q \in \mathbb{N}$. Further, for any $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\phi_n$ denote a vertex that is chosen uniformly at random from $G_n$, and let $c \in (0,1)$.
Then there exists a constant $\gamma \in (1,\infty)$ that does not depend on the color $k$ such that, as $r \rightarrow \infty$, the graph-normalized PageRank with damping factor $c$ satisfies
\begin{align}
&\liminf_{n \rightarrow \infty} \mathbb{P}(R_{\phi_n}(G_n)>r \mid X_{\phi_n}=k) \geq (1+o(1))\frac{2\Gamma(m_k+\frac{2}{\varphi_k^{\boldsymbol{m}}})}{\varphi_k^{\boldsymbol{m}} \Gamma(m_k)}\sum_{s=\lceil \gamma r \rceil}^\infty\frac{\Gamma(s)}{\Gamma(s+\frac{2} {\varphi_k^{\boldsymbol{m}}}+1)} \cr
&\limsup_{n \rightarrow \infty} \mathbb{P}(R_{\phi_n}(G_n)>r \mid X_{\phi_n}=k) \leq \frac{2\Gamma(m_k+\frac{2}{\varphi_k^{\boldsymbol{m}}})}{\varphi_k^{\boldsymbol{m}} \Gamma(m_k)}\sum_{s=\lceil r \rceil}^\infty\frac{\Gamma(s)}{\Gamma(s+\frac{2} {\varphi_k^{\boldsymbol{m}}}+1)}.  
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Power-law bounds for PageRank in undirected multi-type PAM

[Lemma eq:expdecay of arXiv:2411.07157, 'Rough differential equations in the flow approach'] Fix $t_0\in[0,1]$, $N\in\N$, and consider $\lambda\in C^\infty(\R)$ with $\mathrm{supp} \,\lambda\subset[t_0-c\mu,t_0]$ for some universal constant $c>0$. Then, the following holds uniformly in $t_0\in[0,1]$ and $\mu\in[0,1]$:
   \begin{equs}
         \norm{K_{N,\mu}\lambda}_{L^p}&\lesssim_c  \mu^{1/p} \norm{K_{N,\mu}\lambda}_{L^\infty}\;\;\text{for every}\;p\in[1,\infty]\,,\\         
       \norm{(t_0-)K_{N,\mu}\lambda}_{L^1}&\lesssim_c  \mu \norm{K_{N,\mu}\lambda}_{L^1}\,. 
   \end{equs} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma eq:expdecay of arXiv:2411.07157

Fix beta in(0,1/2], n>=1 and a deterministic nonzero x in R^n. Let a_1,...,a_m be independent N(0,I_n) vectors. Define gamma_beta(t)=|t| when |t|>beta, and gamma_beta(t)=t^2/(2 beta)+beta/2 when |t|<=beta. On the probability-one event that a_i^T x!=0 for every i, set F_beta(z)=(1/(2m))sum_i |a_i^T x|^2(gamma_beta((a_i^T z)/(a_i^T x))-1)^2. There are positive C_beta,c_beta,delta_beta depending only on beta such that, if m>=C_beta n, with probability at least1-c_beta exp(-delta_beta m), every local minimum of F_beta is global and every critical point that is not a global minimum has a unit direction v with D_v^2 F_beta(z)<0. Here D_v h(z)=lim_{t down to0}(h(z+t v)-h(z))/t and D_v^2 h=D_v(D_v h), when the limits exist. F_beta is C1 and this is the one-sided directional-curvature convention of the source. This is Theorem1.1 p4 of2101.03540, a geometric result for the stated smoothed amplitude loss.

[Lemma le:tightness_bdry_good_fl_refl of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] There exists $\zeta>0$ such that the following is true. Fix $M,p > 0$, $r \in (0,1)$, and suppose $\delta < r$. Let $h$ be a GFF on $r\mathbf{D}$ with boundary values as in Lemma~(le:reflected_fl_law of the paper). Let $\eta_1,\overline{\eta}_2$ be as defined in Lemma~(le:reflected_fl_law of the paper). Let $z_1 \in \partial B(0,r/2)$, $w_1 \in B(0,3r/16)$, and let $E_\delta$ denote the event that the following hold. 
Let $\eta_{z_1}$ be the flow line starting at $z_1$ and stopped upon exiting $B(0,3r/4)$. Let $\eta_{w_1}$ be the flow line starting at $w_1$, reflected off $\eta_{z_1}$ in the opposite direction, and stopped upon exiting $B(0,r/4)$. Then
\begin{itemize}
 \item $\eta_{w_1}$ intersects the right side of $\eta_{z_1}$ with angle difference $0$ (before reflecting off), and they do not intersect in any other way.
 \item Let $U$ be the region bounded between $\eta_{w_1}, \eta_{z_1}$, and sample the internal metric in $U$. There exist $x,y \in \eta_{w_1} \cap \eta_{z_1}$ such that if $U_{x,y} \subseteq U$ denotes the region between $x$ and $y$, then $\mathrm{diam}(U_{x,y}) \le \delta$ and
\[ D_\epsilon^{\partial U_{x,y}} \ge \delta^\zeta+\epsilon^{a_0} . \]
 \item The angle $\pi$ flow line $\eta^{\pi}_{w_1}$ starting from $w_1$ exits $B(0,3r/4)$ without intersecting $\eta_{z_1}$.
 \item The conditional probability given $\eta_{z_1}$, $\eta_{w_1}$, $\eta^{\pi}_{w_1}$, $X_r^0$, $X_r^{\pi}$, and the values of $h$ on these sets is at least $p$ that
 \begin{itemize}
  \item $\eta_1$ merges into $\eta_{z_1}$ before entering $B(0,r/4)$.
  \item The continuation of $\eta^{\pi}_{w_1}$ does not intersect $\eta_1$ before it hits $\partial B(0,r)$.
 \end{itemize}
\end{itemize}
Then
\[ \mathbf{P}[E_\delta] = o^\infty(\delta) \]
uniformly in the choice of $z_1,w_1$.

body: [Proposition prop:p-Lap-diff of arXiv:2608.21805, 'Logarithmic derivatives of variational and singular stochastic partial differential equati'] For $p > 3$ strictly, the operator $\mathcal{A}(u) = -\mathrm{div}(\lvert \nabla u \rvert^{p-2}\nabla u)$ satisfies conditions (D1) and (D3), the drift side of Assumptions~(ass:diff1 of the paper) and~(ass:diff2 of the paper). The boundary case $p = 3$ falls into the regularised regime alongside $2 < p < 3$ (Proposition~(prop:singular-p-Lap of the paper)); see Remark~(rem:p3-borderline of the paper) below for the precise reason. The range $3 < p < 4$, where (D1) and (D3) do hold but the domination estimate of Proposition~(prop:p-Lap-Lambda of the paper) does not close, is routed through the same regularisation. Conditions (D2)/(D2$'$) and (D4) on $\mathcal{B}$ are independent of the choice of drift and must be verified for the specific noise coefficient under consideration; they hold trivially for any state-independent $\mathcal{B}$ uniformly Hilbert--Schmidt-bounded (with $\mathcal{B}'_u = \mathcal{B}''_{uu} = 0$, so the unified growth bound~(equation eq:B-growth-m of the paper) holds with $\kappa_{m_0} = 0$ at any finite $m_0 \geq 2$, and equally trivially for linear multiplicative noise $\mathcal{B}(t,u) = Lu$ with $\kappa_{m_0} = m_0$). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The $p$-Laplacian satisfies \textup{(D1)} and \textup{(D3)}

[Lemma maximizing first binomial coefficient of arXiv:2507.10294, 'Guessing Strategies for Shelf-Shuffling Machines'] We have
    \begin{equation}\max_{i\geq 1}\frac{\binom{i-1}{j-1}}{2^{i}}=\frac{\binom{2j-2}{j-1}}{2^{2j-1}}\end{equation}
    and this maximum is achieved if and only if $i=2j-1$ or $i=2j-2$.
    \begin{proof}
        Arguing as in the proof of Proposition $(middle terms strategy of the paper)$, we let 
            \[a_i=\frac{\binom{i-1}{j-1}}{2^i}\;\;\;\text{and}\;\;\;R_i=\frac{a_{i+1}}{a_i}=\frac{i}{2(i-j+1)}\]
        We observe that $R_i>1$ when $i<2j-2$, $R_i=1$ when $i=2j-2$, and $R_i<1$ when $i>2j-2$. A similar argument as in Proposition $(middle terms strategy of the paper)$ implies Equation $(maximum of first binomial coefficient of the paper)$.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma maximizing first binomial coefficient of arXiv:2507.10294

[Definition 15 (Admissible Targeted Local-Time Markov Family) of arXiv:2609.03968, 'A one-parameter family of local-time conditioned processes : the generalized Brownian burg'] The family of laws $(\Pb^\lambda_{x \to x_0})$ is \emph{regular} if it satisfies the following conditions :
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Stretching Covariance:} If $g$ is a stretching morphism from $\lambda$ to $g(\lambda)$, then $g$ pushes forward $\Pb^\lambda_{x \to x_0}$ to $\Pb^{g(\lambda)}_{g(x) \to g(x_0)}$, i.e.\ if $X\sim \Pb^\lambda_{x \to x_0}$, then $g(X)\sim \Pb^{g(\lambda)}_{g(x) \to g(x_0)}$.
\item \textbf{Symmetry:} If $X\sim \Pb^\lambda_{x \to x_0}$, then $-X\sim \Pb^{\tilde \lambda}_{-x \to -x_0}$, where $\tilde \lambda$ is the symmetric of the capacity $\lambda$ on the interval $I$, i.e.\ $\tilde \lambda(x) = \lambda(-x)$ for $x\in -I$.
\item \textbf{Local-Time Markov Property:} If $(X_t)_{0 \le t \le T(X)} \sim \Pb^\lambda_{x \to x_0}$, then for any finite stopping time $T$ for the filtration of $X$, conditionally on $X_T$ and $\lambda_T$, we have $(X_{T+t})_{0\le t \le T(X)-T}\sim\Pb^{\lambda_T}_{X_T \to x_0}$ independently on $\F_T$.
\item \textbf{Side-Locality:} If $X\sim \Pb^\lambda_{x \to x_1}$ and $X'\sim \Pb^\lambda_{x \to x_2}$ with $x<x_1<x_2$, then $X$ and $X'$ have same law until reaching $x_1$, i.e.\ in the same time-parametrization, $$\left( X_t \right)_{0 \le t \le \tau_{x_1}}  \overset{(d)}{=}  \left( X'_t \right)_{0 \le t \le \tau'_{x_1}}.$$

\end{enumerate}
title: Admissible Targeted Local-Time Markov Family

[Corollary cor:shift_to_fn of arXiv:2605.22787, 'Invariant measures for half-space geometric LPP: classification and the one force--one sol'] Let $(f_1,\ldots,f_m) \in (\mathbb{R}^\mathbb{N})^m$ be any coupling of initial conditions, jointly independent of the weights $(\omega_{\mathbf x})_{\mathbf x \in \mathbb{Z}^2_{\mathrm{HS}}}$ \rm{(}but $(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ are not necessarily independent\rm{)}. For $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $i \in \llbracket 1,m \rrbracket$, define $f_{n,i}:\mathbb{Z}_{ \ge -n} \to \mathbb{R}$ by
    \[
    f_{n,i}(k) = f_i(n + 1+k),\quad\text{for }k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge -n}.
    \]
    Then, for $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $t \in \mathbb{Z}_{> -n}$, we have 
    \[
    \bigl(G_{f_{n-1,i},-n+1}(t+k,t) \bigr)_{i \in \llbracket 1,m \rrbracket, k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}} \overset{d}{=}  \bigl(G_{f,i}(t+n+k,t+n)\bigr)_{i \in \llbracket 1,m \rrbracket, k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}}
    \]
title: Corollary cor:shift_to_fn of arXiv:2605.22787

body:
[Corollary cor:renewal-law of arXiv:2608.05105, 'Cluster-Cluster model in $\mathbb{Z}^d$'] Fix \(t\) before explosion, and thus \(d(t)>0\).  Conditional on
\(D_t(\{0,1\})\), the successive cluster lengths to the right of
\(\{0,1\}\) are independent and identically distributed with law
\[
    p_k(t):=\frac{c_k(t)}{d(t)},
    \qquad k\ge1.
\]
The same is true to the left, independently. Consequently, if
\(W_{i,j}(t)\) is the density of closed edges whose left and right clusters
have sizes \(i\) and \(j\), respectively, then
\begin{equation}

    W_{i,j}(t)
    =d(t)p_i(t)p_j(t)
    =\frac{c_i(t)c_j(t)}{d(t)}.
\end{equation}

[Theorem thm:domdependence of arXiv:2609.03980, 'Decay Rates and Domain Dependence of a Coupled Wave-Heat System with Spatially Dependant H'] Consider  two Lipschitz interface triples $(\Omega,\Omega_w,\Omega_h),(\Omega',\Omega'_w,\Omega'_h)$  with interfaces $\gamma,\gamma'$, where $(\Omega_w,\gamma)$ is similar to a Lipschitz interface extension of $(\Omega'_w,\gamma')$.
    
    If there exists some accretive heat coefficient $S \in L^\infty(\Omega_h,\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}) $ such that $T_S^\perp$ possesses polynomial decay  on $(\Omega,\Omega_w,\Omega_h)$ with rate $1/d, d>0$, 
  then $T_S^\perp$ possesses polynomial decay on $(\Omega',\Omega'_w,\Omega'_h)$ with rate $1/(2d+2)$ for all accretive $S \in L^\infty(\Omega_h,\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}) .$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem maintheorem2 of arXiv:2601.20502, 'Optimal matching under size priority'] Let $G_n=(V_n,E_n)$ be a sequence of random graphs and choose a root $\overset{\rightarrow}{o}_n$ uniformly among the vertices.
    Suppose that the sequence of rooted weighted random graphs $(G_n,o_n)$ converges locally to an (vertex-rooted) Unimodular Bienaymé-Galton-Watson (UBGW) tree $(\mathbb{T},o)$ with reproduction law $\pi$. Assume further that the ratio $\frac{2|E_n|}{|V_n|}$ converges in probability to the expectation of $\pi$ and that the hypothesis of Theorem~(maintheorem of the paper) holds on the UBGW tree. Now assign i.i.d weights $(w_n(e))_{e \in E(G_n)}$ of distribution $\omega$ on the edges of $G_n$. We have
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item There exists a sequence $(M_n)_n$ of matchings of $G_n$ such that $(G_n,o_n,M_n)$ converges locally to $(\mathbb{T},{o},\mathbb{M}_{\mathrm{opt}})$ given by Theorem~(maintheorem of the paper).
        In particular, we have that:

         \[
        \lim_{n \to \infty} 
        \left(  \mathbb{P}\left( \exists v \sim o_n, \{o_n,v\} \in M_n\right),\mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{v\sim o_n}w_n(o_n,v)\mathbbm{1}_{\{o_n,v\} \in M_n}\right]\right) = \perfE(\mathbb{T},o,\mathbb{M}_{\mathrm{opt}}),
        \]
        
        \item Reciprocally, for any sequence $(M_n)_n$ of matchings of $G_n$, take $(a,b)$ to be any subsequential limit of
        \[ \left(  \mathbb{P}\left( \exists v \sim o_n, \{o_n,v\} \in M_n\right),\mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{v\sim o_n}w_n(o_n,v)\mathbbm{1}_{\{o_n,v\} \in M_n}\right]\right) ,\]
        then we must have that 
        \[ (a,b)\overset{\mathrm{lex}}{\leq} \perfE(\mathbb{T},o,\mathbb{M}_{\mathrm{opt}}).
        \]
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem maintheorem2 of arXiv:2601.20502

[Lemma D_scaled_limit_of_off_diagonal_coefficient of arXiv:2507.22011, 'Random Lozenge Waterfall:\\Dimensional Collapse of Gibbs Measures'] [Off-diagonal coefficients]
	
	Let $\mathsf{t}_l < \mathsf{t} < \mathsf{t}_r$, and the point $(\mathsf{t},\mathsf{x})$ is inside the scaled hexagon $\mathcal{H}$ (equation eq:scaled_hexagon of the paper).
	Under the scaling described before (lemma:D_scaled_limit_of_diagonal_coefficient of the paper),
	the off-diagonal coefficients of the operator $\mathfrak{D}^{\mathrm{scaled}}$ (equation eq:diff_operator_scaling_shifting of the paper) have the following limits (cf. (rmk:discrete_assumptions_at_the_border of the paper) for a discussion of assumptions in the border cases):
	\begin{equation}
		
		\begin{split}
			&
			\lim_{L\to+\infty}
			C_{\mathsf{x}} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{w^{qR}(\tilde x-1)}{w^{qR}(\tilde  x)}}B(\tilde  x-1)
			=
			\lim_{L\to+\infty}
			C_{\mathsf{x}} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{w^{qR}(\tilde x)}{w^{qR}(\tilde  x-1)}}D(\tilde  x)
			\\
			&\hspace{10pt}
			=
			\begin{cases}
				0,
				& \mathsf{x}<\tfrac{1}{2}(\mathsf{S}+\mathsf{t}-\mathsf{N});\\
				-\kappa^{-2}q^{-2\Delta x +1/2},
				& \mathsf{x}=\tfrac12(\mathsf{S}+\mathsf{t}-\mathsf{N}) ,\ \lfloor L\hspace{1pt} \mathsf{x}\rfloor=\tfrac{1}{2}(S+t-N)
				;\\
				-\kappa^{-2}q^{-2\Delta x +1/2},
				& \tfrac{1}{2}(\mathsf{S}+\mathsf{t}-\mathsf{N})<\mathsf{x}<\tfrac{1}{2}(\mathsf{S}+\mathsf{t});\\
				\dfrac{-\kappa^2 q^{2\Delta x+1/2}}{(1 - \kappa^2 q^{2\Delta x})\sqrt{(1 - \kappa^2 q^{2\Delta x-1}) (1 - \kappa^2 q^{2\Delta x+1})}},
				& \mathsf{x}=\tfrac12(\mathsf{S}+\mathsf{t}),\ \lfloor L\hspace{1pt} \mathsf{x}\rfloor=\tfrac{1}{2}(S+t);\\
				-\kappa^{2}q^{2\Delta x +1/2},
				& \tfrac{1}{2}(\mathsf{S}+\mathsf{t})<\mathsf{x}<\tfrac{1}{2}(\mathsf{S}+\mathsf{t}+\mathsf{N});\\
				-\kappa^{2}q^{2\Delta x +1/2},
				& \mathsf{x}= \tfrac12(\mathsf{S}+\mathsf{t}+\mathsf{N}) ,\ \lfloor L\hspace{1pt} \mathsf{x}\rfloor=\tfrac{1}{2}(S+t+N);
				\\
				0,
				& \mathsf{x}>\tfrac{1}{2}(\mathsf{S}+\mathsf{t}+\mathsf{N}).
			\end{cases}
		\end{split}
	\end{equation}
title: Lemma D_scaled_limit_of_off_diagonal_coefficient of arXiv:2507.22011

\[
\alpha_i\frac{\E_i\left[\prod_{m=1}^d\E_m\left[ e^{-\bm \theta\cdot \bo Z_{T-t} }\right]^{ L^{(m)}} \right]}{\E_i\left[e^{-\bm \theta\cdot \bo Z_{T-t} }\right]}{\rm d} t,
\]
and the probability that there are $\bm \ell$ offspring satisfies
\[
p_i(\bm \ell)\frac{\prod_{m=1}^d\E_m\left[ e^{-\bm \theta\cdot \bo Z_{T-t} }\right]^{\ell_m}}{\E_i\left[\prod_{m=1}^d\E_m\left[ e^{-\bm \theta\cdot \bo Z_{T-t} }\right]^{ L^{(m)}} \right]}.
\]

[Definition 78 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Using the notation of \eqref{eq_particles_in_segment}, we say that $p\in\amsmathbb R$ is the position of a hole in $[\mathfrak{a},\mathfrak{b}]$ for the configuration $\boldsymbol{\ell} \in\W_\N$ if \emph{one of the following conditions} is satisfied.
\begin{itemize}
\item $\exists i \in \llbracket i_0 + 1,i_0 + \# I - 1\rrbracket\qquad \ell_i < p < p +\theta_{h,h} \leq \ell_{i + 1}\quad \textnormal{and} \quad p - \ell_i \in \amsmathbb{Z}_{> 0}$.
\item $\exists m \in \amsmathbb{Z}_{\geq 0} \qquad p=\ell_{i_0+1}-\theta_{h,h}-m\quad \textnormal{and} \quad p\geq \max\big(\N\mathfrak a-\theta_{h,h}, a_h, \ell_{i_0}+1\big)$.
\item $\exists m \in \amsmathbb{Z}_{\geq 0} \qquad p=\ell_{i_0+\#I}+m \quad \textnormal{and} \quad p\leq \max\big(\N \mathfrak b +1,b_h,\ell_{i_0+\#I+1}-\theta_{h,h}\big)$.
\end{itemize}
If $i_0=0$ or $i_0+\# I+1=N$, then the corresponding inequalities are ignored.
title: Definition 78 of arXiv:2601.16377

body: Two Latin squares of order n are orthogonal if superimposing them yields every ordered pair of symbols exactly once. A set of Latin squares is mutually orthogonal (a set of MOLS) if every pair in the set is orthogonal. N(n) denotes the maximum number of MOLS of order n; N(n) <= n - 1 always, with equality when n is a prime power via finite-field constructions.
title: Mutually Orthogonal Latin Squares (MOLS)

[Definition 21 of arXiv:2608.30549, '\vspace{-1cm}Maximally Spread Out Measures and Implications\\{} for Phase Transitions in A'] Let $(\XX,\norm{\cdot})$ be a quasi-normed space.
    Let $\SC\subset \XX$ satisfy \ConditionZetaTextAlphaC{(\alpha,C_0)}.
    For every $n\in \NN$ let $\SC_n\subset \SC$ be a non-empty, finite subset.
    Then we define the measure
    \begin{equation*}
        \mu(A)
        := \mu\bigl[ (\SC_n)_{n\in \NN},\alpha,C_0\bigr](A)
        := \PP
           \biggl(\,\,
             \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}
               \frac{Y_n}{C_0 \cdot n^{\alpha}} \in A
           \biggr), 
        \quad A \in \Borel(\XX),
    \end{equation*}
    where the random vectors $(Y_n)_{n\in \NN}$ are independent
    and for every $n$ the random vector $Y_n$ is uniformly distributed on $\SC_n$.
title: Definition 21 of arXiv:2608.30549

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.29148, '2608.29148'] Let $(M, H, J)$ be a $3$-dimensional strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold and $(\mathcal{C}, [g^{\mathrm{F}}_\th])$ the Fefferman space over $M$. Then, there exists an $S^1$-invariant even Poincar\'e metric $g'$ on $X'=\mathcal{C}\times(0, \e)_r$ with the conformal infinity $(\mathcal{C}, [g^{\mathrm{F}}_\th])$ which satisfies 
\[
E'_{ab}=O(r^\infty), \quad L^-_{abcd}=O(r^\infty), \quad F^-_{ab}=O(r^\infty).
\]
The metric $g'$ is unique modulo $O(r^\infty)$ up to pull-back by $S^1$-equivariant diffeomorphisms of $\mathcal{C}\times[0, \e)_r$ fixing points on $\mathcal{C}\times\{0\}$. Moreover, the expansion of each component in the normal form of $g'$ with respect to a representative $g^{\mathrm{F}}_\th$ can be expressed by a universal formula in terms of the curvature and torsion of the Tanaka-Webster connection. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.29148

[Dfn 200 (addition of frozen particles) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] We now define a further modification $\vX^\frstar$, which may be thought of as $\vX^\trstar$ together with an additional \textbf{positive density of frozen particles}. For the spherical perceptron, the process $\vX^\frstar\equiv\vX^{\frstar,\RomI:\RomIII}$ is defined on the augmented space
    \[[M^\frozen] 
    \equiv
    \bigg[ M\bigg(1 + \frac1{\trK^6}\bigg)\bigg]\,.
    \]
For $a\in[M]$ we set
$\vX^\frstar(q_d,a)\equiv\vX^\trstar(q_d,a)$.
The remaining particles
$\vX^\frstar(q_d,a)$ for $a\in[M^\frozen]\setminus[M]$ are spaced evenly over $[-2\trK,2\trK]^3$ and frozen for all time. For the Ising perceptron, we again apply the above procedure to obtain $\vX^{\frstar,\RomI:\RomIII}$. We separately define $X^{\frstar,\Ising}$ on the augmented space
    \[[N^\frozen] 
    \equiv
    \bigg[ N\bigg(1 + \frac1{\trK^3}\bigg)\bigg]\,,
    \]
such that the added particles are spaced evenly over $[-2\trK,2\trK]$ and frozen for all time. We then denote $\vX^\frstar\equiv(\vX^{\frstar,\RomI:\RomIII},X^{\frstar,\Ising})$.
title: addition of frozen particles

body: [Lemma 2.7 of arXiv:2210.03711, 'Matrix tree theorem for the net Laplacian matrix of a signed graph'] Suppose G is a signed unicyclic graph on n vertices with a cycle Ck, 3 ≤k ≤n. Then the determinant of an oriented net incidence matrix N± of G is 0. Also the determinant of the net incidence matrix M± of G is ±2ie−if k is odd and zero otherwise, where e−is the number of negative edges of G.
title: Lemma 2.7 of arXiv:2210.03711: Matrix tree theorem for the net Laplacian matrix of a signed graph

[Theorem Theorem 7.1 in \cite{Meyn_Tweedie_1993} of arXiv:2507.09421, 'Stability of randomly switching stochastic reaction networks with asymptotically linear tr'] Let $X$ be an irreducible continuous-time Markov chain on a countable discrete state space $\mathbb S$ with generator $\mathcal L$. Suppose that there exists a function $V:\mathbb S\to[0,\infty)$ and constants $c\in(0,\infty)$ and $d\in\mathbb R$ such that $\{x\in\mathbb{S}\,:\,V(x)\leq R\}$ is finite for all $R\in [0,\infty)$ and
    \[
    \mathcal LV(x)\le -cV(x)+d
    \]
    for every $x\in\mathbb S$. Then $X$ is exponentially ergodic. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 7.1 in \cite{Meyn_Tweedie_1993}

Let $S\subset E(K_n)$ and write $H\coloneq \big(V(K_n),S\big)$ and  $G\coloneq \big(V(K_n),E(K_n)\setminus S\big)$. Assume $S$ is such that $\max\{\deg(x;H)\mid x\in V(H)\}\;\leqslant\; 2$ and $G$ is still connected.  Let $\mathbf{1}^\perp$ be the orthonormal complement of the all one-vector $\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}$ in the space $l_2\big(V(K_n)\big)$. Then $I-\frac{1}{n}L_H$ is invertible and 
\[
L_{G}^+\mathbf{x}=\frac{1}{n}\big(I-\frac{1}{n}L_H\big)^{-1}\mathbf{x}\,,\,\,\,\forall\,\mathbf{x}\in \mathbf{1}^\perp\,.
\]

AUTHOR-CHECKED; independent w346 audit PENDING. Unconditional convergence, even almost sure convergence, and an exact
survival probability of order 1/n do not suffice for a conditioned scaling limit.
For U uniform on (0,1), let A_n={U<=1/n} and Z_n=a_n*1_{A_n}, with a_n=1
for even n and 2 for odd n. Then Z_n->0 almost surely and n*P(A_n)=1 exactly,
but Law(Z_n|A_n) alternates between point masses at one and two.
A valid sufficient replacement on a Polish state space is: n*P(A_n)->c>0
and n*E[f(Z_n)*1_{A_n}]->c*integral f dnu for every bounded continuous f;
then Law(Z_n|A_n) converges weakly to nu.
Rare events have positive probability
Polish state space for weak-convergence criterion
No assertion that the toy process is percolation

body: In mathematics, the Fatou–Lebesgue theorem establishes a chain of inequalities relating the integrals of the limit inferior and the limit superior of a sequence of functions to the limit inferior and the limit superior of integrals of these functions. The theorem is named after Pierre Fatou and Henri Léon Lebesgue.
title: Fatou–Lebesgue theorem

[Lemma 22 of arXiv:2608.31070, 'Sub-Laplacians on Compact Lie Groups: Heat Kernels, Distance, and Zeta Determinants'] The hyperplanes of the compact roots and isotropy weights form a finite rational arrangement in $\tLie$. Each chamber closure is a pointed rational polyhedral cone and admits a subdivision into rational simplicial cones whose ray generators can be chosen in the cocharacter lattice. On every such cone, the polynomial $P_{\mathcal C}$ has nonnegative coefficients in the ray coordinates, and
		\[
		A_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf n)(v_{\varsigma,i})>0
		\qquad(\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^{N_{\mathrm{iso}}}).
		\]
		The overlaps between distinct cones have Lebesgue measure zero.

[Theorem 10 of arXiv:2609.03830, 'Parabolic Poincar\'e inequalities and maximal function estimates for systems of partial di'] Let $1<q<\infty$. Assume that $|F|\in L^q_{\loc}(\Om_T)$ and that $u\in L^q_{\loc}(0,T;W^{1,q}_{\loc}(\Om;\mathbb{R}^N))$ satisfies \eqref{eq} for every $\varphi\in C_0^\infty(\Om_T;\mathbb R^N)$ and let 
\[
g=M^*(|\na u|+|F|)1_{2Q}.
\]
      \begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] If $1< q< 2$, then for $1< q \le q^* <\tfrac{2q}{2-q}$, then there exists a constant $c=c(n,q,q^*,L)$ such that 
    \[
    \biggl( \fint_{I } \frac{|u(x,t)-u_{I}(x)|^{q^*}}{|I|^\frac{q^*}{2}}\,dt \biggr)^\frac{1}{q^*}
    \le c\biggl( \fint_{I}g(x,t)^q\,dt\biggr)^\frac{1}{q}
    \]
    for every parabolic cylinder $Q=Q_\rho=B\times I$ such that $2Q\Subset \Om_T$ and for almost every $x\in B$.
    \item[(ii)] If $q=2$, then there exists a constant $c=c(n,L)$ such that
    \[
    \fint_I\exp\left(\left(
   \frac{|u(x,t)-u_{I}(x)|}{\displaystyle c|I|^\frac{1}{2}\left( \fint_{I}  g(x,t)^2 \,dt\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}}\right)^{2}\right)\,dt\le c
    \]
    for every parabolic cylinder $Q=Q_\rho=B\times I$ such that $2Q\Subset \Om_T$ and for almost every $x\in B$.
    \item[(iii)] If $q>2$, then there exists a constant $c=c(n,q,L)$ such that
    \[
    \esssup_{t\in I}\frac{|u(x,t)-u_{I}(x)|}{|I|^\frac{1}{2}}
    \le c\left( \fint_{I}g(x,t)^q\,dt\right)^\frac{1}{q}
    \]
    for every parabolic cylinder $Q=Q_\rho=B\times I$ such that $2Q\Subset \Om_T$ and for almost every $x\in B$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

$n$, one can find a centered isotropic log-concave random vector
$X^{(n)}\in\R^n$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \E W_1\bigl(\Law_{X^{(n)}}\ip{X^{(n)}}{\Theta},\gamma_1\bigr)
 \ge \frac{c}{n}.
\end{equation}
One may take $X^{(n)}$ to have independent coordinates, each distributed as
$E-1$, where $E$ has the exponential distribution with mean one. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition NA1-NA2-general of arXiv:2609.00794, 'On operators whose adjoints or second adjoints attain their norms'] Let $X$ and $Y$ be Banach spaces, and let $T \in \mathcal{L}(X,Y^*)$. \begin{enumerate}
        \itemsep0.25em
        \item If $T^\top \in \operatorname{NA}(Y,X^*)$, then $T \in \operatorname{NA}_1 (X,Y^*)$. In other words,
\[
    (\Xi_{X,Y})^{-1}\bigl(\operatorname{NA}(Y,X^*)\bigr)
    \subseteq \operatorname{NA}_1(X,Y^*).
\]
\item If $T^\top \in \operatorname{NA}_1(Y,X^*)$, then $T \in \operatorname{NA}_2 (X,Y^*)$. In other words,
\[
(\Xi_{X,Y})^{-1}\bigl(\operatorname{NA}_1(Y,X^*)\bigr)
    \subseteq \operatorname{NA}_2(X,Y^*).
\]
\end{enumerate}
If $Y$ is reflexive, then both inclusions are equalities.

[Definition 15 (Double hive) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{def:double-hive}
For \(\nu\in\Spec_n\), write
\[
\nu^\vee=(-\nu_n,\ldots,-\nu_1).
\]
A double hive with exterior boundary
\((\alpha,\beta,\eta,\phi)\) and middle side \(\nu\) is a pair of hives
\[
(h_1,h_2)\in
H_n(\alpha,\beta;\nu)\times H_n(\eta,\phi^\vee;\nu^\vee),
\qquad
\phi^\vee=(-\phi_n,\ldots,-\phi_1),
\]
viewed as glued along the common middle side, with opposite orientations on
the two copies of that side.  The corresponding double hive polytope is
\[
\mathcal D(\alpha,\beta,\eta,\phi^\vee)
:=
\bigcup_{\nu\in\Spec_n + \R \one}
H_n(\alpha,\beta;\nu)
\times
H_n(\eta,\phi^\vee;\nu^\vee).
\]
A quadruply augmented double hive is obtained by additionally choosing
Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns on the four exterior boundary components with matching spectra.
title: Double hive

[Prop 3 of arXiv:2609.02173, 'Bounding Selmer Groups of Superelliptic Jacobians via Class Groups'] Every element of $J(F)$ admits a representative given by a degree-zero divisor defined over $F$ whose support contains neither the point at infinity $\infty$ nor any point with $y$-coordinate equal to $0$. In particular, let
		\[
		D = {}^{\sigma_1}Q + \cdots + {}^{\sigma_m}Q - m\infty,
		\]
		where ${}^{\sigma_1}Q,\ldots,{}^{\sigma_m}Q$ are the Galois conjugates over $F$ of a point
		$Q\in \mathcal C(\bar F)$ with $y(Q)\neq 0$. Then
		\[
		(x-T)([D]) \equiv \prod_{i=1}^m \bigl(x({}^{\sigma_i}Q)-T\bigr)
		\pmod{L^{\times p}}.
		\]
		Now suppose that
		\[
		D = (\alpha_1,0)+\cdots+(\alpha_r,0)-r\infty,
		\]
		where the $\alpha_i$ are conjugate over $F$ (possibly after reordering) and $r<d$. Recall that $f(x)=\prod_{i=1}^d (x-\alpha_i)^{s_i}$. If $u_i$ is an integer such that $u_is_i\equiv 1 \pmod p$, then
		\[
		(x-T)([D]) \equiv
		\prod_{i=1}^r (\alpha_i-T)^{u_i}+
		\prod_{i=r+1}^d (\alpha_i-T)^{-u_i}
		\pmod{L^{\times p}}.
		\]

[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2609.02193, 'State-law dynamics of McKean-Vlasov stochastic reaction-diffusion equations on $\mathbb R^'] Let $T>0$, $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\ell\in C([0,T];P)$ and $X_0\in L^2(\Omega,\mathcal F_0;H)$. Then \eqref{Eq4} with $\eta=\ell$ and $U(0)=X_0$ has a unique variational solution
	\begin{align*}
		U_\ell
		\in
		L^2(\Omega;C([0,T];H))
		\cap L^2(\Omega;L^2(0,T;V))
		\cap L^p(\Omega;L^p(0,T;L^p(\mathbb R^n))).
	\end{align*}
	Moreover, if $U_{\ell_1}$ and $U_{\ell_2}$ correspond to $\ell_1,\ell_2\in C([0,T];P)$ and initial data $X_{0,1},X_{0,2}\in L^2(\Omega,\mathcal F_0;H)$, and are driven by the same Brownian motion, then
	\begin{align}
		\mathbb E\|U_{\ell_1}(t)-U_{\ell_2}(t)\|^2
		\leq
		e^{-\bar\gamma t}\mathbb E\|X_{0,1}-X_{0,2}\|^2
		+L_G\int_0^t e^{-\bar\gamma(t-r)}
		\mathcal W_2^2(\ell_1(r),\ell_2(r))dr
	\end{align}
	for all $t\in[0,T]$.

Let mu be full-dimensional log-concave with finite K=C_P(mu). Define Y=X+sqrt(t)G, nu_t=Law(Y), and T_t f(y)=E[f(X)|Y=y] using independent G~N(0,I). If integral |grad T_t f|^2 dnu_t <= q integral |grad f|^2 dmu for all finite-energy tests, where t>0 and 0<=q<1, then K<=t(1+q)/(1-q). Conversely, K<=C implies this contraction with q=C/t whenever t>C. Thus fixed numerical t,q valid for all regular isotropic log-concave measures yield KLS by regular approximation; KLS itself yields such constants. The uniform strict nonlinear contraction is an assumption, not a proved conclusion in this draft.

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, The smallest eigenvalue of the NTK of a deep tanh network in the ordered phase (November 2026), shows that for a fully connected tanh network of depth L in the infinite-width limit with bias variance sigma_b^2 > 0, in the ordered phase chi_1 < 1, and n distinct inputs on the fixed-point sphere, lambda_min(Theta_L) = (q* + B T*/chi_1) lambda_perp_min(-A) L chi_1^L (1 + O(1/L)), where q* is the fixed-point variance, T* = q*/(1 - chi_1), B = chi'(1) and A is the matrix of limiting rescaled correlation gaps. The order L chi_1^L is due to Xiao, Pennington and Schoenholz (ICML 2020); the paper adds the constant, a proof that lambda_perp_min(-A) > 0 for any distinct inputs (every Taylor coefficient of the limiting gap profile is strictly positive, so the Schoenberg and Chen-Menegatto-Sun criterion applies), and the same form for inputs of unequal norm when lambda_perp_min(-A) > 0. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/ntk-smallest-eigenvalue-ordered-phase (commit 73fda1d4e515). Not refereed.

body: [Lemma lem:independence-across-bands of arXiv:2606.10973, 'Quasisymmetric rigidity of the Brownian sphere'] For each $\lambda \in (0, 1)$, $\alpha > 0$, and $b \in (0, 1)$, there exists $p = p(\lambda, \alpha, b) \in (0, 1)$ and $C = C(\lambda, \alpha, b) > 0$ such that the following is true: Let $(\BC, \Phi; 0, \infty)$ be a $\sqrt{8/3}$-LQG cone. Let $\{t_j\}_{j \in \BN}$ be a decreasing sequence of positive real numbers such that $t_{j + 1}/t_j \le \lambda$ for every $j \in \BN$. Let $\{E_j\}_{j \in \BN}$ be a sequence of events such that each $E_j$ is almost surely determined by the $\sqrt{8/3}$-LQG surface parameterized by $A_{t_{j + 1},t_j}^\bullet(0; D_\Phi)$. Suppose that $\BP\lbrack E_j\rbrack \ge p$ for every $j \in \BN$. Then for each $n \in \BN$, it holds with probability at least $1 - C\re^{-\alpha n}$ that there are at least $bn$ values of $j \in [1,n]_\BZ$ for which $E_j$ occurs.
title: Lemma lem:independence-across-bands of arXiv:2606.10973

body:
[Proposition 37 (Naturality and base change of response kernels) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let $f:(M,F^\bullet)\to(M',F^\bullet)$ preserve the decreasing
filtrations, let
$B:(\mathcal Y,K_\bullet)\to(\mathcal Y',K_\bullet)$ preserve the
increasing filtrations, and let
$\mathcal R:M^*\to\mathcal Y$ and
$\mathcal R':(M')^*\to\mathcal Y'$ be filtered responses satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal R'=B\circ\mathcal R\circ f^*.
 
\end{equation}
Write $f_r:G_r(M)\to G_r(M')$ and
$B_r:\partial_r\mathcal Y\to\partial_r\mathcal Y'$ for the induced
maps.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak K_r(\mathcal R')
 =(f_r\otimes B_r)\mathfrak K_r(\mathcal R).
 
\end{equation}
Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{supp}_L\mathfrak K_r(\mathcal R')
 \subseteq f_r\bigl(\operatorname{supp}_L\mathfrak K_r(\mathcal R)\bigr).
\]
If $\mathcal R$ has full support, $f_r$ is surjective, and $B_r$ is
injective on the image of
$\operatorname{gr}_r\mathcal R\circ f_r^*$, then $\mathcal R'$ has full
support on $G_r(M')$.  Thus a quotient observation recovers exactly its
observable ancestry layer.  In particular, spatial pushforwards,
exact-layer identifications, and native boundary readers act on one canonical
kernel rather than creating new detector data.

body:
[Lem Lemma: gamma-twist of a nilfactor of arXiv:2605.16921, '${\ASL_n}(\mathbb Z)$ invariant random subsets of $\mathbb Z^n$'] Let $(X, \mu)$ be an $\ASL_d(\mathbb{Z})$-system and $\pi: (X, \mu) \to (Y, \mu_Y)$ a nilfactor over $Z^0(X)$, with
    $$ Y = \bigsqcup_{n \geq 0} \Omega_n \rtimes_{\rho_n} N_n / \Gamma_n.$$
    Then for every $\gamma \in \SL_d(\mathbb{Z})$, the composition $\pi \circ \gamma$ is a nilfactor over $Z^0(X)$ with range
    $$ \bigsqcup_{n \geq 0} \gamma^{-1} \Omega_n \rtimes_{\rho_n^\gamma} N_n / \Gamma_n,$$
    where $\rho_n^\gamma(\omega)(t) := \rho_n(\gamma \cdot \omega)(\gamma(t))$ for $\omega \in \gamma^{-1} \Omega_n$ and $t \in \mathbb{Z}^d$.

body: [Theorem 7 (Local lower-tail exclusion near \(\log 2\)) of arXiv:2607.07014, '2607.07014'] For every \(\xi>0\), there exist \(m(\xi)\ge1\), \(\varepsilon_\ast(\xi)>0\), and \(n_0(\xi)\ge1\) such that, whenever \(0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_\ast(\xi)\) and \(n\ge n_0(\xi)\), one has \[\mathbb P(n^{-1}\log N_n\le\log 2-\xi)=0.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 25 of arXiv:2608.30570, '2608.30570'] Assume $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ is a properly immersed translating soliton satisfying the same assumptions of Theorem \ref{prop-alpha-decay}. For $\mathcal{A}_k$ and $\hat{\mathcal{A}}_k$ constructed in Lemma \ref{construction of annulus}, let $F$  and $F_k$ be defined as
 \begin{align*}
 F&=\{s\in [-1,1]| s \text{ is a singular value  of } \cos\alpha_J \\
  & \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad  \text{ or }  \cos\alpha_J^{-1}(s) \text{ contains a curve with infinite length }  \} \\
  F_k&=\{s\in [-1,1]|  \cos\alpha_J^{-1}(s) \text{ contains an arc joining } \hat{\mathcal{A}}_k \text{ to } \partial \mathcal{A}_k \}.
 \end{align*}
 Then, $\lim_{k\to \infty}\mathcal{L}^1(F_k)=0$ and $\mathcal{L}^1(F)=0$.

[Thmx 1 of arXiv:2605.09372, 'Sharp weighted norm estimates for martingale square functions'] Let $1<p<\infty$. Given a scalar weight $w\in A_p$, we have
$$\|S f\|_{L_p^w(\Omega)}\lesssim_{p}[w]_{A_p}^{\max\{\frac12 ,\frac{1}{p-1}\}}\|f\|_{L_p^w(\Omega)},\quad \forall f\in L_p^w(\Omega).$$
The estimate is sharp in terms of the dependence on $[w]_{A_p}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thmx 1 of arXiv:2605.09372

[Lemma lem:fixed-chaos-maximal-tail of arXiv:2606.21006, 'Law of the Iterated Logarithm for Weighted Sums of Functionals of Long-Memory Gaussian Seq'] Let \(m\ge1\)
and  \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_N\) be random variables such that every interval sum
\[
    Z(I):=\sum_{j\in I}Z_j,
    \qquad I\subset\{1,\ldots,N\},
\]
belongs to the fixed \(m\)-th Wiener chaos. Assume that for some \(B>0\) and some \(q>1\),
\[
    \operatorname{Var}(Z(I))
    \le
    B^2\left(\frac{|I|}{N}\right)^q
\]
for every interval \(I\subset\{1,\ldots,N\}\). Then there exist constants
\(C_1,C_2>0\), depending only on \(m\) and \(q\), such that for every \(x>0\),
\[
    \mathbb P\left(
        \max_{1\le r\le N}
        \left|\sum_{j=1}^r Z_j\right|
        >
        xB
    \right)
    \le
    C_1\exp\{-C_2x^{2/m}\}.
\]

body:
[Lemma lem:noise_series of arXiv:2411.09482, 'Anomalous Regularization in Kazantsev-Kraichnan Model'] Given any orthonormal basis $\{e_k\}_{k\ge 1}$ of $L^2_{\div} (\mathbb{R}^d)$,  or, equivalently, any orthonormal basis $\{\sigma_k = \mathcal{Q}^\frac 12 e_k\}_{k\ge 1}$ of $U_0$, there exists a sequence $\{W^k\}_{k\ge 1}$ of independent one-dimensional $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t}$-Brownian motions such that
	\begin{equation*}
		W^\mathcal{K}_t 
		= \sum_{k\ge1} \sigma_k W^k_t 
		=\sum_{k\ge1} \mathcal{Q}^\frac 12 e_k W^k_t.
	\end{equation*}
	In particular, if $U_0$ embeds in a Hilbert space $U_1$ with a Hilbert-Schmidt embedding, the series is convergent and defines an $U_1$-valued Wiener process.
title: Lemma lem:noise_series of arXiv:2411.09482

body:
[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2606.07290, 'Boundary behaviour of the Volterra square-root process'] Suppose that $K \in C^1(\R_+)$. Then the following assertions hold:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] The function $V_u$ satisfies the two-sided bounds
        \begin{equation}
            W_u(t) \leq V_u(t) \leq W_u(t) + K(0)L_0(0) \int_0^t W_u(s) \mathrm{e}^{\beta^+ K(0)(t-s)}\, \mathrm{d}s.
        \end{equation}
        where $\beta^+ = \max\{\beta, 0\}$. The function $W_u$ is for $\beta \neq L_0(0)$ given by
        \[
            W_u(t) = \frac{(\beta - L_0(0))K(0)u \mathrm{e}^{K(0)(\beta - L_0(0))t}}{\beta - L_0(0) + \frac{\sigma^2}{2}K(0)u \left( \mathrm{e}^{K(0)(\beta - L_0(0))t} - 1\right)} , \qquad t > 0,
        \]
        while for $\beta = L_0(0)$ it takes the form
        \[
            W_u(t) = \frac{K(0)u}{1 + \frac{\sigma^2 K(0)^2}{2}ut}, \qquad t > 0.
        \]
        \item[(b)] The function $R_u(t) := (L \ast V_u)(t)$ satisfies the upper bound 
        \begin{equation}
            R_u(t) \leq \frac{W_u(t)}{K(0)} + L_0(0)\int_0^t W_u(s) \mathrm{e}^{\beta^+ K(0)(t-s)}\, \mathrm{d}s.
        \end{equation}
        \item[(c)] For any $t>0$ such that $\beta < L_0(t)$, we have
        \[
            \int_0^t V_u(s)\, \mathrm{d}s \leq \frac{L_0(0) - \beta}{L_0(t) - \beta}\int_0^t W_u(s)\, \mathrm{d}s.
        \]
    \end{enumerate}
title: Theorem 16 of arXiv:2606.07290

[Defin 9 of arXiv:2609.00974, 'On Algebraic Integrability\\ of Vector Fields \\ with Rational Function Coefficients\\ tha'] A \textbf{generic point of a curve} is a field $K$ of positive characteristic $p>0$ such that the extension $K/k$, where $k=\bigcap_{n\ge 1} K^{p^n}$, is a finitely generated field extension of transcendental degree $1$.
    
    Concretely, it is equivalent to $K$ being isomorphic to the following construction: take a perfect field $k$, take rational functions in one variable over $k$, i.e., $k(x)$, take a finite separable extension $K/k(x)$. Any choice of such $x$ is called a coordinate for $K$.
title: Definition 9 of arXiv:2609.00974

[Theorem FK rep of arXiv:2411.09614, 'Moment estimates for the stochastic heat equation on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds'] Let $p\geq 2$, $\set{B^{x,j}}_{1\leq j\leq p}$ be Brownian motions starting at $x$ independent of $W$ and each other. The following Feynman-Kac formula for the $p$-th moment of $u(t,x)$ holds if $u_0\in L^\infty(M)$: $$\mathbb{E}[\abs{u(t,x)}^p]=\mathbb{E}_x\left[\prod_{j=1}^p u_0(B^{x,j}_t)\exp\left\{\beta^2 \sum_{1\leq i,k \leq p,i\neq k}\int_0^t G_{2\alpha}(B^{x,i}_s,B^{x,k}_s)ds\right\}\right].$$
    Here $\mathbb{E}_x$ is the expectation with respect to the Brownian motions $(B^{x,j})_{1\leq j\leq p}$.

body:
[Theorem 44 (Multiplicative exterior area reader) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] For every \(g,h\in\mathcal G_2(H)\),
\begin{equation}
 \Sigma_{\wedge}^{\lambda}(g\circ h)
 =\Sigma_{\wedge}^{\lambda}(g)\wedge
  \Sigma_{\wedge}^{\lambda}(h).
 
\end{equation}
If \(a_1(A)\geq a_2(A)\geq\cdots\) are the positive two--plane
singular values of \(A\), then
\begin{align}
 \mathfrak P_A(z)
 &:=\log\|\exp_{\wedge}(z\alpha_A)\|^2
   =\sum_{j\geq1}\log(1+z^2a_j(A)^2) \notag\\
 &=\frac12\log\det(I+z^2A^*A)
   =\mathfrak F_A(z).
 
\end{align}
Consequently, for every \(0<p<2\), the weak and little
\(\mathcal S_{p,\infty}\) scales are read directly from \(\mathfrak P_A\)
by \Cref{cc:prop:weak-detection}.  The full vector
\(\Sigma_{\wedge}^{\lambda}\) is faithful in \(A\) for
\(\lambda\ne0\), whereas the scalar profile remembers precisely the nonzero
singular spectrum, with multiplicity, and forgets the singular subspaces.

body:
[Theorem thm:lyap-intrinsic-damping of arXiv:2608.22910, 'A Commutator Framework for Selective Spectral Alignment in Deep Neural Networks'] Assume (equation eq:lyap-risk-dissipation of the paper), the PL inequality
(equation eq:lyap-PL of the paper), and (equation eq:lyap-damped-defect of the paper) for every
\(i\in\mathcal I\). For \(A>0\) and \(\omega_i>0\), define
\begin{equation}
\mathscr V_{\mathrm{damp}}(t)
:=
A\mathscr E(t)
+
\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\omega_iq_i(t).
\end{equation}
If
\begin{equation}
\delta
:=
A-
\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}
\frac{\omega_ic_i^2}{4\kappa_i}
>0,
\end{equation}
then
\begin{align}
\dot{\mathscr V}_{\mathrm{damp}}
&\leq
-\delta\mathscr D
-
\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}\omega_i\kappa_iq_i,
\\
\mathscr V_{\mathrm{damp}}(t)
&\leq
e^{-\lambda_{\mathrm{damp}}t}
\mathscr V_{\mathrm{damp}}(0),
\qquad
\lambda_{\mathrm{damp}}
:=
\min\left\{
\frac{2\mu\delta}{A},
\min_{i\in\mathcal I}\kappa_i
\right\}.

\end{align}
In particular, \(\mathscr E(t)\to0\) and \(q_i(t)\to0\) exponentially for
all selected modes.

[Proposition prop:positive_time_Sobolev of arXiv:2609.01984, 'Instantaneous shrinking of supports for stochastic PDEs\footnote{JY was supported by a KIA'] Let $u\in C((0,T];C_{\rm tem})$ be a nonnegative solution of (equation eq:SPDE of the paper) with initial measure $\mu_0$, and fix $t_0\in(0,T)$. Assume that for some $q_*\ge0$,
\begin{equation}

    \sup_{r\in[\delta,T]} W_{q_*}(u(r))<\infty
    \qquad
    \text{a.s. for every }\delta\in(0,T).
\end{equation}
Assume also one of the following two alternatives:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm (a)]
$q_*=0$ and $p>6$ is chosen so that
\[
    p\gamma\ge1.
\]

\item[\rm (b)]
$q_*>0$ and $p>6$ is chosen so that
\[
    p\gamma>\frac1{q_*+1}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
If $\lambda\in(1,2)$, we additionally require
\[
    q_*>\frac{\lambda-1}{2-\lambda}.
\]

Then there exists a non-random $\beta>1/p$, depending only on $p$,  such that
\[
    u(t_0,\cdot)\in H_p^\beta(\mathbb{R})
    \qquad\text{a.s.}
\]

body: A (left) action of a group G on a set X is a map G x X -> X, (g, x) -> g.x, with e.x = x and g.(h.x) = (gh).x; equivalently a homomorphism G -> Sym(X). The orbit of x is G.x = {g.x : g in G}; orbits partition X. The stabilizer G_x = {g : g.x = x} is a subgroup, and the orbit-stabilizer theorem gives |G.x| = [G : G_x]. Actions are the bridge from abstract groups to concrete symmetry (Cayley, Sylow, Burnside all run through them).
title: Group Action

[Theorem thm:caract of arXiv:2412.03366, 'Regularity of Weighted Tensorized Fractional Brownian Fields and associated function space'] Let $0 <p,q \leq \infty$, $s \in \mathbb{R}$ and $0 \le \alpha \le 1$ and let $ (c_{\bar{j},\bar{k}})$ denote the sequence of the Meyer wavelet coefficients of a function $f \in \mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}^2)$. The following assertions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f \in T^{s,\alpha}_{p,q}B(\mathbb{R}^2)$,
\item $ (c_{\bar{j},\bar{k}} )\in t^{s,\alpha}_{p,q}b $.

\end{enumerate}
Moreover, there exist two constants $C_1,C_2>0$ such that
$$
C_1 \Vert  (c_{\bar{j},\bar{k}}) \Vert_{t^{s,\alpha}_{p,q}b} \le \Vert f \Vert_{T^{s,\alpha}_{p,q}B(\mathbb{R}^2)} \le C_2 \Vert (c_{\bar{j},\bar{k}}) \Vert_{t^{s,\alpha}_{p,q}b} \, . 
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Then there exists a universal constant $C^\star < \infty$ such that for all large enough $n \geq n(K,\delta,c_1)$, we have
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathbb{P} \left(  T_n  \text{ is $(K,\delta,c_1)$-good} \right) \geq 1- C^\star\left(\frac{   c_1 \log(c_1 K) }{\delta ^2 K}+(0.7)^{\delta K}\right).
    \end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The Bessel law of parameter $t>0$ is the measure
$$b^2_t=e^{-t}\sum_{k=-\infty}^\infty\delta_k\,f_k(t/2)$$
with the density being the following function, depending on $k\in\mathbb Z$,
$$f_k(t)=\sum_{p=0}^\infty \frac{t^{|k|+2p}}{(|k|+p)!p!}$$
which is the Bessel function of the first kind, from classical analysis.

body:
[Definition of arXiv:2512.19897, 'On the convoy of the ASEP speed process'] The multi-type Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process (ASEP) $X\left(t\right)$ on $\mathbb{Z}$ is a random permutation of $\mathbb{Z}$ indexed by $t$, with initial condition $X_i\left(0\right) = i$. Here, $X_n\left(t\right)$ is the type of the particle at position $n$ at time $t$. 
    
    On each interval $\left[n, n+1\right]$, there is a Poisson clock with rate $1+q$ and a uniform random $U$ variable in $\left[0,1+q\right]$. The uniform random variable is refreshed each time the clock rings. When the clock rings at time $t$, if $X_n\left(t\right) < X_{n+1}\left(t\right)$ and $U \in [0,1]$, then $X_n\left(t\right)$ and $ X_{n+1}\left(t\right)$ swap. If $X_n\left(t\right) > X_{n+1}\left(t\right)$ and $U \in [1,1+q]$, $X_n\left(t\right)$ and $ X_{n+1}\left(t\right)$ also swap. 
    
    When $q = 0$, the model is called Totally multi-type Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process (TASEP).
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2512.19897, 'On the convoy of the ASEP speed process'

[Theorem 39 (Well-posedness of the nonlinear memory problem) of arXiv:2609.01826, 'An extension theory for fully fractional Schr\"odinger equations with memory'] Let $0<s<1$, set $a=1-2s$, let $\mu\in\C\setminus\{0\}$, and let
$u_0\in\mathcal H^s$ be a prescribed history.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{(i) The range $0\le a<1$.} Let
\[
p_c=1+\frac{2(1-a)}{d+a+1},
\]
suppose that $1<p\leq p_c$, set $r=p+1$, and let $q$ be determined by
\eqref{E:admissible-positive}. We note that $q>2$ is automatic: since
$2<r\le p_c+1=\frac{2(d+2)}{d+a+1}$, \eqref{E:admissible-positive} gives
$\frac2q\le\frac{d+a+1}{d+2}<1$, the last inequality because $a<1$.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] If $p=p_c$, there exists
$\varepsilon_0=\varepsilon_0(d,a,c_s\mu)>0$ such that
\[
\|u_0\|_{\mathcal H^s}\leq\varepsilon_0
\]
implies that, for every $T<\infty$, the problem has a unique mild solution on
$(0,T]$ with prescribed history $u_0$, in the sense of
Definition~\ref{D:memory-solution}.
\item[(b)] If $1<p<p_c$, there exists
$T=T\bigl(d,a,p,\mu,\|u_0\|_{\mathcal H^s}\bigr)>0$ such that the problem has a
unique mild solution on $(0,T]$ with prescribed history $u_0$. If, in addition,
$\operatorname{Im}(c_s\mu)=0$ --- equivalently, by
Remark~\ref{R:admissible-mu} below, if $\mu\in e^{i\frac{\pi s}{2}}\R$ --- then this
solution extends to a mild solution on $(0,T]$ for every $T<\infty$, by
\cite[Theorem~2.8(2)]{GS2}, applied with vanishing interior forcing and
boundary coefficient $-c_s\mu$.
\end{itemize}

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{(ii) The range $-1<a<0$.} Let
\[
p_c=1+\frac{2}{d+1},
\]
suppose that $1<p\leq p_c$, set $r=p+1$, and let $q,q_\infty$ satisfy
\eqref{E:admissible-negative}.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] If $p=p_c$, then for every $T<\infty$ there exists
$\varepsilon_1=\varepsilon_1(d,a,c_s\mu,T)>0$ such that
\[
\|u_0\|_{\mathcal H^s}\leq\varepsilon_1
\]
implies that the problem has a unique mild solution on $(0,T]$ with prescribed
history $u_0$. One may take
$\varepsilon_1=\varepsilon_0\bigl(C\max\{1,T^{\frac1q-\frac1{q_\infty}}\}\bigr)^{-1}$,
with $\varepsilon_0$ and $C$ as in \cite[Theorem~2.9(1)]{GS2}; since
$\frac1q-\frac1{q_\infty}>0$ in this range, $\varepsilon_1\to0$ as
$T\to\infty$, and no global statement is asserted here.
\item[(b)] If $1<p<p_c$, there exists $T>0$ such that the problem has a unique
mild solution on $(0,T]$ with prescribed history $u_0$.
\end{itemize}

\smallskip
\noindent
In both ranges uniqueness is understood within the extension-induced class of
Definition~\ref{D:memory-solution}. In the range $0\le a<1$ the local Lipschitz
dependence furnished by the fixed-point argument is quantified in
Proposition~\ref{P:contdep} below; no separate continuous-dependence statement
is asserted for $-1<a<0$.

body:
[Theorem thm:upwards of arXiv:2604.10214, 'Large deviations for maximum local time of simple random walk in dimensions \texorpdfstrin'] For any $\beta > 1$ and $u \in \mathbb{R}$, as $t \to \infty$ or $n \to \infty$, we have
\begin{align}
\mathbb{P}\bigl(\ell^*(t) > \beta \cdot \gamma^{-1}\log t + u\bigr)
&= (1+o(1)) \gamma e^{-\gamma u} t^{-(\beta-1)}, \\
\mathbb{P}\bigl(\xi^*(n) > \beta \cdot \alpha \log n + u\bigr)
&= (1+o(1)) \gamma n (1-\gamma)^{\lfloor \beta \cdot \alpha \log n + u \rfloor}. 
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Upward deviations

[Prop 4. prop: precompactness of transition densities of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] Assume that $(F_{n}, R_{n}, \rho_{n}, \mu_{n})$ converges to $(F, R, \rho, \mu)$ in the local Gromov-Hausdorff-vague topology.
  Then, for any $T > 0$ and $r>0$,
  \begin{equation}
    \sup_{n \geq 1} \mathfrak{s}_{F_{n}}(p_{n}, T, r) < \infty,
    \quad 
    \lim_{\delta \downarrow 0} \sup_{n \geq 1} \mathfrak{d}_{F_{n}}(p_{n}, T, r, \delta) = 0.
  \end{equation}

Let U subset R^n be open and bounded, T>0, U_T = U x (0,T], and let the parabolic boundary be Gamma_T = (closure(U) x {0}) union (partial U x [0,T]). Suppose u is continuous on closure(U_T), C^2 in x and C^1 in t on U_T, and satisfies partial u/partial t - Delta u <= 0 on U_T. Then max_{closure(U_T)} u = max_{Gamma_T} u. (Correspondingly, supersolutions with partial u/partial t - Delta u >= 0 attain their minimum on Gamma_T.)

Let F_q be the finite field with q = p^m elements (p prime) and let f_1, ..., f_r be polynomials in F_q[x_1, ..., x_n] with sum_i deg f_i < n. WARNING (1935): the number N of common zeros of f_1, ..., f_r in F_q^n is divisible by p. CHEVALLEY (1935): if in addition every f_i has zero constant term (so 0 is a common zero), then there is another common zero; in particular a homogeneous form of degree d in more than d variables has a nontrivial zero over F_q, so finite fields are quasi-algebraically closed (C_1 fields). Strengthenings: Ax (1964) showed q^b divides N with b = ceil((n - sum deg f_i) / max deg f_i) (Ax-Katz); the theorem gives the Erdos-Ginzburg-Ziv theorem (among 2n - 1 integers some n have sum divisible by n) by applying it to two forms of degree p - 1 in 2p - 1 variables.
F_q finite with q = p^m
sum_i deg f_i < n (total degrees); the bound is sharp, as the norm form shows
Chevalley's form needs the f_i to vanish at the origin

The degree of P is (q - 1) sum_i deg f_i < (q - 1) n. Expand P into monomials c x_1^{e_1} ... x_n^{e_n}; each monomial has total degree < (q-1) n, so some exponent e_j is at most q - 2. The sum of a monomial over F_q^n factors as c prod_j (sum_{t in F_q} t^{e_j}), and sum_{t in F_q} t^{e} = 0 for 0 <= e <= q - 2: for e = 0 the sum is q * 1 = 0 in F_q, and for 1 <= e <= q - 2 the map t -> t^e is a nontrivial character of the cyclic group F_q^* (its order q - 1 does not divide e), whose values sum to 0, while the term t = 0 contributes nothing. Therefore every monomial sums to 0 and sum_x P(x) = 0 in F_q, i.e. N is congruent to 0 modulo p. Chevalley's statement follows: N >= 1 because 0 is a common zero, and p divides N, so N >= p >= 2. The degree hypothesis is sharp: the norm form of F_{q^n} over F_q is a form of degree n in n variables with 0 as its only zero, so N = 1 is not divisible by p when the degree equals the number of variables. Draft author claim, independent review pending. On the SAME finite variable region, let gamma_f be the integer-q zero-field Potts Gibbs law with unit ferromagnetic internal bonds and gamma_b the law with exterior spins fixed. For beta>=0, q>=2 and m crossing bonds, D(gamma_b||gamma_f)<=beta*m and D(gamma_f||gamma_b)<=beta*m. Every mixture rho of the exterior-boundary laws has D(rho||gamma_f)<=beta*m. For n^d lattice boxes this gives D(rho||gamma_f)/n^d<=2*d*beta/n, at every temperature. It does not give an energy gap. Pinning variable sites in only one law would violate the common-support hypothesis.
integer q>=2
beta>=0
unit ferromagnetic bonds and zero field
identical variable sites; only exterior spins are pinned

body:
# Moitra-Risteski: relevant decomposition, uncovered phase-retrieval hypotheses

T321 Target 2. Literature applicability finding, not a new proof of Target 2.
Source: Fast Convergence for Langevin Diffusion with Manifold Structure,
arXiv:2002.05576, primary PDF saved under papers/.

Section 2, PDF page 3, requires the matrix-sensing operator to satisfy
(19/20)||M||_F^2 <= ||A(M)||_2^2 <= (21/20)||M||_F^2
for every matrix M of rank at most 2k. This is an operator-wide assumption,
not concentration for a fixed deterministic M.

For phase retrieval take k=1 and A_ph(M)_j=(a_j^T M a_j)/sqrt(m), so the
squared residual is precisely the normalized empirical quartic loss.
For every nonzero measurement a_i, set u=a_i/||a_i|| and M=uu^T. Then
rank(M)=1, ||M||_F=1 and

 ||A_ph(M)||_2^2=(1/m)sum_j(a_j.u)^4 >= ||a_i||^4/m.

Thus the upper RIP inequality would force
m >= (20/21)max_i||a_i||^4. The witness is allowed to depend on the sample,
because RIP quantifies over EVERY rank-one matrix. This is the exact
deterministic fourth-moment obstruction already relevant to this row,
applied to the paper's stated hypothesis; it is not presented as new.
For Gaussian measurements, ||a_1||^2/d tends to 1 in probability. Therefore
for m=C d log^3 d with fixed C, this necessary inequality fails with
probability tending to 1 as d grows. Multiplication by any fixed scalar
normalization of A_ph does not remove the growing d/log^3 d obstruction.
No claim is made here about operators obtained by data-dependent weighting,
truncation or a changed loss; those require their own arguments.

Section 4.1, Theorem 4, PDF page 7, is nevertheless a relevant generic
decomposition framework: along-level and across-level Poincare control,
control of changing conditional density/Jacobian, and finite-time retention
near the minimizer manifold combine into convergence to a restricted law.
These are hypotheses to establish, not consequences of benign landscape
alone. Our C007 is a different polar decomposition with the same unresolved
need for one conditional spectral-gap estimate.

Section 4.2, Theorem 5, PDF pages 7-8, assumes the matrix measurement
conditions above, a sufficiently large beta, and an absolutely continuous
initial law supported near one minimizer component. The target p_i is
defined just before the theorem as the Gibbs law restricted to points
closer to component E_i than the other component. The theorem's displayed
TV error includes an additive epsilon, as well as a decaying chi-square
term. It is not a statement of the full unrestricted even Poincare constant
for the empirical rank-one measurement model at beta~d/epsilon_loss.
The TV accuracy epsilon in the paper must not be identified silently with
the row's optimization/loss tolerance epsilon_loss.

The discussion on PDF page 9 explicitly leaves reaching the prescribed
initialization by unmodified Langevin for future work, while explaining
that optimization can supply such an initialization in the stated models.
Even if a warm-start sampling guarantee were imported, an additive-error
TV guarantee alone is not a variational Poincare inequality for the full law.

NEXT: adapt the near-well decomposition and retention estimates using the
actual rank-one measurement geometry, without imposing false global RIP;
then control the rest of the quotient to obtain the full polynomial gap.
No claim of a solved parameter range or a scored frontier move is made.
The rank-one diagnostic is analytic and unaudited, not a numerical bound
or a Lean-certified assertion.
Primary-source scope record, not a new polynomial-gap theorem
Matrix sensing application assumes 1/20-RIP on all rank-at-most-2k matrices
The actual row has iid Gaussian rank-one measurements and m at least C d log^3 d

[Theorem l.CLT-Cumulants of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Let $(\mathfrak{m}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$  be a sequence of purely
 atomic random signed measures and assume they admit  correlation functions $m^{\bk k1{p}}(\bk x1{p})= m^{\bk k1{p}}(\bk x1{p};n)$ defined as at (equation eqn:mixedmoment-general of the paper).   Assume  there exist fast decreasing functions $\tilde\phi_{k}$,
 and constants $M_{k}$,	$\tilde C_k$, 
 such that for all $p\ge 2$, $k_1,\ldots,k_p\in \mathbb{N}$, $k_1+\ldots+k_p=k$
 \begin{equation}
   \sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}}\sup_{\bk x1p\in\mathbb{R}^{dp}}m^{\bk k1{p}}(\bk x1{p};n)\le M_{k}<\infty
 \end{equation}
 and statement (i) of Lemma~(l.moments-cumulants of the paper) holds for
 the functions $\tilde\phi =\tilde\phi_k$ and constants  $\tilde C=\tilde C_k$ (uniformly in $n \in \mathbb{N}$).
 If the sequence  $(g_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of real-valued, measurable functions on $ \mathbb{R}^d$, 
 is uniformly  bounded in $n$ (i.e., $\sup_{n \geq 1}  \|g_n\|_\infty\le M<\infty$) and  satisfies
$\|g_n\|_1 := \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}|g_n(x)|\,\mathrm{d} x=O(n^\kappa)$ for some $\kappa<\infty$, and
  ${\rm Var}[\langle g_n,\mathfrak{m}_n\rangle] = \Omega(n^{\nu})$ for some $\nu > 0$, then

$$
({\rm Var}[\langle g_n,\mathfrak{m}_n\rangle])^{-1/2} ( \langle g_n,\mathfrak{m}_n\rangle - \mathbb {E} [\langle g_n,\mathfrak{m}_n\rangle]) \stackrel{d}{\Rightarrow} Z
$$
where $Z$ denotes a standard normal random variable.

[Cor corPhaseTransitionGnp of arXiv:2411.18563, 'Lower tails for triangles inside the critical window'] A phase transition for triangle-freeness in  $G(n,p)$  occurs at $p=c^\ast/\sqrt{n}$ for some $c^\ast \in [1/\sqrt{e}, 4.342)$ in the sense that the function $\varphi_0(c)$ is non-analytic at $c=c^\ast$.
 

   More generally, there exists $\eta_\ell \approx .0091$ so that for every $\eta \in [0, \eta_\ell)$, there exists $c^\ast_\eta \in (0,\infty)$ so that a phase transition occurs in the lower-tail problem at  $c^\ast_{\eta}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:BESQflow of arXiv:2411.04773, 'Meeting of squared Bessel flow lines and application to the skew Brownian motion'] Let $\delta \in {\mathbb R}$.  We call ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow  driven by $\mathcal W$ a collection ${\mathcal S}$ of continuous processes $({\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a),\, x\ge r)_{r\in {\mathbb R},a\ge 0}$ such that: 
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item
for each $(a,r)\in {\mathbb R}_+\times {\mathbb R}$, the process $({\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a),\, x\ge r)$ is almost surely the strong solution of the following SDE  
\begin{equation}
{\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a) = 
a + 2 \int_r^x  {\mathcal W}([0,{\mathcal S}_{r,s}(a)], \, \mathrm{d} s) + 
\delta (x-r) 
,\, x\ge r
\end{equation}
 and which, in the case $\delta<0$, is absorbed when hitting $0$.
 \item Almost surely,
 \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
 \item for all $r\in {\mathbb R}$ and $a\ge 0$, $ {\mathcal S}_{r,r}(a)=a$,
 \item for all $r\le x$, $a\mapsto  {\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a)$ is c\`adl\`ag,
 \item (Perfect flow property) for any $r\le x \le y$ and $a\ge 0$, $\mathcal S_{r,y}(a)=\mathcal S_{x,y}\circ \mathcal S_{r,x}(a)$. 
\end{enumerate} 
\end{enumerate}

We call killed ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow driven by $\mathcal W$ the flow obtained from the ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow by absorbing at $0$ the flow line $\mathcal S_{r,\cdot}(a)$ at time $\inf\{x>r\,:\,\mathcal S_{r,x}(a)=0\}$. 

We call general ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow  a  ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow or a  killed ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow.
title: Definition def:BESQflow of arXiv:2411.04773

$\Phi_A(x)=\int_0^x\1_A(y)\,dy$.  Then $\Phi_A$ is Lipschitz with constant
one.  By the chain rule and the duality between $\D$ and $\delta$,
\[
 \E[\1_A(F)-\1_A(G)]
 =\E\left[
 \delta(u_F)\bigl(\Phi_A(F)-\Phi_A(G)\bigr)
 \right]
 +\E\left[
 \1_A(G)
 \frac{\ip{\D F-\D G}{\D F}_{\cH}}
      {\norm{\D F}_{\cH}^2}
 \right].
\]
The Lipschitz bound
$|\Phi_A(F)-\Phi_A(G)|\le|F-G|$, followed by Cauchy--Schwarz, gives
\[
 |\E[\1_A(F)-\1_A(G)]|
 \le \norm{F-G}_{L^2}\norm{\delta(u_F)}_{L^2}
 +\norm{\D F-\D G}_{L^2(\cH)}
  \norm{\norm{\D F}_{\cH}^{-1}}_{L^2}.
\]
Taking the supremum over $A$ proves \eqref{eq:TV-Malliavin}.

[Theorem Thm.Regularity of arXiv:2411.15485, '\bf\Large Stochastic Volterra Equations for Local Times of Spectrally Positive L\'evy Proc'] The process $L^\xi_\zeta$ is locally H\"older continuous with index strictly less than $1/2$. 
  	Moreover,  for each $\kappa \in (0,1/2)$ and $p\geq 1$, there exists a constant $C>0$ such that for any $\zeta, x\geq 0$, 
  	\begin{eqnarray}
  	\mathbf{E}\Big[\big\| L^\xi_\zeta \big\|_{C^{0,\kappa}_x}^{p}\Big] \leq  C \cdot (\zeta \vee \zeta^{p}) \cdot (1+x)^{p(3-\kappa) }
  	\quad \mbox{and}\quad
  	\mathbf{E}\Big[ \sup_{z\in[0,x]} \big|L^\xi_\zeta(z)\big|^p \Big] \leq C \cdot (\zeta \vee \zeta^{p}) \cdot (1+x)^{3p} . 
  	\end{eqnarray} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.23960, 'Learning from Uncertainty-dependent Missing Labels for Semi-supervised Classification'] Let \((Y,Z)\) have joint density \(p_\theta(Y,Z)\), and let
\(M\in\{0,1\}\) denote the label-missingness indicator, with \(M=1\) if the
label is missing and \(M=0\) if it is observed. Suppose that
\[
  M\perp Z\mid Y
\]
and that the missingness mechanism has the form
\[
  r_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)
  =
  \Pr(M=1\mid Y;\theta,\boldsymbol\xi)
  =
  h\{\eta_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)\},
\]
where \(h\) is a smooth inverse link function and
\(\eta_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)\) may depend on \(\theta\). Then, for known
\(\boldsymbol\xi\), the observed-data Fisher information for \(\theta\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}(\theta)
  =
  \mathcal I_{CC}(\theta)
  -
  \mathcal I_{CC}^{(\mathrm{miss},r)}(\theta,\boldsymbol\xi)
  +
  \mathcal I_{\mathrm{mech}}(\theta,\boldsymbol\xi).

\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}(\theta)
  =
  \mathcal I_{UC}(\theta)
  +
  E_\theta\!\left[
    \{1-r_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)\}
    \operatorname{Var}_\theta\{S_c(Y,Z;\theta)\mid Y\}
  \right]
  +
  \mathcal I_{\mathrm{mech}}(\theta,\boldsymbol\xi).

\end{equation}
The mechanism-curvature term is positive semidefinite. For the logistic inverse
link,
\[
  w_h\{\eta_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)\}
  =
  r_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)
  \{1-r_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)\}.
\]
If \(r_{\theta,\boldsymbol\xi}(Y)\equiv\gamma\), then
\[
  \mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}(\theta)
  =
  \mathcal I_{CC}(\theta)
  -
  \gamma\,\mathcal I_{CC}^{(\mathrm{miss})}(\theta)
  +
  \mathcal I_{\mathrm{mech}}(\theta,\boldsymbol\xi).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.23960
