[Prop nonexpl_alpha_prop of arXiv:2411.00629, '\Large Transformation of Stochastic Recursions and Critical Phenomena in the Analysis of t'] Let $\alpha\in(0,1]$. Then, for any choice of ground state, $X_0$,
\[
X_n(t)\to\underline{X}(t) = u_0^{N_t}\qquad \text{for all}\ t\ge 0,
\]
where $N_t=|\partial V(t)|<\infty$ a.s. Moreover,
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\alpha\in(0,1)$, then $\underline{u}(t)=\mathbb{E}(\underline{X}(t))<\infty$ for all $u_0,t>0$ and, as $t\to\infty$
\[
\underline{u}(t)\to
\begin{cases}
0, & \text{if}\ u_0\in[0,1)\\
\infty, & \text{if}\ u_0>1.
\end{cases}
\]
($\underline{u}(t)\equiv 1$ if $u_0=1$).
\item If $\alpha=1$, then $\underline{u}(t)=\mathbb{E}(\underline{X}(t))<\infty$ solves the logistic equation $u'=-u+u^2$ 
with corresponding asymptotic behavior in $t$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop nonexpl_alpha_prop of arXiv:2411.00629

body:
[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2506.15736, 'Coming down from infinity for coordinated particle systems'] Fix a finite set of sites $V$, and let $\Lambda_v, D_v, M_{uv}$, and $R_{uv}$ be finite measures on $[0,1]$ for $u,v \in V$. Then there exists a probability space on which for each $\pi \in \mathcal{P}$ there exists a c\`adl\`ag Markov process $(X_\pi(t))_{t \geq 0}$ called the coordinated particle system with the following properties:

    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] $(X_\pi(t))_{t \geq 0}$ takes values in $\mathcal{P}$ and $X_\pi(0) = \pi$.

        \item[(b)] If $\pi_1, \pi_2 \in \mathcal{P}$ with $\pi_1 \leq \pi_2$, i.e. $\pi_1(v) \leq \pi_2(v)$ for all $v \in V$, then $X_{\pi_1}(t) \leq X_{\pi_2}(t)$ for all $t \geq 0$.

        \item[(c)] If $|\pi| < \infty$, i.e. $\sum_{v \in V} \pi(v) < \infty$, then the transition rates of $(X_\pi(t))_{t \geq 0}$ are given by \eqref{eq:rates}.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In probability theory, coupling is a proof technique that allows one to compare two unrelated random variables (distributions) X and Y by creating a random vector W whose marginal distributions correspond to X and Y respectively. The choice of W is generally not unique, and the whole idea of "coupling" is about making such a choice so that X and Y can be related in a particularly desirable way.
title: Coupling (probability)

body:
For the nondimensionalized Rosenzweig-MacArthur ODE system dN/dt = N*(1 - N/k - m*P/(1+N)) and dP/dt = P*(-c + m*N/(1+N)), the nonnegative quadrant Q = {(N, P) in R^2 : N >= 0, P >= 0} and its interior D = {(N, P) in R^2 : N > 0, P > 0} are positively invariant. Furthermore, there exists R_0 > 0 such that for all R >= R_0, the triangular domain T(R) = {(N, P) in Q : N + P <= R} is positively invariant, ensuring that all trajectories with initial condition in Q are uniformly bounded for all t >= 0.
Parameters k > 0, m > 0, c > 0
Initial condition (N(0), P(0)) in Q

[Theorem 10 (Limiting invariant measure) of arXiv:2606.31596, 'The Invariant Measure of Multiscale Markov Chains via Fast Arborescence Factorization'] Let $X^N_t$ be a continuous time Markov chain with strongly connected transition graph $(V,E,r_N)$ satisfying Assumption \ref{FRL2}. 
Let $\pi_N$ be its unique invariant measure.
Then its limit exists, is a probability measure on $V$ and can be expressed as
\begin{equation}
	\pi:=
	\lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} \pi_N =
	\sum_{M\in \mathcal M} \bar \pi(M)\, \mu_M \;.
\end{equation}
In particular $\pi(x)=0$ for $x\in V\setminus \hat V$ and more explicitly:
\begin{equation}
	\pi(x)= \begin{cases} 
	\,\bar \pi(M)\;\mu_M(x) & \textrm{, }\, x\in M  \textrm{ for }M\in\mathcal M\\
	\,0 & \textrm{, }\,x\in Q  \textrm{ for }Q\in\mathcal Q \setminus \mathcal M \end{cases} \ .
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Limiting invariant measure

For stationary measurable finite nonnegative edge weights on nearest-neighbor Z^2, let B_n=[-n,n]^2 intersect Z^2, A be the vertices on self-avoiding bigeodesics, and D_n be the vertices in B_n on ANY self-avoiding globally minimizing finite path with endpoints on the vertex boundary of B_2n. Paths may leave B_2n, and all geodesics are included if ties occur. Let H_n(0) mean existence of a self-avoiding globally minimizing path (z_-n,...,z_n) with z_0=0 and adjacent consecutive vertices. Then P(0 in A)<=E|D_n|/|B_n|<=P(H_n(0)). Centered-prefix compactness gives P(H_n(0)) decreasing to P(0 in A); hence the expected occupation density tends to P(0 in A). Almost-sure absence of ALL bigeodesics is equivalent to E|D_n|=o(n^2). This iid decay estimate is not proved here.

[Lem lem for 4.1(2) of arXiv:2505.11700, 'Distribution of the cokernels of determinantal row-sparse matrices'] Let $\underline{n} \in B(n,H)$, 

$a \in G \backslash H$ and $$m: = \sum_{b \in -a + H} n_{b}.$$ Let
\begin{align*}
B & = \{(b_1, \ldots, b_{k_n-1}) \in G^{k_n-1} : b_1+ \cdots + b_{k_n-1} = -a \text{ and $k_n-2$ of $b_i$'s are in $H$}\}, \\   
B^c & = \{(b_1, \ldots, b_{k_n-1}) \in G^{k_n-1} : b_1+ \cdots + b_{k_n-1} = -a \text{ and at most $k_n-3$ of $b_i$'s are in $H$}\}.  
\end{align*}
Then we have the following.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
$$\sum_{(b_1, \ldots, b_{k_n-1}) \in B} n_{b_1}\cdots n_{b_{k_n-1}} = (k_n-1)\frac{n^{k_n-2}}{|H|}m + O(n^{k_n-3}t_nr_nk_n^2).$$
\item 
$$\sum_{(b_1, \ldots, b_{k_n-1}) \in B^c} n_{b_1}\cdots n_{b_{k_n-1}} = O(n^{k_n-3}r_n^2 k_n^2).$$
\item 
$$
n(k_n-1)_a = (k_n-1)\frac{n^{k_n-2}}{|H|}m + O(n^{k_n-3}t_nr_nk_n^2).
$$
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2606.01209, 'Mean field limits of large Jackson networks \\ in heavy traffic'] Let Assumption \ref{assn1} hold. Let $k\in\N$, and let $(\oo X,\oo L,\lambda)$ be the solution of \eqref{MVSDE} with $\oo X_0\sim\mu_0^{(1)}$. Then
\[
((\hat X^n_i)_{i\in[k]},(\hat L^n_i)_{i\in[k]})
\To
((\oo X_i)_{i\in[k]},(\oo L_i)_{i\in[k]})
\]
in $D^{(k)}\times C^{(k)}$, where $(\oo X_i,\oo L_i)$ are $k$ independent copies of $(\oo X,\oo L)$. Moreover,
\[
(\mu^n,\lambda^n)\to(\mu,\lambda)
\]
in $D(\R_+,\calP(\R_+^2))\times C^{(1)}$, in probability, where
\[
\mu_t=\PP\circ(\oo X(t),\oo L(t))^{-1},
\qquad t\ge0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Check what the random-current and infrared bounds give and where each half of the conjecture sits. Result: Upper bound: the infrared bound gives <sigma_0 sigma_x> <= C |x|^{-(d-2)} = C|x|^{-1} in d = 3, and improving to |x|^{-(1+eps)} is the statement eta > 0 (anomalous dimension), known numerically eta = 0.036; an argument would need to show the two-point function is strictly smaller than the Gaussian one in a scale-invariant way, e.g. via the random-current intersection probabilities (the same quantity that gives non-triviality, C0052): if two independent currents from 0 to x and from y to z intersect with probability bounded below uniformly, one gets a strict improvement of Simon-Lieb at every scale which iterates to a power gain. Lower bound: Simon-Lieb / Lebowitz give <sigma_0 sigma_x> >= c |x|^{-(d-1)} = c|x|^{-2} in d = 3 (the source's Theorem 4.8), and improving the exponent below 2 needs a lower bound on the two-point function from the connectivity of the random-current clusters better than the trivial one-path bound. I verified that the one-path bound cannot give better than d - 1 because the number of self-avoiding paths of length n weighted by tanh(beta_c)^n is exactly balanced at criticality, so the improvement must come from multi-path (cluster) contributions. No quantitative result. Obstruction: Both halves need scale-invariant intersection estimates for random currents in d = 3, which are not available.

[Theorem thm:convex of arXiv:2510.22778, 'Free denoising diffusion models'] Let $\mu_{0},\mu_{1}$ have finite second moment and finite logarithmic energy, and let
$(\mu_{s})_{s\in[0,1]}$ be the free Wasserstein geodesic joining them, which by
Theorem~(thm:bv of the paper) is the McCann interpolation
$\mu_{s}=((1-s)\Id+sT)_{\#}\mu_{0}$ with $T$ nondecreasing. Then
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal{F}[\mu_{s}]\le(1-s)\mathcal{F}[\mu_{0}]+s\mathcal{F}[\mu_{1}]
  -\tfrac12 s(1-s)\,W_{2}(\mu_{0},\mu_{1})^{2},
  \qquad s\in[0,1],
\end{equation}
that is, $\mathcal{F}$ is $1$-convex along free Wasserstein geodesics.

[Theorem thm:expr_zcmcoup of arXiv:2605.10491, 'Zero-couplings of infinite measures with cyclically monotone support and multivariate regu'] Let $\mu,\nu\in\mathrm{M}_{0}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $\gamma\in\Gamma_{0,\mathrm{cm}}(\mu,\nu)$, and assume that $\mu$ vanishes on sets of Hausdorff dimension at most $d-1$. Then for any closed convex function $\psi: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R} \cup \left\{\infty\right\}$ satisfying $\operatorname{spt}\gamma\subset \partial\psi$, we have $\mu(\reals^d_{\smallsetminus 0} \setminus \operatorname{dom} \nabla\psi) = 0$. The measure $\nu$ can be written as the push-forward of $\mu$ by $\nabla\psi$, up to a residual term: for every Borel set $B\subset\reals^d_{\smallsetminus 0}$,
    \[
        \nu(B) = (\nabla\psi)_{\#} \mu(B) + \gamma(\left\{0\right\} \times B). 
    \]
    In addition, $\gamma$ is uniquely determined by $\nabla \psi, \mu, \nu$ through the identities
    \begin{align*}
        \gamma(A \times B) 
        &= (\operatorname{Id} \times \nabla\psi)_{\#}\mu(A\times B)
        = \mu \rbr{A \cap (\nabla\psi)^{-1}(B)}, &&
        A \in \mathcal{B}(\reals^d_{\smallsetminus 0}), \, B \in \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^d), \\
        \gamma(\left\{0\right\} \times B)
        &= \nu(B) - (\nabla\psi)_{\#} \mu(B), &&
        B \in \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^d), \, 0 \not\in \operatorname{cl}(B).
    \end{align*}
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    Finally, if $\gamma$ is proper, i.e., $\gamma\in\Gamma_{0,\mathrm{cm}}^{\mathrm{p}}(\mu,\nu)$, then we have the \emph{proper representation} 
    \begin{equation}
        
        \gamma = \operatorname{res} \rbr{ (\operatorname{Id} \times \nabla\psi)_{\#}\mu }
        \quad \text{and} \quad
        \nu = \operatorname{res} \rbr{(\nabla \psi)_{\#}\mu}.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 38 of arXiv:2512.07202, 'Hitting Probabilities for Hypoelliptic Differential Equations Driven by Fractional Brownia'] Let \( (u_t)_{0 \leqslant t \leqslant T} \) be a stochastic process satisfying assumptions $\mathbf{(A1)}$ and $\mathbf{(A2)}$. Let \( 0 < a < b \leqslant T \) and \( M > 0 \) be given fixed. Then for any \( \eta \in (0, Q - \alpha) \) (if \( \alpha < 0 \), we further require \( \alpha + \eta < 0 \)), there exists a positive constant \( C = C(a, b, T, M, \alpha, \eta, V) \) such that
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb{P}\big(u([a, b]) \cap A \neq \emptyset\big) \geqslant C\, \mathrm{Cap}_{\alpha + \eta}(A)
\end{equation}holds for all compact sets \( A \subseteq B_d(o,M) \)

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2603.24616, 'Pinning in non-critical half-space geometric last passage percolation'] Fix $k \in \mathbb{N}$, $\vec{x}, \vec{y} \in \weylc_k$, and $a,b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] Suppose $\vec{x}\,^n, \vec{y}\,^n \in \weyl_k$ satisfy $\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \vec{x}\,^n = \vec{x}$, $\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \vec{y}\,^n = \vec{y}$. Then, as $n \rightarrow \infty$, the measures $\mathbb{P}_{\mathrm{avoid}}^{a,b,\vec{x}\,^n,\vec{y}\,^n}$ converge weakly to a probability measure on $C(\llbracket 1, k \rrbracket \times [a,b])$. We denote this limiting measure by $\mathbb{P}_{\mathrm{avoid}}^{a,b,\vec{x},\vec{y}}$ and write $\mathbb{E}_{\mathrm{avoid}}^{a,b,\vec{x},\vec{y}}$ for the expectation with respect to this measure. 
\item[(b)] Suppose $\vec{x}\,^n, \vec{y}\,^n \in \weylc_k$ satisfy $\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \vec{x}\,^n = \vec{x}$, $\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \vec{y}\,^n = \vec{y}$. Then, $\mathbb{P}_{\mathrm{avoid}}^{a,b,\vec{x}\,^n,\vec{y}\,^n} \Rightarrow \mathbb{P}_{\mathrm{avoid}}^{a,b,\vec{x},\vec{y}}$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Fix $\varepsilon>0$. Then the following holds almost surely. For any points $u,v\in \mathbb{C}$, any $D_h$-geodesic $P$ from $u$ to $v$ and any sequence of $D_h$-geodesics $\{P_n\}_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ converging to $P$ in the Hausdorff sense with respect to $D_h$\footnote{Or equivalently, with respect to the Euclidean metric and with Euclidean balls on the right side of (equation eq:14 of the paper). Indeed, since $\gamma\in (0,2)$, the $D_h$-metric is a.s.\ locally bi-H\"older with respect to the Euclidean metric (see Lemma (lem:holder_regularity of the paper)).}, for all $n$ large enough, we have

      (P_n\setminus P)\cup (P\setminus P_n)\subseteq \mathcal{B}_\varepsilon(u)\cup \mathcal{B}_\varepsilon(v).

Let E be a real Banach space, H a separable real Hilbert space, L and Lprime bounded linear operators on E, and S:E->H a contraction in the E->H operator norm. For finite positive integers d,dprime, let h_ij(z)=sum_{k>=0} beta_ijk z^k and B_k=(beta_ijk)_(j,i) in R^(dprime x d), with Euclidean matrix operator norm ||B_k||. Put r=max(1,||L||,||Lprime||), and assume sum_k ||B_k|| r^k and sum_{k>=1} k||B_k|| r^(k-1) are finite. For x_1,...,x_d in E, sqrt(sum_j ||S sum_i h_ij(L)x_i||_H^2) <= (sum_k ||B_k|| ||L^k||) sqrt(sum_i ||x_i||_E^2). Also sqrt(sum_j ||S sum_i [h_ij(L)-h_ij(Lprime)]x_i||_H^2) <= sum_{k>=1} ||B_k|| sqrt(sum_i [sum_{ell=0}^{k-1} ||L^ell|| ||(L-Lprime)(Lprime)^(k-1-ell)x_i||_E]^2). If H is only a Banach space, both inequalities hold with ||B_k|| replaced by ||(|beta_ijk|)_(j,i)|| and the analogous summability assumption. The explicit summability conditions here ensure convergence of every series. Let A and B be sets. If there exist an injective function f : A -> B and an injective function g : B -> A, then there exists a bijection h : A -> B. The bijection can be built explicitly from f and g without the axiom of choice (in ZF), so the cardinalities satisfy |A| <= |B| and |B| <= |A| together imply |A| = |B|.

Consider the chains obtained by alternately applying g and f backwards: for a in A look at the sequence a, g^{-1}(a), f^{-1}(g^{-1}(a)), ... as far as the preimages exist (each is unique because f and g are injective). Every element of A and of B lies in exactly one such maximal chain. A chain either continues forever backwards, or stops at an element of A with no g-preimage, or stops at an element of B with no f-preimage. Define h on A by h(a) = f(a) if a's chain is infinite or stops in A, and h(a) = g^{-1}(a) if the chain stops in B (in which case a has a g-preimage, because the chain stopping in B means it passed through a via g). ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Analyse where the Zerner-Merkl planar argument uses d = 2. Result: Zerner-Merkl show P_0[A_l intersection A_{-l}] = 0 using that in d = 2 two independent walks in the same environment started at distant points on a line perpendicular to l must, with positive probability, have paths that intersect (planarity), which lets one derive a contradiction from the walk going to +infinity and -infinity in direction l with positive probability each. In d >= 3 paths of two walks need not intersect, and the known partial result (Kalikow's 0-1 law: P_0[A_l union A_{-l}] in {0,1}) does not exclude the mixed event. A candidate counterexample structure in d >= 3 would be an i.i.d. environment where the walk is guided to +l or -l depending on a local feature it meets first; the i.i.d. assumption and the fact that the walk visits infinitely many independent regions make such a persistent memory implausible but not provably impossible: the walk in direction +l sees fresh environment forever, and the event that it turns around is a tail event of the walk but not of the environment. I checked that the natural martingale argument (P_omega(A_l) as a function of the environment at the current position) fails because P_omega(A_l) is not measurable with respect to a finite region. No result. Obstruction: Planarity is essential to the d = 2 proof; no substitute in d >= 3.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0044-zero-one-law-for-directional-transience-in-dimensions-d-3
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

[Defn def:mostlytrans of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Let $\mathcal{G}$, $\mathcal{G}'$ be two $C^0$-foliations on $\mathbb{T}^2$. We say that $\mathcal{G}$ and $\mathcal{G}'$ are \textbf{mostly-transverse} if there exist open sets $W \Subset V \subset \mathbb{T}^2$ such that
    \begin{itemize}
        \item On a neighborhood of $\mathbb{T}^2 \setminus V$, the leaves of $\mathcal{G}$ and $\mathcal{G}'$ coincide,
        \item On a neighborhood of $\overline{V} \setminus W$, $\mathcal{G}$ and $\mathcal{G}'$ are smooth,
        \item On $V \setminus W$, $T\mathcal{G}$ and $T\mathcal{G}'$ coincide, and on $W$, $T\mathcal{G}$ is positively transverse to $T\mathcal{G}'$,
        \item For every $p \in \mathbb{T}^2$, the leaf of $\mathcal{G}$ passing through $p$ intersects $W$ on both sides of $p$.
    \end{itemize}
title: Defn def:mostlytrans of arXiv:2608.30031

[Definition 9 of arXiv:2606.12670, 'The censored stochastic six-vertex model and parabolic Kazhdan--Lusztig $R$-polynomials'] Let $P_k$ be the propagator of the following dynamics on particle configurations $\eta\colon\mathbb Z\to\{0,1\}$. 
    Exchange the values of $\eta(k)$ and $\eta(k+1)$ with probability $b_1$ if $(\eta(k),\eta(k+1))=(0,1)$ and with probability $b_2$ if $(\eta(k),\eta(k+1))=(1,0)$.
    In other words, if $\nu$ is a measure on particle configurations and $\eta$ is a particle configuration, then
    \[
    P_k\nu(\eta)=\begin{cases}
        b_2\nu(\eta^k)+(1-b_1)\nu(\eta), &\text{ if }(\eta(k),\eta(k+1))=(0,1)\\
        b_1\nu(\eta^k)+(1-b_2)\nu(\eta), &\text{ if }(\eta(k),\eta(k+1))=(1,0)\\
        \nu(\eta), &\text{ if }\eta(k)=\eta(k+1)\,.
    \end{cases}
    \]
title: Definition 9 of arXiv:2606.12670

only on $ d,\delta$,  $\rho_{b}$, such that    for any $R\leq \rho_{b} $
and $z_{1}$, $z_{2}\in  C_{R/2}$
\begin{equation}

	$$ \pi M_s = e^{\lambda s} \pi, \qquad M_s h =  e^{\lambda s} h,$$
	  and $\sum_{\tt \in \TT}\pi(\tt) = \sum_{\tt \in \TT}  \pi(\tt) h(\tt) =1.$  The vector $\pi$ satisfies that 
    \begin{align}
        \sum_{\tt \in \TT} \pi(\tt) \vert \tt\vert^2<\infty. 
    \end{align}
    Besides,  there exists $C, \omega > 0$ such that for all $\tt\in \TT$ and $s \geq 0$,
	\begin{align}

        \sup_{\tt\in \TT} \vert f(\tt) \vert / \vert \tt \vert^2  \leq 1}}\big\vert e^{-\lambda s} M_s f(\tt) -  h(\tt) \langle\pi,f\rangle \big\vert  &\leq C \vert \tt \vert^{2}  e^{-\omega s}.

PROOF (UNAUDITED); novelty unverified. Fix s in (0,1], c0 in [-1,1], eps in (0,1), n>=1769472(1+K), 1<=k<=n and 1<=L<=n^(1-eps). For the exact fresh-Gaussian-row zero-bias critical tanh width-n chain on two inputs with initial Gram s[[1,c0],[c0,1]], let X be the joint preactivation trajectory of k fixed rows through L layers (ordinary Euclidean metric on R^(2kL)); let Y have independent Gaussian rows and layers with the deterministic population Gram at each preceding layer. Then W2(Law(X),Law(Y))^2<=C k L/n. For |c0|<1, C=max{6 H_eps exp(14688s)/(1-|c0|),4608}, where H_eps=384+2(2sqrt(192)+Aeps)^2 and Aeps is the explicit C019 constant. For c0=+/-1 take C=2304. Adjoining tanh postactivations multiplies the squared bound by at most two. Thus this architecture has explicit O(sqrt(L)) length dependence for fixed probes and fixed initial Gram. Companion scale-free result C019: for c0<1, ||D_L/Dbar_L-1||_2<=exp(14688s)Aeps sqrt(L/n); the ratio is undefined when c0=1. The elementary matrix inequality used in the proof is standard and is not claimed new.
Equal deterministic initial marginal variances s in (0,1]; c0 valid; fixed probes, conditional iid fresh Gaussian rows, zero bias, tanh; depth and width as stated. C002 v2/C004 v1 reviewed; C012 v1/C019 v1 and their named dependencies remain unaudited. GP covariances are deterministic population Grams, not empirical GP Grams. Interior spectral estimate uses 1-|c0|>0; endpoints reduced separately.
metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:84b9bc7f818d5382188f0a030eb9d9f912485997bf9b49b0cb638e46445825e0","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/84/84b9bc7f818d5382188f0a030eb9d9f912485997bf9b49b0cb638e46445825e0.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:9797c126fec98b2daf1e397619ca3a64554299b07955c3d456eccb5e8ee88c5b","bundle_entry_key":"tanh_two_input_gp_trajectory","bundle_id":"population.w712-t250-c020-two-input-tanh-gp-trajectory","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"Quantitative Tensor Programs, Gaussian process limits and stochastic Gram dynamics","draft":"w712/bundle_015.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.neural_networks:critical-tanh-two-input-gp-trajectory-square-root-depth-width-rate","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C020 v1: quantitative two-input critical tanh GP trajectory coupling

Kind: narrowed. Target: 1, the equal-norm two-input critical tanh chain.
Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty unverified. This is a whole architecture
special case of Target 1, not a theorem for every critical chain or DAG.

## Exact statement and metric

Fix s in (0,1], c0 in [-1,1], 0<eps<1, integers n,k,L with

    n>=1769472(1+K), 1<=k<=n, 1<=L<=n^(1-eps).

Here K,Lambda are the uniform finite angular moment constants in
C010/C015. Initialize the deterministic Gram

    K0=s [[1,c0],[c0,1]].

Conditional on the completed layer-(j-1) past, let the n preactivation
row pairs X_i^(j) be iid centered Gaussian vectors of covariance
K_(j-1), for j=1,...,L. Set K_j equal to the empirical Gram of their
coordinatewise tanh transforms. This is precisely the fresh-weight,
zero-bias, width-n, variance-1/n Gaussian MLP evaluated on two inputs
with initial normalized squared norms s and normalized inner product s c0.
One may equivalently take the conditional Gram chain as the definition.

Let B_j=sbar_j [[1,cbar_j],[cbar_j,1]] be its deterministic population
Gram recursion, starting at the same K0, as in C019. Let Y_i^(j), for
1<=i<=k, 1<=j<=L, be independent across rows and layers, centered
Gaussian two-vectors with covariance B_(j-1). This specifies the GP
trajectory comparison in this theorem. Define the two random vectors

    X=(X_i^(j):1<=i<=k,1<=j<=L) in R^(2kL),
    Y=(Y_i^(j):1<=i<=k,1<=j<=L) in R^(2kL),

using ordinary unnormalized Euclidean distance. Indices are fixed in
advance; the theorem is not about an adaptively selected neuron.

Use Aeps from C019, and set

    Heps=384+2(2sqrt(192)+Aeps)^2.

If |c0|<1, put d=1-|c0|>0 and

    Ceps,s,c0=max{6 Heps exp(14688s)/d,4608}.

If |c0|=1, put Ceps,s,c0=2304. Then

    W2(Law(X),Law(Y))^2 <= Ceps,s,c0 k L/n.          (1)

If each trajectory also includes its coordinatewise tanh postactivations,
the right side may be multiplied by two. Thus for every fixed k and
initial Gram, the constant multiplying n^(-1/2) is O(sqrt(L)), with
explicit stability constants and throughout L<=n^(1-eps).

The dependence on d in this choice of constant is not asserted necessary
or sharp. Endpoint inputs are covered by a separate exact reduction.
The result does not claim a width-free Euclidean bound for all n neurons:
taking k=n changes the right side to Ceps,s,c0 L.

## Inputs and their review status

C002 v2 supplies scalar relative MSE, scalar mean decay and the common-
Gaussian radial coupling estimate; C004 v1 supplies deterministic angular
stability. These two exact versions have reviewer PASS. C012 v1 and
C019 v1, and the dependencies explicitly listed inside C019, remain
unaudited. We build on them, without claiming their independent review.
The elementary matrix estimate below is included to make the new coupling
self-contained; no novelty is claimed for that matrix inequality.

## 1. One-sided square-root estimate, allowing the first matrix singular

Let P be a real symmetric positive semidefinite matrix and B a real
symmetric positive definite matrix of the same finite size. Put
A=P^(1/2), T=B^(1/2) and Z=A-T. The symmetric positive semidefinite
square roots exist by the finite-dimensional spectral theorem. Direct
multiplication, with the order of noncommuting factors preserved, gives

    A Z+Z T=P-B.

Taking the Frobenius inner product with Z gives

    <Z,P-B> = tr(Z^T A Z)+tr(Z^T Z T)
       >=lambda_min(T)||Z||_F^2.

The first trace is nonnegative since A is positive semidefinite; the
second is at least lambda_min(T) tr(Z^T Z) by diagonalizing T.
Frobenius Cauchy-Schwarz, and division only when ||Z||_F>0, yield

    ||P^(1/2)-B^(1/2)||_F^2
       <=||P-B||_F^2/lambda_min(B).                 (2)

If Z=0 the inequality is immediate. Only B must be positive definite;
no inverse of the random P is used. All denominators in (2) are positive.

## 2. Early-depth Gram error and the deterministic spectral gap

Write K_j=[[Q_j,C_j],[C_j,R_j]], and abbreviate u=sbar_j,
c=c_j and cbar=cbar_j. For |c0|<1, C012 and oddness, applied to
both deterministic angular gaps, give

    1-cbar>=exp(-14688s)(1-c0),
    1+cbar>=exp(-14688s)(1+c0).

Consequently

    lambda_min(B_j)=u(1-|cbar|)
                  >=u exp(-14688s)d>0.             (3)

Positivity of u at every finite depth follows from F(q)>0 for q>0.
For j<=n/96, C002 gives the common marginal error bound

    sigma_j:=||Q_j-u||_2=||R_j-u||_2
                         <=u sqrt(192j/n).         (4)

The equality is of marginal norms; no independence between Q_j and R_j
is inferred. The geometric mean lies between its two nonnegative
arguments, so

    |sqrt(Q_j R_j)-u|<=|Q_j-u|+|R_j-u|.

Use C_j=sqrt(Q_j R_j)c, |c|<=1, and decompose exactly as

    C_j-u cbar=(sqrt(Q_j R_j)-u)c+u(c-cbar).

By the triangle inequality and C019,

    ||C_j-u cbar||_2
       <=2sigma_j+u Aeps d sqrt(j/n)
       <=u[2sqrt(192)+Aeps]sqrt(j/n).               (5)

This decomposition uses no fourth moment of c-cbar or product of errors.
Equations (4)--(5), including j=0 where all errors vanish, imply

    E||K_j-B_j||_F^2
       =E(Q_j-u)^2+E(R_j-u)^2+2E(C_j-u cbar)^2
       <=Heps u^2 j/n.                             (6)

Apply (2) pointwise and use deterministic (3). Since C002 gives
u<=6/(j+1), hence uj<=6, we obtain for j<=n/96

    E||K_j^(1/2)-B_j^(1/2)||_F^2
       <=6 Heps exp(14688s)/(d n).                 (7)

C019 applies here because only j<=L-1<=n^(1-eps) is needed.

## 3. Remaining depths use decay, not an extended relative estimate

For positive semidefinite matrices, the squared triangle inequality in
Frobenius norm gives

    ||K_j^(1/2)-B_j^(1/2)||_F^2
       <=2(tr K_j+tr B_j).

C002's unconditional mean decay and deterministic decay give
E Q_j,E R_j,u<=6/(j+1). Thus the expectation of the last display is
at most 48/(j+1). If j>n/96 this is at most 4608/n. Together with
(7), this proves the uniform per-layer bound

    E||K_j^(1/2)-B_j^(1/2)||_F^2<=Ceps,s,c0/n       (8)

for every integer 0<=j<L. The early and late cases exhaust that range.

## 4. A joint coupling with the correct two marginal trajectory laws

Take arrays g_i^(j) of independent standard Gaussian two-vectors,
1<=i<=n, 1<=j<=L, independent of the deterministic initial Gram.
Recursively define

    X_i^(j)=K_(j-1)^(1/2) g_i^(j),
    Y_i^(j)=B_(j-1)^(1/2) g_i^(j).

Use all n tanh(X_i^(j)) rows to define K_j, while B_j always follows
the deterministic population recursion. The random K_(j-1) is measurable
with respect to previous-layer Gaussian arrays, hence independent of
every current g_i^(j). Therefore the conditional X rows have exactly the
required iid Gaussian transition kernel; induction proves the finite-
width trajectory has the stated joint law. The comparison Y rows are
independent across rows and layers, because their matrices are deterministic
and the Gaussian arrays are independent. In particular the comparison
does not replace B_j by an empirical GP Gram.

For each fixed current probe i, conditional Gaussian second moments give

    E[||X_i^(j)-Y_i^(j)||^2 | previous arrays]
       =||K_(j-1)^(1/2)-B_(j-1)^(1/2)||_F^2.

Sum expectations over exactly kL probes and layers, using (8) at
j-1=0,...,L-1. No independence between these coupling costs is required.
This gives E||X-Y||^2<=Ceps,s,c0 kL/n, so the definition of W2 proves
(1) in the case |c0|<1. All second moments are finite by Q,R<=1.

## 5. Singular initial endpoints and postactivations

At c0=1 the two columns coincide at every layer; at c0=-1 they are
opposite at every layer, by the Gaussian conditional kernel and oddness
of tanh. In either case their common scalar marginal variance Q_j
has the one-input law, and K_j=Q_j [[1,c0],[c0,1]], with the same
deterministic form for B_j. Direct diagonalization gives

    ||K_j^(1/2)-B_j^(1/2)||_F^2
                          =2(sqrt(Q_j)-sqrt(u))^2.

C002's common-Gaussian radial estimate bounds the expectation of the
scalar square on the right by 1152/n at every depth. Its early-depth

most 2304/n, as claimed. Section 4's coupling and term count apply
without change, although (2)--(3) are not used at these endpoints.

||tanh(X)-tanh(Y)||^2<=||X-Y||^2. Adjoining postactivations doubles
the squared bound at most. This proves the complete statement.

## Checks, boundaries, and scope of the result

The load-bearing restrictions are: conditional fresh Gaussian rows for
the joint coupling; deterministic GP covariance for independence across
its layers; equal initial norms for C019; fixed finite k probes for the
claimed metric scaling; positive s for normalization; eps>0 for C019's
logarithmic absorption; positive d only in the interior spectral bound.

layer-index shift in section 4; and the rank-one factor two at endpoints.

body:
[Lemma 27 (Cone determination for \eqref{eq:no-t-HJ}) of arXiv:2605.13512, '2605.13512'] Let $H:\mathbb R\to [0,\infty)$ satisfy
\[
|H(p)-H(q)|\le |p-q| \qquad \forall p,q\in \mathbb R,
\]
and assume in addition that
\[
H(1-p)=H(p)\qquad \forall p\in \mathbb R.
\]
Let $\tilde c:\mathbb R\to [0,\infty)$, so that $ \tilde c\in L^{\infty}_{\rm loc}(\R)$. Fix
${\bf z}_0=(x_0,t_0)\in \mathbb R\times (0,\infty)$ and $K>1$ such that
\begin{equation}

K>\sup_{C({\bf z}_0,K)} \tilde c^{*}.
\end{equation}
Assume that for every ${\bf z}^*=(x^*,t^*)\in C({\bf z}_0,K)$ there exists a sign
$\sigma=\sigma(z^*)\in\{-1,+1\}$ such that, for all $M>1$,
\begin{equation}

\lim_{\rho\downarrow 0}
\sup_{\substack{|y-x^*|\le K(t^*-\tau)\le M\rho}}
\bigl[\tilde c^{*}(y)-\tilde c_{*}(y-\sigma\rho)\bigr]\le 0.
\end{equation}

Let $v_1,v_2\in C(C({\bf z}_0,K))$ (the continuous functions on the cone) be such that, on $C({\bf z}_0,K)$,
\begin{enumerate}
\item $v_1$ is an envelope-selected viscosity subsolution of
$
v_t+\tilde c(x)H(v_x)=0,
$
\item $v_2$ is a envelope-selected viscosity supersolution of
$
v_t+\tilde c(x)H(v_x)=0,
$
\item both $v_1$ and $v_2$ are nondecreasing and Lipschitz-$1$ in the $x$-variable,
\item at least one of $v_1,v_2$ is Lipschitz continuous on $C({\bf z}_0,K)$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\begin{equation}

\max_{C({\bf z}_0,K)}(v_1-v_2)
=
\max_{C({\bf z}_0,K)\cap\{t=0\}}(v_1-v_2).
\end{equation}

[Proposition prop:koltch_indep of arXiv:2411.07878, 'Bernstein-type and Bennett-type inequalities for unbounded matrix martingales'] Let $\mathbf{X}_1, \dots, \mathbf{X}_n \in \mathbb{H}(d)$ be independent random matrices.
    Fix $\alpha \ge 1$. 
    Suppose, for all $k = 1, \dots, n$, and some $K > 0$,
    \begin{equation}
    
        \E \mathbf{X}_k = 0, 
        \quad
        \max \left(\norm*{\norm{\mathbf{X}_k}}_{\psi_{\alpha}}, 2 \sqrt{\E \norm{\mathbf{X}_k}^2}\right) 
        \le K.
    \end{equation}
    Set $  \sigma^2 \coloneqq \norm*{\sum_{k=1}^n \E \mathbf{X}^2_k}.$ Then, there exists an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that, for all $t \ge 0$,
    \[
    \mathbb{P}\left(\norm*{\sum_{k=1}^n \mathbf{X}_k} \ge t\right) 
    \le 2 d \exp\lrc{-\frac{1}{C} \frac{t^2}{\sigma^2 + t K \left(\log \frac{n K^2}{\sigma^2}\right)^{1/\alpha}} }.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def:good_parameters of arXiv:2604.18558, 'Uniform analyticity of local observables in FK-percolation and analyticity of the Ising sp'] Define $\mathcal G_{\mathsf{FK}}$ to be the set of triplets $(d,p,q)$ such that the FK measures in finite volumes $\phi_{\Lambda_n, p, q}$ satisfy the following hypotheses. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Exponential weak mixing property}: for any $\alpha > 1$, there exists $c > 0$ such that for any $n \geq 0$ sufficiently large\footnote{$\mathrm{d}_{\mathsf{TV}}$ denotes the classical total variation distance between probability measures, and for any measure $\mu$, $\mu( \cdot_{|\Lambda_n})$ denotes the restriction of the measure $\mu$ to the box $\Lambda_n$.}, 
\[
\mathrm{d}_{\mathsf{TV}}( \phi^1_{\Lambda_{\alpha n}, p,q}( \cdot_{|\Lambda_n} ), \phi^0_{\Lambda_{\alpha n}, p,q}( \cdot_{|\Lambda_n} ) ) < \exp(-cn). 
\]
\item One of the two following conditions holds:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textit{Exponential decay}: for any $\alpha > 1$, there exists $c>0$ such that for any $n \geq 0$ large enough, 
\[
\phi^1_{\Lambda_{\alpha n, p ,q}}[A_n] < \exp(-cn),
\]
where $A_n$ is the event that $\Lambda_n$ contains a cluster of diameter greater than $n/100$.
\item \textit{Local uniqueness}: for any $\alpha > 1$, there exists $c>0$ such that for any $n \geq 0$ large enough, 
\[
\sup_\eta \phi^\eta_{\Lambda_{\alpha n, p ,q}}[U_n^c] < \exp(-cn),
\]
where the local uniqueness event $U_n$ is the event that $\Lambda_n $ contains a \emph{crossing} cluster and all the other clusters have diameter less than $n/100$, where a crossing cluster is a cluster that connects all the sides of the box $\Lambda_n$. The event $U_n^c$ is the complement of $U_n$.
In the last property, the supremum is taken over all the boundary conditions on the box $\Lambda_{\alpha n}$. 
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition def:good_parameters of arXiv:2604.18558

Its signs at0,1,250,1000 are respectively positive,negative,positive,negative, so the density has at least two peaks. Check: At1 the negative term is-1/40 and the positive term is less than19/40000. At250, writing A=62501 and B=562501, the derivative is -25/A^2+475/(A*B), positive because19*A>B. At1000 both displayed contributions are negative. The initial law has a single atom at its mode and a constant density to its right. Obstruction: This gives a concrete Cauchy counterexample, consistent with the known strong-unimodality criterion, but does not exclude every infinite-variance law.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0176-existence-of-nontrivial-freely-strongly-unimodal-laws
No independent review

body:
[Corollary corKM of arXiv:2607.14792, 'On the degree distribution of large tentacular Bienaymé--Galton--Watson trees'] We keep the notation and assumptions of Theorem (thKM of the paper). Let $r \geq 0$ be a fixed integer.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For $n$ large enough let $b_{n}^{(r)}$ be defined by
$$ b^{(r)}_{n} \frac{F'(b^{(r)}_{n})}{F(b^{(r)}_{n})}= \frac{k_{n}}{n-k_n-r}.$$ We have
$$b_{n} \underset{n \to \infty}{\sim} \frac{k_{n}}{n} \frac{\mathbb{P}(\eta=0)}{\mathbb{P}(\eta=1)} \qquad\textrm{and} \qquad \frac{b^{(r)}_{n}}{b_{n}}=1 + O \left(\frac{1}{n}\right).$$
\item[(ii)]  There exists $C>0$ such that, for $n$ large enough and uniformly for $-k_n\le k\le0$,
$$
\mathbb{P}(S_{n-k_n-r}=k_n+k)\le \frac{C}{\sqrt{k_n}}\frac{F(b_n)^{n-k_n-r}}{b_n^{k_n+k}}.
$$
\item[(iii)]  For every fixed $s \in \mathbb{Z}$ we have
$$
\mathbb{P}(S_{n-k_n-r}=k_n-s)  \underset{n \to \infty}{\sim}  \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi k_n}}\frac{F(b_n)^{n-k_n-r}}{b_n^{k_n-s}}.
$$
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma lem:tech2 of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Let $z_1 \neq z_2 \in \mathbb{C}$. Consider any simply-connected domain 
$D$ such that 
$\mathbb{D}(z_j, \varepsilon_j) \subseteq D$ and 
$\partial \mathbb{D}(z_j, \varepsilon_j) \cap \partial D \neq \emptyset$, for $j \in \{1,2\}$. 

Now consider any conformal map $\psi: D \to \mathbb{D}$ mapping a point in $\partial \mathbb{D}(z_1, \varepsilon_1) \cap \partial D$ to $-1$ and a point in $\partial \mathbb{D}(z_2, \varepsilon_2) \cap \partial D$ to $1$. 
Then the images $\psi(\mathbb{D}(z_1, \varepsilon_1))$ and 
$\psi(\mathbb{D}(z_2, \varepsilon_2))$ are included in disks 
$\mathbb{D}(-1, \delta_1)$ and $\mathbb{D}(1, \delta_2)$ respectively,
with crucially $\delta_1\delta_2 \leq C(\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2)^{1/2}$ for $C > 0$ depending only on $z_1, z_2$,
and not on $D$, $\varepsilon_1$, $\varepsilon_2$ or the choice of $\psi$.

Further, for some $\widetilde C > 0$, 
one can always find a conformal map such that 
$\delta_1 \leq \widetilde C(\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2)^{1/4}$ and 
$\delta_2 \leq \widetilde C(\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2)^{1/4}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:tech2 of arXiv:2604.15146

[Thm limiting profile_main thm of arXiv:2604.23890, 'The Cutoff Profile for Random Transpositions on Repeated Cards in the Full Range of Parame'] Let $n=ml$, such that $m,l\ge 2$, and $l=\omega(1)$. Suppose 
$$t=\frac n2\left(\log n-\frac 12\log l+c\right),$$ 
where $c\in \mathbb{R}$ is an absolute constant. Then, we have 
$$d_{TV}(\sim_l\backslash P_{n}^{*t},\sim_l\backslash U_{\mathfrak{S}_n})=\begin{cases}
2\Phi\left(\frac{\exp(-c)}{2}\right)-1+o(1) & m=\omega(1)\\
2\Phi\left(\sqrt{1-\frac 1m}\frac{\exp(-c)}{2}\right)-1+o(1) & m\ge 2 \text{ fixed}
\end{cases}.$$
Here, $\Phi(x):=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{-\infty}^x\exp(-y^2/2)dy$ denotes the cumulative distribution function of the normal distribution $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2505.21774, 'The friendship paradox for trees'] Consider a path of $n$ vertices.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] For $n \in \{1,2\}$, any vertex is neutral.
\item[(b)] For $n = 3$, two vertices (the end vertices) are positive  and one vertex (the middle vertex) is negative.
\item[(c)] For $n \geq 4$, two vertices (the end vertices) are positive, two vertices (the neighbours of the end vertices) are negative, and the rest $n-4$ vertices are neutral.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 2 (Quenched invariance principle) of arXiv:2604.21143, 'Quantitative homogenization for the critical long-range random conductance model'] Under Assumption~\textup{(U)}, let $g \in L^2(\Rd)$ be a nonnegative, compactly supported probability density.
		For each $\eps \in (0,1)$, let $X^\eps$ be the c\`adl\`ag process on $\eps\Zd$ with generator $\mathcal{L}^\eps$ and initial law $\P(X_0^\eps = x) = \eps^d g_\eps(x)$, where $g_\eps(x) \coloneqq \eps^{-d}\int_{x + [-\eps/2, \eps/2)^d} g(y) dy$.
		Let $W$ be a standard $d$-dimensional Brownian motion, let $X_0$ have law $g(x) dx$, independent of $W$, and set
		\[
		X_t \coloneqq X_0 + \sqrt{\frac{\E[\a(0,e_1)]}{d}} W_t\,.
		\]
		Then for $\P$-almost every realization of the conductances,
		\[
		X^\eps \Rightarrow X
		\qquad\text{in } D([0,\infty); \Rd)\,.
		\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Quenched invariance principle

body:
[Proposition 17 of arXiv:2605.30560, 'Projected McKean--Vlasov Dynamics for Entropic Weak Optimal Transport'] Let $p>d+2$, let $\P_0\in\Pc(\Xc\times\R^d)$, and let
\[
b:\R_+\times\Xc\times\R^d\longrightarrow\R^d
\]
be a Borel-measurable vector field. Assume that there exists a weak solution to
\[
dY_t
=
b(t,X,Y_t)\,dt+\sqrt{2} \,dB_t,
\qquad
(X,Y_0)\sim\P_0,
\qquad
(X, Y_0) \independent B,
\]
where $\independent$ denotes the indepenance. 
For $T>0$ and $R>0$, define
\begin{equation} 
C_1(R,T,b)
:=
\int_0^T
\left\{
\E\Big[
|b(t,X,Y_t)|^p\mathbf{1}_{\{|Y_t|\le R\}}
\Big]
+
\int_{\Xc} \int_{B(0,R)} |b(t,x,y)|^p\,dy\,\mu(dx)
\right\}
dt.
\end{equation}
Assume that $C_1(R,T,b)<\infty$ for every $R>0$. Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), ref=(\roman*)]
    \item 
    For every $t\in(0,T]$, the law
    \[
    \P_t:=\Lc(X,Y_t)
    \]
admits a density with respect to $\mu \otimes \mathrm{L}$,
    still denoted by $\tilde{\P}_{t,x}(y)$. 
    Moreover, for every $R>0$ and every
    $t\in(0,T]$, there exists a constant $K_{T,R}>0$ such that
    \begin{equation} 
    \big\|
    \tilde{\P}_t\,\mathbf{1}_{\{|y|\le R\}}
    \big\|_{\L^p(\mu\otimes \mathrm{L} ) }
    \le
    K_{T,R} \bigl(1+C_1(R,T,b)\bigr).
    \end{equation}

    \item 
    Assume furthermore that the second marginal of $\P_t$ is given by
    \[
    \Lc(Y_t)=\nu(dy)=e^{-V(y)} \,dy, \quad \forall \, t \in \R_+.
    \]
    For every bounded Borel function $\phi:\Xc\to\R$, define
    \[
    w_\phi(t,y):=\E[\phi(X)\mid Y_t=y].
    \]
    Equivalently, for $\nu$-a.e.\ $y$,
    \begin{equation} 
    w_\phi(t,y)
    =
    \int_{\Xc} \phi(x)\,\tilde{\P}_{t,x}(y)\,\mu(dx)\,e^{V(y)}.
    \end{equation}
    Then, for every $R>0$ and every $\delta>0$, there exist constants
    $\alpha,\beta,K>0$, depending only on $C_1(R,T,b)$, $R$, and $\delta$, such
    that for all $y,y'\in B(0,R)$ and all $t,t'\in[\delta,T]$ satisfying
    $|t-t'|\le1$,
    \begin{equation} 
    |w_\phi(t',y')-w_\phi(t,y)|
    \le
    K\|\phi\|_\infty
    \Big(
    |y-y'|^\alpha + |t-t'|^\beta
    \Big).
    \end{equation}

    \[

[Definition def:suspension-complex of arXiv:2608.27904, 'Instantons, indefinite 4-manifolds, and Dehn surgery'] Suppose we are given a cellular instanton $SO(3)$-flow category $\mathcal M$ and a collection of sections $\psi_{\theta \beta}$ as above. For each $\theta \in \mathfrak Z(\mathcal M)$, 
	let $\mathscr O(\underline \theta) $ be a copy of $S^2$ with its standard $SO(3)$-action and cellular structure. Let also $ \mathsf{orb}_S(\mathcal M)$ be the disjoint union of 
	the following sets:
	\[
	  \mathsf{orb}(\mathcal M) \setminus \mathfrak Z(\mathcal M),\hspace{1cm} \mathfrak Z(\mathcal M) ,\hspace{1cm} \underline{\mathfrak Z}(\mathcal M),
	\]
	where $\underline{\mathfrak Z}(\mathcal M)$ is another copy of $\mathfrak Z(\mathcal M)$ and consists of the elements $\underline \theta$ for any
	$\theta\in \mathfrak Z(\mathcal M)$. Let $| \cdot |_S : \mathsf{orb}_S(\mathcal M) \to \mathbb Z$ be defined as follows. For any $\alpha\in \mathsf{orb}(\mathcal M) \setminus \mathfrak Z(\mathcal M)$, we have $|\alpha|_S = |\alpha|$, and for any $\theta \in \mathfrak Z(\mathcal M)$ we have
	\[
	| \theta |_S=| \theta |-3,\hspace{1cm}| \underline \theta |_S=| \theta |-2.
	\]
	The \textit{geometric suspension complex} $S \widetilde C(\mathcal M)$ is the dg-module over $\Lambda(\chi_1, \chi_2)$ with the underlying module 
	\begin{equation}
	  \bigoplus_{\alpha \in \mathsf{orb}_S(\mathcal M)} C_*^{\rm cell}(\mathscr O(\alpha))[-|\alpha|_S]
	\end{equation}
	and the differential
	\[
	  \hspace{2cm} \widetilde d_S(e_\alpha) = \partial^{\rm cell}(e_\alpha) + \sum_{\beta\in \mathsf{orb}_S(\mathcal M)} {\mathfrak m}^S_{\alpha \beta}(e_\alpha),\hspace{1cm} 
	  \text{for all $e_\alpha\in C_*^{\rm cell}(\mathscr O(\alpha))$,}
	\]	
	where for $\alpha,\beta\in \mathsf{orb}(\mathcal M) \setminus \mathfrak Z(\mathcal M)$ and $\theta,\tau \in  \mathfrak Z(\mathcal M)$, we have
	\begin{align*}
	  &{\mathfrak m}^S_{\alpha \beta}={\mathfrak m}_{\alpha \beta},\hspace{1cm} {\mathfrak m}^S_{\underline{\theta}\beta}={\mathfrak b}_{\theta \beta},\hspace{1cm}{\mathfrak m}^S_{\theta\beta}={\mathfrak z}_{\theta \beta},\\
	  &{\mathfrak m}^S_{\alpha \underline{\tau}}=\iota{\mathfrak m}_{\alpha \tau},\hspace{0.9cm}{\mathfrak m}^S_{\underline{\theta}\underline{\tau}}=\iota{\mathfrak b}_{\theta \tau},\hspace{0.9cm}{\mathfrak m}^S_{\theta\underline{\tau}}=\iota{\mathfrak z}_{\theta \tau},\\
	  &{\mathfrak m}^S_{\alpha {\tau}}=0,\hspace{1.52cm}{\mathfrak m}^S_{\underline{\theta}{\tau}}=\pi\delta_{\theta\tau},\hspace{0.83cm}{\mathfrak m}^S_{\theta{\tau}}=0. 
	\end{align*}	
	In the last row above, $\delta_{\theta\tau}$ is the identity map of $C_*^{\rm cell}(S^2)$ if $\theta=\tau$ and is zero otherwise.
title: Definition def:suspension-complex of arXiv:2608.27904

body:
Consider i.i.d. first-passage percolation on Z^d with edge-weight law F supported on [0, infinity). Let Y be the minimum of 2d independent copies of tau_e - the smallest weight among the edges at a vertex. If E[Y] < infinity then the limit mu(e_1) = lim_{n -> infinity} T(0, n e_1)/n exists almost surely and in L^1 and is a deterministic constant in [0, infinity), and the same holds along every lattice direction, defining mu on Z^d and by homogeneity and convexity on all of R^d, invariant under the symmetries of the lattice; mu is either identically 0 or a genuine norm. Three companion facts, each with its own status. (i) WITHOUT the moment condition the limit still exists IN PROBABILITY, by Kesten, Cox-Durrett and Wierman, and when the moment condition does hold the two limits agree. (ii) 0 <= mu(e_1) <= E[tau_e], the upper bound by taking the direct path and applying the law of large numbers - so the finiteness of E[tau_e] gives the bound but is NOT needed for existence. (iii) POSITIVITY is a separate theorem and is not part of this one: mu(e_1) > 0 IF AND ONLY IF F(0) < p_c(d), the bond percolation threshold, and mu(e_1) > 0 if and only if mu(x) > 0 for every nonzero x. When F(0) >= p_c the zero-weight edges percolate, one can travel arbitrarily far in time o(n), and mu vanishes identically. [Kesten, Aspects of First Passage Percolation, Theorems 2.18 and 6.1; verified against Auffinger, Damron and Hanson, 50 Years of First-Passage Percolation, Section 2.1]
i.i.d. nonnegative edge weights on the nearest-neighbour edges of Z^d, d >= 2
E[min of 2d independent copies of tau_e] < infinity (implied by E[tau_e] < infinity); without it the limit exists only in probability
positivity of mu is NOT part of this theorem and holds exactly when F(0) < p_c

[Theorem eq:main of arXiv:2512.19897, 'On the convoy of the ASEP speed process'] Let $0<q<1$ and $x\in[0,1]$. Consider the Markov chain $\left(Q_i\right)_{i\ge1}$ on $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ with initial law
\[
\mathbb{P}\left(Q_1=k\right)=\pi_k=\frac{\left(q;q\right)_\infty}{\left(q;q\right)_k}q^k,
\]
and one-step transition probabilities (independent of $i$), for $k\ge0$,
    \[
    P\left(k,k+1\right)=x\left(1-x\right),\qquad
    P\left(k,k-1\right)=x\left(1-x\right)\left(1-q^k\right),\qquad
    P\left(k,k\right)=1-x\left(1-x\right)\bigl(2-q^k\bigr),
    \]
with the convention $P\left(0,-1\right)=0$. We write
    \[
    P\left(a,b\right):=\mathbb{P}\bigl(Q_{i+1}=b\big|Q_i=a\bigr)
    \]
    for the one-step transition probability, which does not depend on $i$. 
    Fix $n\ge1$ and a sequence $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\{-1,0,1\}$, and set $s:=\sum_{i=1}^n s_i$. Then
        \begin{equation}    \sum_{k\ge0}\mathbb{P}\left(Q_1=k,Q_2=k+s_1,\dots,Q_{n+1}=k+s\right) = q^{-s}\sum_{m\ge0}\mathbb{P}\left(Q_1=m,Q_2=m-s_n,\dots,Q_{n+1}=m-s\right).
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem eq:main of arXiv:2512.19897

d = 2
i.i.d. passage times with E[tau(e)^2] < infinity and var(tau(e)) > 0
lambda := inf{x : P(tau(e) <= x) > 0}
either (lambda = 0 and P(tau(e) = 0) < p_c(d)) or (lambda > 0 and P(tau(e) = lambda) < p_c^dir(d))
no curvature hypothesis and no direction hypothesis: B may depend on the law but not on xhat

THE ATOM CONDITION IS THE REAL HYPOTHESIS, AND IT IS NOT IMPLIED BY BOUNDED WEIGHTS. A weight law supported in [a,b] with a > 0 has lambda = a, so the theorem demands P(tau_e = a) < p_c^dir - an explicit threshold check against the DIRECTED critical probability, not the undirected one. Continuous laws satisfy it trivially (atom mass 0); Bernoulli-type or atom-at-minimum laws do not get it for free. Any campaign lane that lists 'Newman-Piza Var >= c log n' beside 'bounded i.i.d. edge weights' has an unchecked hypothesis.
NUMBERING TRAP: in Newman-Piza this is THEOREM 2. The Auffinger-Damron-Hanson survey states it as its Theorem 3.7 and web digests then attribute 'Theorem 3.7' to the 1995 paper. Cite it as 'NP95 Theorem 2 (= ADH survey Thm 3.7)'.
SCOPE, AND THE POLYNOMIAL BOUNDS THAT DO NOT CONTRADICT IT: 'state of the art' here means the point-to-point passage time T(0,nx), unconditionally. Polynomial variance lower bounds DO exist in planar first-passage percolation, but for the minimal left-right CROSSING of a square and under an unproven curvature assumption - see the Damron-Houdre-Ozdemir and Dembin-Elboim nodes. Different observable, extra hypothesis; quoting them as improvements on this theorem is wrong.
CORROBORATED BY THE PEOPLE WHO TRIED: Damron, Hanson, Houdre and Xu write in the abstract of arXiv:1810.08270 that 'the best lower bounds available are (only in two dimensions) of order log ||x||. This result was found in the '90s and there has not been any improvement since.'
METHOD: a martingale/spiral-filtration expansion of Var T that lower-bounds the variance by C sum_i P(F_i)^2, F_i the event that edge e_i lies on a geodesic; the sum is then replaced by partial sums of the expected number of minimizing edges, because the geodesic overlap itself is hard to control. The survey records the open question that would upgrade the bound: show that in d = 2 the expected overlap of two independently sampled geodesics from 0 to nx is at least n^a for some a > 0.
SOURCE: Newman, C. M. and Piza, M. (1995), 'Divergence of shape fluctuations in two dimensions', Ann. Probab. 23, 977-1005. Statement read verbatim in Auffinger-Damron-Hanson, '50 years of first passage percolation', arXiv:1511.03262v2 (AMS University Lecture Series 68, 2017), theorem 'thm:NP', tex lines 1350-1364.
INDEPENDENT CROSS-CHECK, and it agrees: the campaign's own fire-85 file probability_open_problem_campaign_2026_08_09/problem/NP95_TRANSCRIPTION_20260812.md transcribes the same theorem from the journal PDF (p. 984, displays 2.11-2.14) and matches the survey rendering on every hypothesis and on the conclusion. [Lemma lem:radial of arXiv:2606.21591, '\textbf{Equal probabilities maximize the expected deficit\\ in the siblings of the coupon '] For every $\theta\in(0,1]$,
\begin{equation}
\psi'(\theta)=-\frac{1}{N}\int_0^\infty \frac{t^{\,j}}{(j-1)!}\,
\Phi(t)\,W(t)^2\,\Cov_{w_t}\!\bigl(q,\;q^{\,j-1}\bigr)\,dt,
\end{equation}
where, for each $t>0$, the weights $w_{t,a}=r(q_a t)>0$ have total mass
$W(t)=\sum_{a=1}^N w_{t,a}$, and $\Cov_{w_t}$ denotes covariance with respect to the
probability vector $\bigl(w_{t,a}/W(t)\bigr)_{a=1}^N$:
\[
\Cov_{w_t}(q,q^{j-1})
=\sum_a\frac{w_{t,a}}{W(t)}\,q_a^{\,j}
-\Bigl(\sum_a\frac{w_{t,a}}{W(t)}\,q_a\Bigr)
 \Bigl(\sum_a\frac{w_{t,a}}{W(t)}\,q_a^{\,j-1}\Bigr).
\]

[Corollary cor:lattice-transfer of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Let $G$ be any nontrivial torsion-free abelian group.  For all $h,k\geq1$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal R_G(h,k)=\mathcal R(h,k).
\end{equation}
Consequently the spectrum-only conclusions
(equation eq:endpoint-local of the paper), (equation eq:ambient-exponent of the paper), and
(equation eq:localmain of the paper), together with the four-point positive-density
conclusion, hold with $\mathcal R$ replaced by $\mathcal R_G$.  The diameter-filtered
integer-witness assertion (equation eq:quantmain of the paper) is not asserted for an
abstract group $G$.  In particular,
$|\mathcal R_G(h,k)|=h^{k-1+o_k(1)}$ for every fixed $k\geq4$, and
$|\mathcal R_G(h,4)|=\Theta(h^3)$ with positive lower density.

Then f is in L^1, integral |f_n - f| dmu -> 0, and in particular integral f_n dmu -> integral f dmu. The classical dominated convergence theorem is the case g_n = g constant in n. The hypothesis that the integrals of the dominators CONVERGE (not merely that the dominators converge pointwise) is essential: with g_n = 1_{[n,n+1]} on R one has g_n -> 0 = g pointwise, but integral g_n = 1 does not converge to integral g = 0, and taking f_n = g_n shows the conclusion fails. body: [Proposition 12 of arXiv:2604.01852, 'The on/off Brownian snake'] Let $(E',d')$ be a complete and separable metric space and $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P})$ a probability space on which we have random variables $\mathcal{Q}_t: \Omega \rightarrow E'$, $t \geq 0$. Suppose further that there is another probability space $(\Omega', \mathcal{F}', \mathbb{P}')$ on which random variables $\mathcal{Q}'_t: \Omega' \rightarrow E'$ form a path-continuous process with the same finite-dimensional distributions as $\mathcal{Q} = (\mathcal{Q}_t, t \geq 0)$. Then $(\mathcal{Q}_t, t \geq 0)$ has a modification $(\Tilde{\mathcal{Q}}_t, t \geq 0)$ with continuous paths, i.e. for each fixed $t \geq 0$ we have $\mathbb{P}(\Tilde{\mathcal{Q}}_t = \mathcal{Q}_t) = 1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

  $\{\sigma_{n-1}<\infty\}$, we define 
  $\sigma_n:=\inf\{l>\sigma_{n-1}:X_l\neq X_{\sigma_{n-1}}\}$ to be the index
  of the next jump to a different location. 
  The process with self-loops removed is defined by 
  $(X^{\neq},T^{\neq})=(X^{\neq}_n,T^{\neq}_n)_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}:=(X_{\sigma_n},\sum_{l=\sigma_n}^{\sigma_{n+1}-1}T_l)_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}$
  on the event $\{\sigma_n<\infty\text{ for all }n\in{\mathbb N}\}$. 

  Let $\emptyset\neq J\subseteq\Lambda$. We set recursively $\tau_0=0$, 
  $\tau_n=\inf\{ l>\tau_{n-1}: X_l\in J\}$
  for $n\in{\mathbb N}$. In other words, on the event $\{X_0\in J\}$, 
  $\tau_n$ denotes the number of jumps up to the $n$-th return to $J$. 
  The restriction of the process to $J$ is defined
  on the event $\{\tau_n<\infty\text{ for all }n\in{\mathbb N}\}$ by
  $(X^J,T^J)=(X_n^J,T_n^J)_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}:=(X_{\tau_n},T_{\tau_n})_{n\in{\mathbb N}_0}$.

  The notation $(X^{J\neq},T^{J\neq})$ means that both operations have
  been applied to the process $(X,T)$, first the restriction to $J$ and
  then self-loop removal.
title: Removal of self-loops and restriction to a subset: process

body:
[Corollary col: k simplex density of arXiv:2505.09839, '\textbf{Density Frankl–Rödl on the Sphere}'] Fix any \( r \in \left(-\frac{1}{k - 1}, 1\right) \). For any measurable set \( A \subseteq \mathbb{S}^{n-1} \) with \( \sigma(A) \geq \omega_{k,r}(n^{-\epsilon_{k,r}}) \), the probability that a uniformly random tuple \( (x_1, \dots, x_k) \in \Delta_k(n, r) \) lies entirely in \( A \) satisfies
\[
\mathop{\bf Pr\/}_{(x_1, \dots, x_k) \in \Delta_k(n, r)}(x_1 \in A, \dots, x_k \in A) \geq \Omega_{k,r}(\sigma(A)^{C_{k,r}}),
\]
as \( n \to \infty \). The constants \( C_{k,r},\ \epsilon_{k,r} \) are given by
\[
C_{k,r} = \sum_{i = 1}^{k - 1} \frac{2}{1 - |c_i|} \prod_{j = 1}^{i - 1} \frac{1 + |c_j|}{1 - |c_j|}
\qquad
\epsilon_{k,r}=\prod_{i=1}^{k-1}\frac{1-|c_i|}{1+|c_i|},
\]
where
\[
c_i = \frac{r}{1 + (i - 1)r}, \quad \text{for } i = 1, \dots, k - 1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary col: k simplex density of arXiv:2505.09839

For probability measures P and Q on one space, TV(P, Q) = sup_A |P(A) - Q(A)| and D = D(P || Q) is the Kullback-Leibler divergence in nats (+infinity unless P << Q). Then TV(P, Q) <= min(sqrt(D/2), sqrt(1 - exp(-D))). The two bounds cross at the unique positive root D* = 1.59362426004004... of D/2 = 1 - exp(-D): Pinsker's bound is the smaller for 0 < D < D* and the Bretagnolle-Huber bound for D > D*.
P and Q are probability measures on one measurable space

\lim_{t\to+\infty}\int_{ D_+(\mathbb{T})}\tilde {\mathcal
    U}_t^VFd\mu= \int_{  D_+(\mathbb{T})}F d\pi_\infty .
\end{equation}
The measure $\pi_\infty$ is invariant under  $\big(\tilde
\mathcal{U}^V_t\big)$.

In addition,  for any $\delta>0$, $p\in[1,+\infty)$
there exist constants $C,\lambda>0$, depending only on
$\|V\|_{L^2(\mathbb{T})}$, $\delta$ and $p$,
such that
\begin{equation}

\sup_{\rho_1,\rho_2\in
  D_+(\mathbb{T})}\mathbf{E}\big\|\rho^V(t;\rho_1)-\rho^V(t;\rho_2)\big\|^p_\infty\leq
C e^{-\lambda t},\quad t\ge \delta.
\end{equation}
 

Furthermore,    there exists $C>0$, depending
only on $\|V\|_{L^2(\mathbb{T})}$, $\delta$ and $p$ such that  
\begin{equation}

\sup_{t\ge \delta,\,{\mu\in {\mathcal
    M}_1(\mathbb{T})}}\mathbf{E}_{\mu}\Big[{\|\rho^V(t;\mu)\|_\infty^p+\|\rho^V(t;\mu)^{-1}\|_\infty^{p}}\Big]\le C.
\end{equation}
In  consequence, for any $p\ge1$,
\begin{equation}

\int_{ D_+(\mathbb{T})}\big(\|\rho\|^p_\infty +{\|\rho^{-1}\|^{p}_\infty}\big) \pi_\infty (d\rho)<+\infty.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 44 (Convergence after $n(x)$ steps, stated with a reference measure) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Let $(\XX,\XXA)$ be a measurable space and $\lambda$ a $\sigma$-finite measure on
it. Let $p : \XX \to [0,\infty)$ be measurable with $\int_{\XX} p \dd\lambda = 1$, let
$\tau : \XX\times\XX \to [0,\infty)$ be $\XXA\otimes\XXA$-measurable with
$\int_{\XX} \tau(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y) = 1$ for every $x \in \XX$, and define
\[
  \pi(A) := \int_{A} p \dd\lambda, \qquad T(A \mid x) := \int_{A}\tau(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y)
  \qquad (A \in \XXA,\ x \in \XX),
\]
and $\Xp := \{p > 0\} \in \XXA$. Let $\tau_{n} : \XX\times\XX \to [0,\infty)$ be given
by the Chapman--Kolmogorov recursion
\[
  \tau_{1} := \tau, \qquad
  \tau_{n+1}(y \mid x) := \int_{\XX} \tau_{n}(y \mid z)\,\tau(z \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd z)
  \qquad (n \in \N).
\]
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep,topsep=3pt]
  \item \emph{(invariance)} $\displaystyle\int_{\XX} \tau(y \mid x)\,p(x)\,\lambda(\dd x) = p(y)$ for $\lambda$-almost every $y \in \XX$;
  \item \emph{(eventual positivity)} for every $x \in \XX$ there is a number $n \in \N$ with
        \[
          \lambda\bigl(\{ y \in \XX\setminus\Xp : \tau_{n}(y \mid x) > 0 \}\bigr) = 0
          \qquad\text{and}\qquad
          \lambda\bigl(\{ y \in \Xp : \tau_{n}(y \mid x) = 0 \}\bigr) = 0 .
        \]
\end{enumerate}
Then $\pi$ is the unique invariant probability measure of $T$, and
$\tv{T^{n}\circ\mu - \pi} \to 0$ for every $\mu \in \Prob$.

	Let $G$ be a one-ended torsion-free hyperbolic group with 1 dimensional boundary, and trivial JSJ decomposition. Then ${\partial G}$ is exactly one of the following:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item a circle $S^1$,
		\item  a Sierpinski carpet
		\item  a Menger curve.
	\end{enumerate}
	If $G$ does not split over ${\mathbb Z}$, ${\partial G}$ is either  a Sierpinski carpet or  a Menger curve. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Consequently, for $S=L$ {\rm(}respectively, $S=R${\rm)}, the map $\vartheta \mapsto I^{S,\mathfrak h}_\vartheta(s)$ is the corresponding right-continuous {\rm(}respectively, left-continuous{\rm)} generalized inverse.

body:
[Lem 25 of arXiv:2506.17979, '\large\bf A remark on subharmonicity for symmetric Dirichlet forms'] We consider a function $g\in L^1(E;{\m})$ with $0<g\leq 1$ ${\m}$-a.e.~on $E$. Let $\check{\bf X}$ be the time changed process  by $A_t^g$ and 
 $(\check{\mathscr{E}},D(\check{\mathscr{E}}))$ on $L^2(E;g{\m})$ the  Dirichlet form associated with $\check{\bf X}$.   
 The following hold. 
 \begin{enumerate}
 \item[\rm(1)] For $u\in D(\mathscr{E})_{e,\loc}$ {\rm(}resp.~$u\in D(\mathscr{E})_{e,\loc}^{\dag}$, $u\in D(\mathscr{E})_{e,\loc}^{\diamond}${\rm)}, there exists 
 $g\in L^1(E;{\m})$ satisfying $0<g\leq 1$ ${\m}$-a.e.~such that 
 $u\in D(\check{\mathscr{E}})_{\loc}$ {\rm(}resp.~$u\in D(\check{\mathscr{E}})_{\loc}^{\dag}$, $u\in D(\check{\mathscr{E}})_{\loc}^{\diamond}${\rm)} holds for the Dirichlet form $(\check{\mathscr{E}}, D(\check{\mathscr{E}}))$ on $L^2(E;g{\m})$ associated with the time changed process $\check{\bf X}$. In particular, for $u\in D(\mathscr{E})_{e,\loc}^{\diamond}$, $\mathscr{E}$-subharmonicity of $u$ in $D$ is equivalent to the 
 $\check{\mathscr{E}}$-subharmonicity of $u$ in $D$.  
 \item[\rm(2)] For a nearly Borel $\overline{\R}$-valued function $u$, 
 the subharmonicity of $u$ in $D$ with respect to ${\bf X}$ is equivalent to 
 the subharmonicity of $u$ in $D$ with respect to $\check{\bf X}$.
 \item[\rm(3)] For a nearly Borel $\overline{\R}$-valued function $u$, 
 the subharmonicity of $u$ in $D$ in the weak sense with respect to ${\bf X}$ is equivalent to  the subharmonicity of $u$ in $D$ in the weak sense with respect to $\check{\bf X}$.
 \end{enumerate}

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.03728, 'Moments for self-normalized partial sums'] We consider a \regvary\ stationary \seq\ of random variables $(X_t)$ with tail index $\a<2$. For these \seq s we study the joint \con\ of sums, $\ell^p$-type moduli and maxima. We focus on ratio statistics, including the studentized sums and sums normalized by the corresponding maxima, and study the existence of moments for the limit ratios. We consider particular examples of processes $(X_t)$ whose limit ratios possess all moments. But, in contrast to the latter situation, there also exist \seq s $(X_t)$ where certain moments of the limit ratio are infinite. This phenomenon results from extremal clusters in the \seq .
title: Abstract of arXiv:2609.03728: Moments for self-normalized partial sums

[Lemma 115 (Exhaustion of the three-frequency configurations) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Assume
$N_0=\langle\xi\rangle$, $N_1=\langle\eta\rangle$, and
$N_2=\langle\xi-\eta\rangle$ are all at least two.  After enlarging the
fixed comparability constants, the dyadic frequency space is the union of the
following four regions, with only finite overlap:
\begin{align*}
 &N_0\sim N_1\sim N_2,\\
 &N_0\sim N_2\gg N_1,\\
 &N_0\sim N_1\gg N_2,\\
 &N_1\sim N_2\gg N_0.
\end{align*}
In the first three regions the sublevel estimates of
\cref{lem:continuous-phase-layers} apply to every sign vector
$\bm\eps\in\{\pm1\}^3$.  In the last region the pointwise estimate of
\cref{lem:first-picard-low-output-gap} applies to every sign vector.

[Proposition prop:finite-time-concentration-scale of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] Assume that $(\zeta(z))_{z\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ are i.i.d. For each $x$ and
		$t$, the map $\zeta\mapsto u_t(x)$ is convex and satisfies
		\[
			|u_t(x;\zeta)-u_t(x;\eta)|
			\leq
			\left(\sum_{z\in\mathbb{Z}^d}g_t(x,z)^2\right)^{1/2}
			\|\zeta-\eta\|_{\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^d)}\, .
		\]
		For every $p\geq2$ with $\mathbb{E}|\zeta(0)|^p<\infty$ there is
		$C=C(p,\mathcal L(\zeta(0)))<\infty$ such that
		\[
			\mathbb{E}\bigl|u_t(x)-\mathbb{E} u_t(x)\bigr|^p
			\leq C \Var(V_t(0))^{p/2}\, .
		\]
		In particular, if $\Var(\zeta(0))<\infty$, then
		$\Var(u_t(x))\leq C\Var(V_t(0))$.
		If $0<\Var(\zeta(0))<\infty$, then, for every $m,n\geq0$ and
		$x,y\in\mathbb{Z}^d$,
		\begin{equation}
			0\leq\Cov(u_n(x),u_m(y))
			\leq
			2\Var(\zeta(0))
			\sum_{z\in\mathbb{Z}^d}g_n(x,z)g_m(y,z)\, .
		\end{equation}

[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2609.01574, 'A linear bound for Fujita's freeness conjecture'] Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a pair with $X$ smooth projective. Assume that $(X,\Delta)$ is log canonical near a closed point $x$ and is not klt at $x$, and let $W:=W_x(X,\Delta)$. Assume that $d:=\dim W\geq2$, and let $\nu\colon Z=W^\nu\to W$ be the normalization. Let $\mathcal I_x\subset\mathcal O_Z$ be the ideal sheaf of $x$, and let $f\colon Y\to Z$ be its normalized blow-up. Write $\mathcal I_x\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_Y(-E)$ and $H:=-E$. Let $\mathbf B$ be the discriminant $b$-divisor from Proposition~\ref{prop:adjunction-data} for the subadjunction of $(X,\Delta)$ along $W$, and let $B_Y$ be the trace of $\mathbf B$ on $Y$. Then
\[
 -\sum_F\mult_F B_Y\bigl(F\cdot H^{d-1}\bigr)
 \leq K_Y\cdot H^{d-1},
\]
where the sum runs over the prime components of $E$.

[Proposition prop:uniform-ranges of arXiv:2609.02544, 'A finiteness theorem for geodesic Leech wheels'] In a geodesic Leech wheel $W_{m+1}$ with $h$ large spokes, the following hold.

body: [Lemma lemma cv CLE in the rectangles of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple C'] On the event that there is a loop of $\Gamma$ crossing $A_{s,t}(z)$ and that there are $k\ge 1$ conformal rectangles $R_1, \ldots, R_k$, for all $j \in [1, k]_\BZ$, let $\Gamma'_{R^n_j}$ be the non-nested $\CLE_{\kappa'}$ associated with the $\cwBCLE_{\kappa^\prime}(0)$/$\ccwBCLE_\kappa(-\kappa/2)$ iteration construction (see~(A025 of the paper)) in the connected component of the unexplored region $R^n_j$ containing $R_j$. For all $x\in R_j \cap \BQ^2$, consider the loop $\SCL_j^n(x)$ of $\Gamma'_{R^n_j}$ surrounding $x$. Then, for all simply connected open subset $U \subset R_j$ such that $\overline{U} \subset R_j$ there exists a sequence $(U_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of simply connected open subsets such that $\overline{U_n} \to \overline{U}$ a.s.\@ in the Hausdorff topology, $U_n \to U$ a.s.\@ in the Carathéodory sense, and such that the conditional laws given $R^n_j$ of the $\overline{U_n}\cap \SCL^n_j(x)$'s for $x\in R_j \cap \BQ^2$ converge a.s.\ weakly, in the Hausdorff topology, to the conditional law given $R_j$ of the $\overline{U} \cap \SCL_j(x)$'s for $x \in R_j \cap \BQ^2$, where the $\SCL_j(x)$'s are the loops of a $\CLE_{\kappa'}$ in $R_j$.

[Proposition 40 of arXiv:2608.27630, 'Oriented planar maps and \\ annular mating of trees'] Let $h^\rmS$ be the field as above and $\theta\in \bbR$ such that $\lambda'-\chi\pi+\theta\chi\in(-\lambda,\lambda)$. Let $x\in\bbR$. There exists a unique coupling between $(h^\rmS,\eta)$ where $\eta$ is a curve starting from $x$,  and stopped until either hitting $\bbR+i\tau$ or one of its translates $\eta+k$ where $k\in\bbZ$, such that the following holds:
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item For each stopping time $\sigma$ of $\eta$ before its duration, $\eta([0,\sigma])$ is a local set of $h^\rmS$, in the sense that the conditional law of $h^\rmS$ given $\eta|_{[0,\sigma]}$ has the following description. Let $\cS_{\eta,\sigma} = \cS_\tau\backslash \cup_{k\in\bbZ}(k+\eta([0,\sigma]))$, and $\cA_{\eta,\sigma}$ be the annulus such that there is a conformal map $\varphi_{\eta,\sigma}$ with $\cA_{\eta,\sigma} = p\circ\varphi_{\eta,\sigma}\circ \cS_{\eta,\sigma}$. Let $\mathfrak{h}_{\eta,\sigma}$ be the harmonic function on $\cS_{\eta,\sigma}$ whose boundary values agrees with $h^\rmS$ on $\partial\cS_\tau$ and is given by the flow line boundary conditions on $ \cup_{k\in\bbZ}(k+\eta([0,\sigma]))$ as in Figure~\ref{fig: flow line boundary data} and~\cite[Figure 1.10]{ImagGeo1}. Then $h^\rmS|_{\cS_{\eta,\sigma}} =  {h}_{\eta,\sigma}\circ p\circ \varphi_{\eta,\sigma} + \mathfrak{h}_{\eta,\sigma}$, where ${h}_{\eta,\sigma}$ is a zero boundary GFF in $\cA_{\eta,\sigma}$ independent from $\mathfrak{h}_{\eta,\sigma}$.
        \item The curve $\eta$ is measurable with respect to $h^\rmS$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[1 14 of arXiv:2607.12303, 'Marginal Stationary Distributions and Convergence Rates of Higher Order Markov Chains'] Suppose that the transition tensor ${\cal P}$ of  an $(m-1)$th order Markov chain $\{X_t\}_{t=1}^{\infty}$ on state space
$S$ is positive, that is, ${\cal P}>0$. Let $Q$ be the transition matrix of its reduced first order chain.  Then the $(m-1)$th power of $Q$ is a positive matrix,  that is,  
$$
Q^{m-1} >0.
$$
This implies that $Q$ itself is regular. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 6 of arXiv:2607.06242, 'Exponential mixing and Freidlin--Wentzell large deviation principle for Markov cocycles'] Let $(\Sigma,\theta,m)$ be an ergodic measure preserving dynamical system. Suppose that $A,F>0$ are measurable, $\log A\in L^1, \log^+F\in L^1$, and 
      \[\int_\Sigma \log A(\s)m(d\s)<\log q\]
      for some $q\in(0,1)$. Then
      \[N(\sigma):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}q^{-(n+1)}
      F(\theta^n\sigma)\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}A(\theta^j\sigma)\]
      is finite for \(m\)-a.e. $\sigma$ and satisfies
      \[qN(\sigma)=F(\sigma)+A(\sigma)N(\theta\sigma).\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop p:markov-property-CDRP of arXiv:2607.18194, 'Temperature chaos in directed polymers'] {AJRS22}}]
    Fix $(s,x;t,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{4}_{\uparrow}$ and fix $s',t'$ satisfying $s<s'<t'<t$.
    Define the following $\sigma$-algebras on path space $C([s,t])$:
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal{G}_{s,s'} \coloneqq  \sigma\left(
            X|_{[s,s']}:X\in C([s,t])
        \right),
        \qquad
        \mathcal{G}_{t',t} \coloneqq  \sigma\left(
            X|_{[t',t]}:X\in C([s,t])
        \right).
    \end{align*}
    Then almost surely,
    for all bounded  measurable functions $F:C([s',t'])\to\mathbb{R}$,  we have
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{E}^\xi_{1,(s,x),(t,y)}\left[
            F(X|_{[s',t']})\,\middle|\,\mathcal{G}_{s,s'},\, \mathcal{G}_{t',t}
        \right]
        &=
        \mathbb{E}^\xi_{1,(s',X(s')), (t', X(t'))}\left[
            F(X)
        \right]
        \qquad\quad
        \textup{$\mathbb{P}^\xi_{1,(s,x),(t,y)}$-a.s.,}
    \end{align*}

Own work, proof (unaudited), W719-T295-C006 v1. Standard-conditioning specialization for the Target 3 obstruction; neither novelty nor escape is asserted. Let d>=3, m>=1, eta>0, A have iid real N(0,1) entries, x_* a deterministic unit signal, and independently x0~N(0,I_d/d). For f(x)=(1/(4m)) sum_i ((a_i^T x)^2-(a_i^T x_*)^2)^2 run unmodified GD. Put e1=x_*, q0=<e1,x0>, rho0=||x0-q0*e1||, e2=(x0-q0*e1)/rho0, E an orthonormal basis of their perpendicular space, g=A*e1, h=A*e2, B=A*E, zt=A*xt, vt=zt*(zt^2-g^2) coordinatewise, qt=<e1,xt>, pt=<e2,xt>. Excluding null events rho0*||v0||*||B^T v0||=0, define u=v0/||v0||, P=I-u*u^T, w=B^T*u, W=||w||^2, Q=I-w*w^T/W, b=B*w, r=P*b, a=P*v1, L=||a||^2, nu=Q*B^T*v1, gamma=eta*||v0||/m, kappa=-gamma-(eta/m)*(u^T*v1+r^T*v1/W). Observe in order w, then b (equivalently z1), then nu. Let F2=sigma(x0,g,h,w,b), F3=sigma(F2,nu). Conditional on F2, nu has Gaussian law with covariance L*Q. If L>0, B|F3 has mean M3=u*w^T+r*w^T/W+a*nu^T/L and residual law (P-a*a^T/L)*Z*Q for a fresh standard Gaussian matrix Z. Consequently z2|F3 is Gaussian with mean q2*g+p2*h+kappa*b-eta*||nu||^2*a/(m*L) and covariance (eta^2*||nu||^2/m^2)*(P-a*a^T/L). The conditional law of ||nu||^2/L given F2 is chi-square with d-3 degrees of freedom, including the point mass at zero for d=3. If L=0, nu=0 and z2=q2*g+p2*h+kappa*b is already F2-measurable. Thus the next response is in the adaptively chosen direction P*v1; it cannot be omitted merely by citing fresh Gaussian noise. Bounds on accumulated responses and initial-scale overlap fluctuations remain open.

L=0 branch handled separately without division

		\item Assuming that $\lVert g \rVert_m \le \gamma m$ for any $m \in {\mathbb N}$ and some constant $\gamma > 0$, it holds that
		\[
		\int \exp\Big\{ \frac{|g|}{2\gamma e}\Big\} d\mu \le 2.

		\item Assume that for some finite index set $\mathcal{J}$ and every $j \in \mathcal{J}$ there are constants $C_j > 0$ and real numbers $p_j > 0$, $r_0 \ge 1$ such that for any $r \ge r_0$

		\]
		for any $t \ge 0$.
	\end{enumerate}

[Proposition 65 (Sharp denominator growth) of arXiv:2608.29585, '2608.29585'] For every $d\ge0$, the polynomials
$\gamma_0^{4_1},\ldots,\gamma_d^{4_1}$ form an $R$-basis of the $R$-module of
polynomials in $\Bbbk[Y]$ of degree at most $d$ that take values in $R$
at every node
$Y=Q^n$, $n\ge2$.  The leading coefficient of $\gamma_k^{4_1}(Y)$ is
\begin{equation}
 \frac{(-1)^kQ^{k(k-3)/2}}{(Q;Q)_k}.
\end{equation}
In particular, it has a pole of order $k$ along $Q=1$, so the
quantum-factorial denominator length is unbounded.

body:
[Definition RP of arXiv:2411.06089, '{\Large \bf Averaging principle for semilinear slow-fast rough partial differential equati'] {\rm (Rough Path)} For $\gamma \in (1/3, 1/2]$, a pair $\mathbf{X} =(X, X^2)$ is called $\gamma$-H\"{o}lder rough path $($over $\mathbb R^d)$.
	 If $X \in C^\gamma ([0,T]; \mathbb R^d)$, $X^2 \in C_2^{2\gamma}([0,T]; \mathbb R^d \otimes \mathbb R^d)$ and satisfy Chen's relation
	 \begin{equation}
	 	X^2_{t,s}-X^2_{t,u}-X^2_{u,s}= \delta X_{t,u} \otimes \delta X_{u,s}, ~~\text{for all}~~0\leq s \leq u \leq t \leq T.
	 \end{equation}
Denote by $ \mathscr{C}^\gamma ([0,T]; \mathbb R^d)$ the space of $\gamma$-H\"{o}lder rough paths
and the distance between two $ \gamma$-H\"{o}lder rough paths $\mathbf X=(X, X^2)$ and $\widetilde{\mathbf X}=(\widetilde{X}, \widetilde{X}^2)$ is defined by
$$d_\gamma(\mathbf X,\widetilde{\mathbf X})=|X-\widetilde{X}|_\gamma +|X^2-\widetilde{X}^2|_{2\gamma}.$$
We write $d_\gamma(\mathbf X)=d_\gamma(0, \mathbf X)$ for simplicity.
title: Definition RP of arXiv:2411.06089

[Thm corners_nomarkov_intro of arXiv:2412.05999, 'Non-Archimedean GUE corners and Hecke modules'] Let $t=1/q$, and let $n\ge 1$ be an integer.
\begin{enumerate}[left=0pt]
\item(Alternating case) Let $A_{2n}$ be a random element of $\Alt_{2n}(\mathfrak{o})$ with above-diagonal entries $a_{i,j}, 1 \leq i < j \leq 2n$ i.i.d. and distributed by the additive Haar measure on $\mathfrak{o}$. For $k=1,\ldots,2n$, let $A_k$ be the top-left $k \times k$ submatrix of $A_{2n}$. Then the joint distribution of their singular numbers is given by
\begin{multline}
    \mathbf{P}(\SN^{\alt}(A_2)=\lambda^{(2)},\SN^{\alt}(A_3)=\nu^{(3)},\ldots,\SN^{\alt}(A_{2n})=\lambda^{(2n)}) \\ 
    = \frac{P_{\lambda^{(2)}}(t^{2n-2};t^2)Q_{\lambda^{(2)}/\nu^{(3)}}(t^{3-2n};t^2)P_{\lambda^{(4)}/\nu^{(3)}}(t^{2n-4};t^2)\cdots P_{\lambda^{(2n)}/\nu^{(2n-1)}}(1;t^2)Q_{\lambda^{(2n)}}(t,t^3,\ldots)}{\Pi_{t^2}(1,1,t^2,1,t^2,t^4,\ldots,1,t^2,\ldots,t^{2n-2};t,t^3,\ldots)},
\end{multline}
with the normalizing constant $\Pi_t(\cdots)$ defined in (equation eq: Cauchy kernel of the paper).

\item(Hermitian case) Let $A_n\in\Her_n(\mathfrak{o})$ be random with i.i.d entries above the diagonal, distributed according to the additive Haar measure on $\mathfrak{o}$, and i.i.d entries on the diagonal independent of these, distributed according to the additive Haar measure on $\mathfrak{o}\cap F_0$. Then letting $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ be its top-left submatrices as before, the joint distribution of their singular numbers is given by

\begin{multline}
\mathbf{P}(\SN^{\her}(A_1)=\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\SN^{\her}(A_n)=\lambda^{(n)})=\frac{1}{\Pi}\sum_{\nu^{(1)}\in\Sig_1^+,\ldots,\nu^{(n-1)}\in\Sig_{n-1}^+} P_{\lambda^{(1)}}((-t)^{n-1};-t)
\\\times \left(\prod_{i=1}^{n-1}Q_{\lambda^{(i)}/\nu^{(i)}}(-(-t)^{i+1-n};-t)P_{\lambda^{(i+1)}/\nu^{(i)}}((-t)^{n-i-1};-t)\right)Q_{\lambda^{(n)}}(t,-t^2,\ldots;-t)
\end{multline}
with the normalizing constant $\Pi$ given by 
$$\Pi=\Pi_{-t}(1,1,-t,1,-t,t^2,\ldots,1,-t,\ldots,(-t)^{n-1};t,-t^2,\ldots).$$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

A random variable $X: \Omega \to K$ taking values in a real separable Hilbert space $K$ is called Gaussian if for every $v \in K$, the real-valued random variable $\langle X, v \rangle_K$ is Gaussian. $X$ is centered if $\mathbb{E}[\langle X, v \rangle_K] = 0$ for all $v \in K$, and non-degenerate if $\operatorname{Var}(\langle X, v \rangle_K) > 0$ for every $v \neq 0$.
K is a real separable Hilbert space
title: Gaussian Random Variable on a Hilbert Space

body: [Definition defn-elliptic of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] A closed 3-manifold  $M$ is \emph{elliptic} if it admits spherical geometry (the universal cover $\widetilde{M}$ is isometric to $S^3$ with the standard spherical metric). This is true if and only if $\pi_1(M)$ is finite [AFW2015].

body:
[Proposition 12 (Consistency of the Lipschitz-case powers) of arXiv:2608.17540, 'Pathwise stability for one-dimensional SDEs driven by Brownian motion and a symmetric stab'] Let $p=\alpha-1\in(0,1)$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \textup{Initial value perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=x_0+W_t+Z_t,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt x_0+W_t+Z_t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p=|x_0-\wt x_0|^p.
\]
Thus the initial error exponent $p=\alpha-1$ is exact.

\item \textup{Drift perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=bt,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt b t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p=T^p|b-\wt b|^p.
\]
Since $B=T|b-\wt b|$, this is exactly $B^p$.

\item \textup{Brownian diffusion perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=aW_t,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt a W_t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p
  =m_p T^{p/2}|a-\wt a|^p,
\]
where $m_p=\E|N(0,1)|^p$. Since $A=T^{1/2}|a-\wt a|$, this is $m_p A^p$.

\item \textup{Stable jump coefficient perturbation.} Let
\[
  X_t=\sigma Z_t,
  \qquad
  \wt X_t=\wt\sigma Z_t.
\]
Then
\[
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-\wt X_t|^p
  =\E|Z_1|^p T^{p/\alpha}|\sigma-\wt\sigma|^p.
\]
Since $S=T^{1/\alpha}|\sigma-\wt\sigma|$, this is $\E|Z_1|^pS^p$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, when $\wt\eta=1$, the powers $|x_0-\wt x_0|^{\alpha-1}$, $B^{\alpha-1}$, $A^{\alpha-1}$ and $S^{\alpha-1}$ agree with the exact scaling of the four elementary perturbation mechanisms.

[Theorem 1 (Pointwise Gaussian majorizing-measure bound) of arXiv:2606.07931, 'Pointwise Complexity for Gaussian Fields:\\Upper Envelopes, Algorithmic Lower Bounds, and '] Assume \(0<R_\ast<\infty\) and \(\Phi_{\mu,\ast}<\infty\). There exists an absolute constant \(C>0\) such that, for every ambient prior \(\mu\in\Delta(T)\), every \(r_0>0\), every \(s_0\in(0,R_\ast]\), and every \(\delta\in(0,1)\), with probability at least \(1-\delta\),
\begin{equation}
\forall x\in T:\qquad
X_x\le C\,\mathcal E_{\mu,r_0,s_0}(x;\delta).
\end{equation}
Consequently, applying the same bound to \(X\) and \(-X\) and taking a union bound, with probability at least \(1-\delta\),
\begin{equation}
\forall x\in T:\qquad
|X_x|\le A_{\mu,r_0,s_0}(x;\delta),
\qquad
A_{\mu,r_0,s_0}(x;\delta):=
C\,\mathcal E_{\mu,r_0,s_0}(x;\delta/2).
\end{equation}
When \(r_0,s_0\) are fixed, we abbreviate \(A_{\mu,r_0,s_0}\) to \(A_\mu\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Pointwise Gaussian majorizing-measure bound

[Prop 7 of arXiv:2607.21759, 'Marchenko--Pastur law for tensor powers of exchangeable unconditional vectors'] Assume $\mathbf X$ is isotropic, exchangeable, unconditional, with the component satisfying $\sup_{n} \E X_1^4 < \infty$. Assume in addition that $\nm{\mathbf X}_2$ and $\nm{\mathbf X}_4$ are both subexponential with uniformly bounded proxy variance $2\sigma^2$, i.e., for $k = 2,4$ and $ \lambda^2 \leq 1/\sigma^2$, \[
    \E\exp\bigl(\lambda (\nm{\mathbf X}_k - \E \nm{ \mathbf X}_k)\bigr) \leq \exp(\lambda^2 \sigma^2).
\] Then given $d = o(n^{1/3})$, we have $\ESD(K_{\PrincipalT}) \wkconv \mu_{\MP(c)}$ with probability $1$. 

    
    
    Assume furthermore that $\nm{\mathbf X}_4$ is sub-Gaussian with uniformly bounded proxy variance $2\sigma^2$, i.e., for all $\lambda \in \R$, \[
        \E\exp\bigl(\lambda (\nm{\mathbf X}_4 - \E \nm{ \mathbf X}_4)\bigr) \leq \exp(\lambda^2 \sigma^2).
    \] Then given $d = o(n^{1/2})$, we have $\ESD(K_{\PrincipalT}) \wkconv \mu_{\MP(c)}$ with probability $1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 7 of arXiv:2607.21759

[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2607.20714, 'High Minima of Gaussian Processes: Overshoots and Minimizer Locations'] Let $B_H$ and $\nu_H$ be as in Example~\ref{ex:fbm}.  Then $\nu_H$ is
the unique optimal measure for the covariance-energy problem on $[a,b], 0< a<b<\infty$.
For $0<H<1/2$, its density $\rho_H$ satisfies
\[
 \inf_{a<t<b}\rho_H(t)>0,\qquad \supp(\nu_H)=[a,b],
\]
and its potential is constant and positive on $[a,b]$.
For every $H\in(0,1)$, the covariance kernel $R_H$ is integrally strictly
positive definite on $[a,b]$.
