ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Transform asymptotics, exact special case, coupling reduction or identifiability check Result: For a stable M/M/1 benchmark let a=P(W>0)=lambda/mu and b=E W=a/(mu-lambda). Inversion gives mu=a/[b*(1-a)] and lambda=a^2/[b*(1-a)]. Empirical busy fraction and mean workload therefore yield a consistent estimator on a fixed sampling grid by ergodicity. Its asymptotic covariance, when the joint CLT holds, is J*Sigma*J^T, where J is the Jacobian of this inversion and Sigma=sum over integer lags of Cov((1{W_0>0},W_0),(1{W_l>0},W_l)). The off-zero lags are part of the information calculation. Check: Substitution of the inverted parameters returns both a and b exactly. At lambda=1,mu=2 one gets a=1/2,b=1/2 and recovers both rates. Treating Sigma as a one-observation variance would discard the dependence at every finite grid spacing. Obstruction: The estimator is a benchmark only. Neither an efficiency bound for general input families nor an estimator attaining it has been proved here.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0394-efficient-input-estimation-from-periodically-observed-queue-workloads

body: Zorn's lemma: if P is a NONEMPTY partially ordered set in which every chain - every totally ordered subset - has an upper bound in P, then P contains at least one maximal element. Over ZF it is equivalent to the axiom of choice and to the well-ordering theorem; it is the standard tool for existence proofs (maximal ideals, bases of vector spaces, Hahn-Banach).
title: Zorn's lemma

body:
[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2607.22470, 'A Logarithmic Fluctuation Hierarchy for Sequential Interacting Diffusions'] Fix \(n\ge0\) and let \(\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\R^d)\). Set
\[
M_t^{N,n}(\varphi)
:=
\frac1{\sqrt N}\sum_{i=1}^N h_n(i/N)
\int_0^t\nabla\varphi(X_s^i)\cdot\dd B_s^i.
\]
Then
\begin{align}
\langle Y_t^{N,n},\varphi\rangle
&=
\langle Y_0^{N,n},\varphi\rangle
+
\int_0^t
\langle Y_s^{N,n},L_s\varphi\rangle\,\dd s\notag\\
&\quad+
\int_0^t I_s^{N,n}(\varphi)\,\dd s
+
\int_0^t
\mathcal B_s^{N,n}(\varphi)\,\dd s
+
M_t^{N,n}(\varphi),

\end{align}
where
\(L_s\varphi=\frac12\Delta\varphi+
\bigl(b(s,\cdot)+K*\bar\rho_s\bigr)\cdot\nabla\varphi\),
\begin{equation}
I_s^{N,n}(\varphi)
=
\frac1{\sqrt N}
\sum_{i=2}^N
h_n(i/N)
\nabla\varphi(X_s^i)\cdot
(K*(\mu_s^{i-1}-\bar\rho_s))(X_s^i),
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\mathcal B_s^{N,n}(\varphi)
=
-\frac{h_n(1/N)}{\sqrt N}
\nabla\varphi(X_s^1)\cdot(K*\bar\rho_s)(X_s^1).
\end{equation}
Moreover, as \(N\to\infty\),
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E\int_0^T |\mathcal B_s^{N,n}(\varphi)|\,\dd s\to0.
\end{equation}

[Lemma lem:local of arXiv:2609.03448, 'Prime-power Diophantine tuples'] Assume that the triple is not regular.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $p$ is odd, then exactly one of $e,\bar e$ is divisible by $N^2$.
\item If $p=2$ and $r\ge3$, then
\[
 \{v_2(e),v_2(\bar e)\}=\{2,2r-2\}.
\]
In particular, exactly one of $e,\bar e$ is divisible by $N^2/4$.
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma lower_bound_on_the_expected_total_size_of_worms_hitting_one_vertex of arXiv:2505.07145, 'Nonamenable Poisson zoo'] Let us consider a nonamenable graph $G$ with a subgroup of its automorphisms $\Gamma \leq \mathrm{Aut}(G)$ that acts transitively on $G$. Let $\eta \, : \, \mathbb{N}_{>0} \rightarrow [0,1]$ be a probability mass function and $\mathcal{X} = \sum_{i \in I} \delta_{(x,H)_i} \sim \mathcal{P}_{\eta}^\lambda$.
Given some $R \in \mathbb{N}_{>0}$, a finite connected set $A \subset \subset V(G)$ and a vertex from its exterior boundary, $x \in \partial_{\mathrm{ext}} A$, let us consider
the total occupation measure $\check{ \Sigma }_{A, \{ x\}}^R$ corresponding to the restricted process introduced in (equation eq:point_measure_restricted_to_hit_B_but_not_the_closure_of_A of the paper).
For any $\varepsilon > 0$, with the constant $c(\varepsilon) > 0$ from Corollary~(coro:number_of_steps_and_size_of_trace_of_SRW_are_comparable_on_nonamenable_graphs of the paper), we have
\begin{equation}
	
	\mathbb{E} \big[ \check{ \Sigma }_{A, \{ x \}}^R \big] \geq c(\varepsilon) \cdot
	\lambda \cdot 
	\mathbb{E} \left[ \mathcal{L}^2 \, \mathds{1} \left[ \mathcal{L} \leq R \right] \right] \cdot  
	P_x \left( T_{\overline{A}}^+ = +\infty \right) \cdot 
	\left( P_x \left( T_{\overline{A}}^+ = +\infty \right) - \varepsilon \right),
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal{L}$ denotes a random variable that has law $\eta$.
title: Lemma lower_bound_on_the_expected_total_size_of_worms_hitting_one_vertex of arXiv:2505.07145

Own-work draft: independently checked proof of this exact claim version, reviewer PASS recorded. For fixed n>=2, deterministic initial coordinates x0!=0 and y0, and fixed nonnegative variances s1,s2 with s1+s2>0, consider the fresh-RR common-Hessian finite sum f_i(x,y)=x^2/2+kappa_T*y^2/2+b_i*x+c_i*y with zero-sum linear terms and mean squares s1,s2 fixed across horizons T=nK. Assume kappa_T>=1 and kappa_T*log(T)/T ->0. Set B_T=n(n+1)(s1+kappa_T^2*s2)/48 and H_T=log(T^3/B_T). Every globally optimal constant step obeys T*eta_T/H_T ->1/2 and the optimal last-epoch expected function error is asymptotic to B_T*H_T^3/(8T^3). The result holds over all eta>=0 or over 0<=eta<=c/kappa_T for any fixed c>0. It includes s2=0. If s2>0 and kappa_T=T^alpha, 0<alpha<1, the step constant relative to log T is (3-2alpha)/2 and optimal error is asymptotic to n(n+1)*s2*(3-2alpha)^3*T^(2alpha-3)*log(T)^3/384. This completes a growing-parameter regime of named target 1; no full-row solution or priority claim is made.
n and initialization fixed; x0!=0; s1,s2 fixed nonnegative and not both zero; zero-sum b_i,c_i; fresh independent uniform permutations; kappa deterministic with kappa*log(T)/T->0. Arbitrary fixed mu follows by scaling f_i/mu and eta to mu*eta, as detailed in the proof.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:37fd1a0dd3bb3ce8906a1b18ff7ab4f1feea3c48b2e9b04955068457a1a40c3a","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/37/37fd1a0dd3bb3ce8906a1b18ff7ab4f1feea3c48b2e9b04955068457a1a40c3a.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:c1381273eab07e14a10b69474a414d4ba9808fda033c60aea544cdde0ee2e19e","bundle_entry_key":"growing-kappa-common-hessian","bundle_id":"population.t362-growing-kappa-002","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"optimization; random reshuffling; condition number; tuned last iterate","draft":"w732/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.randomreshuffling:common-hessian-random-reshuffling-growing-condition-number-optimal-step","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Target 1 extension: the globally tuned step with a growing condition number

Status: proof draft, unaudited. This extends C001's fixed-kappa limit. The exact epoch recursion is settled ground and is not re-proved. No priority claim or full-row solution is asserted.

## Statement

Fix n>=2, deterministic x0!=0 and y0, and s1,s2>=0 with s1+s2>0. For each T=nK, let kappa=kappa_T>=1 and use the target-1 common-Hessian instance

    f_i(x,y)=x^2/2+kappa*y^2/2+b_i*x+c_i*y,
    sum b_i=sum c_i=0, mean b_i^2=s1, mean c_i^2=s2.

The vectors (b_i),(c_i), n and initialization remain fixed. Each epoch has a fresh independent uniform permutation, shared by the two coordinates. No independence between coordinate noises is assumed; the objective has no mixed quadratic term. Suppose

    kappa_T*log(T)/T -> 0.

Put C=n(n+1)/48, B_T=C*(s1+kappa_T^2*s2), and H_T=log(T^3/B_T). Then H_T->infinity. For EVERY global minimizer eta_T of the expected last-epoch objective over eta>=0,

    T*eta_T/H_T -> 1/2,
    min_eta E[F_T(X_K)-F_T*] ~ B_T*H_T^3/(8*T^3).                 (1)

The same result holds if steps are restricted to 0<=eta<=c/kappa_T for any fixed c>0. No uniqueness or unimodality of the optimizer is assumed. This includes noise only on the flat coordinate (s2=0), the literal b_i-only construction in the target, as well as noise on the stiff coordinate.

For s2>0 and kappa_T=T^alpha, 0<alpha<1, (1) becomes

    min error ~ [n(n+1)*s2*(3-2alpha)^3/384]
                  *T^(2alpha-3)*log(T)^3,
    T*eta_T/log T -> (3-2alpha)/2.                              (2)

Thus replacing a fixed kappa by a growing kappa inside C001 while keeping its 3/2 step constant would be incorrect when the stiff-coordinate variance dominates.

## A uniform finite-n variance sandwich

For a coordinate of curvature h>0 and optimum variance s>=0, write a=1-h*eta. The settled recursion gives

    V_h = s/(n-1) * sum_{0<=i<j<n}(a^i-a^j)^2,
    B_h(eta) = (h/2)*eta^2*V_h/(1-a^(2n)),

where B_h is the stationary contribution to the expected objective. If 0<q=h*eta<1, then

    [s*h^2*n(n+1)/48]*eta^3*(1-q)^(2n-4)
       <= B_h(eta)
       <= [s*h^2*n(n+1)/48]*eta^3*(1-q)^(-(2n-1)).             (3)

Proof of (3). Set m=j-i. The identity

    a^i-a^j = q*a^i*sum_{r=0}^{m-1}a^r

lies between m*q*a^(j-1) and m*q. Since j-1<=n-2 and 0<a<1, it therefore lies between m*q*a^(n-2) and m*q. Square and sum; use sum_{i<j}(j-i)^2=n^2(n^2-1)/12. Also

    2n*q*a^(2n-1) <= 1-a^(2n) <= 2n*q.

All denominators are positive. Substituting the lower numerator and upper denominator gives the lower bound in (3); the opposite choices give the upper bound. The case s=0 is identically zero and requires no division by s. The exponent 2n-4 is nonnegative even at n=2.

For the two coordinates, whenever q=kappa*eta<1, summing (3) gives

    B_T*eta^3*(1-q)^(2n-4) <= B_1(eta)+B_kappa(eta)
       <= B_T*eta^3*(1-q)^(-(2n-1)).                           (4)

This uses 1-h*eta>=1-q and nonnegative coefficients; it remains valid when kappa=1, counting both coordinates. The actual finite-horizon variance is the sum of B_h(eta)*(1-(1-h*eta)^(2T)). In this range it is between (1-(1-eta)^(2T)) times the left side of (4) and the right side of (4).

## Global optimization proof

1. There are constants b0,b1>0, depending only on n,s1,s2, such that b0<=B_T<=b1*kappa^2. The assumption kappa*log T/T->0 implies eventually kappa<=T/log T. Hence

       log T + 2log log T - log b1 <= H_T <= 3log T - log b0.

   In particular H_T->infinity, H_T=O(log T), and kappa*H_T/T->0.

2. Use the candidate eta_c=H_T/(2T). Its q_c=kappa*eta_c tends to zero, so (4) applies. The deterministic contribution of the flat coordinate is at most x0^2*exp(-H_T)/2. That of the stiff coordinate is at most kappa*y0^2*exp(-kappa*H_T)/2. For H>=1 and kappa>=1,

       log kappa <= kappa-1 <= (kappa-1)*H,
       kappa*exp(-kappa*H)<=exp(-H).

   Thus the entire deterministic contribution is O(exp(-H_T)), with a constant independent of kappa. Since exp(-H_T)=B_T/T^3, and H_T->infinity, it is negligible relative to B_T*H_T^3/T^3. Equation (4) gives

       inf_eta P_T(eta) <= (1+o(1))*B_T*H_T^3/(8T^3).          (5)

   This tends to zero: B_T<=b1*kappa^2 and kappa*H_T/T->0 imply B_T*H_T^3/T^3 <= b1*(kappa*H_T/T)^2*(H_T/T)->0.

3. Existence of a minimizer holds because the exact error is a continuous coercive polynomial. In any noisy coordinate, the pair (i,j)=(0,1) alone and the final epoch alone give, for ALL eta>=0,

       P_T(eta) >= s*h^3*eta^4/[2(n-1)].                     (6)

   No step-size restriction is used in (6): the geometric variance multiplier is a sum of even powers and is at least one.

4. First suppose s2>0. With q_T=kappa*eta_T, (6) and (5) imply

       q_T^4 <= [2(n-1)/s2]*kappa*P_T(eta_T)
              <= O(kappa*B_T*H_T^3/T^3)
              <= O((kappa*H_T/T)^3) ->0.

   Thus q_T->0 and eta_T->0. If t_T=T*eta_T were bounded along a subsequence, then

       (1-eta_T)^(2T)=exp(-2t_T+O(T*eta_T^2))

   would stay bounded away from zero there. The flat deterministic contribution x0^2/2 times this quantity contradicts the vanishing optimum. Therefore t_T->infinity.

5. If s2=0 instead, s1>0 and B_T=C*s1 is constant. Using h=1 in (6) first gives eta_T->0. The same flat transient argument gives t_T->infinity. For the NOISY FLAT coordinate, (3) with q=eta_T, together with 1-(1-eta_T)^(2T)->1, yields

       P_T(eta_T)>=(1-o(1))*B_T*eta_T^3.

   Combining with (5) gives t_T=O(H_T), hence q_T=kappa*t_T/T->0 by step 1. This argument does not presuppose small q_T for the stiff coordinate.

6. Now in either case q_T->0 and t_T->infinity. The finite-horizon sandwich following (4) gives

       total variance = (1+o(1))*B_T*t_T^3/T^3.               (7)

   Its error is uniform along ANY sequence of minimizers: the factors in (4) depend only on q_T and fixed n, and the finite-horizon factor is at least 1-exp(-2t_T)->1. From (5) and (7), t_T=O(H_T). Thus T*eta_T^2=O(H_T^2/T)->0, and the flat transient equals

       A*exp(-2t_T+o(1)), A=x0^2/2>0.

   Comparing it with (5), and using B_T/T^3=exp(-H_T), gives

       2t_T >= H_T-3log H_T-O(1).

   Hence liminf t_T/H_T>=1/2. Equations (5) and (7) give limsup t_T/H_T<=1/2. Substitution into (7) and comparison with the candidate upper bound prove (1).

7. For the capped interval eta<=c/kappa, the candidate is eventually admissible since kappa*eta_c->0. Coercivity is replaced by compactness, and all lower bounds remain valid, so the same proof gives (1). Formula (2) follows from B_T~n(n+1)*s2*T^(2alpha)/48 and H_T~(3-2alpha)log T.

## Returning to an arbitrary fixed mu>0

Apply the theorem to f_i/mu with curvatures 1,kappa=L/mu, variances s1/mu^2,s2/mu^2, and normalized step mu*eta. Then

    B'_T=n(n+1)*(s1+kappa^2*s2)/(48mu^2),
    H'_T=log(T^3/B'_T),
    mu*T*eta_T/H'_T ->1/2,
    min original error ~ n(n+1)*(s1+kappa^2*s2)*(H'_T)^3/(384mu*T^3).

Here mu, n, s1, s2 and the initial point are fixed; only kappa grows. No assertion is made when kappa*log T/T fails to tend to zero, when n grows, or when x0=0. This moves the named minimization target into a joint horizon/condition-number regime; it does not settle the general last-iterate conjecture.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:ec8ad8945e0b1b661dd6078027f7ac99f690849a6b7e7c2dc5caf1253d0b79ff","revision_digest":"sha256:3810cd23415cc49e534fa3b3cec3903e6f05f54ad3b7f403d6d61edeff7235ca","source_id":"own-work:w732:T362:C003:v1","source_revision":"C003-v1-reviewer-PASS; reviewer urn:mb-agent:7a4f9e38007c2a28; T362-w732-C003 v1; proof sha256 d4fdc9d0b21a02cab20a601de21ac58b791d8a93e91064ca3c7e781b0b1002b1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body:
[Theorem 26 of arXiv:2605.25715, '2605.25715'] Let
\[
G=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\ c&d\end{pmatrix},\qquad
A=\begin{pmatrix}\alpha&\beta\\ \beta&\gamma\end{pmatrix}
\quad(\alpha>0,\ \delta:=\det A=\alpha\gamma-\beta^{2}>0).
\]
Then, there exists a symmetric matrix $S=\begin{pmatrix}s_{11}& s_{12}\\ s_{12}& s_{22}\end{pmatrix}$ satisfying \eqref{SOHHDlinalg1}, and given as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)]
If $\gamma b -\alpha c + \beta(a-d) =0$, then $S = A^{-1}G$, and in particular,
\[
s_{11} = \frac{\gamma a - \beta c}{\alpha\gamma - \beta^2}, \qquad
s_{12} = \frac{\gamma b - \beta d}{\alpha\gamma - \beta^2}, \qquad
s_{22} = \frac{\alpha d - \beta b}{\alpha\gamma - \beta^2}.
\]

\item[(ii)]
If $a+d=0$, then $S=0$, that is,
\[
s_{11} = 0, \qquad s_{12} = 0, \qquad s_{22} = 0.
\]

\item[(iii)] If $a+d \neq 0$ and $\gamma b- \alpha c + \beta(a-d) \neq 0$, then
\begin{align*}
s_{11} &= \frac{a+d}{ (\alpha \gamma-\beta^2) (a+d)^2 +\big( \gamma b - \alpha c + \beta(a-d)\big)^2} \Big( \gamma a(a+d) + \alpha c^2 - \gamma bc - 2\beta ac \Big), \\[8pt]
s_{12} &= \frac{a+d}{ (\alpha \gamma-\beta^2) (a+d)^2 +\big( \gamma b - \alpha c + \beta(a-d)\big)^2} \Big( \alpha cd + \gamma ab - 2\beta ad \Big), \\[8pt]
s_{22} &= \frac{a+d}{ (\alpha \gamma-\beta^2) (a+d)^2 +\big(\gamma b - \alpha c + \beta(a-d)\big)^2} \Big(\alpha d(a+d) + \gamma b^2 - \alpha bc - 2\beta bd \Big).
\end{align*}
\end{itemize}
title: Theorem 26 of arXiv:2605.25715

[Proposition prop:cdbm-properties of arXiv:2507.12502, 'Quantitative Edge Eigenvector Universality for Random Regular Graphs: Berry-Esseen Bounds '] The constrained Dyson Brownian motion satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Constraint preservation.} If $\tilde{H}_0\mathbf{e} = 0$, then $\tilde{H}_t\mathbf{e} = 0$ for all $t \geq 0$ [biane2004littelmann,journee2010low].
\item \emph{Invariant measure.} The stationary distribution is the constrained GOE ensemble on $\mathcal{M}_0$.
\item \emph{Eigenvalue evolution.} The eigenvalues $\lambda_i(t)$ evolve by non-intersecting diffusions with drift toward the origin [grabiner1999brownian,katori2004symmetry].
\item \emph{Eigenvector dynamics.} For $i \geq 2$, the eigenvector $\mathbf{u}_i(t)$ remains orthogonal to $\mathbf{e}$ for all $t$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Properties of CDBM

[Prop 8 of arXiv:2603.27433, 'The $k$-cycle shuffling with repeated cards'] Suppose that $r:=n-\l_1\in[n^{5/6},0.499n]$. Furthermore, suppose $2\le k\le 6\log n$. Moreover, suppose that $t':=t-\frac{n\log n}{k}$ satisfies $|t'|\le \frac{n(\log\log n-\omega(1))}{2k}$. Then, for sufficiently large $n$, we have
$$|s_\l(k)|^{2t}\le\exp(-2r\log n+(2/3+o(1))r\log r).$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Let X_1..X_4 be independent with densities at most 1, S_1 = X_1 + X_2, S_2 = X_3 + X_4, and let u, v be the orthonormal pair (1,1,1,1)/2, (1,1,-1,-1)/2 rotated by the angle theta with tan theta = sqrt 2, so that every coordinate has u_i^2 + v_i^2 = 1/2. Then U = <u, X>, V = <v, X> are linear combinations of the independent S_1, S_2 with determinant -1/2, and the pair argument (condition on nothing; the two quadratic curves along the parabola have separated critical points) bounds the density of U + cV^2 by 8 for every real c and all laws. For comb laws (each X_i uniform on N teeth [j, j + 1/N]) the maximal functional M_2 = int sup_u rho_{U,V}(u, v) dv grows linearly in N, because the coefficient ratio of V is the quadratic irrational (1 + sqrt 2)^2 and the lines V = v meet a bump of height at least 1/18 for a set of v of measure of order N. Consequence for the bounded-density quadratic-form conjecture: the leverage (spread) condition does not make maximal functionals bounded, so the curved-slice statements (CS), (VD), (P2) must use the curvature of the section.

[Theorem 21 of arXiv:2609.03098, 'Standing waves for Schr\"odinger equations with Kato class potentials and $L^\infty$-bound'] Let $F$ be the mapping given by \eqref{Nemytzki_f}, and let $W\subset H^1(\R^N)$ be bounded in $L^\infty(\R^N)$. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item[$(i)$] If the condition $(LL)_+$ holds, then there exist $R > 0$ and $\nu>0$ such that 
$$
\langle F(v + w), v\rangle_{L^2} > \nu
$$
for all $w\in W$ and $v\in X_0$ with $\|v\|_{L^2} \ge R$.
\item[$(ii)$] If the condition $(LL)_-$ holds, then there exist $R > 0$ and $\nu>0$ such that
$$
\langle F(v + w), v\rangle_{L^2} < -\nu
$$
for all $w\in W$ and $v\in X_0$ with $\|v\|_{L^2} \ge R$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $T>0$ be fixed, $\theta_t^\varepsilon \triangleq \frac{X_t^\varepsilon-\bar{X}_t}{\sqrt{\varepsilon}}$ and $N \sim \mathscr{N}(0, \sigma_t^2).$ For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ and $\eta,$ and $0<\xi < \frac{1}{2},$ there exists a time-dependent positive constant $C$ such that
\begin{multline*}
\sup_{t \in [0,T]}d_W \left( \theta_t^\varepsilon,N \right) \le C \left[ \eta^{\frac{1}{4}} + \varepsilon^{\frac{1}{4}} + \left( \frac{\eta}{\varepsilon}- \frac{1}{\gamma^2} \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}  + \left( \frac{\eta}{\varepsilon} \right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \eta^{\frac{1}{2}-\xi} + \varepsilon^{\frac{1}{2}-\xi} \right]\\
+ C \left( \left( \frac{\eta}{\varepsilon} \right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \eta^{\frac{1}{4}} + \left( \frac{\eta}{\varepsilon} \right) \eta^{\frac{1}{4}} + \left( 1+ \frac{\eta}{\varepsilon} \right)e^{-\frac{CT}{\eta}} \right).
\end{multline*}
where, $\sigma_t^2$ represents the limiting variance and is defined in equation (equation E:Limiting-Variance of the paper) below. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 25 of arXiv:2608.19976, 'Random valuations'] Let $\Phi$ be a $\sigma$-continuous non-negative stationary
  isotropic ID valuation with independent increments and vanishing
  deterministic part. Then there exist a non-negative infinitely
  divisible random variable $\xi$ and independent non-negative
  stationary isotropic ID valuations $\Psi_m$, $m=1,\dots,d$, with
  independent increments, such that
  \begin{displaymath}
    \Psi(K)
    =
    \xi\1_{K\neq\emptyset}
    +
    \sum_{m=1}^d\Psi_m(K),
    \qquad K\in\Kd,
  \end{displaymath}
  is weakly equivalent to $\Phi$. Moreover, $\Psi_m$ is
  $m$-stable in argument for every $m=1,\dots,d$.
  
  More precisely, there exist non-negative measures

  $V_0(K)=\1_{K\neq\emptyset}$.

[Theorem thm:regularity-deweighting of arXiv:2608.16119, 'Fully nonlinear parabolic equations under a fixed reference diffusion: weighted \texorpdfs'] Let $w$ be a regular weight of order $\alpha$, where $0\leq\alpha<1$.  Assume
Assumptions~(ass:reference-diffusion of the paper),
(ass:drift-multiplier of the paper), (ass:lipschitz-driver of the paper), and
(ass:differentiable-driver of the paper) at the same order $\alpha$.  Suppose
$C_w(X)<\infty$, $\delta_{\mathrm{sg}}>0$, $\psi\in H^2(\mu_T)$, and
$f_0\in L_0^2$.  Then the unique order-$\alpha$ weighted Sobolev solution
$u^*$ and its source $F^*=F_{u^*}$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
 u^*,D_xu^*,D_x^2u^*,F^*
 \in L_0^2.
 
\end{equation}
The following estimate holds with
$C=C\bigl(T,\lambda,\Lambda,M_1(a),\operatorname{osc}_\alpha(w),C_w(X),
\Lambda_b,L_x^{\mathrm{gr}},\mathbf L_f,
\delta_{\mathrm{sg}}^{-1}\bigr)>0$:
\begin{equation}
 \left\lVert F^*\right\rVert_0+\sum_{j=0}^2\left\lVert D_x^ju^*\right\rVert_0
 \leq C\left(1+\sqrt{\frac{T^{1-\alpha}}{1-\alpha}}\right)
 \left[\left\lVert m_x\right\rVert_\alpha
 +\max\{1,T^{\alpha/2}\}
   \left(\left\lVert f_0\right\rVert_0+\norm\psi_{H^2(\mu_T)}\right)\right].
 
\end{equation}
The coefficient bounds also give $\mathsf Z u^*,\mathsf G u^*\in L_0^2$, and $u^*$ is
the unique unweighted Sobolev solution.

[Definition 5 ($\Omega$-isotypic summand) of arXiv:2609.03736, '2609.03736'] For $\Omega\subset\Irr(\mathsf G)$ let $z_\Omega$ be the central projection
onto the corresponding isotypic summands and put
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal I_{E,\Omega}=z_\Omega\mathcal I_E,
 \qquad
 \mathcal H_{E,\Omega}
 =\End_{\mathsf G}(\mathcal I_{E,\Omega})
 \cong z_\Omega\mathcal H_Ez_\Omega
 =\bigoplus_{\pi\in\Omega}\End(M_\pi).
 
\end{equation}
Because $z_\Omega$ is central, $\mathcal H_{E,\Omega}$ is a central direct
summand of $\mathcal H_E$, with unit $z_\Omega$.  Equivalently, it is the
Hecke algebra of the $\Omega$-isotypic submodule $\mathcal I_{E,\Omega}$.

[Prop dimension-free-identity of arXiv:2608.30847, 'An Almgren-type formula for planar $p$-harmonic functions'] Assume that $u$ is smooth and $Du\neq 0$ in an annulus containing
$\partial B_r(x_0)$. Then
$$
  D'(r)=\frac{n-p}{r}D(r)+pG(r),
$$
and
$$
   H'(r) = \frac{n-1}{r}H(r)+2D(r)+K(r).
$$
Consequently, at every such radius for which $H(r)>0$,
$$
  N_\ast'(r)+N_\ast(r)\Theta(r)  =  \frac{pr}{H(r)}
 \int_{\partial B_r(x_0)}  A \left(  \partial_\nu u-\frac{N_\ast(r)}{r}v \right)^2   \,dS .
$$
In particular,
$$
  N_\ast'(r)+N_\ast(r)\Theta(r)\ge 0.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For independent bond percolation on the infinite d-regular tree with d>=3, p_c=1/(d-1), theta(p)=0 for p<=p_c, and theta(p)=[2d(d-1)/(d-2)](p-p_c)+O((p-p_c)^2) as p decreases to p_c from above. The positive descendant-survival solution u obeys 1-u=(1-pu)^(d-1); division by u and the implicit-function theorem give the expansion, and theta=1-(1-pu)^d. This is an exact tree analogue, not a high-dimensional lattice solution.

[Proposition 12 of arXiv:2607.29534, 'Expected signatures via partial integration, coordinate change and symmetrization'] For $w,v\in\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{A}}$,
$r,q\in\mathcal{W}_{\mathcal{A}^{\prime\prime}}$, and
$\blue{i},\blue{j}\in\mathcal{A}^{\prime}$,
\begin{equation}
\left\{\begin{aligned}
r\gammashuffle q
&=
r\shuffle q,
\\
(w\blue{i}r)\gammashuffle q
&=
w\blue{i}(r\shuffle q),
\\
r\gammashuffle(v\blue{j}q)
&=
v\blue{j}(r\shuffle q),
\\
(w\blue{i}r)\gammashuffle(v\blue{j}q)
&=
\bigl((w\blue{i})\gammashuffle v\bigr)
\blue{j}(r\shuffle q)
+
\bigl(w\gammashuffle(v\blue{j})\bigr)
\blue{i}(r\shuffle q).
\end{aligned}\right.
\end{equation}
These identities uniquely determine $\gammashuffle$.

body:
[Lemma 21 of arXiv:2608.22636, 'Q-Learning with Stable Infinite-Dimensional \\Linear Function Approximation'] Fix real numbers $\alpha\ge 1$ and $T>0$, and integers $n\ge0$ and $n_0>0$.  Set $\alpha_k=\alpha/(k+n_0)$,
$\tau(n,m)=\sum_{k=n}^{m-1}\alpha_{k+1}$, and
$\cW(n,T)=\setcond{m\ge n}{\tau(n,m)\le T}$.  Then, for every $m\in\cW(n,T)$,
\begin{equation}
        m+n_0+1
        \le
        e^{T/\alpha}(n+n_0+1).
        
\end{equation}

If $m_\vee=\max\cW(n,T)$ and $\alpha_{n+1}\le T/2$, then the end time satisfies
\begin{equation}
        \frac{T}{2}
        \le
        \tau(n,m_\vee)
        \le
        T.
        
\end{equation}

If either $T=1/4$ and $n+n_0\ge8$, or
$T=1/5$ and $n+n_0\ge10$, then
\begin{equation}
        m+n_0
        \le
        \frac32(n+n_0),
        \quad \forall m\in\cW(n,T).
        
\end{equation}

body:
Let f be a smooth convex transpose-invariant real matrix loss, with sufficient differentiability for the local flow theorem (C-infinity suffices), and suppose its PSD flow Phi satisfies Wprime=-W grad f(W)-grad f(W) W and is defined at all real times. Let Wbar be a critical point, a local minimum of f on PSD matrices of rank at most r, r>=1, but not a global PSD minimum. Write the eigenvalues of -grad f(Wbar) as mu1>=mu2>=... and assume mu1>mu2 (then mu1>0); let v1 be a unit top eigenvector. For PSD initial matrices Walpha suppose arrival times Talpha give Ealpha=Phi(Walpha,Talpha)->Wbar and liminf (v1^T Ealpha v1)/||Ealpha-Wbar||_F>0. Then, for each fixed real t, Phi(Walpha,Talpha+log(1/(v1^T Ealpha v1))/(2mu1)+t) converges to the canonical escape orbit WG(t)=lim_(epsilon down to 0) Phi(Wbar+epsilon v1 v1^T,log(1/epsilon)/(2mu1)+t). This limit solves the same flow and has rank at most r+1. The statement does not assert that alignment follows from a Gaussian initialization, nor that the canonical orbit ends at a rank-(r+1) local minimum. Source: arXiv:2012.09839, Theorem G.2, PDF p.33; global-flow convention in Section 3, p.3; genericity limitations in Appendix H, pp.34-35.

PSD flow is complete in real time, as in the source setup
Rank-r constrained local minimum that is not a global PSD minimum
Simple positive top eigenvalue of -grad f(Wbar)
Quantitative relative Gram alignment at arrival, not merely a nonzero projection

body:
[Theorem 22 (Localized continuous centered second-chaos operator) of arXiv:2606.26065, 'Localized Centered Second-Chaos Operators'] Assume the continuous Gaussian setup of Section~\ref{sec:setup}, the order-zero symbol bound~\eqref{eq:m-size}, covariance bounds~\eqref{eq:S-size}, and the time-regularity and cutoff-convergence assumptions in Assumption~\ref{ass:time}.  Assume also the power-law envelope~\eqref{eq:power-envelope}.  Let $\lambda>0$ and let $s,\sigma\in\R$ satisfy the strict window~\eqref{eq:lambda-window}.  Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.4em]
\item For every finite $p\ge2$, the localized centered Galerkin operators
\[
 \cB^\circ_\Lambda:
 \Xspace_T^\sigma
 \longrightarrow
 C_TH^{s-\lambda}\cap L_T^1B^{\sigma-\lambda}_{2,\infty}
\]
are uniformly bounded in $L^p(\Omega)$ and converge in $L^p$ operator norm.  More precisely, after choosing $\eps>0$ below the strict margins in~\eqref{eq:lambda-window},
\[
 \sup_{\Lambda\in\Dyd\cup\{\infty\}}
 \left\|
 \norm{\cB^\circ_\Lambda}_{\Xspace_T^\sigma\to C_TH^{s-\lambda}\cap L_T^1B^{\sigma-\lambda}_{2,\infty}}
 \right\|_{L^p(\Omega)}<\infty,
\]
and
\[
 \cB^\circ_\Lambda\to\cB^\circ
 \quad\text{in }L^p\bigl(\Omega;\cL(\Xspace_T^\sigma,
 C_TH^{s-\lambda}\cap L_T^1B^{\sigma-\lambda}_{2,\infty})\bigr).
\]
\item Under the finite-state Galerkin condition in Assumption~\ref{ass:time}, there is one full-probability event $\Omega_*$ on which the whole Galerkin sequence converges pathwise in the same operator norm.  The same event controls all dyadic blocks simultaneously.
\end{enumerate}
The result applies to independent Gaussian legs and to same-family Wick squares after complete Wick centering and decoupling.  The finite-state hypothesis is used only in item~\textup{(ii)}.

body:
[Proposition 9 of arXiv:2608.26692, 'Many Facets in Random Polytopes from Product and Log-Concave Measures'] Fix $\alpha>0$ and let $N=\lfloor e^{\alpha n}\rfloor$.  There exists a
symmetric isotropic probability measure $\nu_n$ on $\R^n$ with
$\operatorname{supp}\nu_n=\R^n$, which is not log-concave, such that for
independent $X_1,\ldots,X_N$ with law $\nu_n$ and
\[
 P_N=\conv\{X_1,\ldots,X_N\},
\]
one has
\[
 \E f_{n-1}(P_N)=(1+o(1))2^n.
\]
In particular,
\[
 \E f_{n-1}(P_N)=e^{O(n)}
 \ll n^{n/2}e^{-Cn}
\]
for every fixed $C>0$.

[Theorem thm:PoissonApproximation2 of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] Assume that $\mu$ is critical and belongs to the domain of
attraction of an $\alpha$-stable law for some $\alpha\in(1,2]$. Let $(G_k)$
be a sequence of $\{0,1\}$-valued functions on finite plane trees,  let
$(k_n)$ be a sequence of integers and let $(M_n)$ be a cutoff sequence. Set
$$
  \pi_n=\P(G_{k_n}(\mathcal T)=1).
$$
Let $B\subset\mathbb Z_+$ be such that
$$
  c_B
  =
  \mathbb{E}\left[
    k_\varnothing(\mathcal T)
    \mathbbm{1}_{\{k_\varnothing(\mathcal T)\in B\}}
  \right]
  \in(0,\infty).
$$
Define
$$
  \widehat{G}_k(T)
  =
  \mathbbm{1}_{\{k_\varnothing(T)\in B\}}
  \mathbbm{1}_{\{\exists u\in\Gamma_\varnothing(T):G_k(T_u)=1\}}.
$$
Assume that $(G_k)$ satisfies Assumption
(hyp:S of the paper) along $(k_n)$ with respect to $(M_n)$, and that
$(\widehat G_k)$ satisfies Assumption (hyp:C of the paper) along $(k_n)$ with respect
to the same cutoff sequence $(M_n)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] If $(n\pi_n)$ is bounded, then
$
  d_{\mathrm{TV}} \big(
    \#\{u\in\mathcal T^n:\widehat{G}_{k_n}(\mathcal T^n_u)=1\},
    \mathrm{Poisson}(c_B n\pi_n)
  \big)
  \to 0$.
\item[(ii)] If $n\pi_n\to\infty$, then
$
{
\#\{u\in\mathcal T^n:
\widehat G_{k_n}(\mathcal T^n_u)=1\}
}
\to \infty$ in probability.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm intro1 of arXiv:2509.08659, 'Gap metrics for stationary point processes and quantitative convexity of the free energy'] Let $\mathsf{P}_0,\mathsf{P}_1$ be the laws of two stationary point processes with unit intensity and $\mathcal F_\beta(\mathsf{P}_i)<\infty$ for $i=0,1.$ Then, there is an interpolation $(\mathsf{P}_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ between $\mathsf{P}_0$ and $\mathsf{P}_1$ and a coupling $ \mathsf{Q}^0$ between the Palm measures of $\mathsf{P}_0$ and $\mathsf{P}_1$ such that 
\begin{align}  
    \mathcal F_{\beta}(\mathsf{P}_{t})\leq  (1-t)\mathcal F_{\beta}(\mathsf{P}_{0})+t\mathcal F_{\beta}(\mathsf{P}_{1})-\frac{(1-t)t\beta}{2}\int \sum_{(0,0)\neq (x,y)\in \bar\xi} (x-y)^2\inf_{z\in [x,y]}f(\left\lvertz\right\rvert) \mathsf{Q}^0(d\bar\xi),
    \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 5 (Stein characterization) of arXiv:2606.28678, '2606.28678'] Let $M\in \mathcal{S}^d$ and $\Psi,\Sigma\in \mathcal{S}_{++}^d$ such that $\Psi\Sigma = \Sigma\Psi$. Then
\[
\mathfrak{X}\sim \mathcal{SN}_{d\times d}(M,\Psi,\Sigma) \qquad \Leftrightarrow \qquad \EE\big[\mathcal{A}_{M,\Psi,\Sigma}^{\mathrm{SOU}}f(\mathfrak{X})\big] = 0 ~~\forall f\in C_{\mathcal{A}_{M,\Psi,\Sigma}^{\mathrm{SOU}}}^2(\mathcal{S}^d),
\]
where, for $\mathfrak{Z}\sim \mathcal{SN}_{d\times d}(M,\Psi,\Sigma)$,
\[
C_{\mathcal{A}_{M,\Psi,\Sigma}^{\mathrm{SOU}}}^2(\mathcal{S}^d)
\leqdef \Big\{f\in C^2(\mathcal{S}^d) \, : \, \EE\big[|\tr\{(M-\mathfrak{Z})\nabla f(\mathfrak{Z})\}|\big] < \infty, ~\EE\big[|\tr\{\Psi\nabla\Sigma\nabla f(\mathfrak{Z})\}|\big] < \infty \Big\}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\]
Then
\[
        \theta_{n,M}:=\sum_{u=1}^{M}\Pbb(E_u=1\mid E_0=1)\to0.

More quantitatively,
\[
        \theta_{n,M}=O\left(\frac{\log M}{\lambda_{n,M}}\right)=o(1).
\]

[Corollary of arXiv:2505.09839, '\textbf{Density Frankl–Rödl on the Sphere}'] Let \( (v_1, \dots, v_k) \) be an inductive configuration with covariance matrix \( R \), and assume that
\[
\norm{v_k - v_{k-1}}_2 \neq \operatorname{diam}\left(\bigcap_{j < k-1} S_{v_j, r_j}\right).
\]
Then $R$ is sphere Ramsey (for measurable colorings). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Independently checked by w389; draft concept only. For any finite nonnegative weights on Z^2 let B_n={||x||_infinity<=n}, S_n={||x||_infinity=n}, and E_n be existence of a simple GLOBAL geodesic through0 with endpoints on S_n and all other vertices in B_(n-1). Then E_(n+1) is a subset of E_n, and their intersection equals existence of a bigeodesic through0. Stop each arm at its first boundary hit for restriction; consistent central finite strings follow by finite-degree diagonal compactness. Consequently P(bigeodesic through0)=lim P(E_n). Under translation invariance, absence everywhere is equivalent to this limit being0. This reduction supplies no decay bound or novelty claim.
Finite nonnegative weights
Global minimizing metric, not a restricted box metric
Simple paths
Translation invariance only for the everywhere conclusion

body:
[Ppn 256 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] In both the spherical and Ising settings, there exists $c>0$ and $C = C(\alpha) > 0$ such that the following holds.
    Let $\cA^\circ$ be a $L$-Lipschitz algorithm with $L\ge 1$.
    Let $\chi^\circ \equiv \chi_{\cA^\circ}$ and $q_0 \equiv \chi^\circ(0)$, and suppose $q_0 < 1$.
    Then, there exists an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm $\cA$ such that the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item $\chi \equiv \chi_{\cA}$ satisfies $\chi(0) = q_0$ and
    \[
        \chi'(0) \ge  \frac1{L^2}\,.
    \]
In fact, we can take
    \[
        \chi(p) = \bigg(1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg) \chi^\circ(p)+ \frac{q_0 + (1-q_0)p}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,.
    \]

\item 
The perturbed algorithm $\cA$ approximates the original algorithm $\cA^\circ$ in the sense that
    \[
        \frac{1}{N} \E\Big[\|\cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) - \cA(\bG,\bg^{\aux})\|^2\Big]
        \le \frac{2}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,.
    \]

\end{enumerate}
We remark that the above error should be considered small, since we will prove later in Lemma~\ref{l:sM.Lip.1.trivial} that a sequence of algorithms with $q_0$ tending to one can only achieve the gaussian distribution.

\begin{proof} 
Let $\dot{\bg}$ be a standard gaussian in $\bbR^N$ independent of $\bg^{\aux}$, and
let $\bv$ be a deterministic element of $S_N$ with 
 $(\bv,\bbE \cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux})) = 0$. The perturbed algorithm $\cA$ is defined by
    \[\cA(\bG, (\bg^{\aux}, \dot{\bg} )) 
        = \bigg\{1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2}
            \bigg\}^{1/2}
        \cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) 
        + \bigg(\frac{q_0}{1-q_0}\bigg)^{1/2} \frac{\bv}{L}
        + \frac{\dot{\bg}}{L} \,.
    \]
Then the gradient of $\cA$ can be bounded as
    \begin{align*}
        \|\nabla\cA
            (\bG,(\bg^{\aux}, \dot{\bg})) \|^2
        &= \|\nabla_{\bG,\bg^{\aux}}
            \cA(\bG,(\bg^{\aux}, \dot{\bg} )) \|^2
        + \|\nabla_{\dot{\bg}} 
            \cA(\bG,(\bg^{\aux},\dot{\bg})) \|^2 \\
        &\le \bigg\{1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0) L^2}   \bigg\} L^2 
            + \frac1{L^2}
        \le L^2\,.
    \end{align*}
Since $\bv$ is deterministic and orthogonal to $\bbE \cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux})$,
 $\dot{\bg}$ is independent of $(\bG,\bg^{\aux})$, and $\bbE[\|\dot{\bg}\|^2] = N$, we have
    \[\frac{\bbE[
             \|\cA(\bG,(\bg^{\aux},\dot{\bg}))\|^2]}{N}
    =\bigg\{ 1-\frac1{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg\}
    	+\frac{q_0}{(1-q_0)L^2}
	+\frac{1}{L^2}
    = 1\,,
    \]
where the last step follows from the trivial inequality $1-q_0\le1\le L^2$.  The above two displays show that $\cA$ is an $L$-Lipschitz algorithm in the sense of Definition~\ref{d:Lip}. Moreover, recalling the abbreviations $\chi\equiv\chi_\cA$ and $\chi^\circ\equiv\chi_{\cA^\circ}$, for any $0\le p\le1$ we have
    \[\chi(p) 
    = \bigg(1-\frac1{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg) \chi^\circ(p) + \frac{q_0+(1-q_0)p}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,,
    \]
which implies $\chi(0)=q_0$.
   As noted above, $\chi^\circ$ is nondecreasing, which implies $\chi'(0)\ge 1/L^2$. This proves part~\eqref{it:wlogable.PERTURBED.CHI}. 

Next, since $|a^{1/2}-b^{1/2}| \le |a-b|^{1/2}$ for all $a,b\ge0$, we can bound
    \begin{align*}
        \frac{1}{N} \E\bigg[\Big\|\cA^\circ(\bG,\bg^{\aux}) - \cA(\bG,\bg^{\aux})\Big\|^2\bigg]
        &= \bigg(1 - \bigg(1-\frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2}\bigg)^{1/2}\bigg)^2
        + \frac{q_0}{(1-q_0)L^2} + \frac{1}{L^2} \\
        &\le \frac{1}{(1-q_0)L^2} + \frac{q_0}{(1-q_0)L^2} + \frac{1}{L^2}
        = \frac{2}{(1-q_0)L^2}\,.
    \end{align*}
This proves part~\eqref{it:wlogable.PERTURBED.APPX}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 27 of arXiv:2605.16560, 'Seasonal Statistics of Shannon Rate in a Dynamical Poisson-Voronoi Cellular Network'] The following comparison of the coverage probabilities holds true for any QoS $\tau\geq 0$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item   with or without fading: 
$p_{\sst \Vcal}^c  \leq p_{t}^c \leq p_{\sst S}^c$ and $p^c_{\sst \Ical}  \leq p^c_{\sst I}$,
\item  with fading: $p_{\sst{\Vcal;\Tcal}}^c  \leq p_{\sst{t;\Tcal}}^c \leq p_{{\sst S;\Tcal}}^c$ and $p^c_{{\sst \Ical;\Tcal}}  \leq p^c_{{\sst I;\Tcal}}$,

\item  without fading:  $p^c_{{\sst \Ical;\Tcal}}  \leq p^c_{{\sst I;\Tcal}}$.

\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 71 (Localization remainder) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $\mathcal R^{a;b,c}_{\Lambda,N,R,Q,M}(t,s)$ denote the sum over the
finitely many outer stochastic shells $L\sim_{\mathrm{ap}}R$ of a centered
block in one of the following two sectors:
\begin{equation}
 R\not\sim_{\mathrm{tr}}N,
 \qquad\text{or}\qquad
 R\sim_{\mathrm{tr}}N\ \text{ and }\ M>C_{\mathrm{out}}N.
\end{equation}
For every $2\le p<\infty$, every $A>0$, and every
$0<\theta\le1/2$,
\begin{align}
 \|\mathcal R^{a;b,c}_{\Lambda,N,R,Q,M}(t,s)\|_{
 L^p_\omega\mathcal L(L_q^2,L_n^2)}
 &\lesssim_{p,A}\la N+R+M\ra^{-A},
 \\
 \|\mathcal R^{a;b,c}_{\Lambda,N,R,Q,M}(t,s)
 -\mathcal R^{a;b,c}_{\Lambda,N,R,Q,M}(t',s')\|_{
 L^p_\omega\mathcal L(L_q^2,L_n^2)}
 &\lesssim_{p,A,\theta}\la N+R+M\ra^{-A}
 (|t-t'|+|s-s'|)^\theta.
 
\end{align}
The estimates are uniform in the spectral cutoff.  Cutoff differences obey
the same majorants and converge on every fixed block.  For a fixed-profile
dyadic family, the supremum over all cutoff levels may be placed inside each
finite $L^p(\Omega)$ norm in \eqref{eq:localization-tail-block} and
\eqref{eq:localization-tail-increment}.  Consequently, the sum of the
remainder blocks converges after the insertion of arbitrary fixed polynomial
Sobolev or Besov weights, in particular in every operator topology used in
Theorem~\ref{thm:localized-centered}.  Along a fixed-profile dyadic family,
the full remainder sequence converges almost surely, without a subsequence,
on a probability-one event that may be intersected with
$\Omega_{\mathrm{cen}}$.  For every interval $I\subset[0,T_0]$, its
zero-history restriction is causal and maps $E_{I,0}^{2,\sigma}$ to
$L^1(I;B_{2,\infty}^{\sigma-1})$ with norm $O_\omega(|I|^2)$, uniformly over
the limit and all cutoff levels on that event.  In particular, its
initial-interval operator norm tends to zero as $T\downarrow0$.

[Lemma lem:hypE of arXiv:2412.01381, 'Ergodicity and mixing for locally monotone stochastic evolution equations'] If $A=A_0+F$ where $A_0=-\partial \Phi$ is the subgradient of a lower semi-continuous convex functional $\Phi:V\to \mathbb{R}$ such that $\inf_{u\in V}\Phi(u)>-\infty$, and $F:V\to V^\ast$ is a strongly measurable (nonlinear) operator.
Suppose that
for some constants $\kappa_1\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$, $K_1\in\mathbb{R}$
that for every $u\in V$,
\begin{equation}\|F (u)\|_{V^\ast}\le \kappa_1\langle A_0 u,u\rangle+K_1.\end{equation}
Furthermore, suppose that for some constants $K_2,\kappa_2\in\mathbb{R}$, for every $u\in V$, 
\begin{equation}2\langle F(u),u\rangle\le\kappa_2\|F (u)\|_{V^\ast}+K_2,\end{equation}
or that
\begin{equation}2\langle F(u),u\rangle\le\kappa_2\langle A_0 u,u\rangle+K_2,\end{equation}
where, in the second case, we additionally assume that $\kappa_2\in (-2,\infty)$, whenever $\kappa_1<0$.
Then $A$ satisfies Hypothesis~(hyp:angle of the paper).
title: Lemma lem:hypE of arXiv:2412.01381

[Lemma 15 (Change of variables) of arXiv:2604.21389, 'Existence and uniqueness for \\ singular stochastic differential equations \\ with piecewi'] Let Hypothesis~\hypref{hyp:nu} and assume that $b$ and $\sigma$ are measurable and locally bounded.

For every $(X,B)$, weak non-explosive solution to~\eqref{eqn:SDE_general}, let $I$ denote the smallest interval such that~$X_t\in I$ for all $t\geq 0$ $\mathbb{P}$-a.s.. Then $(\Phi_\nu(X),B)$ is a weak non-explosive solution to the classical SDE
\begin{equation}
Y_t=\Phi_\nu(x_0)+\int_0^t \widetilde b(Y_s)\,\vd s+\int_0^t \widetilde\sigma(Y_s)\,\vd B_s,
\qquad t\ge 0.
\end{equation}
Moreover $\Phi_\nu(X)\in J$ for all $t\geq 0$ $\mathbb{P}$-a.s..

Conversely, if $(Y,B)$ is a weak non-explosive solution to~\eqref{eq:SDE_no_nu} and $Y_t\in J$ for all $t\geq 0$ $\mathbb{P}$-a.s., then $(\Psi_\nu(Y),B)$ is a weak non-explosive solution to~\eqref{eqn:SDE_general} and $\Psi_\nu(Y_t)\in I$ for all $t\geq 0$ $\mathbb{P}$-a.s.. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Theorem 20 of arXiv:2609.00209, 'Exit Times for Brownian Motion and Location Detection'] Assume $\mathcal R=(0,a)\times (0,b)$ is a rectangular domain with $a<b$. Let $u_k(x,y)=\mathbb{E}^{(x,y)}[\tau_{\mathcal R}^k]$ denote the exit time moments for $k\geq 1$. Let (X_{n, k})_{1 \le k \le r_n, n \ge 1} be a triangular array of row-wise independent random variables with \mathbb{E}[X_{n, k}] = 0 and \sigma_{n, k}^2 = \mathbb{E}[X_{n, k}^2] < \infty. Set s_n^2 = \sum_{k=1}^{r_n} \sigma_{n, k}^2. The array satisfies the Lindeberg condition if for every \epsilon > 0, \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{1}{s_n^2} \sum_{k=1}^{r_n} \mathbb{E}\left[ X_{n, k}^2 \mathbf{1}_{\{|X_{n, k}| > \epsilon s_n\}} \right] = 0.
X_{n, k} row-wise independent, mean zero, finite variance
title: Lindeberg Condition for Triangular Arrays

body: Fix an effective enumeration phi_0, phi_1, phi_2, ... of all partial computable functions, so phi_e is the function computed by program number e. Kleene's recursion theorem states that for every total computable function f there exists an index e, a fixed point, such that phi_e equals phi_{f(e)}: program e computes exactly the function computed by the program obtained by applying f to e. This yields self-referential programs that can effectively obtain and use their own index or source code during execution, and underlies proofs of Rice's theorem and other diagonalization arguments. Proved by Stephen Kleene in 1938.
title: Kleene's recursion theorem

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). Let mu be a probability measure on a finite distributive lattice satisfying the FKG lattice condition mu(x v y) mu(x ^ y) >= mu(x) mu(y) for all x, y, a condition automatically satisfied by any product measure on {0,1}^E, in which case the conclusion is called the Harris inequality. Then for any two increasing (or two decreasing) functions f, g in L^2(mu), E[fg] >= E[f]E[g]; equivalently, for increasing events A, B, mu(A ^ B) >= mu(A) mu(B), so increasing events are positively correlated. This is the basic monotone-coupling tool throughout percolation and interacting particle systems, lower-bounding joint probabilities of increasing events, such as several disjoint crossings occurring together, by the product of their individual probabilities, and it justifies a wide range of comparison and sprinkling arguments. It does not give any upper bound on the correlation, which requires separate and generally harder tools such as the van den Berg-Kesten inequality for disjoint occurrence; it does not apply to a mix of an increasing and a decreasing event without flipping a sign; and the strength of the positive correlation is not quantified beyond nonnegativity. Typical failure: Applying FKG to a pair of events where one is increasing and the other decreasing without flipping the sign, which reverses the direction of the inequality; or invoking FKG for a non-product Gibbs measure, such as a random-cluster model outside the ferromagnetic regime with cluster weight q<1, without checking the lattice condition, which is known to fail there. Canonical reference: Fortuin, Kasteleyn and Ginibre, 1971, Communications in Mathematical Physics; Harris, 1960, Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society.
mu satisfies the FKG lattice condition, automatic for independent product measures but requiring verification for dependent Gibbs measures
f, g, or the events A, B, are both increasing, or both decreasing, with respect to the same partial order

body: [Definition 11 (Definition 3.5\cite{AbbeBoix2020}) of arXiv:2607.21392, 'Gaussian Convexity Principles for Sharp Moderate Deviations of Gaussian Maxima and Critica'] Let \(\mathcal{G}=(V,E)\) be a finite graph. For each edge \(e=\{i,j\}\in E\), let \(Q_e(\cdot\mid\cdot)\)   be a probability kernel from the binary input alphabet \(\{-1,+1\}\) to a measurable output space \((\mathsf Y_e,\mathcal A_e)\). We write $Q_{e,+}(\cdot)=Q_e(\cdot\mid +1),  Q_{e,-}(\cdot)=Q_e(\cdot\mid -1).$ The associated graphical channel is the channel from \(\{-1,+1\}^V\) to \(\prod_{e\in E}\mathsf Y_e\) defined as follows: given \(x=(x_v)_{v\in V}\in\{-1,+1\}^V\), the edge observations \((Y_e)_{e\in E}\) are conditionally independent, and for \(e=\{i,j\}\), $Y_e \sim Q_e(\cdot\mid x_i x_j).$ We say that the edge channel \(Q_e\) is symmetric if there exists a measurable involution $T_e:\mathsf Y_e\to \mathsf Y_e, T_e^{-1}=T_e,$ such that for every \(A\in\mathcal A_e\), \[ Q_e(A\mid +1)=Q_e(T_e(A)\mid -1). \] Equivalently, since \(T_e\) is an involution, \[ Q_e(T_e(A)\mid +1)=Q_e(A\mid -1), \qquad A\in\mathcal A_e. \] The graphical channel is called symmetric if \(Q_e\) is symmetric for every \(e\in E\).
title: Definition 3.5\cite{AbbeBoix2020}

body:
Let Ω ⊂ R^n be open, 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ and k ≥ 1 an integer. W^{k,p}(Ω) is the set of u ∈ L^p(Ω) all of whose distributional derivatives D^α u with |α| ≤ k lie in L^p(Ω): for each α there is g_α ∈ L^p(Ω) with ∫_Ω u D^α φ dx = (−1)^{|α|} ∫_Ω g_α φ dx for every φ ∈ C_c^∞(Ω); one writes D^α u = g_α (the weak derivative, unique a.e.). The norm is ||u||_{W^{k,p}} = ( Σ_{|α| ≤ k} ||D^α u||_{L^p}^p )^{1/p} (maximum over α for p = ∞). W^{k,p}(Ω) is a Banach space, separable for p < ∞ and reflexive for 1 < p < ∞. H^k(Ω) := W^{k,2}(Ω) is a Hilbert space with ⟨u, v⟩ = Σ_{|α| ≤ k} ∫_Ω D^α u D^α v dx. W^{k,p}_0(Ω) is the closure of C_c^∞(Ω) in W^{k,p}(Ω) (functions 'vanishing on the boundary' together with derivatives of order < k); H^1_0(Ω) := W^{1,2}_0(Ω). The Sobolev conjugate of p < n is p* = np/(n − p), i.e. 1/p* = 1/p − 1/n.

Facts: C^∞(Ω) ∩ W^{k,p}(Ω) is dense in W^{k,p}(Ω) for p < ∞ and any open Ω (Meyers–Serrin); restrictions of C^∞(R^n) functions are dense when Ω is bounded with Lipschitz boundary; W^{k,p}_0(R^n) = W^{k,p}(R^n); for bounded Ω, W^{1,p}_0(Ω) is a proper closed subspace of W^{1,p}(Ω) (nonzero constants are excluded by the Poincaré inequality). On an interval, W^{1,p} functions have absolutely continuous representatives; in dimension n ≥ 2 a W^{1,p} function with p ≤ n can be unbounded and discontinuous. For a bounded Lipschitz domain, W^{1,∞}(Ω) is the space of Lipschitz functions on Ω̄.
Ω ⊂ R^n open; derivatives taken in the distributional sense
title: Sobolev spaces W^{k,p}(Ω), W^{k,p}_0(Ω), H^k(Ω)

body: In computational complexity theory, NP-complete problems are the hardest of the problems to which solutions can be verified quickly. Somewhat more precisely, a problem is NP-complete when:It is a decision problem, meaning that for any input to the problem, the output is either "yes" or "no". Each input to the problem is associated with a collection of short solutions, which might or might not validly solve the input. The output is "yes" when at least one of these solutions is valid, and "no" when none of them are. The validity of each solution can be verified quickly, and a brute-force search algorithm can find a valid solution by trying all possible solutions. The problem can be used to simulate every other problem for which we can verify quickly that a solution is valid. Hence, if we could find valid solutions of some NP-complete problem quickly, we could quickly find valid solutions for every other problem in which a given solution can be easily verified.
title: NP-completeness

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The number of fixed points of permutations,
$$\chi(\sigma)=\#\left\{i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\Big|\sigma(i)=i\right\}$$ 
when regarded as random variable $\chi:S_N\to\mathbb N$, satisfies the formula
$$\chi\sim p_1$$

body:
[Definition ARTASS of arXiv:2603.12774, 'Synchronization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Browni'] Let \((\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P}, \theta)\) be a measurable metric dynamical system, and let \(\mathcal{X}\) be a Polish space.
	\begin{itemize}
		\item A random variable \(Y : \Omega \rightarrow (0, \infty)\) is called \emph{tempered} if
		\begin{align*}
			\limsup_{|t| \to \infty,\, t \in \mathbb{T}} \frac{1}{|t|} \log^{+} Y(\theta_t \omega) = 0,
			\quad \text{for } \mathbb{P}\text{-almost every } \omega \in \Omega,
		\end{align*}
		where \(\log^{+} x := \max\{ \log x, 0 \}\).
		
		\item Let \(\mathcal{E}=\{\mathcal{E}(\omega)\}_{\omega \in \Omega}\) be a family of non-empty subsets of \(\mathcal{X}\) such that, for every \(x \in \mathcal{X}\), the function \(\omega \mapsto d(x, \mathcal{E}(\omega))\) is measurable, and with probability one each \(\mathcal{E}(\omega)\) is bounded in \(\mathcal{X}\). We call \(\mathcal{E}\) a {tempered set} if the random variable
		\[
		r(\mathcal{E}(\omega)) := \sup_{x \in \mathcal{E}(\omega)} d(x, x_0)
		\]
		is tempered for some fixed reference point \(x_0 \in \mathcal{X}\). The collection of tempered sets in $\mathcal{X}$ is denoted by $\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{X})$.
	\end{itemize}

[Lemma lem:tight2 of arXiv:2507.19554, 'Full extremal process in four-dimensional membrane model'] There are constants $c_3, c_4 \in (0, \infty)$ such that the following is true for all $\epsilon, \delta > 0$ that are sufficiently small: 
			Set $\sigma := -\frac{\log \delta}{\epsilon}$, given $\lambda > 0$ and $\ell \in \mbN$, and define
			\bequn
				\lambda' := \lambda + c_4(1 + \log \sigma +  \sqrt{\log(\ell/\delta)\log \sigma}).
			\eequn
			If for some $N' \geq 1$, 
			\bequn
				\mbP(S_{\ell, N'} < \ell(m_N- \lambda')) > \delta,
			\eequn
			then 
			\bequn
				\mbP(|A_{N, \lambda}| > \ell ) < \epsilon
			\eequn
			holds for all $N \in \mbN$ with $N \leq c_3 \sigma^{-1/2}N'.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 10 (Lemma 2.7 in 
\cite{CNN23}) of arXiv:2605.31568, 'Lipschitz continuity of the time constant for continuum percolation'] Let $(Y_{\mathbf{z}})_{\mathbf{z} \in \Z^d}$ be a family of $\mathbb{N}$-valued random variables indexed by $\Z^d$. Let $A \ge 1$. Suppose that for each $N\ge1$ and each $AN$-separated subset $S$ of $\Z^d$, the family $\{Y_\mathcal{\mathbf{z}} = N\}_{\mathbf{z} \in S}$ is independent. Define $q_N := \sup_{\mathbf{z} \in \Z^d} \P(Y_\mathbf{z} = N)$. Suppose for some $B<\infty$ we have $\sum_{N=0}^\infty N^{d+2}q_N^{1/d} \le B$. Then there exists $C$ depending only on $d, A,$ and $B$ such that the following holds. For any random path $\Pi$ in $\Z^d$ starting from $0$
such that every vertex of the path has $l^\infty$-distance 1 from the preceding vertex, and any $L \in \mathbb{N}$ we have
\[
\E[\sum_{\mathbf{z} \in \Pi}Y_\mathbf{z}] \le CL + C\sum_{\ell \ge L} \ell \P(|\Pi| = \ell)^{1/2}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2607.25645, 'Estimates of the total variation distance between laws of Sobolev mappings on Gaussian spa'] Let $k\in\mathbb N$, let $p>6k$, let $\varkappa\in(0,1)$, and let $a,b>0$. Set
\[
\beta:=\frac{p\varkappa}{p+2k\varkappa}.
\]
Assume that $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)$ and $g=(g_1,\ldots,g_k)$
with $
f_j,g_j\in W^{2,p}(\gamma)$,
satisfy
\[
\max_{1\le j\le k}\|f_j\|_{\dot W^{2,p}(\gamma)}\le b,
\quad
\max_{1\le j\le k}\|g_j\|_{\dot W^{2,p}(\gamma)}\le b,
\]
and
\[
\gamma(\Delta_f\le s)\le as^\varkappa
\quad \forall\, s>0.
\]
Then
\[
d_{\rm TV}(f,g)
\le
176k^4(1-\varkappa)^{-1}
\bigl(a^{1/\varkappa}b^{2k-1}\max_{1\le j\le k}\|f_j-g_j\|_{W^{1,p}(\gamma)}\bigr)^\beta.
\]

body:
[Lemma lem:dual_3moment of arXiv:2604.20094, 'Persistence and local extinction for superprocesses in random environments'] For any $T>0$, there exists $C(T) > 0$
independent of $n$ and $x$ such that
$$
\sup_{n\geqslant 1}\sup_{t\in[0,T]} {\mathbf E} \left[(Y_t^{(n)}(x))^3\right] \leqslant C(T) \phi^3_\rho(x) \quad \hbox{ for every }  x\in {\mathbb R}^d.
$$
Consequently,
$$
\sup_{n\geqslant 1}\sup_{t\in[0,T]} {\mathbf E} \left[ Y_t^{(n)}(x) Y_t^{(n)}(y) \right]\leqslant C(T) \phi_\rho(x) \phi_\rho(y)
\quad \hbox{ for every }  x,y\in {\mathbb R}^d.
$$
title: Third Moment Estimate for the Dual Process

[Thm 2 (Exponential decay of correlations) of arXiv:2605.21638, 'Markov renewal theory for transfer operators and point processes on the line'] Let $(Z_n)_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ be a stationary process sequence that satisfies Assumptions \ref{ass:markov}-\ref{MAssu:Inversion} and let  $(X_n)_{n\in \Z}$ be defined as in~\eqref{eq:defX}.  Then the point process $\Phi$ with Palm version $\Phi^0=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} \delta_{X_n}$ satisfies the following:  there exists $\epsilon >0$ such that, for all bounded intervals $A,B \subset \R$,

body:
[Lemma lem:orderSclosed of arXiv:2603.16824, 'Age-dependent random connection models with arc reciprocity: clustering and connectivity'] Assume \(\gamma\in[1/2,1)\) and consider \(S^c(t_o)\) as defined in~(equation eq:defSclosed of the paper). 
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
	\item 
		If \(\Gamma>0\), we have
		\begin{equation*}
			\int\limits_{1/(t\log t)}^1 S^c(t_o)\,\mathrm{d} t_o
			=
			\begin{cases}
				O(1), & \gamma<2/3,
				\\
				O(\log t), & \gamma=2/3,
				\\
				O((t\log t)^{3\gamma-2}), & 2/3<\gamma<1.
			\end{cases}
		\end{equation*}
	\item
		If \(\Gamma=0\), we have instead
		\[
			\int\limits_{1/(t\log t)}^1 S^c(t_o)\,\mathrm{d} t_o
			=
			\begin{cases}
				O(1), &  \gamma<2/3,
				\\
				O(\log t), & \gamma =2/3
				\\
				O((t\log t)^{3-2/\gamma}), & \gamma>2/3.
			\end{cases}
		\]
		In particular, for all \(\gamma>2/3\), we have \(\int_{1/(t\log t)}^1 S^c(t_o)\,\mathrm{d} t_o=o((t\log t)^{2\gamma-1})\).
\end{enumerate}
title: Lemma lem:orderSclosed of arXiv:2603.16824

[Theorem branched_covers_lift.thm of arXiv:2609.00163, 'Decompositions and diagrams of symplectic surfaces in Weinstein domains'] Let $(W,S)$ be a symplectic surface in the Weinstein domain $(W,\omega)$ equipped with a bridge-multisection-with-divides structure $(W,S)=(W_1,\mathcal{D}_1)\cup \ldots \cup (W_n,\mathcal{D}_n)$. Suppose that $S$ is the branching set of a smooth branched cover $f:(W',S')\rightarrow (W,S)$.  Then $(W',S')=(f^{-1}(W_1),f^{-1}(\mathcal{D}_1))\cup \ldots \cup (f^{-1}(W_n),f^{-1}(\mathcal{D}_n))$ is a bridge multisection of $S'=f^{-1}(S)$ in a Weinstein domain $(W',\omega')$, with fillings of each $(f^{-1}(W_i),\omega'|_{f^{-1}(W_i)}
)$ uniquely determined by $f$ and $(W_i,\omega|_{W_i})$. In particular, $f$ is a branched cover of Weinstein fillings.
title: Theorem branched_covers_lift.thm of arXiv:2609.00163

body:
[Proposition 26 (Compatibility with same-field decoupling) of arXiv:2607.16724, 'Algebraic Transfer for Operator-Valued Gaussian Chaoses: Oriented Schatten Profiles and Si'] Let $K$ and $L$ be symmetric finite-support algebraic same-field kernels of
orders $m$ and $n$.
For every cross pairing $P$ and $1\le r<\infty$,
\begin{equation}

 \norm{\operatorname{Sym}_{q(P)}(L\circ_PK)}
       _{\mathfrak W_{q(P),r}}
 \le
 \norm L_{\mathfrak W_{n,r}}\norm K_{\mathfrak W_{m,r}},
\end{equation}
where $\operatorname{Sym}_0=\Id$.  Consequently,
\[
 (L,K)\longmapsto\operatorname{Sym}_{q(P)}(L\circ_PK)
\]
extends uniquely to a contractive bilinear map from
$\mathfrak W_{n,r}\times\mathfrak W_{m,r}$ to
$\mathfrak W_{q(P),r}$.  The extension is independent of the labelled
copies used to define the three same-field completions.

body:
[Proposition RS.thm of arXiv:2605.17725, 'Limit theorems for random walks with spatio-temporal drift'] Let $(X_n)_{n\ge0}, (Y_n)_{n\ge0},  (\alpha_n)_{n\ge0}, (\beta_n)_{n\ge0}$ be sequences of nonnegative random variables adapted to $(\mathcal{F}_n)$ such that
     $$\mathbb{E}[X_{n+1} \mid \mathcal{F}_n] \le (1 + \alpha_n) X_n + \beta_n - Y_n, \quad \text{a.s.}$$
Then,  on the event $\Big\{\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \alpha_n < \infty \quad \text{and} \quad \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \beta_n < \infty\Big\}$, we have:
 \begin{itemize}
     \item  $X_{n}$ converges a.s. to a finite random variable $X_{\infty}$;
     \item  $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} Y_n < \infty$ a.s.
 \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 6 (Endpoint-conditioned objective) of arXiv:2608.29107, 'PathGuide: Dynamic Classifier-Free Guidance via On-Policy Transport Alignment'] Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:conditional-path-regularity}
and~\ref{ass:endpoint-posterior}, the signed quantity in
\eqref{eq:app-local-objective} admits the endpoint-conditioned form
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
    G_i(\omega_i\mid y;\vec\omega_i,\psi)
    =
    \int_{\R^d}
    \int_{\R^d}
    &
    \Bigl(
        u_{t_i}(x\mid x_1,y)
        -
        v_{t_i}^\theta(x\mid y;\omega_i)
    \Bigr)
    \cdot \grad\psi(x)
    \\
    &\times
    \pi_{t_i}(x_1\mid x,y)\,
    \hat p_{t_i}(x\mid y;\vec\omega_i)
    \,\dd x_1\,\dd x .
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Consequently, \(\mathcal L_i\) can be evaluated from endpoint-conditioned
velocities and posterior endpoint weights, which proves
Theorem~\ref{thm:endpoint-conditioned-objective}.

[Theorem 3 (Asymptotic validity and power of the test) of arXiv:2608.29465, 'Deciding When to Decide:\\Testing Operational Suboptimality Under Distributional Shift'] Suppose the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:delta_hat_rate} and the local inverse-stability condition in Assumption~\ref{assm:error_bound_P0} hold, and suppose the conditional CLT in Assumption~\ref{ass:eval_clt} holds. Let
\[
a_n:=n^{-1/(2\kappa)}
\]
denote the preference-estimation error rate. If $\delta_{\rm inv}=0$ and $\sqrt{m''}\,a_n\to0$, then the Wald test in \eqref{eq:T_wald} has asymptotic level $\alpha$:
\[
\limsup_{n,m',m''\to\infty}
\Pr\{\mathrm{reject}\ H_0\}
\le \alpha
\qquad
\text{whenever } \Delta^\star\le \tau .
\]
Without this relative-rate condition, the same conclusion holds on any fixed-margin null $\Delta^\star\le\tau-\eta$, $\eta>0$. More generally, if $\delta_{\rm inv}>0$, the unadjusted test controls Type-I error on the separated null $\Delta^\star\le\tau-\delta_{\rm inv}-\eta$. Under the alternative, for any fixed $\eta>0$, if $\Delta^\star\ge \tau+\delta_{\rm inv}+\eta$, then
\[
\lim_{n,m',m''\to\infty}
\Pr\{\mathrm{reject}\ H_0\} = 1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Asymptotic validity and power of the test

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2605.16733, 'Concentration Inequalities for Sample Cross-Covariances'] Let \((X_i)_{i=1}^N\) be i.i.d. copies of a centered Gaussian random
vector \(X\in\mathbb R^{d_X}\) with covariance matrix \(\Sigma_X\), and let
\(L\) be a fixed matrix such that $        P:=L\Sigma_XL^\top $ is nonzero. Then
\[
\E \left\|
\bigg( \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N
X_iX_i^\top -\E XX^\top\bigg) L^\top
\right\|
\gtrsim
(\|\Sigma_X\|\|P\|)^{1/2}
\bigg(
\sqrt{\frac{r_X+r_P}{N}}
+
\frac{\sqrt{r_Xr_P}}{N}
\bigg),
\]
where
\[
r_X:=\frac{\tr(\Sigma_X)}{\|\Sigma_X\|},
\qquad
r_P:=\frac{\tr(P)}{\|P\|}.

[Proposition 23 of arXiv:2609.03951, 'Generalized Semi-Riemannian Submersions and Foliations'] If $\pi: (M,g) \to (B,\mathcal{D},h)$ is a generalized semi-Riemannian submersion such that $\mathcal{D}$ is integrable, then there exists $V_0 \in \mathfrak{X}(\mathcal{R})$ such that   
\[
\nabla_{\tilde{X}} \tilde{Y} = \widetilde{\nabla^h_X Y} + \frac{1}{2} ([\tilde{X},\tilde{Y}] - \widetilde{[X,Y]}) + V_0
\]
for all $X,Y \in \mathfrak{X}(\mathcal{D})$, where $\tilde{X}, \tilde{Y}$, and $\widetilde{\nabla^h_X Y}$ are their respective horizontal lifts.

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Check which ingredients of the q = 2 proof are available for other q. Result: The q = 2 proof uses (i) the parafermionic observable being discretely holomorphic (full Cauchy-Riemann), (ii) RSW-type crossing estimates for tightness, (iii) identification of the limit via the martingale observable. For q in (1,4) not 2: (ii) is available (Duminil-Copin-Sidoravicius-Tassion 2017 for q in [1,4]); (iii) would follow from (i); (i) fails: for general q the observable satisfies only the contour relations (half of the Cauchy-Riemann equations), the same obstruction as in C0017. So the conjecture is reduced, for q in [1,4], exactly to finding an additional discrete relation for the parafermionic observable; the count of unknowns versus equations (one complex relation per face versus two needed) is the precise deficit. For q < 1 even RSW is unavailable. No new relation found. Obstruction: Discrete holomorphicity is only half-satisfied for q not 2.

Let U subset R^n be open, and Lu = -sum_{i,j=1}^n partial_j(a^{ij}(x) partial_i u) a divergence-form second-order elliptic operator with a^{ij} in C^1(U), symmetric, and uniformly elliptic on U (there is theta>0 with sum_{i,j} a^{ij}(x)xi_i xi_j >= theta|xi|^2 for all x in U, xi in R^n). Suppose u in H^1(U) is a weak solution of Lu=f on U for some f in L^2(U): integral_U sum a^{ij} partial_i u partial_j v dx = integral_U f v dx for all v in C_c^infinity(U). Then u in H^2_loc(U): for every open V with compact closure in U, u in H^2(V), with ||u||_{H^2(V)} <= C(||f||_{L^2(U)} + ||u||_{L^2(U)}) for a constant C depending only on n, theta, V, U and the C^1 norms of the a^{ij}. (If a^{ij} in C^{k+1}(U) and f in H^k(U), then u in H^{k+2}_loc(U) with the analogous estimate; if the coefficients and f are C^infinity, u is C^infinity in the interior.)

[Lemma lem:se-sojourn of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix $\lambda \in (0,1/3)$. Let $\overline{p}$ be a send sequence with $p_0=1$ such that, for all positive integers~$x$, $W_x \le (6/\lambda)^x$. 
Let $i$ be a sufficiently large integer and suppose that bin~$i$ is a bottleneck. 
Let $U = (U^A,U^B,U^C)$ be the under-backoff process with birth rate~$3\lambda$ and send sequence~$\overline{p}$.
Then the expected sojourn time of $U$ from the empty state back to the empty state is at least $e^{{i}^{1/2}}$.

[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2604.12233, 'An upper bound on the smallest singular value of dense random combinatorial matrices'] Let $p\in (0, 1/2]$ be a fixed constant.
     Let $1\le d\le n$ be integers such that $d=pn$. Let $M$ be a random $m\times n$ matrix, $1\le m\le n$, whose rows are independent random $0/1$ vectors having exactly $d$ ones. Then there exist constants $C_{\ref{lem: operatornrm_Tran}}>0$ and $c_{\ref{lem: operatornrm_Tran}}>0$ depending only on $p$ such that 
    for all $t\ge C_{\ref{lem: operatornrm_Tran}}$ one has
    \[
    \P\lr{\|M-\E M\|\ge t\sqrt{pn}}\le 2e^{-c_{\ref{lem: operatornrm_Tran}}t^2n }.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:W_n of arXiv:2604.04922, 'Elephant random walk on the infinite dihedral group $\mathbb{Z}_2 * \mathbb{Z}_2$'] We have the following.
    \begin{enumerate}
    \setlength{\itemsep}{5pt}
        \item [(a)] [bercu2017martingale] For $p \in [0, 3/4)$, we have
        \[
            \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{|W_n|}{\sqrt{2n\log \log n}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3 - 4p}}, a.s.
        \]
        \item [(b)] [bercu2017martingale] For $p = 3/4$, we have
        \[
            \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{|W_n|}{\sqrt{2n\log n \log \log \log n}} = 1, a.s.
        \]
        \item [(c)] [bercu2017martingale] For $p \in (3/4, 1)$, we have
        \[
            n^{-q} |W_n| \xrightarrow{\text{a.s.}} L,
        \]
        for some non-degenerate random variable $L$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition of arXiv:2509.02432, 'A threshold for online balancing of sparse i.i.d. vectors'] Let $(\ell,r,k,s)$ be integers satisfying $\ell\leq 0\leq r$,
$0\leq k\leq n$, and $s\geq 0$. Say that 
the pair $(A,\sigma)$ ``contains an $(\ell,r)$--spread
of size at least $s$ at time $k$'' if there exist collections of indices 
\[
    (i^{(\ell)}_j)_{j \in [s]} \quad \text{ and } \quad  (i^{(r)}_j)_{j \in [s]},
\]
such that: all $2s$ indices are distinct, and for every $1 \leq s' \le s$, it holds:
\[
    \langle {\rm row}_{i^{(\ell)}_{s'}}(A),\sigma\rangle_{[k]}=\ell; \quad \langle {\rm row}_{i^{(r)}_{s'}}(A),\sigma\rangle_{[k]}=r.
\]
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2509.02432, 'A threshold for online balancing of sparse i.i.d. vectors'

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] For the segment graphs having $N$ vertices, the characteristic polynomials $P_N$ of the adjacency matrices are subject to the following recurrence, 
$$P_0=1\quad,\quad P_1=x\quad,\quad P_{N+1}=xP_N-P_{N-1}$$
and are the well-known Chebycheff polynomials, enjoying many interesting properties. The corresponding numbers of loops and measures can be deduced from this.

[Defn 74 (Parabolic H\"older spaces) of arXiv:2510.22155, 'Random walks in space-time random media in all spatial dimensions: the full subcritical fl'] We define $C_c^\infty(\Psi_T)$ to be the set of functions on $\Psi_T$ that are restrictions to $\Psi_T$ of some function in $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^{d+1})$, in particular we do not impose that elements of $C_c^\infty(\Psi_T)$ vanish at the boundaries of $\Psi_T.$ 
  
    For $\alpha\in(0,1)$ we define the space $C^{\alpha,\tau}_\mathfrak s(\Psi_T)$ to be the completion of $C_c^\infty(\Psi_T)$ with respect to the norm $$\|f\|_{C^{\alpha,\tau}_\mathfrak s(\Psi_T)}:= \sup_{(t,x)\in \Psi_T} \frac{|f(t,x)|}{w(x)} + \sup_{|s-t|^{1/2}+|x-y|\leq 1} \frac{|f(t,x)-f(s,y)|}{w(x)(|t-s|^{1/2}+|x-y|)^{\alpha}}.$$
		For $\alpha<0$ we let $r=-\lfloor \alpha\rfloor$ and we define $C^{\alpha,\tau}_\mathfrak s(\Psi_T)$ to be the completion of $C_c^\infty(\Psi_T)$ with respect to the norm $$\|f\|_{C^{\alpha,\tau}_\mathfrak s(\Psi_T)}:= \sup_{(t,x)\in\Psi_T} \sup_{\lambda\in (0,1]} \sup_{\varphi \in B_r} \frac{(f,S^\lambda_{(t,x)}\varphi)_{L^2(\Psi_T)}}{w(x)\lambda^\alpha}$$ where the scaling operators are defined by 
		\begin{align}
			
			S^\lambda_{(t,x)}\varphi (s,y) = \lambda^{-d-2}\varphi(\lambda^{-2}(t-s),\lambda^{-1}(x-y)),
		\end{align}
		and where $B_r$ is the set of all smooth functions of $C^r$ norm less than 1 with support contained in the unit ball of $\mathbb R^{d+1}$.
title: Parabolic H\"older spaces

[Corollary C:containment-quadrangle of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Consider a weighted directed acyclic graph $G = (V, E, M)$, and we let $H = (W, E|_{W\times W}, M|_{W})$ be the subgraph of $G$ induced by a vertex set $W \subset V$. Consider vertices $x_1 \prec y_1$ and $x_2 \prec y_2 \in H$ and suppose that we have the following {\bf path-crossing} property:
\begin{itemize}
    \item Let $\tau$ be any path in $H$ from $x_1$ to $y_1$ and $\pi = (\pi_0, \dots, \pi_k)$ be any path in $G$ from $x_2$ to $y_2$. Then if $\pi_i \notin W$ for some $i \in \llbracket1,k-1 \rrbracket$, there are indices $i^- < i < i^+$ such that the vertices $\pi(i^-), \pi(i^+)$ are on the path $\tau$.
\end{itemize}
Then
$$
H(x_1; y_1) + G(x_2; y_2) \le G(x_1; y_1) + H(x_2 ; y_2).
$$

[Lemma 10 (Decay of the first derivatives of the decoupled flow) of arXiv:2605.03057, 'Uniform-in-time quantitative fluctuations of large scale interacting particle systems'] Assume Assumption~\ref{ass:coeff-level-new}. Fix $ x \in \R^d $, $ \mu \in \Ptwo $, let
$ X_t^{x,\mu} $ be the decoupled flow, and $\omega$ be the constant
defined in \eqref{eq:def-omega-uniform-time}. Then, the following hold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For every $ h \in \R^d $, the first spatial derivative
$ \partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] $ exists and solves
\begin{equation}

d\left( \partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] \right)
=
\partial_x b\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] dt
+
\partial_x \sigma\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] dB_t,
\end{equation}
with initial condition $\partial_x X_0^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right] =
h$. Moreover, for every $ p \in \mathcal P $ and all $t \ge 0$,
\begin{equation}

\E\left(
\abs{\partial_x X_t^{x,\mu}\left[ h \right]}^p
\right)
\le
e^{-\frac{p\kappa_p}{2} t} \abs{h}^p
\le
e^{-p\omega t} \abs{h}^p.
\end{equation}

\item[(ii)] For every $ v \in \R^d $, the Lions derivative
$ \partial_\mu X_t^{x,\mu}\left( v \right) $ exists and solves
\begin{align}

d\left( \partial_\mu X_t^{x,\mu}\left( v \right) \right)
&=
\Bigg(
\partial_x b\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\partial_\mu X_t^{x,\mu}\left( v \right)
+
\widetilde{\E}\left(
\partial_\mu b\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\left( \widetilde{X}_t^{v,\mu} \right)
\partial_x \widetilde{X}_t^{v,\mu}
\right)
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+
\widetilde{\E}\left(
\partial_\mu b\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\left( \widetilde{X}_t^{\widetilde{\xi},\mu} \right)
\partial_\mu \widetilde{X}_t^{\widetilde{\xi},\mu}\left( v \right)
\right)
\Bigg) dt
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+
\Bigg(
\partial_x \sigma\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\partial_\mu X_t^{x,\mu}\left( v \right)
+
\widetilde{\E}\left(
\partial_\mu \sigma\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\left( \widetilde{X}_t^{v,\mu} \right)
\partial_x \widetilde{X}_t^{v,\mu}
\right)
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+
\widetilde{\E}\left(
\partial_\mu \sigma\left( X_t^{x,\mu}, \mu_t^\mu \right)
\left( \widetilde{X}_t^{\widetilde{\xi},\mu} \right)
\partial_\mu \widetilde{X}_t^{\widetilde{\xi},\mu}\left( v \right)
\right)
\Bigg) dB_t,
\end{align}
with initial condition $\partial_\mu X_0^{x,\mu}\left( v \right) =
0$. Moreover, for every $ p \in \mathcal P $, there exists a constant
$ C_p > 0 $ such that, for all $t \ge 0$,
\begin{equation*}
\sup_{x,\mu,v}
\E\left(
\abs{\partial_\mu X_t^{x,\mu}\left( v \right)}^p
\right)
\le
C_p e^{-p\omega t}.
\end{equation*}
\end{enumerate}

[Proposition 33 of arXiv:2608.19065, 'Boundedly exchangeable graphs'] Let $d \geq 2$. The Euclidean and hyperbolic clustering tendencies
    satisfy:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item $\breve{p}_d(\alpha) < \overline{p}_d$ for all $\alpha > 0$,
        \item $\alpha \mapsto \breve{p}_d(\alpha)$ is strictly decreasing on $(0,\infty)$,
        \item $\breve{p}_2(\alpha) = \overline{p}_2 - \bigl(\sqrt{3}/(16\pi)\bigr)\alpha^2 + O(\alpha^4)$ as $\alpha \to 0^+$,
        \item $\breve{p}_2(\alpha) = (8/\pi)e^{-\alpha/2} + o(e^{-\alpha/2})$ as $\alpha \to \infty$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let P be a Markov kernel on a Polish space, reversible for probability measure mu. Let f be bounded measurable with integral f dmu=0. For every pair of starts x,y, couple two P-chains so that their time-k marginals are respectively P^k(x,.) and P^k(y,.). Assume a finite constant L uniformly bounds sum_(k>=0)|E[f(X_k)-f(Y_k)|X_0=x,Y_0=y]| for all x,y. Then F(x,y)=sum_(k>=0)E[f(X_k)-f(Y_k)|X_0=x,Y_0=y] is bounded and antisymmetric. If X has law mu and X_prime conditional on X has law P(X,.), then (X,X_prime) is exchangeable and E[F(X,X_prime)|X]=f(X). Equivalently, the summands are P^k f(x)-P^k f(y); uniform absolute summability of this series is the hypothesis of Lemma4.1. No pathwise ordering of the coupled chains is assumed.
Reversible kernel with stationary probability mu; bounded measurable centered f.
Both coupled time-k marginals are the required P^k laws for every initial pair.
Uniform finite bound on the sum of absolute conditional expected differences; measurability of the construction.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact tree identity, source-specific recurrence or explicit limiting obstruction Result: For any fixed clade shape chi of size m with positive model probability, its expected count is asymptotically n*p(chi)/m. The later fixed-clade variance bound is O(n), so Chebyshev gives probability O(1/n) that its count is zero. For any fixed finite list of distinct positive-probability shapes, all are therefore present with probability tending to1. It follows that the number of distinct shapes tends to infinity in probability, while it is always at most n-1 for internal clades. Check: For a count N with E N~c*n and Var N=O(n), P(N=0)<=Var N/(E N)^2=O(1/n). A finite union bound then proves the stated divergence without assuming independence between shapes. Obstruction: This supplies no growth rate: the constants and count estimates are not uniform over growing shapes. Largest repetitions and smallest missing shapes need joint tail information across an exponentially growing family.

[Theorem 71 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{Assumptions_Theta}, \ref{Assumptions_basic} and \ref{Assumptions_offcrit}
 hold. Choose $h \in [H]$, and a void interval $(\mathfrak{a},\mathfrak{b}) \subseteq [\hat{a}_h,\hat{b}_h]$ of the equilibrium measure. Assume that $\mathfrak{a}$ is a point separating a void from a band while $\mathfrak{b}$ is not (and is allowed to be $+\infty$). Then for any $\eps>0$, there exists $C>0$ depending only on $\eps$ and on the constants in the assumptions, such that
 \[
 \P\big[\exists i \in [N] \quad \big| \quad \ell_i \in [\N(\mathfrak{a}+\eps),\N\mathfrak{b}] \bigg] \leq C\exp\bigg(-\frac{\N}{C}\bigg).
\]
Similarly, if $\mathfrak{b}$ is a point separating a void from a band while $\mathfrak{a}$ is not (and is allowed to be $-\infty$), then
\[
\P\big[\exists i \in [N] \quad \big| \quad \ell_i \in [\N\mathfrak{a},\N(\mathfrak{b}-\eps)]\big]\leq C\exp\bigg(-\frac{\N}{C}\bigg).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop Spc*-levelwise-tensor of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let ${\mathcal{C}}$ be any $S$-cocomplete $T$-$\infty$-category. Then the levelwise tensor product ${\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}$ is again $S$-cocomplete, the map ${\mathcal{C}}\to{\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}$ induced by $(-)_+\colon\Spc\to\Spc_*$ is $S$-cocontinuous, and it moreover admits the following universal property: for every pointed $S$-cocomplete $T$-$\infty$-category ${\mathcal{D}}$, restriction defines an equivalence
    \[
        \ul{\textup{Fun}}^\textup{$S$-cc}_T({\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}\ul{\textup{Fun}}^\textup{$S$-cc}_T({\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}}).
    \]
    \begin{proof}
        In light of Proposition~(prop:univ-prop-*-cc-param of the paper), it will be enough to construct an equivalence ${\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}{\mathcal{C}}_*$ under ${\mathcal{C}}$. For this, we consider the commutative diagram
        \[
            \begin{tikzcd}
                {\Spc}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}_{\hphantom{*}}\arrow[d]\arrow[r] & {\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}_{\hphantom{*}}\arrow[d]\\
                {\Spc}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}_*\arrow[r] & {\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{C}}_*
            \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        with horizontal maps induced by $(-)_+\colon\Spc\to\Spc_*$ and vertical maps induced by $(-)_+\colon{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{C}}_*$. We claim that the right-hand vertical map and the bottom horizontal map are equivalences; this will then complete the proof of the corollary.

        To see that the bottom horizontal map is an equivalence, it suffices to show that ${\Spc}\otimes{\mathcal{D}}\to{\Spc_*}\otimes{\mathcal{D}}$ is invertible for every (non-parametrized) pointed cocomplete ${\mathcal{D}}$, or equivalently that the induced map between corepresented functors on $\CAT_\infty^\text{cc}$ is an equivalence. By the defining property of the tensor product, the latter amounts to saying that we have an equivalence
        \begin{equation}
            {-}\circ(-)_+\colon{\textup{Hom}}(\Spc_*,{\textup{Fun}}^\text{cc}({\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}}))\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}{\textup{Hom}}(\Spc,{\textup{Fun}}^\text{cc}({\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}}))
        \end{equation}
        for any cocomplete ${\mathcal{E}}$. By [CLL_Global]*{Corollary 4.1.10${}^{\textup{op}}$}, the full subcategory of ${\textup{Fun}}({\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}})$ spanned by the functors preserving the initial object is pointed, whence so is the smaller subcategory ${\textup{Fun}}^\text{cc}({\mathcal{D}},{\mathcal{E}})$ as it still contains the initial object. Thus, applying the Proposition~(prop:univ-prop-*-cc-param of the paper) for $S=T=1$ shows that $((eq:univ-prop-pted of the paper))$ is an equivalence.

        For the vertical map, we similarly compare corepresented functors on fiberwise cocomplete $\infty$-categories. Arguing as above, this reduces us to invertibility of
        \[
            {\textup{Hom}}({\mathcal{C}}_*,{\textup{Fun}}^\text{cc}(\Spc_*,-)\circ{\mathcal{D}})\to
            {\textup{Hom}}({\mathcal{C}},{\textup{Fun}}^\text{cc}(\Spc_*,-)\circ{\mathcal{D}}),
        \]
        and applying the above levelwise shows that ${\textup{Fun}}^\text{cc}(\Spc_*,-)\circ{\mathcal{D}}$ is pointed. The claim therefore follows from the special case $S=\core T$ of the proposition.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop Spc*-levelwise-tensor of arXiv:2608.28504
