[Lemma Upcrossing_lemma of arXiv:2608.08299, 'Non-linear optimal stopping with Bermudan strategies: the infinite horizon case'] Let $\rho$, depending on the first index only, satisfy properties (i),(iv),(v),(vii),(viii),(ix),(x), and the normalisation property $\rho_0[1]=1$. 
\\
   Let $X$ be a \textbf{non-negative} \emph{$(\Theta, \rho)$}-supermartingale.
    Let $0<a<b<+\infty$ ( $a,b \in \mathbb{Q}$).
    We define, by induction, the following stopping times: 
   $ T_0:=0 $
 and for all $k\in \mathbb{N}^*$, 
 \begin{align*}
S_k&:=\inf\{n \geq T_{k-1}:X_n \leq a\},  \\
T_k&:=\inf\{n \geq S_{k}:X_n \geq b\},
\end{align*}  
 with the convention that $inf \emptyset = + \infty$.
 \\ 
 Let $N_{\infty}([a,b])$ be the number of upcrossings of the interval $[a,b]$. 
  Let $N_{n}([a,b])$ be the number of upcrossings of the interval $[a,b]$ before time $n$.
  \\ Then, 
   \begin{compactenum}
   \item[(i)] $\rho_{S_k \wedge n}[\mathbb{I}_{\{T_k \leq n\}}]\leq (\frac{a}{b})\mathbb{I}_{\{S_k \leq n\}}$.
   \item[(ii)] $\rho_0[\mathbb{I}_{\{T_k<+\infty\}}]\leq (\frac{a}{b})^k$.
    \item[(iii)] 
  $P(N_{\infty}([a,b])< +\infty ) =1$.
   \end{compactenum}

Let Omega be open, delta_n tend to zero, and complex nodal functions f_n on Omega intersect delta_n Z^2 converge uniformly at grid nodes on every compact set to continuous f. Let D_n(c) be the counterclockwise trapezoidal edge-integral sum around cell c. If, for every axis-aligned rectangle R compactly contained in Omega and grid rectangle approximants R_n tending to R, the signed sum of D_n(c) over cells of R_n tends to zero, then f is holomorphic. Exact interior-edge cancellation and bounded-perimeter quadrature give zero limiting rectangle integrals; a local rectangular primitive proves holomorphicity. Deriving this summed estimate for an actual square-bond event observable remains unproved here.

[Lemma lem:one-hole of arXiv:2608.20480, 'When Clean Data Hurts: Learning with Monotone \\ Corruptions Beyond Binary Classification'] Let $F_i:O_i\hookrightarrow\Omega_r$, $i\in[d]$, where each $O_i$ is a union of complete petals, and put
\[
    Y
    =
    \{y\in\Omega_r:\bigcup_iF_i[y]\text{ is injective}\}.
\]
Exactly one of the following holds.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Roman*),leftmargin=2.5em]
    \item The raw union $\bigcup_iF_i$ is injective. Fix a bijection $u$ extending it. For $y\in Y$, if $u^{-1}(y)=\infty$, then every profile is internal; if $u^{-1}(y)=e_{B,a}$, then precisely the tables containing the $B$-petal use the common profile $(B,a)$, while all remaining tables are internal.

    \item The raw union is not injective. Either $|Y|\le1$, or $|Y|=q$ and there are one direction $B$, a bijection $\theta:Y\to\mathbb{F}_q$, and constants $\beta_i\in\mathbb{F}_q$ for the tables containing $E_B$ such that, for every $y\in Y$, tables hiding $B$ are internal and a table seeing $B$ uses profile $(B,\theta(y)-\beta_i)$, with exponent zero interpreted as internal.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: One-hole synchronization

body: [Definition 1 (Reversible process) of arXiv:2506.09462, 'Transition Path Theory For L\'{e}vy-Type Processes: SDE Representation and Statistics'] The process \(X_t\) in \eqref{eqn:SDE} is said to be \textbf{reversible} if its generator \(\mathcal{L}\) in \eqref{generator} coincides with the corresponding time reversal operator \(\overleftarrow{\mathcal{L}}\) in \eqref{reversalgenerator}, i.e., \(\mathcal{L} = \overleftarrow{\mathcal{L}}\). Consequently, this implies that \(\overleftarrow{q} = 1 - q\).

body:
Pointwise identity. Let Ω ⊂ R^n be open, x the position vector, and u ∈ C^2(Ω). Then, everywhere in Ω,
   div( (x·∇u) ∇u − (1/2)|∇u|^2 x ) = (x·∇u) Δu − ((n−2)/2) |∇u|^2.
The same holds almost everywhere for u ∈ H^2_loc(Ω) (all terms are then in L^1_loc). Replacing x by x − x_0 for any fixed x_0 gives the same identity (translation invariance).

Integrated form (Rellich). Let Ω be a bounded open set with Lipschitz boundary, ν the outward unit normal, dS surface measure, and u ∈ C^2(Ω̄), or u ∈ H^2(Ω) with the boundary integrals read through the L^2(∂Ω) traces of ∇u. Then
   ∫_Ω (x·∇u) Δu dx = ((n−2)/2) ∫_Ω |∇u|^2 dx + ∫_∂Ω [ (x·∇u)(∂_ν u) − (1/2)|∇u|^2 (x·ν) ] dS.

Dirichlet case. If in addition u = 0 on ∂Ω (trace sense), then the tangential gradient vanishes on ∂Ω, ∇u = (∂_ν u) ν there, and the boundary term collapses to (1/2) ∫_∂Ω (x·ν) (∂_ν u)^2 dS. If moreover −Δu = λu in Ω, then
   λ ∫_Ω u^2 dx = (1/2) ∫_∂Ω (x·ν) (∂_ν u)^2 dS,
the Rellich formula expressing a Dirichlet eigenvalue by a boundary integral; equivalently 2λ||u||^2_{L^2(Ω)} = ∫_∂Ω (x·ν)(∂_ν u)^2 dS. For a domain star-shaped with respect to the origin (x·ν ≥ 0 on ∂Ω) the right side is nonnegative term by term. The same computation with −Δu = f(u), u = 0 on ∂Ω, is the Pohozaev identity.

Where it fails / hypotheses that matter. The integrated form needs enough regularity to give ∇u a boundary trace: u ∈ H^2(Ω) (or C^2 up to the boundary). A Dirichlet eigenfunction on a Lipschitz domain that is not convex (a re-entrant corner) need not belong to H^2(Ω), and the identity is then not available in this form without a separate justification. Without u = 0 on ∂Ω the tangential gradient contributes and the simplified boundary term (1/2)∫(x·ν)(∂_ν u)^2 is wrong: the full bracket must be kept. The sign of x·ν is not fixed for a general domain, so conclusions that use x·ν ≥ 0 (star-shapedness, Pohozaev-type nonexistence) fail otherwise. In dimension n = 2 the interior term ((n−2)/2)∫|∇u|^2 vanishes. The identity is for the Laplacian; for a variable-coefficient operator div(A∇u) extra terms involving x·∇A appear.
pointwise form: u ∈ C^2(Ω) (or H^2_loc, a.e.)
integrated form: Ω bounded with Lipschitz boundary, u ∈ C^2 up to the boundary or u ∈ H^2(Ω)
eigenvalue formula: additionally u = 0 on ∂Ω and −Δu = λu in Ω

Fix \(r\ge1\), and let $d_1, \dotsc, d_r$ be specified in \eqref{eq:defn_d_i}, $\w_1, \dotsc, \w_r$ be deterministic orthonormal vectors, and the spiked model $H^{(D)}_N$ be the $N \times N$ random matrix defined in \eqref{eq:defn_H^D_N}.

Let
\[
\lambda_1^{(D)}\ge \lambda_2^{(D)}\ge \cdots \ge \lambda_N^{(D)}
\]
be the eigenvalues of \(H_N^{(D)}\), and let \(\x_k^{(D)}\) be a unit eigenvector associated with \(\lambda_k^{(D)}\). Fix \(i\in\{1,\dots,r\}\) and let \(k\ge1\) be independent of \(N\). Let $\beta = 1$ for the GOE case and $\beta = 2$ for the GUE case. Put
\begin{equation}
  \Theta^{(i)}
  =
  (\theta_1,\dots,\theta_{i-1},\theta_{i+1},\dots,\theta_r),
  \qquad
  \mathcal G^{(\beta)}_{(r-1),i^c}:=\mathcal G^{(\beta)}_{\Theta^{(i)}},
\end{equation}
where \(\mathcal G^{(\beta)}_{\Theta^{(i)}}\) is the Airy-Green function from Proposition~\ref{pro:multispike_airy_green}. Let \(s_{\beta, k}^{(i)}\) be the unique solution in
\[
\bigl(
a_{\beta,k}^{(\Theta^{(i)})},
a_{\beta,k-1}^{(\Theta^{(i)})}
\bigr), \qquad a_{\beta,0}^{(\Theta^{(i)})}:= +\infty,
\]
of
\begin{equation} 
  \mathcal G^{(\beta)}_{(r-1),i^c}(x)=\theta_i.
\end{equation}
Then, as \(N\rightarrow\infty\), we have the joint convergence in distribution
\begin{align}
 N^{2/3}\bigl(\lambda_k^{(D)}-2\bigr) \Longrightarrow {}& s_{\beta,k}^{(i)},  & N^{1/3}\bigl|\langle \w_i,\x_k^{(D)}\rangle\bigr|^2
\Longrightarrow {}&
-\frac{1}{(\mathcal G^{(\beta)}_{(r-1),i^c})'\!\bigl(s_{\beta, k}^{(i)}\bigr)}.
\end{align}
Moreover, for any finite $K$, \eqref{GOE_Airy Green fun} holds jointly for $k = 1, 2, \dotsc, K$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 19 (Replicated Jacobi transfer) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Let \(\Sigma\in\operatorname{Sym}_r^{++}(\R)\) and
\(\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)\) with \(t_1\cdots t_r\neq0\).  For the
replicated phase
\[
 F_{\Sigma,\boldsymbol t}(\boldsymbol x)
 =
 -\frac12
 \sum_{a,b=1}^r
 (\Sigma^{-1})_{ab}\langle x_a,x_b\rangle
 +
 i\sum_{a=1}^rt_aP(x_a),
\]
the principal Koszul differential is
\[
 i\sum_{a=1}^rt_a\,\mathrm dP_m(x_a)\wedge.
\]
It is regular, and the twisted de Rham module has exact rank
\[
 \mu_r=(m-1)^{rd}.
\]
Every replicated polynomial insertion, in particular
\(\prod_{a=1}^rP(x_a)\), has exact Jacobi coordinates rational in
\(\Sigma,\boldsymbol t\), and the coefficients of \(P\).  After choosing
Jacobi, de Rham, and thimble frames as in
\cref{thm:thimble-factorisation}, now in \(rd\) variables, denote the
resulting rational frame change and thimble period matrix by
\(B_{\mathrm{Jac}}^{(r)}\) and
\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{th}}^{(r)}\).  The period matrix against the Jacobi
normal-form frame then factors as
\[
 \Pi_{\mathrm{Jac}}^{(r)}
 =
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{th}}^{(r)}
 B_{\mathrm{Jac}}^{(r)}.
\]
For chosen cycles it is left-multiplied by their Betti coordinate matrix,
as in \eqref{eq:correct-global-factorisation}.

[Definition 8 (Top-AE and diff-AE manifolds) of arXiv:2608.29427, '\small Positive mass and rigidity \\ for asymptotically flat tangent bundles'] A manifold \(M^n\) is called \emph{topologically asymptotically Euclidean} (top-AE), respectively \emph{differentially asymptotically Euclidean} (diff-AE), if there exists a compact set \(K\Subset M\) such that
	\[
	M\setminus K=M_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup M_k,
	\]
	where each end \(M_a\) is homeomorphic, respectively diffeomorphic, to
	\[
	\mathbb R^n\setminus\overline{B_{R_a}}
	\]
	for some \(R_a>0\).
	\par Moreover, the corresponding homeomorphisms or diffeomorphisms are assumed to be restrictions of maps
	\[
	\varphi_a:M_a\longrightarrow\mathbb R^n
	\]
	whose expression in polar coordinates is
	\[
	\varphi_a(p)=(r,q),
	\]
	with \(r\) increasing monotonically toward infinity along the end. More precisely, if
	\[
	K_1\Subset U\subset K_2,
	\]
	where \(U\subset M_a\) is open, then every point of \(M_a\setminus K_2\) has strictly larger \(r\)-coordinate than every point of \(U\setminus K_1\). See \cite[Definition 1.1]{AsadiFathiLakzian2025}.
title: Top-AE and diff-AE manifolds

[Theorem thm:prime-filter-amplification of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Fix integers $d\geq1$ and $t\geq0$, and a shift-stable $d$-chart.  For all
sufficiently large integers $h$ and every admissible pair
$(\theta,\boldsymbol\ell)$, the value
$V_{\theta,\boldsymbol\ell}(h)$ in (equation eq:amplifier-value of the paper) is realized as
$|hC|$ by a primitive $(d+1+t)$-set obtained from $B_\theta$ by $t$ cyclic suspensions,
and
\begin{equation}
 |\mathcal R(h,d+1+t)|
 \gg_{d,t,I_1,\ldots,I_t}
 \left(\frac h{\log h}\right)^t\frac{N_h^2}{E_h}.
\end{equation}
If, throughout the shift window,
\begin{equation}
 c_0 h^d\leq |(h-J)B_\theta|\leq C_0 h^d
\end{equation}
for fixed $0<c_0<C_0$, then every value used to prove
(equation eq:prime-suspension-quantitative of the paper) lies in a fixed interval
\begin{equation}
[c_{d,t,\mathbf I}h^{d+t},C_{d,t,\mathbf I}h^{d+t}],
\end{equation}
where these constants also depend on the fixed bounds $c_0,C_0$ in
(equation eq:amplifier-macroscopic-seed of the paper).

Every counted value admits a witness $C$ satisfying
\begin{align}
 \mathcal H_C(z)
 &=\mathcal H_{B_\theta}(z)\prod_{i=1}^t[\ell_i]_z,
 \\
 \mathcal K_C(z)
 &=\mathcal K_{B_\theta}(z)\prod_{i=1}^t(1-z^{\ell_i}),
 \\
 \mathcal B_C(\xi,z)
 &=\mathcal B_{B_\theta}(\xi,z)\prod_{i=1}^t(1+\xi z^{\ell_i}),
 \\
 r_q(C)&=r_q(B_\theta)+\#\{i:\ell_i\leq q\}
 \qquad(q\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}),
 \\
 \operatorname{ndiam}(C)&=\left(\prod_{i=1}^t\ell_i\right)\operatorname{ndiam}(B_\theta).
 
\end{align}
If the seed projective coordinate ring is Cohen--Macaulay, then projective
Cohen--Macaulayness and Cohen--Macaulay type are preserved.  Since every
$\ell_i<h$, maximal degree-$h$ active rank propagates from the seed to $C$.

DRAFT source-to-need comparison. Ahlberg-Hoffman arXiv:1609.02447, A1 and Theorem 2.1, apply to atomless iid weights with finite E[min(X1,X2,X3,X4)^2]; all deterministic diverging endpoint sequences have origin-hit probabilities tending to zero. Maximizing over each finite S_R pair set therefore yields q_R->0, but supplies no adaptive union decay rate. Dembin-Elboim-Peled arXiv:2204.02332v5 Theorem 1.2 instead needs absolute continuity, a finite exponential moment, and more than 40 limit-shape extreme points; its bound C log^2(D+2)/D^(1/16) is insufficient for summing 32R^2-4R pairs. Theorem 1.3 bounds the union over common-height pairs ((-n,s),(n,s)), s in Z, by C log^2(n)/n^(1/24), already handling that restricted selector family. An arbitrary bigeodesic through 0 is not proved to have witnesses in that family. Source checks and these failed substitutions do not prove P0117. body: [Lemma 3.1 in the first version of arXiv:2512.19063, 'Sharp Decoupling Inequalities for the Variances and Second Moments of Sums of Dependent Ra'] Consider a sequence of possibly dependent random variables $d_{1},..,d_{n}$, and a decoupled sequence $e_{1},..,e_{n}$ given a $\sigma$ -algebra $\mathcal{G}$. Then we have the following equality $\mathbb{E}\left(\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n}e_{i}\right)^{2}=\mathbb{E}\left[\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n}e_{i}-\mathbb{E}\left(\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n}e_{i}\Big|\mathcal{G}\right)\right]^{2}+\mathbb{E}\left[\mathbb{E}\left(\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n}e_{i}\Big|\mathcal{G}\right)\right]^{2}$

body: [Theorem 24 (KLT optimality \citep{huang1963block,goyal2001transform}) of arXiv:2608.25188, 'Transforms for LLM Quantization:\\ The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design'] Let $x\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma)$ with $\Sigma\succ0$ be coded by an orthogonal transform $U$ followed by independent high-rate quantizers under the optimal logarithmic allocation at total rate $R$, every coordinate receiving positive rate. (Positive definiteness is needed for the logarithmic allocation: a singular $\Sigma$ puts a KLT coordinate at zero variance, so the interior allocation no longer applies and \Cref{prop:waterfill} governs instead.) Among orthogonal $U$, the transform coding gain $G_{\mathrm{TC}}(U)$ of \eqref{eq:codinggain} is maximized, and the distortion minimized, by $U=U_{\mathrm{KLT}}$, the eigenbasis that diagonalizes $\Sigma$.

body:
[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2609.00087, 'Translational tiles without spectra\\ in finite abelian $p$-groups'] Let $H$ and $L$ be finite abelian groups.  Let $A\subset H$, and for each
$y\in L$ let $C_y\subset H$ satisfy
\[
 A\oplus C_y=H.
\]
Put
\[
 R=\bigcup_{y\in L}(C_y\times\{y\})\subset H\times L,
 \qquad q=|C_y|=\frac{|H|}{|A|}.
\]
For a nontrivial $\chi\in\widehat H$, define
\[
 W(\chi)=\sum_{y\in L}\widehat{\1_{C_y}}(\chi),
 \qquad
 D=\{\chi\ne0:W(\chi)=0\}.
\]
Let $\mathcal G_D$ be the Cayley graph on $\widehat H$ in which distinct
$u,v$ are adjacent when $u-v\in D$.  If $\mathcal G_D$ has no clique of
size $q$, then $R$ tiles $H\times L$ but is not spectral.

[Dfn 119 (continuous-time smoothed coefficients) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Analogously to Definition~\ref{d:sp.smooth}, we define the spatially smoothed continuous-time coefficients
	\[\srrr(t,y)\equiv
	\frac{\overline{\varrho_{\rrr,t}*\sphi}(y)}
		{\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)}\,,\quad
	\swww(t,y)\equiv
	\frac{\varsigma_{\www,t}*\sphi(y)}
		{\varsigma_t*\sphi(y)}\,,\]
as well as
	\begin{align*}
	\sB(t,y)
	&\equiv
	\frac{\overline{\varrho_{D,t}*\sphi}(y)}
		{\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)}
	\equiv
	p'(t)^{1/2} \cdot \sbbb(t,y)\,,\\
	\sV(t,y)
	&\equiv
	\frac{\overline{\varrho_{V,t}*\sphi}(y)}
		{\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)}
	\equiv
	p(t) \cdot \svvv(t,y)\,,\\
	\sU(t,y)
	&\equiv
	\frac{\overline{\varrho_{U,t}*\sphi}(y)}
		{\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)}
	\equiv
	\Big[ p(t) \cdot t p'(t) \Big]^{1/2}
		\cdot \suuu(t,y)\,.
	\end{align*}
Analogously to Definition~\ref{d:t.smooth}, we define the 
temporally smoothed continuous-time coefficients
	\beq
	
	\tB(t,y)
	\equiv
	\int_{\R} \tphi(s) \sB(t-s,y)\,ds
	= \tE\Big[ \sB(t-\sss,y)\Big]
	\eeq
and similarly $\tV$, $\tU$, $\trrr$, $\twww$. We define also the scaled coefficients
	\begin{align*}
	\tbbb(t,y)
	&\equiv\frac{\tB(t,y)}
		{p'(t)^{1/2} }\,,\\
	\tvvv(t,y)
	&\equiv \frac{\tV(t,y)}{p(t) } 
	\,,\\
	\tuuu(t,y)
	&\equiv
	\frac{\tU(t,y)}{[ p(t)
		\cdot t p'(t)]^{1/2}} \,.
	\end{align*}
and abbreviate $\tGam\equiv(\tbbb,\tvvv,\tuuu)$. Likewise, analogously to Definition~\ref{d:t.smooth.variant}, we define $\TGam\equiv(\Tbbb,\Tvvv,\Tuuu)$ as well as $(\iB,\iV,\iU,\ir,\iw)$.
We then let
	\begin{align*}
	\sF(t,y)
	&\equiv\Big\{ \sV+2\sU+\srrr\Big\}(t,y)\,,\\
	\tF(t,y)
	&\equiv\Big\{ \tV+2\tU+\trrr\Big\}(t,y)\,,\\
	\iF(t,y)
	&\equiv\Big\{ \iV+2\iU+\ir\Big\}(t,y)\,,
	\end{align*}
analogously to \eqref{e:sp.smoothed.F.N}, \eqref{e:temp.smoothed.F.N}, and \eqref{e:ideal.smoothed.F.N}.

[Proposition prop:SCinf-characterizations of arXiv:2608.11931, '\texorpdfstring{Nonlinear parabolic characterizations of stochastic completeness at infini'] Let $G$ be a graph.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \(G\) satisfies \hyperref[def:SC-infinity]{\textup{{(SC\textsubscript{$\infty$})}}}{}.
\item For one (equivalently, all) \(\lambda>0\),
      \(S_\lambda=\operatorname{id}+\lambda\Delta\) is injective on \(\ell^\infty(X)\).
\item For one (equivalently, all) \(\beta>0\), every
      \(0\le h\in\ell^\infty(X)\) satisfying
      \((\Delta+\beta)h\le0\) vanishes.
\item Bounded solutions of the heat equation are uniquely determined
      by bounded initial data.
\item $G$ satisfies the weak Omori--Yau maximum principle.
\end{enumerate}

    and
    \[
    \lim_{K\to \infty} \sup_{\substack{1\leq n\leq L\\mathbb{N}\in[N_K^\downarrow,N_K^\uparrow]}} \left\vert \binom{n}{2}(\mathfrak{v} + \mathfrak{m}) - K^2\sum_{i,j\in\mathbb N_0} p_{i,j}^-(n, N)\nu_K(i,j)\right\vert = 0.
    \]

the model is a continuum rotationally invariant Riemannian first passage percolation on the PLANE
the model lies in the class for which Basu-Sidoravicius-Sly (2023) established their fluctuation estimates for passage times and geodesics
rotational invariance is used; the lattice Z^2 has none, so the result does not transfer as stated
the value of epsilon is not stated in the abstract

MECHANISM, in the authors' words: the argument 'uses fluctuation estimates for passage times and geodesics derived in Basu, Sidoravicius and Sly (2023) together with a multi-scale argument to establish that the geodesic exhibits disorder chaos, i.e., upon resampling a small fraction of the underlying randomness, the updated geodesic has on average a small overlap with the original one; this, established at a large number of scales, leads to a polynomial improvement of the variance bound.'
SO THE CAMPAIGN'S TARGET SHAPE IS THE RIGHT SHAPE: geodesic disorder chaos telescoped over many scales is the only route that has ever produced a polynomial gain. What it has never produced is a LATTICE gain, and the reason is that rotational invariance is consumed.
118 pages, 23 figures. Vladas Sidoravicius died in 2019; the authorship is as listed on arXiv.
SOURCE: arXiv:2604.01214v1, official arXiv API record retrieved by lane P4 on 2026-08-22; no journal reference as of that date.
VERIFICATION STATUS: theorem-checked-against-source at the level of the authors' abstract, which states the model class, the conclusion, the dependency and the mechanism. The 118-page proof was NOT read, so nothing is asserted here about the internal hypotheses, the size of epsilon, or which steps consume rotational invariance.
title: Basu-Sidoravicius-Sly (arXiv:2604.01214, submitted 1 April 2026): for a class of ROTATIONALLY INVARIANT RIEMANNIAN first passage percolation ON THE PLANE, the variance of the passage time is O(n^{1-epsilon}) for some epsilon > 0. This is the first polynomial improvement over the n/log n barrier in any variant of first-passage percolation - and it is a continuum, rotationally invariant result, NOT a lattice result: on Z^d the best known upper bound is still n/log n.

body:
[Definition 13 ($\vartheta$-self-concordant barrier) of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Fix $\vartheta\ge1$. Let $N\ge1$, and let
$\Omega\subset\R^N$ be convex and relatively open in its affine hull,
that is, in the smallest affine subspace containing $\Omega$. Set
	\[
	\mathsf V_\Omega
	:=\operatorname{span}\{z-z':z,z'\in\Omega\}.
	\]
	Let $\Psi:\Omega\to\R$ be convex and $C^3$ along line segments in
	$\Omega$. Define the local seminorm
	\[
		\|h\|_{\Psi,z}^2:=\mathrm D^2\Psi(z)[h,h],
		\qquad z\in\Omega,\quad h\in\mathsf V_\Omega.
	\]
	We call such a convex function $\Psi$ a \emph{$\vartheta$-self-concordant barrier} for
	$\Omega$ if $\Psi(z)\to\infty$ as $z$ approaches the relative boundary
	of $\Omega$ and, for every $z\in\Omega$ and $h\in\mathsf V_\Omega$,
	\begin{equation*}
		\tag{SC}
		\bigl|\mathrm D^3\Psi(z)[h,h,h]\bigr|
		\le 2\|h\|_{\Psi,z}^3.
	\end{equation*}
	It must also satisfy the barrier-parameter bound for all $h\in \mathsf V_\Omega$
	\begin{equation*}
		\tag{$\mathrm{BP}_\vartheta$}
		|\mathrm D\Psi(z)[h]|
		\le \sqrt{\vartheta}\,\|h\|_{\Psi,z}.
	\end{equation*}
title: $\vartheta$-self-concordant barrier

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple...'] We consider the conformal loop ensemble (CLE) with the parameter $\kappa=4$, the critical value at or below which the loops are simple and do not intersect each other or the domain boundary. We show that the loops of a $\CLE_4$ uniquely determine a conformally invariant, local, and geodesic metric so that the metric ball growth from the domain boundary coincides with the uniform exploration of Werner and Wu. This metric was previously constructed in unpublished work of Sheffield, Watson, and Wu. Our approach differs in that we show that the metric arises as the renormalized limit of the graph metric on $\CLE_\kappa$ loops as $\kappa \downarrow 4$. In this first paper in a series of three, we prove that the subsequential limits exist and define a non-trivial conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ which is local and such that the metric ball growth from the boundary is given by the uniform exploration of Werner and Wu. In subsequent work, we will show that the subsequential limit exists as a true limit.

[Lemma l:der-psi of arXiv:2411.16913, 'Entropies of the Poisson distribution as functions of intensity: ``normal'' and ``anomalou'] For all $\alpha>0$ and $\lambda>0$, the function $\psi(\alpha, \lambda)$ introduced by (equation psifunction of the paper) is well defined and continuously differentiable in two variables, moreover, the partial derivatives can be computed as follows:
    \begin{gather}

    \sum_{i=0}^\infty (p_i(\lambda))^\alpha \log p_i(\lambda),
    \\
    
    \frac{\partial}{\partial \lambda} \psi(\alpha, \lambda) = \alpha e^{-\alpha \lambda} \sum_{i=0}^\infty (i-\lambda) \frac{\lambda^{\alpha i - 1}}{(i!)^\alpha},
    \end{gather}
    where $p_i(\lambda) = e^{-\lambda} \frac{\lambda^i}{i!}$.

body:
[Theorem th:probageod of arXiv:2601.05361, 'Noise sensitivity in last-passage percolation'] There exists $0<c,C<\infty$ such that for all $n\ge1$ and $v \in [0, n]^2 \cap {\mathbb{Z}}^2$ such that $|v|_1 \leq n$ then
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item
$\displaystyle{
{\mathbb{P}}\big(v \in \pi(0,n\mathbf{e}_+)\big) \leq C \exp \left( - c \frac{|v_2 - v_1|^3}{|v|_1^2} \right)};
$

\item
$
\displaystyle{{\mathbb{P}}\big(v \in \pi(0,n\mathbf{e}_+)\big) \leq C \left(\frac{ \log |v|_1}{|v|_1} \right)^{2/3}}.
$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem th:probageod of arXiv:2601.05361

[Cor skorokhod of arXiv:2605.29073, 'Volterra clocks and their pure-jump limits: \\hitting times of curved boundaries'] With everything as in
	Corollary~(cor:inf_sup of the paper), consider the Skorokhod map $	x^n \mapsto (l^n,\hat{x}^n)$ given by $l^n(t) := -\inf_{s \le t} x^n(s)$
	and $\hat{x}^n(t):= x^n(t) + l^n(t)$.
	If each $\tau^n$ is continuous, then $ l^n = -\underline{\phi}^n \circ \tau^n $ and $\hat{x}^n
	= \hat{\phi}^n \circ \tau^n$ with
	$(\underline{\phi}^n, \tau^n)
	\to (\underline{\phi}, \tau)$ and $(\hat{\phi}^n, \tau^n)
	\to (\hat{\phi}, \tau)$ in $D^\circ[0,T]$.
    If $\sup_{t \in D(\tau^n)}
	\Delta \tau^n(t) \to 0$, the same holds up to $\varepsilon^n(t)$ as in Corollary (cor:inf_sup of the paper). In particular, when $\sup_{t \in D(\tau^n)}
	\Delta \tau^n(t) \to 0$, we have $l^n \to -\underline{\phi} \circ \tau$
	in $(D[0,T], M_1)$ and $\hat{x}^n$ satisfies (equation eq:jump_range of the paper) with limiting ranges $I_t=\hat{\phi}([\tau(t-), \tau(t)])$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem berry of arXiv:2411.06006, 'Mixing time of the torus shuffle'] Let $Y_1, \dots, Y_N$ be independent random vectors in ${\mathbf R}^2$ with mean zero,
  and let $S = Y_1 + \cdots + Y_N$. Suppose that the covariance matrix $\Sigma$, of $S$, is
  invertible. Let $Z$ be a centered normal random vector with variance matrix  $\Sigma$.
Then for any convex set $U \subset {\mathbf R}^2$, we have
\begin{align}
    \left \vert { \mathbb P}(S \in U) - { \mathbb P}(Z \in U) \right \vert \leq C(2)^{\frac{1}{4}}\gamma,
    
\end{align}
where $C$ is a universal constant and $\gamma = \sum_{q=1}^{N}{\mathbf E}\left[\abs{\Sigma^{-1/2}Y_q}_2^3\right]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a Hilbert space $H$, with scalar product $<x,y>$ and norm $||x||=\sqrt{<x,x>}$, the norms, or lengths, are subject to the parallelogram identity
$$||x+y||^2+||x-y||^2=2(||x||^2+||y||^2)$$
and the scalar products can be recovered from lengths via the polarization identity:
$$<x,y>
=\frac{||x+y||^2-||x-y||^2+i||x+iy||^2-i||x-iy||^2}{4}$$
Also, we can say that two vectors are orthogonal when their scalar product is zero.
title: Unnumbered proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'

	\begin{equation} \langle f, M_{\lambda}({\sf e}) \rangle = \int_0^1  \int_{0}^{{\sf e}_x}    \frac{2}{R(x,y)-L(x,y)}  f\Big( R(x,y)-L(x,y) \Big)\1_{S(x,y)\geq \lambda} \mathrm{d} y \mathrm{d} x.\end{equation}
	{\tiny $\blacksquare$ } Almost surely, $\langle f, M_{\lambda}({\sf e}) \rangle$ is well defined and finite,\\
	{\tiny $\blacksquare$ } $M_{\lambda}({\sf e})$ is a positive (random) measure on $[0,1]$ (equipped with the Borelian $\sigma$-field).\\
	{\tiny $\blacksquare$ } The measure $M_{\lambda}({\sf e})$ has a.s. infinite total mass. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem lemma:calcul_ps_Mlambda of arXiv:2507.00737

body: [Lem 3 of arXiv:2606.24584, '2606.24584'] Let $D\in \ds$ with eigenvalues $1=\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_n \in \mathbb{C}$, and let $\alpha\in\mathbb{C}$ be a complex number. Then the eigenvalues of $D-\alpha J_n$ are $1-\alpha, \lambda_2, \dots, \lambda_n$.
title: Lem 3 of arXiv:2606.24584

body:
[Coro indepasympt of arXiv:2601.20502, 'Optimal matching under size priority'] Let $(\mathbb{T},o)$ be as in Theorem~(th:decay of the paper) and let $(G_n,o_n)_{n\geq 0}$ be a sequence uniformly rooted finite graphs such that $(G_n,o_n)$ converges locally to $(\mathbb{T},o)$. Assume in addition that if $o_n'$ is a uniform edge chosen independently from $o_n$, then $(G_n,o_n')$ converges locally to an independent copy of $(\mathbb{T},o)$. 
    Then $(G_n,M_{\mathrm{opt}}(G_n),o_n)$ and $(G_n,M_{\mathrm{opt}}(G_n),o_n')$
    converge to two independent copies 
    of $(\mathbb{T},o,\mathbb{M}_{\mathrm{opt}})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Coro indepasympt of arXiv:2601.20502

[Theorem 2 (Bessel-zero obstruction for \({}_0F_1\)-gamma deformations) of arXiv:2606.22066, 'A Bessel-zero obstruction to hyperbolic complete monotonicity of noncentral chi-square den'] Let \(a,b>0\) and \(\theta\ge0\).  Then
\begin{equation}
p_{a,b,\theta}\in\HCM
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\theta=0.
\end{equation}
Equivalently, every positive \({}_0F_1\)-gamma deformation of a gamma density fails to be hyperbolically completely monotone. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Bessel-zero obstruction for \({}_0F_1\)-gamma deformations

[Theorem main-thm of arXiv:2608.23202, 'Locally finite Fixed points of Branching Brownian Motion'] Let $\lambda \geq \sqrt{2}$ and $\Pi$ be a point process. Then $\Pi$ is a fixed point of BBM with drift $\lambda$ in the sense of Definition (def-fixed-point of the paper) if and only if there exists a $[-\infty, \infty)$-valued random variable $S$ independent of $\widetilde{\mathcal E}_\infty^\lambda$ such that 
\[ \Pi \overset{d}{=} \widetilde{\mathcal E}_\infty^\lambda (\cdot - S). \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem main-thm of arXiv:2608.23202

[Theoaen of arXiv:2608.25865, 'Instability of Böhm's Einstein metrics'] If $(g_i)$ denotes a sequence of Böhm metrics on $S^{k+1}\times S^l$ or $S^{k+l+1}$, with $k,l\geqslant 2$, $k+l\leqslant 8$, and if $\nu_i$ denotes the number of negative eigenvalues of the Lichnerowicz Laplacian associated with $g_i$ (called the \textit{index}), then
$$\nu_i\underset{i\to+\infty}{\longrightarrow}{+\infty}.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered theoAen of arXiv:2608.25865, 'Instability of Böhm's Einstein metrics'

body: [Lemma 21 of arXiv:2506.15736, 'Coming down from infinity for coordinated particle systems'] Suppose a $\Lambda$-coalescent with death according to $D(dz)$ has an infinite number of particles enter before time $t_0$, i.e. particles enter at random times $(s_n)_{n \in \N}$ where $s_n \leq t_0$ for all $n \in \N$. Denote the block counting process of this coalescent by $(\mathring{N}(t))_{t \geq 0}$. Then there is a coupling such that $N(t_0) \leq \mathring{N}(t_0)$ where $(N(t))_{t\geq 0}$ is the block counting process of the $\Lambda$-coalescent with killing according to $D(dz)$ starting with infinitely many particles.
title: Lemma 21 of arXiv:2506.15736

Let X be a centered Gaussian measure on a real separable Hilbert space K with covariance operator Q_X, and let (P_u) be its Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup, P_u h(x) = E[h(e^{-u} x + sqrt(1 - e^{-2u}) X)]. For a test function h in C_b^2(K), the infinite-dimensional Stein equation Tr(Q_X D^2 U(x)) - <x, DU(x)>_K = h(x) - E[h(X)] is solved, uniquely up to an additive constant, by U(x) = -int_0^infinity (P_u h(x) - E[h(X)]) du (Shih); substituting t = e^{-2u}, U(x) = -int_0^1 (1/(2t)) (E[h(sqrt(t) x + sqrt(1 - t) X)] - E[h(X)]) dt.

[Lemma 23 (It\^o's formula) of arXiv:2606.08776, 'Approximation of certain stochastic integrals with anticipating integrands'] Assume $f: [0,1]\times\R\times\R^{K} \to  \R$ such that the partial derivatives $f_x, f_t, \nabla_y f, f_{xx}, \nabla_y f_x$ exist, are continuous,
and polynomially bounded in $(x,y)$ uniformly in $t$.  Assume that $L=(L_1,\dots,L_K)$ is a  random variable such that  $L_i \in \DD_{1,4}$.
Then for $0\le s < t \le 1$ one has, a.s.,
\begin{align*}
   f(t, X_t,L)
& = f(s, X_s,L) + \int_s^t f_u(u, X_u,L) du \\
&\quad  +\int_s^t f_x(u, X_u,L) \sigma(X_u) \delta W_u \\
&\quad  +\half \int_s^t f_{xx}(u, X_u,L) \sigma^2(X_u) du \\
&\quad  + \int_s^t\nabla_y f_x(u, X_u,L) \sigma(X_u) \cdot D_uL du.
\end{align*}
title: It\^o's formula

Let $f\in L^1(\mathbb T)$, $x\in\mathbb T$ and $s\in\mathbb C$. (Dini) If $\int_0^{1/2}\frac{|f(x+t)+f(x-t)-2s|}{t}\,dt<\infty$, then the symmetric partial sums converge: $S_Nf(x)\to s$. In particular, if $f$ is Holder continuous at $x$ of some order $\alpha>0$ (i.e. $|f(x+t)-f(x)|\le C|t|^\alpha$ for all small real $t$, of either sign), or differentiable at $x$, or more generally if the two-sided Dini integral $\int_{|t|\le1/2}\frac{|f(x+t)-f(x)|}{|t|}\,dt$ is finite, then $S_Nf(x)\to f(x)$ (the two-sided condition dominates the symmetric one with $s=f(x)$, by the triangle inequality). (Riemann localization) If $f,g\in L^1(\mathbb T)$ agree on an open interval containing $x$, then $S_Nf(x)-S_Ng(x)\to0$; so convergence or divergence of a Fourier series at $x$ depends only on the behaviour of $f$ near $x$, even though the coefficients depend on $f$ globally.
f integrable on the circle
Dini: the integral of |f(x+t)+f(x-t)-2s|/t over (0,1/2) is finite; mere continuity at x is NOT enough
the Holder / two-sided Dini conditions must control t of both signs
symmetric partial sums (the statement is about S_N, not about arbitrary summation orders)

[Corollary 70 of arXiv:2609.02850, 'Canonical-row Chern flow on Bott--Samelson towers:\\ realizable-volume models for Schubert'] For every $w\in S_n$, the support of $G_w$ is $M^\natural$-convex.  In
particular,
\begin{equation}
 \Supp(G_w)=\Newt(G_w)\cap\ZZ^n.
\end{equation}
The positive-parameter polynomial $\Groth_w^+(x;\beta)$ is SNP in
$\ZZ^{n+1}$.  Thus Conjecture~5.5 of Monical--Tokcan--Yong holds.

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.26565, 'A Horizon-Free Extrinsic Penrose Inequality'] The end $\mathcal E_+$ is \emph{asymptotically flat} if, after a rigid motion, there
are $R_0>0$, $\tau>1/2$, a compact set $K\subset S$, and a smooth function
$\psi:\mathbb R^2\setminus B_{R_0}\to\mathbb R$ such that
\[
 S_+=\{(y,\psi(y)):|y|>R_0\},
\]
where $S_+$ is the component of $S\setminus K$ representing
$\mathcal E_+$. Along this component, the chosen outward normal is
\[
 \nu_S(y,\psi(y))
 =\frac{(D\psi(y),-1)}{\sqrt{1+|D\psi(y)|^2}}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 |D\psi(y)|+|y||D^2\psi(y)|
 =O(|y|^{-\tau}).
\]
With this orientation, the \emph{extrinsic mass of the distinguished end} is
\begin{equation}
 m_+(S)=\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac1{2\pi r}
 \int_{|y|=r}y\cdot D\psi\,d\mathcal H^1.
 
\end{equation}
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.26565

[Corollary 19 (Spectral consequences) of arXiv:2608.04824, 'Strong Convergence for a General Class of Random Matrix Models'] On the probability-one event of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] If \(Q=Q^*\) is a fixed self-adjoint \(*\)-polynomial, then
\[
 d_{\rm H}\bigl(\spn(Q(X_n,X_n^*)),
                    \spn(Q(c,c^*))\bigr)\longrightarrow0.
\]
\item[(2)] For every fixed \(*\)-polynomial \(Q\),
\[
 d_{\rm H}\bigl(\operatorname{sv}(Q(X_n,X_n^*)),
                    \operatorname{sv}(Q(c,c^*))\bigr)\longrightarrow0.
\]
\item[(3)] If \(Q(c,c^*)\) is invertible, then \(Q(X_n,X_n^*)\) is invertible
for all sufficiently large \(n\), and
\[
 \|Q(X_n,X_n^*)^{-1}\|\longrightarrow\|Q(c,c^*)^{-1}\|.
\]
\item[(4)] For every \(1\leq\kappa\leq d\),
\[
 \|X_{\kappa,n}\|\longrightarrow2\sigma_\kappa.
\]
\end{enumerate}

[Prop prop-vmexist of arXiv:2411.14350, 'Randomized Geodesic Flow on Hyperbolic Groups'] [bh-book] Given $\delta \geq 0$, there exists $a > 1$ such that if
	$(X,d)$ is $\delta-$hyperbolic, then for any base-point $o$,
	a visual metric $d_v $
	with parameter $a>1$ exists on $\partial X$ with respect to the base-point $o$.
	Further, for any $o' \in X$, let $d_v'$ be a visual metric on $\partial X$
 with respect to the base-point $o'$ and
	with parameter $a>1$. Then $d_v'$
	is equivalent (as a metric) to $d_v$.
	
	There exists a natural topology on $\hat{X} = X \cup \partial X$ such that
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item $X$ is open and dense in $\hat X$,
		\item $\partial X$ and $\hat{X}$ are compact if $X$ is proper,
		\item the subspace topology on $\partial X$ agrees with that given by $d_v$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop prop-vmexist of arXiv:2411.14350

body:
[Lemma 30 of arXiv:2506.17045, '\LARGE{On bivariate Archimax copulas: Level sets, mass distributions and related results}'] Let $I_1,I_2,I_3$ be open sub-intervals of $\mathbb{R}$ and let $\iota \colon I_1 \rightarrow I_2$ be a function whose left-hand derivative $D^-\iota$ exists. Moreover, let $\eta \colon I_2 \rightarrow I_3$ be an arbitrary function. Then the following assertions hold:
      \begin{itemize}
          \item[$(i)$] If $\eta$ is strictly decreasing and convex, then
          $$
          D^-\eta^{-1}(z) = \frac{1}{D^+\eta(\eta^{-1}(z))}
          $$
          holds for every $z \in I_3$, whereby $\eta^{-1}$ denotes the inverse function of $\eta$.
          \item[$(ii)$] If $D^-\eta$ exists and $\iota$ is a non-decreasing function, then
          $$
          D^-(\eta\circ\iota)(t) = D^-\eta(\iota(t)) \cdot D^-\iota(t)
          $$
          holds for every $t \in I_1$.
        \item[$(iii)$] If $D^-\eta$ exists and $\iota$ is a non-increasing function, then
          $$
          D^-(\eta\circ\iota)(t) = D^+\eta(\iota(t)) \cdot D^-\iota(t)
          $$
          holds for every $t \in I_1$.
      \end{itemize}
title: Lemma 30 of arXiv:2506.17045

body:
[Theorem result2 of arXiv:2607.01463, 'Two Multi--Draw Coupon Collector models with different retention rules'] Consider the  $d$ coupon collector's problem (d--CCP), where in each run we keep \textbf{the least} collected coupon so far. Let $T_{N,1}$ be the number of trials until all $N$ different types of coupons, which are uniformly distributed, are collected (at least once). Then, as $N\rightarrow \infty$
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}[T_{N,1}]=
\frac{N}{d}\log N
+\left(\frac{\gamma}{d}+
C_d\right)N
-
\frac{d-1}{2d}\log N
+
D_d
+
\mathcal{O}\!\left(\frac{\log N}{N}\right),

\end{equation}
where,
\begin{equation}
C_d:
=
\int_0^1
\left(
\frac{1}{1-(1-x)^d}-\frac{1}{dx}
\right)\,dx,

\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
D_d:
=
\frac{2d^2-3d+3-2\gamma \left(d-1\right)}{4d}
-\frac{d-1}{2}C_d.

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let {e_i : i in I} be an orthonormal basis of a Hilbert space H. Then for every x in H, x = sum over i of <x, e_i> e_i (with at most countably many nonzero terms, converging in norm), and ||x||^2 = sum over i of |<x, e_i>|^2. More generally <x, y> = sum over i of <x, e_i> times the conjugate of <y, e_i>. Conversely, an orthonormal family for which ||x||^2 = sum over i of |<x, e_i>|^2 holds for every x is an orthonormal basis.
H is a Hilbert space

[Theoremi thm_main_directed of arXiv:2604.04672, 'Connected components and topological ends of stationary planar forests'] Assume additionally that with probability one, $G$ is oriented with out-degree $1$, non-empty and all directed infinite path $(\pi_n)_{n\geq0}$ in $G$ satisfies $\lim_{n\to\infty}\pi_n\cdot e_2=+\infty$, where $e_2\coloneqq (0,1)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\cdot$ denotes the standard scalar product. Then, exactly one of the following holds almost surely:
        \begin{itemize}
            \item $G$ is a single one-ended tree, or
            \item $G$ consists of infinitely many disjoint two-ended trees.
        \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition prop:ito-centered-lyapunov-differential of arXiv:2605.20697, 'Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for \\ Second-Order Consensus-Based Optimization'] Let \(p\geqslant2\), and assume the conditions of (assump:centered-decay of the paper).
Let
\[
    L_p(t):=L_p(\mathcal X_t^J,\mathcal V_t^J)
\]
denote the pathwise centered Lyapunov functional defined in
(equation eq:random-Lp-def of the paper) for \(p>2\), and in (equation eq:random-L2-def of the paper) for \(p=2\).

Define the local martingale \(M_{p,t}:=J^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^J M_{p,t}^j\) by
\begin{equation}
    \mathrm d M_{p,t}^j
    :=
    \begin{cases}
        \displaystyle
        2\left\langle \hat Z_t^j,\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}\right\rangle
        +
        \frac5\gamma
        \left\langle Y_t^j,\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}\right\rangle,
        & p=2,\\[1.2em]
        \displaystyle
        p|\hat Z_t^j|^{p-2}
        \left\langle \hat Z_t^j,\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}\right\rangle
        +
        \frac m\gamma |Y_t^j|^{p-2}
        \left\langle Y_t^j,\mathrm d M_t^{j,\mathrm{center}}\right\rangle,
        & p>2.
    \end{cases}
\end{equation}
Then there exists a local martingale \(M_{p,t}\) such that, in the sense of semimartingale differentials,
\begin{equation}
    \mathrm d L_p(t)
    \leqslant
    -\lambda_p L_p(t)\,\mathrm d t+\mathrm d M_{p,t},
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
    \lambda_p
    :=
    \begin{cases}
        \displaystyle
        \frac{\min\{v_1,v_3\}}{c_2^{(2)}},
        & p=2,\\[1.2em]
        \displaystyle
        \frac{p\mu_{\mathrm{gap},p}}{4\gamma},
        & p>2.
    \end{cases}
\end{equation}
Here, for \(p=2\),
\[
    v_1:=\frac1{m\gamma}+\frac3{\gamma^3}-K_\sigma,
    \qquad
    v_3:=\frac{2\gamma}{m}-\frac3\gamma,
\]
and \(c_2^{(2)}\) is the upper norm-equivalence constant associated with \(\psi_2\).

Moreover, when \(p>2\), the stronger componentwise estimate holds:
\begin{equation}
    \mathrm d L_p(t)
    \leqslant
    -\widehat\lambda_Y
    \left(\frac1J\sum_{j=1}^J |Y_t^j|^p\right)\mathrm d t
    -\widehat\lambda_Z
    \left(\frac1J\sum_{j=1}^J |\hat Z_t^j|^p\right)\mathrm d t
    +
    \mathrm d M_{p,t},
\end{equation}
where
\begin{align}
    \widehat\lambda_Y
    &:=
    \frac1\gamma
    \left[
        C_{\mathrm{pos}}
        -
        \gamma\left(\frac2m+\frac1{\gamma^2}\right)
        \left(\frac4\gamma\right)^{p-1}
        +
        \frac{m(p-1)}{\gamma^2}
    \right],
    \\
    \widehat\lambda_Z
    &:=
    p\left(\frac\gamma m+\frac1\gamma\right)
    -
    \left(
        \frac{p-1}{2m}\gamma+\frac{p-1}{4\gamma}
    \right)
    -
    \frac{2m(p-1)}{p\gamma}
    -
    \Lambda_p\sigma^{\frac{2p}{p-2}}\gamma^{\frac2{p-2}}\,,
    
\end{align}
where $C_{\mathrm{pos}} = 1-\frac{3\mu_{\mathrm{gap},p}}{16} - \frac{m(p-1)(p-2)}p$ as defined from (equation eq:Cpos-def of the paper). Under (assump:centered-decay of the paper), these coefficients satisfy
\begin{equation}
    \widehat\lambda_Y
    \geqslant
    \lambda_p
    \left(
        a_p+\frac{m(p-1)}{p\gamma}
    \right),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
    \widehat\lambda_Z
    \geqslant
    \lambda_p
    \left(
        1+\frac{m}{p\gamma}
    \right).
\end{equation}

body: [Corollary 3.12 of arXiv:2603.27659, 'Operator Norm Bounds for Multi-leg Matrix Tensors and Applications to Random Matrix Theory'] With $Y$ the partial-trace matrix of partial permutations $\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k}\in\mathcal{P}^{\prime}([m])$ applied to contractions $A_{1},\ldots,A_{m}\in M_{N}(\mathbb{C})^{\otimes k}$, $N^{M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})}\leq\max_{\|A_{1}\|,\ldots,\|A_{m}\|\leq 1}\|Y\|\leq N^{C(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})}.$ The lower bound is attained by the same permutation tensors as in Theorem 3.11. Here, for the graph $G_{\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k}}$ of the permutations, $M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})$ is the maximum over blue-edge configurations of the number of directed cycles, and $C(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})=\min_{G^{\prime}}R_{G^{\prime}}$, the minimum over full simple partial graphs $G^{\prime}$ (partial graphs keeping every rectangle and containing no directed cycle for any blue-edge configuration) of the number $R_{G^{\prime}}$ of colored edges removed to obtain $G^{\prime}$ (Definition 2.1).

[Proposition prop:sharp-lri-4d of arXiv:2608.23135, 'Graph distance and effective resistance of the random walk trace in four and five dimensio'] ([ShiraishiWatanabe2026])

Let $S^1$ and $S^2$ be independent simple random walks on $\mathbb Z^4$ started from
$0$.  For $k\ge1$, set
\begin{align*}
        f(n,k)=
        \mathbb P\bigl(S^1[0,n]\cap S^2[kn,(k+1)n]\ne\emptyset\bigr).
\end{align*}
Then, uniformly in the range of $k$ used in this paper,
\begin{equation}

        f(n,k)=
        \frac{1}{2\log n}
        \log\left(1+\frac{1}{k^2+2k}\right)
        \left\{1+O\left(\frac{1}{k(\log n)^{3/25}}\right)\right\}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.03497, 'Connective Constants on Nested Fractal Graphs'] The limits of the rooted and uniform self-avoiding walk counts exist and
are equal:
\[
  \mu
  :=
  \lim_{n\to\infty}c_n^{1/n}
  =
  \lim_{n\to\infty}u_n^{1/n}
  =
  \inf_{n\ge1}u_n^{1/n}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
  1\le\mu\le D-1<\infty.
\]
Thus \(\mu\) is the connective constant of \(F_\infty\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Proposition 42 (Conditional LAN for coarser windows) of arXiv:2604.10792, 'Variable-Length Markov Chains on Finite Quivers: Boundary-Window Identifiability, Exact De'] Fix $m<r$ and assume exact depth $r$ at $\theta_0$. Then $Z^{(m)}$ is a deterministic function of the hidden finite-state Markov chain $Z^{(r)}$. Suppose, in addition, that the projected family satisfies the hypotheses of a standard finite hidden-Markov-model LAN theorem appropriate to this deterministic-emission setting, including the required fixed hidden support, irreducibility/mixing, smooth dependence of the positive hidden transitions on $\theta$, and any domination or identifiability conditions used by the invoked theorem. Then the experiment generated by $Z^{(m)}$ is LAN at $\theta_0$ on every fixed tangent block $T\subset T_{\theta_0}\Theta$. This statement provides only bare LAN for the coarse observation scheme and does not by itself yield the factorized shift representation required in \cref{ass:lan}.

[Theorem 27 (Block contraction theorem) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Under the standing fixed-threshold application, fix \(\delta_0\geq c_0\).
There are constants
\[
        T_{\mathrm{blk}}<\infty,\qquad
        \eta_{\mathrm{blk}}>0,\qquad
        \theta_{\mathrm{blk}}>0,\qquad
        \Lambda_*<\infty
\]
with the following property.  The constants
\(\eta_{\mathrm{blk}},\theta_{\mathrm{blk}},\Lambda_*\) depend only on
\(K,\delta_0,N,\sigma\).  The start-time threshold \(T_{\mathrm{blk}}\) may
additionally depend on the fixed Bamler tail data \(T_B(c_0)\) and
\(\eps_B^{c_0}\) for the given flow.

Let \(p(\tau)\) be a parabolically rescaled \(\delta_0\)-large block starting
at \(S\geq T_{\mathrm{blk}}\), fix a torus fibration \(\pi:M\to S^1\), and put
\[
        q(1)=p(1),\qquad r(1)=\overline{q(1)}.
\]
Suppose that \(r(1)\) is Riemannian and, with
\[
 b=\|q(1)-r(1)\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,r(1))},
 \qquad d=d_{\TT^2}(r(1)),
\]
one has
\[
        b<\eta_{\mathrm{blk}},\qquad
        d<\theta_{\mathrm{blk}},\qquad
        \BG_N(r(1);\Lambda_*).
\]
Equivalently, \((q(1),r(1))\) is an admissible stage start in the sense of
Definition~\ref{def:admissible-stage-start}, with constants
\(\Lambda_*,\eta_{\mathrm{blk}},\theta_{\mathrm{blk}}\).
Then the invariant Ricci flow \(r\) and the Ricci--DeTurck flow \(q\) relative
to it exist on \([1,100]\).  At the rescaled endpoint, put
\[
        q^+(1)=100^{-1}q(100),\qquad
        \rho^+=100^{-1}r(100),\qquad
        r^+(1)=\overline{q^+(1)},
\]
and set
\[
        b^+=\|q^+(1)-r^+(1)\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,r^+(1))}.
\]
Then \(r^+(1)\) is Riemannian and
\begin{equation}
        b^+\leq\tfrac12 b,\qquad
        d_{\TT^2}(r^+(1))<\theta_{\mathrm{blk}},\qquad
        \BG_N(r^+(1);\Lambda_*).
\end{equation}
Thus the same admissible-start conditions hold at the restart.  The ordinary
Ricci flow corresponding to \(q\) is \(p\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 12 of arXiv:2606.03534, 'Construction and simulation of a path-valued model of dendrite development'] The \textit{graph representation} of a measure $\mu \in \mathcal{N}_\mathcal{S}^{\#}$ is a graph $G=(V,E)$ describing the spatial embedding of $\mu$, defined as follows. Let 
    \begin{align*}
        V &= \Big\{ x \in X \, \Big| \, \exists \, (\omega,a) \in [\mu] \text{ s.t. } x = \omega(0) \text{ or } x=\hat{\omega}  \Big\} \,, \\
        E &= \Big\{ (x,y) \in V \times V \, \Big| \, \exists \, (\omega,a) \in [\mu] \text{ s.t. } \omega(0)=x \text{ and } \hat{\omega}= y  \Big\} \,.
    \end{align*}
    To an edge $(x,y) \in E$ we assign the corresponding path $\omega_{xy} \in \mathcal{W}$ to be the element $(\omega_{xy},a) \in [\mu]$ with $\omega_{xy}(0)=x$ and $\hat{\omega}_{xy} = y$. 
    This network is fully determined by $\mu$ and so defines a mapping $\mu \mapsto (V,E)$ from $\mathcal{N}_\mathcal{S}^\#$ into a space of networks. Denote this mapping by $G(\mu)$.

body:
[Theorem 41 of arXiv:2609.03070, 'Variants of order semicontinuity in Banach lattices'] Let $F$ be an AM-space. Then:
\item[(i)] $F$ is semicontinuous if and only if it isometrically embeds as a regular sublattice of $C\left(K\right)$, for some compact Hausdorff space $K$.
\item[(ii)] $F$ is demicontinuous if and only if it isomorphically embeds as a regular sublattice of $C\left(K\right)$, for some compact Hausdorff space $K$. In this case it is topologically semicontinuous.
\item[(iii)] $F$ is pointwise demicontinuous if and only if it injectively embeds as a regular sublattice of $C\left(K\right)$, for some compact Hausdorff space $K$.\medskip

    Moreover, ``regular'' can be replaced with ``order dense'', while $K$ can be assumed extremally disconnected.

[Defn degree of arXiv:2608.29914, 'Fixed points in abstract provability structures'] The \emph{degree} $d(\triangle)$ of a one-variable meet APS term $\triangle v$ is recursively defined as follows: 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $d(v)=0$, 
    \item $d(\Box\triangle_0)=d(\triangle_0)$, 
    \item $d(\boxtimes\triangle_0)=d(\triangle_0)+1$, 
    \item $d(\triangle_0\land\triangle_1) = \max\{d(\triangle_0),d(\triangle_1)\}$. 
\end{enumerate}

[Corollary 4 (Selected chart pullbacks) of arXiv:2608.06393, 'Intrinsic Tangential Hadamard Differentiability of Rough-BSDE Solution Maps'] Let $B$ be a Banach space and let
$J:B\to\mathbb T_{\mathbf x}^p$ be continuous and linear. Suppose a
set-theoretic representation $\mathfrak r(Ju)=(\mathbf Z_{Ju},a_{Ju})$ is
defined for $u\in B$, is bounded in the budget
\eqref{eq:representative-budget} on bounded subsets of $B$, and is
ray-homogeneous:
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf Z_{\lambda\tau}=D_{1,\lambda*}\mathbf Z_\tau,
 \qquad
 a_{\lambda\tau}=\lambda a_\tau,
 \qquad
 D_{1,\lambda}(v,w)=(v,\lambda w).
\end{equation}
Define $\chi(0)=\mathbf x$ and, near zero,
\begin{equation}
 \chi(u):=\mathbf x^{1;\mathbf Z_{Ju},a_{Ju}}.
\end{equation}
Then the pullback $\mathcal S\circ\chi:B\to\mathcal X$ is Fr\'{e}chet
differentiable at zero, with
\begin{equation}
 D(\mathcal S\circ\chi)(0)=A_{\mathbf x}\circ J.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Selected chart pullbacks

[Theorem eq:wiener_hopf_factors of arXiv:2604.08889, 'Matrix Representations for Scale Functions of Spectrally Negative Lévy Processes with Rati'] Let $\{W_t\}_{t\geq 0}$ be a Brownian motion with variance $\sigma^2>0$, drift $d\in \mathbb{R}$ and starting point $W_0=0$. 
Let $U$ be a stopping time, and for fixed $\lambda+q > 0$ let $E\sim {\rm Exp}(\lambda+q)$, independent of $\{W_t\}_{t\geq 0}$. 
Then, $W_U-\min_{t\in [0,E]}W_{U+t}$ and $W_{U+E}-\min_{t\in [0,E]}W_{U+t}$ are independent and exponentially distributed random variables with respective rates
\begin{equation}
\omega_{\lambda+q} = \frac{\sqrt{d^2 + 2\sigma^2 (\lambda+q)} + d}{\sigma^2}, \qquad \eta_{\lambda+q} = \frac{\sqrt{d^2 + 2\sigma^2 (\lambda+q)} - d}{\sigma^2}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Wiener-Hopf factorisation for Brownian motion

[Lemma lem:hkexpansion of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] As $\delta \to 0$, we have the following expansions
$$
\mu^{\rm loop}_{\mathbb{D}}
(t_{\gamma}>\delta, \indx_{\gamma}(0) \text{ odd})= (\zeta_{\Delta/2}(0)-\frac{1}{2}\zeta_{\Delta_{1/2}/2}(0))\left(\log (\delta^{-1})-\gamma_{\rm EM}\right) + \zeta'_{\Delta/2}(0)-\frac{1}{2}\zeta'_{\Delta_{1/2}/2}(0) +o(1)$$
and
$$
\mu^{\rm loop}_{\mathbb{D},g_{\rm cone}}
(t_{\gamma}>\delta, \indx_{\gamma}(0) \text{ odd})
= (\zeta_{\Delta_2/2}(0)-\frac{1}{2}\zeta_{\Delta/2}(0))\left(\log (\delta^{-1})-\gamma_{\rm EM}+2\log 2\right) + \zeta'_{\Delta_2/2}(0)-\frac{1}{2}\zeta'_{\Delta/2}(0) +o(1)$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:hkexpansion of arXiv:2604.15146

[Definition 2 (Complex array normal distribution) of arXiv:2608.21551, '\bf Sparse Separable Factor Analysis in the Complex Domain with an Application to Local Fi'] Let $\Mcal\in\CC^{c_1\times\cdots\times c_d}$, and let $\Vb_j\in\CC^{c_j\times c_j}$ be Hermitian positive definite for $j=1,\ldots,d$. A $d$-mode array $\Ycal$ follows a proper complex array normal distribution with mean $\Mcal$ and mode-specific covariance matrices $\Vb_1,\ldots,\Vb_d$ if
\begin{align}
  
  \operatorname{vec}(\Ycal)
  \sim
  \CC\Ncal_{\prod_{j=1}^d c_j}
  \left(
    \operatorname{vec}(\Mcal),
    \Vb_d\otimes\cdots\otimes\Vb_1
  \right),
\end{align}
where $\otimes$ denotes the Kronecker product. We write $\Ycal\sim \CC\Ncal_{c_1\times\cdots\times c_d} (\Mcal,\Vb_1,\ldots,\Vb_d)$.
title: Complex array normal distribution
Prop T2latching of arXiv:2608.30031

[Corollary cor:tensor-bounds of arXiv:2606.27073, 'Retention Profiles and KL Contraction Bounds in Finite Markov Chains'] Under the hypotheses of Proposition~(prop:tensor of the paper):
\begin{enumerate}
  \item $M_P \le \max(M_1, M_2)$.

  \item If both $\pi_1, \pi_2$ are uniform on $n_1, n_2$ states respectively:
  \[
    \bar{r}_P = \frac{\bar{r}_1 \log n_1 + \bar{r}_2 \log n_2}{\log(n_1 n_2)}.
  \]

  \item If $P_1 = P_2$ with uniform $\pi$, then $\bar{r}_P = \bar{r}_1$ and $L(P) \ge L(P_1)$.
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Cor 17 (\cite{MR51275}; see also \cite{MR317760}) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Take $A,b,C,d$ as in Theorem~\ref{t:hoffman} with $(b,d)\in F(A,C)$.
Let $B(M_0)$ denote the ball of radius $M_0$ in $\R^n$, centered at the origin.
\begin{enumerate}[a.]
\item  Suppose $(b',d')\in F(A,C)$, and
suppose further that the (nonempty) sets
$S_{A,C}(b,d)$ and $S_{A,C}(b',d')$ are both contained in $B(M_0)$.
Then
	\[d_H\Big(S_{A,C}(b,d),S_{A,C}(b',d')\Big)
	\le c\left\| \begin{pmatrix}
	b-b'\\d-d'\end{pmatrix}\right\|_2
	\]
where $c$ is a finite constant depending only on $A,C,M_0$.
\item 
Now suppose we have $(A,b,C,d)'$ of the same dimensions,
with $(b',d')\in F(A',C')$. 
Suppose further that the (nonempty) sets
$S\equiv S_{A,C}(b,d)$ and $S'\equiv S_{A',C'}(b',d')$ are both contained in $B(M_0)$.
Then, for any $x'\in S'$ there exists $x\in S$ with
	\[\|x-x'\|_2
	\le c \left\| \begin{pmatrix} A-A'\\ C-C'\\
	b-b'\\d-d'\end{pmatrix}\right\|_2\,,
	\]
where $c$ is a finite constant depending only on $A,C,M_0$, and on the right-hand side we treat $A$ and $C$ as vectors of length $mn$ and $qn$ respectively.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{proof}
Suppose $x'\in S'$. Then
	\[
	Ax'-b
	=[A'+(A-A')] x'- [b' + (b-b')]
	\le (A-A')x'-(b-b')\,,
	\]
from which it follows that
	\[
	\|(Ax'-b)_+\|
	\le \| [(A-A')x'-(b-b')]_+\|
	\le \|A-A'\|_\textup{op} M_0 + \|b-b'\|\,.
	\]
Similarly, we can bound
	\[
	\|Cx'-d\|
	\le \|C-C'\|_\textup{op} M_0 + \|d-d'\|\,.
	\]
The operator norm is bounded by the Frobenius norm, so the conclusion of part~\eqref{i:hoffman.semicty} follows.
Part \eqref{i:hoffman.rhs} then follows from part~\eqref{i:hoffman.semicty}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{MR51275}; see also \cite{MR317760}

body:
[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2605.24445, 'Matrix concentration inequalities for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains'] \label[lemma]{lem:tropp_step}
Let $P$ be a Markov operator on a Polish metric space $(\Omega,d)$. Let $G\colon \Omega \to \Hm$ and $x \in \Omega$ such that $PG(x) = 0$. Let $A \in \Hm$ such that $G(y)^2 \preceq A^2$ for any $y \in \supp P(x,\cdot)$.
Then, for any deterministic $H \in \Hm$,
\[
P \tr\exp\left( H + G \right)(x) \le  \tr\exp\left( H +  2 A^2 \right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 14 of arXiv:2605.24445
